prs.title: fix(core): suppress warning when transient subdirectories disappear during scan
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes spurious `Warning: Could not read directory ...: ENOENT` log messages during workspace folder structure scans when transient subdirectories (such as `proper-lockfile` lock directories like `projects.json.lock`) are removed between parent directory enumeration and child directory traversal.

### Key Changes
- **Transient Subdirectory `ENOENT` Handling (`packages/core/src/utils/getFolderStructure.ts`)**: Preserve the `debugLogger.warn` and `null` return when the root directory itself does not exist (`currentPath === rootPath && error.code === 'ENOENT'`), and preserve warnings for genuine permission errors (`EACCES` / `EPERM`) on subdirectories, while silently skipping subdirectories that disappear mid-scan with `ENOENT`.

prs.title: fix(core,cli): emit ACP retry progress updates and enforce retry delay cap and model fallback
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #29805.

In ACP (`--acp`) mode, when a model request hits a 429 quota or capacity exhaustion error, the CLI previously failed to emit any ACP progress signals while retrying, could treat multi-hour quota reset messages (`Your quota will reset after 14h31m12s`) as transient capacity exhaustion and sleep for hours, and did not persist model fallback transitions for non-interactive/ACP sessions or background utility models (`flash-lite`).

This PR addresses all three root causes:
1. **ACP Retry Progress Notifications**: Adds session attribution (`sessionId`) to `RetryAttemptPayload` and subscribes `acpSession.ts` to `CoreEvent.RetryAttempt`, forwarding retry progress as `agent_thought_chunk` updates with structured `_meta.retry` metadata (`attempt`, `maxAttempts`, `delayMs`, `error`, `model`) so ACP clients have visibility during retries.
2. **Retry Delay Budget Enforcement**: Excludes explicit quota-reset messages (`quota will reset after`) from transient capacity retry promotion and enforces `maxDelayMs` (and `MAX_RETRYABLE_DELAY_SECONDS`) in `retryWithBackoff`, promoting excessive retry delays to `TerminalQuotaError` so fallback is triggered immediately instead of sleeping for hours.
3. **Persistent Non-Interactive & Utility Model Fallback**: Resolves the failed model's own policy chain in `handleFallback` when a utility model (such as `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`) fails, enables `onPersistent429` fallback in `BaseLlmClient` and automatic fallback in `handleFallback` for non-interactive/ACP sessions, and preserves `ModelAvailabilityService` terminal states in `activateFallbackMode` so subsequent calls in the session skip exhausted models immediately.

## Details

- `packages/core/src/utils/events.ts`: Add optional `sessionId` to `RetryAttemptPayload`.
- `packages/core/src/core/baseLlmClient.ts`, `packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts`, `packages/core/src/core/client.ts`, `packages/core/src/tools/web-fetch.ts`: Include `sessionId` when emitting `CoreEvent.RetryAttempt`, enable `onPersistent429` in `BaseLlmClient`, and respect `getFallbackOverride` during retries.
- `packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.ts`: Subscribe to `CoreEvent.RetryAttempt` for the active session and emit `agent_thought_chunk` updates with `_meta.retry`; unsubscribe on `dispose()`.
- `packages/core/src/utils/retry.ts` & `packages/core/src/utils/googleQuotaErrors.ts`: Export `MAX_RETRYABLE_DELAY_SECONDS` and enforce `maxDelayMs` budget for both silent capacity retries and `RetryableQuotaError` backoff delays.
- `packages/core/src/fallback/handler.ts` & `packages/core/src/config/config.ts`: Resolve failed utility model policy chains, enable automatic fallback in non-interactive sessions when no UI handler is registered, and avoid resetting `ModelAvailabilityService` or overwriting the active chat model when a non-active utility model falls back.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29805

## How to Validate

- Run unit and integration tests:
  - `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/retry.test.ts src/fallback/handler.test.ts src/availability/autoRoutingFallback.integration.test.ts src/config/config.test.ts src/config/flashFallback.test.ts`
  - `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/acp/acpSession.test.ts`

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Added/updated unit tests
- [x] Tested changes locally
- [x] Highlighted any breaking changes (none)

prs.title: fix(core): keep the unsent request when loop recovery starts before a turn
prs.body:
## Summary

When the loop check at the start of a turn reports a loop, `_recoverFromLoop` sends only the loop feedback and drops the pending request. That request is usually the `functionResponse` of a tool that already ran, so the call is closed as `"Response was lost or interrupted."` and the model loses the record of what the tool did.

## Details

`processTurn` now passes the unsent request to `_recoverFromLoop`, which sends the request parts first and the feedback text after them, in one user turn. `isFunctionResponse` matches a turn with any `functionResponse` part, so `closeUnansweredToolCallsTurn` no longer replaces the real result.

The loop check during streaming is not changed, because there the request was already sent. I did not postpone the check while a tool response is pending: late in a prompt a response is almost always pending, so the check would almost never run.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29815

## How to Validate

- `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/core/client.test.ts`. The new test `should keep an unsent tool response when the loop is found before the request is sent` fails on `main`, because the recovery request contains only the feedback text.
- The `--fake-responses` script in #29815: `step-29.txt` is answered with its real `functionResponse`, followed by the loop feedback.

prs.title: fix(core,cli,sdk): discard buffered tool calls on mid-stream error or retry
prs.body:
## Summary

When a model stream emits one or more `ToolCallRequest` events and then fails mid-stream (`Error` / `InvalidStream`), retries mid-stream (`Retry`), or terminates abnormally (`UserCancelled`, `AgentExecutionStopped`, `ContextWindowWillOverflow`, `LoopDetected`, `MaxSessionTurns`), `GeminiChat` rolls back the incomplete model turn from `agentHistory`. Previously, several stream consumers retained the buffered `toolCallRequests` (and `Turn.pendingToolCalls`) and still scheduled them after the stream loop exited, producing an orphaned `functionResponse` turn with no preceding `functionCall` in `agentHistory`.

This change:
- Clears `this.pendingToolCalls` (and resets per-attempt state on `Retry`) in `Turn.run()` when a stream retries, aborts, stops, or throws.
- Clears buffered `toolCallRequests` and tracks `StreamProcessingStatus` in `useGeminiStream.ts` when `Retry`, `Error`, `InvalidStream`, `UserCancelled`, `AgentExecutionStopped`, `ContextWindowWillOverflow`, `MaxSessionTurns`, or `LoopDetected` occurs, preventing orphaned tool execution and suppressing empty-response auto-nudges on non-completed streams.
- Clears buffered `toolCallRequests` / `toolCallsToSchedule` on mid-stream `Retry` and terminal stream events across `nonInteractiveCli.ts`, `acpSession.ts`, `legacy-agent-session.ts`, `sdk/src/session.ts`, and `a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29842

## How to Validate

- Run unit tests:
  - `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/core/turn.test.ts src/agent/legacy-agent-session.test.ts`
  - `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx src/nonInteractiveCli.test.ts src/acp/acpSession.test.ts`
  - `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-sdk -- src/session.test.ts`
- Run `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint`.

prs.title: fix(core): preserve file search results across query changes
prs.body:
## Summary

File searches can silently omit valid results after an earlier query populates the result cache. For example, searching `Src` and then `Src*` hides lowercase paths that a fresh `Src*` search finds. Reuse cached results only for identical queries so a new query always starts from the complete candidate list.

## Details

- Remove the assumption that a longer query must match a subset of its string prefix's results. Fuzzy search uses smart case, while glob filtering is case-insensitive.
- Cover the same failure within glob matching: `!*.ts` followed by `!*.tsx` must recover `.ts` files excluded by the first query. Separating caches by matcher alone would not fix this case.
- Preserve exact-query cache hits, filtering, ordering, cancellation, file-watcher invalidation, and result limits. Rename the existing broad-to-narrow integration test to describe the behavior it checks.
- Each new glob query now filters the full candidate list rather than a cached prefix subset. Repeated queries remain cached; fuzzy matching already searches the full list. No settings, dependencies, or matching rules change.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29055.

## How to Validate

```bash
npm exec -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- vitest run src/utils/filesearch --coverage.enabled=false --reporter=dot
npm run typecheck -w @google/gemini-cli-core
npm run preflight
```

Before the implementation change, all four new integration cases failed: a nonempty fuzzy result, an empty fuzzy result, and negated-glob extension with fuzzy search enabled and disabled. The cache unit test also failed. With the fix, all 84 file-search tests pass, including existing file-watcher tests, and core type checking and targeted lint pass on macOS arm64 with Node.js 24.16.0.

Full preflight completed installation, formatting, all package builds, repository-wide lint, and type checking. Its workspace test run passed all 8,518 core tests, 182 A2A-server tests, 29 SDK tests, and 68 VS Code companion tests. The CLI run passed 7,431 tests and failed nine existing startup/workspace-trust cases in `src/gemini.test.tsx`.

Those same nine failures reproduce with the original cache source and built implementation restored. After restoring this fix, running that startup suite with `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true` (also set by `.github/workflows/ci.yml`) passes all 45 enabled tests (one skipped):

```bash
GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true npm exec -w @google/gemini-cli -- vitest run src/gemini.test.tsx --coverage.enabled=false --reporter=dot
```

The setting was scoped to that test process; no persistent trust settings were changed.

The separate script suite initially passed 183 tests and failed 19 in `patch-create-comment.test.js`, whose helper invokes a script with an unquoted checkout path containing `Open Source`. All 202 script tests pass from an isolated copy of unchanged upstream sources at a path without spaces. All 17 SEA launcher tests also pass. The file-search suite was rerun after the baseline comparison and again passed all 84 tests.

The default `npm run preflight` invocation is therefore **not green** in this local environment; the failing cases pass with the environment/path corrections above. This is a draft while maintainers triage contribution eligibility and review the validation notes.

prs.title: fix(core): handle Windows libuv zero-device stat reporting in readSecureFileBuffer
prs.body:
## Summary

<!-- Concisely describe what this PR changes and why. Focus on impact and
urgency. -->
On Windows environments running Node.js `22.12.0` through `22.16.x` (bundling `libuv` `1.49.x`–`1.50.0`), path-based `fs.promises.stat(filePath)` reports `dev: 0` while descriptor-based `fileHandle.stat()` reports the volume serial number (`dev !== 0`) alongside an identical `ino`. Because `readSecureFileBuffer` in `packages/core/src/utils/fileUtils.ts` required strict equality on both `dev` and `ino` between `initialStats` and `handleStats`, file reads on affected Windows runtimes consistently failed with `File device or inode changed during read`.

This PR updates the pre-read file identity comparison in `readSecureFileBuffer` to permit a `dev` discrepancy on `win32` when either `dev` value is `0` and `ino` matches, while preserving non-zero `dev` comparisons, `ino` identity verification on all platforms, and post-read `stat` consistency checks.

## Details

<!-- Add any extra context and design decisions. Keep it brief but complete. -->
1. **Windows zero-`dev` handling in pre-read identity validation (`packages/core/src/utils/fileUtils.ts`)**:
   - Updated the pre-read `initialStats` vs. `handleStats` comparison in `readSecureFileBuffer` to treat `dev` as unchanged when `process.platform === 'win32'` and either `initialStats.dev === 0` or `handleStats.dev === 0`.
   - Preserved unconditional `initialStats.ino !== handleStats.ino` validation, non-zero `dev` mismatch checks on `win32`, strict `dev` + `ino` checks on non-Windows platforms, and post-read `initialStats` vs. `postStats` verification.
2. **Unit test coverage (`packages/core/src/utils/fileUtils.test.ts`)**:
   - Added unit tests for `readSecureFileBuffer` verifying successful reads on `win32` when `stat.dev = 0` vs. `handle.stat.dev = 12345` (and vice versa) with matching `ino`.
   - Added negative test cases verifying that `readSecureFileBuffer` continues to reject `ino` mismatches on `win32` when `dev = 0`, non-zero `dev` mismatches on `win32`, and `dev = 0` mismatches on non-Windows platforms.

## Related Issues

only related to an issue or is a partial fix, simply reference the issue number
without a keyword (Related to #123). -->

prs.title: fix(core): honor .git/info/exclude and core.excludesFile in shadow repo
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes an issue where `/restore` deletes or reverts files that should be ignored under Git configuration rules coming from `.git/info/exclude` or the user's global `core.excludesFile`.

## Details

When session checkpointing is enabled, `GitService` creates an isolated shadow Git repository in `<historyDir>`. Because the shadow repository isolates its global config (via `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`) and uses a distinct `.git` directory (`<historyDir>/.git`), it only observed working-tree `.gitignore` files, ignoring rules configured in `.git/info/exclude` and global `core.excludesFile`.

Consequently:
- Files excluded via `.git/info/exclude` or `core.excludesFile` created after a checkpoint were treated as unignored, untracked files and deleted by `git clean -f -d`.
- Files excluded via `.git/info/exclude` or `core.excludesFile` present before a checkpoint were staged and committed during snapshotting, causing `/restore` to overwrite recent changes with their previous content.

This fix:
1. Queries the user's global `core.excludesFile` via `git config --global --path --get core.excludesFile` and sets it in the shadow repository's `.gitconfig` (handling backslash sanitization on Windows). Setting this in `.gitconfig` preserves Git ignore precedence over `info/exclude`.
2. Locates the project's private exclude file using `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path info/exclude` (with fallbacks to `rev-parse --git-path` and default `.git/info/exclude`, supporting linked worktrees and subdirectories) and mirrors its contents into `<historyDir>/.git/info/exclude`.
3. Adds comprehensive unit tests in `packages/core/src/services/gitService.test.ts` and integration tests in `integration-tests/checkpointing.test.ts`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29654

## How to Validate

1. Run unit tests:
```bash
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/services/gitService.test.ts
```

2. Run integration tests:
```bash
GEMINI_SANDBOX=false npx vitest run checkpointing.test.ts --root ./integration-tests
```

prs.title: fix(cli): surface 429 rate limit cool-down and countdown in loading indicator
prs.body:
## Summary

Improves the terminal user experience during HTTP 429 (Rate Limit / Quota Exceeded) events by immediately surfacing a cool-down notice on Attempt 1 and rendering an active, second-by-second visual countdown ticker in the loading indicator.

## Details

- **Early Visibility for Rate Limits:** In default `low` error verbosity mode, generic retries are suppressed on Attempt 1 until later retries. For rate limits (`429` status code, `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`), this suppression caused perceived "silent hangs". We now detect rate limit errors via `isRateLimitRetry()` and surface them immediately on Attempt 1.
- **Active Countdown Ticker:** `useLoadingIndicator` now manages an active 1-second countdown interval while `isTimerActive` is true, decrementing remaining seconds (`delayMs / 1000` down to `1s`) to give continuous visual feedback:
  `Rate limit reached. Cooling down... Retrying in 12s (Attempt 1/3)`
- **Multi-Attempt Clean Reset:** When subsequent retry attempts arrive, the countdown cleanly resets to the new backoff duration.
- **Status Code Propagation:** Enriched `RetryAttemptPayload` in `packages/core` with optional `status?: number`, and forwarded `status: getErrorStatus(error)` from `geminiChat.ts`, `baseLlmClient.ts`, and `client.ts`.
- **Zero Regression / Full Backward Compatibility:** Generic network retries (e.g., 500s) maintain their exact existing behavior and strings. No new `eslint-disable` rules introduced.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29357

## How to Validate

1. Run the dedicated 429 countdown unit test suite:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/useLoadingIndicator_429.test.tsx

2. Run related UI and loading indicator suites:

prs.title: fix(core): resolve symlinked paths canonically in GlobTool
prs.body:
## Summary
This PR fixes `GlobToolInvocation.execute()` in `packages/core/src/tools/glob.ts` so that symlinked workspace roots and symlinked entries within the workspace are consistently resolved to canonical realpaths during filtering, workspace boundary validation, and output generation.

Key changes:
- Cache each entry's canonical path (`resolveToRealPath(entry.fullpath())`) in a `resolvedPathMap` during `relativePaths` construction so no extra filesystem calls are made.
- Resolve `filteredPaths` against `realTargetDir` (instead of raw `this.config.getTargetDir()`) and validate each candidate with `!this.config.validatePathAccess(p, "read")`.
- Filter `allEntries` using the entry's canonical path and deduplicate entries that resolve to the same canonical target.
- Map `sortedEntries` to canonical paths in `sortedAbsolutePaths` so the paths returned to the LLM match what `read_file`, `edit`, and `write_file` expect.

## Details
Previously, `GlobToolInvocation.execute()` resolved `realTargetDir` and each entry's `realFullPath` when building `relativePaths`, but then:
1. Reconstructed `filteredAbsolutePaths` using `path.resolve(this.config.getTargetDir(), p)` (unresolved target dir).
2. Checked `filteredAbsolutePaths.has(entry.fullpath())` (unresolved entry path from `glob`, which does not resolve symlinks when `follow: false`).
3. Returned `entry.fullpath()` in `sortedAbsolutePaths`.

Whenever `targetDir` or a matched entry involved a symlink (such as `/tmp` -> `/private/tmp` on macOS or a symlinked file/folder inside the workspace), `filteredAbsolutePaths` and `entry.fullpath()` mismatched, either dropping valid matches (`No files found`) or returning non-canonical paths.

## Related Issues
Fixes #28416

## How to Validate
1. Run the `GlobTool` unit tests (including symlinked workspace root, symlinked workspace files, and outside-workspace symlink filtering):
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/tools/glob.test.ts
   ```
2. Run lint and typecheck:
   ```bash
   npm run lint && npm run typecheck
   ```

prs.title: fix(cli): add missing active and focus keys to custom theme ui schema
prs.body:
## Summary

    Completes the `CustomTheme` settings validation schema, runtime focus-background derivation, and documentation fix by adding the missing `ui.active` and `ui.focus` properties—complementing PR #25822 (`text.response`) so the custom theme schema mismatch reported in #25689 (and #25610) is now resolved in full.
    
    ### How PR #25822 and This PR Complement Each Other
    
    1. **Shared Root Cause (#20745):** Commit `d25088956d11` introduced three new semantic tokens—`text.response`, `ui.active`, and `ui.focus`—into the runtime `CustomTheme` interface (`packages/core/src/config/config.ts`) and `createCustomTheme` (`packages/cli/src/ui/themes/theme.ts`), while removing `border.focused`, without updating `SETTINGS_SCHEMA_DEFINITIONS.CustomTheme` in `packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts` or `docs/cli/themes.md`. Because `settings-validation.ts` enforces `.strict()` (`additionalProperties: false`) on object schemas, configuring any of these three keys in `ui.customThemes` triggered `"Unrecognized key(s) in object"` validation errors at startup.
    2. **Part 1 — `text.response` (Fixed in PR #25822):** Issues #25610 and #25689 reported the validation error when setting `text.response` in a custom theme. PR #25822 added `text.response` to `CustomTheme.properties.text`, resolving `text.response` while #25689 remained open.
    3. **Part 2 — `ui.active` and `ui.focus` (Fixed in This PR):** Auditing #25689 against the original #20745 changes showed that the sibling `ui.active` and `ui.focus` keys still lacked schema definitions, full runtime `FocusBackground` precedence, and documentation. Adding them here completes 100% alignment across the TypeScript `CustomTheme` contract, Zod runtime validation, IDE JSON Schema (`schemas/settings.schema.json`), custom theme color derivation, and user documentation.

## Details

    - **Settings Validation & JSON Schema (`packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts`, `schemas/settings.schema.json`):**
      - Added `active: { type: 'string' }` and `focus: { type: 'string' }` to `SETTINGS_SCHEMA_DEFINITIONS.CustomTheme.properties.ui.properties` and regenerated `schemas/settings.schema.json`.
      - Retained `border.focused` in `settingsSchema.ts` for backwards compatibility so existing user `settings.json` files created from older docs do not fail strict validation.
    - **Custom Theme Runtime Consistency (`packages/cli/src/ui/themes/theme.ts`):**
      - Updated `FocusBackground` (`semanticColors.background.focus`) in `createCustomTheme` to prioritize `customTheme.ui?.focus` before falling back to `customTheme.status?.success ?? customTheme.AccentGreen ?? '#3CA84B'`, matching `Theme` and `ThemeManager.getColors()`.
    - **Documentation (`docs/cli/themes.md`):**
      - Documented `ui.active` and `ui.focus` under UI properties, added them to the custom theme JSON example, and removed the obsolete `border.focused` entry so users are guided to the supported keys.
    - **Unit Tests (`packages/cli/src/config/settings-validation.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/ui/themes/theme.test.ts`):**
      - Added schema validation tests verifying `ui.active` and `ui.focus` are accepted in `ui.customThemes` while unrecognized keys in `customThemes.ui` continue to be rejected.
      - Added theme builder tests verifying `createCustomTheme` applies `ui.active` and `ui.focus` overrides to `semanticColors.ui.active`, `semanticColors.ui.focus`, `colors.FocusColor`, and `semanticColors.background.focus`.

## Related Issues

    Closes #25689
    Related to #25610
    Related to #25822

## How to Validate

    1. Run the settings validation, theme, and schema-generation test suites:
       ```bash
       npx vitest run \
         packages/cli/src/config/settings-validation.test.ts \
         packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.test.ts \
         packages/cli/src/ui/themes/theme.test.ts \
         packages/cli/src/ui/themes/theme-manager.test.ts
       npm run test:scripts
       ```
    2. Run formatting, linting, and typecheck checks:
       ```bash
       npm run lint
       npm run typecheck
       ```
    3. Configure a custom theme in `~/.gemini/settings.json` with `text.response`, `ui.active`, and `ui.focus` overrides and launch Gemini CLI:
       ```json
       {
         "ui": {
           "theme": "MyCustomTheme",
           "customThemes": {
             "MyCustomTheme": {
               "name": "MyCustomTheme",
               "type": "custom",
               "text": { "response": "#E6EDF3" },
               "ui": { "active": "#58A6FF", "focus": "#3FB950" }
             }
           }
         }
       }
       ```
       Verify that Gemini CLI starts with zero settings validation warnings and applies all three semantic color overrides.

prs.title: fix(cli): serialize concurrent extension installs with per-extension lock (#29036)
prs.body:
## Summary

`installOrUpdateExtension()` checked whether the destination directory existed and then ran several asynchronous steps (removing the previous version, prompting for settings, copying files, writing install metadata) before loading the extension. Two installs or updates of the same extension running at the same time, in one process or in separate CLI processes, could both pass the check and write into the same directory, leaving a mix of files and metadata from both sources.

This PR serializes installs and updates per extension with a `proper-lockfile` lock and re-checks the destination once the lock is held. The second install now fails with the existing "directory already exists" error instead of writing over the first one.

## Details

- **Per-extension lock** (`packages/cli/src/config/extension-manager.ts`): a new `acquireExtensionInstallLock()` helper locks `<extensionsDir>/<name>` using the lock directory `<extensionsDir>/<name>.lock` (`realpath: false`, because the install directory usually does not exist yet).
  - The lock is keyed on the extension's own directory rather than the shared extensions directory. `proper-lockfile` tracks held locks per key within a process, so a shared key would let locks for different extensions (for example from `gemini extensions update --all`, which updates extensions concurrently via `Promise.all`) release each other and leave lock directories behind.
  - `stale: 15000` lets a lock left behind by a terminated process be taken over. `retries: { retries: 15, minTimeout: 200, maxTimeout: 500 }` waits up to about 7 s for a concurrent install of the same extension to finish.
  - If the lock cannot be acquired in that window, the install stops before writing anything and reports: `Cannot install extension "<name>" because another installation or update of it is already in progress. Please try again later.`
  - The lock-loss callback logs a warning instead of using the library default, which throws from a timer.
- **Check, lock, re-check**: the existing destination check still runs first as a fast path and runs again after the lock is acquired. Its error message is unchanged. The lock is released in the existing `finally` block, and release errors are logged so they cannot mask the result of the install.
- **Loader**: `_buildExtension()`, used by both `loadExtensions()` and `loadExtension()`, skips `*.lock` files and directories, so lock directories are never parsed as extensions. Extension names cannot contain dots (`validateName`), so no installed extension is affected.
- **Tests**:
  - `extension-manager.test.ts`: four tests in a new `concurrent installs` block, using real filesystem locks:
    - two concurrent installs of the same extension: exactly one succeeds, the destination contains only that install's files and metadata, and no lock directory remains
    - concurrent installs of different extensions: both succeed, each with its own lock
    - a lock held elsewhere: friendly error, nothing written
    - lock artifacts: ignored by the loader
  - `extensionUpdates.test.ts`: this suite mocks the filesystem, so `proper-lockfile` is mocked as well (the same approach as `projectRegistry.test.ts` and `trust.test.ts` in core). The update test now also asserts that the lock is acquired and released.
- No new dependencies (`proper-lockfile@4.1.2` is already a dependency of `@google/gemini-cli`), no breaking changes, and no documentation changes needed.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29036

## How to Validate

1. Run the extension manager tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/extension-manager.test.ts
   ```
   *Expected result*: 39 tests pass, including the 4 tests in `concurrent installs`. On `main`, these 4 tests fail; for example, the same-extension test finds files from both sources in the destination directory.

2. Run the update tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/extensions/extensionUpdates.test.ts
   ```
   *Expected result*: 2 tests pass.

3. Run the full CLI package suite, lint, and type check:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli
   npm run lint
   npm run typecheck -w @google/gemini-cli
   ```
   *Expected result*: 475 test files / 7588 tests pass (4 skipped), 0 lint errors or warnings, and no type errors.

4. Optional manual check: run `gemini extensions install <local-path>` for the same extension in two terminals at the same time.
   *Expected result*: one install succeeds. The other reports that the directory already exists (or that an installation is already in progress), and no `<name>.lock` directory remains in `~/.gemini/extensions`.

Verification run on macOS: `extension-manager.test.ts` passed 39/39, the `concurrent installs` block passed 10 consecutive runs, and the full `@google/gemini-cli` suite passed (7588 tests).

prs.body:
### Description
When `telemetry.logPrompts` is disabled (the default recommended setting in enterprise/corporate environments to prevent collecting code, secrets, and PII), all `function_args` in `gemini_cli.tool_call` are omitted and metadata keys are strictly filtered against `TOOL_CALL_METADATA_SAFE_KEYS`.

As a result, organizations cannot audit which Agent Skills are being adopted or executed. Unlike user prompts or shell arguments, a skill's name is an enum identifier defined in the skill catalog that contains no private data.

This PR:
1. Adds `skill_name` to `TOOL_CALL_METADATA_SAFE_KEYS` in `packages/core/src/telemetry/types.ts`.
2. Emits `data: { skill_name: skillName }` from `ActivateSkillToolInvocation.execute()` in `packages/core/src/tools/activate-skill.ts`.
3. Adds unit tests verifying that `skill_name` is preserved in telemetry metadata even when `logPrompts` is `false`.

- Added unit test in `packages/core/src/tools/activate-skill.test.ts`
- Added unit test in `packages/core/src/telemetry/loggers.test.ts`

prs.title: fix(core): gate background log stream initialization on execution lifecycle transition
prs.body:
When backgrounding a shell execution in `ShellExecutionService.background()` (`packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts`), background logging resources (the `fs.WriteStream` and process tracking in `backgroundLogStreams` and `backgroundLogPids`) were previously set up unconditionally before invoking `ExecutionLifecycleService.background()`.

If a command marked for background execution completes or terminates before background promotion occurs (e.g. within the background transition delay window), `ExecutionLifecycleService.settleExecution()` has already settled the execution and deleted the active resolver. As a result, subsequent calls to `ExecutionLifecycleService.background()` returned early without transitioning state, leaving the newly initialized write stream open and unmanaged.

This change updates `ExecutionLifecycleService.background()` to return a boolean indicating whether the lifecycle transition was successful, and gates all background logging stream creation, PID tracking, and process history registration in `ShellExecutionService.background()` on a successful transition. If the execution is already settled or cannot be backgrounded, no stream is opened and any associated temporary directories are cleaned up cleanly.

## Details

- **`ExecutionLifecycleService.background(executionId)` (`packages/core/src/services/executionLifecycleService.ts`)**:
  - Updates return type from `void` to `boolean`.
  - Returns `false` if `activeResolvers` or `activeExecutions` does not have an entry for `executionId` (e.g. process already exited, execution settled, or unknown execution ID).
  - Returns `true` after resolving the initial background execution result, updating `execution.backgrounded`, and dispatching notifications to registered background start listeners.
- **`ShellExecutionService.background(pid, sessionId, command, tempDir)` (`packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts`)**:
  - Updates return type from `void` to `boolean` to communicate transition status to callers.
  - Gates background log stream initialization (`fs.createWriteStream`), `backgroundLogStreams` mapping, `backgroundLogPids` registration, `backgroundTempDirs`, and `backgroundProcessHistory` tracking on `ExecutionLifecycleService.background(pid)` returning `true`.
  - Cleans up `tempDir` immediately if the lifecycle transition does not succeed or if the process is untracked.
- **Unit Test Coverage**:
  - `packages/core/src/services/executionLifecycleService.test.ts`: Verifies `ExecutionLifecycleService.background()` returns `true` on active transitions and `false` for unknown IDs, duplicate invocations, and already-settled executions.
  - `packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.test.ts`: Verifies that invoking `ShellExecutionService.background()` on an already-settled execution returns `false` without opening a write stream or registering the process ID in `backgroundLogStreams` or `backgroundLogPids`.
  - `packages/core/src/tools/shellBackgroundTools.test.ts`: Updated test mocks to register executions in `ExecutionLifecycleService` during simulated child process executions.

## Related Issues

Fixes #22814

## How to Validate

1. **Automated Unit Tests**:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/services/executionLifecycleService.test.ts src/services/shellExecutionService.test.ts src/tools/shellBackgroundTools.test.ts
   ```
2. **Full Preflight**:
   ```bash
   npm run preflight
   ```
3. **Interactive CLI Validation**:
   1. Build the CLI package:
      ```bash
      npm run build
      ```
   2. Launch the interactive CLI:
      ```bash
      node packages/cli/dist/index.js
      ```
   3. Trigger a quick background shell execution that terminates rapidly (e.g. within 50ms):
      ```text
      Run the shell command `echo "quick task finished"` with is_background set to true
      ```
   4. Verify background process tracking state:
      ```text
      /tasks
      ```
   5. **Expected**:
      - The short-lived command completes and settles without registering orphaned background log stream handles.
      - The CLI remains fully responsive and subsequent background processes can be initiated, tracked, and inspected via `/tasks` normally without file descriptor or stream warnings.

This PR decouples `ToolGroupMessage` and `DenseToolMessage` from internal core type guards (`isFileDiff`, `hasSummary`) and raw payload property inspection (`summary`, `payload`) by moving dense payload detection and `FileDiff` extraction into the `toolMapping` adapter layer.

Key changes:

prs.title: fix(core): tolerate dev 0 from Windows path stat in secure file reads
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #29898.

On Windows with libuv 1.49.x–1.50.x (Node 22.12–22.16, 23.x), `fs.promises.stat(path)` returns `dev: 0` while `fileHandle.stat()` on the same file returns the real volume serial. `readSecureFileBuffer` compared the two, so every read failed with "File device or inode changed during read".

## Change

- The identity comparison moves into `fileIdentityChanged()`, used by both the open-handle check and the post-read check.
- On win32, a `dev` of 0 on either side is treated as unknown and only `ino` is compared.
- Unchanged: an `ino` mismatch is still rejected on every platform, and a `dev` mismatch is still rejected on non-Windows platforms. Missing dev/ino values (mocked fs) are handled as before.

## Tests

Three new cases in `fileUtils.test.ts` → `readSecureFileBuffer`:
- win32, path `dev: 0`, handle real `dev`, same `ino` → reads
- win32, path `dev: 0`, different `ino` → still rejected
- linux, path `dev: 0`, handle real `dev` → still rejected

Results on Windows 11, same machine:

| Suite | Node 22.14.0 before | Node 22.14.0 after | Node 22.23.3 after | Node 20.20.2 after |
|---|---|---|---|---|

prs.title: fix(core): prevent $-pattern corruption in LLM prompt templates
prs.body:
## Summary

Migrates the LLM prompt templates in `packages/core/src/utils/summarizer.ts`, `packages/core/src/utils/llm-edit-fixer.ts`, and `packages/core/src/services/sessionSummaryService.ts` from `String.prototype.replace(placeholder, value)` to single-pass `safeTemplateReplace()`.

Previously, dynamic tool outputs, edit payloads, and conversation text containing ECMAScript `GetSubstitution` `$`-patterns (`$&`, `$'`, `` $` ``, `$$`) silently corrupted the prompts sent to the summarizer, edit-fixer, and session-summary models (e.g., `$'` duplicated the remainder of the prompt template mid-payload, `$$` collapsed to `$`, and `$&` injected the matched placeholder token). Additionally, the 5 chained `.replace()` calls in `FixLLMEditWithInstruction()` allowed earlier inputs containing later placeholder tokens to cause sequential double-interpolation.

## Details

- **`packages/core/src/utils/summarizer.ts` (`summarizeToolOutput`):** Updated `SUMMARIZE_TOOL_OUTPUT_PROMPT` placeholders to `{{maxOutputTokens}}` and `{{textToSummarize}}` and substituted via `safeTemplateReplace()`.
- **`packages/core/src/utils/llm-edit-fixer.ts` (`FixLLMEditWithInstruction`):** Updated all 5 `EDIT_USER_PROMPT` placeholders (`{{instruction}}`, `{{old_string}}`, `{{new_string}}`, `{{error}}`, `{{current_content}}`) and replaced the 5 chained `.replace()` calls with a single-pass `safeTemplateReplace()` call.
- **`packages/core/src/services/sessionSummaryService.ts` (`SessionSummaryService.generateSummary`):** Updated `SUMMARY_PROMPT` placeholder to `{{conversation}}` and substituted via `safeTemplateReplace()`.
- **Unit tests:** Added 4 regression tests across `packages/core/src/utils/summarizer.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/utils/llm-edit-fixer.test.ts`, and `packages/core/src/services/sessionSummaryService.test.ts` covering `$&`, `$'`, `` $` ``, `$$`, and placeholder-injection (`{{current_content}}`, `{current_content}`, `{{error}}`) in `FixLLMEditWithInstruction()`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29044

## How to Validate

1. Run targeted unit tests in `@google/gemini-cli-core`:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/summarizer.test.ts src/utils/llm-edit-fixer.test.ts src/services/sessionSummaryService.test.ts src/utils/textUtils.test.ts
   ```
   Confirm all 4 test files (`107` tests) pass, including the 4 new `$`-pattern and double-interpolation regression tests.
2. Build, typecheck, and lint:
   ```bash
   CI=true npm run build
   npm run typecheck
   npm run lint
   ```

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any)
- [x] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
    - [ ] Podman
    - [ ] Seatbelt
  - [ ] Windows
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
  - [x] Linux
    - [x] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker

prs.body:
Bumps the actions-dependencies group with 3 updates in the / directory: [lycheeverse/lychee-action](https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee-action), [preactjs/compressed-size-action](https://github.com/preactjs/compressed-size-action) and [google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli](https://github.com/google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli). Updates `lycheeverse/lychee-action` from 2.6.1 to 2.9.0
Release notes

Sourced from lycheeverse/lychee-action's releases.

v2.9.0

Summary

This release updates the default lychee version from v0.23.0 to v0.24.2.

The main reason for this release is compatibility with the new lychee 0.24.x release artifacts. Starting with lychee v0.24.0, the archive layout changed, and the lychee binary may now be packaged inside a subdirectory. lychee-action now detects that layout automatically, so users can upgrade without changing their workflows.

If you use:

uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2

you will get the new version once the floating v2 tag has been updated. If you pin exact versions, update to:

uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2.9.0

What’s new from lychee v0.24.x

Better diagnostics

lychee now reports line and column numbers for detected links. This makes broken link reports easier to act on, especially in larger documentation sites or generated reports.

Text fragment checking

lychee can now check URL text fragments, such as links containing #:~:text=.... This helps catch links that point to a valid page but no longer points to the intended highlighted text.

Sitemap support

lychee can now read sitemap.xml inputs. This is useful for checking published websites or generated documentation sites where the sitemap is the easiest source of URLs to validate.

JUnit output

lychee now supports JUnit output. This makes it easier to integrate link checking results with CI systems and test reporting tools that understand JUnit XML.

Redirect and remap visibility

lychee can now show redirects and remaps more clearly. This helps explain why a URL was checked as a different final URL and makes debugging link-checking behavior easier.

Multiple config files

lychee now supports multiple configuration files and expanded config handling. This is useful for repositories that split documentation, website, or package-specific link-checking settings.

Timeout handling

lychee can now accept timeouts explicitly. This gives users more control over how strict their link checks should be for flaky or slow endpoints.

Fixes and reliability improvements

prs.title: fix(cli): anchor .git suffix removal to end of repo URL
prs.body:
## Summary

Repository name parsing in `tryParseGithubUrl` previously used substring
replacement (`parts[1].replace('.git', '')`), which removes the first occurrence
of `.git` anywhere in the name rather than only a trailing suffix. As a result,
repository names with an internal `.git` substring were parsed incorrectly (for
example, `blog.github.io` was parsed as `bloghub.io`), and a non-lowercase
extension such as `.GIT` was not removed. This change strips only a trailing
`.git` suffix, case-insensitively.

## Details

- **Solution:** Replaced the substring replacement in
  `packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.ts` with a regular expression
  anchored to the end of the string: `parts[1].replace(/\.git$/i, '')`.
- **Impact:** Callers of `tryParseGithubUrl`, such as GitHub release lookup and
  `getExtensionId()`, now receive the correct repository name. Only names with
  an internal `.git` substring or a non-lowercase `.git` suffix parse
  differently than before.
- **Tests:** Added a unit test matrix to
  `packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.test.ts` that covers internal
  `.git` substrings, a trailing `.git` suffix, and case handling:

| Input repository     | Parsed name      |
| -------------------- | ---------------- |
| `blog.github.io`     | `blog.github.io` |
| `my.git.repo`        | `my.git.repo`    |
| `tool.git`           | `tool`           |
| `tool.GIT`           | `tool`           |
| `blog.github.io.git` | `blog.github.io` |

## Related Issues

Fixes #29037

## How to Validate

1. Run the GitHub extension unit tests:

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/extensions/github.test.ts
   ```

   Expected: all tests pass, including the five new
   `should strip only a trailing .git suffix` cases.

2. Optional: revert the one-line change in
   `packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.ts` and rerun the command above.
   Four of the five new cases fail; `tool.git` passes either way because its
   only `.git` is the trailing suffix.

prs.title: fix(core): use PowerShell CIM fallback for Windows IDE process lookup
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the Windows IDE process detection fallback in `packages/core/src/ide/process-utils.ts`, which previously called the Unix-only `ps` utility whenever the PowerShell process-table snapshot failed or omitted the current PID, silently returning an empty `command: '' `without logging any warning and degrading IDE detection.
    

## Details

 - **Windows single-PID CIM fallback (`getProcessInfoWindows`)**: Added a Windows-compatible single-process lookup using PowerShell (`Get-CimInstance Win32_Process
    -Filter 'ProcessId=${pid}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object ProcessId,ParentProcessId,Name,CommandLine | ConvertTo-Json -Compress`) with integer PID
    validation, a 3s timeout, and safe JSON normalization (handling single object, array, `null`, and nullable `Name`/`CommandLine` fields).
    - **Replaced broken `ps` fallback**: Updated `getIdeProcessInfoForWindows()` to invoke `getProcessInfoWindows(myPid)` when `myPid` is missing from
    `getProcessTableWindows()`, avoiding any `ps` execution on `win32`.
    - **`GEMINI_CLI_IDE_PID` resilience on Windows**: Added a fallback to `getProcessInfoWindows(idePid)` when `GEMINI_CLI_IDE_PID` is set on Windows and the full
    process-table snapshot fails or omits `idePid`.
    - **Observability**: Added `debugLogger.warn` diagnostics when Windows snapshot retrieval/JSON parsing fails, when `myPid` is missing from the snapshot, and when
    the single-PID CIM fallback fails.
    - **Unit & Integration Tests**: Added unit tests in `process-utils.test.ts` and real `child_process.exec` + `IdeClient` integration tests in
    `process-utils.integration.test.ts`.
    

## Related Issues

 Fixes #28998

## How to Validate

    1. Run the unit and integration tests for IDE process detection and client connection:
       ```bash
       npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/ide/process-utils.test.ts src/ide/process-utils.integration.test.ts src/ide/detect-ide.test.ts
       src/ide/ide-client.test.ts src/ide/ide-client.sandbox.test.ts src/ide/ide-connection-utils.test.ts
  2. Run typecheck and lint:
    npm run typecheck
    npm run lint -w @google/gemini-cli-core
  3. Verify edge cases covered by the test suites:
      • Windows process-table snapshot timeout/error or malformed JSON recovers process command via Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter 'ProcessId=<pid>' and
      accurately detects VS Code forks (vscodefork) and specific JetBrains IDEs (e.g., intellijidea).
      • Snapshot omitting the current PID or GEMINI_CLI_IDE_PID falls back to single-PID CIM lookup.
      • Total PowerShell/CIM failure (both snapshot and single-PID query failing) logs via debugLogger.warn, never invokes ps, and degrades gracefully to { pid,
      command: '' }.

prs.title: fix(core,cli): fix instances of incorrect \n escape behavior
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes multiple instances of naive `\n` escaping/unescaping across `@google/gemini-cli-core` and `@google/gemini-cli` that corrupted valid `\n` escape sequences inside string literals, regular expressions, and inline/fenced code spans during file edits and UI/tool text normalization.

## Details

1. **Model family detection for `aggressiveUnescape` in `write_file` (`packages/core/src/config/models.ts`, `packages/core/src/tools/write-file.ts`)**:
   - When `experimentalDynamicModelConfiguration` is enabled, `isGemini3Model` previously only checked `modelConfigService.getModelDefinition(resolved)?.family === "gemini-3"`. For Gemini 3 models without an explicit entry in `modelDefinitions` (such as `gemini-3-flash` or `gemini-3.0-pro`), it returned `false`, causing `aggressiveUnescape` to become `true` in `write_file` and stripping valid `\n` escape sequences inside string literals via `unescapeStringForGeminiBug`. `isGemini3Model` now falls back to `/^gemini-3(\.|-|$)/` when no model definition family is present.
   - Updated `isGemini2Model` to accept `config?: ModelCapabilityContext`, resolve model aliases (such as `auto-gemini-2.5`), and match hyphenated Gemini 2 model names (`/^gemini-2(\.|-|$)/`).
2. **File content correction & LLM escaping prompt (`packages/core/src/utils/editCorrector.ts`)**:
   - Short-circuit `ensureCorrectFileContent` before running `unescapeStringForGeminiBug` when `disableLLMCorrection && !aggressiveUnescape`.
   - Fixed template literal escaping in `correctStringEscaping` where `\\n` vs `\n` was unescaped in the prompt template, which previously instructed the LLM to replace `"bar\nbaz"` with a multi-line string containing a literal newline and referenced `corrected_new_string_escaping` instead of `corrected_string_escaping`.
3. **Context-aware newline normalization (`packages/core/src/utils/textUtils.ts`, `packages/core/src/tools/ask-user.ts`, `packages/cli/src/ui/utils/textUtils.ts`, `packages/cli/src/ui/components/Banner.tsx`, `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useBanner.ts`)**:
   - Replaced naive `.replace(/\\r\\n/g, "\n").replace(/\\n/g, "\n")` calls with `normalizeEscapedNewlines`, which converts unescaped `\n` and `\r\n` sequences to actual newlines while preserving double-escaped backslashes (`\\n`), inline/fenced markdown code spans (e.g. `` `\n` ``), and standalone quoted escape tokens (`"\n"`, `'\n'`).

## Related Issues

Fixes #22466

## How to Validate

1. Run unit tests for `@google/gemini-cli-core` and `@google/gemini-cli`:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/config/models.test.ts src/utils/editCorrector.test.ts src/tools/write-file.test.ts src/utils/textUtils.test.ts src/tools/ask-user.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/utils/textUtils.test.ts src/ui/components/messages/ThinkingMessage.test.tsx
   ```
2. Run lint and typecheck across the monorepo:
   ```bash
   npm run lint && npm run typecheck
   ```

prs.title: feat(cli): report working, blocked and idle status to the terminal (OSC 7501)
prs.body:
## Summary

The interactive TUI now reports its status to the terminal with OSC 7501 Program Status reports: working, blocked (permission, question, or auth), done or error, and idle. With several sessions open in different tabs, a supporting terminal can show which one needs you without anyone parsing screen text.

## Details

- State comes from the existing streaming state: responding is working; tool confirmation, ask-user and auth dialogs are blocked; a finished turn is done or error; otherwise idle. Reports are sent only when the status changes, and idle is sent on exit.
- Uses the same tmux/screen passthrough as the existing terminal notifications.
- Interactive TTY only. Nothing is written in `-p`, JSON / stream-JSON output, ACP, or when stdout isn't a TTY.
- `ui.programStatus` (default on) turns it off. Terminals that don't support the sequence ignore it.

## Related Issues

Closes #29710

## How to Validate

1. In a terminal that supports OSC 7501, run `gemini`, send a prompt, and watch the tab go working → done → idle. Ask for a shell command and the tab shows blocked while the confirmation is up.
2. `gemini -p "hi" --output-format json | xxd | grep 1b5d` finds no OSC sequence.
3. `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- programStatus`.

prs.title: fix(core): preserve session history during tool output masking
prs.body:
## Summary

Preserve the user's first prompt when resuming sessions whose tool outputs were masked.

## Details

`getHistory()` is prepared for API requests: for modern Gemini models it coalesces adjacent user turns and removes durable IDs. Writing this view back after masking merges the first prompt into the `<session_context>` message, which is skipped on resume.

Mask the stored history contents and reattach each original turn ID before updating the recording. This preserves turn boundaries and thought parts while allowing the recording service to update the masked tool response.

The masking service replaces contents at their original indices without filtering or reordering turns.

The regression test exercises `sendMessageStream`, real masking and recording, and `convertSessionToClientHistory`, with masking enabled and disabled. Existing chat mocks now include their durable history.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30015

## How to Validate

- With Node 20.19.0, run:
  ```sh
  npx vitest run --root packages/core src/core/client.test.ts src/context/toolOutputMaskingService.test.ts src/utils/sessionUtils.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=1

prs.title: feat(core,cli): make command substitution block user-configurable
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #27393

- Adds a `security.allowCommandSubstitution` setting (default: `false`) so users can deliberately opt into shell command substitution (`$()`, backticks, `<()`/`>()`), replacing the hardcoded, unconditional block in the shell tool.
- In YOLO mode—where the user has explicitly opted into unsupervised execution—command substitution is allowed by default, instead of silently blocking the command and wasting the whole turn.
- When still blocked, the error message now tells the model it can suggest enabling `security.allowCommandSubstitution` or splitting the work into separate plain commands, so the model can adapt instead of dead-ending.

## Details

- **Settings schema** (`packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts`): new `security.allowCommandSubstitution` boolean, category `Security`, default `false`, requires restart.
- **Core config** (`packages/core/src/config/config.ts`): new `allowCommandSubstitution` param with `getAllowCommandSubstitution()` getter (defaults to `false`).
- **CLI wiring** (`packages/cli/src/config/config.ts`): passes the setting through to the core config.
- **Shell tool** (`packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts`): the substitution block in `execute()` is now gated on `getAllowCommandSubstitution() || approval mode == YOLO`.
- **Docs**: regenerated `docs/cli/settings.md`, `docs/reference/configuration.md`, `schemas/settings.schema.json`, and added a manual "Command substitution" section to `docs/tools/shell.md`.

The safe default is preserved for everyone; the block remains in default mode, and the setting is only an explicit opt-in for users who understand the risk.

## Testing

- `packages/core/src/tools/shell.test.ts`: 4 new tests (default still blocks + mentions the setting; allowed when setting is enabled; allowed in YOLO mode). `102 passed | 1 skipped`.
- `packages/cli/src/config/config.test.ts`: 2 new tests (default `false`; pass-through when enabled). `223 passed | 1 skipped`.
- Core package `tsc --build` typecheck passes; `prettier` and `eslint` clean.

cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/tools/shellBackgroundTools.test.ts

Against main's source 4 of them fail; with this change the file passes 14/14 (macOS, Node 25). I didn't run the CLI end to end.

prs.title: fix(core): treat project temp paths as local in untrusted flag checks
prs.body:
## Summary

The agent's own helper scripts under Gemini CLI's session project temp directory
(`~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/...`) were reported as untrusted shell arguments. Once
shell output such as a Python traceback mentioned the script path, the next
`python3 <path>` invocation requested confirmation even in YOLO mode.

This change treats the project temp directory as local for untrusted-flag
detection, alongside the workspace.

## Details

`findUntrustedFlags()` exempts path arguments that resolve inside the workspace
(`isPathWithinWorkspace`). The project temp directory lives outside the
workspace, so a local script written there and later named in its own traceback
was flagged as untrusted — the false positive reported in #30004.

- `packages/core/src/utils/untrustedContextTracker.ts`: `UntrustedFlagOptions`
  gains `projectTempDir`; `isWorkspaceLocalPath()` now also accepts paths below
  it via `isSubpath()`, and `isPathWithinWorkspace` is optional so the temp-dir
  exemption works without a workspace callback.
- `packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts`: passes
  `config.storage?.getProjectTempDir()` when finding untrusted flags.

This mirrors the project temp directory trust that `Config.isPathAllowed()`
already applies for file access.

The remaining issue items are intentionally unchanged here: executable scripts,
URLs, and paths with shell expansions (`~`, `$VAR`) stay out of the
workspace-local exemption, and output from remote-retrieval commands keeps
external provenance, per #29833. The settings toggle is a separate design
decision.

## Related Issues

Related to #30004

## How to Validate

- `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/untrustedContextTracker.test.ts src/tools/shell.test.ts`
  - New tests: `should not flag project temp paths that appeared in local shell output`
    and `should not flag project temp paths printed by earlier shell output`.
    Both fail before the change and pass after it.
- Manual check: in a session, run a command whose output names a file under the
  project temp directory (for example a traceback), then run `python3 <path>`.
  No confirmation should appear in YOLO mode. Paths outside both the workspace
  and the project temp directory are still reported.
- `npm run preflight` passed locally (Linux, Node 20.19.0) on the initial
  commit; the review follow-up was validated with the affected suites, ESLint,
  Prettier, and the core `tsc` check.

prs.title: fix(core): drop tool calls streamed by failed attempts on retry
prs.body:
## Summary

On a mid-stream retry, `GeminiChat` has already yielded the failed attempt's chunks, while only the successful attempt's model turn is written to history. Every front end collected `ToolCallRequest` events from both attempts, executed both calls and answered both. A side-effecting command therefore ran twice, and the extra `functionResponse` no longer matched the model turn, so the next request failed with `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` and every later request in the session was rejected too.

This implements the existing `RETRY` contract ("The UI should discard any partial content from the attempt that just failed") for tool calls in every consumer.

## Details

- `core/Turn`: reset `pendingToolCalls` when a retry is signalled, so calls that never entered history are not reported as pending.
- ACP (`acpSession`), interactive UI (`useGeminiStream`, including `pendingToolCallRequestsRef`), headless (`nonInteractiveCli`), a2a-server (`executor`) and the subagent `LocalAgentExecutor`: drop the collected tool call requests on `Retry`.
- No behavior change when a turn is not retried; clearing only happens when the backend signals a retry.
- Out of scope (unchanged): partial text from a failed attempt is still displayed, and headless stream-json may still emit a `tool_use` event for a call that is dropped.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30014

## How to Validate

Each new test streams a tool call, then `Retry`, then a second call, and asserts that exactly one call is executed and answered. All of them fail without the source change.

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/turn.test.ts src/agents/local-executor.test.ts
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp/acpSession.test.ts src/nonInteractiveCli.test.ts src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx
cd packages/a2a-server && npx vitest run src/agent/executor.test.ts
```

Additional checks:

- `tsc --noEmit` (core/cli/a2a), `eslint --max-warnings 0` and `prettier --check` pass.
- Full `@google/gemini-cli-core` suite: 8555 passed. The single failure is the pre-existing macOS-only `/dev/ttys001` test from #30008.
- Full a2a-server suite: 183 passed.
- Affected suites also pass in a Linux Docker container (`node:22-bookworm`, linux/arm64) after a clean `npm ci` + `npm run build`.

## 中文说明

修复 #30014。流式中途重试时，失败 attempt 的 tool call 已经发给前端但不会进入 history，导致同一命令被执行两次，且多余的 functionResponse 与 history 不匹配，后续请求持续 400。现在各前端在收到 `Retry` 时丢弃失败 attempt 收集到的调用，并清空 `Turn.pendingToolCalls`；无重试时行为不变。

prs.title: fix(core): keep oversized and boundary lines in read_background_output
prs.body:
## Summary

`read_background_output` reads the last 64KB of a log and always dropped the first line of that window when it didn't start at byte 0. A log that is one line longer than 64KB came back as `Full Log Output:` with nothing after it, a complete first line was lost when the window started right after a newline, and truncated output was still labelled "Full Log Output".

## Details

- read one extra byte before the window to tell whether it starts mid line
- drop the partial first line only when other lines follow; when it's the only line, keep it as a fragment
- skip the continuation bytes of a UTF-8 character cut by the cap, so the fragment doesn't start with U+FFFD
- the header says when earlier output was truncated
- the read stays bounded at 64KB plus one byte, and the session ownership check is unchanged

## Related Issues

Fixes #29944

## How to Validate

```
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/tools/shellBackgroundTools.test.ts
```

New tests cover a 70,000 character single line, a window that starts right after a newline, a partial first line followed by a full one, and an "é" split by the cap. Against main's source all 4 fail; with this change the file passes 14/14 (macOS, Node 25). I didn't run the CLI end to end.

prs.title: chore(deps): bump undici from 7.10.0 to 7.30.1
prs.body:
Bumps [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici) from 7.10.0 to 7.30.1.
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v7.30.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped Agent options

CVE-2026-109383 · GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

Agent used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as checkServerIdentity. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

Cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure through cross-origin redirects

CVE-2026-109829 · GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26

When an originless Agent combined redirect and shared-cache interceptors as compose(redirect(), cache()), a response from a cross-origin redirect could be stored under the original URL. This could allow persistent cache poisoning or disclosure of user-specific responses to later callers. This release verifies the response origin before caching and preserves redirect-hop cache-control policy.

Denial of service through excessive Content-Encoding values

CVE-2026-109869 · GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although fetch() rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

Medium severity

Denial of service through the decompress interceptor

CVE-2026-87029 · GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6

An exception thrown by a downstream response handler from an asynchronous decompression callback could escape as an uncaught exception. A server could trigger this when decompress was composed with a handler such as dump with a size limit. This release converts downstream handler exceptions into per-request errors.

Subresource Integrity bypass with non-lowercase algorithm tokens

CVE-2026-109841 · GHSA-f72v-6w45-q472

fetch() treated valid mixed-case or uppercase SRI algorithm tokens, such as SHA256, as unknown and could accept a response whose body did not match the configured digest. This release normalizes algorithm tokens before validation and digest selection.

Denial of service through unbounded EventSource parser state

CVE-2026-109924 · GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685

A malicious Server-Sent Events endpoint could exhaust process memory by sending many tiny data: fields without completing an event, or by splitting an unfinished line across many chunks. This release bounds retained EventSource parser state, including field counts, buffered chunks, unfinished-line length, and retained field data.

Denial of service through unbounded automatic WebSocket PONG buffering

... (truncated)

Commits
  • 7507102 Bumped v7.30.1 (#6022)
  • 7d60c7b [v7.x] fix(cookies): backport #5663, #5808 and #5832 (#6019)
  • 0227d5d fix: avoid unbounded recursion in Set-Cookie attribute parser (#5757) (#5997)
  • 5394462 fix(websocket): bound automatic PONG writes under backpressure
  • 2991627 fix(eventsource): bound retained SSE parser state
  • 18bc8a1 fix(sri): accept non-lowercase algorithm tokens
  • 63cba77 fix(decompress): converge downstream handler throws to per-request errors
  • 07ded49 fix(fetch): abort excessive content encoding responses

  • 04cb74b fix: preserve Agent connection options
  • Additional commits viewable in compare view

issues.title: plugin marketplace add fails entirely if any single plugin description exceeds 1024 chars

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Environment
- Copilot CLI: `1.0.88`
- OS: macOS

### Problem

`copilot plugin marketplace add <owner>/<repo>` performs strict Zod validation
of `marketplace.json` and rejects the **entire marketplace** if *any* plugin
entry has a `description` longer than 1024 characters. There is no partial
load, warning-and-skip, or truncation — a single non-conformant plugin entry
makes the whole marketplace (hundreds of otherwise-valid plugins) unusable.

This may be related to/duplicate work for #3494 (SKILL.md `description` >1024
chars silently dropped from `skills.list()`), but the failure mode here is the
opposite and arguably worse: instead of silently dropping the *SKILL.md* entry
in an *installed* plugin, the CLI hard-fails to *add* an entire marketplace
because of a handful of over-length `description` fields in `marketplace.json`.

### Reproducer

```
$ copilot plugin marketplace add Rippling/claude-marketplace
Failed to add marketplace: Error: Request plugins.marketplaces.add failed with message: Invalid marketplace.json: plugins.27.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.89.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.147.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.171.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.394.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.406.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.417.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.439.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.580.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.610.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s)
```

The referenced `marketplace.json` has 672 plugin entries; 10 of them have
`description` fields between 1084 and 6103 characters (one is nearly 6x the
cap). Trimming just those 10 descriptions to ≤1024 chars allows the
marketplace to be added successfully — every other field/entry is otherwise
valid.

### Impact

- A single contributor adding an overlong description (easy to do
  accidentally, e.g. via generated/templated descriptions) blocks marketplace
  adoption for the *entire org*, not just their plugin.
- The error message lists the offending indices but not plugin names, making
  it hard to locate/fix the entries without manually indexing into the JSON
  array.
- There's no `--force`/lenient mode to add the marketplace while skipping or
  truncating invalid entries.

### Suggested fix

- Validate per-plugin-entry and skip/warn on individual invalid entries
  (matching the description in #3494) instead of failing the whole
  marketplace add, OR
- Include the plugin `name`/`id` (not just array index) in the validation
  error so it's actionable, and/or
- Document the 1024-char `description` cap for `marketplace.json` plugin
  entries (currently not called out anywhere in
  https://docs.github.com/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/plugins-marketplace).

issues.title: Context window rollover fails: "checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover"

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
# Context window rollover fails: "checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover"

### Describe the bug
Long-running agent sessions crash when the context window fills and the runtime attempts a rollover:

```
Execution failed: Failed to start a fresh context window: checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover
```

The turn ends and the session (or sub-agent) is effectively dead; it recurs on subsequent turns in the same session.

### What we observed
- The agent **had** written a `checkpoint.md` to the session's `files/` folder (via a normal file write / patch) ~7 minutes before the first failure, yet the runtime still reported it as absent "for this agent".
- The native runtime contains related errors ("Replacing checkpoint.md requires expected_revision; read or stat it first, or use append", "Stale checkpoint writer…"), which suggests checkpoints must be written through a runtime-managed store/tool rather than a plain file write. In our sessions the model did not appear to have any tool exposed for that store, so it could never satisfy the precondition.
- Seen repeatedly across multiple sessions/sub-agents (custom agents and the main agent), mostly in long tool-heavy sessions (builds, test runs, large tool outputs).

### Expected behavior
Either the runtime writes/derives the checkpoint itself before rollover, or the agent is given (and prompted to use) the tool needed to create it. Failing that, it should fall back to normal compaction instead of terminating the turn.

### Environment
- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.100 (also seen on 1.0.98)
- Windows 11 x64, PowerShell
- Models: GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 sessions

### Workaround
Manual `/compact` before the context fills avoids it.

issues.title: [High severity] 1.0.60 WSL2 regression: CLI MainThread spins at ~215% CPU while idle, TUI output frozen until restart (regression of #2208)

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:terminal-rendering
labels.description: Display and rendering: flickering, scrolling, line wrapping, output formatting

issues.body:
## Severity / Impact

- **Severity: High** — the TUI becomes effectively unusable; live output (assistant reasoning and streamed text) never paints until the CLI is restarted.
- **Impact: High** — reproduces on every fresh session, immediately after a clean machine reboot, with default usage. Workflow-blocking.
- **Regression of previously-fixed [#2208](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/2208)** ("copilot cli in wsl spinning on the cpu with an unresponsive tui", reported on 1.0.10, closed as completed 2026-04-07). The same class of bug is back in 1.0.60.

### Describe the bug

On **1.0.60** under **WSL2 (Ubuntu-22.04)**, the CLI process spins at ~**215–220% CPU continuously, even while idle** (between turns, with no prompt running). The render/event loop is CPU-starved, so after I submit a prompt the assistant's reasoning and streamed output **do not appear on screen** — the UI looks frozen. The work is actually completing in the background (events are written to `events.jsonl`); **only restarting the CLI makes the result appear**.

### Affected version

`GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.60` (latest; `dist-tags.latest = 1.0.60`).

### Environment

- WSL2, Ubuntu-22.04, x86_64
- TERM=xterm-256color, not inside tmux/screen (WSL relay PTY)
- 31 GiB RAM (not memory-constrained), load average ~2–4

### CPU / thread profile (the signature)

Measured on a **freshly rebooted** machine, fresh process, **idle** (no active turn):

```
PID 73114  total %CPU = 215–221  (cumulative since start, i.e. continuous spin)
  MainThread   ~98%   (full core)
  V8Worker     ~30%   x4   (GC/JIT helper threads thrashing)
  tokio-rt-worker ~0%
/proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/wchan = 0   (RUNNING, not blocked on I/O — confirmed busy-spin)
```

On **1.0.59** (same machine, same session, launched via `--prefer-version 1.0.59`) the identical session is healthy: MainThread idle at ~0%, no V8Worker spinning, cumulative %CPU actually *decreases* over time (proving near-idle). **Downgrading to 1.0.59 fully resolves it.**

### Steps to reproduce

1. On WSL2 (Ubuntu-22.04), run `copilot` on 1.0.60 (interactive TUI).
2. Submit any prompt that streams reasoning/output.
3. Observe: output does not render live; `top` shows the CLI MainThread pegged at ~98% (≈215% total) even when idle between turns.
4. Restart the CLI — the previously "missing" output now appears.

### Expected behavior

Idle CPU near 0%. Streamed reasoning and assistant output render live in the timeline without requiring a restart.

### What was ruled out (so it's clearly a CLI regression, not user config)

All of the following were tested and did **not** fix it on 1.0.60; the spin persisted on a cold-booted machine with a fresh process:

- `/compact` (timeline reduced to ~120 KB)
- Trimming MCP servers (74 → 30 child processes)
- Removing a large custom-agent data folder from `~/.copilot/agents/` (stopped a 1,139-file scan, but unrelated to the spin)
- Lowering reasoning effort `high → medium`
- Lowering `logLevel` `all → info`
- No background subagents/sidekicks active (`GITHUB_CONTEXT_SIDEKICK_AGENT=false`)
- Bundled Node runtime (not the system/nvm Node)

The only change that resolves it is **version 1.0.60 → 1.0.59**, which strongly implicates a render/event-loop regression introduced in 1.0.60.

### Additional context

- Prior fixed issue (same symptom class): #2208.
- The 1.0.60 changelog adds a new max reasoning-effort tier and several render-related changes; a busy-loop in the streaming render/poll path is the most likely area.
- Happy to capture a CPU/devtools trace if useful (as was attached to #2208).
