issues.body:
### Describe the bug

# Copilot CLI sandbox enforcement preflight fails with `CreateProcessW` error 2 on supported Windows host

## Describe the bug

On a managed Windows 11 device whose enterprise policy requires local sandboxing (`sandbox.enabled: true`, `failIfUnavailable: true`, `allowBypass: false`), every session is blocked at the sandbox enforcement preflight:

```text
This session is blocked because your organization's sandbox policy requires enforcement, but the sandbox is unavailable: backend_error: CreateProcessW failed with error code 2 (0x00000002). (CreateProcessW(PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_SECURITY_ENVIRONMENT) failed: WIN32_ERROR(2) (working directory: C:\Users\<user>\sandboxes\test (from process.cwd))). Start a new session after resolving the sandbox problem.
```

The host supports the sandbox. Outside Copilot, `@microsoft/mxc-sdk` 1.0.0 (the version bundled in Copilot 1.0.105) and 1.0.1 both successfully launch `cmd.exe`, Windows PowerShell 5.1, and PowerShell 7.6.9 on the same machine.

The standalone MXC tests use the same working directory and the same filesystem/network policy reported by `/sandbox policy`.

The failure has only been reproduced through Copilot's sandbox enforcement preflight. Because Copilot does not log the preflight image path or command line, I cannot determine which path is producing `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`.

**Important**: Local sandboxing works successfully on the same device when the enterprise-managed sandbox settings are not applied. The failure occurs when the enterprise-managed sandbox configuration is present and Copilot performs its managed sandbox enforcement/revalidation preflight.
## Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105, installed via WinGet (`GitHub.Copilot`).

WinGet reports:

```text
Name: GitHub Copilot CLI
Id: GitHub.Copilot
Version: 1.0.105
Installer Type: wix
Dependency: Microsoft.PowerShell >= 7.0.0
```

The standalone installation is located under:

```text
%LOCALAPPDATA%\GitHubCopilotCLI
```

and contains:

```text
copilot.exe
copilot-taskbar-activator.exe
GitHubCopilotCLI.sparse.msix
```

The same failure occurs through the VS Code Copilot shim and when invoking the standalone `copilot.exe` directly.

The 1.0.105-1 prerelease bundles the same `mxc-sdk` 1.0.0.



### Affected version

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use Windows 11 Enterprise 25H2, OS build 26200.9711.
2. Apply these managed settings from a GHE.com tenant:
   - `sandbox.enabled=true`
   - `sandbox.failIfUnavailable=true`
   - `sandbox.allowBypass=false`
3. Change to an empty local folder.
4. Run Copilot CLI and send any message.
5. Observe that the session is blocked by the sandbox enforcement preflight.

This occurs:

- on every new session;
- after restarting Windows;
- from different working directories;
- through the VS Code Copilot shim; and
- when invoking the standalone executable directly:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\GitHubCopilotCLI\copilot.exe"
```

## Expected behavior

The sandboxed session starts.

If the enforcement preflight cannot launch its process, the error or debug log should identify the image path and command line passed to the process creation operation.

## Additional diagnostics

### MXC platform support

Using `@microsoft/mxc-sdk/v1`:

```text
getPlatformSupport():
  isSupported: true
  isolationTier: "base-container"
```

`probe()` returns `base-container` with no warnings.

The following capabilities are reported as available:

```text
baseContainerApiPresent
baseContainerSupportsDenyPaths
baseContainerSupportsEnumeratePaths
baseContainerSupportsIngressHostLoopbackAllow
baseContainerSupportsIdentitylessLoopbackProxy
```

### Standalone MXC using Copilot's sandbox policy

A standalone MXC test uses:

- all 21 paths reported by `/sandbox policy`;
- egress allow;
- host loopback allow; and
- the same working directory that fails from Copilot.

Results:

| Program | mxc-sdk 1.0.0 | mxc-sdk 1.0.1 |
|---|---:|---:|
| `cmd.exe` | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| Windows PowerShell 5.1 | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| PowerShell 7.6.9 | exit 0 | exit 0 |

This is significant because `mxc-sdk` 1.0.0 is also the version bundled with the affected Copilot CLI release.

### PowerShell resolution checked

PowerShell 7.6.9 is installed per-user without relying on the WindowsApps alias:

```text
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe
```

`Get-Command pwsh.exe -All` returns this executable before:

```text
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe
```

and:

```powershell
pwsh.exe --version
```

returns:

```text
PowerShell 7.6.9
```

The executable reports product/file version `7.6.9.500`.

The standalone MXC test successfully launches this unpackaged PowerShell executable.

### VS Code shim eliminated as cause

Both Copilot installations are visible on PATH:

```text
C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code\bin\copilot-shim\copilot.exe
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\GitHubCopilotCLI\copilot.exe
```

The VS Code shim is normally resolved first.

However, explicitly bypassing the shim and running:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\GitHubCopilotCLI\copilot.exe"
```

produces the same sandbox enforcement failure.

Therefore, the failure is not specific to invoking Copilot through the VS Code shim.

### Other troubleshooting already performed

None of the following changed the error:

- Installed PowerShell 7.6.9.
- Put an unpackaged PowerShell 7 executable ahead of the WindowsApps alias on PATH.
- Verified that the real `pwsh.exe` is selected by `Get-Command` and `where.exe`.
- Added `C:\` and the PowerShell directory to `sandbox.userPolicy.filesystem.readonlyPaths`.
- Set `sandbox.auth.git=false`.
- Set `sandbox.auth.gh=false`.
- Set `allowLocalNetwork=false`.
- Confirmed those settings through `/sandbox policy`.
- Used different working directories.
- Restarted Windows and started fresh sessions.
- Bypassed the VS Code shim and invoked the standalone CLI directly.
- Reproduced equivalent MXC launches successfully using both mxc-sdk 1.0.0 and 1.0.1.

## Logs

With `--log-level all`, the relevant output is:

```text
[WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::services::sandbox_service] managed sandbox enforcement revalidation refused the session {"error":"...CreateProcessW failed with error code 2..."}

[ERROR] [sandbox] enforcement preflight failed: Error: ...same message...

[WARNING] Failed to process event type 'session.sandbox_enforcement_blocked' for timeline reconstruction: Error: Unhandled event type in timeline: session.sandbox_enforcement_blocked
```

No image path or command line for the failed preflight process appears in the log.

## Current findings

The tests appear to rule out a general lack of MXC/base-container support on the host:

- MXC reports the platform as supported.
- MXC `probe()` succeeds.
- mxc-sdk 1.0.0 successfully creates sandboxed processes.
- mxc-sdk 1.0.1 successfully creates sandboxed processes.
- The Copilot-reported sandbox policy works in the standalone MXC test.
- The working directory works in the standalone MXC test.
- `cmd.exe`, Windows PowerShell, and PowerShell 7.6.9 all launch successfully through MXC.
- PowerShell 7 resolves to the real executable rather than the WindowsApps alias.
- Bypassing the VS Code shim does not change the result.

The remaining difference I have been unable to inspect is **the exact image, command line, and process creation configuration used by Copilot's managed sandbox enforcement preflight**.


### Expected behavior

Sandbox works without error

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.title: MCP OAuth: expired dynamic client registration is reused forever (invalid_client), no re-registration

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

For remote HTTP MCP servers that use OAuth dynamic client registration (DCR), Copilot stores the registered client in `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/<hash>.json` and reuses it indefinitely. It ignores the registration's expiry and does not register again when the authorization server rejects the client.

GitBook-hosted docs MCP servers (`https://<site>/~gitbook/mcp`, authorization server `https://sites.gitbook.com/oauth2/v1/<site_id>`) issue registrations that expire after 7 days. The `/register` response includes `client_id_issued_at` and `client_secret_expires_at`, and the difference is exactly 604800 seconds. The cached JSON only stores `issuedAt`, not `client_secret_expires_at`. After 7 days, every sign-in attempt fails at `/authorize` (and `/token`) with:

```
{"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"Client authentication failed- Invalid client <client_id>"}
```

Clicking **Sign in** again (in the Copilot app: Customize → Installed → Sign in) gets the same error, because the expired client is reused. The only way to recover is to delete or move the cached `<hash>.json` and `<hash>.verifier` files by hand and restart. A new registration then works immediately.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.102-0.unstable.r40141230562.g130d689 (via the GitHub Copilot app)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure a GitBook-hosted docs MCP server, for example:
   ```json
   { "mcpServers": { "traksys-docs": { "type": "http", "url": "https://docs.parsec-corp.com/~gitbook/mcp" } } }
   ```
2. Sign in. Copilot registers a client via DCR and caches it in `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/`.
3. Wait more than 7 days (or check the registration's `client_secret_expires_at`).
4. Sign in again. Authorization fails with `invalid_client` / `Client authentication failed- Invalid client …`, and retrying never recovers.
5. Move the cached `<hash>.json` / `<hash>.verifier` aside and restart. Sign-in succeeds with a newly registered client.

To show that a new registration works while the cached one doesn't:

```sh
curl -s -X POST https://sites.gitbook.com/oauth2/v1/<site_id>/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"client_name":"test","redirect_uris":["http://127.0.0.1:33418/callback"],"grant_types":["authorization_code","refresh_token"],"response_types":["code"],"token_endpoint_auth_method":"none"}'
# -> client_secret_expires_at - client_id_issued_at == 604800
```

### Expected behavior

- Store `client_secret_expires_at` from the DCR response (RFC 7591 §3.2.1) and register again before using a client that has expired.
- If the authorization or token endpoint returns `invalid_client` for a dynamically registered (non-static) client, discard the cached registration, register again, and retry sign-in automatically.
- At minimum, provide a way to clear one server's cached OAuth registration (for example, a "Reset sign-in" action in the app or a CLI command) so users don't have to find hash-named files by hand.

### Additional context

- OS: Windows 11 (x64); GitHub Copilot app
- The cached file contains `serverUrl`, `authorizationServerUrl`, `clientId`, `clientSecret`, `redirectUri`, `resourceUrl`, `issuedAt`, `isStatic: false`, `httpsRedirect`. There's no expiry field.
- Possibly related to the other MCP OAuth caching issues, but distinct: #4695 (duplicate cache keys), #3973 (cached redirect port), #5229 (refresh token not used).
- We've added a workaround script for our users that moves only the affected server's cache entries aside.

issues.title: SDK: unbounded concurrency in listSessions() exhausts file descriptors with a large session-state

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`LocalSessionManager.listSessions()` in `@github/copilot/sdk` fans out over every directory in `~/.copilot/session-state` with an unbounded `Promise.all`, and per session reads `workspace.yaml`, reads `events.jsonl` for the first user message (summary), and reads `events.jsonl` again for detached-status detection. With N sessions the calling process briefly holds N to 2N open file handles.

Observed with 42,329 sessions (19 GB, created by `copilot -p` batch runs at roughly 470 per day; nothing prunes the store): a single `listSessions()` call from a VS Code extension host was captured via `lsof` with 19,985 `events.jsonl` files open at the same instant (20,043 of the process's 20,086 descriptors). Each call took 92 to 137 s. With 449 sessions it still takes 7 to 12 s.

Two consequences:

- Per process: on macOS `uv_spawn` returns `EBADF` once the child's stdio pipe descriptors are numbered above 10239, whatever the process limit is (libuv/libuv#5204, attributed to Apple libc). While `listSessions()` holds more than ~10k handles the host cannot spawn or fork at all. In VS Code this killed the ESLint language server (microsoft/vscode-eslint#2136), ripgrep and Copilot's own workspace indexer with `spawn EBADF` in the window that was listing.
- System wide: five VS Code windows calling it in parallel at startup drove `kern.num_files` to 122,477 (limit 122,880) and unrelated processes got `ENFILE`; `git rev-parse` took 1.5 to 3.4 s instead of ~50 ms.

De-minified shape of the code (`sdk/index.js`):

```js
async listSessions(e){
  let n=await _t.directoryFilesWithMetadata(this.settings), r=e?.metadataLimit, s=e?.includeDetached??!0,
  o = s ? n : r===void 0
      ? (await Promise.all(n.map(async l=>({file:l,isDetached:await this.isDetachedSession(l.file,l.mtime.getTime())})))).filter(...)
      : await this.getVisibleSessionEntriesWithBoundedDetachedDetection(n,r),
  a=(await Promise.all(o.map(async(l,c)=>{ ...
    let p = s ? await this.isDetachedSession(u, ...) : !1;      // opens events.jsonl (readDetachedStatusFromSessionStart)
    let m = await GI(u,this.settings);                           // reads workspace.yaml
    if(!f){ let b=await qI(y); f=b.summary; h=b.isEmpty }        // opens events.jsonl again (sessionExtractFirstUserMessage)
```

Notes: the bounded helper `getVisibleSessionEntriesWithBoundedDetachedDetection` is only used when `metadataLimit` is set and `includeDetached` is false, so the default path has no bound; the detached cache only helps on later calls in the same process; nothing is cached across processes, so every client pays the full cost.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

```bash
cd ~/.copilot/session-state
for i in $(seq 1 20000); do d=$(uuidgen | tr A-Z a-z); mkdir "$d"
  printf 'id: %s\ncwd: /tmp\ncreated_at: 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z\nupdated_at: 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z\n' "$d" > "$d/workspace.yaml"
  printf '{"type":"session.start","data":{"sessionId":"%s"}}\n{"type":"user.message","data":{"content":"hello"}}\n' "$d" > "$d/events.jsonl"
done
# same construction the VS Code extension uses
node -e 'import("@github/copilot/sdk").then(async m=>{const sm=new m.internal.LocalSessionManager({createFeatureFlagService:m.createLocalFeatureFlagServiceCreator()(),telemetryService:new m.internal.NoopTelemetryService,autoModeManager:new m.AutoModeSessionManager},{}); console.time("list"); await sm.listSessions(); console.timeEnd("list")})' &
while kill -0 $! 2>/dev/null; do lsof -p $! 2>/dev/null | grep -c events.jsonl; sleep 0.5; done
```

On macOS the open count climbs toward N; on a default `ulimit -n 256` shell it fails with `EMFILE`. Adding a `child_process.spawn` inside the script while the listing runs yields `spawn EBADF` past ~10k open files.


### Expected behavior

- Concurrency in `listSessions` is bounded (a `p-limit` style pool of 16 to 64), including the detached-detection pass, so the caller never holds more than a few dozen handles.
- `events.jsonl` is read once per session; detached status and the first user message come from the same prefix read.
- `metadataLimit` is effective on the default `includeDetached: true` path, with entries sorted by mtime first so the limit covers the most recent sessions.
- The derived summary is persisted (in `workspace.yaml` or in the existing `session-store.db`) so later listings do not open `events.jsonl` at all.
- A prune or retention option exists for `~/.copilot/session-state` (`copilot sessions` currently has only `import`).

### Additional context

- macOS (Darwin 27.2.0, arm64), zsh. `kern.maxfiles` 122,880, `kern.maxfilesperproc` 61,440.
- VS Code side: microsoft/vscode#327021 (slow repeated re-walks) and a separate new issue for the descriptor exhaustion in the extension.

issues.title: Shell command runner does not inherit environment variables from PowerShell

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

Environment variables available in the PowerShell process that launches Copilot are not visible to Copilot's shell command runner. This prevents commands and integrations launched by the runner from using user-configured environment variables such as `GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

## Affected version

Copilot CLI 1.0.105

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. On Windows, store `GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` in the User environment-variable scope.
2. Open a new PowerShell 7 prompt.
3. Load the User-scope value into the current process and verify it without printing the secret:

   ```powershell
   $env:GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN', 'User')
   $env:GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN -ne $null
   ```

   This returns `True`.

4. Launch Copilot CLI from that same PowerShell prompt.
5. In the Copilot session, run:

   ```text
   ! $env:GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN -ne $null
   ```

   This returns `False`.

6. The runner reports the following scope state without exposing the secret value:

   ```text
   Process: False
   User:    True
   Machine: False
   ```

The behavior reproduces in a newly opened PowerShell prompt and a newly launched Copilot session. No token value was printed or included in this report.

## Expected behavior

The shell command runner should inherit the environment of the Copilot process that was launched from PowerShell, or the behavior should be clearly documented if credential variables are intentionally filtered.

## Additional context

- Operating system: Windows
- Shell: PowerShell 7
- The runner and launcher are running under the same Windows account; account/domain details are intentionally omitted.
- The issue appears specific to the Copilot command-runner process boundary. It may be intentional credential sanitization, but this is not documented and prevents expected environment-based authentication for child commands.

issues.title: [Feature request] Authoritative foreground-session change hook for terminal integrations, including warm resume

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Problem

Terminal integrations need to associate a pane with the **currently foreground**
root conversation, rather than the last conversation that submitted a prompt.
Command `sessionStart` hooks do not appear to provide a complete foreground-change
stream when switching between already-loaded sessions.

### Isolated observation

Tested Copilot CLI **1.0.105 on Linux**, using an empty disposable project, separate
`HOME`/`COPILOT_HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, user-level command hooks for `sessionStart`,
`sessionEnd` and `userPromptSubmitted`, normal folder consent and Manual Approval.
No auto-approval, production hooks or existing conversations were used.

1. Start the interactive CLI and submit a synthetic prompt in session A.
   Observe `sessionStart(A, source=new)` and `userPromptSubmitted(A)`.
2. Run `/new` and submit another synthetic prompt in B.
   Observe `sessionStart(B, source=new)` and `userPromptSubmitted(B)`.
3. Run `/resume <A-id>`, then `/session id` to independently confirm A is foreground.
4. Repeat `/resume <B-id>`, `/session id`, then `/resume <A-id>`, `/session id`.

Across these warm A-B-A switches, there were **no additional Start, End or
Prompt hook invocations** within the bounded 5-8 second observation windows.
A file written only by Start hooks would still identify B while A is displayed.
New idle conversations likewise produced no Start until the first submitted
prompt in this run.

A same-version `/restart` changed the observed CLI owner PID/start identity.
After restart, the first submitted prompt emitted Start with `source=resume`.
This was not a cross-version handoff test.

**Limitation:** model requests were rejected by account billing-entity
configuration, so this observation does not establish successful-completion,
subagent, background-model or all-platform behavior. The foreground switches,
session IDs and hook events were nevertheless observed independently. Please
confirm whether this limitation affects the intended lifecycle contract.

### Requested capability

Please provide or document one supported identity-only integration surface:

- A complete, causally serialized **foreground-session-changed** event covering
  warm switches, startup, new/clear/no-current transitions, with ordering and
  failure/supersession semantics; or
- A read-only authenticated accessor for current root identity (or no-current),
  resolved session-store location and an activation revision/conditional-current
  operation suitable for safely publishing asynchronous identity records.

An equivalent supported in-process integration would also work. Explicit revision
fields are not essential if the API guarantees complete serialized publication.
Session-only snapshots or hook-arrival counters alone do not establish that
delayed work still belongs to the current activation, particularly A-B-A.

This is not a request for tool approval, busy/idle authority, a heartbeat service,
or access to transcript contents. The goal is to stop relying on diagnostic log
registration lines to identify the displayed conversation.

Related but different: #4365 discusses prompt-hook/new/clear behavior; this request
concerns **command-hook coverage of warm foreground switches**.

issues.body:
### Description of the bug

With a BYOK model deployed in Microsoft Foundry, a long Copilot CLI session becomes unusable because requests exceed the deployment's token rate limit, even though the displayed model context window is far from full. Ordinary messages fail, and `/compact` also fails, leaving no working in-session recovery through compaction.

The CLI did not give me an actionable warning about the deployment's TPM limit before the session reached this state. Its context display still shows substantial free space.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.104.

### Environment

- Operating system: Windows.
- Provider: BYOK using a Microsoft Foundry deployment.
- Model: `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- Region: `eastus`.
- Deployment token rate limit: 250,000 TPM (user-reported configuration).
- CLI-displayed context capacity: 922k tokens.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure Copilot CLI to use a Foundry BYOK deployment with a large model context window but a substantially lower TPM allocation.
2. Continue a long conversation until `/context` shows approximately 257k/922k tokens.
3. Send an ordinary message. It fails to obtain a model response.
4. Run `/compact` to reduce the history and continue the session.
5. Compaction also fails with the deployment token-rate-limit error below.

### Actual behavior

Exact user-visible compaction error:

```text
Compaction Failed: Error: Failed to get response from the AI model; retried 5 times (total retry wait time: 5.00 seconds) Last error: Your requests to gpt-6.1-sol for gpt-6.1-sol in eastus have exceeded token rate limit.
```

Relevant `/context` output:

```text
gpt-6.1-sol: 257k/922k tokens (28%)
Messages:   239.5k (26%)
Free Space: 618.7k (67%)
Buffer:      46.1k (5%)
```

The error identifies a token-rate-limit failure, not exhaustion of the advertised 922k model context window. The displayed accumulated context is already greater than the deployment's reported 250k TPM allocation.

### Expected behavior

- Distinguish model context capacity from deployment throughput limits in BYOK diagnostics. Explain that a large context window does not guarantee the deployment can accept the corresponding request under its current rate limit.
- Provide proactive, actionable warnings using provider rate-limit headers when available, and/or support a user-configured effective request budget for BYOK deployments. Account for prompt overhead and the provider's output-token reservation/estimation where applicable.
- Trigger compaction early enough to remain within that effective budget.
- Provide a recovery path when the session is already too large for a normal compaction request, such as bounded/chunked compaction or export of a handover that can be used in a fresh session. Preserve the original conversation rather than silently discarding history.
- Respect provider retry timing for temporary throttling, but do not rely only on resubmitting an unchanged request if its estimated token cost exceeds the deployment's entire available rate budget.

### Additional context

This report distinguishes observed behavior from the suspected mechanism: the exact error confirms token-rate-limit rejection, but I have not captured the HTTP status, rate-limit headers, actual compaction request size, or concurrent deployment traffic. The context display alone does not prove the exact provider-side token estimate or that the compaction request resubmits the entire history.

Related reports:

- #3679: BYOK Azure OpenAI throttling retries/backoff. This report additionally concerns missing quota-aware warning and inability to recover using `/compact`; the observed retry wait here is 5.00 seconds.
- #4950: BYOK context-overflow/compaction hangs with another provider. This report concerns a Foundry token rate limit while model context usage is only 28%, not the sampling regression described there.

No API keys, endpoint URLs, client data, conversation contents, or private logs are included.

issues.title: Support default-deny tool permissions with explicit allowlist in non-interactive mode

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Non-interactive mode cannot enforce a strict tool allowlist because `--deny-tool` always overrides `--allow-tool` and some tools are allowed by default.

Currently, GitHub Copilot CLI does not provide a straightforward way to enforce a strict tool allowlist in non-interactive mode.
Some tool invocations, such as read-only shell commands, are allowed by default. Since `--deny-tool` rules always take precedence over `--allow-tool` rules, it is not possible to deny a tool broadly while explicitly allowing specific invocations.

For example, the following configuration does not work as intended:

```bash
copilot --deny-tool='shell' --allow-tool='shell(path/to/script)'
```

This limits the ability to enforce least-privilege execution policies in automated workflows, such as CI/CD pipelines, where tool execution must be restricted without relying on interactive approval.

### Proposed solution

Introduce a **default-deny permission mode for non-interactive execution**, in which all tool invocations are denied unless explicitly permitted through allow rules, including tools and commands normally allowed by default.

Ideally, this should integrate with the existing permission mechanisms and apply consistently across subagents.

This would make unattended runs more secure and predictable, remove the need for custom hooks, and make it easier to adopt Copilot CLI in CI/CD and security-sensitive environments.

### Example prompts or workflows

A CI/CD pipeline runs Copilot CLI in non-interactive mode. Copilot should be permitted to execute a specific validation script (`path/to/script`) while all other shell commands, including read-only commands, are denied.

### Additional context

A workaround for this feature is possible using `preToolUse` hooks, but this requires custom permission-checking logic and additional safeguards against bypasses, such as modifying hook scripts or configurations, or delegating execution to subagents.

Native support would simplify configuration and provide a more reliable way to enforce least-privilege policies in unattended environments.

issues.title: web: side-panel "Open file" is a silent no-op on insecure HTTP origins (v2.2.0 regression)
issues.body:
### Description

On the Web UI served over **plain HTTP from a non-localhost origin** (LAN IP / hostname / Tailscale), clicking **Open file** in the side panel's new-tab view does nothing: no tab opens, no toast, no request. The console shows:

```
Uncaught TypeError: crypto.randomUUID is not a function
```

Review and Terminal launchers in the same panel work. The same server and session work over `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`.

Root cause: `packages/gui-plugins/src/file/renderer.tsx` opens a new launcher tab with an unguarded `crypto.randomUUID()`:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.2.0/packages/gui-plugins/src/file/renderer.tsx#L170

```ts
if (selected || layout.narrow())
  layout.open(`file:${selected ?? OPEN}`, session, { tab: "preview", background: options?.background })
else layout.open(`file:${OPEN}:${crypto.randomUUID()}`, session, { tab: "select" })
```

`crypto.randomUUID` exists only in secure contexts, so on an insecure origin the call throws inside the click handler before `layout.open`, and the click is silently lost. Both the `+` → “Open file” launcher and `Ctrl+Alt+P` reach this branch; narrow layouts (<768px) take the other branch and are unaffected.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the Web UI (`opencode serve`, or the background service) and open it from a non-localhost HTTP origin, e.g. `http://<LAN-IP>:<port>/` (Chrome shows “Not secure”).
2. Open any session and open the side panel (Toggle review).
3. Click `+` (Add tab), then **Open file**.
4. Nothing happens; devtools shows `TypeError: crypto.randomUUID is not a function`.

Expected: the file browser tab opens on any origin (id generation should not require a secure context).

### Regression / history

- `v2.1.4` used a fixed key (`file:open`) in `openPicker` and worked on insecure origins.
- `#57182` (`879479b467`, “allow multiple open file tabs”) introduced `file:${OPEN}:${crypto.randomUUID()}`; `#55246` moved it to `packages/gui-plugins/src/file/renderer.tsx`. First release containing it: **v2.2.0**.
- The app already has a guarded helper for exactly this: `uuid()` in `packages/app/src/runtime/persistence/uuid.ts` (falls back when `crypto.randomUUID` is unavailable, when `isSecureContext` is false, or when it throws), with unit tests. Earlier fixes `#51783` and `#53501` were the same class of bug.
- Related open issues: `#46168`, `#48144`, `#55777` (other unguarded `crypto.randomUUID` calls that silently fail on insecure origins).

### Suggested fix

Use the guarded helper here — e.g. promote `uuid()` to `@opencode/util` and import it from both the app and `packages/gui-plugins`, or add a local fallback before `layout.open`:

```ts
const uuid = () =>
  typeof globalThis.crypto?.randomUUID === "function" && globalThis.isSecureContext !== false
    ? globalThis.crypto.randomUUID()
    : Math.random().toString(16).slice(2)
```

Worth auditing the other direct calls reachable from the web UI: `packages/gui-plugins/src/btw/model.ts:107` and `packages/app/src/runtime/plugin/host-apis.tsx:1026`.

### Verification

Control experiment on the same server/session in Chromium:

- `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`: clicking Open file opens the “Open file” tab and shows “Select a file to open”.
- Same page with `Crypto.prototype.randomUUID` removed (equivalent to an insecure context): the click logs `TypeError: crypto.randomUUID is not a function`, the tab strip still shows only “New tab”; clicking Terminal right after opens “Terminal 1” normally.
- On the insecure origin, `typeof crypto.randomUUID` evaluates to `"undefined"` and `isSecureContext` is `false`.

### Environment

- OpenCode: v2.2.0
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 7.0.0-34-generic)
- Browser: Chrome 155.0.8059.39
- Web UI: served by the local service, accessed via `http://<LAN-IP>:<port>`
- Plugins: none relevant (built-in `file`, `terminal` GUI plugins only)

issues.title: Free tier issues: read this first, then post your report here

labels.name: zen
labels.description: Relates to Zen

issues.body:
This is the **main issue for free tier problems**. If you see any of these, you're in the right place:

- `Free usage exceeded, subscribe to Go`
- `Free usage limit reached`
- `You've used today's free messages. They reset at ...` and the reset never happens
- `This version of OpenCode Desktop no longer supports free models`
- `OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`
- `OpenCode 1.18.0 or newer is required to use the free tier`

**Please comment here instead of opening a new issue.** We're closing duplicates and pointing them here so everything is in one place.

## 1. Make sure you're on the latest OpenCode v2

Most free tier reports come from **OpenCode v1** (versions `0.x` and `1.x`, for example Desktop or CLI `1.19.5`). v1 no longer supports free models and only gets fixes for critical bugs. Updating to v2 has fixed this for many people.

Check your version:

- **Terminal:** `opencode --version`
- **Desktop:** Settings → About

The latest v2 release is **2.2.1**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The v1 Desktop app's built-in updater keeps you on `1.x`. Download v2 manually from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**.

### Desktop

Download v2 Desktop for macOS, Windows or Linux from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**, or on macOS:

```sh
brew install --cask opencode-desktop
```

### Terminal (TUI / CLI)

All install options are listed at **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**. The quickest on macOS and Linux:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash
```

Or use a package manager:

```sh
npm install -g @opencode/cli
bun install -g --trust @opencode/cli
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2
paru -S opencode-beta
```

v1 and v2 both use the `opencode` command. If you installed v1 with a package manager, remove it first, for example `npm uninstall -g opencode-ai`. Windows package managers (Chocolatey, Scoop) don't support v2. On Windows, use the Desktop app, npm, or a [standalone binary](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/).

### Useful docs

- [Install OpenCode v2](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/)
- [Migrate from v1](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1/)
- [Free models, limits and privacy](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/models/#free-models)
- [OpenCode Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/)
- [Troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting/)

## 2. Other things to check

- **Free models only work inside OpenCode.** Other clients, proxies and direct API calls can't use them. Use a paid model or [Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/) there instead.
- **Subscribed to Go but still seeing free limits?** Run `/connect`, sign in with **OpenCode Console** in your browser (make sure you authorize the workspace with your Go subscription, or choose **OpenCode Go** if you use a Go API key), then pick a Go model (`opencode-go/...`) with `/models` rather than a free model (`opencode/...-free`).
- **Hit the real daily limit?** Wait for the reset time shown, subscribe to [Go](https://opencode.ai/go), or connect another provider with `/connect`.

## 3. Still broken on the latest v2? Comment with:

- OpenCode version, and whether you use Desktop, TUI, CLI or web
- Operating system
- The free model you used
- The exact error message (a screenshot is fine)
- When it started and the reset time you were shown
- Whether you have Go or Console credits

> [!WARNING]
> Don't post email addresses, payment details or other account information here. This issue is public.

## 4. Still don't know what's going on?

If you're on the latest v2 and none of the above helps, or the problem is about your account, billing or Go subscription, email **help@anoma.ly** with the details from step 3. Billing and account issues can't be fixed in GitHub issues.

issues.title: tui: Ctrl+V text paste silently fails on Linux without xsel (v1 line, clipboardy fallback not bundled)
issues.body:
### Description

`prompt.paste` (Ctrl+V) is a silent no-op in the TUI on Linux when `xsel` is not installed: nothing is pasted, and no error, toast, or log entry is produced. `Ctrl+Shift+V` (terminal bracketed paste) still works, so the terminal side is fine.

Cause is the text branch of `read()` in `packages/tui/src/clipboard.ts`, which is still delegated to `clipboardy`:

```ts
const { default: clipboardy } = await import("clipboardy")
const text = await clipboardy.read().catch(() => undefined)
if (text) return { data: text, mime: "text/plain" }
```

On Linux clipboardy only runs `xsel --clipboard --output` (it never tries `xclip` or `wl-paste`), and its bundled fallback `node_modules/clipboardy/fallbacks/linux/xsel` is referenced by the compiled single-file binary but the fallback binary itself is not shipped inside it. So without `xsel` on PATH the read rejects and the `.catch()` swallows the error.

The same file is already Wayland-aware for *writing* (`copyCommand()` returns `wl-copy` when `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set), and the *image* read path already tries `wl-paste` then `xclip` before falling back — only the text read path is stuck on xsel. On a stock Debian/Ubuntu GNOME Wayland desktop (`xsel` is usually not installed) Ctrl+V therefore does nothing. Installing `xsel` fixes it; installing only `wl-clipboard` or only `xclip` does **not**.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Linux desktop without `xsel` (`command -v xsel xclip wl-paste wl-copy` → all absent). Reproduced on Debian 13 + GNOME 48 Wayland.
2. Start the TUI, copy some text in any GUI app, press Ctrl+V in the prompt.
3. Nothing is inserted and no error is shown.
4. `sudo apt install xsel`, restart the TUI → Ctrl+V works.

Deterministic check without a GUI clipboard (pty, injecting raw keys):
- no `xsel` on PATH → sending `\x16` produces no input change;
- a stub `xsel` on PATH printing a fixed string → sending `\x16` inserts that string;
- a stub `wl-paste` only, or a stub `xclip` only → still nothing, i.e. the text path uses neither.

### Screenshot

N/A — there is no visible output (that is part of the bug).

### Operating System

Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie), GNOME Shell 48.7, Wayland session

### Terminal

GNOME Terminal 3.56.2 (VTE)

### OpenCode version

1.19.4 (`npm opencode-ai`). `packages/tui/src/clipboard.ts` is identical at tag `v1.19.5`, so the latest v1 release is affected as well.

### Plugins

none

### Additional context

Suggested fix (essentially the auto-closed #29881): before the clipboardy fallback, try `wl-paste -n --no-newline` when `process.env.WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set, then `xclip -selection clipboard -o`, and stop swallowing the failure — surface a toast instead of `.catch(() => undefined)`.

I did check the v2 line: it goes through `@opentui/core`'s native host clipboard (Wayland data-control), so this report is specific to the v1 line that `npm i -g opencode-ai` still installs. If v1 is maintenance-only and will not take clipboard changes, documenting the `xsel`/`wl-clipboard` requirement (or warning at startup when no text backend exists) would at least remove the silent failure.

Related reports, both closed by automation rather than by a maintainer decision:
- #29880 — same bug, closed as NOT_PLANNED after 60 days of inactivity
- #29881 — the fix PR for this exact file, closed by the "older than 1 month / fewer than 2 reactions" cleanup; the author commented "Bug is still relevant, I believe this should still be open"
- #51293 / #50847 — different, v2 native-clipboard paste issues, still open
- #32370 / #43176 — open, Linux PRIMARY-selection support (different request)

issues.title: tui: all pastes hang after one clipboard read timeout (Linux/Wayland)
issues.body:
## Summary

After a single TUI clipboard read hits the 1s timeout ("Clipboard read timed out"), every later paste in that OpenCode instance hangs forever. No attachment, no text, no error. Only restarting OpenCode fixes it.

## Environment

- opencode 2.0.14
- Arch Linux, Hyprland 0.56 (Wayland), foot 1.28
- Paste goes through the OpenTUI native host clipboard (Wayland data-control), `timeoutMs` default 1000, preferredTypes `["image/png","text/plain"]`

## Repro

1. `wl-copy --type image/png < screenshot.png`
2. In a shell loop, `wl-copy` a slightly different PNG every ~1.3s, so the clipboard owner keeps changing
3. In opencode, press Ctrl+V repeatedly
4. Eventually one paste shows "Clipboard read timed out"
5. Stop the loop and copy plain text. Every Ctrl+V after that hangs: 20 out of 20 attempts hung, waiting 15s each

## Expected

A timed-out read fails once. Later pastes work normally.

## Actual

All later pastes (`prompt.paste` / bracketed paste with an empty body) hang forever until OpenCode restarts. `wl-paste` in another shell returns instantly the whole time, so the system clipboard itself is fine.

## Suspected cause

The native clipboard operation that timed out is never settled or cancelled, or a concurrency slot or pending-op flag leaks. Every later read then queues behind it or waits on it forever. The timeout path should cancel or release the in-flight Wayland data-control read and reset the service state.

## Workaround

Paste the image file path instead; the TUI attaches image paths.

Not the same as #42162 (wl-copy left in the process group after Ctrl-Z).

issues.title: tui: TUI freezes on Ctrl+V paste over SSH (Windows); clipboard read appears to hang
issues.body:
### Description

## Summary

Pasting into the OpenCode TUI with `Ctrl+V` freezes the UI indefinitely when OpenCode runs on a remote Windows host over SSH (Windows Terminal is the client). The process stays alive at ~0% CPU and must be killed. The pasted bytes arrive intact (bracketed paste is complete), so the transport is not the cause; the hang appears to be in the TUI's native clipboard read path.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.24 (npm global `@opencode/cli`; latest on npm at report time: 2.0.29)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro, Build 26300 (x64) on the client; the remote host is also Windows (10.0.26300)
- Terminal: Windows Terminal 1.24.12741.0 (`WT_SESSION` set), `TERM=xterm-256color`
- Shell: cmd.exe on the remote host (`COMSPEC=C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe`)
- Install/channel: latest (npm global)
- Remote transport: `OpenSSH_for_Windows_9.5p2` (sshd on the remote Windows host)

## Reproduction

1. From Windows Terminal, SSH into a remote Windows host and start OpenCode (TUI).
2. On the local machine, copy a URL from a browser address bar.
3. Focus the OpenCode prompt and press `Ctrl+V`.
4. The TUI freezes (no redraw, no response to keys); the process stays alive at ~0% CPU and has to be killed.

Variations observed:

- Same freeze when pasting via `Win+V` (Windows clipboard history).
- No freeze when the same-length text is copied from Notepad instead of the browser.
- No freeze when OpenCode runs locally (no SSH) and the same browser URL is pasted.

## Expected Behavior

The pasted text appears in the prompt and the TUI stays responsive.

## Actual Behavior

The TUI becomes completely unresponsive and stays hung until killed. No error is shown, and nothing is written to the OpenCode log at the moment of the freeze.

## Additional Context

**Transport is fine** (rules out a Windows Terminal bracketed-paste problem): a raw-mode probe over SSH captured exactly `ESC[200~` + `<url>` + `ESC[201~` in a single read (a 6-byte start marker, then the text together with the end marker). The bracketed paste is delivered intact.

**Points at a native clipboard read hang:**

- The v2 binary (`@opencode/cli` 2.0.24) contains clipboard-provider strings: `Clipboard read timed out`, `Clipboard content exceeded configured read or image conversion limits`, `Unexpected clipboard MIME type:`, `preferredTypes`, `all-available`, `getClipboardText`, `hasClipboardImage`, `useClipboard must be used within a ClipboardProvider`, plus Win32/COM imports `OpenClipboard`, `GetClipboardData`, `GetClipboardSequenceNumber`, `IsClipboardFormatAvailable`, `CoInitializeEx`, `CoCreateInstance`.
- During the freeze the OpenCode process shows ~0% CPU over a 2 s sample (blocked, not busy-looping) with a ~200 MB working set.
- The log shows no clipboard/paste/error entries at the freeze time, i.e. the hang is below the JS server layer.
- This matches the reported regression where a single clipboard-read timeout wedges every later paste: #50847 (#52422 was auto-linked to it).

**Why the clipboard read can block here:** the clipboard is read on paste. Over SSH the TUI runs on the remote host, where that read can block/time out; per #50847 the failed read is never reset, so every subsequent paste also hangs.

**What does not reproduce:** feeding the exact same bracketed-paste bytes (URL / empty body / 5 KB of text / 200 lines) into an OpenCode TUI over a local sshd on the same machine does not hang; the TUI stays responsive and large pastes collapse to a placeholder. The freeze needs the real interactive terminal/clipboard environment.

**Candidate deterministic repro (not yet verified by the reporter):** hold the Win32 clipboard open in another process for ~60 s (`OpenClipboard` without `CloseClipboard`), then press `Ctrl+V` in OpenCode; a blocked clipboard read should reproduce the hang.

**Workarounds:** none help consistently; only restarting OpenCode clears the stuck state.


### Plugins

_No response_

### OpenCode version

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

_No response_

### Screenshot and/or share link

_No response_

### Operating System

_No response_

### Terminal

_No response_

issues.title: tui: image paste fails on WSL2/WSLg with libwayland-client 1.18 — Wayland clipboard backend is rejected, X11 fallback can't serve images
issues.body:
### Description

WSL2 + WSLg (Ubuntu 20.04, Windows 11). Copy an image on the Windows side, press
**ctrl+v** in the TUI: no attachment. The first time I got a popup whose text started
with "X11 ..." (I didn't copy the full line); after that the same paste does nothing
at all — no error, no attachment.

Why: the 2.0.29 TUI reads the clipboard through OpenTUI's native host clipboard,
which prefers Wayland. Ubuntu 20.04 ships libwayland-client 1.18.0, which has no
**wl_proxy_marshal_array_flags**, and OpenTUI's loader in
**packages/native/src/clipboard/linux.zig** declares that symbol as required (only
fields typed optional are tolerated). **So the Wayland backend is dropped entirely
and it falls back to X11.** Under WSLg the X11 CLIPBOARD owner is Weston's Xwayland
bridge and **it only serves UTF8_STRING**, so image/png is refused — that's where the
"X11 clipboard ..." text comes from.
```bash
  $ dpkg -l libwayland-client0
  ii  libwayland-client0:amd64 1.18.0-1ubuntu0.1
  $ nm -D /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libwayland-client.so.0 | grep marshal_array
  T wl_proxy_marshal_array
  T wl_proxy_marshal_array_constructor
  T wl_proxy_marshal_array_constructor_versioned        # no ..._flags
```

**/mnt/wslg/weston.log** while pressing ctrl+v (property OPENTUI_CLIPBOARD is only
used by the X11 backend):
```log
  [14:14:33.594] selection request, CLIPBOARD, target image/png, property OPENTUI_CLIPBOARD
  [14:14:33.594] can only handle UTF8_STRING targets...
  [14:14:33.745] selection request, CLIPBOARD, target image/png, property OPENTUI_CLIPBOARD
  [14:14:33.745] can only handle UTF8_STRING targets...
```

Workaround that works here: give the process a **libwayland-client >= 1.20** (I put a
self-contained copy in a private dir and prepend it to **LD_LIBRARY_PATH**). After
that image paste works and weston.log shows no more **OPENTUI_CLIPBOARD** requests.

Suggested fix: make **wl_proxy_marshal_array_flags** optional in the loader, the way
**wl_display_set_max_buffer_size** already is in the same struct — that file even
documents the convention. Right now one missing symbol silently downgrades image
paste to a code path that can never work under WSLg.

Related, not duplicates:
- #50847 same native host clipboard path, but a different symptom (hang after a
  read timeout) on Arch/Hyprland.
- #49895 same WSL "nothing happens", but it assumes the Linux read goes through
  wl-paste/xclip. On 2.0.29 it goes through the native host clipboard (as #50847
  notes), so installing wl-clipboard changes nothing.
- #48931 (closed) NixOS, same "missing wayland library" class. There, adding a
  library path was enough because the distro lib was new enough; on Ubuntu 20.04
  the system lib is too old, so a newer lib is needed, not just a path.

### Plugins

none

### OpenCode version

2.0.29

### Steps to reproduce

1. WSL2 with WSLg, Ubuntu 20.04 (libwayland-client 1.18).
2. Open opencode v2 in the TUI.
3. Copy an image on the Windows side.
4. Press ctrl+v in the prompt.
   -> nothing is attached; on some attempts an error popup starting with "X11 " appears.

### Screenshot and/or share link

_No response_

### Operating System

Windows 10 + WSL2 (Ubuntu 20.04, WSLg); kernel 6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2

### Terminal

Windows Terminal

issues.title: tui: IME preedit (composition) text renders white and is invisible on light themes
issues.body:
## Description

When typing Chinese with the Microsoft Pinyin IME in the TUI, the **preedit / composition string (the pinyin before you confirm it)** is rendered in white. On any light theme the prompt background is also light, so the composition text is effectively invisible — you cannot see what you are typing until you press space and the characters are committed.

Committed text is fine (renders in the normal dark `text` color); only the composition string is affected.

## Environment

- opencode CLI **2.2.0** (`opencode-cli.exe`, Windows x64, bundled with the desktop app)
- OS: Windows 11 Insider `10.0.28020`
- Terminal: Windows Terminal `1.25.2733.0`
- Terminal app theme: `light`, color scheme: `VSCode Light Modern` (so the terminal's default foreground is already dark — this is **not** a terminal color-scheme problem)
- IME: Microsoft Pinyin (default Win11 IME)
- Reproduced with `theme.mode` = `light` and also with the `system` theme while the terminal is in a light scheme
- Not reproducible on dark themes (white composition text is visible there)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Put the terminal and opencode in a light theme (`theme.name = "one-light"` / `"github-light"` / `"catppuccin-latte"`, or `system` with a light terminal scheme).
2. Focus the prompt input.
3. Switch to a Chinese IME and start typing pinyin, e.g. `zhe yang` — do **not** commit yet.
4. Observe the composition string in the input line.

## Expected

The composition string should be readable — ideally using the theme's `text` color (or a new dedicated token such as `textComposition` / `textPreedit`) and optionally an underline to mark it as provisional.

## Actual

The composition string is drawn in white (`#ffffff`-ish), producing near-zero contrast on the light prompt background.

## Additional context

- The theme schema has no token for IME/composition/preedit text. I dumped the full token list from the docs (`text`, `textMuted`, `background`, `backgroundPanel`, `backgroundElement`, `border*`, `diff*`, `markdown*`, `syntax*`) and there is nothing that maps to this element, so **a custom theme cannot work around it** — the color appears to be hard-coded.
- Changing the Windows Terminal color scheme to a light one (dark default foreground) does not help, which confirms the color is set by opencode rather than inherited from the terminal.
- Related but distinct: #55101 (Chinese IME preedit overlaps the prompt placeholder) — same area of the UI, different symptom.

## Suggested fix

Use `theme.text` (or add a `textPreedit` token defaulting to `text`) for the composition string instead of a fixed white, and keep the underline as the provisional-state indicator.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Per-request provider transport timing in debug logs (request ID, headers, first event, stream end)
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

When a prompt stalls on a large-context session, the logs don't show where the time went. On `dev`, `model-transport.ts` logs WebSocket connect/reuse/send at debug level. Nothing records when response headers arrive, when the first stream event arrives or when the stream ends, and nothing ties those lines to one request. So you can't tell provider queueing or rate limiting (slow headers) from slow generation (fast headers, long stream) or from a local delay (lock wait, WebSocket connect timeout followed by HTTP fallback).

Proposal: a debug-level structured event per milestone, at most once per request attempt. Each event carries a local request ID, an attempt ID that links an HTTP fallback to its WebSocket attempt, and monotonic elapsed ms:

- request started
- transport selected (http or websocket, new or reused); websocket connect begin / open / error / timeout
- request sent
- response headers: HTTP status plus a strict allowlist of provider request-ID headers (`x-request-id`, `request-id`, `cf-ray`)
- first raw bytes or frame, and first decoded event
- stream ended (completed / failed / interrupted)

It logs no URLs, prompts, bodies, tool arguments or credentials, and never logs individual frames. It would only run with debug logging on. Timeouts, retries and fallback stay the same.

Two real cases where an earlier, smaller version of this trace answered the question:

- #57849: headers arrived 21.7–178.2 s after the request started, and the first event 2–5 ms after the headers. The wait was at the provider, before it responded. It wasn't generation or the client.
- Two stalls on a reused WebSocket: the first event came after 3.4 s and 10.7 s, then the stream ran 363 s and 467 s before it was interrupted. That time was spent inside the stream, so blaming a slow provider would have been wrong.

I have this working on 2.2.0 (in `packages/ai/src/route` and `packages/core/src/session/model-transport.ts`, with tests). CONTRIBUTING asks for design review before core changes, so I'm asking here first and will only open a PR if you want one.

Related: #49381 (a UI performance tab built from persisted message times; it doesn't cover the transport layer), #57178 (first-provider-event timing for `step.streamed`), #35935 (a closed OTLP tracing PR; this proposal is smaller and needs no collector).


### Tested upstream
upstream dev bf94de965df728eb78f37362f4249b81acd9c126 (2026-10-30): packages/ai/src/route and core session/model-transport.ts have no request-level timing (only WebSocket connect/reuse/send debug logs); local implementation 66973af42a on v2.2.0: transport-timing 6/0, provider-trace 5/0, http-timeout 8/0, route 9/0, session-transport-timing 6/0, session-model-transport 33/0, session-model-transport-live 7/0

issues.title: desktop: browser tools disappear from a running session after auto-update (2.2.0 -> 2.2.2)
issues.body:
## Summary

After the desktop app auto-updated from 2.2.0 to 2.2.2 and restarted, an already-running session lost the entire `browser` tool namespace (`search("browser")` returned 0). The browser attach RPCs returned HTTP 499 exactly at restart and were never retried for the resumed session. New sessions are not affected.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.2 (upgraded from 2.2.0 during the session)
- OS: Windows 10 (10.0.19045), x64
- Terminal: desktop app (no terminal env vars set)
- Shell: `C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe`
- Install/channel: desktop app, channel `latest`, generic auto-updater (`https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/desktop/opencode/`)
- Active plugins: none found (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` only contains a `providers` block)

## Reproduction

1. Start the desktop app on 2.2.0 and open a session in a project.
2. Use browser tools successfully in that session (open a tab, take a screenshot).
3. Let the app auto-update to 2.2.2 and restart.
4. Resume / re-open the same session (the conversation is still live).
5. Run `search("browser")` → 0 matching tools; `browser.*` calls are unknown.

Expected reproduction rate: consistent for the session that was running during the update; a brand new session gets the tools back.

## Expected Behavior

The resumed session should keep the browser tools, or the desktop client should re-attach the browser bridge after restarting on the new version.

## Actual Behavior

The tool catalog for the resumed session no longer contains `browser.*`, even though browser calls worked minutes earlier. The desktop UI still works and the session continues on the new server.

Server log excerpt (UTC; local time is UTC+8):

```
01:24:04 cli starting version=2.2.0 channel=latest
...
02:21:15 Sent HTTP response ... POST /api/rpc/experimental.browser/attach http.status=499
02:21:15 Sent HTTP response ... POST /api/rpc/experimental.browser/attach http.status=499
02:21:15 Sent HTTP response ... POST /api/rpc/experimental.browser/attach http.status=499
02:21:39 cli starting version=2.2.2 channel=latest args=["serve","--service"]
```

The running process list shows the desktop app restarted at 10:21:25 local time and the install directory was updated at 10:21:23.

## Additional Context

- The three `499` responses are the only browser-related errors around the update; there is no later re-attach attempt for the resumed session.
- Tool registration appears to be negotiated when the session/agent starts; because the session was started under 2.2.0, the new client did not re-advertise the browser capability for it.
- Workaround used: start a new session (tools return), or drive a local headless Chrome with `puppeteer-core` from the shell instead of the built-in browser.
- Related symptom: the same restart also canceled a running background dev-server command with "server restarted", which is expected behavior for the restart itself.

If it helps, I can provide the full `opencode.log` slice around the update with paths redacted.
