issues.title: desktop: sessions missing from server cannot be deleted (DELETE 404 not handled)
issues.body:
## Summary

The desktop app shows "ghost" sessions that exist only in local state (drafts.sqlite) but not on the server. Deleting them calls `DELETE /api/session/{id}`, the server responds `404 SessionNotFoundError`, and the app treats this as a failure without cleaning up its local references — so the ghost entry can never be removed from the UI.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.18 (desktop app, sidecar service `opencode-cli.exe serve --service`)
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26200 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: N/A (desktop app)
- Shell: cmd.exe / PowerShell
- Install/channel: desktop app, latest
- Active plugins: oh-my-openagent (fails to load: "Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function")

## Reproduction

1. Get a session entry in the desktop app that has no server-side record. On my machine this happened naturally: during a service port conflict (see Additional Context), 8 sessions were created in a ~28h window and were never persisted to the server database.
2. The ghost sessions still appear in the workspace session list — local references survive in `%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop\drafts.sqlite`:
   - `document` table: `opencode.workspace.<ws>.dat:session:<id>:prompt` (empty prompt draft)
   - `state` table: `opencode.browser.dat|sidecar` row keyed by the session id
3. Click delete on such a session.
4. The app calls `DELETE /api/session/<id>` → server responds `404 {"_tag":"SessionNotFoundError",...}` → the app reports a delete failure and keeps the entry.
5. The entry is permanently undeletable from the UI.

## Expected Behavior

A `404 SessionNotFoundError` on delete should be treated as "already gone": remove the local references (prompt draft, browser sidecar state) and drop the entry from the list. Optionally, the session list should not render entries that have only local draft state with no server backing (or should render them as discardable drafts).

## Actual Behavior

Delete fails with an error and the ghost session stays in the list forever. Verified server-side evidence:

- Server log: `DELETE /api/session/ses_f16d31626ffeONweIVod05774k http.status=404` (attempts at 2026-09-28T18:01:52Z and 2026-09-28T20:21:43Z, and again after a full service restart)
- The session id is absent from both `session_v2` and `session` tables in the server database (checked read-only)
- All 8 ghost sessions have empty prompt drafts and no messages anywhere

## Additional Context

Origin of the ghost sessions (why they have no server record): on 2026-09-28 between 17:41-17:53 UTC the log shows dozens of `Managed service port 49374 on 127.0.0.1 is already in use by another process` errors (then port 49375 as well) — multiple service instances were fighting. Sessions created in that window were never persisted; after the service situation settled, they only lived on in the desktop app's local state.

Workaround (manual, requires quitting the app): delete the leftover rows from `drafts.sqlite` — the `document` row `...:session:<id>:prompt` and the `state` row `opencode.browser.dat|sidecar` / `<session id>` — then restart the app.

Frequency: consistently reproducible for every ghost session; the creation of ghosts itself was a one-time event tied to the service conflict window.

issues.title: client: a permanent 404 SessionNotFoundError is retried indefinitely with exponential backoff (one id: 94 requests / 43 min)
issues.body:
### Description

When the desktop client holds a reference to a session the server does not know, it issues `GET /api/session/<id>`, receives a standard, correctly-tagged `404 SessionNotFoundError`, and keeps retrying that permanent error forever with exponential backoff capped at 30 s. The retries surface a recurring "Session not found" toast/modal. A restart of the desktop renderer stops it immediately, without touching the background `opencode serve`.

This is distinct from the existing reports (see duplicate/related check below): regardless of why the id does not exist (a short-lived create/delete race, a stale snapshot resurrection, or a survivor UI reference), a 404 for a session is a terminal condition and should not be retried on a loop. There should be a defence in the retry/error layer that is decoupled from how the phantom id was produced.

Observed behaviour (measured from the local server access log):

- One specific id `ses_e78950f37ffe…` was requested 94 times over 43 minutes (11:28:54 → 12:12:28) after it was already returning 404.
- Retry cadence is exponential backoff `+1s, +2s, +4s, +8s, +16s, +30s` and then stays at one request every 30 s indefinitely.
- Across the day there were 103 `GET /api/session/<missing-id>` → 404 responses, 42 of them from a single id.
- The error body is the canonical V2 tagged shape, i.e. it is recognised as session-not-found rather than a generic error:

  {"_tag":"SessionNotFoundError","sessionID":"ses_…","message":"Session not found: ses_…"}

Workaround that worked: restarting only the desktop renderer stopped it — in the 60 s after restart the 404 rate fell from ~2/min to 0, while the background `opencode serve` kept running and all real sessions/history were preserved. This localises the loop to renderer/client state rather than the server.


Expected behavior：
A not-found for a session is a terminal condition:
1. stop retrying that id (no unbounded backoff for a deterministic 404);
2. drop the id from the tab/list/recent references that keep requesting it;
3. do not raise a user-visible toast/modal for a session the client itself can prune.

Transient failures (network/5xx) can keep the existing retry policy; only the permanent SessionNotFoundError class should short-circuit.
Actual behavior：
The client retries the deterministic 404 forever (capped cadence 30 s) and keeps notifying the user with a "Session not found" toast/modal.


How the phantom ids arose in this case (context, partly inferred): the retry loop above is fully measured from logs; the origin of the ids is less certain and likely overlaps the existing create/delete-race and stale-snapshot issues. The desktop client appears to create sessions optimistically (a client-generated ses_ id followed by an async POST); a failed POST can leave an id the server never knew. A bulk delete of hundreds of test sessions also left some UI references (drafts / closed tabs / layout) pointing at deleted sessions. Most phantom ids are requested only 1–2 times; a single id entered the long loop — i.e. "producing a phantom id" is common, "retrying it forever" is the rarer, more damaging bug this report focuses on.

Suggested fix area (not implemented): in the client data/query layer, classify `SessionNotFoundError` (any shape the existing predicates already accept) as a terminal error for that session key — cancel the retry chain, prune references, and suppress the notification. Keep retrying only on non-terminal transport/5xx errors. A focused regression would assert that a 404 response to `session.sync(id)` produces no second GET and removes the id.


Related but distinct:
- #57026 recurring session-not-found modal for ids that never existed (create/delete race); reproduced — covers where the phantom id comes from.
- #56736 delayed metadata/family reads resurrect a deleted session in the client cache; reproduced.
- #48012 isSessionNotFoundError only matching the exact V1 shape — covers whether the error shape is detected. Here the canonical tagged shape IS already detected and is still retried, so the predicate gap does not explain this case.
- #47516 / #47683 / #51940 stale subagent rejections, survivor references, missing-session handling on delete.

This report is specifically about unbounded retry of a permanent 404 after it has already been correctly recognised.

### Plugins

Local third-party plugins are present, but the retry loop is client-side renderer behaviour (it stops on renderer restart while the service and plugins keep running), so it is not attributable to a plugin.

### OpenCode version

2.2.1

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use the macOS desktop app connected to the shared local background `opencode serve`.
2. Leave the client holding a reference to a session id that does not exist server-side (this happens naturally after an optimistic create whose POST fails, or after bulk-deleting sessions while tabs/drafts/layout still reference them).
3. Observe `GET /api/session/<id>` returning the canonical 404 SessionNotFoundError in the server log.
4. The client keeps retrying that deterministic 404 with +1/+2/+4/+8/+16/+30 s backoff, then every 30 s indefinitely (one id observed: 94 requests over 43 minutes), repeatedly raising a "Session not found" notification.


### Screenshot

_No response_

### Operating System

macOS (darwin, arm64)

### Terminal

Desktop app (Electron), connected to a shared local background `opencode serve`

issues.title: client: delayed metadata and family reads resurrect deleted sessions in the client cache
issues.body:
Title: client: delayed metadata and family reads resurrect deleted sessions in the client cache

## Summary

A successful metadata or family response started before `session.deleted` can restore the deleted record after the event has already removed it from the client data store.

There are two reproducible sequences: a session's own delayed metadata read, and a parent's delayed family read containing a concurrently deleted child. In the family case, an immediate subsequent `session.sync(child)` makes **no new GET request**, because publication of the stale family snapshot also marks the child synchronized.

This is a client projection/cache consistency issue. It does **not** restore a session in authoritative server storage, and no server-side resurrection or durable data loss is claimed.

## Environment

- Windows; Bun 1.4.2.
- Dynamically reproduced against a custom checkout at `72d0dce8ea437ea061e0680110fa19a81aa118fd`.
- Compared official references: `63c1a27af5a391d9caa55b82694f496911e1859b` and latest-checked `60a5a6ca7ce176b04cd2321ffd1819b1ea8e6006`.
- The metadata/family sync implementation is identical at all three revisions. **The official revisions were source-compared, not dynamically executed.**
- The fixture calls real production `createData` and the generated Promise client, with injected in-memory HTTP responses and an event bus. It does not copy the reducer or access a real service, database, model, or user session.

## Reproduction

Use a Solid `createRoot`, instantiate `OpenCode.make` with an injected fetch implementation, and pass that client and an in-memory event emitter to the production `createData`. This follows the fixture pattern in `packages/client/test/solid-data.test.ts`.

Deliver correctly shaped synthetic durable `session.deleted` events through the emitter's `listen` handlers. All session labels below refer to fixture-only records. Use deferred promises to control response completion, not sleeps or network timing.

### A. Delayed metadata response

1. Call `data.session.remember(A)` with a valid fixture `SessionInfo`.
2. Call `data.session.invalidate(A.id)`, then start `data.session.sync(A.id)`.
3. Have the mocked `GET /api/session/<A>` signal that it has started, but withhold its pre-deletion snapshot response.
4. Emit `session.deleted` for A.
5. Assert that `data.session.get(A.id)` is absent and `data.session.family(A.id)` is empty. These checks pass before releasing the response.
6. Resolve the deferred request with `Response.json({ data: A })` and await the actual sync promise.
7. Assert that A is still absent. This fails: A is present again and its family is `[A]`.

### B. Delayed parent-family response

1. Remember a root R and child C, where `C.parentID === R.id`.
2. Start `data.session.sync(R.id, { children: true })`.
3. Return R normally from `GET /api/session/<R>`. Withhold the child-list response from `GET /api/session?limit=200&order=desc&parentID=<R>`, retaining a snapshot containing C.
4. Once the child-list request has started, emit `session.deleted` for C.
5. Check that C is absent from `get` and from R's family.
6. Release `Response.json({ data: [C], cursor: {} })` and await the root-family sync.
7. Observe that C has returned to both the metadata store and R's family.
8. Call and await `data.session.sync(C.id)` while counting injected fetch calls. The count remains **two total requests**: the original root GET and child-list GET. There is **no child GET** to check the resurrected record.

## Expected Behavior

- An observed deletion takes precedence over an earlier metadata or child-list snapshot.
- The deleted record remains absent from client session information and family membership after the earlier response completes.
- A stale family snapshot must not silently establish a deleted child as a successfully synchronized cache entry.

## Actual Behavior

| Sequence | Immediately after deletion | After the older response completes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Own metadata read | A absent; family empty | A present; family `[A]` |
| Parent family read | C absent; R's family excludes C | C present; R's family `[R, C]` |
| Child sync after family resurrection | Two requests already made | Still two requests; no child GET |

Both deletion-ordering assertions fail against the tested production data layer.

## Additional Context

Source locations are repository-relative:

- `packages/client/src/solid/data.ts:607–635` in the tested custom checkout: `removeSession` invalidates the session/family keys and removes metadata and family membership.
- `packages/client/src/solid/data.ts:687–689` in that checkout: `session.deleted` dispatches to `removeSession`.
- `packages/client/src/solid/data.ts:1662–1683` in that checkout, corresponding to **`:1656–1677` in both official references**: the sync callback unconditionally publishes `[info, ...children]`, calls `sync.complete` for each member, and registers family membership.

Deleting C invalidates C's own keys, not the pending family read keyed by R. Consequently, checking only whether R's own read remains current would not address sequence B.

Controls in the same isolated run:

- Completing a metadata read **before** delivering deletion leaves the record absent afterward.
- A delayed transcript read cannot republish after deletion on the tested custom checkout, which has additional transcript-discard protection. This control is **not** claimed as an official-runtime result.
- Across this and the companion retention reproduction, the final run recorded **3 passing controls and 3 failing product assertions**, including these two failures. Exit status was **1**, not a passing gate. All fixtures finished with zero pending responses, zero event listeners, and zero captured request errors; no fallback fetch occurred.

This report concerns the shared client data owner, not Home's separate query-cache merge behavior. The Home-only candidate related to #49419 is not being reported here. No full rendered-Home reproduction is claimed.

## Suggested solution — not implemented

Maintainer decision requested: make deletion precedence part of metadata/family snapshot publication, including deletion of members while an ancestor's listing is in flight. A per-member generation or equivalent bounded reconciliation mechanism may be appropriate; ordinary refresh invalidation alone does not revoke the old response's ability to write.

Preserve the valid normal-order case and avoid treating every refresh as a deletion. Retain both sequences as focused regression coverage, particularly the family case and its subsequent no-GET cache hit. No implementation or production behavior change is included in this report.

issues.title: desktop: pending send retries forever, minting a new session ID per attempt ("Session not found")
issues.body:
## Summary

With the Desktop client connected to a remote server, a pending send retries forever. Each attempt mints a fresh session ID (and a fresh message ID), so the retry never converges: the server answers `SessionNotFoundError` and the app raises a new "Request failed — Session not found: ses_…" toast every few seconds. It began within seconds of the remote server restarting and ran at ~11 requests/minute for 3.5 hours.

## Environment

- opencode version: `2.2.1` (server, `opencode --version`). The Desktop client reports `2.2.2`; the server does not record the client version, so that number comes from the reporter.
- OS: Linux 4.19.0-gvisor aarch64 (server, EC2 + gVisor sandbox). Client OS: Unavailable — it connects from a separate machine.
- Terminal: n/a (Desktop client; no terminal environment on the server).
- Shell: n/a.
- Install/channel: server is `latest` from the npm platform tarball, pinned in the image, with `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1`; Desktop updates itself.
- Active plugins: none server-side.

## Reproduction

Not reproduced from a clean state — observed on a live setup:

1. Desktop app connected to a remote OpenCode server over a tunnel.
2. The remote server process restarted (host reboot). Its session database was intact; nothing was deleted.
3. On reconnect, the app started retrying queued sends for sessions that do not exist on that server.
4. Each attempt issues `GET /api/session/<new id>` → 404, `POST /api/session/<new id>/prompt` → 409, `GET /api/session/<sibling id>/message/<msg_st…>` → 404, then repeats with new IDs.

## Expected Behavior

A send for a session the server does not have should fail once with a terminal, actionable error, or be dropped/reconciled against the server. It should not mint a new session identity on every retry.

## Actual Behavior

The loop never stops. The toast reappears with a different ID each time, including after dismissing it, and the server receives 11–12 requests per minute indefinitely.

## Additional Context

Server-side log (`role=server`) over 3.5 hours:

- 2,385 responses with status 404 covering 2,376 distinct session IDs; the first was 9 seconds after the server booted. 425 prompt responses returned 409.
- Every failing ID is absent from `session_v2`, `session_message`, and the event sequences. The database is healthy: 698 sessions and 37,552 messages, nothing deleted or archived.
- Session IDs are time-sortable. Sorting the failing IDs against known session creation times places each one at the moment of its own request, i.e. they are minted per attempt rather than replayed.
- The message IDs in the retried prompts are `msg_st<20 hex>` (e.g. `msg_stba57dd822d96fe95520a`). The server's database contains zero rows in that format; it produces `msg_<24 base62>` (e.g. `msg_189ef3fdc001NtyR0nMG9xWRbv`). All 420 observed message IDs were distinct — no retry reuses one.
- This is not a client/server compatibility failure: a new session created from the same client against the same server worked end to end (7 messages, two prompts answered, tools ran).
- `POST /api/session` on 2.2.1 accepts a caller-supplied `id` (verified: create, get and delete with a chosen ID returned 200/200/204), so client-minted IDs are not the obstacle.
- Prompting an unknown session returns 404 `SessionNotFoundError`, and reusing a message ID on an existing session is idempotent (200). I could not reproduce the 409 path in isolation, so I am not claiming its cause.
- No `POST /api/session` appears in the log for the failing IDs. Caveat: successful creates are not logged (verified with a probe), so this is suggestive rather than conclusive.

Impact: continuous server load, unbounded log growth, a toast the user cannot clear, and repeated failures that point at a session the user cannot find. Nothing is lost on the server.

Screenshots of three toasts (distinct IDs) are available from the reporter on request.

issues.title: desktop: recurring Session-not-found modal for session IDs that never existed (v2.0.32, Windows)
issues.body:
## Summary

The desktop app periodically (observed every ~20 minutes, as two interleaved cadences ~2 minutes apart) issues `GET /api/session/<id>` for session IDs that never existed in the server's store, receives `404 SessionNotFoundError`, and surfaces a modal error (`请求失败 / Session not found: ses_…`). Impact: recurring modal interruption while working; no data loss observed.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.32 (desktop `@opencodedesktop` 2.0.32.0, staged CLI 2.0.32, npm global `@opencode/cli@2.0.32`)
- OS: Windows 11, 10.0.26200.9711 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: Desktop app (Electron) — not applicable
- Shell: `C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe` (PowerShell 5.1.26100.9711)
- Install/channel: latest; background service at `http://127.0.0.1:45278`
- Active plugins: `opencode-feishu-plugin` 0.2.30 (from `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`), local TUI plugin `plugins/tui-tps` (from `cli.json`)

## Reproduction

1. Start the desktop app connected to the local background service, with at least one real session open (a TUI/CLI client was also connected on the same machine).
2. Leave it running idle; no user interaction is required.
3. Within ~20 minutes a modal appears: `请求失败 / Session not found: ses_<id>`; it recurs on a ~20-minute cadence. Two interleaved series were observed, e.g. at `:49:53 / :09:53` and `:51:52 / :11:52` (server log clock).
4. The same second, the server log shows (verbatim):

```text
timestamp=2026-10-19T08:09:53.912Z level=INFO run=80c266f5 message="Sent HTTP response" http.span=2 role=server http.method=GET http.url=/api/session/ses_eacca402fffeN7u3VJ0c4Amhrr http.status=404
timestamp=2026-10-19T08:09:53.914Z level=INFO run=80c266f5 message="Sent HTTP response" http.span=1 role=server http.method=GET http.url=/api/session/ses_eacca402fffeN7u3VJ0c4Amhrr http.status=404
timestamp=2026-10-19T08:09:53.916Z level=INFO run=80c266f5 message="Sent HTTP response" http.span=1 role=server http.method=GET http.url=/api/session/ses_eacca402fffeN7u3VJ0c4Amhrr http.status=404
timestamp=2026-10-19T08:09:54.364Z level=INFO run=80c266f5 message="Sent HTTP response" http.span=1 role=server http.method=GET http.url=/api/session/ses_eacca402fffeN7u3VJ0c4Amhrr http.status=404
timestamp=2026-10-19T08:11:52.684Z level=INFO run=80c266f5 message="Sent HTTP response" http.span=3 role=server http.method=GET http.url=/api/session/ses_eacc87069ffeJISQHT2U1BD7oA http.status=404
timestamp=2026-10-19T08:11:52.695Z level=INFO run=80c266f5 message="Sent HTTP response" http.span=3 role=server http.method=GET http.url=/api/session/ses_eacc87069ffeJISQHT2U1BD7oA http.status=404
```

Response body (retrieved from the desktop renderer's Chromium HTTP cache):

```json
{"_tag":"SessionNotFoundError","sessionID":"ses_eae1dfbb5ffe69zYeau2G1dAkc","message":"Session not found: ses_eae1dfbb5ffe69zYeau2G1dAkc"}
```

## Expected Behavior

No modal error for internal/ephemeral session IDs. Either the request should not be issued, or a 404 for a session the UI itself did not create should be handled silently (e.g. dropped from the tab/list) instead of raising a modal dialog.

## Actual Behavior

A modal error `请求失败 / Session not found: ses_…` with a dismiss (×) button, recurring roughly every 20 minutes for the duration of the app session.

## Additional Context

**The requested IDs never existed server-side.** I queried every table and text column of the live `opencode.db` (25 tables) plus the migration backup of the same DB — 0 rows for each offending ID. They appear only in session transcripts (self-reference from discussion of the bug). Session rows increased normally across the same period (240 → 245), so this is not lost data.

**The list endpoint is healthy.** `GET /api/session?limit=5000&order=desc&parentID=null` returns 191 sessions and each one fetches fine individually — so it is not a "list contains unreadable rows" problem.

**The desktop renderer is the requester** (at least for one series): the 404 responses are cached under `%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop\Cache\Cache_Data\data_1` for URLs `http://127.0.0.1:45278/api/session/ses_…`.

**The desktop app's own persisted UI state does not contain these IDs**: `drafts.sqlite` (`state.tabs`, `tabs.closed`, `tabs.recent`, and per-session documents) and the Local Storage leveldb only reference real, existing sessions. So the IDs are not restored from local state.

**Hypothesis (unconfirmed):** a temporary/ephemeral session is created and then deleted quickly, and a UI component races the deletion. For example, the installed Feishu plugin implements:

```js
const created = await doFetch(`${base}/api/session`, { method: "POST", ... })
const tempID  = extractSessionID(await created.json())
try   { await doFetch(`${base}/api/session/${tempID}/generate`, { method: "POST", ... }) }
finally { await doFetch(`${base}/api/session/${tempID}`, { method: "DELETE" }) }
```

Any client that reacts to the corresponding `session.created` event by fetching session details will hit 404 after the `DELETE`. I could not confirm which component creates the sessions in this case (the plugin's summary path ran only 7 times overall, mostly a day earlier, so it does not match the 20-minute cadence).

**Workarounds tried, none helped:** closing/restarting the desktop app; restarting the background service; clearing the app's HTTP cache; removing a stale draft tab from `drafts.sqlite`; disabling an unrelated plugin watchdog.

**Frequency:** consistent (~every 20 min) while the app is open.

**Note:** the machine clock jumped by ~5 hours during the investigation, so wall-clock times above should be read from the server log's UTC timestamps.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Persistent right-side message navigation sidebar in the desktop app session view
issues.body:
### Description

In long sessions on the desktop app, reviewing earlier turns means scrolling or relying on URL hashes. There's no in-app way to jump straight to a specific user question from a persistent overview.

A persistent navigation sidebar on the right of the session view — listing each user message (truncated question text) and jumping to it on click — would make navigating long conversations much faster.

### Request

Add a persistent right-side navigation panel in the session view that:

- Lists every user message in the session, showing the truncated question text as each entry
- Is always visible (not a modal)
- On click of an entry, scrolls the message timeline to that message

Rough sketch:

```
┌─────────────────────────────┬──────────────┐
│  message timeline           │  Messages    │
│                             │              │
│  ▸ user: How do I parse...  │  How do I... │ ← click → jump
│  ▸ assistant: ...           │  Add a test  │
│  ▸ user: Add a test for...  │  Fix the bug │
│  ▸ assistant: ...           │  ...         │
│                             │              │
└─────────────────────────────┴──────────────┘
```

### What already exists in the code (so this is low-friction to implement)

While reading `packages/app`, I found the building blocks are all already there — this feature is mostly wiring, not new infrastructure:

- `visibleUserMessages()` — already computed in `packages/app/src/pages/session.tsx:227` (the exact list of user messages to show).
- `scrollToMessage(message, "smooth")` — already implemented in `packages/app/src/pages/session/use-session-hash-scroll.ts:88`, handles reveal + DOM scroll + hash update.
- `anchor(id)` — DOM id resolver, passed into `MessageTimeline` at `session.tsx:1672`.
- `SessionSidePanel` (`packages/app/src/pages/session/session-side-panel.tsx`) — the right-side panel already exists and hosts tabs (review / context / file-tree). A new "Messages" tab or sub-panel would slot in here naturally.

So the implementation is roughly: a new panel/tab inside `SessionSidePanel` that maps over `visibleUserMessages()`, renders truncated text, and calls `scrollToMessage(msg, "smooth")` on click.

### Current behavior

- No in-app navigation between user messages; only scrolling and URL hash (which isn't user-discoverable)
- The TUI (`packages/tui`) has a `/timeline` "Jump to message" modal and `session.message.next/previous` keybinds, but the desktop app has none of these

### Expected behavior

- A persistent, always-visible right-side list of user messages (truncated)
- Click any entry → timeline scrolls to that message

### Environment

- opencode desktop app (Windows), latest
- Long sessions where scrolling back to a specific turn is tedious

### Notes

- I searched existing issues and didn't find one covering a persistent message-navigation sidebar (the TUI's `/timeline` is a modal, and is TUI-only). Apologies if I missed one.
- I'm happy to open a PR for this — the change is contained to `SessionSidePanel` + a small new component, reusing `visibleUserMessages` and `scrollToMessage`.

issues.title: desktop: renderer unresponsive - infinite layout loop (scrollToEnd and resizeItem) in virtualized message list
issues.body:
## Summary

OpenCode Desktop (Windows) renderer becomes permanently unresponsive on startup when it auto-restores a tab pointing to a very large session. Stack samples show an infinite layout loop between the virtualized message list's auto-scroll (`scrollToEnd` → `scrollToIndex`) and `resizeItem` → `Map.forEach` → reactive update → `scrollToEnd` again. The window thread never yields, so Electron fires `renderer-unresponsive` repeatedly and shows the "OpenCode is not responding" dialog. Reproduced on 2.1.2 and 2.1.3 (Electron 44.9.1 / Chrome 152).

## Environment

- opencode version: desktop app 2.1.3 (also reproduced on 2.1.2 before updating); CLI 2.1.3
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.19045 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: Unavailable: desktop Electron app (no terminal involved)
- Shell: PowerShell 5.1
- Install/channel: latest (packaged desktop install, auto-updater)
- Active plugins: none found in config

## Reproduction

1. Use OpenCode Desktop with a long-running session containing a very large number of message parts (session that accumulated a ~7 MB server log).
2. Close and reopen the desktop app; it restores the tab via `localStorage` key `opencode.desktop.window.<windowId>.last-active-url`, which points at `/server/<server>/session/<ses_…>` (the large session).
3. Within ~10–20 s of window load, the renderer stops responding; the "OpenCode is not responding" dialog appears (Reabrir / Exportar logs / Continuar aguardando).
4. "Reabrir" reloads the same restored tab and the loop re-triggers.

## Expected Behavior

The session view should render (even if slowly), and/or the auto-scroll logic should not feed back into item-resize observers in an unbounded loop. There should also be a way to disable session/tab restore on startup.

## Actual Behavior

UI thread is stuck in a synchronous loop; the window is dead until killed. Exported `window.log` reports `renderer unresponsive` with these samples (identical shape on 2.1.2 and 2.1.3, only bundle names differ):

```text
[error] (window) renderer unresponsive { currentURL: 'oc://renderer/index.html' }
<4> at Te (oc://renderer/assets/route-*.js:9:58274)
<3> at Array.Re (main-*.js:2:12237)
    at Object.active (route-*.js:10:9062)
    at n (route-*.js:9:52592)
    at Object.scrollToFn (route-*.js:9:54800)
    at w._scrollToOffset (esm-*.js:1:20352)
    at w.scrollToIndex (esm-*.js:1:18902)
    at Proxy.scrollToEnd (esm-*.js:1:19335)
    at Te (route-*.js:9:58258)
<1> at Map.delete (<anonymous>)
    at Fg.F.resizeItem (route-*.js:9:55294)
    at route-*.js:9:58629
    at Map.forEach (<anonymous>)
    at route-*.js:9:58600
<1> at Fg.F.resizeItem (route-*.js:9:55184)
    ... (same cycle)
Total Samples: 14
```

The pattern `scrollToEnd → scrollToIndex → resizeItem → reactive update → scrollToEnd` repeats across every sample, indicating an unbounded render/layout feedback loop in the virtualized message list.

## Additional Context

- Fully reproducible on every start while the large session is the restored tab; the app becomes usable only after clearing the restore state.
- Workarounds tried: holding Shift at launch (does not prevent restore); updating 2.1.2 → 2.1.3 (loop persists); clearing/replacing the `Local Storage` folder finally stops the freeze.
- Suggest: (a) break the loop (e.g. guard auto-scroll while resizing / rAF-scheduled scroll, item-size measurement caching), (b) add a setting or startup flag to disable tab/session restore, (c) a fallback to open a new-session tab if the restored route triggers the unresponsive watchdog.
- Debug log bundles (window.log / main.log / renderer.log samples) available on request; they contain full `renderer unresponsive` stacks and netlogs (several privacy-redacted identifiers).

issues.title: desktop: ResizeObserver loop makes app unresponsive
issues.body:
## Summary

The desktop app (Electron) becomes unresponsive due to an infinite `ResizeObserver` loop. The renderer floods with `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` errors, making the UI unusable. Restarting the app temporarily fixes it, but the issue returns.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.21 (also occurs on 2.0.22)
- OS: macOS Darwin 25.6.0 (arm64)
- Terminal: Apple Terminal (xterm-256color)
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: latest (desktop app)
- Active plugins: none

## Reproduction

1. Open the OpenCode desktop app
2. Use the app normally (switch tabs, resize panels, work in editor)
3. After some time, the UI becomes unresponsive
4. Check logs — hundreds of `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` errors

## Expected Behavior

The app should remain responsive without flooding the renderer with ResizeObserver errors.

## Actual Behavior

The renderer process enters an infinite loop of ResizeObserver notifications, causing:
- UI freeze / unresponsiveness
- Hundreds of error logs per second
- Need to restart the app to recover

## Additional Context

**Log excerpt (renderer.log):**
```
[2026-10-02 09:59:10.580] [error] ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.
[2026-10-02 09:59:27.346] [error] ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.
[2026-10-02 09:59:49.663] [error] ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.
... (hundreds more)
```

**Workarounds tried:**
- Restarting the app — temporarily fixes until the loop restarts
- Updating from 2.0.21 to 2.0.22 — did not resolve the issue

**Frequency:** Intermittent but frequent. Occurs multiple times per day during normal use.

**Impact:** Makes the app unusable for extended periods. Forces frequent restarts.

issues.title: tui: root OSC 7501 status is not cleared on exit
issues.body:
### Description

When the TUI exits, it doesn't clear its OSC 7501 root status record. Terminals that show program status keep showing `opencode` as `idle` after OpenCode has quit and the shell prompt is back. This happens with both `/exit` and Ctrl+C. Claude Code clears its status on exit in the same terminal.

### Cause

- `packages/tui/src/context/program-status.ts` sends the root clear from `onCleanup(() => send(ROOT, { state: "clear" }))`.
- The exit callback in `packages/tui/src/app.tsx` (around lines 324–328) calls `destroyRenderer(renderer)` before the Solid tree is disposed.
- By the time the cleanup runs, the renderer is destroyed, `setProgramStatus` can't write, and the clear is dropped.

Sending the root clear from the exit path before `destroyRenderer` should fix it.

### Additional context

- Flagged in review on #55172 ([comment](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/55172#discussion_r4261134511)), but no issue was opened.
- #60411 assumes the shutdown clear reaches the terminal.
- #54560 (not merged) sends a namespace clear on exit.


### Plugins

None relevant

### OpenCode version

2.2.0 and 2.2.2 (unchanged on dev as of Oct 30)

### Steps to reproduce

1. `script -q oc.log opencode`
2. Wait for the prompt, then run `/exit` (Ctrl+C behaves the same).
3. `LC_ALL=C grep -ao $'\e\\]7501;[^\e\a]*' oc.log | sort | uniq -c`

**Expected:** The output ends with a root `]7501;state=clear`.

**Actual:** No clear is sent:

```
   1 ]7501;?
   1 ]7501;state=idle:app=opencode
```


### Screenshot

_No response_

### Operating System

macOS 26.3

### Terminal

Herdr desktop app (herdr-core 0.1.14); the raw output above is captured with script, so it is not terminal-specific

prs.title: feat(mcp): trust private-network server certificates on first use
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Part of #40111. Stacked on #60039 (per-server `tls` config); once that lands, this diff is just the first-use flow.

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Trusting a private-network MCP server's self-signed certificate becomes a first-use decision instead of up-front TLS config:

1. The first connect to an `https` server at a private IP fails with the presented certificate — fingerprint, subject — and the command to trust it.
2. `opencode mcp trust <url>` shows the certificate's subject, validity, and fingerprint and asks for confirmation. `--yes` skips the confirmation (required without a terminal); `--force` is only needed to re-pin after the certificate rotated.
3. The pin is stored per project in a new `mcp_trusted_host` table (new migration). Later connects are pinned by fingerprint, so a rotated certificate fails the connection instead of being silently accepted, and certificates without IP SANs work because the fingerprint is the identity check.

The trust hint is only added for actual TLS verification failures (self-signed, expired, alt-name, and the Node-style codes); network, protocol, and HTTP failures keep their original message. Hostnames never qualify — the IP literal in the config is the trust boundary, not DNS. An explicit `tls` config takes precedence.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/core/test/mcp-trust.test.ts`: private-host classifier, per-project store, first-use → trust → reconnect, rotation → re-pin with `--force`, and an appliance certificate without IP SANs.
- `packages/server/test/mcp-trust.test.ts` (end-to-end over HTTP), `packages/cli/test/mcp-auth-choices.test.ts`, 56 TLS tests, 92 schema and 10 protocol tests.
- `tsc` clean in schema/core/protocol/client/server/cli; `bun run migration --check` passes.

### Visual



### Screenshots / recordings

No UI change (CLI + server).

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(cli): report usage for steps that end after run goes idle
prs.body:
`opencode run --format json` was dropping the `step_finish` line for the last step of a run, so anyone summing cost and tokens from the stream got numbers that were too low.

After `session.wait` resolves, the run loop sets `finalizing` and ignores everything except `session.execution.*` events. `reconcile()` then re-emits any text, reasoning and tool parts we missed from the projected messages, but it never emitted step boundaries. The final `session.step.ended` usually shows up over SSE right after the wait resolves, so its usage was lost.

On a real run the JSON stream summed to $0.1932 while the stored session cost was $0.2050, with about 143k cache-read tokens and the last step's output tokens missing.

```diff
 reconcile()
   for each projected assistant message
+    if no live step_start was seen
+      emit step_start
     emit missed text / reasoning / tool parts
+    if message finished and no live step_finish was seen
+      emit step_finish with finish, cost, tokens, snapshot
```

A single map records whether each step got a live `step_start` or `step_finish`, so steps that streamed normally don't get duplicated. I didn't keep reading step events after idle instead, because the terminal execution event isn't guaranteed to arrive and the late event could race with reconcile.

Tests in `packages/cli/test/run/noninteractive.test.ts`: one where the step end arrives too late (usage is now reported), one where it was seen live (no duplicate), and the existing reconcile test now expects the projected `step_start`. I ran `bun test test/run/noninteractive.test.ts` and `bun typecheck` in `packages/cli`, and `bun run check` at the root. All pass.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="currentColor" font-family="ui-monospace,monospace" font-size="9">
<style>
.r{animation:in 3.6s ease-out infinite both}
```

prs.title: fix(client): bypass environment proxies for loopback service traffic
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes #52054
Related: #51247
Supersedes #60441, #57030, #57744

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Exempts loopback traffic from `HTTP(S)_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` at both the transport boundary (`@opencode/client`, `@opencode/core`) and process startup (`@opencode/cli`, `@opencode/desktop`), stopping `/api/event` SSE stalls, false unresponsive-service kills, and Basic-auth password leaks to forward proxies.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  CLI["CLI / TUI / SDK"]
  Proxy["HTTP(S)_PROXY"]
  Svc["127.0.0.1 / [::1] / localhost"]
  Shell["Session bash tool"]

  CLI -- "proxy: false + merged NO_PROXY/no_proxy" --> Svc
  CLI -. "remote egress only" .-> Proxy
  CLI -- "unmutated caller NO_PROXY" --> Shell
```

- **Transport-level bypass (`@opencode/client`, `@opencode/core`):** `service-probe` and `OpenCode.make` wrap default `fetch` with Bun's `{ proxy: false }` for `localhost`, `*.localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8` (e.g. `127.0.0.2`), and `[::1]`, protecting standalone SDK callers and early probes before any CLI entrypoint runs; `WebSocketConstructor.proxy` now matches bracketed IPv6 `[::1]`, `127.0.0.0/8`, and `*.localhost`.
- **Unified `NO_PROXY` / `no_proxy` merge (`@opencode/cli`, `@opencode/desktop`):** Bun and Node's `EnvHttpProxyAgent` read lowercase `no_proxy` alone whenever set while `WebSocketConstructor` reads uppercase `NO_PROXY` first, so both spellings receive one case-insensitively deduplicated list (`corp.internal,127.0.0.1,localhost,::1`).
- **Wildcard `*` preservation:** Keeps `NO_PROXY=*` intact as `"*"` instead of `"*,127.0.0.1,..."`, which otherwise breaks Node/Electron's `EnvHttpProxyAgent` exact `noProxy === "*"` check under `http.setGlobalProxyFromEnv()`.
- **Saved service env & Desktop startup ordering:** Applies the merge inside `ServiceConfig.processEnv` and after `Object.assign(process.env, ...)` in `server-process.ts` so `opencode service set env no_proxy ...` cannot recapture loopback; runs `ensureLoopbackNoProxy()` before Desktop's `startSidecarProbe()` and `BackgroundService.connect`, dropping the duplicate `loadProxyEnvironment` call.
- **Unpolluted session tool shells:** `Env.session()` restores the caller's pre-startup `NO_PROXY` / `no_proxy` snapshot so `bash` tool subprocesses do not inherit synthetic loopback exemptions.

```ts
type Fetch = typeof globalThis.fetch

export const loopbackAwareFetch: Fetch = Object.assign(
  (input: Parameters<Fetch>[0], init?: Parameters<Fetch>[1]) => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    return globalThis.fetch(input, isLoopbackUrl(url) ? Object.assign({}, init, { proxy: false as const }) : init)
  },
  { preconnect: () => undefined },
)
```

### How did you verify your code works?

Unit and integration coverage across `@opencode/client`, `@opencode/cli`, `@opencode/core`, and `@opencode/desktop` against a recording `502` proxy with `HTTP(S)_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` set and `NO_PROXY` empty or split.

prs.title: fix(opencode): end an ACP prompt when its session goes idle
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #60065

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

When a durable write fails during an ACP turn (for example `SQLITE_FULL`), the `session.execution.*` outcome can be lost. The adapter only ended a prompt on that event, so `session/prompt` stayed pending and every later prompt was refused with `Session already has an active ACP prompt`.

- `packages/cli/src/acp/turn.ts`: once the prompt is delivered, the turn also waits on `POST /api/experimental/session/:id/wait`. If the session goes idle before an outcome event arrives, the turn ends through the normal `settle` path, which still reports a step or execution error that was recorded.
- `packages/cli/src/acp/translate.ts`: a `session.execution.failed` that arrives before `session.inbox.delivered` now ends the turn instead of being ignored. That turn can never deliver its prompt, so there was nothing left to wait for.

Normal turns are unaffected: the terminal event is published before `awaitIdle` resolves, so an event still ends the turn first.

Only the ACP side is in scope here. Core storage retries stay in `fix/disk-full-session-recovery` / #53704.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun test test/acp` from `packages/cli`: 102 pass.
- Two new cases in `test/acp/turn.test.ts` cover the lost outcome and the pre-delivery failure. Both fail without the source change (the first times out at 5s, the second never gets the error) and pass with it.
- `bun run typecheck` from `packages/cli`: no type errors.

prs.title: feat(mcp): support per-server TLS trust for remote MCP servers
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Part of #40111

Related: #23506, #14696, #26862, #1694

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Adds an optional `tls` block to remote MCP server config, so a server with a self-signed or private-CA certificate can be trusted for that one server without changing verification anywhere else (no `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`):

- `ca_file` / `ca_pem`: PEM CA bundle, from a file (with `~` or workspace-relative paths) or inline, or both.
- `fingerprint`: pins the exact certificate the server presents, like an SSH host key. OpenCode compares the presented certificate against the fingerprint and then uses the fingerprint as the identity check for the connection. Name matching is deliberately not enforced: LAN appliance certificates often omit the IP SAN a hostname check would require (a self-signed `CN=OPNsense` with no SANs is the common case), and the fingerprint already identifies the certificate.

The TLS options are scoped to the fetch used by that server's transport. A missing CA file or a fingerprint mismatch fails the connect with a specific error instead of the first request. Docs: new "TLS Trust" section on the MCP servers page.

### How did you verify your code works?

- 56 tests in `packages/core/test/mcp-tls.test.ts`: unit coverage for PEM/fingerprint/path validation, plus integration tests that connect a real MCP server over TLS with fixture certificates, including a new appliance-style certificate that has a CN and no SAN (the case a name check rejects).

prs.title: fix: find empty directories in filesystem search
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #60293

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

The ripgrep-backed search index derives directories only from the parent paths of `rg --files` entries, so a directory with no indexed files can never be returned by `/api/fs/find`, even though it exists (TUI `@` completion and the app directory picker both use it). The `fff` backend already indexes directories; this closes the gap for the ripgrep backend, which is selected for non-git locations, home, Windows, workspace-backed locations and when `fff` is unavailable.

`packages/core/src/filesystem/search.ts`
- After the ripgrep scan, walk the location through its `Environment` file listing (the same location-scoped seam ripgrep uses) and stage the directories whose subtree contains no visible files. Those are exactly the empty directories a file index cannot describe, so `emptydir/` and `.gitkeep`-only directories become searchable.
- Directories already indexed from a file are still descended, so empty children of non-empty directories are found. A non-known directory that contains a visible file ripgrep did not index is treated as excluded content and pruned. Additions are staged per subtree and published only once the root visit completes, so an ignored directory with files never leaks its empty descendants (or an empty sibling next to an unlistable directory) into the index.
- Ignore rules are evaluated for the staged candidates before publishing. Ripgrep has no directory-aware ignore query, so for git-backed locations the candidates are sent in one batch to git's own matcher, `git check-ignore --no-index --stdin -z`, spawned through the location's `Environment` spawner (works for workspace-backed locations). Ignored directories and their descendants are dropped. If the check cannot run (spawn failure or an unexpected exit code), we fail closed: no discovered directories are published and one warning is logged; the file index is untouched.
- The walk is bounded by a 3s deadline and a semaphore of 8 concurrent listings, reuses prepared fuzzy targets across refreshes, and a listing failure never fails the scan. Because additions are staged and published atomically, a completed walk publishes a deterministic set (a timed-out walk publishes none) instead of a timing-dependent subset.
- `fff`, the schema and the API are unchanged.

`packages/app/src/workspaces/selection/domain.ts`
- `createDirectorySearch` now always combines the direct listing with `file.find` results instead of only using the listing when search returns nothing, so a listing-only match such as an empty directory cannot be dropped just because the index matched something else. ### Issue for this PR

Closes #60466

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

The root OSC 7501 clear was only sent from `onCleanup` in `context/program-status.ts`. Every exit path calls `destroyRenderer` before the Solid tree is disposed, so by the time that cleanup ran `setProgramStatus` returned `false` and the clear was dropped. ### Issue for this PR

Closes #59110

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

`compaction.buffer` was doing two jobs: reserving headroom before compaction and capping the summary's completion tokens. With a small buffer (2048 in the report) and a reasoning model, the model spends the whole budget thinking, so compaction fails with `finish_reason: length` and "Compaction summary reached the output token limit" even though the conversation fits the window.

The summary request now also keeps the default reserve free (15% of the window, or 16k) and aims the transcript at the rest, so the reply has room to reason before it writes the summary. `buffer` keeps its documented job of deciding when compaction triggers. ### Issue for this PR

Closes #58909

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature

### What does this PR do?

When `model` names a provider whose config entry the schema rejected, the provider is dropped from the catalog. `Model.default` then returned the first available model, so the configured default silently resolved to a different provider — in practice the built-in free one — and the prompt and its tool calls ran there.

The default now resolves to nothing when its provider was never registered, and `ModelResolver` no longer picks an arbitrary model as a second fallback. prs.title: refactor(core): share provider discovery through a simple cache
prs.body:
Provider, model and integration state is per Location, so built-in provider plugins that fetch credential-scoped data redid the same fetch in every Location. With 30 Locations open, GitHub Copilot hit `/models` 30+ times at startup and again on every account switch, and DigitalOcean, Azure and Modal did the same.

I added a small internal global cache, `SharedCache`. It is not part of the plugin API.

```text
SharedCache.get({ key, load, maxAge })
  value for key newer than maxAge  -> return it
  load for key already running     -> join it
  otherwise                        -> run load, store { value, time }
  load fails                       -> last good value if any (and log), else fail; next call retries
```

There's no background loop, refcounting or notifications. Each Location's plugin keeps its own triggers (startup, account switch) and its own 10 minute timer, calls `get`, and only reloads providers when the value differs from what that Location applied last. So the network cost is one request per key per `maxAge`, however many Locations are open. Unread entries are dropped after an hour.

Keys are the integration, the connection (credential ID or env name, never a token) and any Location config that changes the answer, like base URL or Copilot headers. Each `load` resolves the connection's current credential when it runs, so a refreshed token is always used.

Plugins moved onto it: GitHub Copilot, DigitalOcean, Azure and Modal. Along the way:

- DigitalOcean routers and Modal models are sorted after decoding, so a reordered response isn't a change.
- DigitalOcean re-checks the active connection after loading, like the others. With an expired token it reuses whatever is cached for the connection (so a newly opened Location still shows routers) and stops retrying and warning every interval.
- Azure deployments now refresh every 10 minutes. Switching to the account that is already active reuses the cached list instead of refetching, so I removed the Azure test that relied on that refetch and changed the stuck-discovery test to block on the first account's initial load.

Requests to Copilot, DigitalOcean and Azure from server start through opening N Locations, and Copilot `/models` during an account switch (fake upstream from the location-duplication harness, 100 ms latency):

| Locations | Start + open: Copilot / DO / Azure | Copilot switch |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3 / 3 / 3 -> 1 / 1 / 1 | 2 -> 1 |
| 10 | 12 / 12 / 12 -> 1 / 1 / 1 | 11 -> 1 |
| 30 | 32 / 32 / 32 -> 1 / 1 / 1 | 31 -> 1 |

Every Location still ends up with the same 216 models. Modal isn't covered by the harness because it needs a configured base URL.

I looked at Effect's `Cache`, but it can't keep the last good value on failure or take a per-call `maxAge`, so a small map was simpler.

Out of scope: Console (it fits `get` with a 1 minute poll and a 30 second `maxAge` re-check on 401/403, follow-up), wellknown remote config, and local discovery, which already shares its fetch.

prs.title: fix(desktop): retain renderer permissions across shared-session windows
prs.body:
﻿All open desktop windows now keep notification, clipboard, and voice-call permissions when multiple windows share Electron's default session.

Fixes #51748

- **Per-session handler registration:** Installs `setPermissionRequestHandler`, `setPermissionCheckHandler`, and `webRequest` header hooks at most once per `Session` (`WeakMap` / `WeakSet`) instead of overwriting them on each `BrowserWindow` creation.
- **Live `WebContents` membership:** Evaluates permission requests and checks against the session's active renderer `webContents.id` set, revoking each window on `destroyed` / `closed` without affecting sibling windows or admitting embedded `WebContentsView` guests.
- **Origin-only checks:** Requires at least one live renderer window in the session (`allowed.size > 0`) when Electron invokes `setPermissionCheckHandler` with `webContents === null`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  W1["Window 1 (id=1)"] -- "register / closed" --> S["WeakMap<Session, Set<id>>"]
  W2["Window 2 (id=2)"] -- "register / closed" --> S
  E["Embed View (id=99)"] -. "unregistered" .-> H
  S --> H["Single Session Permission Handler"]
  H -- "allowed.has(id)" --> G["Granted (W1 & W2)"]
  H -- "!allowed.has(id)" --> D["Denied (Embed / Closed)"]
```

```ts
export function allowRendererPermissions(win: BrowserWindow) {
  if (win.isDestroyed() || win.webContents.isDestroyed()) return
  const webContents = win.webContents
  const session = webContents.session
  const allowed = allowedBySession.get(session) ?? registerPermissionHandlers(session)
  const id = webContents.id

  if (allowed.has(id)) return
  allowed.add(id)

  const remove = () => {
    allowed.delete(id)
  }

  webContents.once("destroyed", remove)
  win.once("closed", remove)
}
```

prs.title: feat(desktop): spellcheck toggle and system-language dictionaries
prs.body:
The desktop composer always spellchecks against the OS locale only, with no way to turn it off. Someone with a German locale writing prompts full of English code terms gets red underlines on almost every word (#32155, #26112).

## Changes

- **Default dictionaries follow the system languages** (Windows/Linux): one dictionary per entry in `app.getPreferredSystemLanguages()`, matched exactly or by base language. US English is added when none of them is English, because prompts mix prose with English code terms. The defaults are recomputed on every launch until the user picks dictionaries themselves.
- **Spellcheck toggle** in Settings → General (desktop only, next to Pinch to zoom). It sets the Electron session's spellchecker, so it covers every text field, not just the composer.
- **Spellcheck context menu** on editable fields: a `Spellcheck` checkbox, plus a `Spellcheck Languages` submenu on Windows/Linux listing Electron's dictionaries by name in the app language. The last selected dictionary can't be unchecked; the checkbox is the off switch. macOS gets only the checkbox because the system spellchecker detects the language itself.
- Both settings live in `opencode.settings` (`spellcheckEnabled`, `spellcheckLanguages`), like `pinchZoomEnabled`, and are applied right after `app.whenReady()`.
- New strings are English only. The four locales that map desktop strings by position (`hr`, `hu`, `is`, `lt`) now map only the strings they have, so the new keys fall back to English instead of `undefined`.

## Notes

- Electron's `setSpellCheckerLanguages` also turns the spellchecker back on, so startup sets the languages first and the stored on/off state second. An Electron 44 smoke test caught this: before the fix, turning spellcheck off didn't survive a restart.
- If the context-menu checkbox changes while Settings is already open, the Settings toggle doesn't update until Settings is reopened, same as Pinch to zoom today.

## Verification

- `bun test src/main/native/spellcheck-languages.test.ts` covers system-language → dictionary defaults, including Chromium's aliases such as `de`/`de-DE`.
- App i18n and settings unit tests pass; `bun typecheck` passes in `packages/app` and `packages/desktop`; oxlint and prettier are clean on the changed files.
- Ran the bundled `native/spellcheck.ts` under Electron 44.9.1 on Linux/Xvfb with `LANGUAGE=de_DE:en_US`:
  - Defaults were `de-DE` + `en-US`.
  - The submenu built 57 entries.
  - Adding French and removing German persisted and applied.
  - Turning spellcheck off persisted, disabled the languages submenu, and stayed off after re-applying on restart.
- Not yet tested in the packaged app on Windows.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

With more than one TUI window connected to the same server, a single session event produced one desktop notification (and sound) per window. prs.title: fix(ai): keep tools with a throwing execute runnable
prs.body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60407.

`tool(...)` decided between a runnable tool and a declare-only one by looking at `execute`'s return type, using `never` to mean "no `execute`". A sync `execute` that only throws also returns `never`, so it got the declare-only type and `ai.llm.loop` / `LLM.loop` rejected it:

```ts
const fail = tool({ description, parameters, execute: () => { throw new Error("Unavailable.") } })
ai.llm.loop({ model, prompt, tools: { fail } }) // was a type error
```

Now an omitted `execute` defaults the inferred result to a private `NoExecute` marker that no function can return, and the tool is declare-only only when the result is exactly that marker. A `never`, `any`, `unknown` or `object` result counts as runnable. This is type-only; runtime behavior doesn't change. I added type tests showing that `ai.llm.loop` accepts tools whose `execute` only throws, returns `any` (`JSON.parse`) or returns `unknown`.

prs.title: fix(app): never hide every server from Home
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #53834

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

When stored server state flags every server as hidden, `servers.visible` comes back empty and Home sits on its loading skeleton forever. This is an alternative to #59050 that fixes it without an effect writing back to the store:

- **Read:** `resolveVisibleServers` filters out hidden servers but never returns none. If every server is flagged hidden, it shows the built-in server, or the first server if there isn't one. `isHidden` returns true only for a server that is flagged *and* not shown, so the settings menu matches the project list.
- **Mutations:** `remove` and `setHidden` clear the hidden flag on any server shown despite being flagged, all inside the same `batch`. Removing the only shown server therefore leaves the fallback unhidden in storage, and hiding the only shown server does nothing. Toggling a different server in an all-hidden stored state also keeps the server that was already shown, so it doesn't disappear when you show a remote.

Stored state from older builds or hand edits displays correctly through the read path. Its flags get fixed by the next mutation that touches them.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New unit test for `resolveVisibleServers`. The `runtime/server`, `servers` and `home` unit tests pass (180 tests).

prs.title: feat(app): page the timeline from the composer
prs.body:
**PageUp and PageDown now scroll the conversation while you're typing, like Slack or Messages.**
Before, they moved the cursor inside your draft. Now your draft, cursor and focus stay where they are while the conversation moves a page.

❌ **Before**
1. You're typing a message and want to check something a few screens up.
2. ❌ PageUp jumps the cursor to the start of your draft, and the conversation doesn't move.
3. You have to click into the conversation, scroll, then click back into the composer.

✅ **After**
1. PageUp and PageDown scroll the conversation by most of a screen, the same amount as when the conversation itself has focus.
2. Paging to the top loads older messages, and paging back to the bottom follows new output again, just like scrolling with the mouse wheel.
3. While a suggestion popup (@, / or history) is open, the keys do nothing, so the popup and its query stay as they are.
4. Shift+PageUp/PageDown and other modified page keys keep their normal meaning, so you can still select text. Home and End are unchanged.

**Long drafts:** the page keys always scroll the conversation, even when the draft is long enough to scroll on its own. That's what Slack and Messages do. You can still move through a long draft with the arrow keys, the mouse or Shift+PageUp/PageDown.

```diff
- PageUp in composer -> browser moves the cursor in the draft
+ PageUp in composer -> timeline scrolls 80% of its visible height (unpins, may load older messages)
+ PageDown at the end -> timeline follows new output again
+ popup open          -> key ignored
```

prs.title: fix(app): feather the sidebar list's scroll edges
prs.body:
Scrolled sidebar rows now fade out under the nav instead of being sliced off.

**Before:** scroll the sidebar's session list and the top row (and its selected background) is cut off hard under New session. The bottom edge always faded, even with nothing below.

**After:** each edge feathers by as much as there is left to scroll past it, up to 16px. At the top of the list, or when the list fits, there's no fade, so the first row and its selected background stay crisp.

```
TitlebarTabStrip (vertical)
  on scroll, or when the list or scroller resizes:
    --fade-top    = min(16, scrollTop)
    --fade-bottom = min(16, room left below)
titlebar.css
  mask: transparent → black at --fade-top … black → transparent at --fade-bottom
```

The mask is the same gradient shape as the one in `packages/ui/src/components/list.css`. I tried that file's scroll-timeline approach first and dropped it: with 30 tabs open it kept the page busy at idle (about 0.07s of main-thread work every 2s, against 0.001s without it), which delayed the sidebar's hover-dwell prefetch enough to fail `tabs.spec.ts` "loads a tab's transcript while the pointer rests on it". prs.title: feat(core): let agents ask another session a question
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #60072

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Multi-session work is normal today: subagents, forks, background jobs, and the desktop voice delegator all run beside the session that started them. But the only sanctioned cross-session path is parent to child, so an agent that needs an answer from a sibling session improvises through a shared file or asks a human to relay it.

This adds two native tools over the existing session inbox. `ask({session, question})` resolves an existing top-level session by exact id or exact title, lists metadata only, and queues one bounded question into that session's inbox. `answer({replyTo, answer})` lets the target reply once back to the asker as a message. Texts are capped at 4000 characters, three questions per pair, and no message text or system prompt is read; the duplicate-answer guard compares stored metadata only. Zero schema, protocol, table, or client changes.

Core is the right home because the voice delegator already messages sessions by reading their transcripts. An agent tool should read no message text and be cooperative: the target decides whether to answer, and answers with a tool call.

### How did you verify your code works?

`bun test test/tool-ask.test.ts` — 7 tests covering admission (queued synthetic, envelope, metadata), every refusal class (self, child caller/target, archived, cross-project, unknown, ambiguous with ≤10 candidates), single-answer enforcement (forged `replyTo` and non-ask synthetics refused, second answer refused), the 3-per-pair and duplicate-pending caps, inbox promotion making the question model-visible, and permission denial through an agent ruleset. prs.title: refactor(core): resolve configured model variants once across config layers
prs.body:
Fixes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/59836
Fixes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/55226

Supersedes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60097 and https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/55979.

### Problem

`opencode.config.provider` partially seeded models in `provider.transform` (copying only `base` and `limit`) and then built variants inside each config document's loop in the late `model.transform`:

1. Custom models without `variants` in `opencode.json` always regenerated default `low/medium/high` variants in the late pass, overwriting tiers (or `[]`) supplied by an earlier `model.transform` plugin (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/59836).
2. Overriding a provider's `package` in `opencode.json` (for example pointing `zai` at `@opencode/ai/providers/anthropic`) left catalog models with variants spelled for the old package (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/55226).
3. Multi-layer `opencode.json` files resolved variants before later documents finished overriding `package` or `limit`, or wiped `variants` configured in an earlier file when a later file changed the provider `package`.

### Change

Build the complete configured model and its default or repackaged variants once in `provider.transform` (before external `model.transform` plugins run), then in the late `model.transform` only re-apply explicit `opencode.json` fields (`overlayFields` and `applyExplicitVariants`). Production code in `packages/core/src` shrinks by 6 net lines (`provider.ts` goes from 283 to 273 lines).

```diff
 opencode.config.provider
   provider.transform (before external model transforms)
-    copy catalog base + limit only
+    apply all config layers' provider and model fields
+    resolve default custom variants and repackaged catalog/provider variants once
+    overlay explicit config capabilities.reasoning and variants

   model.transform (after external model transforms)
-    re-copy base, apply fields, regenerate !base / repackaged variants (clobbers plugins)
+    restore model if removed by a plugin, then re-apply explicit config fields and variants only
```

| Setup | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Custom model in `opencode.json` + plugin sets `[none, low, medium, xhigh]` or `[]` | Overwritten with `[low, medium, high]` | Keeps plugin's variants |
| Layer 1 sets `modelID: "claude-opus-4-8"`, layer 2 sets `package: "aisdk:@ai-sdk/anthropic"` | Spelled for layer 1 package | Spelled once for Anthropic (`low..max`) |
| Provider `package` overridden (`zai` to `anthropic`) | Keeps stale `zai/chat` variants | Respells for Anthropic |
| Layer 1 sets model `variants`, layer 2 overrides provider `package` | Loses layer 1 or keeps stale fields | Respells base for new package, then overlays layer 1 `variants` |

### Verification

- `bun run --cwd packages/core script/test.ts test/config/provider.test.ts --rerun-each 10 --randomize`: 430 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run --cwd packages/core script/test.ts test/models.test.ts test/plugin/models-dev.test.ts test/plugin/provider-opencode.test.ts test/variant.test.ts`: 104 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run --cwd packages/core typecheck:tsc`: clean
- `bun run check`: 35/35 tasks pass, 0 errors

prs.title: fix(core): preserve plugin-supplied model variants
prs.body:
Fixes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/59836

### Problem

When a custom model is configured in `opencode.json` without `variants` or `capabilities.reasoning` and a plugin supplies its reasoning tiers in `model.transform` (for example `none`, `low`, `medium`, `xhigh`), `opencode.config.provider`'s late `model.transform` overwrites those variants with the default `["low", "medium", "high"]` list.

### Change

Skip default variant generation on custom models when an earlier `model.transform` already populated `model.variants`. Catalog model package-change respelling (`repackaged`) stays unchanged.

```diff
 late config model.transform
   overlay explicit opencode.json fields
   if config omits variants and capabilities.reasoning:
-    if custom model or catalog model repackaged:
+    if (custom model with empty variants) or catalog model repackaged:
       model.variants = Variant.resolve(model)
```

| `opencode.json` | Plugin `model.transform` | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| omits `variants` | sets `[none, low, medium, xhigh]` | `[low, medium, high]` | `[none, low, medium, xhigh]` |
| sets model `package`, omits `variants` | sets `[none, low, medium, xhigh]` | `[low, medium, high]` | `[none, low, medium, xhigh]` |
| omits `variants` | none | `[low, medium, high]` | `[low, medium, high]` |
| sets `variants` or `capabilities.reasoning` | sets `[none, low, medium, xhigh]` | config wins | config wins |

### Out of scope

- A plugin that sets `variants = []` on a custom model still receives default variants when `opencode.json` omits `capabilities.reasoning`.
- Provider-level `package` overrides on catalog providers (covered separately by https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/55979).

### Verification

- `bun run script/test.ts test/config/provider.test.ts --rerun-each 10 --randomize` in `packages/core`: 400 pass, 0 fail

### Highlights

- **Unified Quotes and Annotations**: Timeline quotes, terminal quotes, and browser annotations now share a compact optional-comment editor, while source highlights remain attached to local drafts. ([#60164](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60164))

### Core

#### Improvements

- Enabled `experimental_image_generate` by default when an image-capable provider is connected. ([#60258](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60258))
- Recorded the start time of each session’s latest execution.

#### Bug fixes

- Rejected persistent terminal requests whose working directory no longer exists.
- Preserved media when sessions are forked or imported.
- Associated image-generation notices with the correct background job.

### TUI

- Preserved captured attachments and their original source paths. Thanks [@OpeOginni](https://github.com/OpeOginni). ([#60222](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60222))
- Prevented middle-truncated paths from overflowing at very narrow terminal widths.

### Desktop

issues.title: stripAnsi leaves private-parameter CSI payloads in tool output (ESC[<...M mouse reports, ESC[>...c replies)
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

`stripAnsi` in `packages/coding-agent/src/utils/ansi.ts` treats `<`, `=` and `>` as a valid CSI final byte, so for these sequences it strips only the first three bytes and leaves the parameters as text:

| input | returns |
| --- | --- |
| `ESC [ < 35 ; 59 ; 1 M` (SGR mouse report) | `35;59;1M` |
| `ESC [ > 0 ; 276 ; 0 c` (device attributes reply) | `0;276;0c` |
| `ESC [ 3 8 ; 5 ; 1 9 6 m` (control) | `` |

A private parameter byte should only belong to the sequence when digits or `;`/`:` follow it.

### Why?

The transcript renders tool output through `getTextOutput()`, which is `sanitizeBinaryOutput(stripAnsi(text))` (`src/core/tools/render-utils.ts:67`). `sanitizeBinaryOutput` then drops the leftover ESC, because `0x1B` is inside `[\x0E-\x1F]`, so the parameters get drawn as ordinary characters. On 1.4.0, `node -e "process.stdout.write('\u001b[<35;59;1Mstep 1\n')"` through the bash tool shows `35;59;1Mstep 1`.

The sanitizer also contradicts the input side of this repo: `packages/tui/src/stdin-buffer.ts:113` already parses this shape as one sequence (`/^<\d+;\d+;\d+[Mm]$/`). 8bf2bfab aligned `stripAnsi` with chalk `strip-ansi`, so the current behavior is deliberate. I think correctness wins for this one shape, since the two halves of pi disagree about it.

### How?

Insert `"[<=>]?(?:\\d{1,4}(?:[;:]\\d{0,4})*)?"` before the final byte, leave `CSI_FINAL` alone. Patch and two regression tests are ready: 0 of 237 existing cases change, and in a 720-case sweep only the 432 private-parameter shapes change. I can send a PR after `lgtm`.

issues.title: pi update: git clean -fdx fails on Windows against npm staging dirs (use -ffdx)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### Environment

- pi 1.4.0 · Windows 11 · git 2.52.0.windows.1 · msys2/Git Bash
- git-type extension installed under `~/.pi/agent/git/`
- Reproduced on both update paths: `pi update --extensions` and `pi update --all`

### What happens

```
Updating https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>...
Error: git clean -fdx failed with code 1
```

pi's update runner resets each git-type extension checkout with `git clean -fdx` before re-fetching/re-installing. On Windows that call exits 1 whenever the working tree contains npm's *staging* directories, which look like:

```
node_modules/@ast-grep/.cli-win32-x64-msvc-<hash>/ast-grep.exe
node_modules/@ast-grep/.napi-win32-x64-msvc-<hash>/ast-grep-napi.win32-x64-msvc.node
```

These are the left-over extraction dirs npm uses when installing platform-specific optional packages. `git clean -f` reports `Invalid argument` against them and bails with exit 1; `git clean -ffd` (double force) removes them without complaint, which is why the same repo is trivially fixable by hand but not via `pi update`.

### Repro steps

1. Install an extension whose `prepare`/`postinstall` pulls `@ast-grep/cli` (e.g. `pi install git:https://github.com/apmantza/pi-lens`) on Windows.
2. Run `pi update --extensions` (or `--all`) more than once. Each cycle re-installs `@ast-grep/cli`, so a `.<name>-<hash>` staging dir is produced.
3. The clean step hits that dir and fails; the whole update aborts even though the fetch and the rest of the install would have worked.

### Suggested fix

A single flag in pi's update runner — `git clean -ffdx` (or `-ffd`) instead of `-fdx` — makes the reset robust against these artifacts. It is also what `git-clean` itself recommends on Windows where the file may be momentarily locked/rename-blocked.

issues.title: pi-durable: pass the model call's origin to HarnessOptions.models

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

pi-durable: pass the origin of each model call to `HarnessOptions.models`, and export the summarize phase's request builder.

### Why?

A host that checks model requests before they are sent (authorization, audit, egress) can't tell why a request is made. Generation, a compaction summary, a hook call and host code all reach `models` the same way. The host has two choices. It can allow everything, which lets a hook send content under the phase's identity. Or it can refuse what it can't attribute, which means turning compaction off. Verifying that a request is exactly the summary of a committed checkpoint also means copying the private logic in the summarize phase.

### How? (optional)

- `models: Models | ((origin: ModelOrigin) => Models)`, with the origin derived by the Harness:
  - `phase`: conversation, task, mode, checkpoint, a unique `run` and an abort signal.
  - `hook`: hooks get the hook origin, never the phase's models.
  - `host`: everything else.
- Export `summaryRequestMessages(view, firstKept, instructions, timestamp)` and have the summarize phase use it.
- This is additive: existing `Models` and `() => Models` hosts are unchanged, and nothing changes in execution or the compaction algorithm.
