issues.title: Bug: Cached models disappear after remote catalog metadata is reset to zero

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

Model `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-terra` intermittently disappears from `pi --list-models`, apparently after system sleep or VPN connectivity issues (or wrong country selection).

```
❯ pi --list-models | Select-String -Pattern "terra"

openai         gpt-5.6-terra                       272K     128K     yes       yes
openai-codex   gpt-5.6-terra                       272K     128K     yes       yes
```

The model is still present in ~/.pi/agent/models-store.json, but its catalog metadata changes:

Field | Before | After
-- | -- | --
lastModified | 1793193879000 | 0
checkedAt | 1793240351635 | 1793295007994
etag | Present | Missing
gpt-6.1-terra in cached models | Yes | Yes
Model visible in Pi | Yes | No

Even with PI_OFFLINE=1, the model remains hidden.

Running pi update --models restores it immediately. This has happened repeatedly.

# Suspected cause
In withRemoteCatalog(), HTTP 404/501 responses reset lastModified to 0 and clear etag, while preserving stored.models.

remoteModels() then rejects the cached models because their timestamp is older than the built-in catalog.

A successful response missing the Last-Modified header is another possible cause.

Source: [remote-catalog-provider.ts (v1.4.0)](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.4.0/packages/coding-agent/src/core/remote-catalog-provider.ts)

---

- Pi 1.4.0
- Node.js 26
- Windows 11

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run pi update --models and verify gpt-6.1-terra is listed.
2. Allow a periodic catalog refresh, potentially during unstable VPN connectivity.
3. Observe that the model disappears while remaining in the stored model array.
4. Run pi update --models again. The model reappears.

The network trigger is intermittent; the exact HTTP response has not been captured.

### Expected behavior

A transient catalog endpoint failure should not invalidate a previously valid cached catalog or hide working models. The last known good catalog should remain available until a valid replacement is received.

```
❯ pi --list-models | Select-String -Pattern "terra"

openai         gpt-5.6-terra                       272K     128K     yes       yes
openai-codex   gpt-5.6-terra                       272K     128K     yes       yes
openai-codex   gpt-6.1-terra                       500K     128K     yes       yes
```

### Version

1.4.0

issues.title: False skill collision on Windows when cwd and home drive-letter casing differs

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

 Description

 ### Summary

 Pi reports false skill-name collisions on Windows when:

 - The current working directory uses a lowercase drive letter, such as c:\Users\...
 - The home directory is returned with an uppercase drive letter, such as C:\Users\...
 - Global skills exist under ~/.agents/skills
 - The current directory is not inside a Git repository

 The conflicting entries point to the exact same files. Windows treats these paths as identical, but Pi compares them
 case-sensitively and loads the global skill directory once as a project resource and again as a user resource.

 ### Environment

 - Pi: 1.0.3
 - OS: Windows
 - Node.js: v24.21.0
 - Global skill directory: C:\Users\user_name\.agents\skills
 - Working directory: c:\Users\user_name\project_name
 - The working directory is not a Git repository
 - There is no .agents directory inside the working directory or its direct project structure

 ### Actual behavior

 Pi displays warnings such as:

 ```text
   [Skill conflicts]
     "herdr" collision:
       ✓ auto (project) c:\Users\user_name\.agents\skills\herdr\SKILL.md
       ✗ ~\.agents\skills\herdr\SKILL.md (skipped)
     "karpathy-guidelines" collision:
       ✓ auto (project) c:\Users\user_name\.agents\skills\karpathy-guidelines\SKILL.md
       ✗ ~\.agents\skills\karpathy-guidelines\SKILL.md (skipped)
     "ponytail" collision:
       ✓ auto (project) c:\Users\user_name\.agents\skills\ponytail\SKILL.md
       ✗ ~\.agents\skills\ponytail\SKILL.md (skipped)
 ```

 The winner and loser paths differ only by drive-letter casing:

 ```text
   c:\Users\user_name\.agents\skills\herdr\SKILL.md
   C:\Users\user_name\.agents\skills\herdr\SKILL.md
 ```

 The loaded skill is also incorrectly classified as project-scoped rather than user-scoped.

 ### Verified comparison

 Using Pi's resource loader with otherwise identical inputs produced:

 ```text
   cwd: c:\Users\user_name\project_name
   skill conflicts: 3
   herdr scope: project
 ```

 Changing only the drive-letter casing produced:

 ```text
   cwd: C:\Users\user_name\project_name
   skill conflicts: 0
   herdr scope: user
 ```

 ### Suspected root cause

 In package-manager.js, Pi attempts to exclude the global Agent Skills directory from ancestor project discovery:

 ```js
   const projectAgentsSkillDirs = projectTrusted
       ? collectAncestorAgentsSkillDirs(this.cwd).filter(
             (dir) => resolve(dir) !== resolve(userAgentsSkillsDir),
         )
       : [];
 ```

 This comparison is case-sensitive. On Windows:

 ```js
   resolve("c:\\Users\\user_name\\.agents\\skills")
       !== resolve("C:\\Users\\user_name\\.agents\\skills")
 ```

 The same issue affects duplicate detection because canonicalizePath() uses realpathSync(), which preserves the input
 drive-letter casing in this environment. Consequently, the realPathSet check does not recognize the paths as
 identical.

 A similar case-sensitive comparison exists in project trust detection in trust-manager.js, so the global
 ~/.agents/skills directory may also be incorrectly treated as a project trust-requiring resource.

 ### Suggested fix

 Use a platform-aware normalized path key for path equality and deduplication. For example:

 ```js
   function comparablePath(filePath) {
       const canonicalPath = canonicalizePath(resolve(filePath));

       return process.platform === "win32"
           ? canonicalPath.toLowerCase()
           : canonicalPath;
   }
 ```

 This helper could be used for:

 - Excluding ~/.agents/skills from ancestor project discovery
 - Skill real-path deduplication
 - Project trust resource detection
 - Other path equality or containment checks on Windows

 The exact implementation may differ, but Windows path comparisons should not depend on drive-letter or path-component casing.

### Steps to reproduce

 1. Add one or more global skills under:

    ```text
      C:\Users\user_name\.agents\skills
    ```

 2. Create a non-Git working directory below the home directory:

    ```text
      C:\Users\user_name\project_name
    ```

 3. Start Pi with a cwd whose drive letter is lowercase.

    A deterministic way to preserve the lowercase cwd is:

    ```js
      // repro.mjs
      import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";

      process.chdir("c:\\Users\\user_name\\project_name");
      console.log("cwd:", process.cwd());

      spawnSync("pi.cmd", [], {
        stdio: "inherit",
      });
    ```

 4. Run:

    ```powershell
      node .\repro.mjs
    ```

 5. Observe that each global skill is reported as a collision between project and user scopes.

 ### Expected behavior

 C:\... and c:\... should be treated as the same path on Windows.

 The global ~/.agents/skills directory should:

 - Be loaded only once
 - Be classified as user-scoped
 - Not produce a collision warning
### Version

1.0.3

issues.title: WSL: clipboard image paste silently fails when pi's cwd is deep (PowerShell interop hits MAX_PATH)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

On WSL, `readClipboardImage()` returns `null` when pi's working directory is deep enough that its Windows path exceeds MAX_PATH, so an image on the Windows clipboard silently fails to paste. Nothing is reported: `runClipboardCommand()` spawns with stderr set to `ignore`, so the failing `powershell.exe` interop call is invisible and the PowerShell backend (the one that actually supplies images on WSL) just returns `null`.

### Steps to reproduce

Pi 1.4.0, Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2/WSLg (kernel `6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`), node 24.15.0, screenshot on the Windows clipboard (Win+Shift+S).

1. Run pi's own reader from a shallow and a deep cwd:

```bash
node --input-type=module -e 'const m = await import("./dist/utils/clipboard-image.js"); console.log(await m.readClipboardImage())'
```

Measured with the same clipboard contents:

- cwd 228 chars (Windows path ~254): `{ mimeType: 'image/png', bytes: 23883 }`
- cwd 232 chars and above (Windows path ~258+): `null`

The Windows path is the interop UNC form `\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\<linux cwd>`, so the Linux budget is roughly 233 characters.

2. Minimal repro — spawning `powershell.exe` itself fails from the deep cwd:

```bash
node -e 'require("child_process").execFile("powershell.exe", ["-NoProfile","-Command","Write-Output ok"], (e,o)=>console.log(e && e.message, o))'
```

stderr: `/mnt/c/WINDOWS/System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0//powershell.exe: Invalid argument` (exit 1). The same command from `/tmp` prints `ok`.

Notes: `wl-paste` is not installed here and `xclip` only lists text targets, so the PowerShell backend is what supplies the image; the same limit applies to an alternative reader that returns the PNG as base64 over stdout, so it is the cwd and not the temp-file/UNC technique.

### Expected behavior

The image pastes, or at least a diagnostic is surfaced instead of returning `null`.

### Why it matters

Any deep repo path (common under `~/source/...` monorepos) silently loses clipboard image paste on WSL, which is also the symptom people report as "image paste is broken" (#2469, #11259).

Suggested direction: spawn `wslpath`/`powershell.exe` with a short cwd, and stop discarding stderr so a failed backend can report instead of failing silently.

### Version

1.4.0

---

_Report drafted with my Pi agent from evidence measured locally on my machine; I reviewed it before posting._

labels.name: bug

### What happened?

Disclosure: I drafted this text with an AI agent. I reproduced the split-read case locally with the shipped StdinBuffer and Editor and pasted the observed output above.


### Steps to reproduce

```
   ```ts
   const buffer = new StdinBuffer({ timeout: 10, escapeTimeout: 10 });
   const editor = new Editor(tui, theme);
   buffer.on("data", (sequence) => editor.handleInput(sequence));

   buffer.process("\x1b[<35;4");                 // first half of an SGR motion report
   await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 40));  // longer than the timeout: head is flushed
   buffer.process("8;27M");                      // second half arrives as new input

   editor.getText();  // "8;27M"
   ```

   8;27M. A report that arrives in one read is consumed by the fullscreen mouse handling as expected; only the
   split case leaks.

   In a terminal: run pi, move the mouse while it is busy (the escape timeout is 10 ms, so a busy event loop
   splits the report), and fragments like 8;27M appear in the prompt.
 ```

   the input stream and swallows the continuation that follows, or Editor.handleInput() refuses to type a string
   that is an obvious control-sequence remnant (an ESC-less report such as [<35;48;27M is typed as-is today).
   Today a moving mouse fills the prompt, and Ctrl+C only clears the line, which reads as "pi prints garbage and
   will not exit".
 ```

Related: #11170 is the other half of the same symptom (an exiting pi leaves the terminal in mouse-tracking    state, so the shell echoes the reports). issues.title: Shift+Enter queues a follow-up instead of inserting a newline in Apple Terminal
issues.body:
# Shift+Enter submits instead of inserting a newline in Apple Terminal

## Summary

On macOS with Apple Terminal (`Terminal.app`), `Shift+Enter` submits (queues as a follow-up
message) instead of inserting a newline. `Ctrl+J` works.

Measured on the reporter's machine: `Terminal.app` sends **`ESC` + `CR` (`0x1b 0x0d`)**, which
pi parses as `alt+enter` and routes to `app.message.followUp`. The macOS modifier fallback
documented in `docs/terminal-setup.md` never fires, because `forwardInputSequence` only
considers the sequence when it is exactly `CR` (`0x0d`).

## Verification status (please read before triage)

Verified on the reporter's machine against pi 1.4.0 / `@earendil-works/pi-tui` by importing the
package and driving it directly:

- `parseKey("\x1b[13;2u")` → `shift+enter`; `matchesKey("\x1b[13;2u", "shift+enter")` → `true`
- `tui.input.newLine` defaults to `shift+enter`, `ctrl+j`
- The Darwin native helper loads and `isModifierPressed("shift")` returns `true` while Shift is
  physically held, so this is not an Accessibility/SSH problem
- `StdinBuffer` merges `ESC` + `CR` into a single `"\x1b\r"` sequence even when the two bytes
  arrive in separate writes (escape timeout 10 ms)
- `parseKey("\x1b\r")` → `alt+enter`; `matchesKey("\x1b\r", "alt+enter")` → `true`;
  `matchesKey("\x1b\r", "shift+enter")` → `false`; `matchesKey("\x1b\r", "enter")` → `false`
- `app.message.followUp` defaults to `alt+enter`

Measured with a raw timestamped capture (single `Shift+Enter` press, tty in raw mode):

```
1885 ms  1b 0d  b'\x1b\r'
```

So the bytes are `ESC` + `CR`, i.e. exactly what `Alt+Enter` produces. `parseKey("\x1b\r")`
returns `alt+enter`, and `matchesKey("\x1b\r", "alt+enter")` is `true`; `app.message.followUp`
defaults to `alt+enter`. That is why the keypress reads as a submit/queue rather than a newline.

The modifier state would disambiguate here — pi can and does read it on local macOS — but the
gate rejects the sequence before the modifier is ever consulted.

## Environment

- pi 1.4.0 (npm `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`), Node v26.3.1
- macOS 27.0.1 (build 26A434), arm64
- Apple Terminal: `TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal`, `TERM=xterm-256color`
- No `keybindings.json` override; `tui.input.newLine` is at its default (`shift+enter`, `ctrl+j`)
- Not over SSH, not in tmux; pi runs on the same machine as `Terminal.app`
- No extension intercepts key input

## Repro

1. Open pi in Apple Terminal.
2. Type `foo`, press `Shift+Enter`, type `bar`.
3. Expected: two-line prompt. Actual: no newline is inserted (reportedly nothing visible happens;
   please confirm it is a no-op and not a submit).

### Byte capture

```sh
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, sys, tty, termios, time, select
fd = sys.stdin.fileno()
old = termios.tcgetattr(fd)
tty.setraw(fd)
sys.stderr.write("press Shift+Enter exactly once\n")
chunks, t0 = [], time.time()
while time.time() - t0 < 5:
    r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.2)
    if r:
        chunks.append((round((time.time() - t0) * 1000), os.read(fd, 64)))
termios.tcsetattr(fd, termios.TCSADRAIN, old)
for ms, d in chunks:
    print(ms, "ms", d.hex(" "), repr(d))
PY
```

## Evidence: what Terminal.app actually sends

In a fresh `Terminal.app` window:

```
$ cat -v
^[
```

One `Shift+Enter` produces `^[` followed by a line break, i.e. the byte sequence
`ESC (0x1b)` + `LF (0x0a)`. It is *not* `CR (0x0d)`, and it is not a kitty CSI-u sequence.

## Why the fallback misses it

`docs/terminal-setup.md` (Apple Terminal section) says pi treats plain `Return` as `Shift+Enter`
when the local modifier state says Shift is held. Two problems:

1. The normalization is gated on an exact `CR` match:

   ```js
   function normalizeNativeShiftEnterInput(data, shouldDetect, isShiftPressed) {
     return shouldDetect && data === "\r" && isShiftPressed
       ? NATIVE_SHIFT_ENTER_SEQUENCE   // "\x1b[13;2u"
       : data;
   }

   forwardInputSequence(sequence) {
     const shouldDetect = sequence === "\r" && (isAppleTerminalSession() || process.platform === "win32");
     ...
   }
   ```

   Since `Terminal.app` sends `\x1b\n`, `shouldDetect` is `false` and the modifier state is never
   consulted.

2. Whatever arrives is therefore never attributed to `Shift+Enter`. `ESC` + `CR` parses as
   `alt+enter`, which is bound to `app.message.followUp`, so the message is queued instead of
   getting a newline.

The native modifier helper itself is fine: loading
`@earendil-works/pi-tui/native/darwin/prebuilds/darwin-arm64/darwin-platform.node` and polling
`isModifierPressed("shift")` returns `true` while Shift is held, on this machine. So this is not
an Accessibility/permission problem and not an SSH/local-modifier problem.

## Verified-good links (so the report is not over-broad)

- `parseKey("\x1b[13;2u")` → `"shift+enter"`
- `matchesKey("\x1b[13;2u", "shift+enter")` → `true`; for `"enter"` → `false`
- `tui.input.newLine` default includes `shift+enter`
- 1.4.0 already contains the fix from the earlier changelog entry
  ("Fixed Apple Terminal `Shift+Enter` by detecting local macOS modifier state")

## Suggested fix

Accept the sequences Apple Terminal actually emits when Shift is held, e.g.:

```js
// Apple Terminal sends ESC + CR for Shift+Enter; ESC-only or plain CR for other shapes.
const shouldDetect =
  isAppleTerminalSession() && (sequence === "\r" || sequence === "\x1b\r");
```

With that gate, `isModifierPressed("shift")` decides: Shift held → rewrite to
`\x1b[13;2u` (`shift+enter`); Shift not held → leave `\x1b\r` alone so genuine `Alt+Enter`
still reaches `app.message.followUp`. The modifier check already exists and works — only the
sequence gate is wrong.

Note `parseKey` maps `\x1b\r` / `\n` to `shift+enter` only when `_kittyProtocolActive` is true,
and Apple Terminal never activates it (it does not answer the kitty query), so that branch is
dead there.

## Workaround for users

- Use `Ctrl+J` for a newline in Apple Terminal.
- Or switch to a terminal with the kitty keyboard protocol (Ghostty, iTerm2 3.5+, kitty,
  WezTerm), where `Shift+Enter` is a real event.

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add a supported atomic, non-cancelling idle-close operation for Pi sessions. It should refuse busy or unknown ownership without cancelling/draining accepted work. Success must prevent new work admission before cleanup and acknowledge completion.

### Why?

LazyPi needs to close a session before archiving its owned workspace, without interrupting accepted work.

On upstream `4954d760504c11df9b2cbdc040346107b6a8153d`, two local SDK/faux-provider probes reproduced this trace:

1. An accepted extension command or `input` handler awaits a barrier.
2. Its context reports `isIdle() === true` and `hasPendingMessages() === false`; no provider request has started.
3. Releasing the barrier starts a model run and produces `agent_settled`.

These getters are observations, not a safe shutdown reservation. Related: #10704 and #9632; this request concerns non-cancelling close rather than idle submission.

### How? (optional)

Pi-owned accepted-work tracking and an identity-bound idle reservation shared by SDK/native/extension entry points, followed by awaited non-cancelling cleanup. Queues, preflight, commands, shell work, compaction and continuations must participate; unknown extension background ownership should refuse closure, not be inferred idle.

The account owner would like to contribute an implementation after API agreement and maintainer approval. Existing prompt tests (21), the two probes, and `npm run check` passed locally; no implementation or PR is claimed.

AI-authored and submitted at the account owner's explicit request; disclosure follows in a comment.

issues.title: Mouse wheel scrolls prompt history instead of transcript in fullscreen on Windows + Zellij

issues.body:
### What happened?

Mouse wheel in fullscreen mode scrolls through the editor's prompt history instead of the conversation transcript when running inside Zellij on native Windows (Windows → Alacritty → Zellij → Pi).

Direct terminal (no multiplexer) works correctly. Linux with tmux also works correctly.

**Root cause:** `TuiAltScreen.beforeTerminalStart()` writes mouse DECSET sequences (`?1000h`, `?1002h`, `?1006h`) before `ProcessTerminal.start()` calls `process.stdin.setRawMode(true)`. Windows ConPTY silently consumes these sequences while stdin is in cooked mode, so the multiplexer's inner pane never enables mouse tracking. Zellij then falls back to emitting `ESC[A`/`ESC[B` arrow keys for wheel events on alternate-screen panes, which the editor interprets as history navigation. I made a PR #9655 already, please review.

**Fix:** Move the alt-screen entry and mouse DECSET writes from `beforeTerminalStart()` to `afterTerminalStart()`, after raw mode is active. I'd like to submit a PR for this.

**Environment:** Pi 0.85.1, Zellij 0.45.1, Alacritty 0.17.0, Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200), Node 22.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82f73340-89d6-490d-9f55-534e6efee08b

### Steps to reproduce

Mouse wheel in fullscreen mode scrolls through the editor's prompt history instead of the conversation transcript when running inside Zellij on native Windows (Windows → Alacritty → Zellij → Pi).

_No response_

issues.title: V8 OOM (SIGABRT) in long sessions: giant ConsString flatten/regex-replace inside flatMap, 5 production crash reports

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## What happened?

Long-running pi sessions (2+ days, ~8MB session file) die with `zsh: abort` (SIGABRT / `FatalProcessOutOfMemory`). I captured 5 macOS crash reports over 2 days; they share two stack signatures, both ending in a single giant string allocation inside V8:

1. `[giant ConsString].flatMap(t => regexp.exec(t))` → `Runtime_FlattenString` → `String::SlowFlatten` → `NewRawOneByteString` → OOM
2. `[giant string].flatMap(t => t.replace(...))` → `Builtins_RegExpReplace` → `Runtime_StringBuilderConcat` → `NewRawTwoByteString` → OOM

Minimal repro (512MB heap, mechanism only — not pi-specific):

```
$ node --max-old-space-size=512 -e "
let acc = '';
const chunk = '中文内容'.repeat(8 * 1024 * 1024);
for (let i = 0; i < 14; i++) acc += chunk;   // ~470M chars two-byte ConsString
const res = [acc].flatMap(t => t.replace(/[\u0000-\u001f]/g, ' '));
"
# → FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit … + same RegExpReplace/SlowFlatten family, Abort trap: 6
```

Interesting detail: at crash time the process RSS was only ~270MB (per the .ips `vmSummary`). The heap "fill" is logical — one huge flatten/concat target — not thousands of live small objects. So raising `--max-old-space-size` only postpones the wall.

Related context: I also found `SessionManager.list()/listAll()` reads every session file fully and builds `allMessagesText` via `allMessages.join(" ")`, and `session-selector-search.js` then runs regex/fuzzy search over that concatenated text per keystroke. With a 367MB sessions dir that is another giant-string path, though my captured crashes are from the in-session pipeline (timestamp correlation with the active session's last write).

I read #9010 (compaction in-process string duplication, auto-closed but maintainer-noted) — same family. My crash reports add production evidence that the pattern also kills cloud-API sessions in the main pipeline, not only local-LLM compaction.

## Steps to reproduce

Run a pi session for ~2 days with heavy tool output, let it compact a few times. It dies with `zsh: abort` mid-run. Full crash reports available (`node-*.ips`, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, node v24.22.1).

## Expected behavior

The agent pipeline should not build/re-flatten unbounded strings; streaming or chunked processing would keep peak memory bounded regardless of session age.

## Environment

- pi: 1.4.0
- node: v24.22.1
- OS: macOS 26.6.2, arm64, 24GB RAM

Happy to share the 5 `.ips` files or dig into specific frames.

**What do you want to change?**

I want bidirectional rendering: reorder RTL lines into visual order before they are written, and put a line against the edge its script reads from. Behind two settings — `terminal.rtl.enabled` (default off) and `terminal.rtl.align` — so nothing changes for lines with no RTL content.

**Why?**

Windows Terminal paints cells in the order the program writes them and does not implement UAX #9 (microsoft/terminal#538, the same blocker raised in #3301). Text stored correctly in logical order therefore reads mirrored on screen: an Arabic user cannot read the transcript, and the caret in the prompt sits on the wrong side of the word being typed.

Copy, search, the saved transcript and column widths are all correct today — only the painted order is wrong. The terminal will not fix it, so the TUI can: write the visual order, keep the logical state.

**How?**

`reorderLine()` in `packages/tui/src/bidi.ts` runs one rendered line through UAX #9 (bidi-js) on grapheme clusters and returns it in visual order. Only the string written to the terminal changes; caret offsets, selection, copy, wrapping and widths stay logical. Code blocks, table borders, list markers and quote bars stay where the renderer put them, and content inside them is reordered where it is produced. Alignment follows the script that dominates the line, so `npm install ثم build the package` stays on the left.

Tests: `packages/tui/test/bidi*.test.ts` (52 tests) and `packages/coding-agent/test/rtl-settings.test.ts`. The implementation is on [rtl-bidi](https://github.com/AliQaseef/pi-rtl-bidi/tree/rtl-bidi) and the PR is [#11580](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11580), auto-closed until this issue is approved.

Screenshots (Windows Terminal, RTL on):

![Arabic reply and tool output in visual order](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AliQaseef/pi-rtl-bidi/rtl-screenshots/rtl-patch/screenshots/pi_reply.png)

![Lists, tables and blockquotes on the reading edge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AliQaseef/pi-rtl-bidi/rtl-screenshots/rtl-patch/screenshots/pi_list_2.png)

issues.title: Add "Ask in Side Chat": ask about selected text in a side panel without interrupting the main conversation

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add an "Ask in Side Chat" action: select text or code from the transcript, a diff, or tool output, then open a lightweight secondary conversation in a side or bottom panel.

Core behavior:
- Capture selected text, ideally with keyboard actions to select a code block, message, or tool output.
- Open the side chat through a configurable keybinding or message action.
- Give the panel its own input, scrollback, and follow-up conversation.
- Keep its context independent: selected text plus side-chat turns, with optional main-session reference context.
- Keep side-chat questions and answers out of the main session history and compaction.
- Allow returning focus to the main conversation without interrupting its ongoing work.

Optional conveniences:
- Use a separately configured model for side chat.
- Copy an answer into the main editor as a prompt draft.
- Explicitly send relevant findings to the main conversation.
- Configure the panel size and keep it open for follow-up questions.

The side chat would answer questions only. File edits and long-running agent tasks would remain outside its scope.

### Why?

When reading an agent's output, I often want to ask a small question such as "What does this snippet do?" or "Why is this line wrong?" without derailing the main task.

Asking in the main conversation adds unrelated questions and answers to its history and future compaction, and requires using the main agent's potentially large context for a narrow question.

A separate side chat would let users understand a selected snippet while preserving the main conversation's focus. For example, I could select a parse() call in a diff and ask how it handles invalid input, then continue reviewing the main task.

This would be especially useful during code review, debugging, and reading tool output.

### How? (optional)

One possible approach is to expose extension APIs for:
1. Reading a transcript selection, including its source message or tool output.
2. Opening a split panel with independent input and focus handling.
3. Running a secondary model conversation with isolated history and cancellation.

The initial version could support selecting an entire message or code block, with finer-grained selection added later.

Side-chat turns should remain separate from the main session unless the user explicitly chooses to send something back. Model choice and panel dimensions could be configurable.

I would be happy to prototype the panel and keybinding integration once the necessary APIs are available, and provide detailed UX feedback.

issues.title: The codemode annotation spells `tools.<name>`, and small local models copy `tools.` into the tool-call name

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## Symptom

With a local model and `codemode` enabled, a tool call comes back as prose, with the word `tools` stuck on the name:

```
<tool_call>
<function=tools__web_search>
<parameter=queries>
["Ptyxis new tab current directory", "Ptyxis terminal profile working directory"]
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
```

The call is correct apart from the name: right tool, right parameters. The session then stops, because as far as the client can see the turn ended normally, and it only resumes when the user types something.

## Setup

pi 1.4.0 (and `main` at v1.4.0-53), `defaultTools: ["+codemode"]`, one local model: a Qwen3.8 GGUF (`iq3_xxs`, `iq3_s`) served by a Strata engine behind llama-swap, 16 tools active, sessions of 200-450 turns. Nothing in the session records it: there is no tool result, no error entry, and the assistant message has the ordinary `stop` finish. It is the only class of tool call failure that leaves no trace in a Pi session.

## Four sessions, four spellings

Four turns from my own sessions on this machine where a call was emitted as text. Each is the **first** assistant turn of its session, so this is not deep-context drift:

| session | name the model wrote | tool it meant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 01a18713 | `<function=tools__web_search` | `web_search` |
| 01a18776 | `<function=tools`, with the real name in the first `<parameter=` slot | `web_search` |
| 01a1878b | `<function=tools`, then `<function=tools.web_search` | `web_search` |
| 01a1833c | `<function=tools=web_search` | `web_search` |

Every bad name contains the token `tools`, which appears in no declared tool name. In those four sessions `web_search` is declared, and the same sessions went on to call tools successfully 33, 47, 73 and 236 times (of those, 2 to 6 calls each were `web_search`). The model has the tool and wants it; it wrote the name wrong once.

What happens next is up to the server's policy for a call naming something the request did not declare. Under a llama.cpp style server the junk name reaches the client as a call, the client answers `Tool "tools__web_search" not found`, and the model retries. Under a server that instead returns such a call as text — Strata does this deliberately for undeclared names — the turn ends with `stop`, no error surfaces anywhere, and the session sits. Same model, same slip, very different blast radius.

## Cause

Every tool that is callable from a script gets this line appended to its description, in `packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/codemode/tool.ts:305` (`describeScriptCall`):

```ts
return `${tool.description.trim()}\n\nCodemode: \`tools.${toCodemodeIdentifier(tool.name)}(args)\` resolves to ${describeOutput(toCodemodeDeclaration(tool).outputSchema)}.`;
```

In the default codemode mode, declared tools get the annotation too. From a captured request of the first session in the table above (llama-swap capture 25: two messages, the 24 156 character system prompt plus a 211 character user turn), 15 of the 16 declared tools end with it:

```
… Prefer 2-4 varied queries.

Codemode: `tools.web_search(args)` resolves to `{ responseId, fetchId, queries }`.
```

So the request spells `tools.web_search` fifteen times, each time directly under the description of a tool the model may be about to call. A model that slips while writing the name slot copies the word it just read there, and the resulting name matches no declared tool.

## Measurement

I replayed those four requests exactly as captured (real system prompt, real user turn, the 16 real tool schemas, `enable_thinking: true`, `reasoning_effort: medium`, temperature left at the server default) and changed only the text of that annotation. Three arms, four contexts, three replays each:

| tool description | requests | emitted as text with a `tools…` name | calls parsed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| as shipped | 12 | **5** | 7 |
| rewritten to name the script member, no `tools.` prefix | 12 | **0** | 12 |
| annotation removed | 12 | **0** | 11 (one ran out of tokens) |

The five leaked requests wrote `tools` three times and `tools.web_search` twice, the same spread as the four real sessions. Fisher exact, shipped against the two changed arms combined: p = 0.0021. An earlier run on reconstructed contexts of the same sessions gave the same direction: 4 leaks in 12 requests with the annotation, 0 in 24 without it (p = 0.008).

It is not the thinking level: on this model's sessions 1428 turns at `medium` produced 8 leaked turns and 368 turns with thinking off produced 1 (p = 0.70), and a 16-request replay at `medium` against `xhigh` was 8 of 16 against 3 of 16 (p = 0.14).

## Proposed change

Name the script member without spelling the member access. The spelling is already documented once, in the codemode tool's own description (`await tools.<name>({ ...args })`, `tool.ts:119`), so scripts lose nothing:

```diff
@@ -300,9 +300,13 @@ function describeOutput(schema: CodemodeJsonSchema | undefined): string {
 /**
  * A declared tool's description followed by how scripts call it and what the call resolves to. The
  * arguments are the tool's declared parameters, so they are not repeated.
+ *
+ * The script member is named on its own, never written as `tools.<name>`: a small local model that
+ * drifts when it writes a tool call copies the `tools.` it read here into the call's name slot, and
+ * a call named `tools.web_search` matches no declared tool.
  */
 function describeScriptCall(tool: AgentTool<any>): string {
-	return `${tool.description.trim()}\n\nCodemode: \`tools.${toCodemodeIdentifier(tool.name)}(args)\` resolves to ${describeOutput(toCodemodeDeclaration(tool).outputSchema)}.`;
+	return `${tool.description.trim()}\n\nCodemode: callable in scripts as \`${toCodemodeIdentifier(tool.name)}\`, resolves to ${describeOutput(toCodemodeDeclaration(tool).outputSchema)}.`;
 }
 
 /**
```

Branch `codemode-script-name-annotation`, commit f14912eb1, also updates the three test expectations it moves (`test/suite/agent-session-codemode.test.ts:155`, `:166`, `test/suite/agent-session-mcp.test.ts:686` and `:689`) and asserts that the annotation never contains a `tools.` prefix. `vitest --run test/suite/agent-session-codemode.test.ts test/suite/agent-session-mcp.test.ts` gives 77 passed. For anyone running the suite in a fresh clone: `packages/ai/src/providers/data/` is generated and gitignored, so vitest cannot import `pi-ai` until `npm run generate-models` has run, and `npm run build:offline` fails instead when that directory is empty.

The middle arm is only there to show the shape of the fix. What matters is that the string `tools.` stops sitting next to tool names in the request; keeping the annotation and rewording it was enough.

## Two related gaps, separate from this one

- A provider that rejects a tool call reports it, and the report is dropped here. Strata puts `strata_rejected_tool_calls: [{name, reason}]` on the completion and counts it in `/metrics`, but `pi-ai` keeps only `content`, `tool_calls` and `finish_reason` (`createPartialCompletion`, `packages/ai/src/utils/error-body.ts:130`), so the client cannot tell the user that its own call was refused. Half of "the session stalled for no reason" is that nobody downstream knows.
- A call the provider will not accept should not end the turn quietly. That belongs mostly to the provider; I have asked there too.

## Repro

The three-arm replay (36 requests against a local server), the extracted first-turn contexts and the capture decoding script are in `~/scratch/pi-toolcall` on this machine; say the word and I will put them somewhere you can run them. The recipe: pull the four leaked turns out of `~/.pi/agent/sessions/*/*.jsonl`, keep the context up to and including the first user turn, take the system prompt and the 16 tool schemas from a llama-swap capture of that same day, then replay with the annotation matched by `Codemode: `tools\.([a-z_0-9]+)\(args\)` resolves to` and either reworded or deleted.

I would rather file this than a PR, because the middle arm shows the same effect and I do not know which wording you want; happy to open a PR for either.

issues.title: `/export`: `--no-tools` and `--no-thinking` to export a plain conversation

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add two switches to `/export` (and `pi --export`):

```
/export [path] [--no-tools] [--no-thinking]
```

- `--no-thinking` drops `thinking` blocks from assistant messages.
- `--no-tools` drops `toolCall` blocks from assistant messages and removes `toolResult` messages. Assistant messages left with no content are dropped.

This applies to both HTML and JSONL output. It filters the entries exported, applied before serialization, not a viewer toggle.

Another thing I thought was `--single-branch` but it could be discussed separately.

### Why?

I often want to share or archive *the conversation itself*: what I asked and what the agent answered. The current export can't produce that:

- The HTML viewer's "Toggle thinking" / "Toggle tools" only hide content in the browser. The embedded session data still has every thinking block, every tool argument and every tool result (file contents, command output, env details). This matters even more for `/share`, where the HTML goes to a gist or a Radius artifact.
- JSONL export copies entries as they are.
- For long sessions, tool output is most of the file, so the result is huge and hard to read.

Filtering at export time makes the exported file contain only what the user meant to share.

### How? (optional)

The change stays small and doesn't depend on any format:

- a shared `filterEntriesForExport(entries, { tools, thinking })` used by both `serializeSessionBranch` and `exportSessionToHtml` (and `exportFromFile` for the CLI);
- parse the flags in `handleExportCommand` next to the existing path argument;
- custom/extension tools need no special handling: when `--no-tools` is set, their calls and results are simply left out.

This also gives a clean base for the markdown export from [#3129](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3129) later on: with tools and thinking stripped, the transcript is plain user and assistant text, so markdown output no longer has to know how to render custom tools or messages.

issues.title: `pi -p` text mode: exit 0 with 0-byte stdout when the final assistant message also carries a run-terminating tool call

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## Summary
`pi -p "<prompt>"` (text mode) exits **0** and writes **0 bytes** to stdout, while the same session in `--mode json` contains a normal assistant text message. Observed twice (reproducible), and it broke a scripted smoke test that treated empty output as success.

## Environment
- pi 1.4.0, Windows 11, launched via `pi.cmd` -> `node pi-launcher.js` (not `pi.ps1`)
- Extensions loaded from user settings; the session in question also used a custom tool that ends the run (`notify_task` from the pi harness prompt)

## Steps to reproduce (as far as I can reduce it)
1. `pi -p "用 pc_remember 记录一条持久记忆，text 写「pi 写闸门端到端测试」。不要先调用 pc_search。" --no-session > out.txt 2>&1`
2. Wait for exit (35 s in my runs).
3. `out.txt` is 0 bytes, `echo $LASTEXITCODE` is 0.

Same prompt with `--mode json` prints the assistant text and the tool results normally. Same prompt with `--exclude-tools notify_task` also prints the text in text mode (and includes the tool-blocked reason), so the empty output correlates with the final assistant turn containing both text **and** a tool call that terminates the agent.

## Expected
The assistant's final text is printed to stdout (as in `--mode json`), or the exit code is non-zero when nothing is printed.

## Actual
Exit 0 + empty stdout. For automation this is a silent-success failure mode: a CI/script check that asserts `exit 0` cannot distinguish "model answered" from "nothing was printed".

## Evidence
- `out.txt`: 0 bytes, exit 0, reproducible twice (35.17 s / 37.53 s, stdout/stderr separated as well)
- `--mode json` run of the same prompt: assistant text present, tool_result present
- `--exclude-tools notify_task` run: text mode prints 605 bytes including the expected tool-blocked reason
- Related: #9718 (`--print` exits 0 with empty output when the model exhausts its output budget) — different trigger as far as I can tell, but the same silent-success shape.

## Workarounds
- `--mode json` and consume the message stream
- `--exclude-tools <the terminating tool>` (not always acceptable)

## Suggestion
In text mode, always emit the final assistant text; if the run ends with no printable text, exit non-zero or print an explicit marker to stderr.

issues.title: Interactive TUI stalls provider request uploads while writing inline images to the terminal

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
> **AI-drafted.** An AI coding agent found and reproduced this on my machine and wrote this report; I asked it to file it. The numbers are from that reproduction.

### What happened?

In interactive mode, a provider request with a multi-MB body (a history with many screenshots) sometimes reaches the server 0.3–3.5 s late. The headers arrive at once; the rest of the body comes later. This is intermittent and only happens in the TUI. A `pi -p` run sending the same bodies never stalls.

Cause, as far as we can tell:

1. undici corks the headers and the whole JSON body into one write. On a fresh connection the kernel takes about 128 KB, and the rest waits for `drain`.
2. The render that the tool result scheduled (`requestRender` → `doRender`) then runs and writes the kitty image sequences with `process.stdout.write` (`pi-tui/dist/terminal.js`). On a TTY that write blocks.
3. The upload waits for the whole terminal write.

The dispatcher in `core/http-dispatcher.js` sets no `keepAliveTimeout`, so once tool plus model time exceeds about 4 s, most requests open a fresh connection.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `pi --no-extensions` against a local OpenAI-compatible server that answers with `read` tool calls on PNGs (~170 KB base64 each) and logs when the headers and the full body arrive. Use one connection per request.
2. Let the history grow to 2–5 MB (12–30 images).
3. Read the pty at a capped 2 MB/s, standing in for a slow terminal.

Result:

| Setup | Stalled requests | Stall |
|---|---|---|
| Reader capped at 2 MB/s | 10/20 | 231–266 ms |
| Reader capped at 0.5 MB/s | 4/12 | ~1 s |
| `pi -p` | 0/20 | |
| `PI_IMAGE_PROTOCOL=none` | 0/20 | |

A Node `--require` hook showed the same order on every stalled request: body write starts, a ~485 KB blocking stdout write starts 6 ms later, and `drain` fires when that write returns.

In real use under herdr (kitty images) I see 0.3–3.5 s gaps from interactive sessions only. A subagent sending similar bodies at the same time sees 25–39 ms.

### Expected behavior

Rendering should not hold up a request upload. Some ways to get there:

- defer the render until the body is flushed;
- place kitty images that were already sent by id, instead of re-sending them on full redraws;
- set a longer keep-alive in `core/http-dispatcher.js`.

### Version

1.4.0 (macOS 26.7.1, Node 26.10.0, herdr terminal)

issues.title: A throwing tool renderer exits pi, and a resumed session then crashes on every attempt

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## What happened

pi 1.4.0 exited with an uncaught exception raised inside an extension's tool renderer. The session file was already written, so afterwards **every** resume of that session crashed the same way; three attempts, three exits, and no way to open the conversation again.

```
pi exiting due to uncaughtException:
TypeError: args.questions.map is not a function
    at tableLines (…/@juicesharp/rpiv-ask-user-question/view/transcript.ts:83:50)
    at WidthLines.layout (…/view/transcript.ts:58:3)
    at MouseRegion.render (…/pi-coding-agent/dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-T726RZZU.js:106:6834)
    at ToolExecutionComponent.render (…/chunk-T726RZZU.js:71:30038)
    at TuiMainScreen.render (…/chunk-T726RZZU.js:71:30038)
```

The first crash happened as the tool result arrived; the next two were `pi -r` attempts. `~/.pi/agent/crashes.json` holds the three records, all pointing at the same session file.

## Two defects behind it

**1. A renderer exception is fatal.** The TUI transcript path has no guard around `renderCall` / `renderResult`, so any extension bug takes the process down. `exportSessionToHtml` already wraps both calls in `try { } catch { }` (`createToolHtmlRenderer`), which suggests the contract was meant to be tolerate-and-degrade rather than exit.

**2. Replayed tool calls reach the renderers unprepared.** `prepareToolCallArguments` runs `prepareArguments` only on the execute path. On a session replay the assistant message keeps the raw recorded arguments, and those raw arguments are what `renderCall` and `renderResult` receive.

That combination is what made this session unrecoverable. The provider (CodeBuddy, serving `claude-opus-5.5`) stringified the nested `questions` array. The extension's `prepareArguments` decoded it, the questionnaire worked, and the answers were recorded — but the session file kept the string. Drawing the receipt then read `questions.length` on a 1825-character string, took the `> 1` branch, and called `.map` on it.

## Reproduction

Any extension whose renderer assumes the shape `prepareArguments` guarantees reproduces both halves. In a session file, one assistant `toolCall` entry whose `arguments.questions` is a JSON string is enough; resume the session and pi exits before the transcript is drawn.

## Suggested fix

- Guard extension renderers in the transcript path: catch, log once, and fall back to the plain text rendering for that component. A broken renderer should cost one component, not the session.
- Feed renderers the prepared arguments (the object the tool actually ran with) instead of the raw recorded ones, so `prepareArguments` is one contract for execution and display.

## Workaround

Disable the extension, or patch it to decode before drawing. The extension-side fix is juicesharp/rpiv-mono#339.

issues.title: coding-agent: support namespace-scoped tool_search queries

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to built in mcp extension

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add namespace-scoped discovery to `tool_search`, for example `+docs read_page`, so a model can constrain discovery to one MCP server.

### Why?

When several servers expose similar tools, `+docs read_page` is currently treated as ordinary search text. The `+` does not filter candidates, so another server's tool can rank first, particularly with `limit: 1`. Exact-name prioritization does not solve this: the entire query no longer matches the tool name.

Code Mode already has `searchTools(query, { namespace })`; `tool_search` has no equivalent constraint. This is a proposal for new syntax, not a claim that Pi already promises to support `+`.

### How? (optional)

Parse a leading `+namespace`, match the registered namespace name or alias, then rank the remaining query with the existing BM25 implementation. This keeps tools from other namespaces out even when their descriptions mention the requested service. Unknown namespaces return no matches; ordinary queries and exposure restrictions remain unchanged.

The prefix would mean a namespace selector, not a general required-keyword operator. Would you prefer this syntax or an explicit `namespace` argument?

I have an implementation on my fork with regression tests; `npm run check` and `./test.sh` pass. I would like to submit a PR once the approach and contributor approval are confirmed.

issues.title: pi-durable: hand off at the context limit and keep the run going
issues.body:
We run pi-durable 1.4.0 in a Cloudflare Durable Object for a coding agent. We want to use the whole context window and never compact: near the limit, the model writes a handoff note, and the work continues in a fresh context built from the note.

`reset(note)` and a tool's `control: { handoff }` start the new context, but they also end the current run (`finishToolRound` → final boundary). To carry on, the host has to notice that, submit a new input itself, and pick what that input should be.

Automatic compaction does continue the run. It can be bent into a handoff (`keepRecentTokens: 1`, `backgroundTokens: 0`, a `beforeCompact` hook that returns a model-written note), but the summary is framed by the fixed `SUMMARY_PREFIX`, and mid-run it keeps the last tool round rather than the latest user message.

Request: a first-class "handoff and continue" mode, for example `compaction.mode: "handoff"` or `reset(note, { continue: true })`. In that mode:
- the run carries on in the new context: system prompt, the note, then the latest user input;
- the host supplies the note, from a hook or the model;
- the wording around the note is configurable.

Happy to test a prerelease.

issues.title: Responses relay account rotation: invalid_encrypted_content makes the session unrecoverable

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## What happened?

Behind a Responses-API relay that fronts a pool of upstream accounts (several third-party OpenAI-compatible relays do this), pi sessions die permanently after the pool rotates or fails over mid-session.

Mechanism:

1. pi requests `reasoning.encrypted_content` and stores it in `thinkingSignature` for replay (store:false stateless multi-turn).
2. The relay encrypts each reasoning item for the specific upstream account that produced it.
3. On the next turn the relay routes to a different account; replaying that item returns HTTP 400 `invalid_encrypted_content` / "encrypted content for item <id> could not be verified".
4. `isRetryableProviderError` treats 400 as non-retryable, so the turn fails — and the poisoned reasoning item stays in history, so every subsequent turn fails the same way. The session is unrecoverable short of compaction or manual editing.

## Steps to reproduce

Needs a Responses endpoint whose account pool rotates between requests (observed on account-pool relays; not reproducible against api.openai.com directly). Locally it can be simulated by mutating one stored `thinkingSignature` in a session file, then continuing the session: every turn keeps 400ing.

## Expected behavior

On `invalid_encrypted_content`, drop the offending reasoning items (e.g. strip `thinkingSignature` on assistant thinking blocks for the current provider) and retry once, degrading to a text-only replay, instead of failing the turn. `transformMessages` already drops thinking blocks when the model changes; this is the same idea for a same-model/same-provider mismatch it can't see — the relay rotated, not the model.

I run a local wrapper extension that does exactly this (poisons signatures on that error signature and lets the retry path rebuild the payload) and it has been holding up in daily use; happy to implement the fix in `packages/ai` if you want it in core.

prs.title: perf(tui): virtualize the transcript and resize the fullscreen layout lazily
prs.body:
issue: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9549

## Summary

The interactive transcript rendered the full message tree on every frame: every component stayed alive for the whole session, so scrolling, typing and the working indicator all cost O(transcript) instead of O(viewport), and a width change remeasured every entry. This branch virtualizes the transcript, adds a reproducible benchmark for long sessions, and makes resizes in fullscreen cost O(window).

Three commits:

1. `9b6241f` **virtualize the transcript with a windowed container** — entries become build factories, components exist only while on screen, the line cache stays for search/prompt jumps/selection.
2. `6b93965` **benchmark long-session scroll and interaction** — `scripts/bench-session-interaction.mjs` (`npm run bench:session`) drives a real CLI in a tmux pty and samples `/proc`; `--compare-tree` diffs two built trees.
3. `1d9ffd3` **resize the fullscreen transcript lazily** — a width change measures only the window; opt-in through `lazyResize`, enabled for `tuiMode: fullscreen` only.

Partially addresses #9549. Regular-screen whole-transcript emit and the first-frame full measurement remain O(transcript) (see Limitations).

## What changed

### 1. Windowed transcript (`packages/tui/src/components/windowed-container.ts`, `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts`)

- `chatContainer` is now a `WindowedContainer`: each entry stores a `build()` factory plus a `pinned` flag. A component is created when its entry first enters the window and released when it leaves, except while streaming or awaiting a result.
- Entries are measured from cached line arrays, so layout does not need the component tree.
- Released entries keep their rendered lines, because fullscreen search, prompt jumps and selection read the
whole transcript (`retainLines`).
- `interactive-mode` appends messages lazily, rebuilds an entry from the final message when its stream ends,
and feeds tool execution updates through entry state so a component recreated later keeps its args, flags and result.

### 2. Benchmark tool (`scripts/bench-session-interaction.mjs`)

Resumes a session in the built CLI inside a throwaway tmux server and drives page scrolls, a sustained scroll burst, mouse wheel, typing, the working indicator and resizes. It samples the pi process from `/proc` for CPU time, RSS and bytes written to the terminal, and reports medians over interleaved runs. `--compare-tree` runs a second built tree in the same rounds and prints per-metric deltas; `--phases` narrows a run to one interaction. Linux only (reads `/proc`, needs tmux).

### 3. Lazy resize for fullscreen (`WindowedContainer.lazyResize`)

- With `lazyResize`, a width change keeps the heights measured at the previous width as the layout estimate,
measures only the entries the window reaches, and remeasures history as it scrolls back in.
- Safe only for renderers that clip lines on write, which `TuiAltScreen` does. `TuiMainScreen` replays its whole line buffer, so lines kept from a wider terminal would wrap there and break its line accounting; regular
mode therefore keeps the eager remeasure.
- `InteractiveMode` passes `lazyResize: () => renderer.mode === "fullscreen"`.
- The resize phase waits for the process to go CPU-quiet between resizes and reports them split by direction; the previous fixed gap let a slow build coalesce several resizes into one measurement.

## Benchmark

Session: 13,067,138 bytes, 2418 entries, about 100k rendered lines, resumed in the built CLI, 120x40 tmux pty, Linux, 3 interleaved runs, median. Base is the parent of `9b6241f`.

### Interaction, `tuiMode: fullscreen`

| Metric | Before | After | Delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Page-up CPU / key | 28.5 ms | 17.5 ms | -39% |
| Page-down CPU / key | 19.5 ms | 16.0 ms | -18% |
| Mouse wheel CPU / event | 14.8 ms | 11.6 ms | -22% |
| Typing CPU / keystroke | 6.5 ms | 3.2 ms | -51% |
| Working indicator | 7.5% of one core | 3.5% | -53% |
| RSS after the run | 520 MB | 321 MB | -38% |
| Peak RSS | 524 MB | 350 MB | -33% |
| Cold load | 9.1 s, 300 MB | 9.4 s, 300 MB | unchanged |

### Interaction, `tuiMode: regular`

Regular mode gains less, because `retainLines` keeps the full line buffer that the main-screen diff walks:

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typing CPU / keystroke | 39.8 ms | 36.5 ms |
| Working indicator | 49.8% of one core | 42.5% |

### Resize, `tuiMode: fullscreen`

| Metric | Before | After | Delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Resize CPU, shrinking | 3,790 ms | 10.0 ms | -100% |
| Resize CPU, widening | 3,500 ms | 10.0 ms | -100% |
| Resize bytes, shrinking | 5,950 | 5,942 | 0% |
| Resize bytes, widening | 7,989 | 7,899 | -1% |
| RSS after six resizes | 354.7 MB (55 MB above cold load) | 302.5 MB (3.2 MB above) | -15% |

### Resize, `tuiMode: regular`

Unchanged by design (eager remeasure kept):

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resize CPU, shrinking | 3,920 ms | 3,890 ms |
| Resize CPU, widening | 3,620 ms | 3,590 ms |
| Resize bytes | 6.52 MB / 6.73 MB | 6.52 MB / 6.73 MB |

## Correctness

Screen equality was checked by driving real resizes through tmux in both builds (eager vs this branch), shrinking 120x40 to 100x34, paging up three times, scrolling to the top and growing back, then comparing the captured screens after normalising trailing blanks and the two tree paths:

- 13 MB session, both modes: initial, after shrinking, after growing back — identical. The widest line after
shrinking is exactly 100 of 100 columns, so nothing is written past the terminal width.
- 207 KB session, `regular`: every step identical, including the three page-ups.
- 207 KB session, `fullscreen`: initial, after shrinking, at the top, after growing back — identical. Three page-ups immediately after a shrink land about one screen off, because heights above the window are still estimates from the wide width until those entries are visited; scrolling to the top remeasures them and both builds show the same first screen (38 page-ups eager, 36 lazy).

## Limitations and follow-ups

- **Regular mode still emits the whole transcript.** `TuiMainScreen` treats a width change as a full re-render and replays its line buffer, which is why regular mode keeps the eager remeasure and why its resize cost is unchanged. Making regular mode cheap needs "do not replay history on a width change", a separate change to `TuiMainScreen`.
- **The first layout still measures every entry**, because a height is only known after rendering; cold load
therefore stays at about 9.4 s and 300 MB on this session.
- **Fullscreen scroll offset after a shrink** is approximately one screen off for the first pages up, until the entries above the window are remeasured. Content is unaffected.
- **Resize coalescing is possible** when a build is slower than the driver's resize interval; the benchmark waits for CPU quiescence to avoid mixing two resizes into one sample.

prs.title: fix(tui): drop space after styled word at wrap boundary, reset strikethrough at line end
prs.body:
Fixes #10925.

## Problem

`splitIntoTokensWithAnsi()` attaches pending escape codes to the next visible character. The code that closes a styled word therefore lands on the following space: `**commodo** consequat` tokenizes as `\x1b[1mcommodo`, `\x1b[22m `, `consequat`.

`wrapSingleLine()` detected whitespace with `token.trim() === ""`, which is false for `"\x1b[22m "`. When the styled word ended exactly at the wrap width, that space was treated as a word and moved to the next line:

```
before: ["aaaa \x1b[1mbold", "\x1b[1m\x1b[22m next", "word"]   (width 9)
after:  ["aaaa \x1b[1mbold\x1b[22m", "next word"]
```

Because the closing code moved to the next line, the style also stayed open into the right padding of the wrapped line. Separately, `getLineEndReset()` closed only underline at line end, so strikethrough that spans a wrap continued into the padding.

## Fix

- Detect whitespace tokens after stripping escape codes.
- When a whitespace token is dropped at a wrap, append its escape codes to the wrapped line and update the tracker, so the style closes there and is not re-opened on the next line.
- Close strikethrough (`\x1b[29m`) at line end, like underline. `getActiveCodes()` re-opens it on the next line. Background is unaffected.
- Whitespace wider than an empty line that carries codes (e.g. background spaces followed by a trailing reset) keeps only the codes. Without this, treating it as whitespace skipped the long-token path, and the trailing reset blocked the final `trimEnd()`, leaving a line wider than `width`.
- When a long word follows, the line before it is now trimmed before the line-end reset is added. Otherwise the reset (now also emitted for strikethrough) blocks the final `trimEnd()` and leaves trailing spaces.

## Tests

- `wrap-ansi.test.ts`: boundary closing code, dropped space with a color reset, strikethrough reset and restore across a wrap, strikethrough reset with background preserved.
- `markdown.test.ts`: padded Markdown with a background at an exact boundary for bold and strikethrough.
- The new tests fail without the fix. With the old code, rendering the issue text through `UserMessageComponent` (dark theme, padding 1) at widths 40-120 produced 5 bad lines at width 78. With the fix it produces none.
- Fuzzing over 1.2M random styled inputs with SGR and OSC 8 codes found no line wider than `width`, and no case where the old wrapper laid out text the same as the unstyled input but the new one does not.
- Benchmark (`wrapTextWithAnsi`, width 77, about 5-18k chars, median of 6 processes) against `main`: plain -5%, light styling -0.5%, heavy styling +1%, long strikethrough +0%, all within noise. The whitespace check scans character codes and stops at the first visible text instead of allocating a stripped copy.
- `npm run check` passes. All `packages/tui` tests pass. `./test.sh` shows no new failures; the remaining failures are environment-specific: the clipboard tests also fail on `main` here, and the durable, env (ssh), and chord failures are in packages that do not depend on `pi-tui`.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): compare paths case-insensitively on Windows
prs.body:
Fixes #10488

## Problem

On Windows, `c:\Users\me` and `C:\Users\me` are the same directory, but pi compared paths as exact strings (`===`, `startsWith`, map and set keys). `realpathSync` keeps the input casing, so canonicalizing does not help.

The reported case, with cwd `c:\Users\me\project` and home `C:\Users\me`:

1. Ancestor discovery finds `c:\Users\me\.agents\skills`. The exclusion of the user dir `C:\Users\me\.agents\skills` does not match, so global skills load as project skills.
2. The same dir loads again as user skills. Dedup does not match either, so every skill is reported as a name collision.
3. `hasTrustRequiringProjectResources` treats `~/.agents/skills` as a project resource that requires trust.

The same pattern affected other places:

- Saved trust decisions in `trust.json` were not found when cwd casing differed, so pi asked for trust again.
- With a custom session dir, `--continue`, resume by id, and the session list hid sessions recorded with different cwd casing.
- Git worktree `AGENTS.md` shadowing failed when cwd casing differed from git's paths.
- Local package matching (`pi remove c:\pkg` vs configured `C:\pkg`) and package identity across global and project settings.
- Extension preload matching, skill scope classification, resource source info, the config and session selector keys, and the session import self-check.

Separately, home-to-`~` shortening used an unanchored `startsWith(home)` in four places, so `/home/me2/x` was shown as `~2/x`.

## Fix

New helpers in `utils/paths.ts`, all based on one comparison key:

- `getPathComparisonKey(path)`: the resolved path, lowercased on Windows. It does not touch the filesystem.
- `pathsEqual(a, b)`
- `isPathWithin(parent, child)`: true for equal paths or paths inside `parent`, matching whole path segments.
- `shortenHomePath(path, home?)`: replaces a leading home dir with `~`.

The helpers pick `path.win32` or `path.posix` from `process.platform` at call time, so tests can exercise real Windows paths (drive letters, UNC).

`getResourcePathKey(path)` in `source-info.ts` is the dedup key for resources. Synthetic identifiers (`builtin:<name>`, `<inline:...>`) stay unchanged, because they are not filesystem paths and their lookup is case-sensitive. File paths go through realpath plus the comparison key.

The helpers are used only for comparison; stored and displayed paths are unchanged. Trust store lookups and `set` match keys case-insensitively on Windows.

Unchanged on purpose:

- The package install-root guards (`resolveManagedPath`, `pruneEmptyGitParents`, the `node_modules` dependency check) keep exact string checks. Both sides come from the same root string, and exact is the stricter option.
- Checks based on `path.relative()` (`getCwdRelativePath`, the changelog containment check) were already correct: Node's `path.win32.relative` ignores case.

NTFS can enable per-directory case sensitivity, but it is rarely used outside WSL interop, so it is ignored (see the comment on `getPathComparisonKey`).

## Tests

- `test/paths.test.ts`: Windows drive-letter, UNC and root cases, POSIX case sensitivity, segment-boundary containment, and home shortening, including root and UNC homes.
- `test/source-info.test.ts`: file paths fold case on Windows; builtin and inline identifiers keep their case.
- `test/trust-manager.test.ts`: the `.agents/skills` exclusion with a lowercase `HOME`, plus saved trust decisions matched and replaced across casing (simulated win32).

An end-to-end test of the reported loader scenario is not feasible on Linux: the loader resolves paths with POSIX `node:path`, and the filesystem is case-sensitive.

`npm run check` passes. The coding-agent suite passes, except for 13 failures that also occur without this change: clipboard tool detection in this environment, and one test that needs built `dist/` output.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): refresh unpinned temporary npm extensions when a newer version exists
prs.body:
`pi -e npm:<pkg>` installed the package once into `~/.pi/agent/tmp/extensions/npm/<hash>/` and reused that copy on every later run. When `resolvePackageSources` decides whether to reinstall, it only compares the installed version against a configured range. An unversioned spec or a dist-tag such as `@latest` has no range, so any installed version counted as up to date. Temporary sources are not covered by `pi update` either, so the only way to update was to delete the cache by hand. Temporary `-e git:` sources, by contrast, are already refreshed on every load.

The change: when an unpinned temporary npm source is already installed and offline mode is off, `resolvePackageSources` now calls the existing `npmHasAvailableUpdate`. If a newer version exists, it reinstalls.
- **Install spec:** the reinstall uses `name@latest` for unversioned specs, otherwise the configured spec. This is the same rule `pi update` follows. It is needed because a bare `npm install name` keeps the `^x.y.z` range already saved in the temporary `package.json`, so the package would never move to a new major version.
- **Failed refresh:** the cached install is kept and loaded, as with temporary git sources.
- **Unchanged cases:** pinned exact versions (`@1.2.3`) and offline mode work as before.

The cost is one `npm view` call per unpinned temporary npm source at startup, the same trade-off already made for temporary git sources.

**Testing**
- Added two tests to `test/package-manager.test.ts`:
  - An outdated unpinned temporary source triggers an install with `example@latest`, and if that install fails the cached copy still loads.
  - Temporary sources that are up to date or pinned do not reinstall, and pinned ones skip the npm check.

  Both fail without the change.
- `npm run check` passes, and `test/package-manager.test.ts` passes (133 tests).
- Manual run with the built CLI and `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=/tmp/agent`: I first installed `pi -e npm:is-number@6.0.0`, then ran the commands below.

  | Command | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | `pi -e npm:is-number` | stayed on 6.0.0 | updated to 7.0.0 |
  | `pi -e npm:is-number@latest` | stayed on 6.0.0 | updated to 7.0.0 |
  | `pi -e 'npm:is-number@>=6'` | – | updated to 7.0.0 |
  | `PI_OFFLINE=1 pi -e npm:is-number` | – | stays on 6.0.0 |

Fixes #11375

Requested by @petrroll

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): create session directories as 0700 and session files as 0600
prs.body:
## Problem

Session directories and files are created without a mode, so they follow the process umask. With the common umask `0022`, that is `0755` for directories and `0644` for files, which any local user can read.

Whether other users can actually read conversations then depends on the parent directories. On Fedora/Arch home directories are `0700`, which blocks access. On Debian 12 and older Ubuntu home directories are `0755`, so `~/.pi/agent/sessions/*/*.jsonl` is readable by every local user. The same applies to custom `--session-dir` locations and to copies that keep the mode.

`auth.json` already avoids this: it is created as `0600`, and its directory as `0700` when missing. opencode creates its session database as `0600`; Codex has the same umask behavior as pi.

## Change

New session directories are created as `0700` and new session files as `0600`:

- `ensureSessionDir()` in `session-manager.ts` creates missing session directories, and any missing parents, as `0700`. It is used by `getDefaultSessionDir()`, the `SessionManager` constructor, `forkFrom()`, and `/import`.
- Session files are opened with `0600` on first write (`_persist`), on rewrite (`_rewriteFile`, which only applies the mode when it creates the file), and when forking.
- `/import` wrote the stored copy with `copyFileSync`, which copies the source file's mode. It now writes the copy with `wx` and `0600`.

The modes apply only on creation, like `auth.json`. Existing session directories and files keep their modes, so this does not override modes or ACLs set by an administrator, and existing `0644` sessions stay `0644`. The umask can still remove bits but cannot add them back.

On Windows, Node ignores these modes.

## Tests

- `test/session-manager/file-permissions.test.ts`: new directories (including a missing parent) are `0700` and files `0600` under umask `0022`; an existing `0755` directory and `0644` file keep their modes after appending; forked sessions are `0600`.
- `test/suite/agent-session-runtime.test.ts`: an imported `0644` session is stored as `0600` and the source is unchanged.

Some Apple Terminal setups send `ESC` + `CR` (`\x1b\r`) for Shift+Enter. Without the kitty protocol this parses as `alt+enter`, which is bound to `app.message.followUp`, so the prompt is queued instead of getting a newline. - Native Windows, legacy mode: `Shift+Alt+Enter` (indistinguishable from `Alt+Enter` there) now inserts a newline instead of queueing a follow-up. A Windows Terminal `sendInput` remap of `Shift+Enter` to `\x1b\r` now works too.

In some Apple Terminal versions (for example Terminal.app 488 on macOS 27), Shift+Enter sends `ESC CR` (`\x1b\r`) instead of a plain `CR`. Testing:

prs.title: Add Arabic RTL rendering to the TUI (bidirectional text, Windows Terminal)
prs.body:
fixes #11579

### Problem

A terminal paints cells in the order the program writes them. Windows Terminal does not implement the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UAX #9), so text kept in **logical** order — the order every editor, clipboard and model keeps it in — appears mirrored. `مرحبا` written cell by cell left to right reads backwards: an Arabic transcript reads in the wrong order, and the caret in the prompt sits on the wrong side of the word being typed.

The terminal side of this is a known limitation (microsoft/terminal#538), which is why #3301 was closed. The TUI can carry the fix instead.

### What changes

Only the string written to the terminal changes. Logical state is untouched: caret offsets, selection, copy, search, wrapping and every column calculation stay logical.

Two independent behaviours:

1. **Glyph order.** `reorderLine()` turns one rendered line from logical order into visual order with UAX #9 (bidi-js), working on **grapheme clusters** so an Arabic letter and its combining marks travel as one cell. Bracket mirroring is applied here because the terminal does not do it. Leading and trailing whitespace is anchored: indentation is layout the renderer produced, not content the reader is reading.
2. **Line placement.** With `terminal.rtl.align` on, a line goes against the edge its dominant script reads from: Arabic and Persian lines right, English left, a mixed line whichever script has more strong characters (a tie falls back to the first strong character, the same rule UAX #9 uses for direction). List markers, blockquote bars and table columns follow the same edge, so `- عنصر` reads with its bullet on the right and a mirrored RTL table has its first logical column on the right.

A line with no strong RTL character returns from the early check in `hasStrongRtl`, so ordinary rendering is byte for byte what it was before.

Styling travels per grapheme through an SGR state model, so a reordered line closes only the attributes that end. A bare `ESC[0m` at the end of a reordered line would also clear the background the renderer wraps the line in, and the padding would paint black.

### Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `packages/tui/src/bidi.ts` | The engine: `hasStrongRtl`, `detectBaseDirection`, `dominantDirection`, `reorderLine`, `reorderLineWithCaret`, `stepCaretVisual`, `alignRight`, `configureBidi` |
| `packages/tui/src/components/markdown.ts` | Wrap logical, paint visual; chrome (code blocks, table grid, list markers, quote bars) stays put |
| `packages/tui/src/components/text.ts`, `truncated-text.ts` | Tool rows and single lines: truncate logically, paint visually |
| `packages/tui/src/components/editor.ts` | Visual arrow-key stepping, painted caret at the visual edge, padding moved to the reading side |
| `packages/coding-agent/src/core/settings-*` | `terminal.rtl.enabled` / `terminal.rtl.align`, `PI_RTL=0` override |
| `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/` | Wiring: `configureBidi` on startup and on toggle |

### Settings

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `terminal.rtl.enabled` | `false` | Reorder RTL text for display |
| `terminal.rtl.align` | `true` | Put a line against the edge its dominant script reads from |
| `PI_RTL=0` | — | Off regardless of settings |

### Tests

`node --test test/bidi.test.ts test/bidi-markdown.test.ts test/bidi-editor.test.ts test/bidi-text.test.ts test/bidi-settings.test.ts` — 52 tests: strong-script detection, grapheme reordering, bracket mirroring, whitespace anchoring, positional escapes bail out, width preservation, styling and OSC 8 hyperlinks travel with their grapheme, background fill survives the reorder, wrap-then-reorder, code blocks stay left to right, the table grid is kept while cell content reorders, visual arrow-key stepping, painted caret placement, disabled fallback, plus a reference test that compares the reordering with bidi-js's own UAX #9 output on the same graphemes.

`packages/coding-agent/test/rtl-settings.test.ts` — 4 tests: settings defaults, persistence, the `PI_RTL=0` override, a hand-written settings file.

Full tui suite on this branch: 1321 pass, 8 fail — the same set that fails on unpatched `main` in the same Windows environment (symlink autocomplete, terminal-image path shortening, terminal-restore timing). Nothing new is introduced.

### Performance

200-line markdown render at width 80, Node 26, Windows: English 0.35 ms, Arabic 7.65 ms, Arabic with bidi off 0.92 ms. The extra ~6.7 ms for 200 RTL lines is the UAX #9 pass, about 33 µs per line; lines with no strong RTL character return before it.

### Limits

- Positional escapes (cursor-position codes, the editor `CURSOR_MARKER`) are not moved: if a line contains them, `parseCells` bails and the line is left as written.
- bidi-js reorders by code unit, so the app path deliberately keeps combining marks attached to their base letter; the reference test excludes those samples.
- Alignment is per line. A paragraph that mixes scripts on one wrapped line is aligned by that line's dominant script.
- `bidi-js` (MIT, pure JS, no native code) is a new runtime dependency of `packages/tui`.

### Screenshots

Rendered in Windows Terminal, RTL on: RTL paragraphs, mixed lines with English islands left to right, lists with the marker on the reading edge, mirrored tables, code blocks unchanged. And with `PI_RTL=0`, the mirrored baseline.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): pick the smaller of PNG and JPEG when resizing images
prs.body:
When an image needs resizing, `resizeImageInProcess` builds a list of encodings: PNG first, then JPEG at decreasing qualities. It returned the first one under `maxBytes`. Since PNG was always first, it was used whenever it fit, even when it was many times larger than the JPEG. The doc comment says "Try both PNG and JPEG formats, pick the smaller one", and the code worked that way before v0.62.0. Because of this, photos were sent as multi-MB PNGs, which made requests large enough to fail or time out.

This change compares PNG with JPEG at the configured quality at each size step and tries the smaller one first. It tries the other one next, and the lower JPEG qualities only after that. Screenshots and other images where PNG is smaller still go out as PNG.

**Testing**
- Added a regression test to `test/image-processing.test.ts`: a generated photo-like 1200×800 JPEG resized to 1000 px must come back as `image/jpeg`. The test fails without the fix (PNG is returned) and passes with it.
- `node ../../node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js --run test/image-processing.test.ts test/image-resize-callers.test.ts`: all pass.
- `npm run check`: no issues in the changed files. It does report type errors, all in `packages/ai/test` (model ID unions), which this change does not touch.
- Reproduction with a photo-like 2400×1620 JPEG (460 KB base64):
  - before: `image/png`, 4,008,480 bytes base64, at 2000×1350
  - after: `image/jpeg`, 255,316 bytes base64, at 2000×1350

Fixes #11551

Requested by @davidbrai
