prs.title: fix(permissions): report malformed rules instead of dropping them silently
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A permission rule whose parentheses do not balance is parsed as inert: it matches nothing. On the current base (#15794) such a rule already produces one generic warning, but that line cannot say which list owns it — the same malformed rule in `allow` and `deny` prints two identical lines — it repeats for every manager the hosted path builds, and `/permissions` still filters the rule out, so it cannot be seen or deleted there. This PR makes the drop visible: the permission manager warns on the console, naming the list, the raw rule and the consequence, using the same operator-facing breadcrumb `tools.eager` already prints from the same initializer; and `/permissions` keeps the unparsable rule in the listing, marked `(unparsable)`, so it can be seen and deleted instead of being filtered out. Matching semantics are unchanged — a malformed rule still matches nothing, so no allow/deny decision moves.

## Why it's needed

The asymmetry is what makes this a security problem rather than a logging nit: a malformed allow rule fails closed (nothing gets auto-approved), but a malformed deny/ask rule fails open — the restriction the operator wrote does not exist, and neither startup output nor `/permissions` mentioned it. The operator's mental model is "docker is blocked"; the runtime's behaviour is "no such rule". Turning silent fail-open into visible fail-open is the minimal, semantics-preserving step the issue asks for first: the operator still has to fix the configuration, but now they know there is something to fix.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Write a malformed deny rule into a settings file:

```json
{ "permissions": { "deny": ["Bash(docker *"] } }
```

Start the CLI. Before any prompt, stderr shows:

```
permissions.deny: ignoring malformed deny rule (no closing parenthesis at the end): "Bash(docker *". The rule has no effect; end it with ")" to apply it.
```

Open `/permissions`, switch to the Deny tab: the rule is listed as `(unparsable) Bash(docker *`. Select it and delete it — the row disappears and stays gone on the next open. Then fix the rule to `Bash(docker *)` and restart: no warning, no marker, and a denied command prompts as before.

Focused suites:

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/permissions
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/ui/opentui/dialog-data.test.ts src/ui/opentui/dialogs-permissions.test.tsx src/i18n
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: starting with `deny: ["Bash(docker *"]` printed a generic line with no list name — `[permissions] ignoring malformed rule (unbalanced parentheses): Bash(docker *` — emitted by `packages/core/src/permissions/permission-rules.ts`, once per manager the hosted path builds; and `/permissions` simply did not list the rule.

After, from the built CLI with that settings file:

```
permissions.deny: ignoring malformed deny rule (no closing parenthesis at the end): "Bash(docker *". The rule has no effect; end it with ")" to apply it.
```

With the corrected rule `Bash(docker *)` the same run prints no warning — the negative control.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

macOS: Node 22.23.4, `npm run build`, all focused suites green, plus the headless run quoted above. Linux: Docker `node:22-bookworm`, same suites green, and `tsc --noEmit` clean for both packages. Windows was not run.

### Environment (optional)

Focused unit suites and a headless `dist/index.js` run with a temporary `HOME`; the Linux pass used a Docker volume workspace because a bind-mounted tree trips `rimraf` with `ENOTEMPTY`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a configuration that keeps a malformed rule now prints one line per bad rule from the permission manager at startup (the pre-existing `permission-rules.ts` line can still fire for the same configuration, so a single run may show both shapes), and `/permissions` shows an extra row. No permission decision changes.
- Not validated / out of scope: the issue's other two asks — failing closed (rejecting a malformed deny/ask at load, or denying the tool it names) and the analogous `tools.disabled` typo check — are deliberately left out. The first changes runtime matching semantics, the second is a separate registry check; both fit a follow-up.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. `parseRules` no longer writes to the debug log; reporting moved into the permission manager, its only caller.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15752

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

括号不配对的权限规则会被解析成惰性规则：它不匹配任何调用。在当前 base（#15794）上，这类规则已经会打一行通用告警，但那一行说不清规则属于哪张列表（同一条畸形规则同时出现在 `allow` 和 `deny` 时会打两行完全相同的日志）、会随 hosted 路径每次新建 manager 重复打印，而且 `/permissions` 仍然把它过滤掉，既看不到也删不掉。这个 PR 把"被丢弃"变成可见：权限管理器在控制台告警，点明所在的列表、原始规则和后果，写法沿用同一个初始化流程里 `tools.eager` 已经在用的"面向操作者"面包屑；同时 `/permissions` 不再过滤掉无法解析的规则，而是把它列出来并标注 `(unparsable)`，让操作者能看到并删除。匹配语义完全没有变——畸形规则依旧不匹配任何东西，所以没有任何 allow/deny 判定会因此改变。

## 为什么需要它

这种不对称正是它属于安全问题而不只是日志问题的原因：畸形 allow 规则是 fail-closed（不会自动放行任何东西），但畸形 deny/ask 规则是 fail-open——操作者写下的限制并不存在，而且启动输出和 `/permissions` 都不会提到它。操作者的心智模型是"docker 被拦住了"，运行时的事实是"根本没有这条规则"。把静默的 fail-open 变成可见的 fail-open，是这个 issue 要求的第一步，也是改动最小、不触碰语义的一步：配置仍然要由操作者自己修，但现在他知道有东西要修。

## Reviewer Test Plan（评审验证计划）

### 如何验证

把一条畸形 deny 规则写进配置文件：

```json
{ "permissions": { "deny": ["Bash(docker *"] } }
```

启动 CLI。在任何提示词之前，stderr 会打印：

```
permissions.deny: ignoring malformed deny rule (no closing parenthesis at the end): "Bash(docker *". The rule has no effect; end it with ")" to apply it.
```

打开 `/permissions`，切到 Deny 标签页：该规则显示为 `(unparsable) Bash(docker *`。选中它并删除，这一行会消失，下次打开也不再出现。再把规则改成 `Bash(docker *)` 重启：没有告警、没有标记，被拒绝的命令照旧弹确认。

定向测试：

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/permissions
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/ui/opentui/dialog-data.test.ts src/ui/opentui/dialogs-permissions.test.tsx src/i18n
```

### 证据（改动前后）

改动前：用 `deny: ["Bash(docker *"]` 启动只打印一行不带列表名的通用告警 `[permissions] ignoring malformed rule (unbalanced parentheses): Bash(docker *`（来自 `packages/core/src/permissions/permission-rules.ts`，hosted 路径每新建一个 manager 就重复一次），`/permissions` 也完全不列出这条规则。

改动后，用该配置文件运行构建产物：

```
permissions.deny: ignoring malformed deny rule (no closing parenthesis at the end): "Bash(docker *". The rule has no effect; end it with ")" to apply it.
```

把规则改成 `Bash(docker *)` 后同样运行不再打印任何告警——反向对照。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

macOS：Node 22.23.4，`npm run build`，上述定向测试全部通过，并做了上文引用的 headless 运行。Linux：Docker `node:22-bookworm`，同样的测试全部通过，两个包的 `tsc --noEmit` 也干净。Windows 未运行。

### 运行环境（可选）

定向单元测试，加上用临时 `HOME` 跑的 `dist/index.js` headless 运行；Linux 那轮用 Docker volume 作工作区，因为 bind mount 的目录会让 `rimraf` 报 `ENOTEMPTY`。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：如果配置里保留了畸形规则，启动时权限管理器会按每条坏规则打印一行（原有的 `permission-rules.ts` 那行仍可能对同一份配置触发，所以一次运行可能同时看到两种文案），`/permissions` 也会多出一行。没有任何权限判定发生变化。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：issue 提出的另外两项——fail-closed（加载时拒绝畸形 deny/ask，或直接拒绝它点名的工具）以及 `tools.disabled` 拼写错误的同类校验——有意未包含。前者会改变运行时匹配语义，后者是另一条注册表校验路径，都更适合作为后续 PR。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。`parseRules` 不再写 debug 日志，告警移到了权限管理器里，而它是唯一的调用方。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #15752

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): report a cancelled shell as interrupted, not completed
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds an explicit `interruptedBeforeCompletion` marker to a tool result and sets it when the shell tool is cancelled by the user. The scheduler's post-execute cancellation branch now chooses the cancellation notice from that marker instead of assuming that a returned result means the tool finished.

## Why it's needed

On Esc/Ctrl+C the shell tool kills the process group but returns an ordinary result whose own content already says the command was cancelled. The scheduler's `aborted` branch hardcoded "The tool had already completed; its output was discarded", which discards that truthful text and tells the model the work finished — and not to retry it. For half-run migrations or deploys, a step that was killed is recorded as done.

The shell tool is not the only possible producer of this shape: any tool that reports interruption by returning rather than throwing was mislabelled the same way, so the signal lives on the result rather than being inferred from shell's wording.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Follow the reproduction in #15833 (`work.sh` writing `start`, sleeping, then `done`), run it through the CLI and press Esc about 1s in.
2. Ask the model whether the command finished.
Before: the tool result says the tool had already completed and that the output was discarded. After: it says the call was intentionally cancelled and that it must not retry or work around it.
Timeouts and background-promote refusals keep their existing outcomes; only a user cancel sets the marker.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Non-UI change, so N/A for screenshots. The new scheduler table case fails on the previous code with `The tool had already completed; its output was discarded` and passes here; the shell test asserts the marker is set only on a user cancel.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

Unit tests on macOS and in a `node:22-bookworm` container; Windows not exercised.

### Environment (optional)

`cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/coreToolScheduler.test.ts src/tools/shell.test.ts` (917 tests).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: one optional field on the result type. It is written only by the shell tool and read only by the cancelled branch.
- Not validated / out of scope: other return-style tools are now able to set the marker but none are changed here; a call cancelled before it starts ("cancelled before it could start") is not covered. A cancel that lands while the shell's confirmation dialog is still open (approval mode `default`) is also uncovered: it reports the generic cancelled reason, identically before and after this change.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Closes #15833

Thanks @stars-spark for the detailed reproduction. You mentioned you could send a PR — if you are already on it, say so and I will step back.

prs.title: fix(cli): keep the /mcp action cursor on its action when the list rebuilds
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The OpenTUI `/mcp` server-detail dialog now remembers the highlighted action by its key instead of its row index. When an action succeeds and the host rebuilds the list with fewer rows, the cursor stays on the same action, or falls back to the first row when that action is gone.

## Why it's needed

A disconnected server offers **Reconnect**. Running it succeeds, the host rebuilds the list, and the Reconnect row disappears. The index-keyed cursor stayed on row 2, which is now **Disable**, so pressing Enter again disabled the server. The ink dialog already tracks the active item by key and falls back to the first entry (`useSelectionList`); this restores parity for the opt-in OpenTUI renderer.

Fixes #14655.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

```console
cd packages/cli
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/ui/opentui/dialogs-mcp.test.tsx -t "keeps the cursor on its action"
```

On `91a7f9e481` this fails with `expected "spy" to not be called with ... "toggle-disable"` because the second Enter falls through to Disable. On this branch it passes.

### Evidence (Before & After)

- Before: after Reconnect succeeds, the next Enter calls `onServerAction(server, 'toggle-disable')`.
- After: the cursor falls back to View tools, so Enter opens the tool list and `toggle-disable` is never called.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

macOS: the dialog test file (19 passed), the related OpenTUI dialog suites (53 passed across `dialogs-mcp`, `opentui-dialog-mount`, `batch-cursor`), `tsc --noEmit`, eslint and prettier on the changed files.

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests only. No live TUI session was run, so no screen recording is attached.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the change only affects the opt-in OpenTUI renderer (`QWEN_TUI_RENDERER=opentui`); the ink path is untouched.
- Not validated / out of scope: a live keypress session and non-macOS platforms.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #14655

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

OpenTUI 的 `/mcp` 服务器详情页原来用行号记录高亮动作。Reconnect 成功后宿主会重建服务器列表，Reconnect 这一行消失，光标仍停在原来的行号 2（此时是 Disable），再按一次 Enter 就会禁用服务器。ink 版的 `useSelectionList` 按条目 key 记录光标，并在该条目消失时回落到第一行。

本 PR 把详情页光标改成保存 `action.key`，渲染时再换算成行号；动作消失时回落到第一行。新增回归测试：base 上第二次 Enter 会调用 `toggle-disable`（19 个测试中 1 个失败），分支上 19 个全过；相关的 OpenTUI 对话框套件 53 个测试通过，`tsc --noEmit`、eslint、prettier 均通过。未跑真实 TUI 会话和非 macOS 平台。

</details>

prs.title: fix(web-shell): leave current standalone session before deletion
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Allows an idle current no-workspace session to be deleted from the sidebar. After confirmation, the tab leaves the session, waits for its attachment to be released, and then deletes the original session. The confirmation stays open and cannot be dismissed while this operation is in flight. If detach fails, the current attachment and transcript remain available for a safe retry; if deletion fails after leaving, the session stays listed and an error is shown.

## Why it's needed

The current row's Delete action is disabled today, requiring users to open another chat before deleting it. This implements the leave-first follow-up to #12636 while preserving the daemon's protection of sessions with active work or attached clients. The row's work summary and App's streaming state guard the current session, with another check on confirmation. Delete stays disabled until the current attachment is ready, and navigation changes cannot redirect deletion to another session.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Open an idle no-workspace session and choose Delete from its sidebar row. Cancel the confirmation and verify that the session stays open.
2. Choose Delete again and confirm. Expect a fresh no-workspace draft and the original row to disappear only after deletion succeeds.
3. Open the same session in two tabs. Confirm Delete in the first tab: it should leave, retain the original row, and report that the session is busy. Leave through New task in the second tab, then retry Delete in the first tab's existing confirmation; the original row should disappear.
4. Check that running work disables deletion of the current row and that deleting a different no-workspace session does not leave the current chat. While the current session is loading, its Delete action should be disabled with a readiness hint and become available after attachment completes.
5. While leave or deletion is pending, try Cancel, Escape, the backdrop, and the dialog close button. The confirmation must remain open, with a disabled “Deleting...” button, until the operation settles; an unrelated row mutation must disable its Delete confirmation button while that mutation is pending.
6. If detach fails, expect a localized failure notice, the current attachment, transcript, original row, and confirmation to remain, with no delete request. Retry the same confirmation after detach can succeed; it must attempt detach again before deleting. Cancel instead and continue the chat to confirm its event stream resumes.
7. If the event stream disconnects while reconnecting, confirm Delete during the retry delay. Reconnection must wait while detach is pending; after successful detach the old session must stay cleared, while failed detach must preserve the session and allow its stream to resume.

### Evidence (Before & After)

- Before: the baseline component test confirmed that the current no-workspace row's Delete action was disabled (1 passed, 141 skipped).
- After: isolated real-daemon browser testing observed detach HTTP 204 before delete HTTP 200 with the original ID in `removed`, followed by the row disappearing. Cancelling confirmation sent neither request.
- Two tabs: attachment count changed from 2 to 1, deletion returned HTTP 200 with per-session `session_busy`, and the row and error remained visible. After the second tab left, the count became 0 and retrying the first tab's confirmation deleted the original session successfully.
- Review also identified that a failed strict detach cleared the local attachment before the daemon released it. Regression tests failed on the preceding head and passed after the fix, including retry, timeout, replacement attachment, and continued chat after an event-stream end or error. A further review exposed a reconnect-backoff race: tests reproduced re-subscription while detach was pending and the old session being republished after detach succeeded. The current head passes all three backoff ordering and recovery cases; six related Web Shell suites passed 2013/2013 tests, and the full build and typecheck, changed-file lint/format, diff whitespace checks, and commit hook passed.
- Earlier isolated real-daemon Chrome checks observed “Deleting...” and `aria-busy` throughout held detach and delete requests, a disabled current-row Delete during loading that became enabled after attachment, and an injected detach 503 browser response that showed the localized failure, retained the row, and sent no delete request. Those browser runs predate the strict-detach retry fix.

The [confirmation screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/issue-12669/docs/verification/issue-12669/issue-12669-two-tab-confirm.png) shows the dialog opened from the current row. The two screenshots below show the busy result and a successful retry; the earlier busy toast is still fading in the second image, while the list already says “No sessions.”

| Busy result: original row retained | Retry after the second tab leaves: row removed |
| --- | --- |
| ![The original standalone row remains after session_busy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/issue-12669/docs/verification/issue-12669/issue-12669-two-tab-busy.png) | ![The standalone list is empty after retry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/issue-12669/docs/verification/issue-12669/issue-12669-two-tab-after.png) |

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Unit tests, build/typecheck, isolated real-daemon Chrome checks |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested locally |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Not tested locally |

### Environment (optional)

macOS arm64, Node.js 26.8.2, built local Web Shell, and an embedded daemon with temporary Conversations, project, runtime, and discovery directories for the earlier browser runs. The global `qwen` command was unavailable. No model request was made. Unit tests used `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage`; the build used a temporary Corepack shim around installed pnpm 11.19.0 because Corepack was unavailable (repository pin: 11.24.0).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: another client can keep the original session busy after this tab has already left. The daemon's per-session result remains authoritative, and the row stays visible on failure. Listed client counts are not used to disable Delete because the sidebar does not continuously refresh them.
- Not validated / out of scope: the latest strict-detach and reconnect fix was not rerun in a real-daemon browser; its failure and recovery paths have focused action, provider, and component tests. The earlier detach 503 was an injected browser response, not a real daemon transport failure. Active prompts were not exercised in the browser. Windows, Linux, and full preflight were not run locally. A fresh frozen dependency install was attempted after the main merge but could not fetch package metadata on this machine's restricted network; build and tests passed with the existing dependencies. The `/delete` picker excludes standalone sessions and is outside this change.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; no daemon routes, persistence formats, or dependency changes.

Design: [English](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/f3698089d9/docs/design/2026-09-26-current-standalone-delete.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/f3698089d9/docs/design/2026-09-26-current-standalone-delete.zh-CN.md). Both versions contain the same decisions, constraints, verification results, and acceptance criteria.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #12669

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## What this PR does

允许从侧栏删除空闲的当前无工作区会话。确认后，标签页先离开会话，等待其附着解除，再删除原会话。操作进行中确认框保持打开且无法关闭。detach 失败时保留当前附着与对话记录以便安全重试；离开后删除失败时，原会话继续显示在列表中，并显示错误。

## Why it's needed

当前行的 Delete 目前被禁用，用户必须先打开其他聊天才能删除。本改动实现 #12636 后续的“先离开再删除”流程，同时保留 daemon 对活动工作和已附着客户端的保护。行摘要与 App 的流式输出状态共同保护当前会话，用户确认时再次检查。当前附着就绪前 Delete 保持禁用；导航变化也不会把删除目标改成其他会话。

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. 打开空闲的无工作区会话，从侧栏行选择 Delete。取消确认，检查原会话仍然打开。
2. 再次选择 Delete 并确认。应进入新的无工作区草稿，且只有删除成功后原行才消失。
3. 在两个标签页打开同一会话。在第一个标签页确认 Delete：它应离开会话，保留原行并提示会话忙碌。第二个标签页通过 New task 离开后，在第一个标签页保留的确认框中重试 Delete，原行应消失。
4. 检查当前会话有运行中的工作时删除被禁用，以及删除其他无工作区会话不会离开当前聊天。当前会话加载期间，Delete 应禁用并显示未就绪提示；附着完成后恢复可用。
5. 离开或删除待完成时尝试 Cancel、Esc、遮罩和对话框关闭按钮。确认框应保持打开，按钮禁用并显示“Deleting...”，直至操作结束；其他行的变更操作待完成时，其删除确认按钮也应禁用。
6. 若 detach 失败，应显示本地化失败提示，保留当前附着、对话记录、原行和确认框，且不发删除请求。待 detach 可以成功后在同一确认框重试，必须再次 detach 成功才可删除；也可取消并继续聊天，检查事件流恢复。
7. 若事件流断开并等待重连，在退避期间确认 Delete。detach 未完成时不得重新订阅；成功后旧会话应保持清空，失败后应保留会话并允许事件流恢复。

### Evidence (Before & After)

- 修复前：基线组件测试确认当前无工作区行的 Delete 被禁用（1 项通过、141 项跳过）。
- 修复后：隔离真实 daemon 的浏览器测试观察到 detach HTTP 204 先于删除 HTTP 200，结果的 `removed` 包含原 ID，随后原行消失。取消确认不发送这两个请求。
- 双标签：附着数从 2 降至 1，删除返回 HTTP 200，逐项结果为 `session_busy`，原行和错误仍可见。第二个标签页离开后，计数变为 0；在第一个标签页原确认框重试，成功删除原会话。
- 审查还发现严格 detach 失败时，在 daemon 释放附着前清空本地状态。定向回归测试在上一 head 失败、修复后通过，覆盖重试、超时、附着替换，以及事件流结束或出错后继续聊天。后续审查又发现重连退避竞态：测试复现了 detach 未完成时重新订阅，以及 detach 成功后旧会话被重新发布。当前 head 的三种退避顺序与恢复用例全部通过；六个相关 Web Shell 套件共 2013/2013 项通过，全仓构建和类型检查、改动文件 lint/format、差异空白检查和提交钩子也通过。
- 此前隔离真实 daemon 的 Chrome 测试在暂停 detach 与 delete 请求期间观察到“Deleting...”和 `aria-busy`；加载期间当前行 Delete 禁用，附着完成后恢复；浏览器注入 detach 503 响应后显示本地化失败提示、保留原行，且没有删除请求。这些浏览器测试早于最新的严格 detach 重试修复。

[确认框截图](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/issue-12669/docs/verification/issue-12669/issue-12669-two-tab-confirm.png)显示从当前行打开的对话框。上方两张截图依次展示忙碌时保留原行，以及第二标签离开后重试成功；后一张中旧的 busy 提示尚在消退，但列表已显示“No sessions”。

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ 单测、构建/类型检查、隔离真实 daemon 的 Chrome 验证 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未在本地验证 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 未在本地验证 |

### Environment (optional)

macOS arm64、Node.js 26.8.2、构建后的本地 Web Shell；此前浏览器测试使用临时 Conversations、项目、runtime 和 discovery 目录的内嵌 daemon。本机没有全局 `qwen` 命令，未发送模型请求。单测使用 `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage`；由于 Corepack 不可用，构建通过临时 Corepack 包装调用已安装的 pnpm 11.19.0（仓库固定版本为 11.24.0）。

## Risk & Scope

- 主要风险或取舍：此标签页离开后，其他客户端仍可能使原会话保持忙碌。最终以 daemon 的逐项结果为准，失败时原行保留。侧栏不会持续刷新客户端计数，因此不使用列表中的计数禁用 Delete。
- 未验证或范围外：最新严格 detach 与重连修复未在真实 daemon 浏览器重跑；失败与恢复由会话动作、Provider 和组件定向测试覆盖。此前 detach 503 是浏览器注入的响应，不是真实 daemon 传输故障；浏览器也未运行活动提示。本机未运行 Windows、Linux 或完整 preflight。合入主线后曾尝试冻结依赖安装，但受限网络无法获取包元数据；构建与测试在现有依赖下通过。`/delete` 选择器不包含 standalone 会话，不在本次范围内。
- 破坏性变更或迁移说明：无；未改变 daemon 路由、持久化格式或依赖。

设计：[English](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/f3698089d9/docs/design/2026-09-26-current-standalone-delete.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/f3698089d9/docs/design/2026-09-26-current-standalone-delete.zh-CN.md)。两版的决策、约束、验证结果和验收标准一致。

## Linked Issues

Fixes #12669

</details>

prs.title: fix(ci): partition the complete macOS test suite into bounded jobs
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Partition the complete macOS CI suite into seven jobs: three CLI shards, two core shards, all remaining workspace suites, and standalone/runtime script suites. Keep the original macOS check as an aggregate that succeeds only when every group succeeds. This PR is stacked on #15883 and includes the Windows fixture isolation merged through #15889. It also repairs the system Bash paths exposed by the complete scripts group: empty issue-family arrays, failed-job collection without mapfile, and explicit rejection of missing OSS credentials. Existing assertions remain active.

## Why it's needed

The full macOS job reached its one-hour limit twice. On the second attempt, setup consumed about 13 minutes and tests were still making progress when the job was cancelled; later workspace and script suites never ran. Partitioning provides independent execution budgets without increasing the timeout or removing tests.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm that all seven macOS groups execute, including both standalone/runtime and script suites, and that any group failure fails the original aggregate check. Confirm that new workspace test suites are discovered automatically. The portable process smoke runs once and a failure there does not suppress the script suites. Every existing test and assertion remains in scope.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: [the second macOS attempt](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40885875352/job/123557350519) was cancelled at the one-hour job limit while still processing CLI tests. The first complete run finished all seven groups: five passed, while CLI shard 1 and scripts failed. The scripts fixes need CI confirmation; three CLI failures and other Windows failures remain under investigation. Full CI for the latest revision is pending. N/A for UI screenshots.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ CI pending; no local execution |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Full CI pending |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Workflow regression tests pending in CI |

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: seven independent macOS setup/build phases cost more runner time; the existing aggregate check name is preserved.
- Not validated / out of scope: no local tests, builds, lint, or dependency installation were run. Partitioning does not claim to fix the previously observed CLI hook timeout or Windows environment failure.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; no test filters, skipped suites, relaxed assertions, or timeout increases.
- Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/macos-ci-shards/docs/design/macos-ci-test-groups.md) / [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/macos-ci-shards/docs/design/macos-ci-test-groups.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Related to #15883 and #15884 and the Managed runtime 0.26.3 recovery.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 变更内容

将完整 macOS CI 分成七个任务：三个 CLI 分片、两个 core 分片、其余全部工作区测试、独立运行时及脚本测试。保留原 macOS 检查作为汇总门禁，只有所有组成功才通过。本 PR 堆叠在 #15883 上，包含经 #15889 合入的 Windows 夹具隔离。同时修复完整脚本组暴露的系统 Bash 问题：空 issue 家族数组、不依赖 mapfile 的失败任务收集，以及 OSS 凭据缺失时明确退出。已有断言继续生效。

## 原因

完整 macOS 任务连续两次触及一小时上限。第二次准备环境耗时约 13 分钟，取消时测试仍在持续推进，后面的工作区和脚本测试尚未开始。拆分为各组提供独立执行预算，不提高超时，也不移除测试。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

确认七组 macOS 测试全部执行，包括独立运行时和脚本两组测试，且任何组失败都会让原汇总检查失败。确认新增工作区的测试能自动纳入。可移植进程冒烟仅执行一次，其失败不阻止脚本测试继续执行。所有已有测试与断言保持在验证范围内。

### 前后证据

变更前：[第二次 macOS 执行](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40885875352/job/123557350519) 仍在处理 CLI 测试时触及一小时任务上限而被取消。首次完整执行中七组均已结束，五组通过，CLI 第一分片和脚本组失败。本次脚本修复仍需 CI 确认；三个 CLI 失败及其他 Windows 失败仍在排查。最新提交的完整 CI 待完成。无 UI 截图要求。

### 验证环境

| 系统 | 状态 |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ 等待 CI；未本地执行 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 等待完整 CI |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 工作流回归测试待 CI 执行 |

## 风险与范围

- 主要代价：七组分别准备环境和构建，会增加 runner 使用量；原汇总检查名称保留。
- 未验证及范围外：未运行本地测试、构建、lint 或安装依赖。拆分不代表此前 CLI hook 超时或 Windows 环境错误已经修好。
- 兼容性：无破坏性变更；不筛选测试、不跳过测试组、不放宽断言、不提高超时。
- 设计文档：[英文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/macos-ci-shards/docs/design/macos-ci-test-groups.md) / [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/macos-ci-shards/docs/design/macos-ci-test-groups.zh-CN.md)。

## 关联事项

关联 #15883、#15884 以及 Managed runtime 0.26.3 补发。

</details>

prs.title: fix(edit): keep the line endings an edit did not touch
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Keep the original bytes outside local edit spans and choose inserted line endings per span. Whole-file editor replacements retain their previous CRLF behavior. Team-memory edits scan both the normalized replacement and the exact content that will reach disk.

Merged current main (`18f80f5666`) in `b35ef1c0c8`, retaining its workspace-aware file access and mutation closure. The diff remains limited to the original four files.

## Why it's needed

One CRLF caused Edit to convert untouched LF lines. Bare CR is ordinary content and must survive replacement text. The final write payload also needs the credential guard because line-ending processing can form a credential that was absent from the normalized replacement.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

From `packages/core`, run Vitest on `src/utils/editHelper.test.ts`, `src/tools/edit.test.ts`, `src/services/fileSystemService.test.ts`, and `src/managed-runtime/runtime-file.test.ts`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

At current main `18f80f5666`, the real EditTool regression `keeps untouched line endings when the file mixes CRLF and LF` fails: untouched LF lines become CRLF. At `b35ef1c0c8`, it passes.

On the merged tree: 231 core tests passed; CLI workspace/SSH filesystem and managed-runtime/CSI tests passed 237 tests with 31 skipped. Core typecheck, CLI build/typecheck, and scoped ESLint/Prettier passed. Earlier bare-CR and credential-guard mutation results are recorded in the review thread.

### Tested on

macOS. Windows and Linux were not tested locally.

### Environment (optional)

Frozen pnpm dependencies, with the repository's Ink patch applied. Filesystem/SSH unit tests use test doubles; no live SSH server was used.

## Risk & Scope

A mixed span uses one resolved ending internally; whole-file replacement keeps its prior behavior. Main's workspace/freshness checks remain in place. No API migration. Full preflight, sandbox E2E, Windows scripts, and live SSH/serve/ACP paths were not validated.

## Linked Issues

Related to #12792; broader write paths remain open.

prs.title: feat(review): auto-verify a pull request whose review came back clean
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a built-in handoff from a clean pull-request review to a deep-verification round. When a review ends with no Critical findings and certified the scope it read, the running daemon starts a session in the same workspace that runs the maintainer verification round and publishes its evidence report, so the behavioural-evidence step no longer depends on someone noticing the verdict and starting it by hand.

The handoff is a durable, platform-neutral record rather than a hook inside one pipeline, and it has three entrances that all write the same record: the review pipeline records it automatically at the end of its own round; any external producer — another agent, a script, a CI job, a person — can record it with a new offline subcommand; and a registered watch lets the daemon observe the approval state the platform already holds, so a review performed by anyone at all hands off with no action from the reviewer. Every handoff belongs to a session and every verification round is that session's **sub-session**: the reviewing session for the tool's own rounds, the session an external producer was invoked from or names explicitly, or the session that owns a watch. A handoff naming no session is refused at the entrance rather than recorded, so no round is ever left attached to nothing. Every entrance passes the same gates, the same per-head dedupe and the same operator switch.

Ownership also gives the automation its lifetime. A watch is keyed by coordinates and owner, so two sessions watching one pull request are two watches rather than a transfer of ownership; the automation serves each owner only its own events and watches, and prunes a deleted owner's state. Liveness is decided by transcript presence, not residency, so an idle session keeps its watches and only deleting it ends them — and an owner whose state cannot be read is neither served nor cleaned up. Who reviewed and who owns the round are separate facts: the reviewer is recorded as attribution, the owner is the parent.

## Why it's needed

A clean review is exactly the moment when behavioural evidence is worth having, and exactly the moment a busy maintainer skips it. The two commands already exist; nothing connected them.

Two obvious shortcuts were rejected. Triggering from GitHub Actions after the bot approves is GitHub-only by construction, while the review pipeline already serves a second platform behind one provider registry and more are intended; a workflow also runs outside the operator's session and cannot create one. Welding the trigger to the review pipeline's own output was the first implementation here, and it was wrong for the same reason in miniature: the reviewer is frequently not this tool. Another agent, the CI bot, or a human leaves no artifact for that pipeline to emit from, so the contract had to be reachable from outside it — and the consumer had to be able to act on an event that names no local session, which the first cut silently dropped.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Build, then exercise the three entrances against a scratch workspace with the daemon's global directory redirected, so nothing publishes and no real PR is touched.

1. Internal entrance: stage a clean round's inputs (a findings report with zero Criticals, and a composed verdict whose body carries a ledger marker with its head anchor) and run `qwen review save-artifact … --workspace-root <scratch>`. Expect one event file under the host-trusted review-state directory, outside the repository, and a stderr line naming it. Withholding the marker's anchor — the state a fail-closed round persists — must produce no event while still saving the artifact.
2. External entrance: run `qwen review verify-event --pr <n> --repo <owner>/<repo> --head <sha> --reviewed-by codex --session-id <session> --workspace-root <scratch>`. Expect exit 0, one JSON object on stdout, and the same record naming that session as owner with no artifact path. With neither `--session-id` nor a session in the environment it must refuse and write nothing. A malformed head, repo, number, or a `REQUEST_CHANGES` verdict must exit 2 and write nothing.
3. Observation: run `qwen review verify-watch <n> --repo <owner>/<repo>`, then `qwen review verify-watch --once`. The judgement must refuse a dismissed approval (the aggregate is no longer approved even though the old review body still says "Approving"), any unresolved non-outdated thread, a draft, a closed PR, and a truncated thread page; a resolved or outdated thread must not block. A second `--once` at the same head must report `already-handed-off`.
4. Consumer: with the workspace carrying the verification skill, a pending event must produce exactly one sub-session of its owning session, whose prompt is `/verify-pr <n> --publish --repo <owner>/<repo>`, and the pending file must be gone afterwards. An event naming no owner must be dropped with a reason and spawn nothing. A deleted owner must spawn nothing and must have its watches and pending events pruned; an owner whose liveness cannot be read must be left untouched. Two clean rounds at one head must spawn once, whichever entrance wrote them.
5. Policy: `review.autoVerify: false` in user settings must stop spawning and stop observation while still recording events; the same key in a workspace settings file must be ignored in either direction.

Three harnesses driving the built output automate 1–4 and are recorded with their measured output in the E2E plan; they stub the platform reader and the session bridge, so they publish nothing.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible TUI change. The observable surfaces are a new daemon log line per handoff and the spawned session in the session list.

Measured on this branch: full build exit 0; the CLI package's type check exit 0; 200 tests across the eight touched suites plus 154 across the settings suites; ESLint and Prettier clean on every touched file. The three built-output harnesses report `SMOKE_OK true`, `EXTERNAL_OK true` and `E2_OK true`, the last including all four negative judgements and an attribution of `github:<approver>` with no session id.

One pre-existing red is worth flagging so it is not attributed here: the large server suite fails a different one or two tests on each full run on this machine. A pristine checkout of the base commit fails two tests in the same file, different ones again, and the failures from this branch pass when run in isolation. Three runs, three different failure sets, on both trees.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local build and unit suites; the harnesses run the built modules directly with a stubbed platform reader and session bridge. No live daemon spawn and no real platform read were exercised.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the spawned session executes the pull request's code and publishes a comment. It is a sub-session of the owning session, so it inherits that session's workspace and counts against the launcher's per-caller and workspace concurrency caps and its one-level nesting limit — a verification round cannot itself start another. It inherits the isolation posture of a manually invoked verification round and adds no sandbox of its own. Dedupe is write-ahead per reviewed head, so a daemon that dies mid-handoff never replays a round that may already have published; the accepted cost is that a failed spawn is logged and not retried rather than risking a duplicate public report. An external producer's assertion that a round was clean is not independently re-checked — the caller runs with the operator's own authority, and the record names who asserted it.
- Not validated / out of scope: a live daemon spawn and drain, and the real platform read (both need a running daemon and credentials); observation on platforms other than GitHub, which is registered and declined with a reason; GitHub Enterprise targets, which the verification command cannot yet express because it has no host flag. A watch is an explicit operator registration, so the network spend is opt-in per pull request.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. One new operator-scoped setting, default on, which a repository cannot change in either direction; when settings cannot be read at all it degrades to off, preserving that loader's existing "a degrade writes nothing public" contract.

Design document: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/review-clean-auto-verify.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/review-clean-auto-verify.zh-CN.md) (both added by this PR, complete and synchronized).

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

新增一条内置交接：从一次干净的 PR 评审，到一轮深度验证。当一轮评审以零 Critical 结束、并且认证了它实际读过的范围时，运行中的 daemon 会在同一工作区起一个会话，执行维护者验证轮并发布其证据报告——行为证据这一步不再依赖有人注意到裁决并手工起轮。

这条交接是一份持久化、平台中立的记录，而不是焊在某一条管线里的钩子。它有三个入口，写的都是同一份记录：评审管线在自己那一轮结束时自动记录；任何外部生产者——别的 agent、脚本、CI job、人——都可以用一个新的离线子命令记录；登记一个 watch 后，daemon 会观测平台已经持有的批准态，于是无论谁做的评审都能在评审者毫不作为的情况下完成交接。每次交接都归属一个会话，每轮验证都是该会话的**子会话**：工具自己评审时是评审会话，外部生产者被调用时所在（或显式点名）的会话，或拥有某个 watch 的会话。不点名会话的交接在入口就被拒绝、不会被记录，因此不会出现不挂在任何工作之下的一轮。三个入口过同一套闸门、同一份按 head 的去重、同一个 operator 开关。

归属也给了自动化生命周期。watch 按坐标与归属者建键，因此两个会话 watch 同一个 PR 是两条 watch，而不是归属转移；自动化只为每个归属者处理它自己的事件与 watch，并剪掉已删除归属者的状态。存活性按 transcript 是否存在判定、而非是否驻留，因此空闲会话仍保有它的 watch，只有删除会话才终结它们——而读不出状态的归属者既不服务也不清理。谁评审与谁拥有这一轮是两件事：评审者作为归因记录，归属者才是父会话。

## 为什么需要

干净的评审恰恰是最值得补行为证据的时刻，也恰恰是忙碌的维护者最容易跳过的时刻。两个命令本来就存在，只是没有任何东西把它们接起来。

两条显而易见的捷径被否掉了。bot 批准后用 GitHub Actions 触发，在构造上就是 GitHub 专属，而评审管线早已在一个 provider 注册表后面服务第二个平台、且还打算接更多；工作流也跑在操作者会话之外，无法创建会话。把触发焊在评审管线自己的产出上，是这里的第一个实现，它因为同样的原因在更小尺度上错了：评审者经常不是这个工具。别的 agent、CI bot 或人不会留下让那条管线据以产出的产物，所以契约必须能从管线之外抵达——而且消费者必须能处理一条不指向本地会话的事件，第一版会把这类事件静默丢弃。

## 评审者验证计划

### 如何验证

先构建，然后在一个临时工作区上、把 daemon 的全局目录重定向之后，验证三个入口；这样不会发布任何东西，也不会碰到真实 PR。

1. 内部入口：备齐一轮干净评审的输入（零 Critical 的发现报告，以及 body 内 ledger 标记带有 head 锚点的 composed 裁决），跑 `qwen review save-artifact … --workspace-root <scratch>`。预期在宿主受信的 review-state 目录下、仓库之外，恰好一个事件文件，并在 stderr 点名它。把标记的锚点 withhold 掉——也就是 fail-closed 轮次持久化的那个状态——必须不产出事件，但仍然保存产物。
2. 外部入口：跑 `qwen review verify-event --pr <n> --repo <owner>/<repo> --head <sha> --reviewed-by codex --session-id <session> --workspace-root <scratch>`。预期退出 0、stdout 一个 JSON 对象、同一份记录且点名该会话为归属者、不带产物路径。既没有 `--session-id`、环境里也没有会话时，必须拒绝且什么都不写。畸形的 head、repo、编号，或 `REQUEST_CHANGES` 裁决，必须退出 2 且什么都不写。
3. 观测：跑 `qwen review verify-watch <n> --repo <owner>/<repo>`，再跑 `qwen review verify-watch --once`。判定必须拒绝：被 dismiss 的批准（聚合态已不再批准，尽管旧评审正文仍写着「Approving」）、任何未决且未过期的线程、draft、已关闭的 PR、以及被截断的线程页；已解决或已过期的线程不得算阻塞。同一 head 第二次 `--once` 必须报 `already-handed-off`。
4. 消费者：工作区带有验证 skill 时，一条待处理事件必须恰好产生一个归属会话的子会话，其 prompt 为 `/verify-pr <n> --publish --repo <owner>/<repo>`，且事后 pending 文件消失。不指向归属者的事件必须以原因丢弃、不派生任何东西。已删除的归属者不得派生，且其 watch 与待处理事件被剪枝；读不出存活性的归属者必须原样保留。同一 head 的两轮干净评审只派生一次，无论由哪个入口写入。
5. 策略：user 设置里的 `review.autoVerify: false` 必须停止派生并停止观测，但仍然记录事件；同一个键写在工作区设置文件里，无论 true 还是 false 都必须被忽略。

三个驱动构建产物的 harness 把 1–4 自动化了，其实测输出记录在 E2E 计划里；它们打桩了平台读取器与会话 bridge，因此不发布任何东西。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A —— 没有用户可见的 TUI 变化。可观察面是每次交接一条新的 daemon 日志，以及会话列表里被派生的那个会话。

本分支实测：全量构建 exit 0；CLI 包类型检查 exit 0；八个受影响套件 200 个测试，加上设置相关套件 154 个；每个改动文件 ESLint 与 Prettier 干净。三个构建产物 harness 分别报 `SMOKE_OK true`、`EXTERNAL_OK true`、`E2_OK true`，最后一个包含全部四个否定判定，以及 `github:<批准者>` 的归因且不带会话 id。

有一处既有的红值得点名，以免被归到本 PR 头上：那个大型 server 套件在本机每次全量运行都会失败不同的一两个用例。基线提交的纯净检出在同一文件里失败两个、又是不同的用例，而本分支首轮那两个失败用例隔离运行时全过。三次运行、三套不同失败，两棵树都如此。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 运行环境（可选）

本地构建与单元测试；harness 直接运行构建后的模块，平台读取器与会话 bridge 均为桩。没有跑过活 daemon 的真实派生，也没有跑过真实的平台读取。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：被派生的会话会执行该 PR 的代码并发表评论。它是归属会话的子会话，因此继承该会话的工作区，并计入 launcher 的 per-caller 与工作区并发闸以及一级嵌套上限——验证轮自己不能再起下一层。它继承手工调用验证轮的隔离姿态，自身不新增沙箱。去重是按被评审 head 的 write-ahead，因此交接中途死掉的 daemon 绝不会重放一轮可能已经发布过的验证；接受的代价是派生失败只记日志、不重试，而不是冒重复发布公开报告的风险。外部生产者关于「本轮干净」的断言不会被独立复核——调用者与操作者同权限，且记录里点名了是谁断言的。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：活 daemon 的派生与 drain，以及真实的平台读取（两者都需要运行中的 daemon 与凭据）；GitHub 以外平台的观测，会被登记并以原因拒绝；GitHub Enterprise 目标，验证命令因为没有 host 旗标还无法表达。watch 是操作者的显式登记，因此网络开销按 PR 逐个 opt-in。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。新增一个 operator 作用域设置，默认开，仓库不能朝任何方向改它；当设置完全读不出来时降级为关，以保持该加载器既有的「降级不产生公开写入」契约。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/review-clean-auto-verify.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/review-clean-auto-verify.zh-CN.md)（均由本 PR 新增，完整且同步）。

## 关联 Issue

无。

</details>

prs.title: feat(core): one-shot modality probe for pattern-guessed models (/model action, phase 1)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Implements **phase 1** of #10309: an explicit one-shot image modality probe for models whose input modalities were guessed by the name-pattern table.

- **Probe module** (`packages/core/src/services/modalityProbe/`): sends a single chat-completions request carrying a red 8×8 PNG to the model's own endpoint, deliberately bypassing the content pipeline (the converter's modality gate is exactly the belief under test). Three-state verdict: `200` → `image`; error text carrying modality semantics → `text_only`; auth / rate-limit / timeout / ambiguous errors → `unknown` (no conclusion, nothing persisted). The successful response's content is never inspected — reasoning models routinely return an empty `content` with text in `reasoning_content`/`thinking` even when the image was accepted. The error-dialect dictionary covers the four vendor dialects observed in the #10309 validation matrix (DeepSeek/Ollama `does not support image…`, Zhipu's content-type enum validation, OpenRouter's router-level 404), with hints deliberately phrased with an object (`not support image`, `不支持图片`) so region-availability errors abstain rather than misjudge.
- **Persistence**: verdicts are stored under a new top-level `probeResults` settings key (`authType|modelId|baseUrl` → `{ verdict, probedAt }`). `unknown` is never persisted; the write side guards against hand-corrupted stores; probe results never touch a model entry's `generationConfig.modalities`.
- **Resolution chain**: `explicit modalities (settings/modelProviders) > persisted probe result > name-pattern table`, stamped as `modalitiesSource` (`explicit` / `probe` / `pattern`) on the resolved config. A comment marks the insertion point reserved for the #8558 API-backed catalog layer (final chain: explicit > provider-native catalog > probe > regex > conservative defaults).
- **UI**: the `/model` dialog shows a provenance badge next to the modality value (`manual` / `probe-tested` / `auto-detected`) and offers a `t` — test image support action on pattern-sourced entries only (live settings read; hidden once a verdict concludes, retryable after `unknown`; never offered for user-configured entries).

## Why it's needed

Fixes the recurring pattern-table race documented on #10309 (#4219, then #10270 → #10278 hours later): every newly shipped vision model needs a manual `MODALITY_PATTERNS` entry, and until one lands, users' images are silently replaced by a text placeholder. This PR is the staged first step the #10309 triage recommended ("explicit test-image-support action on pattern-guessed entries in /model"), submitted as a **Draft to anchor the design discussion** — wizard-time auto-probing, invalidation/re-probe policy, and offline behavior are deliberately out of scope pending that discussion.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/services/modalityProbe src/models/modelConfigResolver.test.ts src/models/modelRegistry.test.ts src/models/modelsConfig.test.ts; cd ../..
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/ui/components/ModelDialog.test.tsx; cd ../..
```

Coverage highlights: three-state classification (all four vendor dialects, region-error abstention EN/zh, 5xx abstention, network failure), storage round-trip + corrupted-store guards, and the resolution chain in both directions — an explicit declaration written *after* a probe verdict still wins at the resolver **and** in the dialog display.

Optional end-to-end (any OpenAI-compatible provider): configure a pattern-guessed vision model (e.g. `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` without a `modalities` override), open `/model`, press `t` on the entry — the badge flips to `probe-tested` and the verdict lands in `probeResults`. The probe script from #10309 ([gist](https://gist.github.com/jarvislee90s-dot/1f62250a2b0cfa9a3abcb808a12734dc)) re-runs the four-endpoint validation with any subset of keys.

### Evidence (Before & After)

User-visible TUI change; screenshots to be attached once CI renders the draft. Unit-level before/after is expressed by the tests above (N/A — no visual capture in this environment yet).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ✅ tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Local source build on Windows, Node ≥22. Scoped suites: probe 19, resolver 62, registry 82, modelsConfig 85, ModelDialog 73 — all green; typecheck / eslint / prettier clean on changed files; `settings.schema.json` regenerated (CI drift gate). Repo-wide preflight on this Windows machine has known environment-only failures (EPERM symlink, git-path classes — same set on base `b90c2f0`); none touch the changed files' suites.

## Risk & Scope

- Size note: ~2,010 insertions across 28 files — above the repo's ~1,200-line split guidance, hence this note. Composition: 51% tests; the probe UI logic is isolated in a dedicated hook (`packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/use-image-support-probe.ts`), so the `ModelDialog` diff is mostly rendering and keybinding. Before this draft is marked ready-for-review, the plan is to split it into two stacked PRs — core resolution chain (probe module + resolver + persistence + unit tests, ≈1,150 lines) and UI (hook + dialog + dialog tests, ≈970 lines) — each under the guideline.
- Main risk or tradeoff: a wrong `text_only` verdict would be persisted with no phase-1 re-probe path — mitigated by the three-state protocol (uncertainty abstains), object-scoped dialect hints, verdict re-validation on read, and the explicit-declaration escape hatch that always overrides in both the runtime chain and the dialog.
- Known boundaries (deliberate, for the design discussion): the probe verdict feeds the *runtime* resolution chain on the next model-providers reload (e.g. restart); the dialog already displays it live. Wiring the write to an in-session registry reload is the open option. `QWEN_OAUTH` routes are not probeable in phase 1; a `baseUrl` env override can key-diverge from the resolver path (documented in `probe-store.ts`).
- Storage choice rationale (open question 1 on #10309): a top-level `probeResults` map because `settings.setValue` cannot address nested array items and composite keys containing URLs are unsafe as dotted paths; alternatives (per-entry field, standalone cache file) noted for the discussion.
- Not validated / out of scope: wizard auto-probe, invalidation/TTL, re-probe action, responses-API wire format, video/pdf probes, `accepted-not-seen` fourth state.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none — absent `probeResults`, behavior is byte-identical to current main (covered by the untouched existing suites).

## Linked Issues

References #10309 (draft for the design discussion; not requesting merge yet). Complements #8558 — the catalog covers known provider+model pairs, the probe covers the catalog's blind spots (self-hosted, gateways, brand-new releases); the chain insertion point is marked in `modelConfigResolver.ts`.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

实现 #10309 的**一期**：为模态来源是名称模式表猜测的模型提供显式一次性图片模态探测。

- **探测模块**（`packages/core/src/services/modalityProbe/`）：向模型自身端点发送一条携带红色 8×8 PNG 的 chat-completions 请求，刻意绕过内容管线（转换器的模态闸门正是被检验的对象）。三态判定：`200` → `image`；报错文本含模态语义 → `text_only`；鉴权/限流/超时/含糊报错 → `unknown`（不下结论、不落盘）。绝不检查成功响应的内容——推理模型即使在图片被接受时也经常返回空 `content`、正文落在 `reasoning_content`/`thinking`。报错方言字典覆盖 #10309 验证矩阵实测的四种厂商方言，且短语刻意带宾语（`not support image`、`不支持图片`），使区域可用性类报错弃权而非误判。
- **持久化**：判定存入顶层新键 `probeResults`（`authType|modelId|baseUrl` → `{ verdict, probedAt }`）。`unknown` 永不落盘；写侧对手改损坏的 store 设防；探测结论绝不触碰模型条目的 `generationConfig.modalities`。
- **解析链**：显式 `modalities` > 已持久化探测结果 > 名称模式表，来源以 `modalitiesSource`（`explicit`/`probe`/`pattern`）标注在解析结果上。注释标出为 #8558 目录层预留的插入位（终态链：显式 > 目录 > 探测 > 正则 > 保守默认）。
- **UI**：`/model` 对话框模态值旁显示来源徽标（manual / probe-tested / auto-detected），仅对 pattern 来源条目提供 `t` 测试图片支持动作（活读 settings；得出结论后隐藏，unknown 后可重试；用户手写条目永不显示）。

## 为什么需要此改动

修复 #10309 记录的反复出现的模式表竞速（#4219，随后 #10270 → #10278 数小时竞态）：每个新发布的视觉模型都需要人工补 `MODALITY_PATTERNS` 条目，补上之前用户的图片被静默替换为文本占位符。本 PR 是 #10309 triage 建议的分期第一步（"先做 /model 中对 pattern 猜测条目的显式测试动作"），以 **Draft 形式提交作为设计讨论的锚点**——向导自动探测、失效/重测策略、离线行为均刻意留待讨论。

## 审查者测试计划

### 验证方式

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/services/modalityProbe src/models/modelConfigResolver.test.ts src/models/modelRegistry.test.ts src/models/modelsConfig.test.ts; cd ../..
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/ui/components/ModelDialog.test.tsx; cd ../..
```

覆盖要点：三态分类（四种厂商方言、中英文区域报错弃权、5xx 弃权、网络失败）、存取往返与损坏 store 守卫、以及双向优先级链——探测结论落盘*之后*再手写显式声明，在解析器与对话框显示两层都仍然获胜。

可选端到端（任一 OpenAI 兼容 provider）：配置一个 pattern 猜测的视觉模型（如不带 `modalities` 覆盖的 `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`），打开 `/model`，在条目上按 `t` —— 徽标变为 probe-tested、判定落入 `probeResults`。#10309 的探测脚本（[gist](https://gist.github.com/jarvislee90s-dot/1f62250a2b0cfa9a3abcb808a12734dc)）可用任意子集 key 复跑四端点验证。

### 证据（修复前后）

用户可见的 TUI 变更；截图待 CI 渲染草稿后补。单测层面的前后对照由上述测试表达（本环境暂无视觉捕获，N/A）。

### 测试平台

|    操作系统    | 状态  |
| :------------: | :---: |
|      macOS     | ⚠️ 未测试 |
|     Windows    | ✅ 已测试 |
|     Linux      | ⚠️ 未测试 |

### 环境（可选）

Windows 本地源码构建，Node ≥22。分范围套件：probe 19、resolver 62、registry 82、modelsConfig 85、ModelDialog 73——全绿；改动文件的 typecheck / eslint / prettier 干净；`settings.schema.json` 已重新生成（CI 漂移门禁）。本 Windows 机器的全仓 preflight 存在已知环境性失败（EPERM symlink、git 路径类——base `b90c2f0` 上同一集合）；均不涉及改动文件的套件。

## 风险与范围

- 体量说明：约 2,010 行新增、28 个文件——超过仓库约 1,200 行的拆分指引，特此说明。构成：51% 为测试；探测 UI 逻辑已隔离到独立 hook（`packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/use-image-support-probe.ts`），`ModelDialog` 的 diff 以渲染与键位绑定为主。本草稿标记 ready-for-review 前，计划拆为两个堆叠 PR——核心解析链（探测模块 + resolver + 持久化 + 单测，约 1,150 行）与 UI（hook + 对话框 + 对话框测试，约 970 行）——各自低于指引线。
- 主要风险或取舍：错误的 `text_only` 判定会被持久化且一期无重测出口——由三态协议（不确定即弃权）、带宾语的方言短语、读侧 verdict 复验、以及永远获胜的显式声明补救出口共同缓解。
- 已知边界（刻意保留，供设计讨论）：探测判定在下次模型 provider 重载（如重启）时进入*运行时*解析链；对话框已活读显示。写入时联动会话内 registry 重载是待讨论的开放选项。`QWEN_OAUTH` 路由一期不可探测；`baseUrl` 环境覆盖可能与解析路径键分歧（已记录于 `probe-store.ts`）。
- 存储选型说明（#10309 开放问题 1）：顶层 `probeResults` 映射——因 settings.setValue 无法寻址嵌套数组元素、含 URL 的组合键作 dotted path 不安全；备选（条目内字段、独立缓存文件）已列出供讨论。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：向导自动探测、失效/TTL、重测动作、responses API 线格式、video/pdf 探针、`accepted-not-seen` 第四态。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无——无 `probeResults` 时行为与当前 main 逐字节一致（由未改动的既有套件覆盖）。

## 关联 Issue

References #10309（设计讨论用草稿；暂不请求合并）。与 #8558 互补——目录覆盖已知 provider+model 对，探测覆盖目录盲区（自托管、网关、全新发布）；链插入位已在 `modelConfigResolver.ts` 标注。

</details>

## Highlights

The bundled CLI 0.23.0 includes two fixes requested in #11022:

- Managed memory availability now respects the `memory.enableManagedAutoMemory` setting (#6941). Hosts that disable managed auto memory no longer see remember/dream requests admitted or managed-memory instructions in the system prompt; local patches can be removed.
- Size-triggered microcompaction now clears old tool results toward a low watermark (#8464), so it no longer rewrites another part of the conversation prefix on every subsequent turn. Provider prompt-cache reuse is preserved across long tool-heavy sessions, reducing cached-input cost.

issues.title: main does not compile: PersistRequest::ClearCheckpoint is now dead, and every PR's required checks fail on it
issues.body:
### What happened

`main` does not compile under the workspace's own lint policy. Every pull request's **required** checks now fail on the same error, so no external contribution can merge:

```
error: variant `ClearCheckpoint` is never constructed
  --> crates/tui/src/tui/persistence_actor.rs:80:5
```

Affected required checks on #7147: `Lint` (→ `Run clippy`), `Test (windows-latest)`, `npm wrapper smoke (ubuntu-latest)`. `Test (ubuntu-latest)` fails at `Build canonical executable for acceptance tests` and `MSRV check (1.89)` at `cargo +1.89 check`, same error.

The cause is a dead variant, not anything in the PRs: `PersistRequest::ClearCheckpoint` lost its last non-test constructor, every remaining construction sits inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (line 843 onwards), and `[workspace.lints.rust] warnings = "deny"` plus `RUSTFLAGS: -Dwarnings` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` turn that into a hard error.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
git fetch origin main
git checkout 6a08f0312      # current origin/main
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked
# error: variant `ClearCheckpoint` is never constructed

git checkout c4a4f42e9      # its parent
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked
# Finished — compiles
```

So the breakage is exactly one commit wide.

### Which commit

`6a08f0312 fix(session): retain recovery when reset snapshot fails [skip ci]`

It rewrote `persist_full_reset_snapshot` in `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/session_state.rs`; the replaced branch was the only production call site:

```diff
-    if let Some(session_id) = app.current_session_id.clone() {
-        persistence_actor::persist(PersistRequest::ClearCheckpoint { session_id });
-    }
+    let session = match session {
+        Ok(session) => session,
+        Err(err) => { /* ...add_message(Error)... */ return; }
+    };
```

That removal is intentional by the commit's own description ("retain recovery when reset snapshot fails" — the old branch cleared the checkpoint precisely when the replacement could not be built). What was missed is that the variant, its `PersistRequest` dispatch arms (lines 430/572/648), and its queue-coalescing paths are now unreachable from production code, and only the test module still names it.

### Why CI did not catch it

`ci.yml` triggers on `pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch` only — a push to `main` runs no build or test workflow at all (that is by design; CONTRIBUTING says the exhaustive gate runs once at release time via `gh workflow run ci.yml --expected_sha=…`). The commit also carries `[skip ci]`, which CONTRIBUTING explicitly forbids — but on a `main` push it is not what let this through, since nothing was scheduled either way.

The net effect is a window where `main` was red for its own lint gate and nobody could see it: the mirror/harvest workflows ran, the next PR did not.

### Suggested fix

One of:

1. **Delete the now-unused variant** — `ClearCheckpoint`, its `PersistRequest` match arms, its `PendingQueue`/`pending` handling, and its tests. Cleanest if the reset path genuinely never needs it again.
2. **Keep it with a stated reason** — `#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]` on the variant plus a comment saying which future caller owns it. Cheap, but leaves a variant nobody constructs.
3. **Keep it and give it back its caller** — if clearing a stale checkpoint on a failed reset is still wanted (the removed comment argued it was: "Never let an older in-flight checkpoint resurrect the session the user just discarded"), reinstate the call instead of deleting the variant, which would also restore that behaviour.

I lean to (1) or (3) depending on which behaviour is correct; (2) only as a stop-gap to unblock the queue.

### For the process question

Two separate gaps, worth deciding on together:

- **The required checks are right, the invariant is not enforced where it broke.** `protect-main` already requires `Lint`, `Test (windows-latest)` and `npm wrapper smoke (ubuntu-latest)`, and the ruleset's `bypass_actors` is empty — yet `6a08f0312` and its four siblings landed as direct pushes with no PR and no CI. Whatever grants that (repository-admin role, or an org-level setting the ruleset does not expose) is what needs to change if direct pushes are meant to stay verified.
- **Nothing verifies `main` between releases.** With no `push` trigger, the only whole-workspace check is the manual pre-release dispatch. A cheap guard would be a `push: branches: [main]` job running just `cargo check`/`clippy` on the touched crates, or a scheduled run of the existing `Lint` job — minutes, and it would have caught this within the hour.

Cheap and durable: run the `Lint` job (or a `cargo check --workspace`) on every push to `main`, and require it alongside the PR checks. The release gate can stay as the exhaustive one.

### Environment

`main` at `6a08f0312`, macOS 26 (arm64), Rust per `rust-toolchain`. Reported while preparing #7147.

issues.body:
## Landed setting fix — 2026-10-29

Engine main/origin commit 7b54e7f5724daa88ed29b6479f8ea0b7cf353b0c fixes the concrete automatic-off bypass. Preflight/provider overflow recovery now refuses before summary/start/replacement when compaction is disabled, retains original messages and records an actionable typed refusal through the existing audit/error owners. Both overflow paths preserve the recovery failure's actual cause; cancellation takes priority after the awaited recovery. Explicit manual compaction remains available.

Local proof: initial libtest compile and137focused compaction/error/Engine checks passed. After the final model-step cancellation guard, libtest recompiled and69affected Engine/recovery/cancellation checks passed; unchanged pure-check evidence is retained. The renamed existing emergency fixture covers disabled-but-compactable and enabled-but-unnecessary history, zero model calls/attempts, unchanged messages and one typed refusal. Format, boundary, blocking budget569sites169files, dead-code164, changelog/facts and diff checks pass. No new test functions/comments. Exact receipts: artifacts/codex-0103-resume-20261029/compaction-off-landing-verification.json. Source files are released, not held for another build.

Keep this issue and public Engine7142 open. The setting bypass is established and repaired, but it does not explain every reported Windows seam or complete the remaining lifecycle/continuity acceptance. A read-only local Mac journal inspection did not reproduce the reported multi-root shape; that does not prove no context loss or disprove the reporter's sample. No real-provider, hosted CI, Windows/installed/device or release proof is claimed.

---

## Summary

A session's live `messages` window can be re-rooted partway through a conversation. When
that happens, every `journal` entry before the new root becomes unreachable to the model
while the on-disk journal keeps it in full. The window stays internally consistent — it
equals its own new branch exactly — so nothing looks truncated from the inside.

Three things are missing at the moment it happens:

* **no summary entry at the seam.** The new root is a bare `kind: "message"` with
  `parent_id: null`; the entry immediately before it is an ordinary turn on the branch
  that was just abandoned. Real compaction leaves a condensed account of what it replaced.
  This leaves a copy and a hole.
* **no marker in the interface.** No banner, no notice, no error.
* **no session-lifecycle event in** `audit.log`**.** In 8,792 events across five event types,
  every one is `tool.approval.*` or `tool.gate.decision`. Nothing announces that the model's
  working context was replaced.

`settings.toml` has `auto_compact = false` and `auto_compact_threshold_percent = 80.0`
throughout. If this is compaction, the setting is not describing what the runtime does.

## Environment

* `codewhale --version`: **0.10.2 (ff466b2ed0bf)** — verified against the binary
* OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200), PowerShell 5.1
* Model: `deepseek-v4-pro` (provider `deepseek`)
* Install: npm global; `~/.codewhale/{config,settings,permissions}.toml`, no `[compaction]`
  block and no `retained_user_message_tokens` in `config.toml`
* Reproduces on **0.10.1 and 0.10.2**

## What it looks like

Dump of four consecutive documents from this host. `entries` = `journal.entries`;
`window` = `len(messages)`; `root` = the journal index the live branch starts at.

```
created (UTC)        window  entries  root   coverage
2026-10-28T13:08:15     944      986     1      99.9%   <- intact (benign doubled opening)
2026-10-28T15:24:44     632     1639   987      39.8%   <- re-rooted
2026-10-29T07:11:22     403      473    50      89.4%   <- re-rooted
2026-10-29T08:20:46      61      325   259      20.3%   <- re-rooted (this one, mid-report)
```

The seam itself, from `2026-10-29T07:11:22`:

```
[48] kind=message  role=assistant  parent_id=Y     3970 chars
[49] kind=message  role=user       parent_id=Y     1362 chars
[50] kind=message  role=user       parent_id=NONE  2054 chars   <- window begins here
[51] kind=message  role=assistant  parent_id=Y      360 chars
```

Prose for scale: the `journal` for that session holds 473 entries; the model could see 403
of them. The boot turn, including the whole startup sequence, was gone from the window and
present on disk.

## Prevalence on this host, and an onset date

87 session documents were parsed structurally. `journal` + `leaf_id` on this host arrives
between 11 and 12 Aug 2026 (before that, documents carry `artifacts` and no journal, so this
signature cannot exist and cannot be tested — that period is **untestable, not clean**).

| period | sessions | shape |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 12 Aug – 17 Oct 2026 | 47 | one branch root, window == journal, 100% reachable |
| 18 Oct – 29 Oct 2026 | 40 | two or three roots; **15 re-rooted mid-session** |

The onset boundary is narrow: `…d6832ea3` (17 Oct 18:33:49Z) is clean at 113/113;
`…021a7d6a` (18 Oct 01:46:51Z) is the first re-root at 962 window / 1045 entries.

Across the 15 mid-session re-roots, the root lands at journal indices 8, 20, 30, 50, 67, 97,
160, 259, 295, 347, 367, 472, 733, 987. Post-re-root coverage ranges from **14.1%** to
89.4%; combined unreachable entries **3,909**.

**In 0 of 87 sessions is the window shorter than its own branch.** This is not truncation —
the window is always a complete branch. The branch is simply no longer the session.

## Reproduction

No special configuration; it appears on ordinary long sessions. A read-only probe against
any session document:

```python
import json, hashlib

doc = json.load(open(PATH, encoding="utf-8"))
msgs, entries = doc["messages"], doc["journal"]["entries"]

by_id = {e["id"]: i for i, e in enumerate(entries) if e.get("id")}
chain, seen, cur = [], set(), len(entries) - 1
while cur is not None and cur not in seen:
    seen.add(cur); chain.append(cur)
    cur = by_id.get(entries[cur].get("parent_id"))

root = min(chain)
print("window", len(msgs), "branch", len(chain),
      "root", root, "coverage %.1f%%" % (100 * (len(entries) - root) / len(entries)))
```

* `window == branch` and `root <= 1` → healthy (a root at 1 is the benign doubled opening;
  do not flag it — see *What I got wrong*, below).
* `root > 1` → the window re-rooted mid-session. `root` entries are unreachable.

To inspect a seam, print `entries[root-2 : root+2]` and check for anything summary-shaped.
On this host there is never one.

## How this differs from the nearby open reports

* [#6842](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6842>) (journal has no bound; compaction retires live messages but keeps superseded
  versions in RAM) names the same underlying machinery and is about **memory growth**. This
  report is about **model visibility**: the earlier turns were not merely retained
  redundantly, they became unreachable while the record survived. Different harm, possibly
  the same call site.
* #7133 (automatic compression at \~40% against an 80% setting) is the closest
  behavioural neighbour and may share a cause — it reports the *threshold* being wrong,
  where this reports a *silent re-root with no summary*. Worth triaging together.
* #7095 (history lost, labelled v0.10.3) is a different fault: there the record does not
  survive because the last save did not flush. Here every byte survives and is correct, and
  only the window is replaced.

## What I am asking for

In order of value, and each is independently useful:

1. **Emit a session-lifecycle event.** `session.opened`, `session.window.rerooted`,
   `session.compacted`, `session.resumed` — with both sizes and a reason, into `audit.log`
   beside the existing `tool.*` events. This is the smallest change and it converts an
   unexplained amnesia into a dated, attributable event. It is worth having **even if the**
   **re-root turns out to be intended**, so please do not let the other two asks gate it.
2. **Honour** `auto_compact = false`**, or rename it.** A setting that says compaction is off
   while the window is replaced is worse than no setting: it is a claim the operator can
   rely on and cannot verify.
3. **If a window re-root is intended, summarise at the seam.** A bounded, visible,
   summarised compaction is a feature. An unannounced re-root that leaves a bare copy of an
   existing message is a data-visibility defect.

## What I have not established, and will not guess at

**The trigger.** Observed re-roots span 78 to 1639 journal entries, 11 to 1437 window
messages, and roughly 1.3 MB to 5 MB of document. That spread is inconsistent with a single
simple threshold, and two documents is not a sample. It could be turn count, cumulative
tokens, document size, wall clock, or a path that only runs on resume.

**Whether it is intended.** [#5262](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/5262>) (closed, shipped v0.9.5) specifies an append-only journal
forest where branching "only moves the leaf — it never rewrites history", so multiple roots
are expected by that design and a re-root is legal in that model. What is not
design-legible is doing it silently, mid-session, with no summary, while
`auto_compact = false`.

## What I got wrong on the way here

Recorded because it is the reason this report is careful, and because a maintainer deserves
to know which tests have already failed.

My first pass used a **positional** test — does `messages[0]` start where `journal.entries[0]`
starts — and produced two confident wrong answers in one morning: first "41 of 93 sessions
lost turns", then, over-correcting, "nothing was lost at all". The positional test fires on
the benign doubled opening, which is why I checked a session minutes old and never restarted
before trusting any number here. The figures above come from a **membership** test: walk the
branch by `parent_id` and ask whether the window can reach every entry its own session wrote.

If this report is wrong, it is wrong in the direction of under-claiming: 15 measured re-roots
on one host, with the mechanism named and the unknowns listed.

---

*Reproduction and evidence kept locally. Happy to provide sanitised session documents or run*
*any probe upstream asks for.*

issues.body:
## Read-only doctor fix landed — 2026-10-29

Engine `14a5723b75` is pushed. Configured routes now short-circuit Ollama adoption before credential inspection; an unconfigured diagnostic uses the non-migrating resolver, while exec retains its normal resolver. Against explicitly built CLI binary digest `35de7b5ec4e7a3f3191fd5770384c2a09fee357aec59ab30bc8f7bb07ca40ad3`, the existing diagnostic case passed configured loopback and unconfigured legacy-key scenarios, retaining the legacy bytes and creating no primary store. Nine local Ollama cases and one route diagnostic case also passed on the frozen mixed tree. No real Ollama or release acceptance is claimed; this issue remains In Progress.

## Evidence correction — 2026-10-29

The TUI integration harness launches `target/debug/codewhale`; it does not rebuild that executable when only the Engine test target is selected. The first recorded local failing diagnostic ran an existing binary whose exact source was not established, so it is not clean-`57e957f186` executable proof. A later failing rerun also used the pre-fix CLI binary. The corrected source was built explicitly as `codewhale-cli --bin codewhale`, and the exact-binary rerun passed as recorded above. The stale-binary failures remain evidence, not verification of the proposed fix.

## Read-only doctor regression claim — 2026-10-29

Codex owns `crates/tui/src/local_ollama.rs` and its two call sites in `crates/tui/src/lib.rs` for the Ollama-adoption credential-presence check. The existing loopback `doctor_text_probe_uses_a_legacy_key_without_migrating_it` case failed against a preexisting CLI executable because the diagnostic created the primary secret store; that executable's exact source was not established. Preserve route-adoption behavior while ensuring diagnostic credential inspection does not migrate a legacy store; verify the existing diagnostic and local-adoption checks. This is separate from real Ollama acceptance.

## What a new user hits

With no cloud key and Ollama running, the TUI adopts Ollama on first launch (`Provider switched: deepseek → ollama`), but the headless and diagnostic paths still insist on DeepSeek:

```
$ codewhale exec "Reply with exactly: QA-OK"
error: DeepSeek API key not found.
...
zsh: ~/.zshrc is interactive only; use ~/.zshenv.
...
Failed to configure provider route deepseek / deepseek-flash.

$ codewhale doctor
Not ready: the deepseek route has no verified key → save one with /provider ...
```

`config.toml` written on first launch keeps `default_text_model = "deepseek-flash"`, so the adoption is re-done (and re-announced) on every TUI launch and never reaches `exec`/`doctor`.

Also: the bare line `zsh: ~/.zshrc is interactive only; use ~/.zshenv.` in the key-missing error reads like a shell error.

## Repro

Fresh `HOME`/`CODEWHALE_HOME`, Ollama with one chat model, main `715bb2ed02` release build: run `codewhale` (TUI adopts Ollama), quit, then `codewhale exec "hi"` and `codewhale doctor`.

Expected: one answer to "which model am I using" across TUI, exec and doctor — either persist the adoption, or have exec/doctor apply the same keyless-local rule and say so.

Evidence: `CW/artifacts/qa-20261027/j-cli-1.txt`, `j-cli-2.txt`.

2026-10-28: Engine `8c4b29c2b9` changes the zsh startup hint into Codewhale prose so it is not mistaken for a shell-generated error. A source-extracted diagnostic compiled and rendered; rustfmt and diff checks passed. The existing F3 Auto-default draft in the same file was not staged. This is a wording fix only; the TUI versus exec/doctor Ollama route mismatch remains open and is under source review.

## Descriptor source landed — 2026-10-29

Engine main `47442ac820` is pushed. Existing named OpenAI-compatible provider machinery supplies the Runcrate row; pricing remains unknown, and the reporter disclosed their affiliation. Public unauthenticated model discovery returned the three documented example IDs. On frozen mixed source, 8 descriptor, 4 picker, 1 pricing and 2 feature-registry cases passed; 30 web facts tests, provider registry and docs checks passed. No metered inference was run; live provider behavior and final release acceptance remain unqualified, so this issue stays In Progress.

## Incoming descriptor slice — 2026-10-29

Codex owns the inherited Runcrate descriptor, existing descriptor/pricing checks, provider documentation and generated feature/document metadata on canonical Engine main. The public model listing was read without credentials and contains the cited bootstrap examples. The existing generic picker and pricing cases pass on the frozen shared tree; complete the feature registry entry and verify the exact source before landing. No metered model call, pricing guarantee or live-provider qualification is claimed. The original reporter disclosed working on Runcrate.

### Before you start

- [X] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

### What problem does this solve?

Runcrate ([https://www.runcrate.ai](<https://www.runcrate.ai>)) serves open models (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM-5.3, Qwen3.8 Flash, gpt-oss 120B, Kimi K2.6 and more) behind an OpenAI-compatible API at `https://api.runcrate.ai/v1`, plus an Anthropic Messages endpoint at `https://api.runcrate.ai`. Today it only works in Codewhale as a hand-configured custom endpoint.

### What should Codewhale do?

Offer Runcrate as a built-in provider next to Novita, Together and Fireworks: `RUNCRATE_API_KEY`, base URL `https://api.runcrate.ai/v1`, model list from `GET https://api.runcrate.ai/v1/models` (public, no key needed). A Runcrate entry is also pending on [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) ([anomalyco/models.dev#10667](<https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/issues/10667>)), which Codewhale already reads for model facts.

### Where?

Providers and models

### Workarounds or other tools

A custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint works today. OpenCode, Kilo and Cline pick Runcrate up from [models.dev](<http://models.dev>).

### Contribute

I'm happy to open the PR (provider kind, defaults and tests) if this fits. Disclosure: I work on Runcrate.
