## Localization activity slice landed — 2026-10-29

Engine main commit `896e781fbb` is pushed. Grouped activity, tool status and file receipts use the 15-locale catalog and the group cache tracks locale changes. On frozen `9fc5c898c7` plus the inventoried shared dirty tree, TUI lib and feature registry compiled and 197 focused existing cases passed; localization lib had 54 passes on unchanged localization inputs, and all 15 packs have 2,732 keys. The earlier broader mixed-tree run had 2,118 passes and one separate compaction failure. Rendered non-English journeys, native-speaker review, Windows, installed artifacts and final CI remain unverified; issue stays In Progress. Raw tool names in grouped summaries remain visible as names and deserve broader localization review.

## Incoming Engine takeover — 2026-10-29

Codex owns the existing localization/activity batch and the paths in the implementation claim below on canonical Engine main. The previous Claude session has stopped; its later source and verification receipts are being reviewed before landing. Latest recorded focused TUI run: 2,118 passed, one compaction failure; this is not release acceptance. The source has additional inherited provider, session, fixture and documentation changes that require separate review. No final CI, live-provider or release qualification is claimed.

## Current implementation claim — 2026-10-29

Coordinator owns the remaining ordinary-session activity and patch chrome on canonical Engine main bd7c7bba47b908df0ddff46de294bed1c6e608c2. Earlier question/approval/handoff/waiting/color, contributor /diff codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7101 and @Aboysky's merged /undo codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7121 remain landed; the undo fallback retains SyncSession. Do not reapply those contributions.

Finish the existing tool-run and file-activity counts, cached summary locale, typed file-mutation outcomes, patch/status headers and their current consumers. Reuse the existing ToolFamily MessageId mapping and locale catalog; migrate final consumers instead of adding another translation store or renderer-local language switches. Preserve raw tool output, filenames, diffs, receipt authority, timing, collapsed/expanded behavior and user text. Rebuild projection and rendered rows when the UI locale changes.

Exact paths: crates/localization/src/lib.rs and all 15 existing locale packs; TUI [history.rs](<http://history.rs>), history/tool_run.rs, history/file_mutation.rs, history/agent_activity.rs, history/checklist.rs and history/plan.rs; widgets/mod.rs, widgets/transcript_legacy.rs and widgets/tool_card.rs; [app.rs](<http://app.rs>); work_surface/model.rs, work_surface/views.rs, shell_job_routing.rs (explicit English diagnostic-format compatibility), tool_routing.rs, ui/activity_detail.rs and directly affected existing history/ui/render tests; key_shortcuts.rs only if the existing mutation detail hint requires the same locale plumbing; both changelog copies and documentation copy in docs/design/TUI_DECONSTRUCTION.md. No new test functions or code comments. One frozen native batch/build owner after edits, focused existing checks only.

Current preceding source proof: bundled controls and MCP status are complete with scoped receipts under artifacts/codex-0103-resume-20261029. No native build or source lease from those packets remains. No real provider/device, native-speaker review, full/hosted CI or release acceptance is established.

## Original report — observed on 0.10.2

**Version:** 0.10.2 (`ff466b2ed0bf`, npm build), Linux, `locale = "zh-Hans"` in `settings.toml`.
**Target:** 0.10.3

With the UI in Simplified Chinese, the main flow is translated: the composer placeholder 输入消息…, approval options 仅允许本次 / 不允许, the pet status 思考 / 回复 / 完成, the plan-handoff question 你想如何继续？, and the footer. But several messages you see in an ordinary session stay in English. None of these strings are in `crates/localization/locales/*.json`; they're hardcoded at the call site:

| What you see | Source |
| -- | -- |
| `/undo` note: `Undid your request "…". 1 file is back as it was before it: … The request and its reply were removed from the conversation.` | `crates/commands/src/debug/undo.rs:323` (`format!("Undid {request}. {count} before it:…")`) |
| `/diff` pager title `Changes since session start` | `crates/commands/src/debug/undo.rs:174` |
| `/color` note `Composer color for this chat: red` / `…reset to the theme default` | `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/session/color.rs:73-74` |
| Tool card status `… · waiting for approval` | `crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:1411` |
| Plan handoff / question chrome: `Action required`, `Question 1 of 1`, `Other`, `Type a custom response`, `1-4 quick pick ↑/↓ move Enter confirm ←/h back Esc cancel` | `crates/tui/src/tui/user_input.rs` (e.g. `:459`) |
| Approval card `Save:   always ask first` | `crates/tui/src/tui/widgets/mod.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tui/approval/ask_rules.rs` |
| Grouped activity `Explored 3 files: explore +3 ›`, `patch done · Updated tides.py · +1 -1` | `crates/tui/src/tui/history/tool_run.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tui/widgets/mod.rs` |

## Repro

1. Put `locale = "zh-Hans"` in `$CODEWHALE_HOME/settings.toml`, or choose 简体中文 in `/settings`.
2. In a Git repo, ask for a fix that runs a shell command and edits a file, approve the card, then run `/diff`, `/undo` and `/color`.

## Expected

These go through `tr(locale, MessageId::…)` like their neighbours, and appear in `en.json` and every locale pack. `scripts/check-tui-locale-parity.py` only checks keys that exist, so it can't catch strings that never became keys.

## Notes

* The CHANGELOG for 0.10.2 also says the pet's activity words and the update note follow the UI language, and both do. These strings are the visible gap next to them.
* Fix direction: move each string to a `MessageId`, add the en/zh-Hans/zh-Hant/ja values (the other locales can fall back), and consider a small lint that flags new user-facing `format!`/string literals in `crates/tui/src/tui/` and `crates/commands/src/` outside the localization crate.

Found while recording a Chinese-language 0.10.2 demo.

It records fixed configured/connecting/failed/authorization_required/unknown/connected states from the pool, current catalog generation, reviewed authority and captured turn ceiling. Relevant failures/authentication needs precede the24-name limit; names are bounded/inert and raw errors, commands, URLs and credentials are excluded. Without tool_search, only servers resolved from actual visible tools are named.

Each snapshot supersedes earlier observations. Verified recovery replaces failure; stale generations do not claim readiness. Contention, changed configuration sources, removed scope and restore withdraw earlier status and guidance. Child/RLM/ACP/isolated discovery ceilings remain intact. Connected is an observation, not a guarantee of schemas, tool permission or successful execution; the existing manager owns recovery and authorization.

The two prior Engine capture paths are replaced by one capture; existing event kinds, session history, deduplication and cached-prefix semantics remain. No extra prompt, store, boot-failure/recovery event authority or server-error classifier was added. English/Chinese MCP guidance, feature metadata and changelogs match the source.

No new test functions. Receipts: artifacts/codex-0103-resume-20261029/mcp-landing-verification.json and mcp-source-freeze.json.

The existing oversized eh_frame test-link warning remains. No full-suite/hosted CI, provider/auth action, installed/device or release qualification is claimed. The contributor report informed this independently implemented extension of the existing owner; the fork patch was not harvested.

## Original design discussion — historical source details

**Title:** `Brief the model when MCP boot servers fail — and when they recover (design discussion)`

**Body:**

## Problem

When MCP servers fail during session boot, the model gets no signal. Its tools simply don't appear: it names a tool it was told exists, gets `unknown tool`, and cannot distinguish "server failed to connect this session" (retryable, maybe transient) from "never configured" (permanent). Recovery is equally invisible — a server that reconnects mid-session makes its tools reappear without the model learning it can retry the earlier failure.

Upstream already carries the host-facing half: `Event::McpSessionBoot` receipts reach the UI (`engine.rs` ~:7103) and reconnect reporting exists for users. But nothing reaches the *model*, and the model is the party that has to adapt its next tool call.

## Proposal

Model-facing runtime-handoff briefings for boot failure and recovery, rendered as internal briefings on the session timeline:

- New runtime-handoff event kinds (e.g. `mcp_boot_failed` / `mcp_boot_recovered`) carried through the existing handoff machinery, so SyncSession reconciliation re-briefs consistently on session reload.
- The failure briefing distinguishes *failed* from *not configured* and names the affected server(s) with the connect error.
- The recovery briefing names the server and tells the model previously-missing tools are callable again (with the deferred-tool activation path, since the tools won't be in the first-round catalog).
- Hardening that has to ride along, because server-reported strings would now reach the model: control-character flattening on briefing reasons, and no echoing of raw server-authored envelope fields (anti-injection surface).

Scale: the fork-side implementation is ~400 lines including tests (`crates/tui/src/runtime_handoff.rs` briefing constants + engine bookkeeping + reconcile + tests).

## Why an issue first

This is model-facing prompt content — the contribution guide's trust-boundary surface — so I'm looking for a design sign-off (and any naming/placement preferences) before opening a PR. The reference implementation exists and is tested on the fork side: Pinvou/CodeWhale `6f780290f` (with the hardening above); happy to re-derive it onto current main's handoff architecture whatever way reviewers prefer.

## Coordination

Checked against current main: no `mcp_boot_failed`/`mcp_boot_recovered` kinds exist in the runtime-handoff kind list yet, and lazy boot (#6033) plus connection supervision (#6187) changed the failure semantics since the fork implementation — the recovery briefing in particular needs to key off the supervisor's reconnect results rather than boot-time state.

issues.body:
## Current remaining work — verified 2026-10-29

This issue remains open for **usage replay identifiers and retained journal archive growth**. The original0.10.1-dev report below is historical; its claims that no pruning exists and resume always reads twice no longer describe canonical Engine main2231d73df5d6d4538653a54920695a389d575451.

Already implemented:
* Off-branch journal entries are durably archived before pruning, normally at4096dead/1024retained; oversized documents archive all off-branch entries. Failed archive writes prune nothing. Active branches and recoverable ancestor chains remain intact, and live memory consumes the archived-ID result.
* Ended, non-durable, unpinned Work Graph operations are pruned to256 by the live registration path, as well as by oversized-session projection. This is not merely a serialization bound.
* Session entry bodies are shared through Arc, so the UI snapshot no longer deep-copies every body. Snapshot assembly still occurs on the UI task; no new latency/RSS benchmark is claimed here.
* Metadata reads grow geometrically from64KiB to16MiB before a full-file fallback. Fingerprints no longer force a whole transcript read as soon as metadata exceeds64KiB.
* Normal attach/resume parses the saved document once. A newer crash checkpoint still requires reading and validating the document before replacement, preserving the unreadable-document guard. Stale checkpoint cleanup happens after successful attach.

Carrying commits verified as ancestors of current main: d9ccf8f3e4017aba8e9595a706b50961b78277bb; e20aaedf199afd0b8166cd09c2d2825c5eeb62f4; 1e66ad3837c81afe879c3d69c7a966d331c7c8ec. Current owners are runtime/session_tree.rs, TUI session_manager.rs, work_graph/runtime.rs/reducer.rs, tui/ui/frame.rs and persistence_actor.rs.

Remaining acceptance, in order:
1. Bound the in-memory/persisted usage replay index through the existing late-usage authority while preserving exact spend deduplication after restart and late delivery. Do not truncate the current unordered fingerprint set: forgetting a still-replayable identifier can double-count money. Read/migrate every producer and restore consumer together.
2. Define and implement the retained journal archive's storage/retention behavior through the existing archive owner. Preserve branch restoration and receipts; no silent deletion of historical branches or user files. A memory bound is not a disk-retention policy.
3. Reuse/extend existing archive-failure, failed-document-write, archived-branch restore, large-metadata and late-usage dedupe checks. Measure long-session save/attach cost on current source before making performance claims; the reporter's six-day Linux RSS record is historical evidence, not a new qualification result.

The read-only source audit is recorded under artifacts/codex-0103-resume-20261029. No source, live session or billing state was changed for this reconciliation. The separate lock-contention issue remains separate. This is unreleased source status, not a shipped0.10.3 claim.

## Original report —0.10.1-dev historical measurements

# Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

Searched open and closed for: session journal grows, compaction memory,
memory grows in session, rebranch, metadata too large. Closest matches, and why
each is a different store or mechanism:

- **#4217** (`subagents.v1.json` grows unbounded) — same class of defect, but the
  sub-agent ledger rather than the session journal.
- **#5262** (session tree design) — introduced the append-only entry journal; that
  is the design issue, not a report that the journal is unbounded.
- **#5472** (TUI memory retention of Bash stdout/stderr) — shell-output
  retainers, a different structure with a different growth mechanism.

# What happened?

A long session grows without bound, and RSS grows with it. On one 6-day session:

- process: **872 MB RSS**, reaching **1694 MB** high-water since start
- session file: **98.7 MB**, of which **99.6% is dead weight**

(MB = 10⁶ bytes throughout; `kB` in the log excerpts below is KiB from
`/proc`.)

The active branch holds **181 entries**. The rest of the file is history that
nothing reads. A high dead share is expected of an append-only journal; the
problem is the absolute size, which keeps growing.

The transcript is the main grower. `SessionJournal.entries` is a plain `Vec`
(`crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs:131`) with **no trimming path at all** —
`grep -n "trim_front\|clear\|retain"` over that file returns zero matches for
`entries`; the only mutation is `self.entries.push(entry)` at `:168`.

Every compaction rewrites the active tail via `rebranch_active_messages_stamped`
(`crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs:343`), and the superseded versions stay
behind forever. Four samples of that session:

| sample | `entries` | active branch | dead share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 15:43 | 45 793 | 4 072 | 91.1% |
| 00:15 | 48 653 | 2 861 | 94.1% |
| 01:00 | 49 232 | 155 | 99.7% |
| 01:42 | **49 258** | **181** | **99.6%** |

Across the 9 h 59 m the samples span, the live branch shrank **22×**
(4 072 → 181, not monotonically — it rose from 155 to 181 in the last interval)
while the journal grew by 3 465 entries. Compaction is doing its job; it just
trades live history for retained history rather than releasing it.

## The same pattern in `WorkGraphSnapshot.nodes`

`crates/tui/src/work_graph/model.rs:889` — also a plain `Vec`. The neighbouring
fields are bounded: `history` is a `BoundedVec<_, HISTORY_CAP>` with cap 256
(`:891`, constant at `:34`) and `seen_keys` is capped at 1024 (`:897`).

That session's graph had **16 838** nodes at the first sample and **18 004** by
the last, **16 696** of them `operation` rows — one per shell call — each keeping the full command text in `title` and the output
reference in `binding.last_observation`. Removal happens only through
`proposal.removed_nodes` (`crates/tui/src/work_graph/reducer.rs:420`); there is no
age- or count-based eviction.

## The 64 KB metadata fast path is defeated

`load_session_metadata` (`crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs:3175`) deliberately
reads only a 64 KB prefix, carrying the comment *"One bounded metadata-prefix
read, not a transcript scan"* (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/frame.rs:1172-1175`).

But `usage_source_fingerprints` lives inside `SessionMetadata.cost`
(`crates/tui/src/cost_status.rs:86`) and has no bound of its own. Each entry is a
64-character hex string plus JSON quoting, so 8 919 of them add roughly
0.59 MB to `metadata` — already past the 64 KB prefix, which is truncated
mid-object. `extract_top_level_metadata` then cannot find the object's end, and
the fallback at `session_manager.rs:3193-3195` reads the remainder of the file
and re-concatenates it. The 64 KB read becomes pure overhead on top of a full
~98.7 MB read.

This fires on two paths: `merge_persisted_lifecycle`
(`frame.rs:1176` → `session_manager.rs:3124`), and `list_session_records`
(`session_manager.rs:3062`), which calls it for every `.json` in `sessions/`
on each save.

## Each snapshot costs ~659 ms on the UI task

`build_session_snapshot` (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:82` →
`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/frame.rs:1129`) deep-clones the whole journal at
`frame.rs:1147` (`app.session_journal.clone()`).

The comment at `crates/tui/src/tui/persistence_actor.rs:1-13` records that disk
I/O was moved off the event loop, but the snapshot construction was not — and the
comment at `event_loop.rs:3256` ("Offloaded to the persistence actor so the UI
stays responsive") sits above a block that still builds it inline.

Reproduced per operation against the same data:

| operation | size | cost |
|---|---|---:|
| journal deep clone | 48 964 entries (benchmark snapshot) | ~484 ms |
| graph deep clone | 18 004 nodes (last sample) | ~166 ms |
| `root_to_leaf` | HashMap over all entries | ~9 ms |

Each figure is a standalone replay of that one operation against the same
on-disk session, not an in-process measurement of the code path.

≈ **659 ms** in total. It runs on every `EngineEvent::SessionUpdated`, i.e. on every message added to
the session — once per assistant response and once per tool result.

## `resume` reads the whole session file, twice

`crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs:2829-2830` reads the session file in full with
`fs::read_to_string` + `serde_json::from_str`, with no size limit and no prefix
fast path — unlike `load_session_metadata`. `resume` reaches it through
`attach_session` (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:917`), and
`promote_interrupted_checkpoint` (`session_manager.rs:2929`) calls it a second
time via `load_session`, which is the same `recover_session_for_resume`
(`:3003-3005`). A resumed 100 MB session therefore reads the file at least twice
before the first frame.

# Steps to reproduce

1. Start a session in a project and work for several hours (the measured run was
   ~6 days with regular tool use and several compactions). Reopening it later
   with `codewhale resume` takes noticeably longer as the journal grows.
2. Watch the file and the process:
   ```
   watch -n 60 'ls -l ~/.codewhale/sessions/<id>.json; ps -o rss= -p $(pgrep -n codewhale)'
   ```
3. Compare the journal's active branch against its total entries:
   ```python
   import json, os
   d = json.load(open(os.path.expanduser("~/.codewhale/sessions/<id>.json")))
   e = d["journal"]["entries"]; by_id = {x["id"]: x for x in e}
   on, cur = set(), d["journal"]["leaf_id"]
   while cur in by_id: on.add(cur); cur = by_id[cur].get("parent_id")
   print(len(e), len(on), f"{(len(e)-len(on))/len(e):.1%} dead")
   ```
4. Observed end state matches the figures quoted above and the log section
   below.

To see the metadata-prefix effect (finding 3) rather than just the file size,
check where the `metadata` object ends in the serialized document:

```python
import json, os
raw = open(os.path.expanduser("~/.codewhale/sessions/<id>.json"), "rb").read(2_000_000)
end = raw.find(b'"messages"')
print("metadata block ends at byte", end,
      "-> prefix path works" if end <= 64*1024 else "-> falls back to full read")
```

At 8 919 fingerprints this prints an offset above 65 536, which is what forces
`load_session_metadata` off its fast path. To see the UI cost (finding 4), run a
turn that uses several tools and watch for input latency while a session with a
large journal is open.

# Codewhale version 版本

`0.10.1 (dev)`, source build from git.

# Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface)

# Operating system 操作系统

Linux

# How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

Built from a git checkout

# Provider and model 提供商和模型

Not observed to be provider-specific.

# Terminal and shell 终端

any

# codewhale doctor (optional)

Not captured.

# Logs

```
on active branch : 181 entries
journal entries  : 49 258
dead share       : 99.6%
session file     : 98.7 MB
process RSS      : 872 MB
VmHWM            : 1694 MB (peak since process start)
```

`VmHWM` is the peak since launch and never decreases; RSS returns to its
baseline between writes, so the current figure is well below it.

RSS tracks checkpoint writes rather than idle time. Selected rows from a 3 s
sampling of `/proc/<pid>/status`, aligned with the checkpoint's mtime
(`kB` = KiB):

```
23:59:56  rss= 887104 kB   mtime=23:59:13
23:59:59  rss= 981216 kB   mtime=23:59:57   <- +94 MB at the checkpoint write
00:00:05  rss= 882012 kB   mtime=23:59:57   <- back to baseline
00:00:44  rss= 981736 kB   mtime=00:00:42   <- +99.7 MB, repeats, ~45 s apart
```

The amplitude matches the per-snapshot cost above: the transient copies exist only
while the write is in flight.

A quieter leak appears in the same logs: `work-graph registration skipped;
running without a bound operation` occurs **1 351 times** over ~25 h, always with
`error=To-do state is busy` — `retry_lock`
(`crates/tui/src/work_graph/runtime.rs:1462-1473`, loop at `:1466`,
`yield_now` at `:1470`), called with `retries = 100` from
`runtime.rs:134`, doing 100 `std::thread::yield_now()` per attempt and then
failing, so `ShellSpawnIntentGuard`
(`crates/tui/src/tools/shell.rs:1191`) discards the registration. Reported
separately in #6435 (open).



# References

- #6435 — the `retry_lock` / To-do lock contention visible in the same logs
- #5262 — introduced the append-only entry journal reported on above
- #6193 — no runtime performance gate exists

issues.body:
## Implemented on main — 2026-10-29

Canonical Engine main/origin now contains 2231d73df5d6d4538653a54920695a389d575451. This is unreleased candidate source; the issue's requested implementation is complete.

* `[skills.bundled]` supports `auto`, `all`, `none`, `selected`, `disabled` and `explicit_only`, with independent profile merges and explicit empty-list clears. Canonical aliases share policy. Disabling a recognized bundled copy happens before first-wins resolution so a compatible user copy can win.
* Writes use the owned global root, including explicit `CODEWHALE_HOME`, independently of discovery overrides. `none` leaves bundle files and marker untouched; `all` restores enabled missing copies while preserving edited and managed bodies. Bundle settings never delete skill files. Legacy v4 retirement deletion is removed, and nonregular markers are refused without deleting their contents.
* One scoped skills configuration and one registry/renderer now serve parents, children, tools, App, runtime API and native MCP resources. Existing invocation and activation-state owners remain authoritative; no parallel store was introduced.
* Doctor JSON/text and `/skills inspect` report mode, marker, installed/missing/disabled/explicit-only/shadowed state, unknown and ignored entries, and per-path reasons. Configured-name control characters are escaped. English, Simplified Chinese and abbreviated Indonesian guidance plus current feature metadata were updated.

Local verification: 182 distinct skills cases resolved through scoped reruns, runtime config 2 and command-contract 11 passed; all 466 distinct affected host cases are resolved (464 initially passed, two fixture failures corrected, final affected manager/inspect/registry 10 passed). Production-feature CLI build and current TUI lib/registry compilation passed. Real debug macOS doctor JSON/text ran in a hermetic sandbox with network and personal-home access denied: none mode, generation 17, explicit-only PDF, compatible debug fallback, unknown/ignored names and unchanged bundle/marker bytes were observed. Website metadata 30, docs, formatting, boundaries and local ratchets passed. No new test functions.

The existing oversized test-link unwind warning remains. No full or hosted CI, real provider, installed/device, Windows or release qualification was performed. Other 0.10.3 implementation and full decomposition remain open.

## Original report and design — historical 0.10.2 source

The source locations below describe the original report. Current skill implementation lives in `crates/skills`; runtime configuration lives in `crates/runtime/src/config.rs`.

- [X] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

*Searched open and closed issues for "bundled skills", "skills_dir", "system skills", "disable bundled", "per-skill", and "explicit-only"; related work is listed under References. I did not find a per-skill install/disable policy.*

## What problem does this solve?

Codewhale ships a starter pack of bundled skills and installs it into `~/.codewhale/skills` on first launch and on generation upgrades. The pack is effectively all-or-nothing, and the only supported-looking way to stop installation is an undocumented side effect of `skills_dir`:

1. **Install is coupled to discovery.** `Config::bundled_skills_install_dir()` returns `None` whenever top-level `skills_dir` is set (`crates/tui/src/config.rs:7155-7158`). The installer is then never called (`crates/tui/src/lib.rs:13656`, `crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:1735`). Setting `skills_dir` to the default path works as an off switch, but that is not documented; setting it to another path also changes discovery precedence.
2. **There is no per-skill control.** `SkillsConfig` has only `registry_url`, `max_install_size_bytes`, `scan_codewhale_only`, and `flat_workspace_root` (`crates/tui/src/config.rs:2993-3011`). To stop one bundled skill, a user must delete or move its directory. That is not discoverable, and the generation marker makes the result fragile: a missing `.system-installed-version` treats a missing directory as a fresh install (`crates/tui/src/skills/system.rs:581-591`). Deleting the marker while `skills_dir` is set changes nothing, because the installer never runs — a surprising interaction I hit while testing.
3. **A bundled name shadows a user's own skill.** The owned global root is discovered before `~/.agents/skills` (`crates/tui/src/skills/roots.rs:133-235`), so a bundled `debug` or `security-review` wins over a same-named skill in `~/.agents/skills`. Today the workarounds are to delete or move the bundled directory, create a project-level copy, or point `skills_dir` at a higher-precedence copy. None of these is a declarative per-name policy.
4. **Prompt visibility is per-file, not configurable.** The system prompt carries a bounded index of model-invocable skills (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:1968-1975`, budget at `:53-89`); bodies load only through `load_skill` (`crates/tui/src/tools/skill.rs:120`, `:193-197`). `explicit-only` skills cost zero prompt space, but a user cannot mark a bundled skill explicit-only in place without editing its `SKILL.md`; the edited body is then treated as user-owned and stops updating. On 0.10.2-dev, 43 model-invocable bundled skills in the current 47-skill pack contribute \~9.4k characters / \~2.4k tokens of index at full descriptions, while `batch`, `dependency-update`, `help`, and `release` are explicit-only and cost zero. That is small compared with a large `.agents` pack, but it is exactly the kind of cost a user should be able to trim declaratively.

## What should Codewhale do?

Add a declarative policy for bundled skills, separate from discovery:

```toml
[skills.bundled]
# auto (default): current behavior — install/update existing copies when
#                  skills_dir is unset; a missing directory stays gone
# all: config-authoritative — install/update every enabled name, including
#      missing ones, into the owned global root
# none: never copy or update bundled skills
install = "auto"          # "auto" | "all" | "none"

# Empty = all bundled names. Non-empty = allowlist for install and discovery.
selected = []

# Never install or discover these bundled names. Wins over `selected`.
disabled = []

# Keep these bundled names loadable through `/skill <name>`, but omit them
# from the ambient prompt index.
explicit_only = []
```

Semantics:

* `install` controls writes only; it never deletes existing files.
* `selected` (when non-empty) limits bundled names for both install and discovery.
* `disabled` wins over `selected` and `explicit_only`; the bundled copy is ignored, so a lower-precedence root such as `~/.agents/skills` can supply the same name.
* `explicit_only` applies to enabled bundled names. The skill stays available through `/skill <name>`; `load_skill` already refuses explicit-only skills for model invocation (`crates/tui/src/tools/skill.rs:193-197`).
* Aliases follow their canonical skill: disabling `docx` also disables `documents`, and selecting `docx` keeps `documents` available. List canonical names in the config; alias names are accepted and mapped to the canonical skill.
* Names in all three lists are validated against `BUNDLED_SKILLS`; unknown names must produce a `doctor` warning, not silently do nothing. Entries in `explicit_only` that are not enabled by `selected`/`disabled` are reported as ignored.
* Defaults preserve current behavior. `skills_dir` remains a discovery override; in `auto` mode it keeps its current implicit install-off behavior, and `install = "all"` is the explicit override. With `install = "none"` (or `auto` plus `skills_dir`), the generation marker is irrelevant because the installer never runs.
* Config never deletes files. A disabled bundled skill remains on disk until the user removes it.
* Disabled names are reported as disabled, not as unrecognized or missing.
* The existing user-edited-body guard remains: `all` does not overwrite a modified `SKILL.md`.
* The policy applies to the bundled copy only; manually installed skills and compatible-root copies with the same name are not disabled implicitly.

### Installation and re-enabling

* `auto` (default): install/update existing copies; an enabled name whose directory is missing stays gone. This preserves today's deletion-as-opt-out heuristic.
* `all`: config is authoritative; install/update every enabled name, including missing ones, even if `.system-installed-version` is current. To keep a skill gone, list it in `disabled`; deleting its directory is not an opt-out in this mode.
* `none`: no files are written; `selected`/`disabled` only filter discovery.
* `selected`/`disabled` always filter which bundled names participate. In `auto`, they do not force a missing name back; in `all`, an enabled missing name is installed.
* `install = "none"` leaves the marker untouched; switching back to `auto` resumes the marker heuristic, while `all` forces enabled names.

Diagnostics:

* `codewhale doctor` should print a bundled-skills line: install mode, marker generation, installed count, selected-but-not-installed names, disabled count, explicit-only count, shadowed names, and unknown/ignored names from the lists.
* `/skills` or `/skills inspect` should show the same status with paths and a reason per skill (`installed`, `disabled by config`, `explicit-only by config`, `shadowed by <path>`).
* `codewhale skills bundled status` is optional; config is the source of truth.

Implementation sketch:

* Add a `bundled` sub-struct to `SkillsConfig`.
* Gate `bundled_skills_install_dir()` and `install_one()` on `install`, `selected`, and `disabled`.
* During discovery, filter bundled names through `disabled`/`selected` before the first-wins merge; apply `explicit_only` to the bundled copy only, before prompt rendering.
* Reuse `SkillInvocation::ExplicitOnly` for presentation.
* Tests: `install_none_writes_nothing`, `install_none_leaves_marker_and_files_untouched`, `selected_installs_only_selected`, `disabled_bundled_copy_reveals_agents_copy`, `install_all_reinstalls_enabled_missing_skill`, `auto_keeps_deleted_bundled_skill_gone`, `disabled_bundled_skill_is_not_reinstalled`, `explicit_only_bundled_skill_is_not_in_index_but_user_invocable`, `disabling_a_canonical_alias_hides_both`, `unknown_bundled_names_are_reported_not_silent`, `doctor_reports_bundled_policy`, `defaults_preserve_current_behavior`.

### Options considered

**A. Minimal install-only switch.** Add `[skills] install_bundled = false` and `bundled_exclude = [...]`. Low effort; solves copy/update but not shadowing or prompt visibility for existing files.

**B. Separate install, discovery, and presentation (preferred).** The `[skills.bundled]` table above. Medium effort; one coherent policy, no file deletion, covers all three problems.

**C. B plus CLI/UI management.** Add `codewhale skills bundled disable/enable/status` and `/skills` toggles backed by config. Higher effort; useful for discoverability, but B is enough for a first slice.

### Use cases

* "Only `fleet-manager`, `github`, `goals`, `pdf`; do not install the rest." → `selected = [...]`, `install = "none"` or `"all"`.
* "Use my `~/.agents/skills/debug`, keep the bundled copy on disk." → `disabled = ["debug"]`.
* "Keep `handoff` installed but out of the ambient prompt." → `explicit_only = ["handoff"]`.
* "Stop all bundled installs, keep discovering what I already have." → `install = "none"`.
* "Fresh start without changing discovery of my own skills." → `install = "none"` plus `disabled = [...]` for existing bundled names.

### Impact

* No behavior change with defaults.
* Users can stop installation without a fake `skills_dir`.
* Users can choose their own version of a skill without deleting bundled files.
* Prompt budget can be trimmed without editing files.
* `doctor` and `/skills` become truthful about what is installed, disabled, shadowed, and visible.

### Open questions

* Should `disabled` reveal the next root with the same name, or hide the name entirely? Proposal: reveal the next root (the common "use my `.agents` version" case).
* Should `selected` filter discovery as well as install, or install only? Proposal: both, with `disabled` winning.
* Should `skills_dir` keep its implicit install-off behavior, or should `install` be the only switch? Proposal: keep it in `auto` mode for compatibility; `install = "all"` overrides.
* Should `explicit_only` apply to user copies too, or only bundled copies? Proposal: bundled only for the first slice; a general per-name presentation override can follow.
* Should `auto` reinstall an enabled-but-missing skill, or keep deletion-as-opt-out? Proposal: keep deletion-as-opt-out in `auto`; `all` is the explicit force-install mode.
* Should the hidden-from-index state remain `explicit-only` (user invocation only), or should there be a separate `ambient = false` state that keeps model `load_skill` available? Proposal: reuse `explicit-only` for the first slice; a separate state is a follow-up.
* Nested `[skills.bundled]` vs flat `[skills]` keys? Nested reads better; flat is easier to parse.

## Where?

TUI (terminal interface), CLI (`codewhale doctor`, proposed `codewhale skills bundled`), Docs.

## Workarounds or other tools (optional)

Today: set top-level `skills_dir` to the default path (disables the installer by side effect), delete or move individual directories, or edit a bundled `SKILL.md` to `explicit-only` (which stops updates). These work but conflate discovery and installation, are invisible to `doctor`, and are easy to undo by accident.

## Contributing

- [ ] I would like to open a pull request for this.

## References

* `crates/tui/src/config.rs:7155-7158` — `bundled_skills_install_dir()` returns `None` when `skills_dir` is set.
* `crates/tui/src/skills/system.rs:627` — `install_system_skills()`; `:581-591` — per-skill install decision.
* `crates/tui/src/lib.rs:13656`; `crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:1735` — installer call sites.
* `crates/tui/src/skills/roots.rs:133-235` — global owned root before global `.agents`.
* `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:53-89` — prompt budget; `:1274-1283` — configured `skills_dir` union; `:1968-1975` — index header; `:2037-2050` — full-description tier.
* `crates/tui/src/tools/skill.rs:120` — `name="list"` filters model-invocable; `:193-197` — explicit-only refusal.
* `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:2566-2581`; `docs/SKILLS.md:363-376` — current docs.
* `2c550fa8c` — commit that introduced the `skills_dir` install gate.
* [#4691](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/4691>) — original default skill-pack design; [#4698](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/4698>) — routing metadata and explicit-only follow-up; [#4876](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/4876>)/[#4891](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/4891>) — marker repair; [#4879](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/4879>) — explicit invocation and alias routing; [#6779](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6779>) — configured skills dirs and workspace trust.

issues.body:
## Resolved in source — 2026-10-29

Implemented option B (loss signals plus both configurable index limits) in commit 2d55b9745fc41d593e683f0874a1a7dc3de0aa6f: validated per-entry cap and route-window fraction, independent profile overrides, shared parent/child/context rendering, trigger-preserving shortening, load warnings, all15 localized inspect notes and current en/zh docs, with focused existing checks passing; 0.10.3 has not been released.

Local proof: skills182/runtime config2/localization54/contract11; native TUI+registry compiled;276selected TUIlib checks and2registry checks pass; generated metadata30 pass. Existing fixtures were updated, no new test functions added. Exact source/input receipts are in artifacts/codex-0103-resume-20261029/skills-controls-landing-verification.json. codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7066 bundled-selection/explicit-only policy remains a separate open issue; the optional per-skill name-only design alternative is not represented as implemented by this control.

---

- [X] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Searched open and closed issues for "skill description", "skills index", "skill catalogue", "truncat", "MAX_SKILL_DESCRIPTION_CHARS", "skills budget", "prompt budget". Related but distinct: #7066 (bundled install / per-skill disable / explicit-only policy), [#6526](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6526>) (same failure class on standing instructions: hard-coded ceilings, no knobs, invisible trim), [#4698](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/4698>) (routing metadata for the bundled pack, closed). This issue is about the ambient skills index: what the model is allowed to see, and what nobody is told when text is cut.

## What problem does this solve?

Codewhale puts a bounded index of skills into every system prompt. Each row is a name, a slice of the skill's `description`, and the `SKILL.md` path. The slice is capped by a compile-time constant; the block is capped by a share of the route window. When either limit bites, the model gets a shortened description — and the only disclosure anywhere is a per-skill note behind `/skills inspect`, a diagnostic subcommand.

**The mechanics, verified at** `f19aa7772` **(0.10.2):**

* Per-row cap: `MAX_SKILL_DESCRIPTION_CHARS = 400` — `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:52`.
* Block budget: `window_tokens × 4 chars × 5%`, floor 2 400, ceiling 40 000 chars — `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:56-68`, `:84-97`. Neither value is configurable.
* Three tiers — `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:1948-1954`:
  1. full rows, each capped at 400;
  2. proportional shortening when the total does not fit, with a 40-char floor (`:71`);
  3. names only, plus an omission line (`:2167`).
* A row is split into summary + trigger at an English marker, and the trigger is promised at least half the cap when both exist (`:1903-1946`). Only four markers are recognized: `use when:`, `use when `, `use this when `, `use this skill when `.
* Cut text ends in `…`, added by `truncate_for_prompt` (`:2177-2188`).

**What is surfaced today — and credit where it is due.** `/skills inspect` prints a per-skill note when a description exceeds the cap, added in `ba386a0cf` (2026-09-02):

```
note: description is N chars; the model index shows at most 400 — trim it,
or end it with `Use when: <trigger>` so the trigger survives shortening
```

`crates/tui/src/commands/groups/skills/skills.rs:486-501`, inside `inspect_skills` (`:445`). Reachability matters: bare `/skills` opens the Extensions UI (`:313-315`), and `/skills <prefix>` prints descriptions without this note (`:376-441`). The comment above the note states the intent exactly: "say so here instead of cutting an imported skill mid-sentence with nobody told."

That note is useful, and the authoring advice in it is correct. It is also the whole of the disclosure:

* **It is user-facing only, and behind a diagnostic subcommand.** Bare `/skills` opens Extensions; the note is in `/skills inspect`. The model's prompt does not carry the count, a footer, or a marker beyond `…`; the Usage paragraph tells the model to use `load_skill` "if the index was truncated" (`mod.rs:1971-1976`), a condition the model cannot reliably detect.
* **It fires only for the tier-1 cap** (`description > 400`). When the pack overflows the block budget, tier 2 shortens descriptions proportionally — including descriptions well under 400 — with no note anywhere, and tier 3 drops names with an in-prompt omission line only.
* **It is not a startup or discovery signal.** Nothing is written to the log, and `/context` reports the rendered block with no note that rows were shortened (`crates/tui/src/context_report.rs:595-622`). A user who never runs `/skills inspect` never sees it; a session that loads a new pack never sees it.
* **It is not a count.** With 50+ skills the note appears in a long list, per skill, with no aggregate ("23 of 47 descriptions shortened").

**Measured on a real 52-skill pack under** `~/.agents/skills` **(identifiers redacted):**

* 32 099 chars of `description` in total; 20 091 (\~63%) can reach the model.
* 47 of the 52 carry a "Not for" clause; in 23 of them the clause is absent from the rendered row. Checked by re-implementing `split_trigger` + `description_split` from the code and comparing the rendered string, not by raw offsets.
* 18 of the 52 have no recognized trigger marker, so their row is cut mid-sentence before the triggers.
* Fixed scaffolding (names + paths) is \~3 300 chars. At a 400 cap this pack renders \~23.8k chars.

The budget is not the binding constraint on large routes; the constant is. On a 1M-token route the index budget is \~36 000 chars after the fixed header/usage cost and the warning reservation; the pack's untruncated rows would need \~35.8k (the four bundled skills add \~0.75k), so the budget would force only a small trim — yet the 400 cap removes \~12.0k chars. The warning reservation is easy to miss: when discovery produced any warning, the renderer withholds up to 20% of the block budget for warnings, capped at 3 232 chars (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:2026-2032`). On a 150k route the index then gets \~26 000 chars, and the cap could rise to \~450 before tier 2 begins; on 128k the index gets \~21 600, which this pack at 400 already exceeds, so it is already in tier 2 with no note anywhere.

**Why this matters beyond one pack.** Most users install published skills rather than writing them. Sampled `description` lengths in `anthropics/skills` are 204, 277, 319, 437, 837 and 952 chars, while the Agent Skills spec allows 1024. A large share of published skills therefore arrives truncated, and the authoring fix ("keep it short, end with `Use when:`") is advice the author only meets if they happen to run `/skills inspect` on the machine where the skill is installed.

**The recovery path exists but is unbudgeted.** `load_skill name="list"` returns full descriptions (`crates/tui/src/tools/skill.rs:140-146`) — \~32k chars for this pack, i.e. a large unbudgeted read the model has no reliable reason to take.

**Prior art inside the repo.** `/skills inspect` already names the cap; [#6526](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6526>) proposes the same pattern for standing instructions — config-optional ceilings plus a bounded first-turn notice when content is trimmed. The skills index has the ceiling and the human note, but not the config, the aggregate, the log line, or the first-turn notice.

## What should Codewhale do?

Four separable pieces, smallest first.

**1. Extend the existing notice beyond** `/skills inspect`**.**

* Add one aggregate line to the block when any row is shortened at any tier: `- ... descriptions shortened for N of M skills; load_skill name="list" returns full text.` Cost \~90 chars.
* Emit a discovery-time warning when `description` exceeds the cap and no `when_to_use` is present, through the channel that already exists: the `### Skill load warnings` section (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:1976`, `:2153-2165`) and `logging::warn` — the same path that already reports shadowed skills and unknown frontmatter keys. The `/skills inspect` note and this warning should come from one computation, not two.
* Record the same fact in the context report entry for `SourceKind::SkillsBlock` (`crates/tui/src/context_report.rs:613-622`), so `/context` shows a degradation, not only a size.

**2. Tell the model that something was lost — open question below.**

A footer is the cheapest honest signal. A per-row marker costs chars on every row, and `…` is ambiguous because authors use it. Keep `…` as the visual cue; make the count explicit once per block.

**3. Make the limits configurable, mirroring the ecosystem.**

* `[skills] listing_max_description_chars` — per-entry cap. Default today is 400; the spec allows 1024, Claude Code defaults to 1 536 for `description + when_to_use`.
* `[skills] listing_budget_fraction` — share of the route window. Default 0.05 today; Claude Code uses 0.01.
* Precedence: explicit config > window-derived default, resolved in one place and used by both prompt build (`crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:1367`) and `/context` (`crates/tui/src/context_report.rs:595`).

**4. Add a per-skill "name-only" state.**

Today the only per-skill lever is `disable-model-invocation: true`, which removes the skill from the model catalogue entirely (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:866-877`, `docs/SKILLS.md:151-153`). A middle state would keep the name in the index and spend zero description budget — the same idea as Claude Code's `skillOverrides: "name-only"`. It is also a better fallback than the current 40-char floor: a 40-char fragment costs almost as much as a name and routes worse than no description at all. This overlaps with #7066's proposed `explicit_only` list; the two could share one policy surface.

**Sequencing options** (maintainers decide; effort/risk are estimates):

* **Option A — report only.** Footer + discovery warning + context-report note, sharing one computation with the existing `/skills inspect` note. Small diff, no config, no behaviour change. Risk: \~90 chars per request.
* **Option B — A + two config keys.** Adds docs and, if the flag is user-visible, a `docs/features.toml` row (`AGENTS.md:114-116`). Medium diff. Risk: two knobs that interact with the window-derived default; needs one resolver.
* **Option C — B + name-only state.** Larger; touches prompt rendering and the skills manager; coordinate with #7066. Risk: policy surface grows; must stay distinct from `explicit-only` (which hides the skill from the catalogue entirely).
* **Option D — raise the default cap to 1024 without knobs.** Small diff, large prompt-cost change on small windows: at a 128k window the index budget is \~21.6k after the warning reservation and this pack already exceeds it, so a higher cap deepens tier 2 instead of revealing more text.

Recommendation: A first, then B; C with #7066. Do not raise the default before the total budget is configurable.

## Where?

* TUI (terminal interface)
* Docs

## Workarounds or other tools (optional)

Today: keep `description` short by hand and end it with `Use when: …` (the advice `/skills inspect` already prints); set `disable-model-invocation: true` per skill; restrict discovery with `[skills] scan_codewhale_only = true` (`docs/CONFIGURATION.md:2582`); move skill directories out of the scanned roots. None of these makes a shortened row visible to the model or at startup, and none covers tier 2.

Claude Code, for comparison:

* Listing budget is 1% of the context window by default (`skillListingBudgetFraction`), or a fixed character count via `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET`. Ours is 5% of the window — more generous in total, not configurable.
* Per-entry text (`description` + `when_to_use`) is capped at 1 536 chars by default (`skillListingMaxDescChars`), configurable. Ours is 400, below the spec's 1024.
* On overflow Claude Code keeps every skill name and drops descriptions starting with the least-used skills. Codewhale shortens every row proportionally to a 40-char floor, so every skill degrades a little instead of a few degrading to a name.
* It warns in the debug log, reports the applied listing size in `/context`, and estimates cost per skill in `/doctor`. Codewhale reports the block size, and only a per-skill note in `/skills inspect` for the 400 cap.
* `skillOverrides` has four per-skill states written from the `/skills` menu: `on`, `name-only`, `user-invocable-only`, `off`. Codewhale has on / fully off.
* `when_to_use` is a first-class Claude Code field appended to the description and counted toward the same cap; Codewhale implements the same field (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:855`) — good — but spec-only distribution paths reject it, so it is not a portable substitute for a well-formed description.

The Agent Skills specification: `description` is required, 1–1024 characters, and must say both what the skill does and when to use it; `name` is ≤64 chars; `compatibility` ≤500; progressive disclosure is metadata (name + description) always, body on activation, `scripts/`/`references/`/`assets/` on demand.

## Open questions

1. **Should the model be told that rows were shortened?** Arguments for: the model is the only consumer of the routing surface, and today it can only suspect a cut from `…`; a footer lets it decide to call `load_skill name="list"`. Arguments against: \~90 chars on every request, and the model rarely needs the full text; a per-row marker is noisier still. Precedent: [#6526](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6526>) proposes a bounded first-turn notice for trimmed instructions, and `AGENTS.md` says "Model-visible means logged".
2. Should truncation be a session event? The rendered prompt is logged, but the decision to shorten is not.
3. Usage-based dropping vs proportional shortening: Claude Code drops descriptions of the least-used skills first. Does Codewhale have or want usage data? Is a uniform 40-char fragment the right fallback?
4. Default cap: 400 (today), 1024 (spec), or 1 536 combined (Claude Code)? What happens to prompt-cache stability when the cap depends on the route window?
5. `when_to_use` is appended unconditionally (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:855`). When the description already contains `Use when:`, this produces a second marker; `split_trigger` resolves by marker priority and then first occurrence, so the appended sentence ends up in the trigger tail and can be cut when the combined text exceeds the cap. Should the append be skipped when a marker is already present?
6. Companion files: `collect_companion_files` lists only files directly beside `SKILL.md` (`crates/tui/src/tools/skill.rs:321-346`); `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/` are never enumerated, so the spec's resource layer is invisible unless the body names the files. Intended (body must reference them) or a gap?

## References

* Agent Skills specification — [https://agentskills.io/specification](<https://agentskills.io/specification>)
* Optimizing skill descriptions — [https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/optimizing-descriptions](<https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/optimizing-descriptions>) ("the description carries the entire burden of triggering")
* Claude Code skills documentation (frontmatter reference; "Skill descriptions are cut short"; `skillOverrides`) — [https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills](<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills>)
* Claude Code settings reference (`skillListingBudgetFraction`, `skillListingMaxDescChars`) — [https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference](<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference>)
* Public skill samples — [https://github.com/anthropics/skills](<https://github.com/anthropics/skills>)
* Related issues: #7066 (bundled install / per-skill disable / explicit-only), [#6526](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6526>) (config knobs + visible notice for trimmed standing instructions), [#4698](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/4698>) (routing metadata for the bundled pack, closed)
* Code at `f19aa7772`: `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:52`, `:56-71`, `:84-97`, `:855`, `:866-877`, `:1903-1946`, `:1948-1954`, `:1971-1978`, `:2153-2170`, `:2177`; `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/skills/skills.rs:313-315`, `:376-441`, `:445`, `:486-501`; `crates/tui/src/tools/skill.rs:140-146`, `:273`, `:321-346`; `crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:1367`; `crates/tui/src/context_report.rs:595-622`; `docs/SKILLS.md:151-153`, `:264-265`; `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:2582`

## Reproduction

1. Put \~50 skills with 600–1000-char descriptions under `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, or install a published pack.
2. Start a session with `CODEWHALE_DUMP_SYSTEM_PROMPT=1` (`crates/tui/src/client/chat.rs:1949`) and read the `## Skills` block from the dump.
3. Rows end in `…`. The block carries no count; `/context` reports only the block size; the log has no line. `/skills inspect` prints a per-skill note, but only for descriptions over 400 chars and only when the user runs that subcommand.
4. Force the block over budget (e.g. a small route window) to see tier 2 shorten descriptions below 400 with no note anywhere.
5. `load_skill name="list"` returns the full descriptions, i.e. the text exists and was silently cut from the routing surface.

Environment: codewhale 0.10.2 (dev), commit `f19aa7772`, Linux; reproduced on a 1M-token route and a 150k-token route.

## Contributing

- [ ] I would like to open a pull request for this.

issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): not started. Filed against v0.9.3 (filed 2026-08-02 for the v0.9.4 milestone).
>
> **What remains**
> - Introduce one typed Responses dialect policy (as data, per the 2026-08-07 overlay) covering store/include, instructions vs system item, sampling fields, max_output_tokens, reasoning shape and replay for the three live dialects: OpenAI Codex, DeepSeek, Concentrate
> - Refactor crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs (`build_responses_body_for_provider` and the input-replay builder near :815) to read that policy instead of ProviderKind checks
> - Add JSON-in / expected-wire-out golden fixtures for request bodies and SSE (split function-call args, usage, malformed/out-of-order events) runnable offline
> - Document how to add a new profile and its fixtures
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - No `ResponsesDialectProfile` or equivalent type at the tag: `git grep -il 'ResponsesDialect\|responses_dialect' v0.10.1` matches only crates/tui/src/integrations/dsh/tests.rs
> - `build_responses_body_for_provider` still takes a ProviderKind and branches on it: crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs:45-58 (signature, `is_deepseek`, `is_concentrate`), :64, :72, :75, :109, :118, :127
> - Input replay also branches on provider identity: crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs:815, :903, :913, :930, :987
> - A third hard-coded Responses dialect (Concentrate) was added since filing, so the branch count grew: crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs:51-58
> - No language-neutral fixture harness for Responses: the tag has only Rust unit tests in crates/tui/src/client/responses/tests.rs; crates/tui/src/conformance/ holds events/golden/hooks/mcp/prompt/sse/stream_json and nothing for the Responses dialect
> - No commit in v0.9.3..v0.10.1 references #5093 (`git log --grep '#5093'` empty)

---

## Problem

The Responses bridge already covers substantial request construction, streaming, tool calls, and usage handling, but provider-specific branches are embedded in the adapter and exercised as individual cases. Adding custom Responses routes without a table-driven dialect contract would make regressions likely in tool loops, reasoning, caching, and normalized usage.

v0.9.4 needs a typed dialect-policy seam backed by deterministic conformance fixtures. Both built-in and custom Responses routes should share one normalized runtime contract while declaring their wire differences explicitly.

## Current evidence

- `crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs` owns Responses request construction, SSE event parsing, function-call assembly, and usage extraction.
- `build_responses_body_for_provider` currently receives an `ApiProvider` and contains provider-specific request branches.
- `crates/tui/src/client.rs::prepare_outbound_request` is the shared no-I/O preparation seam used by execution and request preview.
- `crates/tui/src/client/prepared.rs` provides a typed prepared-request boundary suitable for snapshot and contract tests.
- #3019 and #3084 established the reliability and provider-adapter baselines that this work should preserve.

## Scope

1. Introduce an internal typed `ResponsesDialectProfile` (name may vary) that owns declared differences in:
   - endpoint and header policy
   - stateful versus stateless turns
   - reasoning field shape
   - supported sampling and output-token fields
   - `store` and `include` behavior
   - input replay requirements
   - supported server-side capabilities
2. Refactor request preparation to consume the profile instead of scattering provider identity checks through body construction. Provider identity may select a profile; it must not implicitly grant unrelated capabilities.
3. Add a table-driven conformance harness covering at least the standard and stateless/plain-reasoning profiles.
4. Cover outbound request fixtures for:
   - instructions/system input and exact model identity
   - function tools and schema sanitation
   - parallel tool-call policy
   - function-call outputs and multi-turn replay
   - reasoning configuration and reasoning summaries
   - stateful/stateless `store` and `include` behavior
5. Cover SSE fixtures for:
   - text and reasoning deltas
   - split function-call arguments
   - completion and usage events
   - unknown, malformed, duplicated, and out-of-order events
   - UTF-8 boundaries, idle timeout, retry, and terminal errors
6. Verify normalized usage and cache accounting for input, output, reasoning, cache hits, cache misses, and cache writes. Do not fabricate cost when a route has no known SKU.
7. Add a deterministic error matrix:
   - invalid profile/configuration fails before network
   - 400/401/403 errors fail fast with sanitized diagnostics
   - 429/5xx behavior follows the declared retry policy
8. Document how to add a new typed profile and its fixtures.

Tests must use loopback or in-process fixtures only; no live provider traffic.

## Key files

- `crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client/prepared.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/models.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client/cost_status.rs`
- Existing cache-guard and provider-native-search tests where capability gating intersects the profile

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Standard and stateless/plain-reasoning profiles pass the same normalized transcript and tool-loop contract wherever the capability is supported.
- [ ] Unsupported features fail before network access with an error naming the selected profile and capability.
- [ ] Production execution and request preview use the same profile-derived prepared request.
- [ ] Function-call argument fragments assemble correctly across event boundaries and never emit a partial tool call.
- [ ] Unknown or malformed events produce deterministic, sanitized behavior without hiding terminal provider errors.
- [ ] Reasoning, token, and cache usage survive normalization without double counting.
- [ ] Cost remains unknown unless the exact route/model SKU is registered.
- [ ] Fixture snapshots contain no credentials or account identifiers.
- [ ] The full harness runs offline and documents how another profile is added.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui client::responses`
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui client::prepared`
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui cache_guard`
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- Confirm all fixtures are deterministic and require no provider credentials.

## Out of scope

- Live provider certification
- A user-programmable adapter language
- New provider authentication flows
- Default enablement of server-side tools
- Pricing additions without a verified SKU

## Related

- Parent architecture issue: #5092
- Responses reliability baseline: #3019
- Provider descriptor and adapter baseline: #3084

## Triage note

Milestone: **v0.9.4**. This is the adapter-extraction and offline proof slice for the parent architecture issue.

issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): partly done. Filed against v0.9.3 (filed 2026-08-02 for the v0.9.4 milestone).
>
> **What remains**
> - Replace the `is_deepseek` / `is_concentrate` / `OpenaiCodex` branches in crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs with one typed profile selected at route resolution (this is #5093's work)
> - Per the 2026-08-07 overlay, express the profile as a data table (JSON/TOML) rather than Rust branches
> - Add the optional `responses_profile` key for named custom providers that already accept `wire = "responses"` (left open when #5094 closed)
> - Fail unsupported profile/feature combinations before network I/O with a provider-named error
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - Child #5094 is CLOSED/COMPLETED (2026-09-02): custom providers can select the Responses wire explicitly - crates/tui/src/client.rs:2513-2525 (`provider_wire_format_for_config`, `wire = "openai" | "anthropic" | "responses"`), crates/config/src/lib.rs:1042 (aliases wire/api_style/protocol/wire_format/dialect), crates/config/src/provider.rs:89
> - No typed Responses dialect/profile exists: `git grep -il 'ResponsesDialect\|responses_dialect' v0.10.1` matches only crates/tui/src/integrations/dsh/tests.rs
> - Loose provider booleans still drive the Responses body: crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs:50 (`is_deepseek`), :58 (`is_concentrate`), :64, :75, :133, :145, :815, :930, :1051
> - Further ProviderKind::OpenaiCodex branches in the same builder: crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs:72, :109, :118, :127, :161 (`is_chatgpt`), :903, :913, :987
> - The shared prepared-request seam the issue asks to preserve is in place: crates/tui/src/client.rs:2826-2855 (WireDialect chosen before body build) and :4218-4221, :4318-4321 (dispatch on prepared.dialect)
> - No commit in v0.9.3..v0.10.1 references #5092 or #5093 (`git log --grep` empty)

---

## Problem

Codewhale can resolve `WireFormat::Responses` from a provider/model offering, but the Responses serializer still chooses important wire behavior from provider-enum branches. That makes a new Responses-compatible route more than a base-URL change: request fields, endpoint shape, reasoning representation, replay/state behavior, tool events, headers, and usage normalization can drift independently.

For v0.9.4, Responses behavior should be selected through a typed provider/dialect profile attached to the resolved route. The route resolver still chooses the provider and model; the profile only describes how that exact Responses endpoint speaks.

## Current evidence

- `crates/config/src/provider.rs::WireFormat` and `WirePolicy` already separate Chat Completions, Responses, and Anthropic Messages at the route layer.
- `crates/config/src/provider.rs::Deepseek::wire_policy` is model-aware, while `Custom::wire_policy` is fixed to Chat Completions.
- `crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs::build_responses_body_for_provider` derives an `is_deepseek` boolean and branches on request fields, reasoning, and replay behavior.
- `crates/tui/src/client.rs::prepare_outbound_request` selects Responses body construction, endpoint URL, and route shape using `ApiProvider` checks.
- `crates/tui/src/client/prepared.rs` already provides the typed prepared-request seam that production dispatch and request preview share.
- Closed #185 established that wire format comes from the exact route offering, not a model slug. Closed #3084 established the provider-descriptor/wire-adapter ownership boundary.

## Architecture contract

1. A resolved route carries both `WireFormat::Responses` and a typed Responses dialect/profile.
2. The dialect owns endpoint-path policy, supported request fields, reasoning encoding/replay, tool item/event variants, statefulness, provider-only headers, and usage/cache extraction.
3. `prepare_outbound_request` remains the single no-I/O seam used by production and `/preview-request`.
4. Provider/model selection remains in route resolution. The Responses adapter must not infer a dialect from a model slug or rewrite the selected provider.
5. Profiles are typed and allowlisted. Do not add arbitrary JSON body patches, arbitrary event remapping, or a prompt hook.
6. Existing OpenAI API, ChatGPT OAuth/Codex, DeepSeek, and model-aware gateway behavior must remain byte/fixture compatible unless a fixture demonstrates an existing bug.

## Implementation issues

- [ ] #5093 — extract the typed Responses dialect policy and prove it with an offline conformance harness.
- [ ] #5094 — let named custom providers explicitly select Responses plus an allowlisted dialect profile while preserving the Chat Completions default.

Together these two issues implement the architecture contract above; neither should add model-name or base-URL inference.

## Key files

- `crates/config/src/provider.rs`
- `crates/config/src/provider_kind.rs`
- `crates/config/src/route/resolver.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client/prepared.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs`
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No Responses request-body or endpoint decision depends on a loose `is_deepseek`/`is_codex` boolean when the same fact can come from the typed dialect profile.
- [ ] Exact route resolution selects wire format and dialect before request serialization.
- [ ] Current OpenAI API, ChatGPT OAuth/Codex, DeepSeek, and model-aware gateway fixtures still pass.
- [ ] One named custom provider can select Responses explicitly without model-name inference.
- [ ] Request preview and production dispatch produce the same normalized prepared request.
- [ ] Unsupported profile/feature combinations fail before network I/O with a provider-named corrective error.
- [ ] All verification is provider-free and uses redacted loopback fixtures; no live credential is required.

## Verification

    cargo fmt --all -- --check
    cargo test -p codewhale-config --locked
    cargo test -p codewhale-tui --bin codewhale-tui --locked client::responses
    cargo test -p codewhale-tui --bin codewhale-tui --locked prepared
    python3 scripts/check-provider-registry.py
    git diff --check

## Out of scope

- Adding or privileging a new built-in provider or model.
- A hosted API proxy or Codewhale-operated inference service.
- Arbitrary user-authored request/response transformation code.
- Pricing claims without an exact provider/model SKU source.
- Live-provider, OAuth, billing, publishing, or release actions.

## Related

- #185 — exact route offerings choose Responses versus Chat Completions; this issue begins after that selection.
- #3019 — existing Responses reliability and tool-result behavior that must not regress.
- #3084 — provider descriptors and wire-adapter ownership contract.
- #5084 — current named-custom-provider compatibility spike; it remains Chat Completions unless this work explicitly enables Responses.

_Triage note: filed for the v0.9.4 milestone on 2026-08-02 from verified current source anchors._

issues.body:
Hey! o/

Quick intro — I use Claude Code backed by DeepSeek and I've been eyeing DeepSeek-TUI for a bit. I'm on FreeBSD and I finally gave `npm install -g deepseek-tui` a shot today. Here's what I got:

```
root@worker:/home/user # npm install -g deepseek-tui
npm error deepseek-tui install failed: Unsupported platform: freebsd.
Supported platforms: 'linux', 'darwin', 'win32'.
npm error No prebuilt binary is available for this platform/architecture combo.
```

Fair enough — I knew it was a long shot :]

So here's my humble request: would you consider adding FreeBSD to the supported platforms? Two possible paths (not mutually exclusive, one can come way later than the other):

- **Ship a FreeBSD prebuilt binary on GitHub Releases** — The npm package already does the heavy lifting (downloads + installs binaries). It just needs a `freebsd` binary to pick up. This would unblock `npm install -g deepseek-tui` for us BSD folks right away.
- **`pkg install deepseek-tui`** — A proper FreeBSD port/package down the line. That's the long game, and I'm not expecting anyone to drop everything for it. But if it could land on the roadmap somewhere, that'd be amazing.

I know maintaining packages and build matrices isn't free. If you have no time for it right now, no worries — could you maybe plan it and add it to the roadmap? That way I know it's on the radar and I can keep an eye out. Totally fair if it's a "someday maybe" thing.

And hey, if you ever want someone to test the BSD side of things, I'm around and happy to help. Break my system, I don't mind :]

Cheers for the work you put into this — looking forward to trying it one way or another!

issues.body:
### Engine local-catalog slice landed — 2026-10-28

Engine main `7c49574a6b` probes unknown Ollama tag capabilities with bounded concurrency, publishes an authoritative catalog only when the probe is complete, and fences automatic adoption against superseded discovery and changed endpoints. Four focused existing checks passed on the shared frozen Engine source; the local discovery checks used synthetic loopback fixtures. Receipt: `CW/artifacts/engine-shared-check-20261028/focused-checks.log`.

Desktop installed-model discovery and a real Ollama interaction have not been requalified with the current app and Engine. The issue remains open; no live-model or release proof is claimed.

## What a new user hits

Fresh desktop app (QA bundle codewhale-app `40766826`, bundled Engine 0.10.2, isolated `HOME`/`CODEWHALE_HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), with Ollama running two tags: `qwen3:4b` (chat) and `nomic-embed-text:latest` (embedding).

1. Composer → **Choose a model** → the **Ollama** chip shows *Ready*; the Model list offers only **Default**.
2. Send "Reply with exactly: DESKTOP-QA-OK" → `Invalid request (400): "nomic-embed-text:latest" does not support chat`, card "Couldn't finish: this model can't chat. Pick another model."
3. **Choose model** again: the list still shows only `nomic-embed-text:latest`; `qwen3:4b` is not offered. The user has to know to expand **More** and type `qwen3:4b` into *Model ID* → **Use** (Return in that field does nothing).

So on the desktop, "Default" for Ollama resolves to an embedding model, and installed chat models are not listed. The TUI on main picks `qwen3:4b` from the same Ollama, using `choose_chat_tag` (`crates/tui/src/client/ollama_catalog.rs`, capability `completion`), so the desktop/app-server default path appears to bypass that rule.

Expected: the Ollama default is a chat-capable tag, and the model list shows the installed chat tags from `/api/tags`.

Not yet rechecked against current codewhale-app main + main Engine (build slots were busy); the 0.10.3 desktop bundles a newer Engine.

Evidence: `CW/artifacts/qa-20261027/jD1-desktop-default-embed-model.jpg`.

## 2026-10-28 current Engine + real local Ollama

People must be able to remove Codewhale reliably, whichever supported route installed it. This is a required 0.10.3 acceptance item requested by the founder.

Current source already contains removal instructions and a Windows NSIS uninstaller, so this ticket is about completing and proving the whole uninstall journey. It does not assume that every existing uninstall path is broken.

Source baseline: main `916d3227e8`.
- [Install guide: uninstalling](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/916d3227e8/docs/INSTALL.md#L864) currently relies on manual binary deletion/package-manager commands and separate data removal.

- [ ] Give users a discoverable, supported uninstall path for direct shell/manual installs, npm, Cargo, Homebrew, Windows PowerShell/direct installs, NSIS, WinGet and Scoop. Package-managed copies use their package manager's removal mechanism.
- [ ] Remove the installation's owned executables and aliases (`codewhale`/`codew`), bundled extension-host artifacts, launchers, shortcuts, completion files and exact product-owned PATH/shell integration. Respect custom install directories and ownership/symlink boundaries; preserve shared runtimes and unrelated files.
- [ ] Preserve user configuration, credentials, sessions and workspace content by default. Any optional data purge must clearly list its scope and require an explicit choice; normal uninstall must not search broadly and delete matching directories.

Validate retained data and unrelated sentinel files. Mark unavailable platform evidence explicitly; documentation alone does not qualify the flow.

---

# ACP regression in 0.10.1: `sandbox_mode` / `ask` from config ignored again — Paseo ACP sessions run sandboxed and approval-gated

## Summary

The ACP posture bug from #6310 (fixed in the 0.10.0 nightlies and verified in Paseo) is back in stable **0.10.1**: sessions launched via `codewhale serve --acp` ignore `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` and `ask = "never"` from `~/.codewhale/config.toml`, and run with the OS sandbox on, network off, and approval gates firing on every shell call.

## Environment

- codewhale **0.10.1** (build `fead51eeea0f`), macOS (Apple Silicon)
- Launched as an ACP provider for the Paseo app (verified: multiple `codewhale serve --acp` processes owned by Paseo)
- `~/.codewhale/config.toml`:
  ```toml
  approval_policy = "suggest"
  sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"
  ask = "never"
  ```

## Observed (live session, 2026-10-15)

- `CODEWHALE_SANDBOX=seatbelt` is set in the session environment → the OS sandbox is applied despite `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`.
- `python3 -c 'import socket; s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX); s.bind("/tmp/x.sock")'` → `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted` — the exact #6310 signature; this breaks Node test runners and Playwright webServer.
- `ps` → `operation not permitted` (can't even list processes).
- Network is blocked: `curl -sI https://example.com` returns nothing (`000`).
- Every shell call still hits the typed-ask gate and requires a manual approval in the client UI, even though `ask = "never"`. (`gh` could not even read its own config at `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` — EPERM — until the shell was escalated.)
- The policy engine itself agrees these should be skipped: `codewhale sandbox check --ask never 'ls -la /tmp'` → `{"allow": true, "requires_approval": false}`. So the disconnect is between the policy engine and the posture actually applied to live ACP sessions.

## Difference vs the original #6310 report

- Writes to `/tmp` now succeed (in 0.9.13 they were EPERM), but AF_UNIX socket creation is still blocked — the one thing Playwright/Node runners need.
- Approval prompts now reach the Paseo UI and can be approved manually (in 0.9.13 they were auto-denied). Still: `ask = "never"` should not gate at all.

## Suspected relation

#6473 (Full Access now requires per-session confirmation) combined with #6310's fix ("makes Full Access discoverable **without letting a client select it**") leaves the ACP path with no way to enter Full Access at all. `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` is effectively dead config for Paseo users, and every real workflow — network, sockets, process listing, CLI tools like `gh` — breaks. If per-session confirmation is the intended mechanism, the ACP client needs a way to request/confirm it. Until then this is a regression from the verified-working 0.10.0 nightly.

## Ask

1. Restore config-derived posture for ACP sessions when the client does not pin one, or
2. Expose a Full Access selection/confirmation path to ACP clients (Paseo), or
3. At minimum, honor `ask = "never"` so gated commands skip instead of prompting.

Happy to provide full transcripts or run a nightly/repro build. Greetings from Colombia 🇨🇴

https://github.com/yc-duan/fastctx

A significant reduction in token consumption through FastCtx, rather than through model compression or conversation summarization. The actual amount of token savings depends on how the Agent is used and the type of tasks.

Core principles:

**1. Batch reading:** Read multiple files or code ranges in a single call, reducing the number of tool invocations and repeated reads.
**2. Limit output length:** Set output budgets for file reading, searching, and command execution to avoid irrelevant content consuming context.
**3. Reduce redundant operations:** Simplify command execution through structured tools, minimizing syntax errors, failed retries, and redundant work.
**4. Optimize truncation handling:** Clearly indicate omitted content and allow on-demand log retrieval, avoiding repeated execution of already completed commands.
**5. Simplify tool descriptions:** Shorten MCP tool descriptions to reduce token consumption from the tool definition itself.
**6. Background task execution:** Run time-consuming tasks such as building and testing in the background, and retrieve results only when needed, reducing repeated polling and output.

issues.title: Deferred-toolbox eviction is economically net-negative under provider prompt caching: full-prefix re-prefill + write premiums, permanent stale recovery notes, wire-byte-blind budget

milestone.title: v0.10.3
milestone.description:
Engine 0.10.3 implementation and release qualification. Includes the planned runtime, context, review, localization, terminal and installation/uninstall work, plus the full crate decomposition: no crate above 50,000 production lines, aiming for about 10,000.

Track concrete remaining acceptance on each issue; a landed slice or local check does not mean the complete issue or release has shipped. Contributor PRs retain their authorship.
