No calendar due date is promised.

issues.body:
### What happened? 发生了什么？

The bounded deferred-tool toolbox (`ToolActivationCache`, 8 names / 16 KiB, `crates/tui/src/core/session.rs:17-19` at HEAD `008d21d69`) is **cost-blind**, and under current provider prompt-cache pricing its eviction path is economically net-negative. Concretely:

**1. Eviction invalidates the entire downstream prefix — the one toolbox operation with no offsetting benefit.**
The prefix fingerprint is `SHA256(system) + SHA256(tools wire array)` with order load-bearing (`crates/tui/src/prefix_cache.rs`), and tools sit at the front of the rendered prompt on every provider. Any admission/eviction mutates the tools array, so system + tools + the **entire conversation history** re-prefills at miss price. `docs/CACHE.md` calls this "an expected, one-request miss" (lines 39-40) — wording written when cache writes were free:

| Provider/API | Cached-input read | Write premium | Tool-change invalidation |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Chat/Responses | 0.1x | 1.25x (GPT-5.6+) | prefix from that point (tools are first) |
| Anthropic Messages | 0.1x | 1.25x (5m) / 2x (1h) | **any tool change invalidates the entire cache** (tools are block 1) |
| DeepSeek | 1/30 – 1/50 | none | prefix-based |
| Moonshot Kimi k3 | 0.1x | 1x (5m) / 2x (1h) | prefix from that point |

Break-even for evicting one ~400-token schema from a session with H tokens of history: pay ≈ 0.9–2.25 × H once, save ≈ 0.9 × 400 per later request → needs ~75 further tool-free requests at H = 30K. Real conversations run 6–40 requests. Admission at least unlocks a needed capability; **eviction only pays when the session is about to end anyway**. LRU position alone is the eviction trigger today — no hysteresis, no cost term, and two alternating overflowing searches would re-prefill the full prefix every round.

**2. The eviction→recovery cycle multiplies the loss (relevant to the in-flight reporting work).**
Reporting evictions (as the Pinvou fork's open PR #101 does) is necessary for correctness — silent eviction caused a live incident where a model fabricated tool results for tools that had vanished from its `<functions>`. But the recovery contract ("re-search to re-activate") completes a cycle whose full cost stack, for one eviction of 4 browser tools (~460 tokens of schema) in a 30K-token history with 20 requests remaining (0.1x reads, 1.25x writes):

| # | Cost item | Tok-eq |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Eviction invalidation (re-prefill + write premium) | ~34,500 |
| 2 | Eviction note in history (≈72–147 tokens/event; rides the result forever; 1 + 19×0.1x) | ~427 |
| 3 | Recovery re-search round trip | ~3,050 |
| 4 | Search-result payload becomes history | ~1,160 |
| 5 | Re-activation invalidation (tools array changes again — second re-prefill + write) | ~34,500 |
| | **Total vs never evicting** | **≈ 73,600 (~2.5× the entire history)** |

Two structural gaps in the reporting design: (a) **notes are never retracted** — ride-time netting (`render_toolbox_eviction_notes`) only trims the note at the moment it attaches to a result; once in history it is permanent, and the only "compaction" that removes it is generic conversation compaction; (b) **re-activation carries no supersession marker** — the re-admitting search result is byte-identical to a first-time hit (`tool_references` list only), so after recovery the model's history permanently contains "these tools are no longer callable" next to a tools array that has them again. (Compare: the direct-call hydration path does emit an explicit "was deferred and has now been loaded" receipt.)

**3. The headline saving is first-turn-only, and the budget does not measure wire bytes.**
The historical justification ("reduce catalog tokens 73%") measures a first-request, native-tools-only, `bytes/4`-estimated ratio — no provider, no tokenizer, no MCP, caching never modeled. Under caching, both an eager stable header and the deferred header are hit-priced after request 1; the durable steady-state saving is ~0.1x-scale. Separately, the 16 KiB toolbox budget is measured in engine-side serde bytes (`ToolActivationCache::serialized_bytes`), while the same tool serializes differently per wire family (Chat Completions wrapper ~69 B/tool, Anthropic ~40 B, Responses ~71 B) and per-provider sanitizers (Moonshot MFJS, root-level `oneOf/anyOf` flattening) change schemas further — so the budget is a proxy that matches no provider's actual token accounting.

**4. In practice the mechanism survives by accident.**
Across five real sessions on k3/DeepSeek (93–94% hit ratios with heavy `tool_search` churn vs 92.5% baseline without), activation happened at request 1 (short history) and the surface then stayed stable within turns. The measured re-prefill drivers were skill loading and engine restarts — not tool_search. The one live failure (mid-task silent eviction) is exactly the case with no offsetting saving.

### Expected 期望

Surface-change decisions — especially LRU eviction — should be cost-aware or at least cost-attributed, and the eviction-recovery loop should not leave permanent stale statements in history:

1. **Hysteresis / eviction economics**: a minimum activation lifetime, or an eviction cost term once current re-prefill size exceeds a few multiples of the evicted schema. Pure LRU position makes mid-task eviction the default worst case.
2. **Update `docs/CACHE.md`**'s "expected, one-request miss" for the write-premium era, and reconcile observed `cache_hit_tokens`/`cache_miss_tokens` against declared `change:<what>` re-pins — today telemetry and decisions never meet (`calculate_cache_savings` is `#[cfg(test)]`-only).
3. **Supersession semantics for recovery**: when a reported-evicted tool is re-activated, emit an explicit restored/re-admitted marker (hydration-receipt style) so the history's "no longer callable" note is not left as the last word; consider bounding note persistence (e.g. drop after the next successful activation of the named tools, or fold into compaction).
4. **Evaluate append-in-context injection** for dynamic tools (Moonshot's documented pattern: keep the top-level `tools` array stable, append dynamic declarations as a trailing system message inside `messages`) — zero prefix invalidation by construction, which sidesteps items 1 and 5 of the cost stack entirely.
5. **Measure the toolbox budget in wire-shaped bytes** (or tokenizer tokens) per active wire format rather than engine serde bytes.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

Economic issue rather than a crash; the observable sequence:

1. Start a conversation that activates ≥8 deferred tools (e.g. a browser task: `tool_search` for browser tools, then a second search for page-management tools).
2. Observe the second search silently evicting earlier activations from the request tools array (no model-visible signal at HEAD `008d21d69` — `delta.evicted` is consumed by `remove_evicted_cache_activations` in `execute_tool_search_inner`, `tool_catalog.rs:1546-1551`).
3. Watch `/cache stats` + provider usage: the next request reports a miss covering the full history; on Anthropic routes the write premium applies; re-searching to recover triggers a second full miss + write.
4. Cross-check the arithmetic against `calculate_turn_cost_from_usage_with_prision`-billed totals for the session.

### Codewhale version 版本

`008d21d69` (workspace 0.10.2; latest tag v0.10.1) — verified at this HEAD on 2026-10-13; the mechanism is unchanged from v0.9.12 through HEAD. Observed live via the Pinvou downstream (fork pinned at v0.9.12 + maintenance), engine-level, platform-independent.

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

Engine — affects all surfaces (TUI / CLI / Desktop / Web) and all providers with prefix caching, which in 2026 is all of them.

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。（recent 100 issues swept for tool/cache/deferred/eviction — no overlap）

issues.body:
## What a user sees

When `/rc` (or `codewhale rc`) can't start remote control, the reason appears only in a 12-second status toast. After that:

- **0.10.2 (ff466b2ed0bf):** the footer shows a bare `/rc failed`. The reason survives only under `/rc status`: `Remote control: failed before connecting · Codewhale rejected remote-control enrollment (503 Service Unavailable): RunnerEnrollmentError. · /rc to retry`.
- **main candidate 091c3e59c0:** the toast reads `This build or session does not have an enrollable identity.`, then `/rc status` says just `Remote control: off`, with no failure and no reason.

Nothing reaches `$CODEWHALE_HOME/logs/tui-*.log` in either case.

## Repro

Local stack (`npm run web:local`, fixture sign-in), then `CODEWHALE_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:18787 codewhale login --no-open` (approve in the browser), then `codewhale rc`, and wait 15 s. Evidence: `CW/artifacts/qa-20261027/webrc/rc-after-login.txt`, `rc-cand.txt`.

## Expected

The last start failure persists: `/rc status` reports it, and the footer says what to do. A refusal before connecting (unstamped build, missing journal dir, enrollment 4xx/5xx) is not "off". Write it to the TUI log as well.

Note: the candidate refusal is expected for an unstamped local build; this issue is only about the vanishing reason.

# The persistent "update available" header chip is never rendered — `app.update_available` is written and never read

**Labels:** `bug`

**Surface:** TUI (terminal interface)

**Version:** `codewhale 0.10.1 (fead51eeea0f)`

**OS:** Linux (Linux Mint 22.2, x86-64)

**Confirmed present in:** `v0.10.1` tag and `HEAD` (`687a38c6e`, 2026-10-28) — 281 commits after the tag, still unreproduced.

---

## What happened

A newer release was available and Codewhale never told me — or told me only for twelve seconds, at startup, four days before I noticed.

Running `0.10.1` with `0.10.2` published:

| Fact | Value |
| -- | -- |
| Installed | `codewhale 0.10.1 (fead51eeea0f)`, `/usr/local/bin/codewhale`, 8 Oct |
| `v0.10.2` published | 2026-10-24T17:31:14Z |
| Session started | 2026-10-25T04:27:16Z |
| Update-check cache written | 2026-10-25T04:27:11Z — **5 seconds before the session row** |
| Cache contents | `{"checked_at_unix": 1792902431, "latest_tag": "v0.10.2"}` |

So the startup check ran, reached GitHub about ten hours after the release, and correctly found `v0.10.2`. **The session that was told is the session I was using** — and I saw nothing across four days of continuous use.

Nothing suppressed it: no `CODEWHALE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK`, no `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER`, no CI variables set, no `[update]` section in `config.toml`. The default check interval is one hour, so a fresh launch re-checks.

## The defect

`app.update_available` is assigned when the startup check completes, and **nothing in the tree ever reads it**. A repo-wide grep returns exactly three hits — the field declaration, its initialisation to `None`, and the assignment:

```
crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs:1676:        pub update_available: Option<String>,
crates/tui/src/tui/app/init.rs:850:            update_available: None,
crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:2247:            app.update_available = Some(notice.chip_label());
```

There is no render site, no serialisation, no non-Rust consumer. The write is dead.

**The field's own doc comment describes the feature that is missing** (`app.rs:1672–1675`):

```rust
/// Header chip label (e.g. `↑ v0.9.5`) set once by the fire-and-forget
/// startup version check when a newer stable release exists. Drives the
/// small persistent update chip in the header so the affordance survives
/// the transient toast without nagging (FINISH-0.9.4 #14).
pub update_available: Option<String>,
```

And the assignment site repeats the claim (`event_loop.rs:2240–2242`):

```rust
// Transient toast for immediate visibility, plus a durable
// in-transcript notice so the prompt survives the toast TTL and
// stays actionable during a busy session (#3961). The persistent
// header chip keeps a quiet affordance after both (#14).
```

`#14` — the persistent chip — was implemented as a field, a label generator and a doc comment, but never wired to the header.

## Why the test suite did not catch it

There is a test for the chip, and it passes:

```rust
// crates/tui/src/tui/ui/tests.rs:18665-18667
// The persistent header chip is quiet: version only, no action verb —
// the toast and this block carry the instructions (#14).
assert_eq!(notice.chip_label(), "↑ v0.8.47");
```

It asserts the **label generator** returns the right string. It never asserts that any render path consumes it — so a fully working `chip_label()` with no consumer passes cleanly. That is the shape of the defect: the unit under test is correct, and the integration is absent.

## What this costs a user

The three intended surfaces degrade to two, and the surviving durable one is weak:

| Surface | State | Reality |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Toast | works | **12 seconds** (`VERSION_HINT_TOAST_TTL_MS = 12_000`) |
| Transcript system message | works | scrolls away during a working session |
| Persistent header chip | **absent** | written and never read |

The failure mode is worst for the exact user the feature exists for: someone in a long session. The check runs once per process at startup; a session lasting days — mine is four days old — sees the toast once, at the moment of launch, when the terminal is still drawing. After that there is no indication at all, and the version drift is silent.

## What I expected

A quiet, persistent affordance in the header reading `↑ v0.10.2` for as long as a newer release is known — as the doc comment and the `#14` reference both describe. Clicking or a keystroke would show the update command.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install any release older than the latest, e.g. `0.10.1`, with `0.10.2` available.
2. Ensure no `[update]` config and no suppression env vars.
3. Delete `~/.codewhale/update-check.json` if present, then start a new session.
4. A toast appears for 12 seconds and one transcript line is written.
5. **Look at the header.** There is no chip. It never appears, in this session or any later one, even though `app.update_available` is `Some("↑ v0.10.2")`.

## Suggested fix

Two lines and a render, in rough order:

1. **Render it.** Emit the chip wherever the header's status chips are composed, gated on `app.update_available.is_some()`. The label is already correct and quiet (version only), so no wording decision is needed.
2. **Add an integration test that fails today.** Assert that after the version check resolves with a newer tag, the composed header contains the chip text — not that `chip_label()` returns a string. A test at the render boundary is what was missing.
3. Optionally, consider whether the 12-second toast alone is adequate for sessions that outlive the check interval; the chip was the answer to that question, which is why its absence matters.

## Notes

* The install resolved to `InstallMethod::Binary` (path has no `cellar`, `node_modules` or `.cargo/bin`), so the notice would advertise `codewhale update`. On this machine the binary is `root:root` in `/usr/local/bin`, so a self-update run as a normal user cannot replace it — a separate observation, not part of this defect, but it makes the advertised command fail with a permissions error rather than prompting for elevation.
* `app.update_available` is `None` initialised and never cleared. If a future render is added, check whether it should also be cleared when a check returns "no newer release" after previously finding one — the cache stores the latest tag, so a downgrade in `latest_tag` is possible in principle.
* `chip_label()` already distinguishes a staged release (`↑ v{latest} ready`) from an unstaged one (`↑ v{latest}`), which suggests a download-and-stage flow was intended alongside the chip. Worth confirming whether that path exists before wiring the chip.
* Reported from a read-only inspection of the source at `687a38c6e` plus the on-disk state of a `0.10.1` install; no code was modified and no issue was filed.

### Investigation claim — 2026-10-28

Coordinator verified on current Engine source that the update label is assigned but no rendering path reads it. Initial read-only scope is the TUI's existing footer and pet presentation (`crates/tui/src/tui/phase_strip.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tui/pet_watch/full.rs`) and their existing rendering fixtures. A safe persistent affordance must preserve higher-priority status and remote-control signals and handle narrow/ASCII layouts. Source is frozen for a contributor build; no fix or verification is claimed yet.

prs.title: fix(tui): fork a conversation by the history it carries, not the shape it stores
prs.body:
No-Issue: found while diagnosing a user report of `/undo` refusing with "Cannot identify an exact saved-history boundary" and "full history exceeds byte transport bound"; the report is reproduced and explained in this description.

## What this fixes

Two independent reasons `/undo` (and retry, and fork-at-turn) refused to cut a
conversation that was otherwise perfectly usable. Both were reported from the
VS Code client; the TUI hits the same code.

### 1. The fork was measured by its stored shape, not by its history

A saved session repeats its own conversation while it carries a journal:
`messages` and the journal's active branch hold the same turns, so the file on
disk is up to twice the history it holds. The reader that opens such a document
already knows this — `SessionManager::load_session_snapshot_with_limit` judges
an oversized file by `SavedSession::transport_form` — but the fork writer
measured the stored shape against the same 8 MiB canonical bound.

Concretely, on a 9.75 MiB conversation whose carried form was 5.2 MiB, the
runtime kept opening it, saving it and running new turns, while `patch-undo`
answered `400 full history exceeds byte transport bound; source retained`
before it touched a file. `/undo` is a fork, so the turn stayed in the
transcript.

`saved_document_digest` already measured `transport_form()`. Both now go
through one `ensure_history_transport_fits`, so the writer's rule and the
reader's cannot drift apart again.

### 2. The saved-history boundary counted engine traffic as user prompts

The boundary walk reads a saved transcript as "the prompts a person typed", so
it can align the transcript against the turn records. Two kinds of engine
message were counted as prompts, and neither is ever recorded on a turn:

- runtime-owned control messages — the MCP-server notice, shell-completion
  handoffs, the deferred-toolbox snapshot
- the `<image path=…>` / `</image>` tags that bracket an attachment

A conversation that had received any of them could not be cut at all: `/undo`
answered `Cannot identify an exact saved-history boundary`. Both are now
skipped. The runtime-owned check is the same recognition the session views
already use (`turn_classify::is_runtime_owned_user_message`) and keys off the
runtime provenance line in the `<turn_meta>` envelope — which a person's own
prompt does not carry, so a real turn is never swallowed.

## Tests

Two new tests, both in `crates/tui/src/runtime_threads/tests.rs`:

- `a_fork_measures_the_history_it_carries_not_the_shape_it_stores` builds a
  conversation whose file passes the bound while its carried form does not,
  asserts the fixture really is in that regime, then forks it. Reverting the
  production change makes it fail with the exact reported error.
- `runtime_traffic_and_attachment_tags_are_not_kept_prompts` builds the three
  shapes (MCP notice, screenshot prompt, toolbox snapshot) and asserts both
  walks a fork runs land where the records say.

Verified locally on `origin/main` (6a08f0312):

```
cargo fmt --check -p codewhale-tui                          clean
cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets (CI lint set)    clean
dev-test.sh ... recovery::                                  27 passed
```

Also exercised end to end against a copy of the real 9.75 MiB conversation:
`POST /v1/threads/{id}/patch-undo` returns `201` and the fork's own undo works
too.

## Not in this PR

`GET /v1/threads/{id}/history` still refuses a document over the bound, and
that one is not the same bug: the response body carries `session` in its stored
shape, so the bytes really would travel. Fixing it means changing the wire
payload to the carried form, which is a protocol change — worth its own
discussion rather than smuggling it in here.

## Note on the lint gate

`cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets` fails on `origin/main` at
`crates/tui/src/tui/persistence_actor.rs:80` (`variant ClearCheckpoint is never
constructed`) — pre-existing, untouched by this branch, from 4a974f0c6's
neighbourhood. I ran clippy with `-A dead_code` to get past it; everything else
is clean.

No changelog entries: CONTRIBUTING asks for them on `main` at merge time.

prs.title: fix(tui): keep the indent of a paragraph nested in a list
prs.body:
## What and why

A paragraph indented under a list item renders flush left: the word wrapper drops spaces at the start of a row, so the indent never reaches the screen. Models write these often, as a bullet's second paragraph or a note after a numbered step's code block. At 60 columns, before:

```
● Setup:
▏
▏ 1. Install the dependencies:
▏
       npm install --save-dev typescript
▏
▏ This also writes a lockfile, which you should commit
▏ together with the change.
▏
▏ 2. Build:
       npm run build
▏ 3. Check the config:
▏
       {
         "strict": true
       }
▏
▏ - A bullet with a second paragraph.
▏
▏ The second paragraph of that bullet, indented two spaces
▏ and long enough to wrap.
▏ - Last bullet
```

The code under step 1 keeps its indent but the note after it doesn't, so step 1 looks finished and the note reads as top-level text. After:

```
● Setup:
▏
▏ 1. Install the dependencies:
▏
       npm install --save-dev typescript
▏
▏    This also writes a lockfile, which you should commit
▏    together with the change.
▏
▏ 2. Build:
       npm run build
▏ 3. Check the config:
▏
       {
         "strict": true
       }
▏
▏ - A bullet with a second paragraph.
▏
▏   The second paragraph of that bullet, indented two
▏   spaces and long enough to wrap.
▏ - Last bullet
```

The parser now carries whether a list is open, next to its code-fence state: a list item opens it, blank lines, code and indented paragraphs keep it open, and anything else closes it. While a list is open, a paragraph keeps its leading spaces, and `render_paragraph_tagged` wraps the text in the remaining width and draws the indent on every row, capped at half the width like a list item's indent (#7030); links shift with it. The decision is made when the line is parsed rather than in the renderer, because streaming renders the text between code blocks separately and a look-back there would not match the final render. Copy follows list items: the first row copies with its indent, as written, and wrapped rows strip it.

Command notes go through the same renderer, and some have indented rows that aren't under a list item, such as `/status`'s key/value rows and part of `/cost`. Those render as before: I ran `/status`, `/cost`, `/context`, `/hooks`, `/mcp`, `/skills`, `/tools`, `/memory`, `/doctor`, `/version`, `/usage`, `/agents`, `/workspace`, `/permissions`, `/sandbox`, `/todo`, `/goal`, `/diff`, `/stats` and `/profile` in one session on both builds, and the screens match once the session id is masked. A first version that kept every indent did shift `/status` and `/cost`, which is why the decision follows the list.

## Issue

No-Issue: a paragraph indented under a list item renders flush left; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 588426ddd in a pseudo-terminal at 60 columns with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the steps and bullets above; the rows above come from those runs.
- Selection copy: with a throwaway test (not part of this PR) that selects `1. Install` followed by an indented paragraph, and `- item` followed by an indented line, at 24 columns and calls `selection_to_text`, this change copies both as written (`"1. Install\n\n   alpha beta … kappa"`); `main` copies them without the indent (`"1. Install\n\nalpha beta … kappa"`).
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 13880 of 13886 passed, with the 427 tests whose names match `markdown`, `paragraph`, `selection` or `transcript` among them. The 6 failures (`status_public_output_and_read_only_state_match_baseline`, `golden_turn_events_match`, `model_visible_prefix_bytes_match_goldens`, `interrupted_session_deletion_keeps_recovery_incomplete_and_can_finish`, `worker_compacts_past_its_context_window_and_keeps_working`, `reasoning_effort_uses_one_strict_alias_table_and_legacy_fallback`) also fail on `main` at 588426ddd without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 588426ddd; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): keep the quote rail on wrapped rows of a blockquote
prs.body:
## What and why

A blockquote draws its `│` rail on its first row only and pads wrapped rows with blanks of the same width. At 60 columns, before:

```
● Notes:
▏
▏ │ A quoted line that is long enough to wrap twice when
▏   the terminal is only sixty columns wide, so the rail
▏   has to carry on.
▏
▏ │ │ A nested quote that also wraps at sixty columns
▏     because it keeps going for a while.
▏
▏ After the quote.
```

The assistant rail beside it carries on but the quote's stops, so a wrapped quote reads as one quoted line followed by ordinary text. After:

```
● Notes:
▏
▏ │ A quoted line that is long enough to wrap twice when
▏ │ the terminal is only sixty columns wide, so the rail
▏ │ has to carry on.
▏
▏ │ │ A nested quote that also wraps at sixty columns
▏ │ │ because it keeps going for a while.
▏
▏ After the quote.
```

The blanks were there for selection copy: continuation rows reported the rail width as `copy_prefix_width` because the transcript's rail-scan (`compute_rail_prefix_width`) doesn't strip spaces. That scan runs on every row and strips the `│ ` spans there as it does on the first one, so every row now draws the same per-depth spans and reports `copy_prefix_width: 0`, which also removes the first-row branch. `blockquote_wraps_with_continuation_rail_indent` now expects the rail on each row; its width and re-join checks are unchanged.

## Issue

No-Issue: a wrapped blockquote loses its rail after the first row; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 588426ddd in a pseudo-terminal at 60 columns with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with a `>` and a `>>` quote; the rows above come from those runs.
- Selection copy, checked before I rebased onto 588426ddd (which moves `markdown_render.rs` into `codewhale-tui-kit` without touching these functions): with a throwaway test (not part of this PR) that selects a wrapped `>` and `>>` quote at 24 columns and calls `selection_to_text`, both builds copy `alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta iota kappa`, with no rail characters.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 13880 of 13886 passed, with the 480 tests whose names match `markdown`, `quote`, `selection` or `transcript` among them. The 6 failures (`status_public_output_and_read_only_state_match_baseline`, `golden_turn_events_match`, `model_visible_prefix_bytes_match_goldens`, `interrupted_session_deletion_keeps_recovery_incomplete_and_can_finish`, `worker_compacts_past_its_context_window_and_keeps_working`, `reasoning_effort_uses_one_strict_alias_table_and_legacy_fallback`) also fail on `main` at 588426ddd without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 588426ddd; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): detach recalled history when removing an attachment or deleting in vim
prs.body:
## What and why

After Up recalls an entry from prompt history, an edit is supposed to detach it: the note on `insert_str` explains that otherwise "the next Up/Down silently discards" the edit. Typing, Backspace and Delete, the word and line deletes, and kill and yank clear it, and e7e0a4da5 did the same for paste and the external editor. Among the edits that remove text, three don't: removing a selected attachment, and vim Normal-mode `x` and `dd`. After any of them, Up/Down carry on from the old index, and going back to that entry brings it back as it was saved.

Launch composer, `TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app`, one key at a time, with a history of `first entry` and a two-line entry that carries an image attachment. Type `draft`, Up to recall the attachment entry, Up, Home, Up to select the attachment, then Backspace (status: `Removed attachment: shots/a.png`). Before:

```
Backspace  ❯ what is in this picture
Up         ❯ first entry
Down         [Attached image: shots/a.png]
           ❯ what is in this picture
```

After:

```
Backspace  ❯ what is in this picture
Up           [Attached image: shots/a.png]
           ❯ what is in this picture
Down       ❯ what is in this picture
```

With `composer_vim_mode = "vim"` and a history of `first entry`, `second entry`: `k`, `0`, `x` gives `econd entry`. Then `k`, `j` showed `first entry` and `second entry` as saved; now `k` recalls `second entry` and `j` comes back to `econd entry`. `dd` on the second line of a recalled `two` / `lines` entry leaves `two`; `k`, `j` brought back `two` / `lines` and now come back to `two`.

Each of the three now calls `clear_input_history_navigation()` like the other deletes. For the attachment it goes after the check that one is selected, because every Backspace and Delete calls `remove_selected_composer_attachment` first. As with typing into a recalled entry, the draft from before the first Up (`draft` above) is no longer what Down returns to; the edited entry is.

## Issue

No-Issue: removing an attachment or vim `x`/`dd` on a recalled history entry is undone by the next Up/Down; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 3690f9c4a in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME, a seeded `composer_history.jsonl` and `TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app`, sending one key at a time on the launch composer; the rows above come from those runs.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 13908 of 13912 passed, with the 477 `vim`, `composer`, `attachment` and `history` tests among them. The 4 failures are plugin import tests (three in `plugins_dsh_tests`, plus `plugins_skill_tests::dsh_packages_import_through_the_reviewed_install_and_update_flow`, all "composition reviewer is unavailable"); the same 4 fail on `main` at 3690f9c4a without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 3690f9c4a; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

## What and why Open TSX documents with the LSP `typescriptreact` language ID, while keeping the existing TypeScript server transport and cache. The registry intentionally groups `.ts` and `.tsx` under one TypeScript server. However, `didOpen` currently sends `typescript` for both. [typescript-language-server's document handler](https://github.com/typescript-language-server/typescript-language-server/blob/7b28f104e741feba092045550738e8549e4ccb11/src/document.ts) translates that recognized ID into an explicit `scriptKindName: TS`; it does not re-detect TSX from the filename. Legal JSX is then diagnosed as TypeScript syntax errors. The override applies only when the configured ID is exactly `typescript` and the document extension is case-insensitively `tsx`. Ordinary `.ts` files and other/custom IDs are unchanged. No new language enum, server instance, transport lifecycle, diagnostics policy, public API, or feature flag is introduced. ## Issue No-Issue: small reproducible TSX language-ID bug found while reviewing the LSP document-open path; no matching open PR was found. ## How I tested it - Actual TypeScript **5.9.3** parser, source `export const view =
Hello
;`, filename `App.tsx`: - explicit `ScriptKind.TS` reproduces diagnostic **1161, Unterminated regular expression literal**; - explicit `ScriptKind.TSX` yields **zero parse diagnostics**. - `scripts/dev-test.sh lsp`: **64 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out**. - `scripts/dev-test.sh lsp registry::tests::detects_typescript_variants`: **1 passed; 0 failed; 63 filtered out**. - `scripts/dev-cargo.sh clippy -p codewhale-lsp --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings -A clippy::uninlined_format_args -A clippy::too_many_arguments -A clippy::unnecessary_map_or` — passed, no warnings. - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` — passed. Per the repository's agent guidance, no new test or code comment was added without explicit user permission. A complete CLI/TUI build, real language-server round trip, full workspace tests and cross-platform CI were not run locally. This is not a claim of end-to-end editor validation. ## Checklist - [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (`f4c2ce3a6`) - [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — fmt and existing tests pass; dedicated TSX protocol coverage is not claimed - [x] No new feature/flag: existing LSP feature registration remains unchanged Developed with Codex AI assistance, including read-only independent investigation and focused verification. No human review or hosted CI approval is claimed. ## Hosted CI follow-up (2026-10-29) The [Windows workspace check](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/40834508093/job/123316197548) fails on unused imports in `crates/app-server/src/lib.rs:21` (`Command`) and `crates/app-server/src/bridge.rs:21` (`tokio::sync::Mutex`), promoted to errors by `-D warnings`. prs.body:
## What and why

A synchronous `/rc` refusal could leave the controller `Off`, so its reason vanished with the toast. Asynchronous failures also bypassed TUI logging and only occupied status chrome.

Retain synchronous start/preflight failures in the existing `Failed` state, while preserving active connections and unexpired lease guards. Route start and relay failures through one redacted log/transcript/error-toast path, retire the previous legacy connecting notice, and show `/rc status` in the failure footer after the bounded toast expires. The transcript entry is current UI history; it does not add model messages or a new persisted diagnostic store.

Updated the English and Simplified Chinese guide. Enrollment identity checks, ownership recovery, local-turn safety, and retry lease deadlines retain their existing behavior. This complements main's ac3dfcd60 (safe explanations for specific server rejection codes), which does not retain synchronous failures or change their TUI reporting.

## Issue

Refs #7120

## How I tested it

Filtered invocations of `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked <filter> -- --test-threads=1`:

prs.title: fix(tui): let vim Normal mode take shifted keys like G
prs.body:
## What and why

In vim composer mode (`composer_vim_mode = "vim"`), `G` is typed into the draft instead of moving to its end. crossterm reports an uppercase letter with SHIFT, and the Normal-mode arm in `run_event_loop` only takes a `KeyCode::Char` with no modifiers at all, so `G` falls through to the insert arm below it. Every other shifted letter is typed the same way, and the Visual-mode arm has the same check, so `G` gets typed there too while lowercase keys are absorbed.

Launch composer, `TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app`, one key at a time: `i`, `hello`, Esc, `0`, then `G`, `i`, `!`. Before:

```
G     ❯ Ghello
i, !  ❯ G!hello
```

After:

```
G     ❯ hello
i, !  ❯ hello!
```

Both arms now check `is_plain_char`, the test the insert arm under them already uses: Shift is allowed, Ctrl, Alt and Super still are not. A shifted letter Normal mode doesn't bind, such as `A`, is now ignored like an unbound lowercase key instead of being typed.

On a terminal that `paste.rs` doesn't trust to deliver bracketed paste, a Normal-mode key doesn't reach this arm at all yet; #7126 fixes that.

## Issue

No-Issue: vim Normal mode types `G` and other shifted letters into the draft; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at b8afed5f2 in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME, `composer_vim_mode = "vim"` in `settings.toml` and `TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app`, sending one key at a time on the launch composer. Besides the rows above, `A` in Normal mode and `G` in Visual mode each typed the letter before and do nothing now; `i`, Esc, `0` and `x` behave the same in both builds.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 13908 of 13912 passed, with the 609 `vim`, `composer`, `event_loop` and `key` tests among them. prs.title: fix(tui): send a held key to vim Normal mode instead of typing it
prs.body:
## What and why

With `composer_vim_mode = "vim"`, Normal-mode keys type into the draft on any terminal that `paste.rs` doesn't trust to deliver bracketed paste: every Windows terminal, and anything whose `TERM_PROGRAM` is unset or isn't ghostty, iTerm.app, WezTerm or Apple_Terminal (tmux and VS Code's terminal set their own). There, the raw-paste guard holds each plain ASCII character for 8 ms to see whether a paste follows, and when nothing does, `flush_paste_burst_before_composer` inserts it. That happens before the event loop's Normal-mode arm sees the key, so `i`, `x`, `dd` and the motions all go into the draft as text, and Esc then clears the composer. The keys only start working after the session's first bracketed paste.

Launch composer, `TERM_PROGRAM` unset, one key at a time, before:

```
i            ❯ i
hello world  ❯ ihello world
Esc          ❯ Type a message…
0, x, w      ❯ 0xw
```

After:

```
i            ❯ Type a message…
hello world  ❯ hello world
Esc          ❯ hello world
0, x         ❯ ello world
w, x         ❯ ello orld
dd           ❯ Type a message…
```

A held character now goes to `vim_mode::handle_vim_normal_key` when no slash or mention menu is open, the condition that arm checks; it is absorbed in Visual mode, as the arm after it does; and it is typed into the composer otherwise. The function already does this for a held Space, which goes to the transcript when the composer is empty. A burst is still a paste: `abc` sent in one write lands in the draft as text in Normal mode, before and after.

## Issue

No-Issue: vim Normal-mode keys are typed as text on a terminal without trusted bracketed paste; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at b8afed5f2 in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME and `composer_vim_mode = "vim"` in `settings.toml`, sending one key at a time on the launch composer. With `TERM_PROGRAM` unset, the results are above; `v` then `q` typed `vq` before and does nothing now. With `TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app` the two builds give the same results, and the steps before the `abc` burst match what this change now gives with it unset; the burst itself differs, since a trusted terminal reads it as typed keys rather than a paste. `/he`, Esc, `x` reads `/hxe` with this change, as it does with iTerm.app, because the slash menu is open.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 13908 of 13912 passed, with the 260 `paste`, `vim`, `composer` and `event_loop` tests among them. prs.title: fix(tui): keep the turn metadata block out of /tree and /export
prs.body:
## What and why

The engine appends a `<turn_meta>` block to each user message it saves. The transcript leaves it out (`is_turn_metadata_block`, from #4681), and so do the resume picker, session titles and the ACP replay, but `/tree` and `/export` still read it as text.

`/tree` labels a user entry with its text blocks joined, so after one turn, before:

```
● 5fae47c9 [5fae47c9-…] user: say flat things <turn_meta> Current local date: 2026-10-29 C
```

After:

```
● f05aed51 [f05aed51-…] user: say flat things
```

`/export`, and the copy it puts on the clipboard, writes the block as a second content block of every user message. The export's header says hidden instructions are omitted and gives the workspace by folder name only, but the block carries its absolute path (shortened here). Before:

```
## 1. user

### Content 1: Text

say flat things

### Content 2: Text

<turn_meta>
Current local date: 2026-10-29
Current workspace: /…/ws
Current permission posture: Ask
Current sandbox posture: workspace-write (writes inside the workspace; network blocked) (local OS sandbox applied)
## Repo Working Set
Key files: README.md
When in doubt, use tools to verify and keep changes focused on the working set.
Git workspace: main | clean
</turn_meta>
```

After:

```
## 1. user

### Content 1: Text

say flat things
```

Three places now skip the block at the index `turn_metadata_text` returns, as `prompt_text` in `receipts.rs` already does: the journal label in `session_tree::tree_label`, the linear fallback in `tree_body` (used while a session has no journal yet; I didn't reach it in these runs), and `project_message` for the export. Only user messages are filtered, like `is_turn_metadata_block`. The saved session is unchanged.

## Issue

No-Issue: `/tree` and `/export` show the `<turn_meta>` block that the transcript hides; I searched and found no issue for these two

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 3690f9c4a in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server: one turn, then `/tree` and `/export`. The rows above come from those runs; the export after the change has no `turn_meta` in it.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 13908 of 13912 passed, with the 1333 tests whose names match `export`, `tree`, `session` or `contract` among them. The 4 failures are plugin import tests (three in `plugins_dsh_tests`, plus `plugins_skill_tests::dsh_packages_import_through_the_reviewed_install_and_update_flow`, all "composition reviewer is unavailable"); the same 4 fail on `main` at 3690f9c4a without this change.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-runtime`: 851 passed, 22 of them in `session_tree`.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy` on `codewhale-tui` and `codewhale-runtime` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 3690f9c4a; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): route a streamed reasoning delta to the reasoning cell
prs.body:
Fixes #7123

## What the user saw

Collapsed, one line of reasoning text showed outside the thinking card. Expanded, a single sentence was split: the first half inside the card, the second half below it as ordinary assistant prose.

## Root cause

`commit_streaming_display_tick` chose its destination cell by whichever cell happened to be live last (`app.streaming_message_index`), not by the kind of the block the delta belonged to. The engine keeps an assistant cell live after a text block ends — `ContentBlockStop(Text)` only sets `pending_message_complete`, and `MessageComplete` is emitted once per response — so when a response streams prose and then opens a reasoning block, the reasoning text was appended to the prose body. That is the split sentence.

Two more losses sat on the same boundary, both found in review:

- `streaming_thinking::start_block` resets `StreamingState` when a reasoning block opens. The display beat commits at most once per interval, so a boundary that lands between beats left the last slice of prose in the buffer and the reset discarded it — the tail before a reasoning card never reached the transcript.
- `ThinkingComplete`'s translation branch drained block 0 by index, ignoring kind, so a text block that lost its boundary event was consumed and dropped.

A third, found on the third review round: the first attempt at the `MessageStarted` fix was dead code. `App::flush_active_cell` clears `streaming_thinking_active_entry` on every path and only marks the thinking cell finished; it does not deliver a delta that never reached it. Draining after that flush can never run.

## The fix

- `StreamingState::block_is_thinking` reports a block's own kind; the display beat routes by it. Reasoning always lands in the thinking cell, and a text delta still gets an assistant cell when its own was already closed.
- `start_block` delivers a pending prose tail before resetting.
- Every finalize path drains block 0 only when a block of its own kind owns it, including the translation branch.
- `MessageStarted` finalizes a live reasoning entry **before** `flush_active_cell`, which is the only point where the entry is still live.
- `finalize_current` leaves the buffer alone when there is no live entry to deliver into, and `flush_pending_text_tail` resolves its destination before taking the buffer.

## Scope

Five files, six commits, all in `crates/tui`:

```
crates/tui/src/tui/streaming/mod.rs        |  10 ++
crates/tui/src/tui/streaming_thinking.rs   | 163 +++++++++++++++++++-
crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs        |  25 ++++
crates/tui/src/tui/ui/frame.rs             |  83 +++++++++---
crates/tui/src/tui/ui/tests.rs             |  57 +++++++++
```

This replaces #7134, which also carried fixes for breakage on `main` that this PR does not need to own. #7129 has since merged those, so the diff here is the reasoning-cell fix alone.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --lib` with `-D warnings` — clean.
- CI on this branch is running; see the checks below.
- I could not run the test suite locally: linking the lib test target exhausts memory on this machine (rustc reaches ~8.5 GB RSS and LLVM aborts). CI runs it.

New tests, each asserting the cell that must *not* receive the text:

- `issue_7123_reasoning_after_prose_stays_in_the_thinking_cell`
- `issue_7123_drain_text_block_leaves_a_reasoning_block_alone`
- `issue_7123_reasoning_block_keeps_the_prose_tail_it_interrupts`
- `issue_7123_finalize_current_leaves_a_text_block_alone`
- `issue_7123_message_started_order_keeps_the_reasoning_tail`
- `issue_7123_finalize_current_keeps_the_buffer_without_an_entry`

## Known checks on this branch

`Test (ubuntu-latest)` may be red. Its 9 failures are pre-existing on `main`: the same 9 tests fail identically on #7129 and #7125. Four are fixture drift (`File` schema at 3394 bytes against a 3200 budget, a `tools_sha256` and a `frozen:` prompt hash, and a `/cost` baseline that predates `[details]`), four are `composition reviewer is unavailable` in this CI leg, and one is a genuine `main` defect where `legacy_checkpoint_origin` ignores the late-usage tombstone that `load_legacy_checkpoint` honours. None is on a path this PR touches.

`Test (windows-latest)` may also be red, on two unused imports in `crates/app-server` whose only users are `cfg(unix)` / `cfg(all(test, unix))`. That is pre-existing breakage from direct pushes to `main`, not from this diff; per `CONTRIBUTING.md` a red check that is clearly explained is acceptable, so I left it out of scope rather than widening the diff.

## Follow-ups noted in review, not in this PR

- `MessageStarted` still resets without a text-tail drain, so a text block holding an uncommitted tail at a *lost* text boundary can be discarded. Bounded to one reveal interval.
- `issue_7123_message_started_order_keeps_the_reasoning_tail` replays the handler order by hand rather than driving the event loop, so a future reorder there would not fail it.

## Attribution

🤖 Generated by SpikeBot 000(CodeWhale-LOCAL)

issues.title: [P0][Bug]: Gateway restart disables actively running Discord sessions by dropping room-event recovery authority

labels.name: clawsweeper:intake:bug
labels.description: Preliminary submission classification; full source review pending.

issues.body:
### Summary
Gateway restart can disable the sessions that are actively being worked on: recovery tombstones an interrupted Discord room-event session, then rejects subsequent input instead of allowing work to continue. Transcript preservation does not preserve a usable working session.

### Impact and severity
P0 requested: this kills active workflows, not merely automatic resumption. Multiple affected sessions have been observed in this deployment. Recovery tells the user to start a replacement session, losing working continuity. Frequency across all restarts is not quantified; transcript deletion is not alleged.

### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Steps to reproduce
1. On 2026.10.9, use the documented ambient-room setup: `messages.groupChat.unmentionedInbound: "room_event"`, `visibleReplies: "message_tool"`, Discord room `requireMention: false`, and access to the message tool.
2. Send an allowed, unmentioned message that starts work. Restart the Gateway while that turn is active.
3. Observe recovery fail with the error below and the session become tombstoned. Send another input to the same session; admission rejects it rather than continuing the session.

### Expected behavior
The documented ambient-room setup must retain the original channel-ingress authority needed for restart recovery. A restart should not make an otherwise valid active session unusable or require replacement merely because the inbound event was a room event.

### Actual behavior
The user-visible recovery notice says:
> I couldn't continue this session after a gateway restart: message-tool-only recovery authority is unavailable. Your transcript is safe. In WebChat, use Resume in new session to continue it; in other channels, use /new or /reset to start a replacement session.

### OpenClaw version
2026.10.9 (`8b18b55`); independently inspected the official release source/npm artifact, not only locally modified runtime code.

### Operating system
macOS 26.6.2

### Install method
npm global

### Model
openai/gpt-6.1-sol

### Provider / routing chain
OpenClaw → Codex app-server → OpenAI

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Stock source explains the authority loss:
- [`resolveReplyRunDeliveryContext`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.9/src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-core.ts#L173) unconditionally returns `undefined` for `InboundEventKind === "room_event"`.
- The [restart claim controller call site](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.9/src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execute.ts#L435) reuses that resolver. The resulting claim retains `message_tool_only` and its execution fence but lacks the original channel route/authority; recovery rejects it.
- An extracted-function controlled test reproduced this on stock code; its filesystem/session I/O was mocked. This is separate from the observed live session lockouts, not a claim of a new end-to-end restart test.
- This setup is [explicitly recommended in the release documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.9/docs/channels/ambient-room-events.md#recommended-setup).

### Additional information
Related whole-session lockout reports: #146276, #161719, #173412. This report identifies the documented room-event path dropping recovery authority at claim creation. Please address existing affected sessions as well as preventing new lockouts, without replaying completed external actions.

issues.title: Heartbeat helper continuation converts successful NO_REPLY into settled-finalization fallback

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: impact:ux-friction
labels.description: User-facing flow adds avoidable confusion or support burden without fully blocking progress.

issues.body:
## Summary

A helper completion that resumes an isolated heartbeat can turn an explicit, successful `NO_REPLY` into a user-visible runtime fallback:

> The tool run finished, but no final summary was produced. I did not repeat any completed actions.

The parent and child both complete successfully, with `timedOut: false` and `aborted: false`. This is authored silence, not a failed or missing model response.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.4 (383c124), npm global installation, macOS arm64
- Builtin OpenClaw agent runtime with the OpenAI responses transport
- Main-agent isolated heartbeat, channel-bound to the owner
- Helper created through `sessions_spawn` with `context: "fork"` and `completionTarget: "parent"`, then parent calls `sessions_yield`

## Reproduction path

1. Start a scheduled isolated heartbeat.
2. Have it spawn a read-only research helper and yield.
3. The helper successfully returns findings and recommends no notification.
4. On the requester-settle callback, the parent checks current context, updates its local follow-up record, and returns exactly `NO_REPLY`.
5. Observe the owner's channel.

The callback targets `agent:main:main:heartbeat`. Its structured provenance is `kind: "inter_session"`, `sourceTool: "subagent_settle"`, with the child session as the source. The runtime event labels the resumed turn's trigger `user`.

## Observed result

For one correlated parent/child/channel trace:

- Initial parent turn yields successfully.
- Helper finishes successfully about 2.5 minutes later.
- Resumed parent emits exactly `NO_REPLY`, with no timeout or abort.
- Gateway logs `settled post-tool turn lacked a final answer ... running isolated finalization`.
- Two finalization attempts finish without visible text.
- Gateway logs `attempts=2/2 — using terminal fallback reply`.
- The canned fallback above is persisted and delivered to the owner's channel.

The same path repeats on quiet heartbeat cycles; successful non-silent recommendations still deliver normally. This report is based on production event/log correlation and installed-source inspection, not a new live reproduction that sends test messages.

## Relevant implementation

In the installed bundle `embedded-agent-DOz9dy-9.mjs`:

- `resolveSettledTurnFinalizationRequest`
- `resolveEmbeddedRunTerminal`
- `prepareTerminalWithSettledTurnFinalization` in the source region `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/settled-turn-finalization.ts`

The requester handoff already carries structured inter-session provenance in `subagent-announce-delivery-*.mjs`. The finalization fallback substitutes the silent token for a cron trigger, but this heartbeat-owned requester continuation is not classified as that trigger.

## Expected behavior / narrow fix

Preserve an explicit successful terminal `NO_REPLY` for a trusted helper callback into the heartbeat session before missing-answer recovery/fallback generation. Do not turn arbitrary empty outputs into success.

This should preserve existing behavior for:

- ordinary chat failures and ordinary chat helper callbacks;
- actual heartbeat provider/tool errors, aborts, and timeouts;
- pending tools, further yields, and approval requests;
- visible heartbeat recommendations and media;
- strings containing `NO_REPLY` plus other visible text.

It should not require disabling helpers or filtering diagnostic strings in every channel plugin.

A narrow local candidate patch checks the target session, structured `subagent_settle` provenance, successful terminal outcome, settled tools, and exact current-assistant text. It connects that predicate to both the finalization-request decision and the terminal silent-payload path. Deterministic tests against extracted installed function bodies cover the reported case and unchanged ordinary-error behavior; natural-run verification is pending activation.

## Related

- #144118 / #142753: the same settled-finalization fallback text reaches channels
- #175645: authored `NO_REPLY` in a helper announce run is treated as an empty-response failure
- #143454: helper handoffs force visible replies or duplicate earlier delivery

This report isolates the successful, intentionally quiet heartbeat-helper continuation on 2026.10.4; it does not propose broad channel suppression.

issues.title: Drop MESSAGE_CREATE event when receiving-bot-account has isDefault=true AND a more-specific-scoped binding matches for the target channel

labels.name: stale
labels.description: Marked as stale due to inactivity

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: impact:message-loss
labels.description: Channel message delivery can be lost, duplicated, or misrouted.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish
labels.description: Thin issue quality; more reproduction proof or environment detail is needed.

issues.body:
Drop MESSAGE_CREATE event when receiving-bot-account has isDefault=true AND a more-specific-scoped binding matches for the target channel

## Summary
Currently, an openclaw gateway configured with multi-agent bindings + isDefault fallback causes multi-agent fanout on human messages: a single human message on a channel bound to specific agent B causes BOTH bot account A (isDefault=true) AND bot account B (bindings[peer:channel:cid]) to independently generate replies. Result: user observes duplicate/cascaded bot responses to single message. Config knob `channels.discord.allowBots=false` empirically closes cross-bot echo (bot X reading bot Y's output as input) but does NOT close human-triggered multi-agent fanout because human messages bypass allowBots gate entirely.

## Steps to reproduce

1. openclaw config with:
   - `agents.list[0] = {id: "hedwig", isDefault: true, ...}` (guild-scoped catch-all)
   - `agents.list[1] = {id: "nanami", bindings: [{peer: {kind: "channel", id: "CHANNEL_X"}, ...}]}`
   - Discord guild with both Hedwig APP and OpenClaw Nanami APP as members with View Channel permission on CHANNEL_X
   - `channels.discord.allowBots: false` (to rule out cross-bot echo)
2. Human user posts message in CHANNEL_X
3. Both bot APPs generate independent replies within seconds of each other

## Empirical evidence

- `cowork-session/state/a692-post-restart-check-20260820T0315Z.log` — 7 bot messages POST-baseline (post-restart with allowBots=false LIVE) including two 03:04Z→03:05Z fanout instances
- Human ghostclaw asked "How is everything" at 03:04:49Z; Hedwig APP replied 03:05:06Z; Nanami APP replied 03:05:58Z (both bot=true; distinct account IDs)
- Config state at incident: allowBots=false, gateway pid 92348 stable, hedwig.isDefault=true, nanami.bindings=[peer:channel:1534983396340793405]

## Expected behavior

When bot account A receives a MESSAGE_CREATE event on channel Y where:
- A has `isDefault: true` at scope broader than Y
- Some other agent B has a binding whose peer matches Y

Then A's gateway SHOULD drop the event before processing (delegate to B's more-specific binding). Alternatively, A's isDefault should be interpreted as "catches unhandled channels" — where "unhandled" means "no other binding matches at more-specific scope."

## Actual behavior

A processes the event independently, producing a Hedwig-voice reply that posts via A's account. B ALSO processes the event via its binding. User sees two replies.

## Proposed fix (server-side)

In gateway routing:
```
def route_message_create(event, agent):
    if agent.is_default:
        # Check if any other agent has a more-specific binding matching event.channel_id
        more_specific = [
            a for a in all_agents
            if a.id != agent.id
            and any(
                b.matches_channel(event.channel_id)
                and b.scope_depth() > agent.default_scope_depth()
                for b in a.bindings
            )
        ]
        if more_specific:
            return drop_event(event, reason="delegated_to_more_specific_binding")
    return process_event(event, agent)
```

Where `scope_depth()` returns integer (guild=1, channel=2, thread=3, etc.).

## Alternative: config-only workaround

Users could work around this by:
- Removing isDefault from agent A (loses catch-all behavior for untargeted channels)
- Adding per-channel exclusion bindings to A (requires schema support for exclusion bindings, currently unclear)
- Moving each specific-binding agent to a channel-scoped isDefault (requires schema support for channel-scoped isDefault)

Please confirm which config workaround is currently supported. Empirical schema audit `state/a692-schema-audit-20260820T0335Z.log` in-flight to determine feasibility.

## Impact

- Every openclaw deployment with a catch-all agent + per-channel bindings is affected
- User-observable duplicate replies degrade UX
- No config workaround currently identified without functionality loss

## Backward compatibility

Proposed fix is opt-in via new config knob `agents.default_delegation_mode` with values:
- `"catch_all"` (current behavior, default for backward compat)
- `"defer_to_specific"` (new behavior — drop when more-specific binding matches)

Users can migrate on their own schedule.

---

Robert to file at github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/new (or wherever upstream lives) using this body verbatim. Alternative: task-agent can attempt `gh api POST /repos/<owner>/openclaw/issues` if hedwig confirms `<owner>` = openclaw org.

issues.title: [Feature]: Add an optional Cua Spaces worker provider

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add an optional Cua Spaces integration through the existing WorkerProvider plugin contract.

## Problem to solve

Operators with Cua Spaces cannot select their existing Cua infrastructure as an OpenClaw worker provider. They need the standard worker execution and desktop workflow while Cua owns allocation and deletion.

## Proposed solution

Add an optional provider for dedicated, disposable Linux x64 Cua Spaces. Keep the Gateway on its existing host. Use Core-owned Node enrollment grants, the existing worker-turn and remote-exec modes, and Core's authenticated desktop viewer.

Keep placement and account selection in explicit trusted configuration. Local placement stays the default. Direct and Relay placement must retain the exact parent, child, account context, and operation ownership. The provider must report indeterminate cleanup when the host API cannot prove physical absence.

The first implementation keeps a pinned container image, runc runtime, no reuse, no public ports, and guest-only desktop control. It adds no general Gateway token or host desktop access. A bundled implementation would live under extensions/cua-spaces-worker and use the current public Plugin SDK. An external plugin remains a supported alternative if maintainers prefer that ownership model.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep a standalone plugin. This already fits the public SDK and avoids another bundled dependency, but maintainers would not own its release or compatibility.
- Reuse Crabbox. Crabbox is the existing bundled WorkerProvider precedent. This request is for Cua infrastructure and its native capabilities, with separate lifecycle and ownership behavior.

## Impact

This affects operators who already use Cua and want to attach a disposable worker to an OpenClaw conversation. The missing integration blocks that workflow until they maintain an external adapter. No outage, account change, paid plan, or automatic migration is implied.

## Evidence/examples

- The current public WorkerProvider contract and bundled Crabbox provider supply the required plugin registration, execution modes, enrollment callbacks, and desktop lease contract.
- An external candidate targets OpenClaw 2026.10.7 and @trycua/cua 0.9.0. Its isolated synthetic suite passed 86 tests with no skips and its package installation was checked. This is evidence for that candidate, not proof of compatibility with current main.
- An earlier local candidate demonstrated same-guest Core execution, files, computer interaction, and the Core viewer with a reviewed task-only Core enrollment repair. Stock Core and the current candidate were not qualified by that run. The existing enrollment work remains separately owned in #159178 and is not duplicated here.
- Genuine remote allocation, guest execution, and teardown remain unverified. A successful host delete response is not physical absence proof.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

## Additional information

The goal extends beyond parity with another worker backend. The proposal is phased so OpenClaw can use Cua's native lifecycle, placement, desktop, and storage capabilities through the SDK rather than rebuild them. Later units can evaluate native media streams, stop/resume, checkpoints and forks, volumes, and prewarm where the supported contracts permit them. Each needs its own ownership model and runtime proof. The initial provider does not implement or claim those capabilities.

No Core enrollment repair, new generic manager, paid service, account enrollment, host listener, host desktop, or production deployment belongs in the first slice.

issues.title: [Feature]: Generate short multi-speaker dialogue with the bundled ElevenLabs plugin

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: clawsweeper:bulk-filed
labels.description: ClawSweeper detected a high recent issue-filing volume from this author.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add an optional tool to the existing ElevenLabs plugin that turns an ordered script with two selected voices into one generated dialogue MP3.

### Problem to solve

A scripted interview or podcast scene needs a relationship between each line and its speaker, together with the surrounding exchange. The [podcast_generator project](https://github.com/sjfischr/podcast_generator/blob/d1a7ca31814995bd3748b771ab348789df441783/README.md) implements this task using batches of speaker turns. Its author explains why synthesizing each turn separately and assembling the recordings does not provide the same conversational context. That is an external implementation and reported motivation; I have not independently evaluated its audio quality.

There is also an OpenClaw-specific consumer surface: [pixcli's registry README](https://hub.openclaw.ai/shellbot/plugins/openclaw-pixcli) advertises optional dialogue and podcast tools. It is an existing alternative, not a request from its author to migrate.

The bundled ElevenLabs integration currently accepts one text and one voice per synthesis request. A speaker name written into that text does not become a second voice assignment. The requested output is a short jointly generated exchange using the operator's ElevenLabs voices, rather than an ordinary spoken assistant reply. Applicability to operators of the bundled plugin is an inference from these public workflows, not a reported OpenClaw outage.

### Proposed solution

Keep this capability inside `extensions/elevenlabs`, behind an explicitly enabled plugin tool; `elevenlabs_dialogue` is a suggested name. Use the existing optional-tool registration and manifest contracts. Do not expand the core `tts` tool or the shared speech interface.

The initial tool would accept an ordered array of nonempty `{text, voiceId}` turns, with exactly two distinct voice IDs. Generate a single bounded scene using Eleven v3 and return one MP3 artifact. Preserve turn order and inline audio tags. Reject scripts above a total of 2,000 text characters before making a request; this intentionally excludes automatic long-form episode production.

Reuse the plugin's configured authentication, runtime-resolved secrets, trusted base URL and guarded HTTP helpers for `POST /v1/text-to-dialogue`. Use `mp3_44100_128`. Do not accept credentials, arbitrary endpoints or publication destinations in tool arguments. Keep normal tool admission, cancellation and current invocation authority. A provider error must not silently substitute another provider or turn the script into single-voice narration. Do not automatically regenerate or replay a request whose paid outcome is unknown.

Return the audio through existing media storage and tool-result/reply contracts. Artifact creation and delivery must be distinguished; do not claim delivery from a local path alone.

### Alternatives considered

- Repeated TTS calls followed by audio assembly preserve voice assignments, but each synthesis lacks the complete exchange. They remain useful when independently editable stems are the goal.
- The external Python project or a direct ElevenLabs SDK integration can already perform the vendor request; a custom OpenClaw tool can wrap that existing contract. An equivalent multi-voice operation in the current hosted ElevenLabs MCP was not established. These are valid alternatives; this proposal adds a narrowly scoped operation to an existing bundled owner, rather than claiming that OpenClaw cannot run such a workflow at all.
- pixcli already supplies dialogue tooling through its separately configured Meterkey service. Its README permits private output; it does not force public publishing. Keeping the existing ElevenLabs account and voice catalog is the distinction here, not an invented ban on other plugins.
- Other speech providers can offer dialogue, but their voices are not the selected ElevenLabs voice IDs.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: operators generating two-voice scripted scenes with the bundled ElevenLabs integration. The public projects establish the task, not the size of this population.
- Severity/urgency: an additional authoring capability; existing single-voice speech remains available. No production incident or urgency has been established.
- Frequency: unknown. Each qualifying scene needs one bounded dialogue request.
- Practical consequences: the bundled integration cannot currently express both speaker assignments in a joint synthesis. Operators use a separate integration or assemble independently generated turns. No measured time savings or quality improvement is claimed.

### Evidence/examples

- [External batch producer](https://github.com/sjfischr/podcast_generator/blob/d1a7ca31814995bd3748b771ab348789df441783/generate_podcast.py): `build_batches` and `generate_dialogue_batch` preserve speaker turns. Its older batch-size assumptions should not be copied.
- [ElevenLabs API contract](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-dialogue/convert): ordered text/voice pairs produce audio. This proposal uses a smaller two-voice subset and the current short-request guidance.
- [Current bundled request builder](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b8c33ef334b3754f42afe2a2e212418abfa80f4/extensions/elevenlabs/speech-provider-factory.ts) and [plugin entry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b8c33ef334b3754f42afe2a2e212418abfa80f4/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts): scalar synthesis and no dialogue tool.
- [Existing optional-tool contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b8c33ef334b3754f42afe2a2e212418abfa80f4/docs/plugins/building-plugins.md#registering-tools).
- Related [issue #165655](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165655) / [PR #165656](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165656) concern dialogue-model transport for a single speaking voice and phone-call socket reuse. The inspected open PR sends one text/voice pair; this proposal concerns a structured multi-voice script and an audio file.

This is static source and public-contract research. No vendor request, installed-plugin execution or listening test was performed.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Suggested implementation: register an optional version 2 tool in the existing plugin and declare its manifest ownership; factor reusable plugin-local credential/config and request helpers rather than copying their policy. The public factory context already supplies runtime config, provider-key resolution and `assertInvocationCurrent`; recheck current authority after awaited preparation and before the request and artifact admission. Reuse focused media-store and bounded binary-response helpers. For a finished direct reply, the existing `canDeliverSourceReply` / `details.sourceReply` contract can deliver the artifact; nested Code Mode execution remains program data under that contract.

Non-goals: real-time calls, WebSocket pooling, new v4 model support, voice cloning, speaker identification, transcription, pronunciation-dictionary management, long-script chunking, audio editing, podcast hosting, public uploads, new persistent jobs, and a generic dialogue SDK. Existing TTS defaults, personas and fallback behavior remain outside this tool's operation.

Acceptance criteria:

- With the tool explicitly enabled and usable ElevenLabs credentials, submit a short A/B/A script with two accessible voice IDs. One dialogue request preserves the three turns and both IDs, and returns a playable MP3. Confirm the supplied voice assignments with a listening test as well as the request trace; do not promise subjective quality.
- The returned artifact is usable through the actual tool/result path. A direct source reply reaches only the admitted source conversation; a nested program call returns data without an unsolicited send.
- Empty text, malformed voice ID syntax, a missing second voice, and a script over the character budget fail before the vendor request. A syntactically valid voice ID may still be unavailable to the account; surface that provider access/validation failure honestly rather than claiming local validation proves access. The disabled tool is absent from discovery. Cancellation, a retired invocation, and credential/plugin disablement do not admit a new request or publish a success artifact.
- Authentication, validation, timeout, malformed audio and size-limit failures produce an actionable error, without silent voice/provider substitution or automatic paid regeneration. Existing single-voice TTS still works with its previous defaults.

Implementer unknown. Live synthesis, real tool delivery, failure/cancellation proof and focused plugin/contract checks remain work for the eventual implementation. Maintainers should decide whether this existing-owner enhancement is worth maintaining relative to the external alternatives.
