issues.title: [Feature]: Support keyterm prompting in ElevenLabs batch transcription

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: clawsweeper:bulk-filed
labels.description: ClawSweeper detected a high recent issue-filing volume from this author.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let operators pass an explicit vocabulary to Scribe v2 through the bundled ElevenLabs batch transcription provider using the existing `providerOptions.elevenlabs` configuration.

### Problem to solve

When transcribing recordings containing product names or specialized terms, an operator may want to supply a specific list of recognition hints. A [LiveKit developer requested this integration control](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408) on February 27, 2026, and supplied an implementation for that product. This is an external demand signal; applying the task to OpenClaw's recorded-audio workflow is an inference, not a report that this person uses OpenClaw.

OpenClaw already transcribes audio through Scribe v2. Its [current ElevenLabs implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts) reads only `no_verbatim`, `tag_audio_events`, and `diarize` from provider options. A configured `keyterms` array reaches the provider request context but never enters the multipart request. The [provider documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/docs/providers/elevenlabs.md#provider-options) explicitly limits support to those three fields.

The missing capability is selecting the terms used by Scribe's recognition-bias mechanism within this native transcription path. This does not promise correct spelling for every recording or a general improvement in accuracy.

### Proposed solution

Support one additional, opt-in provider option, `keyterms: string[]`, for `scribe_v2` batch transcription. Reuse current provider-scoped configuration and merge precedence; no new top-level configuration or tool is needed. For example:

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "media": {
      "models": [{
        "provider": "elevenlabs",
        "model": "scribe_v2",
        "capabilities": ["audio"]
      }],
      "audio": {
        "enabled": true,
        "providerOptions": {
          "elevenlabs": {
            "keyterms": ["OpenClaw", "Acme Research", "PostgreSQL"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Serialize the list as repeated multipart `keyterms` fields, following the provider's array contract and [official SDK request construction](https://github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python/blob/f5d53e09e35717523435cee238ac5cc7f51966fb/src/elevenlabs/speech_to_text/raw_client.py#L177). Preserve each term's spelling and Unicode content; do not comma-join the list or encode it as one JSON string. Keep all option fields before the original file, preserving its filename, MIME type, and bytes; the shared multipart builder documents this ordering for streaming parsers. Keep array assembly provider-local rather than widening the shared scalar helper. A model-entry list replaces the audio-default list, as existing options already do. An empty list clears inherited terms; an absent or empty effective list sends no keyterms.

Keep this an explicit allowlisted addition. Preserve dedicated fields, existing scalar options, authentication, guarded HTTP transport, cancellation, and the synchronous transcript-text result. Reject an incompatible option shape or unsupported model rather than silently applying a different control. Surface provider validation errors through the existing error/fallback handling without truncating terms silently.

Document the option and its extra provider charge before users choose it. The [current API reference](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/speech-to-text/convert) currently permits up to 1,000 terms, requires each term to have fewer than 50 characters and at most five normalized words, and specifies disallowed characters. It adds a 20% surcharge; more than 100 terms also impose a minimum billable duration of 20 seconds per request. The provider remains authoritative for validation and future billing changes. No vocabulary is inferred from conversation history or sent by default.

### Alternatives considered

- **Explicit transcription prompt:** OpenClaw already forwards a configured prompt as context. It may help some tasks, but the current ElevenLabs API reference does not specify it as equivalent to structured `keyterms`. Preserve existing prompt behavior; this proposal does not claim it is useless.
- **Deepgram:** OpenClaw supports repeatable Deepgram keyterms after [#176781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176781). Switching providers is valid. This proposal retains the selected ElevenLabs account and model.
- **Official ElevenLabs skill or SDK, a CLI transcription model, or a custom provider plugin:** These can perform vocabulary-guided transcription outside the bundled adapter. The [official skill reference](https://github.com/elevenlabs/skills/blob/9a1a4b7fbb6ca02fbdc7f44f2271e6c829d0f421/speech-to-text/references/transcription-options.md) includes keyterms. These are real alternatives; native support avoids maintaining a separate transcription script or provider registration for one additional input.
- **Correct text afterward:** This can repair known spelling errors but does not give the recognizer a selected term list. An uncertain correction can also change meaning.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: Operators using bundled ElevenLabs transcription for recorded audio with specialized vocabulary. The affected OpenClaw population is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: The requested recognition control is unavailable in that adapter; ordinary transcription remains usable. No production outage or measured urgency is established.
- Frequency: A configured list would apply to matching transcription requests. Actual usage frequency is unknown.
- Practical consequences: Operators must accept transcription without that control, correct text, switch providers, or maintain another integration. Time savings and accuracy gains have not been measured. Enabling keyterms can increase provider charges.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original integration request and follow-up](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408); [LiveKit implementation #4967](https://github.com/livekit/agents/pull/4967). These concern the same author and task, not two independent users.
- [Official keyterm guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/speech-to-text/batch/keyterm-prompting) describes vocabulary biasing and distinguishes batch and realtime inputs.
- [Current options schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/config/zod-schema.core.ts#L627), [runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts#L86), and [registered provider](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts#L22) establish the input path and missing mapping.
- [#177975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177975) already implemented three scalar options. This request adds a vocabulary input; it does not reopen that repaired bug or propose unrestricted forwarding.

Verification was static against the pinned main revision. No installed Gateway, live ElevenLabs transcription, or recognition-quality comparison was run for this proposal.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

The implementation owner is `extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts`; its former standalone media-understanding module was consolidated into registration. Suggested work is provider-local array serialization and validation, focused registered-provider coverage, and documentation. Public `AudioTranscriptionRequest.query` already accepts string arrays. A new SDK contract, provider manager, dictionary store, or model-facing tool is unnecessary.

Preserve the existing media authorization, HTTP guards, and cancellation behavior applicable to the caller at dispatch; this option does not introduce a new universal execution context. A vocabulary does not authorize a transcription request. Keep terms out of diagnostic logs; they may contain names absent from the audio. No retention or permission change is requested.

Non-goals: Realtime/Voice Call/Google Meet transcription, TTS pronunciation dictionaries, vocabulary management, speaker-label output, asynchronous webhooks, redaction, multichannel results, unrestricted form overrides, or guaranteed accuracy. No implementer has committed.

Acceptance criteria:

- With an isolated configuration selecting `elevenlabs/scribe_v2`, native recorded-audio transcription sends two configured terms as separate multipart fields alongside one unchanged audio file, and returns the transcript through the existing path.
- Capture the actual HTTP body from the shipped transcription entry point, not only a helper call. Verify model-entry replacement of defaults, an empty list clearing defaults, and unchanged requests without a list.
- Existing scalar `false` values and dedicated model/language/prompt fields retain their behavior. Other providers do not receive the ElevenLabs vocabulary; unsupported response-changing keys remain excluded.
- An incompatible scalar value or unsupported model does not silently send an unconditioned Scribe request. Provider-side term rejection surfaces without truncation. With an actual cancellation-capable execution context, cancellation before dispatch prevents a request.
- In an authorized live check, submit a synthetic name-bearing recording with a valid small vocabulary and confirm provider acceptance and native transcript return. Recognition output is observational evidence, not a promise that every supplied term appears.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a turn fails with `Session capability metadata changed` before any provider call, model fallback treats it as a provider failure and tries every configured fallback model. Each candidate fails the same way in about one second. The user sees "Model fallback" banners even though the error has nothing to do with the model.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a primary model with fallbacks (here `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` → `opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` → `bailian-token-plan/qwen3.8-max`).
2. Run a busy parent session that spawns subagents, so that a subagent completion announce turn fails with `Session capability metadata changed | Session capability metadata requires worker preparation`. The trigger is in a separate issue (see Additional information).
3. Look at the `model_fallback_decision` events for the announce run.

### Expected behavior

The error comes from OpenClaw session coordination, not from a model. Changing models cannot fix it. Fallback should stop the chain for this error, as it already does for `PreparedModelRuntimeOwnerNotPublishedError` (#156975) and the names in `RUNTIME_COORDINATION_ERROR_NAMES`.

### Actual behavior

Every candidate fails with the same error hash, and the chain moves to the next model each time:

```text
16:31:11.518 model_fallback_decision candidate_failed anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 errorHash=sha256:810bb62a0f4a -> opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor
16:31:11.743 lane task error: lane=main durationMs=152 error="Session capability metadata changed | Session capability metadata requires worker preparation"
16:31:11.748 model_fallback_decision candidate_failed opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor errorHash=sha256:810bb62a0f4a -> bailian-token-plan/qwen3.8-max
16:31:12.803 lane task error: lane=main durationMs=1016 error="Session capability metadata changed | Session capability metadata requires worker preparation"
16:31:12.920 Subagent completion direct announce failed for run 5a170c88-…: Session capability metadata changed | Session capability metadata requires worker preparation
```

The Control UI then shows `MODEL FALLBACK: OPENCODE-GO/MUSE-SPARK-1.3-CONTRIBUTOR → BAILIAN-TOKEN-PLAN/QWEN3.8-MAX` and "Couldn't finish this reply".

Cause, from the code:

- `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-session-store.ts:272,329,362` throws a plain `Error` (name `Error`), with a `SessionCapabilityReadRequired` cause.
- `resolveModelFallbackError` (`src/agents/failover-error.ts:687`) returns `kind: "coordination"` only for specific error classes, or for names in `RUNTIME_COORDINATION_ERROR_NAMES` (`failover-error.ts:57`). The capability error matches neither, so it continues to `coerceToFailoverError` and fallback continues to the next candidate.
- `resolveChainStopReason` (`src/agents/model-fallback-attempt.ts:196`) has no case for it either.

### OpenClaw version

main (code unchanged between e4ab503e5bf and 930ece0c5f1)

### Operating system

macOS 26

### Install method

git (source build)

### Model

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 via claude-cli, with configured fallbacks

### Provider / routing chain

claude-cli → opencode-go → bailian-token-plan (configured fallbacks)

### Additional provider/model setup details

None.

### Logs

From one gateway on 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21 (UTC+8). Every `model_fallback_decision` with `errorHash=sha256:810bb62a0f4a` belongs to a subagent completion announce run:

| Day | Capability-metadata errors | Fallback decisions with this hash | Announce runs affected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-20 | 15 | 4 | 2 |
| 2026-10-21 | 35 | 10 | 5 |

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The Control UI shows the fallback banner followed by "Couldn't finish this reply". Each candidate fails in 42–1016 ms (`lane task error … durationMs`), which is too short for a provider round trip.

### Impact and severity

Users see model fallback banners and lose replies for a failure that no model caused, which sends them to debug the wrong layer.

### Additional information

Suggested direction (not verified): throw a named error class for the capability-metadata invalidation (for example `SessionCapabilityMetadataChangedError`) and add it to `RUNTIME_COORDINATION_ERROR_NAMES`, or check for `SessionCapabilityReadRequired` in the error graph in `resolveModelFallbackError`.

The reason these announce turns fail at all is filed separately: #179289.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug: an internal transcript conflict is classified as a model failure and walks the whole fallback chain.

### Summary
On 2026.10.5, a Slack DM turn failed with `Transcript idempotency key "channel-user:v1:<hash>" conflicts with the admitted message`. The failover layer read it as a model error (`reason=unknown`), retried the primary three times, then fell back across models **and providers**: `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` → `anthropic/claude-opus-5` → `openai/gpt-6-astra`. Every provider call in the window returned HTTP 200, so the fallback could not help. It only made the turn slower and more expensive. The user then saw "Model Fallback cleared" once a later turn succeeded on the primary.

### Sequence (timestamps UTC, single gateway)
1. `00:42:14` Gateway restart. `main-session-restart-recovery` marks 2 startup-orphaned main sessions; both are Slack DM **threads** of the same user, recovered "with pending payload"; both reach `status=ok` by 00:43:32.
2. `00:58:24` A new message arrives in that user's **top-level DM session** (`agent:main:slack:direct:<user>`). `compaction-safeguard`: `finalized artifact truncated; loss=preserved-turn-head,suffix-head`.
3. `00:58:27` The run ends `isError=true` with `stopReason=error non-visible-output`; `[empty-error-retry]` resubmits 1/3, 2/3, 3/3, each failing on the same conflict.
4. `00:58:32` `embedded run failover decision: decision=fallback_model reason=unknown ... rawError=Transcript idempotency key "channel-user:v1:<hash>" conflicts with the admitted message.` Then `model fallback decision: candidate_failed ... next=anthropic/claude-opus-5`.
5. `00:58:38` Same conflict on `claude-opus-5` → `next=openai/gpt-6-astra`.
6. `01:02:19` `candidate_succeeded candidate=openai/gpt-6-astra reason=unknown`.

### Expected
- A transcript idempotency/admission conflict is not a provider failure. It should not consume model retries or trigger `fallback_model`, and it should never cross providers. Classify it like other non-retryable session errors (or as its own reason) so the failover policy can skip it.
- Separately: the user message key should not conflict after a preflight compaction rewrite plus restart recovery on sibling thread sessions of the same user. This looks related to #142224 (restart re-admission of keyed users), and to #144627 (a conflict masking the real error, closed for the cron `terminal-error` path).

### Impact
Real cost and latency (the fallback model is ~2.5× the primary per token), a misleading "fallback" signal that looks like a provider outage, and no config knob to limit `fallbacks` to provider-error reasons. Our only lever today is removing cross-provider fallbacks entirely, which loses outage protection.

### Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9), Linux container (Kubernetes), Slack channel in socket mode
- `agents.defaults.model`: primary `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`, fallbacks `anthropic/claude-opus-5`, `openai/gpt-6-astra`
- Busy agent: large agent DB (~5 GB); compaction safeguard active

### Suggested fix
1. In the failover classifier, map `Transcript idempotency key ... conflicts with the admitted message` (and sibling admission/fence errors such as `keyed user is outside the current turn`) to a non-model reason that does not trigger `fallback_model` or `[empty-error-retry]`.
2. Optionally, expose a policy such as `agents.defaults.model.fallbackOn: ["provider_error","rate_limit","overloaded","context_overflow"]` so operators can keep cross-provider fallback for outages only.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Files Preview loads session-relative CSS and JavaScript, but then converts them to inline content that an authored `style-src 'self'; script-src 'self'` policy rejects. An HTML document can therefore lose both its styling and initialization even though its relative assets are available to the session reader.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a session HTML file that uses a meta Content Security Policy with `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'` and references a relative stylesheet and deferred classic scripts. The observed document referenced `styles.css`, followed by `data.js` and `app.js`, both with `defer`.
2. Open that file in the Control UI's Files Preview using the default `scripts` sandbox mode.
3. Observe the unstyled, uninitialized page and inspect the browser's CSP diagnostics. The asset request contains all three filenames; the missing-asset notice does not appear.

The current-source reproduction uses the existing `chat-html-preview.e2e.test.ts` browser path with the original synthetic four-file document, deterministic session-file RPC responses, the production preview transformer, and the actual isolated sandbox HTTP listener. It reproduces the failure at the rendering boundary without replacing browser CSP enforcement.

### Expected behavior

The [documented session-file preview behavior](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9fa6391b5dbf802f6a7566fa28f16f1a76e112cb/docs/web/control-ui/chat.md#L1071-L1085) supports relative stylesheets and scripts, including deferred classic execution. Resources allowed by the authored document should retain that behavior without relaxing its CSP or the preview sandbox. Resources forbidden by either policy should remain forbidden.

### Actual behavior

On commit `9fa6391b5dbf802f6a7566fa28f16f1a76e112cb`, Chromium reports one blocked inline stylesheet and two blocked inline scripts. The page remains at its initial zero-record state with its creation control disabled.

The source explains the changed resource classification: [the asset transformer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9fa6391b5dbf802f6a7566fa28f16f1a76e112cb/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-html-preview-assets.ts#L309-L376) replaces `<link rel="stylesheet">` with `<style>` and external scripts with inline code; deferred classic scripts become inline module trampolines. The authored CSP remains present, so its restriction on inline content applies to those replacements.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.9 source build, commit `9fa6391b5dbf802f6a7566fa28f16f1a76e112cb`.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 remote browser runner; Chromium 156.0.8078.4.

### Install method

Repository browser E2E harness with the bundled Control UI and native sandbox listener, using locked dependencies.

### Model

Not involved in the current-source reproduction; it opens an existing HTML document.

### Provider / routing chain

Control UI → session-file asset RPC fixture → production asset transformer → native sandbox HTTP listener → Chromium. The fixture supplies file bytes only; it does not simulate CSP or script execution.

### Logs

```text
Applying inline style violates the following Content Security Policy directive 'style-src 'self''.
Executing inline script violates the following Content Security Policy directive 'script-src 'self''.
Executing inline script violates the following Content Security Policy directive 'script-src 'self''.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The browser reproduction observed a successful asset request for `styles.css`, `data.js`, and `app.js`, no omitted-asset notice, all three CSP rejections above, and an inner sandbox of `allow-scripts allow-forms`. No production code was changed during reproduction.

### Impact and severity

This blocks supported relative-asset rendering for the observed self-only CSP document. It does not establish data loss or an isolation escape, and the original file/download bytes remain separate from the transformed preview. The same failure was observed in the original interactive Files workflow and reproduced on the current source through the browser harness. Frequency across other authored policies has not been established.

### Additional information

The original application's use of `localStorage` is a separate limitation: the opaque preview sandbox intentionally denies that storage. Correcting asset handling must preserve that denial; fully enabling that particular application's persistence-dependent controls is not the acceptance criterion for this bug. A sandbox-compatible interaction should verify relative CSS/script initialization and deferred ordering while denied content remains blocked. No CSP relaxation or new serving mechanism has been implemented or selected.

## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect CI fixture input).

## Beta release blocker

No.

## Summary

The selected Linux service correspondence test retains the caller's profile even when the installed command declares none, so the existing positive admission assertion fails after the intentional installed-payload isolation in #187901.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use source `7601807fbb5fd4dba7aeebc9df9f5966a4e63f7a` with its locked dependencies on Linux x64.
2. Run the complete `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-maintenance-identity.test.ts` owner through the maintained test runner, explicitly selecting `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun` and the repository's pinned `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1` Bun executable.
3. Observe `keeps selected linux correspondence at before-stop: no declared profile` fail at line 416.

## Expected behavior

The fixture should represent a current selected observation: installed-payload environment plus the selected native unit. The same unit, UID and command should be admitted when the payload declares no profile. The existing changed-declared-profile and foreign-unit cases must still refuse admission.

## Actual behavior

The complete owner runs 31 cases: 30 pass and one fails. The positive assertion rejects with `UpdatePreMutationError`, reason `runtime-artifact-publication`, from `update-command-service-revalidation.ts:284`.

The fixture constructs `serviceEnv` with profile `selected` and unit `custom-selected.service`, while the command environment has only HOME. Current service observation instead records the payload-projected environment, which does not inherit an omitted profile. The real manager-admission policy also rejects a named profile paired with that unrelated custom unit. The fixture calls the publication guard with its constructed selected record, bypassing those producer/admission steps.

## OpenClaw version

Source `7601807fbb5fd4dba7aeebc9df9f5966a4e63f7a`, tree `10ab446d9f32a4bf46f0a3fc660be940d4107995`.

## Operating system

Linux x64. Distribution/version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

## Install method

Locked-dependency source checkout; Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Vitest 5.0.5 and the pinned Bun test runtime.

## Model

No model request was made.

## Provider / routing chain

Existing service-identity fixture → actual managed-Gateway artifact-publication guard. Native inventory and service-state reads are mocked.

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The same assertion failed in [scheduled CI run 40965892209, small-32 job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40965892209/job/123770580038). An independent unchanged full-file Linux reproduction reached the same line 416/guard 284 failure with all 31 cases accounted for. Vitest reported 44.50 seconds, dominated by transformation; the test wrapper took 47.40 seconds.

The declared-selected positive and changed-profile/foreign-unit negative controls remain among the passing cases. This is boundary-test evidence; no real service was stopped, replaced or restarted, and no full CLI update failure is established.

## Impact and severity

This makes the selected Linux CI owner fail while exercising a stale fixture observation. It was observed in the linked scheduled job and the unchanged full-file reproduction. Installed-payload isolation and live-consumer refusal must remain intact; the evidence does not justify relaxing production matching or restoring caller-profile inheritance.

## Additional information

A fixture-only correction is being validated. No earlier passing runtime has been independently established, and supported historical serialized handoffs are not ruled out by this test result.

issues.body:
## Summary

Coordinate the remaining work needed for Skill Workshop to capture useful procedural discoveries during ordinary work and demonstrate that an authorized skill revision improves a later task. Build on existing learning, proposal, evaluation and publication contracts; measure gaps before adding mechanisms.

This is a contributor proposal for discussion, not an accepted roadmap or a claim that OpenClaw lacks self-learning.

## Problem to solve

After an agent discovers a reliable procedure or receives a useful procedural correction, the operator needs to know whether that lesson was captured in the right skill, whether it was applied, and whether it works beyond the original example.

Those are separate outcomes. A pending proposal is not an active skill; a valid file is not behavioral proof; completion of maintenance does not necessarily mean a file changed. The proposed outcome is reliable, inspectable reuse—not more generated skill files.

The supplied static review identified possible coverage gaps between foreground authoring, immediate repair and delayed experience review. It did not measure their frequency or run behavioral trials. In particular, short-turn admission is a hypothesis to investigate, not sufficient evidence for lowering a scheduler threshold.

## Existing behavior and related ownership

OpenClaw already documents immediate repair and experience review. Workshop owns proposal application, while automatic background maintenance can edit its directory directly. These paths must not be given identical validation or publication guarantees by implication. See [self-learning](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/self-learning.md) and [Workshop ownership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/skill-workshop.md).

| Existing work | Relationship to this proposal |
|---|---|
| steipete’s merged [#100692](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100692), closing [#95477](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/95477) | Existing reusable-workflow suggestion work. Reconcile its current behavior and subsequent changes before proposing additional recognition guidance. This umbrella does not reopen the old “missing self-learning” premise. |
| [#123992](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/123992), closed with linked fix #123994 | Existing evaluator-result visibility work. Reuse or verify its projection rather than proposing outcome visibility as entirely new. |
| Zeus-Deus’s [#111943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/111943) | Adjacent model/reasoning policy proposal. No routing or model-policy change is included here. |
| anyech’s [#141102](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/141102) | Existing collection-review eligibility/diagnostics discussion. Keep that decision on its owning issue; reuse its eventual contract. |

This is a coordination proposal, not a takeover of those items. If an existing umbrella already owns the remaining scope, attach the work there instead of opening a competing tracker.

## Proposed solution

Keep proposals and publication in Workshop, loading and refresh in the skills runtime, and permissions and execution capacity with their existing owners. Prefer an optional evaluator plugin over a new core controller. A quality result never grants authority to publish.

### Dependency-ordered workstreams

These are candidate PR units, not existing PRs or assignments. A workstream proceeds only after its gap and owner boundary are established.

| Unit | Change and independent value | Dependency / acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Characterize learning coverage** | Establish a synthetic behavior matrix for manual, foreground and experience-review paths, including current modes and runtime eligibility. Reconcile #100692 and later changes. | First evidence milestone. Separate contract tests from live-model trials. A prompt-text assertion does not prove recognition. Submit a standalone characterization PR only if maintainers want that artifact; otherwise carry its useful fixtures with the first demonstrated fix. |
| **B. Close demonstrated foreground capture gaps** | Improve existing guidance or authoring behavior only where A demonstrates a missing case. Prefer the owning skill or pending proposal; create a distinct skill only for a distinct procedure. | Depends on A. Show correct capture without an explicit learning request, no duplicate for covered work, and no failed attempt stored as a working solution. Preserve publication semantics and mode/permission boundaries. |
| **C. Demonstrate reuse and explain outcomes** | Use existing status, usage and evaluation projections to connect a proposal, its applied revision and a later task. Add only missing information. | Baseline fixtures from A; integrate B if needed. A fresh session must discover and use the authorized revision on changed input. Distinguish pending, applied, evaluated, failed, unavailable and abstained states. Do not silently reload the current session. Coordinate collection diagnostics with #141102. |
| **D. Reference behavioral evaluator** | Exercise exact candidate and baseline revisions through the existing evaluation extension contract; produce interpretable task outcomes. Prefer an optional plugin. | Requires agreement on placement and supported API. Use isolated synthetic tasks, baseline/candidate comparison or a no-skill control where meaningful. An incorrect skill must fail; evaluator absence must not be reported as a pass. Storage and publication remain Workshop-owned. |
| **E. Bounded evaluation and revision** | Optionally coordinate evaluate → revise → re-evaluate → stop through existing owners, without another persistent scheduler or proposal store. | Depends on D and explicit policy agreement. Bound attempts, elapsed time and resource use; honor cancellation; invalidate stale results. Any required-evaluation policy must define missing/error/timeout/skipped outcomes without changing advisory behavior silently. |
| **F. Short-turn review admission, only if justified** | Admit a demonstrated high-value short-turn case through the existing reviewer when foreground capture remains insufficient. | Depends on A/B evidence and a maintainer admission-policy decision. Preserve quiet-time, capacity, identity and authority controls; avoid duplicate or recursive review. No blanket threshold reduction or model call after every message. Omit this unit if the earlier work solves the gap. |

**First milestone:** A, the justified portion of B, and C. Reliable capture and reuse must not depend on building an optimizer.

**Second milestone:** D, then E if accepted. F is an evidence-triggered branch, not a mandatory feature.

### Proof required

Use scenarios covering a useful new procedure, a correction to a used skill, an already-covered lesson, routine work, a successful recovery, an unresolved attempt, denied authority and unavailable runtime capability.

For reuse, withhold the original solved answer and change the input. For optimization, reserve validation cases not used to select edits. Correctness and critical regressions take precedence over token or tool-call savings. Human review or inconclusive results are legitimate outcomes.

Fixtures, skill text and transcripts are evidence, not permission. Tests must not act on real external accounts or collect private conversations, credentials or personal facts.

## Alternatives considered

- **Use existing guidance unchanged:** preferred if characterization demonstrates sufficient coverage; retain useful regression proof rather than adding a feature.
- **Rely on explicit learning requests:** remains valid, but does not establish whether useful discoveries are consistently captured during ordinary work.
- **Lower review thresholds globally:** adds work without establishing that the lost cases contain reusable lessons.
- **Build a new learning service:** duplicates existing owners and is unnecessary unless a specific missing contract is demonstrated.
- **Apply an evaluation gate only to proposals:** cannot support a universal validation promise while direct maintenance remains outside that path. Either state the narrower guarantee or obtain agreement on a coherent change to the owner contract.

## Impact

Affected users are operators relying on learned skills across sessions. The intended benefit is fewer repeated procedural corrections and clearer evidence about what was learned. Frequency and magnitude have not been measured; no reliability percentage, runtime regression or release blocker is asserted.

## Evidence/examples

The input research was a static review pinned to OpenClaw `ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d`; it reported no executed tests or agent trials. Its relevant source pointers are [foreground guidance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/agents/skill-workshop-prompt.ts), [review admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/skills/workshop/experience-review-scheduler.ts), and [proposal evaluation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/skills/workshop/service-evaluation.ts). These are research provenance, not freshly reproduced current-main defects.

The related tracker items and current documentation above were inspected while revising this proposal. Current-source history and behavioral reproduction remain the first implementation step. Hermes supplied UX inspiration in the original research; neither Hermes parity nor a claim of mandatory automatic benchmarking is an acceptance criterion.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself, after agreement on scope and ownership. I would start with the coverage evidence and the smallest demonstrated foreground gap.

## Additional information

**Maintainer decision requested:** does the first milestone belong on a new coordination issue or an existing owner surface? Separately, should a reference behavioral evaluator start as an external plugin, and is an optional required-evaluation/revision policy wanted at all? Neither question assumes approval for a new core contract.

Initial scope excludes a new memory backend, model training, registry, persistent controller, external skill installation, automatic sharing, protected third-party skill edits, model-routing changes, mandatory auto-publication, age-only retirement and same-session context replacement.

### Closure criteria

- [ ] Each workstream is completed with evidence, shown unnecessary, or explicitly deferred with maintainer agreement and a linked owner where appropriate.
- [ ] Accepted learning cases demonstrate correct capture and later reuse; negative controls show meaningful abstention and preserved authority.
- [ ] Evaluation claims identify the tested revision, environment and limits; untested direct maintenance receives no implicit validation badge.
- [ ] No duplicate proposal store, scheduler, publication authority or ownership takeover was introduced.
- [ ] Accepted changes include relevant regression tests, documentation and actual runtime evidence where required.

Intermediate PRs should use `Related: #<umbrella>` and explain which workstream they advance. Only the change satisfying all remaining closure criteria should close the umbrella. Preserve the original contributors’ authorship when extending or reusing their work.

issues.body:
### Summary

OpenClaw binds a model provider to a CLI runtime only when the registered CLI backend declares a `modelProvider` field. When the field is missing, `addCliRuntimeModelBinding` returns early without creating the binding and without emitting any diagnostic. Every model of that provider then falls through to the regular HTTP transport. Because such providers carry a `cli://` `baseUrl`, the user gets `Invalid URL: must be http or https` — an error that points at provider configuration while the actual cause is an incomplete plugin registration contract.

Nothing is logged at plugin load time and nothing is logged at call time. In agent runs the failure is invisible: the run completes with `status: ok` on a fallback model, and the run record contains no trace that the requested model was ever attempted.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (`59cb447`); also reproduced on 2026.10.2 (`b8952d4`)
- Self-hosted Gateway, Docker (OrbStack), Linux arm64, Node v24.21.0
- Plugin: `@jeehou/openclaw-cursor-cli` 0.0.6 (third-party), enabled, capabilities `cli-backend` + `text-inference`
- Provider: `models.providers.cursor-cli`, `baseUrl: "cli://cursor-agent"`, `api: "openai-completions"`, 44 models
- Binary `cursor-agent` 2026.10.14 works standalone; `CURSOR_API_KEY` present in the Gateway environment

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install a plugin that calls `api.registerCliBackend({ id, config, ... })` **without** a `modelProvider` field.
2. Declare a provider catalog with `baseUrl: cli://<binary>`.
3. Run:

```
openclaw infer model run --agent <id> --model cursor-cli/grok-4.7 --prompt "test"
```

### Expected behavior

Either the call is routed to the CLI backend, or the system reports the real cause — that the registered CLI backend declares no `modelProvider`, so no provider↔runtime binding exists. A registration missing a required contract field should be logged at plugin load time, naming the plugin.

### Actual behavior

```text
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] error provider=cursor-cli api=openai-completions
model=grok-4.7 message=Invalid URL: must be http or https
No text output returned for provider "cursor-cli" model "grok-4.7": Connection error..
```

In agent runs not even this appears: the run reports `status: ok` on the fallback model with no error and no diagnostic about the failed primary.

### Root cause

`dist/cli-backends-DNm7Vv7X.mjs`:

```js
function resolveCliBackendModelProvider(backend) {
  const provider = backend.modelProvider?.trim();
  return provider ? normalizeProviderId(provider) : void 0;
}

function addCliRuntimeModelBinding(bindings, params) {
  const provider = resolveCliBackendModelProvider(params.backend);
  const runtime  = normalizeProviderId(params.backend.id);
  if (!provider || !runtime) return;        // <-- silent drop
  bindings.set(`${provider}:${runtime}`, { provider, runtime, ... });
}
```

Built-in backends do set the field — `dist/cli-backend-BCcgnXM1.mjs:78` → `modelProvider: "anthropic"`, `dist/cli-backend-_dS2dNnJ.mjs:64` → `modelProvider: "google"` — so the requirement is real but undocumented for third-party authors and unvalidated at registration.

Verified in isolation (plugin copy + symlinked SDK, outside the Gateway):

```text
backend.id            = cursor-cli
backend.modelProvider = cursor-cli
BINDING OK -> cursor-cli:cursor-cli
args for grok-4.7/high: ["-p","--model","grok-4.7-high"]
```

Adding the single field restores routing. `registerCliBackend` appears 11 times in `dist`, so the extension point is live and is being called; only the binding step opts out.

### Impact

- Any third-party CLI backend written before `modelProvider` existed stops working after a Gateway upgrade, with no signal at all.
- The visible error points at the provider's `baseUrl`, sending the operator into model configuration while the defect is in the plugin registration contract. This cost hours of diagnosis here.
- The agent silently runs on a model the operator did not configure, and the run record preserves no evidence of the substitution.

### Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

1. Log a warning when a CLI backend registers without `modelProvider`, naming the plugin.
2. Or default `modelProvider` to `backend.id` when the field is absent (for this plugin the two are identical).
3. When a model whose `baseUrl` uses the `cli://` scheme reaches the HTTP transport, report the missing CLI runtime binding instead of an invalid URL.
4. Record the primary model's failure reason in the agent run record before falling back.
5. Document `modelProvider` as required in the `registerCliBackend` plugin API reference.

### Related

- #160317 — same subsystem (custom `registerCliBackend` plugin), different symptom: the static model catalog never reaches the configured `models.list` view. Possibly a shared root in how third-party CLI backends are wired into model resolution.

### Workaround

Patch the plugin locally to add `modelProvider: PROVIDER_ID` to the object returned by its `buildCliBackend()`. Lost on plugin update.

## Summary
On Windows, the owner WhatsApp DM repeatedly fails before replying with `Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn: <redacted-id>`. The same error persists after a fresh-session command, a targeted deletion/archive of the owner DM session, and upgrading OpenClaw from 2026.10.7 to 2026.10.8. This report is based on operator screenshots and sanitized logs; no deterministic isolated reproducer yet.

## Environment
- Windows, PowerShell 5.1, npm global OpenClaw
- OpenClaw 2026.10.7 -> 2026.10.8 (dc2523e)
- Windows Scheduled Task gateway, loopback 127.0.0.1:18789
- WhatsApp direct owner session on agent `main`; separate public group agent
- Cloud model attempts included gpt-oss and gemma4 (not established as model-specific)
- Custom operator-managed plugin loaded; possible interaction **unknown**

## Observed
1. A simple owner DM such as "Salam, sirf OK bolo" receives the generic "OpenClaw couldn't finish this request" message.
2. Gateway log contains:
```
diagnostic lane task error: lane=session:agent:main:whatsapp:direct:<redacted> durationMs=~6900 error="Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn: <uuid>"
Embedded agent failed before reply: Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn: <uuid>
```
3. After the owner DM session was deleted through the supported session CLI, the transcript was archived and cross-session cleanup completed. The **next new DM turn** failed with the same assertion and a new turn UUID.
4. After the upgrade to 2026.10.8, the same error occurred again on new owner DM turns.
5. Read-only `doctor --session-sqlite inspect --session-sqlite-agent main --json` earlier reported `integrityCheck: ok` and zero listed issues; this does **not** prove transcript-level correctness.
6. During the upgrade/startup, agent databases underwent background inspection and recovery; gateway health later responded but reported event-loop utilization 1.0 and degraded. Whether this load contributes to the turn assertion is unknown.

## Expected
An ordinary owner WhatsApp DM should start/admit a user turn and return a response, including after a fresh session, without requiring transcript deletion or manual database repair.

## Actual
Turn admission/append fails with the keyed-user assertion before any useful reply, across successive new turns.

## Request for maintainers
- Identify the exact turn ownership / transcript append condition that produces this assertion for ordinary WhatsApp direct turns.
- Clarify whether there is a safe, supported non-destructive recovery or diagnostic path on 2026.10.8.
- Advise whether custom plugin hooks, concurrent sessions, or database startup admission can trigger this mismatch and what minimal evidence is needed to distinguish them.

## Safety/privacy
No phone numbers, chat contents beyond a generic test phrase, session UUIDs, tokens, filesystem usernames, or private logs are included. No claim that the model, SQLite, or plugin is the root cause.

Related: #168456, #182487, #148053 (similar assertion, potentially different triggers).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Since 2026.9.6, almost every `POST /hooks/agent` on our gateway fails with `503 hook agent run did not start before admission timeout`. Preparing the run now takes about 15s, which is the same length as the hardcoded start deadline (`HOOK_AGENT_START_ADMISSION_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000` in `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`). A retry with the same idempotency key usually gets in, so the caller still gets a response, but late. On 2026.9.5 and earlier this never happened.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Gateway 2026.9.6 on Linux (systemd user service), multi-agent config (3 agents), `claude-cli` backend on the target agent.
2. POST to `/hooks/agent` with `{ name, agentId: "main", sessionKey: "hook:<caller>:<id>", idempotencyKey, message, deliver: false }`.
3. The first POST for a new message returns 503 at ~15.0s. Direct probes to a scratch session: 4 of 5 got the 503 at ~15.0s, and the fifth got in at 15.18s.

### Expected behavior

The run is admitted, or the caller can say it tolerates slow admission. The run is not cancelled just because its preparation was slow.

### Actual behavior

The run is cancelled with a 503 at exactly 15s. Our caller now retries at once with the same idempotency key, up to 2 times, and the retry usually lands. Counted from the caller's log after a full host reboot (fresh gateway, RSS ~1.8 GiB), messages 4, 6, 8 and 10 on one thread:

- every first attempt: 503 at 15s
- 3 of 4 got in on the first or second retry
- 1 of 4 used up all three attempts (503 after 45s) and only went through on the caller's next periodic flush, about a minute later

A reboot did not help. The same pattern continued an hour after boot, so this is not warm-up or long-uptime memory pressure. Before the reboot (gateway up about 9h) we also saw RSS 3.1-3.5 GiB and SQLite lock waits of 2-6s on the state DB during the probes, but the post-reboot runs fail the same way with low memory.

The gateway logs nothing while preparation runs, so we cannot tell which stage takes the 15s. The only nearby line is an occasional `slow SQLite transaction lock wait ... database=.../state/openclaw.sqlite ... operation=state.write elapsedMs=1463`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.6 (eb377ac)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (VM), Node v26.10.0

### Install method

npm global

### Model

claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5 (claude-cli backend, resumed sessions)

### Provider / routing chain

hooks/agent -> agent `main` -> claude-cli backend

### Additional provider/model setup details

3 agents configured. The main agent DB is ~83 MB, with ~400 session files (state migrated to SQLite in 2026.6).

### Logs

```
tandem: bridge admission timed out for <thread> (#4) after 15s, retrying (1/2)
tandem: bridge admission timed out for <thread> (#4) after 30s, retrying (2/2)
tandem: bridge hook failed for <thread> (#4): 503 after 45s; the messages are owed again and go out on the next flush
...
tandem: bridge admission timed out for <thread> (#6) after 15s, retrying (1/2)
tandem: bridge run for <thread> finished: ok after 93s
```

Response body on refusal: `{"error":"hook agent run did not start before admission timeout"}`

### Impact and severity

Every hook-driven reply starts 15-75s late. Without the caller-side retry, every first post fails. Messages are not lost, because the idempotency key keeps the failed admission retryable.

### Additional information

**Suggested fix.** `hooks.ts` already has a way out: dispatches with `admissionMode: "background"` skip the start deadline. The comment on `HookAgentDispatchPayload.admissionMode` says a fixed deadline "would cancel every item of a slow cold batch, cache nothing, and turn each redelivery into the same cold burst forever". That fits here too, but only internal fan-out can set it, and `/hooks/agent` callers cannot. Either of these would fix it for callers that already retry idempotently:

1. Let `/hooks/agent` callers request `admissionMode: "background"`, or
2. Make the start deadline configurable (for example `hooks.agentStartAdmissionTimeoutMs`).

Separately, a debug log per preparation stage (with elapsed times) would show where the 15s goes.

**Related, not duplicates:** #156455 (SQLite admission stalls under concurrency; its 5s refusal fix #154682 is already in 9.6 and does not cover this), #157686 (multi-second session-reclamation SQLite holds on 9.6), #145588 (cron/heartbeat run spends its budget in pre-run admission).

I searched for the exact error string and found no existing issue or PR. As of today, the constant on `main` is unchanged.

issues.body:
### What happened

During a genuine upstream provider outage (primary model accepting requests then stalling), the model fallback chain walked through **every** configured candidate and marked each one failed, even though the failure was a session/run-state error rather than a provider error. The turn died, and the operator-facing error copy named the **last fallback model tried** as the failing model — so an outage plus a run-displacement bug was surfaced as "model X is broken".

The chain never self-healed. It only recovered after the operator manually switched the primary model and restarted the Gateway.

This is a different angle from #148707 (reply loss itself): here the concern is the **behaviour and diagnosis of the fallback chain** under that condition. Full log evidence for the displacement itself was posted there: #148707 (comment).

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), npm global install, Node v24.20.0, Debian 13 x64
- Channel: Telegram, session `agent:main:main`
- Heartbeat every 45m (`isolatedSession: true`), plus inbound `sessions_send` from subagent workers and interactive operator turns
- Primary `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, 6 configured fallbacks

### Evidence

Provider timeout on the first candidate, then every subsequent candidate failing within ~30-50 ms with a harness error:

```
21:01:34 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_failed requested=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash candidate=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash reason=timeout next=google/gemini-3.8-flash detail=LLM request timed out.
21:01:34 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_failed candidate=google/gemini-3.8-flash reason=unknown next=openrouter/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free detail=Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot
21:01:34 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_failed candidate=openrouter/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free reason=unknown next=openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash detail=Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot
21:01:34 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_failed candidate=openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash reason=unknown next=openrouter/tencent/hy4-preview detail=Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot
21:01:34 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_failed candidate=openrouter/tencent/hy4-preview reason=unknown next=deepinfra/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct detail=Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot
21:01:34 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_failed candidate=deepinfra/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct reason=unknown next=deepinfra/Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct detail=Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot
21:01:34 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_failed candidate=deepinfra/Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct reason=unknown next=openai/gpt-5.6-terra detail=Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot
```

Embedded-run durations for those candidates were 44ms, 34ms, 39ms, 35ms, 31ms, 33ms — no model was actually consulted for any of them.

The operator-visible error, emitted while a fallback was on screen:

```
21:13:16 [telegram] embedded run agent end: runId=... isError=true model=gemini-3.8-flash provider=google error=Agent run failed (model: google/gemini-3.8-flash). rawError=Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn: 6f65b538-...
21:13:16 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_succeeded candidate=google/gemini-3.8-flash next=openrouter/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free
```

Note the `candidate_succeeded` marker recorded immediately after an `isError=true` run end.

A `config.patch` hot reload landed mid-incident; the next failure carried a different detail (flagged as a possible additional trigger, not a claim of causation):

```
21:46:35 [gateway] config.patch write actor=openclaw-control-ui ... changedPaths=models.providers.deepseek.models,models.providers.google.models,agents.defaults.model.primary,agents.defaults.model.fallbacks
21:46:36 [reload] config hot reload applied (agents.defaults.model.primary, agents.defaults.model.fallbacks)
21:50:20 candidate_failed candidate=google/gemini-3.8-flash reason=unknown detail=prepared model catalog owner config was replaced during the read (/home/radek/.openclaw/agents/main/agent)
```

### Expected

- A harness/run-state failure should be classified as such, and should not be reported as a per-candidate provider failure.
- The chain should not walk every remaining candidate when the failure is demonstrably not model-specific.
- Operator-facing failure copy should name the underlying condition, not the last fallback model that happened to be current (cf. #134103).
- Ideally: either queue/serialize concurrent turn sources on one session key, or re-admit the displaced turn once, rather than dropping it and giving up.

### Impact

Total loss of availability for ~50 minutes despite seven healthy, separately verified models. The misleading error copy ("Agent run failed (model: google/gemini-3.8-flash)") sent the operator down the wrong diagnostic path — the operator reasonably concluded the first fallback was broken and hand-switched models, which is what actually masked the real cause.

### Related

- #148707 — reply lost when a second run displaces an in-flight turn (same incident; full trace posted there)
- #144908 — "no active tool authority snapshot" recurs repeatedly
- #148053 — model fallback chain never consulted (reason=none); this report is the inverse failure mode

## Summary

The session tool preview omits `github_publish` and `github_identity_status` in managed Gateway conversations, even though the supported live tool path offers those tools. This makes the preview misleading when someone checks whether a conversation supports GitHub work.

## Reproduction and evidence

Reproduced at 620e1fb31537ea6a3df583f08173e66607fdd2e5 through the real `tools.effective` request handler, using the real effective-inventory resolver and tool registration. The fixture supplies an existing managed session and fixed external session/model facts; it performs no model request or GitHub mutation.

The added handler regression expects the returned inventory to contain `github_identity_status` and `github_publish`. It receives neither. The other 21 tests in `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.test.ts` pass in the same run.

```text
Expected: ["github_identity_status", "github_publish"]
Received: []
```

The source path explains this result: `resolveBaseToolsEffectiveInventory` does not pass the existing `githubPublicationAvailable` input into tool assembly. Registration omits both tools when that input is undefined. Live managed dispatch supplies it for supported OpenClaw tool runtimes independently of background credential discovery.

## Expected behavior

The prospective preview should include the supported GitHub tool surface and describe runtime-dependent actions accurately. Inclusion must remain separate from execution authority: current requester, workspace, credential and action checks still belong to the Gateway when an action is invoked. Unsupported runtimes and explicit tool restrictions must stay excluded.

## Environment and limits

Source checkout on Linux with Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0. This reproduction covers the request-handler-to-registration boundary with fixed external fixtures. A live guest/maintainer UI comparison is still pending; this report does not claim a successful GitHub operation or a completed fix.

issues.body:
## Environment
OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9), macOS, native OpenAI Responses route, 15-minute main-session heartbeat. Installed bundle filenames below identify the exact inspected build.

## Duplicate search (GitHub REST, 21 October 2026)
Searched `repo:openclaw/openclaw is:issue` with `heartbeat runtime-context`, `"heartbeat-filter"`, `"heartbeat" "filter" "context" in:title`, `"delivery" "stale"`, and `"Child results awaiting delivery"`. Results are bounded, not an exhaustive duplicate exclusion.

Closest matches:
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/166267 (closed): finished subagents retain requesterSettleWake forever, including already-delivered results. Strong match to the stale-continuation half; this issue adds current-version evidence (2026.10.5) rather than duplicating it.
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/155163 (open): orphaned delivery pointers cannot be cleared after task retention. Related operator-recovery gap; task-retention cause is NOT established here.
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/154834 (closed): failed child delivery repeats in every runtime context. Related symptom.
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/168339 (open): blocked notices remain queued after settle delivery. Related lifecycle bug, distinct notice path.
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/95796 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/113912 (closed): heartbeat filtering with thinking blocks. Related filtering history, not the adjacent custom-message condition demonstrated here.
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/95811 (closed): decouple delivery suppression and transcript stripping.

No exact adjacent-runtime-carrier duplicate identified among the inspected search results.

## Reproduction and actual behavior
1. Enable 15-minute scheduled heartbeats on a native Responses session, allowing model-only `openclaw.runtime-context` custom messages.
2. Let quiet heartbeat turns settle, including terminal heartbeat artifacts. Retain the normal adjacent runtime-context custom message between the heartbeat user message and its assistant/tool terminal artifacts.
3. Run the installed pure heartbeat-history filter on that existing bounded history.
4. The artifact scan encounters the custom message, stops before the terminal artifact, and leaves the quiet heartbeat in retained history.

Existing read-only audit: 351 message/custom-message records before and after filtering; zero removed; all 34 scheduled heartbeat prompts retained. Each heartbeat's persisted model projection contains roughly 4,192 characters despite a short visible stub. This is a filter-stage reproduction, not a claim that every provider transform was replayed.

Code evidence:
- `dist/heartbeat-filter-B3v9xWrh.mjs:113`, `resolveHeartbeatArtifactSpanEnd`: scan stops at a non-assistant/non-tool custom message.
- `dist/attempt-system-prompt-prepare-DDHkO-l9.mjs:3988`: heartbeat filter stage.
- Same bundle :3012–3016: projected prompt handling and append-only runtime carriers on native Responses.

Separately, 46 runtime carriers repeated 235,099 characters of pending child-result prose. Current targeted lifecycle read finds two terminal runs with `delivery.status=delivered`, cleanup timestamps set, but `requesterSettleWake={status:pending,attemptCount:0}`; two further terminal runs retain pending delivery, one also retaining a pending requester wake. Another visible-session run has suspended delivery with `suspendedReason=expiry`.

`hasOutstandingCompletion` in the same prepare bundle :2549–2557 returns true whenever a requesterSettleWake exists, including delivered runs. Pending rows at :2602 are selected from all visible records, not only the latest run per child. Rendering at :2639 repeats them. No supported operator acknowledgment/dismissal method was established in the installed CLI/tool surface. Session archive is not a demonstrated fix: it preserves transcript and changes session visibility, while this predicate examines registry delivery/continuation state.

## Expected behavior
Quiet heartbeat cleanup should safely traverse explicitly trusted runtime carriers associated with the heartbeat while retaining useful work and unrelated custom messages. Terminal acknowledged/superseded child deliveries should stop being emitted in future runtime carriers. Operators need a non-destructive per-run consume/dismiss mechanism that leaves visible sessions and transcripts intact.

## Suggested regression coverage
- Quiet heartbeat → trusted runtime carrier → terminal silent artifact, with and without tools/thinking.
- Useful heartbeat output, unrelated custom message and next real user turn must remain protected.
- Delivered child + leftover requesterSettleWake; superseded runs in the same child session; expired required delivery associated with a live visible session.
- Acknowledge/dismiss is idempotent, does not resend externally, preserves child/session history, and survives restart.

## Local mitigation and limits
Configured main heartbeat active hours 06:30–23:30 Australia/Sydney, retaining 15m cadence; defaults cache-TTL pruning shortened 55m→10m (per-agent pruning rejected by schema). These settings hot-applied. They do not repair heartbeat filtering or delivery state, and no post-change nonzero prune operation is yet verified. No core patches, session deletion, compaction/reset, or Gateway restart performed. Original audit evidence was reused, not re-audited.

(Diagnosis was done with an OpenClaw agent on my behalf; I had the findings and source references checked against the installed bundle before posting.)

issues.body:
## Feature request

Please make the **Decision assistance conversational tool-prefilter deadline configurable**, while retaining the current **500 ms default**.

This is a request for an operator-controlled latency trade-off, not for raising the default for everyone or changing tool permissions.

## Current behavior

On OpenClaw **2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)**, the consumer calls the shared Decision runtime with:

```ts
{
  purpose: "tool-prefilter.semantic-gate",
  rubricVersion: "9",
  timeoutMs: 500,
  // ...
}
```

The same fixed budget is still present in upstream `main` when checked on 2026-10-21:

- [Consumer implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-decision-prefilter.ts)
- [Documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/concepts/experimental-features.md#conversational-tool-filtering): “The current internal budget is 500 ms, not a configuration option.”

A longer timeout inside a Decision provider plugin does not solve this: the outer consumer's deadline expires first.

## Motivation

The Decision contract supports both local classifiers and hosted providers. A hosted provider can be usable for an operator's workflow yet routinely need more than 500 ms due to network and inference latency.

With a custom DashScope `DecisionProviderV1` adapter, thinking disabled and bounded JSON output, an illustrative small Boolean/Choice/Score batch using `qwen-flash` completed in approximately **0.94 seconds** in a standalone provider test. Explicit `decision_evaluate` calls also succeeded through the Gateway. These are individual samples, **not** a p95 benchmark or a measurement of the automatic prefilter's success rate.

The motivation is to allow a user to explicitly accept, for example, a **2,000 ms maximum budget**, rather than having no supported way to test this trade-off. A local one-line `500 -> 2000` dist patch is possible, but is fragile across upgrades. We have applied such a patch locally; it is **not yet evidence of end-to-end latency or token-cost savings**.

## Proposed behavior

- Keep the default at **500 ms** for backward compatibility.
- Add a validated positive-integer budget setting for this consumer, e.g. the following **proposed, not currently supported** configuration:

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      experimental: {
        decisionAssistance: true,
        decisionAssistanceTimeoutMs: 2000,
      },
    },
  },
}
```

The exact name/nesting is open to maintainer preference. An agent-level override would be useful if consistent with the existing configuration design, but a global setting alone would address the immediate need.

- Bound the accepted range to prevent accidentally unbounded waits.
- Apply the budget specifically to the automatic conversational tool-prefilter, not globally to explicit `decision_evaluate` or unrelated Decision consumers.
- Continue honoring cancellation, consumer authority, and any shorter parent deadline.
- Preserve current conservative behavior: ordinary timeout/unavailability retains the normal permitted tool surface; this must not grant tool permissions or bypass independent restrictions.
- Preserve the distinction between a caller-budget deadline and an actual provider outage; increasing/configuring this budget should not change shared provider circuit-breaker semantics.
- Include the effective budget in existing safe diagnostics, alongside evaluation status/reason and elapsed time, so operators can evaluate whether the extra wait is worthwhile. Do not log conversation evidence or credentials.
- Document that a larger budget can add foreground latency and is not a promise of faster or cheaper overall runs.

## Suggested validation

1. Unset configuration preserves 500 ms.
2. A configured 2,000 ms value is passed to the automatic consumer's evaluation call.
3. Invalid values are rejected by the schema.
4. A timely low-probability conversational result can propose filtering; action/uncertain results retain tools.
5. Deadline/unavailable outcomes preserve normal tools and existing health semantics.
6. `decisionAssistance: false` still prevents automatic inference regardless of the timeout setting.
7. Explicit `decision_evaluate` behavior is unchanged.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)
- Node.js: v24.20.0
- OS: Linux / WSL2
- Automatic consumer: built-in runtime, `tool-prefilter.semantic-gate`

issues.body:
## Summary
On released OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9), intentional `NO_REPLY` in an always-on Telegram group is treated as a missing required answer. The embedded runner requests a visible-answer continuation; if the model stays silent again, it posts a generic run-failure notice into the group. With two bot participants, notices/forced acknowledgements become fresh inputs and sustain a feedback loop.

This is a release-specific production report and request to track the Telegram/embedded-runner case and release coverage, not a claim that current main lacks a fix. Related #168306 (group prompt/default-policy mismatch) and #164946 (Discord bot reply loop, now closed; closure references bd5f760aecae47a8e26c10625005909091eac4ec as a main-only fix).

## Environment
- macOS, Node 26.12.0; global package installation.
- CLI and running gateway both 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9).
- Telegram polling; always-on group (`requireMention=false`), message-tool source delivery.
- Embedded runner, OpenAI provider; no fallback configured for the observed failing candidate.
- Initially neither agents.defaults.silentReply nor surfaces.telegram.silentReply was configured.
- Gateway connectivity check OK and Telegram connected during diagnosis.

## Reproduction
1. Admit ambient messages in a Telegram group with the default silent-reply policy.
2. Let the model follow the group prompt's instruction to remain silent for low-value chatter and return exactly `NO_REPLY`.
3. Observe a same-model visible-answer retry.
4. If the model repeats `NO_REPLY`, observe a public generic failure notice. If it obeys the retry instead, an unnecessary acknowledgement is published.
5. In a room with another bot receiving these messages, the emitted messages can trigger another round. Do not reproduce in a production group.

## Observed evidence (2026-10-20, UTC+03, identifiers removed)
The affected group had 17 `empty response detected` records and 3 exhausted retries during the incident. Conversation history contains intentional `NO_REPLY` messages at the matching times.

```text
22:23:23.777 agent/embedded: empty response detected: runId=<same-run> sessionId=<group> provider=<provider/model> stopReason=stop — retrying 1/1 with visible-answer continuation
22:23:28.697 agent/embedded: empty response retries exhausted: runId=<same-run> sessionId=<group> provider=<provider/model> attempts=1/1 — surfacing incomplete-turn error
22:23:28.720 model-fallback/decision: candidate_failed; reason=format; fallbackConfigured=false; fallbackStepFinalOutcome=chain_exhausted
```
The group then receives `OpenClaw couldn't finish this request...`. The peer also emitted `I finished the turn, but it did not produce a visible reply...`; its internal logs have not been independently verified, so the peer's exact failure path is not asserted here.

## Installed-code cause
- `src/shared/silent-reply-policy.ts`: group policy defaults to `disallow`.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/source-reply-delivery-mode.ts`, `resolveSourceReplyExpectation`: only an unmentioned group turn with policy `allow` becomes optional; otherwise required.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/terminal-resolution.ts`: required empty output triggers one visible-answer continuation, then incomplete-turn failure.
- Installed `src/auto-reply/reply` failure rendering also contains the literal `I finished the turn, but it did not produce a visible reply...` message.
- Telegram reply-to-bot detection sets `reply_to_bot` implicit mention; the admission function does not distinguish ambient bot acknowledgements from actionable human requests.

The group prompt still tells the agent to mostly lurk and stay silent. Thus default policy and model-facing guidance conflict. The failure is not evidence of a Telegram transport outage or provider rate limiting.

## Mitigation and limits
Set `surfaces.telegram.silentReply.group: "allow"`. Config validation passes. Calling the installed admission function with the saved config proves:

```text
Telegram group, WasMentioned=false -> optional
Telegram group, WasMentioned=true  -> required
```
This changes only Telegram silence policy, not other surfaces. Channel reload is deferred until active operations finish; no public failure-generating test was performed. Mentioned/reply-to-bot messages remain a limitation of this mitigation.

## Expected / requested
- Intentional silence for ambient group messages should not generate error notices or forced acknowledgements.
- Group instructions should agree with configured requiredness.
- Track release coverage/backport of the terminal-silence fix for the embedded Telegram path, with regression tests for unmentioned ambient input, implicit bot reply mentions, and message-tool-only delivery.
- Preserve genuine error reporting and required answers to actionable human requests; do not globally suppress all failures.

The policy-changing PR #153800 merged on 2026-09-20. The mechanism is confirmed on this installation, but the first locally affected upgrade has not been bisected.

AI-assisted report, published with the operator's explicit authorization. No private conversation content, chat identifiers, credentials, or raw logs attached.

issues.body:
## Summary

The managed `memory-core` Dreaming automation can encounter repeated narrative-generation failures, finish with pending narratives, and still record the cron run as fully successful with zero errors. Pending narrative work is not retried after Gateway admission recovers; the next scheduled attempt remains the following day.

This makes a degraded Dreaming run invisible to normal automation health checks and failure notifications.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.3 (`1391f7c`)
- Linux x64
- Node.js 24.20.0
- Built-in `memory-core`
- Managed `Memory Dreaming Promotion` automation
- Light, REM, and deep phases enabled

## Observed behavior

During one managed run, Gateway admission was draining. Narrative generation repeatedly failed and used fallback output:

```text
[plugins] memory-core: narrative generation failed for light phase: Gateway is draining; new tasks are not accepted
[plugins] memory-core: narrative generation used fallback for light phase because the narrative run failed (...)
[plugins] memory-core: narrative generation failed for rem phase: Gateway is draining; new tasks are not accepted
[plugins] memory-core: narrative generation failed for deep phase: Gateway is draining; new tasks are not accepted
```

One later attempt also failed while inspecting Codex processes:

```text
[plugins] memory-core: narrative generation failed for light phase: Cannot inspect Codex processes. Process inspection exceeded its deadline. Retry when the host is responsive.
```

The promotion owner then repeatedly logged:

```text
[plugins] memory-core: dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=26, candidates=4, applied=0, failed=0, degraded=0, narrativesPending=5).
```

Despite `narrativesPending=5` and the explicit narrative failures, the managed automation state was:

```json
{
  "lastRunStatus": "ok",
  "lastStatus": "ok",
  "consecutiveErrors": 0,
  "lastFailureNotificationDeliveryStatus": "not-requested",
  "lastDurationMs": 224675
}
```

The next run remained scheduled for the normal daily interval. No bounded retry was scheduled after Gateway admission recovered.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable the managed `memory-core` Dreaming automation with narrative phases enabled.
2. Start a Dreaming run while the Gateway is draining and rejecting new task admission.
3. Allow narrative generation to fail and fallback handling to run.
4. Observe the final `dreaming promotion complete` record and the managed automation state.

## Expected behavior

At least one of the following should happen:

1. The run records a degraded or failed status when narrative generation fails or `narrativesPending > 0`, so automation health/failure notification surfaces the condition; and/or
2. Pending narratives receive a bounded retry after Gateway admission returns, with durable retry state and no duplicate diary writes.

The completion metrics, automation status, and notification state should agree.

## Actual behavior

- Narrative generation fails repeatedly.
- Fallback diary entries may be written.
- Five narratives remain pending.
- Completion reports `failed=0, degraded=0`.
- The automation records `ok`, zero consecutive errors, and requests no failure notification.
- No retry occurs before the next daily schedule.

## Impact

Operators see a healthy managed automation even though Dreaming work is incomplete. A transient Gateway drain can silently defer narrative work for at least one schedule interval, and ordinary health checks do not expose the degraded result.

## Duplicate check

Searched open issues for `narrativesPending`, Dreaming fallback/status, Gateway draining, restart recovery, and managed Dreaming failures. Related Dreaming timeout, event-loop, and crash-recovery reports exist, but none found covered the specific invariant that a run with explicit narrative failures and pending work is persisted as `ok` with no retry or failure notification.

## Privacy

Paths, hostnames, agent names, session identifiers, credentials, prompts, and memory contents have been removed. The counts and sanitized log messages above are sufficient to describe the observed state transition.
