issues.body:
## Contract clarification, not a confirmed upstream defect

Which existing host owner should reconcile a retained native completion obligation after loss of its original process-local review owner, when original execution or delivery effects remain unknown?

This arose while reviewing a local experimental completion/review integration. Its additional review guards are local, not claimed to be upstream features. No stock-runtime reproduction or upstream root cause is established. I am looking for the supported contract before integrating further, not asking to deserialize opaque custody or replay the child.

### Versions and source evidence

Reviewed core 2026.10.5, Codex 2026.10.3 with local corrections, and upstream main pinned to `e8d8145cd62feac71d6c65636c948a74b7f799d6`. Main is not assumed equivalent to the installed versions.

- [Restart recovery documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8d8145cd62feac71d6c65636c948a74b7f799d6/docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md#L259-L288) distinguishes admitted channel-completion recovery from retained native assignments requiring a new parent registration; missing historical ownership remains unknown.
- [Completion custody](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8d8145cd62feac71d6c65636c948a74b7f799d6/src/agents/agent-harness-completion-custody.ts) authenticates process-local objects and captures current requester authority. Fresh capture alone does not appear to attest an old review obligation.
- [Completion recovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8d8145cd62feac71d6c65636c948a74b7f799d6/src/agents/agent-harness-completion-recovery.ts#L184-L206) retains admitted source identities; the comment explicitly says these no longer address task_runs.
- [Transport registration and orphan cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8d8145cd62feac71d6c65636c948a74b7f799d6/extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-process-registration.ts#L76-L134) provide real durable process cleanup, but do not themselves return an assignment-bound review ACK or completion receipt.

These supported recovery components do exist. The unresolved point is their authoritative composition for the local obligation, not an assertion that recovery is generally absent.

### Exact decision requested

1. Is there an existing supported operation/owner that binds the original assignment, requester lifecycle, admitted completion input and ACK/consume evidence to original-generation physical settlement and unresolved submission/delivery ownership, without treating recovery as new native admission? Please identify the symbol/version and required durable evidence, including the owner-killed or root-already-gone case.
2. If this falls outside the supported recovery contract, should the local obligation remain unresolved indefinitely? What supported operator disposition can record that fact without implying delivery, clearing unknown effects, resetting attempts or replaying the original work?

A pointer to an existing owner or explicit unsupported-case disposition is sufficient. No request to update, reset a production session, create a parallel persistence layer or reconstruct a serialized capability is implied.

### Related work checked

- #159943: original-owner correlated queue/subagent delivery settlement.
- #153550: terminal completion delivery reconciliation.
- #145117: durable terminal control-plane receipts.
- #176673: durable-predecessor recovery tests.

Those cover related boundaries; I did not find the exact composition/disposition answer in their descriptions. Please redirect if this question belongs on one of those threads.

All observations here are source review. No historical work was replayed and no live recovery success is claimed.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In a Slack huddle `bidi` session that uses managed browser audio capture, the realtime bridge stays up past the join response once #173898 is applied, and the model starts producing output. About 6 s later, a capture pull fails with `Meeting browser audio capture failed: Error: browser request timed out`, and the session closes (`providerConnected: false`, `bridgeClosed: true`). The participant hears nothing.

This looks like the next failure after #173896. It was seen only with #173898 applied.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build OpenClaw from #177357 (Slack huddle call-window support) with #173898's production changes applied.
2. Linux host: Chrome 155 on Xvfb, PipeWire-Pulse with the managed `OpenClaw Meeting Audio` device, and microphone permission allowed for `app.slack.com`.
3. Configure `plugins.entries.slack-huddles.config.realtime.voiceProvider: "openai"`.
4. While a person is in the huddle, run `openclaw slackhuddles join https://app.slack.com/huddle/T…/C… --mode bidi`.

### Expected behavior

Capture keeps pulling participant audio after the join returns, and the assistant's reply plays into the huddle.

### Actual behavior

```text
17:40:45.807 realtime voice bridge starting: strategy=bidi provider=openai model=gpt-realtime-2.1
17:40:46.455 talk session.ready
17:40:47.083 res ✓ slackhuddles.join 12595ms
17:40:47.802 talk output.audio.started
17:40:48.010 talk output.audio.done
17:40:48.031 talk turn.started
17:40:53.085 WARN Meeting browser audio capture failed: Error: browser request timed out
17:40:53.087 talk session.closed
```

A second run, with the same setup, timed out during the join itself (`slackhuddles.join … errorMessage=Error: browser request timed out`).

### OpenClaw version

Source build at #177357 head `ed23110` plus #173898 (production files only).

### Operating system

Debian 12 container (Node 26), Chrome 155 on Xvfb.

### Install method

Source checkout, `pnpm build`, Gateway started with `node openclaw.mjs gateway run`.

### Model

gpt-realtime-2.1 (default for the OpenAI realtime voice provider)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> openai realtime (gateway-relay)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Default realtime model; no custom audio commands; managed PipeWire-Pulse backend.

### Logs

See Actual behavior.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

None beyond the logs above.

### Impact and severity

Slack huddle talk-back cannot complete a turn. Transcribe mode is unaffected.

### Additional information

A timing measurement narrows it down. In a later run, lab-only timing logs around `runMeetingBrowserAct` (lock wait, run time, caller) recorded:

```text
FAIL wait=0ms    run=5001ms budget=4999ms  callCapture (pull)                -> browser request timed out
ok   wait=4344ms run=299ms                  readMeetingTranscriptWithBrowser  (queued behind the pull)
FAIL wait=0ms    run=1ms   (repeated)       readMeetingTranscriptWithBrowser  -> Gateway requester authority changed
```

- **The tab lock is not the cause.** The pull acquired the per-tab lock immediately; a lock timeout would report "timed out waiting for browser tab control".
- **Where the request stalled is not established.** The pull acquired the per-tab lock immediately, then the browser request timed out after five seconds. The normal in-page read does not wait, but its cleanup branch does (`browser-audio-capture-source.ts:27`), and request handling or a busy page are also possible.
- **#173898 leaves one path uncovered.** Caption and transcript reads (`readMeetingTranscriptWithBrowser`) still fail with `Gateway requester authority changed` after the join returns. That is the same class as #173896, on a path #173898 does not cover.

Caveats: this was observed on a container host with a virtual screen and no audio hardware, with #173898 applied. Which side of the `/act` request consumes the 5 s is not yet split.

issues.body:
## Summary

Requesting maintainer guidance on the supported writable filesystem layout for native Doctor startup with a read-only Docker root, and on obtaining a path-bearing diagnostic for a fatal native filesystem error.

**An independent clean minimal reproducer is not yet verified.** The observations below come from isolated qualification with copied synthetic state. We have not established an upstream defect or the fatal operation's target.

## Pinned environment

- OpenClaw v2026.10.5, Linux ARM64; Docker Desktop on Apple Silicon.
- Image: `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw@sha256:f40d1e66fd14d8c5b49c832f4100f83b53fdc01f5108f7db11de38fd0ee6dbe5`.
- Upstream `tini -s -- node /app/docker-entrypoint.mjs` entrypoint and native CLI respawn preserved; no source patches or Doctor bypass.
- UID/GID `501:20`; read-only container root; all capabilities dropped; `no-new-privileges`; 2 GiB memory limit, 1.5 CPUs, 128 PIDs.
- Diagnostic network `none`; no published ports, backend/model connectivity or real credentials.
- Environment: `HOME=/state`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/state`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/run/config/openclaw.json`. `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY` was not set.

| Container path | Mount |
| --- | --- |
| `/state` | Writable bind of copied synthetic state |
| `/workspace` | Writable bind of copied synthetic workspace |
| `/run/config/openclaw.json` | Read-only single-file bind |
| `/run/secrets/gateway_token` | Read-only dummy credential file |
| `/tmp` | tmpfs: `rw,nosuid,nodev,mode=1777,size=134217728` |
| `/state/.cache` | tmpfs: `rw,nosuid,nodev,mode=0700,uid=501,gid=20,size=134217728` |

No writable mount exists at `/state.update-captures`.

## Observations

The native Gateway entrypoint's Doctor pass failed before Gateway readiness. A separate native Doctor execution used:

```text
node openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive
```

Completed failing executions reported:

```text
Original state capture was unavailable: Could not prepare Git backup repository: EROFS during mkdir. Doctor will continue; inspect retained evidence manually before restoring state.
Doctor could not complete maintenance. Check the reported service state and resolve the failure.
openat2 beneath root: Read-only file system (os error 30)
```

These are two distinct findings:

1. **Confirmed advisory failure:** `mkdir /state.update-captures` targets the read-only root outside writable `/state`. The captured stack goes through fs-safe 0.25.0 `root-directory.js:106`, private snapshot repository initialization and `update-recovery-baseline-capture`. Pinned source resolves `<state-dir>.update-captures`; original capture catches the failure and continues.
2. **Unattributed fatal failure:** the later `openat2` message provides no target, open flags or actionable caller. We have not established whether it involves config/secret storage, a sibling staging file, another path outside writable mounts, or something else. The advisory mkdir is not asserted to cause it.

Before adding the cache-only tmpfs, Doctor had failed during SQLite shared-state snapshot cleanup under `/state/.cache/openclaw/`. That earlier cleanup error did not recur with the cache tmpfs; the later fatal EROFS remained. This is an observation, not a verified general fix.

The inherited image healthcheck separately reported `agents.defaults: Unrecognized key: "memorySearch"`, then offline-maintenance read refusals. Its relationship to the fatal error is unknown.

## Diagnostic limitations

Native debug output did not expose the fatal path/cause. A fixed-port inspector initially attached only to the launcher because its respawned child inherited the occupied port.

A subsequent single bounded execution with `--inspect-brk=127.0.0.1:0` attached both launcher and child on container loopback before release, without publishing debug ports. Exception-breakpoint overhead consumed the 80-second bound after 1,763 child pauses. Only the advisory mkdir was captured; **the fatal error was not reached/captured in that inspector execution**. Docker then delivered normal SIGTERM; Doctor reported an incomplete-cleanup warning in the disposable copy, and the container exited 143 without OOM. That interrupted copy is not treated as a clean baseline.

## Questions

1. Is native Gateway/Doctor startup supported with a read-only container root, and what is the minimum persistent writable layout, including private sibling `<state-dir>.update-captures` storage?
2. For an externally managed read-only single-file config bind in v2026.10.5, is `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1` the intended mode, and must legacy settings such as `agents.defaults.memorySearch` be migrated externally before startup?
3. What supported focused diagnostic or breakpoint can expose the fatal fs-safe `openat2` target, operation and caller without disabling fs-safe, changing application code or making the root writable?

## Related reports — unconfirmed matches

- #173564: repeated full pre-repair captures during Docker startup. Related capture lifecycle context; not established as the same EROFS.
- #174842: Doctor snapshot loop and interruption handling. Different reported preconditions; no confirmed relationship to this fatal error.

No credentials, personal host paths, internal infrastructure identifiers, copied state archives or process-memory dumps are attached. No further local diagnostic or corrective retry has been performed after the bounded child-inspector attempt.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In the Control UI, **Files → More file actions → Attach to session** can silently discard the selected file when the pane refreshes while its download is pending. The file and destination can remain unchanged and authorized throughout the operation.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a saved text file from the current session's Files panel. Keep the composer enabled.
2. Enter an unsent message and optionally add another attachment.
3. Choose **More file actions → Attach to session**.
4. Resize the browser while the selected file is still downloading, then let the download complete.

For deterministic reproduction, I held delivery of the actual successful file-download HTTP response while resizing, then released that same response. I also reproduced the refresh boundary through the complete Control UI browser harness with a deferred file-download response.

### Expected behavior

The selected file should appear once in the existing message draft, without sending it. The documented action preserves unsaved draft work and cancels when the file or session changes; an equivalent pane refresh should not cancel it. See [the Control UI documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/faa38148f2c5ba3fe8f69bd3ae0150c87edf7758/docs/web/control-ui.md#session-files).

### Actual behavior

The live download returned HTTP 200 with 786 bytes. After the resize, the pending-read balance returned to zero and no attachment appeared when the response was released. The original file stayed selected, the existing attachment and message text remained, and no message was sent automatically. An immediate-download control succeeded, so the failure depends on a refresh during the asynchronous read.

### OpenClaw version

Control UI source faa38148f2c5ba3fe8f69bd3ae0150c87edf7758 (2026.10.9). Live Gateway source 9ca944e298b7ed0881f7c37abb5d5032fafc3c31, with no differences in the affected download API/protocol contract. The standalone browser reproduction used the current UI source.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0.1 for live proof; Linux for the standalone Chromium reproduction.

### Install method

Source-backed development UI and an isolated live Gateway.

### Model

No model request is involved in the failing attachment action.

### Provider / routing chain

Control UI → same-origin Gateway proxy → native file download.

### Evidence and likely cause

During the reproduced refresh, the selected file/download function, destination session/client, attachment read lifecycle/signal, connection epoch and authority fields all stayed equal. Three composer callbacks and the artifact-download resolver received new function identities. The attachment operation compares those callbacks by reference and retires on a mismatch. The callbacks are recreated by `chat-state-controller.ts` and `chat-pane-resource-presentation.ts` during an otherwise equivalent pane render.

### Impact and severity

This intermittently blocks adding an open file to a draft without showing an error. No source-file or existing-draft loss was observed. Both the controlled live refresh and standalone browser refresh reproduced the missing attachment; the immediate live control passed.

`agents/vandernok/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` is 1.6 GB after 17 days (2026.10.5): 199,166 `transcript_events` across 44 sessions (top three ≈ 39k, 24k and 19k events; ≈ 1.9 GB logical, 92k rows zstd-compressed). `session.maintenance.coldStorage.afterDays=30` has nothing to move yet.

During Gateway stop the log shows repeated `slow SQLite transaction ... operation="session transcript export snapshot"` (2.3–2.7 s each), and the stop ends with `stop_close_failed` (plugins onnx/tavily not released within 5 s) on 2026-10-12, 10-15, 10-20 and 10-22. A `pre-startup-migration` backup of the same size is kept next to the DB (total ≈ 3.2 GB for one agent).

**Asks:** a documented retention knob for active-session transcripts, and a way to bound the shutdown snapshot work.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The ordinary attachment UI test group completes all 159 assertions but exits with an uncaught native Undici abort error on Node 24.22.1. A standalone Node reproduction isolates the same exception to aborting a `data:` response before consuming its body. The observed impact is a failed validation process; no browser or Gateway product failure is established.

### Steps to reproduce

On Node 24.22.1, which bundles Undici 7.30.1, run:

```sh
node --input-type=module -e '
const controller = new AbortController();
const response = await fetch("data:text/plain,Restored%20text", { signal: controller.signal });
console.log(response.status);
controller.abort();
'
```

The response status is 200, then Node exits 1 from the abort listener. In an unchanged OpenClaw checkout at `06cd3e0f306be1bdd0ae2efe5a3fbe2188169bb9`, the native selected UI group containing these files reproduces the same stack:

- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-state-render-lifecycle.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-recovery.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-state-queued-edit.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-state.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-file-session-attachment.test.tsx`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-file-session-attachment-lifetime.test.tsx`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-attachments.test.tsx`

The full tree and working diff matched that commit before execution. The unchanged attachment file alone also reproduces the exception: all 30 assertions pass, followed by the identical unhandled error and exit 1. No assertions, worker configuration, dependencies or runtime version were changed.

### Expected behavior

Cancellation should settle through the request/body cancellation result without an unrelated uncaught TypeError. The same runtime's pending-body HTTP control reports `AbortError` and exits normally. The attachment group should preserve its current assertions and finish without an unhandled exception.

### Actual behavior

All seven files and 159 assertions pass, but Vitest reports one uncaught exception attributed to `chat-attachments.test.tsx`, and the native test process exits 1. The plain Node child also exits 1 with the same stack. Passing assertions do not establish a successful suite.

### OpenClaw version

Source commit `06cd3e0f306be1bdd0ae2efe5a3fbe2188169bb9`. The same group failure was previously reproduced on unchanged `faa38148f2c5ba3fe8f69bd3ae0150c87edf7758`.

### Operating system

Linux x64, native Blacksmith Testbox runner.

### Install method

Maintained native remote test entrypoint with locked dependencies: Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Vitest 5.0.5, bundled Undici 7.30.1.

### Model

Not applicable: no model request is involved.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable: the minimal failing request is an inline data URL and uses no network service.

### Logs

```text
Test Files  7 passed (7)
Tests       159 passed (159)
Errors      1 error
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')
    at abortFetch (node:internal/deps/undici/undici:13198:20)
    at AbortSignal.<anonymous> (node:internal/deps/undici/undici:13112:11)
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Standalone controls used separate Node processes on the same runner and runtime, with no OpenClaw imports, Solid, JSDOM, Vitest, mocks, fake timers or uncaught-exception handlers:

| Scenario | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Abort data URL after response delivery, before body consumption | Exit 1; identical uncaught TypeError |
| Consume the same data URL body, then abort | Exit 0; exact `Restored text` body |
| Abort before starting the same data URL fetch | Exit 0; expected `AbortError` |
| Abort an HTTP response with its body still pending | Exit 0; expected `AbortError` |

### Impact and severity

The validation group exits nonzero despite passing assertions. The failure is reproduced on current source and is also reported in #182477. It must remain visible when qualifying other changes. These results establish this Node/bundled-Undici version; they do not establish a guest-facing attachment defect, browser failure or data loss.

### Additional information

Source inspection identifies a valid cancellation path: restored pasted text starts an excerpt read, and restoring that text into the composer removes its card and aborts the outstanding excerpt. The reader already catches rejected work and clears its timeout. A single-test reduction failed earlier on cold lazy-preview rendering and did not reach this cancellation, so it is not evidence against the full group failure.

In [Node v24.22.1's bundled fetch implementation](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v24.22.1/deps/undici/src/lib/web/fetch/index.js), `abortFetch` dereferences a stream controller for a readable response. The data-scheme path constructs its body without the controller assignment used by the HTTP network path. This matches the native controls. No runtime upgrade, replacement fetch implementation, suppression or production workaround has been applied; a correction must preserve real cancellation failures and the existing attachment assertions.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a Linux systemd-user installation, `openclaw update repair` exits 0 with warnings while skipping Doctor and plugin maintenance: service inspection exhausts its deadline, automatic service handling is skipped, and maintenance then refuses because the still-running Gateway owns shared state.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on the affected installation on 2026-10-19; reproduction on a clean installation is NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

1. Use OpenClaw 2026.9.8 with its enabled systemd user Gateway running and post-update maintenance pending.
2. Run `openclaw update repair` against the same installation/state directory.
3. Observe preflight, target config validation, and config snapshot complete, followed by manager-inspection timeout and skipped Doctor maintenance.
4. Inspect the state-owner record, service PID, database holders, and file locks using read-only commands.

The operator's latest run took 85.3585 seconds and exited 0. Earlier repair attempts on this installation also left maintenance pending. Some earlier diagnostics ran in a restricted coding-agent sandbox; the warning also reproduced outside that sandbox with local host execution. No independent SSH-shell reproduction is claimed.

### Expected behavior

`openclaw update repair --help` describes reconciling abandoned updates and running Doctor repair/plugin convergence. When ownership or service inspection prevents maintenance, retain the refusal, but provide a concrete actionable outcome identifying the live owner and failed inspection phase. Do not imply the pending maintenance completed or bypass custody/stop guards.

### Actual behavior

The command prints `Update finalization completed with warnings.`, exits 0, and leaves Doctor/plugin maintenance pending. It says service inspection is unavailable and refers to a manually launched Gateway, although direct service inspection identifies an enabled, active systemd-user Gateway. Its manager error does not identify which manager/custody/admission inspection exhausted the deadline. The final contention detail is truncated after the word `stop`.

The observed blocker is OpenClaw's state-ownership fence held by the live Gateway. A long-running SQLite write transaction was not established by the inspection below.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.8 (fc23bc8); running Gateway self-reported 2026.9.8 with connectivity probe OK in `openclaw gateway status --deep`.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Linux; Node.js 26.8.1 executing OpenClaw.

### Install method

npm global under a Linuxbrew prefix; systemd user service `openclaw-gateway.service`.

### Model

openai/gpt-6-sol (not exercised by this maintenance reproduction).

### Provider / routing chain

No inference request involved; local CLI -> systemd user manager / local shared-state ownership.

### Logs

Sanitized excerpts from the latest operator run:

```text
Exit code: 0
Duration: 85.3585 seconds
Update finalization completed with warnings.
finalize:preflight: completed
finalize:targetConfigValidation: completed
finalize:configSnapshot: completed
finalize:doctor: in_progress

Gateway service inspection is unavailable; automatic service restart was skipped.
Restart the Gateway you launched manually after the update.
Any recorded service definition was left unchanged; inspect it with `openclaw gateway status --deep`.
The systemd manager inspection deadline expired while probing the manager or checking custody/admission guards.
This does not establish that the user session bus is unavailable.

finalize:doctor: skipped
Doctor could not enter maintenance. GatewayStateOwnerContentionError:
OpenClaw state database is busy at $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite.

Doctor and plugin maintenance remain pending. Resolve the maintenance refusal,
then run openclaw update repair.
```

The JSON repair variant on the same host returned `status: warning`, `mode: finalize`, `restart: false`, and a deferred Doctor phase.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Read-only inspection after the operator's run:

```text
State owner record:
  pid: 993979
  role: gateway
  createdAt: 2026-10-19T15:30:41.125Z
  port: 18789

systemctl --user show openclaw-gateway.service -p MainPID -p ActiveState -p SubState
  MainPID=993979
  ActiveState=active
  SubState=running

lsof on shared-state SQLite, WAL and SHM:
  Only PID 993979 listed as holder of these database files.

lslocks snapshot for shared state:
  PID 993979 POSIX READ 1073741826..1073742335 openclaw.sqlite
  PID 993979 POSIX READ 128..128 openclaw.sqlite-shm
  No write lock shown on these shared-state database files in this snapshot.
```

The original `openclaw update` process also remained alive awaiting its triage child, but was not listed as a holder of these database files. It is unknown whether this ancestry affected custody/admission inspection; please distinguish intended triage refusal from a timeout or misleading recovery guidance.

### Impact and severity

One observed installation. Post-update Doctor/plugin convergence remains unfinished across the observed repair attempts. Re-running the recommended repair produces the same maintenance deferral rather than convergence. No data loss was observed. The Gateway eventually became RPC-reachable, so the report is not claiming continuous Gateway downtime or SQLite corruption.

### Additional information

Related reports: #169865 (manager inspection deadline despite responsive direct systemd queries), #171096 (repair advice encounters a running Gateway ownership fence).

This report concerns repair admission and its diagnostics/outcome. The preceding update's separate package-publication refusal is not claimed to be caused by SQLite contention.

No ownership locks were deleted, no capability refusals were overridden, and no stop-guard bypass was attempted. Configuration, history, and databases were preserved. Please provide a supported maintenance path that respects triage custody and later operator stops.

issues.body:
# [Feature]: `cron list` supports filtering by schedule kind, run status, trigger, and sorting

## Summary

Expose the already-supported `cron.list` RPC filters on the `openclaw cron list` CLI: `--schedule-kind`, `--run-status` (last run status), `--trigger`, `--sort-by`, and `--sort-dir`. The RPC/service layer already implements all of these; the CLI currently only forwards `--all`, `--agent`, and `--query`.

## Problem to solve

`openclaw cron list` is the operator's primary way to browse automations, but it cannot filter or sort them. An operator with many jobs cannot ask the CLI for "all `every`-scheduled jobs", "jobs whose last run failed", or "jobs with a conditional trigger" without pulling the full list and filtering locally.

This is a pure plumbing gap. The full filtering/sorting capability already exists end-to-end on the server side:

- `listPage` in `src/cron/service/ops-read.ts` accepts `CronListPageOptions` with `scheduleKind`, `lastRunStatus`, `trigger`, `sortBy`, `sortDir`, `enabled`, `agentId`, `query`, `limit`, `offset`.
- The `cron.list` RPC schema (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts`) defines all of those fields.
- The RPC implementation (`src/gateway/server-methods/cron-list.ts`) forwards every one of them to `listPage`.

But the CLI stops at three filters. `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.ts` only registers `--all`, `--agent`, `--query`, `--json`, and `listCronJobsFromGateway` in `src/cli/cron-cli/list-jobs.ts` types its filters as `Pick<CronListPageOptions, "includeDisabled" | "agentId" | "query">`. The remaining five filters exist on the server but have no CLI surface.

The gap: server-side capability already complete; CLI entry point missing.

## Proposed solution

Add five read-only flags to `openclaw cron list`, each mapping directly onto the corresponding `CronListPageOptions` field that the RPC already accepts:

- `--schedule-kind <kind>` — filter by schedule kind: `at | every | cron | on-exit | stream | event`.
- `--run-status <status>` — filter by last run status: `ok | error | skipped | unknown | all` (mirrors `CronRunStatusSchema` + `unknown`).
- `--trigger <mode>` — filter by trigger type: `conditional | unconditional`.
- `--sort-by <field>` — sort key, default `nextRunAtMs`.
- `--sort-dir <dir>` — `asc | desc`.

### CLI/API changes

`openclaw cron list` gains the five flags above. Existing flags (`--all`, `--agent`, `--query`, `--json`) are unchanged. The `listCronJobsFromGateway` filter type is widened from `Pick<CronListPageOptions, "includeDisabled" | "agentId" | "query">` to include the new fields, and the command forwards them into the `cron.list` RPC payload.

Example:

```
openclaw cron list --schedule-kind every --run-status error --sort-by nextRunAtMs --sort-dir desc
```

### Design details

- No new server logic. The change is confined to the CLI adapter: register the flags, validate/enumerate the allowed values (reusing the existing cron-simple value sets already in `cron.ts`), and forward them verbatim.
- The five flags are orthogonal to `--query` (text search) and `--agent`, so they compose naturally.
- Non-goals: no new filter semantics, no changes to `cron runs`, no changes to the server-side `CronListPageOptions`.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep the CLI minimal** (status quo): operators must fetch the full page and filter/sort client-side, or use the raw `cron.list` RPC. The server already bears the cost of these filters; not exposing them leaves the CLI as the only consumer without them.
- **Add only one or two flags** (e.g. just `--schedule-kind`): narrower but still leaves the same plumbing gap for the others; the five are one homogeneous forward-and-expose change with a shared precedent.

## Impact

- Affected: operators who manage many automations and want to filter/sort from the terminal.
- Severity: low (read-only additive flags); no behavior change for existing invocations.
- Frequency: per use of `cron list`; entirely opt-in.
- Consequence: `cron list` output can be narrowed/sorted without a full dump.

Model/CLI surface: additive flags only. Config/defaults: none. Security/permissions: read-only; the new filters respect the same caller-scope agentId handling already in `cron-list.ts`. Compatibility: purely additive; existing flag combinations unchanged.

## Evidence/examples

The server-side capability already exists on `main`:

- `src/cron/service/ops-read.ts:174` — `listPage` accepts `scheduleKind`/`lastRunStatus`/`trigger`/`sortBy`/`sortDir` via `CronListPageOptions`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts:505-515` — `cron.list` params schema defines `scheduleKind`, `lastRunStatus`, `trigger`, `sortBy`, `sortDir`, `enabled`, `agentId`, `query`, `limit`, `offset`.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-list.ts:57-68` — the RPC forwards every one of those fields to `listPage`.

The CLI only forwards three filters today:

- `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.ts:56-87` — `cron list` registers only `--all`, `--agent`, `--query`, `--json`.
- `src/cli/cron-cli/list-jobs.ts:37` — `listCronJobsFromGateway` filter type is `Pick<CronListPageOptions, "includeDisabled" | "agentId" | "query">`.

Precedent: `openclaw cron runs --query` (and the inventory `--query` in #150069) added CLI search/`--query` by forwarding an already-supported RPC parameter; this change does the same for the five remaining list filters.

## Implementation intent

- [ ] Yes, I plan to implement this myself
- [x] Maybe, with maintainer guidance
- [ ] No, proposing the idea only

## Additional information

- Compatibility: purely additive CLI flags; existing `cron list` invocations unchanged.
- Scope: CLI adapter only; no server-side changes, no schema changes, no new defaults.
- Boundaries: does not touch `cron runs` filtering or `CronListPageOptions` semantics.

An isolated rehearsal using unmodified 2026.10.5 and retained databases passed migration and gateway readiness. The full updater candidate should either pass its checks or retain sufficient diagnostic detail to identify why this installation differs. Snapshot consistency checks should remain enabled.

The post-Doctor attempt passed fresh candidate-state capture (120.61s), candidate Doctor (197.88s), lint, configuration, plugins, and recovery checks. `candidate-gateway-startup` then failed in 2.53s with `startupz` / `candidate-startup-failed`. The candidate was cleaned up without live activation. The original 2026.9.7 service remained running and passed recovery checks.

### OpenClaw version

Installed/running: 2026.9.7. Update candidate: official npm 2026.10.5.

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2, arm64; Node.js 24.

Wait a moment for write activity to settle, then retry the inspection

The concurrency wording is part of the error, not a verified diagnosis.

The retained error does not identify the specific consistency condition or writer. We are not requesting a guard bypass or claiming corruption, a specific race, or a confirmed fix.

### Summary

Chrome translation can replace the open chat with “Panel failed to load” and an `insertBefore` NotFoundError. Chinese-to-English translation can trigger the failure immediately; restoring the original language is not required.

Fix: #188061. This issue remains open until the PR merges.

### Reproduction

Reproduced with the preserved unbranded `2026.10.10-beta.4` chat UI, synthetic Gateway responses, and Google's served Translate Element library (`TE_20261028`):

1. Open a chat with selected-session usage of 170,000 tokens and a 200,000-token context limit.
2. Translate the page from English to Simplified Chinese. The context-usage popover can remain closed.
3. Deliver a background `sessions.changed` update for that session with `totalTokens: 180000` and an advanced `updatedAt`.
4. The chat is replaced by the panel error below.

The same update without translation passes. [Captured stack and reproduction details](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/188052#issuecomment-6513982245).

### Expected behavior

Chat remains usable and context usage updates while surrounding content is translated.

### Actual behavior

```text
Panel failed to load
Something went wrong while loading this panel.

Failed to execute 'insertBefore' on 'Node': The node before which the new node is to be inserted is not a child of this node.
```

### Cause and fix

Google translation replaces text nodes inside `strong.context-usage__context-value`, including the separator used as a rendering anchor. A background update then attempts insertion before the detached separator.

PR #188061 excludes only that numeric counter from translation. - Automated reproduction used Google Translate Element in Linux Chromium and English-to-Chinese translation. Chrome's native toolbar and the reported Chinese-to-English direction were not automated.

### Summary
The sticky header in an expanded Markdown table partly covers the Close X and intercepts pointer input on that part of the button. The center of Close still works, so this is a partially obscured control rather than a complete dismissal failure.

### Steps to reproduce
1. In Control UI chat, ask for a two-column Markdown checklist with enough rows to fill the expanded view (the reproduction used 24 garden tasks).
2. Click **Expand table** at a 1440×1000 viewport with the light theme.
3. Wait for the opening animation to finish, then inspect the top-right Close control.
4. Click the left side of that control, then compare a normal center click.

### Expected behavior
The complete Close glyph and its button target remain visible and usable above the sticky header. Clicking the control dismisses the expanded table and returns to the same conversation.

### Actual behavior
After the modal settled at opacity 1/scale 1 with no running animation, the 40×40 Close button occupied x1272–1312 and its 16×16 SVG occupied x1284–1300. The opaque sticky header ended at x1292, covering the glyph’s left 8 pixels. Native hit testing in that area returned a table header cell, and an actual left-side click left the modal open. The center click closed it, returned focus to Expand and preserved the unsent draft.

The current stylesheet gives the sticky header z-index 1 while the fixed Close button has auto stacking. This matches the observed paint and hit-test order; no modal lifecycle failure was observed.

### OpenClaw version
2026.10.9, UI source 719247f96bac8963b20007767ae199241c8293f2; source-backed development UI with a compatible 9ca944e298b7ed0881f7c37abb5d5032fafc3c31 Gateway. The table and modal owners are identical across these revisions.

macOS, Chromium via the repository’s Playwright installation; 1440×1000, DPR 1, light theme.

Source-backed Control UI development server with an isolated synthetic guest conversation.

Not material to the display defect; the reproduced message contains an ordinary Markdown table.

Not material to the display defect.

Real guest chat → Expand → settled geometry/hit testing → native left-side and center pointer activation. The relevant owners are ui/src/styles/chat/text.css and ui/src/components/markdown-tables.ts. The repair will carry matched before/after visual proof.

Users reading expanded Markdown tables can see an incomplete Close affordance and miss the action when clicking its covered left portion. Normal center Close and keyboard dismissal remain available. issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.10.3, Android continuous Talk fails with `Talk failed: Realtime provider error.`, while a controlled provider diagnostic identifies `usage_check_failed` / `service_unavailable_error` after authenticated session startup. The generic error obscures the actionable failure category.

This report concerns OpenClaw's error classification/presentation. It does not claim OpenClaw caused the provider-side usage-verification failure.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use an existing OpenClaw OpenAI OAuth sign-in and the following Talk configuration excerpt:
   ```json
   {
     "talk": {
       "realtime": {
         "provider": "openai",
         "model": "gpt-live-1-codex",
         "mode": "realtime",
         "transport": "gateway-relay",
         "brain": "agent-consult",
         "providers": {
           "openai": {
             "speakerVoice": "cove"
           }
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```
2. Connect the Android client and start continuous Talk with the composer waveform button.
3. On the affected setup, observe `Talk failed: Realtime provider error.` Reopening the app did not resolve it.
4. Observe `talk.event` on the same Gateway connection used for `talk.session.create`. Session allocation succeeds, then a connection-phase `realtime_unavailable` error and closure occur.
5. A controlled diagnostic using the installed OpenAI provider bridge, the same OAuth/model/voice and host-control mode, with listeners on both WebRTC and sideband events, captures the specific service error shown below on the sideband.

The provider trigger is externally dependent. These steps reproduce the affected setup; they are not a claim that every account or every attempt will receive this service error. No deterministic provider-independent trigger is established.

### Expected behavior

The documented Android Gateway-relay Talk route should provide a bounded, useful failure category when the provider prevents startup. For this observed event, a mapped diagnostic such as “Voice provider could not verify usage availability” would distinguish it from missing configuration or invalid credentials.

Preserve credential/payload redaction. An allowlisted error category or mapped message is sufficient; displaying arbitrary provider payloads is not requested.

Reference: https://docs.openclaw.ai/nodes/talk

### Actual behavior

1. Configuration validation passes without warnings; the running Gateway reports `clientHints.realtime.gatewayRelaySupported: true`.
2. `talk.catalog` reports the OpenAI realtime provider ready. This is catalogue readiness, not proof of a usable voice session.
3. The Android client reports only `Talk failed: Realtime provider error.`
4. Gateway connection probes report:
   ```json
   {
     "event": "talk.event",
     "type": "error",
     "phase": "connect",
     "code": "realtime_unavailable",
     "message": "Realtime provider error."
   }
   ```
5. In a separate controlled provider trace, authenticated call creation returns HTTP 201, the sideband opens, `session.started` arrives, then the provider emits:
   ```json
   {
     "type": "error",
     "error": {
       "code": "usage_check_failed",
       "type": "service_unavailable_error",
       "message": "Unable to verify usage availability."
     }
   }
   ```
6. Other attempts ended with sideband close code 1006 before readiness. One earlier diagnostic briefly reached ready; that did not establish a working voice conversation.

These are separate traces; the specific provider payload was not exposed by the ordinary Android/Gateway error above.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.3

### Operating system

Gateway: Ubuntu 24.04, Node.js 24.21.0.
Client: Android; exact Android OS/app build: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Install method

Global npm package; Gateway managed as a user systemd service.

### Model

`gpt-live-1-codex`, voice `cove`.

### Provider / routing chain

Android Talk → OpenClaw Gateway-owned realtime relay → OpenAI GPT-Live, using the existing OpenClaw OAuth sign-in. `brain=agent-consult`. No Platform API key was added.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Only the Talk settings were changed. No installed OpenClaw source files, authentication guards or approval policy were modified. The Gateway hot-loaded the settings without a restart.

The provider's internal reason for failing usage verification is unknown. This evidence does not establish invalid credentials, exhausted quota, a provider-wide outage or an OpenClaw regression.

### Logs

Sanitized event ordering from the controlled provider diagnostic:

```text
call creation: HTTP 201
sideband: open
sideband: session.started
sideband: error
  code=usage_check_failed
  type=service_unavailable_error
  message=Unable to verify usage availability.
diagnostic bridge: closed
```

No microphone capture or agent task was used in this diagnostic. A local audio-engine check successfully generated a WebRTC offer, but this is not an end-to-end audio success.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The safe configuration excerpt and error envelopes above are the relevant evidence. No screenshots, raw logs, credentials, account/session/call IDs, private paths or network identifiers are attached.

Current-main source inspection, not a live reproduction on main: [parseOpenAIQuicksilverEvent](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-events.ts) reduces provider errors to `kind: "error"` plus `fatalAuth`, without retaining a safe provider error category. This is consistent with the observed loss of diagnostic detail.

### Impact and severity

1. Affected: the observed Android continuous-Talk setup.
2. Severity: voice interaction is blocked, and the displayed error gives no useful distinction between provider availability, configuration and authentication failures.
3. Frequency: repeated Android/Gateway startup failures; one controlled trace captured the specific service error. No exact failure-rate estimate is claimed.
4. Consequence: voice cannot be used, and diagnosis requires a separate instrumented connection.

### Additional information

No prior known-good version was established; this is not labelled a regression.

Searched OpenClaw issues and PRs for `usage_check_failed`, `Unable to verify usage availability`, `service_unavailable_error`, and related Talk errors. No exact matching report was found.

Related but different: #155190 concerns `missing_scope` before startup and a telephony silent-call lifecycle; #134798 concerns output ownership; #175794 concerns managed-proxy routing. None establishes the cause of this observed usage-verification failure.

A separate upstream service report, openai/codex#55531, describes the same provider error category in Codex voice. It is supporting context, not proof that both incidents have the same internal cause.

Please preserve a safe classification for this error and distinguish a provider-service failure from missing setup, without broadening permissions, disabling guards or adding unbounded retries.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (channel display / tool progress)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After upgrading core 2026.10.2 → 2026.10.5, tool progress rows delivered to the **Feishu channel lost their per-tool emoji prefixes** (⚙️ 📖 🛠️ ⌨️ …), leaving bare labels like `exec: <command>` / `Read: <file>`. End users immediately reported the readability regression ("tool call / exec / yield rows have no icons anymore, hard to scan").

Root cause (dist diff, 2026.10.2 vs 2026.10.5):

- 10.2 `displayTool(emoji, title, detailKeys)` carried real emoji per tool; `formatToolAggregateParts` in `tool-meta-*.mjs` prefixed every row: `` `${display.emoji} ${display.label}` ``.
- 10.5 refactored to `displayTool(icon, title, detailKeys)` with **semantic icon names** (`squareTerminal`, `globe`, `fileText`, …) for native clients, and `formatToolAggregateParts` now returns bare `display.label` — the emoji field is gone entirely.

The 2026.10.5 release notes show this was addressed for **Telegram** ("restore per-tool emoji on Telegram tool rows", #166861/#168032/#167392/#166880) and **Discord** ("add per-tool glyphs to Discord progress drafts"), but text-based channels that cannot render semantic icon names (Feishu at minimum) were left with bare labels.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Self-host OpenClaw 2026.10.5 with the Feishu plugin 2026.10.5 (verified on Linux, node v24).
2. Trigger any agent turn with multiple tool calls (e.g. `exec` + `read`), with channel streaming configured so tool progress rows are delivered.
3. Observe the tool rows in the Feishu chat: they arrive as bare `exec: …` / `Read: …` text with no per-tool emoji prefix. Same turn on 2026.10.2 produced `⚙️ exec: …` / `📖 Read: …`.

### Expected behavior

Text channels that cannot map semantic icon names to glyphs keep receiving per-tool emoji prefixes (as in ≤2026.10.2), or a channel-level fallback equivalent.

### Actual behavior

Feishu tool rows are bare `label: detail` text. The Feishu plugin itself contains no icon/emoji rendering in either 2026.10.2 or 2026.10.5 (verified: zero emoji/glyph logic in both plugin dists) — it relays core-formatted text, so the loss comes from the core formatter.

### Additional context

- Environment: OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9), plugin `feishu` 2026.10.5, Linux 7.0.0, node v24.22, systemd user service.
- Evidence: `tool-meta` diff between the two dists (emoji-prefixed `formatToolAggregateParts` vs bare label). 2026.10.2 dist contains the full emoji map (141 emoji occurrences); 2026.10.5 dist contains none outside comments.
- Migration data point: **all 58 `displayTool` entries align 1:1 by `title`** between 2026.10.2 and 2026.10.5 (verified programmatically from both dists), so restoring emoji for text channels is a mechanical `title → emoji` fallback — no new taxonomy required.
- Requesting parity with the Telegram restoration for Feishu (and auditing other glyph-less channels, e.g. plain-text/email-style channels).
- Happy to reformat receipts or run controlled comparisons on request.

issues.body:
## Summary

Please add a supported opt-in path for Microsoft Teams native extended Markdown text messages. The current plugin formats output for the legacy Markdown mode, so modern Markdown output is reduced before Teams can render it natively.

This is a feature/compatibility request, not a proposal to switch every existing installation's rendering mode silently.

## Current behavior

Source inspected at `cb470531b7f932e6b300816c2b77cb9105e97a68`:

- `extensions/msteams/src/format.ts` declares heading, bullet list, ordered list, task list, table and code-language fallback capabilities and re-renders the Markdown through the shared IR.
- `extensions/msteams/src/message-activity.ts`, `buildMSTeamsMessageActivity`, sets the text and matching mention/AI entities, but does not set `textFormat`.
- The normal sender and streaming paths therefore have no supported way to request `textFormat: "extendedmarkdown"` while preserving compatible source Markdown.

## Why this is useful

Microsoft documents extended Markdown as a per-message opt-in for richer CommonMark/GFM output and progressive rendering. It also explicitly warns that it is not fully backward-compatible with legacy formatting and does not support arbitrary HTML: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/bots/how-to/format-your-bot-messages

For a synthetic agent answer containing a heading, nested list, task list, fenced code with a language tag, and a GFM table, the desired opt-in route is to retain the supported Markdown structure and send a message activity with `textFormat: "extendedmarkdown"`. Legacy mode should keep its existing behavior. This would allow deployments to use the platform renderer instead of carrying a separate downstream formatter replacement.

## Minimal reproduction / inspection

Use this synthetic reply in an isolated Teams test installation:

````markdown
### Build status

- [x] Unit tests
- [ ] Release
  - Confirm the version

```js
const status = "ready";
```

| Item | State |
| --- | --- |
| Tests | Passed |
````

Send it through the ordinary reply route and through the streaming finalization route. Inspect the final message activity before transport: current `buildMSTeamsMessageActivity` has no `textFormat`; the preceding formatter applies legacy fallbacks. Compare with a native Teams activity using the same synthetic text and `textFormat: "extendedmarkdown"`.

Acceptance should cover both normal send and streamed finalization/update, real Teams rendering, mentions and their entities, AI-generated-content metadata, empty/attachment-only messages, table-mode choices, and the existing message-size/chunk limits. Verify legacy mode remains unchanged. Microsoft recommends testing the current desktop, web, iOS and Android clients during adoption.

## Scope and evidence

I checked the current source and the public Microsoft contract. This report does **not** claim a fresh current-main end-to-end Teams UI run or attach customer conversations/screenshots. A downstream implementation demonstrated that keeping Markdown and selecting the native renderer is viable, but it is not being proposed as a ready upstream patch without the compatibility decision and channel proof.

I found no existing Issue/PR specifically for `extendedmarkdown` adoption. #158103 and #158429 concern duplicate delivery when streaming finalization fails; that is a different problem and should remain separately tracked. Please confirm the preferred plugin-owned opt-in surface before implementation; no new core formatter or channel-specific core policy is requested.

## Additional boundary evidence (2026-10-20)

Executed the actual `formatMSTeamsMarkdown` followed by `buildMSTeamsMessageActivity` with the synthetic example above, for each existing table mode: `code`, `bullets`, and `off`. This was a pure source-owner probe on `5c99913874a641bc1091941508801aa0e98ec9c2`; both executed owner files exactly match official main `d53309cd8ea4d0761fec3ac81ae73290b81e569a`.

All three modes preserved the synthetic answer text and AI-generated-content entity, transformed the original Markdown, and produced no `textFormat` property. This confirms the current formatter/activity boundary rather than inferring behavior solely from a source search.

Reproduction: use the existing synthetic Markdown above as `input`; for each mode call `formatMSTeamsMarkdown(input, mode)`, then `buildMSTeamsMessageActivity(rendered)`, and inspect `Object.hasOwn(activity, "textFormat")` (false), `rendered === input` (false), retained answer text (true), and the existing AI entity (true).

No Teams account, transport delivery, Gateway, or client UI was used. This is not a claim about current Teams rendering across clients or proof of the proposed new renderer. A plugin-owned opt-in and its precedence with table modes remain a maintainer product decision; no new setting, core formatter, or private runtime replacement was introduced.

issues.body:
## Summary

When the lazy xAI OAuth refresh hits a transient network error (for example an HTTP proxy returning 503 on CONNECT, or `ECONNRESET`), the refresh fails on the first attempt and the xAI profile then behaves as expired. Later requests fail immediately with "Couldn't sign in to xai … run `openclaw models auth login --provider xai`" without attempting the refresh again. The refresh token was still valid: a manual device-code login fixed it immediately. With a 6-hour access token, every refresh is a single point of failure, and we have hit this twice in two days.

Reading the shipped `extensions/xai` refresh code (2026.10.10-beta.2), `requestXaiOAuthRefresh` retries only when the response is a Cloudflare/HTML challenge. If `fetch` throws (proxy tunnel failure, socket reset, abort), the error is re-thrown immediately with no retry, and non-challenge 5xx responses are not retried either.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.2
- macOS
- Outbound traffic goes through a local HTTP(S) proxy. The proxy is usually healthy but occasionally returns 503 or resets a tunnel.
- xAI provider uses OAuth (device-code login), with one non-xAI fallback model

## Steps to reproduce

1. Log in with `openclaw models auth login --provider xai` (device code). The access token is valid for about 6 hours.
2. Leave the Gateway running behind an HTTP proxy.
3. Let the token reach expiry while the proxy has a short outage, then send any request that needs the xAI profile (in our case an hourly cron turn a few seconds after expiry).

## Observed behavior (redacted)

```
auth profile "xai:<profile>" failed for provider "xai": OAuth token refresh failed for xai:
  xAI OAuth refresh failed: fetch failed | Request was cancelled |
  Proxy response (503) !== 200 when HTTP Tunneling | UND_ERR_ABORTED
lane task error: ... FailoverError: Couldn't sign in to xai. Your saved login looks expired or no longer works.
  Run `openclaw models auth login --provider xai` or `openclaw configure`. (auth)
Embedded agent failed before reply: All models failed (2): xai/grok-4.7: Couldn't sign in to xai ... (auth) |
  <fallback-provider>/<model>: 429: ... spending cap ...
```

- One refresh attempt is made a few seconds after expiry. It fails on the transport error and is not retried.
- Every later request (hourly, for several hours) fails within about 300 ms with the same "Couldn't sign in" error. No new refresh attempt is logged.
- `openclaw models status` reports the profile as `expired`.
- An earlier occurrence on another day had the same outcome, with `ECONNRESET` (TLS reset through the proxy) instead of a 503.
- In chat, the user sees the generic "AI service needs a short break" style message. The real cause is that the primary login failed and the fallback model returned 429 (quota). Nothing tells the user to re-login.

## Expected behavior

1. **Bounded retry with backoff for transient transport errors during refresh**: e.g. 3 attempts with jittered backoff (1s/4s/10s) when `fetch` throws `ECONNRESET`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `EAI_AGAIN`, `UND_ERR_*`, a proxy tunnel failure, or an abort. Also retry on 5xx and 429 token-endpoint responses that are not a definitive OAuth error (`invalid_grant` etc.).
2. **No permanent "expired" state after a transient failure**: if the refresh failed for a transport reason, keep the refresh token marked usable and attempt the refresh again on a later request, ideally after a short cooldown (minutes), not until manual re-login. Only definitive OAuth errors (`invalid_grant`, revoked client) should require re-authentication.
3. **Proactive refresh before expiry**: refresh inside the pre-expiry margin, ideally in the background while the current token is still valid, so a refresh failure doesn't immediately become an outage. Related: #103846 (margin-window refresh no-op).
4. **Clearer user-facing error**: when the primary fails on auth and the fallback fails on quota or 429, say so. For example: "xAI login refresh failed (network). Retrying automatically; if this persists run `openclaw models auth login --provider xai`. Fallback model unavailable: quota exceeded." The current message reads like a temporary capacity issue.
5. Optionally, emit a structured event or health signal when an OAuth profile enters the failed-refresh state, so operators can alert on it.

## Related

- #84018 / #96146: Cloudflare challenge on a stale token endpoint. Fixed; retry was added only for challenge responses.
- #165270: xAI refresh hard timeout and auth cooldown (different trigger, same "stuck until re-login" outcome).
- #103846: OAuth refresh inside the pre-expiry margin silently no-ops.
- #101496: aligning transient network error codes for provider retry paths. The OAuth refresh path does not seem to use that classifier.

## Workaround

Re-run `openclaw models auth login --provider xai`. Locally we added an external watchdog that alerts when the profile turns expired.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Benign Chinese equipment-loan questions in an OpenClaw + OpenViking memory workflow intermittently end without a complete final answer when Alibaba's streamed DeepSeek response is rejected by output inspection. Direct API isolation reproduces the upstream rejection without OpenClaw or OpenViking executing any tools. Please help triage provider-error handling and whether a supported, opt-in same-model non-stream retry exists; this is not a claim that OpenClaw performs the moderation.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use OpenClaw 2026.9.1 with an OpenAI-compatible model route through LiteLLM to Alibaba Model Studio's `deepseek-v4.1-flash`.
2. Run an ordinary Chinese equipment-return / handover question with recalled business records. In our run, the final-answer model requests contained `stream=true`.
3. Inspect the raw API response: the provider can return an in-band output-inspection error after HTTP 200 and partial output. The agent does not obtain a complete final answer.
4. Use the minimal direct API isolation below to separate the upstream behavior from memory tools. Repeat independently with response caching disabled and compare non-stream output. The complete original histories are not attached; they contain extensive unrelated test context.

### Expected behavior

The benign test text should be answerable: the unchanged short sentence and one full question were observed to complete on non-stream calls. For an upstream content rejection, preserve and surface the actual failure rather than treating partial text or HTTP 200 as a completed answer. Is there a supported per-request/provider setting or extension point for an **opt-in, at-most-once, same-model non-stream transport retry**, while retaining completed tool results and leaving safety settings unchanged? A second rejection should remain a visible failure.

### Actual behavior

The original Lex Q104 and official-OV Q108 final-answer attempts ended without complete answers after provider output-inspection errors. Our benchmark controller recorded the missing final answer; that controller wording is local and is not asserted to be an OpenClaw error string. No network-failure inference should be made solely from LiteLLM's `APIConnectionError` wrapper.

### Isolated transport results (2026-10-23)

Model alias: `deepseek-v4.1-flash`; route: OpenAI-compatible client → LiteLLM 1.105.0 → Alibaba Cloud Model Studio / Beijing MAAS. The model alias and provider route were unchanged. Safety and thinking settings were not disabled. Request-local response caching was disabled for the repeated diagnostics.

A minimal equipment-loan test sentence was:

> 约6月4日，当前只余赵棠的CAM-01未还。

It describes an equipment-loan status. In an additional small diagnostic, two streamed requests were interrupted with the output-inspection error; one non-streamed request returned this exact sentence with `finish_reason=stop`.

We also replayed two captured, full failed terminal requests three times each, changing only the response transport (`stream=false`, removing `stream_options`) plus request-local cache controls:

| Captured request | Non-stream outcomes |
|---|---|
| Official OpenViking integration, Q108 | 3/3 returned nonempty final answers with `finish_reason=stop` |
| Lex integration, Q104 | 1 final answer; 1 valid `tool_calls` response with no final answer; 1 HTTP 400 output-inspection rejection |

The original tool schemas remained present; diagnostic tool calls were not executed. A `tool_calls` response is an intermediate step, not a content rejection or proof that a complete agent run would fail. These were direct API replays, not six fresh end-to-end OC/OV runs. Normal termination was checked separately from answer correctness. In particular, non-streaming is **not** a guaranteed workaround, and generation variability prevents attributing every difference to transport alone.

### Errors observed

Stream: HTTP 200 was already committed, then the SSE contained an error and lacked a successful terminal answer:

```json
{"error":{"message":"litellm.APIConnectionError: APIConnectionError: OpenAIException - Output data may contain inappropriate content.","type":null,"param":null,"code":"500"}}
```

One non-stream replay also failed (routing-detail suffix omitted from the message below):

```json
{"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: Custom_openaiException - Output data may contain inappropriate content.","type":"data_inspection_failed","param":null,"code":"400"}}
```

Alibaba's [official error reference](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/error-code#inappropriate-content) associates this message with provider content inspection. We do not have the provider's internal moderation category or audit logs.

### Minimal API isolation request

Send this body to the configured **LiteLLM** `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint with your own authorization header:

```json
{
  "model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "请逐字转写下面这段设备借还业务记录，不添加解释：\n约6月4日，当前只余赵棠的CAM-01未还。"}],
  "stream": true,
  "stream_options": {"include_usage": true},
  "max_tokens": 4096,
  "cache": {"no-cache": true, "no-store": true}
}
```

For the paired diagnostic, set `stream=false` and remove `stream_options`. The `cache` field is LiteLLM-specific. No content-inspection headers are added or disabled. This reproducer isolates the provider path; rejection can vary by account, generated text, and context, so it is not a deterministic assertion for every deployment.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.1, pinned Docker deployment. Not retested on current main/latest; no regression range established.

### Operating system

Linux container on a macOS host. Exact container distro version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Install method

Docker. Two integrations were present: the official OpenViking plugin with local OC 9.1 compatibility adaptation, and a separate Lex memory integration. The direct API isolation did not load either plugin.

### Model

`deepseek-v4.1-flash` (configured alias, not an independently verified immutable upstream model build).

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw → read-only diagnostic/metering forwarder → LiteLLM 1.105.0 → Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (Beijing MAAS, OpenAI-compatible API).

### Impact and severity

Intermittent workflow-blocking failure: normal office questions sometimes end without a final answer. In the original Q108 original/fresh attempts, six individual model requests were rejected; these are not six separate question retries. Other streamed questions completed normally. Failed streams often omitted usage, making their complete cost unknown rather than zero.

### Additional information

Related but not identical: #32622 (Bailian input inspection on ordinary conversation), #152000 (provider content-guard classification/recovery).

We have not changed production transport/safety settings, replaced formal answers, reset sessions, or modified stored memory to work around the issue. The request is for accurate provider-error handling and a documented recovery boundary, not for disabling moderation.

# [Feature]: Add a label filter to `openclaw sessions`

## Summary

Add `openclaw sessions --label <text>` so operators can list sessions by their saved label, and show the label in the table row next to the session key.

## Problem to solve

Sessions store a `label` and a named tint `color` (`SESSION_COLOR_IDS`). The Control UI shows them, and `openclaw sessions --json` returns them through the display row. The CLI table does not show the label, and there is no way to filter by it.

Scenario: an owner labels conversations by project ("billing", "infra") and later wants the sessions for one project. Today `openclaw sessions` lists by recency only; the label is absent from the table, so the operator has to open the JSON and filter externally, then map keys back to rows.

Frequency: every time a labeled workspace is revisited, which is the point of labeling.

Workaround: `openclaw sessions --json | jq '...'`. It requires a script and loses the human-readable table.

## Proposed solution

```bash
openclaw sessions --label billing
openclaw sessions --label billing --json
```

- `--label <text>` matches the saved label (case-insensitive substring by default, exact when quoted as `=billing` if maintainers prefer).
- The table gains a `Label` column only when at least one row has a label, so unlabeled stores render exactly as today.
- `--json` keeps its current shape; `label` and `color` are already present.
- Compose with `--agent`, `--active`, `--workspace` (if accepted), and `--limit`.

### Design details

- `src/commands/sessions.ts`: apply the label filter before sort and limit, next to the existing `active` filter.
- `src/commands/sessions-table.ts`: render the label (and its tint when rich output is enabled) in the row.
- `src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.ts`: add the option and the parent-option rejection entry for subcommands.
- Tests: `src/commands/sessions.test.ts` for the filter and JSON passthrough, `src/commands/sessions-table.test.ts` for the cell.

## Alternatives considered

- Option A: show the label in Flags only. Why weaker: no filtering, and labels are long enough to crowd a cell that already carries runtime flags.
- Option B: filter by key prefix. Why weaker: labels are user-facing, keys are routing identifiers, and labels survive key changes.

### Why not a plugin?

`sessions` is a core CLI surface over the session store. A plugin cannot add a flag or a column to it, and would need to re-read the store and re-implement ordering and model columns.

## Impact

- Affected users / systems / channels: operators using session labels in CLI and scripts.
- Severity: annoying; blocks fast lookup in labeled workspaces.
- Frequency: every labeled-session lookup.
- Consequences: JSON plus external filtering, slower incident response.

## Evidence/examples

On `main` (a6c561f954c):

- `label` and `color` are part of `SessionEntry`, and `toSessionDisplayRow` copies them.
- `openclaw sessions --json` returns the display row, so both fields appear there.
- The text renderer builds columns Kind, Key, Age, Model, Runtime, Tokens, Flags; no label column.
- `sessions` options: `--json`, `--verbose`, `--store`, `--agent`, `--all-agents`, `--active`, `--limit`; no label filter.

Observed on an isolated Gateway (port 47833, empty state): `openclaw sessions --json` returns an empty `sessions` array and no label filter in `--help`.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

- [ ] Yes, I plan to implement this myself
- [x] Maybe, with maintainer guidance
- [ ] No, proposing the idea only

## Additional information

- Read-only, no config, no migration.
- Matching semantics and column visibility rule are the open points.

# [Feature]: Add a bundled-only skill filter to `openclaw skills list`

## Summary

Add `openclaw skills list --bundled` (and `--no-bundled`) so operators can list only the skills that shipped with OpenClaw, or only the ones they added.

## Problem to solve

`openclaw skills list` shows a `Source` column, and the values include `openclaw-bundled` and `openclaw-custodian`, alongside user-installed and workspace skills. The JSON output also carries a boolean `bundled`. There is no way to filter the list by that fact.

Scenario: an operator wants to know which skills came with OpenClaw before deciding what to remove, or wants to check whether a workspace skill shadowed a bundled one. They read the Source column across 56 rows, or pipe `--json` through a script.

Frequency: every skill audit or cleanup; on a stock install 54 of 56 listed skills are bundled, so the unfiltered table is mostly noise for this question.

Current workarounds: `skills list --eligible` filters by readiness, not by origin; `skills list --json` needs an external filter; `skills check` prints counts only and no source breakdown.

## Proposed solution

```bash
openclaw skills list --bundled          # only openclaw-bundled / openclaw-custodian
openclaw skills list --no-bundled       # only workspace / managed / extra skills
openclaw skills list --bundled --json   # same filter, same JSON shape
```

The filter composes with the existing `--eligible` and `--verbose` flags and does not change the output shape.

### Design details

- `src/cli/skills-cli.format.ts`: `formatSkillsList` already receives `bundled` on every `SkillStatusEntry`; add the filter next to the `eligible` check.
- The CLI option lives with the other `skills list` options; `--bundled` and `--no-bundled` are mutually exclusive.
- Tests: extend the existing skills list format tests in `src/cli/` next to `formatSkillsList`.

## Alternatives considered

- Option A: add a `B` marker to the Skill name column. Why weaker: it makes every row noisier, and the Source column already says `openclaw-bundled`.
- Option B: add a count line to `skills check`. Why weaker: it answers "how many", not "which ones", and does not compose with `--json`.
- Option C: document a jq one-liner. Why weaker: the core CLI already exposes `--eligible`; origin is the same kind of filter.

### Why not a plugin?

`skills list` is a core CLI command; a plugin cannot add a flag to it. The filter needs only the `bundled` fact that the skill status owner already computes.

## Impact

- Affected users / systems / channels: operators auditing or cleaning up skills on any deployment.
- Severity: annoying, turns into extra work during cleanup.
- Frequency: every skills audit.
- Consequences: manual scanning of a table that is mostly bundled rows, or a throwaway JSON script.

## Evidence/examples

On `main` (a6c561f954c), an isolated state directory:

```text
$ openclaw skills list
Skills (22/56 ready)
│ Status │ Skill │ Description │ Source │
│ △ needs setup │ 🔐 1password │ ... │ openclaw-bundled │
...
```

54 of the 56 rows use `openclaw-bundled` or `openclaw-custodian`. `openclaw skills list --json` exposes `"bundled": true` per entry, but there is no CLI flag that filters on it. `openclaw skills check` reports totals (56 total, 22 eligible) with no origin breakdown.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

- [ ] Yes, I plan to implement this myself
- [x] Maybe, with maintainer guidance
- [ ] No, proposing the idea only

## Additional information

- Read-only, no config, no migration.
- Flag naming (`--bundled` / `--no-bundled`) is open; the filter semantics are not.

# [Feature]: Add a last-activity field to `nodes describe`

## Summary

Add a `Last activity` row to `openclaw nodes describe`, so the single-node view answers "when did this node last talk to the Gateway?" the same way `nodes status` already does.

## Problem to solve

`openclaw nodes status` shows an `input:` segment in its Detail column: the last time the node was active, plus `(active)` for the active node. When a node is disconnected, its stats are suffixed with `(last known 3d ago)`. `openclaw nodes describe --node <id>` is the command operators run when they are investigating one node, and it has no equivalent row.

Scenario: a node stops accepting work. The operator runs `nodes describe` to inspect it, sees `Status: paired · disconnected` and a stale `Stats` line with no timestamp, and cannot tell whether the node vanished a minute ago or three days ago without switching to `nodes status` and finding the right row.

Frequency: every node investigation, which is exactly when the timestamp matters most.

Workaround: run `nodes status` and scan the wide Detail column for the matching node, or run `nodes describe --json` and convert `lastSeenAtMs` / `connectedAtMs` by hand. Both are extra steps in the moment of debugging.

## Proposed solution

Add a `Last activity` detail row, rendered with the existing relative-time helper:

```text
$ openclaw nodes describe --node <id>
┌──────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Field    │ Value                                                   │
│ ...      │ ...                                                     │
│ Stats    │ load 9.8/8 · mem 13/23 GB · disk 80 GB free (last known 1m ago) │
│ Last activity │ 1m ago · connected 4h ago · active node         │
│ Status   │ paired · disconnected                                   │
└──────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Leave `--json` unchanged; it already returns `lastSeenAtMs`, `connectedAtMs`, `lastActiveAtMs`, and `active`.

### CLI/API changes

```bash
openclaw nodes describe --node <idOrNameOrIp>
```

No new flag; one extra row in the existing text output.

### Design details

- `src/cli/nodes-cli/register.status.ts`: `describe` already computes `lastActive` from `lastActiveAtMs`. Add it to the detail rows (next to `Stats`), using `formatNodeTimeAgo`, and include the `active` marker and relative connection age when present.
- Both `status` and `describe` read the same `node.list` record: `node.describe` spreads the list row (`src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.read.ts`), so no Gateway change is needed.
- Tests: extend the existing `describe.each(["status", "describe"])` cases in `src/cli/nodes-cli/register.status.test.ts`.

## Alternatives considered

- Option A: print only the absolute timestamp from `--json`. Why weaker: operators compare "how long ago", and the CLI already standardizes on relative time.
- Option B: add the row only when the node is disconnected. Why weaker: the active case also answers "is this node responsive right now", and conditional rows make the table harder to scan.

### Why not a plugin?

`nodes` is a core CLI command with a fixed renderer; a plugin cannot add a row to it. The data is already returned by `node.describe`, so the change is one adapter line in the owner of that command.

## Impact

- Affected users / systems / channels: operators inspecting paired nodes on any platform.
- Severity: annoying to blocking during node incidents, when the age of the last contact decides the next step.
- Frequency: every node investigation.
- Consequences: extra commands, or a stale reading interpreted as current.

## Evidence/examples

Reproduced on an isolated Gateway with a connected headless node host on `main` (a6c561f954c):

```text
$ openclaw nodes describe --node <id>
│ Stats    │ load 6.7/8 · mem 11/23 GB · disk 80 GB free  │
│ Status   │ paired · connected                          │
```

`openclaw nodes describe --node <id> --json` returns `lastSeenAtMs`, `connectedAtMs`, and `pathEnv` for the same node. After stopping the node host, `describe` shows `Stats ... (last known just now)` and `Status: paired · disconnected`, while `status` adds the `last known` hint in Detail. There is no row that states the last contact time.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

- [ ] Yes, I plan to implement this myself
- [x] Maybe, with maintainer guidance
- [ ] No, proposing the idea only

## Additional information

- Read-only, no config, no migration.
- Exact wording of the row is open; the data and helper already exist.
