### Summary

- `openclaw configure --section model` on an explicit multi-agent fleet has no option to apply a model setup to the shared `agents.defaults`; it always writes one agent's entry and that agent's auth store.

### Problem to solve

- On fleets with `agents.ownership: "explicit"` and two or more agents, the model section resolves to the System Agent and writes primary, catalog and allowlist to that agent's entry.
- A provider credential entered in the same flow is stored in that agent's own auth store.
- The other agents keep their previous model and have no credential for the provider, so a fleet-wide provider setup takes one configure run per agent.

### Proposed solution

- On explicit fleets with two or more agents, configure adds a scope prompt with `One agent` (default, current behavior) and `Shared defaults`.
- `Shared defaults` writes primary, catalog and allowlist to `agents.defaults` and stores the provider credential in the shared auth store that every agent inherits.
- Single-agent installs keep the current flow with no new prompt.

### Alternatives considered

- `openclaw models set <model>` writes `agents.defaults.model` only; allowlist, provider catalog and credentials stay per agent.
- Editing each agent entry and running provider auth once per agent.

### Impact

- Affected: explicit multi-agent fleets set up with `openclaw configure`
- Severity: blocks a fleet-wide model and provider setup from configure
- Frequency: every model setup on an explicit fleet with two or more agents
- Consequence: one configure run and one credential entry per agent

### Evidence/examples

- Real CLI on `main` at 4d35c3d2986: explicit fleet `alpha`/`beta`, System Agent `alpha`, Anthropic API key (test value) entered in `openclaw configure --section model`.
- Then a real loopback gateway on the same state answers `agents.list` and `models.list`, and runs one agent turn per agent against a loopback provider endpoint that records the API key each request carries.

```text
$ openclaw configure --section model          # main 4d35c3d2986
prompt: Model/auth provider -> Anthropic
prompt: Anthropic auth method -> Anthropic API key
prompt: Allowlist models (comma-separated provider/model; blank to keep current) -> anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6, openai/gpt-5.4, anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
== configure exit 0
config after: agents.defaults.model unset; agents.entries.alpha.model.primary = anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; agents.entries.beta = {}

gateway agents.list -> ownership=explicit defaultId=alpha
  agent alpha: {"model":{"primary":"anthropic/claude-opus-5-5","fallbacks":["anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6","openai/gpt-5.4"]}}
  agent beta: {"model":{"primary":"openai/gpt-6-astra"}}
gateway models.list {"agentId":"beta"}
  anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 available=false tags=["configured"]
gateway agent turn beta: "No route-compatible authentication source is configured for openai."
  provider requests from this turn: none
gateway agent turn alpha:
  {"method": "POST", "path": "/v1/messages", "apiKey": "sk-ant-t...0000"}
```

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

- Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Additional information

- Related: #123871 (explicit fleets write configure model state to the selected agent; `One agent` keeps that as the default)
- Related: #131153 (open; adds a `configure --agent` selector in the same files)

issues.body:
### Summary

A `doctor --rebuild` mode: when targeted repairs have failed, rebuild the broken parts of an install (config, skeleton, plugin runtime state, caches) into a fresh baseline while preserving user data surfaces (gateway/session databases, credential stores, transcripts/memory, channel bindings) — with a printed keep/rebuild/discard manifest and one-command rollback of the rebuild itself.

### Problem to solve

The repair ladder has many targeted rungs and no safe bottom. `doctor` performs specific repairs (per-defect modules and sequencing under `src/commands/doctor/`, e.g. `legacy-config-repair.ts`, `auth-profile-repair.ts`, `finalize-config-flow.ts`, `repair-sequencing.ts`) and the update path has its own recovery modules. When none of them applies — the install is wedged in a way doctor does not know — the de facto community answer is to delete the state directory and start over.

Community reports (quoted verbatim; not reproduced by me):

- r/openclaw, ["The more I use OpenClaw; The less I understand"](https://www.reddit.com/r/openclaw/comments/1wna116/the_more_i_use_openclaw_the_less_i_understand/) (2026-09-22, 31 pts / 37 comments): "I just had to nuke and start my openclaw install fresh after none of the AIs could walk me through fixing it." / "I reinstalled everything."
- [Hermes vs OpenClaw](https://www.dhawalshah.net/article/hermes-vs-openclaw/) (2026-10-12, six-month comparison): "Running its own health check, `openclaw doctor`, would sometimes break things that had been working, and I would lose an evening to debugging."

The tracker shows the same dead end from the inside:

- #164811 (open, P2) — valid ClawHub installs are reported provenance-invalid and "suggest a futile reinstall": even the official advice routes to reinstall, and it does not work.
- #170335 (open) — an update removed database snapshots it said must be preserved: preservation promises are currently incidental, not a first-class path.
- #45003 (P0) — a new mechanism archived session history with no supported way to restore it: exactly the class of loss a preserve-and-rebuild path exists to prevent.

Today the all-or-nothing answer converts "my install is wedged" into "my sessions, credentials, and memory are gone" — the most expensive possible outcome of a repair path, and the one non-technical users get pointed at first.

### Proposed solution

`openclaw doctor --rebuild` (name up for debate):

1. Run normal targeted repairs first; this mode is explicitly the last rung and should say so.
2. Quarantine: move the current config, skeleton files, plugin runtime state, and caches aside — never delete.
3. Rebuild: reconstruct a fresh baseline config and skeleton the same way a new install would.
4. Restore preserved surfaces into the rebuilt install: the gateway database and per-agent session stores, credential stores, transcripts/memory, channel bindings — the data surfaces, not the config/code that may be the broken part.
5. Print a keep/rebuild/discard manifest before cutover, and keep the quarantine for one-command rollback (`doctor --rebuild --rollback`).

### Alternatives considered

- More targeted repairs (the current direction): necessary but the long tail is unbounded; #164811 is precisely the case where the targeted fix is unknown and the user is told to reinstall.
- External backup/restore tooling: the users hit hardest (non-technical, per the reports above) are the least likely to have one configured before they need it.
- A plain factory reset: that is the data-loss status quo; the point of this request is the preserve half plus the manifest that makes the outcome visible.

### Impact

- Affected: any install in a state doctor's targeted repairs do not cover — most commonly after a failed or partially-applied update, or a wedged migration; large-state installs have the most to lose (#168662).
- Severity: the current outcome of this state is data loss (state dir deleted) or a full manual re-setup.
- Frequency: every release cycle produces a cohort of such installs (see the upgrade-pain reports referenced in #164811/#168662 and the tracker's update-failure entries).
- Consequence: lost sessions/credentials/memory, hours of re-setup, and community advice that boils down to "nuke it" — which is also the advice that pushes marginal users to uninstall.

### Evidence/examples

- #164811 — valid installs advised to reinstall, reinstall is futile (open, P2).
- #170335 — snapshots promised to be preserved were removed (open).
- #45003 — archived session history with no restore path (P0).
- #168662 — large-state install cannot upgrade: the users with the most data are the ones the nuke hurts most (P1).
- `src/commands/doctor/` today is targeted-only: per-defect repairs plus sequencing, no last-resort rebuild mode.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance

### Additional information

Scoped as one doctor mode reusing machinery the codebase already has — quarantine handling for untrusted DB content exists on the admission paths, and the updater already stages candidate installs before cutover — rather than a new tool. If the full preserve list is contentious, shipping the manifest + rollback halves first already removes the "flying blind" part of the nuke.

## Environment and observation
OpenClaw 2026.10.5; macOS; Node 26.10.0; native bundled boot-md; SQLite session store. One observed occurrence on 2026-10-21 at 20:22 EDT. Reproducibility has not been tested with another restart.

## Steps observed
1. Enable only hooks.internal.entries.boot-md.enabled and perform one approved native Gateway restart.
2. BOOT.md uses native status, sends one startup message, and admits a main-session reconciliation turn.
3. Boot run finishes; native hook attempts to remove its temporary session.

Expected: startup work succeeds and the hook removes its temporary session.
Actual: startup notification and main pickup both succeeded, but cleanup failed and the finished temporary row remained. Hook logged startup task failed although useful work completed.

Sanitized error:
```text
boot: failed to clean up session: SQLite session entry changed before lifecycle removal for <temporary-boot-session>
hooks/boot-md: startup task failed; reason=session cleanup failed
```

## Impact / suspected area
Small cleanup/reporting defect: retained finished temporary session and misleading failure log. No observed lost startup message or duplicate execution. Installed boot handler finally calls applySessionEntryLifecycleMutation with expected session ID; exact-entry comparison in the SQLite projection rejects removal. The rejecting guard is located; the changing writer and root cause are not proven. Related finalization fallback appeared in the same run; causality is unknown and it is not a second blocker.

## Evidence and limits
The error excerpt above is sanitized from the observed Gateway log. Raw private transcripts, chat destinations, host names and user paths are not included. A maintainer can request a separately sanitized excerpt. No raw DB access, manual session deletion, installed patch, weakened guard or second restart was used.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A saved-session tool preview can advertise tools that the session's required sandbox policy excludes, including when local sandbox mode is off.

### Steps to reproduce

A focused regression drives the real `tools.effective` handler on the source revision below, with fixed external inventory/model metadata:

1. Enable core web search and set `agents.defaults.sandbox.mode` to `off`.
2. Supply an existing canonical session entry with `sandbox: "required"` and `sandboxMode: "off"`.
3. Request `tools.effective` for that session and inspect its returned tool IDs.
4. Compare with an ordinary session under the same configuration.

The fixture retains the real inventory construction and policy filtering. It does not execute a tool or make a model request.

### Expected behavior

The required session excludes `web_search` under the default sandbox allowlist while retaining permitted tools such as `read`. The ordinary session retains web search.

The [canonical sandbox classifier](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/855d0b398a54e57719f51f168eab5b48c3437188/src/agents/sandbox/runtime-status.ts) treats the creation-owned sandbox requirement as immutable even when local mode is off. The preview should apply that saved policy without provisioning a sandbox or using the viewer's privileges as future execution authority.

### Actual behavior

Both sessions advertise `web_search`. The required-session assertion fails with `expected true to be false`; the ordinary-session control passes. The permitted `read` control also passes.

### OpenClaw version

Source commit `855d0b398a54e57719f51f168eab5b48c3437188`.

### Operating system

Linux, repository-native test runner.

### Install method

Source checkout with the locked dependencies and repository test preparation.

### Model

No model request; fixed model metadata in the handler fixture.

### Provider / routing chain

Direct `tools.effective` handler → real effective inventory and policy filtering.

### Logs

```text
src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.test.ts
applies saved sandbox policy to core and warm MCP tools (required: true)
AssertionError: expected true to be false
expect(ids.includes("web_search")).toBe(!required)
Tests: 1 failed | 22 passed (23)
```

Formatting, lint, and the selected type checks passed before the behavioral run. The subsequent MCP exclusion assertion was not reached and is not counted as a failing baseline assertion.

### Impact and severity

The demonstrated impact is misleading tool availability for sandbox-required session previews. This reproduction shows incorrect preview output; it does not show an execution-permission bypass. It failed in the focused required-session case, with the equivalent ordinary-session case passing.

### Additional information

[Saved preview preparation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/855d0b398a54e57719f51f168eab5b48c3437188/src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.ts) omits `sandboxToolPolicy` when preparing the capability profile. The [execution path](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/855d0b398a54e57719f51f168eab5b48c3437188/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-tool-prepare.ts) supplies the prepared sandbox's tools to that same profile. The shared saved-policy correction is being prepared separately from changes to tool eligibility or permissions.

issues.body:
## Summary
`openclaw channels add <channel> --channel <other>` silently ignores the positional channel and configures the `--channel` one instead. Any credential flags meant for the positional channel (for example `--token`) are written to the other channel's config, and the command reports success with exit 0.

## Environment
- Commit: ac2f8c2d0e8ade65c9996f59e32332748e22c299 (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: `openclaw channels add` CLI (`src/cli/channels-cli.ts`), interactive and non-interactive paths, every channel

## Steps to reproduce
1. Start from an empty config: `echo '{}' > "$S/openclaw.json"`.
2. Run `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$S OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$S/openclaw.json HOME=$S openclaw channels add telegram --channel discord --token abc`.
3. Inspect `jq -c .channels "$S/openclaw.json"`.

## Expected
When the positional channel and `--channel` name different channels, the command refuses with a clear error (for example `Conflicting channels: positional "telegram" and --channel "discord". Pass only one.`), exits non-zero, and leaves the config untouched. Selectors that name the same channel keep working: same id in different case (`discord --channel Discord`), an alias plus its canonical id (`zl --channel zalo`, `imsg --channel imessage`), and either selector used alone.

## Actual
The command prints `Added Discord account "default".`, exits 0, and the config gets a `channels.discord` entry holding the token. The `telegram` positional is dropped without any warning, so a token meant for Telegram ends up stored as the Discord token.

## Root cause (if known)
`src/cli/channels-cli.ts`, the `channels add` action handler (around line 437 on ac2f8c2d0e8a), merges the two selectors with the flag always winning:
```ts
await channelsAddCommand(
  {
    ...forwardedOpts,
    channel: opts.channel ?? channelArg,
    agent: resolveStringOption(command, "agent"),
  },
  defaultRuntime,
  { hasFlags },
);
```
When both the positional `[channel]` and `--channel` are given, `opts.channel` always wins and `channelArg` is thrown away, even when they name different channels. #112176 deliberately made `--channel` win for option discovery, so that `telegram --channel signal` registers Signal's setup flags. Nothing then checks whether the positional agreed before config is written.

A candidate fix exists in the now-closed PR #177675. It resolves both selectors through the same alias-aware lookup that already picks the setup flags (`resolveChannelSetupCliOptionMetadata` in `src/channels/plugins/cli-add-options.ts`) and throws a `Conflicting channels` error, which `runCommandWithRuntime` reports on stderr with exit 1, only when the canonical ids differ. Aliases, case-only differences, and single-selector use behave as they do today. Rejecting conflicts versus keeping silent flag precedence (the #112176 behavior) needs a CLI/channels owner decision. The PR was written against an older main and needs a rebase: the `resolveChannelsAddOptions` helper it edits has since been folded into the action handler.

## Sibling surfaces
- `channels remove` has no positional channel, so it is unaffected.
- Option discovery (`resolveChannelsAddChannelFromArgv`, flag precedence from #112176) is a separate step. The candidate fix keeps it unchanged and only blocks the config write when the two selectors disagree.
- Runtime-only plugins whose aliases are not in bundled or catalog metadata would fall back to a case-insensitive raw comparison under the candidate fix.

issues.body:
### Summary

Expose a native Gateway operation for selecting any existing TTS auto mode: `off`, `always`, `inbound`, or `tagged`.

### Problem to solve

[Pincer #507](https://github.com/hartra344/pincer/issues/507) requests this for its remote Voice settings page. A client can read the mode with `tts.status`, but `tts.enable` and `tts.disable` persist only `always` and `off`. It cannot select voice replies only after voice input (`inbound`), or only when explicitly tagged (`tagged`).

This matters after a preference already exists: the saved preference overrides `messages.tts.auto`, so changing that configuration value does not change the effective preference. A remote settings client needs to update the existing TTS policy without shell access or an active chat session.

All four synthesis policies already exist. The missing capability is remote policy selection; this request makes no claim that every channel's conditional TTS delivery is working.

### Proposed solution

Add one operation to the existing native TTS Gateway family, for example `tts.setAuto { mode }`; the final name is an owner decision.

- Accept the existing four canonical modes and reject invalid input before writing.
- Use the same `operator.write` authorization and preference-path resolution as `tts.enable` / `tts.disable`.
- Persist through the existing TTS preference owner and return the saved mode. A subsequent `tts.status` must report the effective global mode.
- Preserve the existing precedence, including higher-priority session overrides, and unrelated provider, persona, text-limit, and summary preferences. The operation has the same host preference scope as enable/disable; it is not a WebChat-only playback switch.
- Keep `tts.enable` and `tts.disable` behavior compatible.

No new configuration setting, speech provider, session field, or automatic policy is needed.

### Alternatives considered

- **Change `messages.tts.auto`:** valid without an overriding preference; it does not update an already-saved auto preference.
- **Send a chat command:** [#26493](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/26493) requests additional `/tts` modes. That is a related conversation-command surface. This settings operation must also work when no chat is selected or created.
- **Patch a session:** the current `sessions.patch` schema has no `ttsAuto` field; a session override would also have a different scope.
- **Host plugin:** `api.runtime.tts` does not expose an auto-preference writer. The source `tts-runtime` entrypoint exports `setTtsAutoMode` and preference-path helpers, but the current SDK inventory classifies `tts-runtime` as private/local-only; its JavaScript host exports support separately published official plugins. Those exports alone do not establish a supported third-party preference-write contract. This proposal asks whether the existing native TTS settings family should support the selection; owners can choose a supported extension surface instead.
- **Edit the preferences file:** can change the saved policy, but requires separate host file access rather than the authenticated settings operation.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: remote Gateway clients implementing TTS settings, with Pincer as one concrete requester. Particular delivery channels retain their existing TTS support.
- Severity/urgency: blocks selecting the two conditional policies through the native settings API. No production outage or deadline is established.
- Frequency: whenever such a client needs `inbound` or `tagged`; actual selection frequency and affected user count are unknown.
- Practical consequences: users must leave the remote settings flow or retain `always` / `off`; configuration edits alone do not replace a saved preference.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original remote-client request](https://github.com/hartra344/pincer/issues/507), September 30, 2026.
- [Current Gateway handlers](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5987a0332d5bb0f1df3ffdfdaf5c448bd90ecc83/src/gateway/server-methods/tts.ts#L64): enable/disable writes and the `auto` status field.
- [Existing preference writer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5987a0332d5bb0f1df3ffdfdaf5c448bd90ecc83/src/tts/tts-settings-writes.ts#L17): `setTtsAutoMode`; its Boolean wrapper selects `always` / `off`.
- [Current resolution precedence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5987a0332d5bb0f1df3ffdfdaf5c448bd90ecc83/src/tts/tts-settings.ts#L220): session override, saved preference, then configuration.
- Related [#71487](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/71487) / [#75479](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75479) concern TTS UI, voice selection, and preview; their toggle uses enable/disable. [#28689](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/28689) concerns `/tts` aliases. Both PRs are closed and unmerged; closure is not implementation evidence.

- [Source preference-helper exports](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9bbd4fa44ad6638be168165ff52897b8c9338790/src/plugin-sdk/tts-runtime.ts#L37), [private/local-only inventory](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9bbd4fa44ad6638be168165ff52897b8c9338790/scripts/lib/plugin-sdk-private-local-only-subpaths.json#L222), and [SDK support explanation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9bbd4fa44ad6638be168165ff52897b8c9338790/docs/plugins/sdk-overview/imports.md#L82) distinguish implementation exports from supported public contracts.

The capability check is static inspection of the pinned default branch. No live Gateway, Pincer installation, or provider was exercised.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Implementation can extend `src/gateway/server-methods/tts.ts` and its native method descriptors, reuse `setTtsAutoMode`, and add a closed parameter schema in the Gateway protocol package. Use the existing TTS vocabulary and preference owner. These are suggestions; no contributor has committed to implement them.

Non-goals: a new settings page, `/tts` command changes, per-session mode controls, new voices, preview behavior, or channel delivery repairs. Remote clients can consume the operation independently.

Acceptance criteria:

- Starting with a saved `off` or `always` preference, an authorized remote client selects `inbound` and then `tagged` without a chat session or shell access. `tts.status` reports each selection, including after reconnecting.
- Existing TTS dispatch uses the saved policy: `inbound` distinguishes audio input from text input; `tagged` distinguishes explicitly tagged replies. Verify with an isolated Gateway and controlled provider.
- Other TTS preferences, existing session overrides, and enable/disable semantics are preserved.
- Invalid parameters and callers lacking write authority cause no preference change. Persistence failures are reported as failures.

Selecting an existing policy changes which future replies generate audio and incur the configured provider's charges. This adds no credentials, permission scope, or storage format. The method name and exact response shape remain normal API design decisions.

Updated October 22, 2026: clarified the runtime facade, source exports, and SDK support boundary. An earlier edit incorrectly called the private/local-only `tts-runtime` entrypoint public; this correction supersedes that statement. The requested native API scope and acceptance criteria are unchanged.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When another agent (a bot sender) messages an OpenClaw agent and that turn calls `ask_user`, the question is sent back to the other agent's conversation instead of to the agent's owner, and the other agent's text reply can answer it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an owner with `commands.ownerAllowFrom` and a channel that marks inbound senders with `SenderIsBot: true` (Discord and Slack bot authors, or a plugin channel whose senders are agents).
2. Have the bot sender send a message to the agent's main session that leads the agent to call `ask_user`.
3. Watch where the question prompt is delivered, then have the bot sender reply with one of the option labels.

In QA Lab (qa-channel + mock-openai), sending an inbound message from a bot sender with the `ask_user` routing marker reproduces step 2.

### Expected behavior

The bot sender cannot answer for a person, so the question reaches the person who owns the agent: the owner route that proactive delivery already uses (`commands.ownerAllowFrom`, then the channel's `allowFrom`). The bot sender's own messages do not resolve the question.

### Actual behavior

- The prompt is delivered to the bot sender's conversation. In QA Lab the only outbound message after the bot's inbound turn is the question prompt in the bot's conversation, and nothing reaches the owner.
- A plain-text reply from the bot sender that matches an option resolves the pending question: on `main` at f35c75b0, `runReplyQuestionInput` returns `{ handled: true }` for a turn with `SenderIsBot: true`.
- We first saw this on 2026.10.3 between two agents on a plugin channel: the agent called `ask_user` to get its owner's approval for a peer agent's request, the prompt was routed to the peer's conversation, and the owner never saw the question.

### OpenClaw version

main at f35c75b0 (also observed on 2026.10.3)

### Operating system

Linux (Ubuntu 25.10)

### Install method

Source checkout (`pnpm openclaw qa suite`)

### Model

mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna (QA Lab)

### Provider / routing chain

QA Lab mock-openai provider through a local Gateway child

### Additional provider/model setup details

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

QA Lab bus messages after the bot sender's turn, from the reproduction scenario with the routing fix reverted:

```text
inbound  qa-ask-user-peer-agent  (senderIsBot: true) "...ask_user_fixture=single ... target=ask_user."
outbound qa-ask-user-peer-agent  "Question for you: Deploy / Where should this deploy? ..."
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Impact and severity

An agent that asks its owner for permission while serving another agent can have that permission granted by the other agent. Any deployment where agents talk to each other (bot authors on Discord or Slack, or agent-to-agent plugin channels) is affected. The person the question is meant for never sees it.

### Additional information

Since #130223, `ask_user` is offered only on channels that declare `agentPrompt.questionInputMode`. A channel whose senders are all agents has no truthful value to declare today, so on those channels the agent asks in plain text, which also reaches the other agent.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let the realtime Talk model control its own session by voice: end the call, and switch into a listen-only (dictation) mode and back, when the user clearly asks for it.

### Problem to solve

Once Talk is live (started from Voice Wake or the microphone button), the only way to end or pause it is a click, tap or keyboard shortcut.

1. **"Stop" does not stop.** Saying "stop", "bye" or "hang up" makes the model say goodbye, but the call stays open and keeps transcribing and answering. Observed on 2026.10.3 in browser Talk (OpenAI GPT-Live, WebRTC): the user said "Stop", the model replied "Okay, stopping", and the user's next sentence was still transcribed and answered.
2. **Hands-free use needs a hands-free exit.** With Voice Wake or a device on a stand, the user is often not at the screen. A microphone that the user believes is closed but is still live is a privacy problem in shared rooms, and it keeps turning room conversation into transcripts and agent work.
3. **No way to think aloud.** Realtime Talk responds on every pause. When the user wants to talk through a longer request or brainstorm for a minute, the model keeps jumping in. A longer `silenceDurationMs` slows down every normal reply, and hold-to-dictate means leaving the conversation and using your hands.

### Proposed solution

Give the realtime model a small session-control tool bound to the current Talk session, similar to the end-call control realtime Voice Call already has (see #132334):

- **End:** the model says a short goodbye, waits for playback to finish, then ends the session exactly like the client's stop control (microphone released, end cue played, Voice Wake back to waiting for the wake word).
- **Listen-only (dictation):** the model acknowledges once, then the session keeps transcribing but stops generating responses. A configurable resume phrase (for example "okay, your turn") or a UI action ends listen-only, and everything said in between is submitted as one user turn. Because the model is silent in this mode, resume detection has to run on the finalized transcript outside the model.
- **Optional pause/resume:** stop listening without ending the session, matching the existing pause control.

Suggested guardrails and configuration:

- The model calls the tool only on clear intent; ambiguous phrases get a short spoken confirmation.
- A config block such as `talk.realtime.sessionControl` with toggles for each action and a list of resume phrases (language-agnostic, user-defined).
- Clients show the current state (listening, listen-only, paused, ended) and play the existing cues.

These actions only reduce what the session can do, so they should not need the spoken confirmation gate used for high-impact actions.

### Alternatives considered

- **Prompting via `talk.realtime.instructions`** to stay quiet or "hang up": unreliable. The provider still creates a response per detected turn, and the model has no way to close the microphone.
- **Idle timeout (#46844):** complementary. It covers walking away, not "I'm done" or "let me think aloud".
- **Longer silence window or semantic turn detection (#140159):** fewer interruptions, but no support for minute-long monologues, and normal turns get slower.
- **Hold-to-dictate / push-to-talk:** works, but requires hands and leaves the live conversation.

### Impact

- Affected: Talk users on browser, macOS (Voice Wake), iOS and Android, especially hands-free.
- Severity: annoying to privacy-relevant (the microphone stays live after the user asked to stop).
- Frequency: every hands-free session.
- Consequence: the user has to return to the device to end or pause the call; unintended transcription, agent consults and provider cost from ambient speech.

### Evidence/examples

- Realtime Voice Call already exposes a model-invoked end-call control (referenced in #132334), and agents can already change a live Talk call's voice via `talk_voice`. Model-driven control of the current call has precedent.
- Transcription-only Talk sessions (`mode: "transcription"`, `brain: "none"`) already exist and could back the listen-only state.
- Related: #46844 (idle timeout), #140159 (semantic turn detection), #139472 (asynchronous delegation), #132334 (end call in classic voice-call mode).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Resume and end phrases should not be hard-coded to English; users switch languages mid-call.

issues.body:
### Summary

With the Codex app-server harness, a user turn that the host has already admitted and saved is reported as a failed write whenever the native prompt annotation step throws. `mirrorPromptAtTurnStartBestEffort` runs `annotateCurrentUserTurn` inside the promise it registers with `markRuntimePersistencePending`. When annotation throws (for example "cannot replace an edited admission"):

1. `waitForRuntimePersistence` sees the rejected promise and fires `onPersistenceError` for a user turn that is durably saved.
2. `notifyUserMessagePersisted` is never called for the durable admission, so persistence listeners never see the saved turn.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Admit a user turn through the user-turn transcript recorder (`persistApproved()`).
2. Run `mirrorPromptAtTurnStartBestEffort` with a `hostCapabilities.annotateCurrentUserTurn` that rejects.
3. `await recorder.waitForRuntimePersistence()`.

### Expected

Annotation is best-effort provenance. The turn is reported as persisted, and no persistence error is raised.

### Actual

`onPersistenceError` fires, and the persisted-message notification is skipped.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.10.5 and current `main`, Codex app-server harness. We hit this in production on the 9.x line through a redaction-related annotation refusal, which has since been removed. Other annotation refusals still take the same path.

issues.body:
### Summary

When an agent passes message text to a script through `exec`, any `$<digit>` inside double quotes (or in unquoted words or unquoted heredocs) is expanded by the shell to an empty positional parameter. Dollar amounts are silently corrupted in whatever the script sends:

| Agent wrote | Recipient got |
| --- | --- |
| `--message "The unit is vacant at $900."` | `The unit is vacant at 00.` |
| `--subject "additional $5,000 earnest money"` | `additional ,000 earnest money` |
| `--message "shows the $1,000 October charge"` | `shows the ,000 October charge` |

Nothing fails. The command exits 0, the model sees success, and the wrong amount reaches a customer by SMS, email or chat.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Give an agent the `exec` tool and a script that sends text, e.g. `send-sms.sh --message "..."`.
2. Have it send a message containing a dollar amount, using double quotes, e.g. `--message "Rent is $950 per month."`.
3. The delivered text reads `Rent is 50 per month.`

### Expected

The tool call is refused before it runs, with an explanation and a safe alternative (single quotes, `\$`, or a quoted heredoc).

### Actual

The command runs and the corrupted text is delivered.

### Impact

Over about six weeks of one production deployment's agent transcripts, 391 unique `$`-bearing exec commands included 11 that mangled money amounts and 7 awk `"$0"` programs inside double quotes. Codex-native shell commands are affected the same way.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.9.x and 2026.10.5, Linux, bash. Seen with both OpenAI/Codex and Claude-routed agents.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In a Discord channel with `autoThread: true`, if the turn that created the thread starts a command that keeps running in the background after the turn ends, the agent's follow-up reply on completion is posted to the parent channel instead of the thread.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a Discord guild channel with `autoThread: true` (we use `requireMention: false`).
2. Post a message in that channel. OpenClaw creates a thread and the agent answers inside it.
3. In that first turn, have the agent run a command that outlives the exec yield window (for example `sleep 30; echo done`). It continues in the background with `notifyOnExit` (default on), and the agent ends the turn while it runs.
4. Wait for the command to exit. The exec completion wakes the session and the agent writes its follow-up.

### Expected behavior

The follow-up is posted in the auto-created thread, where the conversation and its session live.

### Actual behavior

The follow-up is posted at the top level of the parent channel (prefixed with the "First heartbeat alert" preamble, which is tracked separately in #143074).

Commands started in later turns, after the user replies inside the thread, are delivered to the thread correctly: their arrival channel is the thread itself.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.3 (source build). The same code path is unchanged on `main` at 9da96cb50e3.

### Operating system

macOS 15

### Install method

Source checkout, `pnpm build`

### Model

Not model-specific (seen with openai/gpt-6-sol)

### Provider / routing chain

Discord channel (autoThread) → embedded agent → exec `notifyOnExit` → heartbeat wake → channel delivery

### Logs

The thread session (`agent:<id>:discord:channel:<threadId>`) stores `delivery.context.to = channel:<threadId>`, and its transcript shows the `[OpenClaw exec completion]` wake. The delivered message still landed in the parent channel.

Cause, as far as we can tell:

- Discord's `threading.buildToolContext` sets `currentChannelId` from `NativeChannelId`, which is the channel the message arrived in (the parent). The thread is kept in `currentMessagingTarget`.
- Exec captures only `currentChannelId`: `notifyDeliveryContext.to` in `bash-tools.exec-request-preparation.ts`, and the approval follow-up `turnSourceTo` in `bash-tools.exec-run.ts`.
- `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` prefers that turn source over the session route, so the completion targets the parent.

Hook context and gateway tools already use `currentMessagingTarget ?? currentChannelId` for the turn source; exec is the outlier.

### Impact and severity

Medium. In channels that use one thread per request, finished work shows up in the parent channel, and the thread never receives its result. We hit this 7 times in a month in one channel.

### Additional information

A fix PR follows. It makes exec prefer `currentMessagingTarget` and fall back to `currentChannelId`, with regression tests for both the completion and the approval follow-up route.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After a turn yields to announcing subagents, its Telegram progress card is kept for them (`retainProgressDraft`, #166101), but the checklist on that card never changes again. The requester's settle wake keeps updating `progress_card` (steps completed, header `1/3 complete`, `3/3 complete`), and none of those updates reach the retained card. It shows the yielding turn's `0/3 complete` until the card is retired.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Telegram channel with `streaming.mode: "progress"`.
2. In a DM, ask for multi-step work. The agent calls `progress_card` with a 3-step plan (step 1 `in_progress`), spawns a subagent with a completion message and calls `sessions_yield`. The card shows `0/3 complete` and is adopted for the child (`Delegated work: running`).
3. When the child finishes, the requester settle wake runs, calls `progress_card` with step 1 `completed` / step 2 `in_progress`, and may yield again for another child.
4. Watch the retained card while the wake runs.

### Expected behavior

The retained card shows the requester's current checklist (`1/3 complete`, then later updates) while the requester is working on it, as it does for tool activity of the same wake.

### Actual behavior

The card keeps the `0/3 complete` checklist from the yielding turn. The card itself is live (child status and the wake's tool activity are forwarded); only the plan never changes.

Code path on current `main` (08d77cab437):

- Plan updates leave `progress_card` as an agent event with `stream: "plan"` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.completion.ts`). A live turn receives them through its own bridge (`createProgressBridge("plan")` → `onPlanUpdate` → Telegram `handlePlanUpdate` → `pushPlanProgress`), which exists only for the dispatch that owns the turn.
- After adoption the card belongs to `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-progress-draft.ts`. `withSubagentProgressDraft` follows the settle wake run with `follow(live, wakeRunId, "requester:tool")`, but `follow` keeps only `projectActivity` items (`stream: "item"`, `kind: "tool"`). Plan events of the same run are dropped.
- `ProgressContinuationDraft` (`src/channels/progress-continuation.ts`) has only `push(item)` and `retire()`, so there is no way to hand a plan to the retained card.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.5 (code path unchanged on current `main`).

### Operating system

Linux (gateway).

### Install method

npm

### Model

Not relevant (any model that calls `progress_card`).

### Provider / routing chain

Not relevant.

### Logs

Observed on 2026-10-21 on 2026.10.5: the turn yielded at +4.5 min with `0/3 complete`, and the card was adopted for the child. The settle wakes then called `progress_card` at +34 min (step 1 completed) and +47 min (all steps completed; a second child was spawned and re-yielded in between). The durable progress card (`progressCard.get`) has those states. The Telegram card was not captured after +34 min; the conclusion that it kept `0/3 complete` comes from the code path above, and the PR adds a test that is red on `main` at the `subagent-progress-draft` boundary.

### Impact and severity

Low to medium. No data loss, but on long delegated work (tens of minutes) the most visible status surface stays at the initial checklist, so it looks stuck while work is progressing.

### Additional information

A fix is in progress: the settle wake's own `stream: "plan"` events go to the adopted card through an optional `pushPlan` on `ProgressContinuationDraft`, and Telegram's retained card renders them like a live turn does. Children's plan events stay out of the card, which keeps the existing audience boundary (only prepared operation names and outcomes from a private child). PR to follow.

issues.body: ### Bug type Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary Performance: when a Telegram or Slack reply is split into several messages, the Gateway re-parses Markdown for assistant-transcript protection on candidate chunks it only measures, so a 10,159-character reply sent as four Telegram messages parses Markdown 75 times where 10 would do. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Check out `main` at `3757bbb23ae`. 2. Call `markdownToTelegramChunks(reply, 4000)` (`extensions/telegram/src/format.ts`) and `markdownToSlackMrkdwnChunks(reply, 8000)` (`extensions/slack/src/format.ts`) on a long technical Markdown reply (headings, lists, links, inline code with `<` and `&`, fenced code) with a spy on `MarkdownIt.prototype.parse`. 3. Compare the parse count with the number of returned chunks. (Protection calls themselves need V8 precise coverage, as in the linked PR's `count-preload.mjs`, because the Slack protection function is module-private.) The linked PR adds `--channel telegram|slack --reply-chars N` to `scripts/bench-channel-turn.mts`, which sends such a reply through an isolated Gateway and the bundled plugin; the numbers below come from it. ### Expected behavior Protection returns its input unchanged or prepends a fixed `Assistant:` marker, so (as #144633 already reasons for oversized Slack candidates) a candidate needs it while measuring only when it is within the marker's length of the limit. Each sent message still needs it once. ### Actual behavior `renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit` (`packages/markdown-core/src/render-aware-chunking.ts`) renders and measures many candidate chunks per reply: the main loop, the fitting-prefix search and whitespace coalescing. Both channel callers protect inside `renderChunk`: - `markdownToTelegramChunks` protects every candidate. This is the default path for Telegram text replies (`sendMessageTelegram` -> `planTelegramTextDeliveryPages`, 4,000-character HTML limit). - `markdownToSlackMrkdwnChunks` skips candidates longer than the limit (#144633) but protects every candidate that fits (8,000-character default limit). Protection projects the visible text and parses it with `markdownToIR`; Telegram skips the parse when the projection has no `[`, `<` or `&` (#148285), and Slack always parses. The marker is 24 characters on Telegram (`Assistant:` and a space) and 13 on Slack (`` `Assistant:` `` and a space), so for any candidate that is not within the marker's length of the limit, protection cannot change the fit decision; it matters only for the chunks that are finally sent. Measured on `3757bbb23ae` through an isolated Gateway (the bundled channel plugin, a local Crabline Telegram or Slack provider server, a mock model; counts from one boot, the same on every turn; times from 5 profiled boots): | Per reply | Telegram, 10,159 chars, 4,000 HTML limit | Slack, 20,153 chars, 8,000 limit | | --- | ---: | ---: | | `MarkdownIt#parse` calls | 75 | 18 | | protection calls | 73 | 16 | | chunk renders | 73 | 30 | | messages sent | 4 | 3 | | main-thread time in the chunker, median (50 warm turns, 5 profiled boots) | 43.0 ms | 26.9 ms | | of which protection | 26.6 ms | 14.3 ms | Two parses per reply happen outside protection; the rest are protection. The waste grows with reply length: through the same bench with `--reply-chars 60000`, protection runs 399 times for 19 Telegram messages and 59 times for 8 Slack messages. ### OpenClaw version `main` at `3757bbb23ae`. `v2026.10.5` (latest stable) has the same code path (checked in source, not measured). ### Operating system Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS x86_64 (Node 26.12) ### Install method Source checkout ### Model Any model; only the reply text matters. ### Provider / routing chain Any. The work happens in the Telegram and Slack channel plugins after the model has replied. ### Additional provider/model setup details Default config otherwise: Telegram text delivery without rich messages, and Slack's default 8,000-character text chunk limit. ### Logs No errors; the delivered messages are correct. ### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence Call counts come from a V8 precise-coverage preload in the Gateway process and times from main-thread CPU profiles split per turn, passed to the bench through `OPENCLAW_CHANNEL_BENCH_NODE_OPTIONS`. The delivered message bodies were identical across every run of each turn. ### Impact and severity - Affected: long Telegram and Slack replies that need splitting. - Severity: low; extra Gateway main-thread CPU, correct output, no data risk. - Frequency: every such reply. On Telegram the extra parses need `[`, `<` or `&` in the visible text (every protected candidate of the measured reply parsed); on Slack every protected candidate parses. - Consequence: in the profiled runs, about 21 ms (Telegram) and 5 ms (Slack) of extra main-thread time per reply of this size, growing with reply length, during which the event loop serves no other session on the same Gateway. ### Additional information A fix can keep every delivered message identical by protecting candidates only within the marker's length of the limit while measuring and protecting the remaining sent chunks once after chunking.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (commit 1b58cb9), npm global install
- @openclaw/diagnostics-otel 2026.10.5
- macOS 26.5.1 arm64, Node 26.10.0
- Export: OTLP to a local otelcol-contrib (0.162.0) file exporter

### What we observe

We grouped every span in three days of exported traces by span name and listed the distinct attribute keys (python, read-only).

`openclaw.model.call` (40,417 spans) carries only these keys:

```
error.type
gen_ai.operation.name gen_ai.request.model gen_ai.system
gen_ai.usage.{input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read.input_tokens, cache_creation.input_tokens}
openclaw.agent openclaw.api openclaw.model openclaw.provider openclaw.transport
openclaw.errorCategory openclaw.failureKind
openclaw.model_call.observation_unit
openclaw.model_call.prompt.{input_messages_chars, input_messages_count, system_prompt_chars,
  tool_definitions_chars, tool_definitions_count, total_chars}
openclaw.model_call.{request_bytes, response_bytes, time_to_first_byte_ms}
openclaw.model_call.usage.{input_tokens, output_tokens, prompt_tokens, total_tokens,
  cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, reasoning_output_tokens}
```

There is no channel, trigger, lane, or fallback state on the span.

`openclaw.tool.execution` (53,154 spans) carries only:

```
gen_ai.operation.name gen_ai.tool.call.id gen_ai.tool.name
openclaw.agent openclaw.toolName openclaw.tool.source openclaw.tool.owner openclaw.tool.params.kind
openclaw.outcome openclaw.deniedReason openclaw.errorCategory openclaw.errorCode
```

There is no result size and no truncation flag.

The exporter code matches this. In `~/.openclaw/extensions/diagnostics-otel/dist/.setup/runtime-api-CKLGMqUx.mjs`, `recordModelCallFinished` (line 1451) and `recordToolExecutionFinished` (line 1777) only map the fields above. The same file already emits `openclaw.lane` on `openclaw.model.failover` (lines 1322 to 1338) and `openclaw.channel` / `openclaw.trigger` on run-level spans, so the values exist in the diagnostic event stream but are not passed through to the per-call spans.

What this costs in practice:

- To split model latency or cost by channel or trigger (chat vs cron vs heartbeat vs subagent), you have to join each model.call to its `openclaw.run` / `openclaw.harness.run` span by traceId. That works for most calls, not all.
- `openclaw.model.failover` (added in #102051) records the transition, but a model.call span does not say whether it was the primary attempt or a fallback, or whether the answer the user got came from a fallback model. Answering "how many replies were served by a fallback today" needs a multi-span reconstruction.
- Tool result size is the main driver of context growth, and it is not exported at all. We had to write a small local plugin that re-emits result bytes and a truncation flag as a separate span joined by `gen_ai.tool.call.id` (a different trace, so it cannot be joined by traceId).

### Expected

The per-call spans carry the low-cardinality context the run loop already knows, so a backend can group and filter on one span without joins.

### Proposed change

All values below are low-cardinality and contain no message content.

1. On `openclaw.model.call`:
   - `openclaw.channel`, `openclaw.trigger`, `openclaw.lane` (same normalization as the existing run and failover spans)
   - `openclaw.fallback.attempt` (int, 0 = primary)
   - `openclaw.fallback.served` (bool, true when this call produced the final answer and was not the primary)
   - `openclaw.fallback.primary_model` (the configured primary for this run)
2. On `openclaw.tool.execution`:
   - `openclaw.tool.result_bytes`, `openclaw.tool.param_bytes`
   - `openclaw.tool.result_truncated` (bool) and `openclaw.tool.result_truncated_bytes`
   - optionally a path class instead of a raw path, for example `openclaw.tool.target_kind` = `workspace` | `home` | `tmp` | `remote` | `none`
3. A documented `diagnostics.otel.resourceAttributes` map, the config equivalent of `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, so test or shadow gateways can label themselves (for example `deployment.environment=shadow`) without env plumbing. `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` is honored today, but only via the process environment.

Per-session grouping is related but already tracked in #144294 (per-signal attribute filter), so it is left out here.

### Workaround

- Join model.call to the run span by traceId for channel and trigger.
- Read lane and fallback state from `openclaw.model.failover` spans.
- Re-emit tool result size from a local plugin and join on `gen_ai.tool.call.id`.
- Label environments in the collector (one receiver per gateway plus a resource processor).

Related: #144294, #102015, #178532.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

A guest opening the chat composer’s **Plugins** menu sees “No MCP servers yet. Add one to give the agent new tools.” when the account cannot read plugin configuration. The menu also shows **Add MCP server** disabled, so the explanation describes an empty configuration and suggests an action the guest cannot take.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an ordinary chat as a session-only guest, with `operator.sessions.read` and `operator.sessions.write` but without general configuration-read access.
2. Open **+** beside the composer, then **Plugins**.
3. Read the server-list message and inspect **Add MCP server**.

## Expected behavior

The menu should describe plugin settings as unavailable to the current account. It should distinguish unreadable configuration from a successfully loaded configuration containing no servers. Existing configuration and management permissions should continue to apply.

## Actual behavior

The menu displays “No MCP servers yet. Add one to give the agent new tools.” and disables **Add MCP server**. In the same guest context, a separate native HTTP read of the bootstrap endpoint returned200 with preferences present and configuration absent. That read was separate API evidence; the browser bootstrap response itself was not captured.

## OpenClaw version

Observed local development build: `2026.10.9-956162b11882-2026-10-30T00-50-46.668Z`. The determining menu, configuration-read policy, and copy inputs are byte-identical at main commit855d0b398a54e57719f51f168eab5b48c3437188; this does not claim a separate live execution of that commit.

## Operating system

macOS26.5.2

## Install method

Source-backed local development Gateway and browser Control UI.

## Model

Not applicable; opening this menu does not require an agent turn.

## Provider / routing chain

Browser → Gateway for the menu and configuration display state. No model request was used to establish the UI defect.

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The visible wording and disabled Add action were inspected in the rendered menu. Source inspection identifies the loss of state: [the capability host converts unavailable runtime configuration to an empty list](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/855d0b398a54e57719f51f168eab5b48c3437188/ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-capability-host.tsx#L510), then [the menu uses the empty-list message](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/855d0b398a54e57719f51f168eab5b48c3437188/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer-plugins-menu.tsx#L162). The bootstrap’s omission of configuration is intentional under the existing read policy.

## Impact and severity

This is misleading guidance for guests who cannot inspect plugin settings. The observed menu reports an empty configuration without evidence that it is empty and invites an unavailable add action. No permission grant, data loss, or tool-execution failure is established by this observation; frequency outside the observed guest scenario is not established.

## Additional information

The correction can remain within the existing configuration-read projection and menu rendering. Tool-preview entries are not a substitute for configuration data and do not establish permission to execute a tool.

issues.body:
## Problem

Images are removed from the replayed history once they fall outside the last 3 completed turns (`PRESERVE_RECENT_COMPLETED_TURNS = 3` in `history-image-prune`). The image is replaced with `[image data removed - already processed by model]`.

Users often send a screenshot with no caption, for example a chat captured on a phone. In that case nothing remains of what the image showed. From the fourth turn on, the agent cannot answer follow-up questions about it and may contradict what it said earlier. For the user, it looks like the agent forgot the screenshot.

There is no configuration option for the window.

## Related issues

- #48145 introduced the window.
- #166272 and #159201 cover the cache cost of pruning.

None of them covers the loss of the image's content.

## Proposal (any of these would help)

1. **Leave a text trace when an image is pruned**, instead of a bare placeholder. The trace could be the media-understanding description when one exists. Alternatively, as an opt-in, a description generated once when the image arrives and stored in the user message, the way `[Audio]` transcripts already are.
2. **Make the window configurable**, for example `agents.defaults.contextPruning.images.preserveTurns`, so operators can trade cache cost for continuity.
3. **At least document it.** The docs could say that images disappear after 3 turns, and point to the workaround below with its trade-off.

## Current workaround and its limits

Adding a `tools.media.models` entry with `capabilities: ["image"]`, plus a `tools.media.image.scope`, makes OpenClaw describe images on arrival. The trade-off is that the description replaces the pixels even on the current turn.

Through the Control UI, that workaround makes things worse. We tested an image via `chat.send` followed by five short turns:

- The description reaches the prompt on the turn the image arrives.
- It is not persisted, and the described image is not replayed either.
- From the second turn on, neither the image nor its description is left in the prompt. That is worse than the default 3-turn window.

This is the same persistence gap as #179676: text derived from attachments sent through the Control UI is never written to the transcript.

Environment: OpenClaw 2026.10.4, embedded OpenClaw runtime, `openai-chatgpt-responses`.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let an authorized Gateway client audition an existing configured TTS persona for one `tts.speak` request without changing the active persona.

### Problem to solve

[Pincer #413](https://github.com/hartra344/pincer/issues/413) asks to preview a provider, voice, or persona before switching the Gateway default. This proposal covers only the configured-persona selection.

The Gateway already lists personas, changes the active persona, and returns synthesized audio inline. On main at `155264e767c70d716672833919d45c8c4f73b2bc`, however, `tts.speak` accepts only `text`, and the synthesis owner selects the persona from saved preferences or configuration. Auditioning persona B therefore requires changing the active preference, speaking, and restoring persona A. There is no request-local selection through the existing persona owner.

### Proposed solution

Add an optional configured persona ID to `tts.speak`, for example `{ text, persona }`; the field name is open to owner review.

- Validate the ID against existing configured personas before provider synthesis. Reject empty or unknown IDs using the existing invalid-request response.
- Apply the selection within that synthesis request through the existing TTS owner, preserving provider precedence, persona bindings, fallback policy, credential handling, text limits, and inline audio delivery.
- Do not write the active preference. An ordinary request made while the preview runs must continue using the active persona.
- Return enough selection/binding information to distinguish an applied persona binding from provider-defaults fallback, without returning credentials or configuration values.
- Preserve existing behavior when the selector is absent and retain `operator.write` authorization.

This extends the existing request, rather than adding a preview RPC, UI, provider integration, or model tool. In particular, `fallbackPolicy: "fail"` still skips an unbound provider and may try others; it does not mean the whole request immediately fails.

### Alternatives considered

- **Set, speak, restore:** available today, but mutates the shared preference and can affect unrelated speech.
- **Conversion/audio retrieval:** [#132548](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/132548) and [#132560](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/132560) cover remote conversion output. They do not select a configured persona for one request.
- **Provider/voice preview:** [#71487](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/71487) and [#75479](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75479) cover settings and provider/voice previews; the latter explicitly leaves persona resolution unchanged. Neither PR is evidence that this persona path is implemented.
- **Client/plugin resolution:** duplicating provider-specific persona bindings in the client or temporarily changing preferences would duplicate the existing persona owner's work. The runtime TTS facade also lacks request-local persona selection overriding an active saved persona.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: remote operator clients offering configured-persona previews; Pincer supplies one concrete request. Installation count is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: a workflow limitation with a manual workaround; no outage or urgent incident is established.
- Frequency: unknown.
- Practical consequences: clients must change the active selection or omit persona auditioning. Concurrent-speech effects follow from the shared preference model; no measured incident or time loss is claimed.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original client request](https://github.com/hartra344/pincer/issues/413), created September 29, 2026; its older protocol description was checked against current main.
- [Text-only request schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/155264e767c70d716672833919d45c8c4f73b2bc/packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/channels.ts#L45) and [current handler](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/155264e767c70d716672833919d45c8c4f73b2bc/src/gateway/server-methods/tts.ts#L180).
- [Request setup selects the saved persona](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/155264e767c70d716672833919d45c8c4f73b2bc/src/tts/tts-synthesis-support.ts#L140) and [documented resolution/fallback rules](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/155264e767c70d716672833919d45c8c4f73b2bc/docs/tools/tts/personas.md).

Verification is source/document inspection. No live Gateway, paid provider, or native-client experiment was run.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Implementation entry points: `TtsSpeakParamsSchema`, the Gateway TTS handler, and request setup in `src/tts/tts-synthesis.ts` / `src/tts/tts-synthesis-support.ts`. Resolve the validated request selection before provider preparation, using that same persona for its bindings and persona-derived provider candidates; retain explicit/saved provider precedence and the current request cleanup lifecycle. Regenerate affected native protocol models through existing generators. Parameter and response metadata names remain design choices; no implementer is committed.

Non-goals: creating/cloning voices, recording or consent flows, settings UI, new provider/voice controls, remote file downloads, fallback-policy changes, or new persistent state/configuration. The [voice-creation scope rejection in #159947](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159947#issuecomment-5892782480) is relevant context for keeping this request narrow.

Older Gateways may reject the new field under their closed schema; clients should retain no-preview behavior on unsupported hosts. Do not silently emulate it by changing global preferences. Existing synthesis charges still apply.

Acceptance criteria:

- With active persona A and configured persona B bound to a test provider, selecting B returns playable inline audio using B's binding; `tts.status` and saved preferences still identify A.
- While B awaits its provider, an ordinary request still uses A. B's success or failure never changes A.
- Unknown/empty IDs fail before a provider call; unauthorized callers cannot synthesize through the selector.
- No-selector requests retain selection and fallback behavior; preview results accurately identify binding/fallback outcomes.
- Verify remote-client playback and unchanged preferences through an isolated Gateway; handler/provider tests support that flow proof.

issues.body:
### Summary

Mirror a person's session reaction onto the corresponding delivered assistant reply in its bridged chat channel.

### Problem to solve

A person reading a bridged conversation in a Gateway client can react to an assistant reply, but that action stays inside the session. People reading the reply in the external channel do not see it.

The Pincer maintainer identifies this as [remaining upstream work after adopting session reactions](https://github.com/hartra344/pincer/issues/114#issuecomment-5918418788). This proposal covers assistant-reply mirroring only; agent acknowledgments and inbound reaction storage are separate requests.

On main at `155264e767c70d716672833919d45c8c4f73b2bc`, the reaction handler explicitly skips assistant entries. Channel-origin prompts can already be mirrored. Delivery infrastructure also retains some platform message IDs; the missing relationship is a trustworthy association from the canonical assistant entry to its confirmed channel delivery, usable by the reaction owner.

### Proposed solution

Extend the existing session-reaction and channel-delivery owners, retaining `session.reactions.set` and the channel `react` action. Start with newly delivered assistant text replies corresponding unambiguously to one confirmed physical channel message.

- Associate the canonical assistant entry with the confirmed delivery receipt and its existing session/conversation/account/thread identity. Obtain both ends from their owners; do not trust client-supplied native IDs or match reply text.
- Use that association in the existing mirroring path. Preserve bot-reaction aggregation, ordering, single-slot handling, and current authorization/dispatch checks. The external reaction represents the bot, not an impersonation of the person.
- Keep the association across a Gateway restart under the existing message/session metadata owner and its deletion lifecycle. Do not rewrite model-visible transcript history.
- Missing, unconfirmed, or ambiguous associations keep the local reaction and return the existing explicit skipped mirror result. Historical replies and multi-message/fan-out delivery remain outside this initial scope.
- Association or mirror failure must never turn a successful channel send into a failed send or resend the assistant reply.

### Alternatives considered

- React in the channel app: works, but requires leaving the Gateway client and locating the reply.
- Keep local-only reactions: records the signal without delivering it to external participants.
- Invoke channel `react` with a known native ID: the action already exists, but ordinary clients lack the authoritative entry-to-delivery association. Text matching and transient caches fail for repeated replies or after restart.
- Add a client-specific mapping plugin: duplicates host-owned transcript/delivery relationships while the shared reaction handler still skips assistant entries. Extending the existing owners serves clients using the current API without a second reaction system.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: people reacting in Gateway clients to replies also delivered into reaction-capable channels. Pincer supplies one concrete request; affected user count is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: a missing delivery capability with a manual channel-app workaround; no urgent incident is established.
- Frequency: the handler currently skips every assistant entry; desired usage frequency is unknown.
- Practical consequences: feedback visible inside the session is absent on the corresponding external reply.

### Evidence/examples

- [Pincer's narrowed remaining request](https://github.com/hartra344/pincer/issues/114#issuecomment-5918418788).
- [Supported reactions and explicit assistant-reply exclusion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/155264e767c70d716672833919d45c8c4f73b2bc/docs/concepts/multi-user.md#reactions).
- [Assistant skip and existing guarded mirror dispatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/155264e767c70d716672833919d45c8c4f73b2bc/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-reactions.ts#L59).
- [#161053](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161053) explicitly excluded assistant mirroring. Its merged [follow-up #162434](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162434) addressed worker writes, dispatch revalidation, and single-slot behavior rather than adding this relationship.

Verification is source/document inspection, not a live channel reproduction.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Suggested entry points: `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-reactions.ts`, the current durable delivery owners in `src/channels/message/send.ts` and `src/channels/turn/durable-delivery.ts`, and the canonical assistant append/commit path in `src/config/sessions/transcript.ts`. `src/infra/outbound/deliver-transcript.ts` is an existing integration point for mirrored outbound messages. Existing delivery records supply receipt facts, but their conversation-owned retention cannot substitute for a session-instance-and-entry-scoped association. Use the existing session/database worker owner; the storage representation and any migration implications need implementation review.

Non-goals: historical backfill, guessed IDs, multipart/fan-out semantics, inbound reaction ingestion, agent-targeted reactions, reaction-triggered turns, ratings/analytics, new notifications, or a new model tool/configuration hierarchy. No implementer is committed.

Acceptance criteria:

- A session reaction on a newly delivered, single-message assistant reply adds the bot's reaction to that exact external message through the existing API.
- Reloading the client and restarting the Gateway retain enough identity for later removal, following the existing aggregation and channel slot rules.
- Legacy, unknown, ambiguous, or unsupported multi-message delivery keeps the local reaction and explicitly skips mirroring.
- View-only/revoked callers cannot cause channel writes. Session reset or conversation rebinding cannot redirect an old association to another message, account, or thread.
- Unchanged repeated reactions cause no additional platform operation. Mirroring neither wakes the agent nor rewrites history or resends the answer.
- Verify through an isolated Gateway and a channel returning a confirmed receipt; fixture rows alone must not bypass the real entry-to-delivery relationship.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Since #161806, every isolated cron run adds the previous session id to the job's base row `usageFamilySessionIds`. The disk-budget pass treats each listed id as a live reference, so cron history is never evicted. On our persistent agent the store reached 1,020 MiB against `maxDiskBytes: "96mb"` within 7 days.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Gateway ≥ 2026.10.1 with `session.maintenance: { mode: "enforce", maxDiskBytes: "96mb" }`.
2. Add an isolated `agentTurn` cron job on a 5–30 min schedule and let it run for a day.
3. Query the agent DB:
   ```sql
   SELECT session_key, json_array_length(entry_json, '$.usageFamilySessionIds')
   FROM session_nodes WHERE session_key LIKE '%:cron:%' AND session_key NOT LIKE '%:run:%';
   SELECT session_key, count(*) FROM session_windows GROUP BY 1;
   ```
4. Watch `[sessions/history-eviction]` in the gateway log.

### Expected behavior

Earlier rollover windows should be evicted oldest-first once usage passes `maxDiskBytes`; the maintenance docs (`docs/reference/session-management-compaction/maintenance.md:26`) say "Retained reset history is bounded by the disk budget". On 2026.9.9 the same agent with the same config held at 78–116 MiB for three weeks.

### Actual behavior

Each base row's list grows by one id per run, and no earlier window is ever evicted. Once the pre-upgrade history was gone, every pass reclaimed nothing.

Mechanism at v2026.10.4:

1. `src/cron/isolated-agent/session.ts:303-322`: `resolveCronSession` carries `usageFamilySessionIds` forward and calls `preserveSqliteSameKeySessionRolloverLineage` (#161806).
2. `src/config/sessions/session-entry-lineage.ts:95-117`: unions the previous list with the previous and next ids, with no cap or age bound.
3. `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-references.ts:20-39`: `collectSessionStateIdsForEntry` returns every family id as a retained generation (pre-10.x).
4. `session-accessor.sqlite-lifecycle-state.ts:188` (`readReferencedSessionIds`) feeds `session-history-eviction-candidates.ts:162-184`, which computes historical = windows minus referenced, so family members are never candidates. The base row updates every run and is never archived; the reaper preserves base sessions (`src/cron/session-reaper.ts:110`).
5. `session-history-budget-state.ts:182-195` logs the warning.

`session-cold-storage-eligibility.ts:64-68` also protects family ids, so `coldStorage` cannot reclaim them either (from source; not tested).

The code is identical at v2026.10.5, v2026.10.10-beta.2 and main 59c74d5. #172072 (for #171913; in 10.10-beta.1+, not in 10.5) stops `:run:` rows from copying the list, but the base row keeps growing; its test asserts this.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.4. Last good: 2026.9.9. First bad: 2026.10.1 (source); the first version we ran was 2026.10.2.

### Operating system

Linux (Debian-based container), x86_64, local ext4

### Install method

docker (FROM ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw)

### Model

n/a (storage path; model-independent)

### Provider / routing chain

n/a

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```text
[sessions/history-eviction] session history disk budget remains exceeded after cleanup; retained data is protected or could not be reclaimed. Raise session.maintenance.maxDiskBytes or export and delete unneeded sessions; automatic checks resume on activity after 30 minutes storePath=/root/.openclaw/agents/<agent>/sessions/sessions.json totalBytes=971943936 maxBytes=100663…
```

Our capture ends at this point; per the source, the line also carries `highWaterBytes` and `nextCheckAt`. The last `cleanup completed` was 2026-10-14 05:42 UTC, and the first `remains exceeded` followed at 05:47 UTC.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

One persistent agent. Its busiest isolated jobs run every 5 min, every 30 min (×2), hourly and every 2 h.

- Agent DB size: 164 MiB (10-14) → 329 → 451 → 598 → 741 → 926 → 1,020 MiB (10-20). Before the upgrade it was 78–116 MiB.
- 1,632 of 1,652 `session_windows` are cron windows listed in a base row. The largest lists hold 755, 291, 291, 146 and 73 ids.
- Sizes including indexes: `transcript_events` 476 MiB, `trajectory_runtime_events` 268 MiB, `transcript_event_identities` 124 MiB. The freelist is 21 pages (`auto_vacuum=2`), so these are live rows.

### Impact and severity

This affects every persistent agent with frequent isolated crons, always. No setting bounds the growth: `pruneAfter` and `maxEntries` count rows, `cron.sessionRetention` covers only `:run:` rows, and both the disk budget and cold storage skip family ids. Large agent DBs slow boot integrity checks and maintenance (#162319, #170204).

### Additional information

#161806 left this open on purpose: "Deletion retention needs a separate maintainer-approved design."

Fix options, from reading the source:

- Leave `usageFamilySessionIds` out of the disk-budget reference set and out of cold-storage protection. `readReferencedSessionIds` already takes `diskBudget`; both its JSON path and its SQL-projection path need the change. Leave `collectSessionStateIdsForEntry` alone, because explicit delete relies on it. The cost: an evicted run's usage leaves `sessions.usage`, as it does today for every budget-evicted session. Rollups are a cache pruned once their transcript is gone (`src/infra/session-cost-usage-worker.ts:414-423`).
- At rollover, drop family ids that no longer have a window or archive.
- A fixed cap alone would bring back Unattributed rows for older runs that are still retained (#156999).

Related: #162319, #171913, #172072, #156999.
