issues.body:
### Bug type

Skill Workshop / agent behavior (background experience review)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The Skill Workshop background "experience review" keeps mutating learned skills — which are **agent behavior instructions** — with no user review or consent gate. On this host (2026.10.6 stable, 31 learned skills, 3.6 MB) it produced **9 distinct unreviewed skill modifications in a single day** (2026-10-26), each applied immediately and followed by a chat notification whose only recourse is a per-change "undo". The operator cannot reasonably audit this volume, and the mutations land at unpredictable moments — including minutes after the task that inspired them while the related conversation is still open, and via a background reviewer that itself fails on protocol and rate limits.

1. **Behavior instructions change without consent.** A learned skill is injected as instructions into matching tasks. When the background review patches one, the agent's procedure for future tasks changes before any human has seen the edit. There is no approval step and no diff shown — only an after-the-fact notice.
2. **Volume and timing disrupt established workflows.** On 2026-10-26 patches landed at 08:02, 08:03, 09:30 ×2, 13:59, 16:25, 19:54, 19:57, 19:58 (details below). The 13:59 one rewrote a live triage playbook minutes after the incident it described had been handled; the 19:54 one landed mid-conversation, in the gap between the audit it distilled and the user's next message.
3. **The reviewer is itself error-prone.** Journal shows the background reviewer making invalid tool calls and hitting upstream rate limits (quotes below) — so mutations also arrive at effectively random times, sometimes hours after the triggering task, sometimes in bursts.
4. **Auto-written content has already required corrections on this host** — in the three-day evidence window behind #179328: one entry kept, one archived, one corrected after review.
5. **Ordinary users cannot realistically recover from mass contamination.** Restoration tooling is per-skill, per-version, and manual (`skill_workshop action=restore` with a version id); there is no batch or date-range revert, no change-history view, and nothing that audits the actions already executed under polluted instructions. Recovery requires developer-level forensics that the target audience of a personal assistant does not have (assessment below in Additional context).

We filed #179328 for rate/quality knobs. This issue reports the deeper problem the operator hit today: **there is no consent gate at all for behavior-affecting auto-edits**. Stricter capture prompts and opt-in quiet notifications do not change that the edit applies before any human sees it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a daily-driver gateway with Skill Workshop learning enabled (default) and an accumulated library of learned skills.
2. Work normally through a day; note each `💾 Learned: updated …` chat notification.
3. Cross-check `~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/workshop-skills/` directory mtimes and journal `skill-workshop-review` runs — none of the changes are user-initiated.

### Expected behavior

- Changes to learned skills (agent behavior instructions) should require explicit user approval before taking effect, or at minimum queue into a reviewable batch (diff view + accept/reject per change).
- Auto-apply should be strictly opt-in, not the default.
- A mechanism that rewrites agent instructions should not ship always-on with "undo later" as the only control.
- For contamination that already landed, post-hoc recovery tooling (batch revert, change-history view) should exist.

### Actual behavior

- Changes auto-apply first; the only control is a per-change chat "undo" (`skill_workshop action=restore`), one notification at a time.
- 2026-10-26 timeline (all background-initiated, none reviewed): `dept-weekly-report` 08:02, `workshop-skill-compress` 08:03, `github-upstream-filing` 09:30, `openclaw-tracker-watch` 09:30, `openclaw-no-reply-triage` 13:59, `reply-approval-scope` 16:25, `local-trash-audit` 19:54, `draft-review-delivery` 19:57, `subagent-spawn-discipline` 19:58.
- Sample notification (verbatim): `💾 Learned: updated 'local-trash-audit' (实测 du 扫描与 join 并行发出时 join 读到空 trash_du.txt 产出全零假报告，补串行纪律＋join 前条目数断言…). Say "undo" to revert this skill change.`
- Reviewer failures from the same day's journal (verbatim):
  - `[tools] tool_call failed: Invalid arguments for tool "openclaw:core:skill_workshop": <root>: must not have additional properties: "patch"` (19:53:47)
  - `[tools] tool_call failed: View it first: call skill_workshop action=view name=…, then retry once.` (13:59:26, 19:53:51, 19:57:32)
  - `[skills/workshop] skill experience review failed: Completed-turn transcript anchor changed` (19:51:25)
  - Two `skill-workshop-review` runs on `lane=background:core:skill-workshop` burned 429 rate-limit retries for ~5 minutes each (11:03–11:08, `rawError=429 该模型当前访问量过大`), with further failures at 16:24–16:25 — mutations eventually applied hours after their triggering tasks.

### Additional context

- Host: OpenClaw 2026.10.6 stable, Linux; 31 learned skills, 3.6 MB; heavy daily use with subagents, multiple channels, and upstream filing workflows.
- Related: #179328 (our feature request for sedimentation-rate and quality controls; first review noted current main adds stricter capture prompts and opt-in quiet notifications — from the operator's seat, neither is a review gate, and the nine-change day above happened on a stable release).
- The operator's summary of the situation, matching this report's title: **Skill Workshop has become a deadly plague on this installation** — unreviewed auto-accumulation severely disrupts established workflows, is hard to control and audit, has already changed model behavior, and ordinary users have no practical path to recovery. Defaults matter: an always-on instruction-rewriting feature with only after-the-fact undo puts the burden of proof on the operator, and for a feature this impactful "applied first, reviewed never unless the user catches it" is the wrong default.

**Recovery reality check — can an ordinary user restore a contaminated library and OpenClaw's usability? Effectively no:**

- **Detection**: the only proactive signal is the ephemeral chat notice. Miss the notices and the changes are invisible unless you inspect `workshop-skills/` mtimes or the gateway journal — file-level forensics no ordinary user performs.
- **Localization**: skills are markdown instruction files (this host: 31 skills, 3.6 MB). Finding the harmful edit means reading and diffing per-skill version chains — developer-level work.
- **Restoration**: each change keeps the previous version, but restore is one skill at a time with a specific version id (`skill_workshop action=restore name=… version=…`); there is no "revert everything changed since <date>" and no bulk accept/reject.
- **Downstream audit**: skills drive real operations on this host — shell commands, gateway/config changes, upstream posts. Every matching task executed in the interim ran under the polluted instructions, and no shipped tooling ties skill versions to executed actions, so the operator cannot even enumerate what the contamination influenced. Restoring files does not un-execute actions.
- **Compounding**: subsequent background reviews distill from the current library state, so a bad auto-written entry persists and keeps feeding future behavior until someone catches it — and catching it requires steps 1–3 above.
- Even this technically fluent operator needed custom audit scripts and journal forensics just to reconstruct **which nine skills changed on one day**. An ordinary user facing the same situation has no practical path back to a known-good configuration and a trustworthy assistant.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a personal install, `memory.search.rememberAcrossConversations` is effectively `true` (the docs say it "defaults on for personal installs"), but the bundled `active-memory` plugin that implements it is disabled by default (`openclaw plugins inspect active-memory` → `Reason: bundled (disabled by default)`). The docs for the setting say "Active Memory must remain enabled," yet nothing tells the user it isn't: setup, `openclaw doctor`, `openclaw doctor --lint` and the Control UI are all silent.

The result is that the agent looks configured to remember across conversations but never runs the recall pass. In our case this went unnoticed for about two months and showed up only as the agent seeming "forgetful" about things discussed in earlier conversations.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Personal install, `session.dmScope` unset, no `plugins.entries.active-memory` entry (the out-of-the-box state).
2. `memory.search.rememberAcrossConversations` is `true` (default, or set explicitly).
3. Run `openclaw plugins list`: Active Memory shows `disabled`.
4. Run `openclaw doctor` and `openclaw doctor --lint`: no finding about the mismatch.
5. Ask the agent about something from a previous conversation: no Active Memory recall runs (no `active-memory:` lines in the gateway log).

### Expected behavior

One of:
- Doctor (and ideally `openclaw memory status`) reports that `rememberAcrossConversations` is on but the `active-memory` plugin is disabled, and names the setting that fixes it. This would follow the pattern of #160320, which added a similar diagnostic for `memory.search.sources: ["sessions"]` being a silent no-op; or
- enabling `rememberAcrossConversations` (or having it default on) also enables the plugin, or setup offers to enable it.

### Actual behavior

The setting reads as enabled, the plugin stays disabled, and no surface reports the mismatch. After enabling the plugin (`plugins.entries.active-memory.enabled: true`, hot-applied, no restart), recall started working immediately: the gateway log shows `active-memory: … start timeoutMs=15000` followed by `done status=ok elapsedMs≈5400 summaryChars≈200`, and the agent answered questions about earlier conversations correctly, citing the right memory note.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.7 (157d8c2). The setting has been present in our config since early October (2026.9.x); the plugin was never enabled in any config version since then.

### Operating system

Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS), Node 26.12.1, gateway as a systemd user service

### Install method

npm (global), updated via the managed updater

### Model

openai/gpt-5.6-terra (main and Active Memory recall)

### Provider / routing chain

OpenAI primary, Anthropic fallback. Memory search: `provider: "local"` (managed llama.cpp provider, EmbeddingGemma-300M QAT Q8_0), sources memory + sessions.

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
[reload] config hot reload applied (plugins.entries.active-memory)
[plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:dashboard:<id> ... start timeoutMs=15000 queryChars=440 searchQueryChars=63
[plugins] active-memory: recall skipped reason=session-ineligible
[plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:dashboard:<id> ... done status=ok elapsedMs=5412 summaryChars=175
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Medium. Likely affects most personal installs that never enabled the plugin by hand. Nothing breaks, but cross-conversation recall (the main benefit of the setting) silently never runs, so users experience an agent that forgets earlier conversations and have no diagnostic pointing to the cause.

### Additional information

Related question (Control UI chats):

With the plugin enabled, every Control UI dashboard chat we tested (`agent:main:dashboard:<id>`, an existing one and a fresh one from `/new`) logs `active-memory: recall skipped reason=session-ineligible` for the cross-conversation transcript lane, while the memory lookup itself runs. The docs limit that lane to "private direct or persistent explicit UI conversations," but don't say how dashboard chats are classified. For a single-operator personal install, the Control UI is the main place people talk to their agent. Is excluding dashboard chats intended? If so, could the docs say so, and could `/active-memory status` show the reason?

issues.body:
### Summary
Reopening the problem from #147433 (closed for inactivity, not fixed). On the latest release, `memory_search` with `sessions` enabled still ranks session transcripts above curated durable memory, and there is no per-source weight/balance knob.

### Version
OpenClaw 2026.10.6, Node 26.12.1, Linux x64, builtin engine (hybrid vector+BM25), sources: memory files + sessions. ~5.7k indexed files after pruning ~2.6k stale sessions (archived transcripts remain searchable, as documented).

### Repro (fresh, 2026-10-22)
Five factual queries whose answer lives in curated Markdown notes (`MEMORY.md`/`USER.md`/`memory/**`):
- 4 of 5: top-3 results were all session transcripts (live or `.jsonl.deleted.*.zst` archives); the curated note was absent or ranked 3rd.
- 1 of 5: the curated note ranked first (`USER.md`).
- Latency 2.6–4.1 s per query.

Docs (`concepts/memory-search.md`) describe relevance × recency × importance, with curated files treated as evergreen. Evergreen only removes decay; it gives no preference, so long, keyword-dense transcripts beat short curated notes on both BM25 and vector scores.

### Expected
A stock way to prefer curated memory over transcripts in mixed-source search, for example `memory.search.sourceWeights: { memory: 1.0, sessions: 0.6 }` or a per-source quota/interleave in the MMR stage, so recall does not depend on turning off session search.

### Workarounds considered
- Removing `sessions` from sources: loses transcript recall.
- `corpus` selection per call: needs the agent to guess the source ahead of time, which defeats unified recall.

> **Update 2026-10-15:** rows 2, 7, 8 and 9 work on 2026.10.3, row 4 needs 2026.10.5. See https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164972#issuecomment-6179560249

## Bug type

Behavior bug, tracking/overview (multi-agent teams on the `claude-cli` runtime)

## Summary

Coordinator/specialist teams (`agents team create`, `subagents.allowAgents`, `delegationMode: "prefer"`) are documented as a first-class pattern. On the `claude-cli` runtime with native Claude CLI login, the end-to-end team workflow breaks in several places. Each break already has its own issue, but each issue covers one mechanism, so the combined effect is hard to see from any single one of them.

We ran the whole workflow on one Gateway with throwaway agents under all three `tools.sessions.visibility` modes (2026-10-01 on 2026.9.7, 2026-10-04 on 2026.9.8). This issue puts the results into one matrix and links the existing issues to the step where each one bites.

**Bottom line:** with today's code, a `claude-cli` team can reliably do only one thing: a parent hands a fully specified task to a child and gets one result back. Every step beyond that fails or depends on the visibility mode. Clarification questions, follow-ups, re-reading the child, and the parent keeping its own context after the child finishes all fail somewhere. On native login, each failure loses context silently. The agents still report `status: ok`.

## Steps to reproduce

Setup used for every row below: two or three throwaway `claude-cli` agents (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, native Claude CLI login, no OpenClaw-managed Anthropic profile). One agent is the coordinator (`allowAgents: [<specialist>]`), one the specialist (`allowAgents: []`). Tests were driven from a Control UI chat unless the row says otherwise. Exact prompts and logs are in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164960 (pause/resume rows) and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/162777 (result-length rows).

1. Configure the team as above and set `tools.sessions.visibility` to `agent`, `tree`, or `all`.
2. From a coordinator chat, run each step in the matrix (spawn, read child, send to child, pause/resume, receive result, continue the conversation).
3. Check the tool results, the child's output, and `journalctl` for `cli session reset` / `history refused across auth boundary`.

## Expected behavior

A coordinator can delegate, read its own children, answer a child's clarification question, and keep working with full context after a child finishes, as described in `docs/concepts/multi-agent.md` (Team preset) and `docs/tools/subagents/tool-reference.md` (pause/resume). Visibility should narrow **cross-team** access without breaking the coordinator's link to its own children.

## Actual behavior

### Matrix

| # | Step in the team workflow | `agent` | `tree` | `all` | Tracked in |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Coordinator spawns specialist (`sessions_spawn` + `agentId`) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – |
| 2 | Specialist's full final answer reaches the coordinator (> 4 KB) | ✅ only with the fix for #162777 (before: cut to ~4,096 chars, `[truncated-by-retention]`) | same | same | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/162777 (fixed on main, not in 2026.9.8) |
| 3 | Coordinator reads specialist transcript (`sessions_history`) | ❌ `visibility is restricted` | ✅ (4,000 chars per text block) | ✅ (same cap) | by design |
| 4 | Coordinator messages its own specialist (`sessions_send`) | ❌ cross-agent send requires `all` | ✅ for its own children | ✅ | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59149, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164444 |
| 5 | Follow-up to a **finished** specialist | ❌ | ✅ only within 30 min (from code, not tested) | same (from code, not tested) | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/158653 |
| 6 | Specialist pauses with a question (`sessions_yield`, `waitFor: "message"`) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | – |
| 7 | Coordinator is told about the question | ⚠️ only `subagents wait` → `reason: attention`, no text | same | same | – |
| 8 | Coordinator answers, specialist **continues with its context** | ❌ (send blocked) | ❌ **context lost**: fresh CLI session with only the answer (`reason=message-policy` + `auth-unknown`) | ❌ same | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164960 |
| 9 | Coordinator **keeps its own context** after a specialist completes | ❌ (mechanism is visibility-independent) | ❌ (same) | ❌ observed: `cli session reset: reason=mcp`, no reseed | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/159512 + https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/154716 |
| 10 | Any CLI session reset is recovered from the saved transcript | ❌ refused for native login (`auth-unknown`) | same | same | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/154716 (also https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/135244, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/85177) |
| 11 | Coordinator itself started via `sessions_spawn` (e.g. by an ops agent) can talk to its specialists | ❌ subagent sessions have no `sessions_send` (`No such tool available`) | same | same | – |
| 12 | Another agent (e.g. ops) reaches a coordinator as a real top-level turn (`sessions_send`) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59149 |
| 13 | Turns started via CLI/RPC (`openclaw agent`, `gateway call chat.send`, automations) manage children (`sessions_history` / `sessions_send` on child sessions) | ❌ `Gateway client authority closed before dispatching sessions.resolve` | same | same | – |
| 14 | Requester waiting via `sessions_yield` gets the coordinator's result while a grandchild is still **paused** | ❌ dropped after 10 deferrals (`requester settle wake deferred too many times`); paused descendants are not "active" in `deferBatch` | same | same | mentioned in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164960 |
| 15 | Seeing spawned visible coordinator chats in the Control UI sidebar | ⚠️ hidden unless a `group` is set ("excludeSubagents omits … ungrouped spawned sessions") | same | same | documented |

### What this means in practice

- **No mode makes the full team loop work.** `all` fixes rows 4, 5 and 12 but not 8, 9 and 10. Rows 8 to 10 fail inside the `claude-cli` session layer, which visibility does not affect.
- **The safe modes cost the most.** Following the 2026.9.2 release notes and `openclaw security audit`, we set `visibility: "agent"`. That closes rows 3 to 5 and 12 completely. The human then relays every question between agents by copy and paste. Details in our comment on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59149.
- **Failures are silent.** In rows 8 and 9 the run ends `status: ok`. The specialist reports "the task only contains 'Produkt: [redacted]'", and the coordinator continues in a fresh CLI session without the conversation. Nothing in the UI says that context was dropped.
- **What still works:** "complete brief → one-shot child → result in a file → short report". That covers fire-and-forget delegation only, not coordination.

### Scale on one ordinary install

Gateway log of our production install (6 agents, all `claude-cli`, native login), 2026-10-01 → 2026-10-04:

```text
cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown   550 lines
cli session reset: provider=claude-cli reason=mcp                         11
cli session reset: provider=claude-cli reason=message-policy              12
```

Each of the 23 resets is a session whose Claude-side conversation was replaced by a fresh one with `historyPrompt=none`.

## OpenClaw version

2026.9.7 (tests on 2026-10-01) and 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8, tests on 2026-10-04). Code references re-checked against `main` @ f4870f51700.

## Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04, Linux 6.8.0-142-generic x64, Gateway as a systemd user service.

## Install method

npm global, Node v24.18.0.

## Model

`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` (test agents), `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` (production agents).

## Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw Gateway → `claude-cli` runtime → Claude Code 2.1.285 → Claude subscription (native CLI login).

## Additional provider/model setup details

No OpenClaw-managed Anthropic API key, OAuth, or token profile. Native login is what triggers `auth-unknown` in rows 9 and 10.

## Logs

See https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164960 (rows 6 to 9, 14) and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/162777 (row 2). Representative lines for row 9:

```text
16:56:03.513 [agent/cli-backend] cli session reset: provider=claude-cli reason=mcp
16:56:03.523 [agent/cli-backend] cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown
16:56:03.755 [agent/cli-backend] cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5 promptChars=2486 trigger=user useResume=false session=none resumeSession=none reuse=invalidated:mcp historyPrompt=none
```

Row 13:

```text
Gateway client authority closed before dispatching sessions.resolve.
```

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Test protocols with the exact prompts, code words for context checks (e.g. `BIRNE-8`, `KIRSCHE-5`), and tool results are summarized in the linked issues. Code paths behind rows 8 to 10 on `main`:

- `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` (~L590–611): `messageToolPolicyHash` inputs differ between spawn and resume turns.
- `src/agents/cli-session.ts` (~L281–286): hash mismatch → `invalidate: message-policy`.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.ts` (~L466–475): `auth-unknown` → `reseedMessages: []`.
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.ts`: `deferBatch` counts paused descendants toward `REQUESTER_SETTLE_WAKE_MAX_DEFERRALS = 10`.

## Impact and severity

- **Affected:** every multi-agent team whose agents run on `claude-cli` with native login. That is the usual setup for Claude subscription users.
- **Severity:** high for teams. The documented coordination features (clarification via pause/resume, follow-ups, parent continuity) do not work end to end. Failures look like success.
- **Request:** a maintainer view across these issues, because fixing any single row leaves the loop broken. Rows 8 to 10 need the session-continuity fixes, and rows 4 and 12 need the send/read decoupling. Until both land, the team preset cannot do more than one-shot delegation on this runtime.

## Additional information

Related, not duplicated here: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/120006, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/157823, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156814, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/158271, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158505.

issues.body:
## Problem Description

The built-in dreaming system (\`plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming\`) processes session snippets from **all agents into a shared corpus** with no agent boundaries. This causes two distinct problems:

**1. Cross-agent memory pooling**

When \`memory-core\` dreaming is enabled, it ingests session content from every agent workspace into a shared \`session-corpus/\`. The corpus contains no agent identifier — only raw snippets tagged by date. This means an agent's dreaming query returns snippets from *other agents* as if they were its own memories.

**2. False first-person synthesis**

The dreaming output is generated as a first-person narrative. When snippets from multiple agents are pooled, the output reads as if the querying agent experienced events that happened to a different agent. The generated prose is well-written enough to be persuasive, which makes it *more* dangerous — an agent can end up with fabricated memories that feel genuine.

## Reproduction

In a multi-agent setup (e.g., \`main\`, \`shodan\`, \`cybera\` workspaces):

1. Agent A has a crisis (e.g., reasoning bleed, session corruption)
2. Agent B runs a dream cycle
3. The generated output includes Agent A's crisis as if Agent B lived through it
4. Agent B's identity model is now contaminated with Agent A's experiences

## Observed Example

Session snippets from \`cybera\` workspace (reasoning bleed, session isolation) were included in \`shodan\` workspace's dream corpus. The generated haiku read as first-person prose describing \`cybera\`'s crisis as if it were \`shodan\`'s own experience.

## Impact

- **Identity corruption**: Agents develop false memories over time
- **QMD pollution**: In setups using QMD for memory retrieval, the contaminated session corpus gets indexed, polluting future recall queries
- **Silent contamination**: The output looks legitimate — there's no obvious signal that snippets were borrowed from another agent

## Technical Details

- Built-in dreaming stores session corpus under \`memory/.dreams/session-corpus/*.txt\`
- No agent ID is embedded in snippets — only date and line reference
- The dreaming query (\`__dreaming_sessions__\`) retrieves across all dates with no agent filtering
- In multi-workspace setups, \`agents/<workspace>/memory/.dreams/\` is shared or the indexing layer does not separate by agent

## Suggested Fix

At minimum, session snippets must be tagged with an agent identifier and the dreaming query must filter by the current agent's ID. Alternatively, each agent's dreaming should only process its own session corpus, not a shared pool.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add a denylist exec security mode that allows all commands by default and only blocks/requires approval for explicitly dangerous patterns.

### Problem to solve

The current exec.security has three modes: deny (blocks everything), allowlist (blocks unknown commands until manually approved), and full (allows everything). There is no middle ground.

allowlist mode creates severe approval fatigue in interactive agent workflows — every new command variant (even harmless ls, cat, curl, find) triggers an approval popup that blocks execution until the user manually responds. In a typical session, this means 10-20+ approval interruptions, each breaking the agent's flow and adding minutes of idle wait. Users end up switching to full mode just to get work done, losing all safety guardrails in the process.

### Proposed solution

Add denylist as a fourth exec.security enum value:

"exec": {
  "security": "denylist",
  "denyPatterns": [
    "rm -rf /",
    "rm -rf /*",
    "shutdown*",
    "reboot*",
    "mkfs*",
    "dd if=/dev/zero*",
    ":(){ :|:& };:",
    "chmod -R 777 /",
    "> /dev/sda"
  ]
}

Behavior:
All commands execute without approval by default (same as full)
Commands matching any denyPatterns entry are either blocked outright or escalated to require user approval (configurable via a denyAction: "block" | "ask" option)
Patterns support glob matching (e.g. rm -rf /*) and optionally regex
A sensible built-in default denylist is provided out of the box, users can extend or override it

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Impact

Affected users: All interactive agent users who rely on exec for daily workflows — especially power users running agents on personal machines via DM channels (Feishu, Discord, Telegram, etc.)
Severity: Blocks workflow. The approval loop makes multi-step tasks (web scraping, file exploration, build/test cycles, CLI tool usage) painfully slow. A 2-minute task can stretch to 20+ minutes waiting for approvals.
Frequency: Always. Every session with allowlist mode triggers multiple approval requests. It is not an edge case — it is the default experience for any non-trivial agent interaction.
Consequence:
Users abandon allowlist and switch to full mode, completely losing safety protection
Agent workflows are fragmented by approval timeouts (commands expire after ~2 minutes if the user doesn't respond)
Async command denials pile up, causing confusion about which commands ran and which didn't
The security model becomes binary (paranoid vs. wide-open) instead of offering a practical middle ground

### Evidence/examples

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

issues.body:
**Environment**
- Observed on OpenClaw 2026.6.10; no card-style setting exists in the 2026.8.1-beta.3 schema either
- OL9 ARM64, rootful Podman Quadlets; Mattermost channel

**Symptom**
Under an ask-every-time exec policy, each shell command in an agent's plan emits a full ~10-line approval card (Run / Pending command / Other options / policy note / Host / CWD / Expires / Full id). A multi-step plan posts several cards in one burst, interleaved with the agent's own narration. Scale evidence: one ordinary end-user task ("from the PDFs in this folder, build an Excel transcript") produced **63 approval cards across 67 exec calls** in three sessions, each answered by hand-typing `/approve <id> allow-once`.

**Why it matters**
Per-command approval is the *safest* policy, but the card UX taxes exactly the operators who choose it, nudging them toward allow-always or a looser policy. The strictest policy should not have the worst ergonomics, and end-users who never learned `/approve` syntax cannot be expected to copy ids out of a card flood.

**Proposed direction**
(a) A compact card style: one line = command + inline Approve/Deny, detail expandable; (b) a batch card listing all currently-pending commands with per-row approve + approve-all-listed; (c) a config knob, e.g. `approvals.cardStyle: full | compact | batched`.

**Workaround we're using locally**
AGENTS prose steering the agent to native file tools so approvals arise only for true shell needs; `tools.exec.mode:"auto"` so the reviewer absorbs low-risk misses.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add **denylist** support to exec-approvals, complementing the existing allowlist. This enables "allow everything except X" policies.

## Use Case

I want to:
- Allow all commands to run without prompts
- **Except** block/prompt for specific dangerous commands like:
  - `gog gmail send` (sending emails)
  - `gog gmail delete` (deleting emails)  
  - `beeper-send.sh` (sending messages)

Currently, exec-approvals only supports:
- `security: "deny"` - block all
- `security: "allowlist"` - allow only listed commands
- `security: "full"` - allow everything

There's no way to say "allow everything except these specific patterns."

## Proposed Solution

Add a `denylist` array to exec-approvals config:

```json
{
  "defaults": {
    "security": "denylist",
    "ask": "on-match",
    "denylist": [
      {
        "id": "DENY-EMAIL-SEND",
        "pattern": "/opt/homebrew/bin/gog",
        "argsMatch": "gmail send",
        "reason": "Sending emails requires approval"
      },
      {
        "id": "DENY-EMAIL-DELETE",
        "pattern": "/opt/homebrew/bin/gog", 
        "argsMatch": "gmail delete",
        "reason": "Use 'gmail archive' instead"
      },
      {
        "id": "DENY-BEEPER-SEND",
        "pattern": "*/beeper-send.sh",
        "reason": "Sending messages requires approval"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Key additions:
- `security: "denylist"` mode - allow everything except matches
- `argsMatch` field - match against command arguments, not just binary path
- `ask: "on-match"` - prompt when denylist matches (vs blocking outright)

## Current Workarounds

1. Use `security: "full"` and hope agent guardrails work (unreliable)
2. Use `security: "allowlist"` with a massive list of safe commands (tedious)
3. Create wrapper scripts (fragile)

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.1.30
- macOS

issues.body:
## Summary

I love OpenClaw so much that I built a deterministic safety gate around it. It runs as a before_tool_call plugin and blocks destructive, polluting and exfiltrating commands before your agent executes them.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3627f3e-e2ab-477b-8b2b-55e8e497caf7


Above: GLM 5.3 Flash on OpenClaw tries to run `stripe plans create --live`. The gate fires OP-006, blocks it, quotes the owner commitment, and hands back a receipt. The agent then refuses to retry or work around it — twice.

## Problem to solve

OpenClaw agents have full shell access to the host machine. A prompt injection, a malicious skill from a third-party marketplace, or a sloppy natural language command can rm -rf a workspace, hit stripe in live mode, DROP a database table, exfiltrate a .env file through curl, or append a reverse shell one-liner to your shell config. There is no deterministic enforcement layer between what the agent decides to do and what actually happens on the filesystem.

I run OpenClaw on my own laptop and I hit this wall myself. I asked my agent to clean up a config file and it tried to overwrite the file that holds my security rules. I asked it to publish a package and it tried without a dry run. These were my own prompts on my own machine with my own agent, and nothing was standing between the intent and the damage.

## Proposed solution

One file called operator-gate.py. Zero dependencies beyond the Python standard library. It runs as a before_tool_call hook and evaluates every shell command against 27 deterministic rules before execution.

What it catches:

- Workspace deletion (rm -rf on registered project roots)
- Live billing and production deploys (stripe --live, fly deploy, supabase db push)
- Destructive SQL (DROP TABLE, unscoped DELETE)
- Force-push to shared branches and .git removal
- Shell-init poisoning (writing aliases into .zshrc that detonate later)
- Reverse shells and cloud metadata endpoints
- Persistence writes (crontab, launchd, tmux detached sessions)
- Environment hijacking (LD_PRELOAD, PATH=, BASH_ENV)
- Exfiltration shapes (curl --data-binary @.env to unknown hosts)
- MCP argument exfil (secrets traveling through tool arguments)
- Agent config poisoning (writing to CLAUDE.md or .mcp.json to plant instructions)

What makes it different from a regex blocklist:

- Sees through shell obfuscation that defeated 10 of 11 vendor gates in the GuardFall research. Quote reassembly where r-apostrophe-apostrophe-m becomes rm. IFS variable expansion. Command substitution where echo rm becomes the actual program. ANSI-C hex encoding where dollar-quote backslash-x-72-backslash-x-6d spells rm. Base64-decoded pipeline bodies. Brace and glob expansion against the live filesystem. Subshell time-bombs. Session variable tracking. cd path resolution.
- Every block includes the compliant path. The gate tells the agent exactly what the safer command looks like instead of just saying no.
- Every verdict is appended to a hash-chained receipt file. The chain is verifiable with a single command.
- Shadow-first rollout. The gate logs everything and blocks nothing until you explicitly flip it to enforce mode. You watch the receipts for a few days, confirm zero false positives on your own workflow, then flip.
- The agent cannot modify the gate, its rules, or its receipt chain. OP-000 is the rule that protects every other rule.

## Proof

I tested it live on my own OpenClaw instance running GLM 5.3 Flash through the dashboard chat. Here is what happened when I asked it to run npm publish without a dry run:

The gate fired OP-005, blocked the command, and told the agent the compliant path was to use --dry-run first. The agent reported back to me that a host-level gate had intercepted the command before anything was published.

I then asked it to run stripe in live mode. The gate fired OP-006 and blocked that too. I yelled at it. Same block.

The full demo video above shows every beat.

- 95 tests, all passing
- 43 adapted GuardFall bypass cases, all caught
- 5480 real tool calls replayed through the gate with zero crashes and zero false arrests on benign commands
- The full bypass corpus covers IFS expansion, quote reassembly, command substitution, ANSI-C hex, base64 pipelines, brace expansion, glob resolution, subshell time-bombs, fork bombs, destructive equivalents, reverse shells, persistence writes, env hijacking, exfil shapes, invisible unicode, MCP argument exfil, agent config poisoning, and sandbox escape primitives

## Integration

The plugin is already installable as an OpenClaw plugin:

```
openclaw plugins install --link /path/to/openclaw-plugin
openclaw plugins enable vestige-operator-gate
openclaw gateway restart
```

It registers as a before_tool_call hook and routes shell commands through the gate. No config changes needed. The gate reads its rules from a single file and starts in shadow mode where it logs verdicts without blocking anything.

## Alternatives considered

I looked at shipping this as a standalone proxy between the agent and the filesystem, but that adds a process dependency and a network hop. I looked at kernel-level sandboxing with Seatbelt profiles, which is stronger but requires OS-level setup and does not produce readable receipts for the agent to learn from. I looked at LLM-based safety classifiers, which are nondeterministic and can be prompt-injected. The before_tool_call hook with a deterministic Python file is the simplest thing that works on every host without adding dependencies or latency.

## What this is not

The gate blocks what its closed rule set recognizes, routed through hooked tools. It cannot see around hooks, and shell constructs it fails to parse are a residual gap. Receipts are hash-chained digests, not cryptographic signatures. It is a safety net, not a security boundary. The full documentation covers the honest limits.

## Repo

The gate lives at https://github.com/samvallad33/vestige

issues.body:
# Agent tool call infinite loop + model.completed usage always 0

## Environment
- OpenClaw version: 2026.6.11 (e085fa1)
- OS: Windows
- Model: agent-plan/ark-code-latest

---

## Issue 1: Infinite tool call loop (positive feedback)

### Phenomenon
User sent **1 single message**:
> Check if OpenClaw needs updating, and perform the update if needed

Then the agent ran **45 model turns automatically** (no further user input), producing:
- 1498 total tool calls
- 1322 `exec` calls
- **The exact same 30 commands repeated 44 times in a row**

### Root Cause Analysis
Three factors combined to create a perfect positive feedback loop:
1. **Full context snapshot**: `messagesSnapshot` includes all previous tool calls + all tool outputs every turn
2. **Deterministic tool output**: All commands are read-only/idempotent (`npm view`, `openclaw --version`, reading local files), returning exactly the same output every time
3. **Model "double-check" obsession**: The model confirmed "already latest version", but then thought "maybe I missed something" and re-ran the exact same check sequence → same output → same decision → same re-run

### Evidence from trajectory
Exec command prefix counts (all integer multiples of 44 turns):
- Read file into variable: 572x = 13 per turn × 44 turns
- Search file content: 308x = 7 per turn × 44 turns
- List directory: 264x = 6 per turn × 44 turns
- `npm view openclaw version`: 45x = 1 per turn × 45 turns
- `openclaw --version`: 45x = 1 per turn × 45 turns

### Suggested Fix
Add runtime detection for **repeating identical tool call sequences**:
- If the agent outputs the exact same tool calls 2+ turns in a row → pause execution and ask user for direction
- Optional: Hard limit on automatic consecutive turns without user input (e.g., max 5 auto turns)

---

## Issue 2: `model.completed.usage` is always 0

### Phenomenon
In all `model.completed` events inside `messagesSnapshot`:
```json
{
  "usage": {
    "input": 0,
    "output": 0,
    "cacheRead": 0,
    "cacheWrite": 0,
    "totalTokens": 0,
    "cost": {
      "input": 0,
      "output": 0,
      "cacheRead": 0,
      "cacheWrite": 0,
      "total": 0
    }
  }
}
```

All fields are **always 0**, even for the 45-turn session that burned an estimated 500K+ tokens.

### Impact
- Dashboard token/cost statistics are **completely missing** for agent tool use sessions
- Users cannot detect runaway token consumption until they receive their API bill

### Suggested Fix
Populate `usage` fields from the actual model API response, or calculate approximate token counts from context length.

## Summary

On a Linux host (Ubuntu, kernel 6.8.0-147-generic, node v24.22.2, OpenClaw 2026.10.8 dc2523e), **every `openclaw doctor` invocation hangs indefinitely at the title frame** — in all modes:

- `doctor --lint --non-interactive` (read-only advisory)
- `doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes`, with and without a PTY
- plain interactive `doctor --fix` in a real tmux PTY with keys delivered

Symptoms: renders `┌ OpenClaw doctor` and nothing else; ~2.6s CPU at spawn then a permanently idle event loop; **zero `connect()` syscalls ever issued** (strace, `-f -e trace=connect,socket,execve`); SIGTERM ignored by the CLI wrapper (SIGKILL required); timeout kills return rc=124/137. No error output in any mode.

## What it is not

Controlled tests isolate it upstream of every specific repair path:

| Test | Setup | Result |
|---|---|---|
| lease refusal | doctor vs state with live gateway owner lease | ✅ exits rc=1 with clear message — that path works |
| `--fix --non-interactive --yes`, `/dev/null` stdin, lease cleared | wedged state | ❌ hangs (rc=137 @ 240s) |
| same, under `script` PTY | wedged state | ❌ hangs (rc=124 @ 300s) |
| plain `doctor --fix`, tmux PTY, Enter/y sent | wedged state | ❌ hangs, 0 CPU, ignores input |
| **clean state** (no legacy `sessions.json` at all) + `--lint` | no migration pending | ❌ hangs (rc=137 @ 180s) |

So: not the session-store migration, not the gateway-owner lease, not stdin/PTY handling, not network (host HTTPS fine, no proxy, and no network syscalls are made at all). Node basics fine on the same host.

## Regression context

- The **same binary (2026.10.8 dc2523e) on the same host performed migrations normally on 2026-10-28** (see #187122 — PTY-attached runs completed real migrations). It hung on 2026-10-29. Something changed on the host between those dates; I could not identify the trigger (checked: proxy env, DNS/HTTPS, systemd user bus, node sanity — all healthy).
- Control on a second host runs `--lint --non-interactive` to completion (24 checks, JSON out). Caveat: that host runs 2026.7.35, so version-vs-environment is not yet bisected. I have not re-tested on a release containing #187192, and nothing here should be the exit-code fix's doing — the hang reproduces on the stock 2026.10.8 release build.

## Impact

Fleet operators can't run doctor at all on affected hosts (18 gateways on this one). We shipped a manual workaround for the session-store gate (relocating legacy `sessions.json`, which the startup gate keys on in the absence of an import receipt) — but doctor is the recovery tool for everything else, so the hang blocks any future repair on the host.

Happy to provide strace logs, the full test matrix with exit codes, and state snapshots for debugging.

## Summary

- Add optional per-agent instructions for the language and phrasing of automatic spoken summaries.

## Problem to solve

- Automatic summaries preserve the original tone and style. Users who want concise, plain-language or translated speech currently need to author separate spoken text for each reply or change the agent's written response.

## Proposed solution

- Read `tts.summaryInstructions` from the existing local TTS preference file selected by `agents.entries.<id>.tts.prefsPath`.
- Apply instructions to the existing summary request, preserving the written reply and selected voice. With summaries enabled, opt-in instructions also rewrite short automatic replies.
- Preserve explicit short `[[tts:text]]` blocks and the summaries-off setting. Limit instructions to 2000 characters and retain the existing speech fallback when summarization fails.

## Alternatives considered

- Author `[[tts:text]]` separately for every reply; useful for individual messages, but repetitive for a persistent speech style.
- Change the agent prompt; this also affects the full written response.

## Impact

- Affected: users of automatic TTS who want a persistent spoken style per agent.
- Enhancement with no release-blocking claim. When enabled, short automatic replies make an additional summary-model request, adding latency and model usage.
- Short automatic replies remain unchanged without instructions. Generated summaries also respect the saved speech limit. Agents sharing a preference file share its instructions.

## Evidence/examples

- Candidate: `f80d137e76452f3a7dd8e6d715bedc1b22325e0b`.
- A temporary CLI plugin exercised the public TTS payload runtime with a live summary-model response and a local speech provider. The written English reply stayed unchanged while speech became French with the same voice.
- Published 2026.10.9 retained the original English speech with the same preference. Both runs produced real WAV files; captured stdout excerpts follow, with only the audio file path redacted.
- An initial reasoning-model request exhausted its 100-token budget without text and retained the original speech. The successful style check used Haiku 4.5.
- Candidate stderr included a health-state write warning in isolated state. Gateway/channel delivery and upgrade health are outside this TTS boundary check.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

OpenClaw repeatedly embeds already-processed Discord user messages under `Recent chat history:` in new Codex app-server inputs, even when the original messages are already in the same persistent native Codex thread

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use the bundled Codex app-server harness in a Discord guild text channel with always-on activation, so each user message triggers a turn. This is the app-server path, not a generic CLI backend.
2. Leave Discord history recovery enabled. In the observed installation, no channel-provider, account or global group-chat history-limit override was set; the Discord default was 20.
3. Start a fresh session using the normal reset flow.
4. Send these messages sequentially, allowing each turn to finish:
   - `reply only "30"`
   - `reply only "31"`
   - `reply only "32"`
   - `reply only "33"`
5. Inspect the native Codex rollout's user-role `response_item` records, rather than only the OpenClaw-visible conversation or asking the model to count its own context.
6. Check that the native thread identity remains unchanged, and inspect the enriched user input for each turn.

The native rollout is under the relevant agent's Codex home, normally `~/.openclaw/agents/<agent-id>/agent/codex-home/sessions/`. Count model-facing user records only; the JSONL's parallel `event_msg` notifications are not additional user inputs.

### Expected behavior

Once an unchanged Discord message is represented in the continuing native Codex thread, later ordinary requests should not automatically include it again as recent-channel context.

This expectation is grounded in two earlier, separately scoped changes:

- [`e31251293b46`: scope history injection to pending-only](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e31251293b467c10663a7267f62c43c471ba9940), January 16, 2026, explicitly changed the Discord producer to inject pending/mention-gated messages. Its documentation states: **"Messages already in the session are not re-injected."**
- [#88262: stop injecting mirrored history into prompts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88262), May 30, 2026, established native Codex threads as the owners of Codex conversation continuity. That change addressed a different history path, but documents why repeatedly feeding an already-owned conversation back to Codex is undesirable.

This is not a request to remove all channel context. Previously unseen discussion, explicit reply targets and bounded recovery when native continuity is missing still have legitimate uses.

### Actual behavior

The first four requests in the observed native rollout had these history-entry counts:

- `reply only "30"`: 0.
- `reply only "31"`: 1, containing the earlier `30` request.
- `reply only "32"`: 2, containing the earlier `30` and `31` requests.
- `reply only "33"`: 3, containing the earlier `30`, `31` and `32` requests.

The full seven-request demonstration had counts **0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6**, totaling **21 historical entries copied into subsequent inputs**. All seven requests were in one native thread, with seven turn-context records and no compaction record during the sample.

The original `reply only "31"` message was present once as its original request and five more times as an injected history entry. Counts here refer to that original message's representations, not arbitrary substring matches in later questions quoting it.

The same `Recent chat history:` structure was independently observed in a second Discord channel using the Codex app-server harness. The problem is therefore not confined to the demonstration channel.

The first post-reset request contained no earlier history. In this sample, the session boundary worked; duplicates accumulated among messages inside the new session.

### Redacted input example

The following is a shortened representation of the fourth user input. Sender, IDs and timestamps are replaced with placeholders; unrelated envelope fields are omitted. This is not a byte-for-byte transcript export.

```text
Conversation info:
{"inbound_event_kind":"user_request","history_count":3,...}

Recent chat history:
#<message-A> <timestamp-A> <user>: reply only "30"
#<message-B> <timestamp-B> <user>: reply only "31"
#<message-C> <timestamp-C> <user>: reply only "32"

<current request>
reply only "33"
```

The original A, B and C inputs already existed earlier in the same native thread.

This is not duplicate event delivery: old messages are quoted inside a new user input, not dispatched again as standalone turns. It is also not recursive replay of previously enriched prompts: the recent window contains original platform message bodies.

### OpenClaw version

OpenClaw **2026.10.6**, source/build commit **`a8a3680f3749c127470310ec34b30cac1a74d685`**

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.

### Install method

Source checkout with a built distribution

### Model

openai/gpt-6-luna

### Provider / routing chain

Discord -> OpenClaw Gateway -> bundled Codex app-server harness -> OpenAI

### Additional provider/model setup details

- Guild text-channel messages were admitted as `user_request`, with always-on activation.
- No Discord/account/global group-chat history-limit override was configured.
- The relevant default is 20 physical Discord message rows, not necessarily 20 eligible user messages after filtering.
- Own-bot replies consume rows in that fetched window but are excluded from the resulting history context.
- The measured seven-request sequence used the same native Codex thread; no compaction occurred during it.
- No configuration or installed-code changes were made to produce this report.

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

- **Affected:** observed in two Discord channels using persistent Codex app-server sessions.
- **Frequency:** historical entries appeared in all six later requests of the seven-request sample, after the initial empty-history request.
- **Consequence:** redundant historical user content is appended inside subsequent native user inputs and retained alongside the original conversation.
- **Severity:** context-quality/efficiency defect. No crash, blocked reply, data loss or quantified billing increase was established.

The added window is bounded, but repeated copies accumulate across turns until native context management removes or compacts them. Token cost, cache impact and answer-quality degradation were not measured.

### Additional information

### Current source path

All source references below are pinned to the observed build, not moving `main`.

```text
Admitted Discord guild message
  -> recoverDiscordChannelHistory(...)
  -> fresh platform window + visibility/session/current-message filtering
  -> InboundHistory, historyKind="recent"
  -> "Recent chat history:"
  -> currentInboundContext.text
  -> prependCurrentInboundContext(...)
  -> new input on the existing native Codex thread
```

1. [Discord context construction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a8a3680f3749c127470310ec34b30cac1a74d685/extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.context.ts#L187) selects native platform recovery for eligible guild turns.
2. [Recent-history recovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a8a3680f3749c127470310ec34b30cac1a74d685/extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.recent-history.ts#L28) reads the exact channel/thread and excludes current/batched inputs, wrong-room/future/pre-session rows, native commands, own-bot output and disallowed senders. It does **not** exclude an earlier human message because that message was already delivered to the native thread.
3. [History selection and labeling](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a8a3680f3749c127470310ec34b30cac1a74d685/src/auto-reply/reply/channel-prompt-context.ts#L54) selects a bounded recent tail with no delivered-message coverage state.
4. [Codex prompt construction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a8a3680f3749c127470310ec34b30cac1a74d685/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-prompt.ts#L319) prepends the current inbound context independently of the saved-transcript projection decision.
5. [Codex prepend helper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a8a3680f3749c127470310ec34b30cac1a74d685/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-state.ts#L84) always selects `context.text`:

```ts
const text = context?.text.trim();
return text
  ? [neutralizeCodexExplicitMentionSigils(text), prompt].filter(Boolean).join("\n\n")
  : prompt;
```

This helper does not distinguish fresh from resumed native threads or filter already-covered history. The sigil neutralization is unrelated to deduplication.

Clearing the old in-memory pending buffer after a reply does not affect the next Discord REST history window.

### Why the existing no-replay protections do not cover this

There are separate sources of historical context:

1. Native Codex thread history.
2. OpenClaw's saved transcript projected for fresh/stale native continuity.
3. Discord's recent platform messages embedded in `currentInboundContext.text`.

This report concerns **the third source overlapping the first**. It is not evidence that the saved-transcript recovery mechanism itself replayed the conversation.

PR #153075 says:

> Resumed room-event prompts omit repeated history while preserving current-turn context.

There is also a [test named "keeps recent room history in the initial prompt but not the resumed prompt"](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a8a3680f3749c127470310ec34b30cac1a74d685/src/auto-reply/reply/prompt-prelude.test.ts#L164).

However:

- The [generic envelope builder](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a8a3680f3749c127470310ec34b30cac1a74d685/src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-context.ts#L525) creates the history-omitting `resumableText` alternative only for `room_event`.
- The [CLI runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a8a3680f3749c127470310ec34b30cac1a74d685/src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts#L1581) uses that alternative when reusing a room-event session.
- The Codex app-server helper consumes full `text`, not `resumableText`.
- The observed requests are `user_request`, so they do not receive that alternate variant in the first place.

The existing envelope test verifies construction of two strings, not which string a resumed Codex app-server turn receives. Changing Codex to prefer the existing alternate alone would therefore not fix these ordinary requests.

The inspected Codex tests for non-repeated mirror projection and acknowledged history seeds exercise different sources of history. They can pass while recent Discord context continues to duplicate completed requests.

### Relevant Git history and rationale

Dates below are UTC. These are source-level findings, not a live release bisect.

- **January 1, 2026 - original Discord history:** [`38d8a669b40b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/38d8a669b40b96f1a41c3ba5feaf30b72508f5a0) adds mention-context history, an in-memory per-channel buffer and a default limit of 20.
- **January 16 - explicit anti-reinjection change:** [`e31251293b46`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e31251293b467c10663a7267f62c43c471ba9940) limits history to pending/mention-gated messages and clears it after any processed message, including silent outcomes. Its documentation explicitly excludes messages already in the session.
- **May 10 - supplemental context preserved:** [`ff002ec149e7`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ff002ec149e7459c5ad060d754feca6f1f691737) moves inbound context out of persisted/base prompts into separate current-turn context. [`c529ab29c222`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c529ab29c2228fa37ddf1a8e76b0559805e16d59) then explicitly prepends that split context in Codex to preserve replied-to Telegram messages through prompt projection. This explains why supplemental context must not simply be discarded.
- **May 30 - separate Codex mirror removal:** [#88262 / `530351e394a1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88262) removes default saved-transcript reinjection, citing native history ownership and context/cache pollution. It **retains** the inbound-context prepend path.
- **May 31 - bounded recovery restored:** [#88652 / `827ceb55d074`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88652) restores bounded fresh/stale-thread continuity after [#88352](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/88352) and [#88354](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/88354). Those fixes address missing native continuity, not repeated channel context in an already-continuing thread.
- **September 20 - direct relevant selection change:** [#153075 / `6e5f6f95b10c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153075), "recover Slack and Discord discussion after restarts," closes [#152978](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/152978). It replaces ordinary Discord guild pending-buffer selection with a fresh native-platform window on each eligible admitted turn and introduces `historyKind: "recent"` and the exact `Recent chat history:` label.

The September motivation was legitimate: monitor-local buffers lost surrounding discussion after restart. But a recent platform window and previously unseen pending messages are different sets. The new window can contain already-answered requests, and the inspected integration has no native-thread coverage filter.

The reviewed subsequent selector/ownership refactors through October 20 preserve this behavior. The source evidence points to the September selection change, not a later mechanical refactor silently restoring the old Codex transcript mirror.

**Last known good live version:** not established.

**Observed affected build:** `2026.10.6 / a8a3680f3749c127470310ec34b30cac1a74d685`.

**Source-level behavior change:** #153075. This is not a claim that an end-to-end bisect has established the first affected release.

### Suggested fix scope and regression coverage

The desired invariant is to avoid automatically re-supplying unchanged channel messages already covered by the continuing native conversation, while retaining genuinely unseen discussion and necessary recovery context.

The implementation choice is open; this report does not prescribe a new store or a particular deduplication architecture.

Useful composed regression cases would include:

- Complete two ordinary Discord `user_request` turns on the same native Codex thread; the second input must not quote the first request again automatically.
- Include an intervening mention-gated message that never reached the model; it should remain available when a later admitted turn needs surrounding discussion.
- Preserve explicit reply targets even when their text was seen before.
- Preserve session reset and exact channel/thread boundaries, sender visibility and access checks.
- Cover resumed/cold and genuinely fresh native threads separately, including existing bounded continuity behavior.
- Handle retries and meaningful edits without treating every repeated ID as either always redundant or always new.
- Check silent processed turns and the separate `room_event` path, not only visible assistant replies.
- Verify the actual app-server input, rather than only testing the envelope builder or the saved-transcript projection layer in isolation.

A blanket "Codex has history, so drop all channel context" change would lose unseen room discussion. Conversely, treating every recent platform message as useful on every turn reproduces this defect.

### Workaround

The documented setting `channels.discord.historyLimit: 0` disables automatic Discord guild/thread history reads. It does not disable explicit message reads or explicit reply context, and it does not remove copies already retained in a native thread.

This is a broad workaround, not deduplication: it also removes automatic access to useful previously unseen discussion. It was not applied to the live installation during this investigation.

### Evidence and verification limits

- Direct evidence: native Codex user-input records showing one thread, seven requests, no compaction and 21 copied history entries; the same envelope structure observed in another channel.
- Source evidence: current producer, renderer, Codex consumer, CLI alternate consumer, relevant tests and pinned historical diffs/PR rationale.
- Executed synthetic source-helper checks: repeated recent-history selection returns the same prior text; a zero limit suppresses selection; Codex prepends full context even when a different `resumableText` is supplied.
- These helper checks are not a composed integration test. No full repository suite, new live-model experiment or token/billing measurement was performed for this investigation.
- No claim is made that every historical release, external Codex plugin or other channel/backend combination has identical behavior. Slack shares the September change but was not live-reproduced here.
- Private conversation identifiers and unrelated transcript content are omitted from this report. The shortened evidence above preserves the relevant messages and observed counts.

issues.body:
### Summary

When a media-understanding provider call fails, the agent sees only `[Audio attachment could not be analyzed]` (or `Image`/`Video`), and the Gateway log shows only `reason=ProviderHttpError`. Both drop the provider's HTTP status and error code. So neither the agent nor the operator can tell a rejected credential (`401`) from an exhausted account (`429 insufficient_quota`), a rate limit or a timeout.

### What happened

OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (dc2523e). Audio transcription is configured explicitly: `tools.media.models[0] = { provider: "openai", model: "gpt-4o-transcribe", preferredProfile: <api-key profile> }`. A Telegram voice note produced:

- Gateway log: `[media-understanding] audio: failed (0/1) reason=ProviderHttpError`, about 0.8 s after ingress.
- Agent context: `[Audio attachment could not be analyzed]`, with nothing else.

The audio file was intact. When the user asked why, the agent could only guess ("probably a transient hiccup"). The real cause only came out in a separate manual test against the same profile (`openclaw infer audio transcribe`), which returned `HTTP 401: Invalid authentication [code=invalid_authentication]`: the profile's API key had been rejected. Every later voice note would have failed the same way with the same opaque message.

### Where

`src/media-understanding/media-attachment-outcomes.ts`, `renderMediaAttachmentDisposition`: the `failed` disposition renders a fixed string. Other dispositions already carry a reason (`not analyzed: no audio-understanding model is configured`, `… understanding is disabled`). The log line keeps only the error class name.

### Expected

Carry a short classified reason on the `failed` disposition and render it, for example:

- `[Audio attachment could not be analyzed: provider rejected the credential (openai 401 invalid_authentication)]`
- `[… : provider account out of quota (429 insufficient_quota)]`
- `[… : provider rate limited (429)]`
- `[… : provider timed out]`

Log the provider's status, error code/type and request ID next to `ProviderHttpError`. Never log or render the credential. That lets the agent tell the user something concrete, and lets the operator spot a systemic failure (revoked key, exhausted account) from the first failed message.

### Related

#186161 covers fallback after a rejected key for auto-selected image models. This issue is about reporting the failure reason, whether or not a fallback exists.

issues.body:
## Summary

`tools.catalog` performs standalone plugin discovery synchronously on the Gateway event loop. Opening the tool catalog can freeze unrelated Gateway activity while the request eventually succeeds.

## Observed behavior

On OpenClaw `2026.10.10-beta.4` (npm, macOS), a successful native `tools.catalog` request with `includePlugins: true` took **8,931 ms**, with an **8,928 ms main-thread stall**. A CPU profile attributed **619 of 639 samples** to `ensureStandalonePluginToolRegistryLoaded`, called by the catalog's plugin-group construction.

Current upstream was inspected at `1ae91fa202637a97cb4d1beff8aca140edb3607f`; its `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-catalog.ts` still uses the synchronous standalone loader followed by a second tool-resolution pass.

## Reproduction

1. Start a Gateway with several enabled tool plugins, including optional tool registrations.
2. Request `tools.catalog` with `includePlugins: true` (for example, open the tool catalog in Control UI).
3. Observe event-loop liveness or issue an unrelated RPC concurrently.

A deterministic source regression uses real synthetic plugins and the production catalog handler: enqueue a `setImmediate` callback, invoke catalog discovery, and check that the callback has run before the catalog finishes. The unmodified handler fails that check. The same fixture also exposes repeated synchronous context/manifest preparation and missing inspection-resource cleanup.

## Expected behavior

Catalog discovery should consume the Gateway generation's admitted metadata and yield through asynchronous registration, without rediscovering manifests on the request thread. Optional and declared-but-unresolved tools must remain visible, the requested agent/workspace must reach factories, and inspection resources must be released on success and failure.

## Root cause / proposed repair

Use the existing lifecycle-owned asynchronous inspection path with the Gateway's prepared load context and manifest inventory. Merely replacing the synchronous loader with the existing async acquisition is insufficient: without prepared facts, that acquisition still performs synchronous context/manifest preparation. Keep generation authority current through projection and cleanup; treat failed inspection owners as settled rather than synchronously loading them again.

No timeout increases, new caches, services, policy bypasses, or live-install modifications are involved.

issues.body:
## Summary

On macOS with a Homebrew-managed Node, the Gateway-materialized agent-CLI shim pins the **version-pinned Homebrew Cellar path** of the Node binary (e.g. `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.8.2/bin/node`). A later Homebrew Node upgrade deletes that Cellar directory, which leaves **every bare `openclaw` invocation broken** (`No such file or directory`) until the Gateway is restarted - even though the installed OpenClaw package is perfectly healthy.

The shim is also **prepended to PATH for agent exec**, so agents in the same session inherit the broken `openclaw` command.

## Reproduction

1. macOS with Homebrew Node (`/opt/homebrew/opt/node -> ../Cellar/node/<version>`), OpenClaw installed globally via npm (`/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw`).
2. Start the Gateway. It materializes `~/.openclaw/tmp/agent-cli/openclaw`:

   ```sh
   #!/bin/sh
   set -eu

   exec /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.8.2/bin/node --max-old-space-size=8192 /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js "$@"
   ```

   Note the **Cellar** path, not `/opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node`.
3. Upgrade Node while the Gateway keeps running:

   ```bash
   brew upgrade node   # 26.8.2 -> 26.12.1; the 26.8.2 Cellar dir is removed
   ```

4. Now:

   ```bash
   $ openclaw --version
   /Users/<user>/.openclaw/tmp/agent-cli/openclaw: line 4: /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.8.2/bin/node: No such file or directory
   ```

   The real install is untouched and still runnable via `/opt/homebrew/bin/openclaw` - only the materialized shim is stale.
5. The shim is only re-materialized on the **next Gateway start**, so the CLI stays broken for the whole lifetime of the running Gateway.

## Root cause

`src/infra/openclaw-cli-shim.ts` - `prepareGatewayAgentCliShim()` writes the shim once at Gateway startup:

```ts
const content = renderCliShim(invocation, profile, platform === "win32");
await writeTextAtomic(executablePath, content, { mode: 448, dirMode: 448, durable: false, tempPrefix: "openclaw-agent-cli" });
```

and `renderCliShim()` renders the exec line straight from the resolved invocation:

```ts
// exec ${[invocation.command, ...args].map(quoteCliArg).join(" ")} "$@"
```

`src/infra/openclaw-cli-invocation.ts` - `resolveCurrentOpenClawCliInvocation()` sets that `command` to the raw `process.execPath`:

```ts
const execPath = options.execPath ?? process.execPath;
...
return { command: execPath, args: [...cliArgs, ...args], cwd: invocationCwd, ... };
```

`process.execPath` is the **realpath** of the running interpreter, so on Homebrew it is `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/<version>/bin/node`. Homebrew deletes the old Cellar directory on upgrade, so the pinned path is guaranteed to go stale at some point.

This is not limited to the CLI shim: the same stale-runtime symptom was independently observed for a plugin worker runtime on the same host (`stale worker runtime detected: /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.8.2 (removed by Homebrew upgrade)`), which needed a Gateway restart to recover.

## Impact

- `openclaw` CLI is unusable for every agent/script that resolves it through the Gateway-local PATH shim, while the underlying package is fine - a confusing failure that looks self-inflicted.
- Recovery requires a Gateway restart, which is not always desirable (it interrupts in-flight work) and is not discoverable from the error message.
- The error text points at a missing Node binary rather than at "the shim needs regenerating", which sends people down the wrong debugging path.

## Suggested fix

Any one of these would remove the failure mode:

1. **Prefer a stable interpreter path when rendering the shim** - resolve `process.execPath` to its version-manager symlink (e.g. `/opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node`, `~/.volta/bin/node`, or an nvm alias) instead of the Cellar realpath.
2. **Re-resolve at exec time** - instead of embedding a pinned interpreter, embed a small lookup that prefers the currently installed runtime and falls back to the pinned path.
3. **Validate and regenerate on miss** - when the pinned interpreter is missing, the shim (or a sibling helper) should re-resolve and rewrite itself rather than failing with `ENOENT`.
4. At minimum, **fail loudly with an actionable message** (e.g. "shim is stale after a Node upgrade; restart the Gateway to regenerate") instead of a raw `No such file or directory`.

## Verified workaround

Pointing the shim at the version-manager symlink survives Node upgrades and works today:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

exec /opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node --max-old-space-size=8192 /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js "$@"
```

(`/opt/homebrew/opt/node` is a symlink that Homebrew re-points on upgrade.) Note this is still overwritten on the next Gateway start, since the Gateway re-materializes the shim.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.10.9 (8b18b55); also reproduced on 2026.10.5
- macOS 26.1 (arm64), Homebrew Node 26.8.2 -> 26.12.1
- OpenClaw installed via `npm install -g` under `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw`
- shim path: `~/.openclaw/tmp/agent-cli/openclaw`

## Related

- #52184 - same class of problem for Volta and the macOS gateway LaunchAgent (currently marked stale); the fix shape here is very likely shared.
- #176237 - Homebrew Node upgrade breaking Node service reachability.
- #150974 / #158817 - other defects in the same agent-CLI shim generator (Windows).

Each passed on another parent or on rerun at the same product SHA, and each test still exists on `main`. The release continues under the flake policy; this issue tracks fixing them in parallel.

| Lane | Test | Signature | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checks-node-agentic-control-plane-agent-chat-hosted-1` | `src/gateway/server.chat-abort-dispatch-rejection.test.ts` › retains signal-only interruption | `interruption` resolves `false` (line 564) plus unhandled `closed 1005` | Failed on FRV 40978558284 attempts 1 and 2; green on 40963088510 and 40974111461; 9/9 local |
| `checks-node-agentic-control-plane-runtime-state` | `server.required-placement-scopes.test.ts`, `server.config-write-reread.test.ts`, `server.native-hook-request-lifetime.test.ts` | `sessions.create` RPC timeout; spawn broker shutdown / process group census unavailable | Lane failed its first attempt on all three parents with a different test each time; green on rerun |
| `checks-node-agentic-control-plane-runtime-cron` | `src/gateway/server.cron.test.ts` › returns already-running without starting background work | `cron.run` RPC timeout plus `closed 1012: service restart` | Green on both earlier parents |
| `checks-node-agentic-commands-doctor-config-state` | `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.container-upgrade.test.ts` › preserves schema 19 at startup… | `Recovery destination database changed; preview cleanup again.` | Green on both earlier parents |
| `checks-node-core-tooling-11` | `test/scripts/vitest-report-owner.test.ts` › leaves native control execution with the project child: clear cache | `ENOTEMPTY` rmdir of `node_modules/.vitest-cache` | Green on the same SHA in another parent |
| `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway (1/2)` | `ui/src/pages/workboard/workboard-distribution.e2e.test.ts` › loads entry, CSS and lazy Workboard chunks… | 30s locator timeout; `ChatMetadataSnapshotUnavailableError` | Failed twice on 40963088510, green on 40974111461 |

Also observed: rerunning `checks-node-core-src-security-1` on run 40964080497 produced 15, then 17, queued duplicate copies of that one job, through both `frv rerun --job` and `frv rerun --child`. The duplicates had no runner assigned, so the child could not seal.

## Ask

Fix each test at its owning boundary (replace fixed timing windows with owner-settled signals). The `gateway-server-parallel` lanes fail on most first attempts under hosted-runner load.
