Do not stop at a plan, scaffold, screenshots, or a partially wired feature and call it complete.

```text
UPSTREAM SUBMISSION AND PROMPT DISCLOSURE

Preserve this exact kickoff prompt and relevant owner steering from the start. When preparing the submission, look up the current official OpenClaw contribution instructions, PR template, AI-assisted contribution rules, and the maintainer request I described as Peter asking contributors to include their prompts. Verify what is actually requested and follow its current format; do not guess from memory or invent a policy. Refresh those requirements immediately before posting.

Include the requested prompt/session evidence alongside the submission in the required place and format. Clearly distinguish the original user requests, this assistant-drafted kickoff prompt adopted by me, and later steering. Do not rewrite a cleaner prompt and present it as the historical original. Remove secrets and unrelated private material from anything public, mark necessary redactions, and preserve the private original. Do not publish private Mini Me data or unrelated conversations.

Follow the current required discussion/issue/PR order and any maintainer review gates. Submit only evidence-backed work; disclose remaining limitations honestly. Handle relevant review feedback within scope. Upstream acceptance is not guaranteed, and my local prototype authorization does not override the maintainers' right to accept or reject a contribution.

Add this exact line to the main feature submission, in an appropriate place alongside the required technical content:

P.S. If y’all are hiring, I’m available. Figured I’d fix a few things before asking for a job.
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Relevant owner steering and attribution</summary>

The owner selected these answers to setup questions before implementation:

- Learning: “Automatically learn from selected sources; let me review and undo later”
- Action scope: “Yes—explicit action permissions and limits per agent (Recommended)”
- Training scope: “Mini Me first; leave Champion for a later build”

Visual direction, owner message: “I approve this. The onboarding needs a little work tho. Should match openclaw design system but that is fine as a layout concept”

The attached concept was approved as a layout, not blanket approval of an independently styled UI. Later acceptance inputs and learned records are private and omitted. Helper selection changed during the session; actual work used a mix of OpenAI and Anthropic agents, with independent review. This appendix is the relevant prompt record, not a claim to be a complete session transcript.
</details>

P.S. If y’all are hiring, I’m available. Figured I’d fix a few things before asking for a job.

---

### Requirements → existing contracts (design follow-up)

Source review pinned to `19fe87965eaae2ad4fcf7039793b53f6d1f9770d`. This is a **plugin-first contract map for maintainer discussion**, not a conversion of the prototype or a claim that the feature works as a plugin. [VISION][vision] favors optional plugins and generic extension seams. The original feature scope remains unchanged; core versus plugin ownership and security/storage design acceptance remain open.

| Requirement | Existing coverage / decision still needed |
| --- | --- |
| Optional owner-named separate agent; visible home; six editable documents | [Plugin registration][api] covers RPCs, tools and UI contributions. [Agent-file handlers][files] restrict the built-in editor to canonical bootstrap files, not the proposed six-document model. Decide owner-private agent visibility and plugin document/editor ownership. |
| Explicitly selected past/ongoing private sources | [Profile][profile] and [session-access][access] owners retain live identity/sharing authority; plugin RPCs can declare profile/session access [api]. A scoped [ended-transcript reader][transcript] exists. Still prove selected-source consent, withdrawal, original-owner binding and saved-progress reuse through public contracts; do not depend on private internal imports. |
| Evidence-backed inference, correction/undo suppression; frozen prediction versus later human choice | [Plugin state][state] supplies action-bound stores, atomic comparisons and worker-operation receipts. Mini Me policy must define evidence links, correction precedence, undo suppression, exclusion of generated projections, and immutable prediction/human-outcome provenance. These feature semantics are not supplied automatically by a storage API. |
| Per-agent attachment and four modes | [Session state/context injection][api] supplies advice integration points. Agent-level attachment semantics still need mapping. The four modes are feature policy, never permission. |
| Explicit grants, resource/expiry/action/byte limits, concurrent accounting and revocation | [Trusted policies][policy] participate in pre-tool admission; the [execution owner][effect] rechecks host capability after awaited work, and the [host file writer][write] checks source authority before overwrite. This does not demonstrate persistent host-held Mini Me file grants at each write with atomic reservation/settlement and recovery. That integration is unproven, not declared absent. |
| Persistence, recovery, export, source removal, pause/detach/disable/delete | [State][state] supports retained namespaces and deletion; [lifecycle hooks][api] cover cleanup integration. Still specify canonical/projection ownership, export, logical deletion/backup treatment and uncertain-write recovery. [Storage policy][storage] requires acceptance for material persistence/permission changes. |
| Optional Decision/Jev | [Decision][decision] supplies typed evaluation/admission/provenance, not human approval. Retain the matcher and owner-selected extraction model; no silent fallback. |

**Generic host questions, only where current public contracts cannot meet a demonstrated requirement:**

1. Can authenticated plugin consumers retain an owner-authorized, selected private-source snapshot through extraction and publication, including withdrawal and lifecycle invalidation?
2. Can the host own bounded existing-file grants and atomic concurrent accounting, carrying current authority through asynchronous preparation to each actual file effect and reconciling unknown outcomes?
3. Can an owner-private agent attachment and inspectable authored-document projection use existing identity, state and UI owners without duplicate authority or retention policy?

These are questions for contract review, not promised new APIs. Public plugin APIs are experimental; host-version qualification remains necessary [api]. Existing action-bound storage and transaction facilities should be reused rather than described as missing or replaced with a second storage owner.

**Mini Me policy stays separate:** opt-in/defer-with-no-profile-or-model-work; owner naming; SOUL.md, OPINIONS.md, PREFERENCES.md, MORALS.md, TASTE.md and DECISIONS.md; selected-source learning and correction/undo rules; grounded uncertainty and frozen predictions; the four modes and per-agent attachments. Model output cannot manufacture human decisions or approval. Grants stay host-held, fail closed after revocation, and are checked immediately before effects. Scope remains bounded edits to explicitly granted **existing text files through the embedded runtime**; other harnesses are advice-only. No message sending, shell, spending, native/remote effects, training or Nightly Champion.

This is source inspection with AI assistance, not new behavioral testing or upstream acceptance. Coverage is limited to the cited owners. “Unproven” means no complete public integration path was established in this review, not repository-wide absence. The isolated prototype evidence and its existing limitations above remain unchanged. The next external decision is plugin versus core ownership plus acceptance of the private-source, grant and retention contracts; no implementation PR is opened ahead of that decision.

---

### Follow-up: owner-scoped agent access and group participation

The original prototype evidence and its limitations above are historical. The local custom build is not an upstream release, product acceptance, or proof that the proposed agent-facing and group flows work end to end.

1. An attached agent should be able to inspect and consult the authenticated requester's existing Mini Me. At the owner's explicit request, that same Mini Me can be enabled or attached, then disabled or detached through its normal lifecycle. An administrator role or a supplied owner identifier must not grant access to another person's profile. A prediction is advice; it does not grant action authority.
2. For an eligible group message, the owner's attached Mini Me should be able to help decide whether that agent needs to wake and respond. Where the host supports it, this decision should happen before the main-model wake. Wake admission, retained room context, and permission to send remain separate. Direct requests, trusted commands, supported media, and urgent cases must remain reachable; a permitted quiet result must not produce a fallback message or retry loop.

A group decision should use only bounded, permitted context from that same room and the existing owner-scoped profile. It must not make the group a learning source or expose private profile contents to other participants. Provider unavailability needs a bounded, explicit policy, and the interface should remain provider-neutral. Different owners' and rooms' context must stay isolated.

A generic decision backend by itself does not establish that a person's Mini Me is consulted. Natural inbound group acceptance and model-wake savings have not been demonstrated for this follow-up. Any implementation would need exact-head tests plus real admitted inbound and consultation evidence before a PR.

**Maintainer design question:** Would this fit as plugin-owned policy using existing host contracts? If not, which narrowly scoped host seams for authenticated owner attachment, pre-wake admission, and same-room continuity would be acceptable? This extends the existing contract map; it does not assume a core implementation or change the request for private-source, grant, and retention review.

This follow-up was prepared with AI assistance.

## Problem

The PR-preparation handoff test fails after #187925 enabled tool previews for sessions a guest can read. The resumed guest correctly retains `operator.sessions.read` and `operator.sessions.write`, but the fixture still uses an own-session `tools.effective` request as its broad-read denial control.

In [CI run 40978612951, job 123813293631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40978612951/job/123813293631), head 9691edd1f1f973909bdff7e879164adb5cc0408a fails `hands PR preparation to its registered owner after cleanup: prepared` in `src/agents/tools/github-publish-tool.handoff.test.ts`. The embedded callback reports `promise resolved "{}" instead of rejecting`; its later settlement assertion consequently receives `failed` instead of `completed`.

The request includes the caller's own session key. #187925 explicitly added `tools.effective` to session-read admission, so reaching the fixture endpoint is expected. The handoff test and determining admission/dispatcher policies are unchanged on main revision fe8a0ce9b4e89d48e7e0ccbcd572d0924acce823. Run this existing test through the native Bun test route to exercise the same real event admission and Gateway dispatch; model execution is stubbed by the fixture.

The handoff should complete with its original guest authority, and its negative controls should demonstrate denial of a genuinely broad-read method and an admin method. `tools.catalog` retains the broad `operator.read` requirement and has no session-read exception; `plugins.reload` remains admin-only. Updating the negative-control method in both registration and request would preserve those assertions without changing product permissions or adding duplicate preview coverage.

This is a test-fixture regression, not evidence of a guest privilege escalation. The corrected fixture has not yet completed validation.

labels.name: bug

labels.name: clawsweeper:source-repro

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a condition-trigger evaluation returns `busy`, cron advances the job to its next natural occurrence without retrying the unevaluated check or recording a visible skipped/deferred occurrence. This can repeatedly starve aligned watches while they remain enabled.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed production sequence on the affected build:

1. Run several enabled condition-triggered cron watches with overlapping read-only checks, the same hourly schedule, and no staggering:
   ```json
   {"kind":"cron","expr":"0 7-19 * * *","tz":"America/Edmonton","staggerMs":0}
   ```
2. At an hourly boundary, three peer watches complete trigger evaluations. The affected watch advances `nextRunAtMs` but never records a trigger evaluation or payload run.
3. Leave the schedule enabled. In this incident the watch remained unevaluated from its creation on October 28 through the afternoon of October 29. The source reader worked when invoked directly and returned `changed: true` with unreported updates.
4. Change only this job's `schedule.staggerMs` to `120000`. Its stable offset becomes approximately 62 seconds after the hour. The next actual scheduled check evaluates successfully, runs its payload and delivers the result. The following scheduled check records a successful quiet evaluation.

This is one observed affected watch, not a separately executed four-job synthetic reproduction. The per-occurrence `busy` debug event was not retained, so attribution of this production incident specifically to capacity rejection is inferred from the state signature, peer timings and workaround. The busy-result handling below is directly verified in source.

### Expected behavior

An unevaluated due check should remain pending and be queued or retried fairly after capacity becomes available, rather than consuming its scheduled occurrence as a quiet check. If it cannot be serviced, expose a distinct deferred/skipped condition.

This is different from a genuinely quiet `fire: false` evaluation, which the [documented contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82fa5f465a9dc4bae8052f3dba7e920e0de4f898/docs/automation/cron-jobs/schedules.md) says persists evaluation state and counters. The configured hourly watch should actually inspect its source.

### Actual behavior

Before the workaround:

- Job remained enabled and its next scheduled timestamp advanced.
- `automations get` had no `lastTriggerEvalAtMs`, `triggerEvalCount`, `lastRunAtMs` or error in the job state. Its state contained only `nextRunAtMs`.
- Run history was empty. Three synchronized peer jobs had completed evaluations.
- No failure alert was emitted; the read-only source check had not handled updates that were available.

After changing only the stagger:

- The real scheduled occurrence at `2026-10-29T21:01:02.379Z` finished successfully, with `triggerFired: true`, completion succeeded and delivery confirmed.
- By the following occurrence, `triggerEvalCount` was 2 and `lastTriggerEvalAtMs` plus the source-check timestamp were populated. No additional payload run was needed for that quiet check.
- Payload model/routing, source reader, tools and destination were unchanged. The recovery was not a forced manual payload run. A local pending-recovery flag requested one confirmation from that first actual scheduled execution; it did not bypass the trigger. The following scheduled evaluation was quiet.

### OpenClaw version

Runtime observations: `2026.10.8`, commit `82fa5f465a9dc4bae8052f3dba7e920e0de4f898`.

The same relevant implementation was verified on upstream main at `cb156d027f0232e31b6837b6cf34c2618facaec2`. That newer revision was source-inspected, not separately runtime-tested here.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0, arm64, local Gateway.

### Install method

Native local Gateway, repository-sourced build.

### Model

Not reached for the unevaluated occurrences. The unchanged agent-turn model ran successfully after staggering.

### Provider / routing chain

No inference request was admitted for the affected occurrences. The condition gate precedes the payload model call.

### Additional provider/model setup details

The condition script used an approved read-only source reader. Direct source reading succeeded. No model fallback, authentication change or provider reconfiguration was used as the workaround.

### Logs

Sanitized state observations, with job/account/session/source identifiers omitted rather than replaced with realistic identifiers:

```text
Before:
  enabled = true
  schedule.staggerMs = 0
  state contained nextRunAtMs only
  lastTriggerEvalAtMs and triggerEvalCount absent
  run-history entries = []

After the real scheduled occurrence:
  schedule.staggerMs = 120000
  run status = ok
  triggerFired = true
  completionStatus = succeeded
  deliveryStatus = delivered

After the following scheduled occurrence:
  triggerEvalCount = 2
  lastTriggerEvalAtMs present
  triggerState.lastCheckAt present
```

These are selected observations, not fabricated log lines. The list UI rendered some missing fields as `null`; the raw job-state observation above describes their absence instead. No per-job busy debug trace is claimed.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The source path explains how a capacity rejection acquires this state signature:

1. [`trigger-script.ts:106,663-677`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82fa5f465a9dc4bae8052f3dba7e920e0de4f898/src/cron/trigger-script.ts#L663-L677) caps simultaneous evaluations at 3 and immediately returns `{ kind: "busy" }` above that cap.
2. [`timer-execution.ts:283-289`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82fa5f465a9dc4bae8052f3dba7e920e0de4f898/src/cron/service/timer-execution.ts#L283-L289) converts busy to an `ok`, non-firing trigger result. There is a debug log, but no error.
3. [`timer-trigger.ts:36-46`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82fa5f465a9dc4bae8052f3dba7e920e0de4f898/src/cron/service/timer-trigger.ts#L36-L46) deliberately skips evaluation bookkeeping for busy results.
4. [`timer-outcomes.ts:617-674`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82fa5f465a9dc4bae8052f3dba7e920e0de4f898/src/cron/service/timer-outcomes.ts#L617-L674) nevertheless advances that no-fire result to the next natural cron slot. The quiet-result branch also produces no normal run history.

Suggested deterministic regression coverage, not executed as a separate test here: hold three evaluations on a barrier, admit a fourth due check, release the first three, and verify the fourth is retried without waiting for its next natural slot. Repeat with stable job ordering to verify eventual service and observable deferral. Scheduler concurrency must permit at least four attempted evaluations to overlap for this capacity guard to be exercised.

### Impact and severity

- Affected observation: one enabled communications watch among synchronized condition-triggered jobs.
- Severity: blocks the watch's purpose without a visible failure.
- Frequency: no completed evaluation was recorded from creation on October 28 until the October 29 stagger workaround. Individual rejected attempts were not separately logged, so an exact rejection count is unavailable.
- Consequence: meaningful source updates were not reported until a manual diagnostic read. Other jobs showed a similar state pattern, but I have not independently attributed each one.

### Additional information

Regression status and introducing commit: `NOT_ENOUGH_INFO`. No last-known-good version was established.

A small nonzero stagger worked around this incident; it does not fix capacity fairness or distinguish a check that was never evaluated from one that successfully found no change. No Gateway restart, installed-runtime patch, source change or duplicate automation was used for the workaround.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (plugin fails to load)

### Summary

After upgrading 2026.8.2 → 2026.9.33 (extended-stable), the `@openclaw/discord` channel plugin fails during register on every Gateway start. The failure is in the Gateway's plugin source capture, not in the installed plugin: the install is complete, `openclaw plugins doctor` reports that module loading passes, and `openclaw plugins inspect discord` records 2026.9.33. The captured copy is missing `mdast-util-to-string`, which is a declared `dependencies` entry of the plugin's nested dependency `mdast-util-from-markdown`.

```
[plugins] discord failed during register from ~/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-discord-<hash>__openclaw-generation__g-<id>/node_modules/@openclaw/discord/dist/index.js
[gateway] [plugins] plugin failed during register: runtime dependencies are missing for externally distributed plugin discord; reinstall or update the plugin package, then restart the Gateway. (Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'mdast-util-to-string' imported from ~/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures/<uuid>/captures/openclaw-plugin-build-<id>/package-0/node_modules/@openclaw/discord/node_modules/mdast-util-from-markdown/lib/index.js)
```

`openclaw health` then reports `Plugin discord: failed - runtime dependencies are missing for externally distributed plugin discord …`. Other external plugins in the same install (e.g. `@openclaw/diagnostics-otel@2026.9.33`) load fine.

### What I verified in the installed tree

- `~/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-discord-…/node_modules/@openclaw/discord/node_modules/` holds 51 packages, including both `mdast-util-from-markdown` (2.0.3) and `mdast-util-to-string` (4.0.0), as real directories (not symlinks), both `inBundle: true` in the project `package-lock.json`.
- `mdast-util-from-markdown/package.json` lists `mdast-util-to-string` in `dependencies`.
- So plain Node resolution from `…/@openclaw/discord/node_modules/mdast-util-from-markdown/lib/index.js` finds `mdast-util-to-string` in the install; only the capture lacks it.
- Reinstalling (`plugins install … --force`) and restarting the Gateway do not help; the error reproduces on every start.
- `@openclaw/discord@2026.8.2` has the same dependency layout and worked on the 2026.8.2 Gateway, so this looks like a regression in the 9.x source-capture path rather than in the plugin package. The same layout is still in `@openclaw/discord` 2026.10.4 and 2026.10.10-beta.1; I have not tested those Gateway versions.

Possibly related capture issues: #162585, #159698, #160214.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Linux x86_64 (Debian 12), Node v24.22.0 (NodeSource), npm 11.19.1.
2. `npm install -g --prefix /opt/openclaw-npm openclaw@2026.9.33 --allow-scripts=openclaw,@google/genai,esbuild,koffi,protobufjs` (upgraded in place from 2026.8.2 with the Gateway stopped).
3. As the Gateway user: `openclaw plugins install @openclaw/discord@2026.9.33 --pin --force --accept-capabilities`, then `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`.
4. Start the Gateway (system-scope systemd unit) with the Discord channel configured.
5. The journal shows the error above.

### Expected behavior

The capture includes every package a captured dependency declares and the install provides, so the Discord plugin registers as it did on 2026.8.2.

### Actual behavior

The Discord channel never starts; the Gateway stays up with the plugin quarantined.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.33 (5873f81); `@openclaw/discord` 2026.9.33.

### Operating system

Debian 12 (QEMU VM), x86_64.

### Install method

npm global install with a custom prefix (`/opt/openclaw-npm`), system-scope systemd service; plugins installed with `openclaw plugins install`.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The dreaming deep phase never promotes anything once the short-term recall store is at its 512-entry cap. The nightly session-transcript ingestion stages hundreds of zero-recall entries, all stamped with the sweep time. `enforceShortTermRecallStoreRetention` then keeps the 512 most recent entries by `lastRecalledAt`, and only compares signal counts when timestamps tie. So every entry that collected real `memory_search` recalls during the day is evicted before ranking, `recallCount` never builds up across days, and `minRecallCount` can never pass.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable `memory-core` dreaming (default) with session transcript ingestion, and use `memory_search` normally for a few days on an agent with active interactive sessions.
2. Once a single day's session corpus contributes ≥512 candidates, run the nightly sweep.
3. Inspect the `memory-core` / `short-term-recall` plugin-state entries and run `openclaw memory promote`.

Minimal deterministic repro using the functions shipped in `dist/short-term-promotion-store-*.mjs` (`compareShortTermRecallRetention`, `enforceShortTermRecallStoreRetention` and helpers extracted verbatim):

```js
const entries = {};
// 3 entries genuinely recalled 5 times during the previous day
for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) entries["recalled" + i] = { key: "recalled" + i, recallCount: 5, dailyCount: 0,
  groundedCount: 0, totalScore: 4.5, maxScore: 0.95, lastRecalledAt: "2026-09-16T10:49:00.000Z" };
// 512 fresh zero-recall entries staged by the nightly session ingestion
for (let i = 0; i < 512; i++) entries["ingest" + i] = { key: "ingest" + i, recallCount: 0, dailyCount: 1,
  groundedCount: 0, totalScore: 0.58, maxScore: 0.58, lastRecalledAt: "2026-09-17T01:00:00.303Z" };
const store = { version: 1, entries };
const removed = enforceShortTermRecallStoreRetention(store);
// => removed 3, kept 512, recalled survivors 0
```

### Expected behavior

Entries with real recall signal survive retention in preference to freshly staged zero-signal entries, so `recallCount` / query diversity accumulate across days and strong candidates can reach the deep-phase gates.

### Actual behavior

All recalled entries are evicted every night. On the affected install:

- All 512 `short-term-recall` entries have `recallCount: 0` and the same `lastRecalledAt` (the 01:00 sweep time); max `maxScore` is 0.62. 432 of the 512 come from a single `memory/.dreams/session-corpus/<day>.txt`.
- The memory event log shows real `memory.recall.recorded` events every day (115 non-dreaming queries this month), hitting daily-note ranges such as `memory/2026-09-10.md:313-324`. None of those ranges exist in the store the next morning.
- Nightly log: `memory-core: normalized recall artifacts before dreaming (rewrote recall store)` followed by `dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=1, candidates=0, applied=0, failed=0, degraded=0, …)`.
- `openclaw memory promote` → `No short-term recall candidates.`
- No new `MEMORY.md` promotion block for about two weeks.

`main` still has the same ordering in `extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-utils.ts` (`compareShortTermRecallRetention` compares `lastRecalledAt` first; `SHORT_TERM_RECALL_MAX_ENTRIES = 512`).

Suggested fix: rank retention by signal (`totalSignalCountForEntry`, and/or recall count + unique queries) before recency, or cap/partition session-corpus ingestion so it cannot displace entries that carry recall signal.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)

### Operating system

macOS 27.0 (arm64), Node 26.8.2

### Install method

npm global (Homebrew node)

### Model

anthropic/claude-opus-5 (not model-dependent; retention is deterministic)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw → claude-cli runtime → Anthropic

### Additional provider/model setup details

`plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming`: `enabled: true`, `phases.deep: { minScore: 0.9, minRecallCount: 4, minUniqueQueries: 4 }`. Default frequency. Single agent.

### Logs

```
memory-core: normalized recall artifacts before dreaming (rewrote recall store) [workspace=…].
memory-core: dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=1, candidates=0, applied=0, failed=0, degraded=0, narrativesPending=2).
```

### Impact

Deep-phase promotion is silently disabled on any install where daily session ingestion reaches the 512 cap. Light/REM phases and the diary still run, so dreaming looks healthy.

Related but different root cause: #82755 (same `recallCount=0` symptom, caused by active-memory timeouts).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A terminal run failure with warning text before its actionable cause can record and display only the warnings. The session row can retain the cause while the persisted failure notice loses it, leaving different diagnostic surfaces inconsistent.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use source revision `620e1fb31537ea6a3df583f08173e66607fdd2e5` and the existing accepted-run fixture in `src/gateway/session-lifecycle-run-failure.test.ts`.
2. Pass this synthetic error string through `persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent` as the accepted run's terminal error:

   ```js
   `codex app-server exited: code=1 signal=null stderr=${JSON.stringify("warning: ".repeat(50) + "fatal: startup owner unavailable")}`
   ```

3. Read the stored `run-failed-before-reply` report and project the session messages through `projectChatDisplayMessages`. Compare `details.error`, the displayed notice, and the session row's `lastRunError`.

This uses the real lifecycle persistence, transcript recorder, SQLite storage, and display projection. The failure input is synthetic; it does not require crashing a provider process.

### Expected behavior

The bounded failure diagnostic should retain the terminal cause after redaction, as the existing session-row formatter already does. The ordinary visible notice should stay concise. Private diagnostic fields and display-only failure notices should retain their existing visibility and model-context rules.

### Actual behavior

The persisted error stops at `fatal: sta`, losing `startup owner unavailable`. Both `details.error` and the generic visible notice use the first 512 characters. The session-row formatter independently preserves the end of the same input.

The stderr fixture is 482 characters and the complete wrapped error is 535 characters. It survives the Codex producer's 500-character stderr preview limit unchanged, so this is a separate loss at the session recorder.

### OpenClaw version

Source commit `620e1fb31537ea6a3df583f08173e66607fdd2e5`.

### Operating system

Linux remote runner; distribution version was not collected.

### Install method

Source checkout with locked project dependencies.

### Model

No live model was invoked by this focused reproduction.

### Provider / routing chain

Synthetic terminal lifecycle event through the production Gateway persistence and display owners.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The extended lifecycle regression file ran with unchanged production code: 32 existing cases passed and four new assertions failed. These demonstrate the lost terminal diagnostic, redacted-tail retention gap, and overlong generic notices. Browser and live-agent verification remain separate obligations.

### Impact and severity

Users and operators inspecting these terminal failures can see warning text without the useful cause, complicating diagnosis. The loss is deterministic for the supplied input. This report does not establish the cause of any historical crash, change automatic recovery, or imply that a failed tool means the whole run failed.

issues.body:
## Summary

Let a user pin a dashboard so it is available from the **+** menu of every session, instead of being reachable only inside the session that owns it. A fresh, scoped follow-up to the closed design record #110296, as suggested in its closing comment.

## Problem

Boards are strictly session-owned: "A board belongs to a session ... There is no `dashboard_create`, no board registry" ([`docs/web/dashboard-architecture.md#L25-L29`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/cffc912d42dda900b4935a7d216e63b0079cd404/docs/web/dashboard-architecture.md#L25-L29)); the panel opens "the current task's board" ([`#L70-L72`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/cffc912d42dda900b4935a7d216e63b0079cd404/docs/web/dashboard-architecture.md#L70-L72)) and `board.get` resolves one session ([`src/gateway/server-methods/board.ts#L72-L80`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/cffc912d42dda900b4935a7d216e63b0079cd404/src/gateway/server-methods/board.ts#L72-L80)). The **+** menu offers panel types from a catalog of built-in panels (plus plugin panels via `plugin:<id>/<name>` slots) (browser, terminal, dashboard of this session, portal, ...) ([`ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-sidebar-region-header.tsx#L111-L127`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/cffc912d42dda900b4935a7d216e63b0079cd404/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-sidebar-region-header.tsx#L111-L127), slot ids in [`ui/src/pages/chat/sidebar-layout-types.ts#L1-L16`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/cffc912d42dda900b4935a7d216e63b0079cd404/ui/src/pages/chat/sidebar-layout-types.ts#L1-L16)).

The Dashboards gallery lists boards across sessions, but selecting a card navigates to the owning chat with its dashboard panel expanded (see `docs/web/dashboards.md`). So a dashboard that is useful everywhere (an overview, a project status view, a personal radar) cannot be docked as a panel next to another conversation; the user has to leave the current session. Portals already appear as a panel type in the same menu; the dashboard panel type only ever shows the current session's board.

The closing comment on #110296 (2026-10-24) says remaining Home/Pages ideas "should be tracked as a fresh, scoped issue against the current dashboard". This is that issue, narrowed to one capability: **an existing dashboard selectable as a docked panel from the **+** menu in any session**. Home docks and a Pages shelf are out of scope.

## Evidence

Checked on `main` at `cffc912d42dda900b4935a7d216e63b0079cd404`; the gallery navigates to the owning session, and the **+** menu has no cross-session dashboard panel (I did not trace every code path). Searched open and closed issues/PRs for pinned/shared/global dashboards; only #110296 (closed, broader) is related. #156328 (session-scoped browser dashboards) concerns access rights, not pinning.

## Solution shapes (smallest first)

1. **Pin by reference**: a per-user (or per-gateway) list of "pinned dashboards" pointing at existing `sessionKey + tab`. The **+** menu lists them; opening one shows the owning session's board. No copy, no new storage for widget bytes.
2. **Shared board scope**: allow a board to be declared shared (stable id, owner agent), listed in the **+** menu everywhere.
3. **Open any visible session's dashboard** from the **+** menu via a session picker (no pin list).

## Open design questions

- Whose authority do data bindings and capability grants use when a board is viewed from another session? My assumption: grants stay bound to the owning session and exact widget bytes, as today; the viewing session gains no new reach.
- Visibility: who may see a pinned board (owner only, same-user, anyone with session access)?
- Lifecycle: what happens to a pin when the owning session is archived or deleted.

## Asks

Please pick a shape or reject the direction. No implementation starts before scope agreement; I can prepare a small PR for shape 1 once visibility rules are settled.

## Summary

There is no single place in the product that answers "is this Gateway healthy and what needs maintenance?". The signals exist as separate RPCs and pages (health, cron, usage, systems), so operators rebuild the same overview by hand, typically as a pinned HTML widget in one session. Propose a generic, read-only **Maintenance / Ops** surface as a product feature.

## Problem

Operators running a long-lived Gateway need one glance at: gateway health (event loop, plugin errors/unavailable, failed delivery queues), automations (errors, next runs, disabled), provider quota/cost, and active sessions per agent. Today each lives elsewhere:

- `health` carries plugins, event-loop state, delivery queues and per-agent session counts (`src/gateway/server-methods/health.ts`, `src/gateway/health/collector.ts`).
- Cron status/errors live on the Cron page; usage/quota on the Usage page.
- The Systems page is inventory-centred; it has some telemetry and backups, but no cross-source gateway health, cron or quota view ([`ui/src/pages/systems/systems-data.ts#L1-L30`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/cffc912d42dda900b4935a7d216e63b0079cd404/ui/src/pages/systems/systems-data.ts#L1-L30)).
- Session dashboards can host such a view, but only as agent-authored HTML bound to one session ([`docs/web/dashboard-architecture.md#L25-L29`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/cffc912d42dda900b4935a7d216e63b0079cd404/docs/web/dashboard-architecture.md#L25-L29), "A board belongs to a session"). I built exactly this as a pinned widget using the read bindings available to widgets for health, cron, usage and sessions; it works, but it is hand-written, per-session, and each operator has to maintain their own copy.

I found no open issue or PR for this. Related but different: #22427 (closed, experimental local scripts, no runtime surface), #110296 (Home dashboard design record, closed; about pinning, see my separate request), Workboard (task cards, not system health).

## Evidence on current main

Tested against `main` at `cffc912d42dda900b4935a7d216e63b0079cd404`. To my reading of `ui/src/pages` (`systems`, `usage`, `cron`, `activity`, `dashboards`, `custodian`, `debug`), no page or panel combines gateway health, plugin errors, delivery-queue failures, cron errors and quota; `debug` shows health as raw diagnostics, not an overview, and `custodian` covers alerts only. I did not claim this is exhaustive.

## Solution shapes (smallest first)

1. **Docs recipe + starter widget**: ship the read-only widget (fixed binding allowlist) as a documented template for session dashboards. No new surface; still per-session.
2. **Built-in Ops page** in the Control UI that reads the existing RPCs and shows the sections above with freshness, per-source error states and last-good data. No new write paths, no new RPCs required for a first version.
3. **Ops as a registered widget kind / panel** so it can be docked in any session (needs a way to show one board across sessions; filed separately as a pinned-dashboard request, this issue does not depend on it).

## Asks

Which shape do maintainers prefer, and is a first-party read-only ops view in scope? If shape 2 is acceptable I can open a small PR limited to a read-only page over existing RPCs, with tests, after scope agreement. No implementation work starts before that.

issues.body:
**Version info:** OpenClaw 2026.10.3 · Node v24.18.0 · macOS 26.5.2 (arm64, 16 GB RAM) · gateway run under launchd with `--max-old-space-size=8192`.

### Expected behaviour
1. The prepared-model-catalog worker's heap should stay bounded: the model catalog is finite and refresh/expiry exists.
2. Gateway worker population should return to its startup baseline (8) after load subsides — idle workers should be retired or pooled.

### Actual behaviour
1. `prepared-model-catalog.worker.js` heap grows monotonically and never shrinks. Sampled by the gateway's own `[diagnostics/memory]` reporter on the same worker thread over ~12 h of normal traffic: heapUsed 227 MB → 314 MB → 338 MB → 406 MB. A previous day's instance plateaued at ~304 MB until process restart — growth is bounded only by restarting the gateway.
2. `worker startup state` reports 8 workers at every fresh start, but `workerCount` climbs to 14–18 within hours and never returns to 8. Lifecycle records show repeated starts of `sqlite-store.worker.js`, `session-transcript.worker.js` and `openclaw-state-read.worker.js` with `retired: []` — no idle retirement.
3. `[diagnostics/memory]` `level=warning/critical reason=rss_growth` events recur every 1–2 h (rssGrowth 0.5–1.9 GB per window); peak RSS 3.55 GiB (heap 2.23 GiB) observed over two days.

### Reproduction steps
1. Run the gateway on a long-lived host (16 GB) with a normal multi-agent messaging workload for ~24 h; do not restart.
2. Observe `[diagnostics/memory]` lines in the gateway log: heapUsed for `prepared-model-catalog.worker.js` increases monotonically between samples taken hours apart on the same threadId.
3. Compare successive `[gateway] worker startup state` lines: `workerCount` exceeds the startup baseline (8) and stays elevated; per-worker `retired` arrays remain empty while new instances of the same worker scripts appear.
4. Restart resolves both until load recurs.

### Source observations (2026.10.3, from the published package)
- `prepared-model-runtime-*.mjs`: catalog/auth materialization creates new frozen owner objects per refresh; retirement (`retirePreparedModelRuntimeOwnerIfUnused`, `retirePreparedModelRuntimeGeneration`) is usage/generation-triggered only; the oldest-owner cap exists but no idle-timeout retire for workers.
- No documented configuration key exposes a catalog cache limit, TTL or worker idle timeout.
- Diagnostics text acknowledges: `workerLimitScope=js-heap-only; external/ArrayBuffers are not capped; nested workers are not included`. RSS grows faster than JS heap (RSS 1.6–3.5 GiB vs heap 0.6–2.2 GiB), consistent with uncapped external/native retention.

### Impact
Memory-pressure warnings accumulate until operator restart; on 16 GB multi-service hosts the gateway reaches ~3.5 GiB RSS within a day and competes with other services for RAM/swap. Workaround: scheduled daily restart.

### Environment / privacy notes
Logs contain no secrets; would submit a redacted log slice or a `gateway diagnostics export` bundle on request. (Private paths in the working evidence have been genericised here.)

### Suggested direction (non-prescriptive)
Eviction or snapshot-reuse in the prepared-model-catalog worker; idle retirement or pooling for duplicate workers; cap/sampling of worker external + ArrayBuffer usage in memory diagnostics.

*(End of prepared issue. Draft also exists locally at `~/openclaw-audit/db-stability/UPSTREAM-ISSUE-SUMMARY-model-catalog-memory.md` — that earlier draft contains private paths and must NOT be submitted; this Part A version is the sanitised replacement.)*

issues.body:
## Summary

Let `openclaw plugins reload` apply while agent turns are running. A running turn moves to the new plugin generation at its next step boundary, instead of holding the old generation until it ends. This is the in-process equivalent of a session resuming after a Gateway restart.

## Problem to solve

Today a plugin reload cannot apply while any agent turn is running.

- **Turns hold the generation.** Every admitted turn takes leases that retain work on every plugin instance in its registry for the whole turn, not only the plugin being reloaded (`src/agents/runtime-plugin-work.ts`).
- **The reload waits for them.** Its first drain stage (`src/gateway/server-plugin-reload.ts`, `server-plugin-reload-cleanup.ts`) waits for that retained work to reach zero.
- **Long turns make it roll back.** With the default 60 s budget, or 600 s with `--wait`, the reload times out and rolls back. The previous generation keeps serving and the operator has to retry later.
- **Agents that are always busy are the worst case.** Coding agents, long research turns and subagent trees may never reach a quiet point, so a reload effectively requires a Gateway restart.
- **The plugins that most need updates are the ones held for a whole turn:**
  - context engines, such as lossless-claw (`plugins.slots.contextEngine`);
  - memory plugins, such as Knowledge (`plugins.slots.memory`).

Observed on a production self-hosted Gateway: `plugins reload lossless-claw` and `plugins reload knowledge` failed on drain with 6, then 14, retained work items, and still failed with `--wait`.

Related defect seen during those reloads:
- **What happens:** between `quiesce()` and publish, the old registry stays published while it refuses calls. Fresh calls made in that window fail with `PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin <id> was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools`.
- **What it hits:** `plugins.sessionAction` from Control UI panels, best-effort one-shots such as `onSubagentEnded` (the subagent-end notification is lost), and hook dispatch.
- **How long:** the window lasts as long as the drain, so up to the whole budget.

## Proposed solution

### Behavior

**Hand over, never overlap.** The reload keeps its stop-old-then-start-new order, because exclusive resources and recovery depend on it: pollers, SQLite handles, ports and memory managers. Running turns stop at a safe point while the swap happens:

1. **Signal.** The reload reserves the replacement, and the plugin instance publishes a "replacement requested" signal.
2. **Park.** Some running turns hold the generation being replaced, and every replaced plugin they hold has opted in (see Plugin contract). Each such turn requests its own refresh. At its next step boundary (`prepareNextTurn`: after the step's tool calls settle, before the next provider request) it stops, releases all its holds and parks on the existing new-run gate.
3. **Swap.** The reload drains the remaining short in-flight calls, stops and disposes the old instance, then registers, starts and publishes the new one. The order is unchanged.
4. **Resume.** Each parked turn continues on the new generation through the existing plugin-runtime refresh continuation. The pause lasts only for the swap, usually seconds.

**Other turns keep today's behavior.** Turns that hold any replaced plugin that has not opted in still hold the reload until they end.

**Most of the step-boundary mechanism already exists.** Since #145648, the agent `plugins` tool can end an attempt at `prepareNextTurn` (`run/attempt-permission-prompt.ts`). `continueAfterAttempt` (`embedded-agent-runner/plugin-runtime-refresh.ts`) then continues the same logical run on a fresh generation (`run-orchestrator.ts`). What's missing is a trigger from `plugins reload`, and releasing the holds that last the whole turn.

### Core changes

1. **Replacement signal.** `PluginInstance.reserveReplacement()` fires a replacement-requested signal. The instance owns the fact, and consumers decide what to do with it. Rollback clears it.
2. **Release every hold that lasts the whole turn.** Each needs a hand-over that drops its work retention and keeps custody, the same shape as publication `retain()`, and then rebinds to the current generation:
   - the inbound dispatch lease (`auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts`), which also covers final delivery;
   - the reply-level prepared lease (`auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.ts`);
   - the Gateway `agent` RPC lease (`gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-execution-phase.ts`), used by Control UI, webchat and subagent children;
   - cron isolated runs (`cron/isolated-agent/run.ts`) and `agent-command-local`;
   - the channel `dispatchReply` work consumer (`plugins/runtime/runtime-channel.ts`).

   If any outer lease is still held when the continuation reacquires, the continuation waits on its own reload until the drain cap.
3. **Context-engine rebind.** Today the continuation runs its steps on a fresh context-engine wrapper, but `finalizeAcceptedContextEngineTurn` still commits through the original run-entry lease, which is the old generation's engine. The logical-turn lease (`agents/harness/context-engine-logical-turn.ts`, `embedded-agent-runner/run-entry.ts`) needs a `rebind()` that:
   - releases the old engine's sources;
   - lazily resolves the same engine ID from the current registry before the next attempt's `begin` and before finalization;
   - fails closed if that ID is missing or incompatible after the swap. Silently falling back to the legacy engine mid-turn is not allowed.
4. **Refresh trigger in the runner.** The embedded refresh owner (`agents/plugin-runtime-refresh.ts`) requests a refresh on the replacement signal when:
   - every replaced plugin it holds has opted in;
   - the attempt has a refresh consumer;
   - the new generation's tool names and schemas match the turn's (fingerprint). This keeps the tool surface and prompt-cache prefix stable mid-turn. If they differ, the turn keeps today's behavior.
5. **Continuation fidelity.** Fix the ways a refreshed turn differs from an uninterrupted one:
   - **Prompt wording:** make the continuation prompt depend on why the turn was handed over. Today it says "The plugin runtime has been refreshed… using the updated tools. Verify the requested change", which is wrong when an unrelated plugin was reloaded.
   - **Hooks re-run on the synthetic prompt:** `before_prompt_build`, `agent_turn_prepare` and `before_agent_reply` run again against it (for example, Active Memory recalls on the wrong text, and reply-claiming hooks could intercept the turn). Mark refresh continuations for hooks, or skip the claim hooks.
   - **Replayed injections:** don't replay queued plugin next-turn injections into the continuation (`plugin-turn-context.ts`).
   - **`agent_end` and `llm_output`:** fire once per logical turn, not once per attempt.
   - **Discarded commit intent:** the continuation's turn start must recognize its own logical turn. Today it discards the original attempt's pending context-engine intent twice, logging "discarded unaccepted turn advancement". The final commit still lands, but a crash in between loses the turn's recovery intent.
   - **Tool summary:** merge the result's `toolSummary` across attempts; today it counts only the last attempt.
   - **Back-to-back or failed reloads:** a refreshed acquisition is allowed only 3 gate waits (`prepared-model-runtime-lease.ts`), and a rejected gate is rethrown. Either one fails the continued run after its tools have already run. Refreshed acquisitions need a defer or retry policy instead of a terminal error.
6. **Calls during the swap.** Plugin RPCs, one-shots and hook dispatches that reach an instance with `!acceptingCalls && replacementPending` should wait on the reload gate, then resolve once against the current registry. The fallback is a retryable `UNAVAILABLE` with reason `plugin-reloading`, matching `gateway-restarting`. Separately, `memory-provider-adapter.ts` reports a call that completed after quiesce as a failure; fix that too.
7. **Status and output.**
   - Reload status says "waiting for N turns to reach a step boundary".
   - When a reload still has to wait for whole turns, its output names the plugins that kept them pinned.

### Plugin contract

Built into the manifest and SDK where possible, with docs explaining the rule.

- **Manifest opt-in.** A field such as `reload: { turnHandover: "between-steps" }` in `openclaw.plugin.json`. If it's absent, behavior stays as today. The host decides from the metadata of the generation being retired, without running plugin code. One field per plugin is enough, because the whole instance is swapped.
- **What opting in promises:**
  - **No in-memory state that a later call depends on.** Cross-call state lives in `api.runtime.state` or the plugin's own database.
  - **Disposal releases everything the plugin started.** `api.lifecycle.onDispose` callbacks are awaited and wait for the plugin's own workers.
- **What the host guarantees in return:**
  - two generations of one plugin never run calls at the same time;
  - the old instance's `gateway_stop` and dispose run only after its admitted calls drain;
  - calls during the swap wait rather than fail.

  These guarantees remove most of the burden from plugin authors.
- **Conformance kit** in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/testing`:
  - a two-instance run: instance A runs a step, A is disposed, instance B runs the next step;
  - leak checks after dispose: new global symbol keys, and active handles or workers.

  Bundled opted-in plugins run it in CI.
- **Docs.** A "Reload-safe plugins" page covering the rule, the host's guarantees, the kit and examples, linked from the manifest field docs and from the reload output. Update the Reload section of `docs/cli/plugins/uninstall-and-update.md`, plus `docs/plugins/sdk-runtime.md` and `docs/concepts/context-engine.md`.
- **Consider:** making `api.lifecycle.onDispose` required for managed instances rather than optional and feature-detected.

### What first-party plugins need to opt in

These were assessed from source.

**lossless-claw** (context engine)
- Durable state is already safe to continue on another instance:
  - transcript ingestion is idempotent per entry;
  - `commitTurn` uses idempotent receipts;
  - pending summaries use real leases with publish-time checks.
- Required: persist delegated expansion grants (`expansion-auth.ts`) in SQLite, or keep a delegated `lcm_expand_query` child on its parent's generation. Today a child that lands on the new generation fails closed with "Delegated expansion requires a valid grant".
- Fix: ingestion drops the transcript's `internal_system` / `display:false` provenance, so the continuation prompt is stored as a plain user message (see Evidence).
- Optional hardening in case the no-overlap guarantee ever regresses:
  - re-check the planned `context_items` range inside the compaction write transaction;
  - turn the compaction-debt `running` flag into a real lease;
  - make lease owners unique per instance;
  - replace the process-global engine singleton (`shared-init.ts`) with a per-registration engine.

**Knowledge** (memory)
- No cross-call in-memory state:
  - SQLite connections open and close per call;
  - cursors and references carry their store;
  - every write has a `requestId`.
- Required: `Stores.stop()` must wait for store runtime and registry shutdown, ideally through `onDispose`, so old workers are gone before the new instance starts.
- Recommended: give the "service reloaded", "runtime retired" and "storage stopped" errors a stable retryable code.

## Alternatives considered

- **Run both generations at once and hand over gradually.** Rejected:
  - It breaks the host's exclusive-resource and recovery contract.
  - It would need cross-instance coordination in plugins. For lossless-claw: the process-global engine reuse, per-session operation queues, the compaction-debt flag, and compaction that can replace the wrong rows if another writer runs during the LLM call. For Knowledge: the spec's single-writer rule, an in-memory revocation fence, and false "publication pending" / "recovery review is required" read errors.
- **End the turn and resume it (`reloadAndResume`).** It already exists for the in-turn `plugins` tool, but it splits one logical turn into two. The yielded tool result reads "Aborted", the first part is never committed to the context engine, and prompt-cache reuse drops on resume.
- **Longer drain budgets.** These only move the timeout and block all new runs for longer.
- **Documentation only.** Without the manifest opt-in and host guarantees, no plugin can safely be handed over. The host can't know which plugins tolerate it.
- **Opt-out instead of opt-in.** That would silently change the lifecycle contract for every third-party plugin. It could be reconsidered once the kit exists and adoption is broad.

## Impact

- **Affected:** operators and developers who reload plugins on a busy Gateway, mainly context-engine and memory plugins, and plugin authors iterating against a live Gateway.
- **Severity:** blocks the workflow. Today the reload either fails or needs a Gateway restart, which interrupts every session.
- **Frequency:** every reload while any long turn is running. That's routine on Gateways with long-running agents.
- **Consequence:** failed reloads, forced restarts, and Control UI panel errors and lost subagent-end notifications during the drain window.

## Evidence/examples

**Live test on an isolated Gateway, current `main`.**
- Setup: lossless-claw and Knowledge built from their `main`, a real model, and temporary logging around every context-engine call.
- The test: one multi-step turn that searched and wrote Knowledge, enabled an unrelated plugin with the `plugins` tool (forcing today's refresh continuation), then searched and wrote again. It was compared with the same task run uninterrupted.
- **Identical to the uninterrupted run:**
  - the final reply and the number of assistant turns, with no repeated tool calls;
  - the system-prompt hash, tool-list hash and cache key across the continuation. The prompt cache held: about 31k tokens were read from cache and 769 weren't;
  - lossless-claw's database: integrity check OK, every transcript entry ingested exactly once, and one turn-advancement row per logical turn;
  - Knowledge's store: integrity check OK, each write present once, all Git jobs committed;
  - no `PluginInstanceUnavailableError`.
- **Different:**
  - The final `commitTurn` ran through the original run-entry lease's old-generation wrapper. It worked only because lossless-claw shares one engine per process, and lossless-claw wasn't the plugin being replaced. This is the case core change 3 addresses.
  - The continuation prompt was stored in lossless-claw as a plain `role=user` message.
  - Two "discarded unaccepted turn advancement" warnings were logged per refresh.
  - The tool summary in the turn's JSON result counted only the calls after the refresh.
  - Knowledge's service was stopped and restarted mid-turn on every generation swap, even though Knowledge's instance was unchanged and the reloaded plugin was unrelated. Worth investigating: an in-flight Knowledge call from another session can hit Knowledge's service-reload fence.
- **Today's behavior when one of these plugins is reloaded mid-turn:**
  - an in-turn `reload` of lossless-claw or Knowledge is refused ("cannot replace itself from its own active turn");
  - `reloadAndResume` ends the turn and resumes it as a separate one;
  - an external `openclaw plugins reload lossless-claw` waits for the turn to finish, so there is no hand-over.
- **Not yet tested:**
  - an Anthropic model, whose system-prompt renewal in `prepareContinuation` wasn't exercised;
  - memory-provider search and auto-recall;
  - turns longer than 60 s;
  - the commit after lossless-claw itself is replaced, which needs the prototype.

**Prior art in this codebase:**
- the plugin runtime refresh continuation (#145648) and the Codex managed-thread refresh consumer;
- code-mode refresh `hold()`;
- publication `retain()` without work;
- Gateway restart recovery (`docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md`) for the resume-from-transcript model.

**Pre-existing defects found during the audit**, to be filed and fixed separately:
- **Session maintenance uses the retired generation.** It runs after the reply ends but reinstalls the reply's captured plugin registry (`session-maintenance/run.ts`). If a reload lands in between, Knowledge's memory flush resolves the retired generation and fails ("Optional session maintenance failed") or stays pinned.
- **Follow-up turns keep the previous generation.** The follow-up drain (`queue/drain.ts`) leaves the prepared-model scope but not the plugin generation scope. A queued follow-up sees the previous reply's generation until its embedded run sets up its own.
- **`load.paths` plugins can't be reloaded when a stale install record shares their ID.** `plugins reload` refuses a `plugins.load.paths` plugin in that case (`installed-plugin-package-ownership.ts`), reporting "no authoritative package-owner metadata", although the docs say `load.paths` plugins can be reloaded.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

## Additional information

**Suggested order:**
1. Fix calls during the swap (core change 6). It's independent and useful on its own.
2. Replacement signal, context-engine rebind, and the hold hand-overs. Build a prototype with a hardcoded allowlist instead of the manifest field.
3. Side-by-side check on an isolated Gateway: the same scripted turns with and without a mid-turn reload of lossless-claw and Knowledge, comparing context-engine and Knowledge state, transcripts and per-hook call counts. It must also cover overflow compaction, `lcm_expand_query` delegation, memory recall, subagent end, an Anthropic model, and turns longer than 60 s.
4. Only then: the manifest field and SDK kit, which are a public contract needing SDK-owner sign-off. Then docs, then the plugin opt-ins.

**Accepted trade-offs:**
- **Opt-in only.** One plugin that hasn't opted in keeps the turns using it pinned.
- **The opt-in is a promise.** Native plugins aren't sandboxed; the kit catches common violations, not all of them.
- **Long single steps still delay the swap.** For example, a slow tool, or overflow compaction waiting on an LLM summary.
- **A handed-over turn gets one internal continuation prompt and a new provider request.** Gateway restart recovery has the same property.
- **Changes take effect at different points:**
  - new skills snapshots and `before_model_resolve` results apply from the next turn;
  - tool-surface changes keep the turn pinned for its whole length.

**Out of scope for the first cut:**
- CLI-backend runs (no step boundary);
- ACP and worker-environment turns (an external loop);
- making `reloadAndResume` non-terminating;
- whether the Codex harness consumer joins.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On the Control UI Sessions page, the agent image avatar beside the agent name in the session table is clipped to a thin crescent/sliver, while the agent picker displays the full image for the same agent.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed sequence in the reporter recording:

1. Open the Sessions page with an image-avatar agent selected in the top-right agent picker.
2. Compare the picker avatar with the avatar in the agent-name attribution line inside the table's Key column.
3. Switch to another agent and then back using the picker.
4. Observe that the image avatar in the table remains visibly clipped.

The recording confirms the symptom and agent-switch sequence; these are not independently reproduced setup instructions. The exact conditions that introduce the defect are NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Expected behavior

The session-table image avatar should remain recognizable rather than appearing as a thin sliver. In the same recorded frame, the picker provides a concrete reference showing the full image for that agent.

### Actual behavior

At approximately 2 seconds, the selected agent's image is fully visible in the top-right picker, but appears as a narrow dark crescent next to its name in the table attribution line. Both visible session rows show the defect. Sampled frames also show the defect after switching away and back. The recording does not establish whether this is image sizing, clipping, overlap, or another rendering cause. No claim is made that the wrong avatar asset is selected.

### OpenClaw version

Gateway host checked immediately after these reports: **2026.10.10-beta.2 (`2b85c4c`)**. `openclaw --version` and the installed package agree; the running Gateway process points to this installed package. The recording itself does not display a version/build identifier, so browser asset identity is not independently confirmed.

### Operating system

Gateway host: **Debian GNU/Linux 13.7 (trixie), Linux 6.12.111+deb13-amd64, x86_64**. Browser/client OS and browser version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO; the recording does not identify them.

### Install method

Global Node.js package under the Node v24.16.0 installation; Gateway running as a user systemd service. Confirmed from the installed package path and running service/process.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

Inspected the Gateway user-service journal for **2026-10-19 20:30–20:50 America/Halifax (ADT)**, covering report receipt (not a verified recording capture timestamp). Examined 183 entries; no entries matched Activity/Sessions/avatar terms together with error/warn/fail/clip/distort. This does **not** establish the absence of a frontend error: browser console and DOM/computed-style traces were not captured. Unrelated runtime messages are omitted.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Confirmed by inspecting extracted frames from the reporter's 15.25-second recording. The following are **unscaled crops of the same frame at 2 seconds**, not separate runs.

Full image in the agent picker:

![Agent picker shows a complete avatar image](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/DonnieFi/546b6fe7cb4e77ebad781dc1e003d976/raw/picker-avatar.png)

Clipped avatar beside the same agent name in the Sessions table:

![Sessions table agent avatar is clipped to a narrow crescent](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/DonnieFi/546b6fe7cb4e77ebad781dc1e003d976/raw/table-avatar.png)

[Evidence provenance and files](https://gist.github.com/DonnieFi/546b6fe7cb4e77ebad781dc1e003d976).

The supplied recording is 1342 × 722 encoded pixels; these are not confirmed browser CSS viewport dimensions. The full recording is intentionally not published because unrelated session titles are visible. Both hosted PNG files were verified as HTTP 200, image/png, and byte-identical to the extracted crops. Hosted browser rendering has not been independently verified.

### Impact and severity

Affected surface: agent identity attribution in the Sessions table. The image is difficult to recognize in the recorded rows, even though its name remains readable. The defect is visible before and after switching agents. Frequency outside this recording and number of affected users are NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. No navigation failure or data loss is claimed.

### Additional information

Focused duplicate searches found no matching Sessions-table avatar distortion report. #158168 concerns a different surface/mechanism: sidebar rows choosing a delivery-origin avatar rather than the agent avatar. This report concerns visible clipping/distortion in the Sessions table, not proven incorrect asset selection. #83628 concerns unrelated README contributor avatars. #149361 tracks broader WebUI stability.

The original recording alone did not establish an independent runtime reproduction or cause; the production-main follow-up below adds browser evidence. No shipped fix or regression range is claimed. This report is separate from #177845 (vertically clipped Activity navigation labels).

### Current-main browser reproduction (follow-up to review)

**Reproduced** with a production-built UI at main commit `fd12f93cf4fd2cec0ce03be8f183a9dd1b41809e`, original stylesheet order, and synthetic Gateway fixtures. Playwright 1.64.0 / Google Chrome 155.0.8059.84 headless; Debian 13.7 x86_64, Node 24.16.0; viewport 1342 × 900 CSS pixels. No real Gateway or credentials were used or changed.

**Concrete setup:** an agent with both a loaded image avatar and emoji fallback; open Sessions, then select **All agents** via the visible scope picker. Current main renders the affected chip in its Agent column, not the older Key-column attribution line. The reproduction performs the real page boot, mocked handshake, Sessions list RPC, and scope selection with unmodified production styles.

| State | Container | Image offset X | Visible image width | Hidden fallback width |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original production CSS (`flex`) | 18 px | −6.796875 px | 11.203125 px | 13.59375 px |
| Temporary grid diagnostic | 18 px | 0 px | 18 px | 18 px |
| Diagnostic removed | 18 px | −6.796875 px | 11.203125 px | 13.59375 px |

The image itself remains 18 × 18 px and successfully decoded (natural width 64). Its **visible intersection with the overflow-clipped container**, rather than image width alone, is the failing invariant. Hidden emoji fallback content remains a flex participant and displaces the image. A no-emoji image-only control filled its container in this setup, so the fallback is a material reproduction condition.

The assertion exits 1 on the original bundle: `RED: loaded avatar visible image width is less than 90% of its avatar container`. The diagnostic asserts original failure → restored containment with only `.agent-row-chip__avatar { display: inline-grid; }` → original failure after removing that style. This sequence passed, with no browser page errors. Separate original-bundle runs produced identical failure measurements.

**Original production UI:**

![Current main Sessions All agents: clipped loaded image avatar](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/DonnieFi/546b6fe7cb4e77ebad781dc1e003d976/raw/current-main-before.png)

**Same page with temporary grid diagnostic:**

![Same Sessions row after temporary grid diagnostic restores avatar containment](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/DonnieFi/546b6fe7cb4e77ebad781dc1e003d976/raw/current-main-grid-diagnostic.png)

[Runnable harness and instructions](https://gist.github.com/DonnieFi/546b6fe7cb4e77ebad781dc1e003d976) · [Measurement JSON](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/DonnieFi/546b6fe7cb4e77ebad781dc1e003d976/raw/current-main-geometry.json)

The harness builds the production UI by default and uses existing repository E2E helpers. It also accepts an existing immutable bundle for fast replay. All four uploaded evidence files were checked for HTTP 200 and exact downloaded bytes; the screenshots were visually inspected before publication.

**Scope:** this confirms the layout defect and a reversible layout-mode diagnostic on current main. It is not a committed regression test, compiled source repair, or claim that all image-error/emoji/fallback/theme states pass. The review's focused unit/type/style checks remain repair acceptance criteria, not checks claimed as passed here. No operator Gateway change was made.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add a supported, preservation-safe pre-relay budget for Codex native image-bearing replay, including subscription/OAuth sessions.

### Problem to solve

An image-bearing tool result can push the next decoded `/responses` request over the relay's 33,554,432-byte limit. The same oversized history can also prevent native compaction from succeeding, leaving the operator unable to recover simply by retrying compaction.

Our sanitized incident measurements include a 43,574,904-byte decoded request. Gateway connectivity remained healthy. Preserving work and moving to fresh text-only context restored usability, but that is operator-managed containment rather than prevention.

Support reports that published `@openclaw/codex@2026.10.9` still maps this preparation failure to a generic retryable 502 on the shared subscription/OAuth route. We distinguish that report from our directly measured 2026.10.8 incident and do not claim to have reproduced every behavior on 2026.10.9.

### Proposed solution

Provide a supported mechanism that:

1. Bounds the final decoded native replay request **before relay admission**, rather than relying solely on a transcript-file or selected-history size proxy.
2. Preserves saved conversation history and customer-work checkpoints. Reducing active replay must not require deleting or manually editing saved history or native state.
3. Handles the boundary case where **one newly added image-bearing tool result alone** pushes the next request over the limit. Detect and handle that condition before submitting/retrying an oversized request.
4. Offers an explicit safe continuation/reduction path, with a bounded text handoff or other supported preservation semantics, when the existing history cannot be compacted through the same relay.
5. Reports a clear actionable refusal when safe reduction is unavailable, instead of repeatedly retrying unchanged oversized content.

Implementation details are for maintainers to determine. The request is for the supported behavior and preservation guarantees, not for a particular history-rewrite technique or a higher relay cap.

### Alternatives considered

- **PR #169145:** fail-fast error classification is useful, but it does not prevent oversized image-bearing replay. Please track this preventive capability separately, or link an existing preventive request.
- **`agents.defaults.compaction.maxActiveTranscriptBytes`:** preventive risk reduction on a different measurement surface, not a guaranteed budget for the final decoded request or a newly added image-bearing result.
- **Text-only fresh-context handoffs with isolated visual review:** usable containment, but manual coordination remains necessary and native visual workflows remain constrained.
- **Retrying the known-oversized history or compaction:** does not resolve the measured hard admission boundary.
- Raising the cap or editing native state is not the requested solution.
- Native-history storage retention, including #150940, is a separate concern from preventing this admission failure.

### Impact

- Affected: image-bearing Codex native sessions, including subscription/OAuth workflows and chat sessions coordinating visual work.
- Severity: blocks the affected conversation/workflow until preservation-first recovery is performed.
- Frequency: observed across repeated image-bearing incidents in our installation; not claiming all native sessions or every generic 502 has this cause.
- Consequence: exhausted retries, failed compaction, manual checkpoint/handoff work, interruptions and risk of repeating partially completed work if recovery is not carefully reconciled.

### Evidence/examples

Existing sanitized real-world measurements:
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/168794#issuecomment-6486703941

Error-classification PR (separate from this preventive request):
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169145

Documented transcript-byte guard:
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.9/docs/concepts/compaction.md#active-transcript-byte-guard

Related native-history issue, not assumed to solve relay admission:
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150940

No raw transcripts, customer content, credentials, or private diagnostic attachments are included.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Please confirm whether this will be tracked as a separate preventive feature request or linked to an existing one, and route it to the appropriate native replay maintainers. Support clarified that the support conversation itself cannot create backlog entries or assign an owner; this submission requests normal GitHub triage.

No owner, release commitment, or ETA is assumed. A merged error-classification PR should not be interpreted as a shipped preventive budget.
