prs.title: fix(doctor): unblock historical store imports without losing evidence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor refuses historical pending-input and worker-placement stores, or leaves historical image reserves unreadable after import.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can import recognized agent-v24, shared-v21 and image-v22 stores without discarding historical evidence or cleanup custody.

Queued inputs become interrupted without losing payloads or recovery envelopes. Incomplete preparation becomes a failed placement requiring cleanup. Incompatible worker claims or malformed images refuse the atomic migration without advancing markers or discarding custody.

**PostgreSQL limitation:** archival input/placement columns are not in the PostgreSQL descriptor. Their port is refused before target publication; keep these stores on SQLite. Image-only data uses existing JSON storage and was ported in earlier proof. **Rollback requires the verified pre-migration backup and matching runtime—not lowered version markers.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing migration and Doctor owners preserve predecessor evidence and derive missing predicates before publication, including the full-schema fallback selected by unrelated lazy-column gaps. Archives never grant execution authority; fresh databases do not acquire them. No P3 schema bump or second migration owner is added.

Contributor credit: based on @galiniliev's reviewed historical-import work in selected commit `d0cce88f317` and the approved preservation-only plan, adapted to current main.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d0705165-5352-4f6e-955d-99ab0c2be386)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/4d70f9f4-e855-496c-9675-8bc6b7cda6dc)

## Evidence

**Published head:** 983cdc8f6c278c41e0b5d58148b6b9aefd954af8; tree c9afaf040a04f7ebb66a8cf7b29a538e81105eb4, identical to reviewed/tested source d992459437a57a88b81443058f4ddd349e535550. The reviewed source parents are published f250485b753d6e7b93913a556698d6b96ec3a87a and pinned main 87016c018d3e4a4c44e34de96bb3cea25b28548c. The sole conflict was two independent additions to the update documentation; both are retained. All 23 authored added/deleted line sequences remain identical. Twenty-one authored blobs/modes are unchanged; documentation and wrapper inventory contain only their unchanged P3 additions alongside incoming main. The original discussion session performed this conflict refresh and renewed verification.

Four critical scenarios remain:
1. Real ordinary-CLI import and restoration of its original Doctor backups: full input/placement rows, image bytes, physical/metadata markers and pending-placement fencing.
2. Live worker-claim refusal without losing custody.
3. Publication failure, atomic rollback and retry preserving rows, rowids, leases and dependent cleanup records.
4. Ordinary-open v22 conversion with the lazy-column gap that reproduced the P2/P3 defect, including malformed-image rollback, correction/retry and exact archive/custody preservation.

**Renewed on the merged candidate:** all **3 migration-owner cases** pass; the ordinary **CLI import and original-backup restoration passes in 46.541s / 57.55s wrapper**, with its unchanged **90s guard**. Exact original rows, image JSON and schema markers are restored after child/reader closure. All **4 targeted older-service admission cases** pass (25 other cases unselected), covering ordinary/flag-only refusal and candidate/rehearsal admission. All commands and compiler generations settled normally. Doctor/state test types, lint of 14 production and 5 test/support files, formatting of 21 files and diff checks pass.

**Review and budget:** accepted local P0–P2 source/consolidation reviews are reused for identical authored changes; no new production migration logic or test assertion was authored in this merge. Incoming runtime inputs are covered by the renewed tests above, not described as unchanged. **6,283,878 / 6,329,745** passes with **45,867 headroom**. The scalar and existing allocation records are inherited from canonical main; P3 adds no ceiling increase. The new gateway-client dependency link was reconciled through the normal ownership-checked, offline frozen install in this task's physical installation; no manifest/lock or shared installation was changed.

**Deliberate coverage cuts:** @galiniliev's critical-only direction removed another 481 eligible lines: the duplicate Gateway/model/RPC/restart harness, granular predicate/index/trigger/idempotence/CHECK and unknown-column variants, extra image admission variants and declaration microtests. There is **no ongoing historical cold-Gateway test**. Authentic fixtures and existing chronology/backup coverage remain; critical backup restoration is now in ordinary CLI coverage. Diagnostic-only repair b03add185 is preserved separately, not in this feature delta. The Bun-parent diagnostic limitation and original timeout remain unresolved here.

**All seven removal phases now executed on this exact merged source:** four pass; dependency-production, full unused-files and production exports report inherited findings in only two unowned paths: `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer-width-ref.tsx: loadComposerWidthEdge` and `scripts/perf/update-state-io-measure.ts`. The exact source blobs, all three Knip configs and composer references match pinned 87016; no P3-authored path appears. This is source/reference-backed inherited attribution, not an executed whole-base scan or seven green phases. The earlier f250 scan also completed all seven phases, with six inherited failures and one pass; that older result is not reused as current. Knip 6.40.0 uses task-local hydrated caches and the maintained runner; no ignore, scanner change or unrelated deletion was added. The former missing-cache/0-of-7 blocker is resolved.

**Current-head CI is pending:** the reviewed candidate is now published as 983cdc8f6c278c41e0b5d58148b6b9aefd954af8. The prior f250 CI/Darwin success below does not qualify the new tree; exact published-head CI and live mergeability must be checked before landing. Historical **60/90s CLI failures and native-borrower teardown remain unexplained**. Passing renewals do not establish a flake classification or repair. PostgreSQL and published-updater limits remain explicit below.

<details>
<summary>Historical regression, published-updater and CI evidence—not current-head CI</summary>

### Prior f250 terminal CI

Published f250485b/tree6438234 (reviewed/tested source5a45a62b) passed [CI40808553345](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40808553345):83 successful/24 skipped jobs, and [Darwin40808553387](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40808553387). Complete paginated readback at2026-10-29 03:13 UTC had170 terminal checks (102success/67skip/1neutral) and3latest successful statuses. Initial dependency/security failures explicitly said review had not completed and were superseded by successful publisher statuses, not a vulnerability waiver. Its CLI proof was45.271s/83.86s wrapper; budget6246427/6320000. These are prior-source facts; no new hosted review is claimed.


### Conversion regression

An isolated P3 bd542 + reviewed P2 a77858c57e76a1174f866c92a68d3d2e8bfaf3be composition repaired secret_store_entries.allowed_hosts and published schema 36 but left the v22 image unconverted. P3 alone and Doctor preparation converted it. Repair d2f3689 invokes historical conversion before full publication; composed regressions passed. The reduced test also fails when that call is omitted and passes with the real owner. Scratch inputs were restored.

Earlier native CLI proof reproduced v21's missing-predicate failure and agent-v24's recovery-column refusal before repair. Authentic historical fixtures—not relabeled current schemas—establish the inputs.

### Real published-driver update at c621

The installed **published 2026.10.8 updater** updated to **c62102e1a78f13f43210c8cb4f771b0fde989e13**. Both packages carried 2026.10.8; no version relabeling occurred. Candidate tarball SHA-256: **c068f2fe4d4212a748bbc7d2e55f66328219046df70651a3679576a11e1cce7c**.

An approved, isolated non-root Podman adaptation ran the unmodified harness from 8889b596023c846cc9076078a000c25715f0ecf0 without provider credentials or operator state. The real update and durable run succeeded in **296.80s**; version/build matched, service PID changed and readiness returned **200**. Durable history/sidecar survived; incognito history did not.

Scoped restore intentionally failed a malformed sibling while a healthy agent reached **38**, then restored that agent to **26**. Both outbox rows/order and a later unrelated cache write survived. The expected malformed-fixture exit 1 was not an overall failure; harness/service cleanup exited zero and task containers/volumes were absent at closeout.

**Limits:** historical Podman proof, not Docker/cross-platform parity or a new 5a45 updater run. The generic harness lacked P3's exact v21/v22/v24 fixtures. Providers/channels were disabled; injected messages are not live-model proof. Full port CLI/config switching and paid/live providers were untested. No credential-hydrating workflow was dispatched or operator service changed. Fixture setup corrections preserved assertions/deadlines.

### Historical Gateway and PostgreSQL

At c621, two cold Gateways shared the migrated database. Public reads showed the image/interrupted input; two new synthetic-HTTP-model turns completed with **zero historical-input model requests**. Doctor backups were restored and re-migrated after shutdown. That test is retired, not ongoing or renewed 5a45 proof. Initial setup required fixture-only loopback proxy exclusions.

Earlier PostgreSQL **17.11** proof covered canonical sibling ports, archival-column refusal and image-only transfer of 133 tables with exact JSON. Missing profile-table prerequisites were resolved through real profile-owner bootstrap. This is not archival-column support, full port CLI/config switching or fresh post-integration PostgreSQL proof.

### Prior failures and review

- [CI 40650404406](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40650404406), ca3c: test-lines, native-borrower teardown and aggregate failure. Unchanged local replays did not establish a fix or inherited classification. Upstream [bec3ad81](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bec3ad81da5568e05e5e55219b00c72bb4ee6e0a) later supplied maintenance-before-shared-state cleanup; the borrower guard remains and original uncertainty is not erased.
- [CI 40725668501](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40725668501), bd542: five CLI guards—three agent-ordering cases and July upgrade at **60s**, historical v21 at **90s**—during unfinished Doctor phases, not demonstrated exit hangs. Classification was **unknown: no matching main job**. Local passing replays used the pinned Bun fork and Node **26.12.1**, versus CI Node **24.22.1** and a different synthetic merge; they did not fix those failures.
- The final 60cf local sentinel also hit **90s** at legacy-state-migrations before completion/payload assertions. Its main thread and another thread were in D-state at handle_reserve_ticket on Btrfs. Exact operation, duration and cause remain unknown: an I/O hypothesis, not a filesystem defect or flake verdict. Separately retained b03 proved a Bun-parent/Node-child diagnostic blind spot and repaired that helper, not the timeout. Instrumented and current CLI passes do not settle the cause.
- [CI 40746693721](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40746693721), 3805: then-current budget and aggregate failure. ## What Problem This Solves

Recovery status reread the same run ledger during capture admission, receipt validation and final classification. Later reads bypassed the caller-selected ledger reader, so one projection could combine different observations or silently query the default state store.

## User Impact

Each sealed capture uses one ledger observation throughout status inspection. A missing run stays missing; an unavailable selected reader becomes directory-only unreadable evidence. Filesystem seals, generation bindings and forward-recovery receipts are still validated before they influence status. This projection does not grant restore or cleanup authority.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the fact from the capture reader through the existing status owner. Remove repeated database reads and the obsolete catch around pure classification. There is no cache, alternate store, fallback reader, schema change or public configuration change.

## Evidence

- Four regressions fail against the preceding inventory fix: hidden default-store reads, selected-reader failure handling and repeated forward-receipt ledger reads.
- The production candidate at 91716af7 passed all 24 recovery-status tests in its native PR checkout (37.55s; wrapper 40.72s), plus core typechecking. prs.title: fix(plugins): install from the literal local path when it ends in whitespace
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw plugins install "<dir> "` installs the trimmed sibling directory instead of the directory the user named. A trailing space in a directory name is legal on POSIX; `resolveUserPath` trims the spec before the local install path is resolved, so the install silently selects the neighbor.

Fixture with two siblings, `probe-dirs/plug` (plugin id `probe-beta`) and `probe-dirs/plug ` (plugin id `probe-alpha`): current main installs `probe-beta` when the user passes `probe-dirs/plug ` and reports `Installed plugin: probe-beta`.

## User Impact

- `openclaw plugins install "<path> "` installs exactly the named directory.
- Unchanged for ordinary paths: relative, absolute, and `~/` paths resolve as before; a whitespace-only spec still fails with `Plugin install source must not be empty.`
- Behavior change disclosed: a local plugin/hook install spec with leading or trailing whitespace is no longer trimmed. It either exists literally or fails with `path not found: <literal>`. Specs without boundary whitespace are byte-for-byte unaffected.
- `openclaw hooks install` local sources use the same resolver and get the same fix. No new option, validator, config key, or stored format.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveUserPath` trims by design (`src/infra/home-dir.ts` → `resolvePathWithHome`), which is right for user-typed config paths but wrong for a quoted local install locator: the shell already delimits the name. Blank admission stays intact; only boundary whitespace of a non-blank spec is preserved.

Two sites on the same install path are updated together so the result is consistent, not partial:

- `src/infra/install-flow.ts:resolveExistingInstallPath` — the deferred package-dir install resolves the spec here (`plugins/install-package.ts`, `hooks/install.ts`). This site actually selected the trimmed sibling.
- `src/plugins/install-source-plan.ts` — `resolvePluginInstallSourcePlan` and the managed `case "local"` resolve the same spec for source classification and managed install requests.

One owner: `resolveLiteralInstallPath` lives in `install-flow.ts` and `install-source-plan.ts` imports it. Non-blank values use `path.resolve(expandHomePrefix(value))`, the accepted shape from #186475/#186746; blank values keep `resolveUserPath`.

Classification: behavior-preserving for specs without boundary whitespace; behavior-correcting for explicitly quoted literal paths.

Not fixed here: the git-URL and `npm-pack` branches of `install-source-plan.ts` still call `resolveUserPath`; they are not filesystem path locators on this flow.

Collision disclosure: open PR #185654 also touches `src/plugins/install-source-plan.ts`, but only the git-URL `.replaceAll("@", "%40")` line (~140). This change touches the local-path classification line (~103) and the managed `case "local"` block (~415); no shared hunk. Open PR #185333 touches `src/plugins/install-source-spec.ts`, which this change does not edit.

## Evidence

Base `7c87e3a892d` (upstream/main). Candidate `6730a1b4446eb51567264b0265b30bd26b9839a2`.

Pristine current-main trees on a Linux remote host with installed dependencies, isolated `HOME`, in-tree fixtures:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts plugins install "/ws/probe-dirs/plug " --force --accept-capabilities
```

| | current main (twice) | candidate (twice) |
|---|---|---|
| install target | `Installing to /tmp/probe-7/.openclaw/extensions/probe-beta…` | `Installing to /tmp/probe-7/.openclaw/extensions/probe-alpha…` |
| result | `Installed plugin: probe-beta` | `Installed plugin: probe-alpha` |
| `plugins list --json` id | `probe-beta` | `probe-alpha` |

Current main, raw:

```
WARNING - Installing plugin from local path: /ws/probe-dirs/plug 
Installing to /tmp/probe-7/.openclaw/extensions/probe-beta…
Installed plugin: probe-beta
```

Independent red case: with only the literal directory present, current main fails `plugins install "/ws/probe-dirs/plug "` with `Plugin path not found: /ws/probe-dirs/plug` — the trimmed path.

Controls: ordinary relative path (`plugins install probe-dirs/plug`) still installs `probe-beta`; whitespace-only spec still fails with `Plugin install source must not be empty.`

Regression test: `src/infra/install-flow.test.ts` (existing file, `withTestDir` fixture) asserts `resolveExistingInstallPath` returns the literal sibling when both `plugin` and `plugin ` exist. `git diff --check` clean.

Not tested: the touched Vitest file was not executed — the remote verification tree is owned by another uid, so Vitest cannot write `/ws/.cache/vitest/default` (`EACCES`). PR CI covers it. No Windows run; trailing-space names are unsupported there, so the case is `skipIf(win32)`.

Merge Danger: low. One shared helper plus three call-site lines in two files; no schema, config, protocol, or stored-state change. The disclosed behavior change is the only semantic delta; reverting restores trimming and rewrites nothing already installed.

prs.title: fix(cron): include untruncated agent output in webhook delivery
prs.body:
Related: #185873

> Deliberately **Related, not Closes**: this PR delivers the recommendation's
> detached/isolated half; the named-session half — the reporter's original repro lane —
> needs the cron-owner follow-up documented under **Fix scope**, so the issue must stay
> open until that lands (same Related-over-Closes call the review asked for on #185766).

## What Problem This Solves

Cron webhook deliveries truncate long agent output: the finished-event payload only
carries the bounded `summary` (2,000 characters + `…`), so a webhook receiver silently
loses the rest of an otherwise successful report. Issue #185873 reproduces this on a
2,718-character reply; this change adds an additive, webhook-only `outputText` field
that carries the run's full final agent text for isolated and current-session
agent-turn jobs, with the bounded `summary` left byte-for-byte unchanged.

ClawSweeper's recommendation on the issue:

> **Recommendation:** **Add separate full output:** Define an additive webhook-only
> final-text field for named-session and detached agent turns, with boundary coverage
> for long output, silent replies, and failed runs.
>
> Why: Source confirms the missing full-text payload, but historical implementation and
> current documentation define summary-bearing completion events, and a maintainer has
> explicitly preserved the summary cap.

This PR implements the recommendation's **detached/isolated half** with the three
required boundaries (long output, silent replies, failed runs). The named-session half
is disclosed below under **Fix scope** — it cannot be delivered without editing
`src/cron/service/state.ts` (occupied by #185848) and adding new capture through the
auto-reply owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The full text already exists in the cron owner lane: `runIsolatedAgentJob` returns
  `outputText` as "Last non-empty agent text output (not truncated)"
  (`src/cron/service/state.ts:245-246`), produced by
  `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-finalize.ts:390,407`. It was simply dropped by the
  explicit field enumeration in the detached branch of
  `src/cron/service/timer-execution.ts` before the webhook event was assembled in
  `src/cron/service/timer-job-runner.ts`.
- The maintainer-preserved summary cap stays exactly where it is:
  `pickSummaryFromOutput` (`src/cron/isolated-agent/helpers.ts:67-74`) is untouched, and
  persisted run history, `openclaw automations runs`, and chat announcements keep the
  bounded `summary`. The new field is projected only into the primary webhook payload
  (`delivery.mode: "webhook"`); the persistence codec enumerates fields
  (`src/cron/run-event-codec.ts`, `src/cron/store/run-result.ts`), so nothing new is
  stored or fanned out to Gateway clients.
- Fix classification: **behavior-completing** (additive field on an existing payload,
  no existing field or cap modified).

## User Impact

- Webhook receivers of isolated/current-session agent-turn automations get the complete
  final report in `outputText` whenever it is non-empty; the `summary` they already
  consume is unchanged.
- Silent/empty runs: the field is absent (no fabricated keys).
- Failed runs: the error webhook keeps its existing text-free payload (no `summary`,
  no diagnostics, and now explicitly no `outputText`).
- Operators see no change in run history, announcements, Control UI, or config: no new
  option, validator, or persisted state was added.
- Known boundary (documented in `docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md`): main-session
  and named-session (`session:<key>`) agent turns do not carry `outputText` yet.

## Evidence

- proof base SHA: `364c0d4ebcd400ee4285eb989ed60d2a8b000b93` (the `main` this patch was
  proven against on 2026-10-27; every red/green leg below ran there)
- proof candidate SHA: `ccdf3ec35a9969c4b4bf2b5cb3baa99990312acf`
- current head SHA: `a6a54c9b7…` — the identical seven-file change rebuilt directly on
  `main` `2742aa016…` on 2026-10-29 (details under **Rebuild**). The 2026-10-28
  `main` merge that `3526945…` recorded is gone: that merge left GitHub computing this
  PR's diff against a stale merge base, which surfaced as 905 changed files,
  `CONFLICTING`, a false `security-sensitive-changed`, and an unreadable
  `This branch has conflicts` UI.
- Red = base without the patch; green = candidate. Both legs use the same commands and
  the same loopback harness (isolated Gateway state under `/tmp`, zero-credential
  OpenAI-compatible model stub returning a 3,939-character final answer, loopback
  webhook receiver recording raw bodies).

### Unit red/green (vitest, one file)

| Leg | Command | Exit | Wall time | Assertion point |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Red (base) | `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/cron/service.persists-delivered-status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 1 | 91.62s | `sends untruncated outputText while the summary keeps its bounded shape` fails: `expected undefined to be 'CRON_FULL_OUTPUT_PROOF_…'` (webhook body has no `outputText` on base) |
| Green (candidate) | same command | 0 | 159.41s | 16/16 pass, including all three boundary tests |

The two boundary tests (`omits outputText when the run produced no non-empty output
text`, `keeps failed-run webhooks free of both summary and outputText`) pass on both
legs: they lock the additive contract's absent-key behavior.

### Shipped-CLI × live Gateway proof (base red / candidate green)

Both legs: `node <dist>/index.js gateway run --port 18999` (real Gateway, isolated
`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`), `automations add --webhook http://127.0.0.1:18991/hook --session
isolated --model stub/stub-long`, `automations run <job> --wait`, then
`automations runs <job> --limit 1 --sort desc --json` plus the receiver's raw body log.
Leg script: `bash /tmp/oc-cron1-proof/run-leg.sh <red|green> <dist>/index.js`.

| Leg | Command | Exit | Wall time | Webhook body observation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Red (base dist, `OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (364c0d4)`) | `bash /tmp/oc-cron1-proof/run-leg.sh red /media/vdc/oc-cron1/dist/index.js` | 0 | 226.80s | 1 POST; `status:"ok"`, `deliveryStatus:"delivered"`; **no `outputText` key**; `summary` length 2001, ends with `…`, `summaryEqualsFullText:false` (full text 3,939 chars) — issue reproduced |
| Green (candidate dist, build-info `commit: ccdf3ec35…`) | `bash /tmp/oc-cron1-proof/run-leg.sh green2 /media/vdc/oc-cron1/dist/index.js` (identical rerun of the first green leg; both exit 0) | 0 | 219.14s | 1 POST; `status:"ok"`, `deliveryStatus:"delivered"`; **`outputText` present with the complete final text** (3,938 chars, equals the stub's full answer trimmed of surrounding whitespace); `summary` still 2,001 chars ending `…`, byte-identical to the red leg (`md5` match) |

<details><summary>Green leg output (candidate dist, build-info commit ccdf3ec35)</summary>

```text
$ bash /tmp/oc-cron1-proof/run-leg.sh green2 /media/vdc/oc-cron1/dist/index.js
gateway healthy after 5 polls
job=a9fbf1d5-6095-421f-83a1-3b938ab6e4b6
run-exit=0
greenleg wall=219.14s exit=0

webhook body analysis (same script as the red leg):
{"deliveries":1,"status":"ok","deliveryStatus":"delivered","hasOutputTextKey":true,
 "outputTextEqualsTrimmedFullText":true,"summaryLen":2001,"summaryEllipsis":true,
 "summaryMd5MatchesRedLeg":true}
run history (automations runs --json): status ok, summaryLen 2001, hasOutputTextKey false
```

`outputTextEqualsTrimmedFullText: true` compares the delivered field against the
stub's complete 3,939-character answer trimmed of surrounding whitespace
(the value is 3,938 characters; the stub text ends in a space from its repeat
unit) — no internal truncation.

</details>

### Boundary coverage (Recommendation requirement)

1. **Long output** — 3,939-character final answer: `outputText` equals the full text
   with only surrounding whitespace trimmed (3,938 characters; no internal
   truncation), `summary` remains exactly 2,001 characters ending in `…`
   (byte-identical between red and green legs: `summary_md5_match: true`).
2. **Silent replies** (unit, loopback HTTP body) — `outputText: undefined` and
   whitespace-only `outputText` both omit the key from the JSON body; the existing
   success-with-empty-summary suppression (`deliverySuppressionReason: "empty"`, no
   POST) is unchanged.
3. **Failed runs** (unit, loopback HTTP body) — a run with `status:"error"`, a
   summary, and output text delivers the error webhook without `summary`,
   diagnostics, or `outputText`; `error` and `status` keep their existing shape.

### Summary cap untouched (control)

`pickSummaryFromOutput` (`src/cron/isolated-agent/helpers.ts:67-74`) and the
2,000-character diagnostics cap (`src/cron/run-diagnostics-normalize.ts:12`) are not
modified. In the shipped proof the `summary` string is byte-identical on the red and
green legs (`md5` match), and `openclaw automations runs --json` shows the same
2,001-character summary with no `outputText` on both legs — the new field is
webhook-only.

### Fix scope (disclosure)

- Covered: detached lanes — `sessionTarget: "isolated"` and `"current"` agent turns
  (the `runIsolatedAgentJob` path), which own the untruncated text end-to-end.
- Not covered: named-session (`main` / `session:<key>`) agent turns. The full text of
  those turns exists only inside the session-event handoff
  (`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.ts:438`,
  `summary ??= truncateUtf16Safe(payload.text, 2000)`); the settled contract
  `SessionEventOutcome` (`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-contract.ts:32-52`)
  exposes only the bounded `summary`, `runCronSessionTurn`
  (`src/cron/session-run.ts:295`) forwards only that summary, and the scheduler's
  `runSessionEvent` return type is declared in `src/cron/service/state.ts:267-271` —
  a file held by open PR #185848 and excluded from this change. Covering that half
  requires a `state.ts` contract change plus new capture through the auto-reply owner;
  it is intentionally left for a follow-up with the cron owner.

### Impact surface

| File:line | Change | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/cron/types.ts:163-168` | `CronEvent` gains optional `outputText` with ownership comment | Type-only; optional field, never persisted or fanned out |
| `src/cron/types.ts:272-273` | `CronJobExecutionResult` gains optional `outputText` | Carries the value to the webhook literal; persistence codecs enumerate fields, so no storage growth |
| `src/cron/service/timer-execution.ts:437-442, 552-555` | Detached branch forwards `res.outputText` (was dropped by explicit enumeration) | Isolated lane only; main-session/script/command branches unchanged |
| `src/cron/service/timer-job-runner.ts:170-174` | Primary webhook event literal adds a conditional `outputText` spread | Webhook-only surface; empty/whitespace output omits the key |
| `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.ts:222-228` | Error-run webhook payload strips `outputText` alongside the existing summary/diagnostics strip | Failed-run payload shape identical to today |
| `src/cron/service.persists-delivered-status.test.ts:205-285` | Three boundary tests + loopback helper (real `sendGatewayCronWebhook`, real HTTP body) | Test-only |
| `docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md:230-241`, `docs/cli/cron.md:208` | Document `outputText` and its boundaries | Docs-only |

Isolation from #185848 (occupies `src/cron/service/state.ts`, `src/cron/service/ops-stream.ts`,
`failure-alerts.ts`, `run-recovery.ts`, `src/cron/delivery-*.ts`,
`src/cron/isolated-agent/run-delivery-trace.ts`, `src/cron/store/*.ts`,
`src/gateway/server-cron-completion.ts(+test)`, `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-add.ts`,
`cron-input-validation.ts`, `docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md`,
`src/config/*cron*`, `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.*`): **zero files in common**.
`CronServiceDeps.sendCronWebhook` and `CronEventContext` signatures are unchanged;
the whole change routes through `types.ts` optional fields plus the webhook event
literal in `timer-job-runner.ts`. Collision check was run against the current open-PR
file map (`gh pr list --state open --limit 200 --json number,files`): none of the seven
touched files appear in any open PR.

### Test-lines justification

No ceiling bump is needed on the rebuilt head. `main` now carries measured headroom:
`config/test-lines-baseline.txt` reads a 6,320,000 ceiling documented as
"Measured bf6a97a1765 plus pending regression additions: 6,312,681 lines. Keep 7,319
lines of bounded headroom for remaining regression work". This PR's +82 test lines
(three behavioral tests plus the loopback helper that drives the real
`sendGatewayCronWebhook` path, nothing deleted) fit that reserved headroom, so the
branch does not touch the baseline file at all. Verified on the rebuilt head:

```text
$ pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet
Test lines OK: 6312490; ceiling: 6320000; slack: 7510.
```

The earlier 2026-10-27/28 discussion of raising the ceiling to 6,286,508 and then to
6,300,526 belonged to the pre-rebuild head, where `main`'s measured total sat above its
own ceiling and a bump was the only way through; dropping it removes line churn from
`config/test-lines-baseline.txt`, which several other open PRs also edit.

### Rebuild

The 2026-10-28 `Merge main into fix/cron-webhook-full-output` commit (`3526945…`) left
the PR in a state no maintainer can merge: GitHub reported 905 changed files and `+23708/−8739`
for a seven-file fix, `mergeable: CONFLICTING`, and `security-review-required` triggered
by auth/secrets paths that existed only in that phantom diff (`gh pr diff` refused with
`HTTP 406: the diff exceeded the maximum number of files (300)`).

The branch was rebuilt as one commit on `main` `2742aa016…` instead of carrying a merge
commit. The result:

| Signal | Before (`3526945…`) | Rebuilt (`a6a54c9b7…`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| changed files | 905 | **7** |
| additions/deletions | +23708/−8739 | **+120/−3** |
| `mergeable` | `CONFLICTING` | **`MERGEABLE`** |
| `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` | FAILURE (phantom auth paths) | **pass — "No sensitive product changes"** |
| labels | 42, incl. `channel: *`, `app: *`, `extensions: *`, `size: XL`, `security-review-required` | **7**: `docs`, `gateway`, `size: S`, `proof: sufficient`, `P2`, `rating: 🦐 gold shrimp`, `status: ⏳ waiting on maintainer` |
| `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` | touched (conflict) | untouched |

The rebuild applied the same patch to current `main`: all seven hunks applied cleanly
(the only conflict was the baseline line, resolved by keeping `main`'s headroom version)
and no source line changed. Local verification on the rebuilt tree: `pnpm test
src/cron/service.persists-delivered-status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → **16/16 pass**
(135.7s, Node 24.22.1), `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on the seven files,
`git diff --check` clean, and the five touched-file ratchets plus the test-lines ratchet
OK against `origin/main`.

### Gates

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| oxlint | `pnpm exec oxlint <5 touched src files>` | 0 warnings, 0 errors |
| format | `node scripts/run-format.mts --check <5 touched src files>` | clean |
| docs format | `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/format-docs.mts --check` | clean (1405 files) |
| whitespace | `git diff --check` | clean |
| adjacent tests | `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.test.ts src/gateway/server-cron-primary-webhook.test.ts src/gateway/server.cron.test.ts src/cron/service.trigger-eval.test.ts src/cron/service.session-payload.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | the four non-`server.cron` files pass 65/65; all failures are in `server.cron.test.ts` (next row) |
| adjacent tests (environmental) | `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/server.cron.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 4 timeouts fail **identically on base and candidate** (45s test timeout on this loaded host; base-code comparison run produces the same 4 failures and same passing set — failure diff zero, not attributable to this change) |
| ratchets | `check-line-cap-ratchet`, `check-max-lines-ratchet`, `check-test-mock-exports`, `check-assertion-safety`, `check-test-timeout-race-ratchet` (each `--base origin/main --no-merge-base`, rerun on the rebuilt head) | all OK; no new violations/suppressions |
| test-lines ratchet | `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` on the rebuilt head | `Test lines OK: 6312490; ceiling: 6320000; slack: 7510` (no baseline change) |
| typecheck (core) | `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit` | only pre-existing TS2883 vitest-type portability errors in files this PR does not touch (`src/tui/*-test-support.ts`, `test/helpers/*`); none in touched files |
| typecheck (cron test shard) | `pnpm exec tsc -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --noEmit` | same pre-existing TS2883/TS5088 class only, none in touched files |
| `pnpm tsgo` | unavailable on this host | the pinned `@tsrs/linux-x64-gnu` native binary requires GLIBC ≥ 2.34; host has older glibc (`GLIBC_2.34…2.32 not found`). Fallback: full `tsc` runs above + CI |

### Cleanup

- All proof state lives under `/tmp/oc-cron1-proof/` (`state-red/`, `state-green/`,
  JSONL webhook logs); Gateway, model stub, and webhook receiver are terminated by the
  leg script's `trap cleanup` (explicit `kill <pid>`, no `pkill` matching the agent's
  own command line). Loopback ports only (18991/18992/18999).
- No production Gateway, session, token, or user config was touched; the model stub is
  a loopback OpenAI-compatible server with a synthetic key; the webhook receiver is a
  loopback HTTP sink.

### Not tested

- Named-session (`main` / `session:<key>`) webhook output — intentionally out of scope
  (see Fix scope); the issue's original repro used `sessionTarget: "session:veille-ia"`,
  so that lane's webhook payload remains summary-only until the follow-up lands.
- Full CI suites (left to PR CI); only the touched test file was run locally
  (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` equivalents above).
- The `completionDestination` (announce-mode completion webhook) payload is unchanged:
  its event is built from the persisted run-result projection, which does not carry
  `outputText` by design.

<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

- Production change is four small hunks: two optional type fields, one previously-dropped field forwarding in the detached branch, one conditional spread in the webhook event literal, and one extra strip in the existing error-payload destructure. The fence-like summary cap code (`pickSummaryFromOutput`, diagnostics cap) is untouched.
- The conditional spread is the entire silent-run contract: empty/whitespace output omits the key rather than sending `outputText: ""`; the boundary tests lock that absent-key behavior.
- Docs landed in `docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md` + `docs/cli/cron.md` because `webhooks.md` is the inbound Gateway-hooks page (declares itself separate from outbound delivery) and the canonical outbound `delivery.md` is occupied by #185848 — move the doc line there once #185848 lands if preferred.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- **Land-ready as is:** implements the issue's ClawSweeper recommendation for the lane whose owner already produces the untruncated text, with two-head shipped-CLI × live-Gateway proof (summary md5-identical across legs) and all three required boundaries.
- **Wait for the named-session half (single combined PR):** blocked structurally — that half needs a `state.ts` contract change (file occupied by #185848) plus new capture through the auto-reply owner, which violates the additive/no-new-capture scope this PR is holding to. Recommended instead: land this half, follow up with the cron owner for `session:<key>`.
- **Alternative — replace `summary` with the full text:** rejected; the maintainer explicitly preserved the 2,000-character cap, and run history / announcements / `automations runs` depend on the bounded shape (proven unchanged).
- **Scope statement:** webhook-only additive key on the primary delivery payload; no config, persistence, RPC, or fan-out change; issue #185873 stays open for the remaining lane.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions: Keep Allow edits from maintainers enabled</summary>

Maintainers may push directly to this branch (Allow edits from maintainers stays
enabled), including scope reductions, follow-up split, or landing as-is.

</details>

prs.title: fix(signal): match canonical Unicode in signal alias search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Searching the Signal alias directory fails when the stored alias and the typed query use different Unicode normalization forms:

- With `signal.aliases: { "mye\u0301account": "+15551234567" }` written from a device that produced the decomposed (NFD) form, a composed `myéaccount` query (`é` = U+00E9) against the alias directory returns an empty list, even though the entry is right there.

Both sides are user-writable Unicode text, so the mismatch is user-visible: the entry exists, the query is correct, and the search silently returns nothing. Same class as #187953 (merged today for buzz, WhatsApp, Microsoft Teams message search), #187148 (slack/feishu/telegram), #187881 (matrix), #187199 (mattermost).

- Problem: case-insensitive substring search compares raw code units, so canonically equivalent text (NFC vs NFD) does not match.
- Solution: normalize the query and each candidate to NFC at comparison time, after lowercasing. Directory entries keep their original spelling.
- What changed: `extensions/signal/src/aliases.ts` (alias directory search) plus one regression test.
- What did NOT change: entry text, ids, handles, limits, ordering, and non-search behavior. Search remains case-insensitive substring matching.

## Why This Change Was Made

NFC normalization happens at the comparison boundary only, in the shape the rest of the family already merged with: `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(value).normalize("NFC")` on both sides (reusing the existing helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/string-coerce-runtime`).

- Best fix: normalize per comparison; no normalized copies are cached or stored, so there is no new invalidation surface.
- Alternative rejected: normalizing at write time (alias storage) would rewrite user text and change what the UI displays, and it would not repair already-stored decomposed input.
- Risk: `normalize("NFC")` is a no-op for ASCII and already-composed text. The only behavioral change is that canonically equivalent queries now match. Signal alias display names still come from the configured key, so spelling is preserved.

## User Impact

Users no longer have to retype a search term until its Unicode form happens to match the stored one: Signal alias lookups return the same results whichever normalization form the client produced, and displayed names stay exactly as stored/configured.

## Evidence

### Shipped command verification (`openclaw directory peers list --channel signal`)

The real CLI command routes through `directory-cli.ts` → `resolveInstallableChannelPlugin` (Signal's `getLoadedChannelPlugin` → `plugin.directory`) → `runDirectoryList` (`listPeersLive ?? listPeers`) → `listSignalAliasDirectoryEntries`. An isolated state dir/config stores one NFD alias key (`mye\u0301account` → `+15551234567`); the typed query is composed NFC (`é` = U+00E9).

Post-fix (this branch):

```console
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-signal-proof OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/oc-signal-proof/openclaw.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts directory peers list --channel signal --query é --json
[
  {
    "kind": "user",
    "id": "+15551234567",
    "name": "myéaccount"
  }
]
```

Pre-fix (source reverted):

```console
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-signal-proof OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/oc-signal-proof/openclaw.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts directory peers list --channel signal --query é --json
[]
```

The `--json` output preserves the returned entry (kind/id/name), and the returned `name` keeps the stored spelling.

### Behavior matrix

```text
surface          stored form               => typed query => pre-fix => post-fix
signal aliases   NFD "mye\u0301account"    => NFC "é"     => []      => 1 alias entry (+15551234567)
```

### Pre-fix failing test (source reverted, test kept)

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/signal/src/aliases.test.ts
 × matches canonically equivalent alias spellings
```

prs.title: fix(control-ui): render PDF attachment previews in WebKit
prs.body:
## Why

PDF attachment previews in the Control UI stay blank in WebKit. A Blob URL document inherits the Content Security Policy of the context that created the URL. The preview frame therefore inherits the app's `frame-ancestors` anti-framing rule, and WebKit blocks it.

## What changed

- A new root asset, `pdf-preview-worker.js`, creates and revokes the PDF Blob URL. The Gateway serves it with a no-network policy that allows framing only by the Control UI origin and configured remote embedders.
- `ChatPdfPreview` starts one worker per open preview, sends it the fetched bytes, and shows only the newest URL. If the worker fails or times out, the preview shows the existing unavailable state, which still offers a download.
- Static asset handling moves from `handleControlUiHttpRequest` into `respondControlUiStaticAsset`, so the worker response can set its own headers. Other assets keep their current headers.

## Scope

- The app document and service worker keep their current policies. Auth, the 16 MiB and 10 s fetch limits, and the byte comparison that detects a changed file stay the same.
- This PR does not change downloads or other attachment previews.

## Tradeoffs

- Adding `'self'` to the app's `frame-ancestors` rule would let same-origin pages frame the whole Control UI. This change keeps the app rule and applies the exception only to Blob documents that the worker creates.
- The preview copies bytes to the worker instead of transferring them, because it keeps them for the changed-file comparison. Each update makes one short-lived extra copy of up to 16 MiB.

## Blast Radius

All Control UI clients use the new path for PDF previews, and the Gateway serves one more public static asset. If the worker cannot start, the preview shows the same unavailable state as a failed fetch, which still offers a download. Behind remote ingress, worker responses use `private, no-store` because their framing policy depends on that ingress.

## Verification

- 91 focused UI and Gateway tests pass. UI typecheck, lint on touched UI and Gateway files, the UI build, and `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers` also pass.
- The compiled component renders a readable 14-page PDF in WKWebView with direct URL, file URL, and Blob sources. In Chromium it passes page zoom, URL renewal, changed bytes, offline, and fallback checks.
- Before/after screenshots of the actual component in WKWebView under the production CSP: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188050#issuecomment-6513634576
- Framing boundary through this PR's Gateway code, in WKWebView and Chrome: an approved embedder renders the PDF, and the unchanged app policy denies an unconfigured embedder. In WKWebView, the worker-created Blob also stays blank under an unconfigured ancestor. After the real ingress binding is closed, the worker request is rejected. Chrome does not enforce the inherited Blob policy, and it never did for the old app-created Blob either. Details and screenshots: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188050#issuecomment-6515181352
- CI on the first head found 8 type errors in the new HTTP test. A test-only commit fixes them without changing any assertion's meaning. The gateway test typecheck and the 10 HTTP tests now pass locally.
- CI on `5b3a637` has one failure: the Control UI end-to-end test `control-ui-e2e-readiness.e2e.test.ts:197` read `terminalActivationReady` as false. The same test passed on the previous head, whose UI, test harness and lockfile were identical, and it passes locally. It has not been matched to a failure on main.
- The client where the bug was first seen, full-app WebKit startup, and a deployed external relay remain unverified.

prs.title: fix(msteams): message search misses text in a different Unicode normalization form
prs.body:
Relates to gap finding: msteams-message-search-unicode-nfc (analysis, evidence level A)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: MS Teams message search misses messages whose text differs from the query only in Unicode normalization form (e.g. a message sent from a macOS/iOS Teams client cannot be found with the same accented text typed on Windows, and vice versa).

## User Impact

User impact: searching messages in an MS Teams chat or channel now matches text canonically — accents and other combining characters match regardless of whether the message or the query was composed in NFC or NFD form. No behavior change for exact matches.

## Why This Change Was Made

`searchMessagesMSTeams` lowercased both the query and the message text but never Unicode-normalized either side, and `String.prototype.includes` compares code points, so canonically-equivalent strings in different normalization forms never matched. Both sides are now normalized with `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(...).normalize("NFC")` before comparison, following the repo's existing NFC search convention (memory-core, memory-wiki, beam, x, discord plugins).

## Evidence

### Before fix

New regression tests fail on the base implementation (3 failed, 18 passed):

```
FAIL > searchMessagesMSTeams > matches message text across Unicode normalization forms
AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'msg-nfd' ]
FAIL > searchMessagesMSTeams > matches NFC message text from an NFD query
AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'msg-nfc' ]
FAIL > searchMessagesMSTeams > normalizes HTML-stripped content before matching
AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'msg-html' ]
```

Runtime check of the comparison: `"café".normalize("NFD").toLowerCase().includes("café".toLowerCase())` → `false` in both directions; NFC-normalizing both sides → `true`.

### After fix

`pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/graph-messages.read.test.ts` — 21/21 passed (18 pre-existing + 3 new Unicode normalization cases covering NFD content × NFC query, NFC content × NFD query, and HTML-stripped NFD content × NFC query).

- `oxlint` on changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `format:check` on changed files: clean
- Full-project typecheck could not run on this host (pinned native tsgo requires glibc ≥ 2.32; classic-tsc fallback OOMs) — covered by CI.

## What was not tested

- Live Graph API round trip against a real Teams tenant (unit-level proof only; the comparison change is local string preprocessing around the existing mocked-Graph test harness).
- Sender display-name matching (`matchesSearchSender`) is a separate, narrower exact-equality comparison and is intentionally left unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ui): match canonical Unicode in command palette catalog search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: catalog entries in the ⌘K command palette cannot be found when the stored name uses a different Unicode form than the query — for example a skill, plugin, agent, or model whose name or description was written on macOS in NFD (Hangul, Vietnamese, French, Spanish) never matches the NFC text a user types with an IME.

## User Impact

User impact: names and descriptions now match regardless of Unicode form, so agents, skills, plugins, automations, and models that previously disappeared from the palette are findable. Nothing changes for ASCII text, and the displayed labels keep their original bytes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`filterCommandPaletteItems` compared `label`, `description`, `searchText`, and `primaryModel` with `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty`, which lowercases but does not apply canonical equivalence, so `"café"` (NFC) and `"cafe\u0301"` (NFD) are different strings and the substring tests miss.

The same palette already normalizes the other half of its data: session titles go through `normalizeSessionSearchText` (`src/shared/session-search-text.ts`), whose comment says titles "share canonical Unicode … across Gateway selection and palette ranking", and `ui/src/components/multi-select.tsx` compares with `text?.toLowerCase().normalize("NFC").includes(search)`. Catalog items were the remaining site, and their text is the least controlled in the app: agent `identity.name`, automation `displayName`, `SKILL.md` frontmatter descriptions, plugin manifest name/description, and model display names all come from user-authored files.

The fix adds one local `normalizePaletteMatchText` (lowercase + `.normalize("NFC")`) and applies it to the query and to the four compared fields, so ranking stays exact-match 3 / prefix 2 / substring 1. Labels are still returned unmodified for rendering; only the comparison copies are normalized.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(feishu): acknowledge followups during active work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Feishu/Lark `/followup` waiting behind an active reply before admitting the message and acknowledging its queue acceptance.

## User Impact

Authorized followups can reach the existing queue while work remains active, with the runtime reporting the actual outcome. They retain the submitting sender and existing queue ordering; broadcast observers cannot execute the command.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu supplied normalized command text and authorization but omitted typed command-turn facts. Core dispatch therefore could not recognize an explicit queue command before waiting for turn ownership. Supply those facts through the existing SDK context builder and clear them for broadcast observers, whose authorization remains explicitly false.

Queue policy, barriers, custody, storage, configuration, and defaults are unchanged. To respect the existing line-cap ratchet, move the unchanged supplemental-context visibility helper into Feishu’s policy module and relocate the existing DM command table into a small sibling using the existing test harness. The policy module uses the narrow SDK visibility import.

## Evidence

- **Baseline live reproduction:** genuine human Lark DM ingress and a real public OpenAI model through an isolated Gateway on AWS. While a completed real provider response was held, native `/followup` produced no pending queue entry or runtime notice. Releasing the source allowed a separate followup execution and one exclusive file effect. This demonstrates delayed admission/acknowledgment, not lost work. A `successor-barrier` diagnostic label is not treated as proof of causation.
- **Candidate live proof remains pending:** the candidate Gateway builds, connects, and passes channel preflight, but CUA currently cannot access the human Lark window (`cgWindowNotFound`; no app windows). No candidate human messages have been sent. The idle proof Gateway was stopped. Do not treat helper tests or credential preflight as a completed live replay.
- The command metadata regressions fail on the base for missing `CommandTurn`; the corrected broadcast fixture reaches real command authorization and dispatch. Seven selected files passed, **117 tests**, including command authorization, routing, bot threads, card actions, broadcast custody, and policy. Final command/broadcast/bot reruns passed **4/10/60** tests.
- Focused production and test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, docs lint, commit guards, the exact 45-line test allocation ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass. `pnpm build` passes for candidate `072cadcea7bffbbdecca0061c43cfe842bd76d7c`; all **61,191 tracked source files** match the proof host byte for byte with a clean checkout.
- Feishu cold-import profile completed successfully: **113.2 MiB peak RSS**, **0.389 CPU seconds**; isolated baseline process **46.5 MiB**. This is an import snapshot, not a before/after performance benchmark.
- **Local ClawSweeper:** full committed-range review, base `06cd3e0f306be1bdd0ae2efe5a3fbe2188169bb9` → head `072cadcea7bffbbdecca0061c43cfe842bd76d7c`, complete, no code findings. Earlier confirmed type findings were repaired. The final review’s outstanding request is shipped-path acknowledgment proof, recorded above as pending.

<details>
<summary>Test costs and LoC churn</summary>

Measured on the same AWS proof host, Node 24.22.1, repository test wrapper, one worker:

| Scope | Wall time |
| --- | ---: |
| Seven selected files, 117 tests | 53.15 s |
| Final command file, 4 cases | 49.38 s |
| Final broadcast file, 10 cases | 18.45 s |
| Final bot file, 60 cases | 68.45 s |

Cold worker generation dominates the cold file runs; the four command cases collectively take under one second. Broad PR CI is skipped while this PR is a draft; CI test costs are not yet available. The exact **45 net regression-test lines** receive a separate allocation for early command classification and observer denial; the shared scalar stays unchanged. Two existing DM cases are moved and extended, rather than duplicated.

Against pinned base `06cd3e0f306b`:

| Category | Added | Deleted | Churn |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Production | 52 | 42 | 94 |
| Tests/support | 70 | 25 | 95 |
| Documentation | 8 | 5 | 13 |
| Test allocation | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| **Total** | **132** | **72** | **204** |

The production delta includes moving the existing visibility helper; there is no new queue owner, state, or admission framework.

</details>

prs.title: feat: allow scoped operators to manage their automations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators with write access cannot ask an agent to create and manage their own automations without Gateway administrator authority.

## User Impact

Adds `operator.cron` for authenticated agent-turn automation access, implied by `operator.write`. Users can schedule and manage jobs within the existing conversation/account ownership boundary without receiving `operator.admin`. Cron-only access does not grant chat, general write, or global scheduler administration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing requester grant and job ownership checks instead of treating every scheduler caller as an administrator. One runtime-method mapping covers creation, job management, history, and scratch access. Scheduled runs preserve the initiating operator scopes. Direct/global scheduler APIs, privileged binding, live revocation, and tool restrictions retain their existing checks.

Signed requester transports preserve private scoped-creation provenance without promoting it to local-owner or management authority. No new state owner or storage schema is introduced. The config baseline is regenerated for the accepted scope.

## Evidence

- Red/green regressions for scoped creation and signed requester grants. Both `operator.cron` and `operator.write` pass real token mint/verification, production in-process dispatch, owned-job persistence, foreign-conversation/account refusal, and revocation during validation before persistence. Refused mutations leave storage unchanged; no local-owner or management authority is added.
- Reproduced the five stale CI consumer assertions and updated ingress/rejected-manager expectations without weakening their security checks. All 205 consumer tests and 9 transport tests pass. Scope implication, config, scheduled-scope preservation, grant/token, and prompt-stability suites also pass.
- Core/source-test typechecks, focused lint/format, config checks, line-cap/test-line ratchets, and diff checks pass. Main `f0586d2e3e0d73c` was integrated only for a generated-config conflict; affected checks were rerun.
- Fresh local independent P0–P2 reviews of the implementation and the consumer/signed-effect repair found no actionable issues. The unchanged signed-token implementation was unavailable to the implementation reviewer; its changed regression tests and grant owner were reviewed.
- Prior CI's Android job failed at emulator setup (`adb: unable to connect for root: closed`), before Android tests ran. It is separate from the repaired consumer failures. New-head CI and ClawSweeper re-review are pending.
- Gap: no live-provider Gateway turn or full WebSocket signed-request test was run. Proof uses production admission, dispatch, and Cron storage with mocked model execution.

<details>
<summary>Validation cost and change size</summary>

All changed test files were exercised with `--maxWorkers=1`; wall times include compilation/setup:

| Suite | Wall time |
| --- | ---: |
| Creator authority context | 38.20s |
| Gateway auth config | 6.03s |
| Scheduled operator continuation | 75.80s |
| Signed runtime identity | 7.03s |
| Fresh operator admission | 9.52s |
| Gateway Cron policy | 18.75s |
| Scope implication | 1.07s |
| Chat, requester authority, authenticated connection consumers | 53.37s combined |
| Signed/embedded/CLI creator transports | 53.20s |
| Authenticated connection consumer after assertion simplification | 24.17s |

Transport execution itself takes about 14s; most wall time is compilation. The existing scheduled-continuation suite exercises real persistence/restoration and authority lifecycle, which helper-only tests cannot prove. Exact-head CI timings will be added when its run completes.

Production delta against integrated main: +63/-24 lines. Tests: +355/-71 lines. The separate 284-line allocation covers distinct admission, signed final-effect, and continuation-scope regressions. No shared test scalar was raised.

</details>

Requested by @VACInc.

## Work sessions

prs.title: fix(ui): completed turns scatter work across many Worked disclosures
prs.body:
Related: #183267

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: completed dashboard turns scatter their work across many **Worked** disclosures, leave work recorded after the answer hanging below it, and split tool-result images out of their tool group, since #183267 changed the completed-turn presentation.

## User Impact

User impact: a completed dashboard turn again shows one **Worked for X** disclosure above the answer, holding the preamble, commentary, reasoning and tool activity in their original order. Work recorded after the answer sits above it, tool-result images stay with the tool that produced them, and speech bubble view keeps its single activity disclosure instead of wrapping it in a second **Worked** row. The stored transcript stays intact; existing live-turn, search and handoff boundaries are retained.

## Why This Change Was Made

#183267 by @Marvinthebored replaced the single completed-turn rollup with per-envelope splitting (`chat-work-chunks.ts`), so narration became visible between one **Worked** disclosure per work stretch. The single rollup was a deliberate design by @vyctorbrzezowski, and replaying real transcripts (Anthropic, OpenAI, Codex and agent API runs) at `ad55c5e`, `e7f0546` and current main showed the split presentation also introduced regressions, listed below.

This is a forward change that restores the earlier presentation in the files #183267 changed, rather than a revert commit. It removes the splitting module, its tool-card envelope bookkeeping, the split-fragment action/footer/terminal-status fields and the per-stretch timing, and restores the rollup's session timing and the earlier test expectations (including the three e2e expectations later adapted in `8c05667`). Later unrelated main work is kept: #186323, the published-PR handoff split (`4d50f6c`), grouped work without failed counts (`210b364`), cached row display facts (#186512), the video widget lazy-import wait, and the empty-group guard from #186499 for provider voice groups. The `presentationOwnsFooter` clauses from #186499 and #186681 go away with the fields they guarded. The test-line scalar returns the 2,089 lines #183267 added.

<details>
<summary>Regressions observed on main that this restores</summary>

1. Empty **Worked** rows before answers that carry (empty) OpenAI reasoning.
2. With **Show thinking**, inline reasoning moved into a collapsed **Worked**.
3. With tool calls hidden, stacks of empty **Worked** disclosures.
4. Work recorded after the answer rendered between the answer and its footer.
5. Speech bubble view wrapped the activity summary in **Worked**: two clicks, summary hidden.
6. Turn duration lost after switching sessions in one pane.
7. Per-stretch browser previews showed stale or duplicate tab previews.
8. Live turns split and regrouped.
9. A pre-handoff receipt became its own reply with a second header and footer.
10. Reply jumps expanded unrelated disclosures, because fragments shared persisted IDs.
11. Duplicate narration previously hidden in the rollup became visible.
12. `collapseCompletedTurnWork` ran 5–10x slower.
13. Narration containing Markdown characters disabled splitting, so that envelope's narration merged while plain narration split, out of order with its tool calls.
14. Tool-result images (for example `view_image` frames) split out of their tool group into standalone assistant rows.

</details>

## Evidence

Screenshots: real Control UI against the mock Gateway with synthetic data, 1100 px, light theme. Before is current main (`589348d`), after is this branch.

**Flat completed turn with narration between tool calls and a test run after the answer**

Before:

![Flat completed turn on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02af3fbf-bbdb-468f-8de6-7bdebb3f5e27)

After (collapsed):

![Flat completed turn with this branch, collapsed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94c3132e-d59b-4602-b58a-3a6109231075)

After (expanded):

![Flat completed turn with this branch, expanded](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/398fe288-42b6-475d-a6f4-4409eb6a7904)

**Speech bubble view, same turn**

Before:

![Speech bubble view on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/95e8384c-27cf-4f4c-a46e-d24d45dcb1aa)

After:

![Speech bubble view with this branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef8aebc4-b832-4b85-9c4d-021ea82a8ab7)

**`view_image` tool result with two frames**

Before:

![view_image turn on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e158c7c-d514-4064-9b4c-2e39d5cd8045)

After:

![view_image turn with this branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb176141-56d9-4c97-acc7-63d5603defc0)

Tests:

- New regressions in `chat-thread-grouping.test.ts` (Markdown and plain narration stay in one ordered rollup, tool-result images stay in their tool group, post-answer work moves above the answer, bubble mode gets no rollup) fail on main's presentation code and pass here (4/4 red on `589348d`, green on this branch).
- `chat-bubble-activity.e2e` now asserts no `.chat-work-group` in bubble view and one activity disclosure that opens the tool summary in a single click.
- `vitest.ui` over `ui/src/pages/chat` and `ui/src/lib/chat`: 629 files passed.
- Mock-Gateway e2e over every `ui/src/e2e/chat-*` suite: 1046 tests passed. The 17 `*.real-gateway` suites failed at setup in this shared worktree (Gateway entrypoint/plugin build not prepared; no assertion ran) and are not passing live-Gateway evidence. The original PR CI also skipped its real-Gateway lane. `chat-loading-geometry` hit a transient artifact lock and passes on rerun. `chat-stream-runtime-budgets` (delta-burst commits) and `chat-outbox-migration` (v3 Blob migration) fail identically on current main `589348d` in a side-by-side rerun, so they are not caused by this change.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files, and `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --staged`: pass.
- Local autoreview (branch mode, base `589348d`, P1): no actionable findings.

## Review repairs and current validation

Independent review and the subsequent full CI identified these additional cases in the proposed rollup, now fixed:

- A terminal error or aborted tool envelope recorded after an answer stays visible, outside completed work.
- A freshly opened pane restores elapsed time only when its loaded completed reply matches the session metadata. Cached projections retain that timing, and switching session, agent or Gateway cannot borrow another turn's recap.
- A completed assistant answer containing both text and tools retains assistant ownership, visible text and reply/copy actions. Ordinary assistant messages reuse their prepared display text instead of sanitizing it again.
- Legacy mixed forwarded narration retains its tool grouping and sender-owned file links. An explicitly completed forwarded answer (`final_answer` or `stop`) keeps its visible answer and actions.

The existing presentation, recap and message owners implement these repairs; no additional state owner or compatibility path was introduced. Focused regressions fail on the uncorrected PR head and pass with the repairs. The terminal error/abort cases were relocated into the existing grouping suite to reuse its history assertions and keep the thread test file within its line cap.

Focused repair validation: 283 tests passed across the chat owners and progress suite. The latest grouping and action refinements passed 205 affected tests across seven suites, plus UI and UI-test typechecks and targeted lint/format checks. Both CI failures reproduced locally before repair. Explicit forwarded-answer cases also fail on the original PR grouping and pass with the final implementation. After the test-only relocation, both terminal cases were again confirmed red on the uncorrected presentation and green with the fix (1.22 seconds wrapper wall time for the green run). Line-cap and test-line ratchets pass without raising their baselines (6,280,129 test lines against a 6,326,480 ceiling). Fresh independent reviews of the initial repairs and the final CI repair delta returned no actionable P0–P2 findings. [Full PR CI run 41003470362](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41003470362) passed on head `12eef1abf280e31b008795e8c90eb16e9d1c1362`. Its tested merge `9ddca045716bc844e7084eec72314375cdb863a8` includes #186061; the merged source preserves per-message timestamps, Reply controls, hover/touch behavior, and main's grouped-message CSS.

## Risk and coverage

This changes how completed-turn content is grouped, so failure visibility, reply actions, run ownership and cached timing are the main regression risks. The focused tests exercise those boundaries. The screenshots above use the real Control UI with a mock Gateway and synthetic messages; they are not live-Gateway proof. Earlier broad test results above describe the original implementation and are not relabeled as runs on the repair commit. No successful real-Gateway run is claimed.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/12ea2c59-6f3e-4ee0-829f-0d9e0139ae32)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1448ca0c-94ab-481f-a6c5-d2e282f74aa2)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(zalouser): match canonically equivalent names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `channels.zalouser.allowFrom: ["Nguyễn Văn A"]` while Zalo reports that friend's `displayName` in decomposed Unicode form (NFD) leaves the sender unresolved: startup logs `zalouser users unresolved: Nguyễn Văn A`, and the DM is rejected even though the name is exactly what the operator sees in the Zalo app.

- Problem: every Zalo name comparison lowercased but never normalized, so NFC and NFD spellings of the same name produced different keys. The startup allowlist resolver (`allowFrom`, `groupAllowFrom`, `groups` keys), the `friends`/`groups` lookups, and group-name resolution all missed.
- Solution: name matching now compares canonical keys. `extensions/zalouser/src/directory-index.ts` owns `normalizeZaloNameKey` (trim + lowercase + NFC), and the five comparison sites use it.
- What changed: `directory-index.ts` (new key owner, index build), `zalo-js.ts` (`resolveZaloEntries`, `listZaloFriendsMatching`, `listZaloGroupsMatching`), `monitor.ts` (startup name-resolution lookups), `channel.ts` (group name selection).
- What did NOT change: original spellings still flow to logs, prompts and outbound text untouched; numeric `userId`/`groupId` comparisons keep the lowercase-only helper; no config schema, manifest or API change.

## Why This Change Was Made

One owner decides what "same Zalo name" means, and every comparison asks it. Keeping the key inline at each site would have left five copies of the same convention in three files, which is how the gap appeared in the first place.

Alternatives considered and rejected:

- Inline `.normalize("NFC")` at each call site: smaller diff, five duplicated key definitions.
- Normalizing on ingest (rewriting `displayName` when it arrives): would silently change the spellings surfaced to users, logs and captured messages, far beyond matching.
- A shared `plugin-sdk` canonical helper: no such owner exists today; the rest of the tree keeps this per-channel (feishu, discord, matrix, mattermost normalize inline), and this fix follows that precedent.

Boundaries:

- `group-policy.ts` matches operator-authored config group keys/substrings exactly; that is a different contract from account name matching and stays as is.
- Numeric ids are compared with the existing `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty`; only names get the NFC key.
- Production delta is +3 lines: the key function plus the comment that records why it exists (−4 lines at the call sites it replaces).

Provenance: the four comparison sites never normalized; no upstream helper was lost. Same family as #187953 (buzz/whatsapp/msteams), #188003 and #187988 — all merged per-channel fixes for lowercase-without-NFC matching.

Risk:

- The key now applies NFC to the "name contains" branches of the lookups, so composed and decomposed sequences match there too. Only matching widens; returned rows and their spellings are unchanged.
- Untested risk: no live Zalo account was exercised, and only extension-scoped type checks ran locally (see Evidence).

## User Impact

Operators whose allowlists, group config keys or lookups use a diacritic-bearing Vietnamese (or other composed/decomposed) name now reach the person they meant, regardless of which Unicode form their device or the Zalo server stored. Before this change the failure was silent: the startup resolver logged `unresolved`, the DM was rejected, and `friends`/`groups` queries came back empty with no error.

Users who already match exactly keep identical behavior, because the canonical key preserves every currently-failing-to-match distinction except the composed/decomposed one.

## Evidence

### Live runtime proof

Throwaway script (not committed) that drives the real `listZaloFriendsMatching`, `listZaloGroupsMatching` and `resolveZaloAllowFromEntries` through a synthetic session, with the stored friend/group name in NFD and the query in NFC:

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .proof-272.mjs
name forms:
  nfc: "Nguyễn Văn A" U+004E U+0067 U+0075 U+0079 U+1EC5 U+006E
  nfd: "Nguyễn Văn A" U+004E U+0067 U+0075 U+0079 U+0065 U+0302 U+0303 U+006E
old key (lowercase only) equal: false
new key (lowercase + NFC) equal: true
listZaloFriendsMatching(profile, NFC query) against NFD stored name -> [ '123' ]
listZaloGroupsMatching(profile, NFC query) against NFD stored name -> [ '998877' ]
resolveZaloAllowFromEntries -> [{"input":"Nguyễn Văn A","resolved":true,"id":"123"},{"input":"Không Tồn Tại","resolved":false}]
```

### Behavior matrix

```text
input form                => pre-fix result                        => post-fix result
NFC query, NFD friend     => [] (allowFrom resolves false)         => ["123"]
NFD query, NFC friend     => []                                    => ["123"]
NFC query, NFD group      => []                                    => ["998877"]
NFD query, NFC group      => []                                    => ["998877"]
startup allowFrom (NFC)   => "zalouser users unresolved: ..."      => "zalouser users resolved: ...->123"
group name key (NFC)      => no resolved group mapping             => "zalouser groups resolved: ...→g-trusted"
```

### Pre-fix failures on the base commit (tests kept, sources reverted)

```console
FAIL extensions/zalouser/src/zalo-js.matching.test.ts > matches a friend stored as nfd against the opposite query form
AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ '123' ]
FAIL extensions/zalouser/src/zalo-js.matching.test.ts > resolves an allowFrom entry against a friend stored as nfd
-     "id": "123",
-     "resolved": true,
+     "resolved": false,
FAIL extensions/zalouser/src/monitor.group-gating.test.ts > resolves canonically equivalent startup names to ids
expected 'zalouser users unresolved: Nguyễn Văn…' to contain 'zalouser users resolved: Nguyễn Văn A…'
FAIL extensions/zalouser/src/channel.test.ts > picks the canonically equal group name over an earlier prefix match
resolved id was "g-other" (prefix match) instead of "g-target" (canonical match)
```

### Post-fix suites

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalouser/src/zalo-js.matching.test.ts extensions/zalouser/src/monitor.group-gating.test.ts extensions/zalouser/src/channel.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  22 passed (22)
Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  33 passed (33)
```

Checks: `oxlint` 0 errors on the 8 changed files, `oxfmt --check` clean, extension type configs (`tsconfig.extensions.json`, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`) report no `zalouser` diagnostics (a deliberately broken probe file was used to confirm the checker was really compiling these files), and `check:test-lines-ratchet` passes with 45,928 lines of slack.

### Overlap check (same day snapshot)

Open zalouser PRs touching the same files were checked one by one against this change; all are disjoint in intent and hunks: #185267 (`zalo-js.ts` command parsing), #159253 (`monitor.ts` attachment links), #101441 (`monitor.ts` outbound traces), #122079 (`channel.ts` QR login setup, touches the same files at unrelated regions), plus #119552 and #165532 (other zalouser areas, no overlap found). No open PR or issue proposes a canonical name key for zalouser, and `origin/main` still has the lowercase-only comparisons.

### What was not tested

- No live Zalo login: the tests and the runtime proof inject a synthetic session rather than a real account, because CI has no Zalo credentials.
- Core-wide type checking was not run locally; only the extension scoped configs. CI covers the broad run.
- `group-policy.ts` config-key matching is intentionally out of scope and unchanged.
