prs.title: fix(codex): match canonical Unicode in codex CLI session search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Searching the Codex CLI session history fails when the stored session text and the typed query use different Unicode normalization forms:

- A Codex history entry contains `Cafe\u0301 backlog notes` (NFD) and the user searches `CAFÉ` (`É` = U+00C9, NFC). The session is omitted even though it is right there.

Both sides are user-writable Unicode text, so the mismatch is user-visible: the session exists, the query is correct, and the search silently returns nothing. Same class as #187953/#187148/#187881/#187199 (already merged for the channel directory-search family), now applied to the Codex CLI session list surface.

- Problem: case-insensitive substring search compares raw code units, so canonically equivalent text (NFC vs NFD) does not match.
- Solution: normalize the query and each candidate session value to NFC at comparison time, after lowercasing/trimming. Sessions keep their original message text.
- What changed: `extensions/codex/src/node-cli-sessions.ts` (`listLocalCodexCliSessions` search) plus one regression test.
- What did NOT change: session ids, cwd, lastMessage text, limits, ordering, and non-search behavior. Search remains case-insensitive substring matching.

## Why This Change Was Made

NFC normalization happens at the comparison boundary only, in the shape the rest of the family already merged with: `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(value).normalize("NFC")` on both the query and each candidate (reusing the existing helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/string-coerce-runtime`).

- Best fix: normalize per comparison; no normalized copies are cached or stored, so there is no new invalidation surface.
- Alternative rejected: normalizing at write time (history ingestion) would rewrite user text and not repair already-stored decomposed input.
- Risk: `normalize("NFC")` is a no-op for ASCII and already-composed text. The only behavioral change is that canonically equivalent queries now match.

## User Impact

Codex CLI session search returns the same results whichever normalization form the client produced, and displayed session text stays exactly as stored.

## Evidence

### Regression (bidirectional)

The new test stores one history entry whose text is NFD (`Cafe\u0301 backlog notes`) and filters with composed NFC (`CAFÉ` = `CAF\u00c9`).

Pre-fix (source reverted, test kept):

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/node-cli-sessions.test.ts
 × matches canonically equivalent filters over stored session text
   - [
   -   {
   -     "lastMessage": "Cafe\u0301 backlog notes",
   -     "sessionId": "...",
   -   },
   - ]
   + []
```

Post-fix:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/node-cli-sessions.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  23 passed (23)
```

### Shipped entry point

The changed search is exposed through the node host command `codex.cli.sessions.list` (`extensions/codex/src/node-cli-sessions.ts:46`, registered via `createCodexCliSessionNodeHostCommands` in `extensions/codex/src/index.ts`), driven by `openclaw node run` + `openclaw nodes invoke --command codex.cli.sessions.list`. A live node-host proof on the shipped CLI (real node process + paired gateway + `nodes invoke` with cross-form stored session text) is being prepared for the next revision.

### Targeted lint

```console
$ node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/codex/src/node-cli-sessions.ts extensions/codex/src/node-cli-sessions.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

`tsgo` itself cannot run in this container (`tsrs` requires GLIBC 2.29+). The touched file only adds `normalize("NFC")` calls to strings already normalized/lowercased via the existing helper, so no type surface changes; CI runs `pnpm tsgo:extensions`.

### Open PR collision check

No open PR touches `extensions/codex/src/node-cli-sessions.ts` for this class.

### What was not tested

No live Codex CLI round-trip yet (node-host shipped proof in progress); the regression above proves the comparison boundary on the real `listLocalCodexCliSessions` function. Client-specific normalization quirks on Windows/macOS are out of scope: the fix compares whatever arrives after NFC normalization.

prs.title: fix(cron): failure repair turns can read and fix the job they repair
prs.body:
Related: #161007, #180304, #187346

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an automation's failure repair turn cannot read or change the job it was asked to repair, so it asks the user to fix it instead.

## User Impact

User impact: when an owned automation fails, the repair turn in its owner conversation can now read the job's runs and update the job when the job's requester is still an owner, so most repairs no longer need a human reply. Scheduler notices about a job follow the same rule.

Risk to note: a job whose requester is not an owner (or whose stored operator source can no longer be restored) now gets read-only automation access in its repair and notice turns, and no session-owner fallback. Jobs that record no requester keep the session owner's current access, as other system turns do since #187346.

## Why This Change Was Made

System-started turns got their authority from what kind of turn they were: a label match for notices (#180304), a caller rule for completions (#187346, which left cron out), and nothing for repairs, which went through the public `agent` RPC. Any client can send the repair's provenance label on that RPC, so it could never carry authority.

Now:
- A scheduler turn about a job acts for the job's recorded requester, the same requester and owner check its scheduled runs use (channel sender, profile, or restored operator source). Owner status is rechecked before each owner-only effect.
- Repairs run on the host session-event path, like notices and completions.
- Every host system turn gets one rule for caller-scoped automation reads; the `sourceTool === "cron"` match is gone.

## Evidence

Production repair transcripts (read-only, one Gateway, since the repair feature shipped): 57 repair turns, 3 fixed their job, 28 asked the user. No repair turn ever completed an `automations` call: before 2026-10-19 the tool was absent, then a schema check failed, and since 2026-10-22 all 18 calls were refused by the owner gate. All 3 script-payload repairs were refused.

New boundary test `src/gateway/server-cron-failure-repair.authority.test.ts` runs the real repair dispatcher, real session-event admission, and the turn's real tool surface (model synthetic):
- owner requester: `senderIsOwner` true; `get` and `update` pass the owner gate.
- non-owner requester: `senderIsOwner` false; `update` gated.
- On the base commit this file fails (the repair cannot dispatch outside the old lifecycle path).

Gateway cron suite (`server.cron.test.ts`): the owner-topic repair and NO_REPLY repair cases now drive the real reply runtime; they check the owner topic's session and thread route, repair pending through retries until the turn settles (success and error), one escalation, and that a forged public `cron_failure_repair` label still gets no silence.

Focused runs (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, wall time):

| File | Tests | Time |
|---|---|---|
| `src/gateway/server-cron-failure-repair.authority.test.ts` (new) | 2 | 32 s |
| `src/agents/agent-tools.turn-authority.test.ts` | 14 | 2 s |
| `src/gateway/server.cron.test.ts` | 15 | 31 s |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-permissions.test.ts` | 27 | 37 s |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-context.test.ts` | 1 | 6 s |
| `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.automation-repair.test.ts` | 1 | 8 s |

The new test adds about 4 s of test time (two cases). `server.cron.test.ts` stays at its prior cost. `oxfmt`, type-aware `oxlint` on changed files and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass. Full CI is pending.

Gaps:
- Operator-source and profile requesters share the scheduled-run owner checks but have no dedicated repair test; the channel requester is the tested path.
- The managed tool host used by `openEventToolHost` does not pass `inputProvenance` into tool construction, so the test cannot show caller-scoped reads for the non-owner case there (the embedded attempt path does pass it). Follow-up.
- Live proof needs a deploy; the next real failing job on a production Gateway will show it.

prs.title: fix(agents): hand delegated failures back to their parent
prs.body:
## Summary
- Return failed subagents' cause and saved progress to their owning parent without waiting on the failed root's descendants.
- Quiet inherited error attention only after durable input/result custody, while preserving child diagnostics, collector ownership and genuine native human questions.
- Keep failure diagnostics in the committed handoff, preserve ready unconsumed failed-collector findings, and count handed-off failures correctly.
- Acknowledge failure custody only for children represented in the committed input. A bounded batch keeps omitted failures unacknowledged and recoverable.
- Bind private settle retries to the findings they replay: a retry that reuses the retained message acknowledges only failed runs whose diagnostics are in those exact bytes and that are still in the current cohort. A legacy retained message without that record adds no acknowledgement, and a new run generation under the same ID does not inherit it.
- Keep the 160,000-character findings budget, with its truncation markers, per-result floors, stable order and overflow summary.
- Keep the receipt in cold reads: the compact SQL session-list projection now selects the four `failureHandoff` fields, including the `parentCompletion` mirror. No schema, writer, codec, migration or retention change.
- Leave ordinary session rows unchanged on the wire: `failureHandedOff` is sent only when true.

## Delivery contracts
- Settle (`subagent_settle`): the complete bounded cohort message, including healthy children's findings, is stored as the hidden replay input, exactly as on `main`. An earlier revision of this PR dropped those findings; that regression is fixed, and the existing settle and replay tests pass unchanged.
- Direct completion (`subagent_announce`): a healthy child's result stays in runtime context only; a failed child's diagnostics are saved with the handoff.
- Collector: results remain an ordinary durable tool result.

## Integration with `main`
- This branch merges `main` at `315380c` (#188047) with no conflicts and no manual edits.
- The PR's diff against `main` is unchanged: 88 files, +3587/−253. 82 changed files are byte-identical to the pre-merge branch; the other 6 differ only by changes already on `main`. Every added and removed line of this PR is unchanged.

## Verification
- Independent shipping verification of the merged source (`43ddaef`): PASS with notes.
  - 110 distinct native tests of the coupled paths pass, including 24 private cold-read cases.
  - One freshly built Gateway and Control UI (build `2026.10.9-43ddaef1f7a6-2026-10-30T04-25-21.835Z`) passes the default, parent-target, yielded and collector modes, covering suggested choices, free text, reload, recovery and final delivery. The runtime entry and served assets were verified in every mode.
  - Two independent behavioral mutations fail as expected: one causes six omitted-tail false acknowledgements, the other one false acknowledgement across a run generation. The restored code passes all 46 affected tests.
  - Screenshots were inspected locally; none are attached.
- Independent review of the `main` integration (`43ddaef`): PASS with notes. It found no integration defect and no new feature material; the six overlaps with `main` compose cleanly. This is a scoped source check, not whole-PR approval.
- Private-retry fix (`a296cbe..801b1a4` only): independent canonical local P0–P2 review, eight passes, scoped-clean with zero findings. It covers that range, not the whole PR.
- Review of `f27f807..a296cbe` (36 passes): incomplete. One pass lacked required context, and one pass found a P2 in private settle retries, since fixed in `801b1a4`. The incomplete status stands; no clean result is claimed for that range.
- Baseline review (source `4599951`): independent canonical P0–P2 API review, eight planned passes, scoped-clean. Historical evidence for that source only.
- CI on earlier published heads found missing mocks, test inventory gaps, an unconditional wire field, unbounded findings, a lint miss and the dropped settle findings. All are repaired in the committed source; those failed runs remain history.
- Pending, not approval: a fresh whole-PR hosted review of the current head, and passing CI.

## CI and `main` prerequisites
- Current head: `checks-ui-e2e (2/7)` fails one of 521 tests. `ui/src/e2e/chat-stream-runtime-budgets.e2e.test.ts` ("commits a streamed delta burst in frame-bound transcript batches") observed 3 native commits where 0 were expected. It passed on the previous head, which does not show it is flaky. Linux reproduction and comparison with `main` are in progress; it is not attributed to `main` or waived.
- Restart-intent tests: an independent run reproduced the six failures before #188047 and saw all 15 tests pass on `315380c`. #188047 is part of this branch through the merge.
- #187979 (publication handoff test), #187933 (shell skip-link checks) and #188056 (project-notice test) are merged on `main` and included through the same merge; none is copied as a separate patch.
- The required `openclaw/ci-gate` check is not waived.

## Limits
- Runtime proof uses a scripted local model on macOS arm64/headless Chromium, not Linux or hosted-model compliance. Active-steering failure timing was not separately exercised. No latest-stable upgrade, restart or PostgreSQL run is claimed.
- No live Odin update, restart or deployment. CI and landing remain separate gates.

prs.title: fix: stop model fallback when session capability metadata changes
prs.body:
Closes #179290

## What problem this solves

A session capability metadata change can send a turn through configured fallback models even though no model caused the local coordination failure. The user sees misleading fallback transitions, and every candidate can fail before contacting a provider.

## Fix

The capability reader gives all three existing invalidation throws a stable error identity. The existing fallback classifier recognizes it as a coordination failure and surfaces the local error without advancing models. The original invalidation checks, causes, and authority boundaries are unchanged. This does not repair completion announces or retry stale preparation from #179289.

The contributor's implementation and regression are retained. Current main was merged because the affected owner migrated to AsyncContext; conflict resolution keeps that owner and the contributor's error class. The existing model-failover documentation now explains coordination stops.

## Evidence

Exact head: `10485be19b6ac747ea3708a03a16f41a3e1f32a3`.

[Maintainer built-Gateway red/green captures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179312#issuecomment-6514996055):

- Current main twice advances through all three models after real retained capability invalidation; each run emits two Gateway fallback transitions and makes zero provider requests.
- Candidate twice stops at the primary, surfaces the local failure, emits no fallback transition, and makes zero provider requests.
- Both no-error controls complete through the primary and one captured local Responses-provider request.
- The trigger is a successful public `sessions.patch` changing execution-host metadata while a scheduling barrier holds real in-attempt retained preparation. The production reader throws the error; no helper, exception, predicate result, or fallback result is mocked.
- Both builds, focused Oxfmt/Oxlint, and the one-file MDX check passed. Local tests: **0** (assignment ceiling); broad checks belong to exact-head hosted CI.

The contributor's earlier retained-store/fallback-runner regression and reported focused test results remain supporting evidence, separate from the maintainer Gateway proof. The earlier restart-tombstone CI failure belongs to the old head; current-head CI is evaluated independently, without rerunning that suite locally.

## Scope and simplification

The complete diff reuses the existing invalidation producer and coordination classifier, without new policy state, retries, recovery layers, or permission changes. Production +20/-3, tests +13/-0, documentation +4/-0 against the current-main merge base. The regression protects the actual invalidation/fallback boundary and is retained.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the previous classification; there is no migration, persisted format, or public API change. Blast radius is model-candidate selection after local session capability invalidation. Provider-error fallback remains unchanged.

prs.title: fix(feishu): accept the documented markdown table mode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes gateway startup rejecting Feishu's documented `markdown.tables` option and applies the selected table mode across sends, replies, presentations, and previews.

## User Impact

Channel and account table settings are accepted, including the delivering/default account. Ordinary `off` table messages settle as authored rich-text posts. In `off`, presentations keep controls and show literal rows in card text and live previews. When idle close reuses a posted answer, missing reasoning follows it without duplicating it.

Accepted-prefix failures keep their receipts and do not replay accepted content. The unchanged post renderer still draws authored Markdown tables as grids.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's strict schema gains the shared table option and keeps the legacy `markdown.mode` and `markdown.tableMode`. Formatting-aware delivery converts whole logical tables before chunking. Presentations and reasoning degrade undrawable block-mode tables to readable lists. For `off`, display-only delimiter escaping leaves authored fallback and deduplication text alone. The PR also declares `block` as Feishu's table default (see Table default).

The generated channel baseline gains two entries, `channels.feishu.markdown.tables` and `channels.feishu.accounts.*.markdown.tables`. Core and plugin counts stay unchanged. [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f659a3576b1/AGENTS.md#L96) permits narrow source-verified exceptions with a reason. This exception is not maintainer approval.

## Evidence

### Upgrade proof

Published stable `2026.10.2` (`b8952d477f0c`) seeded channel `markdown.mode: native` and `markdown.tableMode: ascii`, an account's `mode: escape` and `tableMode: simple`, and two accounts without Markdown settings. The proof head (`effbf8c7a8ab`) used that state, main (`29fc232d40be`) a copy. Both used fresh detached worktrees and separately packed Feishu plugins.

| Check | Stable | Proof head | Upstream main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Legacy config validates, keys and overrides read back unchanged | Yes | Yes, before and after migration | Yes, before and after migration |
| Feishu config object on disk | Seed | Byte-identical | Byte-identical |
| Stored session loads with the same key and ID, and a label update survives restart | Created and patched here | Yes | Yes |
| Documented `markdown.tables` at channel and account scope | Rejected, exit 1 | Accepted, all four values | Rejected, exit 1 |
| Account override wins, unset accounts inherit the channel value | Key rejected | Yes | Key rejected |

Both builds refuse the schema 24 agent database (Gateway exit 78) until `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates it to 26. Repair and shutdown then exit 1 with `ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE`. The cause is undiagnosed and both databases stay readable. This is compatibility evidence, not a clean upgrade. Replacement was manual, not the published updater. Credentials were synthetic and Feishu accounts and transports disabled. Only the Feishu config object is byte-identical. Maintenance changed other config. The diff has no `src/state` change or database migration.

### Table default

Upgrade proof resolves `code` on stable and main and `block` on the proof head for unconfigured or legacy-only accounts. Legacy keys do not select the mode. In `auto`, stable and main route ordinary pipe-bordered tables to raw cards (`markdown.ts:25-27`, `outbound.ts:253-262`, `reply-dispatcher.ts:1289-1293` at main `29fc232d40be`, same logic at stable). Before captures show native grids. `block` retains them. Other modes convert before routing (`outbound-text-plan.ts:48-49`). Head lines use `948b2088919`.

Against main, standalone pipe-less and one-sided-pipe tables now get cards on `auto` sends and non-streamed replies. In chat text, blockquoted and list-opened tables take posts, but forced-card sends bypass that guard. Main sent these shapes to cards in streams or beside a fence or pipe table. Table messages needing multiple static cards also take posts. These posts use `code` unless fences cannot survive the cut. The five-table limit excludes streams. Direct post sends and edits still resolve `code`. Comments now convert raw rows to `code`. Explicit modes and size/fence safeguards apply.

A `code` default would fence those grids in cards (the `code` row at `outbound.markdown-tables.test.ts:640`, line 662 at `948b2088919`). `block` also drops "Avoid Markdown tables." from Feishu group prompts, even with account `code` or `bullets`, because `src/auto-reply/reply/groups.ts:129-131` reads the plugin default. Telegram and Matrix already declare `block`. Maintainers decide the default.

### Current repair verification

CI tested `cf49e1d3c83` merged with main `0858cc64613`. On that head 88 checks passed, none failed, 49 were skipped and CodeQL was neutral. In `checks-node-changed-1`, `telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e.test.ts` passed 20 tests, and the shard's seven other targets, six contract tests and a gateway e2e test, passed 115. Locally at `cf49e1d3c83`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test`, four ratchets and five generated-file check scripts passed, and `extension-feishu` passed 1256 tests.

### Fresh Lark before/after rendering

[Comparison and limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-6093982920) cover four byte-identical synthetic fixture pairs through the production send, reply and streaming components with the real SDK. Captures compare plugin source `e7f29073f4dc` with rendering files published at `34f132a1bb49`, not whole deployments, and were not retaken at `effbf8c7a8ab`. Merges after `34f132a1bb49` left `presentation-card.ts`, `card-table-shapes.ts`, `markdown.ts` and `outbound.ts` unchanged, kept the off-mode projection in `streaming-update.ts`, and moved the reasoning formatter and close route into `reasoning-structure.ts` and `table-routing.ts` intact, so the three off-mode rows render through the same code. The idle row's settlement bookkeeping took upstream's latest-settlement shape, so that row rests on the proof head's regression tests, not the captures.

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Off-mode presentation | ![Native table despite off mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff00b807-a9e6-465b-9f63-5829ea331710) | ![Literal rows and retained button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96bf5ced-1f4e-4375-985f-cf0a9ab4132f) |
| Off-mode answer preview | ![Native answer-preview table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e54aec3f-9a7c-41a7-886d-145522b8feed) | ![Literal answer-preview rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02c9e642-b5dd-4203-a3cf-87be4de7f7aa) |
| Off-mode reasoning preview | ![Reasoning-table rows missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/325f6680-67b2-4de6-99f7-a93a0eb9afb1) | ![Reasoning-table rows visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c07ea2c4-df53-4628-9793-8e1946bbf661) |
| Idle reuse of accepted answer | ![Reasoning disappears after idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4087a562-8abe-4253-8517-ac947981a16c) | ![One answer and separate reasoning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/430c18ca-2774-45cc-9055-44da9e169007) |

Both runs exited 0. Idle settlement adds exactly one reasoning-only post and keeps two actual receipts without replaying the accepted answer. All three dispatcher cases keep byte-identical authored final-post payloads. The button is retained, not clicked. All eight images were verified in the saved comment. The captures used no Gateway, model or mainland Feishu client. Lark still joins adjacent quoted paragraphs in the reasoning preview, not addressed here.

### Historical evidence

Pinned to the commits named, not current-head proof.

- CLI at `dbb422c85a5` (before) and `08c0c469de4` (after). Before, `config validate` rejected `tables` at channel and account scope (exit 1) and `gateway run` refused to start (exit 78). After, validation passed, the Gateway reached ready and shut down with child exit 0, and `doctor --fix --non-interactive` removed no `markdown` key.
- Gateway send RPC at `314ddb95`, HTTPS Feishu stub, real SDK, `renderMode` unset. Accounts resolved `code`, `bullets` and `off` as configured across full, reply and default-account sends, all exit 0.
- Authority proof at `c311d8a5d53` ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5707888042)), registered sender, production components, real SDK. Allowed sent four of four with every receipt. Revoked after one of four was accepted, kept its receipt and exact content in the partial-delivery envelope, and the claim guard refused the pending terminal rather than replay it.
- Lark client round at `9d52663f11b` and `d0f6e3a3ba0` ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5689525610)), real SDK, 62 captures. Blockquote and list-opened tables became readable fenced posts, and a mixed message kept both tables.
- Regression tests for schema acceptance, account selection, off-mode finals, comment delivery, block posts, preview dedupe and presentation cards each failed before the fix and passed after.

prs.title: fix: preserve authored CSP in relative HTML previews
prs.body: Fixes #187905 ## What Problem This Solves Files Preview can fetch a document's relative CSS and JavaScript successfully and still show an uninitialized page when its authored Content Security Policy permits only same-origin scripts and styles. The existing preview converts those external files into inline content. The browser then blocks that content under the unchanged policy, leaving the document unstyled or its controls disabled even though the original files work together. ## User Impact The supported self-only policy subset can load its relative classic scripts and styles in Preview while the browser continues to enforce the authored policy. The preview remains an opaque sandbox: access to localStorage and the surrounding application remains unavailable, and Source and Download retain the original file bytes. Ordinary HTML previews keep their existing asset-inlining path. Support is deliberately bounded. Complex policies, external modules, CSS imports, font loading, and integrity or cross-origin loading attributes use the existing Source/Download recovery with an explicit limitation message. Relative resources resolve at generated preview URLs; documents that depend on their original location or on persistent browser storage may still require downloading the files. ## Why This Change Was Made The correction retains the external-resource loading model that the policy author selected. The session-file owner admits a finite set of authorized relative resources, and the existing isolated sandbox listener serves them through the existing connection-bound grant lifecycle. The inner document inherits that generated resource base, so its policy and relative URL text do not need rewriting. Resource requests reread through the current file/session authority and must still match the admitted bytes and MIME type. Closing or replacing the preview retires its grant, and client disconnection, access revocation, and expiry invalidate further reads. Admission rejects unsupported syntax before creating a grant; the browser remains responsible for applying the policy at the generated URL. ## Evidence A real Gateway/browser scenario opens a synthetic HTML inspection page through the Files panel with its authored self-only policy intact. On the unchanged baseline, the preview loads but remains unstyled with zero records and disabled controls; the decisive initialization assertion fails. On 0b82e020832d87f445595c3612b25c72b0189bee, the same scenario initializes three records, applies the external stylesheet, runs deferred scripts in order, and adds a fourth record that appears in the exported JSON. The fixture uses no persistent storage; storage-dependent applications retain the existing limitation. The same scenario checks policy and lifecycle behavior through the actual preview path. The production ingress integration additionally exercises resource delivery through the real ingress factory and sandbox HTTP handler: | Check | Observed result | | --- | --- | | Authored policy and external assets | Policy text unchanged; stylesheet applied and classic scripts execute in declared order | | Inline script/style, connect, storage and parent access | Disallowed execution/styles/network remain blocked; storage and parent document access denied | | Source, Download and resource bytes | Match the original UTF-8 files; resource responses use `private, no-store` without a CORS grant | | Unknown resource, unadmitted query, escaped path and mixed preview locator | HTTP 404, no resource bytes | | Release and strict-mode replacement | The previously working resource URL changes from HTTP 200 to 404 | | Revoked device token | Current resource URL returns HTTP 404 | | Production ingress ownership | Issuing ingress grant returns HTTP 200 with exact bytes; a different grant and disconnected issuer return 404; revoked ingress is rejected | | Unsupported module or CSS import | Explicit Source/Download recovery; no preview grant for the rejected import | The focused browser case and all eight production ingress integration cases passed. Selected Gateway/UI consumer tests, affected type graphs, declaration compilation, structural checks and the ordinary-preview comparison also passed. A malformed-CSS admission probe exposed repeated suffix scans; returning at the first conclusive rejection reduces the median for the same 64 KiB input from 319.7 ms to 0.05 ms while preserving rejection and the valid stylesheet control. These are bounded parser measurements, not general preview latency claims. The matched screenshots below use a 1440 × 1000 light-theme viewport and identical synthetic data. The recording shows initialization, Add inspection, Export JSON and Source recovery at half speed with factual input captions; nonvisual authority checks are established by the assertions above. The baseline footer lacks the source-build branch badge present after the change; the preview framing is unchanged. Hosted CI passes after one native rerun of the recurring-plugin cron job. The rerun used the same code, pinned runtime, seven selected files and worker limit; its native retry route used GitHub-hosted capacity instead of Blacksmith. The earlier cron failure also occurred in one native reproduction, while the base and later samples passed. Its cause remains unexplained: this PR does not claim a cron fix or an inherited-failure classification. prs.title: fix(cron): scheduled runs fail after a tool error the model recovered from
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scheduled run whose tool call fails, and which then keeps working and ends with `NO_REPLY`, is recorded as failed with a synthetic "⚠️ <Tool> failed" result. Repeated recovered runs count toward the failure streak and can trigger failure alerts, owner repair requests and auto-disable for a job that is working.

## User Impact

User impact: a scheduled job that recovers from a tool error and deliberately stays quiet records `ok`, the same as a chat turn. Runtime failures still fail the run: aborts, provider and runtime errors, timeouts, denied commands and delivery failures keep their existing fatal paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildEmbeddedRunPayloads` respected an intentional `NO_REPLY` after a tool error everywhere except scheduled runs, where it appended a tool-failure warning instead (unless a message-tool send was proven). The cron outcome then treated that warning as fatal. Code was overriding the model's own judgement of a run it had already finished.

This matches the direction of #170267: run status comes from structured runtime results, not from inferring task failure. That PR stopped treating the model's blocker prose as failure; this one stops treating a tool error the model recovered from as failure. The cron exclusion (`isCronTrigger`) is removed, so `NO_REPLY` is respected the same way in all runs. Aborted runs still report the tool failure.

## Evidence

- Production: an hourly stock check failed `view_image` on a screenshot, continued, wrote its report and ended with `NO_REPLY`; the run was recorded as error "⚠️ View Image failed".
- New cron regression in `run.meta-error-status.test.ts`: a failed `view_image` followed by a silent final on an announce job records `ok` through the real outcome path.
- New QA scenario `cron-recovered-tool-error` (mock-openai, real Gateway): the model reads a missing file, receives the tool error and ends with `NO_REPLY`. Two runs of an owned job and two runs of an unowned announce job all record `ok`, deliver nothing, send no failure alert and request no owner repair; both jobs keep `consecutiveErrors: 0`. The scenario also asserts the model received the failed read output in each run.
- QA suite on the PR head (mock-openai, `--concurrency 1`): `cron-recovered-tool-error`, `cron-blocked-outcome`, `cron-failed-tool-terminal-finalization` and `cron-send-then-continue` all pass (4/4). `cron-failure-repair-owner-conversation` fails identically on unmodified `main` ("the repair turn is not in the owner session transcript"); its job fails through a provider error, a path this change does not touch.
- Removed tests that encoded the old rule (scheduled `NO_REPLY` after a read failure must warn; invisible message-tool send still warns in cron). The aborted-run case is kept.
- Local: 322 tests across the payloads, cron isolated-agent, auto-reply and chat dispatch suites pass; oxfmt and oxlint are clean on changed files.

Net change in production code: the cron-only branch and its two delivery-evidence imports are removed. The mock-openai scheduled-job planners now dispatch from one sibling module, so the oversized `server.ts` shrinks.

prs.title: fix: keep session-read failures from switching models
prs.body:
Fixes #188064

## What Problem This Solves

A local session-read consistency failure could consume the next configured model fallback. The fallback runner treated `SessionEntryChangedDuringReadError` as an unknown provider failure, even though switching models does not repair the underlying local read. A successful fallback could conceal that incorrect routing.

## User Impact

Session-read failures now retain the selected model and propagate through the existing local failure path. Existing bounded recovery stays with the reader, including the final serialized transcript read used after repeated contention. If a read still cannot be accepted, the conversation retains its existing check-before-retry guidance and accepted input remains available to a fresh authorized continuation. Genuine provider failures continue to use configured fallback.

No retry policy, configuration, credentials, storage format, or permissions change. This correction does not claim to fix the producer of every session-read conflict.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing runtime-coordination classifier already owns this distinction. Adding the named exception there keeps fallback decisions, embedded prompt handling and diagnostics aligned, including errors preserved through worker serialization and cleanup wrappers. The implementation adds one production entry, with no additional recovery mechanism.

## Evidence

- The current-base regression drives the real ordered session-entry reader, native metadata writer and `runWithModelFallback`. A metadata change invalidates the prepared snapshot before consumption. On base `8dad19d8b7b`, the runner incorrectly completes on the configured fallback with reason `unknown`. With the fix, the original local error propagates, no fallback is attempted, and a fresh admitted attempt reads current metadata and the original committed input on the selected model.
- The terminal-boundary suite covers the actual worker-error encode/decode path around a read failure and cleanup error, plus genuine provider-failure, cancellation and lifecycle controls. The current transcript-reader suite also confirms that repeated ordinary contention still completes through its serialized recovery.
- Changed formatting/lint, refreshed type-graph discovery, both affected agent test-type graphs and all 41 cases in those three focused files passed on this tree. The new regression's measured file duration was 10.99 seconds, including imports/setup. Earlier unchanged classifier/caller proof is retained separately; hosted CI and review for this updated head are pending. The 96-line allocation covers distinct native read/fallback and worker-error transport regressions and leaves the shared ceiling unchanged.
- Existing natural guest evidence independently demonstrated both incorrect fallback and an ordinary terminal failure followed by one successful **Try again**, preserving the original input and failure record. This is retained recovery evidence, not a claim that the natural failure was reproduced on this PR. The original invalidating writer and provider-request phase remain unknown.

prs.title: fix(system-agent): await hosted setup settlement before disposal returns
prs.body:
Closes #127459

## What Problem This Solves

Cancelling or exiting chat setup could say "nothing was changed" and still write the config a moment later; retirement now waits for the exact setup run and locks cancellation at the durable commit point.
- Problem: `ChatWizardHost.dispose()` cancelled the session and dropped the bridge without awaiting `WizardSession.whenSettled()`. A run already past its last authority check kept writing, then reported itself cancelled with `configWritten: false`.
- Solution: one host-owned pre-effect boundary (assert → `beforePersistentApply` → assert → `lockCancellation`) shared by the channel, skills, search, gateway and memory-import runs; the lock fires synchronously immediately before `writeWizardConfigFile`.
- What changed: `chat-wizard-host.ts` (async `dispose()` that cancels while cancellable, awaits settlement, and clears only its own bridge generation; a hooks object carries the boundary into hosted runs), `hosted-setup.runtime.ts` (commit lock before the write), `chat-engine.ts` (await wizard settlement and its turn queue before session cleanup).
- What did NOT change: `WizardSession` primitives, gateway wizard admission (#115856), setup prompts, the config schema, and the synchronous-throw contract in `throwInferenceUnavailable` (it still retires with `void`).

## Why This Change Was Made

`cancel()` is not a fence: the write path never re-checks the abort signal, so only a synchronous lock at the owner's commit boundary makes "cancelled" truthful, and only `whenSettled()` tells retirement that the runner can no longer mutate setup state.
- Best fix: reuse the existing ownership primitives (`lockCancellation`, `whenSettled`) at the canonical lifecycle boundary instead of adding a second completion signal.
- Alternative: awaiting settlement without the lock still lets a post-check write commit while the chat reports cancellation (see the before run below); awaiting only in the TUI caller leaves the gateway paths racing.
- Risk / non-goals: `dispose()` is now `Promise<void>`; exiting during a locked commit waits for that write and reports the truthful outcome. Replacement-bridge generation isolation and TUI `/exit` have no new e2e.

## User Impact

No more "cancelled, nothing changed" followed by a config write. Cancelling before the commit point still discards everything; exiting during an in-flight commit waits for it and shows the real result. Normal setup is unchanged.

## Evidence

Real `ChatWizardHost` driven by `node --import tsx`, with the commit held 400 ms so retirement lands mid-write; same script before and after (Node 24.22.1):

| phase | before (`origin/main`) | after (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| `dispose()` called | t=201 ms | t=201 ms |
| `dispose()` resolved | t=210 ms | t=552 ms |
| locked commit finished | t=402 ms | t=403 ms |
| chat result | `Channel setup cancelled. Nothing was changed beyond completed steps.` | `Done — channel is configured.` |
| `configWritten` | `false` | `true` |

Before: `RESULT: dispose() returned 192 ms BEFORE the locked commit finished -> retirement outran the write`.
After: `RESULT: dispose() waited 149 ms for the locked commit before returning`.

Regression in `src/system-agent/hosted-setup.runtime.test.ts` (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ...`):
- base production code: `Tests 1 failed | 18 passed (19)` — `AssertionError: expected false to be true` for "waits for a locked commit to settle before disposal returns" (retirement reported done while the locked write was still gated).
- this PR: `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 19 passed (19)`.

What was not tested: replacement-bridge generation isolation and TUI `/exit` have no new e2e; local runs needed Node 24.22.1 because Node 24.13.1's embedded SQLite is rejected by the plugin lifecycle lease.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `gh`, `grep`, `git diff` and `node --import tsx` to trace the disposal chain from issue #127459 into `chat-wizard-host.ts` and `hosted-setup.runtime.ts`, implement the fix, and produce the before/after runs. The implementer understands the code: `cancel()` only retires prompts, so retirement must lock cancellation immediately before `writeWizardConfigFile` and await `whenSettled()` before clearing that bridge generation. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix: resume native parents when saved channel aliases fail
prs.body:
Related: #166022

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native worker results failing to resume their parent when the parent's saved channel alias no longer resolves.

## User Impact

Parents can consume completed worker results and continue their tasks. Sending a visible reply still requires the parent's permitted messaging tools. No configuration or schema migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route native completions through the existing private parent-input owner instead of resolving an external destination first. Keep current session-controller custody and exact host-issued source/requester authority. Bind runtime completion facts to the durable processing identity so replay reuses a consumed result and rejects a changed result under the same identity. Processing receipts do not count as external delivery.

This is a separate pre-admission routing failure from the interrupted-input recovery reported in the linked issue; it does not claim to resolve that broader report.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the actual SDK and isolated Gateway on upstream `8e0ae0da7bd5`: a throwing saved-alias resolver ran once, no parent command started, and delivery failed. With the correction, the resolver is not called and the parent runs once.
- 97 focused cases pass across seven files: the three changed test files passed all 40 cases after the CI correction; 57 unchanged sibling cases retain their passing proof. Coverage includes durable replay after clearing warm dedupe, changed-result rejection, forged-source refusal, strict external routing, current/revoked/replaced ownership during compaction, incognito actor admission, and registered completion siblings.
- Removing only the new runtime-event fingerprint reproduced the changed-result replay defect; the reviewed production bytes were then restored.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the production and test changes completed with no actionable findings. Core and affected test types, targeted typed lint, formatting, docs checks, import cycles, assertion safety, line and mock-export ratchets, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The unused-file scan passed for production but failed for one full-tree path, `scripts/perf/update-state-io-measure.ts`. That file, its documented command, the Knip registrations/runner, and package/lock/workspace inputs are byte-identical to the pinned base; neither snapshot registers this maintained command. No changed path was flagged. The original aggregate failure is retained; a pristine-base scan was not rerun, and no unrelated fix or suppression was added.

The Gateway fixture uses real isolated session storage and controlled parent execution. It does not establish a live Codex thread identity or delivery of an external final message. Hosted CI on the corrected head is pending.

The retired-caller success cases use the real Gateway. A separate restart-drain negative verifies that a fabricated warm-cache result cannot claim private consumption or leave an input, transcript, queued controller, or retained root. This preserves the existing restart guard. The CI correction changes tests only; production bytes remain unchanged. The origin mock now preserves real exports, and its one obsolete grandfathered baseline entry was removed through the native guard.

The 172-line test allocation covers these distinct boundary regressions using existing fixtures; the prior compaction table was adapted rather than duplicated. No sleeps, retries, timeout increases, or new production test seams were added.

Changed-test costs from separate single-worker canonical wrapper invocations:

| File | Tests | Wrapper wall |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/agents/agent-harness-completion-authority.test.ts` | 14 passed | 107.983 s |
| `src/gateway/server.native-completion-authority.test.ts` | 10 passed | 110.191 s |
| `src/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-completion.test.ts` | 16 passed | 20.874 s |

The original authority fixture reproduced the CI failure locally: 13 passed, one failed, 109.131 seconds. These wrappers include worker preparation; transformation accounts for most of their time. The Gateway suite exercises actual SDK dispatch, controller serialization, SQLite processing receipts, and compaction admission; helper-only tests cannot prove that wiring. The earlier six-file batch took 390.580 seconds, including 96.333 seconds of shared worker preparation; its unchanged sibling proof is retained.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-harness-completion-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

prs.title: fix(gateway): stop GitHub readiness from copying whole agent databases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Since `sessions.github.readiness` shipped (e2427099948c), every readiness read on a busy Gateway froze the whole Gateway for minutes.

The agent `github_publish` tool calls readiness. The Gateway ran that request inside `withArtifactPreservingStateReads({ agentDatabases: true })`. That scope exists for offline Doctor inspection: it turns every agent-database read into a private whole-file copy. With a live 35 GB agent database, each readiness call:

- copied the full database (about 9 minutes at about 1.6 GB/s; disk queue saturated);
- held up writers. Session patches waited 400–600 s, session creates about 480 s, and simple reads (`users.prefs.get`, `board.get`) hit their 30 s timeouts;
- left the copy behind. About 30 copies (about 640 GB) built up in the snapshot cache in 4 hours.

Production trace on the team Gateway: each `github_publish` failure line has a matching 34 GB snapshot directory with the same timestamp, to the second (for example 21:18:22, 22:08:35, 22:16:07, 22:27:52). At each of those instants every stalled `board.get` completed at once. The copies started at the first readiness call after the build containing e2427099948c went live. Before that, only occasional state-database snapshots existed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway owns its live databases. A Gateway request reads them through that owner, as `sessions.github.options` and `status` already do. Private copies are for outside, offline readers.

- `sessions.github.readiness` dispatch keeps the shared observation scope. That scope gives the existing guarantee that readiness never starts a login refresh, and a test covers it. The `agentDatabases: true` option is removed.
- The duplicate scope inside `readGitHubPublicationReadiness` is removed; dispatch already provides it.
- `qualifyGitHubPublicationSource` keeps the source-retirement watch: a registry witness plus the native retirement signal for the selected agent database. It now applies to every observational (artifact-preserving) read rather than only to copied readers. The watch copies nothing. If the source is closed, unregistered or replaced while readiness is pending, the request is refused before any response, so a replacement database cannot leave an obsolete visibility decision in place.

So that this does not happen again:

- A boundary test fails if any production file under `src/gateway/` requests `agentDatabases: true`.
- `withArtifactPreservingStateReads` documents that the option is for offline inspection only.
- `src/gateway/AGENTS.md` states the rule for Gateway code.

The old scope did two jobs: it checked session-store paths in discovery workers, and it copied agent databases. This change keeps the first and drops the second:

- In session discovery (`session-utils-store-worker.ts`, `session-sharing-preparation.ts`, `session-entry-read-runtime.ts`, `session-store-read-candidates.ts`), any artifact-preserving read now checks paths in a worker. Readiness keeps that scope.
- Only the Doctor-only `agentDatabases` scope adds `preserveSourceArtifacts` or reads a private copy.
- Discovery workers no longer force `preserveSourceArtifacts` on every prepared inventory. Callers add it under that scope.

Doctor and update inspection keep the copy scope, with unchanged results.

@fuller-stack-dev this changes one readiness guarantee from #187152. Readiness no longer promises byte-identical `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars for a cold agent database. SQLite creates those files when the owner opens the database for a normal read. Stored database bytes stay unchanged, and readiness now creates no snapshot copies; both are still tested. The alternative is a whole-database copy on every call, which stalls a production Gateway.

## User Impact

On Gateways with large agent databases, agents calling `github_publish` no longer freeze chat, session updates and the Control UI for minutes, and no longer fill the disk with snapshot copies.

## Evidence

- **Regression, red then green.** In `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-github-readiness.test.ts`, the configured-locator test drives real readiness reads through the registered Gateway method and instruments native SQLite opens in the read workers. It previously asserted "readiness must open private images, not the source". It now asserts that readiness reads the source through its owner.
  - Against `main`'s production code: 3/3 variants **fail** (`expected 0 to be greater than 0`).
  - With this change: **pass**.
- **Path checks stay off the Gateway thread, red then green.** The same configured-locator test now spies on Gateway-thread session-store path checks (`prepareSessionStoreTargetInventory`, `captureSessionStoreReadCandidates`, `captureSessionStoreReadCandidate`) during cold and warm readiness reads.
  - Without the split above, it fails with `[4, 4, 16]` calls.
  - With it: zero.
  - Remaining Gateway-thread `stat`/`realpath` calls on the source are the per-read admission identity checks that every live Gateway session read makes (`sessions.github.options`, chat). Avoiding those would require reading a private copy, which is the bug.
- **Guard, red then green.** `src/state/artifact-preserving-state-reads.boundary.test.ts`:
  - with `main`'s `server-methods.ts`: fails, naming `server-methods.ts`;
  - now: passes (3 s wall).
- **Custody tests:**
  - "Preserves cold DB…" and "keeps an absent shared database absent" now compare the stored database files and the count of private snapshot copies; both pass.
  - The login-refresh, connection, profile, grant, session, visibility and session-metadata post-await checks are unchanged and pass.
  - The `source`, `registry-remove`, `published-replacement` and `registry-same` post-await cases are kept and run against live reads; each now also asserts zero agent snapshot copies. Without the source-retirement watch, the first three fail (the request is not refused); with it they pass.
- **Suites:**
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-github-readiness.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 33 passed, 55 s wall.
  - Related publication, session-access, availability, store-lookup and `github_publish` tool suites: 193 passed.
  - Session discovery, entry-read, sharing, store-worker and Doctor lint/database-inspection suites: 342 passed across 35 files.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes typecheck, lint and guards. The wrapper-shadowing check fails on `src/agents/skill-workshop-prompt.ts` / `src/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime.ts`. This PR does not touch those files, and the failure is already on `main` (from #187661).

prs.title: fix(ui): agent panels interrupt native mobile chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agent-driven panels interrupt chat inside the native iOS and Android apps when a tool presents a panel or a session gains an automatic resource.

## User Impact

User impact: native mobile chat stays visible until the user opens a panel. Manual panel controls and explicit dashboard navigation remain available; macOS and ordinary web browsers, including narrow/mobile browsers, keep their existing behavior. No settings or saved layouts are migrated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identify native mobile WebViews using their existing host/bootstrap provenance and platform, rather than viewport width. This also covers iOS shared-auth pages and Android message-port startup, which do not necessarily provide the embedded-chrome flag. Only host provenance is retained, not credentials.

Native mobile clients no longer advertise agent UI-command support, and discard incoming commands before they can navigate to another session. The existing presentation owners also suppress automatic desktop discovery/reveal, board presentation commands and first-board reveal, and restore chat-first layouts without rewriting saved preferences. Manual controls are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced again on current main `8dad19d8b7b2cd80841e866ec394d8f5119d4d58`: the bundled Control UI opened one Browser panel where the native-mobile assertion expected zero. The ordinary mobile-browser control passed.
- The same native-mobile and ordinary mobile-browser scenarios pass after the fix, including capability advertisement and manual Files opening. The bundled E2E run also includes the previously failing New Session prompt suite: 13 tests passed in 25.38 seconds (native-panel file: 2.45 seconds).
- Focused host/startup, shell-command, active-resource, board, and sidebar coverage: 152 tests passed in 13.39 seconds.
- UI typecheck, lint and formatting of all 15 changed files, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Test-line ratchet passes without an allocation or baseline change: 6,285,592 lines against a 6,330,936 ceiling.
- Fresh independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings, using the full affected presentation owners and the iOS/Android startup sources as context. The reviewer did not execute project code.
- Integrated main to include the canonical stale composer-test correction from #186409. Removed 15 lines of one-off screenshot capture plumbing; all behavioral assertions remain. Final scope is +38 production lines and +234 test/support lines.

## Risk and coverage

The policy changes only native iOS/Android automatic presentation. Tests retain ordinary mobile-browser behavior, manual opening, explicit dashboard navigation, and saved-layout preservation. Native provenance is checked against the existing iOS injected-auth and Android document-start/message-port startup contracts. No credentials are retained by the new host-provenance flag.

The images below show the actual bundled UI with synthetic content and a mocked Gateway at 390 × 844. Native bootstrap metadata is emulated; this is not an installed iOS/Android app or live-agent/model test. Physical-device/native-shell validation remains a follow-up.

prs.title: fix(ui): match canonical Unicode in command palette catalog search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: command palette catalog search misses canonically equivalent Unicode names when the typed query and the stored skill/plugin/agent/automation label use different normalization forms (NFC vs NFD).

## User Impact

User impact: typing `Café` in the Control UI command palette now matches a skill/plugin/agent whose stored name is NFD (`Cafe` + combining acute), and the reverse form also matches. ASCII case-insensitive substring ranking is unchanged; no diacritic folding, storage rewrite, or new option.

## Why This Change Was Made

`filterCommandPaletteItems` lowercased the query and each comparison field (`label`, `description`, `searchText`, `primaryModel`) without `.normalize("NFC")`. macOS and many skill/plugin sources store names in NFD, so a precomposed query never `includes` a decomposed catalog label. This is the same production path already fixed for workspace Files catalog, skills library, and place browser (#186672, #187036, #187988); command palette catalog filtering was the remaining Control UI search owner without NFC.

Reachability: `filterCommandPaletteItems` is the live matcher behind the Control UI command palette (`command-palette-view.tsx` / `command-palette-matches.ts`). Catalog items loaded via `loadCommandPaletteCatalogItems` include skill names, plugin names, agent display names, and automation display names — all user-controlled Unicode. This is not a fallback-only path.

## Evidence

Real shipped entry point: built Control UI command palette (Playwright / Chromium), mock Gateway advertising `skills.status` with an NFD skill name `Cafe` + U+0301 + `-notes`, query typed as precomposed `Caf` + U+00E9 through `.cmd-palette__input`.

- **Base `0f359b36dc4` + this e2e: red.** `locator('.cmd-palette__item-title').filter({ hasText: 'notes' })` timed out after 30s. Palette showed query `Café` with only the synthetic `Main` session row and **no Skills group** (screenshot `before-base.png`, 1280×900).
- **Candidate `a2183028964` + this e2e: green.** Same UI path finds the skill. Palette shows `All 2`, a **SKILLS** group, and row `Café-notes` under query `Café` (screenshot `after-fix.png`, 1280×900). E2E file: `ui/src/e2e/command-palette-catalog-unicode.e2e.test.ts`.
- Unit regression retained (matcher boundary only): `command-palette-catalog-search.test.ts` — NFC and NFD queries both hit the NFD catalog label and exclude an unrelated skill. Fixture-only Unicode inequality assertions removed per review.
- Focused related unit suites on candidate (before e2e commit): catalog-search, session-search, result, input, lifecycle — **27 passed**.

Inspected screenshots (mock Gateway synthetic names only; no credentials/PII):

| Base (no NFC) | Candidate (NFC fold) |
| --- | --- |
| Query `Café`: Sessions only (`Main`), count `All 1`, no Skills | Query `Café`: Sessions + **Skills → Café-notes**, count `All 2` |

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting fully restores prior lowercased comparisons. Blast radius is command palette catalog ranking only.

prs.title: fix(sessions): chat looks like it restarts working right after a turn finishes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a finished chat turn shows the working timer and Stop button again a second later, as if the agent restarted, when OpenClaw runs its post-turn memory flush or compaction on that session.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski with a screen recording from Control UI.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d80a929c-8ab0-4230-b56e-4acef2fed362)

## User Impact

User impact: once the reply finishes, the session stays idle in chat and in the sidebar while background upkeep runs. Upkeep itself is unchanged: it still runs, still yields to a new foreground turn, and still blocks a competing session mutation as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

After a turn, optional session maintenance admits its own controller turn on the user's session so it can safely flush memory and compact. The Gateway's active-run projection counted any unfinished controller operation without a `projectSessionActive: false` attachment, so `hasActiveRun` flipped back to true for the length of that upkeep. In the reported case a memory-flush preparation took about 6 seconds, and Control UI showed a running turn for exactly that window.

`withSessionTurn` can now pass the existing `projectSessionActive: false` presentation fact to its mailbox source, the same flag already used for other hidden work. Optional maintenance sets it. Admission, mailbox ownership, cancellation and writer locking are unchanged; only the presentation of that operation changes.

## Evidence

- **Production trace:** the gateway log for the recorded session shows the turn's final reply at 13:45:10 UTC, then at 13:45:13 a controller turn on the same session, a 5.7s managed-worktree preparation and a `memory flush skipped` at 13:45:19. The recording shows a working timer counting from 1s to 7s with Stop over the same interval, with no new transcript entry.
- **Regression test** (`src/agents/session-maintenance/run.test.ts`): it schedules real optional maintenance against a real SQLite session, holds the flush, and asserts `resolveVisibleActiveSessionRunState(...).active === false`. Red without the flag (`expected true to be false`), green with it.
- **Related suites:** `session-controller.admission.test.ts`, `session-controller.mailbox.test.ts`, `gateway/server-methods/session-active-runs.test.ts` and all of `agents/session-maintenance/`: 101 tests pass.
- **Gates:** `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean on the touched files.
- **Local review:** autoreview (codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium) in branch mode on base `de25af72ff5` → head `27b42ac2d05`, with the P0–P2 range. Result: scoped-clean, no findings.
- **Gap:** I could not run a live Gateway reproduction on this host. The gateway e2e harness (`vitest.e2e.config.ts`) times out before the first provider request here, and the existing `gateway.compaction-hot-reload.e2e.test.ts` fails the same way. So the test above proves the invariant at the Gateway projection the UI reads (`chat.history` / `sessions.list` → `hasActiveRun`), not through a browser.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

<!-- openclaw-publication:e689b1ed-e7da-44fd-b2de-31797845dbbf -->

## Maintainer verification

- Rechecked exact head `55fd1a890534a31b340463c60c49922d6013099c` on tempbook: 101 tests pass across maintenance, controller admission/mailbox and Gateway active-run projection (60.31 seconds across four test shards). The new regression itself took 564 ms.
- Negative control: removing only the maintenance visibility flag fails the new regression with `expected true to be false`; three sibling cases pass. Original source restored without changes.
- Targeted lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Fresh independent Codex review of the full branch and relevant owners found no P0–P2 issues. Existing tests cover foreground preemption, operational cancellation and settlement; the new test covers scheduling through the real SQLite/controller/projection boundary. No live browser replay was added.

## Risk and coverage

The flag changes presentation only. Maintenance keeps its controller, writer admission and cancellation; new foreground turns retain default visibility. The change adds seven production lines and 25 test lines using existing setup.

CI run [40888085151](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40888085151) remains failed: the only non-aggregate failure is `agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts > passes explicit timeout overrides into agent attempts`, which expected 600000 ms and observed 599999 ms. The fixture froze the wall clock but not the monotonic clock used by the budget. Its test/helpers and budget source are byte-identical between baseline `36383b8` and tested merge `2d778d9`. This independent fixture defect is already repaired on main by [#187763](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187763), commit `6676a9d8022`. Landing uses the attributed pre-existing CI exception; it does not claim that failed CI passed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Invitation membership and mention involvement must commit together and immediately reach retained authorization readers.

## User Impact

Adds an atomic membership/involvement operation and publishes exact committed member changes, including actor and in-flight read postimages.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing SQLite transaction and publication owners. Reuse existing tables and watermarks; no schema bump or parallel ACL store.

Stack step **13/17**, now targeting main after the prerequisite landings. Review and merge in order; each upper PR contains only its own slice against its predecessor.

Previous: [wait for public startup admission in chat fixtures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185983), closed as superseded by #186287; the branch is kept. Coordination cleanup #185982 is merged.

Next: [commit invitations with original messages; release retained authority](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184512).

Stack order: [complete stack](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184515#stack-order).

## Evidence

Slice head: `14be106704711b9e0f872ebec1b2ed374e0e1f41`, on fixed main `5bf0c41a03f1dba03d625460607ed5b959710458`. The complete 13-file integration matrix passed 46/46 on pinned Bun at `ddc49fd63d3b82e41eb6c74af4ad935a56aebc8f` before this main rebase. Main's canonical fixture repairs are preserved and duplicate prerequisite changes removed. Prefixes are not separately built locally; this prefix's hosted CI and review are recorded below.

Sharing/involvement worker tests cover stale expected entries, replay watermarks and retained-reader publication. The final real-invitation SessionManager matrix adds actor and non-actor commit/rollback proof, including readers acquired before the write. Existing tables and schema versions are unchanged.

The extracted insert helper is registered with the writer guard. Its native wrapper and atomic involvement transaction are the only permitted callers; negative fixtures reject additional callers, including another function in the same worker file.

The [stack evidence ledger](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184515#evidence) records runtime results, prior build/upgrade proof and limits. Integration tests are owned by the final activation PR. Current-head hosted CI and review remain required before landing.

### Pre-restack qualification (historical)

[Required CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40526292581) passed at `14be106704711b9e0f872ebec1b2ed374e0e1f41`. The [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184511#issuecomment-6414280481) covers the same head and reports no actionable findings or required rank-up moves. Merge in the recorded stack order.

## Change size

Production and tooling **+253/-119**; tests **+200/-36**; generated inventory **+2/-2**. The growth reuses the existing transaction, commit-receipt and retained-publication owners; it adds no store, schema migration, protocol or config activation.

### Test-line allowance

Main’s scalar ceiling and existing allocations are unchanged. Final canonical count: **6,281,410**, below the existing effective ceiling **6,328,569**. No test deletion or assertion weakening was used to fit the budget.

### CI dependency follow-up — 2026-10-30

Both originally reported failures have scoped repairs. The inherited concise-notice test mismatch is merged in [#188056](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188056), squash `b848e52d0490ea31ffe6067a2fbddff83a1552e1`, after green exact-head CI and clean review. The transcript-reader failure is an inherited admission-ordering race in an unchanged owner: a preceding writer renews validation while a queued read retains its revoked receipt. [#188055](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188055) has a deterministic real-worker red/green regression, Node 24 repeated controls on head/base, corrected test types and clean exact-head review at `bf14009ac769a40b83f2c785361d4084fe239fb6`.

That dependency remains unmerged because its artifact-build job timed out rendering bundled root help after 120 seconds. A bounded isolated Node 24 build at its exact head passed, but that is not a fix or CI waiver. No CI rerun was requested. Consequently this stack PR remains at `a17fcb30f8a06286c8f2009f9e9c7f8f6c1d14e3`: it has not been rebased or force-pushed before main contains both repairs. Its completed AWS evidence and released lease below remain pinned to that original tested head, not relabeled as new-head proof. #184512 and upper stack branches are untouched.

The follow-up [bounded root-help audit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188055#evidence) found no matching timeout in 24 readable scheduled-main logs or three executed other-PR logs over the selected 24-hour creation window (33 other-PR jobs skipped). Source tracing at the actual failed synthetic merge found no causal path from the reader repair; the hosted hang remains unattributed, with no proven fix. ### Current qualification — 2026-10-30

prs.title: fix(ci): prevent stale Darwin runs and workflow fixture deadlocks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two avoidable macOS tooling costs: newer PR heads cannot cancel superseded native runs, and ordinary Darwin workflow fixtures can deadlock inside PATH-selected Bash 5.3 here-strings/heredocs until their deadline.

## User Impact

Useful PR events can cancel older work for the same PR while unrelated PRs and skipped drafts stay isolated. Ordinary Darwin shell fixtures use system Bash and finish without the reproduced pipe deadlock. Native workflow coverage and explicit Linux Bash 5 semantics are preserved. No product runtime change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Supersession belongs to workflow admission. Add the existing workflow-prefixed PR/passive-draft concurrency pattern. Triggers, path filters, exact-head checkout, runner, Node version, permissions and native proof commands are unchanged.
- Shell selection belongs to `runWorkflowCommand`. Centralize the ordinary Darwin `bash` choice there and remove two caller-local selections. Absolute executables, including the Linux-workflow Bash 5 resolver, pass through unchanged. PATH spies, environment, deadlines and process-group cleanup retain their contracts.

## Evidence

- Admission regression: 2 failed / 46 passed before the fix; 48 passed after it.
- Real subprocess regression: a 4 KiB here-string under command substitution plus a redirected Node heredoc timed out on the old owner (1 failed / 2 passed); all 3 passed after the fix. No timeout increase or weaker assertion.
- Complete required workflow family: all 10 files passed, 1,028 tests passed / 10 skipped; two runner shards completed successfully in 371.48 seconds locally with Node 26.12.1 and one worker. This includes planning, guards, failure evidence, generated workflows, UI workflow contracts, Swift cache lifetime, native test launch and the shell owner. Aggressive PR selection does not guarantee this whole family, so it was run explicitly.
- `pnpm check:workflows`, targeted type-aware oxlint, targeted oxfmt, test-line ratchet and `git diff --check` passed. Ordinary PR CI covers aggregate root typechecking and other broad proof.
- Independent source review: GO / best fix. Local autoreview of the complete six-file candidate against `315380c4789590e3aff9be3cfc6fcfcb9e1f6eee`: scoped-clean through P2, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its source checkout was dirty; hosted exact-head review is requested separately.
- [GitHub concurrency contract](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency): pending replacement and running cancellation share a group. Admission inputs are covered; actual hosted cancellation/native process cleanup have not been observed here. The latest 12-run sample showed no same-PR overlap, so no measured billing, frequency or elapsed savings are claimed.
- The [Bash maintainer's Darwin pipe repair](https://www.mail-archive.com/bug-bash@gnu.org/msg36171.html) describes the pipe-backed heredoc boundary. This change avoids that path for ordinary Darwin fixtures; explicit Linux Bash 5 host qualification remains separate.

Source: signed commits `856915e3ef10ae8dd15ef41b8f456b68e02857f6` and `cbc186c51bac3ffc93278e7ebe2d6c4f0498574d`. The final diff adds 8 workflow lines, net 28 test-class lines and 2 allocation-metadata lines. Positive workflow growth expresses the admission boundary; test helper growth centralizes shell ownership and removes duplicate policy. No product TypeScript growth, dependency change, schema change or new harness. Converting to draft alone remains unsubscribed, as before.

Follow-up: the aggressive PR planner does not select the entire native-workflow contract family. This PR supplies explicit full-family proof; selection expansion is separate.

## Final Verification

Final head `cbc186c51bac3ffc93278e7ebe2d6c4f0498574d` passed [ordinary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41002164083) and [native Darwin qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41002164002). The [exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188088#issuecomment-6514851508) has zero findings and no before-merge moves.

Squash landed as [`f6458ef678e951b3f6635c2314126c4b06645890`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f6458ef678e951b3f6635c2314126c4b06645890) at 2026-10-30T04:28:16Z. Successful native qualification does not demonstrate overlapping-run cancellation or measured savings.
