prs.title: fix: transcript reads fail after concurrent database preparation
prs.body:
Related: #184511.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes transcript reads failing with a physical-owner validation error when database preparation completes ahead of a queued read.

## User Impact

Queued reads use the current validation receipt for the same physical database. Revocation and foreign-file checks remain in force; no retry, schema, configuration or permission change is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history worker captured a validation receipt before awaiting read admission. A preceding writer can renew that receipt during the wait, leaving the real worker with revoked proof. Capture now occurs inside the existing admitted operation, after its predecessors settle. The owner is byte-identical on guest-stack head a17fcb30 and main base 8da85beb, establishing an inherited race rather than a membership change.

## Evidence

- On Node 24.22.1, the original filtered-sharing file passed 10/10 in three separate runs on each side (30/30 on a17fcb30, 30/30 on main 8da85beb); those passing replays alone did not establish a fix.
- A deterministic owner-bound regression warms a real worker, holds the next admission, renews the same file's writer validation and releases the read. It fails on main with the exact CI error, `Session reader validation does not match its current physical owner`, and passes with this repair. The test does not replace worker execution or returned data.
- Node 24 owner, schema-freshness and original filtered-sharing suites passed 27/27. Core and affected test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks passed. SQLite T1 calls remain 168 → 168. Main's test ceiling is unchanged: 6,283,332 lines against 6,329,653 allowed.
- Combined scoped wall time was 129.98 s, including compiler preparation and real-worker lifecycle. The new owner case took 25.719 s; it boots/joins the real native worker to prove receipt transfer, which a mocked result cannot establish. Hosted CI timing remains pending.
- Independent AutoReview (Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2, full changed modules plus admission/physical-owner context) reported scoped-clean. It did not execute tests. Simplification retained the existing admission owner and moved the existing capture; production net growth is one line, with one 51-line boundary regression and no new state or helper API.
- No CI rerun or dispatch was requested. The historical CI attempt was not instrumented, so the controlled reproduction proves this pre-existing mechanism, not the exact scheduling of that attempt.

### CI typecheck correction

The first head's CI caught a missing `databaseAgentId` in the new regression input. The follow-up binds the request to the fixture's actual database agent; production behavior and the demonstrated admission repair are unchanged. Node 24 reader tests passed **7/7** after this correction, and the actual owning `tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json` leaf, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Prior 27-test and independent source-review evidence remains scoped to the original production move; one exact-head re-review is requested for the corrected head. No test deadline, check or ceiling was relaxed.

### Current exact-head build gate — 2026-10-30

The corrected head `bf14009ac769a40b83f2c785361d4084fe239fb6` has [clean exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188055#issuecomment-6513913355), with no Before-merge items or findings, and its typecheck failure is cleared. [CI run 40998529819](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40998529819) is blocked by [build-artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40998529819/job/123877673340): the bundled root-help renderer timed out after **120,000 ms** in `scripts/write-cli-startup-metadata.ts`. This leaves `openclaw/ci-gate` red.

One bounded local `pnpm build` at this exact head passed under verified Node **24.22.1**, with isolated HOME/config/state: total build phases **3m 30s**, startup metadata **4.22s**. The previous [6c62e05e build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40994523700/job/123864788070) also passed; the only source delta to the corrected head is the regression input binding, not production code. The later main build passed too, and no intervening repair in the helper or root-help owner was found. These passing controls do not establish a causal fix for the failed hosted build. The timeout remains **unattributed / unreproduced locally**, not waived or labeled green. No CI rerun, dispatch, no-op push or timeout increase was used. The PR remains unmerged under the requested green-only gate.

### Bounded root-help timeout audit — 2026-10-30

The [failed bundled root-help child](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40998529819/job/123877673340) reached its **120,000 ms budget, 120,008 ms elapsed**, on Node 24.22.1. The hang remains **unattributed**, not established as inherited or a shared flake.

Read-only run-creation window: **2026-10-29 04:18:24Z through 2026-10-30 04:18:24Z**. Logs were observed October 30 at **04:22:31Z–04:29:38Z**, not backdated to the creation cutoff. All 24 completed scheduled-main runs returned in that window were inspected. The other-PR sample selected the latest six completed non-cancelled distinct branches per four-hour bin, from at most 100 returned candidates per bin, excluding the guest stack and its two repairs. This is a bounded sample, not an exhaustive incident-rate estimate.

- Main: **0 matching timeout hits / 24 readable log misses**; 23 target jobs succeeded and one was cancelled after metadata completed.
- Other PRs: **0 hits / 3 readable executed-job misses**; **33 skipped target jobs** do not count as executions.
- **No unresolved read gaps.** Initial job-list 502s were recovered through the attempt jobs API, reconciling both pages against total counts.
- Successful main metadata phases: **23 samples, min 2.95 s / median 3.75 s / max 6.59 s**. Other-PR phases: **3 samples, 3.23–3.79 s**. These enclosing-phase durations are not individual-child measurements and do not justify increasing its deadline.

The failed job actually built synthetic merge **c87bcb9ca45e19b2f986840c500a471837028fbb**, with main parent **acb102d176c49d7df4360edb58e7b3fc1b490c9e** and PR parent **bf14009ac769a40b83f2c785361d4084fe239fb6**. The previous and corrected PR heads had different hosted integration bases. The prior passing local build was the raw PR head, not this synthetic merge; it cannot exclude a base/composition effect. This audit did not replay the exact synthetic merge locally.

At that executed merge, renderBundledRootHelpText imports the root-help bundle and calls outputRootHelp with fresh isolated HOME/state/workspace and a fixed synthetic config. Root help assembles command descriptors rather than registering live command runtimes. The repository-owned runtime-emitted import graph, erasing type-only imports, visited **1,582 eager source modules** without reaching either changed file. The dynamic legacy-plugin loader requires a nonempty external-plugin list; the isolated render uses bundled assets, not user-installed legacy plugins. Resolution gaps were confined to external fs-safe/proc-safe packages, whose boundaries were inspected; this is not a complete native/bundled runtime trace. The production delta adds no imports or top-level initialization: it moves validation capture inside an already-invoked admitted reader operation. **No causal path from this repair to the help hang was found.**

Existing [#147932](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147932) states a live-config fast-path scope; [#187644](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187644) explicitly changes exit-code diagnostics, not timeouts. Neither provides a proven repair for this hang. With no matching comparison timeout, no reproduced original hang and no demonstrated cause, no speculative owner patch, timeout increase, rerun/dispatch, empty push or chase rebase was made. The requested green-only landing remains blocked and is escalated to the requesting maintainer.

prs.title: fix: restore CLI message sends with agent tool policies
prs.body:
Related: #184964

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw message send` failing with `Cannot verify the installed tool authority for Template-managed agent "main"` when the selected agent has its own tool profile or allowlist. Even text-only sends and `--dry-run` fail for ordinary agents with no Template installation.

## User Impact

CLI message sends work again without changing agent policies or repairing a healthy state database. Explicit attachment read restrictions and genuine Template-consent failures remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The regression was introduced by [3c23d52c93b in #184964](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3c23d52c93b2479d8685564b7e5b4e3dcb47cc1e): the new `resolveEffectiveToolPolicy()` call in `src/media/read-capability.ts` reads Template consent during message preparation, including text-only sends.

The CLI config guard publishes its configuration synchronously, before that consent provenance has been initialized. Initialize the provenance and bind it to the effective command configuration before dispatch, using the same preparation owners as standalone agent commands. No media-policy checks are removed.

## Evidence

- Reproduced with the installed CLI: `openclaw message send --channel discord --target channel:123456789012345678 --message regression-probe --dry-run --json` exits 1 with the error above.
- New command-boundary regressions: **2 fail / 1 pass before**, **3 pass after**. They exercise real config, policy, and dispatch with isolated consent-row I/O. Both an agent-owned profile and a restrictive allowlist can send text; unreadable consent remains rejected.
- **35 focused tests passed** across the command, media workspace-access, and consent-preparation suites. Existing attachment-denial tests remain green. Command-suite wall time was 5.14 seconds for 14 tests; the three sequential test shards completed in 23.93 seconds.
- A separate Node process with no module mocks, isolated empty state, and a local channel adapter reproduced the same consent error before the fix. Afterward, dry-run succeeded without delivery, and a non-dry-run delivered the exact message to the local adapter once with `deliveryStatus: "sent"`. No external channel API was called.
- Changed-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The final isolated regression run also passed all 3 cases (33.16 seconds including cold worker compilation). The 76-line test allocation covers the missing CLI initialization boundary and fail-closed control.

prs.title: fix(media): carry provider status and code into failure markers
prs.body:
Fixes #188043

## What Problem This Solves

When a media-understanding provider call fails, the agent marker is the fixed string `[Audio attachment could not be analyzed]` and the log line keeps only `reason=ProviderHttpError`. Both drop the provider's HTTP status and error code, so a rejected credential (`401`), an exhausted account (`429 insufficient_quota`), a rate limit, and a timeout are indistinguishable — for the agent and for the operator.

## Why This Change Was Made

Failure reasons now keep the provider message and add only what it omits: `HTTP <status>`, `code=<code>`, and `request_id=<id>` are appended when the message does not already contain them, so richer errors are never shortened. Failed attachment dispositions carry that normalized reason, and the marker renderer appends it on one bounded line (160 chars). No credential or response body is added; this only surfaces fields the provider error already retained.

## User Impact

The agent marker names the concrete provider failure, e.g. `[Audio attachment could not be analyzed: provider POST request failed (HTTP 401 code=invalid_authentication)]`, and the log carries the status and code. Successful analyses and disabled/not-selected markers are unchanged. Dispositions that already carried a reason now render it too — for example remote URLs that cannot be handed to native vision explain why — so three existing expectations were updated to the reasoned marker.

## Evidence

New regression test fails on the base and passes with the change:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media-understanding/apply.test.ts --run -t "provider status and code"
# base
AssertionError ... Expected: "[Audio attachment could not be analyzed: provider POST request failed (HTTP 401 code=invalid_authentication)]"
                   Received: "[Audio attachment could not be analyzed]"
# with the fix
Tests  30 passed (30)
```

The test rejects with a real `ProviderHttpError({ status: 401, code: "invalid_authentication" })` and asserts the rendered marker; no live provider call is involved.

Regression coverage for the existing detailed messages and for dispositions that already carried reasons:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media-understanding/runner.auto-audio.test.ts --run
[test] passed            # detailed "Audio transcription failed (HTTP 403): ..." strings unchanged
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media-understanding/audio-preflight.attachments.test.ts \
    src/media-understanding/runner.vision-skip.test.ts --run
[test] passed            # fixture failure and remote-url reasons now render
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-assertion-safety-ratchet.mts
assertion SAFETY ratchet OK: 2396 files, 5441 grandfathered assertions.
```

`tsc -p tsconfig.core.json` reports only the two pre-existing `@noble/hashes` resolution errors in `packages/gateway-client`, unchanged from the base checkout.

What was not tested: a live provider 401 against a real model endpoint, and the Telegram ingress path end to end.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep, git, node, and vitest to trace the failure path from the provider error through the decision, disposition, and marker renderer. The implementer understands the code: attempt reasons preserve their existing detail and only gain missing structured fields, failed dispositions carry that reason, and the renderer bounds it on one line. All evidence above comes from real local runs.

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

prs.title: fix(slack): stop untagged bot loops with opt-in explicit mentions
prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner and generated-output conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner; retired helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing mention sibling to satisfy the shrink-only line-cap. Current canonical generators own the metadata/baselines. The schema regression uses main's direct `safeParse` assertions after its former test helpers were removed; all validity/default/type assertions remain.

## Evidence

prs.title: feat(pdf): add explicit OpenAI native document opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Platform users cannot explicitly choose native PDF document input through the PDF tool while preserving existing upload and model-selection behavior.

## User Impact

`agents.defaults.pdfNativeOpenai: true` opts an already-selected OpenAI vision model into complete-document input. **Unset or false preserves extraction and the existing provider order**, including saved configurations upgraded from the latest stable release. Selecting an OpenAI model alone does not authorize complete-document upload.

Page selection, passwords, unknown completeness, page/text/image truncation, size-limit violations, custom endpoints, Codex/ChatGPT transports and text-only models retain bounded extraction. Completeness checks still require the configured extractor. Existing Anthropic and Google paths are unchanged.

## Implementation

This replaces the earlier automatic-upload/provider-preference proposal with one default-off core boolean at the existing PDF configuration owner. The bundled OpenAI provider implements a narrow optional media-understanding hook using the official [PDF input contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs): inline `input_file`, official Platform HTTPS `/v1/responses`, `store: false`, each PDF under 50 MB and combined PDF input at most 50 MB. There is no persistent Files upload, automatic provider preference or new dependency. The official configuration generator records the single additional core leaf; channel/plugin surfaces are unchanged.

Prepared credentials, headers and symbol-attached request/auth overrides use the existing scoped egress helpers. The native branch also reuses the host-owned `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` scope with `assertModelCurrent`, the **original model's** credential authority and the retained provider-resource assertion. The existing HTTP guard rechecks these synchronously immediately before dispatch after asynchronous preparation and on redirects. This closes the assert-only operator/credential retirement gap across lazy provider and DNS awaits without adding an authorization abstraction or changing shared HTTP behavior.

Capability adoption and the proposed setting placement remain normal maintainer product decisions. This branch provides a concrete default-preserving candidate for that decision.

## Evidence

The complete latest check-run inventory has zero failed or pending lanes.

Product/contract adoption remains with the upstream owner. Older dated evidence blocks retain their original-head scope. No employee runtime, private patch or package distribution changed.

Earlier validated head: `95d83ad28f203ee6ec15ad60f69c06060a7235a5`. Exact-head [CI39994486818](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39994486818) **passed**: 75 jobs (47 success, 28 skipped), no failures or pending jobs.

- **Earlier real OpenAI API proof:** the actual PDF tool/prepared provider/extractor, using synthetic documents only, returned HTTP200 and expected results for native input and four extraction cases (unset, selected page, password/encrypted, configured text-only). ### Real isolated Gateway, normal agent route

[The later evidence reminder](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127770#issuecomment-6051721637) is addressed by this refreshed evidence and description. prs.title: fix(ui): keep chat actions and timestamps with their message
prs.body:
Fixes #186014

## What Problem This Solves

Hovering or focusing a chat message could reveal actions on neighboring messages. Consecutive user messages also shared the first message's timestamp in the closing group footer, so hovering an earlier message showed its actions and a timestamp underneath a different bubble.

## User Impact

Each message reveals its own actions and timestamp together. Moving into its toolbar keeps them available. Existing message grouping, bubble positions, sender identity, saved reactions, and touch access are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use per-message disclosure for actions and metadata. Earlier desktop user messages show their timestamp in their existing action row; the closing user footer reads the last message's timestamp. Assistant run metadata retains its existing ownership.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original defect in a real isolated Gateway session with three steering messages during a live agent response. Existing before/after media below records that scenario.
- Rechecked the same persisted B/C/D messages using the candidate integrated with main `8dad19d8b7b`: ordinary hover and toolbar traversal show only the matching timestamp/actions; Reply quotes each selected message. The middle message's saved reaction remains attached and visible. No injected messages, forced pointer events or styling, Gateway restart, or configuration change.
- Deep review repaired final-toolbar overlap, blocked persistent collaborator links, tablet touch disclosure, and invisible intermediate author links intercepting pointer input. Message grouping and run ownership remain with existing owners.
- Four bundled interaction E2Es pass, covering own/peer grouping, timestamps, Reply, reactions, hidden-name hit testing, keyboard focus, and 560/1024px touch. Forty-four existing group/run/contrast checks pass; three native picker/virtualizer browser cases pass.
- Targeted E2E typecheck, lint/stylelint, formatting and native test-line budget pass. The popup fixture now uses the production reaction-row boundary; redundant literal-opacity coverage was removed while preserving popup lifecycle and overflow checks.
- Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 issues in the integrated candidate. The lead also inspected unchanged grouping, frame/action, identity and run owners.

## Risk and coverage

The change is presentation-only. Current main's message-part ownership, participant palette, avatar and footer changes are retained. The latest real-Gateway check reuses persisted steering history; simultaneous new authenticated multi-account traffic was not rerun. Original real steering/reaction proof and current grouping/run tests provide complementary coverage.

## Visual evidence

Real Gateway conversation. Both screenshots hover the middle message; the after capture also shows the reaction added during verification. Before: `8237bbaee32f`. After: `39be6843a8b0`.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The middle message reveals a timestamp below the last bubble](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3876af3-c3fb-42f8-a01a-84ac7044cd00) | ![The middle message keeps its timestamp and actions together](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ab84623-5837-4acf-ab2c-ec0948e6e5db) |

The recording runs at normal speed for 15.2 seconds. Arrows identify the hovered message; the final pause shows the saved reaction with the transient controls hidden.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bce52a5d-ccb4-4e1f-a766-74300eb07f33

### Current integrated candidate

Candidate `759632da6528` with current main `8dad19d8b7b`, replaying the same real persisted steering conversation. The middle message owns its timestamp and action row; its saved reaction remains visible.

![Current candidate hovering the middle real steering message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74808ad7-4050-4cb0-a878-dedb484bf8ed)

## Final CI assessment

CI run [41001999787](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41001999787) completed on `759632da6528`. Security checks and all other jobs passed; two failures remain explicitly recorded:

- **CSS budget:** total compressed CSS is 308636 B against a 308526 B ceiling, a 118 B increase over the measured base. The maintainer explicitly authorized this CSS-budget exception; no budget or source baseline was changed.
- **Unrelated file-attachment timeout:** `chat-workspace-files.e2e.test.ts` timed out waiting for `Remove notes.md` immediately after Attach to session, before its first message was sent. That scenario starts with empty history, and its file/attachment owners, test and fixture are unchanged by this PR. The focused scenario passed on both base `8dad19d8b7b` and candidate `759632da6528`. The CI timeout was not reproduced or claimed fixed. The scheduled-main failure was a different attachment test, so it is not treated as matching-signature evidence.

An additional 21 existing transcript-grouping tests passed. Native auto-merge was explicitly retired before the maintainer-authorized final CLI merge, preserving the failed CI result and exact reviewed head.

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: fix: preserve file attachments during pane refresh
prs.body: Fixes #188067. ## What Problem This Solves Attaching an open file from **Files → More file actions → Attach to session** could silently produce no draft attachment if the pane refreshed during its download. Resizing the browser is one reproducible trigger, even when the selected file, destination session and access remain unchanged. An immediate-download control worked; the failure was in retaining the accepted action across refresh. ## User Impact The selected file can finish attaching to the existing message draft while the pane refreshes. Existing message text and attachments remain intact, and the action still sends nothing automatically. Actual source, session, read-owner, connection or authority replacement keeps the existing cancellation behavior. Original file bytes, unsaved-editor text, upload permissions and attachment size limits continue through their existing owners. ## Why This Change Was Made The attachment operation compares callback identities before the next UI frame commits. Both composer destination callbacks and the artifact-download resolver were recreated during every pane render, so equivalent frames looked like different owners. Keep the composer callbacks for their captured state, read lifecycle and read signal, and keep the artifact resolver for its captured state. Changing those owners replaces the callbacks; changing attachment membership, limits or availability still produces current values. This preserves the operation's cancellation checks instead of removing them. The two existing producers retain one current binding each, with no new global cache or lifecycle service. ## Evidence The complete browser flow failed on the base when a file-download response was held through a real pane resize: the selected file and authority fields stayed equal, all four callback identities changed, and no attachment appeared. A separate live saved-file reproduction held delivery of the actual HTTP 200 response, resized, then released the same 786 bytes; it produced the same missing attachment while preserving existing unsent work. The regression extends the existing Files → Attach → Send scenario with that held read and resize, plus assertions for unchanged draft text and no automatic send. Existing original-byte, unsaved-editor, cancellation and composer-handoff checks remain in scope. The implementation adds 34 production lines and 9 regression lines; the allocation record covers only those 9 test lines. Changed-file formatting/lint, UI catalog checks and all selected type graphs passed. The nine selected test files reported 185 passing test cases, including the complete four-scenario workspace browser file and 22 composer-handoff tests. The browser file took 19.70 seconds including its 9.80-second build. The ordinary UI test process additionally reported an uncaught Node fetch-abort error in the unchanged attachment suite; the untouched base reproduced the identical exception with the same 159 test cases passing. That inherited failure remains disclosed rather than reported as a green aggregate; it is tracked separately in #188084. The corrected live pending-read case attached the file once while preserving an existing attachment and unsent text. Native file navigation, saved-session replacement and connection retirement canceled pending reads; returning or reconnecting preserved the existing draft. An explicit message then sent the selected file with its original SHA-256, alongside the existing context attachment, and the completed reply used both to answer the planning question. The live UI was built from the exact PR head against an unchanged isolated Gateway with the same affected download contract. Exact-head hosted CI is green. Local AutoReview covered the committed range from faa38148 to 07da80ac at P0–P3 and found no actionable issues. Independent engineering review is clean. [ClawSweeper’s exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188075#issuecomment-6514597718) has no findings and rates the patch Platinum with Gold overall proof; the live capture it requested is included below. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![After the interrupted baseline read, only the existing context\.txt attachment remains\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dbac7f60-e108-4349-880d-135a0804af2b) | ![After resize and download completion, notes\.md joins context\.txt and the draft text remains\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ad796da-f7f4-44a0-a127-dd9c63deb3e9) | ### Exact\-head Files action, pending read, resize, and completed draft attachment https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ef91b72-306e-4ec5-b741-78f310c625d7 ### Visual verification - Baseline: faa38148f2c5ba3fe8f69bd3ae0150c87edf7758 - Exact head: `07da80ac7122b46431b46eddee8523fcd7dfedea` - Scenario: Attach notes\.md from Files while its real download is pending, resize the browser, and preserve existing unsent text and context\.txt\. Images use the same crop from a 1440×1000 desktop viewport\. - Runtime/build: Control UI 2026\.10\.9\-07da80ac7122; compatible isolated Gateway 9ca944e298b7\. Source\-built UI with original authorized file bytes\. - Authorized original file: 786 bytes; identical SHA\-256 before and after - Added attachment: Before 0; after exactly 1 notes\.md - Existing draft: context\.txt and unsent text preserved - Automatic sends: 0 - Original\-resolution before and after images inspected; same file, draft, viewport, theme and crop\. - Focused 8\.24\-second recording inspected across its full timeline, with full\-size menu and result frames\. - Real HTTP response held during resize; no synthetic replacement bytes\. - Production cancellation checks retained; independent review clean\.

prs.title: fix: show managed GitHub tools in session previews
prs.body: Fixes #187861 ## What Problem This Solves The session tool preview omits brokered GitHub tools that managed conversations can use. It can also omit permitted preparation actions or advertise actions and tools excluded by the session's policy or selected Codex runtime. This makes the preview unreliable when deciding what an agent can do next. The shared saved-sandbox policy correction from #188042 is landed and integrated. It makes preview callers use the existing sandbox policy; this PR supplies GitHub eligibility, prospective action metadata, Codex exclusions, and the safe compatibility notice. ## User Impact Supported managed sessions can discover the GitHub tools and actions their saved policy permits before credential or workspace preparation. Workspace-dependent actions remain conditional, and the preview grants no publication or merge authority. Unsupported runtimes, local embedded sessions, ACP ownership and explicit restrictions remain excluded. For a required-sandbox target with default policy, publication remains listed while identity-status is excluded, regardless of whether a guest or administrator views it. Compatible older Codex plugins without preview metadata retain the rest of their inventory. Only the two unqualified GitHub rows are omitted, with a notice that updating the plugin enables their preview. Execution access is unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made The preview supplies the brokered listing fact that tool registration already consumes. It selects the next-turn runtime, carries that runtime into the shared inventory, and keys the existing cache by runtime and GitHub eligibility. The shared sandbox prerequisite supplies the canonical policy to the existing capability profile; no GitHub-specific policy path or second cache is introduced. The GitHub constructor declares prospective actions before normal policy filtering. The inventory renders the surviving action list, so a preparation-only policy retains its tool while an inspection-only policy does not advertise excluded actions. These preview definitions cannot execute. Codex applies its existing exclusion policy through a small plugin-owned metadata surface that accepts and returns tool names. The facade owner distinguishes an absent surface from loading or parsing failures; core retains execution objects. Plugin-owner changes invalidate the cached partial preview. Narrow readers receive only the fixed compatibility notice and safe descriptions. The existing projection and test fixtures now live in coherent sibling files to keep the handler within its file-size limits. ## Evidence The real handler regressions cover managed and unavailable runtimes, historical harness metadata, ACP ownership, whole-tool and action restrictions, non-executable previews, runtime switching, and recovery after older plugin metadata becomes available. The runtime-exclusion regression fails on its prior implementation. The required-sandbox regression also fails on the prior public head: it receives identity-status plus publication where only publication is allowed. All 77 affected cases passed on the qualified `41868fc` tree: 38 handler, privacy and authenticated WebSocket access/revocation cases, 18 inventory-policy cases, and 21 direct-command cases. Formatting, lint, file-size/test-budget/mock-export guards, and the affected production and Gateway type graphs passed. The landed-prerequisite integration preserves every changed production/test file from that tree. Current formatting, structural and affected type checks passed on the exact integrated tree; the positive cases retain their qualified input match. Unchanged constructor, Codex artifact and consumer results retain their earlier qualified proof; the GitHub allocation is 223 lines, separate from the prerequisite's allocation. The combined runtime build passed, and its exported files, symlinks, source inputs and stamp were verified. On that isolated live runtime, guest and administrator previews of the same required-sandbox target contain the same 23 permitted names. Publication, read and search remain; identity-status is excluded. All 12 conditional publication actions match native discovery, with no discovered-tool calls or configuration/scope changes. The separate `/tools` caller passed all 22 cases and returned the same permitted names through ordinary guest and administrator submissions. The recording is pinned to the actual combined runtime `968a3fd`. Current PR source `6a449a6` retains identical policy inputs and an exactly equivalent extracted projection, with current handler/privacy/access tests validating the extraction. The two source identities are not interchangeable build claims. Positive live MCP cache warmth was not independently exposed after restart; warm-policy filtering retains its owner-level proof. The final comparison below shows the correction; the earlier media remains labeled as historical evidence. The original regression was also run on the landed prerequisite target: its successful preview still returned neither eligible GitHub tool. Current-head CI and the independent and hosted reviews are complete. Earlier consumer validation retained two QA health-wait failures reproduced on the clean base, in unchanged code passing fractional milliseconds to `AbortSignal.timeout`. A prior CI failure came from a stale handoff assertion repaired by #187979; that failed run remains failed. An older Bun fixture/snapshot failure did not reproduce in its bounded baseline replay and has no established fixed cause. Current-head CI completed successfully. The independent integration review is clean and confirms applicable regression reuse; the separate automated review remains qualified for the unchanged contribution. The exact-head hosted review rated overall readiness, proof confidence and patch quality Platinum, with no findings. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Guest preview lists 69 tools before applying saved sandbox policy](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89c264c6-c569-4964-a134-30838e9751c8) | ![Same guest preview lists 23 permitted tools after saved sandbox policy](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8cf92bc7-9e76-43ed-ab8e-44e260156ec9) | ### Guest opens Tools with saved sandbox policy applied https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af426e6c-cdc6-4c94-a214-f63ca1d485bb ### Visual verification - Baseline: 956162b118828540593be804143c0e99f60c5810 - Exact head: `968a3fd87707e17c717024ec9e4f33d548f8c8c8` - Scenario: Open Settings → Agents → Tools for the same existing required\-sandbox guest conversation\. The visible listed count changes from 69 to 23\. Complete authenticated responses retain github\_publish, github\_read and github\_search, and omit github\_identity\_status; exact names are outside this viewport\. Private workspace/model fields are masked only in the opening Overview frame\. Recorded source timings are retained in assembly and encoded at 25 fps, without a latency claim\. - Runtime/build: Actual integrated build 2026\.10\.9\-968a3fd87707\-2026\-10\-30T03\-03\-29\.651Z\. This PR retains the same policy and projection behavior; the file extraction and landed\-prerequisite integration have separate source/type/handler qualification\. The recording serves source 968a3fd\. - Visible listed count: 69 → 23 - GitHub membership: Publication/read/search retained; identity\-status excluded - Native discovery: 12 publication actions match; discovered\-tool calls: 0 - Authority: Guest and admin view the same target policy; config/scopes unchanged - Normal Settings navigation produced a complete response bound to the same retained target session\. - Guest and administrator responses contain the same 23 permitted names; richer admin descriptions remain separate\. - The 12 conditional publication actions match actual native search/describe metadata; no GitHub action executed\. - Saved preview 23 and admitted runtime catalog 25 have different contracts; full count/catalog equality is not claimed\. - Positive live MCP cache warmth is unproven after restart; required warm filtering reuses qualified owner\-policy tests\. prs.title: fix(ui): keep live context usage working during browser translation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser translation can replace the context counter's text-node anchors, leaving its displayed token count stale after real usage updates.

## User Impact

The numeric context readout continues updating while surrounding labels remain translatable. Only the language-neutral numeric region is exempt; translation is not disabled for the popover or chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the standard `translate="no"` attribute to the existing numeric region. This keeps external translators from replacing the nodes owned by live counter bindings, without adding rendering handlers, DOM restoration, wrappers or a global translation exemption. Usage accounting and data flow are unchanged. The contributor commit is retained.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway + local provider + Chromium differential, DOM receipts and inspected before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188061#issuecomment-6514752643)

Both refs were independently built, including identity-aligned production Control UI bundles. Real Chromium used the actual Gateways and deterministic local-provider completion/usage responses. Real model turns changed the Gateway context snapshot from 1,000 to 24,000 tokens; the correct displayed result is `24k / 180k · 13%`. No UI props, session usage or WebSocket responses were mocked, and no successful counter value was written by the harness.

Chrome-style nested FONT replacements were applied to the context header's eligible text nodes, respecting `translate="no"`. This is a scoped DOM-mutation simulation, not a claim to invoke Google's remote translation engine.

- **Main, twice:** five numeric nodes are replaced; after the real usage update the header remains stale at `1k / 180k · 1%`, even while Last run shows In 24k.
- **Candidate, twice:** zero numeric nodes are replaced; all five originals remain connected immediately after translation, and the counter updates correctly to 24k / 180k · 13%.
- **Controls:** all four no-translation runs update correctly. On both revisions the neighboring title stays translatable and is visibly translated to “Contexto traducido,” including in the refreshed candidate captures.

No browser exception was observed; the reproduced failure is stale counts. All eight scenarios pass their differential assertions. Full viewport captures and inspected closeups use the canonical same-frame screenshot helper.

The existing retention test now guards semantic translation scope alongside live usage, popover, provider-stat and focus behavior. The focused candidate test passes; the same regression fails on main because the counter is translatable. Formatting and type-aware lint pass with zero warnings/errors. Production +2/−1; tests +3/−3 (net zero), with no new repository test files. Final consolidation changes tests only after the proven production build.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores browser translation eligibility for this numeric region; no stored state or config is migrated. Blast radius is automatic browser translation of the context counter only. Application localization, human-readable labels, usage accounting and message delivery are unchanged.

prs.title: fix: require approval for dynamic shell predicates
prs.body:
## Summary

Require normal exec approval for predicates whose shell source can expand or be interpreted differently from parsed argv. This narrows the safe-builtin exemption introduced by #79363 and extended to predicates in the later builtin work, while retaining ordinary literal predicate checks. It complements the exact `-v` guard from #180880 and corrects the quote scanner added with the shared authorization planner in #84172.

## What Problem This Solves

### What this Problem Solves

In gateway `exec` allowlist mode, a predicate can appear harmless to `src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.ts` while Bash later synthesizes a different operand and runs an external command. `src/infra/exec-authorization-render.ts` can also miss a glob after an escaped quote in an ANSI-C string. Together, these mismatches can let a model supplied command cross the approval boundary without a matching allowlist entry or operator approval. The classifier now withholds automatic trust from ambiguous predicate source, and the renderer catches that escaped quote form before dispatch.

## What was wrong

1. `src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.ts` checked the parsed `test` or `[` argv for an exact `-v` token. Shell expansion could produce a different operand after that check.
2. `src/infra/exec-authorization-render.ts` treated an escaped single quote inside `$'...'` as the end of an ordinary single-quoted string, hiding a following glob from the enforced renderer.

The combined effect was automatic authorization of a command whose final Bash behavior exceeded the reviewed predicate.

## Why this design

- Grant the safe-builtin exemption only to predicate source with static operand syntax; route ambiguous forms through the existing approval policy.
- Track ANSI-C quoting and escaped quotes in the renderer so a later glob fails closed.
- Keep literal `test -d` and `[ -d ]` checks, including quoted paths with spaces, on the existing automatic path.
- Use the existing policy modes and configuration surface.

## Why this does not conflict with related PRs

| PR | Governed layer | Relation to this PR |
|---|---|---|
| #79363 | Safe-builtin convenience | Retains automatic handling for static predicates and other closed builtins. |
| #84172 | Shared authorization planning and source scanning | Corrects one ANSI-C quote-state case in that scanner. |
| #119351 | Preserve shell builtin semantics during enforced rendering | Keeps builtins in the shell; changes whether a predicate is automatically trusted. |
| #180880 | Exact parsed `-v` rejection | Preserves that guard and closes the residual source/argv mismatch. |

These changes are based on `main` after those PRs and change only the predicate trust and renderer checks.

## Evidence of Fix

| Path and mode | Command or probe run | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shared allowlist, no matching entry | `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs --input-type=module` source probe of the benign ANSI-C quote plus glob regression shape | `analysisOk=true`, `allowlistSatisfied=true`, `safeBuiltins`; new classifier test failed | `allowlistSatisfied=false`; classifier test passes |
| Enforced renderer | Same source probe and renderer regression test | Returned the unchanged command as `ok=true`; new renderer test failed | Returns `shell expansion in enforced arguments` |
| Gateway allowlist, approval off | Real Gateway E2E command in Testing; benign dynamic `test -e *.txt` plus allowlisted `printf` | Full gateway baseline was not run; the direct evaluator and renderer results above show the prerequisite automatic authorization | Rejects with `exec denied: allowlist miss` before process launch |
| Gateway allowlist, allow-once | Same real Gateway E2E with operator `exec.approval.resolve` RPC | Baseline approved path was not run | Actual process completed with exit code 0 and output `approved` |
| Gateway policy changed while approval was pending | Same real Gateway E2E; operator `exec.approvals.set` changed security to deny before allow-once resolution | Baseline revocation path was not run | Rejects stale approval with `Exec approval changed before execution`; no process result |
| Model-planned agent turn through a separate Gateway process | Deterministic local mock provider sent `chat.send` turns with `test -e proof.txt && pwd` and `test -e *.txt && pwd` under the same real allowlist/off policy; observed the paired `exec` tool outputs | With the original classifier and renderer temporarily restored, the new QA case failed at its dynamic-denial assertion while the static control passed | Static predicate returned the workspace path; dynamic predicate returned `exec denied: allowlist miss` and no `pwd` output |
| Ordinary static predicates | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | Existing literal checks passed | Literal `test` and `[` checks pass, including a quoted path with spaces |
| Published stable policy to patched head | Published `openclaw@2026.10.9` CLI `approvals set --file <synthetic-policy>`; patched `doctor --fix --non-interactive`, `approvals get --json`, then shared evaluator, all in isolated state | Stable CLI stored version-1 allowlist/on-miss policy with one agent allowlist entry | Doctor migration completed; patched CLI and canonical SQLite row retained defaults and allowlist. With that stored policy, `test -d .` remained automatic and `test -e *.txt` required approval |
| Focused suite | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.test.ts src/infra/exec-authorization-render.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-authorization.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | New classifier and renderer tests failed red before the implementation: 4 failures, 31 passes, 1 skip in the two-file run | 48 passes, 2 skips in the final three-file run |

The real-owner gateway test exercises operator approval RPC and the process supervisor; its approved outcome is observed at the process output, and its denied and policy-changed outcomes stop before execution.

## SDK / caller upgrade contract

Callers using ordinary static predicates keep automatic execution. Predicates with dynamic or ambiguous source syntax require the existing allowlist or approval decision; with approval disabled, they are denied. A policy written by the latest published stable CLI remained readable after the patched runtime's supported doctor migration, with the same defaults and agent allowlist. The classifier and real Gateway boundary tests cover these outcomes.

## Boundary decisions requested from maintainers

1. Exec maintainers: confirm the conservative approval behavior for quoted literal paths containing shell metacharacters is acceptable for this security boundary.

## Testing

- Added classifier, renderer, and gateway boundary regressions; final focused run: 48 passed, 2 skipped.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all 3 tests passed. The new predicate test uses the real Gateway and approval/process owners with no RPC or process mocks; the existing hook reload test now updates config through the Gateway's managed `config.patch` path to avoid a missed file-watcher event.
- Cross-process QA agent-turn E2E: focused case passed after matching each model-planned tool call to its result; the complete QA file passed 10/10 before that final assertion refinement (110.22 s Vitest, 127.03 s wrapper). The local provider is deterministic and does not represent a live model decision.
- Core TypeScript check, targeted oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Existing literal predicate tests and gateway authorization integration tests remain green.

prs.title: fix(ui): tool-call rows render oversized on iPhone Safari
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: collapsed tool-call rows in chat render at about 20px instead of 13px on iPhone Safari, so a single tool summary dominates the transcript.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/024ddc78-ce29-40c1-8995-fa0c5068b4b3)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/48380edf-f279-4c36-9888-cb8eec279e7d)

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone Safari shows compact tool-call rows again, matching desktop proportions. Desktop browsers receive the same CSS as before apart from one iOS-only declaration.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ui/src/styles/base.css` already locks `-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%` on `html, body` to stop iOS text boosting. Since the Control UI build started targeting `safari26.2` (#168595), the CSS minifier treats the prefix as unneeded and drops it from the production stylesheet. WebKit only implements the prefixed property, so iPhone Safari's text autosizing stayed on in production (the dev server never minified it, which is why it did not reproduce there).

iPhone autosizing boosts small single-line text inside blocks that are laid out wider than the screen. Long `white-space: nowrap` tool summaries hit that path; the recent tool-row redesign (#186041) made them prominent, but the boost itself comes from the missing prefix. Adding `ios26.2` to `build.target` (the same 26.2 floor already documented for iOS) keeps the prefix in the built CSS.

## Evidence

- **Regression test** (`ui/src/app/vite-build.node.test.ts`): builds with the real Control UI Vite config and asserts the output keeps `-webkit-text-size-adjust:100%`. Red on `main` (built CSS was `html{-moz-text-size-adjust:100%;text-size-adjust:100%}`), green with the fix. The 15 tests in that file pass.
- **Full production build diff** (`pnpm ui:build` with and without the change): across all CSS chunks, the only difference is `-webkit-text-size-adjust:100%` restored in the connection/boot stylesheet (+30 bytes). Total emitted JS size is byte-for-byte equal.
- **Deployed build**: the currently deployed Team build's CSS also lacks the prefixed declaration.
- **Real-device measurement** from the reporter's iPhone screenshot (390pt viewport): the tool row text measures about 19.7px against 13px specified, while the composer (16px) and chat body (14px) match their CSS. This is consistent with WebKit's one-line autosizing multiplier for 13px text, which only applies when `-webkit-text-size-adjust` is `auto`.
- **Browser captures**: mobile 390×844 (WebKit, light and dark) and desktop 1440×900 (Chromium) of the Control UI with a long exec tool summary show the intended 13px rows. Linux WebKit does not implement iOS text autosizing, so these show the target rendering rather than an iPhone reproduction. Before/after images were delivered in the originating conversation; I could not embed them here because the publishing identity has no supported image-upload path.
- **Local review**: autoreview (Codex engine, default P0 scope) on `origin/main..HEAD`: clean, no actionable findings.
- **Gaps**: no on-device iPhone check after the fix (needs a deploy). `ui/src/app/vite-config.node.test.ts` does not load locally because `@openclaw/net-policy/redact-sensitive-url` does not resolve in this checkout. That import is in an unchanged module, so this is a local setup issue, and CI covers the file.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: feat(claws): add local packages through the gateway and preserve setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Integrations cannot add a converted local Claw package through a running gateway: the gateway Add API only accepts ClawHub coordinates, while an offline writer cannot mutate live gateway state.

## User Impact

An admin-authorized client can plan and add an absolute local package path on the gateway host. Installation uses the existing Claw checks, lifecycle, plugin consent, integrity validation, and rollback. Retrying an installation that rolled back before agent creation preserves its first-run instructions. Imported memory and skills no longer cause the first turn to discard custom setup instructions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The source adapter feeds the existing Add owner:

```text
local package or ClawHub coordinate
  → resolve and inspect
  → plan + integrity check
  → native Add lifecycle
```

Local planning and application require `operator.admin`. Remote clients must transfer their package to the gateway host first. Rollback retires the existing workspace setup state along with a workspace it created and removed.

## Evidence

- Before: local source payload rejected by the gateway schema. After: an actual handler test installs instructions, the exact avatar bytes, and `BOOTSTRAP.md` as an ordinary agent.
- Before: failed Add → rollback → retry reports complete but omits `BOOTSTRAP.md`. After: the same actual-handler regression preserves the setup file.
- Regression coverage follows native Add through first-turn workspace preparation: imported memory and skills preserve a custom `BOOTSTRAP.md`; stock-template cleanup and explicit completion retain their existing behavior.
- Focused plan/apply, authorization, stale-source, schema, plugin handoff, and stateless rollback tests pass. Core type graphs, boundary checks, targeted lint and formatting pass.
- The full build passes, including CLI startup and plugin SDK export checks.
- Live isolated gateway proof at combined stack head `e33e4d5ca2b`: a fresh Stalk Bot installation completed a real agent turn with all 236 characters of custom setup instructions and 3,459 characters of memory injected without truncation. The setup file remains after the turn.
- Real WebSocket authorization regression passes for local packages: admin installation succeeds, nonadmin plan/apply is rejected, and real device-token revocation at the pre-effect gate prevents agent creation and plugin publication. The catalog positive control remains covered. No authority predicate is mocked; assertions cover agent configuration, installed-plugin records, and extension directories.
- Final setup regression and existing workspace sibling cases: 53 tests passed. Final runtime build passed; private workspace-logic changes do not alter the declaration/SDK export surface checked by the preceding full build.

**Merge risk:** reversible code change; affects the Claw Add source boundary and cleanup of newly created workspaces. Existing ClawHub behavior remains covered.

Prior-head CI blocker: the unchanged updater mock check also fails on [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991549274/job/117275051710); the [native classifier](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38992603758/job/117280609263) marks it pre-existing. That aggregate remains red; no exception or unrelated fix is included. The conflict-only stack restack onto `acd27635` preserves all three core patches exactly; current-head CI must run separately.

Additional private-QA full-build check: SDK declarations exceed the private testing budget. An isolated captured-main build produces the same 456 public-reachable declaration files byte-for-byte (5,440,829 bytes versus the 5,340,536-byte cap). No budget change or unrelated repair is included. Runtime/UI artifacts were generated; the full command is recorded as failed.

Compatibility evidence is scoped to the existing state contract and production boundaries. Compared directly with `v2026.10.4`, setup state remains version 1, `WorkspaceSetupState` fields are identical, and the complete `workspace_setup_state` SQL definition is byte-identical. The PR changes no persisted schema or config format. Existing completed state skips reconciliation; rollback cleanup only retires a newly created, uncommitted workspace. The 48 passing workspace cases plus 5 native Add cases cover retained completed timestamps/content, stock cleanup, concurrent completion, custom pending setup, and explicit completion. This is not a claim that a full product upgrade was executed.

Paired saved runtime proof: before the setup fix (`5ffb1320fcc`), `bootstrapExists=false` and `bootstrapInjected=false`; after (`e33e4d5ca2b`), `BOOTSTRAP.md` injected 236/236 characters without truncation and remained present after the turn. The baseline predates the fix; it is not an exact current-merge-base replay.

## Main refresh (2026-10-27)

Merged current `main` (`cfccaef15a4`) into this branch instead of rebasing, so the stacked #174960 keeps its history. Conflicts were resolved against main's publisher package names, Claw drafts, workspace attestation hashes, and rollback effect leases; the gateway validators were regenerated.

Main's Gateway Add now holds plural state leases (#184784), but its bootstrap setup-state write still requested generic worker admission, so lease admission refused every Claw that ships `BOOTSTRAP.md` ("State lease worker ownership was refused"). `8d64690136b` passes the held lease identities to the worker and asserts them inside the transaction, as worktree capacity does. The existing local Add handler test fails on the unfixed code and passes with the fix; it now confirms the Gateway config-write application, which main's Add requires.

Local proof on `ed5ea8ff143`: 14 focused test files pass (Claw Add plan/apply/stateless/manifest, local handler, Gateway method scopes, workspace and bootstrap, agent creation, state-lease transactions; 2m17s wall with `--maxWorkers=1`); `tsgo:core`, core src test types, oxlint, oxfmt, `protocol:check`, and `gateway:validators:check` pass. The real-Gateway e2e was not rerun locally; PR CI covers it.

Upgrade compatibility after the refresh (ClawSweeper's data-model request): the PR's diff against `main` touches no persisted schema, migration, config, or Doctor file. Its only schema change is the Gateway wire protocol (Add request params and the plan-response manifest disclosure), which is not stored. Lease identities travel only in the in-process worker command. The `workspace_setup_state` table and `WorkspaceSetupState` shape belong to `main` and this PR leaves them unchanged. Existing completed setup still skips reconciliation; a never-completed workspace with a custom `BOOTSTRAP.md` now stays pending until setup completes, which is the intended fix.

prs.title: fix(codex): shed abandoned cleared bindings at namespace capacity
prs.body:
Fixes #125910.

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex app-server thread-binding namespace rejects new bindings after 50,000 rows accumulate, leaving later requests unavailable until the state database is cleaned manually.

## Why This Change Was Made

Earlier revisions of this PR moved the namespace to evict-oldest, which let the SQLite store delete binding rows it cannot read: retirement fences, legacy-clear provenance, live leases, and active sessions all ranked the same as garbage. This revision keeps reject-new everywhere and puts capacity recovery at the binding domain boundary.

`session-binding-overflow.ts` wraps the composed binding store's `mutate`, the only insert path. When an insert fails with a row-count limit error, the wrapper pages the worker-backed handle on the same namespace with `entriesInKeyRange` (512-row pages, storage-side ordering, decode in the storage worker) and sheds up to a few strictly validated disposable rows per failure through `observe` + `compareAndApply`, then retries. A lexical cursor persists across calls and wraps at the end of the namespace, so spaced failures keep advancing instead of re-reading the same protected prefix, and rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered. Destructive eligibility is decided on the raw record, not the tolerant codec: a lease in any malformed shape, a retirement marker in any shape at all, and any non-object row are preserved as ambiguous. Everything else (active bindings, retirement fences, live leases, `conversation:legacy-` provenance) fails closed with the original limit error, and hosts without ranged listing stand down the same way instead of scanning inline.

The sync store stays exactly where it was: hot reads. Listing and deletion during recovery run on the worker side of the store broker, so a full namespace never turns into a whole-table decode on the Gateway thread.

Sidecar migration keeps its main-branch reject-new store: at capacity the existing failure path retains the source, and no live row can be displaced by an import.

## User Impact

A namespace clogged with abandoned cleared rows recovers on its own instead of hard-failing every new session. Fences, leases, legacy-clear provenance, live bindings, and every ambiguous existing record are never shed; when nothing strictly disposable exists the limit error surfaces unchanged.

## Evidence

- `session-binding-overflow.test.ts` (17 tests; runs in the database-workers shard on the forks pool for the broker): recovery sheds an abandoned cleared row while an older live binding survives; fail-closed when the namespace holds only a retirement fence plus a live binding; a live lease is never shed; legacy-clear provenance survives recovery while an abandoned row next to it is shed; a cleared row with a non-object lease is preserved while a strictly valid abandoned row next to it is shed; a namespace of only ambiguous rows rejects with both rows intact; a host without ranged listing propagates the limit error with no inline scan; recovery through `createLazyCodexAppServerBindingStore(state, undefined, recoveryState)`, the exact production composition; a scan stalls mid-prefix under a one-page budget and the next insert resumes from the persisted cursor and succeeds (goes red when cursor persistence is broken); rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered.
- `session-binding-overflow.registered-path.test.ts` (new): the real extension entry boots and builds the binding store plus the lazy recovery adapter from `api.runtime.state` itself; the openers delegate to the plugin-state test factories (same worker-backed SQLite stores, fixture module resolution; production additionally needs the Gateway host broker no in-process test has), with the binding namespace cap clamped 50,000 -> 3 as the only knob. Through that registered assembly: a fresh session's lease admission overflows, recovers, starts exactly once, and sheds exactly the disposable cleared row while the live binding and a held row survive; and a caller whose authority is revoked at admission gets zero deletes with the disposable row intact.
- Real run, isolated state dir, production plugin-state store plus the production lazy composition over real SQLite at capacity (3/3: retired fence, live-leased cleared row, abandoned cleared row): the insert recovers, only the abandoned row is shed, both protected rows survive, and a fresh store handle on the same database still shows fence + lease + the new binding afterwards. Verbatim output is in the review reply below.
- `doctor-contract-api.overflow.test.ts`: at capacity the sidecar source is retained, nothing is imported, and the pre-existing row is intact (limit error injected through the production registration path); a revisited legacy sidecar cannot resurrect its cleared thread because the canonical cleared marker wins and the source archives without its row.
- Sibling Codex checkout inspection (`../codex`, origin/main 286d4ecf44): threads persist durably as rollout files plus the state db with paged listing and no retention eviction (`codex-rs/rollout/src/state_db.rs:352`, `codex-rs/rollout/src/maintenance.rs`), so shedding an abandoned OpenClaw binding row can never delete native Codex data.
- Before the final test-lint and format-only follow-ups, the full `extensions/codex` suite, `check-changed` lanes, and fresh `$autoreview` were clean with no actionable findings.
- At prior head `e721d349d2b6c9dca567e240c681829378c8fc45`, the registered-path test lint findings and the two overflow files' formatting were addressed without changing recovery behavior. PR CI at that head was green, including `check-test-types`. The xAI type failure seen at `f8d62fcb212d7adb73e5a51f89a3be618be7623f` was fixed upstream by #177830, and this PR does not change xAI.
- At current head `58efcd3c65f944499b2ff7454f05787e4ecadccc`, the final-delete negative control now starts revocation only after the unbound observation completes, limits rejection to caller-bound stores, and asserts exactly one `compareAndApply(delete)` attempt before rejection while preserving the disposable row. The strengthened assertion failed with zero attempts before the timing correction and passes with one after it. The low-value source-snippet inventory was removed; the registered production-path behavior test remains.
- Current validation: both overflow files passed 18/18 tests in 9.05s warm; the boundary suite passed 12/12 in 4.05s; oxlint, oxfmt, and production extension typecheck passed. Full extension-test typecheck passed with the already-landed #177830 xAI baseline fix temporarily overlaid and then restored. Without that overlay, the local branch reports only the known xAI baseline error, not an error in this PR's changed files.

Remaining evidence gaps: this head strengthens the final-delete negative control but does not supply a shipped Gateway fresh-session recovery trace with real session reset/reassignment lineage, a latest-stable upgrade run, or the maintainer's retention-policy decision. Those gates remain open and are not represented as complete here.

## What this PR is not

This is a partial fix with one open policy decision and no claim to close the underlying issue's storage architecture. Shedding strictly validated abandoned cleared rows is a durable-retention change, and it needs an explicit maintainer decision before merge; the review thread carries the full inventory. The store-level eviction primitive (storage-side disposal by policy rather than a domain-side sweep) remains the owner's call, as does any broader migration of the sync binding reads onto the async handle.
