prs.title: fix(supervisor): service-child anchors abort on Node 26 when stdin is /dev/null (2026.10.10 backport)
prs.body:
Backport of #187803 to `release/2026.10.10`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on Node 26 (macOS), a service-child group anchor whose stdin is `/dev/null` aborts with SIGABRT during retirement, before it sends its closing receipt. This makes `service-child-group-anchor.retirement.test.ts` fail 9 of 16 cases deterministically on Node 26.12.1. The failure is already present at `v2026.10.10-beta.4`, so it is not a beta.5 regression. Hosted CI runs Node 24, so it never saw it.

## User Impact

User impact: service-child anchors retire cleanly on Node 26 whatever their stdin is. In the Gateway's production launch path, anchors get a pipe as stdin whenever input is relayed, so no Gateway failure has been observed. This removes a latent abort and makes the release branch's anchor tests pass on Node 26.

## Why This Change Was Made

The anchor's `process.stdin.destroy()` calls in `finish()` and `stopInput()` now use `releaseProcessStdin()`, which was already on this branch from #187553. On Node 26, destroying a `/dev/null` stdin ReadStream closes fd 0. On this branch the macOS process census then runs `spawnSync("/bin/ps")`, which gets fd 0 for a pipe, and libuv's `uv__close` assertion aborts the process.

Release-only adjustment: the import pushes this file to 701 lines, over `max-lines` (700). Two `destination.once(...)` calls are chained onto one line to stay under the limit, with no change in behavior. The main PR's new regression test is not backported because it depends on main's `anchor-protocol.test-support.ts` fixture. The existing retirement test on this branch already reproduces the failure on Node 26 macOS.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/process/supervisor/service-child-group-anchor.retirement.test.ts`
  - Before, Node 26.12.1: 9 failed / 7 passed. The anchor exits with `{ code: null, signal: "SIGABRT" }`. The macOS crash report shows `abort <- __assert_rtn <- uv__close <- uv__loop_close <- SyncProcessRunner::CloseHandlesAndDeleteLoop`.
  - After: 16/16 pass on Node 26.12.1 and on Node 24.22.1.
- Retirement, input-lifetime and preparation anchor tests plus `release-stdin.test.ts` pass on Node 26.12.1 and on Node 24.22.1.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on the changed file.

prs.title: fix: personal memory hooks miss authenticated webchat users
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes personal-memory hooks receiving no user identity for authenticated Control UI turns, causing integrations such as Honcho to fall back to an owner peer even when the transcript identifies a different person.

## User Impact

Hooks can observe the verified initiating user for each accepted UI turn, including successive turns by different people in one shared session. This does not add command, tool, or MCP permissions. Expired personal bindings skip hook dispatch or discard returned enrichment instead of becoming anonymous owner turns.

Attribution remains per accepted initiating turn; this does not add separate authorship for every coauthor merged through steering. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Control UI intentionally omits the legacy transport sender to preserve authority boundaries. The fix carries a live, host-bound profile observation through the existing run projections solely for hook context. Dispatch rechecks it before invoking a plugin and before accepting returned results, including cached contexts and delegated ingress. The private observer reads in the captured ingress async context, so a later agent tool context does not misclassify the original human request. Live grant checks still run on every read; plugin callbacks never run in that captured context. Existing channel senders retain precedence, and the private resolver is removed before plugin delivery.

An existing pure finalize-result merger is moved unchanged to keep the edited hook runner within the repository line-cap ratchet.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced against the original Gateway turn preparation path: an authenticated profile was recorded, but the hook sender was undefined.
- Eight focused test files initially passed (248 tests); the final Gateway/requester/hook bundle passed **175 tests** after adding the real agent-context regressions, covering Gateway identity, prepared-run projections, CLI/embedded hook consumers, prefix stability, profile switches, delegated revocation/abort, copied bindings, cached contexts, and revocation while handlers resolve or reject.
- Native core production typecheck and both unused-file inventories passed; the extracted helper is reachable. Diff, format, line-cap, and safety-assertion checks passed.
- Independent source/security review and simplification pass completed; the material revocation and claiming-hook findings were fixed. The finalize-merger extraction was also compared byte for byte after dedenting. Optional autoreview/ClawSweeper tools are not installed on this contributor host.
- Clean native build: `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build` passed on Node 24.22.1, including runtime, SDK declarations, Control UI assets and native import/export checks.
- **Real isolated Gateway + real agent + real model:** three authenticated Control UI protocol turns passed: person A in a private draft, A in a shared session, then B in the same shared session. A synthetic probe plugin selected the correct personal marker for each model answer; both lookup and `agent_end` received the correct initiating profile. The fixture used native trusted-proxy authentication, device signatures, explicit roles, matching build admission and provider-scoped plugin activation. This is protocol-level proof with a synthetic memory plugin, not a live Honcho storage migration or visual browser test.
- Final scoped messaging typecheck, native lint on all 15 changed TypeScript files, format, safety assertions, test-line allocation and line-cap gates passed.
- The optional aggregate smart check reported an unresolved unused export (`sanitizeVerboseQuery` in `src/daemon/schtasks.integration-observation.test-support.ts`) outside the touched files. It is not claimed as a pass or as baseline-proven pre-existing; production/full-tree unused-file inventories and the scoped checks above passed.

### Current-main refresh (2026-10-30)

Merged current main `315380c4` without rewriting the original contribution; the PR head is `f9ed2281`. The conflict resolution preserves both the native transferred-requester profile APIs and this PR's hook observation context.

Validation at the refreshed head: 222 tests across five affected files passed, together with the messaging typecheck, focused lint of all 15 changed TypeScript files, formatting and ratchet checks. The earlier real Gateway/model proof remains evidence for `70a2f514`; it has not been repeated at this merge head. Current-head upstream CI is running.

prs.title: fix(codex): show live reasoning and retain separate items in chat history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing live reasoning and combined or hidden saved reasoning items during Codex-backed Control UI conversations.

## User Impact

Users can follow each exposed native reasoning item while a turn runs and revisit those separate items beside commentary and tools after reload. Existing `/reasoning on|off|stream` and **View → Reasoning** controls continue to select visibility. Assistant commentary and previously saved aggregate summaries retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native reasoning projector now publishes live agent events independently of optional channel callbacks and checkpoints completed items through the existing transcript owner. Saved display history retains reasoning-only rows, and the browser snapshot projection version advances so an old cursor cannot keep recovered reasoning hidden.

This reuses the existing event, checkpoint, receipt-clock, and cache owners; it adds no configuration, dependencies, database schema, or parallel renderer. Per-item timestamps and completion facts are necessary to preserve identity and durability.

## Evidence

- **Fresh real-provider proof:** one native Codex turn through an isolated Gateway and actual Chromium Control UI emitted ten reasoning items without prompting for reasoning/status updates. First WebSocket text arrived at 26.116 seconds and partial DOM text at 26.532 seconds; the turn ended at 550.080 seconds. All ten had live DOM observations, persistence receipts, and read-only durable-row observations before completion.
- Native rollout text and saved individual Markdown text/order match exactly. Completed history contains ten distinct full visible-text DOM blocks in durable order; identities, indices, text hashes, and lengths survive reload after loading earlier history.
- **281 distinct locally executed tests passed:** 84 cache/startup/store, 74 Codex projector/checkpoint/transcript, 83 Gateway history, 24 lifecycle, one actual native-process finalization scenario, seven Chromium scenarios, and eight outcome/fallback contract cases. The two cache-upgrade regressions failed before the projection-version repair and passed with it. The repeated visibility subset is not counted twice.
- Full production build, focused type/lint/format checks, test-line allocation, and affected Codex/Telegram/Slack package boundaries passed. The installed candidate's 14,802 compiled runtime/UI files matched its canonical archive and validated build. Later commits only adjust test expectations/allocations; runtime code is unchanged from the validated build commit.
- Local independent source review, final-head ClawSweeper review, and a supplemental live-evidence review found no actionable code/security findings. [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188076#issuecomment-6514713098) also found no actionable correctness/security findings on `30c9fc4b` and accepted the shipped-flow evidence as sufficient. [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41000380458) passed on `30c9fc4ba845bae201454d552122730a6282f07b`: 52 successful jobs, 24 skipped, no failures.

**CI repair:** [The first PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40998878789) passed 50 jobs and exposed one missed consumer expectation: the outcome/fallback contract still expected a turn-wide reasoning identity. The exact failure reproduced locally. Updating that expectation to the fixture’s per-item identity makes the selected scenario and all eight file cases pass; reasoning text, empty-answer, classification, and fallback-code assertions remain intact. The full file took 28.06 seconds locally (91 ms in test bodies); all eight cases also passed in CI (60 ms in test bodies, within a 187-test/18-file shard that took 59.88 seconds). This correction changes no runtime code. Its two additional formatted lines bring the exact test allocation to 239, preserving the separate boundary regressions; no shared baseline changes.

![Earlier baseline conversation without the restored individual reasoning presentation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94156f8d-e7a6-4555-94e1-c48261fc0340)

**After — two separate reasoning blocks alongside commentary and commands while the real turn was running:**

![Separate native reasoning items during the live Codex turn](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/546df5a6-fb6c-421b-a060-70763731af7b)

**After reload — first and last portions retain distinct full-text reasoning blocks:**

![First reasoning items preserved after reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74915d41-db4d-4dab-b9e2-e930de6a2918)

![Last reasoning items preserved after reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3281186d-2873-4ae4-9ac9-d66d39805009)

<details>
<summary>Validation limits and known unrelated check</summary>

The live observer recovered from screenshot/scroll element detachment and a stale work-group click without resubmitting the coding prompt. Original live timing/hash facts were reconciled against durable text; the capture is not an uninterrupted complete WebSocket log. The completed-history check exercises the actual **Show earlier** control and compares complete visible text after the observed Markdown formatting/link-label conversion, separately from raw native/saved equality. Screenshots illustrate selected items; DOM assertions cover all ten.

The package's build-info retains its original base-commit label; the build stamp and complete compiled-file comparison identify the validated runtime. No provenance was relabeled.

`deadcode:unused-files` passed its production scan; its full-tree scan flagged only the pre-existing `scripts/perf/update-state-io-measure.ts`, whose base/head blob is identical. No ignore/baseline exception was added.

Accepted recovery tradeoff: an unfinished reasoning item cannot block completed tools from reaching disk; its partial text is retained at terminal settlement. Historical aggregate summaries are not reconstructed into individual items.

Current-main source/merge audit through `9b09947e66735c29e69d96ab3d26e4782a89d411` has a clean computed merge. That audit is not combined-tree runtime or PR CI proof. Local evidence remains available; credentials, model identities, configs, and unrelated transcripts are excluded from this PR.

prs.title: fix: keep pnpm fallback caches out of guest workspace sync
prs.body:
Closes #188068.

## What Problem This Solves

Installing a nested project from a managed guest shell can make pnpm select `.openclaw/.pnpm-store` when its normal home store cannot hard-link across the protected `.openclaw` mount. That fallback currently enters ordinary workspace synchronization as authored content. A real one-package installation copied 54 generated store files into the canonical project; larger stores can also consume the existing result limits.

## User Impact

The exact checkout-root fallback store stays with its producing runtime. Authored siblings, nested project fixtures and genuine staged inputs retain their existing preservation rules, and the authored-file limits remain unchanged. This does not purge cache files already present on either side.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared generated-path classifier already owns capture, transfer, reconciliation and recovery. Adding this specific native fallback root there keeps those consumers consistent without changing pnpm configuration, HOME, sandbox mounts or permissions. The two embedded manifest consumers are regenerated from that owner.

The existing case matrix now includes the fallback root and its neighboring preserved paths. Its recovery fixture also places dependency caches in the old accepted baseline, so a policy update must preserve physical cache bytes rather than interpret newly ignored entries as authored deletions. Five net fixture lines are allocated for those cases; no new test harness or production abstraction is introduced.

## Evidence

The live before-case used the maintained common image, pnpm 12.15.0 and an authenticated local semver archive with guest networking disabled. A root-launched shell changed into the nested project while retaining HOME at `/workspace`; native pnpm selected `.openclaw/.pnpm-store/v11`. The store was absent from both copies beforehand. After the single install and normal synchronization, both contained 54 files, including a verified content-addressed object hard-linked to the installed package. A separate turn preserved the authored edits, original staged inputs and usable package.

The extended owner regression was red on unchanged production code: it admitted the fallback cache file and its cache-only ancestry; eight other cases passed. The correction passed changed-file format/lint, generated-script consistency, the selected production/test type checks and the test-line ratchet. The eight related files have 140 passing cases and one existing opt-in skip across qualified runs. The strengthened 54-case projection/recovery file passed in 201.77 seconds, including native worker preparation; the tooling file passed seven cases in 1.52 seconds after its required pinned Bun runtime was prepared.

A live recurrence check is still pending on a qualified fixed runtime: a different already-locked semver archive must generate a new cache object absent from the canonical workspace, while the old canonical files and authored/staged controls remain preserved. Hosted CI, independent review and that live after-proof remain required before landing.

The live reproduction did not inflate a file or replay the historical 64 MiB rejection. The existing boundary matrix covers generated-root exclusion and preserved inputs separately from live installation and synchronization.

prs.title: fix(msteams): channel directory search drops channels with NFD-normalized names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: MS Teams channel directory search silently drops channels whose displayName differs in Unicode normalization form (e.g. NFD-stored names from macOS clients vs NFC-typed queries, or NFD queries from macOS input methods vs NFC-stored names).

## User Impact

User impact: searching the Teams channel directory now matches channel names regardless of NFC/NFD normalization differences; previously matching channels were silently missing from results. Pure-ASCII names behave exactly as before, and returned entries keep their original spelling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The channel-name substring filter in `listMSTeamsDirectoryGroupsLive` compared trim+lowercased strings at the UTF-16 code-unit level without canonical-equivalence normalization, so canonically equal names failed `includes()` and were skipped. Both the query side and the displayName side now go through `.normalize("NFC")`, matching the existing directory-search idiom in `extensions/buzz/src/directory-query.ts` ("Canonical forms compare equal here; directory entries keep their original spelling"). Team-name search is unchanged (server-side Graph `$search`); the peers path is also server-side.

## Evidence

### Before fix

New regression tests on unpatched code fail (channels silently dropped):

```
FAIL  extensions/msteams/src/directory-live.test.ts > matches channels by canonically equivalent names across NFC and NFD forms
FAIL  extensions/msteams/src/directory-live.test.ts > matches an NFD channel query against NFC channel names
Tests  2 failed | 7 passed (9)
```

Runtime check of the matching logic:

```
NFD channel name vs NFC query:  raw includes: false  (channel dropped)
NFC channel name vs NFD query:  raw includes: false  (channel dropped)
```

### After fix

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  9 passed (9)   (extensions/msteams/src/directory-live.test.ts)
```

Sibling directory contract tests: `extensions/msteams/src/directory-contract.test.ts` 2/2 passed.

- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json <changed files>`: 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `oxfmt` applied; no other formatting drift
- `tsgo:extensions` could not run on this host (prebuilt tsgo binary requires GLIBC_2.32+; system glibc is older). Stock `tsc -p tsconfig.extensions.json` fallback reports zero errors in the changed files (only pre-existing unrelated declaration-portability noise in codex/line/nostr/etc. remains).

### What was not tested

- Real Microsoft Graph API behavior with NFD-stored channel displayNames (unit level mocked via the existing graph layer mocks; Graph server-side team `$search` untouched).
- `tsgo:extensions` / `tsgo:extensions:test` native gates (glibc limitation on this host; see Evidence for fallback).

Follow-up note: `extensions/slack/src/directory-live.ts` and `extensions/whatsapp/src/directory-config.ts` use the same normalize-then-`includes` pattern without NFC and may share this bug class; intentionally out of scope here.

prs.title: fix: keep expanded table Close above sticky headers
prs.body: Fixes #188053. ## What Problem This Solves In an expanded Markdown table, the sticky header can cover the left half of the Close X and intercept clicks on that part of the button. The center already closes the view normally; this repair restores the complete affordance and pointer target. ## User Impact Readers can see the full Close glyph and dismiss an expanded table from the previously covered side, including after scrolling beneath the sticky header. The table’s layout, content and scrolling stay the same, along with the existing Escape, backdrop and focus-return behavior. No configuration or migration is needed. ## Why This Change Was Made The table header is painted above ordinary positioned content, while Close previously had no explicit stacking order. The fix places the existing Close control just above that header within the modal. It leaves the shared modal owner and table markup unchanged. The existing browser interaction test now checks native hit targets across the button and clicks its left side after scrolling. It retains its Escape and focus checks. The 17-line test allocation covers this distinct missing regression; the shared test ceiling is unchanged. ## Evidence A fresh synthetic guest conversation on the selected source produced a 24-row garden checklist through ordinary chat. At 1440×1000 in the light theme, the settled header covered 8 of 16 pixels of the X and a left-side click reached a header cell. Center Close still worked and preserved the draft. The new regression failed on the original stylesheet at its hit-target assertion. With the correction, the live page returned Close for all nine sampled button points; activating the previously intercepted side dismissed the table and preserved the draft. Remote changed-file formatting, lint, style/i18n checks and the native affected type plan passed on the committed tree. All 12 related test files passed (102 tests), including the full 13-case table interaction suite. That existing multi-route E2E file took 41.80 seconds wall time, including its production UI fixture; the complete related-test invocation took 56.20 seconds. Hosted CI passed the same 13-case table interaction file; Vitest reported 36.10 seconds for the test module (job `checks-ui-e2e (6/7)`). Canonical Auto Review of base 719247f96bac8963b20007767ae199241c8293f2 through head 7458683ce18499ca3b9579bfcc2f132b58384396 completed clean at P0–P3 with no actionable findings. The separate independent engineering review is clean. Exact-head Chromium and WebKit guest checks passed for native hit targets, sticky scrolling, pointer dismissal, draft retention and returned focus; Chromium also covered Escape, backdrop dismissal and a narrow dark view. The initial hosted CI attempt failed in a session-diff color assertion when its token became detached. The identical 57-file, 210-test shard passed on the base, and one unchanged hosted-job rerun passed all 57 files and 210 tests, including that case; the current CI gate is green. No source change was made for this failure, and its cause remains unconfirmed. ClawSweeper also completed an exact-head Diamond review with no findings. ## Visual evidence []() | View | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Desktop light: 1440 × 1000 browser, modal crop | ![Sticky table header covers the left half of Close](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e94b81a-1582-4bb9-88da-7f5cdf6d7150) | ![Full Close glyph appears above the sticky table header](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf75f73f-4b7a-439d-a25d-f51e8c279f34) | | Narrow dark: 760 × 900 browser, modal crop | ![Narrow dark table with partly covered Close glyph](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba4f1c31-f208-4771-83b8-a5e61925a476) | ![Narrow dark table with complete Close glyph](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/afab4410-a27e-48bd-a695-420601cdd642) | ### Exact\-head interaction recording, half\-speed replay with external captions https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6dd0a23-f0a8-4bf4-8248-a8864962cca0 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 719247f96bac8963b20007767ae199241c8293f2 - Exact head: `7458683ce18499ca3b9579bfcc2f132b58384396` - Scenario: Open the garden checklist, scroll beneath its sticky header, and dismiss using the formerly intercepted left side of Close\. Escape, backdrop and draft/focus preservation are also checked\. - Runtime/build: Source\-backed Control UI 2026\.10\.9\-7458683ce184; native guest Gateway 2026\.10\.9\-9ca944e298b7\. Chromium 156 and WebKit 27\.2\. - Covered glyph width: Before: 8 of 16 pixels; after: 0 of 16 pixels - Close pointer target: 9 of 9 sampled points reach Close; formerly intercepted left\-side click dismisses - Sticky header: Pinned and painted at scrollTop 196 after a 500 px wheel input - Conversation state: 24 original rows retained; unsent draft preserved; focus returned to Expand - Each still pair uses the same browser viewport \(1440 × 1000 or 760 × 900\), DPR 1, theme, route, 24\-row content, zoom and modal crop\. Capture dimensions describe the modal crop\. - The recording crops only the top 32 px of unrelated browser chrome and adds a 120 px caption band below the product\. The complete Close target, table and draft remain visible\. Half\-speed playback is labeled\. - Actual committed clean\-head document and loaded CSS/module response hashes verified separately from Gateway/profile identity\. - Chromium and WebKit live pointer, sticky\-header, draft and focus checks passed; narrow dark sibling passed\. - No new model turn during after\-proof; captures contain only synthetic garden content\. - Recording\-only capture avoids clipped screenshots during recording; the scene ends before clearing the disposable test draft\.

prs.title: feat(codex): support command-auth custom Responses providers
prs.body:
Related: #131261 (custom Codex providers and platform credential proxies; this does not implement the historical provider-ID proposal).

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot use a custom Responses provider's Codex-owned token command without OpenClaw looking for unrelated host credentials.

## User Impact

Custom providers can opt into `auth: "native-command"`. OpenClaw selects the provider/runtime without borrowing host profiles or ambient OpenAI credentials; Codex owns its token command and other explicitly configured native authentication, including `gateway_oauth`.

Use an **unowned custom provider ID**, explicitly configure Codex at the model/provider level, and configure a matching native command-auth provider. The effective native route must match the configured HTTPS Responses endpoint. URL credentials/fragments, OpenClaw API keys/profile pins, OpenClaw custom headers and authored request/transport overrides remain rejected. A forced environment runtime alone is insufficient. Native configuration, native headers, primary-auth conflicts and secondary account persistence/refresh remain Codex's responsibility; a native account is not implicitly the Team requester. This adds no OpenClaw login flow or native-to-host credential import.

**Ordinary sessions only:** isolated completions, supervised native sessions, manual compaction and remote-exec cloud placement remain unsupported. Native automatic compaction remains available; final-answer recovery uses the settled-tool fallback rather than another credential. Direct host credential APIs reject this mode. First-party/main-session explicit-profile validation, operator-model policy and approval-review boundaries remain intact. P8 worker-hosted transport is outside this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

One shared eligibility owner serves availability, harness support and preparation. Dispatch skips unrelated automatic OpenAI accounts and stale automatic pins; the native preflight checks the selected endpoint and command before creating a thread. It no longer duplicates Codex's authentication policy or rejects supported native credential composition.

The PR also retains separately reviewed offline-archive and fixed Node/Bun prerequisites in the existing isolated runner. Neither relaxes isolation or changes native dependency versions.

## Evidence

**Published CI-repair head:** `cc3a0fc854b5ac81e0de579ebd4ef876816d5e83`; tree `c66ade1bc207bf045232dd7a8a3bdaae9dfd7257`, identical across all paths to reviewed implementation `b34e1df4ad50bc654430849316e9fb91fd021d76`. The managed publisher added only an empty attribution/receipt commit. **New-head CI is pending verification, not a green result.** GitHub currently reports `mergeable: false` / `mergeState: dirty`; no source integration was performed in this publication-only step. Repair: **8 files, +154/−9**. Whole PR versus integrated canonical `1ae91`: **63 files, +2,010/−353**. No product authentication policy, native version, test deadline, ignore, scanner policy or public configuration changed.

### Prior published-head CI failure and causal disposition

[CI 40992085851](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40992085851) is **terminal red**, not pending. Its actual tested merge source combined published `606da10` with canonical `87016c018d3e4a4c44e34de96bb3cea25b28548c`.

| Failed leaf | Native classification | Source-grounded disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Additional boundaries](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40992085851/job/123857101591) | New | This PR's native OAuth test-support callback used raw fetch. Replaced by the existing guarded-fetch SDK, exact loopback-origin policy, no redirects and final transport release. Guard is red on prior `606da10` source and green on the repair. |
| [Changed Node tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40992085851/job/123857102230) | Unknown/no matching main job | **PR-caused prerequisite defect:** CI actually selected the full native Gateway E2E under pinned Bun. The primary case passed; combined setup lacked `gnome-keyring-daemon`, then emitted an unhandled spawn error and attempted cleanup of an unspawned child. The existing CI manifest/setup owner now provisions the required Linux binaries only for selected native-auth rows; the fixture awaits spawn/error before taking cleanup ownership. |
| [Compact-small tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40992085851/job/123857102228) | Unknown/no matching main job | All five `ci-workflow-planning.test.ts` stripe failures reproduce on exact canonical `87016c` with the same expected [1,4]/actual [1] differences. Canonical `2106751bd18895e92318282a6f881dfa77c1ad67` (#188011) packs two selected type graphs into one stripe; these assertions still expect two. This repair does not alter those assertions or planner behavior. |

**Correction to earlier evidence:** the previous statement that automatic CI never selects this full Gateway composition was wrong. Changed-node CI does select it, including with Bun; docs now say so. No skip, opt-out or lower-frequency route was introduced to hide the failure.

### Repair proof and its limits

- Actual repository raw-fetch boundary: **red → green**, without an allowlist exception. Callback remains `127.0.0.1` on its exact native origin, redirects are refused, and response/dispatcher cleanup is awaited.
- Missing-executable lifecycle regression: **red → green**. The real already-started synthetic bus child is joined and its private root removed; the original ENOENT reaches the caller without an unhandled event or ownership of a nonexistent process.
- Existing manifest/workflow regression: **red → green** for direct and packed native-auth selections, with an unrelated selection remaining false. It verifies the setup action input and required packages. Four final focused tests pass; other cases were deliberately unselected, not reported as a full-suite pass.
- **Real contained pinned-Bun combined-auth proof passed:** 30.108s test / 67.91s Vitest / 300.140s full invocation. It used real task-private D-Bus/Secret Service, native login/storage, a restarted native process, refresh, intended primary+secondary credentials, host decoys and the visible `agent.wait` answer. One combined case passed; primary was unselected in this diagnostic invocation. Container absence was confirmed. Temporary startup stderr/exit observations used for this diagnosis were removed afterward; no runtime behavior or assertion was changed.
- A standalone real private Secret Service probe under pinned Bun passed in 94ms. It establishes capability, **not the cause or repair** of the earlier readiness failure.
- **Full repaired-matrix acceptance is not green:** an initial full Bun attempt failed primary cleanup at the existing 3-second service-child deadline and combined private-service readiness. A subsequent full Node attempt failed both cases at the same 3-second cleanup boundary. Both also encountered the previously observed 30-second outer Podman post-run inspection timeout; task container absence was separately verified. No timeout increase, suppressed error or retry-for-green was used. The passing selected Bun case does not erase these receipts or establish a cleanup fix.

The unchanged core auth feature previously passed both Node flows on the published `606da10` tree (11.725s/30.825s; 78.65s Vitest) and effective endpoint refusal (2.680s). That remains prior-source evidence, **not a full passing result for this repair**. All provider responses are synthetic; no commercial entitlement, live-model reasoning or P8 acceptance is claimed. No real account, host keyring or host D-Bus was used.

### Static, review and budget

Imported-contract types and root tooling types pass; targeted lint/format, raw-fetch boundary, generated Git-owner check, composite-action interpolation check and conflict-marker check pass. Actionlint passes. The full workflow checker remains red on three unchanged medium `ref-version-mismatch` findings in `ci-check-arm-testbox.yml`, `node-runtime-conformance.yml` and `package-acceptance.yml`; those files match the canonical CI base. No exceptions or unrelated workflow edits were made.

Fresh independent review completed with **no actionable P0–P2 findings in the eight-file repair**. It explicitly retained the full-run cleanup/readiness validation limits; it did not independently execute the tests. Simplification keeps prerequisite selection in the existing manifest, installation in the existing setup action, and transport/process lifecycle in existing owners.

**Budget: 6,282,722 / 6,328,989; 46,267 headroom.** The scalar and upstream allocations are unchanged. This repair adds 117 canonical eligible lines, 119 test/support lines including helpers outside those patterns, plus 26 CI setup/selection lines. The prior P0 reductions remain deliberate, non-equivalent coverage cuts; no original endpoint/credential/approval assertion was weakened.

The preceding seven-phase removal scan remains prior-source evidence: six passes, one canonical inherited unused-file finding for `scripts/perf/update-state-io-measure.ts`, no P5-owned finding. This repair removes no maintained file or export and does not claim a new seven-phase run.

### Current handoff

This reviewed published repair addresses the two PR-caused CI defects. New-head CI and conflict reconciliation remain pending; the older red run is not a verdict on the new head. The inherited five planning failures, three unchanged workflow-audit findings and current full-run cleanup/readiness uncertainty are explicitly retained. Parent accepted publication, not full-matrix green or landing; no CI rerun, hosted re-review, scanner override or merge was requested.

Native command plus explicitly configured gateway OAuth remains the human-approved contract. The older hosted credential-source finding and proposed startup ban are historical under the retired single-token documentation, not a reason to invent an OAuth ban or identity binding. Existing host profile/key isolation and routing/approval policy remain unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Historical evidence, failures and prerequisite provenance</summary>

**Prior source and CI, not refreshed-candidate CI.** The published `38bd781` native-ownership tree passed both flows (10.480s/30.003s, 76.45s Vitest) and its seven removal scans had six inherited red phases and one pass; those are superseded locally by the new-base results above. At publication observation, full CI/Darwin had not attached to `38bd781` and GitHub reported dirty mergeability. On `67207`, [CI 40809689209](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40809689209) passed: 91 jobs, 65 passed/26 skipped. [Darwin 40809688885](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40809688885/job/123236803467) passed its selected-Git suite (4 passed/12 platform skips). The October 29 03:20 UTC pre-review snapshot had 153 checks: 91 passed/61 skipped/1 neutral and three successful commit statuses; provisional review statuses were superseded. This is not a current merge-gate declaration. Earlier [b560 CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40728964753) passed 63/89 jobs, 26 skipped, but its [Darwin job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40728964595/job/122959761289) selected a test absent from the older checked-out head. Canonical #185964's complete tooling closure resolved that source skew; the later 67207 run supplies the passing receipt.

**Original input-safety hold.** [6463002323](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186614#issuecomment-6463002323) produced NO VERDICT and two unclassified findings in patch `62177f29` → `59617f87`. The checksum-matched original artifact and pinned scanner source mapped patch line 1733 to `src/agents/runtime-plan/native-command-auth.test.ts:123`: a dummy-credential URL on reserved `inference.example.test`. Galin qualified that fixture as a false positive at 05:30; its old URL is absent from 67207. Raw match/second-finding metadata were unavailable: **no blanket retrospective scanner clearance**. The authorized re-review completed as 6489044017. No values or scanner override were published.

**Retired strict-contract investigation.** A local one-line OAuth rejection had empty-home native thread-admission red/green proof but could not prevent earlier startup catalog authentication. It was never a complete startup fix. That restriction and the zero-primary-command oracle were retired after the native-owned composition decision. Codex 0.164 already permits command+gateway OAuth, validates primary conflicts and header/cookie collisions, and may authenticate its startup catalog. No native API/pin change or OpenClaw login feature was needed.

**Owning repairs.** Eligibility/preparation were red on 86d4d441 before shared eligibility. Actual Gateway proof exposed unrelated automatic OpenAI account selection, fixed at f53f8440. Older native-header restrictions are replaced here; OpenClaw-authored credential/header guards remain. af9c3893 fixed the PR-caused Madge cycle (1→0); 5dc349b0 split concrete inputs from leaf prepared types. ddc4541b sorted both archive arrays before exact equality after Bun reversed enumeration; missing/extra files still fail. Earlier 45fc CI was red in that shard/aggregate. Prior budget failures were not waived; current inherited budget passes.

**Included runner prerequisites.** Four-file `f6a08fc6a7885cc75518848502e2eaf7eaa74b20` admits only public archives selected by fs-safe manifest+lockfile, SRI-verified with hashes—not the surrounding cache. `e49494a26bfb6bd2026824e9186ac2db3c5720d3` adds fixed Node/Bun selection: Node owns default/orchestration/build/entry; Bun is one read-only pinned executable checked at admission and entry. No arbitrary environment/path/command input or isolation relaxation. Focused review and contained Node/Bun proof passed; a sysfs-counting oracle was corrected without weakening isolation. Original P8 patch remains SHA256 `fe004d65b4aa3ccffa44c495ea897938bff59390f9423527374ce1f7550deaca`.

**Setup/cleanup uncertainty.** Initial private-service setup lacked gdbus (added to the task image); native login setup needed the existing configured-command provenance field. prs.title: feat(knowledge): add decision-model recall gate
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Knowledge only injects context automatically from owner-approved `knowledge_recall` summaries, and the standing index gives the main model labels but not content. This adds an opt-in **recall gate**: per user turn, a small local decision model (any OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint with logprobs) sees the Knowledge page list plus the user message and picks the relevant pages. The list goes only to the decision model, never into the main prompt. It is off unless configured, and starts in `shadow` mode (log only).

### What changes

- New `plugins.entries.knowledge.config.recallGate` block: `mode` (`off` | `shadow` default | `live`), `baseUrl`, `model`, `apiKey` (SecretRef-capable via `configContracts.secretInputs`), `highThreshold` (0.85), `mediumThreshold` (0.5), `timeoutMs` (1500), `maxIndexChars` (24000), `maxCandidates` (5).
- New `before_prompt_build` handler (`recall-gate-hook.ts`), registered only when the block is present and not `off`, user-triggered turns only:
  1. Reads every current page (not `source`/`artifact`) as one label line through a new worker op `gateIndex`, using the standing index's label rules (`buildGateEntries` in `memory-index.ts`, same `promptLabel` / exact-alias handle).
  2. One selection call: the model returns entry numbers.
  3. One-token yes/no call per pick with `logprobs`; score = P(yes) / (P(yes) + P(no)) from top logprobs.
  4. `live`: high tier prepends the page body (existing `memoryGet` op, clipped to 2,000 chars), medium tier prepends a one-line `knowledge_lookup` pointer, low adds nothing; whole block capped at 6,000 chars. Injection goes through `prependContext` (user turn), never the system prompt, so the cached prefix is untouched.
- No logprobs (or neither answer in top logprobs): a yes counts as **medium** (pointer only), anything else low. An uncalibrated answer never injects a body.
- Whole-gate deadline (`timeoutMs`) with an abort signal; timeout, HTTP error or any failure injects nothing and never fails the turn. Authority (`access.assertCurrent`, hook lifetime, memory audience) is re-checked right before publication.
- One info log line per turn: mode, outcome, latency, entries offered, and per decision the record ID, score, tier. No message or record text.
- Same audience gate as the standing index: shared via a small extraction, `openPrivatePartition()` in `memory-index-hook.ts`. Ungranted conversations, sandboxed sessions and agents without a store never reach the endpoint.
- Docs: new "Recall gate" section in `docs/plugins/knowledge/memory-provider.md`, config row in `docs/plugins/knowledge.md`, and the "Automatic recall" trust sentence now names the gate.

### Scope boundary

- Plugin-only; no core changes.
- The standing `## Knowledge Index` in the system prompt is unchanged. Dropping it when the gate runs `live` is a possible follow-up once the gate is proven on real traffic.
- No new agent tool ("ask the gate directly"): left out to keep this PR small.
- Config surface budget: `plugin` count raised 4889 -> 4899 in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` for the 10 new `recallGate` keys; this is an opt-in feature block with no defaults that change existing behavior.

### Trust note

In `live` mode the gate injects page bodies chosen by a model, not owner-approved summaries. That is an explicit operator opt-in (`mode: "live"`), the injected block is labeled as stored records that are evidence, not instructions, and `source`/`artifact` pages and instruction-like titles are never offered. The endpoint receives page labels and the user message; docs say to point it only at a model you trust with both.

## Verification

- `pnpm test extensions/knowledge/src/recall-gate.test.ts`: 8/8 pass. Mocked decision endpoint covers: shadow logs and injects nothing (and logs carry no message/record text); live high body / medium pointer / low nothing; logprob parsing incl. case/space variants and the missing-logprobs binary fallback; no-match -> single selection call, nothing injected; HTTP 503 and a hung endpoint cut at the 100 ms budget -> no injection, no throw, logged; the index text reaches only the decision request and the hook returns only `prependContext`; ungranted conversation audience never calls the endpoint.
- `pnpm test extensions/knowledge`: 60/60 test files pass.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, lint, format, SAFETY ratchet and import guards pass. The dead export scan fails only on `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer-width-ref.tsx: loadComposerWidthEdge`, which is already on `main` and untouched here.

### What was not tested

- A tuned decision model. A local live smoke ran this branch (not a Gateway) against a 4B decision checkpoint behind a small OpenAI-compatible shim, using a temp vault of 10 fake pages and 5 messages, in `live` mode. Plumbing worked end to end: selection about 170 ms and each yes/no score about 60 ms model-side, with 0.5 to 1.2 s per turn including a test relay. That checkpoint is not tuned for this prompt, though. It picked the right page for 3 of 4 relevant messages but answered "No" on every yes/no score (P(yes) 0.000 to 0.005), so nothing was injected. Choosing a model and tuning the prompt in `shadow` mode come before turning on `live`.
- No before/after benchmark: with no `recallGate` block the hook is not registered, so the default path is unchanged. With the gate on, per-turn latency is bounded by `timeoutMs`; the smoke above is the only real-model latency measurement.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid automatic profiler hang risk on macOS
prs.body:
Related: #181120

## What Problem This Solves

Automatic continuous CPU profiling exposes macOS Gateways to a native lock-stall risk implicated in #181120.

## User Impact

macOS users no longer need a local patch to keep the automatic CPU flight recorder off. Callback attribution, stall warnings, event-loop delay/utilization, and CPU health metrics stay enabled. The tradeoff is losing automatic trailing CPU profiles on macOS. No configuration change is required; Linux and Windows recording and explicitly requested on-demand profiling are unchanged.

This removes the automatic profiler exposure; it does not fix Apple's lock implementation or claim every Gateway hang is resolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gate the recorder at its existing owner, before the first native profile starts. Eligible macOS processes emit one explanatory warning per monitor. There is no new configuration, dependency, timer, or fallback profiler. Recording can be reconsidered once the native interaction is demonstrated safe.

Maintainer decision requested: @vincentkoc, could you review this macOS-only safety tradeoff promptly? The reported failure leaves the Gateway unresponsive; this change removes automatic CPU profiles while preserving non-profiling diagnostics, without claiming the native OS/Node bug is fixed.

## Evidence

### October 27 refresh and CI repair

- Refreshed against `main` at `7bce7a61639ae959406736876f2f0cf8cee991ce`; current PR head is `c5d431869fab9c7ad3aff4dc67b5da4d68c7bc35`. Resolved the recorder-test conflict while preserving main's interval-object sampling API, 25 ms interval, and timing-attribution tests. The production macOS exclusion is unchanged.
- The newly upstream real-native-profiler test excludes actual Darwin hosts, so its Linux platform mock cannot accidentally enable the unsafe native sampler there. Mocked macOS no-start and Linux/Windows rotation coverage remain active. This is an intentional platform eligibility limit, not a suppressed failure.
- The first refreshed head `e1c3921201ec3d4d5b1d092db5b5a9abcb306cd7` failed the [test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40512027532/job/122216871729) with a net addition of 27 test lines. This repair removes duplicate mock layers, a forwarding fixture, and repeated lifecycle/redaction setup without dropping scenarios or assertions. All six redaction cases remain; additional cases now also check later-sample recovery and shutdown. The complete PR now has **zero net additional test lines** against the refresh base (75 added / 75 removed); production remains +7/-1. The unchanged ratchet passes locally; no ceiling, baseline, or exemption was changed.
- **Linux / Node 26.12.1: 35 focused tests passed**, including the real native-profiler block test (19 Gateway + 16 recorder; wrapper 21.54 s). The preceding test-consolidation revision passed pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+807211511`: 34 passed / 1 skipped because its native V8 profiling API is unavailable (wrapper 12.05 s); the only subsequent source change restores the erased TypeScript cleanup contract. Removing only the macOS guard makes the consolidated macOS no-start regression fail; restoring it passes.
- CI confirmed the [test-line ratchet passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40515606710/job/122229495293) on `f6ac5a2bd09679ccd07b1e35a9a570feab6a8e33`, then exposed an [await-thenable lint error](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40515606710/job/122230905307). The final one-line repair restores the test table's `void | Promise<void>` cleanup contract: skill tracking drains asynchronous work, so removing `await` would be wrong. The exact CI type-aware lint configuration reproduced the error before this repair and passes afterward on all three changed TypeScript files. The gateway typecheck and all 35 Node tests were rerun successfully, and the local test-line delta remains zero.
- Both affected typecheck graphs (`state-logging`, `gateway-server`), targeted lint, formatting and diff whitespace checks passed on this candidate. Earlier MDX validation remains applicable to the unchanged documentation. **Current-head CI passed**: [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40519506734/job/122254287794) succeeded for `c5d431869fab9c7ad3aff4dc67b5da4d68c7bc35`, including all selected aggregate lanes, with no known-main-red waiver. The previously failing [type-aware lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40519506734/job/122244976210) and [baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40519506734/job/122243448980) both passed. GitHub reported the PR cleanly mergeable; it remains open and unmerged.
- Fresh independent Auto Review of the complete final local candidate against the pinned refresh base returned `scoped-clean`, no P0–P2 findings. Its final patch pass covered all four files and explicitly checked the consolidated assertions and fixture semantics; earlier passes contained only the staged base-refresh inventory. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable. The [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181551#issuecomment-6362662214) reported no findings or before-merge items for `e1c3921201ec3d4d5b1d092db5b5a9abcb306cd7`; that is prior-head review evidence, not a claim it reviewed this test-only repair.
- **Proof boundary:** the macOS Gateway A/B below remains evidence for the original head, not a new macOS execution of this refreshed revision. The guard is unchanged; updated sampling and Gateway consumers were checked by the current focused suites.

### Original revision validation

- **Actual macOS Gateway A/B supplied by @Marvinthebored:** [run report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181551#issuecomment-6367004169) and [pinned artifacts](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/aaf4683affe31fde5d83512918ef64610dd31133/PROOF.md) compare original head `00d27c442c5d8b8886f6e40c22b41b241f366c96` with `ded4d430df859f35599fbb4d0ef32d8dec31e3b5` on macOS 26.6.1 ARM64 / Node 26.12.1. Both isolated source-CLI Gateways reached readiness, retained named callback-stall and live event-loop health reporting after the same 1.5-second block, returned final readiness/liveness HTTP 200, and shut down cleanly with exit 0. Native samples before/after the block contain the V8 profiler thread in stock and none in patched; the patched recorder warning appears exactly once. The corrected comparison uses Gateway-PID-only SIGTERM. I inspected the harness, logs, health snapshots and complete native-sample thread inventories and verified all 40 artifact hashes against the pinned manifest; this is a review of the reporter's run, not a separate execution.
- **macOS-host red/green:** the same two suites pass 33/33 on that original head; restoring only stock recorder source gives 32 passed / 1 failed, specifically the new macOS exclusion test. These recorder tests mock native APIs; the separate Gateway A/B above supplies native-runtime evidence.
- CI: [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39935940769/job/120358914893) passed for head `00d27c442c5d8b8886f6e40c22b41b241f366c96`, with no failed or timed-out selected jobs. Native macOS runtime jobs were not selected.
- The reporter's macOS ARM64 reduction stalled with pthread read/write locks plus SIGPROF at both tested signal intervals. The no-signal rwlock control and signaled ordinary-mutex control completed. Repeated native samples showed the same blocked lock waiters.
- The new macOS regression failed before the guard and passes with it: startup, sampling, and shutdown never call the native profiler. Existing rotation/cleanup coverage now runs for both Linux and Windows runtime facts.
- **33 focused tests passed** across the recorder and Gateway event-loop health suites on Linux with Node 26.12.1. The Gateway tests preserve callback reports, health metrics, telemetry, idle sampling, and cleanup.
- Production TypeScript checking, the affected state/logging and Gateway-server test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, documentation MDX parsing, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- **Limits:** the new successful macOS Gateway A/B supersedes the earlier readiness-timeout evidence gap. Both stock and patched complete this short scenario: it proves removal of automatic profiler exposure with working startup, health sampling and shutdown, not reproduction or repair of the original deadlock or long-term stability. Source execution with tsx does not cover a release distribution, channel/model traffic or manual profiling. Short Node port-churn controls also did not reproduce the native hang; manually requested profiling is not made safe by this change.

<details>
<summary>Original revision validation commands, cost, and broader-check gaps</summary>

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/logging/diagnostic-stall-flight-recorder.test.ts src/gateway/server/event-loop-health.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 33 passed; wrapper 39.19 s, including a 33.35 s cold worker build. Regression lives in existing fixtures; no new worker, server, or sleep is added.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`: passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/logging/diagnostic-stall-flight-recorder.test.ts","src/gateway/server/event-loop-health.test.ts"]'`: overall failed. Existing Gateway-root/infra inventories exceed the 720-root budget (726/729); neither test file is new. The runner expanded to all graphs: state/logging and Gateway-server passed, while a later plugin-SDK compiler process exited 139. That compiler crash is unresolved and is not represented as a passing full test-typecheck run.
- Targeted `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`: 0 warnings/errors on the three changed TypeScript files. `scripts/run-format.mts --check`, `scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/gateway/health.md`, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Simplification: one platform decision in the existing recorder owner; production delta +7/-1 lines. No parallel implementation or native patch is introduced.

</details>

Reported and reproduced by @Marvinthebored.

## Worked on by

- @Marvinthebored

  • Report window close through the daemon or Bridge as closed when the app keeps the closed NSWindow alive, instead of exiting 1 with an indeterminate postcondition: the Bridge readback now applies the same exact-window Accessibility presence check as the in-process path. Thanks @​goutamadwant! #1131, fixes #1129.
  • Let peekaboo see observe Chrome and other apps whose Accessibility window title appends the application name or whose WindowServer title is middle-elided, instead of failing with "inconsistent response evidence: window-context window title". Thanks @​L1uYun! #1130.
  • Close windows of apps that re-exec themselves with window close --foreground, whose frontmost PID AppKit reports as -1. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1124.
  • Classify Dock separators and the Trash from their Accessibility subroles, so peekaboo dock list hides separators unless --include-all is passed, reports included separators as separator instead of blank unknown items, and identifies a localized Trash (such as "Papierkorb") as trash. #1120.
  • Use the Mac app's saved Vision model for image analysis even when its provider does not report vision support (OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible, LM Studio and many Ollama models), surfacing the provider's error instead of silently switching models. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1127.
  • Keep the Mac chat's streaming answer together when you queue a follow-up, and keep Retry on the prompt that failed. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1126.
  • Show a failed Mac agent tool as failed, not completed, in the menu bar, while cancelled tools stay cancelled. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1134.
  • Highlight the Inspector control in the front window under the pointer, including floating panels and popup items past their window, instead of the smallest control anywhere on screen; windows of untracked apps such as the Dock now stop the hover from reaching what they cover. prs.title: fix: keep slow history reads from blocking transcript writes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a slow history read can stall transcript writes behind it for the entire history-worker timeout.

## User Impact

Bounded hydration and prepared model-context reads no longer reserve the database writer while awaiting a worker response. Existing source, authority, mutation and synchronous-consumer checks remain enforced. No configuration change or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

An incident trace showed a history hydration read holding the writer for 59,999 ms while a transcript append queued behind it for 59,975 ms. This establishes head-of-line blocking, not a circular deadlock or the underlying cause of the worker timeout.

The two affected paths now share one small read/accept operation: capture the existing mutation witnesses under writer admission, perform the read outside that reservation, then reacquire admission and validate before synchronous consumption. An intervening mutation retries the read once; continued mutation rejects it without invoking the consumer. Already-owned writer execution keeps its existing custody.

Scope is deliberately limited: this does not repair filesystem fragmentation, change SQLite durability, remove whole-file snapshots, or change other ordered-read paths. It has not been deployed to the incident server.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced on the base: both hydration cases failed the writer-progress assertion while the real worker reply was held.
- Real SQLite/worker regressions cover writer progress, rejection of an obsolete hydration result followed by a fresh read, and the separate prepared model-context path. Existing sibling suites cover physical replacement, closed readers, fenced appends/removes and retained actor context.
- Core and agent/session test TypeScript graphs pass; focused lint passes; changed-page MDX check and staged whitespace check pass. The test-line ratchet passes.
- Final focused run: **36 tests passed across 3 files** (2 actor-context reuse tests plus 34 hydration/model-context worker tests); compiler-generation verification passed. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-transcript-anchor-read.worker.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-transcript-context-read.worker.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-actor-transcript-reuse.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Author simplification pass: removes duplicated async writer reservations and shares only the read/accept protocol; no new state owner, queue, schema or configuration. The necessary growth is concurrency validation and three regression cases (148 net test lines, with a scoped allocation). Against the base: production +92/−48, tests +150/−2, documentation +7, allocation +2.

### Review and qualification limits

Independent review of the production patch and the subsequent consumer-test repair found no actionable blocking findings. Reviews were diff/evidence-based; the author separately inspected the ownership contracts and verified test results. Real-provider/Gateway end-to-end validation is not claimed; current-head PR CI remains pending.

Earlier checks exposed and corrected a required-environment type mismatch and test lint issues. An intermediate run passed all 36 assertions but was invalidated because source changed before the worker-generation verification; it is not counted as the final passing run.


CI repair: run 40983725167 exposed three stale model-context consumer expectations. The tests now require refreshed contents after the bounded retry rather than a rejection or stale snapshot. All 32 tests in that consumer suite passed, as did its targeted TypeScript graph, lint, format, and the test-line ratchet. The failed CI receipt is retained; it is not relabeled green.

prs.title: fix: keep concurrent session starts from failing history reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agent turns failing with `Session entry changed during read` when several sessions start concurrently in a shared session store, before restart acceptance can reach its restart checks.

Related: #187989.

## User Impact

Concurrent starts can finish loading history and produce replies. Ordinary slow history reads continue to let transcript writers progress. When both optimistic reads lose to writes, one final bounded read holds the existing writer admission; queued writes can wait for that read. No configuration, schema, stored-data, dependency, or upgrade changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bisect identifies `8bc631709922a7f994253aef52cddf74e627745f` (#187989) as the first bad commit; its direct parent `9abf96a0ac1e53ceb5a1bdbf302452b5b50ac8b5` passes the unchanged restart acceptance test. In `session-transcript-read-cohort.ts`, the second database-wide mutation conflict was rethrown at line 54, turning normal concurrent activity into a terminal turn failure.

Keep the two optimistic attempts, then reread under the existing FIFO admission when both were overtaken. Recheck the live owner, current authority, and freshly captured mutation witness after the awaited read and before consuming. Consume only once. Physical replacement, revocation, cancellation, or a native write that bypasses admission still refuses unsafe consumption.

The existing model-context writer-progress test now performs two real transcript writes and verifies that the consumer receives the newest content once. Production: +12 lines; tests: -2 lines; docs: +2 lines. The simplify pass retained one read owner and no new state.

## Evidence

- Unchanged main `264adfe194c1` and first bad `8bc631709922`: the original restart acceptance fails during initial setup with `Session entry changed during read`; direct parent `9abf96a0ac1e` passes. All nine bisect probes completed; no setup/build failures were treated as product verdicts.
- Focused repeated-contention regression: red on unchanged main with `SessionEntryChangedDuringReadError`; green with this fix.
- Exact head: 66 tests pass across `session-transcript-context-read.worker.test.ts`, `session-transcript-anchor-read.worker.test.ts`, and `session-manager-model-context-snapshot.test.ts` (two shards, 51.83 seconds including orchestration).
- Targeted session-owner TypeScript check, targeted lint, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/test-lines/assertion-safety ratchets, and `git diff --check`: pass. No budget or baseline changes.
- Local Codex autoreview, base `264adfe194c1` to the local snapshot committed as `de60b653589e062be2c68a8b4833f8729c8dfe05`: scoped-clean at P0 only; no accepted/actionable P0 findings. Maintainer review remains pending.
- Exact head `de60b653589e062be2c68a8b4833f8729c8dfe05`: the unchanged restart acceptance passes (1 test, 61.39 seconds including transformation; test execution 36.92 seconds), including both graceful replacement cycles, FIFO queued inputs, and lossy SIGKILL behavior.
- Exact-head PR CI: [run 40998119782](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40998119782) completed successfully. Both reported required `openclaw/ci-gate` checks are SUCCESS. The PR is ready and mergeable; not merged.

All Gateway tests use isolated state and ports with the synthetic Responses provider. No live Gateway, deployment, or release changes.

prs.title: fix(litellm): image edits fail for Gemini models because n is always sent
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #169120

## What Problem This Solves

Single-image edits through the bundled LiteLLM provider always send multipart `n=1`. LiteLLM's Gemini edit backend rejects that explicit unsupported parameter with HTTP 400 `UnsupportedParamsError`, even though omitting `n` already means one output image.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the LiteLLM **edit** request builder changes: include `n` when `count > 1`, otherwise use the endpoint's existing single-image default. Multi-image edits retain their requested count and normal error handling. No global `drop_params`, new retry, model-name special case, or transport change.

The contributor's commit is preserved. A follow-up narrowing commit restores the original generation builder and its default-count assertion. **Image generation is unchanged**, including JSON `n: 1` for a single generated image. The issue reports that generation already works; changing that behavior is unnecessary.

## User Impact

Single-image Gemini edits no longer fail solely because OpenClaw supplies redundant `n=1`. Explicit multi-image requests still send their count rather than silently dropping an unsupported parameter. Other providers and generation requests retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

Current integrated head `401c2aad24c67e9c53aa098d47821341dadba1b2` merges current main `a7fe06b17a966`. The reported conflict was only in the provider test file: upstream’s consolidated layout is retained, with default-edit omission, explicit multi-image count, and generation count=1/count=2 assertions preserved. The production provider is byte-identical to proven `d91502a7840fb0c8a3767a281de3af3ffc74bae0`, so the linked Gateway A/B evidence carries; this integration does not add a real-provider claim. Fresh isolated frozen install, changed-file format check, and provider suite pass **20/20**. Current delta: production **+5/-1**, tests **+13/-5**.

[Built-Gateway A/B multipart captures and output receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169129#issuecomment-6432278843), comparing pinned main `ce503a58dad3b06cfba1cc357bab3e5a0435f024` with narrowed candidate `d91502a7840fb0c8a3767a281de3af3ffc74bae0`:

- Fresh isolated Linux `node:24.22.1` containers installed frozen dependencies and passed supported `pnpm build:runtime`. The runtime artifact contains the final production change; the final amendment only consolidated tests.
- The shipped agent command dispatches to the built Gateway, whose real `image_generate` tool runs the LiteLLM provider against a local LiteLLM-compatible HTTP fixture. It receives a real PNG file part. The fixture models the reported Gemini contract: reject explicit edit `n` with HTTP 400 `UnsupportedParamsError`; accept omission and return a known valid PNG.
- **Main twice:** default count and explicit count=1 each send multipart `n=1`, receive HTTP 400, and persist no output PNG.
- **Candidate twice:** the same default/explicit-one operations omit `n`, receive HTTP 200, and persist one PNG each. Shipped image metadata decoding reads both as 1×1 PNGs, 68 bytes each.
- **Controls on both refs:** shipped `infer image edit` with non-Gemini `gpt-image-2`, count=2 sends `n=2` and writes two PNGs. `infer image generate` with the Gemini route, count=1 still sends JSON `n: 1` and writes one PNG. Generation behavior is unchanged.
- Gateway image work is asynchronous: the first agent turn acknowledges task admission. The recorded failure/success is the actual provider operation and persisted artifact, not a claim that this initial acknowledgement failed.
- Before integration, candidate provider tests passed **10/10** and changed-file format checks pass. The strengthened existing default-edit multipart regression fails on main exactly at `form.has("n")` (true versus expected false) and passes with the fix. Default omission is consolidated into the existing multipart test; explicit multi-image count remains a distinct regression.
- Simplification retains one request builder and adds no helper/state owner. That pre-integration delta was production **+5/-1**, tests **+20/-0**; current integrated totals are listed above.

Earlier contributor evidence exercised the public CLI and a real LiteLLM 1.105.0 proxy with stubbed Vertex AI. That remains earlier-head evidence, not a real Gemini API run. This new run proves the narrowed production path through a built Gateway but also uses local model/provider fixtures.

**Outstanding proof prerequisite:** the [previous review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169129#issuecomment-6109716373) explicitly requests an actual Gemini image returned through LiteLLM because the dependency's AGENTS.md requires real provider APIs. No Gemini credentials are available to this proof lane. The known PNG above is fixture output, not real Gemini output, and does not satisfy that requirement if it remains applicable.

## Not fixed here

Generation is intentionally unchanged. This does not enable Gemini multi-image counts, globally discard unsupported parameters, prove semantic image-edit quality, or establish real Gemini deployment behavior. Unsupported explicit multi-image parameters still surface their normal errors.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores explicit `n=1` on single-image LiteLLM edits; no schema/config migration or durable-state change. Blast radius is LiteLLM multipart image edits. Generation and other providers are untouched.

prs.title: feat(gateway): expose held native state owner identity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

External supervisors need to correlate a Gateway's recorded state owner with the exact workload they stopped. `system.info` currently identifies the process independently of its native state owner, while `gateway recover-lock --json` exposes holder descriptions without structured identities.

## Change

Expose an optional `stateOwner` through the existing `operator.read` `system.info` RPC, taken from this process's active native owner. Capture canonical identity during acquisition and serve lifecycle-held facts without filesystem polling. Release, detected ownership loss or an ambiguous scope omits the observation; admission and heartbeat retain physical-custody checks.

Add structured `ownerRecords` to the existing recovery inspection, using the same canonical database path, owner reference, PID/start identity and process namespace. Persisted foreign records never become a live self-observation; incomplete file identities remain explicit and malformed database leases still fail inspection.

Recovery remains an explicit local CLI operation. Authentication, live-holder refusals, the opaque confirmation fingerprint and unchanged-record checks are preserved. No recovery RPC, automatic reclamation, configuration option or stored schema is added. A supervisor must independently prove that the bound workload stopped before confirming recovery.

## Evidence

At `a47686ed`, all 8 `system.info` tests and all 40 native lock-recovery and owner-lifecycle tests passed. The foreground Gateway reported the owner it held, then omitted it after release even with a copied record on disk. The recovered snapshot retained the existing refusal for live or changed holders. The protocol checks, generated Gateway validator check, targeted lint and formatting passed.

All 24 PostgreSQL recovery cases passed on the merged recovery implementation before the final validator regeneration and equivalent owner-lookup rewrite. The selected PostgreSQL lease is included in the structured inspection result.

End-to-end recovery through an external Docker or Kubernetes supervisor is tracked in [the Enterprise PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/3355).

prs.title: fix: GitHub identity setup failures report no cause in Gateway logs
prs.body:
Closes #181165

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: GitHub identity setup recordings contain no cause in the Gateway log when `tools.github.configure` fails; the operator sees only a generic `GitHub identity setup failed` error.

## User Impact

Operators can read the actual failure cause from the Gateway log (for example a missing `gh` CLI, an expired one-use setup handoff, or a store error) instead of reproducing the failure and guessing across the several fallible setup steps covered by the single try block.

## Why This Change Was Made

The handler's catch block discarded the caught error completely, so nothing about the failure reached anywhere. This change binds the error and logs it using the established gateway logging convention (`logWarn` + `formatErrorMessage`, matching the sibling `mcp-app.ts` catch paths) before responding with the unchanged generic error. There is no behavior change: same error code, same message, same response shape.

## Evidence

- Before (observed in production logs): 10 failed `tools.github.configure` calls on 2026.10.5 (Gateway journal, 2026-10-22 01:44–02:00 UTC), each logging only the `res ✗ … errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage="GitHub identity setup failed"` response envelope, with no cause-bearing log line anywhere near them. Method and context: #181165 (full journal slices inspected, not just grep hits).
- Regression test (per the review's next-step ask), run locally on this change: `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts` — *"logs the unavailable-handoff cause while retaining the generic response"* — handoff consumption throws; the test asserts `logWarn` carries the thrown cause (`tools-github: GitHub identity setup failed: setup handoff expired before use`) while `respond` keeps the byte-identical generic UNAVAILABLE error shape. **Red on the base** (fix stashed): `1 failed | 12 passed` — only the new test fails, at the `logWarn` expectation. **Green with the fix**: 13/13 (`pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, vitest 5.0.3 on Node v24.22.1).
- Runtime note, stated plainly: local runs used Node v24.22.1 (sha256-verified from `nodejs.org/dist/v24.22.1/SHASUMS256.txt`); this host does not have the pinned OpenClaw Bun fork, so vitest fell back to Node (printed by the harness). PR CI runs the standard lane.
- Scope check: 2 files changed, 32 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-) — production: `catch (error)` binding, one `logWarn` line, two convention imports (+4/−1 vs base); the rest is the regression test and its spy setup.
- Known upstream-main statuses observed while running the local check graph (all empty-diff, none from this change): the max-lines suppression ratchet reports three `ui/` files (`ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`) that are identical to base `d5ce64b7` — inherited `main` state, zero hunks from this patch.

prs.title: docs(codex): RFC for recovering pending provider-review linkage
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178923

Builds on merged prevention PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179054.

## What Problem This Solves

An earlier failed acknowledgment can leave an existing conversation bound to a replacement native thread while its pending provider review still identifies the original; the normal review UI then rejects continuation with `Provider review no longer matches the native thread`.

## User Impact

**RFC/design only, not a working recovery fix.** This draft does not restore affected conversations or change runtime behavior. It proposes verifying current authority, restoring the original link through canonical ownership, and then requiring a separate normal acknowledgment with all existing safety checks intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #179054 prevents new replacements but explicitly does not repair an already-mismatched binding. This draft records the recovery contract, a data-only native policy comparator, and an already-mismatched regression specification. It implements no recovery endpoint, authority issuer, binding/review mutation, or acknowledgment path.

The OpenClaw coordinator and native broker remain unimplemented. Confirmation of the provider's ownership/configuration guarantees remains a dependency: Codex 0.160.0 exposes useful policy fields, but matching those fields does not establish exclusive native ownership or a configuration generation valid through canonical commit. If existing native semantics cannot supply that guarantee, provider support is required. Unknown evidence must refuse recovery.

Consistency repair must preserve the pending review and cannot approve continuation, fabricate ownership, spoof a channel sender, bypass catalog/current-policy checks, or replay held input.

## Evidence

- **23 supporting offline checks passed** for the data comparator and scenario fixture (22 data-comparison checks and one fixture consistency check).
- **31 actual recovery acceptance scenarios are specified but unexecuted**, including recovery of an already-mismatched state, authorization failures, changed policy/catalog/review, concurrency, idempotence, partial/uncertain recovery, rollback/crash disposition, and separate normal acknowledgment.
- No successful recovery, live provider acceptance, full Gateway/native integration, repository Vitest/build/typecheck or CI result is claimed.
- Local proposal diff syntax and full-content privacy scans passed. Only generic fixture identities and public source references are included.

Before this can become a recovery fix, implement and validate the coordinator/native broker and catalog preparation, resolve the provider-guarantee dependency, and prove the already-mismatched regression fails on prevention-only #179054 and passes on the implementation. This RFC should not close an existing-mismatch recovery report.
