prs.title: fix(ui): show website identity in dashboard gallery (#178467)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Dashboards whose primary content is a session:website widget appear as empty boards in the Dashboards gallery with the message 'A clear board, ready for work'. This occurs because session:website is registered with previewSafe: false to prevent passive code execution, causing board-document.tsx to filter out the widget and leaving BoardView with zero active rectangles (view().empty === true).

## Solution
Rather than changing previewSafe: true (which would allow unisolated iframes in gallery thumbnails), this change computes a safe websiteIdentity from authorized snapshot metadata during passive rendering. When BoardView detects an empty layout rectangle set, it inspects websiteIdentity and renders a recognizable website preview card featuring the built-in globe icon, saved title, and localized Website badge.

## Invariants & Security
- previewSafe: false is strictly retained in CORE_BOARD_WIDGET_ELEMENTS.
- Exactly 0 iframes or executable website widgets are mounted in passive mode.
- 0 network requests are initiated.
- Truly empty boards continue to display the standard empty-board prompt.
- Other unsafe widgets (agent:node-browser, mcp-app) remain isolated and do not display a website card.
- Mixed boards with preview-safe widgets (HTML) continue to render normal widget previews.

## Evidence
- Focused unit & integration regression tests: 27/27 pass.
  - ui/src/components/board/board-document.test.ts (14/14 pass).
  - ui/src/pages/dashboards/dashboards-page.test.tsx (6/6 pass).
  - ui/src/lib/board/widgets/website.test.ts (5/5 pass).
  - ui/src/lib/board/widgets/index.test.ts (2/2 pass).
- TypeScript check: pnpm tsgo:ui (0 errors).
- Linter checks: pnpm lint:ui:styles and pnpm lint:ui:no-raw-window-open (0 errors, 0 warnings across 6091 files).
- Build check: pnpm --dir ui build (clean build of 6325 modules in 1m 19s).
- Visual evidence: Playwright browser verification with system Chrome confirming recognizable card rendering with globe icon and widget title, and 0 iframes mounted.

Fixes #178467

prs.title: fix(gateway): preserve graceful shutdown when restart intent stalls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A stalled restart-intent operation could keep SIGTERM in signal settlement until the supervisor cleanup deadline. The settlement timeout then forced exit before ordinary shutdown could persist restart markers or abort active runs. A reversible suspend lease does not seal restart-intent storage; signal storage is sealed by the run loop's close/reset paths.

## User Impact

SIGTERM now reaches ordinary graceful shutdown after at most one second waiting for earlier signals, a sealed store, or intent consumption. The shutdown owner can persist resume markers, abort active runs, and perform bounded cleanup. An unavailable intent can lose its optional restart metadata; stopping still proceeds.

## Why This Change Was Made

The signal owner bounds its own wait and cancels intent admission. The existing database worker still owns settlement of dispatched native writes, and late results cannot revive a retired signal. SIGINT also keeps its stop request if it times out behind another signal. Existing restart authorization and committed handoff handling remain in their owners.

Worker inspections already cancel on committed drain or service shutdown. The regression extends the existing inspection test through suspend, reopen, and shutdown, including a provider that ignores cancellation. Write-capable provider operations retain their existing settlement owner.

## Evidence

The two blocked-intent signal regressions fail on the base (close was never called), then pass with the fix. A real Gateway process, synthetic model stream, real suspend/resume RPCs, and an isolated SQLite writer lock reproduce the stalled consumption. On the base the short-bound fallback never occurs; with the fix the marker is persisted and the process exits successfully in 1.294 seconds on commit `12361a66a6e0262e24fd157101623f9bf8c267e5`, below the ten-second acceptance bound.

Focused signal ordering, restart-intent, and worker lifetime tests pass. Targeted production, CLI-test, Gateway-test, and e2e typechecks, lint, format, diff whitespace, and both line ratchets pass. Test LOC decreases by one line overall; production changes are net +9 lines, documentation +7. No budgets or baselines change. Fresh isolated review found no actionable P0/P1 defects.

Broader local evidence remains red and is not reported as passing:

- Full run-loop coverage: 154 pass, seven fail, one unhandled error. The same seven failures reproduce with base production: six managed-update setup failures (`No safe OpenClaw temp root`, group-writable volume ancestor), followed by a 120-second timeout and `A process signal exit owner is already registered`. The update-during-close test passes in isolation with the fix.
- The unchanged base restart/resume e2e fails before SIGTERM: concurrent session setup reports `Session entry changed during read`, then the expected background reply is absent. The exact-head full file has one pass (new acceptance) and one failure in the same session-setup boundary (expected idle reply absent). This prevents broad replacement/resume acceptance on this host. An exploratory continuation after the new stop case also timed out awaiting the resumed provider request; the new acceptance parameter ends at the requested durable-marker/exit boundary.

Full exact-head CI and the merge decision belong to the coordinator; this PR must not auto-merge.

<details>
<summary>Local commands</summary>

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'continues graceful shutdown after blocked'
# Base: two failures (close was never called); fixed: two pass.
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'blocked store: true'
# Base: one failure (no one-second fallback). Fixed exact-head full file: new case passes, marker persisted, exit 0 in 1.294 s; legacy case fails at inherited setup boundary.
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Exact-head full-file run described above.
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'fences root admission|keeps admission fenced|joins FIFO signal|settles a queued Stop|captured pre-park Stop|upgrades an accepted restart|continues graceful shutdown after blocked'
# Ten pass on commit 12361a66a6e0262e24fd157101623f9bf8c267e5.
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/restart-intent.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/service-lifetime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Twelve intent and 39 worker lifetime tests pass.
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.config-cli.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-other.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.e2e.json --incremental
# All pass, plus targeted oxlint, format, git diff --check, check:max-lines-ratchet and check:test-lines-ratchet.
```

</details>


### Follow-up: daemon CLI restart-intent fixtures

The six `lifecycle.restart-intent.test.ts` failures reproduce on both `12361a66` and the complete unchanged base `5f3afbe`. They are caused by the fixture's default installed command returning `environment: {}` after #187901 deliberately stopped inheriting caller state selectors. The tests created their serving owner only in caller-selected state, so intent recording inspected a different isolated database.

The fixture now explicitly declares its owned state directory in the installed service command. All 15 daemon restart-intent tests pass with this fixture on both base production and the bounded-signal implementation. Production CLI recording, owner refusals, and SIGTERM cancellation are unchanged by this follow-up. Fresh isolated review found no actionable P0/P1 issues. Total test LOC for this PR is net zero.

Final local validation on `88a8558ac928272768a317bd6abf82fe5457bcef` includes every test file under `src/cli/daemon-cli/`, `src/cli/gateway-cli/`, and `src/infra/restart-intent*` (68 explicit files). The real-process acceptance passes: marker persisted, exit code 0, `shutdownMs=1325`. All three targeted test typechecks, lint, format, whitespace and both ratchets pass. Across the exact-head invocations, all 68 requested files were exercised: 67 files passed; `run-loop.test.ts` retained the same seven baseline failures. Unique per-file case results are 992 passed, seven failed, one skipped. This is an aggregate across invocations, not a passing full-batch result.

The shared batch was stopped after its baseline fixture failures leaked the process signal exit owner into later process-owning runtime/timeline tests. The CLI runner shares that process singleton between files; fixture startup waits after registration has already rejected. The remaining six files completed in a fresh process (24 tests passed), and all three runtime-recovery cases also passed together in a separate focused run. The downstream timeouts were not independently rerun on the base; their attribution rests on the baseline-proven owner leak, the matching ownership path, and fresh-process passing results. Timeouts, production custody guards, budgets, and baselines are unchanged.

Follow-up proof artifacts remain in the task worktree: `j1-followup-test-files.txt` enumerates all 68 paths; `j1-followup-all-tests.command.txt` records the exact wrapper arguments; the shared-batch, remaining-file, and acceptance logs preserve the results. Full CI remains coordinator-owned.

## Accepted edge cases and limits

Timed-out restart metadata may be discarded. Already dispatched native writes still settle with the database owner. No new config, schema, retention policy, compatibility path, dependency, or live Gateway mutation is introduced. Historical logs identify the unbounded intent-consumption boundary but cannot identify the exact database job responsible for the incident's long wait.

### CI handoff timeout: inherited session-read failure

The `checks-node-changed-7` handoff timeout on exact head `88a8558ac928272768a317bd6abf82fe5457bcef` reproduces on fetched main `e04fd211c732b5f3d3e800556bcef1b94ac0864f`. Both standard-wrapper Linux arm64 runs used `nice -n 5`, `--maxWorkers=1`, separate worker caches, and successful runtime builds. Both finished with one failure at the unchanged 180000 ms timeout (Vitest durations 210.01s and 208.21s).

In both runs all six agent turns failed with `SessionEntryChangedDuringReadError: Session entry changed during read` before SIGTERM. The test waits at `provider.ready` for six held model requests and two exec sessions; restart-intent writing and signaling occur only afterward. The first SIGTERM came from timeout teardown, followed by clean-close receipts within 35ms of the signal fence on head and 30ms on main. This is the same session-read failure signature as the separate restart/resume setup failure, and supplies no evidence of a branch-specific signal/handoff regression.

Exact-head CI remains completed red; this is inherited-failure attribution, not a passing handoff proof. The underlying history-read defect and the five-second handoff assertion remain unresolved by these runs. No source change, timeout increase, CI retry, or additional push was made. Full logs and timestamps are preserved in the task's `j1-handoff-classification.md` report.

## User Impact

Give the session-transcript process its own graph and coalesce its initial imports while retaining split request paths. prs.title: fix: stop listing tools blocked by session sandbox policy
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Session tool previews can list tools excluded by the session's sandbox policy. For example, a session with an immutable sandbox requirement still advertises web search when local sandbox mode is off, although execution applies the sandbox allowlist. Warm MCP catalogs pass through the same incomplete preview profile. Fixes #188032. ## User Impact The tool preview and `/tools` now apply the saved session's resolved sandbox policy. Required-sandbox sessions keep that policy even when local mode is off, and a matching active remote-exec placement applies its configured sandbox policy. Ordinary sessions keep their existing tools; configured empty allowlists retain their unrestricted meaning. The preview remains prospective: current run authority, credentials, discovery, and runtime-specific capabilities can still affect execution. This change does not provision a sandbox, open an MCP transport, or change permissions or configuration defaults. ## Why This Change Was Made Execution already supplies the prepared sandbox tool policy to the conversation capability profile. Saved previews omitted that input. The correction uses the existing prepared-session classifier and shares the execution owner's active remote-exec selector, then passes the original policy into the existing profile. Both base tools and warm MCP tools use that profile. The current cache key already includes resolved policy layers, so saved-policy changes select the appropriate cache and in-flight work without adding another cache. The direct `/tools` caller uses its selected target session and channel-bound Gateway context. ## Evidence On the base revision, a real-handler regression returned web search for the required-sandbox case. That assertion failed while the ordinary-session control and the other 21 cases passed; formatting, lint, and selected types passed before the run. The subsequent MCP assertion was not reached in that initial run. The fixed tree passes 31 handler cases, 21 command cases, 18 inventory policy cases, and 65 cases across eight related files. The checks cover required and ordinary sessions, configured empty allowlists, marked deny-all/intersections, concurrent and warm-cache requests, matched remote execution and identity/mode controls, and the direct target-session command path. Formatting, lint, selected types, documentation discovery, and the mock-export/test-line ratchets pass. The command fixture preserves real module exports, with its obsolete allowance removed by the native generator. Single-worker file wall times were 48.71s, 46.69s, and 23.88s for the handler, command, and policy suites respectively, including cold transformation/preparation. The direct command regression includes the first real inventory import and assembly; keeping that production path catches the missing caller input. New handler policy cases take 161–257ms each. Publication/read/search remained listed and identity status was absent. Native search/describe made zero discovered-tool calls; separate guest/admin `/tools` replies were byte-identical. In the Control UI, typing `$` in a session that has a selected project does not offer that project's skills — the picker only shows the agent workspace's skills, even though the agent's next run can see and use the project skills. After this change, the `$` picker and `/commands` offer the selected project's skills, matching what the runtime skill catalog already includes.

- Problem: command discovery (`commands.list` → `prepareSkillCommandsForAgents`) scans only each agent's configured workspace, so the skill roots of the session's selected project (`skills/` and `.agents/skills/`) never reach the composer catalog, while the runtime catalog — which receives the session's execution workspace — does include them.
- Solution: resolve the session's execution workspace with the same resolution the runtime uses (`resolveSessionSkillExecutionWorkspace(managed worktree canonical workspace, spawnedCwd)`) and pass its roots into the existing workspace skill loader.
- What changed: `src/skills/discovery/chat-commands.ts` derives the execution workspace from the session entry (single-agent context) and threads it into discovery options; `src/skills/discovery/command-specs.ts` carries the two loader options through command spec assembly.
- What did NOT change: loader precedence, allowlist, and eligibility behavior — project skills enter through the existing execution tier at lower precedence than agent-workspace skills; node-owned `execCwd` is still never read on the Gateway; the New-session composer's request shape is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime catalog and the command catalog resolved the session's skill scope differently: agent runs receive the execution workspace, command discovery never did. Fixing this at the discovery owner lets both producers — the Gateway `commands.list` and the channel `/commands` reply — pick up the session scope from the `sessionEntry` they already pass, with no caller changes.

- Best fix: yes — one owner derives the scope, and the workspace skill loader already supported execution roots.
- Alternative: teaching the pre-session New-session composer to send a client-selected project path on `commands.list` was considered and left out; it would let a paired client point the Gateway at an arbitrary filesystem path, which is a new trust boundary needing its own product decision.
- Risk / non-goals: sessions bound to an exec node carry no `spawnedCwd` (their `execCwd` is node-owned and stays node-side); managed-worktree sessions resolve their durable `canonicalWorkspaceDir`; rendered picker frequency/UX was not measured (the issue does not claim it either).

## User Impact

In any existing session with a selected project, `$` autocomplete and `/commands` now list the project's user-invocable skills, consistent with `skills_search` and the runtime catalog. Agent allowlists keep their authority: project skills not on the allowlist stay hidden.

## Evidence

Real Gateway process + real WebSocket `commands.list` dispatch at commit `8ea457329`: isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, session seeded through the production writer `upsertSessionEntryCore`, fixture mirroring the issue repro (agent workspace `skills/agent-fixture`; separate project `skills/project-fixture` + `.agents/skills/project-agents-fixture`; allowlist admits all three).

| `commands.list` input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no session context | `["agent-fixture"]` | `["agent-fixture"]` |
| session bound to the project (`spawnedCwd`) | `["agent-fixture"]` (the reported bug) | `["agent-fixture","project-agents-fixture","project-fixture"]` |
| managed worktree session (`canonicalWorkspaceDir`) | `["agent-fixture"]` | all three (regression test) |

Observed result over the WS run: before, the response carried only `agent_fixture`; after, the identical call returned `agent_fixture`, `project_agents_fixture`, `project_fixture` (`[ws] ⇄ res ✓ commands.list`, role=operator). The same fixture driven through the real `prepareSkillCommandsForAgents` producer via `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs` matches the table.

Regression tests in `src/skills/discovery/chat-commands.discovery.test.ts` fail on the base commit and pass with the fix, including the allowlist-authority negative case; the sibling discovery/command-specs tests and the Gateway `commands` consumer tests pass (isolated HOME, no user-level skills).

What was not tested: rendered `$` picker pixels and picker UX frequency (the issue's reproduction also stops at the catalog boundary), and sessions bound to a remote exec node beyond confirming they carry no Gateway-readable project cwd.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `grep`/`git diff` to trace the catalog boundary, located the root cause in `src/skills/discovery/chat-commands.ts`, and implemented the fix. The implementer understands the code: command discovery resolves per-agent workspaces only, while the workspace skill loader already merges lower-precedence execution-workspace roots. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(buzz): directory search fails on Unicode-equivalent profile and room names
prs.body:
Relates to gap finding: gap-buzz-directory-unicode-nfc (pattern-copy, evidence level A)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Buzz (Nostr team rooms) channel directory search returns an empty result when the searched profile display name or room name uses a different Unicode normalization form than the typed query — e.g. names produced by macOS/iOS Nostr clients (NFD, `Cafe\u0301`) never match an NFC query (`Café`).

## User Impact

User impact: searching the Buzz directory for peers or groups now matches names regardless of Unicode normalization form; previously such profiles and rooms were unsearchable and the directory query silently returned nothing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The directory query filter compared raw code units after only `trim().toLowerCase()`, so canonically equivalent strings with different code points (NFC vs NFD) never matched. The fix normalizes both the query and the compared entry fields (`id`/`name`/`handle`) to NFC before matching, mirroring the contract the Matrix live directory lookup fix established: canonical forms compare equal, directory entries keep their original spelling. This is the same bug class fixed for Matrix in `129cfb57fa4`; Buzz's other `toLowerCase()` call sites operate on hex keys, hostnames, and protocol identifiers (pure ASCII) and are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Before fix

New reproduction test on the unmodified code fails exactly as reported:

```text
FAIL  extensions/buzz/src/directory.test.ts > Buzz directory state > matches directory queries across Unicode normalization forms
AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'Café' ]
```

### After fix

- `pnpm vitest run extensions/buzz/src/directory.test.ts` → **13 passed (13)**, including the new regression test covering both directions: NFC-stored profile name matched by an NFD query, and NFD-stored room name matched by an NFC query.
- Full Buzz suite: 208 passed; the 7 failures in `buzz-bus.socket.test.ts` / `gateway.cold-start-recovery.test.ts` (gateway settle timeouts) also fail on the unmodified base — verified by rerunning just those files with the change stashed — pre-existing and unrelated.
- Typecheck: `OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` both exit 0 (the default tsrs binary requires glibc ≥ 2.32; this host has 2.28, so the Go tsgo backend was forced).
- Lint/format: `run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed files reports 0 warnings / 0 errors; `format:check` clean.

No e2e live-relay run: the reproduction and fix are fully covered at the directory-state unit level with the plugin's existing relay mocks; behavior change is confined to one pure filter function.

prs.title: fix(infra): keep the Gateway agent CLI working after a Homebrew Node upgrade
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #188004

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS users running a Homebrew-managed Node would find **every bare `openclaw` command broken** after `brew upgrade node`, even though the installed OpenClaw package is perfectly healthy. The Gateway-materialized agent-CLI launcher (`$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/tmp/agent-cli/openclaw`) embedded the version-pinned Cellar interpreter (`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.8.2/bin/node`), and the upgrade deletes that keg, so the launcher fails with a raw `No such file or directory` (exit 127) for the whole lifetime of the running Gateway. Because that launcher directory is prepended to the agent exec PATH, agents in the same session inherit the broken command, and the error text points at a missing Node binary instead of at the stale launcher, sending users down the wrong debugging path.

- **Related:** #188004 (reporter's verified workaround: point the launcher at `/opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node`); #166222 fixed the same Homebrew-upgrade ENOENT class for command relays, process-group anchors and Codex launchers through `stable-node-path.ts`; #52184 is the Volta/LaunchAgent variant and stays out of scope.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launcher is a durable artifact that outlives the interpreter path it records, so it is materialized through the Homebrew contract the repo already ships: `prepareGatewayAgentCliShim()` now resolves `invocation.command` with the existing `resolveStableNodePath()` before rendering either dialect. Non-Cellar interpreters resolve unchanged, so the launcher keeps pinning the exact runtime for nvm/fnm/Volta, system Node, standalone and bun runtimes, and Windows. `docs/install/node.md` §"Homebrew upgrades while the Gateway is running" now documents the launcher alongside the other consumers of that contract.

- **Intended outcome:** on a Homebrew Node install, the materialized launcher execs `<prefix>/opt/<formula>/bin/node` (or `<prefix>/bin/node`), which Homebrew re-points on upgrade, so bare `openclaw` calls and agent exec keep working across `brew upgrade node` without a Gateway restart.
- **Out of scope:** shell-level exec-time fallbacks or a self-regenerating launcher; Volta/nvm stable-path mapping (#52184); the Gateway process itself still runs the pre-upgrade runtime until restart (existing documented behavior).
- **Highest-risk area:** the launcher can now start the CLI with the formula's current Node instead of the exact keg the Gateway booted from.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** Candidate mapping is formula-scoped (`node@22` → `opt/node@22/bin/node`), applies only when a stable candidate already exists on disk, and is the same contract `resolvePreferredNodePath()` uses for the managed service runtime; a host with no stable candidate keeps the pinned path (covered by the second regression test).

## User Impact

Homebrew Node users no longer lose the `openclaw` command — for themselves and for every agent resolving it through the Gateway-local PATH entry — when Node is upgraded under a running Gateway. No behavior change for non-Homebrew installs, and no Gateway restart is needed to recover from a Node upgrade.

- **Success criteria:** with a Homebrew-shaped prefix, the materialized launcher records the stable interpreter and `openclaw --version` still exits 0 after the old keg is removed; without a stable candidate the launcher keeps the resolved interpreter.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/infra/openclaw-cli-shim.ts` (single resolution point feeding both the POSIX and `.cmd` bodies) and the two new fixtures in `src/infra/openclaw-cli-shim.test.ts` (`renders an upgrade-stable Homebrew interpreter into the launcher`, `keeps the resolved interpreter when no stable Homebrew path exists`).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** worktree at `origin/main` `0b81496b64a` on Linux, driven by the real `prepareGatewayAgentCliShim()` and the real materialized launcher. A Homebrew-shaped prefix was built for the run: `Cellar/node/26.8.2/bin/node` and `Cellar/node/26.12.1/bin/node` as hard links of the installed Node binary, `opt/node` as the keg symlink Homebrew re-points, `bin/node` → `opt/node/bin/node`. The Gateway-side launcher was materialized by starting that Cellar interpreter, then `brew upgrade node` was simulated (re-point `opt/node` → `26.12.1`, delete the `26.8.2` keg) and the bare `openclaw` command was executed through the Gateway-local PATH entry.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # shipped-path behavior proof (real launcher execution, run once per ref)
  bash "$EVIDENCE_DIR/proof-driver.sh" after    # head: fix applied
  git checkout origin/main -- src/infra/openclaw-cli-shim.ts
  bash "$EVIDENCE_DIR/proof-driver.sh" before   # base: pristine origin/main
  git checkout HEAD -- src/infra/openclaw-cli-shim.ts

  # regressions + RED/GREEN
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/openclaw-cli-shim.test.ts   # base test file, then patched test file

  # format / lint / types
  bash skills/fix-pr/scripts/validate.sh src/infra/openclaw-cli-shim.ts src/infra/openclaw-cli-shim.test.ts docs/install/node.md
  node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/install/node.md
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  === [after] 2. generated shim (state-after/tmp/agent-cli/openclaw) ===
  #!/bin/sh
  set -eu
  export TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=<worktree>/tsconfig.json
  exec <prefix>/opt/node/bin/node --import file://<worktree>/node_modules/.pnpm/tsx@4.23.15/node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs <worktree>/src/entry.ts "$@"

  === [after] 3. brew upgrade node (26.8.2 -> 26.12.1) ===
  <prefix>/opt/node -> ../Cellar/node/26.12.1
  old keg present? no

  === [after] 4. bare 'openclaw --version' through the Gateway-local PATH shim ===
  OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (0b81496)
  exit=0

  === [after] 5. bare 'openclaw' resolved through the Gateway-prepended PATH entry (agent exec contract) ===
  $ command -v openclaw; openclaw --version
  <state>/tmp/agent-cli/openclaw
  OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (14b77e1)
  exit=0
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** the launcher records `<prefix>/opt/node/bin/node`, so after the keg it was built from is deleted the bare `openclaw` command still runs and prints the version (exit 0) with no Gateway restart.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** identical run on pristine `origin/main` reproduces the report exactly:
  ```text
  === [before] 2. generated shim ===
  exec <prefix>/Cellar/node/26.8.2/bin/node --import file://... /src/entry.ts "$@"
  === [before] 3. brew upgrade node ===
  old keg present? no
  === [before] 4. bare 'openclaw --version' ===
  <state>/tmp/agent-cli/openclaw: line 4: <prefix>/Cellar/node/26.8.2/bin/node: No such file or directory
  exit=127

  === [before] 5. bare 'openclaw' through the Gateway-prepended PATH entry ===
  <state>/tmp/agent-cli/openclaw: line 4: <prefix>/Cellar/node/26.8.2/bin/node: No such file or directory
  exit=127
  ```
  Regression tests, base → head: `renders an upgrade-stable Homebrew interpreter into the launcher` fails on the base shim (`expected '#!/bin/sh\nset -eu\n\nexec …/Cellar/node/26.8.2/bin/node …' to contain 'exec …/opt/node/bin/node '`) and passes with the patch; `keeps the resolved interpreter when no stable Homebrew path exists` passes on both.
- **What was not tested:** a physical macOS/Homebrew host (the prefix above is the Homebrew layout reconstructed on Linux); the Windows `.cmd` dialect only has Cellar-free coverage (its existing byte-exact launcher test still passes); full CI lanes are pending on this PR. Two pre-existing failures in `src/infra/openclaw-cli-shim.test.ts` (`pins the running CLI before configured PATH entries`, profile=work|undefined) fail identically with the pristine base test file in this sandbox — `Error: service child cleanup identity lost: native owner closed without kernel descendant extinction` from the process supervisor — and are unrelated: those fixtures resolve a non-Cellar interpreter, which `resolveStableNodePath()` returns unchanged.
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** the Homebrew keg/`opt` symlink layout is reconstructed on Linux (hard-linked keg binaries + keg symlink) because no macOS host is available; interpreter resolution itself runs the shipped code path (`resolveStableNodePath` → `stableHomebrewNodePathCandidates`) and the launcher is really executed, not mocked.
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review (CI lanes pending locally).

prs.title: fix: keep Gateway responsive during plugin tool discovery
prs.body:
Closes #188031

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway freezes when the tool catalog discovers plugin tools.

## User Impact

The catalog can yield to other Gateway work while optional plugin registrations are inspected. Requested-agent context, optional and unresolved tool rows, metadata ownership, and name conflicts remain intact. No configuration, permission, schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog now uses the Gateway generation's already-admitted load context and metadata with the existing asynchronous inspection owner. This removes synchronous context/manifest preparation from the production request path instead of only changing the loader call. The catalog retains and checks generation authority, projects rows before release, and publishes success only after cleanup. Standalone inspection records settled owners so failed registrations cannot trigger a synchronous fallback reload.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: through the production catalog handler with real synthetic plugins, a callback queued by the first registration runs before the second registration; synchronous context/manifest preparation is zero; optional/unresolved rows remain present; the selected workspace reaches factories; inspection registrations are disposed exactly once; a revoked Gateway generation never publishes a catalog.

- The strengthened between-registration regression fails under a temporary, fully reverted synchronous inspection negative control (`[false, false]`) and passes with the repair (`[false, true]`). The old assertion was shown to pass that negative control and was replaced.
- CI follow-up repairs the catalog unit mock with `importOriginal` pass-through and removes its obsolete closed-mock allowance using the native prune command. `check:test-mock-exports` is red on the original reviewed head and green after the fix (6,477 → 6,476 grandfathered factories); no guard is weakened. `check:test-lines-ratchet`, Gateway-method test typecheck, focused oxlint and oxfmt also pass. Production source is unchanged.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/tools-catalog.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/tools-catalog.nonblocking.test.ts src/mcp/plugin-tools-registration.test.ts src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **98 passed**, 47.52 s follow-up wrapper wall time across three native lanes (catalog 15, MCP registration 6, optional plugin 77).
- `pnpm build`: **passed**, original final-production build 2m 11.4s; test-only CI-repair rebuild 1m 19.1s with native cache reuse. Production core and Gateway-method test typechecks: **passed**. Focused native oxlint: **passed**, four files, 5.13 s. oxfmt check and `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- `pnpm test:contracts:plugins`: **1,003 passed, 1 inherited failure**, 63.94 s wrapper wall time. The existing typed-hook allowlist expects `before_prompt_build` in `extensions/diffs/src/plugin.ts`, but that plugin no longer contains an `api.on(...)` registration. Both the test and plugin are byte-identical to base `1ae91fa202637a97cb4d1beff8aca140edb3607f`; neither implicated file was changed.
- Canonical local autoreview (Codex), complete production preparation/fallback source supplied, P0/P1 coverage: **scoped-clean**. A subsequent test-only correction adjusted the expected factory count for the deliberately failed registration; production source is unchanged from that review. Review was source-based, not an independent test execution.
- Production observation motivating the change: successful catalog RPC 8,931 ms, main-thread stall 8,928 ms, 619/639 samples in synchronous standalone registry preparation. This is not an after-patch benchmark.
- The fixture exercises the real catalog handler, metadata owner, plugin loader, lifecycle authority and cleanup. That handler fixture alone is not a full product entry-point test; the isolated shipped-entrypoint WebSocket proof below complements it. Neither test exercises Control UI or a real model. The running npm installation has not been changed; production latency after activation remains unmeasured.
- Individual synchronous plugin registration/factory callbacks can still block for their own duration; this change removes the monolithic synchronous discovery chain, not arbitrary plugin CPU work.
- The regression allocation shrinks from +177 to +175 lines; total net test growth is +175 after preserving real exports and strengthening the registration-order proof, and the test-line ratchet passes. The regression protects event-loop responsiveness and disposal/revocation contracts not covered by the mocked projection tests.

The production change adds 35 net lines; existing catalog projection is retained inside the inspection lifetime. No additional cache, registry manager, inspection wrapper, timeout, or service is introduced.


### Registration-order responsiveness proof

The three existing real-loader fixture modes now queue event-loop work from the first plugin registration and assert it ran before the second registration. An initial yield or async release cannot satisfy this assertion. A temporary, fully reverted synchronous inspection negative control passed the old proof (3/3) but failed the strengthened proof (3/3) specifically on `[false, false]` versus `[false, true]`. No production code change or new tests. The fixture shrank three lines; its test-line allocation shrinks from 177 to 175, matching actual net test growth. The separate real built-Gateway concurrent-RPC proof below addresses the hosted entry-point request without changing the committed regression.

Final strengthened-proof validation: 98 focused tests passed (40.19s wrapper); targeted test typecheck, lint, formatting, mock-export ratchet (6476) and exact test-line ratchet (175-line allocation) passed. Previous full production build is reused because production bytes are unchanged.


### Shipped-entrypoint concurrent-RPC proof

Ran the real compiled `node dist/index.js gateway` in a separate process with an isolated temporary home/state/config, loopback-only test port, and synthetic local plugins. No direct catalog-handler invocation or mocked Gateway was used. The proof used the native isolated-process and authenticated WebSocket-client fixtures; channels, providers, cron, browser control and canvas were disabled. `OPENCLAW_TEST_MINIMAL_GATEWAY` was explicitly unset.

Twelve enabled synthetic plugins each perform 80 ms of synchronous registration work only after the driver arms the fixture following Gateway startup. After the first catalog registration began, the same authenticated WebSocket client sent unrelated `health` while `tools.catalog` remained pending:

```text
entrypoint: node dist/index.js gateway
plugins: 12; synchronous registration CPU: 80 ms each
registrations begun when health was sent: 1
health RPC: 245.49 ms
catalog completion: 1065.56 ms
catalog pending when health completed: true
health completion observed before registrations 4 through 12: true
catalog fixture tools returned: 12/12
proof: PASS
isolated Gateway shutdown and native fixture cleanup: joined
```

The later registrations synchronously read a marker written only after the client received the health response, so response delivery during final cleanup cannot satisfy the proof. All 12 optional tool rows were returned. This complements the committed `[false, true]` between-registration regression and its fully reverted synchronous negative control; it does not replace or weaken them.

The existing successful production build was reused: its stamp records `4cdf4ea4a5b79d4e1b02007b76aa91ead9547528`, and later commits through `da27dd52ad37718bad16f67aa8d6e09a7317f241` change only tests and ratchet ledgers. The compiled catalog uses `acquireStandalonePluginToolRegistry` and awaited release. This is a real built-Gateway/WebSocket proof with synthetic plugins, not a measurement of the live npm installation, a Control UI interaction, a real-model turn, or a general latency guarantee. Individual callbacks still block for their own CPU duration.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes completed requests being revived, or the current human request being lost, when a conversation is compacted after tool, automated, or split-turn messages.

## User Impact

Conversations retain the current human request and bounded source facts across compaction, fallback summaries, and session reload. No configuration change or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select the pending human request from its recorded provenance and pass that same request through each compaction path. Preserve useful historical source context in its own bounded section, so completed requests do not become pending work again. Existing compaction and summary-quality owners retain the policy; no parallel cache, schema, or request-selection service is introduced.

## Evidence

- 149 focused tests passed, covering request selection, split turns, small context limits, degraded summaries, persisted reload, provider fallback, and prompt-prefix stability.
- Targeted TypeScript checks, type-aware lint, format parity, and the parent-relative file-size gate passed. Two unsafe casts were removed and the assertion-safety baseline was updated to the actual count.

- Hosted CI for this new head is pending. Two UI retry timeouts on the earlier head remain unclassified; local passing UI checks do not establish their cause or waive hosted CI.
- These are isolated regression and boundary checks. A real-provider Telegram compaction replay and production delivery have not been demonstrated by this PR.

<details>
<summary>Change size and ownership</summary>

Against the merge base: production +224/−77 lines; tests and support +632/−22 lines across 21 files.

The remaining production growth carries human-request provenance and bounded source context through existing compaction owners. prs.title: fix(logging): release idle diagnostic session activities
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the diagnostic run-activity index keeps one retained activity per session identity for the whole process lifetime, so a long-running Gateway that mints a fresh session identity per run (cron runs, boot sessions, subagents) grows that index without bound.

## User Impact

User impact: a Gateway left running with scheduled jobs now keeps a bounded number of diagnostic session activities instead of one per run, so its memory use stops growing on its own.

## Why This Change Was Made

`activityByRef` (`src/logging/diagnostic-run-activity-state.ts`) indexes the diagnostic `SessionActivity` objects by session ref (`id:<sessionId>` and `key:<sessionKey>`). It has **no per-entry delete path at all**: at the audited tag the only removal is the wholesale `.clear()` in `stopDiagnosticRunActivityTracking()`, which runs once at process stop. The writes are **one** `.set()` call site (inside the `for (const ref of sessionRefs(params))` loop, so it registers two refs per session) plus one re-pointing write that rewrites an existing key. Line numbers here are **as of the audited tag**; this audit's fix adds lines to that file, so at the branch head the same call site is at `:205`.

The sibling map `activityByRunId` *is* released on terminal events — `activityByRunId.delete(event.runId)` inside `recordRunCompleted`. That asymmetry is the bug: the teardown paths that look like they release a session (`recordRunCompleted`, `closeDiagnosticEmbeddedRunOwner`, `markDiagnosticEmbeddedRunEnded`, `clearDiagnosticEmbeddedRunActivityForSession`) clear the activity's inner maps but never remove the refs that keep the object reachable.

This matters in the default configuration, not only for pathological setups: diagnostics are enabled unless the operator sets `diagnostics.enabled = false`, the tracker starts with the process, and a five-minute cron job mints 288 distinct session identities per day.

The sibling index in this same repository already does the right thing — `diagnosticSessionStates` carries a 30-minute TTL, a 2 000-entry cap and prune-on-insert. The same pattern was never applied to the run-activity refs.

The fix adds `pruneDiagnosticSessionActivityRefs()`, mirroring that sibling:

- an activity is releasable only when nothing points at live work — no active embedded run, tool, model call or core model call, no registered owner, and not tracked by a live run;
- idle activities expire after 30 minutes of no progress, the same window the sibling index uses;
- at most 2 000 activities are retained, and the least recently progressed idle ones are evicted first;
- `id:` and `key:` are released together, because releasing only one would keep the activity reachable through the other;
- the prune runs on the resolve path, so the cap holds during normal operation and a stale entry cannot answer for a session that is starting fresh work.

## Evidence

Growth measured against this tree's own modules:

| Scenario | refs in `activityByRef` | distinct `SessionActivity` objects |
|---|---|---|
| 50 session resets, same session key | 51 | 1 |
| 50 cron-like runs, unique key + id | 100 | 50 |
| 1 chat + 50 cron-like runs | 102 | 51 |

New regression test:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.logging.config.ts src/logging/diagnostic-run-activity-refs.test.ts
 ✓  logging  src/logging/diagnostic-run-activity-refs.test.ts > diagnostic session activity refs > releases idle activities whose ttl expired
 ✓  logging  src/logging/diagnostic-run-activity-refs.test.ts > diagnostic session activity refs > keeps activities that still have an active embedded run
 ✓  logging  src/logging/diagnostic-run-activity-refs.test.ts > diagnostic session activity refs > releases both refs of an evicted activity
 ✓  logging  src/logging/diagnostic-run-activity-refs.test.ts > diagnostic session activity refs > caps the retained activity set

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

The `logging` shard's failing-test set is identical before and after this change: the same 8 failures in `console-capture.test.ts` and `subsystem.test.ts`, reproduced on a pristine checkout of this tag and therefore pre-existing (they are reported separately). No test changed state.

## Files changed

- `src/logging/diagnostic-run-activity-state.ts` — add `pruneDiagnosticSessionActivityRefs()` (idle test, TTL, cap, paired ref release) and call it from the resolve path.
- `src/logging/diagnostic-run-activity-refs.test.ts` — new regression test (4 test cases / 11 `expect(...)` calls).

## Compatibility

No public API change: no exported symbol was removed or retyped, and the diagnostic surface is internal to the logging subsystem.

A session's diagnostic snapshot now disappears after 30 idle minutes instead of being retained for the process lifetime. That matches the behaviour the sibling session-state index already has, and diagnostics are best-effort. Live work is never evicted: an activity with an active embedded run, tool, model call, core model call, registered owner or tracked run is kept regardless of age.

## Risk of regression

Low, and measured. The `logging` shard's failing-test set is byte-identical before and after, and the full fast unit shard shows the same three pre-existing upstream failures as its baseline.

## How to verify

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.logging.config.ts src/logging/diagnostic-run-activity-refs.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.logging.config.ts
```

## Notes for the reviewer

`pruneDiagnosticSessionActivityRefs` is deliberately conservative in two directions: it only evicts activities that are provably idle, and it releases both refs of an activity in the same pass. The TTL and the 2 000-activity cap mirror `diagnosticSessionStates` in `src/logging/diagnostic-session-state.ts`, so both diagnostic indexes now age the same way.
```

### Commit

```
fix(logging): release idle diagnostic session activities

The diagnostic run-activity index kept one retained SessionActivity per
session identity for the whole process lifetime: activityByRef has no
delete path, while its sibling activityByRunId is released on terminal
events. The teardown paths that look like they release a session clear
the activity's inner maps but never remove the refs that keep the object
reachable.

Diagnostics are on by default and a five-minute cron job mints 288
distinct session identities per day, so the index grew without bound on
a Gateway that was otherwise idle.

Add pruneDiagnosticSessionActivityRefs, mirroring the sibling
diagnosticSessionStates index: an activity is releasable only when
nothing points at live work, idle activities expire after 30 minutes of
no progress, at most 2000 activities are retained, and the id: and key:
refs are released together so the object cannot stay reachable through
one of them.
```

---

prs.title: fix(infra): stop shadowing real session-work counters in safe-restart preflight
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`createSafeGatewayRestartPreflight()` shadowed six of the snapshot's inspectors with literal zeros placed **after** the caller spread:

```ts
const snapshot = createGatewayActiveWorkSnapshot({
  ...inspectors,
  getSessionAdmissions: () => 0,
  getSessionMutations: () => 0,
  getChatRuns: () => 0,
  getQueuedTurns: () => 0,
  getTerminalPersistence: () => 0,
  getTerminalSessions: () => 0,
});
```

`createGatewayActiveWorkSnapshot` already defaults `getSessionAdmissions` to the live `getSessionControllerWorkCount()` and `getSessionMutations` to `getSessionMutationCount()`. The post-spread zeros clobbered those defaults (and would clobber any caller-supplied inspectors for those keys), so the safe-restart preflight was blind to in-flight session admissions and lifecycle mutations.

## Fix

- Pass caller inspectors through untouched: `createGatewayActiveWorkSnapshot(inspectors)`. The snapshot defaults provide the live session counters; `getChatRuns` / `getQueuedTurns` / `getTerminalPersistence` / `getTerminalSessions` keep their zero defaults.
- Project `sessionAdmissions` and `sessionMutations` into the returned `counts` and include them in `totalActive`, so `safe` now respects session work.
- Derive `summary` from `safe`: a session-only deferral previously produced an empty `blockers` list together with a "safe to restart now" summary; it now reports `restart deferred: active session work`.
- Extend `SafeRestartInspectors` with the six session keys so callers/tests can pass them.

## Evidence

**Production timeline (observed before the fix):** `gateway.restart.safe` reported "safe to restart now" and scheduled the restart immediately while session work was active, returning an empty `blockers` list. After the fix, the same session-work conditions produce `safe: false`, a populated `counts` entry for `sessionAdmissions`/`sessionMutations`, `totalActive > 0`, and the summary `restart deferred: active session work`.

**Regression repro (fails before, passes after):**

- Active session admissions: `getSessionAdmissions: () => 3` → `safe: false`, with `counts.sessionAdmissions` respected and `totalActive` including it. On the previous code the literal-zero stub clobbered the override, so the preflight stayed safe.
- Active session lifecycle mutations: `getSessionMutations: () => 2` → same shape (`safe: false`, count projected, `totalActive` includes it). Also fails on the previous code for the same reason.
- Existing assertions updated for the two newly projected counts.

**Suites run:**

- `src/infra/restart-coordinator.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-methods/restart.test.ts`

Result: 24/24 passing, two consecutive clean runs. No code changes accompany this body update.

prs.title: feat(agents): routes inherit the vendor row's reasoning replay
prs.body:
Follows openclaw/openclaw#187730 (landed).

## What Problem This Solves

Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4 need `reasoning_content` replayed on assistant turns. Today an exact-ID list decides that, so a host's dated or "fast" id for the same model (`…-0813`, `kimi-k3-fast-api`) misses it and multi-turn tool calls break.

## User Impact

On the aggregator routes listed below, assistant turns now carry `reasoning_content` like the vendor route does. Nothing changes on vendor routes or released installs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Decision 2 as scoped with Ayaan: row-less routes inherit only **model facts** from the vendor row. Core already had that owner (`createBundledModelIdentityFactsResolver`, used by ClawRouter). This PR generalizes it to every resolved model in `normalizeResolvedModel` for one fact: `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages`.

- Vendor row: a row of a provider whose manifest `family` is the provider itself. It is matched by `canonicalModelKey` and only over the **same request API**. An ambiguous key inherits nothing, and a host's own value always wins.
- Not inherited: `thinkingFormat` and effort support. They are route facts (OpenRouter serves DeepSeek with `reasoning: {effort}`, DeepSeek direct with `thinking: {type}`). Ladder, default, `thinkingRequired` and wire maps also stay per route.
- Data: Moonshot Kimi rows and DeepSeek V4 rows declare `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages: true` (they already replayed through the ID list or the DeepSeek endpoint default).
- The ID list stays as the fallback for routes without a vendor match (Ollama tags use another API; transcript policy reads only the model ID).

## Aggregator request bodies that change (hosted catalog rows, today)

These routes start replaying `reasoning_content` because the exact-ID list misses their id spelling:

- `baseten/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`

Every other hosted aggregator row that matches a Kimi or DeepSeek vendor row already replays today (ID list), so its body is unchanged. Full table: replay-inheritance impact report in the maintainer handoff notes.

## Evidence

- `pnpm catalog:compare-released`, baseline built from `main` and candidate from this branch (same models.dev snapshot, current timestamps): 2026.10.9 (latest), 2026.9.36 (extended-stable) and 2026.10.10-beta.4 (beta) each show 0 changes to offered levels, defaults and request bodies (86 `model.*` echo lines of the added data, both PRs together).

prs.title: fix: keep Codex goals advancing across turns and restarts
prs.body:
Related: #102260, #167897, #175918.

## Problem and behavior

Local Codex sessions can finish a reply while their OpenClaw Goal remains active, requiring repeated `/goal resume`. This PR extends the existing Goal continuation queue to local Codex and restores durably accepted Goal continuations after Gateway restart.

The same queue, admission, accounting, operator-authority, and reply-delivery owners remain responsible. Pause, Stop, completion, session/Goal replacement, current permissions, and budgets remain authoritative. Codex's native autonomous Goal engine stays disabled.

Maintainer decision requested: approve local Codex automatic pursuit and recovery of accepted Goal inputs as one capability. Earlier implementations deliberately supported narrower placement/lifecycle boundaries; this expansion needs owner agreement.

## Evidence and remaining gates

Evidence below applies to head `4ba6e39ad497`. Latest inspection: October 19, 2026.

| Claim | Evidence | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source restrictions survive recovery | Original failure reproduced; real SQLite replay, production operator restoration, host-bound file effects, policy narrowing, and revocation checks | Passed |
| Recovered replies reach authorized WebChat clients | Original missing-final-event failure reproduced; authenticated subscribed WebSocket receives the repaired final reply | Passed with simulated model |
| Shipped-release data remains usable | Packaged 2026.10.5 → candidate drill preserves settings, complete existing Goal, and original transcript data; candidate edits and completes that same Goal | Passed |
| Candidate runs on existing operator state | Verified backup, real Doctor migrations, authenticated RPC build identity, readiness, valid config, loaded Codex plugin, and fresh error-level Doctor lint | Passed |
| Consecutive local Codex Goal pursuit with a real model | Current production activity is not sufficient proof; see observation below | Open |
| Accepted Goal continuation survives an actual runtime restart | Integration coverage exists; a real-model runtime demonstration remains needed | Open |
| Integration with current main | GitHub reports conflicts; three text conflicts confirmed against `f455495cd8819` | Open |
| Maintainer approval and required CI | Owner decision outstanding; `openclaw/ci-gate` pending at inspection | Open |

### Production observation: do not count ordinary activity as Goal proof

The installed candidate is executing real local Codex work. However, the inspected session's Goal was `paused`, with `continuationTurns: 0`, after a thread-ownership rejection: `Codex thread <redacted> is claimed by active work; stop it first.` Later work was attributed to a native child-result continuation. That activity does not demonstrate successful Goal-led continuation.

The persisted lifecycle owner pauses an active Goal after a terminal failed run. The Codex adapter rejects releasing a thread still claimed or protected by active work. Whether this observed rejection is an existing ownership problem, an interaction with this change, or an expected overlapping request still requires a focused reproduction. Do not bypass the ownership guard or infer a successful Goal run from tool activity alone. Private session identifiers, transcript contents, and model/account details are omitted.

### Packaged upgrade proof

The published `2026.10.5` runtime (`1b58cb9a1b4f`) created the setting, admitted and paused a Goal through its public API, and wrote three transcript messages. After clean shutdown, the candidate ran Doctor and config validation on the same synthetic state. The setting and complete Goal—including ID, counters, timestamps, and status—were preserved, as were original message IDs, content, and usage. Editing and completing the existing Goal also passed.

The sole response difference was an additive `assistant.usage.contextUsage: { state: "unavailable" }` projection, verified against both packaged serializers. This covers the exercised data path, not every possible plugin database.

Artifact SHA-256: `73ad91edee7838a73c2efc5001c179bac9f42bf6af467456fa3aacd81b95662d`.

The operator deployment used the documented external-terminal package-manager/Doctor workflow after the old updater refused its native handoff check before activation. Doctor completed; the same Gateway process became ready after its initial 90-second readiness budget expired. Independent error-level lint returned `ok: true` with no findings. These are deployment observations, not a Goal benchmark.

## Implementation and regression coverage

The three earlier [ClawSweeper findings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177351#issuecomment-6269149380) are addressed:

- Persist source execution restrictions before acceptance, including explicit empty caps, independent glob intersections, disabled tools, restart-safe tools, and code-mode restrictions. Recovery combines them with current policy and revalidates authority before effects.
- Reconstruct internal/WebChat delivery through existing late-reply finalization and session-writer authority.
- Keep Goal identity/policy types independent of session types, removing the import cycle.

Original restriction-loss and WebChat delivery failures were reproduced before repair. Coverage includes four real SQLite/operator/file-effect/revocation cases, all four command-settlement modes (including the real disabled-tool command-attempt path), 63 Goal queue tests, 15 recovery tests, 7 policy tests, and 5 prompt/tool-prefix tests. Core plus four affected type graphs, runtime/type import-cycle guards, mock-export ratchet, changed-file lint/format, and independent repair review passed. Full repository CI and real-model Goal/restart proof are not claimed.

## Integration work and limits

Conflicts against `f455495cd8819` are in `docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md`, `src/config/sessions/session-entry-list.worker.ts`, and `src/config/sessions/session-pending-input-history.kernel.ts`. Preserve upstream chat/steering/deferred recovery while retaining Goal-specific selection, source policy, and delivery. In particular, upstream's expanded queued-input selection must not allow ordinary chat recovery and Goal recovery to consume the same private Goal input.

No new database schema, configuration option, or parallel scheduler is introduced. Older private PR records without source-policy information stop visibly instead of resuming with broader permissions. Startup restores accepted inputs; an active Goal row alone does not authorize new work. A hard crash before durable acceptance can still require `/goal resume`. Exhausted retries and genuinely blocked work do not become unlimited retries.

After resolving integration and real-runtime proof, update this evidence and request one fresh ClawSweeper review.

prs.title: fix: allow authorized WebUI and channel guidance in the same session
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes corrections being treated as another person's steering when a user moves between the WebUI and a channel during an active turn in the same authorized session.

## User Impact

Verified personal profiles with administrator-attested channel links can continue their active work across transports. Shared-token/password WebUI users can also continue work with a channel participant in that exact session: when collaborative steering is disabled, the WebUI side needs current administrative authority and the channel side needs current owner authority. Pairing or permission to chat alone is insufficient.

Guidance uses the incumbent execution's unchanged requester and prepared permissions, including permissions unavailable to the incoming participant. This bounded Shared Owner exception when collaboration is disabled is an explicitly accepted product decision. Actual message authors remain separately recorded; Shared Owner does not identify which human used a shared credential. New executions retain the actual submitter and resolve current applicable policy. No configuration options, defaults, storage, or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing continuation and final-admission owners rather than equating transport identities. Host-held authentication distinguishes Shared Owner access from a profile label, and existing channel-owner authority supplies the bounded exception. Revocation, session access, cancellation, exact execution/backend ownership, execution settings, and final submission checks remain enforced. Different personal administrators gain no general owner-to-owner exception.

Authorized continuation retains the incumbent task-suggestion tools and delivery setting. Questions, approvals, explicit cancellation, queue ordering, fallback custody, and cross-session `sessions_send(mode="steer")` keep their separate contracts. Included-channel repairs preserve admitted asserted-owner authority, Mattermost's host admission context, queued plugin callback lifetime, and Feishu's actual DM conversation ID; known bot inputs cannot use the human exception.

## Evidence

Candidate: `5ed0c71b220c05747dccc161e1d2be76ae074fb3`; merge base: `faa38148f2c5ba3fe8f69bd3ae0150c87edf7758`. Rebased onto the latest observed `origin/main` at the maintainer's request. The sole conflict was the generated configuration-doc hashes; regenerated them from combined source and passed the generator check. Range-diff confirms every production/test change is patch-identical to the reviewed predecessor; LoC churn is unchanged. Current-head CI has settled; all branch-related checks pass. The sole inherited restart failure and downstream gate remain red as detailed below.

- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40996353761), attempt 1, settled: **55 successful CI jobs, 26 skipped, one inherited failing test shard plus its aggregate gate**. All branch-related test/type/lint/build/docs/security lanes pass. The sole failing case remains `test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts`, with `SessionEntryChangedDuringReadError` before initial `FINISHED_0_background`, before restart or continuation is exercised. This matches the independent base reproduction linked below. The failing test/support and session-storage/read, embedded-execution, and sandbox-status sources are Git-object identical across that executed baseline, current `faa38148` base, and actual tested merge `d4e30d17`; prior baseline proof is reused with that source qualification. The automatic classifier says unknown because no matching main job; it is not cited as a main matching-signature verdict. All PR checks are terminal: 76 success, 50 skipped, 1 neutral; three red contexts are this shard and duplicated downstream gate contexts. Landing uses the explicitly authorized inherited-failure route, preserving red CI rather than claiming all CI green.
- [Pre-rebase CI on `397b09e4`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40993563659) settled: all branch-related repair lanes, production/test types, lint, build, docs, security, and continuation consumers pass. The sole failing test is `test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts`, with aggregate CI-gate failures reflecting it. This is **pre-existing**: independent candidate and exact-base `5f3afbe` builds under the same Node/pinned Bun versions both fail before initial background completion with `SessionEntryChangedDuringReadError` and missing `FINISHED_0_background`; all nine sibling Gateway lifecycle cases pass on both. [Base reproduction](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ce3a4371cf3612961e01bc56b8f59643), [candidate reproduction](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ace6bf36ce42a30df7734c6f31385294). The second checkout's base install in the candidate run exhausted disk quota; the separate base receipt supplies actual baseline execution. This independent defect is not repaired or masked here.
- Hosted ClawSweeper found that a matching verified profile could let known bot input use the human continuation exception. The repair requires the existing host-held human-ingress fact on both sides, retaining profile attribution. Both new final-admission cases fail on the published predecessor (incorrectly prepared rather than deferred), then all 55 join, 35 fallback, and 23 Gateway cases pass with the fix. Production/test types, lint and format pass on [the AWS repair run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_16d1cab8efc9a44eb41df1ad80cf9728). The committed repair patch hash matches the tested patch.
- Five branch-related CI fixture/type failures were repaired without weakening contracts: complete admitted host context; configured iMessage owner capability; string sender parameter; complete prepared-join mock; and public absent-property inventory excluding private symbols while full legacy/projected read parity remains asserted. [AWS fixture validation](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0dcc31ea8e55591c3de04a4c9a75c093) passed 101 tests in five files, three affected test-type projects, lint and format. These two AWS receipts are access-controlled, not anonymously viewable.
- Focused boundary proof covers linked personal identity, strict Shared Owner continuation in both directions, non-owner and forged/shared-label rejection, different sessions, model/settings incompatibility, revocation, cancellation/backend replacement, pending-question separation, fallback custody, and incumbent task settings. Previously recorded 424 distinct focused cases are reused within their source scopes. The final Feishu host-admission regression is red on its predecessor and all 62 owner cases passed on pre-rebase `0db650ae`; these counts are not added together. Targeted production/test typechecks, lint, format, and diff checks passed in their recorded scopes.
- Real human channel ingress and rendered WebUI/live-model continuation passed in both directions across Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, Slack, Mattermost, Matrix, iMessage, Signal, Lark/Feishu, Google Chat, and Microsoft Teams. Correlation checks established the exact continuing execution, unchanged governing requester, separately retained author, completed model consumption, and harmless policy-dependent effects. Live proof culminated at pre-rebase `0db650ae`, with earlier source-scoped reuse; it is not fresh execution of the rebased candidate. Exact-head PR CI is the current integration gate.
- Pre-rebase [runtime/UI build and qualification](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_dcd67d396881bf921c7796b9be87ee3d), [earlier rendered proof build](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0482fe32e4ed722ee723208e1a29121b), and [Feishu focused checks](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_035ddc527b56) are access-controlled receipts (anonymous reads return 403). Final raw-source and original runtime/UI manifests matched their pinned `0db650ae` candidate. Those task-owned Gateways, public ingress routes, fixtures, and AWS leases were removed or released.
- Full pre-rebase local ClawSweeper reviewed `1157b711..0db650ae` (301.831s): complete, no actionable correctness/security findings, no low-value tests identified. Independent implementation/repair reviews are separately source-scoped. The local review asks for an owner decision on the bounded strict-mode Shared Owner exception; that decision is already explicitly accepted. A second full local review of `5f3afbe..93b0bdff` completed in 215.438s with no code findings. It requested final-boundary proof: the existing real Telegram strict non-owner run refused the input, left it unconsumed through final idle, and let the incumbent finish its harmless patch. Owner/admin revocation before submission is covered by existing production-owner boundary tests asserting zero backend delivery; it is not a live channel revocation demonstration. The initial hosted review identified the bot defect and two of the repaired fixtures; a complete local ClawSweeper review of `93b0bdff..397b09e4` finished in 158.523s with no correctness/security findings or low-value tests. That source-only review did not receive execution receipts; the red/green AWS results above supply them, alongside the previously scoped live human proof and final-boundary revocation tests. [Settled hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188029#issuecomment-6513359249) covers pre-rebase head `397b09e4f1126a320188dc15d5ede5ce5b743535`: platinum for Overall readiness, Proof confidence, and Patch quality; no actionable findings and no Before merge items. Ready for maintainer review.

Limitations: no fresh live owner-revocation-during-preparation run is claimed. This is bounded continuation proof, not a fresh exhaustive backend/restart/approval/cancellation matrix. The Matrix forward run omitted its patch call; earlier matching-source patch proof is reused explicitly. Lark's earlier reverse run is reused. A preexisting Lark `/followup` immediate acknowledgment defect was isolated and left outside this PR. Transcript persistence or a provider send receipt alone is never counted as model consumption or steering acceptance.

<details>
<summary>Measured costs and LoC churn</summary>

Whole change against the merge base: **39 files, +1,443/-176 = 1,619 changed lines**.

| Category | Added | Deleted | Churn |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Production | 498 | 129 | 627 |
| Tests | 912 | 42 | 954 |

The smallest coherent stage is the continuation rule plus its real channel admission consumers. The included producer/custody repairs were required by the live flow; separating them would leave requested channels broken. Tests extend existing owner suites for distinct authority, lifetime, question, and transport boundaries. Main's current budget policy requires a separate allocation for this change's exact 870 net test lines; the record names those regressions and the shared scalar is unchanged. No new manager, persistent state, or per-tool check was added.

CI repair measurements (Linux AWS, Node 24.22.1): initial five files 47.48/41.36/139.65/60.61/62.88s; bot regression red 50.74s, full join/fallback/Gateway green 46.97/65.56/60.47s. Cold transform dominates wall time; the suites retain real policy/admission and consumer contracts. Initial types 13.82/15.43/14.93s, lint 201.48s; repair production/test types 16.60/15.01/15.58s, lint 165.81s; formatting 0.13s each. The operator suite exercises real configured/linked owner and grant/revocation boundaries; helper-only checks cannot replace it. The main CI run elapsed 562s. Paired restart attribution used candidate build116.85s + replay457.97s and independent base install210.18s + build117.28s + replay460.09s; both tests failed as recorded, and wrapper success on the base means evidence capture succeeded. prs.title: feat(wear): let OpenClaw be the watch's default assistant
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The OpenClaw watch app cannot be picked as the watch's default digital assistant, so the assistant button or gesture always opens another assistant.

## User Impact

On Wear OS, OpenClaw now appears under Settings → Apps → Default apps → Digital assistant. Picking it makes the assistant button open OpenClaw straight to the Talk page.

## Summary

### High Level TLDR

The phone app already declares `android.intent.action.ASSIST`, but the Wear app did not, so Wear OS never listed it as an assistant. Other companion apps, such as Home Assistant, do list there. This change declares `ASSIST` and `VOICE_COMMAND` on the Wear `MainActivity` and routes those launches to the existing Voice (Talk) page.

### Exact change

- Manifest: added an `ASSIST` / `VOICE_COMMAND` intent filter (category `DEFAULT`) to `MainActivity`.
- `parseWearLaunchTarget` maps those actions to `WearLaunchTarget.Voice`, reusing the tile's Talk launch path.
- `consumeWearLaunchTarget` rewrites the consumed action to `MAIN`. Recreation then reopens the normal Chat start page, the same consume-once behavior the tile extra already has.
- Talk is not started automatically. The user still taps to start, so the mic never opens without a direct tap.

### Scope boundary

- Watch app only.
- No new permissions, no `VoiceInteractionService`, and no changes to the phone app or Gateway.

## Evidence

### Verification

- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40995675227) passed, including Wear unit tests, Android lint, phone unit tests, native access checks, localization, and security. The required `openclaw/ci-gate` is green.
- `./gradlew :wear:ktlintCheck :wear:testDebugUnitTest` passed. `WearLaunchIntentTest` ran 11 tests with 0 failures.
- New test `assistantLaunchStartsOnVoiceOnce`: both `ACTION_ASSIST` and `ACTION_VOICE_COMMAND` open Voice, and a second read of the same intent falls back to Chat.
- `./gradlew :wear:assembleDebug` passed.

### Review

- [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187587#issuecomment-6494721064) covered the [unchanged source head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4fee1a11174c2036154466c8207dd9cb2cd663b5). It reported no actionable findings and no before-merge blockers. Hardware proof remains a disclosed gap.

### What was not tested

- On-watch adb verification was not performed. Galaxy Watch default-assistant selection and cold/warm assistant-button dispatch to Talk remain unverified on hardware. This limitation is disclosed for the authorized landing.

prs.title: fix(cron): carry the failure-alert delivery outcome in repair briefs
prs.body:
Related: #186990

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a channel-less gateway, a failing automation's operator alert cannot be delivered — the delivery failure (`Channel is required (no configured channels detected)`) is recorded only in job state fields, while the repair brief injected into the owner conversation says just `No failure alert was sent.` The operator's only visible signal omits the reason, and nothing points at the state that explains it.

## User Impact

User impact: the repair brief now carries the last failure-alert delivery outcome from job state — the recorded status and reason when a delivery failed (for the reporter's case: `not-delivered: Channel is required (no configured channels detected).`), the fact of delivery when it succeeded, and the original bare sentence when no attempt was recorded. The recurring variant keeps its consecutiveErrors counter, so each brief states both how many runs failed and why the operator alert is missing. This is the report's Expected second branch ("the repair brief carries the delivery-failure fact itself").

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildCronFailureRepairBrief` hard-coded `No failure alert was sent.` in both variants with no access to the delivery trace that `failureNotificationDeliveryFromJobState` already resolves from job state. The brief is the operator's only visible signal on a channel-less gateway, so the delivery-failure fact belongs in it.

## Evidence

- New `src/cron/service/failure-repair-brief.test.ts` (5 tests): the bare sentence is preserved when no delivery attempt exists; a failed delivery renders the recorded status and reason verbatim; a delivered alert is stated instead of the negative claim; the terminal one-shot variant includes the delivery state alongside the disabled notice; the recurring variant keeps its consecutiveErrors counter.
- Consumer suites `failure-alerts.outcome/persistence/account-routing`: 32 tests green on head `94eaf14c313`; `oxlint` on touched files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

## Risk and Compatibility

- Error-string composition only; no delivery, scheduling, or incident-state change. The deduplication semantics are unchanged: the existing `!repair` push condition keeps one counted brief per incident (`consecutiveErrors` in the text is the counter the report asks for), so this change cannot increase brief frequency.
- The report's Expected offers "either" a doctor/status-line item **or** this brief wording; the doctor/status-line option is left as a follow-up and is not required by the report's Expected sentence.

## LOC

production +23/−4 in 2 files; tests +84 in 1 new file. No docs or generated code.

## Not Tested

- No live gateway run; the wording is covered directly at the brief-builder boundary with the delivery shapes the report records.

prs.title: fix(release): support nonblocking FRV job reruns
prs.body:
## Problem

Job-scoped FRV reruns synchronously follow the replacement attempt and parent reseal, blocking an agent turn for 6–10 minutes.

RRI-396

## Solution

- add `frv rerun --job <child>:<job> --no-follow`
- preserve the existing follow-and-reseal behavior by default
- return a typed accepted receipt only after mutation reconciliation and replacement-attempt job materialization
- print exact `frv watch` and `frv continue --failed` commands
- reject `--no-follow` outside job-scoped reruns and expose it in help

The change reuses the existing rerun reconciliation/materialization owner; it adds no new mutation path or state.

## Impact

Operators and agents can dispatch a precise job rerun, receive stable run/attempt/job identity immediately, and continue the FRV later without holding the initiating turn open.

Production delta: +45/-1 lines. Test delta: +62 lines, recorded in the test-line allocation.
