prs.title: fix(talk): subagent launches fail during direct agent consults
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes operator-owned Talk agent consults losing the Gateway binding needed for subagent launches when no ambient Gateway request scope is available.

## User Impact

Talk consults retain their original Gateway for delegated tools instead of hitting `Operator subagent spawn requires its current Gateway binding`. No configuration changes, permission expansion, or migration is needed; the spawn guard and source/abort lifetime checks remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Talk runtime already receives the owning resolver but does not bind it to the admitted execution context. Bind it through the existing `onAdmitted` callback, as other ingress paths do, without adding an ambient/global fallback or tying accepted work to the audio transport. The production repair remains four lines.

One three-row regression extends the existing spawn production-boundary suite and shared support, replacing the weaker resolver-only assertions in the terminal-write tests. It enters the production Talk consult runner with a retained authenticated operator, invokes the actual `sessions_spawn` tool without ambient Gateway request scope, and uses real Gateway dispatch and child admission.

- Authorized caller: the original Gateway admits the child; its real admitted run, RPC source, and registry/session ownership are observed.
- Caller revoked after Talk admission and child preparation: real device-source invalidation rejects dispatch before child admission/registration.
- Gateway replaced after Talk admission and child preparation: dispatch rejects, with neither original nor replacement facade admitting child work.

## Evidence

- Red control: remove only the four production-fix lines. The authorized operator case fails at `subagent-spawn.ts:148` with `Operator subagent spawn requires its current Gateway binding`. Production bytes are restored afterward.
- Corrected final fixture: all three Talk child-admission cases pass. Command wall time: approximately 78s including cold compilation; test bodies total approximately 11.23s. The real dispatch/admission composition, not inference, is the required proof boundary.
- Existing Talk terminal-write/abort contracts remain intact: final rerun 3/3 pass, approximately 19s wall. The earlier three-file Talk sibling run passed 24/24, approximately 102s wall.
- Targeted lint, formatting, scoped test typecheck, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh isolated independent AutoReview of the complete corrected candidate: no actionable P0-P2 findings.

### CI import-cycle follow-up

Removed the new result-helper back-import from the shared spawn support, keeping the two deterministic result fixtures local and equivalent. No tests or production behavior were added or changed. The exact failing Madge check went from one cycle to zero; all three affected Talk cases pass again (approximately 91.58s wall, including cold compilation). Targeted lint, format, scoped typecheck, and a fresh independent review of this small repair pass. Current-head hosted CI is separate from this local verification.

### Investigated local failures

The broader spawn owner-file run before the final operator-fixture correction had 80 passing and six failing existing native Stop cases (approximately 313s wall). All six also fail with the owner tests restored to unchanged published-head versions: `preserves routed native Stop authority and existing receipts` for `retained-exact`, `consumed-channel`, `consumed-command-handler`, `consumed-session`, `consumed-generation-replaced`, and `consumed-active-revoked`. Assertions concern existing command-exit/source-abort behavior; these failures remain unresolved and are not reported green. After the fixture correction, only the affected three rows, terminal-write tests, and static checks were rerun; the broad file was not repeated.

## Real-provider after-fix Talk smoke

PASS on exact head 04ec91b6213af1085b6f9878ce4f21f9079fb05e, source-built runtime/UI with matching build identity, isolated fresh-state Gateway. One persistent signed/authenticated public Gateway SDK connection called the shipped Talk relay create/audio/close endpoints. Synthetic spoken input was transcribed by the real voice provider, which initiated the native Talk agent consultation. No chat.send substitution, direct consult helper, inference mock, or driver-issued child spawn was used.

Observed native consult run: talk-realtime-relay-consult-d17cbe3e-5402-4034-a5c5-9adfbb78990d. The real backing model invoked sessions_spawn and received accepted child run c2d42987-f809-40b6-98ec-2124a63fc392. It then invoked agents_wait, which returned that same child as done with exactly TALK_CHILD_OK. Independent child history confirmed the exact output. A reduced/redacted event capture is supplied in the PR discussion; credentials, endpoints/IPs, binary audio and model identifiers are omitted.

One create attempt, no retries. The same owner connection closed Talk successfully. The temporary Gateway shut down cleanly and its container/listener were removed; all 11 task-private databases pass integrity checks. Original Gateway process identity and config/runtime/native-auth hashes remain unchanged.

## Main-merge compatibility repair

After main was merged into this branch, upstream's Talk refactor had relocated resolveTalkAgentConsultAuthority into client-tool-authority.ts. The added boundary fixture still imported it from client-gateway-control.ts, causing the same missing-export/setup error in the three Talk cases and both production/test typechecks. Commit d923b93eb6f537b7da0f7750dc1db1c74aaa46ce changes only that one test import to its current owner.

On the synchronized source, the three focused Talk cases pass (83 unrelated owner-file cases intentionally skipped), both tsconfig.core.json and the agents-sessions test typecheck pass, and one-file lint/format/diff checks plus fresh independent review pass. Production code and test assertions are unchanged. Fresh hosted CI is pending; the earlier accepted live capture remains evidence for its explicitly pinned 04ec91b6 revision, not a new runtime trial.

## Current-main conflict reconciliation

Merge commit 602ceecc042e76350945b53fd4a188551d913b91 incorporates pinned main 904703bef63222ab459cbabdd7556bdb3e542fec. The two manual test conflicts retain both upstream Access-case registrations and all three Talk authority cases, and adopt upstream terminal-write import/type cleanup without restoring tests upstream removed. The terminal-write file matches pinned main exactly. Net PR changes against that main are three files, +254 lines; the only production change remains the four-line admission binding.

Fresh production, agents-sessions, and gateway-other typechecks pass, as do lint/format/diff checks for the resolved files. Independent review of the complete net PR candidate found no actionable P0-P2 defect. Current-main runtime tests are NOT reported green: compiled-subprocess preparation was killed twice by kernel-confirmed host-wide OOM before collecting/executing any tests (exit 137); terminal-write preparation was stopped to prevent another OOM (exit 143). No assertion verdict or current-head runtime proof is claimed. A heap-budget alternative was denied by execution policy and not bypassed. Fresh hosted CI owns runtime verification for this merge; prior passing runtime evidence is pinned to its older revision.

GitHub reports this pushed head mergeable rather than conflicting. Additional upstream movement was checked without editing the branch using merge-tree and was conflict-free; checks/reviews remain separate from mergeability. Nothing was merged into upstream or deployed.

## Proof Limits

Automated regression inference is deterministic and mocked; the separate after-fix Talk relay smoke below used real provider speech/delegation and real backing/child model execution. It is headless relay proof with synthetic speech, not browser UI, microphone, acoustic-playback, native-app, WebRTC, or deployed voice-recovery proof. Exact admitted binding is source-traced through the shipped native Talk path, not a runtime admission-object audit dump. Automated revocation/replacement is triggered immediately before real child dispatch, not exhaustively at every internal suspension. Maintainer/security-review acceptance remains separate. Nothing was merged, deployed, or changed in the running installation.

prs.title: fix(gateway): paired-node Claude continuations retain Gateway context
prs.body:
Closes #145636

## What Problem This Solves

A Claude CLI continuation on a healthy paired node can fail with a Gateway-runtime or capability error after its originating request ends. Detached work retains a live Gateway resolver but deliberately does not retain the direct request context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two paired-node readers now use the existing resolver-first `getInProcessGatewayRequestContext` in the current request-scope owner. This integrates with main's `PluginRuntimeExecutionFrame` storage instead of reintroducing the former AsyncLocalStorage owner or a second accessor. A resolver returning `undefined` remains authoritative: stale direct context cannot revive a retired owner.

The command policy, expected connection and pairing generation, dispatch-time authority, and skill/run/placement lifecycle checks remain intact. There are no configuration, protocol, database-schema, or public SDK changes.

## User Impact

A detached Claude continuation can use its still-live Gateway and connected paired node. A retired owner fails before any node lookup, policy check, or dispatch.

## Evidence

- Conflict refresh onto main `f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe`; current head `eb7a861ea7c06c277806dd2c6d0dba6b0f9c0443` also checks the captured Gateway remains current at dispatch and skill authority use. [Remote focused tests](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/actions/runs/40626335729) passed 18 tests across both affected Gateway suites on a temporary child of this head. Full CI and refreshed real-node proof remain pending; earlier evidence below refers to the revisions identified there.

Reconciled against main `cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984`; candidate `2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d`. The production diff is two reader substitutions, plus focused regression coverage.

### Actual Gateway and signed-node boundary

The same temporary source-runtime fixture starts the actual Gateway with an isolated home, config and state, loads a startup plugin through the normal loader, and captures its real context in an authenticated RPC. A separately signed WebSocket node completes normal local device pairing and command approval, verified in the persisted pairing records. After the capture RPC finishes, the fixture invokes the production `invokeNodeClaudeCliRun` in a resolver-only scope and repeats with a retired resolver plus deliberately stale direct context.

Main before the fix, observed with clean shutdown:

```json
{"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":0,"ok":false,"error":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":1,"ok":true}}
```

Exact candidate after the fix:

```json
{"head":"2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d","expectedFixed":true,"actualGateway":true,"signedNode":true,"devicePaired":true,"commandApproved":true,"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":1,"result":{"ok":true,"payload":{"exitCode":0,"stderrTail":"","truncated":false},"payloadJSON":null,"error":null}},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":0,"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"}}}}
```

The fixture exited 0, and the Gateway reported a clean shutdown.

This exercises real Gateway startup, plugin loading, authenticated RPC, signed WebSocket transport, persisted device/command pairing, NodeRegistry and the changed production invocation owner. The node returns a synthetic successful Claude-command payload. It does not establish live Claude model inference or a full terminal-close/Web-composer UI walkthrough.

The fixture uses synthetic data only. Update checks, telemetry and hosted catalog refresh are disabled with the documented config/environment opt-outs. Proof code and generated logs are temporary and are not committed.

### Regression coverage and checks

- Before the two reader substitutions: 13 failures / 3 passes across the invocation and paired-node skill suites. Detached dispatch failed unavailable; stale-context retirement incorrectly dispatched; skill preparation failed its Gateway/capability boundary.
- After, on the identical candidate tree: 27/27 tests across node invocation (5), paired-node skills (11), request-scope owner (7), and native Bash execution policy (4). Existing coverage for command denial, pairing-await authority retirement, capability requirements, skill delivery/authoring and publication retirement remains active under the resolver-only scope.
- Combined focused command: `pnpm test src/gateway/node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 85.02s wall time including the first compiled-subprocess generation.
- Per-file exact-head cost using `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: `node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts` 5/5, 34.08s wall (21ms test bodies); `node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts` 11/11, 65.68s wall (23901ms test bodies). The existing skill suite exercises real node-command subprocess/SQLite lifecycle boundaries; no new per-test Gateway boots, timers, or serial configuration were added. Hosted [changed-node CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37098465276/job/111133298553) passed both files separately: invocation 5/5 in 22.88s (15ms test bodies), skills 11/11 in 19.83s (9.768s test bodies).
- Independent `autoreview --engine codex --mode local --base cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984 --max-priority P2`: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Four-file type-aware lint (`node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <changed files>`) passed in 22.70s. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The aggregate check passed conflict, line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety, database-worker, timeout-race, dependency, config, plugin-boundary and other prerequisite guards, plus the core graph boundary and full production-core typecheck.
- Hosted [CI run 37098465276](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37098465276) passed on this exact head, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, production types, all selected test-type stripes, lint, selected tests and guards. The [fresh review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145741#issuecomment-5644398815) resolves the previous integration concern and finds no actionable introduced issues: overall Platinum, proof Diamond.
- Full repository build/check/test is not claimed as locally passed. The bounded `check:changed --base cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984 --head HEAD` attempt ran 605.19s and stopped at its 600s budget during the broad 27-graph test-typecheck lane: `agents-root` passed, `agents-other` was interrupted (143). Remaining test graphs and later aggregate checks were not completed locally. The separate changed-file type-aware lint passed; the subsequent hosted CI run completed successfully and covers the selected global verification gates.

### Historical CI failure

[The old head's native-Bash policy job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34680714684/job/103518938237) reported `allowlist/on-miss`: expected `allow`, received `deny`, after 7.764s with a 5s fixture run budget. That is consistent with timeout-sensitive authority rejection, but the historical assertion omitted the denial message and run outcome, so the exact denial reason cannot be established from that log.

The integrated main already contains [the Date-based watchdog change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/62a8182e40d955ddcd509ba977badb37ea691d2a) and the independent [native-Bash fixture stabilization in #115184](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ce11e2e25c3b0ad6360b8c4e5bd7f17357f81c42), which freezes the policy matrix's Date clock and asserts a non-timeout exit. The local native-Bash matrix passes 4/4 on this candidate. No native-Bash production policy, test fixture, or CI configuration is changed by this PR; a passing replay is not being presented as proof of the old run's exact cause.

prs.title: feat(model-catalog): catalog rows own their thinking profile; DeepSeek, Mistral, Moonshot, Kimi move
prs.body:
Replaces the closed stack #187694, #187695, #187707 and #187716. Base: `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Thinking profiles (offered levels, default level, `adaptive`, "cannot turn off", labels) came only from provider hooks keyed by model ID. A new model needed hook code even when its catalog row already described it.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Offered levels, defaults and request bodies stay the same for every migrated row and for released installs (proof below).

## What Changed

**Core (one owner):**
- Approved Tier 1 compat fields (compat-only, so released readers drop them): `compat.defaultThinkingLevel`, `adaptiveThinking`, `thinkingRequired`, `thinkingLevelLabels`. Added to the catalog types and normalizer, the thinking context and the model compat config schema.
- `resolveModelThinkingProfile`: a row with `compat.defaultThinkingLevel` skips the provider hooks and takes the existing generic catalog ladder, plus `adaptive`, labels, its default, and `thinkingRequired` (stays on when `reasoning: false`). Rows without it are unchanged.
- `buildThinkingCatalog`: callers that pass no catalog (thinking default, `/think` menu, isolated completions, plugin runtime, startup log) add the selected model's bundled row. Configured values win per key; a partial configured `thinkingLevelMap` merges over the bundled map.
- Manifest planner: a hosted row published before a fact existed keeps the bundled `thinkingLevelMap` and compat keys it omits.
- `resolveCatalogOwnedModelCompat` keeps the four thinking fields that config states.

**Families (data + code removed):**

| Family | Row data | Removed |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek | `defaultThinkingLevel: high`; map xhigh/max → `max` | `thinking.ts`, the `resolveThinkingProfile` hook, the V4 ID pattern |
| Mistral | reasoning rows: `thinkingLevelMap`, `defaultThinkingLevel: off`, `adaptiveThinking` | the hook and `MISTRAL_REASONING_MODEL_IDS`; the effort map now comes from the rows |
| Moonshot | K3/K3.1: `max` only, `thinkingRequired`; K2.7 Code: `low` labelled `on` | `ALWAYS_THINKING_PROFILES`, `KIMI_K3_MODEL_IDS`; always-thinking and native video come from the rows |
| Kimi Code | K3 rows: efforts, `high`, `adaptiveThinking`, `thinkingRequired`; K3.1 Pro rows (`off: null`) | `KIMI_K3_1_MODEL_IDS`; K3 and enabled-only sets come from the rows |

Kept, with a cited reason: Kimi `kimi-k3` (self-hosted, no row) and `kimi-for-coding` (released readers still offer `off`); the bare-model SDK wrapper `moonshot-thinking.ts` and `@openclaw/ai` Mistral (standalone callers pass no row) are unchanged from `main`.

Moonshot K3 stays max-only. Widening it is a separate product question.

## Evidence

- **Released readers:** `pnpm catalog:compare-released`, baseline built from `main` and candidate from this branch (same models.dev snapshot, current timestamps): 2026.10.9 (latest), 2026.9.36 (extended-stable) and 2026.10.10-beta.4 (beta) each show 0 changes to offered levels, defaults or request bodies; only 86 `model.*` echo lines of the added data.
- **Main:** `catalog-thinking-profiles.contract.test.ts` resolves every row that owns its profile through core, with a provider hook that would return a wrong profile, and matches the profile the deleted hook returned (16 rows).
- **Review regressions** (each failed on its earlier head): catalogless defaults, saved configured rows, Mistral proxy row, partial configured maps (Mistral, Moonshot K3), runtime-row precedence, `/think` menu default model, isolated completions, configured compat overrides, hosted-row fill.
- Live probe records are kept outside the repo. Harness: `pnpm test:live:thinking-probe`. Results (2026-10-29):
  - Moonshot `kimi-k3`: all 7 levels return 200 (shipped: `max` only; not widened).
  - Moonshot `kimi-k2.7-code`: all 7 levels return 200 (shipped: always on, one `on` level; not widened).
  - Kimi Code `k3`: off through high return 200; xhigh/max were not sent (the probe's own ladder stopped them).
  - Kimi Code `k3.1-pro`: `off` returns 400 "does not support disabled thinking mode"; minimal through high return 200.
- Real agent turns on an isolated Gateway (earlier head with the same row-owned profile path): `moonshot/kimi-k3` → `max`, `--thinking low` rejected; `moonshot/kimi-k2.7-code` → `low` (on); `kimi/k3` → `high`, `off` allowed; `kimi/k3.1-pro` → `high`, `off` rejected.

Merge danger: two-way door. The new compat keys are additive and dropped by released readers. Blast radius: thinking pickers and defaults for the four families.

### Review follow-up (head `47d02c8`)

- A configured partial `thinkingLevelMap` now merges per key over the catalog row at both configured owners (`applyLogicalOverrides` and `overlayCatalogMetadata`), so a saved Moonshot K3 row with `{ max: "max" }` stays max-only on the prepared-catalog path. The overlay test now uses a partial map and expects the captured `off: null` to survive.
- The CLI `--thinking` error hint builds the selected model's hydrated catalog (only when it throws). New test: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` with `--thinking bogus` names `xhigh, max`; it fails on the previous head.
- The contract test uses a typed `ProviderThinkingRegistry`; a second case proves a row without `defaultThinkingLevel` reaches the wrong hook, so the bypass check is real.

### Review follow-up (head `a33684b`)

- Profile ownership and its map are one unit. A hosted row published before its bundled row owned the profile (today's `moonshot/kimi-k3` row still maps low/high/xhigh) keeps the bundled map in the planner. A configured row without `compat.defaultThinkingLevel` can only exclude levels from a row that owns its profile (`mergeConfiguredThinkingLevelMap`, used by both configured overlays and `buildThinkingCatalog`). Tests: the published-row composition stays max-only; a config map copied from the earlier docs example stays max-only.
- Subagent and ACP invalid-thinking hints use the selected model's hydrated catalog (test: `moonshot/kimi-k3` names `max`).

### Upgrade from 2026.10.9 (stack head `0e39b18`)

Isolated state (sandboxed HOME/OPENCLAW_HOME/OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, keys from env refs): released 2026.10.9 Gateway runs `kimi/k3 --thinking low` and stores the session. Then `doctor --fix` and this stack's Gateway on the same state: `config validate` passes, the saved `kimi/k3` session resumes at `low`, and `moonshot/kimi-k3` runs at `max`.

prs.title: perf(sessions): keep a bounded warm cache per session on one connection
prs.body:
Fixes #183848

## What Problem This Solves

The SQLite model-context navigation cache kept **one** snapshot per database connection. A retained read-only connection that serves successive sessions for the same agent database therefore replaced its warmed snapshot on every session switch; the reproduction in the report shows `A→B→A→B→A` calling `readRows` on every step, including 30,000-row transcripts.

## Why This Change Was Made

`navigationCache()` stored `{ snapshot?: NavigationSnapshot }`, and `readModelContextNavigationPages()` discarded it whenever `sessionId` differed. The cache now holds a **bounded LRU of session snapshots** made possible by keying entries per session:

- `storeNavigationSnapshot()` inserts the most-recent entry and evicts the oldest until the cache holds ≤4 sessions or ≤16 MiB of estimated row bytes (`navigationSnapshotBytes()` = retained row bytes + prefix bytes).
- `touchNavigationSnapshot()` marks a hit as most-recent, so a session that keeps being read is not the eviction victim.
- Historical anchor reads use their own key (`session\0anchor`), so they can no longer evict the current branch's warmed prefix facts.
- The existing validity checks are unchanged: `generation`, `maxEvents`, `anchorId`, `through`, `leafId`, and the scoped page write token still decide whether a retained snapshot may be reused, and the dispose callback clears the whole cache.

## User Impact

Alternating sessions on one retained connection stop paying the full navigation pass on every switch. Correctness checks and cache invalidation are untouched; the cache stays bounded instead of growing with the number of sessions.

**Not included** (the report asks for them as direction, not as this repair): a measured production memory budget, the page-receipt registration lifetime follow-up from #174435, and the slow-read diagnostic with session/connection correlation IDs. Those need their own owner decisions.

## Evidence

Head `5018f392d`, Node 26.12.1.

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/config/sessions/session-model-context-pages.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
✓ keeps both sessions warm when reads alternate on one connection
✓ evicts the least recently used session once the bound is exceeded
2 passed

# reverting session-model-context-pages.ts to upstream/main:
× keeps both sessions warm when reads alternate on one connection
  AssertionError: expected 2 to be 1     # session A re-read after B replaced the snapshot

$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-model-context.test.ts \
    src/config/sessions/session-model-context-pairing.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
12 passed
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <2 touched files>   0 warnings, 0 errors
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <2 touched files>
All matched files use the correct format.
```

The regression drives `readModelContextNavigationPages` with a synthetic `readRows` counter and mocked admission/write-token checks (the same seams the report's reproduction used): with alternating reads each session seeds once, and after six sessions the first one is seeded again, proving the bound.

### Real-boundary evidence (one store, two sessions, real SQLite)

Throwaway harness on the shipped read path (`readSessionTranscriptModelContext` → `readModelContextNavigationPages`), one store, two 1,200-message sessions, alternating reads. Warm-pass timings only; both runs below are the same script against `upstream/main` and this head:

| run | A1 | B1 | A2 | B2 | A3 | B3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `upstream/main` (single snapshot) | 100.2 ms | 61.0 ms | **79.5 ms** | **50.8 ms** | 51.7 ms | 51.6 ms |
| this head (bounded LRU) | 114.1 ms | 64.9 ms | **5.0 ms** | **3.6 ms** | 3.6 ms | 3.5 ms |
| `upstream/main` (repeat) | 98.0 ms | 68.6 ms | **45.1 ms** | **42.5 ms** | 44.4 ms | 42.6 ms |
| this head (repeat) | 86.3 ms | 62.4 ms | **4.4 ms** | **3.2 ms** | 3.1 ms | 3.3 ms |

On the base every alternating read pays a full navigation pass (41–80 ms); with the cache the second and later reads return in 3–5 ms. The first read of each session stays cold in both, as expected.

```text
# shape of the harness (not committed: timings are not a stable CI assertion)
seed two sessions in one store via SessionManager.appendMessageAsync (1,200 messages each)
for [A1, B1, A2, B2, A3, B3]: time readSessionTranscriptModelContext(scope, undefined, { maxBytes: 8_000_000, maxEvents: 50 })
# run with: node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <harness>.mts 1200
```

The committed unit test still covers the cache decision itself (counter, no timing), so CI is not sensitive to machine speed.

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Reproduced the alternating thrash with the report's mechanism, replaced the single-slot cache with a bounded LRU keyed by session and anchor, and added the regression. The implementer understands the code: cache reuse stays behind the existing validity checks, so eviction only costs a re-read, never correctness.

prs.title: fix(github): managed GitHub identity stays expired after a refresh fails during a network outage
prs.body:
Closes #187494
Related: #181262, #184774

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a managed GitHub OAuth identity stays expired until someone reconnects it when its scheduled refresh runs during a DNS or network outage.

## User Impact

User impact: managed GitHub identities recover on their own after a network outage. When a refresh genuinely cannot be retried safely, Agent Settings shows "Expired — reconnect required" instead of "Refresh failed — retrying", and the Gateway log says to reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

GitHub refresh tokens are single-use, so a refresh whose outcome is unknown must keep its claim and not be replayed. But the GitHub client marked every `fetch()` rejection as dispatched, including DNS lookup and TCP connect failures that never write the request. A single refresh during an outage therefore fenced a still-valid grant permanently.

- The client now treats a rejection as not dispatched only when its cause chain proves the connection never opened: a DNS failure (`getaddrinfo`), a connect failure (`connect`), or undici's connect timeout, with every branch proven for multi-address attempts. The claim is released, and maintenance retries. Resets after writing, closed sockets, aborts, timeouts and coded wrappers stay fenced exactly as before.
- Every failed refresh now logs either "will retry" or "reconnect GitHub".
- A failure that keeps its claim is reported as `expired` (reconnect required). Each claimed attempt now starts without the previous failure, so "claim + failure" always means a stuck grant rather than an in-flight retry.
- `docs/gateway/config-tools/github-identity.md` now says which refresh failures retry and which need reconnection.

The pre-connect predicate mirrors the private one in `src/infra/delivery-recovery.shared.ts`. I left delivery recovery untouched to keep this PR focused; happy to consolidate if maintainers prefer.

## Evidence

- Observed in production: see the linked issue. One refresh during a 4.7-hour outage left the System identity unusable for 12+ hours, with status reading "Refresh failed — retrying".
- Focused tests on this branch (base 011a1703482): 12 files, 218 tests pass (`github-oauth-client`, `github-oauth-records`, `github-tool-identity`, `github-identity-status-tool`, `github-oauth-lifecycle` (+helpers, scheduling), `github-personal-publication*`, `tools-github`, `delivery-recovery.shared`).
- New tests:
  - six pre-connect shapes (ENOTFOUND, EAI_AGAIN, ECONNREFUSED, ENETUNREACH, UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, all-address aggregate) become `before-dispatch` and recoverable;
  - six ambiguous shapes (reset after write, closed socket, timeout, refusal without a syscall, coded wrapper, mixed aggregate) stay `unknown`;
  - a lifecycle regression with the real client: DNS failure releases the claim, and the next refresh succeeds. A reset after write keeps the claim, warns to reconnect, and makes no further request;
  - status projection for released, in-flight and stuck records.
- Negative controls: without the client change, all 7 new retry tests fail. Without the status change, both new status assertions fail.
- Error shapes were checked against real Node 26.12.1 `fetch` (DNS, refused port, blackhole connect timeout at ~10.5 s, multi-address refusal, reset after write).
- `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `format:docs:check`, `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` are clean.
- Gap: `pnpm install` could not run offline against this base's lockfile. Tests used the previous install, and the only lockfile delta is `@noble/hashes` in `packages/gateway-client`, which these tests do not load. Proxy setups were not exercised: connect failures to a proxy are also classified as pre-dispatch, while proxy CONNECT rejections (for example 503) still stay fenced.

This touches OAuth credential refresh, so it needs `/allow-security-sensitive-change`.

The long-lived Mac control connection reads Gateway config on connection and `config.changed`, resolving the saved Gateway preference before `ui.seamColor`. prs.title: fix: avoid blocking database writes while copying inspection snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: database writes can stall behind a read-only inspection snapshot when reflinking a large, fragmented live SQLite database.

Related: #187989 addresses a separate history-read writer-admission stall.

## User Impact

Artifact-preserving inspections no longer request source-inode cloning or copy offload. They still copy and validate the full database image, so they can consume substantial I/O, time, and temporary disk space. This does not defragment existing databases or establish that all reported latency is resolved. No schema, durability, retention, or live deployment changes are included.

## Why This Change Was Made

A read-only incident trace caught a snapshot worker in `FICLONE`/Btrfs metadata reservation while a database writer waited on the same source inode. Use the existing fs-safe byte-copy mode for both synchronous and asynchronous artifact-preserving inspection. Keep source identity checks, coherent-family verification, private recovery, publication, and cleanup unchanged.

The shared file-copy owner accepts the transfer policy; verified offline snapshot publication retains its existing clone-first behavior and space-admission callback before byte-copy fallback.

## Evidence

- Regression failed on the base: the synchronous inspection returned a clone/offload transfer rather than a byte copy. It passes with the fix and also checks the asynchronous owner, retained data, and cleanup.
- 52 focused tests passed across inspection copies, file-copy admission/publication, verified snapshot transfer, and copy-on-write snapshot ownership.
- Native Linux/Btrfs probe exercised both real inspection-copy owners with SQLite data: expected rows, unchanged source bytes, and successful cleanup; `strace` observed zero `FICLONE` or `copy_file_range` calls. This is a local mechanism proof, not a production-scale latency benchmark or live Gateway rollout.
- Final focused regression run: 9 tests passed, including the extracted sync/async byte-copy regression. Core and storage-test TypeScript checks passed. Focused lint/format, documentation MDX, and test-line budget checks passed.
- Fresh independent review of the final patch found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Review was diff/evidence-based; native execution and focused test receipts were verified separately.
- One bounded regression adds 55 test lines, explicitly allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/sqlite-inspection-byte-copy.txt`; no broad snapshot/test expansion.

The exact top-level caller of the incident snapshot and the remaining cost of existing shared extents are not established by this change.

prs.title: fix(discord): thread replies and bindings stop working when a slow channel stop overlaps a restart
prs.body:
Related to #177691. Reviewed snapshots through `206f11bc8903`.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord thread replies and bindings can stop working when a restart overtakes an older task that is still stopping. Each start gets its own binding manager, so the old task's late stop cannot tear down the replacement's manager.

Two paths reproduced on main snapshot `7e81872cbbc`. In round 1, a startup held at `/gateway/bot` resumed late, failed with `Plugin service scheduler is closed`, and stopped the shared manager from its `finally`. In round 2, a slow bind made two replacement starts wait on the old stop. Read-only logpoints observed the mechanism in one run. An aborted start's cleanup stopped the manager that the other start had reused. The account broke in 3 of 4 main runs, including holds before and during the create. Of the three broken runs, only the logpoints run had the inspector attached. The other two match it by symptom only.

Only the narrow config-reload race was exercised. Recovery on a later provider start and other restart entries are read from code, not tested.

## User Impact

A late stop leaves replies working in old bound, newly bound and unbound guild threads. New binds are approved and written to SQLite.

- The old adapter is unregistered at handover. It cannot resurface after the newest owner stops and block session listings for other channels.
- Both native creates check ownership before sending, including direct subagent auto-bind. No built Gateway run measured the subagent path. A bind caught before its create is refused, and no webhook create POST is sent. Built Gateways measured this at `3fe8a885`, `2ae50585` and `206f11bc8903`, the last against real Discord, but not at `900208f1`. In round 2 the approver saw only the deferred update at both snapshots, with the approval prompt unchanged and no error text.
- An accepted thread or webhook create is still published. No built Gateway accepted a thread create. An accepted thread gets no follow-up webhook from the retired manager, so replies use bot sends without the persona. The retired manager sends no intro. This fallback has test and driver coverage, not real Discord proof. No run has shown a webhook-delivered reply.
- A bind settled by the replaced manager keeps that manager's idle timeout, max age and persist flag. The replacement's limits apply only to binds it creates.
- A replaced manager clears its sweep timer at its next tick, even if provider cleanup hangs, so it stops scanning.

A replacement registers without waiting for the old provider to stop. Binding work the old manager already queued, such as an accepted create, settles before queued work on the replacement runs. This includes async session-wide unbinds, idle timeout and max-age updates, inbound activity touches, startup cleanup of stale ACP bindings, and the replacement's own stop. It does not wait for the old manager's stop or the rest of its sweep. Each REST attempt keeps its 15 s timeout and a rate limited request is retried at most three times. Queueing, rate limit delays and persistence mean the total wait has no fixed cap. Deprecated synchronous unbind and duration setters skip the queue and can still overtake the create.

## Why This Change Was Made

`2ae50585` removes manager reuse across starts. Stop removes the account entry and token only for the current manager. #169226 merged the same reuse removal for Feishu.

- `68fb31d6` retires the predecessor's adapter by identity across loaders and guards both native creates.
- `3fe8a885` publishes a native create accepted before replacement, while still refusing new creates by a retired manager. This preserves #153508's accepted-write settlement without granting permission for later sends.
- `900208f1` copies the predecessor's queued-work promise without awaiting it at registration. Async session mutations and replacement stop wait for it, restoring #156627's ordering without joining the old stop.
- `206f11bc8903` makes retired sweepers clear themselves before checking pending work. Cancellation lags at most one 120 s interval.

## Evidence

### Tests

For reviewed snapshots through `206f11bc8903`, all 12 required gates passed. The 19 Discord monitor files passed 182 tests and the 7 binding-consumer files passed 145. Type checks, formatting, typed lint and four ratchets passed.

- The original 3 restart cases fail with main's manager. Creation cases catch old-stop token cleanup and stale adapters resurfacing. The latter fails at `2ae50585` and passes with main's manager and the fix.
- The direct-create cases fail at `2ae50585`. Accepted thread and webhook settlement cases fail with that manager and `68fb31d6`, then pass at `3fe8a885` and `900208f1`.
- The session-wide unbind, idle and max-age cases hold a create across two replacements. All 3 fail with `3fe8a885` and pass at `900208f1`. Wrong-fix controls catch partial inheritance and waiting at registration.
- Two new restart cases hold voice cleanup across two replacements, idle and pending. Both fail at `900208f1`. Guards that skip scans but keep the timer, or check pending work first, fail.

### Built Gateway proof

Rounds 1 to 3 used isolated built Gateways, a Discord stand-in, fake credentials and a local mock response server, not real Discord or model services. Synthesized interactions went only to the newest connected socket at injection time. SQLite rows were checked during runs, not across Gateway restarts. These runs predate the timer commit.

Round 1 compared main `7e81872cbbc` with `2ae50585`. Two `channels.discord.historyLimit` edits about 3 s apart, with one `/gateway/bot` response held about 10 s, overran the 5 s stop grace. The shared edge shim rewrote the gateway URL in `/gateway/bot` and `resume_gateway_url` in READY, renumbered dispatch sequence numbers, and answered interaction callbacks itself. The exact scheduler throw site is inferred.

Main failed in all 4 runs. All 3 guild-thread turns tried after the late stop in the primary run got no reply and logged `SessionWorkStartChangedError`. New binds failed with a binding-owner error.

Round 2 built `3fe8a885` and passed the unchanged late-stop sequence. It also compared main and `2ae50585` on the slow-bind path. At both fix snapshots, refused creates wrote no row, replies kept working, and the pre-create hold sent no webhook create POST. Accepted settlement was unproven because the stand-in returned 404 to every native create.

Round 3 built `900208f1`. Its late-stop run matched round 2 in its outcome rows, but its first replacement start exited with `Skills discovery was retired before publication` and was auto-restarted. The hold lasted 16.1 s, against 10.1 s in round 2, because the harness waited for the usable replacement. The stand-in lacks the webhook create and execution routes, so the edge synthesized four HTTP 200 webhook-create responses with fake IDs and tokens. There was one in each accepted-create run, plus one in a no-reload control at `900208f1`. No webhook-execution response was used. By the edge code, other native REST calls passed unchanged, and the edge answered interaction calls as in round 1.

Each build had one run of this case. At `900208f1`, under a synthetic webhook-create success, the held bind was approved and its webhook ID and token were stored, with no simulated orphan. At `2ae50585`, the same synthetic success was refused, leaving no row and a simulated orphan. Main stored the row but stopped replying and logged 27 ownership-change errors.

Round 3 is PARTIAL for webhook replies. In the bound reply of the accepted run at `900208f1`, a bot send was used despite the stored webhook. The no-reload control, run at `900208f1` only, also used a bot send. The cause of that bot send is read from code, not measured. The reply's agent session key finds no binding row, so no thread id reaches the webhook path. Persona delivery and webhook reply POSTs remain unproven. The optional session-wide probe stopped before its held create, with a Gateway error that begins `Session key does not contain an agent id`. That probe was not run on main or `2ae50585`, so it is not known whether the failure predates this change. Those waits have regression-test coverage only. The separate predecessor socket leak repeated and is not fixed here.

### Live Discord proof

At `206f11bc8903` I ran a built Gateway with real Discord via a TLS proxy and real `gpt-5.6-luna`. A retired manager refused a bind before any webhook create request. A webhook create Discord accepted across a handover was stored by the original bind. L1 was inconclusive, and both attempts needed SIGKILL after a clean-shutdown log. The no-hold control, L2 and L3 each ran once. I ran no base. Details and limits are in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178931#issuecomment-6509058680. L3 receipts are in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178931#issuecomment-6512844287.

### Driver proof

At `206f11bc8903` I ran a scripted driver over the built modules, with a loopback Discord REST stand-in and no Gateway. A retired manager sent no create or intro. Limits are in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178931#issuecomment-6511023964, and redacted receipts in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178931#issuecomment-6511604213.

A second driver added a loopback Gateway stand-in and ran the built channel manager restart over the built provider. Two runs per case were reproduced twice by an independent rerun. After the replacement registered, the older task's startup `finally` stopped only its own manager, and the replacement then took a driver-issued bind and send. The Gateway lifecycle `finally` and a running provider's late stop are unproven. See https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178931#issuecomment-6512196949.

prs.title: perf(doctor): stop re-reading SQLite inspection copies on every check
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor repeats full SQLite inspection copies and discards the shared snapshot's native page cache between checks, multiplying read I/O on slow or contended disks.

Refs #187900 and #178359. Thanks @JordanNewell for the kernel-stack and filesystem-read capture.

## User Impact

Read-only Doctor reports reuse their inspection bytes and readers while preserving live database/WAL artifacts. Writable inspection images, explicit independent verification, and current-authority reads keep their existing boundaries. No schema, config, CLI, dependency, persistence, or rollback change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing artifact-preserving scope owns read-only inspection copies until all native readers close. The report's shared-state scope owns its retained native reader and page cache. Staging v2 lifetime tokens, private WAL recovery, physical admission, current-authority checks, and cleanup failures remain with their existing owners.

## Evidence

Benchmark acceptance rule, recorded before the final comparison: run the real source CLI `doctor --lint --json` serially on synthetic 256 MiB shared/agent state with isolated HOME/state/cache in a private OS temp directory; interleave five baseline/candidate pairs, with warm OS cache. Win requires fewer SQLite read bytes, source-copy comparisons, and native report-reader opens; wall median/p95 must not regress by 20%. Native regular-file read/pread counts measure explicit reads, not mmap page faults or physical disk transfers. Report syscall/byte counts separately from source-loader reads and record host load.

Five interleaved pairs on macOS / Node 26.12.1, baseline `fe8a0ce9b4e8` versus the candidate production blobs:

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full source CLI wall time (median) | 50.364 s | 48.449 s |
| p95 wall time | 51.001 s | 49.023 s |
| Native read/pread calls | 99,411 | 97,219 |
| Native read bytes, all regular files | 5,084,667,095 | 3,993,382,194 |
| Read bytes from SQLite-named files/sidecars | 2,718,598,420 | 1,903,897,644 |
| SQLite opens | 82 | 52 |
| Required quick checks | 1 | 1 |

All work counts were identical within each variant. Every run produced the same 41 checks, 30 skipped checks, five warning findings, and expected lint exit 1. Ranges: baseline 49.326–51.001 s; candidate 47.968–49.023 s. The all-file total includes source-loader work; the SQLite-named subtotal excludes staged payloads called `first` and fs-safe temporary files. This is warm-cache source CLI proof, not a reproduction of the reporter's contended Linux disk. The committed benchmark counts native reads across owned children; mmap page faults and physical disk transfers are outside that metric.

The root waste is full source/copy equality scans and short-lived readers: shared-source comparison passes fall from 11 to 9, agent passes from six to four, and native opens fall by 30. The database-engine inspection worker now owns one shared read scope for its metadata and registry queries. Explicit physical verification and current credential/authority reads retain their independent captures. Required integrity validation is unchanged. Snapshot readers use a 16 MiB page-cache target and 256 MiB mmap limit; mappings are optional under SQLite's VFS.

The five-second `plugin-registration-resources` cleanup message was not reproduced in either variant. Its existing 13-test lifecycle suite passes, including work retained beyond the reporting grace. No deadline or durability change is proposed; the affected host's exact slow disposer remains unproven.

Regression controls fail on the base and pass with the fix: one reader per report with fresh later WAL commits; one image per read-only source/scope with interleaved paths and retained failed-close custody; and one shared metadata producer per engine inspection. The distinct lifecycle boundaries fit the existing test-line ceiling without a new allocation.

Validation: the required import-consumer replay selected 308 files across 16 projects (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <consumer files in rg order> --maxWorkers=1`, with `OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONTINUE_ON_FAILURE=1`). It finished in 3,681.8 seconds: 3,906 passed, three failed, 134 skipped. The failures were in two existing test fixtures: raw SQLite seeding before canonical native-library selection, and an auth observation waiting for any directory event rather than identity change. Both fixture owners are repaired here, retaining their original safety assertions. Final focused proof: retained servicing 2/2; auth file-state 14/14; candidate resource/capacity 25/25; engine report scope 1/1. The retained fixture's first repair exposed an embedded-script scope error; it was corrected and the exact file rerun successfully. No production change followed the benchmark.

Core and touched test typecheck leaves, targeted oxlint/oxfmt, both SQLite ratchets, mock-export, test-line, line-cap/max-lines ratchets, and madge (zero cycles) pass. SQLite T1 calls remain 168, deprecated-only compatibility calls remain 15. Initial candidate test-line check: 6,280,349 against the unchanged ceiling 6,328,452; the CI follow-up adds two test lines; no new allocation or baseline change. The full check:changed SQLite inventory was omitted under the campaign's local gate budget; its two required SQLite ratchets were run separately. Both independent Codex review passes were scoped-clean at P0–P2, including the final fixture repairs. These were static reviews of the patch and supplied owner context; runtime evidence comes from the commands above.

Reproduction commands: `node scripts/perf/doctor-sqlite-inspection.mjs --samples 1 --mib 256 --out <sample.json>` for each of A1/B1 through A5/B5, with the seven production files pinned to baseline or candidate blobs and restored/verified afterward. The benchmark starts the real `doctor --lint --json` CLI and joins its invocation cleanup. All runtime/test commands use private OS-temp HOME/state/cache roots. The six e2e consumer files also passed (21 tests), including isolated Gateways and a real repair/upgrade flow; repair exited 0 in 41.632 seconds, including the 16.815-second Doctor phase. No remote leases or operator Gateway/state access.

The replay exposed one bounded slow assertion fixed here: `update-candidate-rehearsal.resources.test.ts` activation backup capacity case fell from 31.814 seconds to 0.010 seconds by replacing generic deep comparison of two 8 MiB Buffers with native exact `Buffer.equals` assertions.

Pre-existing slow-test follow-ups, recorded without changing timeouts, retries, or assertions:

| Owner / case | Test time | Concrete cost |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Worker artifact tooling / stale dist | 32.596 s; file 159.940 s | About 14,000 fixture inputs, repeated hashes and three real compiler attempts; narrow fixture/compiler closure in a dedicated tooling change. |
| Channel progress / suppressed Slack announcements | 73.001 s; file 216.103 s | Two deliberate 31-second waits cross the observer's 30-second digest threshold; the remaining matrix starts isolated Gateways. Separate observer clock proof from presentation fixtures. |
| Paired node lifecycle / revoked turns | 49.547 s | Intentionally exercises the 30-second cancellation deadline after lost terminal acknowledgements. |
| Paired node lifecycle / local recovery | 95.455 s; file 151.645 s | Seven placements, fourteen turns, two bundle installs, and disconnect/reconnect recovery; event-driven settlement. Profile worker lifecycle stages separately. |
| Required native same session | 35.533 s | Eight real worker turns across four settlement scenarios, event-driven barriers. |
| Paired node upgrade | 149.349 s; file 149.354 s | Full packaged-runtime copy, repair, two Gateway generations and workspace/bundle recovery; Doctor 16.815 s and convergence 19.815 s within repair 41.632 s. Needs packaged-upgrade stage profiling. |
| Native worker slot | 38.846 s | Three worktree dispatches, two native turns, capacity refusal, durable settlement, deletion/reconnect and stale-owner cancellation. |

Change split: production +108/−19 lines (net +89); tests +279/−41 (net +238); benchmark 310 lines; docs +3/−2. The production growth gives lifecycle ownership to existing report scopes rather than adding a process-wide cache.

CI follow-up: the retained reader still opens through the existing sanctioned shared-state read connection. Its cache-size and mmap-size settings are connection-local SQLite primitives on immutable inspection images, not application row queries; existing open helpers do not configure these retained-reader budgets. `sqlite-snapshot.ts` is already the dialect ratchet's snapshot primitive owner. Moving those settings into the general WAL owner introduced two engine-maintenance constructs and failed the dialect ratchet, so this repair adds exactly one reasoned Kysely raw-access allowlist path for the snapshot owner. No dialect classification, baseline, lint suppression, or production code changed. The close-failure fixture now binds each native handle's close callback before the inspection wrapper captures it, retaining the original error/custody assertions.

Final follow-up proof: `node scripts/check-kysely-guardrails.mts` passes; `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` passes for the touched core files and the guard script using their matching configs; the three focused retained-reader files pass 20/20 through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ... --maxWorkers=1`; worker and dialect ratchets both pass against `fe8a0ce9b4e89d48e7e0ccbcd572d0924acce823` (168 live / 15 compatibility calls unchanged). Fresh independent static review is scoped-clean at P0–P2. Overall production remains +108/−19 lines (net +89); this follow-up changes only the guard (three lines) and test.

Follow-up head: `b3b3299590483bb38049801682331d76f6276059`.

prs.title: fix: deliver replies from conversation-bound ACP child sessions
prs.body:
Title: fix: deliver replies from conversation-bound ACP child sessions

Closes #123933

AI-assisted; reviewed and tested by me.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #123933: a persistent ACP session spawned into its own thread (`sessions_spawn({ runtime: "acp", thread: true, mode: "session" })`) never answers in that thread. The user's message is processed, but the reply is dropped and the gateway logs `visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads`.

## User Impact

- Thread-bound ACP sessions reply in their thread again, so multi-turn conversations with a coding session work.
- ACP children that are parent-owned background work and are not bound to the conversation stay silent, so no new channel noise.
- If a parent-owned child's binding is removed or reassigned while a turn is running, that turn's output is no longer delivered to the conversation.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareDispatchDelivery` treats any ACP session with `spawnedBy`/`parentSessionKey` as a parent-owned background session and suppresses user-channel delivery for it. A thread-bound child has that lineage too, even though it is the user-facing owner of the thread it is bound to.

## What changed

This is one commit on top of `main` (76985e4c). v6 is one commit on top of the v5 head `aac39eba`, so the update is a fast-forward.

1. **Bound children answer again.** Gather already resolves the conversation binding (`boundAcpDispatchSessionKey`). It is now forwarded, and `prepareDispatchDelivery` only suppresses a parent-owned ACP child when the conversation has no ACP binding.
2. **The authority is the binding gather selected, never a later lookup (v6).** With route facts, it is the facts' `bindingId`/`boundAt`/`targetSessionKey`/conversation. Without route facts, `resolveBoundAcpDispatchSessionKey` now retains the exact binding it confirmed on the turn context (enumerable symbol, like route facts; never serialized). Delivery setup no longer re-resolves the conversation, so a binding removed or reassigned between gather and delivery is seen as revoked instead of "never bound". A selected binding that targets a different session fails closed.
3. **The authority travels with every send (v6).**
   - Routed sends: `routeReply` → `onPlatformSendDispatch` re-check + `acpBindingAuthority` on the queue row.
   - Normal dispatcher delivery (same-channel turns, `shouldRouteToOriginating` false): the dispatcher `beforeDeliver` hook withholds revoked payloads and stamps the authority onto the payload metadata (`ReplyPayloadMetadata.acpBindingAuthority`, alongside `sessionWriterDeliveryAuthority`). The shared durable send owner (`sendMessageBatch` in `channels/message/send.ts`, used by `deliverInboundReplyWithMessageSendContext` and the structured variant Telegram's final callback uses) reads it, re-checks it at `onPlatformSendDispatch`, and persists it on the queue row so recovery re-checks it before replay.
   - Tool-message edits: checked before and at platform dispatch.
4. **Fail closed** on removed/reassigned binding, failed or throwing session reads (`storeReadFailed`, `withAcpSessionEntryRead` throw). Without a dispatcher pre-send hook only dispatcher-queued sends are withheld.

No public export, config or plugin contract changes; new fields are internal and optional.

Size against main: 20 files, +798/-69 (v6 commit: 7 files, +172/-31).

## Evidence

`src/infra/outbound/route-reply.acp-binding-channel.test.ts` (17 tests) drives the real `routeReply`, real `createReplyDispatcher` + `deliverInboundReplyWithMessageSendContextCore` (the channel durable-final owner), the durable outbound queue, `recoverPendingDeliveries`, and `runMessageAction`. Transport is a registered test channel plugin; the binding service lookup is switched between bound / removed / reassigned.

| Path | Bound | Removed | Reassigned |
|---|---|---|---|
| Routed send | delivered | rejected (`ACP conversation binding was revoked`) | rejected |
| Routed retryable failure → queued row → restart recovery | replayed | withheld (`failed:1`) | withheld |
| **Dispatcher (normal channel) send** | delivered | suppressed | suppressed |
| **Dispatcher send → provider failure → queued row (authority persisted) → recovery** | replayed | withheld, logs "binding was revoked" | withheld |
| Tool-message edit | edited | not edited | not edited |
| **Legacy queue row with no `acpBindingAuthority` (pre-upgrade data)** | recovered and delivered under the old rules | | |

Red on the v5 head: with the `send.ts` change reverted, the three dispatcher durable-recovery tests fail (`acpBindingAuthority` missing from the queue row) — `red-without-send-fix.log`.

Unit tests (`dispatch-acp-delivery-binding.test.ts`): gather-retained binding removed before delivery setup → revoked (and its authority is still the gathered one); gathered binding for another session → revoked; turn gather never routed through a binding → not revoked; plus the v5 cases. Unbound parent-owned children remain suppressed by `prepareDispatchDelivery` (`dispatch-from-config.owner-metadata.test.ts`).

Logs contain no IPs, API keys, phone numbers or non-public endpoints; session keys print as `<redacted len=N>`.

## Checks (base 76985e4c)

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files: clean. `oxfmt --check`: clean.
- opengrep `security/opengrep/precise.yml`: 107 rules on 20 files, 0 findings.
- Mock-exports ratchet and `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base 76985e4c`: OK.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: pass.
- Vitest `--maxWorkers=1`:
  - proof test: 17/17;
  - auto-reply (`dispatch-acp*`, `route-reply*`, `dispatch-from-config.owner-metadata`): 13 files, 174/174;
  - infra/channels (`channels/message/send*`, `channels/turn/durable-delivery*`, `delivery-queue` recovery/backoff/isolation/producer-recovery/preparation/storage/migration): 136/137. The one failure was "Recovery time budget exceeded" under box load, and the test passes when re-run alone.

## Known gaps

- Proof is an in-process harness: test channel plugin, not a live Telegram/Discord socket; binding service lookup stubbed; ACP backend not executed; restart simulated by draining the on-disk queue in one process. I could not run a live ACP-to-channel session from this environment.
- Revocation applies only to parent-owned (`spawnedBy`/`parentSessionKey`) children.
- A send the provider already accepted is not recalled. A binding re-created with the same `bindingId` and `boundAt` passes the check.
- Non-durable dispatcher sends are re-checked live at `beforeDeliver` only; there is no queue row to carry.
- Queue rows written before this change carry no authority and replay under the old rules (tested).
- The binding retained at gather lives on the in-memory dispatch context. If something serializes or copies that context between gather and delivery, the retained binding is lost and the send is not revoked (fails open). I did not find such a copy on the tested paths.
- `sendMessageBatch` uses the first payload's binding authority for the whole batch. That holds while each batch comes from a single turn.

Related: #123930 is an earlier, closed PR for #123933. #146651 and #146898 address #146365; the only overlap is one line in `dispatch-from-config.gather.ts`.

prs.title: fix(telegram): treat forwarded rich messages as debounceable text
prs.body:
Fixes #187677

## What Problem This Solves

A burst of forwarded Telegram rich messages was not batched: each forward dispatched on its own and the receiving agent ran one turn per message, ignoring the 1 s forward collection window. Typed text from the same sender batched correctly.

## Why This Change Was Made

`shouldDebounceTelegramEntry()` decides with `getTelegramTextParts(entry.msg).text`, and that helper only read `text`, `caption`, contact, and poll. A Bot API block message carries `rich_message` instead, so the text part was empty, `hasDebounceableText` was false, and the forward lane took the immediate path.

`getTelegramTextParts()` now renders `rich_message` blocks through `resolveTelegramRichMessageText()` — the same renderer the agent prompt uses — so the debounce predicate and `joinTelegramTextParts()` see the same content the prompt does. Non-text rich messages (for example a divider) still render to an empty string, so media and caption callers keep treating them as non-text.

## User Impact

For users, forwarding several rich messages now gets one combined reply instead of one reply per message, matching the documented forward-batching behavior.

## Evidence

Head `43d6321ac`, Node 26.12.1. Real-Gateway proof: built the worktree to `dist`, ran `node dist/index.js gateway` with an isolated state dir, pointed `channels.telegram.apiRoot` at a loopback mock Telegram Bot API serving one burst of three forwarded `rich_message` updates, and recorded every agent request on a loopback mock OpenAI-compatible provider. No external credentials; the burst was the only traffic.

Observed result on this fix — the burst becomes one turn containing every message:

```text
[telegram] [diag] isolated polling worker batch received queued=3

mock provider: 1 chat-completions request; its user turn:
  [Forwarded from Origin at 2025-01-08T01:33:20.000Z] Alpha forward
  [Forwarded from Origin at 2025-01-08T01:33:20.000Z] Beta forward
  [Forwarded from Origin at 2025-01-08T01:33:20.000Z] Gamma forward
mock Bot API: 1 sendMessage reply
```

Same harness and burst, with `body-helpers.ts` reverted to the base as a red control:

| run | agent requests | how the forwards reach the agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base (fix reverted) | 2 requests, 3 dispatched user messages | each forward enters alone — "Alpha forward", then "Beta forward" as an immediate follow-up, then "Gamma forward" after the first reply; the reported one-turn-per-message behavior |
| this fix | 1 request | one user message joining all three `[Forwarded from Origin]` segments |

Unit-level red/green for the changed predicate stays covered by the committed regression:

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/telegram/src/bot/body-helpers.inbound.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
11 passed
  ✓ renders forwarded rich messages so debounce sees text

# reverting body-helpers.ts to upstream/main:
× renders forwarded rich messages so debounce sees text
  AssertionError: expected '' to be 'first forward'

$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.body.test.ts \
    extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.inbound-pipeline.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
47 passed
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <3 touched files>   0 warnings, 0 errors
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <3 touched files>
All matched files use the correct format.
```

Not covered: a live Telegram forwarding burst from real accounts (needs bot credentials). The mock Bot API reproduces the reported update shape (`forward_origin` + `rich_message`, one getUpdates batch), and the built Gateway above is the shipped entry that consumed it.

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Traced the reported log to `getTelegramTextParts()` returning empty for `rich_message`, reused the existing prompt renderer, and added the regression; the Gateway evidence comes from a local loopback harness (mock Telegram Bot API + mock provider) driving the built Gateway. The implementer understands the code: the debounce decision and the prompt must agree on what text a message has.

prs.title: fix(matrix): image replies in progress mode lose their caption and land below the text
prs.body:
Related: #170261

## What Problem This Solves

With `channels.matrix.streaming.mode: "progress"`, an assistant reply containing text and an image edits its text into the older progress draft, then sends an uncaptioned image. The text appears above the image rather than as its caption.

## User Impact

Progress-mode media replies now use normal Matrix delivery: the first image carries the reply text as its caption, and the progress draft is removed only after accepted replacement delivery. Sean Kennedy's original fix and commits are retained.

## Why This Change Was Made

A progress draft holds status lines, not the answer. The dispatcher excludes non-TTS progress-mode media from final draft editing and reuses existing captioned-media delivery and preview cleanup. Partial, quiet, and TTS behavior is unchanged. Block media replies use this same settlement path.

The normal delivery limits remain: only the first attachment gets the caption, long captions may spill into text events, and voice replies keep their text separate. Failed replacement delivery preserves the progress draft. This is narrower than #170261's requested configurable fresh final delivery.

## Evidence

[Inspectable built-Gateway/Synapse room-event captures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188018#issuecomment-6513386713).

- Frozen main `f3e76d3f2ea31611411da1edfced791237cf196b`: twice, the caption edits the progress notice and the subsequent `m.image.body` is only `image.png`.
- Built candidate `0b959cb9550fd1fe5f4cb3e4c81ab9ea350424a5`: twice, one image carries the caption, no caption text edit is sent, and Synapse records the draft redaction after the image. Includes the contributor's intervening predicate extraction and QA notice-observation correction, merged and rebuilt before repeating candidate proof.
- Controls on both refs: non-progress images remain captioned; progress-mode text-only finals still edit their draft. All eight Gateway processes exited cleanly with code 0.
- Real inbound room messages, normal bundled Matrix plugin startup/sync, real agent and exec tool loop, deterministic local model-protocol fixture, and disposable Synapse. This proves transport and stored events, not Element UI rendering or a paid model.
- Focused Matrix handler suite: **60 passed**, wrapper **12.44 s**, Vitest **10.50 s**. The same consolidated regression on main fails because the media send receives empty text instead of the caption (**1 failed, 59 skipped**). Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Combined caption regression with the existing UTF-16-safe tool-progress test, preserving both behaviors. Flattened two obsolete single-row test tables without removing their assertions. Test/test-support delta: **+85/-85, net 0**, with no new test cases or allocations. Matrix production fix: **+3/-1**. Retained QA scenario/config source: **+107/-4**, plus 22 YAML lines.
- Contributor QA scenario `matrix-room-tool-progress-media-caption` remains available through QA Lab; its streaming configuration now accepts progress mode.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores prior routing without a migration or persistent contract change. Blast radius is Matrix progress-mode replies with non-TTS media; the patch reuses the existing sender and cleanup owner. Other channels and streaming modes are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(projects): retry project listing when a profile merge races recents
prs.body:
Follow-up to #187451

## What Problem This Solves

#187451 made `projects.list` restart its read when config, the session projection or session facts change mid-read. The profile disclosure guard was missed. When a profile merge races the recents read, the New Session picker still shows the internal error "Profile aliases changed while preparing disclosure. Retry the request." and does not retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/state/user-profile-reads.ts` threw plain `Error`s, so `projects.list` could not tell a retryable race from a real failure. The state owner now throws a typed `UserProfileDisclosureChangedError`. The messages are unchanged, so the plugin SDK caller (`session-store-runtime.ts`) sees the same text and keeps its own retry policy.

`projects.list` treats the new error like `ProjectListingChangedError`: it restarts the whole read, which re-prepares the profile aliases. After 3 lost races it returns the same plain, retryable "Projects changed while loading. Try again." Other errors still return immediately.

## User Impact

A profile merge during the project list read no longer appears in the picker as an internal profile error.

## Evidence

- New test `projects.list retries recents when the caller's profile is merged mid-read`: the caller's profile is merged into a new canonical profile during the recents read. The listing restarts (repository lookup runs twice) and returns the caller's recents. Without the fix the same test gets `ok: false`.
- With `--maxWorkers=1`: `projects-recents.test.ts` 4/4 in 33.6s, `projects.test.ts` 30/30 in 28.6s, `user-profile-authority.test.ts` 11/11 in 6.6s. The new test adds about 0.1s.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes except two checks that already fail on `main` in files this PR doesn't touch: wrapper shadowing (`buildSkillWorkshopPromptSection` in `src/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime.ts`) and the dead-export scan, which was skipped.

## Noted, not changed

The alias guard follows profile identity revisions (#166283), so an *incoming* merge (another profile merged into the caller's) does not fire it. A probe confirmed that the alias set changes but `assertCurrent()` still passes. Such a listing can briefly leave out the merged-in profile's recents until the next load. It never over-discloses, and changing the guard would undo #166283's deliberate perf tradeoff, so that is left for the profile owners.

## What Problem This Solves

Reading one update recovery record materialized every recovery payload before selecting its run ID. Large retained histories amplified every named execution read.

## User Impact

## Evidence

- A real SQLite regression measures executed queries, returned rows, and text bytes with 32 unrelated large malformed payloads: a found key must return exactly its one row, including the key; a missing key returns none.
- Direct caller/schema inspection and independent scoped review: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Native red/green: base materializes 33 rows instead of one; candidate returns the single selected payload and no payload for a missing key. All 57 retained-recovery tests pass, including strict legacy/corrupt record refusal and missing-state behavior.
- Formatter, precommit freshness, and diff checks pass. No schema or live-installation change.

Production delta: +1 line. Named and inventory reads share the existing query owner and table guard, removing the initially duplicated query site. Tests: +35 lines with a dedicated allocation.


CI correction: the initial query introduced a second synchronous database call site. The final revision folds primary-key selection into the existing query helper. All 57 recovery tests pass again (38.13s), and the full database-worker ratchet passes with T1 calls unchanged at 168 and deprecated-only calls unchanged at 15. prs.title: fix(pr-tooling): bind prior-CI exceptions to the selected gate
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prior-CI exception admission refuses a valid selected failed run when the same head also has a passing PR-event gate. This blocked [PR #187398](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187398): its [manual gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40829547969/job/123302783086) and [passing PR gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40828239961/job/123299173056) correctly survive as separate required checks.

## User Impact

Maintainers can evaluate the attested failed attempt without mistaking another workflow event for its gate. Every other required event must still pass; security, primary-artifact, review, revocation, and final admission checks remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select the gate by the trusted attempt's check-suite ID and the selected job's exact repository check-run URL before enforcing uniqueness. This follows GitHub's [workflow-run identity](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs) and [attempt-job check-run identity](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-jobs#list-jobs-for-a-workflow-run-attempt) contracts. REST event normalization is unchanged.

The executable production delta is net zero, with two explanatory comment lines. Nineteen verifier cases cover the two-event inventory, identity faults, other-event failures, and successful-primary enforcement. The required test allocation is 140 LF. This operational fix note is recorded here under the repository's release-owned changelog policy.

## Evidence

- Targeted formatter, Node syntax checks, diff checks, and independent source review passed.
- Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its existing checkout was dirty. The documented autoreview fallback completed one full-context P0–P3 pass over `d2d663acabda98f35bd9c079baaece2d4b5d59d3..e0ad41e5d43153540693e753740734c12c1d11d9`: scoped-clean, complete, no findings (source review only). ClawSweeper has already acknowledged this PR; hosted review remains pending.
- Normal signed commit hooks passed at `e0ad41e5d43153540693e753740734c12c1d11d9`.
- Dependency-backed tests, types, and baseline-red/fix-green execution remain **UNRUN**: native worktree dependency qualification refused reuse, so this checkout stayed code-only. Ordinary PR CI is the next proof route.
- Validation remains pending; no current-head CI pass or landing claim.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a WhatsApp group attended by a named (non-default) account gets two approval cards for one exec/plugin approval, the native one and a generic forwarded copy.

## User Impact

User impact: in a group served by a named account, the requester sees one approval card (the native one) instead of two. Default-account groups, DMs, real platform threads and explicit forwarding targets behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

A named account keeps its group session apart from other accounts in the same group with an internal thread id, `<channel>-account-<accountId>`. The session forwarding target carries that thread, but a standard native origin target never carries one, so the "is this the same chat as the native card?" comparison failed and the generic forwarder sent its fallback card as well.

When a standard native approval route compares a session forwarding target, it now leaves out exactly that isolation thread. The thread id is built by one new helper, `resolveGroupAccountIsolationThreadId`, which the group dispatcher also uses, so the two cannot drift apart. Real threads, another account's isolation thread, and explicit (non-session) targets are still compared as-is.

<details>
<summary>Changes</summary>

- `src/routing/session-key.ts`: `resolveGroupAccountIsolationThreadId({channel, accountId})`, `undefined` for the default account.
- `src/auto-reply/group-thread-dispatch.ts`: builds the isolation thread with that helper (same key as before).
- `src/plugin-sdk/approval-delivery-helpers.ts`: `resolveForwardingTargetForMatch` of the sync and async standard routes drops only the matching isolation thread for `source: "session"` targets.
- Tests in `session-key.test.ts`, `approval-delivery-helpers.test.ts` and `extensions/whatsapp/src/approval-native.test.ts`.

</details>

## Evidence

- Focused tests:
  - `extensions/whatsapp/src/approval-native.test.ts`: a named-account WhatsApp group whose session target carries the isolation thread suppresses the forwarded fallback; a real thread and another account's isolation thread do not.
  - `src/plugin-sdk/approval-delivery-helpers.test.ts`: same matching rules on the sync and async standard routes, explicit targets unchanged.
  - `src/routing/session-key.test.ts`: helper output for named and default accounts.
- With the three source files from `main`, the new WhatsApp and plugin-sdk cases fail (3 tests); with this PR they pass.
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/whatsapp/src/approval-native.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/approval-delivery-helpers.test.ts src/routing/session-key.test.ts src/auto-reply`: all changed-area tests pass. 9 tests in 4 unrelated `src/auto-reply` files (`stage-sandbox-media.history`, `reply.stage-sandbox-media.ssh`, `dispatch-from-config.lifecycle`, `reply-turn-admission.module-identity`) fail on this macOS machine identically with and without this change.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and oxlint on the changed files: clean.

Not tested live: I have no spare WhatsApp account to link as a named account in a test group, so there is no capture of the card count from a real WhatsApp group. If maintainers have a WhatsApp test setup, the check is: a group served by a named account, an exec approval in `ask` mode, and counting the cards in the group before and after this patch.
