prs.title: fix(release): prevent ghost FRV reruns
prs.body:
## Problem

FRV recovery still used GitHub's run-wide `rerun-failed-jobs` mutation. Ambiguous 5xx responses could be retried, and GitHub could materialize persistent runnerless duplicate jobs. Duplicate contamination was only surfaced after dispatch or by the watcher, while attempt composition could discard those copies and still produce sealable evidence.

RRI: **RRI-394**

## Change

- admit automatic recovery only when exactly one blocking failed job has an exact, revalidated job identity
- use the exact job rerun endpoint and remove the failed-jobs client mutation
- refuse multi-job or identity-less reruns before any POST, directing operators to a fresh all-group FRV
- reconcile ambiguous child mutations without a second POST
- verify every controller-created child attempt after dispatch
- mark any observed non-skipped duplicate job identity unsealable, including runnerless ghost copies in superseded attempts

## User impact

FRV recovery no longer risks amplifying an ambiguous failed-job mutation into persistent duplicate jobs. Safe one-job recovery remains available with the original run/attempt/job identity and reconciliation guarantees. Attempts already contaminated by duplicate identities cannot be sealed or reused as release evidence.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/frv.test.ts test/scripts/full-release-validation-state.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot` — 261 passed
- `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs root` — all four root shards passed
- `pnpm check:changed` — all checks passed except the initially reported test-root type error, which was fixed and then revalidated with the exact shard command above
- `pnpm exec oxlint scripts/frv.mjs scripts/full-release-validation-policy.mjs test/scripts/frv.test.ts test/scripts/full-release-validation-state.test.ts` — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean
- independent P0/P1 review — no actionable findings; helper launch was unavailable because Codex CLI is not installed, so review used an isolated reviewer over the complete local diff

prs.title: feat(memory): opt topic files into per-entry chunking with a marker
prs.body:
Closes #179954

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: curated memory kept in topic files under `memory/` is indexed with the size-based chunker, so unrelated one-fact bullets are merged into ~400-token chunks. A query pulls in neighboring facts and the mixed embedding ranks specific facts lower than the same bullets in `MEMORY.md`.

## User Impact

User impact: a topic file under `memory/` can opt into per-entry chunking by carrying one marker line. Files without the marker are indexed exactly as before; there is no new config key.

```markdown
<!-- chunking: entries -->
```

## Why This Change Was Made

Shape agreed with @steipete in the issue (option 1, chunking only):

- The marker uses the existing HTML-comment carrier style and is stripped before indexing like the other annotations. It must sit on its own line, so prose or code samples that mention it do not opt a file in. Only `memory/` files honor it.
- `prepareMemoryIndexChunks` gets one more input to the existing `perEntry` predicate; the chunker itself is unchanged.
- Recall metadata eligibility and path provenance are untouched (`memory-path-provenance.ts`, `curated-annotations.ts` extraction). The marker does not make a file a curated root, so trigger and importance annotations stay ignored in topic files. Project scope was already read for topic files and now applies per entry in marked files, which follows from the chunk boundaries.
- Adding or removing the marker changes the file content hash, so the normal per-file reindex handles it. `MEMORY_CHUNKING_VERSION` is not bumped because unmarked files chunk as before.
- Docs updated in `memory-builtin`, `memory`, and `memory-architecture`.

## Evidence

Tests (all pass; the three behavior tests fail on the base without the change):

- `manager-index-preparation.test.ts`: marked file chunks per entry with the marker stripped; unmarked file stays one size-based chunk; marker in prose, unknown mode, and non-`memory/` paths are ignored; trigger/importance stay null and project scope still applies as for an unmarked topic file.
- `manager-per-entry-marker.test.ts` (real manager, SQLite index): file indexed size-based, marker added then a normal sync gives per-entry chunks, marker removed then a normal sync returns the original size-based chunks.
- `curated-annotations.test.ts`: marker detection, stripping keeps line numbers, marker never reaches recall metadata.
- Full `extensions/memory-core`, `packages/memory-host-sdk`, `src/plugin-sdk` vitest run: 463 files pass, 9 skipped, 2 fail (see below). `pnpm check:changed` typecheck/format/guards and `pnpm lint:docs` pass.

Paired corpus: the same 24 synthetic one-line bullets (team facts), once in a topic file with the marker and once without. Chunks were produced by the real `prepareMemoryIndexChunks` (400 tokens, 80 overlap) and embedded with a local embedding model (Qwen3-Embedding-4B 4-bit served by a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint, plain queries, cosine similarity, vector ranking only). The unmarked file becomes 2 chunks (20 and 8 bullets); the marked file becomes 24 chunks.

| Query | marked: top score | marked: bullets returned | marked: target rank | unmarked: top score | unmarked: bullets returned | unmarked: target rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Which food should we avoid when booking a team dinner? | 0.602 | 1 | 1 | 0.395 | 20 | 1 |
| How many API calls per minute are allowed? | 0.892 | 1 | 1 | 0.529 | 8 | 1 |
| Who do I ask to change the analytics warehouse schema? | 0.779 | 1 | 1 | 0.501 | 20 | 1 |
| When is the database backup restore-tested? | 0.710 | 1 | 1 | 0.533 | 20 | 1 |
| What is the Friday deploy rule? | 0.731 | 1 | 1 | 0.584 | 20 | 1 |
| How long do we keep logs? | 0.823 | 1 | 1 | 0.492 | 20 | 1 |

With such a small corpus the right chunk is found either way. The difference is what comes back: one bullet at a clearly higher similarity versus 8-20 unrelated bullets in one chunk at a lower score. The gap grows with file size, since a larger unmarked file has more diluted chunks competing with each other.

Shipped-CLI proof (head `f81c3b246`; built `openclaw.mjs`, local oMLX embeddings `Qwen3-Embedding-4B-4bit-DWQ` through `memory.search.provider: "omlx"`, throwaway `HOME` and state dir, real index untouched). Corpus: `MEMORY.md` (3 bullets), `USER.md` (2), `memory/people-marked.md` (6 bullets + marker), `memory/people-unmarked.md` (6 bullets). `openclaw memory index --agent main`, then `openclaw memory search --json`:

| File | base `bec3ad81d` chunks | PR chunks |
|---|---|---|
| `MEMORY.md` | 3 | 3 |
| `USER.md` | 2 | 2 |
| `memory/people-marked.md` | 1 (lines 1-11) | 6 (1-5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10-11) |
| `memory/people-unmarked.md` | 1 (lines 1-9) | 1 (lines 1-9) |

| Query | base top hit | PR top hit |
|---|---|---|
| who is allergic to peanuts | 0.490 `marked:1-11` | 0.633 `marked:6` |
| who manages the Cluj warehouse | 0.577 `marked:1-11` | 0.794 `marked:7` |
| who is allergic to shellfish | 0.443 `unmarked:1-9` | 0.518 `marked:6` (then 0.445 `unmarked:1-9`) |
| vendor contract with the catering company | 0.503 `marked:1-11` | 0.730 `marked:9` |

Upgrade compatibility (same state dir: index with base `bec3ad81d`, switch to the PR build, run `openclaw memory index` again without `--force`): `MEMORY.md`, `USER.md` and the unmarked file keep identical chunk counts and chunk hashes (sha256 digests `6f2efb3f`, `f8bc8e7a`, `f9c76450`) through every step. The marked file is rewritten to 6 per-entry chunks when it is next touched or edited (7 after appending a bullet); adding the marker to the unmarked file gives 6 chunks and removing it restores the original single chunk with the original hash, with all other files untouched. A file that already carries the marker keeps its old chunks until it changes (or `--force`); the marker is new, so no existing corpus is affected. No index-identity warning and no rebuild were needed. Full tables are in the PR comment.

CI: type, lint and package-boundary checks pass on the earlier head. `test-lines` now passes locally (`slack: 237`, baseline untouched) after consolidating duplicated detector test rows; the add/remove-marker reindex test is unchanged.

Fence detection requires only spaces/tabs after a closing delimiter (as `packages/markdown-core/src/fences.ts` does). Upgrade from the latest stable (`v2026.10.8`) to this branch, with existing settings, files and index data preserved, is documented in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186649#issuecomment-6468411633).

Known gaps, none caused by this change (each reproduces with the three source files reverted to `main`): `manager-search-knn-subprocess.test.ts` ("KNN child loaded unrelated runtime: kysely") and two `qa-runtime.test.ts` waitForHealth tests fail locally. `pnpm check:changed` reports two further failures. The Plugin SDK surface budget fails identically on a clean `main` (public entrypoints 160 > 158), and the SQLite worker ratchet could not run locally because `rg` is not installed. No Ollama was used; the embedding model above is the local provider.

prs.title: fix(channels): searches miss canonically equivalent Unicode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Buzz room lookup, WhatsApp live group lookup, and Teams message search omit existing results when the query and stored text use canonically equivalent NFC/NFD spellings.

## User Impact

Operators can find the same room, group, or message using either Unicode form. Existing ASCII matching, limits, sorting, account/connection ownership, and target authorization remain intact. Returned original names, message bodies, IDs and service wire requests are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply lowercase followed by NFC only to comparison copies at the three existing plugin-local owners. No shared/global normalizer, configuration, schema, SDK export or dependency is added. The query remains local; no server search term or opaque target ID is rewritten.

This combines #187954 and #187955 into earliest #187953, preserving all three contributions by @SunnyShu0925.

## Evidence

[Built CLI differentials, real protocol receipts, and trust disclosures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187953#issuecomment-6512114859)

**84 shipped CLI lookups**, using independently built main and candidate artifacts in isolated Node 24.22.1 Docker:

- **Buzz:** real nostr-tools client against a faithful NIP-11/NIP-42 relay with validly signed room events.
- **WhatsApp:** actual Baileys Noise handshake and encrypted participating-group IQ protocol, credential/connection owner and cleanup against a faithful loopback service. A maintainer-approved, proof-only preload trusts a task-generated Noise CA; original certificate/signature/issuer verification remains enabled. No socket/controller/directory method is mocked, and the preload is outside the product build and PR. No external WhatsApp login/interoperability claim is made.
- **Teams:** actual shipped message-search action and Graph HTTP client against a faithful HTTPS fixture through a supported CONNECT proxy and fixture CA. Synthetic JWT credentials use the existing private-QA SDK bootstrap; TLS verification remains enabled. No Graph fetch/search function is mocked and no Azure-authentication claim is made.

For each owner, both NFC-query→NFD-data and NFD-query→NFC-data run twice per revision. Main misses all 12 cross-form cases; candidate returns all 12 original results. Same-form, ASCII, negative and raw-ID/raw-query controls pass. Wire receipts preserve Buzz room filters, WhatsApp participating-group requests and the exact Graph path including a mixed-case channel ID; query substrings are never forwarded as remote search terms.

The new standalone fixtures were consolidated into existing directory snapshot, group sort/limit and HTML-search contracts. Candidate focused tests pass **39/39**; exactly the three canonical regressions fail on main, with the other 36 passing. Formatting and type-aware lint on all six changed files pass with zero warnings/errors. Production +20/−6 (net +14); tests +9/−9 (net zero). Final consolidation changes tests only after the proven production build.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous local matching behavior; no state, config or stored values are migrated. Blast radius is Buzz directory filtering, WhatsApp live group filtering and Teams target-scoped message filtering. Authentication, message delivery, identifiers and remote query contracts are unchanged.

prs.title: improve(ci): reuse iOS screenshot dependencies
prs.body:
Closes #187985

## What Problem This Solves

iOS screenshot CI repeats Watch RTC compilation and Swift package downloads that can be reused between fresh builds.

## User Impact

No app UI change. Screenshot capture keeps its full iPhone, iPad, and Watch workload and fresh compilation. Cache misses or transfer failures run the normal cold build.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consume the existing checksum-verified Watch RTC simulator cache from trusted main CI. Cache only screenshot `SourcePackages` in a separate namespace; preparation retains those downloads and removes every other DerivedData entry, including hidden state. Automatic package resolution remains enabled.

PRs restore only. Successful trusted current-main captures publish package downloads, including manual CI because hourly main CI skips screenshots. Historical/frozen targets skip the new caches. No new jobs, runner changes, release dispatches, or upload paths.

## Evidence

- Fastlane regression failed before the fix because cleanup removed a cached package source; afterward all 15 cases passed (1.34 s Vitest, 2.49 s complete wrapper). The existing fixture proves warm-source retention, cold fallback, stale build/hidden-state removal, and failed-build behavior.
- Apple cache suite: 6/6 passed (2.36 s Vitest, 3.46 s wrapper), including trusted-main save restrictions, restore-only Watch reuse, cache-off/frozen/historical exclusions, and package-only paths. Existing RTC content/checksum invalidation proof remains unchanged.
- Workflow actionlint/zizmor and repository guards, targeted tooling typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, Ruby syntax, and diff checks passed. At the original base, all 11 required workflow/native-cache files passed: 1,033 tests, 10 existing skips, 334.62 s complete wrapper.
- Independent AutoReview: scoped-clean at P0–P2 with full workflow, Fastfile, Watch builder, and project settings supplied. Author diff cleanup found no additional changes needed.
- Net test growth: 92 lines, with an exact allocation for the package-cleanup regression and cache trust/path contracts. New hosted runner registrations: zero.

### Hosted CI

The initial run [40981704279](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40981704279/job/123823545203) restored verified Watch RTC libraries and completed the cold Swift package resolution/build in 161.51 seconds. All eight iPhone/iPad captures passed, but Watch boot ended in `Shutdown` before installation. The matching boot failure predates these cache changes.

The branch is now rebased onto `766f5e9a8cdf546203182ee642060ce7ce4a3038`, including merged #188014's shared CPU-headroom admission before simulator creation. The cache patch is unchanged; no merge commit, boot/capture retry, or weaker assertion was added. New head: `c4a060b70371df4c79aebfc57706a9f44dd12756`.

All 36 focused cache, Fastlane, headroom, and resource-timeline tests passed together after the rebase, as did actionlint, zizmor, repository workflow guards, and the diff check.

Fresh [CI 40989171984](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40989171984) tested this head through merge revision `3ee6facc379f179b8b1fa5220c7a2f1c0e8d99c2`:

- [Complete screenshot capture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40989171984/job/123847667312) and its evidence check passed on attempt 1. Downloaded manifests confirm all nine PNGs, all eight native screenshot tests passed, and no capture retry. All three owned simulators were shut down and deleted with zero active devices afterward.
- Watch RTC inputs restored successfully in approximately two seconds. The new Swift package namespace missed, and automatic package resolution plus the cold native build succeeded in 154.84 seconds. Source package publication was skipped for this PR, as intended.
- Headroom waits were 78.22 seconds for iPhone, 22.15 seconds for iPad, and 10.13 seconds for Watch. Watch boot completed in 37.69 seconds and capture in 22.36 seconds.
- Artifacts: `ios-release-screenshot-capture-3ee6facc379f179b8b1fa5220c7a2f1c0e8d99c2` and `ios-release-screenshot-diagnostics-3ee6facc379f179b8b1fa5220c7a2f1c0e8d99c2`.

### Pre-existing CI failure

| Check | Result and attribution |
| --- | --- |
| [checks-node-compact-small-5-1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40989171984/job/123847667535) | Five `ci-workflow-planning.test.ts` assertions still expect two separate selected compiler shards. Main's `2106751bd188` (#188011) combines those graphs into one worker. The same ten selected cases produced the same five assertion failures on both this branch and an untouched checkout of exact base `766f5e9a8cdf546203182ee642060ce7ce4a3038`. Neither the planner nor these expectations is changed by this PR. |
| `openclaw/ci-gate` | Fails downstream of that inherited planning-test failure. |

The automated failed-test classifier reported `unknown` because it found no matching main job; the independent exact-base reproduction establishes that this failure is inherited. The branch reproduction took 10.02 seconds and the base reproduction took 10.45 seconds, each with five passed and five failed selected cases. The other 651 cases were outside the focused reproduction; no tracked changes were made for this inherited failure.

CI has settled. Both native Periphery builds and the shared dead-code intersection passed. The planning-test shard and its downstream aggregate gate are the only red checks; no directly branch-related CI failure was identified.

The new Swift package namespace still needs a successful trusted current-main producer before cross-run warm restore can be measured. No overall speedup is claimed from a cache hit alone; complete cold/warm capture wall time remains a measurement to collect after landing.

prs.title: fix(test): preserve RFB stream finalization ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The RFB lifecycle tests use an async-iterator consumer that can destroy the Duplex at readable EOF before its queued writes finish. That observer changes the lifecycle the test is intended to verify.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. The tests continue to require complete terminal responses, queued client bytes, write callbacks, owner cancellation, and writable completion.

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: feat(cron): skip scheduled runs when a shell precheck finds no work
prs.body:
Supersedes #171738 and links the closed replay #112375. ## What Problem This Solves Scheduled jobs that poll for work still start a model turn when the inbox, queue, or watch target is empty. This supersedes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171738 and replaces the closed replay of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/112375. Those branches targeted the previous cron store and could not be applied to current main. This branch is based on current `openclaw/openclaw` main (`7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92`). ## User Impact User impact: an operator can attach a host shell precheck to an `at`, `every`, or `cron` job. Exit code 0 continues into the trigger and payload. Exit code 2 records a skipped run with summary `precheck-no-work` and does not start the model turn. Denied, unapproved, timed out, or unexpected results fail closed and skip the payload. Agent turns cannot create or edit the command. Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/schedules#shell-precheck ## Why This Change Was Made Current cron jobs live in SQLite `job_json`, with validation in the cron service and execution in `executeJobCore`. The precheck is an optional field on that job, not a new config key or schema version. The probe runs through `createExecTool` with `nonInteractiveApproval` and no host-approval bypass, then the existing gateway allowlist and approval floors. `cron.triggers.enabled: false` disables it. Forced manual runs still run the probe; they do not skip it the way they skip a condition script. ## Evidence Local validation on `7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5`: - `pnpm test src/cron/job-precheck.test.ts src/cron/job-precheck-run.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.precheck.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.occurrence.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-precheck.test.ts` — passed. Cron shard: 4 files, 86 tests. CLI shard: 1 file, 3 tests. The exec-policy file proves a marker file is not created when security is deny, ask is always, the job pin requires ask always, `toolsAllow` excludes exec, or run authority is rejected. An allowed `full`/`off` policy covers exit 2 (no work) and exit 0 (work). - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed TypeScript files — passed. - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check` on the 29 changed files — all matched files use the correct format. - `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed. - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-services-cron.tsbuildinfo` — passed. ## Security review ### Threat model A precheck is an unattended host command. The realistic attackers are a model turn that tries to persist one, an operator who saved a command and later tightened exec policy, and a forced or restarted run that might otherwise skip the gate. The command can do anything the exec tool would allow, including reading or writing files on the gateway host. The feature must not add a second spawn path with weaker defaults. ### How approvals are enforced - The runner calls `createExecTool` with the resolved `tools.exec` host, mode, security, and ask, plus the live exec-approvals file that the tool already re-reads. It does not pass `bypassHostApprovalFloors`. - `nonInteractiveApproval: true` makes approval-requiring commands return `approval_required` before spawn. `ask: "always"`, an allowlist miss, and `security: "deny"` therefore do not run the command. - A stored `toolsAllowExecTarget` pin is applied with `pinExecToolTarget`, so a creator floor of `ask: "always"` still denies a headless run when global policy is `full`/`off`. - A defined `toolsAllow` that does not include `exec` denies the probe before the tool is built. - `assertRunCurrent` is awaited in `executeJobCore` and again inside the runner immediately before `tool.execute`. A rejected run does not spawn. - If the gateway does not wire `runJobPrecheck`, or `cron.triggers.enabled` is false, the job errors and the payload does not start. - Agent creates and patches that set a non-null `precheck` are rejected in the automations tool and again in `assertCronModelJobAllowed`. Clearing the field is allowed. `cron.run` of an existing job is not treated as authoring. - Invalid persisted prechecks quarantine the row instead of being dropped, so a bad write cannot fall open into an unguarded payload. - Each run re-reads current policy. A command saved under a looser policy is denied after the operator tightens it. ### Residual risks - Command payloads (`runCronCommandJob`) still spawn from their own runner and do not use this exec-tool gate. That path is unchanged. - Operators who can already persist command jobs can persist a precheck through the CLI or Gateway API. The protection is the run-time policy check, not a second save-time approval dialog. Reusing the stream approval dialog would describe the wrong effect. - `mode: "auto"` remains the existing exec auto-review path. With `nonInteractiveApproval`, a reviewer that approves can still allow a spawn. Tests pin `mode: "full"` so they do not depend on a reviewer. This change does not weaken or special-case auto-review. - When config omits security, the exec tool keeps its own non-sandbox default and the approvals file still applies its floors. That is the same default as other exec callers. - Exit codes are the only work signal. A command that prints a success banner and exits 2 is no-work. A command that exits 0 after doing nothing is work. Overlapping codes are rejected. - The probe runs on the exec host selected by `tools.exec` unless a gateway pin forces the gateway host. It cannot target a node or sandbox that the exec tool itself would refuse.
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Introduces unattended host command execution on the gateway before scheduled agent turns, gated by exec policy but still a security-sensitive automation surface. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). Updated by merging current upstream main (merge commit `ce9c3641f4`); the precheck, occurrence and CLI cron tests (89 tests) and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass on the merged head.

prs.title: fix(memory): reduce transcript stats worker overhead
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory indexing loads the broad session runtime just to read transcript statistics, multiplying unnecessary module cost across worker isolates.

## User Impact

This candidate aims to lower the memory floor of stats-only workers while preserving transcript results and incognito authority. **Maintainer accepted the measured performance tradeoffs on 2026-10-30. Landing still requires CI and exact-head review clearance.** No new configuration, cache, worker pool, schema, migration, or operator action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The grouped read-only accessor and its existing guarded memory wrapper now have narrow owners. Memory-index workers use a private-local SDK subpath; transcript and corpus workers use the core read-only leaf. The original grouping, ordering, missing-store handling, cancellation binding, deprecation warning, and incognito checks remain intact. Existing public SDK exports remain available.

Production code is +14 lines: imports and module boundaries needed to stop stats readers loading actor acquisition and the broader session runtime. Tests are +5 lines net; generated SDK metadata is +12; the existing profiler is +13. No release-owned changelog files are edited; this description supplies release-note context.

## Evidence

Current head: `8e0960520dde4c31ae3521760e48798ae9a32577`.
Benchmarked runtime/harness head: `8619df3c47204111c31ed9d9d12c6a747d1dde35`. The only subsequent changes are four test/documentation files (+6/-3); production runtime, dependency inputs, and benchmark source are byte-identical. The package hashes and measurements below belong to the benchmarked head.
Frozen comparison base: `55d82ecb0da219c6e34284f265a19d12884b80a3`.

- 59 focused tests pass across cold read-only statistics, incognito actor access, actual async stats and corpus workers, memory worker reads, and SQLite usage/data-version callers.
- Core typecheck, targeted lint/formatting, SDK export synchronization/check, diff checks, and test-line budget pass.
- Independent source review and complete P0–P3 committed-range autoreview covered the benchmarked runtime. Fresh independent reviews found no actionable issue in the subsequent integration-test/documentation repairs.
- All four previously failed integration surfaces are repaired: the lazy-import mock now targets the new stats subpath, the boundary inventory lists the two extracted modules, the private SDK catalog documents the subpath, and the handoff denial fixture uses the still-Gateway-wide `tools.catalog` read. The last mismatch arose only after CI merged in [main's guest tool-preview change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/284c109dfe22da3c5eff5d0ef7d1b14f9fe0302a), which intentionally permits `tools.effective` for session readers. Both broad-read and admin denials remain tested. Focused proof passes 27 contract/worker tests plus 75 handoff/scope tests. The final fixture matches [main's independent test repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f00dd960e35c6881c26471e06f3a838c92387ff4) exactly, removing the merge conflict without rebasing runtime inputs; its 8 handoff cases pass again. Fresh merged-context CI is required for this head.
- SDK surface check reports no unauthorized shipped removals, but its public-count budgets are red (160/158 entrypoints, 3841/3822 exports, 2226/2214 callable exports). The exact frozen baseline fails with the same three counts. This inherited budget failure is not recorded as a pass.
- Runtime package build, tarball integrity, and isolated npm installation pass. Installed build-info commits match both arms, and all 591 normalized dependency-lock entries are identical. The private runtime subpath ships; its declaration remains excluded. Both arms emit the same pre-existing UI chat-boot budget warning (1247.0 KiB against 1246.7 KiB). Trusted local proof uses the existing approved fallback after the remote Testbox route was unavailable.
- Package SHA-256: baseline `634b4654e45192af152ee90fe09a63bb3a23b81dbc9dad91797b6c35f548bcde`; candidate `3791b66fd6a839f6e7cb222553c7a79c4d7bcebfb61bd6f8ba0c694e75673b1d`.

### Performance acceptance rule — recorded before scored runs

Run serially on one host with Node 26.12.1, identical runtime dependency locks, exact installed package commits, and no overlapping task builds/tests. Record host load for every run. Five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs for each workload; report median, nearest-rank p95 (maximum of five), and min/max. Keep cold and warm results separate.

1. **Packaged memory-index worker:** use the committed `scripts/perf/worker-module-graphs-measure.mjs` with `--worker memory-index --built --build-dir <installed-package> --samples 1200 --state-dir <isolated-state> --output <result>`. Each task asks for two transcript stats in one missing store and must return exactly `{kind:"transcript-stats",stats:[null,null]}`. This measures the import floor, not populated SQL throughput. Require fewer actually loaded modules and at least 10% lower post-GC retained worker heap; cold first-task latency, warm p50/p95 latency, worker CPU, and allocated bytes must hold or improve. Shared-process RSS is not attributed to an individual worker.
2. **Real Gateway load:** run committed `scripts/bench-gateway-concurrency.ts` against each installed `dist/entry.js`, using the mock provider, 32 seeded sessions, two agents/concurrent turns, 20 turns per agent, 20 history messages of 1024 characters, two history clients, two subscribers, 300 probe rounds at 100ms, 20ms streaming chunks, and control-plane probes. Each run must verify all 40 turns, 600 history reads, all control probes, and clean exit. Require lower peak process RSS; process/main-thread CPU, startup/setup, turn duration, and transport median/tails must hold or improve. Report unforced endpoint heap separately; it is not retained-heap proof.

Any correctness failure rejects the candidate. Any worse user-facing metric blocks landing without explicit owner acceptance recorded here; a 20% regression in any cell is a stop. An isolated heap win cannot waive a Gateway regression. Scored results are below. The measured increases are not waived as noise or hidden by the worker-level gain.


### Measured outcome — packaged runtime at 8619df3

**The strict performance gate was missed; the maintainer has explicitly accepted the measured tradeoffs for this change.** The stats worker retains 60.71% less heap (42.23 MiB saved) and Gateway process CPU falls 14.28%, but median peak RSS is +0.047% (+1.42 MiB). Worst-run readiness, Control UI, and cron latency tails rise more than 20%. These are observed comparison results, not a proven causal attribution. The maintainer accepted these published results on 2026-10-30. This is explicit tradeoff acceptance, not a claim that the adverse measurements passed the original rule. CI and review clearance remain required.

The ten Gateway runs verified all 400 turns, 6,000 history reads, all control probes, and ten clean exits. Worker runs verified 12,000 warm requests plus setup requests, with one identical result hash in all ten runs: `78c13428e021f2884636cff6c4b992e37b54141c41173eeacdacb76bb05fc2f7`.

Each arm has five runs and 1,200 warm requests per run. File counts are unique file-backed script URLs, including dependencies; all belong to the selected installed package apart from the two shared benchmark files. Actor-acquisition, config-runtime, and broad session-facade chunks are absent in the candidate. Both arms start with 67 script files before their first stats request. The worker's Inspector stays attached: heap is isolate-local and post-GC but includes instrumentation; allocated bytes include the whole measured worker and transport, not only the stats function. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the session Advanced menu shows two adjacent dividers above Delete when its optional involvement action is absent or already shown in the root menu.

## User Impact

User impact: Advanced keeps one boundary between visible sections, while preserving the boundaries around Hide from Involving me when that action is present. No configuration changes or user actions are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Advanced menu composition now owns its section boundaries. The involvement divider is included only with a visible involvement action; communication controls, Reset, and settings errors/retry stay in one section. This removes the competing communication closing divider without hiding meaningful boundaries through CSS.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the actual sidebar → Advanced flow with an isolated synthetic mock Gateway, Chromium, dark theme, 1280×900. The reported Involving me state has three dividers before and two after; the duplicate above Delete is gone. [Inspected before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188017#issuecomment-6512629793).
- Base-red / fix-green regression: desktop and compact menus, involvement in the root versus Advanced, missing involvement, settings read-error/retry, and Reset. Four assertions fail on base `6fc01dc6615798ce5bd5b5f9268e8457fcbf5846`; all 11 communication cases pass after the fix.
- Focused shared-consumer validation: **88 tests passed in 5 files**, 13.40 seconds wall time. Includes session-menu, Solid menu, involvement, communication, and chat-header consumers. CI seconds pending.
- CI repair: the core-test-ui-components graph caught an incomplete hello fixture that `pnpm tsgo:ui` does not cover. Reproduced its exact TS2322, then reused the existing typed `gatewayHelloForMethods` fixture without casts or type weakening. `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-components.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-ui-components.tsbuildinfo` now exits 0. The communication/involvement suites pass **15 tests in 2 files**, 5.91 seconds wall time, after this test-only repair. Independent review of the repair found no P0–P3 findings. Production files and the screenshot evidence are unchanged.
- Passed: `pnpm ui:build`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, targeted type-aware lint and formatting, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`, and `git diff --check`. No baselines or budgets changed.
- Independent read-only source review found no actionable P0–P3 findings. Local autoreview (Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2) found no actionable findings in the final local snapshot against the base above; unchanged-source coverage was supplied by the separate independent review. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because the installed checkout was dirty and stale; [hosted review is already acknowledged](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188017#issuecomment-6512614202), so no duplicate request was posted.
- Simplification: production −7 lines, tests +38 lines. One composition owner replaces the detail builder's outer separators; reactive/lifecycle API counts are unchanged. No live shared-session data was modified. Broad CI and WebKit remain PR-CI proof.

Reported by @shakkernerd.

prs.title: feat(plugins): reload edited bundled plugin code in development with OPENCLAW_DEV_RELOAD_BUNDLED_PLUGINS
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Developers working on bundled plugins, such as Knowledge, have to restart the Gateway to test every edit to the plugin's server code. `openclaw plugins reload <id>` refreshes the plugin's registrations, but bundled code keeps running from the host and the reload returns `restartRequired: true`.

## User Impact

A developer can start a Node/Bun source checkout or compiled-on-disk Gateway with `OPENCLAW_DEV_RELOAD_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1`. With it set, `openclaw plugins reload <id>` loads that bundled plugin's edited code from disk and returns `restartRequired: false`, with a warning that the replaced code stays in memory until restart.

**Nothing changes when the variable is unset.** Bundled code stays host-owned, and reload returns `restartRequired: true` with the existing warning. The opt-in must come from the Gateway's launch environment: there is no config key, CLI flag, RPC field or UI toggle, and config `env.vars` can't set it, so `config.patch`, agents and remote clients can't turn it on. Standalone executables (JIT, bytecode and AOT) ignore the variable and say so in the reload receipt.

## Why This Change Was Made

This restores the capture path from #180466, plus the Worker host-link repairs from #181128 and #181458, but only behind the operator opt-in. It reuses the existing captured-generation, worker preparation and recovery owners, so there's no second reload subsystem.

**How this addresses the concerns behind #182403:**

- **Embedded/AOT builds have no physical files to recapture.** Standalone executables ignore the opt-in (`isStandaloneRuntimeExecutable`), keep embedded code, and return `restartRequired: true` with a warning that the variable was ignored. No filesystem discovery runs.
- **Bundled modules get a second code identity.** That never happens by default. With the opt-in, only plugins named in an explicit `plugins.reload` are recaptured: the plugin tree plus the chunks that `dist/runtime-dependency-ownership.json` lists for that plugin. Those chunks are used only by plugins, though other plugins may share them. Host, SDK and core-shared chunks still resolve to the Gateway's loaded modules, including from captured Workers.
- **Embedded provider-auth fix.** Untouched; `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-runtime.ts` isn't modified.
- **Production regressions after #180466** (#181494 setup activation, and the capture-scanner stall from #182194). The capture path can't be reached by default. Even with the opt-in it isn't used for startup, config-driven reloads (including model changes), setup modules or public surfaces, because the reload's lifecycle reason must be `reload`.

**Launch-only opt-in:** `isConfigRuntimeEnvVarAllowed` (the config env admission owner) rejects `OPENCLAW_DEV_RELOAD_BUNDLED_PLUGINS`, alongside the other deployment-owned host controls. A config write can't publish it into `process.env`.

**Fix found end to end:** A bundled capture is rooted at the host package, and binding the plugin's cache root to that capture root merged the host package's cache record into the plugin's. Later cold public-surface loads, for example a web-search provider, then failed to resolve `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`. The plugin now keeps its own cache root, and a regression assertion covers it.

**Env-var budget:** `config/env-var-count-budget.txt` grows from 458 to 459 for this owner-approved name.

**Accepted edge cases (documented):**
- JavaScript module graphs can't be unloaded, so each development reload keeps the previous graph until the process exits.
- If a config-driven reload later replaces a dev-reloaded plugin, it goes back to the Gateway's loaded code.
- Setup modules, public surfaces and host/SDK edits still need a restart.
- **Not yet proven:** plugin state operations (`*-operation-api` modules, for example memory-core recall) for a dev-reloaded bundled plugin. They load from the captured copy rather than the shared bundled operation capture. Knowledge has no operation APIs. Treat this as unverified until a follow-up adds a check.

## Evidence

- **Gateway reload regression** (`server-plugin-reload.installed-package.test.ts`): unchanged main assertions still show an edited bundled helper stays `A` with `restartRequired: true`. With the opt-in, the same reload loads `B`, then `C`, with `restartRequired` absent and a sibling plugin retained. Negative control: disabling the gate makes the new assertion fail (`expected true to be undefined`).
- **Loader matrix restored from #180466** (`plugin-bundled-reload.test.ts`, 12 tests): source TS, compiled CJS/ESM, runtime overlay and denied file links, Worker shared imports across recovery, plus the WASM, directory-cycle and discarded-URL capture regressions. The new cache-root assertion fails on all 5 layout cases without the fix.
- **CommonJS shared imports:** captured CommonJS code reaches shared host modules after #185033 started routing `require` through `module.registerHooks`. prs.title: fix(codex): omit unavailable question-tool and redundant mode guidance
prs.body:
Closes #187061

## What Problem This Solves

Codex has native collaboration modes, such as Default and Plan, with their own model-facing instructions. Ordinary OpenClaw-managed sessions always select Default and do not expose a mode switch, but still receive a `Collaboration Mode: Default` block explaining mode changes. They also receive instructions for the native `request_user_input` question tool even when it is unavailable.

In the reported configuration, this is intentional tool suppression: when OpenClaw's `ask_user` is callable and no native-question opt-in is configured, OpenClaw disables `request_user_input` to avoid a duplicate question interface. The native collaboration prompt is rendered independently, so its question-tool guidance remains. Even when the native tool is registered, using it in Default mode requires a separate opt-in.

The result is a mismatch between the instructions the model reads and the capabilities the integration provides. The existing "only when it is listed" condition prevents an unconditional instruction to call a missing tool, but leaves irrelevant tool-specific guidance and mode boilerplate in the prompt. This PR removes that noise without enabling extra tools or removing native modes from paths that use them.

## User Impact

The agent receives collaboration guidance matching its available question capabilities, without announcing a mode that ordinary managed sessions cannot switch. Explicit native-question opt-ins and native-supervised modes remain supported; OpenClaw's `ask_user` keeps its own contract.

Existing history is not rewritten. On managed resume, an explicit supersession notice withdraws earlier collaboration instructions, including retained Plan-mode guidance. This is a prompt-quality change; no latency, cost, or answer-quality improvement is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw already decides which collaboration mode and question tools an ordinary managed session can use; its instructions should describe those actual capabilities. Enabling native questions just to match the existing prompt would change behavior rather than fix the mismatch. Replacing every `request_user_input` reference with `ask_user` would also be incorrect: the two tools have different contracts.

A shorter caller-supplied collaboration block is not enough, either. Codex can take its effective collaboration text from the selected model's catalogue, overriding that fallback. This PR therefore suppresses the native collaboration block only for ordinary managed sessions and places concise, capability-aware guidance in the existing thread developer instructions, where it survives compaction.

Native `request_user_input` guidance requires both tool registration and Default-mode eligibility. General guidance about autonomy, genuinely required input, and approval boundaries remains. Supervised starts/resumes/forks and specialized cron/side-question policies retain their existing owners. No new user configuration or dependency is introduced.

## Evidence

Current head: `adb0f8db5e18955d503aaea8f5ab035f5d1663b6`. Base: `1a881c5ff7850f03c8e8f1ada9302ba7fd939dab`. Validation dates: October 29-30, 2026.

### Review and CI repairs

- Updated successful managed-lifecycle configuration fixtures to include the `origins` map required by the native protocol. Production handling was not weakened to accommodate incomplete fixtures.
- Corrected canonical prompt reconstruction to use the developer instructions actually returned by thread configuration, including the managed collaboration policy. Regenerated snapshots through the existing generator and added two focused assertions.
- Fixed a related diagnostic undercount exposed by the consumer tests: prompt reports and trajectory rendering now consume the assembled developer instructions, including the collaboration block. Removed a now-duplicate configured-MCP notice from trajectory assembly.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40948797727) is green: 58 successful checks, 55 conditionally skipped, none pending or failed. Both previously failing jobs now pass: [canonical prompt snapshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40948797727/job/123711976572) and [changed extensions bundle 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40948797727/job/123711976931).
- Local verification includes all 14 app-inventory consumer checks, 13 snapshot checks, the unchanged prompt-report regression after its repair, current generated snapshots, relevant project typechecks, targeted lint/formatting, both line-budget checks, and a complete `pnpm build`.

### Native request-boundary proof

The repository-pinned real Codex **0.164.0** app-server was exercised with a local fixture provider. These tests use synthetic model metadata and fixture responses, not a live model.

- **Red/green:** the original prompt-owner code failed because captured developer input still contained the catalogue-owned Default policy; the fixed implementation passed.
- **Four question surfaces:** neither question tool; callable OpenClaw Ask User with native questions disabled; native registration without Default eligibility; and explicit Default eligibility. Only the last receives native-question usage guidance. All four omit the catalogue-owned Default announcement while preserving skill delivery.
- **Retained history and controls:** native replay retains the earlier Plan message, verifies that a later managed-resume notice supersedes it without another Default heading, and confirms that a native-owned sibling still receives native mode guidance. WebSocket refresh and native compaction cases also pass.
- The original native/policy run passed all 10 checks. The reorganized lifecycle/turn-parameter suites passed 191 checks; all 14 prompt-prefix stability checks and two selected canonical-fork cases also passed. These are overlapping focused runs, not a full-suite total.

### Real Gateway/model output

These are selected fields from captured real Gateway RPC, native requests and persisted native developer messages, not expected-output examples. Replies are actual Gateway payload text with whitespace trimmed. Every model turn used **GPT-6 Luna** with native ChatGPT authentication and principal-match checks; no provider responses were mocked. UUIDs identify disposable fixtures.

The observer's `nativeCollaborationInstructions` field records `config.include_collaboration_mode_instructions`; `nativeToolEnabled` records `config["tools.experimental_request_user_input.enabled"]`. Null means the request did not supply an override, not false. `askUserDeclared` is derived from the actual dynamic-tool names. Only known collaboration-policy lines are retained, not the full developer prompt.

**Fresh managed session.** Real native Codex **0.164.0** received this request surface. The same quoted policy sentence was read back from that thread's native developer message:

```json
{
  "request": {
    "method": "thread/start",
    "nativeCollaborationInstructions": false,
    "nativeToolEnabled": false,
    "askUserDeclared": true,
    "optionalNativeQuestionGuidance": false,
    "collaborationExcerpt": [
      "Prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. Ask the user directly when required input prevents progress; silence is not an answer or approval."
    ]
  },
  "result": {
    "status": "ok",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "actualReply": "ORANGE-314"
  }
}
```

**Latest-stable upgraded retained OpenClaw session.** Registry `latest` was independently checked as **2026.10.9** for both OpenClaw and `@openclaw/codex`. The official stable runtime used native **0.160.0**. After a real seed turn, the fixture stopped, selected the fixed core/bundled plugin/native **0.164.0**, and ran supported `doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` against its retained state (exit 0). Service repair was disabled for the fixture. This exercises a retained-state runtime upgrade, not the update installer.

The second input asked for the previous marker without supplying it again. Actual replies and identities:

```json
[
  {
    "phase": "stable-seed",
    "status": "ok",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "actualReply": "BLUE-271",
    "threadId": "01a189c7-f180-7d20-9972-88f5ef1a4d94",
    "action": "started",
    "sessionId": "b7da0c91-3a6a-4d9c-b997-0c31e304cd0b"
  },
  {
    "phase": "stable-upgraded-retained",
    "status": "ok",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "actualReply": "BLUE-271",
    "threadId": "01a189c9-94d0-7170-991e-61d16fa90021",
    "action": "started",
    "sessionId": "b7da0c91-3a6a-4d9c-b997-0c31e304cd0b"
  }
]
```

Stable's actual persisted collaboration excerpt:

```json
{
  "collaborationExcerpt": [
    "Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>"
  ]
}
```

Fixed Gateway request for the retained OpenClaw session; its persisted native developer message independently contains the same new sentence:

```json
{
  "method": "thread/start",
  "nativeCollaborationInstructions": false,
  "nativeToolEnabled": false,
  "askUserDeclared": true,
  "optionalNativeQuestionGuidance": false,
  "collaborationExcerpt": [
    "Prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. Ask the user directly when required input prevents progress; silence is not an answer or approval."
  ]
}
```

**Upgrade limitation:** the OpenClaw session ID and history survived, but the native thread was recreated (`action: "started"`). The strict upgrade test exited 1 because it required an unchanged native thread ID; that failure is preserved in `upgrade-evidence.json`, not relabeled as a passing native-resume test. Later assertions in that test were not reached; the excerpts above come from independently captured request/rollout records. Existing runtime/tool-catalogue rotation guards are unchanged by this PR, and both surfaces changed between stable and fixed versions; the exact first rotation trigger was not logged. This evidence establishes a retained OpenClaw-session upgrade, **not native-thread continuity across versions**.

**Same-build cold native resume.** A separate successful run stopped/restarted the fixed Gateway and retained both identities while recalling the earlier marker:

```json
[
  {
    "phase": "fresh-managed",
    "sessionId": "5f0a0cbd-f477-4558-80c7-be84d5ba7b72",
    "threadId": "01a189c3-422e-71d1-9aa3-eef40e47f891",
    "action": "started",
    "actualReply": "ORANGE-314"
  },
  {
    "phase": "retained-managed",
    "sessionId": "5f0a0cbd-f477-4558-80c7-be84d5ba7b72",
    "threadId": "01a189c3-422e-71d1-9aa3-eef40e47f891",
    "action": "resumed",
    "actualReply": "ORANGE-314"
  }
]
```

**Explicit native-question opt-in.** A separate fresh control set both `features.default_mode_request_user_input=true` and `tools.experimental_request_user_input.enabled=true`. The captured request did not override native questions to false. Its actual persisted developer-policy observations and real reply were:

```json
{
  "policy": {
    "managedPolicy": true,
    "optionalNativeQuestionGuidance": true,
    "oldModeAnnouncement": false
  },
  "result": {
    "status": "ok",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "actualReply": "NATIVE-OPT-IN-OK"
  }
}
```

This control verifies authored configuration/guidance with a real completed turn. It does not claim execution of a blocking question or same-thread opt-in refresh.

**Native-supervised control.** A separate real native seed was continued through `sessions.catalog.continue`. The Gateway completed a real turn with lifecycle action `forked`. Native collaboration rendering was not disabled, the turn did not impose managed Default mode, and the persisted native policy remained native-owned:

```json
{
  "request": {
    "method": "thread/fork",
    "nativeCollaborationInstructions": null,
    "managedPolicy": false
  },
  "nativeDeveloperPolicy": {
    "managedPolicy": false,
    "oldModeAnnouncement": true,
    "collaborationExcerpt": [
      "Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>"
    ]
  },
  "result": {
    "status": "ok",
    "action": "forked",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "actualReply": "SUPERVISED-NATIVE-OK"
  }
}
```

This control passed separately; it was not reached by the strict upgrade test. Native questions remained disabled by the existing tool-selection policy; this checks collaboration-prompt ownership, not native question-tool callability.

**Build provenance:** the checkout and final build stamps identify `adb0f8db5e1`. Generic `dist/build-info.json` retains `d39a5cc5daf8` from build start before the follow-up commit. A read-only reconstruction of the canonical Codex-plugin compiler fingerprint matches current clean source, and all **180** stamped Codex output hashes match. The attached verifier/result document that scope; no metadata was rewritten and no whole-Gateway artifact-equivalence claim is made.

The supplemental 
[openclaw-187856-live-proof.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34158233/openclaw-187856-live-proof.zip)
 contains sanitized per-run records, exact prompt excerpts, source harness/observer/companion modules, package provenance and reproduction instructions. Runs are reported separately, including the strict upgrade failure. No credentials, account identifiers, IP addresses, private endpoints or full private prompts are included. Existing user Gateway/channels/sessions were untouched.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce focused checks and inspect test cost</summary>

Native request-capture and policy tests:

```sh
pnpm test \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.skills.native.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.handoff.native.test.ts \
```

Recorded original result: 3 policy checks plus 7 native checks passed; 111.95 seconds total runner wall time, including worker preparation.

Lifecycle and turn-parameter checks:

prs.title: fix(ios): wait for host headroom before screenshot boot
prs.body:
Closes #188012

## What Problem This Solves

Screenshot capture can start a fresh Watch simulator while the host is still saturated after the phone/tablet captures. In [CI 40981704279](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40981704279/job/123823545203), all eight iPhone/iPad captures and their cleanup passed, but Watch boot ended during migration before installation. The runner had only 4–7% idle CPU around Watch boot. The same shutdown signature predates this branch (#172730); the precise Apple shutdown cause remains unknown.

## User Impact

Before creating each screenshot simulator, require ten continuous seconds with at least 30% idle host CPU. A host that cannot meet that condition within five minutes fails before the next device starts. This is a contention mitigation. Both predeclared fresh hosted screenshot flows passed on their first attempts; the precise Apple shutdown cause remains unknown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse qualification's existing headroom helper through its native Node command-line entry point, within the existing simulator lifecycle owner. No new timer or readiness policy. Fresh devices, serial ownership, clean builds, exact `Booted` verification, cleanup, and all capture assertions remain intact. Boot and capture are not retried, and their deadlines are unchanged. The existing resource timeline recognizes the added headroom phase.

## Evidence

- The lane regression fails on the base with `simulator created without CPU headroom`. With the candidate, all 30 focused Fastlane, headroom, and resource timeline tests pass (1.20 s Vitest; 2.44 s complete wrapper). The lane fixture also proves that a Watch headroom timeout preserves the eight completed screenshots, starts no Watch simulator, and performs no installation.
- Direct native Node command-line execution passed on local Node 26.5 and Node 24.18. Existing headroom tests retain sustained-idle, busy-reset, delayed-observer, timeout, frozen-counter, and cancellation coverage. Tooling-test typecheck, Ruby syntax, Node syntax, script erasability, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Independent AutoReview/Codex review against base `f126f05fd9521e2977f2b7921ff49522fde0b552`: scoped-clean at P0–P2, no findings; complete Fastfile, shared helper, qualification caller and timeline supplied. Hosted ClawSweeper found one P3 timeout-message issue, now addressed with explicit recovery guidance. Its pending-hosted-proof observation is resolved by the results below.
- Author simplification kept one existing readiness owner and added no fallback or retry. No readiness algorithm or capture deadline was changed; regression growth: 17 lines with a separate exact allocation. No visual/product UI change.

### Hosted acceptance, recorded before candidate execution

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled update discovery remaining stuck after installation discovery returns an error result, even after the underlying failure clears.

## User Impact

The next scheduled check can discover the installation and announce an available update. Failed discovery remains visible in status; healthy discovery stays cached. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lifecycle cached both the failed result and its fulfilled initialization promise indefinitely. Cache healthy facts separately from in-flight work, and retire the in-flight promise on either outcome while preserving concurrent healthy adoption.

## Evidence

- Actual-source module probe: base performs one discovery and never recovers; candidate coalesces concurrent discovery, retries the failure, and reuses the healthy result.
- New scheduled-entry regression requires a fresh local probe, remote Git refresh, and countdown campaign after the failure.

prs.title: fix(mxc): resolve literal sandbox file paths without trimming
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The mxc sandbox fs bridge trimmed the tool-supplied `filePath` before mapping it onto its mounts, so a literal file name like `" x.txt"` silently addressed its trimmed sibling `x.txt`. A sandboxed agent reading or writing `" x.txt"` touched the decoy file instead of the one the model chose.

Precedent: #187554 ("The configured directory's whitespace belongs to its filesystem identity"). Sibling: #172869.

## Why This Change Was Made

`MxcFsBridge.resolveTarget` in `extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts` now resolves the caller's literal `filePath`; only the optional invocation base (`cwd`) keeps its blank-check via `trim()`, matching the shape accepted in #187554. The mount-containment guard is unchanged and still operates on the literal-resolved path.

Classification: `behavior-completing` (extends the literal-path contract to the mxc bridge owner).

## User Impact

Agents working in the mxc sandbox backend now read and write the exact file the model named, including names with leading/trailing whitespace. Ordinary paths, absolute paths, and outside-root rejections behave identically.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `ed26a563f` (branch `fix/mxc-literal-file-path`)
- Current-main RED baseline: `c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711`
- Production entry: real dispatch via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/mxc/test/fs-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (Node 24.18, Linux x64, secretless Docker)
- Canonical owner exercised: `MxcFsBridge.resolveTarget` in `extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts:178`, through the public `readFile` with real filesystem files
- Decision surface: the `filePath` parameter of sandboxed agent file tools (`Type.String` schema, no pattern constraint; no upstream trim in the tool chain)
- Recorder/readback boundary: the file bytes returned by `readFile`, asserted byte-for-byte against distinct literal/decoy contents
- Acceptance RED: on current main, the new assertion failed — `readFile(" x.txt")` returned the decoy's contents (`"decoy-data"` instead of `"literal-data"`); the two pre-existing test variants passed (1 failed / 2 passed)
- Acceptance GREEN: on exact head, all 3 tests pass, with both `" x.txt"` → literal and `"x.txt"` → decoy observed through the real bridge over real files
- Legal controls: the trimmed sibling still resolves to itself; the pre-existing native-tool-paths matrix (workspaceOnly true/false) and its mutation denials are unchanged and green
- Cleanup: isolated temp workspaces only; no mxc runtime, Gateway, or production config touched (the bridge owner is host path math plus real fs access checks)

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/mxc/test/fs-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 3/3 (RED run on main: 1 failed / 2 passed at the new assertion)
- `oxfmt --check` on both changed files — clean
- Not tested: live mxc container end-to-end (the changed owner is pure host-side path resolution + fs, exercised with real files here); Windows container-path normalization

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+4/-1`
- Test LOC: `+29/-0` (existing test file only)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the existing mount-containment guard (`isPathInside`) and mount table; no new validator or export
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none
- Two-way door: reverting restores trimmed-path resolution

## Maintainer edits

<details>
<summary>land-ready notes</summary>

- Maintainer edits are allowed on this branch (small, single-owner change).
- Alternative considered: normalizing only in the containment check — rejected: the resolved host path itself must stay literal or the fs target is wrong.
- Scope declaration: this PR changes the mirror/local mapping only; the mxc spawn launcher and readiness owners are untouched.

</details>


## Shipped-run proof (2026-10-30)

Reviewer demand: terminal evidence of **shipped file tools selecting ` x.txt` rather than `x.txt`**, with the Windows-flow boundary disclosed (no shipped Windows MXC flow was captured).

**Entry point: compiled shipped module + real fs** — no vitest, no tsx, no mocks.

- Class: `MxcFsBridge` compiled from this PR's sources by the repo's own extension build (same tsdown build that emits `dist/extensions/mxc/index.js`).
- The mxc Linux registration path is intentionally dormant (`registerMxcPlugin` warns and returns early off-Windows before registering any backend), so the class was imported through a **scratch-only re-export entry** (`extensions/mxc/proof-entry.ts`, worktree-local, never committed) that the same build emitted as `dist/extensions/mxc/proof-entry.js`. It was instantiated with the **exact shipped construction expression** from `mxc-backend.ts`: `new MxcFsBridge(sandbox)` — the same call the backend's `createFsBridge` performs for agent file tools. The compiled class is the shipped build output.
- The mxc read/write path under test is pure Node path-mapping over the mount table plus a real fs-safe root: no MXC binary and no Windows host is required for the code this PR changes.

**Boundary disclosure:** no Windows host is available for this run. The changed owner (`MxcFsBridge.resolveTarget`) is OS-agnostic Node path-mapping; Windows-specific container-path normalization (drive-letter/case semantics) is out of scope for this change and untested. This run is the strongest Linux shipped evidence for the mxc bridge.

Exact commands (scratch worktree at `b17f25996` + this PR's disjoint `extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts`; local-only, nothing pushed from it):

```
export PATH=/tmp/node24/node-v24.22.1-linux-x64/bin:$PATH
cd <scratch-worktree>
pnpm openclaw --version            # full build; emits dist/extensions/mxc/proof-entry.js
node proof/mxc-driver.mjs          # head run -> GREEN below
# red pairing: restore base bridge, rebuild, rerun
git show c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711:extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts > extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-external-plugin-local-dist.mts
node proof/mxc-driver.mjs          # base run -> RED below
# restore head and rebuild
git checkout ed26a563fd3c370651150800d588fa5273ee1737 -- extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-external-plugin-local-dist.mts
```

Seeds: ` x.txt` = `PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content`, `x.txt` = `PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content` (0o644) under the rw agent-workspace mount.

Base `c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711` (pre-fix `.trim()`) — exit 1:

```
read ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> "PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content"          <-- trimmed to the decoy
writeFile ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> ok
  on-disk ' x.txt' -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content"                   <-- literal untouched
  on-disk 'x.txt'   -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-WRITTEN-BY-SHIPPED-BRIDGE" <-- decoy received the write
FAIL  read selects literal (relative+cwd)
FAIL  relative write landed on literal file
FAIL  relative write left decoy untouched
OVERALL: RED
```

Head `ed26a563fd3c370651150800d588fa5273ee1737` (this PR) — exit 0, full output:

```
read '/sandbox/ x.txt' -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content"
read '/sandbox/x.txt'   -> "PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content"
read ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content"          <-- literal selected
read '/sandbox/plain.txt' (control) -> "PROOF_PLAIN_77AA00-roundtrip"
writeFile ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> ok
  on-disk ' x.txt' -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-WRITTEN-BY-SHIPPED-BRIDGE"   <-- literal updated
  on-disk 'x.txt'   -> "PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content"                       <-- decoy untouched
resolvePath '/sandbox/ x.txt' -> hostPath=.../agent-workspace/ x.txt     <-- literal identity kept
resolvePath '/sandbox/x.txt'   -> hostPath=.../agent-workspace/x.txt
PASS  read selects literal (absolute)
PASS  read selects decoy for unpadded sibling
PASS  read selects literal (relative+cwd)
PASS  relative write landed on literal file
PASS  relative write left decoy untouched
PASS  resolvePath keeps literal identity
PASS  resolvePath keeps decoy identity
PASS  control plain round-trip read
PASS  control plain round-trip write
OVERALL: GREEN
```

Controls: absolute-path read/write with only an interior space (`/sandbox/ x.txt`) is not affected by the trim bug and behaves identically on base and head; plain unpadded `plain.txt` round-trips on both. The defect scope is exactly a tool-supplied **relative** name with leading whitespace — the scenario the added regression test pins.

Cleanup: proof temp workspaces under `/tmp` removed; the scratch worktree (including the local-only `proof-entry.ts` re-export and its package.json build-config tweak) was never pushed; the PR branch itself is unchanged — head stays `ed26a563fd3c370651150800d588fa5273ee1737`, no commit/push was needed.

Not tested: Windows container end-to-end (no MXC-capable Windows host available; see boundary disclosure above) and a live mxc runtime turn. The changed owner is host-side path resolution + real fs access, which this compiled-module run exercises directly.

prs.title: fix(codex): materialize native tool-output images from raw response items
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #153949.

Codex's native `ImageView` tool (and other native tools that hand back an
image) surfaces to OpenClaw as a raw `function_call_output` /
`custom_tool_call_output` response item whose `output` array contains a
nested `{"type":"input_image","image_url":"data:image/png;base64,..."}`
entry. `CodexGeneratedMediaProjection.recordRaw` (the Codex media owner)
only recognized raw `image_generation_call` items and returned immediately
for anything else, so this event shape was silently dropped.
`readCodexResponseOutput` deliberately omits non-text tool output from the
text transcript on the assumption that the media owner picks it up
(`extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-tool-output.ts:129`), so
the image bytes never reached the transcript or Control UI at all: the
assistant's reply referenced "the screenshot above" while no attachment
existed anywhere.

## What Changed

- `CodexGeneratedMediaProjection.recordRaw` now also inspects
  `function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call_output` raw items, scanning
  their `output` array for `input_image` entries.
- Each `image_url` is validated through the existing
  `sanitizeInlineImageDataUrl` guard (same validation already used for
  Codex history payload sanitization) and decoded via the existing
  `parseImageDataUrl` helper.
- Valid images are materialized through the exact same
  `recordImage`/`materializeImage` path already used for
  `image_generation_call` results, so they get the same size cap,
  concurrent-completion dedupe, and delivery/transcript wiring as
  generated images, and are marked as a side effect
  (`hadPotentialSideEffects`).
- Invalid or missing `image_url` values are skipped (fail closed): no
  placeholder, no partial write.

This is scoped to the raw-response-item media owner only; it does not
touch the `image_generation_call` path, billing/side-effect
classification for actual image generation, or the separate
dynamic-tool-image rendering path added in #120577 (which covers a
different event shape — dynamic tool results carried on typed thread
items, not this nested raw `input_image` payload).

## Evidence

New regression test, reverted against the pre-fix source
(`git checkout HEAD~1 -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts`)
to confirm it fails without the change:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts -t "saves a native tool-output input_image"
...
FAIL  |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts > CodexAppServerEventProjector media projection > saves a native tool-output input_image as reply media
AssertionError: Target cannot be null or undefined.
 ❯ extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts:394:34
    392|     const mediaUrl = result.toolMediaUrls?.[0];
    393|
    394|     expect(result.toolMediaUrls).toHaveLength(1);
```

Restored the fix and reran — passes:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts -t "saves a native tool-output input_image"
✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts > CodexAppServerEventProjector media projection > saves a native tool-output input_image as reply media 51ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed | 29 skipped (30)
```

Full relevant suites, all passing (89 tests):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.replay-safety.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.final-media.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/tool-media-payloads.test.ts
...
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # media.test.ts + replay-safety.test.ts: 50 passed
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # run-attempt.final-media.test.ts: 9 passed
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # tool-media-payloads.test.ts: 24 passed
```

Formatting/lint on the changed files:

```
$ npx oxlint extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts
(no issues)
$ npx oxfmt --check extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
$ git diff --check
(clean)
```

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs`'s repo-wide "line-cap growth ratchet"
check fails in this checkout, but it fails identically (same file list,
same counts) on unmodified `upstream/main` with these two files stashed
out — it's flagging pre-existing large files unrelated to this change,
not anything this PR touches.

`tsgo --noEmit` on the `extensions/codex` project reports 1618 errors in
this checkout, all `TS2307: Cannot find module 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/*'`
(missing generated plugin-sdk type declarations from a partial/source-only
dependency setup) plus pre-existing `any`/`unknown` findings in unrelated
files (e.g. `src/supervision-tools.ts`, `src/session-cli.ts`). Confirmed
the exact same 1618-error count with this branch's two files stashed out
against unmodified `upstream/main` — the type-resolution gap is an
environment limitation of this sandbox, not something introduced here.

Was not able to run a live Codex app-server round-trip in this sandbox (no
Codex credentials/harness available here); the evidence above proves the
event-projection behavior through the same test harness and fixtures the
existing `image_generation_call` regression tests in this file use.
