prs.title: fix: reject oversized daily memory-flush payloads
prs.body:
Related: #90354. Focused replacement for #96291, following [Peter's request for a fresh smaller PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96291#issuecomment-6378881568).

## What Problem This Solves

Pre-compaction memory flushes can append an oversized payload to a daily note even though the write is append-only; the reported roughly 1,200-character line reaches the file before downstream validation rejects it.

## User Impact

This **draft candidate** rejects a daily-note `content` payload above **800 JavaScript UTF-16 code units** before provenance recording or file mutation, with a model-facing request for a shorter pointer. Accepted content stays byte-for-byte intact. The existing separator can add a newline outside the payload. The limit applies to each new payload, not the total stored note.

**Maintainer policy decision remains open:** the candidate currently applies 800 unconditionally to canonical `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` targets. Default-on, explicit opt-in, or declining this policy remain @steipete's decision. No opt-in configuration contract has been invented. Runtime validation does not resolve this policy question or establish merge readiness.

## Why This Change Was Made

Five changed files, +242/−4 at `24d26272c852c59a66348a2baff6d64ea48bfc39`; production remains +17/−3. The old 58-file branch is not revived. Target admission, containment, authority, duplicate checks, append operations, provenance, and plugin-owned persistence keep their existing owners. No service guard, QA framework, SDK, configuration contract, validation threshold, or baseline is changed.

The original patch is `3f1dee65`; `9f93ebce` adds a legacy-byte fixture and one QA scenario; `d782f1ec` merges main `1b6eb7bf` to preserve upstream test cleanup. The latest fixture-only correction correlates actual Responses tool IDs by exact arguments and waits for the actual foreground reply after any queue acknowledgement.

## Evidence

Executed on 26 October 2026.

Environment: Ubuntu under WSL2, working systemd user bus, pinned Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0. All checks used normal repository wrappers and guards. Isolated HOME/state/workspace/profile and allocated loopback ports kept these tests separate from operator state. No operator service was stopped, restarted, reconfigured, or disabled.

### Real Gateway automatic memory flush

**PASS at `24d26272c852c59a66348a2baff6d64ea48bfc39`**, using the repository QA runner, a real isolated Gateway child, real automatic pre-compaction flush, real tools, and real filesystem. AIMock supplies fixed model replies; this is not live-provider proof.

| Operation | Observed result | Stored bytes | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Read pre-existing 1,239-unit Unicode/CRLF note | Full legacy content and tail read; original bytes unchanged | 3,039 | `88f42d43822630c7c4877b8ca755a090fc1ce77fc9dc6c175325046a58094b4e` |
| Append exact 800-unit whitespace/CRLF payload | Accepted verbatim, with existing append separator | 3,840 | `ec55b7ae244714582a33fb564e41e61195f51be582ab50506a8325df40b4438f` |
| Attempt 801 units | Deterministic max-800 tool rejection; bytes unchanged | 3,840 | same |
| Attempt 1,200 ASCII characters | Deterministic max-800 tool rejection; bytes unchanged | 3,840 | same |

The scenario compares raw Buffers after each operation, correlates actual tool-result IDs with the AIMock request journal, requires successful flush/session completion, and verifies the foreground model reply. Result: 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. The QA suite recorded 90.804 s; the outer CLI invocation took 685.22 s, including its normal 509.4 s rebuild after the Git head changed.

### Stored-note compatibility across a source-runtime upgrade

**PASS: release `v2026.10.7` / `157d8c2bc3ea2fa183afdc11088e69690bf8e64e` → candidate `24d26272c852c59a66348a2baff6d64ea48bfc39`.** Both source runtimes used the same isolated state, configuration, workspace, daily note, token and loopback port.

1. The stable foreground Gateway returned `health.ok=true`; authenticated HTTP `/tools/invoke` → `memory_get` returned the complete Unicode/CRLF daily note, with no truncation.
2. Only the proof Gateway was stopped. The candidate ran `doctor --fix --non-interactive` (exit 0, including normal UI asset preparation) and `config validate` (passed), retaining the state and note.
3. The candidate foreground Gateway returned `health.ok=true`; the same authenticated `memory_get` returned the identical full text. Raw stored bytes matched the pre-upgrade expected Buffer: **1,239 UTF-16 units / 3,039 bytes**, SHA-256 `88f42d43822630c7c4877b8ca755a090fc1ce77fc9dc6c175325046a58094b4e` before and after. Candidate stage completed at 11:31:01 UTC.

Doctor's exit 0 is not a clean-environment/security audit: it also reported the disposable local token field, absent provider credentials/automation authority, and optional environment capabilities. Those warnings were retained; no provider credentials or broader authority were added.

This demonstrates stored daily-note compatibility across a **source-runtime upgrade** using the supported Doctor lifecycle. It does not exercise the package updater, embedding/search rebuilds, or a live model. The automatic-flush boundary is the separate Gateway scenario above.

### Focused regressions and static checks

- **78 tests passed across six files at `d782f1ec`**, 375.92 s wrapper wall time (378 s outer wall), using the repository-selected test runtime. The final commit changes only the YAML scenario; these six test files and production code are unchanged. Includes host and host-backed sandbox wrapper coverage for boundary acceptance, oversized rejection, missing-file preservation, authority/path restrictions, and legacy raw-byte preservation. This is not a container sandbox test.
- Candidate Gateway preparation and stable runtime build passed with pinned dependencies and normal supply-chain/runtime-publication checks.
- Scoped type-aware lint (0 warnings/errors), production core and agents-root test typechecks, five-file formatting including pinned Bun parity, docs MDX, diff whitespace, line-growth/max-lines/environment/assertion-safety ratchets all passed on the exact final content. Lint initially lacked the `eslint-plugin-solid` development dependency omitted by the Gateway install profile; the supported unfiltered frozen install succeeded and the identical lint retry passed. No lockfile/configuration edits or skipped lifecycle checks.
- Native AutoReview of the final YAML-only correction: exit 0, `scoped-clean`, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The helper used its documented GPT-6 Sol fallback after the default GPT-6.1 Sol was unavailable to the account. The review included unchanged transport/AIMock context and verified frozen inputs; it is a source review, not runtime proof.

The focused regression invocation was:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/agents/agent-tools.memory-flush-append-write.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.memory-flush-writer.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.read.workspace-mutations.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.workspace-outside.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.tools.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

## Evidence provenance and limitations

The earlier systemd-user-bus failure occurred before any Gateway scenario ran. The first new runtime attempts exposed fixture assumptions about normalized Responses tool IDs and queued foreground acknowledgements; they were failures, not runtime passes. After correction, attempt 5 passed on `d782f1ec` plus the uncommitted YAML delta. The result above is a fresh run of the published final commit.

Historical 81-test results at `3f1dee65` remain valid for that original revision only; they are not the current 78-test run. The original base-red check had 6 expected failures / 22 passes. No live-provider, package-updater, embedding/search, native Windows, or full monorepo/CI pass is claimed. The QA YAML is classified as an unknown surface by the broad lane classifier; that all-lanes run was not executed. The observed GitHub check snapshot had 8 successes / 73 skipped, with no failures; skipped checks are not passes. The stable health snapshot reported CPU event-loop degradation while its health RPC and full memory read passed; this is not performance validation.

The implementation remains a per-payload policy proposal. Cumulative logical-flush limits, line-count/line-length policy, existing-file read ceilings, and the old branch's stricter daily symlink policy are outside this PR.

## Reproduction

The fresh-checkout procedures below were source-reviewed and Bash-syntax-checked. The recorded runtime invocations ran against already prepared pinned checkouts; these copyable clone/build blocks were not rerun end-to-end. They use the supported CLI and keep service inspection and authentication intact. A guard failure is a blocked run, never a reason to bypass the guard.

<details>
<summary>Real Gateway boundary — fresh isolated checkout</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduction of the real Gateway/AIMock check. See RUNTIME-EVIDENCE.json for executed results.
# This fresh-checkout procedure was source-reviewed and syntax-checked, not run end-to-end.
# The recorded runtime command ran against the same pinned, already prepared checkout.
# Prerequisites: Linux user bus, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Git, and free build space.
set -euo pipefail
for key in OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT OPENCLAW_LAUNCHD_LABEL OPENCLAW_WINDOWS_TASK_NAME \
  OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER OPENCLAW_SERVICE_KIND OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_SERVICE_PID VITEST; do
  if [[ -n "${!key-}" ]]; then
    printf 'Refusing inherited %s; start an ordinary clean shell.\n' "$key" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done
proof=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/openclaw-184049-qa.XXXXXX")
mkdir -p "$proof/home" "$proof/state"
chmod 700 "$proof" "$proof/home" "$proof/state"
exec env -i PATH="$PATH" USER="$(id -un)" LOGNAME="$(id -un)" SHELL=/bin/bash LANG=C.UTF-8 \
  HOME="$proof/home" PROOF_ROOT="$proof" \
```

```bash
assert.equal(result.ok, true);
assert.equal(result.result.details.status, 'ok');
assert.equal(result.result.details.truncated, undefined);
```

prs.title: feat(subagents): show executor agent in list rows
prs.body:
Closes #186424

## What Problem This Solves

`/subagents list` does not identify the agent executing each child. Labels describe the task, and several agents can use the same model, so operators must inspect children individually to check routing.

## User Impact

Active and recent rows now include `[agent: <id>]`, including children running under the requester's own agent. For example: `research worker [agent: research] (shared-model, 2s) done`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared row formatter reuses the existing child-owner resolver. This covers both slash-command replies and the subagents tool's readable text, including recorded owners for raw session keys. Unresolved owners remain omitted; structured results and authorization are unchanged.

The simplification pass retained one formatter change and one regression using existing fixtures. Production: +2/-1; tests: +34; docs: +3.

## Evidence

- Regression through the real `handleSubagentsCommand` path: unchanged main `a29646098` fails because the three rows omit agent identifiers; the final change identifies same-agent, cross-agent, active/recent, and raw-key children sharing a model. The new case took 369 ms on Linux.
- Linux / Node 24.22.1: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-list.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-subagents.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` selected within the focused run: 30/30 passed. The command file shared a 31.93 s shard with ownership tests; the list suite took 38.32 s including transforms and teardown. CI timing is pending.
- Existing tool consumer `src/agents/tools/subagents-tool.registry.test.ts`: 3/3 passed on Windows.
- Production typecheck (`tsconfig.core.json`), test typecheck (`tsconfig.core.test.messaging.json`), type-aware oxlint for the touched TypeScript, oxfmt, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Fresh independent source review of the complete change against `a29646098`: no actionable findings. Local autoreview/ClawSweeper was not run.
- The command regression uses the real slash handler with the existing synthetic registry fixture. No live chat-channel or model call is claimed. Windows list-suite assertions passed but teardown hit an `EPERM`; the complete Linux list suite, including teardown, passed.


### Partial Gateway evidence (2026-10-30)

On Windows with Node 24.22.1 at head `921358f85cfcc591c2f63099ff20eb02eac3804a`, an isolated Gateway accepted `sessions_spawn` through a deterministic local OpenAI Responses fixture. A real `chat.send` of `/subagents list` returned:

```text
active subagents:
-----
1. ACTIVE_CHILD [agent: main] (shared, 20s) running

recent subagents (last 30m):
-----
(none)
```

This confirms a same-agent active row through the Gateway command path. It is partial evidence only: the cross-agent recent child did not reach the list in this fixture, the overall test failed, and the recorded-owner raw-key case was not exercised. No live model or channel is claimed. The reviewer-requested full real-behavior proof and maintainer presentation decision remain open.

## What Problem This Solves

The macOS onboarding guide describes the manual wizard as the default fresh-launch path and incorrectly says the bundled app installs Node.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Align the detailed onboarding and bundled Gateway guides with the production launch path. Explain **Set up manually**, retain existing permission/security/Git guidance, and identify the existing screenshots as earlier manual-flow illustrations. No runtime behavior changes.

Related: #183245 (its permission-prompt explanations are preserved).

prs.title: fix(ui): match canonical Unicode in place browser folder filter
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The New Session place browser misses real folders when their names and the typed prefix are canonically equivalent Unicode with different NFC/NFD encodings.

## User Impact

Operators typing a precomposed accent (e.g. `Café`) still see macOS-style NFD folder names such as `Café-notes`, and the reverse NFD query finds NFC names, without rewriting stored filenames or paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply lowercase-then-NFC only to local comparison copies in the existing place-browser filter ranking. Exact-spelling order, actual filenames, paths, and hidden-folder behavior are preserved.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway + built Control UI, real Chromium and real folders, inspected before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187988#issuecomment-6512602191).

Main twice and candidate twice: NFC `Café` finds NFD `Café-notes` only after repair; NFD `Résumé` finds NFC `Résumé-notes` only after repair. ASCII `APP` returns `App`/`app-old` unchanged; absent stays unmatched. Existing owner test and formatting check pass. Regression vectors consolidated into the existing ranking table; tests net0, production+3/-2; no SDK exports or global coercion. Maintainer built Gateway/Control UI proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187988#issuecomment-6512630370.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: revert restores prior comparisons with no migration. Blast radius only New Session folder suggestion filtering; path identity and filesystem operations unchanged.

prs.title: fix(gateway): record visible activity on chat setup failures
prs.body:
Related: #160003

## What Problem This Solves

When an accepted chat fails during setup or dispatch before its run starts, the terminal failure can be recorded without advancing session activity. A user who has already marked the session read can therefore miss that failure.

The restart-safe recovery path originally addressed by this PR was removed by #185730. This revision targets the remaining setup and dispatch failure paths in the current architecture. It does not claim that the removed mechanism still exists or that every symptom in #160003 is resolved.

## Change

Carry the existing run and RPC-source visibility into terminal lifecycle persistence. Visible failures advance activity; hidden work remains quiet. Lifecycle ownership and the unread predicate are unchanged.

Thanks @wangmiao0668000666 for the original investigation in #159285.

## Evidence

- On upstream main `4e472c7eda03fe91631ee666ca79e08b40206ae7`, the new isolated SQLite regressions fail for visible setup and unstarted dispatch failures because `lastActivityAt` does not advance. The hidden setup control passes.
- On the candidate, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-dispatch-errors.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 25/25 on Windows with Node 24.22.1 using isolated SQLite state. Targeted lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and the test-line ratchet against that upstream snapshot passed. The separate allocation covers 61 net regression-test lines for both terminal paths and hidden controls.
- Independent source review found no actionable defects. This exercises the lifecycle owner, not a browser-rendering or live Gateway flow.
- The updated head `278ccf6b9159efcdcb8d8c08e187cd82538857a8` has a successful `openclaw/ci-gate` status. Consult its checks for details.

The prior PR evidence and old-head CI concerned the removed recovery path and are not validation of this revision.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Small hosted type-check selections repeat checkout and dependency setup across two jobs even when both graphs fit the existing two-compiler worker.

## User Impact

Eligible hybrid/GitHub CI selections use one setup instead of two while retaining both compiler graphs and failure reporting. There is no runtime product change. Realized job-minute savings have not yet been measured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Maintainer context: @joshavant requested this narrow change as part of an organization-wide Actions usage audit, with coverage preservation taking priority over savings.

Batch only changed selections with exactly two single-graph core rows and no root partitions. Reuse the existing worker and its concurrency of two. Full-check stripes, root ownership, lint checks, deadlines, and failure propagation remain unchanged. Broader batching is intentionally excluded because observed full-stripe and lint durations show timeout risk.

The simplification pass retained the existing planner and worker without new execution machinery. The diff adds 15 production lines and 21 net test lines; tests protect both hosted profiles, central graph ownership, and the complete full-check stripe inventory.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox payload passed: 37 focused tests (`ci-check-plan.test.ts`, `tsgo-core-test-shards.test.ts`), scoped oxlint, scripts/tooling typechecks, workflow checks including zizmor/actionlint, and `git diff --check`. Local oxfmt also passed. [Backing workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40981289301) may show cancelled because the one-shot Testbox cleanup stopped it; the validation payload exited 0.
- Local ClawSweeper committed-range review completed with no actionable correctness or security findings: base `239f5ecf43d9fe1a275719ee439eb5f6c366fafa`, head `e9c7c2445a9324be4d46f1a97f7ef56f5f117764`. It inspected source statically and did not execute tests; historical attribution was limited by the shallow base.
- Independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings in the same change. That pass was limited to the diff and supplied worker contract.
- Current-head [PR CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40984950140), including all five full core-type stripes, selected Node tests, lint/baseline checks, and artifact preparation. The required `openclaw/ci-gate` is green. GitHub reports the PR as `CLEAN` and `MERGEABLE`, with no unresolved review threads.

prs.title: fix(qa): preserve literal evidence and artifact paths
prs.body:
Closes #186908

## What Problem This Solves

QA Lab reports missing evidence or displays a different artifact when a valid filename has meaningful leading or trailing whitespace.

## User Impact

QA operators can open those evidence bundles and read the exact declared artifact through the existing URL, form, preview and download workflows. Existing blank-path, allowed-root and declared-file restrictions remain effective.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate path strings as nonblank while preserving their original spelling across the existing evidence schema, gallery resolver, HTTP selectors and browser submission. Semantic metadata still uses its existing normalization. No schema fields, allowed roots, config/defaults, dependencies or migration steps are added.

The existing large-file hook required coherent extraction of both evidence HTTP routes with their private parsing/content-type helpers and the browser evidence-loading action. Their complete callers move together, errors still use the outer server renderer, and the original HTTP fixture writer moves unchanged into existing test support. This is included in the reported scope below.

## Evidence

### CI attribution and earlier regression-red receipt (2026-10-30)

Product head remains `a4d2f2426c03a08bfec3646bebde4baf9d6fc54f`; this is a body-only evidence update. No source, test, assertion, timeout or runtime proof changed, and no new execution is claimed.

The failed [selected QA shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40732321492/job/122972788271) reports46 passed files/1 failed file and584 passing tests/1 failing test. Its sole failure is the existing scenario-name alignment guard in `extensions/qa-lab/src/test-file-scenario-runner.native.test.ts`: scenario `control-ui-browser-screenshot-body-cancel` requests `keeps the status error visible and cancels the unread media body`, while its target file has only `authenticates screenshot media and presents its HTTP failure`. The aggregate CI gate reports this selected failure.

The actual checkout in that primary job is merge `222c23ed04b6beb413e4e2480c7239f6b3e14113`, whose main parent is `5ff57b8e742f05b9e6e73b2bfe95866f394c15fd` and PR parent is the product head above. Each complete participating source below has the same Git blob in that hosted merge, its main parent, this PR head and this PR's original base `61bfde18d87b76db71070e3a715fd34b3b32f53e`:

| Unchanged source input | Git blob on all four refs |
|---|---|

prs.title: fix(gateway): page-cache warming fails every 15 min on kernels without /proc/self/io
prs.body:
Fixes #177056

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the scheduled database page-cache warm fails on every 15-minute cycle and never warms anything on Linux hosts whose kernel has no procfs IO accounting (stock Microsoft WSL kernels, `# CONFIG_TASKSTATS is not set`), because `readIo()` throws `ENOENT` for `/proc/self/io` before warming begins.

## User Impact

User impact: on affected hosts, recent chat history is warmed again after startup memory pressure instead of silently skipping the optimization, and the gateway no longer emits a recurring `database page-cache warm failed (state)` WARN every 15 minutes that masks real warnings. There is no configuration change and no behavior change on hosts where `/proc/self/io` exists.

## Why This Change Was Made

The warmer treats IO counters as an environment capability instead of a hard requirement:

- **Probe once per pass.** `readIo()` returns `null` on `ENOENT`; other errors still propagate. A pass without counters keeps running instead of aborting in `warm()`.
- **Keep the safeguards.** Byte budget, pacing, cancellation and reader cleanup must not be bypassed when counters are missing. The worker now reports conservative per-step byte estimates (`estimatedReadBytes` + `ioCountersUnavailable`), and the scheduler uses those estimates for both pacing and the pass budget via one `accountedBytes()` helper. State warming charges the exact bytes read per chunk; agent warming charges bounded per-query estimates that deliberately over-estimate the work (metadata step ~512 KiB, payload batch = max(payload bytes, 8 x 64 KiB), projection query ~2 MiB).
- **Real counters unchanged.** When `/proc/self/io` is readable, `readBytes`/`diskBytes` and the pacing math are byte-for-byte the previous behavior; the estimate is only consulted when `ioCountersUnavailable` is true.
- **Observability.** Startup trace and the completion log now include `estimatedReadBytes` and `ioCountersUnavailable`, so operators can tell which accounting mode a pass used.

Tradeoff: on counter-less kernels, warming stops earlier than it would with exact byte accounting because estimates intentionally over-estimate. That direction is the safe one for pacing, and the structural caps (4096 sessions, 32 messages/session, 64 KiB/message) still bound the work.

## Evidence

Environment used (real host, not simulated): Ubuntu 26.04.1 on WSL 3.0.3.0, kernel `6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2`:

```
$ zcat /proc/config.gz | grep TASKSTATS
# CONFIG_TASKSTATS is not set
$ cat /proc/self/io
cat: /proc/self/io: No such file or directory
```

Before this change the same gateway emitted 17 x `database page-cache warm failed (state): Error: SQLite read-only worker ENOENT: ... open '/proc/self/io'` in the first ~3.7 h after a 2026.10.4 -> 2026.10.5 upgrade; the previous day on 2026.10.4 had 0.

Tests from the review checklist (3 files, run on the host above, so the unmocked cases exercise the real missing `/proc/self/io`):

```
$ node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/infra/sqlite-page-cache.worker.test.ts \
    src/infra/sqlite-page-cache-residency.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-runtime-services.maintenance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  10 passed | 1 skipped (11)
```

Added regressions (fail before the fix, pass after):

- `completes an agent warm when /proc/self/io is unavailable, using bounded estimates` - forces `ENOENT` for `/proc/self/io`, asserts the pass completes, reports `ioCountersUnavailable`, and closes every reader.
- `enforces the state byte budget via estimates when /proc/self/io is unavailable` - asserts the byte budget is still enforced and the pass stops `limited` with bounded estimates instead of throwing.

Existing tests keep their counter-path assertions and branch only when the host genuinely lacks counters, so CI continues to verify the real-counter behavior unchanged.

Gate checks:

```
$ node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <3 changed files>
All matched files use the correct format.
$ node_modules/.bin/oxlint <3 changed files>
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
$ git diff --check
(clean)
```

`pnpm build` is running locally; CI will also exercise the full build and type gate.

Compatibility: no config, schema, or persisted-state changes. The only payload additions are two fields on the internal `PageCacheProgress` worker result.

prs.title: fix(mcp): unreachable remote MCP server no longer blocks Doctor-gated Gateway startup
prs.body:
Related: #162228, #144911, #143070

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: standalone Doctor lint rejects an otherwise usable installation when a configured remote HTTP/SSE MCP service is unavailable, including a server that initializes but never answers its tool-catalog request.

## User Impact

Recognized remote connection, authentication and deadline failures become actionable warnings tagged `mcp-service-unavailable`. An error-threshold Doctor gate can proceed while the affected remote tools remain unavailable.

**Scope narrowed in response to review:** local stdio startup failures remain errors, including ambiguous `mcp-remote` proxy failures. Numeric JSON-RPC errors, unknown failures, invalid catalogs, pagination-integrity failures and cleanup failures also remain errors. This is a partial fix, not a resolution of every case in #162228; it no longer asks maintainers to accept broken local children as warnings. No config or stored-data migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing MCP owners now retain a typed availability classification through catalog collection and startup backoff. The pagination owner supplies a typed deadline error; classification uses transport provenance and structured error fields, never server-message text. Doctor preserves the strongest finding when different inspection contexts report the same server, so an earlier warning or deferred-auth notice cannot hide an error.

The repair is reconstructed on newer main at `f91bca9546f5`, reusing the existing catalog-projection owner rather than expanding the oversized runtime module. Current updater probe deferral, OAuth inspection ownership, last-good catalogs and retry behavior are preserved. A local merge check against `1e48ec3a9e3` succeeds; its newer enterprise-MCP capability preparation is not overwritten.

## Evidence

### Actual compiled CLI behavior — October 21

Ten independent ordinary standalone invocations used credential-free synthetic private config/state, real loopback MCP transports and the compiled CLI:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json \
  --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --severity-min warning
# Repeat each scenario with --severity-min error.
```

| Synthetic failure | Finding at warning threshold | Exit: warning threshold | Exit: error threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Refused remote Streamable HTTP connection | warning; `mcp-service-unavailable` | 1 | 0 |
| Initialized remote server delays `tools/list` beyond the real 10-second deadline | warning; `mcp-service-unavailable` | 1 | 0 |
| Remote catalog repeats its pagination cursor | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |
| Missing local executable | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |
| Local stdio child exits during initialization | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |

Every invocation reported `checksRun: 1`. At error threshold, remote-only warnings were filtered out (`findings: []`, exit0). Representative sanitized output projection:

```json
{"scenario":"refused-http","threshold":"warning","code":1,"checksRun":1,"severity":"warning","errorCode":"mcp-service-unavailable"}
{"scenario":"catalog-deadline","threshold":"error","code":0,"checksRun":1,"severity":"below-threshold","errorCode":null}
{"scenario":"closed-stdio","threshold":"error","code":1,"checksRun":1,"severity":"error","errorCode":null}
```

**Build provenance/limit:** this CLI proof ran on [assembled fork commit dda926bb935](https://github.com/Grynn/openclaw/commit/dda926bb93528517d02666179d4478579af6e4a9), which contains this exact repair plus separately reviewed immutable-launcher/runtime fixes and other local units. All 13 files in this PR are byte-identical there to `92b501e7e5af68ad01b829ff005739fe69ed45b1`. Its full `pnpm build` passed with the live-service safeguard enabled. This is real compiled CLI evidence, **not an exact standalone PR-head build, a production deployment or a full installed-release Doctor certification**. No serving credentials, user state or model calls were used. The older blocked CLI attempt remains historical evidence, not a success claim.

### Regression and cost evidence

- Production Doctor detector covers real refused HTTP, typed catalog deadline, remote auth and malformed/integrity controls. Same-server warning/error aggregation has genuine baseline failures and repaired passes. Stdio remains error without requesting a severity-policy exception.
- `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/flows/doctor-core-checks.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **60/60 pass**, measured wall **51.65s**, peak RSS **5,591,232 KiB** (includes compiler/bootstrap work; not a steady-state latency benchmark).
- After final owner extraction: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-start-backoff.test.ts src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-retirement-boundaries.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **32/32 pass**, measured wall **57.73s**, peak RSS **5,532,380 KiB**.
- Focused types, type-aware lint, formatting, scoped line-cap and diff checks pass. Final independent P0–P2 review of the full 13-file repair completed scoped-clean; its former compiled-CLI evidence gap is now addressed with the explicitly scoped proof above. Current-head PR CI remains separate from these local checks.
- Simplification: failure/retirement projection uses the existing catalog owner; the old duplicate retired-catalog literal is removed. Necessary growth is typed failure provenance and strongest-severity aggregation, plus distinct real transport/ordering regressions; no new manager, database schema or runtime policy option.

prs.title: fix(mcp-app): pass trusted toolMeta to session resource tool policy checks (#186775, #186777)
prs.body:
Closes #186775
Closes #186777

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: MCP App tool calls are rejected by session tool policy when invoking permitted plugin tools (such as `bundle-mcp`), and standalone apps filter out allowed plugin tools.

## User Impact

User impact: Model-created and standalone MCP App tool calls can reliably execute permitted plugin tools according to the session's tool capability profile without false policy rejections.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `prepareModelCreatedAppToolCall` (in `src/gateway/mcp-app-operations.ts`) and `prepareMcpAppExtensionRuntime.assertTool` (in `src/gateway/mcp-app-extension-runtime.ts`) invoke `resolveSessionResourceToolPolicy`, but previously passed only the string `toolName` while omitting `toolMeta`.

Consequently, the downstream policy evaluator (`isConversationToolAllowed`) cannot determine the tool's plugin ownership (such as `pluginId: "bundle-mcp"`), causing tools allowed under plugin policy profiles (such as the default `coding` profile) to fail session policy checks with `SESSION_RESOURCE_TOOL_POLICY`.

This change:
1. Retains projected tools in the standalone runtime map and passes `toolMeta: getPluginToolMeta(projectedTool)` to `resolveSessionResourceToolPolicy` in `mcp-app-extension-runtime.ts`.
2. Passes `toolMeta: getPluginToolMeta(projected)` to `resolveSessionResourceToolPolicy` in `mcp-app-operations.ts`.
3. Preserves all existing authorization gates: view allowlists, server/session restrictions, explicit tool denials, requester checks, and execution-time approval revalidations.

## Evidence

- Verified unit test suite `src/gateway/mcp-app-extension-runtime.test.ts`: all 12 tests pass, including new assertions confirming `toolMeta` propagation.
- Code style and TypeScript checks cleanly adhere to repository standards.

### CI maintenance (2026-10-30)

The mock-isolation annotation removes one factory from the unannotated-mock inventory. Regenerated the shrink-only baseline with the repository's `check-test-mock-exports.mts --prune`; it removes exactly that stale entry (6565 -> 6564), with no new allowance.

Before regeneration, the check reproduced the same stale-entry failure as CI. After regeneration: `Mock factory ratchet OK: 6564 grandfathered factories.` `git diff --check` also passes. The local command used the repository-declared TypeScript 7.1.0-dev.20261016.1 from an isolated dependency directory because the shared local install had an older version without `typescript/ast` exports; the checker source was unchanged.

This maintenance changes only the generated baseline. It does not change production behavior. Other checks previously passed on head 3abaa2ed; those are prior-head CI evidence, not a result for the proposed next commit. The new commit still needs its own CI run.

prs.title: fix(cli): report unreadable secrets-store input files as usage errors
prs.body:
﻿Closes #187780

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: \openclaw secrets store set NAME --value-file <missing>\ and \openclaw secrets store import --from <missing>\ fail with a raw \ENOENT\ filesystem error and exit code 1, instead of a clean usage error with exit 2 like every other input error in the \secrets store\ command family.

## User Impact

User impact: passing a missing, unreadable, or non-regular path to \--value-file\ / \--from\ now prints a clear message naming the path and the corrective action (e.g. \Input file could not be read (ENOENT): <path>. Check that the path exists and is readable.\) and exits 2, consistent with the command's other input errors (oversized value file, malformed UTF-8, invalid name). The retained error code keeps missing paths (ENOENT/ENOTDIR) distinguishable from denied access (EACCES). Nothing else changes; the success path is byte-identical.

## Why This Change Was Made

\eadBoundedFile\ in \src/cli/secrets-store-input.ts\ let \ s.open\ / \stat\ failures propagate as raw \
ode:fs\ errors, and \mapStoreError\ in \src/cli/secrets-store-cli.ts\ had no mapping for them, so they fell through to the generic exit-1 branch. The fix introduces a small \SecretStoreInputFileError\ (kept in its own module so the CLI can reference it statically without loading the input helpers' heavier deps at command-parse time) and maps it to exit 2 alongside the existing \Utf8InputError\ handling. The not-a-regular-file refusal also moves from a plain \Error\ (exit 1) to the typed error (exit 2).

## Evidence

Before (current main):

\\\
\$ openclaw secrets store set MISSING_VALUE --kind env --value-file C:\nonexistent\set.txt
ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'C:\nonexistent\set.txt'
exit code: 1

\$ openclaw secrets store import --from C:\nonexistent\import.txt
ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'C:\nonexistent\import.txt'
exit code: 1
\\\

After (this change):

\\\
\$ openclaw secrets store set MISSING_VALUE --kind env --value-file C:\nonexistent\set.txt
Input file could not be read (ENOENT): C:\nonexistent\set.txt. Check that the path exists and is readable.
exit code: 2

\$ openclaw secrets store import --from C:\nonexistent\import.txt
Input file could not be read (ENOENT): C:\nonexistent\import.txt. Check that the path exists and is readable.
exit code: 2

\$ openclaw secrets store set DIR_VALUE --value-file C:\Windows
Input path is not a regular file: C:\Windows
exit code: 2

prs.title: fix(sessions): commit selected invitations with original messages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A crash between transcript persistence and Inbox work can leave a posted mention without its invitation, or let an old replay restore revoked access.

## User Impact

Fresh original messages commit selected invitations and involvement watermarks in the transcript transaction; replay cannot regrant membership.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry a private revalidated invitation plan from pending-input custody. Match the final approved text, defer first-session effects until the row exists, and retain each message's own raw sequence.

Stack step **14/17**, based on [fix/guest-access-09-membership-commit-20261026](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/tree/fix%2Fguest-access-09-membership-commit-20261026). Review and merge in order; each upper PR contains only its own slice against its predecessor.

Previous: [commit membership and involvement together](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184511).

Next: [preserve invitation authority through runtime writes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184513).

Stack order: [complete stack](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184515#stack-order).

## Evidence

Slice head: `21b25180cbe921f64db24e6ca3061de57637878e`, on fixed main `5bf0c41a03f1dba03d625460607ed5b959710458`. The complete 13-file integration matrix passed 46/46 on pinned Bun at `ddc49fd63d3b82e41eb6c74af4ad935a56aebc8f` before this main rebase. Main's canonical fixture repairs are preserved and duplicate prerequisite changes removed. Prefixes are not separately built locally; this prefix's hosted CI and review are recorded below.

Six native transaction regressions cover first/existing sessions, reopen/replay, authorization rollback, first-session batch watermarks and hook-removed tokens. The final SessionManager matrix uses real invitation authority and demotes the sender at native commit, proving rollback of transcript events, membership, watermarks and retained readers.

The [retention finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184512#issuecomment-6414277298) is fixed here: settled owners release the invitation closure; collected owners keep source-owner validation without copying the closure. Unknown-outcome custody is preserved. The four-case GC regression showed 2 failures before the fix and 4 passes afterward, including collected inputs. The callback binder moves to the existing live-owner module to keep the pending-input owner within its line cap.

Public SDK append options still exclude invitation authority. The eight-path forged-options regression passed at `979ff80bf2e59f7ea0a10c2ec4ce6ffbb045f6b4`; single, strict, batch, sequence, lock and SessionManager append/persist callers cannot grant membership through forged options. Type-only authority shapes avoid the prior import cycle.

The [stack evidence ledger](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184515#evidence) records runtime results, prior build/upgrade proof and limits. Integration tests are owned by the final activation PR. Current-head hosted CI and review remain required before landing.

### Current-head qualification

[Required CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40526290072) passed at `21b25180cbe921f64db24e6ca3061de57637878e`. The [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184512#issuecomment-6414277298) covers the same head and reports no actionable findings or required rank-up moves. Merge in the recorded stack order.

## Change size

Production **+343/-54**; tests **+318/-4**; generated **+3/-3**.

Invitation authority follows original-message persistence, including first-session and replay handling. Private input custody remains separate from transcript metadata.

### Test-line allowance

`config/test-lines-baseline.txt`: **6,283,633 → 6,283,946** (**+313**). Covers native invitation transactions, forged public SDK options and released pending-input custody. The ceiling equals this prefix's measured 6,283,946 test lines; no spare allowance is added. This is a bounded baseline exception under the repository testing workflow, not a functional-test waiver. No runtime assertion, SDK budget or required CI check is weakened. Change-size test counts include the baseline metadata edit.

Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

prs.body:
Related: #162164 — this is the separate Profile-management slice for channel identity links.

Current head [`92c7dcea650`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/92c7dcea6505779590502e6c96b71bd6f272f885) removes duplicate Profile tests. The retained Profile, channel-link and authority suites pass locally. Passing [canonical CI at parent `d4940bda`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40975412503) and the [Gateway/browser/storage QA at `d605a139`](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/40713289565) retain their recorded revision limits; neither is relabeled as execution of this new head.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway administrators currently have no Profile UI for explicitly associating a channel sender with a personal OpenClaw Profile.

## User Impact

A connected administrator with the negotiated `operator.admin` scope can view, add, and remove exact channel/account/sender identity links for their currently authenticated personal Profile. The Shared Gateway Owner is not a link target. A link is an administrator-entered association; it does not verify control of the external account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Profile page now exposes the Gateway's existing list/link/unlink methods. It adds no backend method, identity store, or automatic name/email matching. Failed writes preserve entered identifiers, and stale results cannot update a replaced Profile or connection. Linking does not merge people, rewrite transcript attribution, assign session ownership, or change session visibility.

## Work sessions

- Original discussion with @TheAngryPit. Work-session reference retained in the local evidence packet.
- Implementation and verification. Work-session reference retained in the local evidence packet.

## Evidence

The other selected CI checks passed.

[Review 19](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164607#issuecomment-5974524801) reviewed this head at 3/6 overall, 5/6 proof and 4/6 patch quality, with no correctness findings. It requests removing a remaining duplicate co-author preference table, consistent with the existing preference-test consolidation. That author follow-up and the CI failure are being addressed. **This is an incremental bugfix, not completion or merge readiness.** Current real-browser/Gateway persistence, authorization-denial execution and before/after screenshots remain missing: Chromium downloaded, but Linux shared libraries are absent, and supported dependency installation failed at sandbox privilege setup. One independent P0–P3 Codex/OpenAI review of the complete fourteen-path PR diff against that main, with six unchanged public contexts, completed with no findings. prs.title: fix(install): keep --beta on a fresh host instead of silently installing stable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes fresh `install.sh --beta` installations silently selecting stable before Node/npm exists.

Fixes #187982. Regression from #187564; the original review identified the cold-host failure in [r4410996147](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187564#discussion_r4410996147). Thanks @McgAtom for the report and installer-entry reproduction.

## User Impact

Cold and warm hosts preserve the requested beta channel. If beta cannot be resolved once npm is available, the installer visibly warns before falling back to latest. Runtime admission checks the package actually selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The early engine resolver consumed beta intent when its npm lookup could not run. It now preserves the unresolved request during conservative runtime bootstrap, then resolves the target and enforces its engines before package installation. The later duplicate beta selector is removed.

PowerShell already preserves its beta tag, but now refreshes the target engine after provisioning npm as well. No options, dependencies, schemas, or baselines change.

## Evidence

- Native macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2.57, Node 26.12.1, and real npm metadata over a loopback registry. The assembled standalone installer runs `parse_args --install-method npm --beta --no-onboard --no-prompt`, `configure_verbose`, and `main`; the real SQLite capability probe runs. Provisioning exposes the native tools, and package installation deliberately records its spec and exits 86, matching the reporter's probe boundary. This is live installer-entry/selection proof, not a completed public-registry installation or Homebrew qualification.
- On pre-fix source: cold beta, missing-beta warning, and stricter-beta admission regressions fail; warm beta passes. On the fix, all four pass: cold/warm select `openclaw@2026.10.10-beta.5`, absent beta selects `openclaw@latest` with a warning, and an incompatible beta engine prevents reaching package installation. Final focused file: 4.066 s test time, 5.46 s wrapper wall time.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/install-sh-beta.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. All HOME/state/cache/prefix/temporary paths are isolated in a private user temporary directory and cleaned up.
- Ten installer-consumer files: 435 passed, 57 skipped, 2 inherited failures (81.38 s wrapper wall time). The failures are `install-sh.test.ts`'s quoted-prefix Bash PATH remedy and literal-safe zsh PATH remedy. Replaying the generated commands against untouched base `f00dd960e35c` and the fix gives identical Bash exit 2 (unmatched quote) and zsh exit 1 (unmatched quote). This patch does not change PATH-remedy quoting. PowerShell execution is among the unavailable-host skips.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json --incremental`, touched-file oxlint and oxfmt, `/bin/bash -n scripts/install.sh`, `git diff --check`, and Madge pass (0 cycles).
- Both ratchets pass: max-lines 404 grandfathered suppressions; environment names 458/458; test lines 6,281,386 against ceiling 6,328,564. No allocation or baseline edits.
- Codex autoreview of the local candidate against `f00dd960e35c`, through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Subsequent edits only fix test lint syntax and remove an unnecessary test-line allocation.
- PowerShell is unavailable on this host: its existing engine fixture is extended with cold beta admission, but PowerShell execution remains for CI. Full `check:changed`/SQLite inventory is omitted under the campaign's local gate budget; targeted gates above ran instead.

Production LOC: +32/-27 (net +5); regression tests: +141; docs: +2. An initial literal-reference search also selected the unrelated package-acceptance workflow suite; that task-owned run was canceled and is not claimed as passing proof. Its existing 256-planner-group admission test passed in 61.699 s for 257 evaluations; the large frozen planner inventory accounts for its cost. The final consumer selection below loads, assembles, or executes the actual installers.

<details>
<summary>Sibling test command</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  test/scripts/install-ps1.test.ts \
  test/scripts/install-sh-beta.test.ts \
  test/scripts/build-and-run-mac.test.ts \
  test/scripts/standalone-installers.test.ts \
  test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts \
  test/scripts/install-sh.provisioning.test.ts \
  test/scripts/install-git-ref.test.ts \
  test/scripts/install-ps1.release.test.ts \
  test/scripts/install-bun.test.ts \
  src/install-sh-version.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(tooling): avoid unused canonical wrapper reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Retained PR commands resolve the complete canonical wrapper inventory even when the only consumer of that result cannot run.

## User Impact

Experiment withdrawn: acceptance was not met, and this PR will not land. This was an internal maintainer-tooling experiment; no product change is being released.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing revision read behind the existing unbound linked-checkout predicates. Bound PR commands already replace this result with a fresh comparison using the anchor's own inventory before consuming it. This removes unused work without caching or changing Git commands or failure handling.

Production: 3 additions / 3 deletions (net zero). Tests: unchanged. The full source inventory and verification after taking the operation lock remain intact.

## Evidence

- A completed main CI job reported 768.232s for the 74-case workflow-successor file. A focused local phase trace found native commands dominate; source copying plus Git setup took 3.17%, so source-seed reuse was rejected.
- The existing mode-drift refusal case passed on the baseline. A subject-only Git trace found eight complete-inventory revision reads across two bootstrap rounds. Five paired samples now confirm six candidate reads versus eight baseline reads.
- A direct batch-read experiment showed no benefit, so this PR keeps the original Git operation.
- Bash syntax and diff checks, fresh scoped autoreview (no findings), and the normal commit hook pass. All ten comparative refusal cases pass with complete Git SID sets. Median runtime and RSS moved in the wrong direction; acceptance is NOT MET and the experiment is withdrawn. No elapsed or billing improvement is claimed.

### Acceptance rule, recorded before comparative runs

Workload: the committed `test/scripts/pr-workflow-successor.test.ts` case `refuses mode drift before retiring qualification`, through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`, one worker, unchanged native owners and all original assertions. Five baseline/candidate pairs run serially in ABAB order on the same qualified macOS/Node 26.12.1 install. Each sample creates its own real repository, signing key, registered PR checkout and authority records. Source/page/dependency caches are warm or uncontrolled; this is not a cold-start claim.

The primary win is actual subject work: all samples must retain the expected refusal and unchanged binding, gates and HEAD while reducing full-inventory reads from 8 to 6 and canonical-HEAD reads from 4 to 2. Every query still covers all 2,787 components. Trace SID sets must show every Git process completed.

Report subject wall, complete-case timing, runner wall, user/sys CPU, maximum RSS and host load for every sample; report median, nearest-rank p95 and range. Wall/CPU/RSS should hold or improve; a worse result requires explicit maintainer acceptance, and a 20% regression is a stop. Counts are the stable acceptance metric on a shared host; do not extrapolate the focused case to the whole CI suite or billed savings.

### Comparative results

**Acceptance NOT MET — experiment withdrawn.** The operation-count invariant passed, but a runtime/cost improvement was not demonstrated.

All 10 cases passed their original assertions. Every baseline had 8 full-inventory reads / 4 canonical-HEAD reads; every candidate had 6 / 2. Each read retained all 2,787 component queries. Git start/exit SID sets matched in every sample.

prs.title: fix: apply configuration when an unrelated older service is installed
prs.body:
Closes #187937

## What Problem This Solves

Creating an agent in an isolated Gateway can save its configuration and then return `UNAVAILABLE` instead of applying it when an older installed service uses a different database. The mismatch can also interrupt background startup work before a configuration write occurs.

## User Impact

An unrelated global installation no longer changes the isolated Gateway's shared-state worker policy. Agent creation can complete its normal runtime application while cron is active, without a recovery restart. The change preserves restrictions belonging to the selected database, including refusal to replace an actor while its policy-bound work is active.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared-state context producer copied all CLI-observed service facts into every database context. Detached background work can have no such facts, so callers of the same database disagreed about worker policy even though the installed service governed another database. The migration owner already limits the restriction to the installed service's database.

The context producer now qualifies those facts using the admission owner's existing identity lookup. Ordinary reads, writable contexts, and WAL maintenance use their own lifecycle's lookup. Native publication also records the canonical alias it just observed, preserving matching-service protection through symlink and hardlink aliases; retained worker publication still cannot restore an obsolete opening alias. No new cache or repeated filesystem lookup is introduced, and the worker's active-operation and migration guards remain unchanged.

## Evidence

On unchanged source 9559c51, a real Gateway with synthetic older-service facts for another database and actual cron startup returned the saved-but-unapplied error from native `agents.create`. A diagnostic startup run separately confirmed differing service-facts presence with equal schema paths while real pending-delivery recovery held the actor. The reproduction uses the production service-context boundary; it does not simulate the configuration reloader or worker and does not claim to exercise service-manager discovery.

The added regression checks native creation and the immediately visible runtime roster. A real-worker negative case preserves changed-policy refusal through a natively published symlink/hardlink alias. Existing configuration-readiness and policy tests remain part of validation.

Formatting/source lint and all selected type-check groups pass. Five changed test files pass 69 cases; the new Gateway case takes 8.292s and the alias negative 0.355s in the measured single-worker run (57.10s for that five-file batch, including setup/import). The distinct regression adds 150 test lines; production code grows by 24 net lines. Hosted checks are tracked separately below.

The consumer batch completed with 3,415 passing cases, seven failures and 154 conditional skips across 265 selected files. The seven failures and a six-file Doctor teardown cascade reproduce on clean 9559c51 under the same Node/pnpm and four-CPU/two-worker settings; the baseline host has more RAM. They concern service-environment assertions, a plugin-metadata timeout and native-worker/Doctor cleanup, with source non-causation recorded separately. No candidate-only failure appeared. These results are scoped evidence, not a claim that the entire baseline is green.

The two adapted synthetic admission mocks now document their intentional isolation, and the native generator removes exactly their two obsolete grandfathered records. No assertion or runtime behavior is changed by that maintenance.

Independent engineering review is clean on `4cdbe19c51725bdc41af533047d11ee03fa380e3`; the separate automated review also found no actionable issue.

### Live configuration application

A real isolated macOS Gateway passed native configuration application after normal cron startup. The tested composition was `7ca8f0cf2625fb593a4081924ce5074a6190fed7`, tree `2e8274bbad4977aa485d14219b4c11c69530308e`; all four changed production files were byte-verified against this PR head. Existing integration fixes and dependency/build inputs were preserved, and the relevant configuration, identity and worker contracts were qualified before building. This records the actual tested composition rather than relabeling it as the PR checkout.

At 00:33:32–00:33:33 UTC on October 30, the native client read the current configuration hash, changed only an existing owned agent's display name through `config.patch`, and immediately read the new name through `agents.list`. It then read a fresh hash, restored the original name through the same owner, and immediately observed the restoration. Both writes returned applied; the saved and active revisions matched. The socket and Gateway boot stayed the same, with no recovery restart. Agent IDs, protected configuration and the guest's narrow session scopes remained unchanged; health stayed ready.

The bounded receipt is:

```json
{
  "sourceHead": "7ca8f0cf2625fb593a4081924ce5074a6190fed7",
  "bothWritesApplied": true,
  "bothWritesChangedOnlyName": true,
  "savedAndAppliedRevisionMatch": true,
  "rosterIdsUnchanged": true,
  "protectedConfigUnchanged": true,
  "socketStayedConnected": true,
  "postObservationSameBoot": true,
  "gatewayHealthReady": true
}
```

The portable build passed in 299.4 seconds. Its 29,264 file hashes and 1,380 link targets were checked before import; the native consumer prepared its metadata and dependency view without local compilation or manual dependency/stamp edits. This live case proves configuration application. It does not replay the original creation operation; the separate real Gateway regression covers `agents.create`.

### Hosted checks

All three selected PostgreSQL conformance rows passed. Two packed jobs reproduced the three pre-existing service-profile assertions already confirmed on clean `9559c51`: the updater publication fixture at line 163 and the two scheduled-task termination assertions at line 390. Their environment producer and failing inputs are unchanged by this PR. Separate repairs own those failures; no CI failure is being called a pass. [The hosted run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40977900656) completed with those two failed jobs and their aggregate; all other selected jobs passed. The inherited signatures are retained in the [updater job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40977900656/job/123810980433) and [scheduled-task job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40977900656/job/123810980481).

Additional native static checks passed, including the complete architecture and database-schema consistency aggregate. Two dead-code wrappers reported the same older unused test-helper export; the canonical check reproduced it on unchanged `9559c51`. [PR #187948](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187948) already removed that export on main. This PR removes no consumer edge. The historical failure remains recorded, and the landed correction will be qualified in the final delivery result.

prs.body:
Fixes #187974

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor rehearsal-capture tests remove their temporary namespace while a retained native worker broker still owns a socket inside it. Later cases report `resource.sock` ENOENT and closing snapshot-owner errors instead of reaching their continuation and namespace-invalidation assertions. The original Doctor cohort reproduces six failed files and three failed test cases from this teardown cascade.

## User Impact

This repairs automated Doctor validation. The existing tests continue checking capture contents, disposable database exclusions, namespace invalidation, and both cached-writer continuation paths. The change is confined to fixture cleanup and does not change Doctor's production behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The rehearsal environment places `TMPDIR` beneath the fixture root. The fixture now finishes its existing session cleanup, checks that idle state readers and their retained broker have retired, and only then allows the original directory cleanup to run. A failed retirement retains the directory for the owner that still needs it.

The local wrapper extends the fixture's cleanup operation while preserving its existing descendant-work drain, unjoined-work retention, and repeated-call behavior. It uses the same retirement APIs as other Doctor fixtures. The 22-line test allocation covers this cleanup code; no additional test scenario, timeout change, skipped assertion, or production seam is introduced.

## Evidence

On the baseline, the original 21-file cohort produced 6 failed / 15 passed files and 3 failed / 318 passed test cases. A temporary observation at fixture removal connected the first rehearsal-capture case to the exact socket subsequently reported missing. That diagnostic code is absent from this change.

The corrected candidate passed the unchanged cohort: **21 files and all 321 tests**, under the same two-worker conditions. The cohort took 587.09 seconds. Changed-file formatting/lint and all selected TypeScript groups also passed on the exact committed tree. Automated P0–P2 review is clean. Independent engineering review and hosted CI are clean. ClawSweeper reported no findings, with Gold proof/readiness and Platinum patch quality.

prs.title: docs: propose retained protection and native Codex coding lane
prs.body:
Related: #187891

## What Problem This Solves

Users need a normal coding subagent that works in an authorized native Codex home, returns useful findings and tests, and accepts same-thread revisions without leaking protected content through retained artifacts or parent context.

## User Impact

**Design-review draft only: no runtime behavior changes, implementation readiness, activation authority, or maintainer acceptance is claimed.** This proposes a generic retained-protection prerequisite followed by a dependent native Codex lane as two eventual implementation PRs.

The proposal intentionally breaks legacy content-bearing approval wire/SDK formats for ordinary and protected payloads together. Complete replacement human reads and ordinary remote publication, retirement, restore and rollback qualification must land before activation. Protected remote redistribution is unsupported; authorized human reads do not create publication custody. Retained original protected-lineage policy permits authorized reads after live-session deletion; original execution authority does not survive by implication. Existing-parent visibility changes require consent, with an explicit protected coordinator when in-place promotion is unsafe.

## Why This Change Was Made

Early owner feedback can resolve the public protocol, retained-policy, parent UX and migration trade-offs before implementation is presented as ready. The document reuses existing storage/sharing, approval/delivery, startup/restore, plugin/harness, binding and paired-node transport owners; it does not introduce a parallel dispatcher or grant service.

The dated native design and subsequent coding-lane contract select owned direct stdio, superseding the earlier shared-daemon proxy proposal. The later retained-policy contract also supersedes the earlier deny-on-live-session-deletion alternative. This draft preserves those decisions while requesting maintainer assessment; it does not make new upstream acceptance claims.

## Evidence

- One documentation file only: `docs/design/protected-content-native-codex-lane.md`, including dependency order, alternatives, review questions, and a claim/evidence limitations map. No implementation candidate, raw log, credential, private path or advisory transcript is included.
- Focused oxfmt formatting/check passed; repository MDX checker passed for the one document; staged `git diff --check` passed; public-sensitive-string scan returned no matches.
- Independent document/security-claim review found no actionable P0–P2 finding in its scoped pre-final draft. The lead subsequently corrected retained-policy wording against the later acceptance contract and added dated transport provenance. That review is not claimed to cover those later edits or constitute runtime security certification.
- Prior source-pinned fixture/design reports are summarized only as **reported evidence**. Failed checks and unvalidated corrections remain explicit; no compiler-green, whole-lane, two-user, old-helper, or deployed-runtime proof is claimed. Private reports are not presented as accessible artifacts. Full accessible sanitized exact-head proof remains required for the later implementation PRs.
- No full test suite/build/runtime campaign was run for this docs-only draft. No hosted ClawSweeper verdict or CI acceptance is claimed. The PR remains a draft for early design feedback.

Review requested on existing owner seams, the all-payload compatibility break, retained policy after deletion, parent consent/coordinator behavior, and completeness of first-party consumer/restore/rollback acceptance requirements.

prs.title: fix(imessage): preserve literal trailing-space in configured cliPath/dbPath
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A configured iMessage `cliPath` or `dbPath` ending in whitespace was silently rewritten to a *different* path before use. macOS allows trailing spaces in file and directory names, so these are legitimate literal values, and the rewritten spelling is usually another real file: OpenClaw could run the wrong `imsg`, read the wrong `chat.db`, and — through the trimmed remote-host cache key — SSH-stage an attachment to one Mac while executing the RPC on another.

- Problem: the extension applied `.trim()` to configured paths at ~20 call sites, conflating "is this configured?" with "normalize this value".
- Problem, second layer: the plugin-state store trims every entry key, so the recovery cursor for a literal `chat.db ` collapsed onto its trimmed spelling and inherited a high-water measured on a different database — the exact cross-database suppression the cursor identity exists to prevent.
- Solution: blank detection now uses the SDK owner `readNonBlankString`, which returns the original bytes. Path *resolution* keeps `resolveUserPath`'s contract — `OPENCLAW_HOME` first, result absolute — through `resolveIMessageLiteralPath`, without trimming. Cursor keys quote only an identity the store would otherwise trim.
- What changed: every configured-path decision point migrated together — `cli-path.ts`, `client.ts`, `send.ts`, `accounts.ts`, `probe.ts`, `actions.ts`, `chat.ts`, `channel.ts`/`channel.runtime.ts`, `setup-core.ts`, `private-api-status.ts`, `message-tool-api.ts`, `approval-handler.runtime.ts`, `cli-output.ts`, `monitor/recovery-cursor.ts`, `monitor/remote-host.ts`. Home-tilde expansion moved to a dependency-free `user-path.ts` because a bare `node` child imports it.
- What did NOT change: business normalizations that are not path identity — `HOME` lookup, shebang/echo matching, configured `remoteHost` validation — keep trimming.

## Why This Change Was Made

One owner per responsibility: "blank vs. literal" belongs to the SDK string-coercion owner, not a locally invented helper. An earlier revision of this PR added a private `readLiteralPath` that was byte-identical to `readNonBlankString`; it is deleted, so there is no second implementation to drift.

The cursor-key encoding is conditional on purpose: an identity the store can already hold byte for byte keeps its exact key, so no operator's stored cursor moves. Only an identity ending in whitespace — which never had a durable key of its own — gets a quoted one.

Also fixed a regression this PR introduced: `send.ts` stopped capturing `shouldClose` and re-read `opts.client` in `finally`, so a mid-request options mutation could close a borrowed client. The captured flag is restored and covered by the existing custody tests.

Risk / non-goals: the local `dbPath` no longer goes through `resolveUserPath`'s trimming step; `~` expansion, the required-home cwd fallback, and absolute resolution are preserved, all pinned by tests.

## User Impact

Operators who configure a literal trailing-space `cliPath`/`dbPath` get exactly the binary and database they wrote, on the host the wrapper names. Fully-blank values are still treated as unset, so empty or absent config behaves as before. No config migration, no new option, no public SDK export, no lockfile change. A literal database that used to share a cursor row with its trimmed neighbour now keeps its own, so a high-water from the other file can no longer silence it.

## Evidence

Two real `sshd` instances on loopback (`mac-a`, `mac-b`), real `ssh`/`scp` behind wrappers that name one host each, a fake `imsg` that logs the exact bytes of its `argv` and every `--db`, a trimmed neighbour binary that must never run, and an isolated Gateway per tree. The `local` account uses the literal `cliPath`/`dbPath`, the `remote` account a literal wrapper plus a literal remote `dbPath`, the `plain` account ordinary paths.

This head (`8be72d5`), media uploaded through the production staging path:

```console
sshd sessions: mac-b=14  mac-a=0
staged on mac-b: sha256 77db3976… == source 77db3976…
--db seen by the child: [chat.db ]   (trailing space intact)
cursor: literal db -> no since_rowid   ordinary db -> since_rowid 777
```

Same harness on `HEAD^`, the tree the shipped channel is built from (2026.10.8 ships this channel as `@openclaw/imessage`, not bundled):

```console
sshd sessions: mac-a=15  mac-b=0
staged on mac-a: sha256 77db3976…   (the upload hit the wrong Mac)
trimmed neighbour binary executed: yes
cursor: literal db -> since_rowid 888   (the trimmed neighbour's high-water)
```

Upgrade: a state dir created by `openclaw@2026.10.8`, then booted by this head — stored config bytes unchanged (same sha256), the cursor row for an unchanged identity still honoured (`since_rowid 777`), both stored rows still present, and the old trimmed-spelling row no longer reaching the literal database.

Unit suites — green with the fix, and both guards red on the base:

```console
$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-imessage.config.ts
 Test Files  38 passed (38)
      Tests  352 passed (352)

$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts recovery-cursor
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

That cursor case and the cache case are the regression guards. On `HEAD^` the cursor readback fails with `expected 888 to be 777` — the literal database inherited the high-water of its trimmed neighbour — and the cache readback fails with `expected { trimmed: true } to deeply equal { literal: true }` because both spellings shared one entry. Other new cases: a literal-vs-trimmed `it.each` for database lookup plus blank-as-unset, an attested-binary resolve returning the literal path, a spawn assertion that the literal `cliPath` and `--db` reach the child, a remote-host case separating two wrappers by SSH destination, a CLI-output assertion that the literal `--db` bytes reach `imsg`, and a spawn-boundary case for the cwd fallback — the parent leaves `~` in place (`/srv/gateway/~/Library/Messages/chat.db`).

prs.title: fix: bound reloadable chat history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long chat sessions retain an expanding transcript while readers page through history. This proposal bounds the reloadable resident window and releases eligible bodies from connected projections and presentation caches.

## Proposed Behavior

The window targets 400 admitted message entries, 3,145,728 serialized JSON code units, and eight reloadable source segments. Reader ownership, an indivisible source group, and live/pending/error custody have explicit bounded exceptions. One speculative packet is accounted separately. These are resident targets, not a whole-pane RAM guarantee.

Older and newer navigation preserve opaque cursor edges. Latest restores the durable tail. Semantic bookmarks preserve reading locations across pane retirement. Search names its loaded-window scope; export acquires complete history independently. Draft and queued-input custody remain separate.

The current repair batches bounded native packets into one presentation admission, refines an unfit read through the same authoritative cursor, preserves reader/source ownership and cache provenance, and gives a visible capacity outcome when navigation must wait for reader movement. Wire and resident limits remain unchanged.

## Current Status

**Draft; the actual integrated source passes the combined asset gate with 225 Chat gzip bytes of headroom.** Only the unchanged 69-line regression bootstrap is published at `95b680f0844621b20e1788e99427c1f02a5b1b4b`, based on actual landed precursor `803d7619edbb1460ab22589278f2d7ba3841a2d0`. The private signed production series is tip `63bceebd977539fc25d278676948f70e7f94302e` / tree `26e5dda24e0b1ce2d4231d2b99a28c6d478012cf`. All 100 candidate path blobs are unchanged from the prior checkpoint. Canonical regeneration and the normal UI build passed; the generated inventory matches the signed tree exactly. Production remains unpublished.

The preceding [metadata](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187708), [creator](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187783), [workspace-notice](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187830), [sharing/subagent cold-copy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187943), and [inspector cold-copy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187961) refactors have landed. The earlier 274-byte excess on actual `878e682` is historical; the new integration was measured directly against actual `803d7619`, rather than inferred from standalone precursor savings. No cap, baseline allowance, gesture delay, or performance threshold was increased.

## Executed Evidence and Remaining Work

- Focused packet/admission/cache/receipt/reader/provenance regressions passed before this patch-identical rebase. Actual `878e682`→`803d7619` has no overlap with the 100 candidate paths. Fresh actual-`803d7619` canonical capture and normal UI builds passed for both arms under matching Node 26.12.1, six dependency inputs, eight fixed build settings and identical proof harnesses. The strict comparison measured Chat **1,276,444 B** gzip against the unchanged **1,276,669 B** cap (**225 B headroom**; baseline 1,270,335 B). New was 782,140 B and startup 90,621 B; requests remained 20/15/3. Chat CSS grew 13 gzip bytes to 126,037 B; New/startup CSS were unchanged. Both precompressed checks passed, violations/warnings were empty, and exact source/UI/non-UI restoration passed. Zero timing pairs were accepted.
- Actual rendered-Markdown-root collection passed on Node and Bun with a live survivor/document, an unowned GC control, and the unsubscribe negative discriminator. The test fixture's observer tracking was repaired at its lifecycle owner.
- The real oversized-history fallback retains only its bounded canonical sequence, preserving the visible unavailable outcome during native admission. Pending-input omission custody and the existing NFC attachment count/layout case have focused proof.
- Historical unbatched source passed both actual-Gateway 900→1→900 functional modes: resident maxima 369 entries / 1,630,839 JSON code units, controlled maximum 0.5 px geometry drift, and bookmark drift 0.46875 px. These results do not qualify the newer batched source or count as timing evidence.
- **The historical ten-pair unbatched comparison failed:** median hold-free traversal wall time was 1,494.757 ms baseline versus 12,061.065 ms candidate (8.07×); p95 was 1,515.995 versus 12,495.032 ms. Candidate traversal passed functionally; the baseline's only expected post-traversal failure was its unbounded-residency assertion. The failed source performed 24 history RPCs / 25 presentation windows versus two RPCs / three windows. Main-thread CPU was reported separately. No additional pairs were credited after the >20% stop.
- The new batch owner has passed combined asset qualification. A fresh full private-QA build and normal runtime preparation are in progress; both functional modes and matched timing remain unproved before production publication. Asset proof alone is not runtime or timing proof. Old backend images and prior functional timings are not credited to this source.

Acceptance remains at least ten matched pairs, median wall regression at most 5% and p95 no worse; a smaller miss requires ten additional pairs, while a >20% miss stops for investigation. Exact-head CI and review remain outstanding.

No whole-pane memory, Firefox, deployment, or performance improvement claim is made. The separate unavailable-selection/cursor-anchor follow-up remains outside this branch.
