prs.title: fix: metadata read test times out during shutdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The startup metadata regression times out after 120 seconds during writer shutdown, even after its live reads and schema-refusal checks succeed. This leaves the metadata test file failing because the parent never receives the child’s aggregate `close` event.

## User Impact

This repairs the test fixture; production metadata behavior is unchanged. The existing test still verifies committed inventory freshness, config-health reads, off-main-thread SQL, newer-schema refusal, and reading without enough space for a database snapshot. Its deadline and process-exit assertions remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parent-initiated IPC disconnect can omit Node’s IPC close receipt, as documented in [nodejs/node#65646](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/65646). The failing fixture reaches process exit code 0 and fully closes stderr, but the missing IPC receipt prevents `ChildProcess.close`.

The parent now sends a close request. The child disconnects itself and runs its existing database/owner cleanup, following the pattern already used by OpenClaw’s SQLite inspection worker. The parent still joins the actual `close` event and checks exit code 0. No additional shutdown framework, retry, or timeout is introduced. The existing fixture grows by five lines, with a matching isolated test-line allocation.

## Evidence

The original fixture timed out on the clean baseline. Observation-only diagnostic runs on Linux with Node 24.22.1 then reached every original read assertion, released the database owner, closed stderr, and observed exit code 0 before the 120-second timeout. Close accounting identified the omitted IPC receipt; all temporary instrumentation is absent from this change.

The corrected `src/plugins/plugin-metadata-state-worker.test.ts` passes all 15 existing cases in a 22.09-second Vitest run, versus 140.43 seconds for the failing file. Changed-file formatting/lint and all selected type-check groups passed through the native remote recipe. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40981311972) is green, full independent review is clean, and [ClawSweeper’s exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187983#issuecomment-6512236471) is Platinum with no findings. No production deployment is involved.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: searching Microsoft Teams messages misses messages whose body is stored in a different Unicode normalization form than the query. Messages written on mobile clients often carry decomposed text (NFD) while a desktop keyboard types the precomposed form (NFC), so the local substring filter compares different code points and silently drops real matches.

## User Impact

User impact: message search now returns canonically equivalent matches even when the typed query and the stored message text use different Unicode forms. Message text is unchanged in the results.

## Why This Change Was Made

`searchMessagesMSTeams` lowercased the query and the extracted search text but compared raw code points. Both now pass through `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(value).normalize("NFC")`, the same shape used by the channel message searches fixed in #187148. Graph paging, sender matching, limits, and truncation are untouched.

## Evidence

- New case in `extensions/msteams/src/graph-messages.read.test.ts` returns an NFD message body from the mocked Graph response and searches with the NFC query.

prs.title: fix(projects): retry project listing reads that race a change
prs.body:
Related: #186844, follow-up to #187062

## What Problem This Solves

The New Session project picker can show "Session projection changed while preparing the listing. Retry the request." The wording is internal, and the user had to retry by hand for a read that could have retried itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

`projects.list` captures one config publication, then reads the registry, session projection and memory stores across several awaits. Its guards correctly refuse a response when config, the projection, caller identity or a contributing session's disclosure facts change mid-read. The handler then returned that internal error instead of reading again, even though the RPC has no side effects.

All five listing guards now throw one `ProjectListingChangedError`. `projects.list` restarts the whole read from a fresh config, identity and memory-store capture, up to 3 attempts. Each attempt runs every guard from scratch, so data from a stale attempt is never returned. Other errors return right away, unchanged. If all 3 attempts hit a change, the caller gets a plain, retryable `UNAVAILABLE`: "Projects changed while loading. Try again."

The stuck mismatch described in #186844 (a projection keeping an old config object) did not reproduce on current `main`. I ran a scratch test against the real projection and `setRuntimeConfigSnapshot` for identical-value, changed-value, agent-identity and new-agent publications, and in every case `projection.state.cfg === getRuntimeConfig()` after the recents preparation. What remains is the genuine race, which this change absorbs.

## User Impact

A config republication or session change during the project list read no longer appears in the picker. Users only see an error if the read loses the race 3 times in a row, and that message is plain language.

## Evidence

- Existing race tests now check that the read restarts and returns current data: a recents visibility change, an observed-session visibility change and replacement, and an incognito memory-store visibility change. Each runs the discovery or registry read a second time and returns the fresh listing.
- The test where config keeps changing on every read checks the new retryable message.
- `pnpm test` with `--maxWorkers=1`: `projects.test.ts` 30/30 in 22.7s, `projects-incognito.test.ts` 8/8 in 12.7s, `projects-recents.test.ts` 3/3 in 12.0s, `projects-recents.perf.test.ts` 1/1 in 10.4s. No new test files; CI cost is unchanged apart from one extra in-process read in four existing cases.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes. The dead-export scan was skipped because it already fails on `main` and lists none of these files.

Not covered: the profile checks in `src/state/user-profile-reads.ts` still throw plain errors and are not retried; that belongs at the state owner as a separate follow-up.

prs.title: fix(infer): sanitize terminal controls in human output
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared inference human-output formatters can emit terminal controls from legal input or provider/result values. For example, `infer embedding create` sends text containing screen-clear/cursor/title sequences unchanged to its configured provider, then prints those sequences as raw terminal bytes.

## User Impact

Shared human envelopes and provider summaries use the existing terminal text policy. Metadata, errors, paths and scalar displays stay on owned lines; output text retains real newlines and Unicode, and tabs display as literal `\t`. Structured `--json` output and provider input preserve their original values.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply existing `terminalText`/`sanitizeTerminalText` at the complete shared display owner. Reuse the existing transcripts per-LF pattern for multiline text. Human serialized values also need this boundary because JSON.stringify leaves C1/bidi controls. Seven inference families share the owner; no per-field renderer, new escape algorithm, public option or caller policy is added.

## Evidence

- Scenario: Shared human envelope and provider-summary displays remove terminal controls while preserving owned line layout and ordinary Unicode; Multiline output keeps LF, tabs display literally, and provider input plus structured JSON retain their original values.
- Entry: node openclaw.mjs infer embedding create --agent main --model openai/text-embedding-3-small --text <fixture-value> [--json]; disputed owner ran unmocked: src/cli/capability-cli/output.ts formatEnvelopeForText and providerSummaryText human projections; emitJsonOrText runs the existing shared owner unmocked from the shipped OpenAI-compatible embedding route.
- Same command on base `5598c3d` and head `3ce6ab4`: `python3 infer-terminal-output-proof.py --checkout "$CHECKOUT" --output "$OUTPUT" --expect "$PHASE"`
  - Before (base): RED legal embedding input reaches actual nativeHTTP unchanged and text stdout contains3 raw ESC bytes; ordinary LF/tab/Unicode and exact JSON controls work. All3 commands exit0 with1POST each.

prs.title: fix(slack): visible spawn completion opens a thread under a top-level request
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/187964

## What Problem This Solves

A visible `sessions_spawn` started from a top-level Slack request captures that message's reply anchor as a thread root. With default `replyToMode: "off"`, its delayed completion then appears in a new thread instead of next to the acknowledgement in the conversation timeline.

## User Impact

Top-level requests keep their visible work-session completions top-level. Requests inside genuine Slack threads keep those threads. No configuration change is needed.

## Fix

Share the existing #187065 `sessions_send` requester-delivery rule at the requester-origin owner and apply it when visible spawn captures its completion origin. Only an off-mode Slack synthetic anchor equal to the current message ID is discarded; current-destination precedence and genuine threads are retained. The added `replyToMode` member is an internal host construction option, not a model-facing or public configuration field.

The existing delayed-send behavior is preserved. `cron`, `ask_user` and `session_status` delivery context is outside this change. The Slack threads documentation names both affected completion paths.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway, real Slack SDKs and actual delayed completion POSTs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187965#issuecomment-6512075230):
- Main `aacb5e162cf1d5414c5a716bfefc2502ed75ce56`, twice: a top-level visible spawn's final `chat.postMessage` carries the request's own ts as `thread_ts`.
- Candidate, twice: the final POST omits `thread_ts` and retains the original channel.
- Genuine-thread control retains its real root on both refs.
- #187065 delayed `sessions_send` control stays top-level and retains the original recipient after a later inbound DM on both refs.
- Actual HMAC-signed Slack HTTP ingress, normal bundled plugin, real Bolt5.1.0/Web API8.2.0 clients, real tool discovery/dispatch, visible child creation, registry, runtime completion event and delivery. Local Slack-compatible API and deterministic provider; no private route/registry callbacks mocked or seeded.
- The actual child task response is held until after the parent acknowledgement and another conversation's acknowledgement, then released. Eight fresh-profile Gateways all gracefully exited0. Config/state/SQLite paths were printed from each exact CLI first. Secretless Node24.22.1 Docker; no real Slack workspace/UI or real model claim.
- Focused tests: **106 passed** across spawn, visible-spawn and sessions-send admission. The retained consolidated origin regression fails on main with the leaked synthetic thread; sender restriction still passes.

Final head `e6fbbf95f0661f126fa8d792e78397c7c4a5603d` is test-only after the proven contributor build, with identical production. Contributor commits retained. Production **+26/-9**, tests **+17/-22 (net−5)**, docs **+1/-1**. The regression is folded into existing policy/receipt coverage while preserving admitted requester, sender and completion-owner policy assertions; redundant exact default creation fields are covered by the broader spawn tests.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: no schema or configuration migration. Reverting restores old route capture for new visible spawns; admitted origins remain ordinary existing metadata. Blast radius is Slack visible-spawn completion placement and the shared requester-thread rule; genuine-thread and delayed-send controls cover the adjacent paths.

prs.title: fix(sessions): keep reply run admission deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: reply delivery can stall or be aborted when the system clock changes while a reply run is waiting for the previous run to release the session — for example after an NTP correction or a laptop resume.

## User Impact

User impact: waiting replies now observe their intended admission budget regardless of wall-clock adjustments; a clock jump no longer extends the wait nor makes a healthy fence look timed out.

## Why This Change Was Made

`waitForReplyRunAdmissionBarrier` in `src/sessions/session-controller.wait.ts` (the followup and successor admission fence behind reply delivery) took its deadline from `Date.now()` and recomputed the remaining budget with `Date.now()` on every loop iteration, while `raceWithTimeout` consumed that budget with a relative `setTimeout`. Mixing an absolute wall-clock deadline with a monotonic timer means a clock rollback inflates the remaining window and a forward jump collapses or negates it.

The change takes the deadline from the shared `src/shared/monotonic-time.ts` owner introduced by #186484 (`monotonicDeadlineAfter` / `remainingMonotonicMs`) instead of open-coding clock arithmetic, so the deadline and the timer consuming it stay in one clock domain. No new parser, policy branch, or per-site arithmetic.

## Evidence

Regression test folded into `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.successor-barrier.test.ts`, next to the existing settlement wall-clock case: a pending successor fence, a second fence taking over so the loop re-reads its budget, then `vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() ± 60_000)` mid-wait. The 30 s budget must stay unchanged.

- Base (fix reverted): both directions fail — `+60 s` returns a premature `{ settled: false }`; `-60 s` never settles at 30 s.
- With the fix: 9/9 pass in the suite.

Real behavior proof, `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs` calling `waitForReplyRunSuccessorAdmission` through a real session controller with real `setTimeout` and `performance.now`; only `Date.now()` is offset to emulate an OS clock step. Budget 2 000 ms, observation window 3 000 ms:

| wall-clock step | base | fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| +60 s | settles at **504 ms** (budget collapsed) | 2 000 ms |
| -60 s | **still waiting** after 3 000 ms (budget inflated to ~61.5 s) | 2 001 ms |
| none (control) | 2 002 ms | 2 001 ms |

`oxfmt` clean and `oxlint` reports 0 warnings / 0 errors on both files.

Gap: `tsgo:core` cannot run in this worktree because dependencies are symlinked from the parent checkout and the compiler rejects declaration inputs outside the checkout (`scripts/lib/local-check-runtime.mts:166`). Both call sites stay `number -> number`; CI typecheck covers them.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes hourly condition watches silently waiting until the next hour when all three condition-evaluation slots are busy.

## User Impact

A capacity-rejected timed condition remains pending for the scheduler to retry, without counting an unevaluated check or overwriting saved condition state. This does not guarantee bounded waiting under continuous saturation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classify the rejected check using the existing unstarted, deferred-admission path. Keep the concurrency cap and cancellation handling unchanged, and retain support for recovering historical busy results.

- A four-watch regression fails on the base revision: the fourth watch advances by an hour without evaluating. With the fix it remains due and evaluates after slots are released through the scheduler actor wake path.
- 43 focused tests pass: condition evaluation, repeated rejection and restart persistence, stream workers, failure alerts, and startup recovery. The 21-test condition file took 59.90 seconds including compilation (about 8 seconds executing tests).
- Cron test type checking, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace, and the staged test-line ratchet pass. The 97-line allocation covers the real-capacity scheduler regression and durable restart regression.
- Independent source review completed; its scheduler-clock test concern was corrected and re-reviewed.

Proof boundaries: headless execution and wake transport are injected; native timer latency and automatic startup retry are not asserted. No live operator Gateway or paid model/API was used. Broader integration checks and CI runtime remain for PR CI.

prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Fixes #187947. A condition check rejected by the evaluator's three-check capacity limit never inspected its source. Treating that rejection as a successful quiet evaluation advanced its hourly schedule and silently consumed the occurrence.

## Change

Route that unstarted capacity rejection through the existing skipped/admission-deferred contract (`executionStarted: false`, reason `busy`, no `triggerEval`). The existing timed-slot owner retains the due occurrence and clears its running reservation so normal scheduler admission can try it after capacity frees. Actual `fire: false` results keep their existing quiet-evaluation counters and cadence.

No new retry interval, backoff, resource budget, configuration, schema, or public API. The contributor's original commit remains in history; its separate busy retry policy is replaced by the existing owner. Regression coverage is consolidated into the existing cadence table, with no net test-line growth. The scheduler reference explains that unevaluated busy checks remain due.

## Evidence

Built Gateway scheduler proof uses four aligned hourly condition watches, real read-only `exec` source reads through a local HTTP fixture, and a native command payload recording its actual effect. No private helper replay, fake busy return, provider key, or forced manual payload run. Main loses the fourth occurrence twice; the candidate preserves it and executes its condition and payload once capacity becomes free, twice. Not-busy and held-until-execution-deadline controls use the same shipped path.

[Built Gateway reproduction and controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187959#issuecomment-6511857405) cover pinned main and candidate, repeated eventual execution, counters, and persisted history.

## Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the prior result classification; there is no migration or new persisted shape. The blast radius is condition-triggered cron work rejected before evaluation starts. Existing abort, stale-owner, evaluated-quiet, and payload settlement paths are unchanged. Whole PR delta: production +5, tests 0, docs +3.

prs.title: fix: avoid copying managed plugin binaries during Gateway startup
prs.body:
Related: #187579

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup copies large managed plugin binaries even when the existing
native admission path can safely reuse them.

## User Impact

Gateway startup avoids redundant writes for managed plugin binaries.
This especially benefits devices with slow storage, such as a Raspberry Pi
running from an SD card.

On our Raspberry Pi500 deployment, the first usable startup was 150 seconds
with the fix, compared with 323 seconds in the earlier baseline. Both times
are measured from Gateway process start. These are separate deployment
observations; they do not establish that this patch alone caused the entire
173-second difference. The helper-only comparison below isolates its measured
effect.

## Why This Change Was Made

Early startup prepares plugin metadata in a read-only admission view. Later,
auto-enable runs in a writable view without the same managed-install facts,
so setup capture falls back to copying binaries.

Run auto-enable inside the existing `withPluginMetadataSnapshotScope` when
a metadata snapshot is available. This prepares the verified install facts
in the current view and uses the snapshot's plugin cache. Existing source
validation, metadata isolation, and cleanup rules still apply. Unmanaged
files still copy.

## Evidence

### Docker comparison and conflicting NO-REPRO

A separate secretless Node 24.22.1 Linux arm64 Docker comparison used real
CLI-managed, trusted-official acpx 2026.10.9 installs. Main was pinned to
`c77b791cf4fca27afe64a6da4ee9ba22f5133a28`; the local candidate applies this PR
to that base, with an identical production helper. Published-stable boots and
conditioning ran separately before the scored pairs; settings and normal
caches were retained.

| Pair | Main native binary copy bytes | Candidate native binary copy bytes | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A1 / B1 | 672,303,640 | 10,519,048 | 98.435% |
| A2 / B2 | 672,303,640 | 10,519,048 | 98.435% |

Early auto-enable accounts for 667,044,116 baseline bytes. Independent inode
and hash readback verifies installed-binary reuse on the candidate. Both
revisions admit exactly `acpx` and pass authenticated read-only health/status.
Direct stable-to-candidate startup retains settings. The ordinary ABAB series
has no repeatable startup/health regression over 20%. Logical copies and Linux
process I/O are reported separately; these Mac-hosted runs do not establish
Pi500 timing.

A follow-up `strace -D -f` run of the same retained baseline, without our
JavaScript observer, confirms exactly **672,303,640 native binary copy bytes
across 114 destination files**. The trace records 148 successful
`copy_file_range` calls: 667,044,116 bytes on the main thread and 5,259,524 bytes
on the preparation worker. Readiness and authenticated health/status pass;
settings and package inputs remain unchanged. Main-process `write_bytes` is
849,637,376, consistent with the earlier ordinary baseline. That process
accounting figure is separate from logical copies. Tracer timings are not
used as a performance comparison.

The maintainer reports zero native payload transfers on main `1dca2e5` using
all-process syscall tracing, including a run without a JavaScript observer.
Our independent syscall reproduction confirms the copies on our workload;
the difference between the workloads remains unresolved. Our configuration
sets `acp.enabled: true` and `acp.backend: "acpx"`. The next comparison needs
the maintainer's exact redacted configuration, launch environment, and setup
sequence.

[Docker ABAB and syscall evidence, harness, and verification](https://gist.github.com/jasonftl/9f793388500d4d61d84fa52dbaac30ca/6d72f296a8920f9243914cfc437be519a7b1582a).

### Earlier Pi500 captures

Real Pi500 Gateway captures now cover a fresh installation of this PR build
and an upgrade/restart from stable 2026.10.9 with existing settings retained.
Both reach readiness and stop normally. The config SHA-256 is identical before
the stable start, after the upgrade, and after the restart. The state database
migrates from schema 20 to 36.

During early auto-enable, real native-file references resolve to the managed
source inodes. Full stacks include `loadGatewayStartupConfigSnapshot`,
`withPluginMetadataSnapshotScope`, `applyAutoEnable`, and `applyPluginAutoEnable`.

| PR build capture | Unique native files of at least 1 MiB reused | Bytes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh installation, first Gateway start | 12 | 653,027,648 |
| Restart after upgrading from stable | 12 | 654,535,112 |

prs.title: fix(git): refresh cached diffs across clock changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After opening a folder and initializing Git, Review can keep showing “not a Git checkout” beyond its one-second reuse period if the wall clock moves backward. The private Git read cache also uses wall time for unversioned expiry and completed-poll reuse.

## User Impact

Cached Git results expire after the existing elapsed retention periods despite wall-clock corrections. There are no configuration, public API, schema or migration changes. Public timestamps and Git mtime/revision validation remain epoch-based and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

All ten private deadline reads/writes now use the existing core `monotonicNow()` helper from `src/shared/monotonic-time.ts`. Cache identity, revision validation, request sharing, capacity, cancellation and retention lengths are unchanged. The existing native performance clock remains the owner of duration diagnostics.

Tests advance the elapsed clock alongside Date where expiry is intended, and independently step Date in the six wall-clock regressions. The regressions extend the existing revisioned-diff, cold-poll and pending-facts cases rather than adding duplicate setup. Shared held-read setup is reused, and the obsolete test-growth allocation is removed. Whole-PR delta against the merge base: **production +1 line, tests -3 lines**.

Original contribution by @Alix-007; both contributor commits are preserved, with the canonical-clock integration, test consolidation and fresh shipped-path proof added on top.

## Evidence

Candidate **`034a330dc8cf3e4ae02670219d24de0a352c6b4b`** was freshly installed, built and executed in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker after integrating the current base to correct an inflated GitHub comparison. Build-info version 2026.10.9 records that exact SHA. Pinned main source **`bbde2b822c133f615d83a9f1db109960c4d68f9e`** was built separately.

The public GatewayClient created sessions without an initial agent turn and called `sessions.diff({ scope: "uncommitted", poll: true })`. Two iterations per revision used fresh folders, a real cached `not_git` result, native Git initialization/commit plus one tracked edit, and a real wait of at least 1.25 seconds. Only the Gateway process's `Date.now()` was stepped backward one hour during the disputed read; native timers/performance and the system clock were untouched.

| Observed result, repeated twice | Main | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No wall-clock step after real expiry | `tracked.txt`, +1 line | `tracked.txt`, +1 line |
| Backward step during public diff RPC | stale `not_git`, 0 files | `tracked.txt`, +1 line |
| Clock restored, same session | `tracked.txt`, +1 line | `tracked.txt`, +1 line |

Successful RPC patches matched independent native Git output. Native HEAD/content hashes and Gateway config bytes were unchanged by the reads. Both Gateways stopped and process-local offsets were restored.

Focused checks executed at `50453a01b37b`, reused for the unchanged Git cache owner and five test files after base integration:

- Owner suite: **31/31 pass**; all six wall-clock rows fail against the pinned main owner.
- PR branch facts: **10/10 pass**; PR discovery/fallback: **26/26 pass**; projects: **30/30 pass**.
- Native session revisions: **14 pass / 7 fail**, including a pass for the edited missing-checkout-expiry case. The seven unrelated native revision/cache assertions also fail on pinned main with the same diagnostics. They are disclosed and classified in the linked capture, not suppressed or claimed green.
- Changed-file formatting and lint pass with zero warnings/errors. Broad types and suites are left to hosted CI.

Current-head readback and clock windows: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187717#issuecomment-6504229951. Original paired main/candidate capture, focused commands and all seven paired local failure cases: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187717#issuecomment-6503915654.

This proof does not adjust the OS clock, start an agent/model turn, or claim runtime coverage of every Git operation or native platform.

## Merge Danger

**Two-way door:** reverting restores the previous in-memory clock choice; no persisted state or public contract needs rollback. The blast radius is Git-backed Review/project/PR reads: a wrong clock could retain stale results or expire shared work too early. The paired public diff proof and forward/backward expiry, retry, poll, revision and cancellation tests protect those boundaries.

## What Problem This Solves

The automatic-build publication test for `openclaw --profile stale-profile doctor` expects runtime inspection to inherit the caller's profile. After #187901, installed services correctly get their state selectors from the installed command environment, so this fixture fails despite the serving-installation refusal working.

## User Impact

This is a test-only correction with no runtime behavior change. The existing case continues to protect a serving installation from automatic source builds and to retain the original profiled stop/retry guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mocked installed command supplied only executable arguments. It now declares a distinct `serving-profile`, and the runtime inspection assertion checks that installed value while the error-message assertion still checks the caller's `stale-profile`. This keeps the installed-service and caller contexts distinguishable without changing service isolation or removing any refusal, no-build, or unchanged-file assertion.

The change adds five fixture lines and a matching test-line allocation. It adds no test case, helper, or production code; the existing environment-merge tests retain coverage for services with no declared selectors.

prs.title: improve: grow desktop chat drafts up to twelve lines
prs.body:
Related: #113270

Height-only alternative to #178226, requested by @vyctorbrzezowski. Preserves @Marvinthebored’s original PR and implementation.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/777be12a-2167-48f8-a690-54b5e1952dc9)
- [Earlier #178226 review discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/77b8168b-a504-4ef4-9c63-7f54908761ef)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e8871224-4350-44ae-ac34-c8fed9af27ad)

## What Problem This Solves

Long Chat drafts start scrolling after six lines even when there is room to show more, while unconstrained pane-based growth can obscure too much of the conversation. A restored long draft also changes height after its first paint.

## User Impact

Desktop Chat grows automatically to **12 lines**, mobile Chat stays at **6**, and shorter panes can constrain the editor further. New Session grows to 12 desktop lines while retaining its existing 10-line floor and mobile behavior. Longer drafts scroll internally; deleting text shrinks the editor again. Embedded composers keep their existing limits.

## Why This Change Was Made

CSS owns the line cap from the first paint. The existing textarea overflow observer now measures the pane-owned editor limit on its first connected pass, accounting for controls, context and short panes, and attaches only in Chat footers or New Session scroll panes; no separate layout module, class or frame queue is added. The redundant JavaScript 80% limits are removed. New Session’s twelve-line allowance keeps its existing ten-line floor.

Accepted edge cases, kept out to fit the boot budget: a keyboard that overlays without resizing the layout (iPad-sized New Session) can cover up to two extra lines, and a caret already scrolled below a shrinking cap is not pulled back into view. Pane resize observers cover window and resizing keyboards.

There are no resize handles, width changes, new preferences, or changes to the existing compact mobile composition model. Width dragging remains in #178226.

## Evidence

- **86 browser/unit tests** pass across composer height, overflow, New Session lifecycle and mounted Chat pane behavior; **24 full-page E2E tests** pass on current main merged with this head.
- Cap, saved-draft reload and mounted embedded-composer regressions fail before their fixes and pass afterward. Reload samples 30 frames from document start.
- A separate populated-chat stress run passes at **1280, 1440, 1920 and 390px**: incremental growth, 5–200-line pastes, typing at the cap and clearing. Frame samples found no height reversals; the transcript stayed at the bottom.
- Production and affected test type checks, lint including pinned-Bun parity, CSS lint, controller guard and line-cap ratchet pass. **Performance:** against main `20121545966a5212dc3783a0375333fb6cd29eeb`, `ui:check-performance:base` passes with Chat boot JS gzip **+309 B** (1,276,344 / 1,276,669 B) and total CSS gzip **+78 B** (308,515 / 308,526 B). No budget was raised.
- Independent **autoreview (Codex, P0–P2)** of the budget simplification commit is clean; earlier full-candidate P0–P2 passes were also clean after the embedded-sizing and New Session padding findings were fixed.
- Prior-head CI E2E failures had matching signatures on ancestral main. Fresh CI assesses the final head.

### Same draft and conversation, 1440 × 900

Before is current main (`2e4ae4432bd48fba9157b521a313a29341282a05`); after is this height-only change. Both use the same synthetic conversation and twelve-line draft. The images below are identically cropped from full-page captures and retain the latest reply above the composer.

![Before: current main shows six lines of the same draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/738d3c54-d7d8-4474-97aa-d40e2faf1e31)

![After: the height-only PR shows all twelve lines](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64450a7b-a693-424e-8fe7-0256a1dea400)

prs.title: fix: keep warnings out of terminal failure notices
prs.body: Closes #187862 ## What Problem This Solves A terminal run error can reach the session recorder with its actionable cause intact, yet leave only warnings in the stored diagnostic. The recorder kept the first 512 characters, and its diagnostic preparation also used a display formatter that can replace errors with friendly copy or retain only a 600-character prefix. Those losses prevent technical consumers from seeing the original cause. Normal notices had the opposite problem: generic failures could expose raw warning or provider diagnostic text. ## User Impact Normal chat history now uses existing classified guidance or a concise neutral notice. The private diagnostic retains redacted opening and terminal context within its existing 512-character budget. Storage, uncertain-completion and established missing-answer guidance are preserved, and unknown failures make no claim about recovery or retry safety. This changes presentation and diagnostic selection, not execution or retries. It preserves the session row's existing 160-character presentation policy, hides private diagnostics from normal history, and excludes terminal notices from model context. Errors already missing a cause cannot recover it through this change. ## Why This Change Was Made Technical diagnostics now use canonical error coercion, internal-text stripping and secret redaction before the existing UTF-16-safe head-and-tail truncation. This preserves actual `Error.message` values and avoids the display formatter's earlier information loss. The normal notice separately uses the existing failure-copy owner. A narrow internal rendering argument lets this caller omit generic raw provider-format excerpts while preserving specialized guidance and existing callers' detailed defaults. Regression coverage exercises lifecycle persistence, real database workers, WebSocket history and display projection. The existing lifecycle setup moves into a test-support file to keep the test file within the enforced line limit; all cases retain their original registered database-worker runtime. The allocation accounts for the resulting 102 net test lines, including support code; no coverage is removed. No schema, configuration or migration is required. ## Evidence On unchanged production, the lifecycle reproduction had four failing regression assertions and 32 passing controls. Its stderr is 482 characters and its wrapped message is 535, so the incoming cause survives the upstream preview and is lost at this recorder. A separate real WebSocket dispatch path reproduced two failures when an `Error` carried a longer warning prefix. A generic HTTP 400 lifecycle case also reproduced raw provider detail in the projected notice while its private cause survived. Changed-file formatting and lint, refreshed type discovery, and the affected compiler checks passed. The candidate has 277 qualified passing cases across 20 files: the latest recorder correction passed 79 cases in seven files, and 198 cases across 13 unchanged copy-renderer consumers retain their earlier passes. The earlier full set of seven selected type groups is supplemented by recompilation of the production and test graphs affected by the final import and fixture extraction. The missing-answer regression also failed through terminal resolution and SQLite persistence before the correction. The existing owner’s exact matcher now preserves both established notices, including the side-effect warning; the same real lifecycle case and both recorder variants pass. Automated source review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Independent engineering review is complete with no actionable findings. An additional 29 history-visibility cases passed, and the requested four-file classifier/context check passed 51 cases on the published head. Hosted checks pass. Both synthetic-history browser cases pass, including one notice after reload. The live isolated Gateway scenario also passed: an actual guest request encountered an intentionally failing sandbox setup command, reached the production recorder, and remained visible after a native browser reload. Before the fix, the notice included the harmless setup marker (61 characters); afterward it contained only the 35-character neutral copy. The canonical receipt retained the 25-character private diagnostic, display and model-context-exclusion flags remained set, and guest history contained exactly one notice without private error details. The private-field exclusion already worked before this change and is preserved. The live consumer was c2de59dce82bc79bac10771a968446e7e152e657, containing the complete patch plus separately qualified runtime changes; all 12 changed PR paths matched eeea442f50fc6024e4ba5ddac29ca450f16c8bb2 byte-for-byte. This short-input case proves the real request-to-recorder-to-reload lifecycle. Long-prefix preservation is covered separately by the production-path red/green regressions above. Neither establishes the historical cause of a live provider startup failure. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Before: terminal notice exposes the harmless sandbox setup failure marker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23309644-9d42-4da0-a15b-bcc020b2a7be) | ![After reload: one concise terminal failure notice without the setup marker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/53539ebf-a2af-460f-af50-a4cf94a5a19f) | ### Real guest request, terminal failure and cued reload https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a567b24-7fae-40a7-8456-592c02b26257 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 193be43cb0541a2d0941a3b6b28f183f90691df0 \(preserved live failure capture\) - Exact head: `c2de59dce82bc79bac10771a968446e7e152e657` - Scenario: Submit an owned guest request through the isolated Gateway while its sandbox setup command intentionally fails, inspect the recorded notice, and reload the conversation\. - Runtime/build: Served build 2026\.10\.9\-c2de59dce82b\-2026\-10\-29T23\-49\-33\.532Z; all 12 PR paths match eeea442f50fc6024e4ba5ddac29ca450f16c8bb2 byte\-for\-byte\. - Visible notice: 61 characters including setup marker before; 35\-character neutral copy after - Canonical run\-failure receipt: Exactly one; private 25\-character diagnostic retained - Guest history after reload: One neutral notice; private diagnostic absent, preserving existing exclusion - Capture conditions: 1280 × 720 browser; matching 970 × 662 crop; dark theme; same owned fixture and setup fault; fresh sessions have different titles - Real Gateway request reached the production failure recorder, persisted one display\-only notice, and remained visible after native reload\. - The combined live source contains the complete PR patch plus separately qualified runtime work; it is not the PR head\. - Private diagnostic retention and model\-context exclusion were verified from selected canonical receipt fields\. - This short setup failure proves the live lifecycle; long\-prefix retention has separate production\-path red/green coverage\. - The 9\.60\-second recording preserves capture timing at 25 fps\. Submission and reload cues use the recorded action times\. - Only the first two frames have an opaque privacy mask over model controls; the failure notice and actual transitions remain visible\. ## Complementary synthetic-history comparison This comparison uses actual baseline and fixed recorder payloads with the same UI bundle, including the warning-prefixed input.
