prs.title: test(ios): observe qualification simulator startup (do not merge)
prs.body:
## Current result

**Temporary diagnostic branch; do not merge. No production optimization qualified.**

- Bare stock boot reproduces the delay without an app build, Gateway, or XCTest: headroom 136.625–206.507 s across two exploratory observations.
- Full stock qualification with the optional collector disabled still waited 149.777 s; both native UI tests and cleanup passed. The optional observer is not necessary for this recurrence.
- Runtime-cache readiness after build was already satisfied (0.763 s). Rejected as a production candidate.
- Device-scoped normal logging produced no qualifying improvement: 241.306 s startup including its 49.961 s command, above the predeclared threshold. Rejected. Two other logging placements/interfaces failed their external command contracts; all failures and cleanup are retained below.
- Blank-OS seed probe passed both unchanged headroom gates and app-absence checks, with both owned devices deleted. Cold preparation 194.170 s + clone consumer 118.236 s = 312.406 s before diagnostic overhead (338.529 s contiguous startup sequence including it). Rejected for serial single-release use; no production candidate selected.
- Early fresh-simulator startup during native preparation failed: the first postboot SDK metadata query timed out at 120.069 s, before compilation or either UI boundary. The baseline passed in 770.680 s. Rejected under the frozen complete-flow reliability rule; no larger campaign or production candidate PR.
- Current head contains temporary diagnostics only. The native qualification owner matches the original baseline byte-for-byte; no logging setter or cache-readiness treatment remains. Fresh-device behavior, native assertions, headroom gate, and deadlines are unchanged. No build was published and no PR was merged.

The evidence points to fresh simulator initialization on this image, with broad runtime-service work and substantial diagnosticd lifetime CPU; it does not identify a single safe removable service or prove all startup cost intrinsic. An initialized blank-OS seed has now been investigated below: its clone was quicker in this ordered probe, but preparation plus consumer cost did not qualify a serial single-release optimization. No cross-run simulator cache was implemented. A separate early-start ordering candidate was tested and rejected below; none of these experiments changed production qualification. Do not substitute the reduced diagnostic for release qualification or introduce a cache without measured benefit.

All runs below are exploratory/necessity observations, not the five interleaved full-qualification baseline/candidate pairs required for an accepted performance claim. No candidate passed the exploratory admission rule, so that expensive comparison was not started. Investigation complete; close this temporary PR without merging. Full observations and pre-run rules follow.

## What Problem This Solves

Recent iOS qualification traces show 137–156 seconds waiting for CPU headroom after Simulator boots. The process sampler timed out during boot, so the retained traces cannot identify the processes responsible.

**Temporary diagnostic branch: do not merge.** This supports the ongoing iOS CI performance investigation following #187920.

## User Impact

No release or upload runs. The existing nonpublishing stock qualification workflow runs its full native pairing/chat/relaunch and independent reader checks on `xcode-27-xlarge`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use `ps ucomm` kernel names instead of requesting executable paths and process argument data, and collect process observations roughly every 20 seconds. Only unique prefixes of the existing fixed role list are attributed; ambiguous or unknown names remain `other`. Paths, arguments, and arbitrary executable names are not emitted.

The collector retains nice 10, the two-second timeout, output bounds, and sanitized artifacts. Periodic process sampling stops after timeout. The revised observation permits exactly one census after qualification passes its existing headroom gate, then keeps process sampling stopped even if that census fails. The native workload, Gateway warmup order, fresh simulator, CPU headroom gate, deadlines, test assertions, and cleanup remain unchanged. The small extension to the existing collector fixture protects attribution, privacy, and timeout behavior; its exact net test-line allocation is temporary with this branch.

## Evidence

### Observation rule, recorded before the first hosted run

- Baseline source: `9559c51dd05184a34e7f791ce950c29c9922765c`.
- Workload: one fresh hosted `ios-release-e2e.yml` dispatch on this branch with `mode=stock` and `resource_diagnostics=true`.
- This is an observation, **not a performance comparison or claimed speedup**. Existing historical timings are context only.
- Useful evidence means successful process observations spanning simulator boot/headroom, with per-role CPU deltas, parent attribution, probe wall time, and host CPU/memory/I/O counters. Record sampler timeouts and coverage gaps explicitly.
- Preserve the existing gate: 10 continuous seconds with at least 30% idle CPU, two-second sampling, and the five-minute deadline. Both UI checks must still run.
- Collect only the existing sanitized proof/timeline artifacts. Do not upload raw native logs, arguments, private paths, or pairing credentials.
- If process sampling still times out, investigate that new evidence before another run; no blind retries or relaxed probe limits.
- A later optimization requires a separate frozen acceptance rule and at least five interleaved baseline/candidate samples on fresh runners, including all preparation, boot, headroom, full qualification wall time, and observed resource use. Moving work earlier does not count as removing it.

Local validation: existing collector suite 9/9 passed (0.575 seconds Vitest; 1.68 seconds complete wrapper), Node syntax check, focused type-aware script/test lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. CI timing is pending. Diagnostic collector delta against the baseline: +54/-20 lines; existing test delta: +80/-17 lines, with an exact 63-line allocation. No new workload, timer owner, or test-only production seam.

Fresh independent AutoReview/Codex review of the complete revised local change against the baseline above returned `scoped-clean` at P0–P2 with no findings. Subsequent edits only added lint-required braces and adjusted the exact allocation count; no behavior changed. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable. The author inspected and simplified the complete diff. Hosted diagnostic results will be added after the run.


### First hosted observation

[Run 40964887370](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40964887370) at `ed3040d7c55a5abe9d9c87a9a5e3b01ad6e0a562` passed both UI checks. Xcode 27.1 / 27A9275, iOS 27.0, five reported CPUs, 14 GiB reported RAM, stable Gateway 2026.10.9.

- Simulator bootstatus: 49.458 s; headroom: 149.735 s.
- Native build preparation: 241.565 s; complete workflow proof: 775.920 s.
- Kernel-name process scans succeeded 15 times before the first boot-time probe, but the first boot-time scan timed out (4.161 s observed termination wall time). Periodic process sampling then stopped as designed. No startup process attribution was obtained.
- Host CPU stayed near saturation during headroom. This is confirmation of the delay, not identification of its cause or a speedup.

### Revised observation rule, recorded before its hosted run

Run one fresh stock qualification on the reviewed revision of this same diagnostic branch. Preserve the complete workload and gate. After the first timeout, issue no more periodic process scans. Once the existing setup-code/live-chat/reader phase proves the headroom gate passed, permit one census using the existing sanitized path attribution; consume that attempt before querying and never repeat it, whether it succeeds or fails.

Emit a fixed `after-headroom` census marker and per-role **lifetime** CPU totals for all surviving processes, including those outside the top-six display. Keep missing interval baselines null. These are not boot-only CPU measurements: exited processes are absent, lifetime totals can include postgate work, and parent attribution is direct-parent only. Use runtime-origin groups to find candidate workers; do not infer a complete boot profile or causal optimization from a census alone.

The existing synthetic workload fixture exercises both successful and timed-out recovery censuses, asserts exactly one attempt, and retains privacy, timeout, cancellation, and workload-exit checks. The branch remains observation-only and must not merge. A production candidate still requires the separate interleaved comparison rule above.


### Recovered census result

[Run 40967169256](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40967169256) at `c38142035370eec5c893b69c62523f27f3a8ef18` passed both UI checks, with the same Xcode/runtime and reported host resources. Bootstatus took 52.231 s, headroom 191.898 s, native build preparation 251.152 s, and complete workflow proof 849.618 s. This run was slower than the first observation; no speedup is claimed.

The one recovery census succeeded in 75 ms, about 4.3 seconds after the gate passed. It counted 977 surviving processes. All surviving runtime-origin groups together had 714.60 lifetime CPU-seconds; 136.91 were attributed to `other`. Largest named runtime groups: `diagnosticd` 93.72 CPU-s, `amsengagementd` 44.40, `STExtractionService` 29.60, SpringBoard 19.88, `apsd` 17.83, `lsd` 17.44, and `mobileassetd` 13.00. These are lifetime counters and lower coverage of the boot population, not exact phase CPU. Search was not a demonstrated dominant named group. The trace records no swap-in/out at the census.

The census filled the process-attribution gap. The data points to broad first-boot service work; it does not prove a single removable service or a safe service-disabling change.

### Runtime-cache readiness experiment, recorded before its hosted run

Apple documents that runtime scanning and dyld shared-cache construction can degrade boot performance, and recommends waiting for cache readiness: [Xcode release notes](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode-release-notes/xcode-26_4-release-notes), [Apple engineer explanation](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/807025). The installed Xcode command help supports updating one selected runtime without `--force`.

This diagnostic revision calls `simctl runtime dyld_shared_cache update` for the already selected iOS runtime after native build, before starting the trial Gateway or simulator. It does not force cache reconstruction or modify simulator services. Build-only and Gateway-only operations skip the call. The existing command supervisor bounds it to ten minutes and retains normal cancellation/cleanup. A separate `runtimeCacheReadinessMs` proof field records its complete cost; the operation is also included in overall workflow time.

Run one fresh stock qualification to verify that Xcode accepts the canonical selected runtime identifier and to observe whether readiness performs material work. This is command-contract/diagnostic evidence, **not an accepted optimization or benchmark sample**. If the cache is already ready and startup remains slow, discard the barrier as a production candidate. If promising, freeze a separate baseline/candidate rule before at least five interleaved fresh-runner samples, with cache preparation + boot + headroom and complete job wall time counted together, identical toolchain/Gateway identities, all failures retained, and no weaker gate or deadlines.


Readiness-probe validation before dispatch: all 96 existing qualification-owner tests passed (2.02 s Vitest / 3.34 s complete wrapper), tooling test typecheck, focused type-aware script lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Fresh AutoReview/Codex review against `c38142035370eec5c893b69c62523f27f3a8ef18` returned scoped-clean at P0–P2 with no findings. The readiness probe is ten source lines; no new flag, helper owner, or test fixture was introduced. These focused tests do not prove the external simctl identifier contract; the hosted experiment does.


### Cache-readiness result and next diagnostic rule

[Run 40969297747](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40969297747) at `f7d34586131c274480bedffeca80e470b6b39e89` passed both UI checks and confirmed cleanup. The selected-runtime cache command succeeded in 0.763 s, while bootstatus took 53.425 s and headroom 172.003 s. Native build took 259.246 s; complete workflow proof took 853.589 s. Toolchain, runtime, stable Gateway, and reported resources matched the earlier observations. The postgate census again recorded about 92.48 lifetime CPU-seconds in runtime diagnosticd. The cache was already ready; **reject the readiness barrier as a production optimization**. No speedup is claimed.

Before the next hosted run, add a temporary `stock_boot_only` manual input on this diagnostic branch. Its separately named job performs no build, dependency install, Gateway, XCTest, cache barrier, or release qualification. Keep the same xlarge runner, Xcode 27.1/27A9275, iOS 27.0 runtime, iPhone17Pro device type, disposable-runner Data-volume indexing setting, stock boot/bootstatus commands, and unchanged headroom gate. Node remains 24.22.1. Record actual CPU counts, image version, runtime build, phase times, headroom outcome, and owned cleanup. Preserve all failures.

Take a short preboot baseline and one unconditional sanitized census after the real gate passes, using truthful stock-boot phase labels. Keep all probe bounds and stop behavior. Add only the public fixed roles `log` and `Console` to distinguish visible command-line logging clients; their absence cannot exclude programmatic clients. After one observation window, delete only the fresh owned device. The artifact kind explicitly says diagnostic, not qualification.

This is a reduced reproduction, **not a baseline/candidate performance comparison**. A recurrence shows the OpenClaw app/build, Gateway, and XCTest are unnecessary for that recurrence. A faster result is inconclusive because removing build changes cache state, host age, and load. Do not promote the reduced flow into release qualification or weaken its gate. Full qualification and the separately frozen interleaved performance comparison remain necessary for any resulting optimization. This PR stays draft and must not merge.

Reduced-diagnostic validation before dispatch: collector 9/9 passed; all required workflow guard files passed in two shards (331.23 s complete wrapper; tooling shard 994 passed / 10 existing skips). Workflow actionlint/zizmor and repo guards passed using the supported Python 3.13 runtime; default host Python 3.9 could not bootstrap pre-commit. Focused script lint, syntax/native dependency imports, formatting, and diff checks passed. No test files or allocations changed in this revision. Fresh independent AutoReview against `f7d34586131c274480bedffeca80e470b6b39e89` returned scoped-clean P0–P2. The reviewer noted missing unchanged collector-default context; author verified collection defaults on unless explicitly set to zero, with no zero override in this diagnostic job. Complete new workload: 143 lines, managed child supervision reused, no new lifecycle owner.


### Bare stock-boot result

[Run 40972021947](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40972021947) at `822a92117660ce9aaede601603113e5131c14929` passed the reduced diagnostic and confirmed owned-device cleanup. Same image `20261026.0314.1`, Xcode 27.1/27A9275, runtime 27.0/24A434, five actual/reported CPUs and 14 GiB RAM. The preboot sample was 92.71% idle. Bootstatus took 45.014 s, followed by 206.507 s waiting for the unchanged headroom gate. The complete reduced workload took 304.802 s, including its 20 s baseline, 25 s census window, and cleanup. It ran no OpenClaw build, Gateway, or XCTest.

The postgate census completed in 86 ms and counted 950 surviving processes, with 714.73 lifetime CPU-seconds across runtime-origin groups. Runtime diagnosticd recorded 90.07 CPU-s; host diagnosticd recorded 45.36 CPU-s. No surviving fixed-role log/Console process appeared in that census. These are lifetime counters, not an exact boot profile; exited workers and implicit consumers remain unobserved. The process probe again timed out during boot and stopped as intended. The headroom wait remained long after a quiet baseline, demonstrating that OpenClaw/build/Gateway/XCTest are not necessary for this recurrence. It does not prove a single causal service or intrinsic/unavoidable OS work. The changed cache state and host age prevent a direct speed comparison.

### Read-only logging configuration diagnostic, before dispatch

The installed Apple help documents `log config --status` as a read operation; changing configuration requires separate `--mode`/`--reset` options. `simctl logverbose` has no status form, so do not invoke it. On the same reduced workload, capture one host system-wide status before boot and one owned-simulator status after the census. Both have a five-second managed-command bound. Emit only recognized fixed system-mode flags, outcome, and duration; omit raw output, subsystem/process names, and paths. Undocumented/unrecognized text remains unknown, never inferred as default. Record presence only for four named inherited logging overrides, never their values. No log streams, setting changes, live sampling, or services disabled.

This run asks whether a persistent system-wide verbose/live logging setting or recognized inherited override is visible on the runner image. A default status cannot exclude per-process/subsystem overrides or implicit consumers; a live setting alone cannot prove a client. Preserve all earlier timings/limitations. This is diagnosis only, not qualification or an optimization comparison.

Logging-status revision validation: focused lint, syntax, formatting, and diff checks passed; unchanged collector/workflow proof reused. Fresh independent review against `822a92117660ce9aaede601603113e5131c14929` returned scoped-clean P0–P2 with no findings. The added probes are bounded optional read-only commands; unknown text and failures remain explicitly unknown/unavailable. No test files or workflow changes in this revision.


### Logging-status result

[Run 40972991532](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40972991532) at `bfb0da6470b24d0ee8a156648af1483592dd0532` passed and confirmed cleanup. Same image/toolchain/runtime/resources. Boot took 1.270 s, bootstatus 39.632 s, headroom 136.625 s; complete reduced workload 227.502 s. The runtime census recorded 513.86 lifetime CPU-seconds, including diagnosticd 50.19 CPU-s; host diagnosticd 26.69 CPU-s. This differs materially from the earlier bare run and demonstrates why unmatched observations cannot establish a speedup.

Host system status recognized `INFO` (24 ms). The simulator system line contained recognized `INFO` and `STREAM_LIVE` tokens (749 ms), plus an unknown token, so its full outcome remains **unrecognized**, not a complete configuration assessment. All four named inherited override variables were absent. A stream setting is not proof of an active logging consumer; per-process/subsystem settings remain unknown.

### Default-stream exploratory rule, before dispatch

On one fresh runner, use the same reduced workload and set only the freshly owned simulator's documented system stream mode to `default`, using `simctl spawn <owned device> log config --mode stream:default` after stock boot and before bootstatus. Never change host logging, verbosity, persistence, profiles, services, or test/gate deadlines. Keep unknown config flags unknown. Capture status after the census using the same sanitized parser. The proof kind explicitly identifies this experiment and never claims release qualification.

Count **boot + policy command + bootstatus + headroom** together, so blocked or relocated readiness work cannot appear as a saving. This is one exploratory command-contract/causality probe, not an accepted benchmark sample. It is promising only if the command succeeds, the fixed `STREAM_LIVE` token is absent from a successfully parsed system line afterward, cleanup succeeds, and the startup sum is at least 25% below even the faster existing bare observation (177.527 s; exploratory threshold 133.145 s). Otherwise discard this as a production candidate. Preserve failures and all timing. An apparently promising result still requires the separate frozen full-qualification comparison with at least five interleaved baseline/candidate fresh-runner samples, complete preparation cost, identical toolchain/Gateway, unchanged assertions/gate, and all failures retained. No production change is selected here.


### Default-stream command result

[Run 40973732451](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40973732451) at `c203f7a2c45b26e7ef25f4e2db33c3c84869325a` failed in the new stream-policy command after 1.587 s. Owned-device deletion succeeded (19.089 s); cleanup confirmed. No headroom or qualification outcome was obtained. This is an external-command contract failure, not evidence of a performance improvement or a product failure. The earlier wrapper intentionally discarded raw native diagnostics, so the rejection's cause is unknown.

Before the next dispatch, retain bounded stderr privately in memory and export only the failing policy command's exit code plus four fixed boolean error categories (permission, unsupported operation, invalid arguments, device not ready). Never export the raw text or device/path values. Reproduce the same entry point once to classify its failure; do not change permissions, boot ordering, logging settings, or deadlines in this diagnostic revision. This is targeted failure diagnosis, not a benchmark retry. A supported alternative requires the reason first; do not repeat the same failed route blindly.


### Stream-policy failure diagnosis and supported alternative

[Run 40974167103](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40974167103) at `492c4094b972b3f485d73c87a3e296ee8ce5f981` again failed at the stream-policy command, exit code **64 (usage error)**. None of the four text classifiers matched; the precise rejected argument remains unknown. No headroom result was obtained. The command took 13.814 s and owned cleanup succeeded after 60.585 s; complete workload 99.395 s. Do not repeat this unsupported route or treat it as a performance sample. The observed live flag does not make this setter a supported simulator interface.

Before the next exploratory run, replace that command with Apple's explicitly device-scoped `simctl logverbose <owned UUID> disable` **before first boot**. The installed help says changes may require reboot, hence apply to the fresh shutdown device. This changes that simulator's verbose logging policy; it does not disable a daemon or change host logging. Record the postgate fixed flags without assuming this API maps to one particular log-config field. The proof kind and phase identify the distinct normal-logging experiment. Retire the rejected setter and its phase label; keep error categorization for the new policy command.

Same exploratory acceptance rule: one fresh reduced workload, identical image/toolchain/device and unchanged gate; include **logging policy + boot + bootstatus + headroom** in startup cost. Require successful command, headroom, and owned cleanup plus a startup sum below 133.145 s (at least 25% below the faster descriptive bare observation) before considering full comparison. Otherwise discard. A result meeting that threshold remains exploratory and needs the separate five-interleaved-pair full qualification rule before production promotion. Any reduced verbose-log availability is a tradeoff to assess with complete native qualification and diagnostics, not an assertion that logging is irrelevant. No release upload or production change.


### Device-scoped policy state contract

[Run 40974654787](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40974654787) at `291d446e1cabf050ea0f43525645444de2255999` failed at the preboot logging policy in 0.141 s, exit 149 with `deviceNotReady=true`. The freshly created device was still shutdown; no boot or headroom outcome was obtained. Owned cleanup succeeded in 0.143 s. This establishes that preboot placement is invalid on this runtime; it is not an optimization sample.

Before the next run, move the same device-scoped command **after stock bootstatus and before the unchanged headroom gate**. This addresses the observed state prerequisite. Do not add a reboot, retries, new permissions, or deadline changes. Count boot + bootstatus + logging policy + headroom together and keep the same 133.145 s exploratory threshold. If the policy requires another boot to have an effect, it is not a useful optimization for this flow and must not be promoted. The postgate flags and errors remain sanitized as before. This is the last narrow logging-policy candidate in this diagnostic series; no daemon-disabling fallback.


### Booted-device policy result: reject candidate

[Run 40974982081](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40974982081) at `0361587e09dc5aaef57d60333c3e43ff184e6ae6` passed the reduced diagnostic and confirmed cleanup. Same image/toolchain/runtime/resources. Boot 1.509 s, bootstatus 41.768 s, logging-policy command **49.961 s**, and headroom 148.068 s: **241.306 s total startup**, above the predeclared 133.145 s threshold and 35.9% slower than the faster descriptive bare observation. Complete reduced workload 290.601 s. The postgate system line still contained INFO and STREAM_LIVE, with the full status still unrecognized. Runtime diagnosticd lifetime CPU was 79.44 s, host diagnosticd 40.83 s. This is neither a causal speed comparison nor an accepted optimization; it clearly fails the exploratory rule. **Reject the logging-policy candidate.** No reboot or daemon-disabling fallback.

Remove both rejected treatments from the current diagnostic head: remove the cache probe so the qualification native owner matches `9559c51dd05184a34e7f791ce950c29c9922765c` (no runtime-cache barrier) and return the reduced workload to read-only stock-boot observation (no logging setter). Remove the retired policy phase. Retain the sanitized observer/configuration reads only on this draft diagnostic branch, never as a production fix.

### Optional-observer control, before dispatch

One fresh full stock qualification with `resource_diagnostics=false` and `stock_boot_only=false` on the reviewed cleanup revision. Keep the original build, pinned stable Gateway selection/install, actual Gateway setup warmup, fresh stock simulator, unmodified headroom gate/deadline, both native UI tests, and owned cleanup. No optional timeline polling/census process will run; built-in qualification proof and Gateway diagnostic snapshots remain, so do not call this an entirely uninstrumented flow. Never upload or publish a build.

This is a necessity control, not an accepted baseline/candidate performance sample. A long headroom wait again demonstrates that the optional periodic timeline collector is not necessary for the recurrence. A faster result cannot establish the collector caused earlier delays; it would require a separate matched comparison. Record exact source/image/toolchain/Gateway identities, boot/headroom/build/UI/complete workflow costs, failures, and cleanup. Do not weaken deadlines or run a new logging-policy treatment. No production optimization has been selected.


### Observer-off full qualification result

[Run 40975748968](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40975748968) at `2af672557042cedb52acd7b26b2553593b27994c` passed **both native UI checks**, confirmed owned cleanup and unchanged source, and reported no errors or diagnostics. The Actions environment explicitly recorded `OPENCLAW_IOS_RESOURCE_DIAGNOSTICS: 0`; the artifact contains the qualification proof only, with no timeline file. The qualification native owner is byte-identical to baseline `9559c51dd05184a34e7f791ce950c29c9922765c`, with neither rejected treatment.

Same image `20261026.0314.1`, Xcode 27.1/27A9275, iOS 27.0, 14 GiB reported RAM, and stable Gateway 2026.10.9/source `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41` with matching package/lock hashes. Actual CPU count was not recorded with the collector disabled; do not infer a fully hardware-matched benchmark from the runner label.

- Native build preparation: 216.284 s, not reused.
- Boot: 1.468 s; bootstatus: 44.879 s; headroom: **149.777 s**; startup sum: **196.124 s**.
- Native test boundary durations: 117.576 s and 85.323 s.
- Complete workflow proof: 767.863 s.
- Setup status/code RPCs succeeded in one attempt (73 ms / 61 ms); one Gateway heartbeat was delayed during boot. Owned cleanup confirmed.

A long headroom wait recurred without the optional periodic collector. This disproves its necessity for this recurrence, **not** zero observer overhead. This is one necessity control, not an accepted speed comparison: the build/UI timings and unrecorded CPU count prevent claiming a speedup from its complete elapsed time. Existing built-in proof/Gateway snapshots remained enabled.

Cleanup validation: 105/105 focused owner/collector tests passed (2.20 s Vitest / 3.49 s complete wrapper), tooling test typecheck, focused type-aware script lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. The unchanged workflow reuses the earlier passing full workflow guards/actionlint/zizmor proof. Fresh independent review of the cleanup returned scoped-clean P0–P2. Earlier narrow revisions also received clean independent review; the normal-logging revision had only mechanical formatter collapse afterward. No test files or allocations changed after the original observer fixtures.


## Initialized blank-OS seed experiment — rule before execution

This is a new exploratory probe, not a production candidate or qualification substitute. Apple documents configuring and shutting down a base before `simctl clone`, noting that clones benefit because the base already paid first-boot work: https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2019/418/ . The source is a fresh task-created iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 27.0 device on the same xlarge image/toolchain. No OpenClaw app, Gateway, XCTest, accounts, credentials, or pairing data are installed in it; there is no device-state cache, cross-run reuse, or restored state.

One fresh hosted reduced run will measure: create → cold boot → bootstatus → unchanged headroom gate → assert OpenClaw absent → shutdown seed → clone → boot clone → bootstatus → unchanged headroom gate → assert OpenClaw absent → delete both owned devices. Only the clone may run after seed shutdown; cleanup independently attempts each owned identity even after failure. Record actual CPU/memory/image/runtime identities, each phase, total workload wall, cleanup, and all failed outcomes. Export only sanitized fixed facts, never application listings, paths, device IDs, or raw diagnostics. The existing 20-second baseline, 25-second postgate census window and optional read-only logging queries remain separately reported diagnostics, not hidden preparation work.

**Decision rule:** a successful clone with at least 25% lower consumer startup (shutdown + clone + boot + bootstatus + headroom + absence checks) than this run's cold seed preparation is mechanistic evidence worth reporting, but cannot qualify a serial one-release optimization. For that, the complete cold seed preparation + consumer startup must be at least 25% below the faster prior bare observation (177.527 s; threshold 133.145 s), with successful unchanged gates, absence checks, and cleanup. Record and reject a non-improving total; do not start five expensive full-flow pairs just because a warm clone looks fast. A one-run observation is not a causal speedup benchmark. Any later overlapping/prebuilt design needs a separately frozen full-qualification rule, at least five interleaved matched baseline/candidate samples, complete preparation/restore/producer costs, both unchanged native UI checks, and no regressed resources/deadlines. No release/upload or merge is authorized here.


### Blank-seed probe revision and validation

Committed probe: `eca9483ec9e85e10340a381e0fc7d6e1511a4f8c`. [Run 40977830961](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40977830961) dispatches only the reduced diagnostic, not qualification. Seed remains app-free by construction; an app uninstall/onboarding reset is not accepted as fresh identity. Installed `simctl help listapps` exposes no JSON option; its private plist is converted by `/usr/bin/plutil -convert json -o - -`, with both exits checked and no raw listing exported.

Collector suite passed 9/9 (0.581 s Vitest; 1.80 s wrapper); focused type-aware script lint, formatting, syntax, and diff checks passed. Fresh independent AutoReview/Codex on the probe delta returned scoped-clean at P0–P2. One subsequent lint-only adjustment explicitly defaults the command's empty stdin to an empty string. Author simplified the delta: no workflow changes or extra mode/cache owner, just the existing reduced diagnostic extended to one clone and independent two-device cleanup. Native qualification owner and its assertions remain unchanged.


### Blank-seed hosted result and decision

[Run 40977830961](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40977830961) at `eca9483ec9e85e10340a381e0fc7d6e1511a4f8c` **passed the reduced diagnostic**, including both unchanged headroom gates, both app-absence assertions, and owned cleanup (2 recorded / 2 deleted). This did **not** run the app, pairing, Gateway, or XCTest, and does not qualify a release.

Same image `20261026.0314.1`, Xcode 27.1 / 27A9275, iOS 27.0 / 24A434, five reported/available CPUs, 14 GiB RAM, Node 24.22.1. No persistent seed, cache transfer, restore, or amortization was involved.

| Phase | Seconds |
| --- | ---: |
| Seed create | 0.253 |
| Seed boot | 1.228 |
| Seed bootstatus | 40.434 |
| Seed unchanged headroom gate | 152.029 |
| Seed app-absence assertion | 0.226 |
| **Cold seed preparation sum** | **194.170** |
| Seed shutdown | 0.801 |
| Clone creation | 3.868 |
| Clone boot | 4.133 |
| Clone bootstatus | 24.618 |
| Clone unchanged headroom gate | 84.275 |
| Clone app-absence assertion | 0.541 |
| **Consumer sum including shutdown and cloning** | **118.236** |
| **Seed + consumer lower bound, excluding diagnostic pause/probes** | **312.406** |
| **Contiguous create → clone absence assertion, including diagnostic work** | **338.529** |
| Both owned deletions | 3.471 |
| Complete diagnostic workload | 364.171 |

The consumer sum was descriptively 39.1% below cold seed preparation, satisfying the mechanistic exploratory rule. **It fails the serial one-release admission rule:** even the 312.406 s lower bound exceeds 133.145 s. A fast clone is not a total-cost saving: this runner first paid for the cold base, and stock qualification only needs one simulator. The ordered observations share a host with evolving caches/load and a 25-second postgate diagnostic pause; they are not independent baseline/candidate samples or a causal performance comparison. The contiguous 338.529 s figure explicitly includes that pause and logging query so settlement time is not hidden.

The collector recorded normal memory-pressure flag 1 and zero swap-in/out bytes in available samples. Its first boot-time process probe timed out and periodic process sampling stopped; the existing single postgate recovery path remained bounded. One iostat probe also timed out during clone readiness. There are no per-process clone-startup CPU observations sufficient for causal attribution. These facts do not rule out memory or other resource contributions. Host logging was INFO; simulator status remained unrecognized with recognized INFO/STREAM_LIVE tokens; no logging configuration was changed.

**Decision:** reject serial per-release seed preparation as a production optimization. Do not start the five-pair full-qualification campaign, add a cross-run device-state cache, weaken readiness, or claim the clone-qualified release flow. A prebuilt-image or overlap design would be a different experiment requiring complete producer/preparation/transfer costs and full qualification evidence. Current canonical qualification remains byte-identical to baseline. This PR stays draft/do-not-merge. No release/upload or merge occurred.

At this head, ordinary PR CI settled without failures. The worktree is clean and pushed. Local focused checks and independent review are recorded above; no further experiment is planned for this serial design.


## Early fresh-simulator startup — exploratory rule before execution

Next investigation authorized by the operator: overlap the SAME fresh stock simulator's initialization with already-required work; no seed, clone, state cache, persisted app state, logging setter, or relaxed gate. Existing timelines show the first ~60–80 s of native build with 41–71% idle CPU, followed by near saturation. Gateway installation/preflight takes only ~20 s; starting before its setup warmup risks the previously observed starvation. Workflow setup has ~55–59 s but cross-step device custody would add a separate lifecycle. Therefore test the smaller harness-local ordering after stable Gateway preflight and before native build. Only stock full qualification changes; comparison, build-only, and gateway-only remain on their original paths.

Baseline is the full stock flow at `eca9483ec9e85e10340a381e0fc7d6e1511a4f8c`, with resource diagnostics enabled. The probe candidate will have identical application/test/tooling source except the adapter scheduling change and its focused regression proof. Create and boot one fresh task-owned simulator before build (no background bootstatus child). The outer adapter owns deletion on build/cancellation failure until the first fixture adopts it. After build, join bootstatus and require the existing headroom criterion before live Gateway/mock startup; retain the original headroom gate after setupStatus and before issuing a fresh pairing credential. Both existing native UI tests, independent reader, assertions, deadlines, and source checks remain unchanged. No app is installed until normal XCTest flow. This adds a necessary admission check for Gateway startup after newly overlapping CPU work; it does not treat a pre-build idle observation as readiness.

Run one fresh full baseline and then one fresh full candidate, serially. This is an exploratory admission pair, not the required performance campaign. Record exact app source identity, image/Xcode/runtime, actual CPU/RAM, stable Gateway version/source/package/lock hashes, overall workflow and harness walls, all native build/boot/gate/UI durations, resource observations, and all failures/cleanup. Count all early preparation and extra gate costs in complete wall time; do not sum overlapping phase durations and call that wall time.

**Exploratory admission:** both complete native flows, source checks and cleanup must pass on comparable image/toolchain/hardware/Gateway identities. Candidate overall workflow time must be at least 10% below this baseline; native build and either UI boundary must not regress by 20% or more, and observed memory-pressure/swap must not introduce a new regression. Any failed or mismatched result is retained, not blindly rerun or silently excluded; a product/harness/infra defect must be diagnosed before any justified replacement. A nonpromising result is removed from production consideration. An admitted candidate still needs a separately frozen rule and at least five interleaved fresh baseline/candidate full-qualification samples before promotion. No release/upload, merge, runner upsize, weakened deadline, or service disabling.


### Ordering simplification before candidate execution

Source audit identified a smaller complete cutover than the initial outer-owned sketch. The candidate keeps the actual live Gateway and setupStatus warmup before cold boot, creates/boots the same fresh device in the existing trial, then performs the deferred native build before the original bootstatus/headroom. The stock build is a local closure called with fixtureSignal, so Gateway/mock death cancels native generation/build. Existing runTrials cleanup already owns every resource because it receives the fixture before prepare begins. Compare/build-only remain eager; gateway-only skips building. No custody transfer, background bootstatus process, or additional headroom check is needed. The native build still targets generic iOS Simulator and requires no completed boot or pairing credential. This replaces the initial implementation sketch only; the predeclared metrics, 10% total-time admission threshold, 20% regression stop, and complete qualification requirement are unchanged. [Fresh baseline run 40979030799](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40979030799) retains the original source `eca9483ec9e85e10340a381e0fc7d6e1511a4f8c`.


### Early-start candidate committed before hosted execution

Candidate `020eea68269ec00820d5da7f4706ebe1c55b8f4b` on `test/ios-qualification-startup-overlap` is a 13-added/4-removed production-owner delta plus focused test updates (35 added/11 removed, exact temporary 24-line allocation). No workflow or application source changed relative to exploratory baseline `eca9483ec9e85e10340a381e0fc7d6e1511a4f8c`. The complete native lifecycle suite passed 97/97 (1.82 s Vitest; 3.02 s wrapper), including deferred build failure, unjoined build preservation/cleanup, and Gateway-exit cancellation during compilation. Tooling-test typecheck, focused type-aware lint, format, and diff checks passed. An initial test run exposed two incomplete diagnostic expectations in the migrated fixture (95 passed / 2 failed); the exact structured context expectations were corrected without changing production behavior, then all cases passed.

Author simplified to one existing resource owner, no custody transfer/extra gate/background bootstatus. Fresh independent AutoReview with full native owner, main caller and build owner evidence returned scoped-clean P0–P2 and confirmed mode guards, fixture cancellation/cleanup, both unchanged native UI tests, and full wall accounting. This remains an unqualified exploratory branch, with no new PR or production promotion yet. Baseline runs first, candidate second, without overlapping hosted qualification executions. Fetched current main `aacb5e162cf1d5414c5a716bfefc2502ed75ce56` has unchanged native owner/workflow/headroom/app sources; experiment intentionally retains the identical baseline checkout/tooling/dependencies for a controlled pair. Broader main differences are not incorporated into a matched sample or silently called qualified.


### Fresh early-start baseline completed

[Run 40979030799](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40979030799), SHA `eca9483ec9e85e10340a381e0fc7d6e1511a4f8c`, passed both full native UI boundaries, the original headroom gate, provider-order checks, unchanged source, and cleanup, with no proof errors/diagnostics. Image xcode-27-arm64 `20261026.0314.1`, Xcode 27.1 / 27A9275, iOS 27.0, five CPUs / 14 GiB RAM. Stable Gateway remains 2026.10.9, source `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`, package SHA256 `1f4f05779400de2d4b3b860e7ae57f97714e1f4d95319e7593730a76e88fdadf`, lock SHA256 `94915ebb0e3953a1bf6972e19f977b580210918d6140d474eafe8bb8f267bdc7`.

- Complete workflow proof: 770.680 s; complete harness: 663.925 s; shared installation: 62 s.
- Native preparation: 233.314 s (not reused); actual xcodebuild: 229.125 s.
- Boot command 1.498 s; bootstatus 39.019 s; headroom 155.768 s.
- Native UI boundary walls: 109.906 / 77.628 s; both passed.
- setupStatus / setupCode: 58 / 46 ms, one attempt each; cleanup confirmed; no Gateway exit.

The recorded 10% admission threshold is therefore **693.612 s complete workflow**, with the independent 20% build/UI regression stop retained. [Candidate run 40980530710](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40980530710), SHA `020eea68269ec00820d5da7f4706ebe1c55b8f4b`, was dispatched only after baseline completion. This pair remains exploratory and cannot establish repeatability or production qualification on its own.


### Early-start candidate result — rejected; investigation complete

[Candidate run 40980530710](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40980530710), SHA `020eea68269ec00820d5da7f4706ebe1c55b8f4b`, failed during preparation. The initial `xcodebuild -version` passed in 66 ms before boot. After stock simulator boot passed in 1.472 s, the next command, `xcrun --sdk iphonesimulator --show-sdk-build-version`, timed out after 120.069 s. Both commands share the proof label `xcode-version`; the failed command was the SDK metadata query, not the initial version command. Native generation/compilation, bootstatus, headroom and both UI boundaries were never reached. No completed build or successful performance sample exists for the candidate.

Image `xcode-27-arm64` version `20261026.0314.1`, Xcode 27.1 / 27A9275, iOS runtime 27.0, five CPUs, 14 GiB, and Node 24.22.1 match the baseline. Candidate stable Gateway 2026.10.9, source `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`, package SHA256 `1f4f05779400de2d4b3b860e7ae57f97714e1f4d95319e7593730a76e88fdadf`, and lock SHA256 `94915ebb0e3953a1bf6972e19f977b580210918d6140d474eafe8bb8f267bdc7` exactly match baseline. This is a controlled source/toolchain observation, not latest-main production qualification.

Eight candidate resource samples were retained. During the blocked SDK query, sampled CPU idle was 0–0.86%, and one-minute load reached 302.51. Available pressure flags stayed normal (1) and recorded swap-in/out remained zero in both baseline and candidate; one candidate pressure probe was unavailable. The process probe timed out during boot and stopped as designed; sysctl and iostat also timed out once. This supports severe CPU/scheduling contention during early simulator startup, but does not identify the blocking process or distinguish scheduler starvation from an internal Apple-tool wait. No claim of a memory-pressure regression or exact causal bottleneck is made.

Candidate fixture cleanup was confirmed, owned simulator deletion passed in 4.375 s, and source-head/status checks passed. Harness wall was 173.359 s and workflow proof wall 286.332 s **to failure**; neither is a speedup over the 770.680 s passing baseline. No retry, increased timeout, relaxed gate, runner upsize, or excluded failure.

**Decision:** reject this implementation under the predeclared requirement that both complete native flows pass. Do not begin the five-pair campaign or open a production PR for it. Moving SDK metadata ahead of boot or choosing another overlap boundary would be a different candidate requiring explicit diagnosis and a new recorded experiment, not a passing interpretation of this failure. Close the temporary diagnostic PR without merging; retain its evidence and the separate unmerged candidate source. Canonical production qualification is unchanged, no release/upload occurred, and no PR was merged.

prs.title: fix(normalization-core): token budget under-counts Tangut, Khitan, and Nushu text
prs.body:
Closes #187849

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the token-budget heuristic under-counts Tangut, Khitan Small Script, and Nushu text by 8x when estimating context/token usage, because those supplementary-plane CJK-family scripts are missing from the weighting table.

## User Impact

User impact: text written in Tangut, Tangut Components, Khitan Small Script, Tangut Supplement, or Nushu is now budgeted consistently with the other supplementary CJK the estimator already covers (Kana Supplement, CJK Ext B–H), so context budgeting and compaction no longer under-allocate for it. There is no change to Latin, BMP CJK, emoji, or any already-covered script.

## Why This Change Was Made

`WEIGHTED_CJK_RANGES` weights supplementary CJK conservatively but omitted the contiguous Tangut/Khitan block (U+17000–U+18D0F) and Nushu (U+1B170–U+1B2FF), so those code points fell through to the unweighted `default` branch and were counted like an emoji surrogate pair. This adds the Tangut/Khitan range to the supplementary bucket and extends the existing Kana Supplement range from U+1B16F to U+1B2FF to include the adjacent Nushu block. `maxCodePoint` stays `0x3347f`, so the `Uint8Array` lookup size is unchanged.

## Evidence

Drove the real `estimateStringChars` from `packages/normalization-core` under `tsx`, before vs after the patch:

| code point | script | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| U+17000 | Tangut | 2 (~1 tok) | 16 (~4 tok) |
| U+18800 | Tangut Components | 2 | 16 |
| U+18B00 | Khitan Small Script | 2 | 16 |
| U+1B170 | Nushu | 2 | 16 |
| U+20000 (control, already covered) | CJK Ext B | 16 | 16 |
| U+1B001 (control, already covered) | Kana Supplement | 16 | 16 |
| U+1F600 (control, emoji) | — | 2 | 2 |

A 4-character Tangut string went from `8` weighted chars (~2 tokens) to `64` (~16 tokens), matching the covered supplementary CJK.

Regression: executed the package's existing `cjk-chars.test.ts` assertions against the patched module — all 41 existing assertions still pass (0 regressions). Added a focused `it.each` case covering U+17000 / U+18800 / U+18B00 / U+18D00 / U+1B170 / U+1B2FF; those 6 new assertions fail on `main` and pass after the patch.

<details>
<summary>What was not tested</summary>

Did not start a live OpenClaw instance and did not run the full `pnpm vitest` suite (no dependency install/build in this environment); only exercised the patched pure function and the package's own unit-test vectors locally via `tsx` with a minimal vitest-compatible shim. Focused proof passes; PR CI runs the full suite.

</details>

prs.title: fix(snapshot): hash PostgreSQL generations without whole-row sort spills
prs.body:
## fix(snapshot): hash PostgreSQL generations without whole-row sort spills

## What Problem This Solves

`inspectPostgresGeneration` (`src/snapshot/postgres-generation.ts`, from #174360) hashes each table through

```sql
DECLARE openclaw_generation_rows NO SCROLL CURSOR FOR
SELECT row_to_json(t)::text AS row FROM <table> t ORDER BY row_to_json(t)::text COLLATE "C"
```

The sort key is the whole serialized row. Nothing can serve that order from an index, so PostgreSQL materializes and sorts the full JSON text of the table. For memory tables that store embeddings, that spills to temp files at roughly 2x the JSON size every time an update capture or a migration before/after check runs.

What we saw on one install (PG 17.11, work_mem 64MB, `memory_index_chunks` 45k rows / 2.2 GB):
- `FETCH FORWARD 128 FROM openclaw_generation_rows` was the top statement in pg_stat_statements: 79,649 calls, 1,207 s total, max 30 s, 40.5M temp blocks written.
- During one update/doctor run on 2026-10-28 (12:40 to 17:42) the runtime role wrote **540 temp files, 332 GB, across 101 backends**, all under this cursor.

## Why This Change Was Made

The order and the resulting sha256 must stay byte-identical, because generation strings are persisted in the update backup (`sourceGenerations`) and compared across builds (`before !== expected` refuses the migration). So this keeps the exact ordering and only changes how it is computed:

1. Each relation is sized as `pg_table_size` (heap plus TOAST), summed over `pg_partition_tree` for partitioned parents. Tables under a quarter of the session's `work_mem` keep the existing whole-row cursor, which sorts in memory at that size and is the fastest path. Trees with a foreign-table leaf also stay on it, since their `ctid` is not usable.
2. Larger tables use a cursor that sorts just `left(row_to_json(t)::text, 256) COLLATE "C"` plus `tableoid`/`ctid`. In the "C" collation, a 256-char prefix orders the same way the full text does. The only rows it can't separate are ones with equal prefixes.
3. Complete runs of equal prefixes are batched (about 128 rows) and re-read by TID (`ctid = ANY($1::tid[])`, a TID scan on PostgreSQL 14+, below the supported minimum of 16) with `ORDER BY` on the full text. Each batch is a contiguous slice of the global order, so hashing the slices in sequence gives the original sequence.
4. A run longer than 10,000 rows is not collected. The client keeps only its count and prefix, then hashes it through a second streamed cursor, `WHERE left(row_to_json(t)::text, 256) COLLATE "C" = $1 ORDER BY row_to_json(t)::text COLLATE "C"`. That bounds client memory and array parameters. In the worst case (one run spanning the table), the server sorts that run the same way it sorted the whole table before.
5. If a TID or run read returns a different row count than the prefix cursor saw, it throws instead of hashing a partial table. The `tableoid` filter keeps partitions apart, since they reuse the same TIDs. The function now documents that callers must hold REPEATABLE READ or write-blocking locks. Both callers already do: `fingerprintPostgresDatabase` opens `REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY`, and the migration attribution path reads under the migration transaction's table and sequence locks.

## Evidence

### Measurements (throwaway PG 17.11 on a Mac Studio, work_mem 64MB, synthetic `memory_index_chunks` with 1536-dim embeddings)

Final code. The host was shared (load average about 20 on 32 cores), so wall times vary by about 20% between runs; temp bytes, statement counts and hashes are exact.

| rows | pg_table_size | variant | temp written | wall | max statement | statements | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 13 MB | before | 0 | 0.35 s | 0.27 s | 21 | 52fa3d7d... |
| 1,000 | 13 MB | after (whole-row path) | 0 | 0.23 s | 0.18 s | 21 | identical |
| 3,000 | 40 MB | before | 110 MB | 0.64 s | 0.54 s | 37 | 31604256... |
| 3,000 | 40 MB | after | **0** | 0.57 s | 0.20 s | 61 | identical |
| 20,000 | 268 MB | before | 736 MB | 4.1 s | 3.5 s | 170 | 700f2ac1... |
| 20,000 | 268 MB | after | **0** | 3.3 s | 1.3 s | 327 | identical |
| 80,000 | 1.07 GB | before | 2.95 GB | 15.0 s | 12.6 s | 639 | 977f5515... |
| 80,000 | 1.07 GB | after | **0** | 15.8 s | 6.1 s | 1,264 | identical |
| 20,000, all rows tie on 256 chars | 276 MB | before | 748 MB | 6.6 s | 5.3 s | 170 | 4a8dc83c... |
| 20,000, all rows tie on 256 chars | 276 MB | after (1 oversized run) | 748 MB | 15.5 s | 11.3 s | 329 | identical |

An earlier, quieter pass of the same prefix path measured 20k at 3.06 s vs 3.37 s before, and 80k at 13.6 s vs 15.4 s.

Choosing the threshold: a sweep at work_mem 64MB showed the whole-row sort staying in memory up to a 20 MB table (1,500 rows, 0 temp) and spilling from 27 MB (2,000 rows, 73 MB temp). Below the spill point it was up to about 15% faster than the prefix path. A fixed 64 MB cutoff would have kept spilling tables on the old path, so the cutoff is `work_mem / 4` (16 MB here, 1 MB at the 4MB default).

Tradeoff: on large tables each row is serialized twice (once for the prefix, once for the hash), and there is one extra statement per 128 rows. That trades a little CPU for zero temp writes, and the longest single statement roughly halves, which also helps the bridge's `statement_timeout`. A table whose rows mostly share a 256-char prefix keeps the old temp cost and takes about twice as long, because it is read once for the prefixes and once for the run.

### Tests

- New `src/snapshot/postgres-generation.postgres.test.ts` (added to the `scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs` targets). It runs the whole-row path, the prefix path and the prefix path with the run cap lowered to 16, and requires all three to equal a reference whole-row "C" sort and each other. prs.title: fix(codex): restore hosted tools for read-only plugins
prs.body:
Related to #180029.

## What Problem This Solves

Enabling `read_only` on a Codex plugin can hide a valid hosted read tool when its runtime name differs from the name OpenClaw constructs.

## User Impact

Read-only plugins can expose eligible tools with dotted or disambiguated names. A write tool stays disabled even when its display title matches an allowed read tool's name.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw now joins the hosted tool's connector and action identity to the app inventory and grants its exact runtime name. Both sources must classify the action as read-only, and the grant preserves native disables and approval settings. Interactive turns, forks, and scheduled runs share the same inventory reader.

## Evidence

- A real Codex 0.163.0 turn against a loopback MCP server executed both requested reads. Codex rejected both attempted writes before they reached the server, including writes whose titles matched the allowed names. The model and provider data were synthetic.
- 145 selected tests passed, including scheduled replay, native fork preparation, and a title-collision regression that failed on the base commit. Scoped TypeScript, lint, and formatting checks passed.

### Native recovery trace at `7aa108864`

A local fixture supplied the model responses, app metadata, and hosted MCP endpoint. The unmodified Codex 0.163.0 binary handled discovery, tool admission, and execution. Each write's title matched its app's readable tool name.

| Attempt | Calls received by MCP | Calls rejected by Codex before MCP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Initial turn | `google_drive.search`, `kepler.query_kepler_cards` | `google_drive.write`, `kepler.write` |
| Same thread after an app-server restart and `thread/resume` | `google_drive.search` | `kepler.query_kepler_cards`, `google_drive.write`, `kepler.write` |

Before resume, the fixture changed the Kepler action's `app/read` classification to writable. OpenClaw refreshed the serialized policy context against the new inventory. The model requested all four tools again. The recording endpoint received only the Drive read, and the model received an `unsupported call` result for each of the three blocked requests.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): resolve literal remote-shell file paths without trimming
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The remote-shell sandbox fs bridge trimmed the tool-supplied `filePath` before mapping it onto its mounts, so a literal file name like `" x.txt"` silently addressed its trimmed sibling `x.txt`. A sandboxed agent reading or writing `" x.txt"` touched the decoy file instead of the one the model chose.

Precedent: #187554 ("The configured directory's whitespace belongs to its filesystem identity"). Sibling: #172869.

## Why This Change Was Made

`RemoteShellSandboxFsBridge.resolveTarget` in `src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.ts` now resolves the caller's literal `filePath` for both container-mount and host-mount mapping; the containment guards are unchanged and still operate on the literal-resolved path.

Classification: `behavior-completing` (extends the literal-path contract to the remote-shell bridge owner, closing the sandbox-backend trio: mxc #187766, OpenShell #187777, remote shell here).

## User Impact

Agents in remote-shell-backed sandboxes now read and write the exact file the model named, including names with leading/trailing whitespace. Ordinary paths, absolute paths, and boundary rejections behave identically.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `091ce5a1b` (branch `fix/remote-shell-literal-file-path`)

- Acceptance RED: on current main, the new assertion failed — `readFile(" x.txt")` returned the decoy bytes (`Buffer.from("decoy-data")`); the 23 pre-existing tests passed (1 failed / 23 passed)
- Acceptance GREEN: on exact head, all 24 tests pass, with `" x.txt"` → literal and `"x.txt"` → decoy observed through the real bridge
- Legal controls: the trimmed sibling still resolves to itself; the pinned-read-source, copy-streaming, ownership-mapping, and mutation-guard tests are unchanged and green
- Cleanup: fixture-scoped temp dirs only; no Gateway, session, token, or config touched

### Verification

Closes #186215

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native macOS New Thread hanging and allocating unbounded memory when creating a conversation.

## User Impact

Native Mac users can create a thread through the sidebar or keyboard shortcut without entering recursive session creation. A missing or retired Gateway connection is rejected rather than silently retargeted. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mac transport now routes ordinary creation through its existing captured new-session lease. This replaces the recursive default-dispatch path without introducing another request builder or changing generic transports and iOS.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep literal node-adopted transcript cwd
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adopting a Codex CLI session that was started in a directory whose name carries whitespace (a valid POSIX name, e.g. `" /tmp/oc-proof "`) rewrote the transcript header cwd to the trimmed sibling. The transcript importer and the session manager consume that header as the session's filesystem identity, so continued sessions resolved files against the wrong directory.

Precedent: #187554 ("The configured directory's whitespace belongs to its filesystem identity"). Sibling: #172869.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createOrReuseNodeAdoptedSession` in `extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-node-adoption.ts` now passes the recorded cwd to `importCodexThreadHistoryToTranscript` verbatim; only the all-blank-as-absent check still consults `trim()`. This matches the transcript importer's contract, which forwards the header cwd verbatim (no downstream re-trim in this chain).

Scope note: the sibling `spawnedCwd` field on the session **entry** is still normalized by the core session-create owner (`src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, `normalizeOptionalString`), and supervision bindings are normalized by `conversation-binding-data.ts`; both are separate owners with their own contracts and are intentionally not touched here. This PR fixes the transcript-header path end to end.

Classification: `behavior-completing` (extends the literal-path contract to the node-adoption transcript owner).

## User Impact

Continuing a node-hosted Codex session from a whitespace-named directory now records the literal directory in the transcript header, so subsequent turns resolve files in the directory the session actually started in.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `1d0be4e8f` (branch `fix/codex-literal-catalog-cwd`)

- Decision surface: the node catalog record's `cwd` produced by the Codex CLI session metadata
- Recorder/readback boundary: the `cwd` argument recorded by the transcript-import boundary mock, asserted byte-for-byte
- Acceptance RED: on current main, the new assertion failed — the importer received `cwd: "/tmp/oc-proof"` (trimmed) instead of the literal `" /tmp/oc-proof "`; the 7 pre-existing tests passed (1 failed / 7 passed)
- Acceptance GREEN: on exact head, all 8 tests pass, with the literal cwd observed at the import boundary
- Legal controls: the pre-existing adoption matrix is unchanged and green (stale-locator rejection, home-change rejection, source-less pages, finalization guards, marker reuse); the untouched `session-catalog-adoption.test.ts` lane also passes 21/21 on the candidate
- Cleanup: fixture-scoped wire doubles only; no Gateway, session, token, or config touched

prs.title: fix(agents): narrow union-parameter tools under Gateway tool policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: tools whose parameters are a `Type.Union` of action variants (`codex_threads`, `feishu_perm`, `feishu_wiki`, `feishu_drive`, `feishu_docx`) are unusable whenever `tools.gatewayPolicy` restricts their actions — the policy layer refused them with "Gateway tool policy requires \<tool\> to declare a top-level string action field" on every turn.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can now restrict these union-parameter tools to specific actions (e.g. allow `codex_threads` `list` only) instead of the tool being hard-refused for every call; variants advertising actions the policy forbids are no longer published in the tool schema.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `src/agents/gateway-tool-policy.ts`, when `schema.anyOf` is present, `narrowActions` now iterates each union variant, reads `action.const` or `action.enum` from the variant's properties, and keeps only variants whose action is listed in `tools.gatewayPolicy.actions.<tool>`. For a variant whose `action` declares a multi-value enum, the enum is intersected with the policy allowlist and the variant's action schema is rewritten, so the published schema never advertises actions the policy forbids; a variant left with no allowed action is dropped, and the tool is withheld when no variant remains. The original refusal is preserved for variants that cannot be narrowed (no `properties`, no `action`, or neither `const`/`enum`).

No field-level path or execution-side assertion was changed; the execution-layer check (`createGatewayToolPolicyAssertion`) is untouched and still enforces `args.action` at call time. Precedent: #186395 fixed the same failure mode for `personal_instructions` by narrowing on the top-level `action` field; this extends the same contract to union-parameter variants.

Affected tools (all declare union-parameter schemas blocked by the refusal when an action policy is configured): `codex_threads` (extensions/codex/src/native-thread-tool.ts), `feishu_perm`, `feishu_wiki`, `feishu_drive`, `feishu_docx` (extensions/feishu).

## Evidence

- Unit red/green on server (docker, Node v24, `--maxWorkers=1`), head `058479d1ba0`:
  - Base (`19bda5c6c6cb` source + new tests): `Tests 1 failed | 12 passed (13)` — the only failure is the new regression test "intersects a union member's action enum with the policy allowlist", which exposes the enum variant being kept whole and still advertising a policy-forbidden action.
  - Candidate (`058479d1ba0`): `Tests 13 passed (13)`; `pnpm test src/agents/gateway-tool-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` wall time ≈ 31s (tests themselves ~5% of that).
  - Earlier red/green for the base union narrowing (`e00a185728d` → `1201c5d905b`): `2 failed | 11 passed` → `13 passed (13)`.
- Shipped-run on an isolated live Gateway (`gateway.mode: local`, token auth, `tools.gatewayPolicy.allow: ["codex_threads"]`, `actions.codex_threads: ["list"]`; codex plugin enabled with `appServer.command` pointing at the real Codex CLI 0.164.0 binary; synthetic `CODEX_HOME` containing exactly one thread seeded through a real `thread/start` + `turn/start` against that binary, so its `state_5.sqlite` records the rollout path consistently). Two WS clients connect over loopback with the CLI client identity: an owner client granted `["operator.admin","operator.read","operator.write"]` and a non-owner client granted `["operator.read","operator.write"]` (granted scopes verified in the connect responses). All fixtures are synthetic; the auth token is a throwaway value redacted below.
  - Base: `tools.invoke {name:"codex_threads", args:{action:"list"}}` → `Gateway tool policy requires codex_threads to declare a top-level string action field.`
  - **Allowed execution (owner client, `action=list`)** → `ok:true`; the plugin spawned the real `codex app-server` child (its process environment verified to carry the synthetic `CODEX_HOME`) and native `thread/list` returned the seeded thread:
    ```json
    {
      "data": [
        {
          "id": "01a1872f-1b27-7592-bec7-2089d23c3194",
          "preview": "hello offline",
          "modelProvider": "openai",
          "model": "gpt-5.4",
          "status": { "type": "notLoaded" },
          "path": "/ws/.proof/codex-home/sessions/2026/10/29/rollout-2026-10-29T10-22-53-01a1872f-1b27-7592-bec7-2089d23c3194.jsonl",
          "cliVersion": "0.164.0",
          "originator": "openclaw",
          "source": "vscode"
        }
      ],
      "nextCursor": null,
      "backwardsCursor": "2026-10-29T10:22:55.288Z"
    }
    ```
  - **Forbidden-action rejection (owner client, `action=read`)** → `{"ok":false,"toolName":"codex_threads","error":{"code":"internal_error","message":"Gateway tool policy denies codex_threads action \"read\"."}}`
  - **Non-owner rejection before native I/O (non-owner client, `action=list`)** → the invocation is rejected at the tool boundary before any Codex app-server call; the WS response is intentionally generic (`"message":"tool execution failed"`), and the Gateway server log records the exact assertion:
    ```
    [tools-invoke] tool execution failed: Error: Codex native thread access requires an owner-authorized sender.
    ```
- Static gates: `tsgo:core` EXIT 0; `oxlint` 0 warnings / 0 errors; `oxfmt --check` PASS; `test-lines` ratchet PASS (6,246,120 vs ceiling 6,320,170, slack 74,050; baseline untouched).

**Not tested / honest gaps.**

- The four Feishu tools were not each booted in an isolated live Gateway; the same `narrowActions` code path is covered by the unit suite and the `codex_threads` shipped-run above, which exercises the full chain end to end (plugin → spawned real `codex app-server` → native `thread/list` → result).
- The non-owner rejection surfaces as a generic WS error message by design (details stay in the server log); the server log line above is the authoritative boundary evidence.
- The shipped-run used the source CLI entry point (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts`) rather than a dist bundle; its argv/config/state path is identical to the packaged CLI.

**Cleanup.** Isolated proof state/config lives only in the temporary container tree and was not merged into any production Gateway, token, or config.

Two-way door: reverting restores the old search behavior; this change does not write or migrate native sessions. Blast radius is OpenCode catalog text filtering. Wrong normalization could omit a result or add a textual match, while exact-ID validation and continuation ownership remain unchanged.

prs.title: feat(control-ui): show worker lifecycle and telemetry
prs.body:
Closes #163982

## What Problem This Solves

The Systems page hides worker lifecycle history, can leave a reclaimed worker shown as `Attached` until reload, and does not connect live dedicated workers to the CPU, memory, and disk telemetry their enrolled nodes already report.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish active workers from recent destroyed or failed workers, inspect lifecycle/provider/profile/lease/error details, see terminal state changes without reloading, and troubleshoot or right-size live dedicated workers from the same resource graphs used for base systems.

Workers without dedicated node telemetry show an explicit not-reported state. Shared-host workers do not expose whole-host statistics as if those measurements belonged to one worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Systems inventory now retains terminal worker records, groups active and historical workers separately, and refreshes canonical `environments.list` data when durable `sessions.changed` events or worker placement changes arrive.

For dedicated workers, the Gateway additionally projects the enrolled node identity. The Systems inventory joins that exact identity to `node.list`, reuses the existing host-stat history and graphs, and continues polling while the worker is selected. No provider shell probe, SSH command, or second telemetry poller is introduced.

## Evidence

### October27 identification repair

Short worker IDs now remain visible beside lifecycle status. [Exact-head regression results and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163995#issuecomment-6456168501). This fixes the same-profile identification finding; history-policy acceptance and main integration remain pending.

### Earlier lifecycle and telemetry evidence

The following results document earlier tested revisions; they are not a new full-suite or live-runtime qualification of the October27 head.

Live Apple Container lifecycle, captured from the same Systems page without a reload:

**Before reclaim — worker is Attached**

![Systems sidebar showing an attached worker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff22cbbe-35d0-4d25-a08c-6799626eb040)

**After reclaim — worker moved to Recent worker history as Destroyed**

![Systems sidebar showing the reclaimed worker as destroyed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee681765-dd7b-4cad-adf6-0708837275eb)

- Live transition observed in about one second and repeated twice without reloading.
- Disposable live telemetry proof: an Apple Container worker reached `ready`, published a dedicated node identity, and reported Linux host stats with 5 CPUs, load averages, 4.26 GB memory capacity, and 541.13 GB disk capacity through `node.list`. The worker was reclaimed; provider and Apple Container inventories were empty afterward.
- Focused validation:
  - Gateway environment projection: 20/20 pass.
  - Gateway protocol schema: 22/22 pass.
  - Systems telemetry/UI: 36/36 pass, including distinct session and telemetry-node names.
  - Changed-file formatting and lint: pass.
  - Core and UI typechecks: pass.
  - Production Control UI build: pass.
- Earlier branch-wide validation:
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: pass (335.15 s).
  - `pnpm test:changed`: 20,926 pass / 3 skip; one unrelated `shell-viewport.test.ts` RAF-coalescing assertion failed under the full parallel lane, then passed 3/3 isolated reruns (11/11 each).
  - Upstream `control-ui-performance`: pass. The local check showed a nondeterministic gzip edge 24–30 B over the 373,454 B startup limit while raw startup JS stayed exactly 1,208,683 B with and without the Systems reconciliation helper, confirming this patch does not change the startup asset set.
  - Repo autoreview helper was attempted but unavailable because its local Codex credential returned HTTP 401; no review verdict was produced.

The two older `Destroying` rows visible in the screenshots predate this worker and are a separate provider-history cleanup issue.

prs.title: feat(knowledge): derive entity Timelines from records instead of page prose
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Knowledge entity pages stop accepting new information once their agent-written `## Timeline` section pushes them past the page size budget (eight of the most-linked people pages in a real vault currently refuse new Timeline lines; the Timeline is 57% of entity page text overall).

## User Impact

User impact: an entity's Timeline is now built from records (one row per dated source, with that source's note about the entity and its claim count) and shown on the record page, so it no longer grows the page body. Agents stop writing Timeline lines and retire existing written Timeline sections as they edit pages; no bulk migration runs. Until a page's written section is retired, the record page shows both.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every written Timeline entry's date and link already existed as a claim or relationship, so the Timeline can be derived instead of authored. `knowledge_timeline` gains `group: "source"` (entity required): rows come from relationships between the entity and a source page, and from claims that name the entity with a `source_page`. A row's note is the body of that relationship (`attended` for meeting participants, `discusses` otherwise), falling back to the source's event claim. Claims with no dated source, or dated apart from their source, keep their own rows. Row notes render as Markdown: wikilinks to records in scope are returned as `links` and open the record, and internal comments are hidden.

Skills now save a source's contribution to an entity as that one-sentence relationship body. When an agent edits a page that still has a written Timeline, or a write is rejected for size, it turns each entry into a `discusses` note or an event claim, checks every entry now appears in the derived rows, then deletes the section (shrinking edits always pass the budget; revision history keeps the text). The budget rejection message says never to extract a written Timeline to another page.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/knowledge`: 59 files, 444 tests passed, including a new grouping test (notes, source-event fallback, standalone and past-dated claims, superseded notes, date range and paging, input validation) and the updated budget-message assertion.
- `pnpm check:changed`: extension typecheck and test typecheck pass; changed Knowledge files are lint-clean. Remaining lint/dead-export reports were in files outside this change.
- `node scripts/sync-skill-references.mjs --check`: generated skill references in sync.
- Retirement trial on the live vault: one person page's 50-entry written Timeline was retired by the skill steps (15 source notes, 10 dated event claims; the other 25 entries already had notes). The derived Timeline went from 42 to 52 rows and covered every entry, then the section was deleted (page 12,848 → 2,264 chars).
- Live operator Gateway running this branch (Knowledge only): Graham McBain's derived Timeline returned 45 source rows; after the link fix, 9 of the first 20 notes carry resolved links, checked in the Control UI by the operator.
- Isolated Gateway built from this branch with a synthetic vault (no real data). Before = `origin/main` record page bundle, after = this branch. No browser page errors.

Before (no derived Timeline):

![Before: Riley Chen record page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4568cf0-99d4-47ae-afb9-640add2298cd)

After (desktop):

![After: Riley Chen record page with derived Timeline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/889be4d4-9168-48d0-a24e-b03e4805b6be)

After, page still carrying a written Timeline (shown alongside until retired):

![After: Morgan Hale record page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6640b7d7-c690-4d49-86bf-7b11e0839640)

After (420px):

![After: mobile width](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c431cf7f-a472-41af-b68d-15a5f7d355c5)

Screenshots predate a review fix that only changes which rows appear in edge cases (past-dated claims, superseded notes), not the layout.
