prs.title: refactor(model-catalog): bundled facts fill hosted gaps; Mistral reads effort from rows
prs.body:
Stacked on openclaw/openclaw#187694, #187695 and #187707. This PR is the last two commits.

## What Problem This Solves

Two blockers to moving model facts into catalog data for every provider:

1. A hosted row replaces the bundled row wholesale, so a fact added to a manifest is invisible until the hosted catalog republishes. Each plugin had to re-read its own manifest to cover that gap (#187695 does this for Kimi).
2. Mistral decides reasoning-effort support by an exact-ID set in two places (plugin and `@openclaw/ai` transport).

## User Impact

No user-visible change on released installs or on `main`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Core (`src/model-catalog/manifest-planner.ts`):** the hosted row still wins, but `thinkingLevelMap` and compat keys it omits fall back to the bundled row. Checked against the served v2 catalog: no hosted row omits a bundled thinking or compat fact today, so nothing changes now. Trade-off: a hosted row can override a bundled fact but can no longer delete it for releases that bundle it.
- **Mistral:** the three reasoning rows carry their level → `reasoning_effort` map as `thinkingLevelMap`. The thinking profile, compat patch and transport read it; the ID sets are gone. `adaptive` (no catalog field yet) stays a Mistral rule, sent as `high`. Putting the same facts in `compat.reasoningEffortMap` was **not** zero-diff (released readers would start sending `reasoning_effort` on all three rows), so the data uses `thinkingLevelMap`.

## Evidence

- `pnpm catalog:compare-released --candidate <bundle>` (bundle built offline from this branch with `scripts/publish-model-catalog.mts`): latest, extended-stable and beta show 0 changes to offered levels, defaults and request bodies. The only lines are `model.thinkingLevelMap.*` echoes of the added data (plus the Kimi rows from #187694).
- `extensions/mistral/api.test.ts` now feeds the manifest rows and still expects the exact previous profile and compat patch.
- `packages/ai` Mistral transport tests pass with row compat; the planner test covers fill and hosted-wins.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions` clean. The catalog-ID guard allowlist shrinks by one file.

Merge danger: two-way door. Blast radius: Mistral reasoning rows; any hosted row that omits a bundled compat or map key (none today).


### Review follow-up

`@openclaw/ai` is also used standalone, where models carry no catalog compat. The Mistral transport now reads declared `compat.supportsReasoningEffort` first and falls back to the three shipped reasoning-effort IDs for bare models, so standalone callers keep their behavior (new test: a bare `mistral-small-latest` model still sends `reasoningEffort`). The guard allowlist keeps `packages/ai/src/providers/mistral.ts` for that fallback.



### Released readers incl. new stable (2026-10-29, after 2026.10.9 shipped)

`pnpm catalog:compare-released` with a baseline built from current `origin/main` and the candidate from this stack (same models.dev snapshot, current timestamps so 2026.10.9 accepts both refreshes):

```
2026.10.9 (latest): no offered-level, default or request-body change (model.* echo lines only)
2026.9.35 (extended-stable): same
2026.10.10-beta.4 (beta): same
```

Behavior lines other than `model.*` echoes: **0** on all three releases, for #187694 alone and for the full stack.

### Upgrade from 2026.10.9

Isolated state (sandboxed HOME/OPENCLAW_HOME/OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR): released 2026.10.9 Gateway runs `kimi/k3 --thinking low` and stores the session; then `doctor --fix` (normal update step) and this stack's Gateway on the same state: `config validate` passes, the saved session resumes at `low`, and `moonshot/kimi-k3` runs at `max`.


### Review follow-up: configured routes without a map

A configured Mistral route (for example a proxy base URL) may list a bundled model without its `thinkingLevelMap`. The compat patch now reads that model's map from the bundled row instead of turning `supportsReasoningEffort` off. New test: a configured `mistral-small-latest` row with only `compat.supportsReasoningEffort: true` keeps effort support and the `none`/`high` map.



The Mistral thinking hook shares the same bundled-map fallback, so a configured proxy row for a bundled reasoning model keeps its default (`off`) and levels (incl. `adaptive`, `xhigh`, `max`). New test fails on the previous head.



Partial or empty configured maps merge over the bundled map per key (null still excludes a level), so `{ max: "high" }` or `{}` keeps the full profile and its `off` default. Tests for partial, empty and null-exclusion maps fail on the previous head.

prs.title: refactor(kimi): read Kimi thinking policy from catalog rows
prs.body:
Stacked on openclaw/openclaw#187694 (catalog data). Land that first; this PR's first two commits are that PR.

## What Problem This Solves

A new Kimi model needs code edits in several exact-ID lists before thinking works. With this PR, a Moonshot or Kimi Code row's `thinkingLevelMap` and `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts` decide it, so the next Kimi model is a manifest row.

## User Impact

No user-visible change for shipped Kimi routes on `main` (proof below). A new hosted row with the same data gets the same behavior without a release.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removed:

- `extensions/moonshot`: `KIMI_K3_MODEL_IDS`, `ALWAYS_THINKING_PROFILES`; native video now reads the bundled row's `input`.
- `src/llm/.../moonshot-thinking.ts`: `MOONSHOT_ALWAYS_THINKING`. `off: null` means always on; the last listed effort is the fixed `reasoning_effort` (direct Moonshot only, as before); no efforts means a plain on switch.
- `extensions/kimi-coding`: `KIMI_K3_1_MODEL_IDS`, `KIMI_K3_MODEL_IDS`, `KIMI_K3_LEGACY_MODEL_IDS`, and the K3.1 part of the enabled-only list. K3 shape = row lists efforts; enabled-only = row maps `off` to null. Aliases go through the manifest alias map.

Hosted rows win; when a hosted row lacks the facts (configured models, or hosted rows published before openclaw/openclaw#187694), the plugin reads its bundled manifest row.

Kept as cited fallbacks (catalog cannot carry them without changing released installs):

- Kimi Code `kimi-k3`: self-hosted wire ID with no row; K3 policy, default `off`.
- Kimi Code `kimi-for-coding`(`-highspeed`) enabled-only: released readers still offer `off`, so `off: null` in hosted data would change them.
- `REASONING_CONTENT_REPLAY_MODEL_IDS` Kimi entries: transcript policy reads only the model ID, and OpenRouter/custom routes have no row. Comment added.

## Evidence

**Before/after golden matrix** (local, not committed: ~24k snapshot lines). Recorded on the pre-change code, rerun on this head:

- Moonshot, 21 cases: every manifest row, every row as the served catalog has it today, and bare IDs. Each × native/proxy base URL × stream/simple × 5 levels: profile, `isModernModelRef`, normalized input, `options.reasoning`, final request body; plus the SDK wrapper on every manifest row for `moonshot` and another provider.
- Kimi Code, 20 cases: manifest, served and bare rows (`kimi-k3`, `KIMI-K3`, `k3[1m]`, `kimi-code`, `k2p5`, …) × anthropic-messages/openai-completions × 9 levels × stream/simple: profile, normalized map, `options.reasoning`, request model facts and body.
- Result: **40 of 41 identical.** One diff: model ID `constructor`. The old core map lookup hit `Object.prototype.constructor` and treated it as always-thinking; now it is not (the plugin test already expected this).

**SDK note:** the deprecated `createMoonshotThinkingWrapper` / `moonshot-thinking` stream family now needs the row facts on the model instead of matching IDs. No bundled caller changes: Moonshot fills the facts from its manifest, and Ollama's `:cloud` IDs never matched the old list. The two core tests that drove the family with bare IDs now pass the row facts.

**New tests** (fail on the old code): a Moonshot row with `off: null` + `["max"]` and no bundled entry gets the max-only profile and `reasoning_effort: "max"`; a Kimi Code row with efforts + `off: null` gets adaptive thinking and ignores `off`.

**Isolated Gateway, real turns** (task-owned HOME/OPENCLAW_HOME/OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, loopback port 19437, keys from env):

| Turn | Result |
|---|---|
| `moonshot/kimi-k3` | OK, thinking `max` |
| `moonshot/kimi-k3 --thinking low` | rejected: "Use one of: max, ultra" |
| `moonshot/kimi-k3.1-pro` | OK, thinking `max` |
| `moonshot/kimi-k2.7-code` | OK, thinking `low` (on) |
| `kimi/k3` | OK, thinking `high` |
| `kimi/k3 --thinking off` | OK, thinking `off` |
| `kimi/k3.1-pro` | OK, thinking `high` |
| `kimi/k3.1-pro --thinking off` | rejected: off not offered |

**Checks:** `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`; Moonshot, Kimi Code, OpenCode, Ollama, OpenRouter suites; `provider-stream`, Moonshot extra-params, model-catalog tests.

pr-simplify: production +163/−88. The growth is the manifest fallback (so hosted rows published before openclaw/openclaw#187694, and configured models, keep today's behavior) and a small effort reader per plugin (plugins cannot import the core one). Tests +80/−8.

Merge danger: two-way door (pure code; revert restores the lists). Blast radius: Moonshot and Kimi Code thinking profile and request shape on `main`; third-party users of the deprecated Moonshot SDK wrapper with bare IDs.



### Released readers incl. new stable (2026-10-29, after 2026.10.9 shipped)

`pnpm catalog:compare-released` with a baseline built from current `origin/main` and the candidate from this stack (same models.dev snapshot, current timestamps so 2026.10.9 accepts both refreshes):

```
2026.10.9 (latest): no offered-level, default or request-body change (model.* echo lines only)
2026.9.35 (extended-stable): same
2026.10.10-beta.4 (beta): same
```

Behavior lines other than `model.*` echoes: **0** on all three releases, for #187694 alone and for the full stack.

### Upgrade from 2026.10.9

Isolated state (sandboxed HOME/OPENCLAW_HOME/OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR): released 2026.10.9 Gateway runs `kimi/k3 --thinking low` and stores the session; then `doctor --fix` (normal update step) and this stack's Gateway on the same state: `config validate` passes, the saved session resumes at `low`, and `moonshot/kimi-k3` runs at `max`.

### Review follow-up: SDK contract

Published plugins call `createMoonshotThinkingWrapper` / the `moonshot-thinking` stream family with bare models. Those keep the shipped always-thinking IDs (cited `LEGACY_ALWAYS_THINKING` table in core); models carrying a `thinkingLevelMap` follow the row. The SDK tests are back to bare models and pass unchanged from `main`.


### Review follow-up: configured partial maps

A configured `moonshot/kimi-k3` row with a partial `thinkingLevelMap` (for example `{ max: "max" }` or `{}`) now merges over the bundled row per key, so `off: null` and max-only survive. The core SDK wrapper treats a map that omits `off` like a bare model and keeps the shipped always-thinking contract. New tests (plugin profile + outgoing payload, and the SDK wrapper) fail on the previous head.



SDK callers that pass a map with `off: null` but no effort metadata (no `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts`) keep the fixed `max` effort for the shipped K3 IDs. The SDK regression now covers `{ max: "max" }` and `{ off: null, max: "max" }`; the second fails on the previous head.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Kimi thinking facts live only in exact-ID code lists, so K3.1 needed four list edits and still missed routes. This PR records the facts the code ships today as catalog data, with no behavior change. A follow-up PR (stacked) makes the code read this data and deletes the lists.

## User Impact

No user-visible change on released installs or on `main`. The hosted catalog picks up these rows within ~4 h of merge; released readers behave the same with them.

## Why This Change Was Made

First family migration of the models/catalog cleanup. Each row now carries what its route does today, using only existing fields:

| Route rows | Data added | Matches the code that ships |
|---|---|---|
| `moonshot/kimi-k3` | `thinkingLevelMap` low/high → `null`; `supportedReasoningEfforts: ["max"]` | Direct Moonshot K3 offers and sends only `max` (fixes the manifest/code disagreement) |
| `moonshot/kimi-k3.1-pro`, `-highspeed` (new manifest rows) | same as K3 | K3.1 shares K3's contract |
| `moonshot/kimi-k2.7-code`, `-highspeed` | `thinkingLevelMap.off: null` | always-on thinking |
| `moonshot` K3 rows | `input` adds `video` | native video; the publisher strips `video` for released readers, so hosted rows are unchanged |
| `kimi/k3`, `kimi/k3-256k` | `supportedReasoningEfforts: ["low","high","max"]` | K3 effort/adaptive request shape |
| `kimi/k3.1-pro`, `-highspeed` (new manifest rows) | K3 map plus `off: null`, same efforts | Kimi Code rejects disabled thinking for K3.1 (probe below) |

Left out on purpose: `kimi/kimi-for-coding` `off: null`. Released Kimi Code readers still offer `off` there, so the data would change them (compare showed `offered ["off","low","ultra"] → ["low","ultra"]`). `main`'s enabled-only rule for those rows stays a cited code fallback.

The two new Kimi Code K3.1 rows also appear in the bundled static provider config (the hosted catalog already lists them); `provider-catalog.test.ts` is updated for that.

- `moonshot/kimi-k3`: existing probe from 2026-10-29 (all 7 levels → 200).

prs.title: test(plugins): freeze production code that names catalog row IDs
prs.body:
Stacked on openclaw/openclaw#187694 and openclaw/openclaw#187695; the last commit is this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Model launches keep adding IDs to code lists instead of catalog rows (35 of 37 launches since July changed code). Nothing stops a new list entry today.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Contributors see a failing contract test when production code starts naming a catalog row ID.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/plugins/contracts/catalog-model-id-rules.contract.test.ts` reads every bundled manifest row ID (222 today) and lists each production `.ts` file under `extensions/`, `src/` and `packages/` that names one as a string literal. The result must equal the frozen `catalog-model-id-rules.allowlist.json` (126 files, 322 names today):

- A new name fails: move the fact into the row, or add the entry with its reason in the PR.
- A removed name fails until the allowlist shrinks, so the list only gets smaller.

It is a test, not a CI hard block. Also drops two unused Moonshot K2.7 ID exports left after #187695.

## Evidence

- Passes on this head.
- Adding `new Set(["kimi-k3.1-pro"])` to `extensions/moonshot/native-video.ts` fails it with that file and ID in the diff.
- Inventory behind the allowlist: 384 exact-ID matchers (52 coverable by existing fields today, 131 kept for routes with no catalog row, 201 needing new fields), kept in the maintainer handoff notes.

Merge danger: two-way door (test only). Blast radius: contributors adding model IDs to code.


### Review follow-up

The literal scan now includes short catalog IDs (no minimum length). Two more names joined the allowlist (`d1` in liquid-ai, `hy3` in tencent): 127 files, 324 names.



### Released readers incl. new stable (2026-10-29, after 2026.10.9 shipped)

`pnpm catalog:compare-released` with a baseline built from current `origin/main` and the candidate from this stack (same models.dev snapshot, current timestamps so 2026.10.9 accepts both refreshes):

```
2026.10.9 (latest): no offered-level, default or request-body change (model.* echo lines only)
2026.9.35 (extended-stable): same
2026.10.10-beta.4 (beta): same
```

Behavior lines other than `model.*` echoes: **0** on all three releases, for #187694 alone and for the full stack.

### Upgrade from 2026.10.9

Isolated state (sandboxed HOME/OPENCLAW_HOME/OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR): released 2026.10.9 Gateway runs `kimi/k3 --thinking low` and stores the session; then `doctor --fix` (normal update step) and this stack's Gateway on the same state: `config validate` passes, the saved session resumes at `low`, and `moonshot/kimi-k3` runs at `max`.

### On the "low-value test" note

What the guard does: a new model-ID literal in production code cannot land without showing up in review, and the allowlist only shrinks as migrations move facts into catalog rows (removing a name fails until the entry goes too). It is a notice ratchet over source spellings, not a behavior proof; `catalog-thinking-profiles.contract.test.ts` (#187730) proves that row data produces the expected thinking profiles.

Not changed here: tying each allowlisted name to the catalog field that should replace it would mean encoding the 384-row matcher inventory into the test. That is a per-matcher judgment, not a cheap check, and it would make every migration edit two lists. Known limits, accepted: IDs built at runtime (prefix or regex matches) are not caught, and moving a file needs an allowlist edit.

prs.title: fix: align task-owner tests with installed service environment
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The scheduled-task stop suite fails its two validated-owner cases after #187901: when an owner becomes unknown or loses its lease, the test still expects PID start-time probes to receive the inspecting CLI’s profile. The installed launcher in this fixture declares only the Gateway port, so the service environment correctly omits that caller-only selector.

## User Impact

This is a test-only correction with no change to Windows task operations. It restores the existing checks for completing termination of the captured process while retaining the exact PID, five-second probe bound, graceful-before-forced ordering, foreign-process exclusion, and prohibition on a kill-tree fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The assertion now names the fixture’s expected service environment directly: its user directory, application-data directory, and installed port. It remains an exact environment comparison and does not derive its answer from the production merge helper. The shared launcher and production environment-isolation contract remain unchanged.

The explicit assertion needs five additional test lines, covered by one matching allocation record. No test case or helper is added.

## Evidence

The clean baseline at 9559c51dd05184a34e7f791ce950c29c9922765c ran all 30 stop-suite cases: 28 passed and these two failed solely because the expected environment contained `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=default`. The fixture, environment merge, process owner and determining test inputs are unchanged at this branch’s fe8a0ce9b4e89d48e7e0ccbcd572d0924acce823 base.

On the candidate, remote formatting, lint, and selected production/test type checks passed. All 131 cases across the seven selected files passed: the full scheduled-task stop suite, its shared-fixture consumers, and the environment-merge owner. The six-file daemon cohort took 36.63 seconds; the complete selected test batch took 39.49 seconds. Hosted CI passed on this exact head. These are Linux-hosted tests with mocked Windows process boundaries; they do not claim a real Windows Task Scheduler run.

prs.title: fix: allow guest tool previews for accessible sessions
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes #187912. A guest with `operator.sessions.read` can open their own conversation but cannot inspect its effective tools: the preview request stops at `missing scope: operator.read` before the inventory is built. Granting general Gateway read access is unnecessary for this session-bound view and would expose unrelated diagnostics. ## User Impact Session readers can preview tools for conversations they are currently allowed to read. Missing and inaccessible sessions remain unavailable, and the request does not grant general read access or tool-execution authority. Full operator readers and administrators retain the existing diagnostic response. The guest preview preserves effective tool names, groups, core summaries, and the GitHub owner's filtered action summary. Runtime descriptions, configuration diagnostics, and MCP connection details are omitted from the narrow response. Unexpected failures return a short retry message while retaining the technical error in Gateway logs. ## Why This Change Was Made The existing session-read admission policy did not include `tools.effective`. The handler now uses that policy and the shared retained session-read owner, which checks profile authority, session visibility, and the selected row again after asynchronous inventory work. This also prevents an in-flight preview from being returned after access is revoked. Response filtering happens after inventory resolution. Cached inventories remain independent of the requester, so a guest read cannot redact the later administrator response. The change reuses the existing inventory and authorization owners; it adds no scope, configuration option, or protocol field. ## Evidence The authenticated WebSocket regression failed on the baseline with the reported missing-scope error after successful narrow-scope connection and `users.self`. It now exercises actual authentication, request admission, session storage and inventory. The shared-session case pauses the inventory owner's existing harness callback, revokes visibility over an authenticated administrator socket, waits for that mutation to commit, then resumes the read and verifies a hidden-session error with no payload. A separate dispatcher fixture supplies sensitive inventory fields to check projection, cache preservation and unexpected-error privacy. Remote formatting, lint, all seven selected type groups and both focused regressions passed on 0172eeade3db1bb2571df3ca4dcc3252de72ae69 (tree d6271ff163281d47f6967cdd4516d0b2db338b85). The related batch passed 170 cases on unchanged surrounding paths. Single-worker measurements: authenticated socket test 15.304 seconds (74.19-second Vitest wall time); dispatcher test 2.616 seconds (57.12-second wall time). A dedicated 345-line allocation covers these authentication and disclosure boundaries. Hosted CI reported 7.210 seconds for the WebSocket test and 0.879 seconds for the dispatcher test. A real guest Gateway and model request changed from `unavailable` / missing `operator.read` to `live-session` with 69 preview entries under unchanged guest scopes. Own and allowed Home sessions succeed; an omitted key is invalid; a foreign draft returns hidden not-found with no payload. In a warm inventory containing two MCP tools, guest responses preserve server/tool identities while both description fields are empty; the administrator response retains the original descriptions and diagnostics. Execution permission remains separate from preview availability. The live source is baseline 193be43cb0541a2d0941a3b6b28f183f90691df0 plus production patch ec85de6325e74b1c3111493a48cc37dd34ae6f90, producing 7783c99dff94212597cd51933737ba7df75d90c2. The startup prerequisite and guest configuration are constant. The final commit changes only tests; production and documentation are byte-identical to that tested patch. Independent engineering review completed clean on 0172eea. Autoreview (P0–P3) is clean for the production patch and the final test-only delta. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40970498955) and the remaining selected checks passed. [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187925#issuecomment-6509808926) rated the same head Platinum with no findings. An earlier Android 16K run reported a TLS enforcement-order mismatch; both native Android lanes passed on the final head, without an Android source change. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Guest capability check fails with missing operator\.read](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/579a4334-de1c-46bf-b095-c251e3b3a136) | ![The same guest sees a session\-scoped capability result](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6bb4d5b9-b793-4ef3-8169-a6fba8065a5d) | ### Actual guest capability request through completion https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ad7316a-7e46-4784-affe-84465c61b9c4 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 193be43cb0541a2d0941a3b6b28f183f90691df0 - Exact head: `7783c99dff94212597cd51933737ba7df75d90c2` - Scenario: An authenticated guest asks session\_status for capabilities in the current owned conversation\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw 2026\.10\.9, build 2026\.10\.9\-7783c99dff94\-2026\-10\-29T22\-15\-28\.444Z\. Tested composition: baseline 193be43 plus the production patch ec85de6 from PR \#187925; the startup prerequisite and guest configuration are held constant\. - Before: unavailable — missing scope: operator\.read - After: live\-session — 69 preview entries - Guest authority: operator\.sessions\.read and operator\.sessions\.write, unchanged - Disclosure controls: Inaccessible session: no payload\. MCP identities retained; runtime descriptions omitted\. - Same owned session, requester and configuration - Fixed 1280×720 browser viewport; identical 970×662 crop - Actual model tool request and native Gateway outcome verified - Preview entries do not grant tool\-execution authority - The prepared request becomes the user message at the recorded 0\.357\-second submission event - Both stills show the settled result; natural chat positioning differs with response length, and no layout comparison is claimed - All 240 source frames and full\-resolution start/submitted/settled encoded frames inspected; no private toolbar/sidebar content - PR head 0172eeade3db1bb2571df3ca4dcc3252de72ae69 changes tests only after the tested production patch; production and documentation are byte\-identical

prs.title: fix(plugins): show tool guidance only while the tool is callable
prs.body:
Related: #173605

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the `diffs` plugin adds its tool guidance to every system prompt, including runs where the `diffs` tool is denied and ACP runs, which have no OpenClaw tools. Plugins also had no way to give tool guidance that appears only while their tool is callable: Codex, Agents API and Copilot each hard-coded the Skill Workshop text instead.

## User Impact

- A run that cannot call `diffs` no longer gets diffs guidance in its prompt.
- Plugin authors can set `promptGuidance` on `api.registerTool(...)`. The guidance appears on every bundled harness only while one of the registration's tools is callable, including tools found through Tool Search.
- `plugins.entries.<id>.hooks.allowPromptInjection: false` still keeps the tool and drops only its guidance, as the diffs docs describe.
- No config change or migration. The Skill Workshop guidance is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

One owner, `listToolPromptGuidance(callableToolNames)`, now decides which tool guidance a run gets. It covers core tools (Skill Workshop) and plugin tool registrations. The embedded system prompt and the Codex, Agents API and Copilot harnesses all call it with their callable tool names. Plugin sections are ordered by plugin id, so plugin load order does not change prompt bytes.

- `diffs` moves its guidance from an unconditional `before_prompt_build` hook to `promptGuidance` on its tool registration.
- A registration with `promptGuidance` must name its tools. Otherwise the guidance can never be gated, so registration fails with a diagnostic.
- `buildSkillWorkshopPromptSection` and `SKILL_WORKSHOP_TOOL_NAME` in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` stay exported unchanged and are marked deprecated, with no removal date. No bundled plugin uses them now. On public ClawHub (checked 2026-10-29) the only users are the first-party `@openclaw/codex` and `@openclaw/copilot` releases, which this PR moves to the new helper; no third-party plugin uses them. About 17% of ClawHub plugins had partial or failed static analysis, so usage there is unknown.

What disappeared: the three harness copies of the Workshop gate and the unconditional diffs `before_prompt_build` hook. Diff against `main`: production +98/-30 (the new owner, the registration option, its rejection and opt-out, and the deprecated SDK wrappers), tests +112/-25, docs +17/-2.

This is the first step from the #173605 audit: build hooks with a second consumer before any Workshop move. Here the consumers are `diffs` and Skill Workshop.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New owner tests (`src/agents/tool-prompt-guidance.test.ts`): guidance shown when the tool is visible or deferred, absent when denied; order independent of load order; unnamed registration rejected | pass. The gating test fails when the callable check is removed. |
| Opt-out test: `allowPromptInjection=false` keeps the tool, drops its guidance, records a warning | passes |
| Workshop contract test from #173557 (`system-prompt.workshop-contract.test.ts`), unedited | passes |
| `system-prompt.test.ts` (includes deferred Code Mode Workshop case) | passes |
| Codex, Agents API, Copilot harness prompt tests | 194 pass |

Closes #140128

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS CLI selection changing when the app inspects a ready managed CLI while an external CLI is selected.

## User Impact

Inspecting installations no longer changes the selected CLI. A successful managed install or update still selects the verified managed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed inspection returns status without persisting selection. Discovery retains its existing selection behavior, while installation and update record the managed CLI only after their success checks. No preference keys or formats changed, and no CLI is removed.

## Evidence

Current product head: `a2c6197e80d459f03b88b8de3030e8ca67e6ddda`. The GitHub web merge on 29 October combined prior head `4298606a9e38b4665dc014a71fd81bfb451d97af` with main `878e682ecc3228e7bb9a535254e0bddaa4d97e7f`. All earlier proof below remains pinned to its actual revision; it is not current-head execution.

- **Current PR CI:** [Run 40975271680](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40975271680) passed its selected preflight, security-fast, and native-i18n jobs. The preflight log records synthetic merge checkout `ada0f18fae53e97108a139c83ca5f708a73d7436`, merging current product `a2c6197` into main `878e682`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped. This is current PR composition evidence, not native runtime proof.

- **Prior-head native-owner proof:** [Hosted macOS run 38597006067](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38597006067) passed with QA/workflow `4cf95ff77fae422b8b380f4a2c49c4101a8f38b1` and clean initial/final product `76ee71b`. macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0, Swift 6.4 arm64: 56 Swift Testing declarations across four suites, expanding to 64 executed cases (50 single-case declarations plus 14 cases from six parameterized declarations). Selection, managed-update success/failure, and older/missing/revoked canonical-verification controls passed. These are executable fixtures, not real npm installations or signed-app proof.
- **Prior-head canonical CI:** [Run 38599555604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38599555604) passed at exact product `76ee71b`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped, not executed; native proof comes from the separate owner run above.
- **Prior applicability:** Source review of then-current main `794d6500f382311cab58f5d474a9ef248598e5f2` still finds the ready `managedStatus` selection write. This is source evidence, not a new live reproduction.
- **Current-head review:** [ClawSweeper Revision 14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) reviewed `a2c6197` on 29 October. It reports no findings, patch quality 4/6, and overall/proof 2/6. App-entry inspection and verified installation/update evidence, plus an existing-state upgrade from `v2026.10.9` preserving settings and data, remain required. - **Prior-head review:** [ClawSweeper's review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) at `76ee71b` identifies no code findings; app-entry and upgrade evidence remains outstanding. Revision 14 above supersedes that historical review.

Whitespace and exact source-delta checks passed. [Previous-head canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121014753) passed, including its CI gate, native i18n, and security-fast. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed; no current-head native execution proof is claimed.

### Remaining qualification

- **App entry and update:** The owner tests and retained real-npm evidence cover the affected **unbundled** discovery/inspection path at their recorded revisions. Signed packaged-app proof is separate: it must establish the actual legacy-service inspection/update routing, selection preservation, and verified canonical selection. prs.title: feat: watch a running command automation's output live in the Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long-running command automation shows nothing in Automations, Run history until it finishes, so an operator cannot tell what a multi-hour job is doing. Only Settings, Logs is live, and it does not contain the script's output.

## User Impact

User impact: while a command automation runs, its Run history shows a **Live output** panel that follows the combined stdout and stderr like `tail -f`. It auto-scrolls, pauses when you scroll up (with a **Jump to latest** button), and stops polling while the browser tab is hidden. When the run ends the panel goes away and the recorded run appears in the list as before. Gateway clients can read the same tail with `cron.liveOutput`.

Risks and limits:
- Live text is redacted with the tool-payload policy, so it can be masked more strictly than the recorded summary of the same run. The recorded summary is unchanged. A private key is masked across polls; one whose start was already dropped from a full tail is masked only while its end line is still held.
- Only the most recent output is kept: at most 256 KiB, or `payload.outputMaxBytes` when that is smaller. The panel keeps the last 2000 lines.
- Agent-turn runs have no live panel. Their transcript is still available only after the run is recorded (see Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway keeps a fixed-size in-memory ring for the active run. The command runner owns it and discards it in its existing `finally`, so exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure all clean up through one path. `cron.liveOutput` (`operator.read`, same job visibility checks as `cron.get`) returns complete lines from a byte cursor, so a reconnect neither loses nor repeats lines. The panel reuses the existing visible-poll and stream-auto-follow helpers. Cursor polling, like `logs.tail`, keeps the Gateway free of timers and per-chunk broadcasts when nobody is watching. No config key, schema or migration; `cron.history` and `cron.runs` are unchanged.

Size: about 360 lines of new production code across 3 modules, about 560 lines of tests, small edits to existing files, plus regenerated validator files.

## Evidence

Before and after screenshots (Run history of a running command job; Live output panel; paused with **Jump to latest**; hand-off when the run ends) are in the first comment below. The extra Error row in the before shot is from restarting the throwaway Gateway while testing.


- Throwaway Gateway (own state dir, port 28789, loopback, throwaway token) and a real headless Chrome against the built Control UI. A command job printed a line per second for 60 to 90 s. Follow reads returned only new lines, replaying a cursor was idempotent, stderr was interleaved in order, a fake `token=sk-...` was masked, and `active` flipped to `false` exactly when `state.runningAtMs` cleared, including after a job timeout. The recorded run was unchanged.
- Tests: buffer bounds and fixed memory, cursor, drop-oldest, UTF-8 safety, redaction (including a private key across polls) and escape stripping, cleanup on exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure; the gateway method (follow, inactive, validation, visibility, access closed mid-read); the UI line bound and panel (follow, hidden tab, hand-off, still polling before the command starts, jump to latest).
- Review round: fixes covered by focused tests and typecheck only; the throwaway Gateway run above predates them. `check:changed` passes except the dead export scan, which flags `flattenRun` in `scripts/lib/catalog-compare-released-diff.mts` (already on main, not in this PR).
- Checks run: `pnpm gateway:validators:check`, `pnpm protocol-registry:check`, the protocol since-guard (new method vintage `2026.10`), the native protocol check, scoped core and UI tests (including the existing `command-runner`, `cron.history` and `cron.runs` suites), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` (all lanes passed). I re-ran the validators, registry and new tests after the work finished.
- Agent-turn runs: not changed. Run history rows, including the transcript binding `cron.history` needs, are written when the run completes, so an in-flight run has no row and **View transcript** is unavailable. Live agent transcripts need an early binding row from the run owner and a follow protocol for transcript pages, which is a separate change.

prs.title: feat: preview Control UI themes before applying them
prs.body:
Related: #151479 (reuse of shared radio/option-card controls; this does not complete the consolidation tracker).

## What Problem This Solves

Choosing a Control UI theme needs a compact, keyboard-friendly way to try it across the window before saving, including matching colors in the embedded terminal.

## User Impact

Users can hover, focus, or tap a theme to preview the current window; Apply theme or Enter saves it, while Cancel, Escape, or leaving Appearance restores the current selection. Other windows and saved preferences are unchanged during preview. All 11 built-in names/IDs are preserved, with palette descriptions and Beacon identified as the high-contrast option.

Arrow keys browse, Home/End jump, and Space previews without saving. The visible keyboard guide is scoped to the picker, not text fields. Plugin and personal palettes use the existing catalog, including cancellation when a previewed plugin disappears.

Themes may optionally author 16 ANSI colors. Existing terminals and scrollback repaint without restarting the shell; explicit true-color output remains application-owned. No database migration or operator configuration change is required. The approved temporary ghostty-web 0.4.0 repair includes rebuilt embedded WASM and generated ESM/CJS/declarations, with pinned sources, hashes, rebuild instructions, and removal gates in patches/README.md and the packaged source patches.

This is Omarchy-inspired groundwork, not an official collaboration or an installed Catppuccin/Tokyo Night theme pack. New wallpapers, continuous animation, and external CLI theming are outside this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing application theme owner now holds transient preview state separately from canonical preferences and rejects stale palette completion after cancellation. The picker reuses shared native radio navigation instead of adding a second keyboard model; the real window is the preview surface rather than a floating miniature. Preview and commit share the font/accent reset policy.

The terminal updates native color defaults directly rather than injecting OSC into the PTY parser, preserving split escape sequences and active-theme reset baselines. The canvas also paints literal-black cell backgrounds correctly. Existing clipboard-success and disposal repairs remain intact. Most patch bytes are reproducibly generated dependency output, not a second terminal implementation.

## Evidence

- Real Control UI browser flow: window preview, all scoped navigation keys, explicit Apply/Enter, Escape/Cancel/route exit, no writes before Apply, a second window retaining its selection, touch, plugin preview/withdrawal, and saved-profile persistence.
- Chromium Appearance consumer suite: 20 tests. Focused keyboard/preview consumer also passed in WebKit. Focused owner/preference/configuration suites: 169 tests, including late palette completion and Gateway-scope retirement. Contrast matrix retains AA, with Beacon AAA for the sampled text pairs.
- Full terminal browser suite: 6 cases, including cold authored palettes, live reload/fallback, clipboard outcomes, input, memory isolation, and disposal. Native regressions cover all 16 colors, scrollback, explicit RGB, cursor preservation, fragmented CSI/OSC, and reset defaults.
- The literal-black canvas regression was red before the renderer repair and green afterward: SGR 40 paints [0,0,0], while untouched default background remains [30,30,46]. A fresh-store frozen install reproduced both generated runtime formats and the native WASM hash.
- UI production typecheck, scoped lint/style/format, docs MDX, and i18n verification passed. Independent P0-P2 review is scoped-clean after resolving the black-background finding. PR CI provides the broad suite; no remote CI or whole-repository typecheck success is claimed.

- After GitHub reported an actual conflict, integrated main at `c64eaf54ad0b609a114d580e29135acd93433bfd`. Kept the new canonical Settings preference owner rather than restoring duplicate bindings. On that exact base, all 9 browser cases, affected Settings/preview owner regressions, UI production typecheck, scoped lint/format, and fresh P0-P2 review passed. The integrated After capture is byte-identical to the image below. Earlier unchanged-contract proof is retained, not relabeled as remote CI.

- Hosted-review follow-up: completed the remaining browser-only `ApplicationTheme` fixture and corrected the radio test callback's return contract. The UI-components test typecheck leaf now passes, along with that browser test and all 5 shared-radio tests. These follow-up edits are test-only; production behavior and the inspected images are unchanged.

Existing persisted preference and theme-definition shapes are unchanged, and ANSI tokens are optional. A full v2026.10.6-to-candidate upgrade run was not performed; it remains an explicit qualification gap rather than a claimed pass.

The earlier editor/test type graph (before base integration) reported errors in untouched native-desktop, quota-reset, and regexp declaration inputs. That broad graph was not rerun or claimed fixed; this is not a clean full-project gate run. No live Gateway was modified or deployed. Browser evidence uses synthetic Gateway fixtures.

### Visual walkthrough

**Revision provenance for every Before/After comparison below:**

- **Before = main at [d75915ee88343c26565b6855fde235525d112ba3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d75915ee88343c26565b6855fde235525d112ba3)**, fetched into an isolated, clean checkout for this recapture.
- **After = pushed PR head [da36d69fe3933fe1675201b26622972a7327b066](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/da36d69fe3933fe1675201b26622972a7327b066)**. The capture checkout's Git tree exactly matches the published commit tree (777b6ea8a27dab54d4656a994a92fe40f70177fc); it contains no unpublished product changes.

Both revisions ran the same scenario script and synthetic Gateway fixtures with matching viewport, locale, color scheme, and reduced-motion settings. Each used its own dependency installation and lockfile. These are real rendered Control UI captures, not design mockups or previous design iterations. Fixture footer version/build strings are synthetic; the source revisions above identify the code being compared. No code was pushed for this description/evidence update.

**How to read the picker:** the checkmark identifies the saved theme; the highlighted/focused radio identifies the preview target. “Previewing … — not saved” is an unsaved window-local state. “Current: …” and disabled Apply/Cancel mean there is no pending theme choice.

#### Main versus PR: hover Tide while Claw is saved

Identical action on both revisions: open Appearance with Claw selected, then hover Tide. Both use a 1440 × 1200 viewport.

**Before — main d75915ee: hover/tooltip only; the window stays Claw**

![Before on current-main snapshot d75915ee: hovering Tide leaves the window in Claw](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f2e11f8-783a-498c-880c-bfc786c8bffc)

**After — pushed PR da36d69: the whole window previews Tide, with Claw still saved**

![After on pushed PR da36d69: hovering Tide previews the whole window without saving](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/efeee2cf-26ea-48d6-b44d-74f88b96d688)

| Same action | Main d75915ee | Pushed PR da36d69 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hover Tide | Window remains Claw; 0 theme-selection requests | Window previews Tide; 0 theme-selection requests |
| Click Tide | Window changes to Tide and sends 1 theme-selection request | Window previews Tide but sends 0 theme-selection requests |
| Separate commit step | None: selecting the theme commits it | Apply/Enter commits the preview; Cancel/Escape restores the saved theme |

The comparison scenarios asserted these rendered states and request counts on both revisions. The PR preview includes typography as well as colors, so surrounding copy can rewrap; the captures do not normalize away that layout change.

#### PR-only state and persistence walkthrough

The following gallery and state sequence are **all from pushed PR head da36d69**. They illustrate individual PR interaction states, not additional main-versus-PR comparisons. This separate PR-state capture checked the rendered window, browser preference mirror, and outgoing **themes.set** requests:

| Action | Window displays | Saved theme | Theme-selection writes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Start | Claw | Claw | 0 |
| Hover/focus Tide | Tide, unsaved | Claw | 0 |
| Escape | Claw restored; focus retained | Claw | 0 |
| Preview Tide again, then Apply | Tide, current | Tide | 1 |
| End from the picker | Miami, unsaved | Tide | still 1 |
| Escape from that keyboard preview | Tide restored | Tide | still 1 |
| Tap Tide in a fresh mobile scenario | Tide, unsaved | Claw | 0 |

Cancel and leaving Appearance use the same saved-selection restoration path. Applying uses the existing preference owner; it does not create a separate theme engine. Other browser windows do not inherit the transient preview.

**Important scope distinction:** Light/Dark/System retain their existing immediate preference behavior; the new Apply button stages the **theme choice**, not every Appearance setting. The light-mode image below is after explicitly choosing Light, not a claim that Cancel rolls color mode back.

**Observed interaction edge for review (not fixed by this metadata-only update):** after Escape, leaving and returning to the exact previous pointer coordinates can leave the saved theme visible until another in-card movement, focus change, or click. The capture reproduced this, then explicitly clicked Tide to continue. It is not presented as repaired behavior.

<details>
<summary>PR-only gallery: saved, Cancel/Escape, and applied states</summary>

**New picker at rest — Claw saved, no pending choice**

![New picker at rest with Current Claw and Apply/Cancel disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6a58fa5-acfd-44fc-97a9-44ca1a691949)

**Escape state on the PR — Claw restored, Tide still has keyboard focus**

The focus outline is not a saved-selection indicator. The Claw checkmark and “Current: Claw” remain authoritative; no theme-selection write occurred.

![Escape restores Claw while retaining focus on Tide](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c23b668-56ef-4534-bbef-9b9bd08b46c5)

**Applied state on the PR — saved checkmark moves to Tide**

“Current: Tide” replaces the unsaved-preview status. Apply/Cancel are disabled again. The capture observed one theme-selection request and the saved mirror changed to Tide.

![Applied Tide with saved checkmark and Current Tide status](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b8d31de4-37f6-4de2-98b2-cbb7f9950554)

</details>

<details>
<summary>PR-only gallery: keyboard navigation, light mode, and touch layout</summary>

**Keyboard — End previews Miami while Tide stays saved**

The actual window and typography change, the Miami focus/preview target is visible, and the saved checkmark remains on Tide. The same run exercised Home, ArrowRight, and Escape and verified no additional theme-selection request.

![Keyboard End previews Miami while saved selection remains Tide](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d17a31d-f249-42e5-b1db-5273a3d37d00)

| Key, with focus in the picker | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | Move through choices and preview |
| Home / End | First / last choice |
| Space | Preview without saving |
| Enter | Apply the focused choice |
| Escape | Restore the saved theme, retaining focus |
| Tab | Normal navigation into/out of the native radio group and actions |

These bindings do not intercept the import URL field or other text inputs; that boundary is exercised by the browser flow.

**Light mode — applied Tide, with real light palette swatches**

![Applied Tide in Light mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/168e1254-8cbf-483a-9df6-98c6daf51bd7)

**Touch — 390-pixel viewport, Tide preview with Claw still saved**

The choices form two columns and actions wrap below the status. One tap previews; Apply is still explicit. This is the actual responsive layout, including the keyboard hint that remains visible on mobile.

![Mobile Tide preview with Claw saved and explicit Apply and Cancel buttons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69aee76a-e415-46a8-855f-f84ff9b8d89e)

</details>

#### Main versus PR: identical authored ANSI fixture

These are **two revision-specific captures**, not one PR implementation with its palette toggled. Both revisions received the same synthetic desired palette and the same four-row terminal output, in a 1280 × 900 viewport. The images crop the same header/output region without altering pixels.

**Before — main d75915ee: terminal retains its fallback indexed colors**

![Before on main d75915ee: identical ANSI fixture renders fallback indexed colors](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f83fae33-995b-4d93-866e-2e4196586c4c)

**After — pushed PR da36d69: terminal uses the authored ANSI colors**

![After on pushed PR da36d69: identical ANSI fixture renders the authored palette](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f15d45b-55f8-44dc-87bc-fe9d9b59e5ed)

The sampled red background was RGB (255,107,107) on main and the authored RGB (243,139,168) on the PR. The synthetic UI fixture supplies the desired optional ANSI fields to both clients; it is not a claim that main's server accepts the new theme-import fields. Import/schema acceptance is tested separately.

Live-update behavior is also tested separately on the PR: the existing canvas/session is retained, terminal.open is called once, removing authored tokens restores defaults, and palette changes emit no terminal.input. Native checks cover all 16 indices, scrollback, explicit-RGB preservation, fragmented escape sequences, and reset baselines. The pictures above compare main with the pushed PR; they do not substitute two states of the same revision for a Before/After comparison.

Concept, UX direction, and feature request: Chris Eckert (@ceckert).

prs.title: fix(exec): dollar amounts in agent messages are corrupted when exec text uses $<digit> in double quotes
prs.body:
Closes #179890

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: dollar amounts in agent-sent messages are silently corrupted ("$900" becomes "00") when an `exec` command passes the text in double quotes.

## User Impact

User impact: exec commands that would deliver a corrupted dollar amount are refused before they run. The refusal shows the text as written next to what the shell would deliver, and how to fix it (single quotes, `\$`, or a quoted heredoc), so the agent retries correctly instead of sending the wrong amount to a customer. It can be disabled with `OPENCLAW_EXEC_DOLLAR_GUARD=off`.

**Open question for maintainers:** this is default-on and uses an environment switch. If you'd prefer it opt-in, or shipped as a plugin on the existing `before_tool_call` hook instead of in core, I'm happy to rework it that way. Tell me which shape you want.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runBeforeToolCallHook` checks `exec` command text for a `$<digit>` that the shell would expand, before any plugin or approval policy runs. Codex-native shell commands reach the same policy through the PreToolUse native hook relay. Relay planning now counts the guard as a before-tool-call policy and keeps `exec` in the PreToolUse matcher, so native commands are covered even with no other policy installed.

The scanner is deliberately conservative. It only flags an expansion it can show would be empty:
- It honours single quotes, `\$`, `$'...'`, quoted heredoc delimiters, `${...}`, `$((...))` and comments.
- It recurses into `$(...)`, including substitutions inside unquoted heredoc bodies, with their own quoting.
- It ignores `$0` (the shell or script name) unless it reads as money (`$0.50`).
- It stays out of commands that define functions or set positional parameters (`set --`, `shift`, `getopts`), where `$1.00` may be intended.
- It fails open on anything it cannot parse.

Code-mode `exec` (JavaScript) is excluded.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/shell-dollar-expansion-guard.test.ts` (35 tests): the hazard shapes, every safe quoting form, `$0`, populated positional parameters, heredoc command substitution, `bash -lc` unwrapping, fail-open, and the `runBeforeToolCallHook` veto, allow and disable cases. The `$0`, positional-parameter and heredoc-substitution cases fail on the previous revision and pass now.
- `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.dollar-guard.test.ts` (6 tests): Codex `Bash` and `exec_command` are denied and single-quoted amounts pass. Relay planning enables PreToolUse for `exec` with no other policy and keeps it in a relay scoped to other tools; these planning cases fail without the relay change.
- The existing `agent-tools.before-tool-call*` and `native-hook-relay*` unit suites pass. `native-hook-relay.participants` and `native-hook-relay.remote-http` fail identically on `main` without this change in my environment.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Replayed against 391 unique `$`-bearing exec commands from a production deployment: 18 were flagged, all genuine expansion bugs, with no false positives.
- Still to add: a gateway trace of a real agent refusing and retrying. I'll attach it before asking for re-review.

prs.title: docs(memory): correct where dreaming keeps state and what schedules sweeps
prs.body:
Closes #180411
Closes #180412

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: two memory docs pages contradict the Dreaming page and the runtime, so operators debugging dreaming look for state files under `memory/.dreams/` and try to fix missing sweeps through heartbeat.

## User Impact

User impact: the memory configuration reference and the `openclaw memory status` troubleshooting text now match [Dreaming](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/dreaming): machine state lives in SQLite-backed plugin state, the `Dreaming` status line reflects configuration only, and scheduled sweeps run as an isolated cron job that does not need heartbeat. Docs only; no behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `docs/reference/memory-config.md` still said "Dreaming writes machine state to `memory/.dreams/`". Recall entries, phase signals, ingestion checkpoints, locks, and `MEMORY.md` rewrite preimages live in memory-core plugin-state namespaces (`extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-state.ts`). Under `memory/.dreams/`, dreaming now writes only the derived session corpus (`session-ingestion.ts` `appendSessionCorpusLines`). `docs/concepts/dreaming.md` already says this, and the same Note block already places `MEMORY.md` preimages in plugin state; the first bullet now agrees and links to the concepts page.
- `docs/cli/memory.md` said the managed dreaming cron "depends on the default agent's heartbeat firing to trigger reconciliation". Reconciliation runs from the `memory-core-dreaming` plugin service at startup and from its runtime reconcile timer (`extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming.ts`). The managed job is `sessionTarget: "isolated"` with an `agentTurn` payload (`dreaming-cron.ts`). Heartbeat only serves as a compatibility trigger when a legacy dreaming system event is already queued. The same paragraph tied the `Dreaming` status line to scheduling, but `formatDreamingSummary` (`cli-status.runtime.ts`) derives that line from config alone. The rewrite separates the two symptoms and points to the existing Scheduling section for the cron-scheduler, system-owner, and Doctor requirements.

prs.title: fix(cron): keep a channel chat's origin when its owner edits an automation
prs.body:
## Summary

An automation created from a channel chat on a named (non-default) account is stored as account-scoped, with an external caller origin (`{kind: "external", channel}`). Editing it from the same chat goes through the cron management grant. `withCronManagementGrant` forwarded only `local` origins, so `reconcileCronChannelRequesterAuthority` re-stamped the job's origin as `unknown`. Every later run then failed in ~50 ms with `Scheduled account "<id>" is unavailable`, although the account was still configured and connected.

This change carries the admitted turn's known origin (`local` or `external`) through the management operation, instead of only `local`.

- The origin is still the server-authenticated one from the admitted turn. `unknown` stays unknown.
- `hasCronCreatorGrantProvenance` is not touched, so requester proof is not widened.
- Who may manage a job is unchanged: the grant is still minted only for an admitted owner/admin turn, and the continuation check still runs before the mutation commits.
- The run-time account check still runs against the channel's configured accounts.

Default-account chats lose the origin the same way, but nothing shows because default accounts skip the account check.

Related: #156895, #161735, #162087 (same error string; this PR fixes the "edited from a channel chat" path only, not the pre-9.7 migration gap described in #162087).

## Changes

- `src/gateway/cron-creator-authority-grant.ts`: `withCronManagementGrant` forwards `entry.scope.callerOrigin` whenever it is not `unknown`.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.test.ts`: an owner edits an account-scoped job through management. The persisted origin stays external, and unknown still persists unknown.
  - Base red / head green: with `cron-creator-authority-grant.ts` from main, the external case fails and the unknown case passes. With this PR, both pass.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** an account-scoped automation created from a Telegram chat on a named account stops running after its owner edits it from the same chat (`Scheduled account "proof" is unavailable`). Round 2 also checks the authority boundary and upgrade compatibility, as asked in review.
- **Real environment tested:**
  - Clean Multipass Ubuntu 24.04 VMs, one per round.
  - Baseline: published `openclaw@2026.10.8` (dc2523e5a5c7) from npm.
  - Candidate: this branch, packed and applied to the same install with `openclaw update --tag file:<tgz> --yes`. Gateway state is kept across the update.
    - Round 1 used `cd869e539660`. Round 2 used `d2871aec847d`, the current head; `build-info` commit `d2871aec847d74be587a63cf1ac12a178f60fa53`, tgz sha256 `404d9131…0fe39`.
    - `cd869e53966` is this PR's fix commit before a rebase onto main. `git patch-id --stable` is identical for `cd869e53966` and `495b7f34be0`: `201a07afd1b8…`. `d2871aec847` adds only the test-file change above.
  - The gateway has a real Telegram bot as the named account `proof` (polling, `dmPolicy=allowlist`). The owner is allowed through `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, and the messages come from the owner's Telegram app.
  - The model is `scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs` with scripted `automations` tool calls (`add` / `update`), so the steps are deterministic and no provider key is used.
  - In round 2, a pass-through recorder in front of the Bot API counts Telegram methods per run, recording only the method name and status.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  - **Round 1:** create a job from the owner DM, edit it from the same DM, then `openclaw cron run <id> --wait`, on baseline and then on the candidate.
  - **Round 2,** on a single install whose state carries across the update:
    1. On the baseline, the owner DM creates J1, which is never edited. It then creates J2 and edits it, so J2 becomes `unknown`.
    2. Update to the candidate. Run `cron show` on J1 and J2, then force-run J1 and force-run J2.
    3. The owner DM edits J1 on the candidate, then force-run J1.
    4. **Non-owner caller:** remove the user from `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, keeping the channel `allowFrom` so the DM is still admitted as an ordinary sender. That user then asks to edit J1. Restore the owner.
    5. **Owner revoked mid-edit:** the owner DM asks to edit J1. The mock holds the model's tool-call answer, so the turn is admitted with owner authority but has not reached `cron.update`. While it is held, the owner is removed from `commands.ownerAllowFrom`.
    6. **Account removed:** remove `channels.telegram.accounts.proof`, then force-run J1.
  - **Round 3, owner revoked inside `cron.update`:** a fresh VM on the same baseline → candidate update. No hook or injected delay: the await is the real one in `cron.update` for a stream-schedule edit, which waits for a native exec approval before committing. Config: `tools.exec.mode=ask`, account `execApprovals` with the owner as explicit approver (so removing the owner does not also remove the approver), approval target DM.
    1. The owner DM creates P1 (cron schedule) on the candidate.
    2. The owner DM asks to turn P1 into a stream schedule. `cron.update` stops on a pending `cron-stream:<id>` approval. Nobody touches the buttons.
    3. While the approval is pending, the owner is removed from `commands.ownerAllowFrom`. After the 300 s reload deferral the reload applies (the approval is still pending), then the approval is granted from `openclaw approvals resolve <id> allow-once`.
    4. Control: owner restored, same edit again, but the change made during the wait is an unrelated account setting (`accounts.proof.linkPreview`) that forces the same deferred channel restart. Then the same CLI approval.
- **Evidence after fix:**

  Round 1, a job edited by its owner:

  | | Baseline 2026.10.8 | Candidate |
  |---|---|---|
  | origin after create | `{kind: external, channel: telegram}` | `{kind: external, channel: telegram}` |
  | origin after owner edit | `{kind: unknown}` | `{kind: external, channel: telegram}` |
  | `cron run` | `status=error`, `Scheduled account "proof" is unavailable. Re-add it to the channel configuration, or recreate this automation from the intended account.`, 0 model calls | `status=ok`, `deliveryStatus=delivered`, 1 model call |

  Round 2, candidate `d2871aec847`:

  | Scenario | Persisted job after | Forced run |
  |---|---|---|
  | J1 created on baseline, carried across the update | loads; origin `external/telegram` | `ok`, `delivered`, 1 model call, 1 `sendMessage` to the owner |
  | J2 created and edited on baseline (already `unknown`), carried across the update | loads; origin `unknown` | `error` `Scheduled account "proof" is unavailable`, 0 model calls, 0 `sendMessage` |
  | Owner edits J1 on the candidate | payload updated; origin stays `external/telegram` | `ok`, `delivered`, 1 model call, 1 `sendMessage` |
  | Non-owner asks to edit J1 | unchanged (same `updatedAt`) | n/a |
  | Owner revoked while the edit turn was held | unchanged (same `updatedAt`) | n/a |
  | Account `proof` removed | n/a | `error` `Scheduled account "proof" is unavailable`, 0 model calls, 0 Bot API calls of any kind |

  The scheduled policy stayed `mode=account`, `ownerAccountId=proof` throughout, with announce delivery through `telegram` on account `proof`.

  Non-owner edit, `automations` tool result returned to the model:
  ```
  automations needs the owner's authority, and this turn was not started by the owner. Do not retry automations.
  ```

  Owner revoked mid-edit, gateway log (the held turn never reached the tool; the job's `updatedAt` is unchanged):
  ```
  22:46:55 [reload] config change requires channel reload (telegram) — deferring until ... 1 admitted agent run(s) complete
  22:51:55 [reload] channel reload timeout after 300239ms with ... 1 admitted agent run(s) still active; reloading channels anyway
  22:51:55 [reload] config hot reload applied (commands.ownerAllowFrom)
  22:51:55 [telegram] [proof] starting account (reason: config-reload)
  ```

  Round 3, owner revoked while `cron.update` awaits its stream approval (candidate `d2871aec847`, real bot, owner's Telegram app):

  | Change during the wait | Reload | Approval after reload | CLI approve | Persisted job |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | owner removed from `commands.ownerAllowFrom` | deferred 300 s, then applied, `[proof] starting account (reason: config-reload)` | still pending | `Approval cron-stream:9404a5c0… was cancelled (run-aborted).` | unchanged: cron schedule, payload v1, same `updatedAt` |
  | `accounts.proof.linkPreview` toggled (control) | deferred 300 s, then applied, same restart line | still pending | `resolved allow-once by runtime:cli` | stream schedule, payload v3, origin `external/telegram`, policy `account`/`proof` |

  Same wait, same channel restart, same approval path; only the owner revocation makes the commit fail. The same pair ran first against a fake Bot API with the same result.

  Round 1: the owner's Telegram chat showed `PROOF_RUN_DELIVERED: scheduled reminder from the proof automation.` after the candidate run, and nothing after the baseline run.
- **Observed result after fix:**
  - An owner's edit from a channel chat keeps the chat's external origin. The edited job then runs on its named account and delivers.
  - Jobs persisted by the published release still load and run after the upgrade.
  - The patch does not widen who can edit: a non-owner sender is refused by the tool and nothing is persisted.
  - An owner revoked while the edit turn is in flight does not get the edit persisted, both before the turn reaches the tool and while `cron.update` itself is awaiting before its commit.
  - A job whose named account is removed fails closed before any model or Bot API call.
  - This prevents the loss but does not repair jobs that an older build already re-stamped `unknown` (J2): they keep failing until the automation is recreated.
- **What was not tested:**
  - Revocation inside an awaited `cron.update` that is not a stream-approval wait. Ordinary edits have no await long enough for a live config reload to land inside it (the gateway defers the reload up to 300 s), so round 3 uses the stream-approval wait; the unit tests cover the general case (`cron-caller-scope.test.ts`, `cron-creator-authority-grant.test.ts`).
  - Other channels (WhatsApp, Signal, Discord) with named accounts. The code path is channel-agnostic.
  - Edits from the Control UI or the CLI (local origin; behavior unchanged).
  - A real provider model.
  - The pre-9.7 carry-over case from #162087.

## Tests

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/gateway/cron-creator-authority-grant.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.test.ts`: 37/37.
- Broad cron and gateway suites: 2510 of 2511 pass. The one failure, `isolated-agent.session-identity.test.ts`, is unrelated to this change: a macOS `/var` vs `/private/var` path difference in the test's temp directory.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint on `src/gateway/`.

prs.title: fix(ui): recover focused Gateway desktops when Host Desktop is off
prs.body:
Follow-up to #177888. Related: #174368 (already closed).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: focused Gateway Desktop windows show an unavailable notice and empty picker when Host Desktop is disabled, instead of the setup recovery already available in chat.

## User Impact

Explicit Gateway desktops and focused sessions targeting that Gateway now reuse setup guidance, authorized enablement, and same-host retry. Back is available during setup/sign-in and other nonconnected focused states, including the unselected picker.

Desktop remains admin-only. Enablement requires the existing config authority and explicit action; OpenClaw does not change OS sharing permissions. No new settings, schema, migration, or setup owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

#177888 fixed chat recovery but deliberately left focused windows unchanged. This follow-up wires those missing entry points into the same setup and runtime-config owners rather than introducing another Systems-navigation flow.

The quality follow-up adds only a small admission regression: an advertised Desktop method must still reject a non-admin connection, offer no Enable action, dispatch no config patch/desktop observation, and retain Back. Production code is unchanged by that follow-up.

## Evidence

**Latest CI repair:** `83ac2b2d3763fb005304fc2e3eb32256f69b19b6`, tree `9cb472af62e872681ee6ade63f6a12201ebac5b3`, a normal child of the approved copy head `b467669acd42a56213f54a91675e88ea5b60f680`. Complete remote tree, parent, four-file delta and human co-author credit were verified.

- **Attachment defect reproduced and repaired:** a pending original-file download was cancelled when a same-session metadata refresh recreated its destination callbacks. The download resolver and attachment-input callbacks now retain identity within their existing host/read lifetime. Snapshot fields still refresh normally; no cancellation, destination, policy, authentication or live-connection guard was removed.
- **Deterministic regression:** the existing file-navigation scenario holds the original HTTP bytes, publishes a same-session title change and commits that frame before releasing the download. It fails at the same missing `Remove notes.md` chip on the pre-repair production code and passes after the producer repair. A plain focused replay had passed before this ordering was controlled; that replay was not counted as a fix.
- **Context test corrected to the actual contract:** the production shell intentionally warms lazy code at idle. The scenario now explicitly waits for that real code preload, then verifies that opening Details still performs **zero context-report RPCs**. It retains the later exactly-one report request and displayed breakdown checks. No idle warmup was disabled and no timeout, retry or skip was added.
- **25/25 browser cases passed** across both failed files and the original Desktop document flow. **71/71 existing consumer tests passed**, including real destination/connection/policy/auth changes, hidden/unmounted readers and pending-read handoff/retirement. Both scoped type graphs, typed lint, formatting and whitespace passed.
- **Fresh independent four-file P0–P3 review: scoped-clean**, with the complete patch and unchanged authority/idle-owner context supplied intact. The review was static; it is separate from the executed tests and earlier review scopes.
- **Automatically triggered repair CI:** [run 40975725218](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40975725218), pending at this update. No manual CI rerun or dispatch was used. Prior CI outcomes remain bound to their original heads.

The approved Desktop copy, buttons, layout, styles, setup behavior and earlier source history are unchanged by this repair. There is no new public API, config option, permission rule or state owner. The production growth retains operation bindings at the existing producers instead of weakening the consumer's cancellation guards.

<details>
<summary>Failure evidence and exact verification scope</summary>

- Original file failure: [UI E2E shard 1/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40915872088/job/123596744832), `chat-workspace-files.e2e.test.ts:175`, timed out waiting for `Remove notes.md` after Attach to session.
- Original context failure: [UI E2E shard 3/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40915872088/job/123596744823), expected no breakdown-module request but observed one. That code-load assertion conflicted with `warmWhenIdle(ChatContextBreakdown.preload)` and the existing shell idle owner; it was replaced by the independent report-I/O condition, not merely deleted.
- The narrow unmodified replay passed six cases. A held download alone also passed. Holding it across a real same-session metadata publication exposed the attachment defect; an earlier probe that waited for a hidden mobile title to become visible was a fixture error, not product evidence.
- Correct pre-repair control: **1 failed / 3 name-filtered**, at the missing attachment chip after metadata publication. Same controlled scenario after repair: **1 passed / 3 name-filtered**. Final owning-boundary batch: **3 files, 25 passed**, 38.65s Vitest / 41.14s enclosing command.
- Consumer batch: **4 files / 49 passed** plus the existing handoff file **22 passed**; 14.88s wrapper time across two assigned Vitest shards. The attachment consumer and its adverse-case assertions are unchanged.
- Cache identity: attachment bindings are per host and renew for a changed read owner or abort signal. The per-host download delegate still reads live host state inside the unchanged download authority owner; it does not capture credentials or connection epochs as cached answers.
- Production delta: **+41 / −13** lines; test delta: **+34 / −11** lines. Existing fixtures were extended rather than adding a new server, production test seam or duplicate regression suite.
- The initial review collection split path-only metadata away from the patch. Those context-only partitions were not counted as complete patch reviews. The completed review supplied the full patch and critical source context intact to every partition; no actionable findings remained.
- Proof remains synthetic Control UI/Gateway boundary evidence, not a new physical macOS permission, real desktop login/pixels or model-inference qualification. No visual component or style changed in this repair; the approved copy comparisons remain below at their recorded source.

</details>

<details>

**Copy predecessor:** `b467669acd42a56213f54a91675e88ea5b60f680`, tree `585e5710e592dfa95ccf38d49c785999f80ea829`, a normal child of `907c72360abab85c9880ae14640fc61fb6bc7467`. The complete published tree and the three-file delta were read back and verified.

No runtime, JSX, CSS or owner code changed in this copy commit.
- The shared administrator explanation is used only by the Desktop setup notice and Systems setup surface; both uses were reviewed. Existing i18n keys and locale coverage are preserved. No foreign catalog, translation-memory or fallback-metadata edits were made.
- **24/24 Desktop/Systems owner tests and 19/19 focused browser cases passed**. Localization baseline/verification, the scoped production type graph, typed lint on both catalogs and the changed existing test, formatting and whitespace passed. Existing copy expectations were updated; no action/authorization assertion was removed or weakened.

Back and the correct setup action remain visible; the network warning precedes activation. No clipping or horizontal overflow was observed. Existing browser cases exercise keyboard navigation and same-host recovery; screenshots are not automated visual lint or full WCAG qualification.
- The existing owner suite retains non-macOS password/network copy, no-config-authority disabled Enable, Check again, config error and unavailable-target coverage. The shared Systems consumer was included because the administrator explanation changed there too.
- Commands: `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline`; `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/desktop/desktop-panel-host-setup.test.ts ui/src/pages/systems/systems-page.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (**24 passed**, 3.89s Vitest / 5.05s wrapper); the existing focused Desktop document browser command (**19 passed**, 23.32s Vitest / 25.631s enclosing command).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Earlier recovery implementation and source-bound proof at 907c7236</summary>

The following retained record describes the recovery predecessor, not the later copy-only commit.

No test assertion was changed or weakened.
- **Scoped production and focused-test type graphs passed. Typed lint passed on five production files plus the test file**, with no problems. Whitespace passed. All seven contribution files retain the verified final hashes from the tested fork source; their formatting proof is reused, not relabeled as a fresh run.

The existing PR and canonical history are preserved through a normal main merge and managed publication. The native focused DesktopPanel retains `runtimeConfig={context.runtimeConfig}`; the obsolete picker predicate is removed. There is no new picker policy, permission widening, configuration owner, or product behavior beyond the intended recovery.

### Source identity and history

- Public tested-source provenance: [TheAngryPit/openclaw@f604653](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/commit/f604653c05bdd6e24db35a66b6064c16f8e6bec9), tree `e0810943307f0d3374f6a26e94c88fb091135a96`. Its fork history is intact. It is provenance, **not claimed canonical ancestry**.

### Regression sensitivity and executed checks

The supplied baseline receipt is an expected failure on `d79c3f3f0f54489173d0ad0336dd2efecd821d36`, not a passing test:

That existing keyboard assertion catches the lost config capability: Tab skips a disabled Enable action. The supplied final fork run passes all 19 cases. On the newly refreshed canonical tree, the unchanged file passed again:


- Fresh proof runtime: **Node 24.20.0** (within the declared engine range), pnpm **12.15.0**, Playwright **1.64.1**, Chromium **1248**. The supplied fork packet used Node 26.12.1; these runs are not conflated.
- Frozen dependency installation passed without lockfile changes.
