prs.title: fix: qualify Android TLS rejection before platform updates
prs.body:
Fixes #187949. Related: #185785.

## What Problem This Solves

Android TLS qualification fails on a freshly booted emulator whose platform certificate blocklist has not updated yet. Both platform-root cases insist that Conscrypt reject the incident key during the handshake, although the production clients then reject the same chain through OkHttp's explicit blocklist.

The [reported 16 KB run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40963177710/job/123761651024) executed all 13 cases: the two platform-root assertions failed and the other 11 passed. The same result was reproduced independently on the unchanged current source with dynamic blocklist files absent.

## User Impact

This corrects the security qualification without changing application TLS behavior. Gateway sessions and inline-widget requests must still reject the verified incident chain before any origin request or WebSocket upgrade. Legitimate connections, wrong pins, wrong hostnames, and all existing native case identities remain covered.

## Why This Change Was Made

Android's runtime blocklist can be updated separately from its image and CA store. The test should establish the actual enforcing layer instead of requiring an external update to have arrived.

When production hostname validation has completed, the shared assertion now uses the existing OkHttp proof: exact raw leaf fingerprint, incident intermediate SPKI, successful hostname verification, and the specific blocklist exception. Otherwise it retains the exact Conscrypt certificate/message/stack assertion and requires no observed peer chain or accepted hostname. Generic connection failures still fail. Both callers retain their zero-origin-request assertions. No production code, certificates, dependencies, test deadlines, images, or CI jobs change.

## Evidence

- Unchanged b53a06bfd93c0c7fd0f4cad105250dd758e18451: actual API 36 revision 7 / 16 KB instrumentation executed 13 cases with the same two failures. Dynamic platform blocklist files were absent before and after. This isolated replay used a 4 GiB guest after smaller-guest attempts failed before tests; those attempts are not test results.
- Corrected tree: documentation formatting, Android ktlint, native-test Kotlin compilation, and both existing JVM TLS suites pass: 6 tests, zero failures/errors/skips. JVM case execution was 3.088 s for Gateway and 0.510 s for widgets; the combined Gradle check/build took 2m10s.
- Corrected exact-tree native replay: all 13 cases pass in 19.407 s on the same 4 GiB / 16 KB emulator with dynamic blocklist files absent before and after. Both platform-root cases complete their no-origin assertions. CA manifests and SELinux restore successfully, task packages are removed, and the emulator/AVD are disposed.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40972929857) is green, including all six Android lanes. Both uploaded native XML reports were inspected: each contains all 13 expected cases, zero failures/errors/skips, matching APK hashes, and successful trust restoration and emulator/AVD disposal. Independent review and automated review are clean.

The hosted build tested merge `1a1db601cb937df1dc813ae6ea7aef64a5951b8a`, combining candidate `c22602191f68ec0818f3c42290f5333c8d45545b` with base `b8d9e83d9c99b17611af6898bcccdb7dce347e25`.

## What Problem This Solves
The macOS guide states an unqualified macOS 26.2 minimum. That matches main, not the stable 2026.10.8 download (macOS 15). Users comparing the install page and this guide can't tell which minimum applies.

New Mac users on macOS 15 to 26.1 see conflicting requirements on their first step and may think the recommended app won't run on their Mac.

Note: the pinned "2026.10.8" will need updating at the next release. Happy to switch to unversioned wording if maintainers prefer.

prs.title: fix: preserve failure causes after repeated warnings
prs.body:
Related: #155378. This is a small existing-limit fix, not a replacement for @freeqaz-openai's broader diagnostics draft.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes failed-request notices losing their terminal error reason when repeated launcher warnings fill the beginning of the diagnostic.

## User Impact

Users retain both initial context and the terminal diagnosis in the saved failure notice. The existing 512-character diagnostic limit and 160-character session-row limit remain unchanged, and redaction still happens before truncation.

This does **not** repair the host's jemalloc profiling setup or establish why every affected request failed. There are no configuration, schema, permission, retry, or failure-settlement changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session rows already retain the beginning and end of long errors, while saved failure notices keep only the beginning. Reuse that UTF-16-safe truncation policy for both surfaces instead of introducing another formatter, increasing retention, or suppressing warnings. Short errors and specialized storage-failure guidance remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before the production change, the focused Gateway regression run failed three assertions: the allocator-warning tail, the long Unicode-context tail, and the redacted upload-failure tail were missing from the saved notice. The session row already retained the cause.
- After the fix, `pnpm test src/gateway/session-lifecycle-run-failure.test.ts src/sessions/session-run-error.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed **43 tests** across the Gateway lifecycle/persistence and session-error owner suites. This exercises the real lifecycle writer and persisted failure report, not a precomputed summary.
- Test wall times: Gateway file **66.27 s**, owner unit file **1.66 s**, combined wrapper **71.09 s**. The newly added allocator scenario took **464 ms**; most Gateway wall time was compiler preparation and the existing persistence scenarios. CI timings are not yet available.
- Production typecheck (tsconfig.core.json), focused repository lint on the three TypeScript files, pinned formatter check, staged test-line ratchet, and staged diff check passed. Command-local logs and exit receipts were inspected because the host bridge intermittently failed during post-command finalization with the same jemalloc warning.
- Independent AutoReview was attempted against local changes based on `92d61ac49882c9c8c815cf5d24dbe145a47f4238` at its default P0 scope. **Review is incomplete:** the reviewer command was terminated after repeated jemalloc warnings exhausted its bounded output capture (exit 143, output-limit flag set). There is no clean review verdict. Independent review and broad CI remain outstanding; the requester has asked to open the PR for review.
- Simplification: reuse the existing error-summary owner; no new state, configuration, or parallel policy. Net production growth is four lines; the twelve net regression-test lines extend existing persistence cases and have their own matching allocation record.
- No live-host profiling repair or live model/Gateway/browser end-to-end run was performed. The original incident's full failing operation remains unverified; the narrower diagnostic-loss defect has red/green persistence-boundary proof.

<details>
<summary>Incident report and operator follow-up</summary>

On 2026-10-29, repeated Team webchat errors showed only:

```text
<jemalloc>: failed to open "/var/tmp/jeprof/gw.<pid>.<sequence>.u<sequence>.heap"
```

The reported payload was exactly 512 characters and matched a prefix-only cut through the repeated warnings. An independent tiny exec command returned exit code zero with both expected stdout/stderr markers while its captured output also contained 17 fresh profile-open warnings. Warnings therefore do not, by themselves, prove that jemalloc caused the request failure.

An inspected sandbox Node process had neither jemalloc environment settings nor a jemalloc mapping, although warnings appeared before its output. The emitting executable in the host-side launch/bridge chain still needs to be identified. The profile directory was absent inside the sandbox; this does not establish its existence or permissions on the host or in a service-private filesystem namespace.

The operator should inspect the actual emitting process's profiling configuration and hooks. Disable unintended profiling, or provision a private service-writable profile directory in the correct namespace with bounded retention if profiling is intentional. Keep jemalloc itself if it is deliberately used as the allocator. Do not create a world-writable profile directory or treat a sandbox-only directory as a host fix.

The same warning flood reproduced an actual helper failure during independent AutoReview: the helper exceeded its bounded output capture and was terminated. This establishes one failure mechanism in this investigation, not the retrospective cause of every reported request failure.

Correlate one actual failed request with the complete Gateway/helper error, process identity, exit status or signal, and effective profiling configuration. This separates profiling-caused failures from unrelated failures hidden behind profiler output.

</details>

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2d7b1559-ad3a-426d-90ee-61017f75b592)

## Worked on by

- @TheAngryPit

prs.title: fix(cron): ignore legacy heartbeat scratch scaffold
prs.body:
Closes #152916

## What Problem This Solves

One-shot main-session automations with `skipIfScratchEmpty` could replay the legacy heartbeat scaffold instead of treating it as an explicitly empty scratch file.

## User Impact

A one-shot automation configured to skip empty scratch state now consumes the legacy scaffold without replaying it. Real edits, unchecked tasks, and unrelated local links remain actionable.

## Why This Is Safe

- The classifier only recognizes the exact legacy scaffold structure.
- It still requires the file to be otherwise empty.
- Checked tasks and the known legacy documentation link are ignored, while unrelated content is preserved as actionable.
- The scheduler behavior remains covered at the one-shot main-job boundary.

## Evidence

Validated at head `81984a7f772a626e7f438176261a97b35607c2b3`.

### Focused automated tests

Ran in an isolated Node 24.22.2 container with dependencies installed from the frozen lockfile:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/scratch-contract.test.ts src/cron/service.runs-one-shot-main-job-disables-it.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Result: 2 test files passed, 11 tests passed. This includes:

- exact legacy heartbeat scaffold is consumed once and is not replayed after restart;
- edits and unrelated local links remain actionable;
- focused negative controls for non-template content.

The redundant positive unit case was removed in `81984a`, leaving the scheduler-level regression as the authoritative positive path.

### Shipped CLI and Gateway proof

Using the current built `openclaw.mjs` and Gateway in an isolated container with a loopback-only synthetic OpenAI-compatible model, isolated state, bundled plugins disabled, no real credentials, and delivery disabled:

- Exact legacy scaffold: `status: skipped`, `completionStatus: failed`, summary `Automation scratch is explicitly empty`, 84 ms.
- The same scaffold with `- Check email` appended: `status: ok`, `completionStatus: succeeded`, summary `PROOF_OK`, 4255 ms.
- Run history contained both outcomes in the expected order.
- The skipped run returns CLI exit code 1 by design because skipped maps to the failed completion state; the returned JSON and persisted run history confirm the intended scheduler behavior.

### Formatting and repository checks

- `oxfmt --check` passes for the changed files.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- All required GitHub workflows for this head are green.

Thanks for your time reviewing this contribution.

prs.title: fix(cli): show session label column in sessions table
prs.body:
Related to #181160

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions` never shows a session's display label or its named sidebar tint. A user who named a session (and gave it a color via `SESSION_COLOR_IDS`) sees that label and color in the Control UI sidebar, but the text table renders neither — `toSessionDisplayRow` already projects `label`/`color` from the store, yet both are dropped when the table columns are built.

- Problem: the terminal table discards the `label` and `color` already present on each session row.
- Solution: add a `Label` column to the `openclaw sessions` text table that renders the session label, tinted with the same hue the Control UI uses for that named color. The column is shown **conditionally**: it appears only when at least one displayed session carries a non-empty label, so unlabelled listings keep their previous layout exactly.
- What changed: `SESSION_TINT_HEX` + `sessionTint()` in the terminal theme, a `formatSessionLabelCell` helper in the sessions table, a conditional `Label` column in the sessions command, and focused tests.
- What did NOT change: the `--label` filter from #181160. It needs a product decision on matching semantics and is intentionally left for follow-up.

## Why This Change Was Made

The data is already present in the session row; the terminal table simply fails to surface it. This change makes the terminal match the sidebar: labels render in the default foreground unless a rich terminal can apply the named hue, and sessions without a label keep an empty cell (no invented values, no noise). When a label has no color or the color name is unknown, `sessionTint` returns no tint and the text falls back to the default foreground.

The `Label` column is conditional so that the common case (no session labelled yet) is byte-for-byte identical to today's output — no spurious empty column. The tint hues are a display-only concern, so they live as a local constant in the terminal theme (`SESSION_TINT_HEX`) kept in sync with the Control UI `--session-color-*` palette rather than adding new palette tokens. This is the display half of #181160 only; the filter half is a separate, product-decision-gated follow-up.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions` now surfaces each session's label, and in rich (color-capable) terminals tints it with the same hue as the Control UI sidebar for that session's named color. Unlabelled sessions and sessions without a color render exactly as before — including the hidden `Label` column when no session is labelled — so no behavior is regressed for existing users.

## Evidence

Focused tests in `src/commands/sessions.test.ts`:
- "renders the label column (and leaves it empty when absent)" — a labelled session shows its label under `Label`; a session without a label keeps that cell empty.
- "hides the label column when no displayed session has a label" — with only unlabelled sessions, the `Label` header is absent and the table keeps its previous column set.

Real `openclaw sessions` CLI proof (four states: labelled/unlabelled × plain/rich). Each store was seeded through the production session-accessor path into a fresh SQLite store, then listed through the actual CLI (`node --import tsx src/entry.ts sessions --store <store>`, FORCE_COLOR=3 for the rich runs). ANSI escapes are shown as `<ESC>`, and this is a throwaway local store with no credentials or private endpoints (dummy ids `labelled`/`plain`, dummy model `gpt-6-astra`).

**Labelled store, plain terminal** — `Label` column shown, label in default foreground, unlabelled row empty:

```console
$ openclaw sessions --store .../sessions.json
┌────────┬─────────────────────┬─────────────────┬────────┬─────────────┬──────────────┬────────────────┬──────────────┐
│ Kind   │ Key                 │ Label           │ Age    │ Model       │ Runtime      │ Tokens (ctx %) │ Flags        │
├────────┼─────────────────────┼─────────────────┼────────┼─────────────┼──────────────┼────────────────┼──────────────┤
│ direct │ agent:main:labelled │ research helper │ 4m ago │ gpt-6-astra │ OpenAI Codex │ unknown/? (?%) │ visibility:shared │
│ direct │ agent:main:plain    │                 │ 5m ago │ gpt-6-astra │ OpenAI Codex │ unknown/? (?%) │ visibility:shared │
└────────┴─────────────────────┴─────────────────┴────────┴─────────────┴──────────────┴────────────────┴──────────────┘
```

**Labelled store, rich terminal (FORCE_COLOR=3)** — the label is tinted with the Control UI's purple hue `#b595e8` (`<ESC>[38;2;181;149;232mresearch helper<ESC>[39m`):

```console
│ <ESC>[38;2;255;90;45mdirect<ESC>[39m │ <ESC>[38;2;255;90;45magent:main:labelled<ESC>[39m │ <ESC>[38;2;181;149;232mresearch helper<ESC>[39m │ ...
```

**Unlabelled store (only unlabelled sessions), plain terminal** — the `Label` column is hidden; the table keeps its previous column set:

```console
$ openclaw sessions --store .../sessions.json
│ Kind   │ Key              │ Age     │ Model       │ Runtime      │ Tokens (ctx %) │ Flags │
│ direct │ agent:main:plain │ 11m ago │ gpt-6-astra │ OpenAI Codex │ unknown/? (?%) │ visibility:shared │
```

**Before (this PR's original unconditional column)** — the same unlabelled store previously always rendered an empty `Label` column:

```console
│ Kind   │ Key              │ Label │ Age     │ Model       │ Runtime      │ Tokens (ctx %) │ Flags │
│ direct │ agent:main:plain │       │ 13m ago │ gpt-6-astra │ OpenAI Codex │ unknown/? (?%) │ visibility:shared │
```

The rich capture confirms the emitted 24-bit code `38;2;181;149;232` matches the Control UI purple `#b595e8`, and the before/after unlabelled pair shows the conditional column hiding, preserving the previous layout when nothing is labelled.

prs.title: fix(state): re-assert read admission before consuming a completed read
prs.body:
Closes #184738

## What Problem This Solves

A state read can hand its value back after the database admission that authorized it was revoked, so a caller acts on a reply from a scope that is no longer admitted.

- Problem: `consume()` re-checks only the caller signal once a read settles, so an admission revoked while the read is in flight still produces a successful reply.
- Solution: re-assert the operation authority in `consume()` (`authority.assertCurrent()`) whenever this operation is not draining, so revoked delivery authority surfaces as an error instead of a reply.
- What changed: one guard plus assertion in `src/state/openclaw-state-read-operation.ts`, and one regression test folded into the existing `src/state/openclaw-state-db-readonly.worker-lifecycle.test.ts` suite.
- What did NOT change: the read transport, snapshot and cleanup ownership, caller-signal handling, or the accepted-reader settlement contract from #175443.

## Why This Change Was Made

#175443 replaced `consumeReadOutcome`, which re-asserted admission, with a version that checks only the caller signal; it also added lifecycle coverage proving that an already-selected query still settles while a failed transport stop is retried. Those two facts constrain the repair: a blanket re-assert rejects supported drainage, because `resource.close()` aborts the internal controller before joining transport retirement.

`authority.assertCurrent()` is the canonical check (signal, maintenance scope admission, captured database admission, open-allowed), so no new mechanism is introduced. It now runs only while this operation still owns its scope; `close()` aborts the controller as its first statement, which makes "draining" exactly the condition that must stay exempt.

## User Impact

Ordinary reads are unchanged, including accepted reads that settle while the database closes or a failed transport stop is retried. When delivery authority is revoked while a read is in flight — for example Doctor clearing a terminal open failure and invalidating the recorded admission — the caller receives an error instead of a reply from a revoked scope.

## Evidence

Verified on `dafc0f8af54`, rebased onto current `main` so the branch carries main's test-line ceiling.

Folded regression `rejects a settled read whose database admission was cleared before delivery` is red on `main` and green with the fix, while the settlement-contract test `retries transport stop and settles the already-selected query` stays green:

```
$ npx vitest run --reporter=dot src/state/openclaw-state-db-readonly.worker-lifecycle.test.ts

main:   × rejects a settled read whose database admission was cleared before delivery
        Tests  1 failed | 10 passed (11)
fix:    Tests  11 passed (11)
```

Related state read suites (worker lifecycle, snapshot admission, signal custody, retained, reader cleanup, error mapping, source identity, warm source, read worker): 52 passed.

Real path proof: real SQLite state database, real shared-state read pipeline, and a real admission mutation through `clearOpenClawStateDatabaseOpenFailure`. `config.health.read` runs through the asynchronous read-only SQLite operation, so the revocation lands while the read is in flight. No mocked transport and no fabricated admission context:

```
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/proof-final-gjhr node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs \
    read-admission-revocation.proof.mts read

control read (backup.runs, no revocation): delivered 1 run(s)
control read (config.health.read, no revocation): delivered ok=true
revocation: clearOpenClawStateDatabaseOpenFailure invalidates the admission
main: revoked read (config.health.read): DELIVERED ok=true from a revoked scope
fix:  revoked read (config.health.read): REJECTED with
      "OpenClaw state database read admission changed"
```

`check:test-lines-ratchet` passes on this head. The folded regression is a **+17** net delta (18 added, 1 removed); current `main` carries a raised ceiling, so the gate reports slack instead of an overage:

```
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base refs/remotes/origin/ci-ratchet-base --no-merge-base
Test lines OK: 6246621; ceiling: 6320357; slack: 73736.
```

Gates: exact-head CI green (71 checks pass, `openclaw/ci-gate` passed), `oxfmt --check` clean, `oxlint` clean, targeted `tsc` on the state test shard reports no diagnostics for the changed files, `check:test-mock-exports` clean.

Accepted edge case: settlement and consumption share one continuation, so the guard cannot separate a reply that settled microseconds before a revocation from one that settles during drainage. It covers authority revoked while the read is in flight, and drainage stays exempt on purpose.

prs.title: fix(infra): reject lossy UTF-8 in managed update handoff output
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The managed update handoff lossy-decodes the updater subprocess stdout with `Buffer.toString()`, so bytes that are not valid UTF-8 are silently replaced with U+FFFD. If that lands inside the JSON diagnostics, `JSON.parse(updaterOutput)` consumes corrupted data with no signal that bytes were lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Decode updater output with the strict `decodeUtf8Input` helper (the canonical approach already used across the codebase, e.g. #180861). When invalid UTF-8 is detected, the corruption is surfaced via a log line ("managed update updater stdout contained invalid UTF-8; retained a lossy copy") while still keeping a lossy copy so the string/JSON contract and the update flow never break.

The decoder binding reaches the spawned helper through the sealed runtime module it already `require`s, so the fix runs in the real child process.

## User Impact

No user-visible change for valid UTF-8 output (including multi-byte CJK split across chunks). Invalid UTF-8 is detected and explicitly annotated instead of silently corrupted, making managed update diagnostics reliable.

## Evidence

### Committed regression (head passes, base fails)

prs.title: fix(infra): use monotonic clock for managed service handoff deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

During a managed service update the parent process waits for the helper's handoff response under an absolute deadline. That deadline was seeded and read with the wall clock (`Date.now()`), so a host clock correction during the handoff skewed the remaining budget: a rewind inflated it and let a wedged handoff hang far past its configured timeout, while a forward jump shrank it and could terminate a healthy handoff early. The deadline now runs on the monotonic clock.

- Problem: `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline(Date.now() + timeoutMs, cb)` computed the remaining budget on the wall clock; a 90 s rewind turned a 5 s handoff budget into ~95 s of waiting.
- Solution: seed and read the deadline with `performance.now()` and pass that clock explicitly to `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline`.
- What changed: `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-control.ts` — the `waitForHandoffResponse` deadline arm only; plus a rewind regression folded into the existing handoff readiness-timeout case.
- What did NOT change: the handoff line reader, exit/error/input-close settlement, and child-process kill logic are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The handoff deadline is purely in-process: it is not serialized, persisted, or reported to the UI, so a full switch to the monotonic clock is safe and needs no dual-clock-domain conversion. This is the same canonical pattern already merged for the update-operation deadline (`scheduleAbsoluteDeadline` with an explicit monotonic `now`), keeping the deadline utilities consistent. Risk is low: `performance` is a Node global and only the deadline arm changed.

## User Impact

Operators running a managed service update no longer risk a stuck or prematurely cancelled handoff when the host clock is corrected (NTP step, manual change, VM restore). The handoff deadline tracks real elapsed time and fires at the configured budget.

## Evidence

All evidence below is for reviewed head `a921354150a843d908ffbeca4f9a2f9e710072fb`.

**1. Completed managed update across the published-driver/candidate boundary.** The repository's own `published-driver-update` cell (`scripts/e2e/published-driver-update-docker.sh`, the same cell CI runs for update changes) upgraded the published `2026.10.8` driver to the package built from this head. Candidate build: commit `a921354150a8`, built `2026-10-28T05:49:28Z`. The cell relabels the branch manifest's `2026.10.7` to the driver version so the future-version guard exercises an upgrade rather than a downgrade.

```console
update: exit=0 durationMs=403636
status=ok phase=finished
serviceRunning=true versionMatch=true readyz=true coreReady=true settled=true
admission owner=candidate checks: config=warn database-schema=ok node-runtime=ok plugin-availability=ok
summary: phase=finished readyz=200 runningVersion=2026.10.8
```

Operator state survived the update (identical durable session row before and after):

```console
durable-before sessionId=c7044560-a175-4d23-bab4-c3eb8cd4584b text=published-driver-durable-5ff70041-42f2-442d-865e-e34e182db80a
durable-after  sessionId=c7044560-a175-4d23-bab4-c3eb8cd4584b text=published-driver-durable-5ff70041-42f2-442d-865e-e34e182db80a
after-ready    {"ready":true,"coreReady":true,"failing":[]}
```

**2. Committed regression: green on head, red on base.** Same test, only `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-control.ts` reverted to its parent:

```console
# head a921354
✓ rejects readiness timeout after a wall-clock rewind and cleans up the sensitive handoff (5016ms)
# base source (Date.now() deadline)
× rejects readiness timeout after a wall-clock rewind and cleans up the sensitive handoff
  Error: Test timed out in 120000ms.   # the rewound budget never expires, so the helper wait never settles
VERDICT=PASS head-green base-red
```

**3. Handoff deadline under a real 90 s rewind.** Isolated systemd-managed install; shipped `update.run` Gateway RPC with the real detached `managed-handoff-runtime` helper; readiness line held 12 s and a `-90 s` wall-clock step applied the moment the deadline timer arms:

| run | driver | deadline armed | handoff settlement |
|---|---|---|---|
| published 2026.10.8 | wall clock | T+8.5 s for 8 s | readiness accepted T+22.7 s (6.2 s late) |
| this head | monotonic | T+8.5 s for 8 s | terminated T+12.5 s (0.4 s late) |

```console

[run 1] helper_readiness_released delayMs=12000
[run 1] managed-service update handoff durationMs=-87080
[run 2] wall_clock_stepped byMs=-90000 trigger=handoff-deadline-armed budgetArgMs=7999.96
[run 2] update.run managed-service handoff failed error=managed update handoff did not signal readiness within 8 seconds
[run 2] update.run reason=managed-service-handoff-failed rpcDurationMs=12541
```

Runs: [managed-update cell](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-managed-upgrade-proof/actions/runs/40640079137), [regression red/green](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-managed-upgrade-proof/actions/runs/40641073469).

Workstation note: this host's systemd 239 `libsystemd` lacks `sd_bus_set_method_call_timeout`, so the published driver cannot inspect a local managed unit here; the completed upgrade therefore ran in CI's own cell (Ubuntu 24.04, systemd 257) with the same script CI uses.

prs.title: fix(daemon): use monotonic clock for scheduled task settlement deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, stopping or updating the Gateway can hang or bail out early when the system clock is adjusted: the scheduled-task settlement probe computes its deadline and remaining budget from `Date.now()` (wall clock) while the PowerShell probe's `spawnSync` timeout and the poll `sleep` are monotonic timers. A clock jump forward shrinks the probe timeout (a 280s budget collapsed to 50s, or 1ms past a 330s roll), killing PowerShell before settlement can be observed; a clock jump backward keeps the wall-clock deadline from ever elapsing, so the loop never exits. The fix uses a monotonic clock (`performance.now()`) for the deadline and remaining budget, matching the sibling `isScheduledTaskDefinitionAbsent` in the same file.

- Problem: `prepareScheduledTaskSettlement` seeds its deadline and reads the remaining budget from the wall clock (`Date.now()`), while the consuming `spawnSync` timeout and `sleep` poll are monotonic timers — a cross-clock-domain budget.
- Solution: compute `deadline`, `remaining`, and the exit comparisons with `performance.now()` so the budget lives entirely on the monotonic clock.
- What changed: all six `Date.now()` usages inside `prepareScheduledTaskSettlement` in `src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.ts` became `performance.now()`, plus a new regression test and an update to the existing settlement test's clock mock.
- What did NOT change: the caller contract (`stopScheduledTask` / `restartScheduledTask`), the settlement result shape, and the default timeout constants all remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareScheduledTaskSettlement` is the only cross-clock-domain spot left in this file: its sibling `isScheduledTaskDefinitionAbsent` already computes `remainingTimeout()` and `expired()` from `performance.now()`, and the file's other deadline helpers use `performance.now()` too. The settlement deadline is a purely process-internal closure variable — never serialized, persisted, or compared across processes — so a full switch to the monotonic clock is safe and keeps the budget aligned with the monotonic timers that consume it. No new parser, policy branch, or configuration surface is introduced. The existing `schtasks.settlement.test.ts` clock mock was moved from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()` while preserving the test's intent (settlement exhausts the full stop budget without a false restart).

## User Impact

Windows Gateway stop/update no longer stalls or fails spuriously when the system clock is adjusted (NTP resync, manual set, DST), because the settlement deadline is no longer skewed by wall-clock jumps. The settlement still waits the full configured stop budget before declaring the task unavailable, and still refuses a restart only when settlement genuinely cannot be confirmed.

## Evidence

**Real shipped command, real runner (before/after)**: a `windows-latest` runner installs a real Scheduled-Task Gateway (`openclaw gateway install`), then runs the actual shipped `openclaw gateway stop --force` while a preload steps the wall clock (`Date.now()`; `performance.now()` stays monotonic) between the settlement deadline seed and budget read — exactly the NTP/manual-set/DST incident. Both builds drive the real `schtasks.exe`/PowerShell subprocess; the only difference is the clock source of the settlement deadline (`Date.now()` pre-fix vs `performance.now()` post-fix):

| wall-clock jump | pre-fix (Date.now deadline) | post-fix (performance.now deadline) |
|---|---|---|
| +280s (forward, in-roll) | `openclaw gateway stop` ok (50s budget) | ok (full 60s budget) |
| +380s (forward, past roll) | **stop FAILS** (1ms budget → settlement unavailable → unverified) | ok (full 60s budget, inert) |
| -280s (backward) | ok (inflated budget, over-waits) | ok (inert) |

Proof artifact + workflow: `SunnyShu0925/oc-winproof` [run #40486854535](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-winproof/actions/runs/40486854535).

**Raw CLI output (inline, current head `e804ccc7dcd`)** — verbatim, redacted to service/port only (no IPs, keys, endpoints):

```console
$ # post-fix (performance.now deadline): clock +280s between deadline seed and budget read
$ openclaw gateway stop --force --json
stop exit=0 elapsed=6.4801074s
{ "action": "stop", "ok": true, "result": "stopped",
  "service": { "label": "Scheduled Task", "loaded": true, "loadedText": "registered" } }
[proof-inject] settlement Date.now reads stepped: 5   # wall clock jumped, deadline monotonic -> inert
VERDICT[post-fix-forward]: STOPPED bounded completion in 6.4801074s

$ # pre-fix (Date.now deadline): same command, clock +380s (past the 330s roll) collapses remaining to 1ms
$ openclaw gateway stop --force --json
stop exit=1 elapsed=4.443505s
{ "action": "stop", "ok": false,
  "error": "Gateway stop failed: Error: Task settlement unavailable; stop unverified.",
  "hints": ["Run openclaw gateway status --deep to inspect the service, then retry."] }
VERDICT[pre-fix-forward-380]: STOP_REFUSED exit=1
```

Under the same wall-clock jump the pre-fix build fails the very `openclaw gateway stop` that succeeds on the post-fix build: the collapsed 1ms budget times out the real PowerShell probe, settlement reports `unavailable`, and `terminate()` refuses to confirm the stop. The backward jump is equally inert post-fix (`stop exit=0 elapsed=5.41s`).

**Unit regression (forward wall-clock skew)**, pre-fix RED / post-fix GREEN:

```console
$ vitest run src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.test.ts   # pre-fix (reverted to Date.now)
AssertionError: expected 50000 to be 60000   (280000 ms)
AssertionError: expected 1 to be 60000        (380000 ms)
$ vitest run src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.test.ts   # post-fix (monotonic)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  18 passed (18)
$ vitest run src/daemon/schtasks.settlement.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  37 passed (37)
```

Full daemon shard: 118 files / 1943 tests passed.

**What was not tested**: the settlement state machine/JSON parsing beyond the clock budget are covered by the existing 37-test settlement suite (unchanged apart from its clock-mock alignment).

**Open PR collision check**: no open PR touches `schtasks-state-probe.ts` / `schtasks.settlement.test.ts` (searched open PR topics `settlement`/`schtasks`/`monotonic clock` and changed-file lists).

Per review: added a real-Windows proof (forward + backward clock steps, before/after table) and fixed the new regression test's floating-promise lint by returning the `withMockedPlatform` promise from the test callback (CI `check-lint-core-2`).

prs.title: fix: session search on PostgreSQL scans every transcript row instead of using the text index
prs.body:
Closes #187908

## What Problem This Solves

Default-agent session search on PostgreSQL can drive the join from every agent transcript row instead of using the selective full-text GIN index. The `LEFT(session_key, N)` expression has no useful column statistics, producing a poor scope estimate and thousands of primary-key lookups.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use PostgreSQL's equivalent parameterized literal-prefix operator `^@` in the existing default-agent branch. It preserves literal underscores (`dev_ops` is not `devxops`) while exposing prefix selectivity to the planner. Explicit selections and other scopes retain their existing paths. No DDL, index, schema, migration, SDK, config or authorization change.

Original fix by @etzelm; contributor commits preserved. The namespace regression is consolidated into the existing scope case, with **zero test-registration growth**. Whole-PR delta: production +1/-1, tests +6/-0, docs +5/-0.

## Evidence

Complete built main/candidate Gateways on Node 24.22.1 and real PostgreSQL 17.8 in secretless Docker. Production schema/indexes, 122 sessions and 9,604 indexed messages (8,000 belonging to the default agent), normal statistics, no planner forcing. Actual default-agent RPC SQL and bound parameters were captured server-side and replayed unchanged through `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` twice per build.

Main performs **8,000 FTS primary-key loops**; candidate uses a GIN bitmap scan of 12 text matches. SQL execution: main **13.062/9.363 ms**, candidate **0.963/0.853 ms**. Thirty warmed public RPC samples per independent run give p50 main **11.092/11.999 ms**, candidate **3.687/4.328 ms** (2.8–3.0× median improvement). Logging was disabled for timed RPCs. Complete result arrays are identical; the real underscore-agent RPC control returns only `dev_ops`, not `devxops`.

Formatting passed; selected PostgreSQL product suite **4/4**. This proves the default RPC branch on this workload, not universal scope speedups, concurrency throughput or SQLite parity.

[Exact-head measured Gateway/SQL evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187909#issuecomment-6509696667).

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the prior predicate without data changes or migrations. Blast radius is PostgreSQL default-agent transcript search planning; result filtering and literal namespace semantics remain unchanged. SQLite and explicitly selected session queries are not changed.

prs.title: fix(memory): dreaming deep phase promotes nothing when the recall store overflows
prs.body:
Closes #150635

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Dreaming's deep phase never promotes anything once the short-term recall store reaches its 512-entry cap, because the nightly session-transcript ingestion evicts every entry that collected real recalls before the promotion ranker can use it.

## User Impact

User impact: durable memories that users actually recall can now accumulate the multi-day recall and query-diversity evidence the deep-phase gates require, so `memory promote` stops reporting `promotedCount: 0` on installs where a single day of session transcripts fills the store.

## Why This Change Was Made

The nightly ingestion stages hundreds of entries carrying only ingestion-derived signal (`dailyCount`), all stamped with the sweep time. Retention kept the 512 most recently stamped entries and compared signal counts only on a timestamp tie, so recall-bearing entries were evicted before they could be ranked. Those staged entries can never be promoted either: the ranker scores unique queries from `userQueryHashes`, which only an interactive recall writes, so `minUniqueQueries` can never be met by ingestion-only signal.

Retention now keeps entries that carry recall evidence ahead of staged entries. Ordering among equally-evidenced entries is unchanged, so entries still lose their slot by recency as before.

## Evidence

### 1. Real behavior proof through the shipped CLI

Seed: five interactive recall signals on `memory/2026-10-01.md` across five distinct queries, then one nightly staging sweep that writes 512 ingestion-only rows (`signalType: "daily"`) to `memory/2026-10-02.md`. The store therefore sits at its 512-entry cap with one recall-bearing row competing against 512 staging-only rows - 513 rows for 512 slots.

The seed calls the shipped producer `recordShortTermRecalls` directly - the same function the nightly ingestion and the memory-search path call - and the ranking and the promotion below are performed by the shipped CLI command rather than by a test assertion. The CLI runs against an isolated state root and workspace (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR` pointed at scratch paths), so no live install is touched - the live state root is Gateway-owned and the command is refused there (ERR-20261028-010):

```
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<scratch>/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<scratch>/config.json OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR=<scratch>/ws node scripts/run-node.mjs memory promote --json --apply
```

Output on this branch. The workspace path and store key are redacted; no keys, IP addresses, phone numbers, or endpoints are involved:

```
"audit": { "entryCount": 512, "promotedCount": 1, "invalidEntryCount": 0, "danglingEntryCount": 0 }
"candidates": [ { "key": "memory:memory/2026-10-01.md:1:1", "path": "memory/2026-10-01.md", "recallCount": 5, "uniqueQueries": 5, "score": 0.7978 } ]
```

`MEMORY.md` in the same workspace afterwards contains:

```
- Joe plays on the GREEN hockey team. [score=0.798 signals=5 recalls=5 avg=1.000 source=memory/2026-10-01.md:1-1] <!-- trigger: joe, plays, green --> <!-- importance: 8 -->
```

The recalled row survives the overflow, it is the only row the ranker can promote, and the fact reaches `MEMORY.md`.

The same seed and the same command, with only the two coupled source files reverted to the merge base of this branch (`short-term-promotion-utils.ts` and `dreaming-consolidation-candidates.ts`):

```
"audit": { "entryCount": 512, "promotedCount": 0, "invalidEntryCount": 0, "danglingEntryCount": 0 }
"candidates": [ ... no candidate with recallCount > 0 ... ]
```

Nothing is promoted and `MEMORY.md` is unchanged: 513 rows competed for the 512 slots, the 512 newer staging-only rows outranked the recall-bearing row, and that row was the one evicted.

### 2. Upgrade proof: recall evidence that already exists survives the first nightly sweep after the upgrade

Here the store is written by the PRE-change comparator, so it holds exactly the on-disk shape an existing install has, and then the first POST-change nightly write overflows it:

| | comparator that writes the store | overflow write | CLI result | `MEMORY.md` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| this branch | pre-change | post-change | `entryCount 512, promotedCount 1`, one recall-bearing candidate (`recallCount 5, uniqueQueries 5, score 0.7978`) | fact appended |
| merge base | pre-change | pre-change | `entryCount 512, promotedCount 0`, no recall-bearing candidate | unchanged |

So recall evidence that is already on disk is not lost by the upgrade: on this branch it survives the overflow and is promoted, and on the merge base the same store loses it.

### 3. Data-model compatibility

No persisted format changes. The diff touches five files - `dreaming-consolidation-candidates.ts`, `short-term-promotion-artifacts.ts`, `short-term-promotion-utils.ts` and the two test files - none of them the store schema or the config surface: `extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-types.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-store.ts` are byte-identical to the merge base, the store is still written as `version: 1`, and no configuration key is added or renamed. An upgrade therefore needs no migration and keeps the existing settings.

Existing rows keep working, covered by two committed cases in `short-term-promotion-flow.test.ts`:

- "still loads and promotes a stored row written before query provenance existed" - a row in the older shape (`queryHashes`, no `userQueryHashes`) still loads, still has its earned diversity restored by normalization, and still promotes into `MEMORY.md`.
- "loads a stored row that carries no earned query diversity without promoting it" - a row that also carries ingestion signal but no earned query provenance still loads rather than being dropped, while the ranker correctly refuses to promote it.

### 4. Base failure, head success (the committed regression test)

```
node scripts/test-projects.mts extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-flow.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

On this branch:

```
 ✓  promotes a recalled memory to MEMORY.md after nightly staging overflows the store
 ✓  still loads and promotes a stored row written before query provenance existed
 ✓  loads a stored row that carries no earned query diversity without promoting it
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

With the two coupled source files reverted to the merge base of this branch, the same command fails on the overflow case and passes the two data-model cases:

```
 ×  promotes a recalled memory to MEMORY.md after nightly staging overflows the store
   → expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3)
```

The test therefore detects this change instead of passing on either side of it.

### Bounded protection

Protection is scoped to rows the promotion ranker can still act on. `isProtectionEligible()` in `short-term-promotion-utils.ts` excludes rows that are already promoted, whose origin is blocked, whose snippet is a contaminated dreaming snippet, or whose path is outside the short-term corpus. Rows that cannot be promoted no longer hold a slot, so fresh staging admission is not starved - the remaining case in `short-term-promotion-utils.test.ts`, `does not let ineligible recalled rows starve fresh staging`, pins that.

Rows that are eligible keep their recall priority; ordering among equally protected rows is unchanged.

### The overflow audit warning now describes the actual policy

The `recall-store-over-limit` audit warning used to say that only the newest 512 entries are kept at runtime, which stopped being true once the comparator began keeping recall-bearing rows ahead of newer staging-only rows - operators were told the wrong thing about which evidence a repair would remove. The warning now states what actually happens: 512 entries are kept, entries carrying recall evidence are kept ahead of newer staging-only entries, and the oldest remaining rows are dropped.

### Test and gate status

- `node scripts/test-projects.mts extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-utils.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` - **1/1 pass** (the duplicated overflow case moved into the flow test above; the case that remains pins that ineligible recalled rows cannot starve fresh staging)
- `node scripts/test-projects.mts extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-flow.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` - **3/3 pass**
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` on the five touched files - clean
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the five touched files - `No problems in 5 files`
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` - exit 0, re-verified cold on the pushed tree (the incremental build cache at `.artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo` was removed first)

### CI on the reviewed revision

The one job that failed on the previously reviewed head was `check-test-types`, and it **was** caused by this diff: the staged-entry fixture in the new test omitted `userQueryHashes`, which `ShortTermRecallEntry` requires, so the extension test type graph rejected it (`TS2741`). The defect was in the test fixture only, not in shipped code. Commit `3b8d48efee0` adds the missing field and the job is green on that commit. `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` is green on the same head.

CI on the pushed head `18502057c73`: **0 failing, 0 pending across 96 checks** (the pass/skip split shifts as upstream matrix jobs settle).

`openclaw/ci-gate` had failed on an earlier head of this branch; that failure is upstream-wide rather than diff-caused - it also fails on the merge base `700930378c79` of this branch and on the unrelated PR #187090. It is green on the pushed head, as are `check-test-types`, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`, `openclaw/dependency-review` and `openclaw/security-sensitive-review`.

### Note for maintainers: the retention-policy decision this PR deliberately does not make

Review item 3 is a product decision for the memory owner, and this PR does not pre-empt it. The question the review raises is whether recall protection should expire with the ranking age window and preserve staging capacity, or whether eligible recalled rows may occupy all 512 slots indefinitely.

- **What this revision does.** It changes only which entries the existing 512-entry cap protects. The cap, the eviction count, and the recency ordering inside a tier are unchanged, and no configuration surface is added.
- **The cost of leaving the aging rule undecided.** Under this revision an eligible recall-bearing row keeps its slot for as long as it stays eligible, so a row older than the ranker's own configured `maxAgeDays` can still hold a slot even though the ranker would no longer promote it. That is a real cost, and it is the cost of not choosing.
- **What is not decided here.** The 30-day protection window and 128 staging slots discussed in #150635 are contributor input, not an established contract, so this revision hard-codes neither.
- **What the memory owner needs to choose.** (a) Whether protection expires, and at what age - the ranker's existing `maxAgeDays`, a separate window, or never. (b) Whether a guaranteed minimum share of the cap is reserved for fresh staging rows. Both can be added on top of this change without touching the retention shape, the evidence path, or the store format.
- **Why the eviction fix is worth landing before that choice.** Without it, a recalled row is evicted on the first nightly sweep that fills the cap, so the evidence is gone before any aging question can be asked. The policy question is about what should happen to evidence that has already survived; today that evidence does not survive at all.

prs.title: feat(agents): expose configured descriptions in agents_list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent configuration accepts descriptions, but `agents_list` omits them. A requester choosing an allowed subagent cannot see the operator-authored capability summary. Fixes #7490.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose bounded, nonblank descriptions only in on-demand discovery. Preserve the complete authorized roster, ordering, resolved model/runtime metadata, and existing child-agent restrictions. Each description is limited to 512 UTF-16 units without splitting a surrogate pair, with a shared 4096 CJK-aware weighted-unit budget. Later description text may be shortened or omitted; agent rows remain.

## User Impact

Names, descriptions and existing model/runtime metadata remain available together. Documentation at the current per-agent-entry and subagent-discovery owners describes model visibility and excludes secrets or tenant-sensitive material. There is no new configuration, authorization, persistence, provider, or automatic prompt-roster mechanism.

Existing nonblank descriptions would become model-visible to already-authorized discoverers after upgrade without an operator editing configuration. That disclosure choice requires the maintainer decision below; the spawn allowlist alone does not establish prior operator expectations.

prs.title: fix(tlon): add opt-in to keep citations inside their source channel [AI]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an admitted Tlon sender can cite a post from another channel the bot ship can read, including a channel the sender cannot read, and the bot adds that post's text to the agent's context.

## User Impact

Operators can set `channels.tlon.crossChannelCitations: false` (or the same key per account) to keep citations inside the conversation they came from. A citation then expands only when it points at the channel the message was posted in. Citations in non-owner DMs and group DMs stay as opaque references. The owner's verified 1:1 DMs keep expanding citations from any channel the bot ship can read.

The default (`true`) keeps today's behavior, so nothing changes unless an operator opts in. Operators who opt in lose cross-channel citation previews for everyone except the owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bot reads cited posts with its own ship session, and Urbit does not check whether the citing sender could read them. Channel rules decide who can trigger the bot, not which posts a sender can pull into context. A same-channel citation is safe because the sender posted in that channel and can already read it.

`contextVisibility` does not cover this case. `allowlist_quote` keeps explicit quotes from any sender, and Tlon citations are explicit quotes. `allowlist` filters by the quoted author against the current channel's allowlist, which admits everyone in an open channel. The question here is which channel the quoted post came from, not who wrote it.

The citation scope check moves into `cites.ts` as `isCitedNestInScope`, and the monitor binds the source channel for each channel message. DMs bind no source channel, so with the setting off only the owner exemption expands citations there. Sender admission still happens before any citation is fetched.

Config surface: this adds two channel config entries (`crossChannelCitations` and `accounts.*.crossChannelCitations`), so the channel budget in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` rises from 4001 to 4003. One boolean is the smallest surface for an opt-in that reuses the existing scope check.

Builds on #186092 (merged), which provides the explicit channel scope, the owner-DM exemption, and the pre-request scope recheck. Since `main` now includes it, this diff contains only the setting.

This pull request was prepared with AI assistance.

## Evidence

- New monitor test in `index.thread-mentions.test.ts` runs with `crossChannelCitations: false` under both auto-discovery modes:
  - A citation of the source channel expands, and its text reaches the agent input.
  - Citations of another listed channel, an unlisted Notebook, and a citation in a non-owner DM make no post request.
  - The owner's 1:1 DM citation of an unlisted Notebook still expands.
- Red check: with the monitor ignoring the setting, the new test fails because the listed other-channel citation is fetched (`/channels/v4/chat/~zod/announcements/posts/post/12345.json`).
- After merging `main` (which includes #186092), the four changed Tlon test files pass 47 tests. Per file with one worker on the earlier head: `cites.test.ts` 6 passed in 83.4 s wall (cold compile), `index.thread-mentions.test.ts` 20 passed in 24.4 s, `index.club-sender.test.ts` 15 passed in 25.2 s, `settings-helpers.test.ts` 5 passed in 5.1 s.
- `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: 41 of 42 lanes passed, including changed-file formatting, core and extension typechecks (production and tests), changed-file lint, the line-cap growth ratchet, bundled channel config metadata, and the config docs baseline. The dead-export scan failed only on exports in files this PR does not touch, inherited from `main`.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main` passed (6,270,606 lines against a ceiling of 6,326,488), so no allocation record is needed. `git diff --check` passed.
- Exact-head CI: `openclaw/ci-gate` and the changed-extensions bundle passed.
- Known gaps: no live Urbit ship was used, and the agent's generated reply was not exercised. The Behavior Proof below runs the production monitor and real Urbit client against a local synthetic endpoint.

prs.title: fix(openshell): resolve literal sandbox file paths without trimming
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The OpenShell sandbox fs bridge (mirror mode) trimmed the tool-supplied `filePath` before mapping it onto its mounts, so a literal file name like `" x.txt"` silently addressed its trimmed sibling `x.txt`. A sandboxed agent reading or writing `" x.txt"` touched the decoy file instead of the one the model chose.

Precedent: #187554 ("The configured directory's whitespace belongs to its filesystem identity"). Sibling: #172869.

## Why This Change Was Made

`OpenShellFsBridge.resolveTarget` in `extensions/openshell/src/fs-bridge.ts` now resolves the caller's literal `filePath`; the mount-containment guard is unchanged and still operates on the literal-resolved path.

Classification: `behavior-completing` (extends the literal-path contract to the OpenShell bridge owner).

## User Impact

Agents in OpenShell-backed sandboxes (the default mirror mode included) now read and write the exact file the model named, including names with leading/trailing whitespace. Ordinary paths, absolute paths, and boundary rejections behave identically.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `b17f25996` (branch `fix/openshell-literal-file-path`)
- Current-main RED baseline: `c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711`
- Production entry: real dispatch via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/openshell/src/openshell-mirror-fs-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (Node 24.18, Linux x64, secretless Docker)
- Canonical owner exercised: `OpenShellFsBridge.resolveTarget` in `extensions/openshell/src/fs-bridge.ts:278`, through the public `readFile` against real filesystem files under the workspace mount
- Decision surface: the `filePath` parameter of sandboxed agent file tools (`Type.String` schema; no upstream trim in the tool chain)
- Recorder/readback boundary: the file bytes returned by `readFile`, asserted byte-for-byte against distinct literal/decoy contents
- Acceptance RED: on current main, the new assertion failed — `readFile(" x.txt")` returned the decoy's contents (`Buffer.from("decoy-data")` instead of `"literal-data"`); the 30 pre-existing tests passed (1 failed / 30 passed)
- Acceptance GREEN: on exact head, all 31 tests pass, with `" x.txt"` → literal and `"x.txt"` → decoy observed through the real bridge over real files
- Legal controls: the trimmed sibling still resolves to itself; the mutation-denial matrix (write/edit/apply_patch across workspace access levels) is unchanged and green
- Cleanup: isolated temp workspaces only; no OpenShell worker, Gateway, or production config touched (the changed owner is host-side path resolution plus real fs access)

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/openshell/src/openshell-mirror-fs-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 31/31 (RED run on main: 1 failed / 30 passed at the new assertion)
- `oxfmt --check` on both changed files — clean
- Not tested: live OpenShell worker end-to-end (the changed owner is pure host-side path resolution + fs, exercised with real files here)

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+4/-1`
- Test LOC: `+7/-0` (existing test file only)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the existing `resolveOpenShellWorkspaceRoot` mount mapping and `isPathInside` guard; no new validator or export
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none
- Two-way door: reverting restores trimmed-path resolution

## Maintainer edits

<details>
<summary>land-ready notes</summary>

- Maintainer edits are allowed on this branch (small, single-owner change).
- Sibling PR: #187766 (mxc bridge, same shape) — the two backends were fixed independently because they are separate owners.
- Scope declaration: the remote-mode bridge (`createRemoteShellSandboxFsBridge`, src core) is a separate owner and out of scope here.

</details>


## Shipped-run proof (2026-10-30)

Reviewer demand: terminal evidence for **mirror-mode literal-file reads and writes** with the sibling unchanged, through a shipped entry point (the earlier vitest run mocked the mirror backend).

**Entry point: compiled shipped module + real fs** — no vitest, no tsx, no mocks.

- Bundle: `dist/extensions/openshell/index.js`, built from this PR's sources by the repo's own build (`pnpm openclaw --version`, build-all).
- The bundle's real plugin-entry `register()` was driven with the minimal plugin-host surface; the `openshell` sandbox-backend factory was then taken from the real registry (`getSandboxBackendFactory("openshell")`, `openclaw/plugin-sdk/sandbox`); the fs bridge was created through the real mirror-mode `handle.createFsBridge({ sandbox })` — the exact production construction in `extensions/openshell/src/backend.ts` (`createMirrorFsBridge`: workspace lease + compiled `OpenShellFsBridge` + real fs-safe root). Every behavior-bearing layer below the host shim is shipped compiled code.
- Mirror-mode **reads** hit the host filesystem directly (no OpenShell daemon involved).
- Mirror-mode **writes** perform the real local write through fs-safe first; the trailing mirror publication (`syncLocalPathToRemote`) shells out to the `openshell` CLI, which is not installed on this host, so it reports `ENOENT` **after** the local write is already on disk. The on-disk bytes below are the path-selection evidence; the `ENOENT` is environmental (missing daemon), not a path-selection failure.

Exact commands (scratch worktree at `b17f25996` carrying this PR's openshell fix and — disjoint files — #187766's mxc fix; local-only, nothing pushed from it):

```
export PATH=/tmp/node24/node-v24.22.1-linux-x64/bin:$PATH
cd <scratch-worktree>
pnpm openclaw --version            # full build; emits dist/extensions/openshell/index.js
node proof/openshell-driver.mjs    # head run -> GREEN below
# red pairing: restore base bridge, rebuild, rerun
git show c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711:extensions/openshell/src/fs-bridge.ts > extensions/openshell/src/fs-bridge.ts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-external-plugin-local-dist.mts
node proof/openshell-driver.mjs    # base run -> RED below
# restore head and rebuild
git checkout b17f25996a47437a97af082d5eadf5f932b8f5dd -- extensions/openshell/src/fs-bridge.ts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-external-plugin-local-dist.mts
```

Seeds: ` x.txt` = `PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content`, `x.txt` = `PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content` (0o644) under the workspace mount.

Base `c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711` (pre-fix `.trim()`) — exit 1:

```
read ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> "PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content"          <-- trimmed to the decoy
writeFile ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> threw after local write: Command failed during launch or output capture (ENOENT)
  on-disk ' x.txt' -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content"                   <-- literal untouched
  on-disk 'x.txt'   -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-WRITTEN-BY-SHIPPED-BRIDGE" <-- decoy received the write
FAIL  read selects literal (relative+cwd)
FAIL  relative write landed on literal file
FAIL  relative write left decoy untouched
OVERALL: RED
```

Head `b17f25996a47437a97af082d5eadf5f932b8f5dd` (this PR) — exit 0, full output:

```
read '/sandbox/ x.txt' -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content"
read '/sandbox/x.txt'   -> "PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content"
read ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content"          <-- literal selected
read '/sandbox/plain.txt' (control) -> "PROOF_PLAIN_77AA00-roundtrip"
writeFile ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> threw after local write: Command failed during launch or output capture (ENOENT)   <-- mirror sync only; local write already on disk
  on-disk ' x.txt' -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-WRITTEN-BY-SHIPPED-BRIDGE"   <-- literal updated
  on-disk 'x.txt'   -> "PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content"                       <-- decoy untouched
PASS  read selects literal (absolute)
PASS  read selects decoy for unpadded sibling
PASS  read selects literal (relative+cwd)
PASS  relative write landed on literal file
PASS  relative write left decoy untouched
PASS  control plain round-trip read
PASS  control plain round-trip write
OVERALL: GREEN
```

Controls: absolute-path read/write with only an interior space (`/sandbox/ x.txt`) is not affected by the trim bug and behaves identically on base and head (PASS on both runs); plain unpadded `plain.txt` round-trips on both. The defect scope is exactly a tool-supplied **relative** name with leading whitespace — the scenario the added regression test pins.

Cleanup: proof temp workspaces under `/tmp` removed; the scratch worktree (including its local-only mxc proof re-export) was never pushed; the PR branch itself is unchanged — head stays `b17f25996a47437a97af082d5eadf5f932b8f5dd`, no commit/push was needed.

Not tested: a live-gateway agent turn in mirror mode (that additionally needs the OpenShell daemon for mirror publication/exec and a model provider; neither is available on this host). The compiled-module route above is the strongest shipped evidence available here.

prs.title: improve(ui): cut Browser panel input and refresh latency
prs.body:
<!-- Related: none -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI Browser panel feels laggy. Soft-keyboard, composition and pasted text sent faster than the Gateway round trip goes out as one request per chunk and queues, so characters land hundreds of milliseconds late. In screenshot fallback, every action also waits a fixed 350 ms before the refresh.

## User Impact

User impact: queued soft-keyboard, composition and pasted text reaches the page sooner, and fallback frames refresh sooner. Desktop key presses still go one request per key, as on main. A live screencast is unchanged for clicks, slow typing, panel open and tab switch. No Gateway, protocol or model-facing tool changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Text queued behind an in-flight request joins one `insertText`. A click or key starts a new batch, so order is kept.
- The post-action refresh counts the time the action already took toward the 350 ms settle delay. If a capture is still pending, retries stay 350 ms apart.
- Wheel dispatch and stream resize timing are unchanged from main.

## Evidence

Real Chrome against the repo's mock-Gateway UI e2e harness with injected latency (40 ms RTT, 150 ms screenshot, 100 ms frame cadence), 20 runs per version per mode. Medians:

"Typing" below means text input events (soft keyboard, composition), not desktop key presses.

prs.title: fix(gateway): don't let ambient caller authority expand sandbox sessions tools without a captured run
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway loopback turn that reaches the sandbox tool catalog with an admitted run that carries no captured operator lease can let the caller's ambient authority silently expand the sandbox allowlist with the `sessions` and `sessions_create` tools. `readAdmittedRunOperatorAuthority` returns `undefined` both when there is no admitted run context and when the admitted run has no captured operator lease, and `prepareSandboxSessionTools` treats `undefined` as "no captured run", which falls back to `hasSessionWriteAuthority()` and reads ambient caller identity. The chat reply path already closes this gap with `snapshot.operatorAuthority ?? null`; the gateway loopback path did not, so the two paths disagreed on whether an ambient `operator.sessions.write` caller can project session tools into the sandbox.

- Problem: gateway loopback sandbox projection expanded `sessions` / `sessions_create` from ambient caller authority instead of the captured run.
- Solution: when an admitted run context is present but carries no operator lease, forward `null` (not `undefined`) so `prepareSandboxSessionTools` keeps the projection pinned to the captured run and ignores ambient authority.
- What changed: `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` (the `readAdmittedRunOperatorAuthority` forwarding is split from the value other consumers see), two focused catalog tests in `src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts` (the ambient case and its authorized-lease control), and a matched effect test in `src/gateway/sandbox-session-authority.effect.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: the no-admitted-context path still forwards `undefined` (non-sandbox and owner turns are unaffected); the loopback owner gate and the tool-execution options still receive the captured authority as `AdmittedRunOperatorAuthority | undefined`, because neither contract accepts a `null` sentinel. Tool execution-time authority intersection is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change makes the gateway loopback path match the already-shipped chat reply contract (`reply-tool-authority.ts` uses `snapshot.operatorAuthority ?? null`), so a sandbox catalog projection is always pinned to the captured run rather than the ambient caller. `prepareSandboxSessionTools` already distinguishes `undefined` (fall back to ambient) from `null` (explicitly project a run without an operator), so this is the minimal change that restores the intended contract without altering tool-execution semantics.

- Best fix: yes — reuses the exact `?? null` convention the reply path already established; no new API surface.
- Alternative considered: making `readAdmittedRunOperatorAuthority` return `null` unconditionally was rejected because `undefined` is still meaningful for "no admitted context" and other callers rely on it.
- Risk: the `null` sentinel is confined to the one projection argument that documents it; `hasSessionControlAuthority` and `OpenClawToolOptions.sessionControlAuthority` keep the non-nullable `AdmittedRunOperatorAuthority | undefined` contract, which is also what the previous commit broke.

## User Impact

Users of sandboxed gateway loopback sessions no longer see `sessions` / `sessions_create` appear in the sandbox tool catalog when the underlying admitted run has no operator lease — even if the ambient caller happens to hold an `operator.sessions.write` grant. Session tool exposure now reflects the captured run's authority consistently between the chat reply and gateway loopback paths, closing an ambient-authority leak that previously widened the sandbox surface.

## Evidence

**Changed caller, shipped path.** The forwarding lives in `resolveGatewayScopedTools`; its loopback caller with an admitted run is the CLI-run MCP projection (`agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` → `prepareCliMcpToolProjection` → `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools`). The trace below drives that production function with a real `prepareAgentRunAdmission` run, the real sandboxed config (`agents.defaults.sandbox.mode: "all"`), a real `runWithOperatorToolGatewayAuthority` ambient operator holding `operator.sessions.write`, and a real sessions read for effects. No mocks, no direct `prepareSandboxSessionTools` calls.

```console
$ node --import tsx/esm proof-cli-projection.mts   # base 5573fd0771e (before this commit)
{"label":"lease-free+ambient-operator","lease":false,"ambientOperator":true,"revokedBeforeCall":false,"catalogsSessionTools":["sessions_create","sessions"],"sessionToolsPresent":true,"sessionsCreateCall":{"ok":false,"error":"Session creation requires its live admitted operator and in-process Gateway"},"sessionsBefore":0,"sessionsAfter":0}
{"label":"authorized-lease","lease":true,"ambientOperator":false,"revokedBeforeCall":false,"catalogsSessionTools":["sessions_create","sessions"],"sessionToolsPresent":true,"sessionsCreateCall":{"ok":false,"error":"Session creation requires its live admitted operator and in-process Gateway"},"sessionsBefore":0,"sessionsAfter":0}
$ node --import tsx/esm proof-cli-projection.mts   # this head
{"label":"lease-free+ambient-operator","lease":false,"ambientOperator":true,"revokedBeforeCall":false,"catalogsSessionTools":[],"sessionToolsPresent":false,"sessionsCreateCall":{"ok":false,"error":"not in projected catalog"},"sessionsBefore":0,"sessionsAfter":0}
{"label":"lease-free+no-ambient","lease":false,"ambientOperator":false,"revokedBeforeCall":false,"catalogsSessionTools":[],"sessionToolsPresent":false,"sessionsCreateCall":{"ok":false,"error":"not in projected catalog"},"sessionsBefore":0,"sessionsAfter":0}
{"label":"authorized-lease","lease":true,"ambientOperator":false,"revokedBeforeCall":false,"catalogsSessionTools":["sessions_create","sessions"],"sessionToolsPresent":true,"sessionsCreateCall":{"ok":false,"error":"Session creation requires its live admitted operator and in-process Gateway"},"sessionsBefore":0,"sessionsAfter":0}
```

Ambient authority widens the catalog on the base commit and no longer does on this head; the authorized lease still projects both tools, so the fence only removes the ambient path. Creation still refuses a lease-free run at the effect (`Session creation requires its live admitted operator and in-process Gateway`) and the sessions store stays empty (`sessionsBefore/After: 0`) on every path.

**Shipped MCP loopback HTTP surface** — real `/mcp` JSON-RPC over TCP, real `mintMcpLoopbackClientGrant` grants, real admitted run contexts, real revocation by closing the run:

```console
$ node --import tsx/esm proof-mcp-http.mts
{"label":"lease-free","lease":false,"revokedBeforeCalls":false,"listStatus":200,"catalogSessionsTools":[],"callStatus":200,"call":{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Tool not available: sessions_create"}],"isError":true}},"sessionsInStore":0}
{"label":"authorized-lease","lease":true,"revokedBeforeCalls":false,"listStatus":200,"catalogSessionsTools":["sessions_create","sessions"],"callStatus":200,"call":{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Session creation requires its live admitted operator and in-process Gateway"}],"isError":true}},"sessionsInStore":0}
{"label":"authorized-lease-revoked","lease":true,"revokedBeforeCalls":true,"listStatus":401,"catalogSessionsTools":[],"callStatus":401,"call":{"error":"unauthorized"},"sessionsInStore":0}
```

**Matched effect pair through the in-process Gateway** — `src/gateway/sandbox-session-authority.effect.test.ts` projects the sandboxed loopback catalog and then runs `sessions_create` through the real Gateway method registry into the real session-creation owner, over a real SQLite session store:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/sandbox-session-authority.effect.test.ts
✓ creates a session through the sandbox catalog when the admitted run carries the lease
✓ refuses the same creation for a lease-free run under ambient authority without an effect
Tests  2 passed (2)
```

The authorized run persists a second store entry with `createdVia: "operator"` and `createdActor.id: "sandbox-authority-operator"`. The lease-free run with a live operator-tool ambient scope (`operator.sessions.write`) projects no `sessions_create`, and a tool constructed directly inside that same scope is refused by the creation owner with `Session creation requires its live admitted operator and in-process Gateway`, leaving only the parent entry.

**Focused tests RED → GREEN.** `does not let ambient caller authority expand sandbox sessions tools without a captured run` plus its control `keeps sandbox sessions tools when the admitted run carries the captured lease`, both in `src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts` (sandboxed loopback, non-owner, ambient `operator.sessions.write` identity):

```console
# base 5573fd0771e
× does not let ambient caller authority expand sandbox sessions tools without a captured run
  → AssertionError: expected [ Array(13) ] to not include 'sessions_create'
Tests  1 failed | 22 skipped (23)
# this head
✓ does not let ambient caller authority expand sandbox sessions tools without a captured run
✓ keeps sandbox sessions tools when the admitted run carries the captured lease
Tests  2 passed | 22 skipped (24)
```

**Gates on the pushed head.** `tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit` and the gateway-root test shard report no `tool-resolution` diagnostics (the base commit reported `tool-resolution.ts(274,60) TS2345` and `(435,5) TS2719`, the two CI failures); `run-oxlint` and `run-format --check` pass on both changed files.

prs.title: improve(ui): copy selected text out of the Browser panel
prs.body:
<!-- Related: none -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: text cannot be copied out of the Control UI Browser panel. The remote page is drawn as a screenshot, Ctrl/Cmd+C was never handled, a native copy copied the panel's empty input and left the clipboard unchanged, and the actions menu only offered "Copy URL". Text the agent selected, or that a page selected itself, could not reach the user's clipboard.

## User Impact

User impact: press Ctrl/Cmd+C with the page focused, use the browser's Copy, or choose **Copy selection** in the Browser actions menu to put the remote page's selected text on your local clipboard; a "Copied!" notice confirms it. An empty selection, a disconnected panel, disabled page scripting (`browser.evaluateEnabled=false`) or a clipboard failure each show a notice naming the next step, and the menu entry is disabled with a reason when there is nothing to copy. Password fields and cross-origin frames are never copied. Mac tabs still copy natively with ⌘C. Known gap: the panel cannot yet create a selection in the remote page (no drag-select, no Ctrl/Cmd+A), so copy works on selections that already exist; the notices tell users to ask the agent to select text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The panel already runs page functions through the existing `act:evaluate` route, so a small page script reads the selection back (input/textarea ranges, open shadow roots, same-origin frames, capped at 1,000,000 characters). No Gateway, protocol or model-facing tool change is needed. The clipboard write needs a live user gesture but the text only arrives after a round trip, so `copyToClipboard` now accepts a pending promise (`ClipboardItem`, then `writeText`, then `execCommand`). The tab and connection are rechecked right before the write so a stale result from another tab is dropped, a read that finishes after a newer copy never overwrites it, and selected text never reaches logs, errors, the local textarea, chat or panel state. Forwarding the key to the remote browser's clipboard was rejected because the Gateway cannot read that clipboard.

## Evidence

- Before/after screenshots (Copied toast, Copy selection menu entry, disabled state) are in the first comment.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/components/browser src/lib/clipboard.test.ts src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.test.ts` in `ui/`: 28 files, 328 tests pass; 23 of the 24 new tests fail without the production change (the chord guard passes trivially on the base).
- Earlier head of this PR: throwaway real-Chrome e2e against the repo's mock Gateway (deleted afterwards): Ctrl+C puts the selected text on the local clipboard with the toast, the menu entry copies, and an empty Ctrl+C shows a toast and leaves the clipboard untouched. Existing browser e2e files (panel width, route handoff, stream startup, tab preview URLs): 17 tests pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, oxfmt check and `git diff --check`: clean. `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` passes on this head merged with current main. oxlint reports one warning at `browser-panel-toolbar.tsx:220`, the existing Copy URL handler, also flagged before this change.
- Not observed: a real managed browser over CDP, Safari/Firefox clipboard behavior, the native bridge, `contenteditable` selections (jsdom lacks them). Screenshots come from the mock-Gateway harness.
