prs.title: fix(gateway): recover every tombstoned main session at startup, not only those with a continuation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #187919. Refs #187099.

Legacy restart-recovery tombstones can survive an upgrade with pending final delivery, obsolete fences, and recovery-created archives. The old startup scanner excluded tombstones, and current canonical projection hides their metadata without settling the raw rows. A tombstone can also coexist with a later lifecycle whose custody must survive recovery.

## User Impact

Startup and `openclaw doctor --fix` settle provably retired tombstoned cycles without requiring a recorded continuation or recent timestamp. Eligible roots receive one ordinary resume input. Session identity and transcript content are preserved, along with manual archives, provider review, and external harness ownership.

Every fence and pending final must match a run identity or lifecycle generation recorded inside the tombstoned cycle. A newer lifecycle, foreign fence, unlinked final, or live owner defers the row's retirement: custody remains intact, automatic resume is withheld, and startup/Doctor name the session with an inspection next step. Scalar legacy pending-final fields can still be normalized without discarding the final, so ordinary admission does not depend on the retired tombstone gate.

Matching pending delivery is retired with a recorded unknown outcome and an owed notice when routing context exists; the original remains in the verified pre-repair database backup. Confirmed delivered/suppressed finals do not generate an unknown-delivery notice. Nothing is replayed under obsolete sender authority.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing pre-canonical lifecycle migration is the single repair owner for startup and Doctor. Its custody inspection uses the cycle's execution identity, reservation, and actual foreground-claim generation/run mapping. Fence generations are checked against that evidence, and pending finals require their own source-run match. Absence of a live owner is never sufficient proof of ownership.

If any custody is unmatched, the whole retirement is deferred instead of partially changing a later lifecycle. The committing writer rechecks the current row and live owners after backup preparation. No schema, dependencies, config options, CLI options, or baselines change.

Thanks @najef1979-code for the preserved-row inventory and upgrade probes. @najef1979-code, please test this candidate against the preserved roots, including the pending-final and eight-fence cases. If Doctor retains unlinked custody, its named session and retained identifiers will identify the state needing inspection.

## Evidence

Candidate head: `1abc6ea44d2611be95b82f7296ef7e307ff0d19f`.

- The newer-generation regression is red on prior PR head `06cdf9865ab001d035f4d85f99b3b8b41c2b5190`: startup and Doctor both delete the newer fence/final (2 failed, 3 passed). The original startup/Doctor repair regressions were also red on base `f421bd20a6fafed028f779666c0e9c97888f6acf`.
- Final focused proof: 13 files passed, 1 optional database-engine file skipped; 160 tests passed, 32 optional database-engine tests skipped, across 5 shards. Command wall time was 315.64s including the runtime rebuild and compiler preparation. All 8 direct-importer files for the three modified production owners were included, plus startup concurrency/registry/ACP, restart-resume, canonical-entry, and live Gateway siblings.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/startup-migration.tombstones.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` reproduces the ownership defect. Final focused execution passes all 5 tests, covering newer lifecycle IDs, independent pending-final ownership, foreign fences, reused IDs with a different generation, missing links, matching retirement, exact original backups, transcript preservation, admission, live-owner protection, manual archives, and repeated-repair idempotence.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/gateway-tombstone-upgrade.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: real isolated Gateway and agent with a synthetic HTTP model; the matching-generation eight-fence/pending-final root resumes, a fresh `chat.send` completes, and the original transcript remains visible. Final live case: 7.167s test time (10.11s E2E shard wall time). This is synthetic-model boundary proof, not an external-provider credential test.
- Core, agents/sessions-test, and root-test typechecks passed. Touched-file oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed; madge reported 0 cycles. Both ratchets passed: no line-cap growth violation, and 6,278,283 test lines against a 6,327,305 ceiling (49,022 slack). No baseline changed.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview of the complete candidate against the original base, with canonical-projection source context and the accepted ownership concern: scoped-clean at P0/P1. Static review only; the reviewer did not execute project code/tests.
- Production: +247/-12 lines (+235 net); tests: +474; docs: +19/-1. The follow-up adds +122 net production lines. One existing transformation serves both paths; the conservative row-level guard avoids a second recovery owner or partial settlement machinery.
- Fixtures use real per-agent SQLite with released legacy fields. The reporter's actual databases and a released-binary update were not exercised. Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory is omitted under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI supplies broad proof.

prs.title: fix(doctor): bound Doctor startup waits and honor SIGTERM
prs.body:
Refs #187900. Reported by @JordanNewell.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can wait indefinitely on asynchronous preparation after its title. Cancelling only the wait can leave an underlying filesystem request or prerequisite subprocess alive. The affected Ubuntu host's exact pending operation is still unknown; this PR does not claim that host-specific cause is diagnosed.

## User Impact

Pre-maintenance package-root discovery, source-config loading, and Tailscale prerequisite inspection each have a 60-second wait limit with phase-specific diagnostics. SIGTERM aborts the CLI invocation's owned work, including package-file reads and prerequisite subprocesses. Doctor joins subprocess settlement and owned cleanup, records the signal exit status, and lets Node exit naturally. There is no forced `process.exit` or `reallyExit`, which can deadlock V8 worker teardown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both dc2523e and current main show the title before awaiting package-root and source-prerequisite preparation. The lease heartbeat already has bounded startup and request deadlines in both revisions; no worker handshake is demonstrated in that early path. Current explicit lint follows a separate runner, so a common all-mode cause cannot be inferred from the title.

The startup flow owns read deadlines and uses the existing command-process scope to stop and join prerequisites before returning. Package-root discovery passes cancellation to its filesystem owner and does not cache cancelled discovery as a missing package. The existing CLI work scope and signal cleanup own cancellation and resource release. No new shutdown manager or termination backstop is added. Synchronous native I/O cannot be preempted by these timers; diagnostic reports from the affected host remain necessary. The candidate runtime must contain this repair; an older installed Doctor is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Current candidate: 43 focused tests passed across six files, covering startup deadlines, package-root contracts, signal ownership, Doctor interruption/service restoration, and SQLite settlement. The corrected filesystem test adapter was checked again separately: 12 passed.
- Three real Node subprocess regressions send SIGTERM while package-root, config, or prerequisite preparation is pending. All exit with status 143, no terminating signal, a `beforeExit` witness, and closed worker/timer/socket witnesses. Package reads observe abort; the real prerequisite child records cancellation and is joined. `process.exit` and `reallyExit` are trapped. The new cases took approximately 0.4–0.7 seconds each.
- Against the previous PR head, the package-root regression exceeds its 10-second harness budget because its pending read retains a handle; the prerequisite case reaches natural exit without having received cancellation and fails its cancellation witness. The source-config case already consumed CLI cancellation and remains covered.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` passed on all touched TypeScript files. The full additional-boundaries lane passed, including `no-forced-process-exit`. Core and owning test-shard typechecks, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh local autoreview found no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Both ratchets passed: max-lines 404 grandfathered suppressions, environment names 458/458; test lines 6,277,968 / ceiling 6,327,305. No baseline or allocation changes.
- Retained earlier healthy-flow proof: isolated `pnpm openclaw --profile doctor187900 doctor --lint --non-interactive` completed 41 checks, 30 skipped, exit 1 for expected unconfigured-state warnings; ordinary non-interactive Doctor reached its sections and `Doctor complete.`, exit 0. The earlier 32-file consumer proof is recorded on the previous head; this follow-up reran the affected owners and signal/settlement consumers. No broad local suite replay was used to repair CI.
- The prior CI UI frame-batch budget failure is unrelated to this change. Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory remains omitted because it routinely stalls on this host; the requested boundary lane ran in full. Ubuntu/kernel 6.8 has not been reproduced on this Mac.

Simplification: remove the forced-exit timer and its synthetic deadline tests; reuse existing cancellation and command-settlement owners. No new state, configuration, CLI switches, dependencies, or compatibility paths. Entire PR: production +57/-20 lines (net +37), tests +167/-8 (net +159), docs +10/-1. The reporter diagnostic reply remains an unposted draft with npm-global debug/SIGUSR2 commands.

prs.title: fix: let common sandboxes run Chromium tests
prs.body:
Fixes #187922.

## What Problem This Solves

The common sandbox image can provide Node and pnpm while still failing to launch the repository's downloaded Chromium. A fresh image built from the current recipe exits on missing `libglib-2.0.so.0` before an existing browser test can run its assertions. Project dependency installation cannot supply the missing operating-system libraries inside a read-only sandbox root.

## User Impact

New common-image builds with `INSTALL_NODE=1` provision Chromium's system libraries and fonts before entering the sandbox. Projects continue to select and download their own matching browser executables into writable storage. The default runtime user remains `sandbox`, and `INSTALL_NODE=0` retains its existing behavior.

Existing installations receive the change when their common image is rebuilt and affected sandboxes are recreated through the existing lifecycle. This does not automatically replace a running container or change its permissions or network settings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The image now uses the existing `playwright-core` version from `package.json` to install Chromium's system prerequisites during the root build phase. That keeps the distribution-specific package list with Playwright and preserves the documented build context containing only the Dockerfile and `package.json`. Provisioning remains independent of whether pnpm itself is installed.

The existing common-image smoke job now downloads the matching headless browser as the unprivileged image user, captures a small synthetic page, and checks for readable installed font data. This reaches the loader boundary that the previous Node/pnpm version smoke did not exercise.

## Evidence

Linux/amd64 validation used the current Debian trixie recipe, Node 24.22.2, pnpm 12.15.0, and Playwright 1.64.1 / Chromium 1248. Optional Bun and Homebrew installation were disabled for the focused image builds.

- The existing `ui/src/components/solid/text-overflow.browser.test.tsx` command failed on the base image before assertions because the headless shell could not load `libglib-2.0.so.0`. It passes **1/1** on the corrected image, with a read-only root, no network, dropped capabilities, and the same `sandbox` user. The passing browser run took 2.10 seconds.
- The new workflow browser/font smoke fails on the base image for the same loader error and passes on the corrected image.
- Builds from only `Dockerfile.common` and `package.json` pass with Node/pnpm disabled, and with Node enabled but pnpm disabled. The first retains no Node/pnpm; the second retains Node and the installed fonts without pnpm.
- Formatting passed oxfmt/Bun parity. Workflow validation passed actionlint, zizmor, and repository guards. All selected type-check families and **67 tests across three related files** passed; the related-test batch took 3.82 seconds.

Autoreview (Codex engine, P0–P2) reviewed the complete committed range from `620e1fb31537` to `fba1e275d9f9` and returned scoped-clean. A separate independent engineering review of that head is clean after inspecting the source and raw image-build/runtime receipts. These source reviews remain separate from the executed tests above.

Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40963359261), [Sandbox Common Smoke](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40963359216), workflow validation, and applicable security checks passed. [ClawSweeper's completed review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187926#issuecomment-6509701967) rates the same head Platinum with no findings.

The proof covers Linux/amd64 source-built common images and actual repository browser execution. It does not establish other architectures, the complete browser suite, a live Gateway guest session, or a rollout to existing deployments.

<!-- Related: none; complements #187032 (queued text, wheel, refresh delay, resize), which does not touch the click path -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking in the Control UI Browser panel (for example filling a captcha) gives no immediate feedback. The first sign a click registered is the remote page's next frame, about 70-100 ms on loopback and a full round trip on a real link.

## User Impact

User impact: a click shows a local press ring in 1.5-3.6 ms instead of nothing for 70-100 ms or more (a cue only; it does not claim the remote click landed). Click order, click serialization and paste focus are unchanged. No Gateway, protocol or model-facing tool changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The panel acknowledges the press locally: a transparent ring animated on opacity/transform only, clipped to the stage, ends by itself after 500 ms, opacity-only fade under reduced motion. Touch and pen show it only after a tap becomes a click, so scrolling shows nothing. Faster click delivery is left to a follow-up with the browser owner (the 250 ms post-action grace in `extensions/browser/src/browser/act-policy.ts:32`).

## Evidence

- Latency measured earlier on a real Gateway, managed Chrome and built Control UI (loopback, 20 clicks): ring 1.5-3.6 ms after pointerdown. Screenshots are in the comment below.
- `pnpm test ui/src/components/browser`: 21 files, 265 tests pass. The new real-Chromium `browser-panel-press.browser.test.ts` fails on the previous head (reduced-motion drift, scroll overflow at the stage edge) and passes now.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm lint:ui:styles`, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`: clean.
- Not run: non-loopback Gateway, native WKWebView, Safari/Firefox.

prs.title: fix(secrets): Node fetch in exec can't reach local HTTP servers with the secret egress proxy on
prs.body:
Closes #181524

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `fetch` in Gateway exec fails with `UND_ERR_SOCKET` against a local HTTP server (llmman, llama.cpp, Ollama) when the secret egress proxy is on.

## User Impact

User impact: local model servers on loopback work from exec with Node `fetch`. Auth, allowlist, audit and sentinel refusal are unchanged. Touches the secret egress proxy.

## Why This Change Was Made

`fetch` sends HTTP through CONNECT and the proxy gave every tunnel to its TLS handler. A loopback tunnel that does not start with TLS now uses the existing HTTP forward path.

## Evidence

- Real Node `fetch` with a proxy grant to a running llmman daemon (`/api/version`): before `UND_ERR_SOCKET`, after 200 and a `forwarded` audit event. 2 MB POSTs over IPv4 and `[::1]` also 200.
- 2 new tests in `proxy-server.test.ts` (undici tunnel agent, the same CONNECT as Node `fetch`): red on base with `UND_ERR_SOCKET`, green after. `src/secrets/egress-proxy`: 104 pass. tsgo, oxlint, format clean. Test lines net -65.
- Prod +87/-29; shared helpers replace three duplicated blocks.
- Gap: no model inference run, only the version endpoint.

## Proof

Real Node 24 `fetch` child, real proxy from source, local HTTP server on 127.0.0.1. Base vs this PR:

```
before plain    {"error":"UND_ERR_SOCKET"}                origin saw []      audit []
after  plain    {"status":200,"body":"loopback-ok"}       origin saw ["/ok"] audit forwarded
after  sentinel {"status":502,"body":"...refused."}       origin saw []      audit refused non-https-request
after  host not in allowlist: fetch fails on CONNECT 403  origin saw []      audit refused host-not-allowed
after  grant revoked after CONNECT: closed, no response   origin saw []      audit []
```

Backports #187913 to the October reviewed branch that received #180323.

## What Problem This Solves

A read-only plugin can lose a valid tool when its MCP runtime name differs from the name constructed from the catalog. OpenClaw now matches the connector and action across both inventories and grants the exact runtime name. Missing metadata disables the tool.

This adapts the patch to Codex 0.160.0 and retains the October branch's scheduled approval rules, including explicit destructive hints. Only plugins with an active read-only restriction gain the new fingerprint field.

## Evidence

I exercised the October implementation with the real Codex 0.160.0 binary against a local model and MCP fixture. Both writes had titles identical to the corresponding read tool's runtime name.

| Turn | Tools received by the MCP endpoint | Calls rejected before MCP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Initial turn | `google_drive.search`, `kepler.query_kepler_cards` | `google_drive.write`, `kepler.write` |
| After restart and resume of the same thread | `google_drive.search` | `kepler.query_kepler_cards`, `google_drive.write`, `kepler.write` |

Before resume, the fixture reclassified the Kepler action as writable. OpenClaw refreshed the saved policy context, and the model requested all four calls again. Focused coverage also exercises scheduled replay, native fork preparation, disabled tools, and stored approval settings.

prs.title: fix(telegram): keep progress and final replies after delegation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram can lose its progress card and final reply after an agent delegates work. A later user message can suppress an already accepted result, and retained cards can show an outdated plan. A yielded requester can also incorrectly treat consumed child input as fulfillment of its own final answer.

## User Impact

The conversation keeps one progress card while delegated work runs and the requester processes its results. A requester that yields while it still owes an answer must deliver its own final or a visible failure outcome. Ordinary child completion events can remain quiet, as intended by [#185388](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185388). Plan changes replace outdated steps; finished work disappears and explicit failures remain visible. Meaningful acknowledgments and streaming preferences are preserved.

Use `sessions_yield` with an acknowledgment for a waiting update when a final is still owed. A normal final “started” acknowledgment alone does not register a pending final. Progress remains process-local and is not restored after Gateway restart. Stop/reset and revoked authority prevent follow-up delivery; private child input is not automatically forwarded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair follows the existing completion and delivery owners:

- Accepted results retain their original caller, conversation and session. A new message retires old automation privileges without discarding a still-authorized result or borrowing the new turn's privileges.
- Progress follows the pending result through waiting and requester processing. Updated plans replace old steps; closed owners retire their rows.
- Telegram confirms initial card delivery before taking it over. The additive `adoptProgressDraftWithReply` contract preserves a normal reply alongside the card; optional `updatePlan` keeps retained cards accurate.
- A yielded requester's final obligation remains until its own visible-final receipt is recorded. prs.title: fix(chat): same-user steering into a completion continuation falls back to a queued turn
prs.body:
Closes #187857

## What Problem This Solves

A Control UI message from the same person, sent while a visible subagent-completion continuation is running, waits for a separate followup instead of steering the active completion. The connection's task-suggestion mode conflicts with the continuation's unset mode, producing `task_suggestion_delivery_mode_mismatch`.

## User Impact

Compatible same-person guidance joins the running completion at its normal steering boundary. It retains the incumbent's authority, tool bindings, capabilities, and approval destination. Other requesters and inputs without an already-prepared continuation join retain the existing strict compatibility checks and followup behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the already-prepared same-requester join omits `taskSuggestionDeliveryMode`, inheriting the incumbent's negotiated surface. Otherwise the caller still supplies its explicit mode. The existing own-property comparison is unchanged, as are all other admission checks. The contributor's production change is preserved.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway and Chromium Control UI before/after evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187899#issuecomment-6509586681): real `sessions_spawn`, yield, child completion, then a human UI send during the running continuation. Main queued a separate run twice; candidate joined the same run twice. A separately authenticated other person still queued a separate run. Ordinary sends without a running continuation behaved identically on both builds. Persisted transcript run IDs and held-input custody discriminate joined versus queued behavior. Provider responses were deterministic local fixtures, not a live external model.

The consolidated gateway regression suite passes all 20 cases on candidate; main fails only the prepared-join case and passes the other 19, including the strict unsupported-join case. The existing real handoff-owner suite passes all 11 authority/custody controls. Changed-file formatting and lint passed. Redundant regression setup was consolidated into the existing fixture. Against the merge base: production +5/−1; tests +62/−65 (net −3); docs +2/−0.

Credit: @yousan's fix and the report in #187857; the contributor's commits are retained.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the prior queue behavior; no migration, configuration, or persisted format changes. Blast radius is Control UI steering into an already-prepared same-requester continuation. If wrong, compatible guidance could be queued or admitted with the wrong task-suggestion surface; unrelated callers continue through the unchanged strict comparison.

prs.title: fix: finish settled preparation timeouts without leaving updates running
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes updater history remaining running after an explicit preparation timeout, even after its work has settled. It also blocks new forward effects after that deadline.

## User Impact

A settled preparation timeout records a failed, finished run so operators can retry. Activation and unresolved recovery keep their custody. The selected timeout and required SDK declaration build are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: fix(brew): stop resolving brew from whitespace-padded PATH entries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveBrewExecutable` trimmed every `$PATH` entry before joining it with `brew`. PATH entries are filesystem identities and the OS exec lookup never trims them, so a whitespace-padded entry such as `" /opt/tools/bin"` (leading space) made OpenClaw resolve and later spawn `/opt/tools/bin/brew` — an executable the user's shell would never run. OpenClaw's filesystem view and the OS execution semantics diverged.

Precedent: #187554 ("The configured directory's whitespace belongs to its filesystem identity"). Sibling: #172869.

## Why This Change Was Made

The PATH scan in `src/infra/brew.ts` now skips only genuinely empty entries (preserving the existing no-cwd safety) and non-absolute literal entries, then joins the literal entry with `brew`. This mirrors `execvp` semantics: a padded entry is not an absolute path and is not silently rewritten into one. The standard install-root fallback is unchanged.

Classification: `behavior-completing` (aligns resolution with the exec contract).

## User Impact

Users with accidentally padded PATH entries (editor-exported env, hand-edited profiles) no longer get a brew picked from a directory the OS would not search; `openclaw skills` install/update fallbacks that swap a resolved brew into spawn argv now execute the same binary a shell would find. Ordinary PATHs, empty entries, and the standard install roots behave identically.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `572938bc9` (branch `fix/brew-literal-path-entry`)
- Current-main RED baseline: `c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711`
- Production entry: real dispatch via `vitest run src/infra/brew.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (Node 24.22, Linux x64, secretless Docker)
- Canonical owner exercised: `resolveBrewExecutable` in `src/infra/brew.ts:30`
- Decision surface: `process.env.PATH`, the same surface the OS exec lookup consumes
- Recorder/readback boundary: the returned executable path, with real executable files created on disk at `0o755`
- Acceptance RED: on current main (`c77cfc122`, base `src/infra/brew.ts` restored), the pinned padded-entry assertion failed — the call returned the trimmed decoy `/tmp/.../pad/bin/brew` instead of the later literal control entry `/tmp/.../control/bin/brew`; recorded on the padded-PATH job before this fix (1 failed / 4 passed)
- Acceptance GREEN: on exact head, all 5 tests pass, covering both leading-space and trailing-space padded entries plus the unpadded control
- Legal controls: an unpadded entry with a real executable still resolves; the pre-existing process-vs-workspace PATH trust test and install-root fallback tests are unchanged and green
- Cleanup: isolated temp dirs only; no production PATH, Gateway, or config touched

### Verification

- `vitest run src/infra/brew.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on head `572938bc9` — 5/5 (RED run with base `brew.ts` restored: 1 failed / 4 passed at the pinned assertion)
- `oxfmt --check` on both changed files — clean
- Not tested: Windows PATH semantics (`;` delimiter and quoted-entry rules are out of scope)

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+4/-3`
- Test LOC: `+21/-0` (existing test file only)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the existing `canAccessSync` executable check; no new validator or helper
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none
- Two-way door: reverting restores padded-entry resolution

## Maintainer edits

<details>
<summary>land-ready notes</summary>

- Maintainer edits are allowed on this branch (small, single-owner change).
- Alternative considered: keeping trim as a "helpful" cleanup — rejected because it makes OpenClaw disagree with exec semantics, the same divergence class fixed in #187554.
- Scope declaration: `resolveBrewOpenClawPath` and `resolveBrewPathDirs` are untouched; only the PATH scan predicate changes.

</details>


## Shipped-run proof (2026-10-30)

**Shipped entry used.** The built dist of the shipped skill-dependency installer owner — `installSkillDependencies` (`src/skills/lifecycle/install.ts:524`, the exact function the Gateway `skills.install` server method and the `openclaw onboard` wizard call for a brew recipe) — driven through a plain Node script that imports the built dist chunks (`dist/brew-*.mjs`, `dist/install-*.mjs`) and calls the real functions. Real filesystem, real `X_OK` access checks, real child spawn via the shipped `runCommandSafely`; no mocks. Boundary, honestly: there is no one-shot CLI subcommand that triggers a brew dependency install (`openclaw skills install` only installs skill sources from ClawHub/git/local; dependency install is reachable only via the Gateway `skills.install` method or the interactive onboard wizard), so the driver is a Node script against the built dist rather than the `openclaw` binary. Both base and head runs used the same entry, same script, same fixtures.

**Setup.** Two executables on disk, each logging its own invoked path to a marker file and exiting 0:

- decoy: `/tmp/proof-brew/pad/bin/brew`
- control: `/tmp/proof-brew/ctrl/bin/brew`

Standard install roots verified absent on the host first (`/usr/local/bin/brew`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/brew`, `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew`, `~/.linuxbrew/bin/brew` all missing), so only the crafted PATH decides. `HOME` pointed at an empty tmp dir so the home fallback cannot fire.

**Commands.**

```sh
# head dist built from 572938bc9, base dist built from c77cfc122 (parent commit)
node proof-driver.mjs <dist-dir> <scenario>
# scenarios: pad-only-trailing | pad-only-leading | pad-trailing | pad-leading | plain
# driver: resolveBrewExecutable() + installSkillDependencies({skillKey:"proof-skill",
#   spec:{kind:"brew",formula:"proof-formula"}, preferences:{preferBrew:true,nodeManager:"npm"}})
```

**BASE output (c77cfc122, pre-fix) — padded entry executes its trimmed sibling (RED):**

```
scenario: pad-only-trailing   PATH="/tmp/proof-brew/pad/bin "
resolveBrewExecutable -> /tmp/proof-brew/pad/bin/brew
installSkillDependencies ok=true message="Installed"
marker.log: EXEC:/tmp/proof-brew/pad/bin/brew      <-- padded entry's trimmed sibling spawned

scenario: pad-only-leading    PATH=" /tmp/proof-brew/pad/bin"
resolveBrewExecutable -> /tmp/proof-brew/pad/bin/brew
installSkillDependencies ok=true message="Installed"
marker.log: EXEC:/tmp/proof-brew/pad/bin/brew      <-- same, leading-space variant
```

**HEAD output (572938bc9) — padded entry does NOT execute; valid literal entries DO (GREEN):**

```
scenario: pad-only-trailing   PATH="/tmp/proof-brew/pad/bin "
resolveBrewExecutable -> undefined
installSkillDependencies ok=false message="brew not installed — ..."
marker.log: <empty>                                <-- nothing spawned

scenario: pad-only-leading    PATH=" /tmp/proof-brew/pad/bin"
resolveBrewExecutable -> undefined
installSkillDependencies ok=false message="brew not installed — ..."
marker.log: <empty>                                <-- nothing spawned

scenario: pad-trailing        PATH="/tmp/proof-brew/pad/bin :/tmp/proof-brew/ctrl/bin"
resolveBrewExecutable -> /tmp/proof-brew/ctrl/bin/brew
marker.log: EXEC:/tmp/proof-brew/ctrl/bin/brew     <-- later literal entry wins

scenario: pad-leading         PATH=" /tmp/proof-brew/pad/bin:/tmp/proof-brew/ctrl/bin"
resolveBrewExecutable -> /tmp/proof-brew/ctrl/bin/brew
marker.log: EXEC:/tmp/proof-brew/ctrl/bin/brew     <-- same, leading-space variant

scenario: plain               PATH="/tmp/proof-brew/pad/bin:/tmp/proof-brew/ctrl/bin"
resolveBrewExecutable -> /tmp/proof-brew/pad/bin/brew
marker.log: EXEC:/tmp/proof-brew/pad/bin/brew      <-- ordinary unpadded entry executes normally
```

**Controls.** Standard-root fallback verified inert (all roots absent, empty tmp HOME). Unpadded negative control (`plain`) shows a valid literal first entry still resolves and executes on head. Both padded variants covered for both spacing directions.

**Cleanup.** Isolated `/tmp/proof-brew` fixtures and temp worktrees only; no production PATH, Gateway, config, or state touched; no secrets involved.

**Not tested.** The `openclaw` CLI binary itself as the driving process (no one-shot CLI entry reaches the brew dependency installer; see boundary note above); Windows PATH semantics; a live real-Homebrew host.

prs.title: feat(backup): recover local Gateway state with PostgreSQL agents
prs.body:
Related: #178971

## What Problem This Solves

Recover a replacement Gateway's local identity and PostgreSQL store pointers while its agent history remains in the existing central stores.

## User Impact

Proposes `openclaw backup local create --output <archive> --json` and `openclaw backup local restore <archive> --json`. The private archive contains the SQLite global database, its matched device/client credentials and configured PostgreSQL anchors. It excludes PostgreSQL records, configuration, workspaces and provider secrets managed through external SecretRefs.

Restore requires a stopped Gateway, original configured paths and fresh database targets. This remains a **draft awaiting maintainer acceptance of the storage/public CLI design in #178971**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing full backups export PostgreSQL history and restore fresh namespaces. Replacing a Gateway that will reconnect to the same central stores needs its native global/client pair and original UUID/schema pointers instead. A global-only snapshot cannot restore that pair.

This reuses native updater capture/restore, custody and matched-client receipt owners. The local profile applies the existing global snapshot sanitizer, including removal of pending outbound delivery intent: an older checkpoint must not resend messages acknowledged after capture. Ordinary full-backup rollback behavior is unchanged.

Restore reads configuration without observing or initializing database targets. Under native custody, it validates images, the global/client pair and anchor identities, creates missing private parent directories durably, then prepares and publishes images. A genuinely empty replacement state root is covered.

The archive is a per-database recovery point, not a distributed atomic snapshot. Anchors created after capture require a newer checkpoint; this does not discover namespaces after every local pointer is lost.

## Evidence

Current upstream head: `3426d311496` merges `origin/main` at `0ded0ed7a8c` to clear the `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` conflict; it changes none of this PR's files. The live proof below ran on the previous head `d553602eda5a5887ba1c5f326e0a34a7db63cb42` (merge of `origin/main` plus the ratchet fixes; `openclaw --version` of that full build reports `2026.10.8 (d553602)`), whose PR-owned sources are identical to the current head.

Live proof on this exact head, run with the built CLI against real PostgreSQL 16 and a real model provider:

1. **Source Gateway with a PostgreSQL agent store** completes a real model turn (`TANGERINE-4471` stored; reply `OK`). The agent namespace `proof_agent_c285…` holds 48 tables; the local tree holds the SQLite global/client pair and the agent anchor.
2. **Pending outbound delivery present at capture**: one `delivery_queue_entries` row is enqueued through the runtime's own storage owner before `backup local create` runs against the live Gateway (3 images, 206 KiB archive).
3. **Refusals before publication**: restore while the source Gateway still owns the state, and restore over existing database targets, both fail with `Local checkpoint restore requires fresh database targets: …` and change nothing.
4. **Replacement root**: the departed state directory is moved aside, an empty directory is created at the original path with the host-managed config kept outside it, and `backup local restore` publishes exactly the global, client and anchor databases.
5. **No delivery replay**: the departed global database still holds its 1 pending row (source acknowledges after capture); the restored global database holds 0; the replacement Gateway log has no delivery recovery activity.
6. **Same PostgreSQL identity**: the restored anchor row is byte-identical (`store_id c285d948-…`, schema `proof_agent_c285d94839f24786`); no new namespace is created. Doctor reports `Agent data: … effective=postgres (configured); observed=postgres`.
7. **Recovery turn**: the replacement Gateway lists the prior session from PostgreSQL and answers the recall turn with `TANGERINE-4471`.
8. **Data-model compatibility**: the released `openclaw@2026.10.8` (dc2523e) creates an all-SQLite installation and runs a turn (`MARIGOLD-2287`); this head refuses to serve its schema 25 until `doctor --fix` upgrades it to 38 with pre-migration backups, then serves it and answers the recall turn with `MARIGOLD-2287`. prs.title: feat(agents): preserve stores during controlled Gateway handoff
prs.body:
Related: #178748

## What Problem This Solves

An agent's identity and history should survive a change in where it runs. An operator may start an agent on a shared Gateway, then move it to a dedicated Gateway for capacity or isolation. Today there is no supported per-agent removal operation for that handoff: `agents.delete({ agentId, deleteFiles: false })` still requests session-store purging. Keeping files does not preserve sessions.

With PostgreSQL, the durable agent data can already stay in the same database. The missing operation releases the source Gateway's use of that store without deleting its contents.

## User Impact

An administrator can:

1. Stop routing new work to the source and wait for `agents.detach({ agentId })` to succeed.
2. Transfer the closed original anchor and required workspace files, keeping the agent ID and PostgreSQL namespace.
3. Use existing `agents.create` on the destination, verify retained identity/history, restore destination settings, then switch routing.

This enables planned capacity changes and maintenance without resetting the agent's history or copying its PostgreSQL rows. Workspace files remain a separate transfer responsibility. This is a new operator capability, with no claim of a current outage or regression.

## Why This Change Was Made

Changing `agents.delete` would weaken its cleanup contract. Editing the roster or copying an anchor alone bypasses admission closure, draining and restart recovery. Detach makes retention explicit while reusing those lifecycle owners.

The implementation records durable detach intent, drains work, closes database owners and retains the store/files. Recovery and destructive retries cannot convert a pending detach into deletion; offline CLI deletion refuses a pending detach, and `openclaw agents detach <id> --force --json` runs the same journaled lifecycle while the Gateway is stopped.

Core supplies the local lifecycle primitive; a controller or plugin orchestrates placement and routing. There is no database schema-version change, new adoption RPC or distributed ownership manager. Three unchanged session-policy constants move out of the method table to meet the repository's file limit.

## Scope and Compatibility

This is administrator-controlled sequential handoff. The controller owns exclusive assignment, routing, database permissions and file transfer. Source tombstones refuse ordinary writes after restart, but cannot prevent explicit source recreation or duplicate adoption.

Detach removes Gateway-local bindings, execution approvals and provenance; restore required destination settings explicitly. It retains cron jobs; the detached agent cannot execute them. Existing restrictions on the sole configured agent and shared/inherited credential owners remain. Local shared state and anchors can remain SQLite.

The new journal phases are a compatibility commitment: binaries without this change reject retained detach journals, including completed records, at the journal read sites (agent re-creation, deletion, recovery) while still starting and serving the remaining agents. Keep a compatible runtime while those records remain.

**Held-scheduler caveat (undecided).** The integration test's `held: true` and `held: offline CLI` cases, and one sentence in `docs/gateway/postgresql.md`, refer to a `cron.migration` RPC (hold / export / resume phases). That RPC exists only in a downstream scheduler-custody overlay, not in upstream OpenClaw, so those two cases fail on upstream with `unknown method: cron.migration`. The unheld path is what this PR proves. Whether to drop the held cases and that doc sentence, or to upstream a scheduler hold first, is an open decision for the author and maintainers; nothing in this revision changes code to paper over it.

## Evidence (exact head)

Head: `fcc6e8302b862be09ab72de1dfe0f8ffe9347318` (PR branch merged with upstream `main` `0661e52a19d`; the reviewed commits are unchanged, conflicts were resolved in the merge commit).

### Live two-Gateway handoff on this head (redacted transcript)

Setup: two real Gateway processes started from this head's source (`startGatewayServer` with a managed restart owner, as under the CLI supervisor), each with its own `HOME`, state directory, config, token and port; one PostgreSQL 16 database (`unaccent`, `pg_trgm`) shared through `database.families.agent.engine = "postgres"` with one schema prefix; SQLite shared state and anchors stay local. Every RPC is a separate client process; the scopes it requests are printed with each call. A third process is an upstream `main` checkout without this change (`54afe289085`), used as the no-PR build. Paths, tokens, the database password and the user name are redacted; nothing else is edited.

What the transcript shows, in order:

1. Source Gateway A creates `traveler` (PostgreSQL store, anchor records store UUID and namespace), a session and one transcript message.
2. Destination Gateway B's state directory is created and written by the no-PR build, then opened by this head: the pre-existing session and message load (existing-data check).
3. An `operator.write`-only caller is refused `agents.detach` (`FORBIDDEN`, missing `operator.admin`); roster and journal are untouched.
4. An administrator's `agents.detach` succeeds (`ok: true`, hot reload applied, no recovery restart). The roster drops `traveler`; the journal records `detach-retiring`, `deleteFiles: false`, `cleanupCompleted: true`; the anchor file, workspace file and PostgreSQL namespace are all still present.
5. Before restart the source refuses a `traveler` write; `keeper` is still listed and readable.
6. After restarting A, `sessions.create` for `traveler` is refused (`Unknown agent id`) and a write into the old session is refused (`deletion is in progress; new work is unavailable`); `keeper` still writes.
7. The closed anchor and workspace are copied to B (same agent id, same namespace recorded in the anchor).
8. B's `agents.create` admits the existing anchor; `chat.history` on B returns the **same session id and message** created on A; a new write on B lands (2 messages). The source still refuses `traveler` afterwards.
9. Offline CLI on the stopped source: a journal left in `detach-retiring` is completed by `openclaw agents detach --force --json` (`detached: true, storePreserved: true`; roster entry removed, workspace and state directories retained); a journal in `retiring` (pending destructive deletion) is **not** converted (`has a pending deletion; finish agents.delete before detaching`); with the Gateway running, the offline command refuses with `requires exclusive offline state ownership`, no mutation.
10. The no-PR build against the source state: its Gateway starts and lists `keeper`, but `agents.create traveler` and `agents.delete traveler` are refused with `Invalid agent deletion journal phase.`, and its journal reader reports the same error.

Not exercised live here: a replaced deletion lease racing a detach between two processes (covered at the journal-authority level by `src/state/agent-deletion-journal.fence.test.ts`, `changed before recovery`), the held-scheduler cases (see caveat), and a packaged v2026.10.5 upgrade.

prs.title: fix(gateway): config.patch hangs after a superseded reload until another config change lands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A persisted `config.patch` / `config.apply` can leave its RPC waiting indefinitely after an in-process Gateway restart. Retained reload candidates were not always rescheduled. Real Gateway verification also exposed a second cause: the effective-unchanged path compared a resolved secrets snapshot with an unresolved SecretRef candidate, classified the permanent mismatch as supersession, and kept retrying it.

## User Impact

Provisioning and other source-equivalent config writes receive their application acknowledgment without an unrelated follow-up edit. Existing credential activation, publication ownership, and rollback checks remain in force. No config option, schema, dependency, or protocol change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Schedule another attempt whenever a superseded write candidate is retained, including candidates retained by either inner catch.
- The second cause this PR originally repaired, a resolved-snapshot versus unresolved-SecretRef comparison that classified an unchanged write as superseded, is fixed upstream by #183964 (merged October 27). This PR's guard for it and its two regression cases were dropped on October 28; `server-reload-managed-secrets.ts` and its test are now identical to `main`.

The complete PR now changes one production line in `config-reload.ts` and adds one focused regression file, reusing the existing retry owner rather than introducing a second resolver, state, or weaker guards.

## Evidence

### October 28 refresh: exact-head real Gateway run on `b7c03efe8cb7da0cdc4af54b36e90b19de79e2d9`

<!-- pr177823-oct28-refresh -->

Upstream `main` moved past the reviewed head `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625`, and the branch picked up test-path and test-line-ceiling conflicts. The branch now carries merge commits of upstream `main` (latest `56eba2fae26`) plus two ceiling-only commits; the reviewed commits are untouched and the production diff against `main` is still the same two files, nine net lines. Everything below ran on the exact pushed head `b7c03efe8cb7da0cdc4af54b36e90b19de79e2d9`, built from source (`dist/build-info.json` commit `b7c03efe8cb7da0cdc4af54b36e90b19de79e2d9`, OpenClaw 2026.10.8), host Node v24.19.0, Gateway native runtime Node 26.12.1, macOS arm64, isolated `--profile` state, token auth, distinct free loopback ports.

#### Executed workload

Identical to the October 19 workload: full `gateway run --verbose`, real `SIGUSR2` **in-process restart**, `config.get`, one source-equivalent `config.patch` (`response:"summary"`) that rewrites the disabled Mattermost account's `baseUrl` to the `${PR177823_MATTERMOST_URL}` placeholder, then, right after the `config.patch write` log line, rotate the file-backed `proof/proof` provider key A→B and call `secrets.reload`, wait 2.5 s, restore B→A and call `secrets.reload` again, no further config write, 30 s RPC deadline, clean shutdown. The client is one process built on the repository's own `callGateway` owner (`src/gateway/call.ts`, CLI client mode), so the rotation reaches the Gateway about 40 ms after the write log line.

| Source | Same restart + file-credential-refresh workload | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Merge parent `953eba4bbeec1c8cf7b255cce1c8c3f1496aaf3b` (current upstream `main` without this PR) | Identical | Original patch answered successfully in **270 ms server / 280.7 ms client**, zero supersessions, clean shutdown. **PASS** |
| Final head `b7c03efe8cb7da0cdc4af54b36e90b19de79e2d9` | Identical | Original patch answered successfully in **420 ms server / 433.2 ms client**, zero supersessions, clean shutdown. **PASS** |

Redacted exact-head Gateway log, **October 28, 2026, UTC−07:00**:

```text
2026-10-28T15:00:42.439-07:00 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
2026-10-28T15:00:42.845-07:00 [gateway] restart mode: in-process restart (unmanaged: use in-process restart to keep custom supervisor PID tracking stable)
2026-10-28T15:01:06.966-07:00 [gateway] config.patch write changedPaths=channels.mattermost.accounts.proof.baseUrl restartReason=config.patch
2026-10-28T15:01:07.196-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 174ms
2026-10-28T15:01:07.298-07:00 [reload] config source revision 1 accepted (write)
2026-10-28T15:01:07.367-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ config.patch 420ms
2026-10-28T15:01:09.852-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 127ms
2026-10-28T15:01:10.503-07:00 [shutdown] completed cleanly in 553ms
```

Raw trace SHA-256 values: final-head Gateway log `ff77f2dd59dd24ba308e09d8f5e5d47af91672bc440ae5ec23b27baac1ad3e26`, final-head client event trace `1fb2d2fb88aaaf73400895f5acea84d45bf221ca0949a97622bb37af374d0cf8`, merge-parent Gateway log `8ea5b86083fef455e0a92d24a318486415e7989ff56d9cb4996e09065952f238`.

#### Exact-head rerun after the guard removal: `c3efb3da9a340c5957702cfbe783b8976593d52b`

Same build procedure, same workload, same client. Original patch answered successfully in **265 ms server / 274.4 ms client**, zero supersessions, clean shutdown. Redacted Gateway log, **October 28, 2026, UTC−07:00**:

```text
2026-10-28T15:21:07.167-07:00 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
2026-10-28T15:21:07.626-07:00 [gateway] restart mode: in-process restart (unmanaged: use in-process restart to keep custom supervisor PID tracking stable)
2026-10-28T15:21:15.624-07:00 [gateway] config.patch write changedPaths=channels.mattermost.accounts.proof.baseUrl restartReason=config.patch
2026-10-28T15:21:15.769-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 110ms
2026-10-28T15:21:15.820-07:00 [reload] config source revision 1 accepted (write)
2026-10-28T15:21:15.873-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ config.patch 265ms
2026-10-28T15:21:18.368-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 83ms
2026-10-28T15:21:18.544-07:00 [shutdown] completed cleanly in 127ms
```

Raw trace SHA-256 values: Gateway log `cda9311452c3a1c967099bd028e9355bb010e6618b097c457a29158af51c4b59`, client event trace `26e14af67145e907356902a48622f308792b534a1217b19cbe629f8896e52941`.

#### What changed upstream, and what this PR still fixes

The merge-parent control **no longer fails** this workload. Upstream [#183964](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183964) (merged October 27) changed the unchanged-write handler in `server-reload-managed-secrets.ts` so an unchanged candidate whose secrets-source form equals the running snapshot's is accepted instead of being reported as superseded. That is the second cause this PR targeted, so the real-Gateway run no longer discriminates between `main` and this head. This PR's `server-reload-managed-secrets.ts` guard sat on top of an equivalent upstream guard (its stable-key and rotated-key regression cases pass on the merge parent without it), so the guard and those two cases were **dropped**: both files are now byte-identical to `main`.

The first cause is still present on `main`: a retained superseded write candidate is not rescheduled. `config-reload.superseded-retry.test.ts` fails on the merge parent (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 3 times, but got 1 times`) and passes at this head with the two-line `config-reload.ts` change. Two attempts to force a genuine supersession on a real current-`main` Gateway (a second concurrent `config.patch`; an external on-disk save of `openclaw.json` inside the first write's apply window) were refused before apply by the base-hash guard (`config base hash required…`, `config changed since last load…`), so no live-supersession trace is claimed for the new head; the scheduler repair remains proven by the focused regression, as stated below.

#### Checks at the final head

- `config-reload.superseded-retry.test.ts` (1) and `server-reload-managed-secrets.test.ts` (19): **20 passed** at `b7c03efe8cb7da0cdc4af54b36e90b19de79e2d9`; the same two files on the merge parent: 19 passed, superseded-retry failed. After the guard removal (head `c3efb3da9a340c5957702cfbe783b8976593d52b`), superseded-retry, upstream's managed-secrets suite and `config-reload.test.ts` pass together.
- Gateway test-path list, test-projects routing and CI node test plan checks: 284 passed on the first merge commit of this refresh.
- Test-line ceiling: `main` keeps `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` at zero slack; this PR adds exactly 118 test lines, so each merge admits the measured total with no future allowance. `main` raised its own zero-slack ceiling twice more while this refresh was running (ceiling-only merges `d9bc85d1ff74122e2188028ddb72876ecf0f366b` and `1b9faf2d32354ceb3d0d93ef68c4da23cc0a1667`). After the guard removal the PR adds 60 test lines, which fit under `main`'s current ceiling, so `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` is back to `main`'s file.
- The merge commits require fresh maintainer security approval on the final head; none is claimed.

### Exact-head real Gateway recovery: `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625`

<!-- pr177823-real-gateway-repair-b8c13e0 -->

The previously stalling workload now completes on the final fixed full Gateway: **437 ms server / 439 ms client**, after a real SIGUSR2 in-process restart and concurrent synthetic credential refresh, with **no later config edit**.

Important distinction: this final run logged **zero supersessions**. The repair prevents the permanent resolved-value/SecretRef mismatch that produced them on the older head. This is not presented as a new-head trace that throws a supersession and then succeeds.

#### Comparable real-runtime controls

| Source | Same restart + file-credential-refresh workload | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct parent `08d04a9d7b97e50849ba089c3837d2e1c3c4f7fd` | One supersession, credential restored, no additional config write | Original patch still pending at the 30 s client deadline. It answered UNAVAILABLE only during shutdown, at 50,016 ms. **FAIL** |
| Initial PR head `ebfffd5599a7ee7c6d793718b96f923107b27691` | Eight supersessions before credential restoration; retries continued afterward | Original patch still pending at 30 s; 482 supersessions were recorded before task-owned forced cleanup. **FAIL** |
| First repair `c337231afc47e7cf137f0273a9051daab79b71ae` | Identical public-RPC/file workload | Original patch answered in **308 ms**, but broader CI exposed a restart-reapply regression. This is prior-head runtime evidence, not the final candidate. |

All runs used OpenClaw 2026.10.5, Node v26.8.1, macOS arm64, independently owned dependencies, isolated synthetic HOME/state/config/workspace, and distinct free loopback ports between control families. The final build and runtime-postbuild stamps both identify exact `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625` with `inputsClean:true`.

No mocked hot-reload callback, injected exception, fake clock, manually settled receipt, inference call, live Mattermost traffic, operator Gateway change, or TEST/PROD mutation was used in these real Gateway runs.

#### Executed workload

1. Start the full maintained Gateway with `node scripts/run-node.mjs --profile pr177823proof gateway run --port <isolated-port> --verbose`; wait for readiness.
2. Send SIGUSR2 only to that fixture's own Gateway PID; verify **in-process restart** and readiness again.
3. Connect through the real token-authenticated Gateway WebSocket protocol (v4). Read `config.get` for the base hash.
4. Submit one `config.patch` with `response:"summary"`:
   ```json
   {"channels":{"mattermost":{"accounts":{"proof":{"baseUrl":"${PR177823_MATTERMOST_URL}"}}}}}
   ```
   The environment placeholder resolves to the existing synthetic URL; the Mattermost account is disabled.
5. After the actual `config.patch write` log, rotate a task-owned JSON file's synthetic provider key A→B and call the real `secrets.reload {}` RPC. The provider is a custom `proof/proof` model pointing at an unused loopback endpoint; no model turn is sent. Its config uses:
   ```json
   {"apiKey":{"source":"file","provider":"proof","id":"/apiKey"}}
   ```
6. Observe for 2.5 s, restore that **credential file** B→A, and call `secrets.reload {}` again. Do not edit config or send another config-write RPC. The RPC deadline stays 30 s.
7. Join Gateway shutdown. On the fixed head, the original patch had already completed before step 6.

```text

18:27:43.192 [gateway] restart mode: in-process restart
```

### Focused behavioral regression and checks

- The stable-key and rotated-key cases once added to `server-reload-managed-secrets.test.ts` were dropped on October 28 together with the guard they covered; upstream #183964 carries an equivalent case ("settles an unchanged activation write whose secrets are still unresolved").

prs.title: fix: resume interrupted chats after database preparation
prs.body: Fixes #187809. ## What Problem This Solves A graceful restart or source update can leave interrupted chats inactive and accepted follow-ups queued when their databases finish preparation after startup's recovery scan. ## User Impact Eligible marked sessions and their accepted follow-ups recover when their stores become usable. Ready agents remain responsive while unrelated databases are still being inspected. Retained inputs acquire their normal queue slots before fresh inputs to the same store, with current sender authority and session identities checked at admission. ## Why This Change Was Made The existing database startup owner now captures actual restart work before publishing writable admission and runs recovery after its temporary preparation access ends. Database readiness and input readiness have separate completion points, so recovery does not wait globally for unrelated inspection or block its own database writes. Initial and deferred recovery share one operation per physical store, including shared stores. Ordinary input preflights consume that readiness through the existing owner. The regression uses the production startup adapter, real shutdown markers and native integrity workers, with controls for initially unreadable stores, shared-store ordering, current-principal refusal and cancellation. The canonical restart-recovery documentation describes the ordering. ## Evidence - The linked issue records a native reproduction and a real source update that retained markers and the original queued input but left the chats inactive. A same-source restart control recovered normally outside the pending-admission interval. - Remote formatting, lint, file caps and all seven production/test type groups passed. Related tests cover the changed owners and callers; all 70 cases in the three corrected fixture files passed, including the five native recovery scenarios. - The required target integration passed refreshed fast checks, all seven type groups and 219 recovery/normalization/reader/startup tests. The target’s existing legacy upgrade rule is preserved, including late recovery of a legacy-only row in the held native store. - Copied-source inventory and native provisioning checks passed: 318 tests, with two macOS-only cases skipped on Linux. - The unchanged PostgreSQL inherited-auth startup test passed: an admitted agent can create a session and run before an unrelated auth owner becomes ready. Both PostgreSQL files passed all three cases. - A real forward source update completed both guest tasks and consumed the original accepted follow-up exactly once. Session IDs, queued-input identity/content and sampled saved work/Git state were preserved. A separate final-build graceful restart also resumed and completed its distinct original queued follow-up once. - The hosted real-Gateway restart test passed, covering eligible roots, retained-input FIFO order and the abrupt-shutdown control. Independent review and canonical AutoReview are clean. The required prompt-prefix test passed all 14 cases, and all 75 selected CI jobs passed. ClawSweeper rated the exact head Diamond with no findings. ## Visual evidence []() | View | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Source update: inactive before the fix; automatic continuation after it | ![On the baseline, the healthy updated Gateway leaves the interrupted guest inactive](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b59802ee-49b3-47b5-8b2e-6b75dbd50d4b) | ![On the fixed build, the guest receives one restart instruction and continues with its original follow\-up retained](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b4d9fdcb-5dfd-4edf-984d-107e646df894) | | Final\-build graceful restart: active request and original queue survive | ![An active guest request and a distinct accepted follow\-up before graceful restart](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3cb7164e-e741-48c7-84a0-be4e30ccb517) | ![The same session resumes automatically after restart with the same queued follow\-up](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2be9e72c-4aec-48da-8997-f73e870e89ff) | ### 38\-second final\-build graceful restart and automatic continuation https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08eaab62-934e-4f3f-88d4-6f55f7e9ba5c ### Visual verification - Baseline: bbde2b822c133f615d83a9f1db109960c4d68f9e \(failed source update\); f606cd3f3c4d68a9adfae6aec0c5d76935e78269 \(before the restart control\) - Exact head: `f606cd3f3c4d68a9adfae6aec0c5d76935e78269` - Scenario: Gracefully replace or restart a Gateway while a guest is working and a follow\-up is queued\. Recovery resumes eligible work after database preparation, without resending accepted inputs\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw 2026\.10\.9\-f606cd3f3c4d\-2026\-10\-29T22\-09\-41\.993Z - Source update completion: Both original sessions completed; each original prompt once; original queued content consumed once; no pending inputs or in\-flight runs\. - Restart control: Same session; new boot; exactly one additional restart instruction; queued ID, run ID and content hash unchanged\. - Comparison scope: The failed update and fixed update use separate retained synthetic cohorts\. Original accepted inputs were never replayed\. Viewport, theme and product surface match; the final\-build restart pair uses the same session and data\. - Native source update and final\-build restart succeeded\. - Recorder synchronized with actual post\-boot UI work and verified runtime identity and queue custody\. - Screenshots and the complete recording timeline were inspected; private model footer excluded\. - Successful source\-update completion is verified separately from the restart recording\.

prs.title: fix(supervisor): service-child anchors abort on Node 26 when stdin is /dev/null
prs.body:
Related: #187516

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on Node 26, a service-child group anchor whose stdin is `/dev/null` or a regular file can abort with SIGABRT during retirement, before it sends its closing receipt.

## User Impact

User impact: service-child anchors retire cleanly on Node 26 whatever their stdin is. In the Gateway's production launch path, anchors get a pipe as stdin whenever input is relayed, so no Gateway failure has been observed. This removes a latent abort and fixes a Node 26-only test failure on `release/2026.10.10`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node 26 closes fd 0 when it destroys a stdin `fs.ReadStream` over `/dev/null` or a file. The next libuv handle can then be given fd 0, and libuv's `uv__close` asserts `fd > STDERR_FILENO` when it closes that handle. The anchor still called `process.stdin.destroy()` in `finish()` and in `stopInput()`. Both calls now use `releaseProcessStdin()`, the owner added in #187516. It leaves file-backed stdin open and still releases pipes, sockets and TTYs.

On `release/2026.10.10`, the macOS process census still runs `spawnSync("/bin/ps")` after `stopInput()`. When the test fixture spawns the anchor with `stdio[0]: "ignore"`, the anchor aborts inside `SyncProcessRunner::CloseHandlesAndDeleteLoop -> uv__close`. On main the failure doesn't show because the macOS census became native in #175368, which removed that sync spawn. The anchor hazard is still on main.

## Evidence

- New regression test `keeps /dev/null stdin on fd 0 through retirement`. It starts an anchor with `/dev/null` stdin, and a preload runs `spawnSync` at `beforeExit`.
  - Node 26.12.1 without the fix: `expected { code: null, signal: 'SIGABRT' } to deeply equal { code: 0, signal: null }`
  - Node 26.12.1 with the fix: passes
- `pnpm test` on the anchor retirement, input-lifetime, deadline and preparation tests plus `release-stdin.test.ts`: 37/37 pass on Node 26.12.1 and on Node 24.22.1.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, lint and format pass. The dead-export scan fails on main on unrelated files (`scribes-state.ts`, `delivery-queue-storage.ts`, `session-delivery-queue-storage.ts`, `schtasks...test-support.ts`, `gateway-restart.test-support.ts`). This diff doesn't touch them.
- macOS crash report of the abort on the release head: `abort <- __assert_rtn <- uv__close <- uv__loop_close <- node::SyncProcessRunner::CloseHandlesAndDeleteLoop`.

prs.title: fix(trajectory): keep quoted tool arguments parseable in exports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Trajectory export can report success while quoted, token-like tool arguments leave its final JSON or JSONL files malformed. This preserves the final masking pass and applies it through the existing JSON scalar editor so shared diagnostic exports remain both parseable and masked.

## User Impact

Exported JSON and JSONL parse correctly, while default, configured and registered-secret masking remains in place. Plaintext behavior, bounded operator-pattern scanning and benign values retain their existing contracts. Related: #113709. Thanks to nimarosa and alfred429 for the escaped-quote and installed-exporter reports.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing JSON edit owner handles the final structured-output boundary; native-value serialization stays under that same owner. No new public option, redaction policy, dependency, schema or protocol is authored.

This maintenance normally merges official main `7a617ad187abe0bb0f9aff7ea2a6cde3491a3698` for named CI failures. It retains @steipete's [#187120](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187120) mock-ratchet repair and @shakkernerd's [#187144](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187144) lint repair, with original author/history preserved. The ancestor also carries the official [#187096](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187096) tooltip repair; its presence alone is not proof that the old keyboard-focus failure was repaired. All seven introduced files are byte-identical to `a800c75c`; this integration authors no production, test, assertion, timeout, baseline or allocation change.

## Evidence

Current head **`f842d2cea3595acb8908667a1f77a95add5a55aa`**, tree `3386e27d8eb5ae36c4330c2ae05e2f0e55e23e6c`; normal merge parents `a800c75c` and canonical main `7a617ad`.

### Current CI follow-up (2026-10-30)

[CI 40916840063](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40916840063) completed **failure** for this exact `f842d2ce` head. The failing test job is **UI shard 2/7**: `chat-comment-lifecycle.e2e.test.ts`, “keeps the annotation-only bubble visible while its sent attachment is read”, times out at the HTTP `page.waitForResponse` boundary after 30,000 ms. This is a different case from the earlier sidebar keyboard failure. The previously repaired lint and mock-ratchet jobs passed; maintainer security approval remains required.

The successful preflight log pins the actual CI merge to `9e95be8c256401da133bd16795b884ce4e1ea3bc` and official base to `bbde2b822c133f615d83a9f1db109960c4d68f9e`. I ran the unchanged existing case through the native production-browser fixture on both exact trees, serially: the official base passed (347.71 s total wrapper), and the CI merge passed (232.40 s). These passing replays do **not** reproduce or repair the original CI failure. Native classification remains **new / matching main job passed, selected scope not compared**; matching UI input blobs do not establish runtime causality.

Source inspection found that the manual canonical-message fixture does not update the mock history snapshot used by later refreshes. An independently reviewed one-line candidate using the existing history owner is retained locally, **excluded from this PR**: its full-file run had 4 passes and 2 initial-roster/route-readiness failures; its focused run hit the same setup failure before the changed line. Types, format, test-line budget, line-cap and whitespace passed, but typed lint stopped during SDK declaration preparation at its existing 300,000 ms timeout. Neither the changed scenario nor lint is claimed green. No assertion, deadline, baseline, allocation or production behavior was relaxed, and no further blind retry was performed.

This PR's source head is unchanged. The original UI failure remains unresolved; the next diagnostic must distinguish stale-history refresh, viewport admission and attachment-reader cancellation at the owning boundary. No workflow rerun, maintainer bypass or merge is requested.

- **Actual lint failure and repaired leaf:** [CI 40796440971](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40796440971) fails `eslint(curly)` at `sessions-send-tool.admission.test.ts:722`. The offending blob is identical in the archived exact CI merge/base and the canonical repair's parent. The official brace-only fix retains route scenarios and assertions. The complete current native **core stripe 2**, including its agents phase, now **passes** with the same selection and one lint thread. Native attribution remains **unknown / selected scope differs from main**; the frozen source comparison is separate and the old run is not reclassified.
- **Mock and budget gates:** the current native staged mock-exports ratchet passes. Test lines pass at **6,246,104 / 6,320,000**, with **73,896** slack. The proposal remains production +83 and tests +168 LF. No author allowance, scalar/allocation increase or grant from another PR is used.
- **Current functional proof:** all six complete redaction/export files pass **118 cases** (40 export, 3 new-file, 75 logging cases in three native shards), **622.89 s measured wrapper elapsed**, including **302.08 s worker preparation**. JSON/JSONL validity, configured/default/registered masking, byte identity, reentrancy and existing export controls remain exercised. These are current-tree tests, not 118 added cases.
- **Current static checks:** production types, test-consumer types, all seven files' typed lint, format, line-cap and whitespace pass. Actual Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 12.15.0 meet the branch requirements; root package/lock match the selected baseline, with no dependency reconciliation. Pinned-Bun staging failed and the wrapper used its supported oxlint fallback; Bun execution is not claimed.
- **Independent review reuse:** the prior complete seven-file P0–P2 product review (`4fb7d771a793f1015e898d12f5445816dffa1195`) retains exact production and caller-context blobs; its only differing fixture is covered by the subsequent scoped-clean correction review (`6bf1711a9cc5f13400974bfcd3640d3db8c0f93c`), whose full supplied context also matches. The unchanged product-plus-fixture review set is reused for this mechanical integration. This is not a newly executed review or a fresh whole-CLI certification.

### UI validation remains uncovered

The first local attempt at the same two complete sidebar files did **not reach UI assertions**: I scheduled UI production build concurrently with the native lint owner, and it waited on the checkout's dist-artifact lock. The outer process records -9, with the native cleanup reporting exit 137; the original 360.93 s attempt and owner observation are retained.

After all other checks had exited and ownership was released, the **serial** attempt also stopped **before assertions**: production UI build returned exit 1 after 21 locale-module errors sharing a Vite `fetchModule` transport timeout of **60,000 ms** while loading `scripts/lib/control-ui-i18n-catalog.ts` (**527.71 s** total attempt). The exact underlying transport/compile cause is unclassified. No deadline, assertion, lock, build configuration or source byte was changed to make it pass, and no third blind retry is performed.

Thus neither attempt reproduces nor resolves the old CI menu-key focus assertion. The older local 9e run's 3 failures / 4 passes remains retained; its canonical-six-production-file control only covered the rail `touch: false` failure, not all three cases or the CI menu case. **Current UI validation is not green.** The test-failure policy keeps original failures, attempts, evidence and uncertainty in the PR and continues under normal CI/review gates; no merge/admin exception is requested.

Current-head broad PR CI is red as recorded above, and applicable maintainer security approval remains required. The author does not grant approval, manually rerun workflows or merge upstream. Prior compiled public CLI proof at `9e00ffa3` retains its fixed support-tree scope: a production-file revert control produced two invalid JSON files; the candidate parsed four JSON documents and five JSONL rows while preserving masking, benign controls, private modes and manifest bytes. The six production files remain unchanged, but later support-tree integration is not a new installed CLI, upgrade, vendor, Windows, Bun or real operator-Gateway proof.

<details>
<summary>Previous-head evidence and original failures, retained verbatim with their source scope</summary>

Closes #113709.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes invalid trajectory JSON/JSONL exports when a tool argument contains quoted text such as `echo "=== deploy token ==="`.

## User Impact

Exported diagnostic files remain parseable while retaining default, registered-secret and configured-pattern redaction. No configuration migration is required. CI and maintainer security approval remain required before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final support-file safety pass currently treats serialized JSON as raw text. A match can consume an escaped quote or delimiter and invalidate an otherwise valid export. JSON and NDJSON files now use the existing JSON scalar redactor; plaintext keeps the existing path. Configured regular expressions retain their bounded matching and capture context. The native JSON origin serializer moves intact into the existing token module to keep the logging owner within its file-size budget. The final safety pass from #89354 stays in place.

Thanks to @alfred429 for the report and end-to-end reproduction, and @nimarosa for isolating the escaped-quote case. The older #113810 was closed without merge; this fix retains the safety pass.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(release): pin Linux builder to request SHA
prs.body:
## Summary

- bind Linux release tooling to the completed request run's immutable head SHA
- verify the executing builder independently at publication with its own workflow SHA
- preserve request authorization, supersession, and builder cancellation checks through the publication owner before every mutation
- allow the builder to continue when `main` advances after the request completes

## Why

The Linux builder previously compared the request's head SHA with the later builder workflow SHA. A normal `main` advance between those runs rejected an otherwise valid release request and required a redundant redispatch.

The completed request records immutable tooling SHA A, while the executing builder has independently authorized workflow SHA B. Publication now keeps those identities separate: A selects and revalidates the request-pinned tooling and exact request attempt; B authorizes the active builder run. The existing publication owner continues to perform those checks immediately before release writes.

## Authority-chain proof

- a production-owner harness publishes with request/tooling SHA A and executing builder SHA B, retaining A in the release manifest
- an unauthorized request head is rejected before release mutations
- a superseded request attempt is rejected before release mutations
- a cancelled builder is rejected before release mutations
- existing mid-flight revocation and cancellation cases continue to reauthorize before subsequent writes

## Testing

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test test/scripts/linux-app-channel.test.ts test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (244 passed)
- `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs root` (all 4 shards passed)
- `pnpm exec oxlint test/scripts/linux-app-channel.test.ts test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` (0 warnings, 0 errors)
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check .github/workflows/linux-app-release.yml scripts/linux-app-channel.mjs test/scripts/linux-app-channel.test.ts test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts`
- `git diff --check origin/main -- .github/workflows/linux-app-release.yml scripts/linux-app-channel.mjs test/scripts/linux-app-channel.test.ts test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts`

`pnpm check:workflows` could not start locally because this host lacks Python venv/ensurepip support for the pinned pre-commit/actionlint runtime. The focused workflow guard suite parses the changed YAML and exercises the affected contracts; CI retains the actionlint gate.
