prs.title: perf(update): read candidate state inventory without copying the shared database
prs.body:
Refs #182616

## What Problem This Solves

Candidate update inventory copies the entire shared SQLite database just to read registrations and installed plugin metadata, adding avoidable I/O before the actual candidate snapshot.

## User Impact

Updates with large SQLite state avoid one shared-database copy when the source supports direct read-only inspection. Snapshot publication, integrity checks, and rollback verification remain intact. The candidate worker must contain this improvement.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing isolated inventory worker now uses the existing native read-only inspection owner to capture registrations and plugin records in one pinned transaction, closing it before filesystem inventory. Sources requiring private recovery retain the existing snapshot fallback. This removes work rather than adding a cache or weakening verification.

The other investigated paths did not produce a safe measured update win. Runtime retention already links eligible immutable files and independently copies sensitive files. The standalone Doctor bloat advisory's rehearsal-copy experiment was discarded because candidate Doctor skips that advisory during an update. That diagnostic-only experiment measured 2.618 s → 0.0127 s medians over five runs, but it cannot improve the update flow and is not included. No retention or Doctor production changes are included, and no native SHA dependency change was made.

Thanks @edith-vitaetpax and @WG-Mojo for the reports and Windows measurements.

## Evidence

The committed benchmark exercises real candidate inventory plus snapshot creation, runtime retention, and the full candidate Doctor command. Synthetic input is 2,155,945,984 bytes across a shared database and two agent databases, plus a 256 MiB runtime/plugin tree. Runs used Node 26.12.1 on this Mac with interleaved baseline/candidate pairs and no cache flushing, isolated HOME/state under a realpath-resolved per-user temporary root, a free Gateway port, and service activation disabled. Each snapshot passed full SQLite integrity checks plus exact zero-BLOB payload checks outside its timed phase. Retention consistently linked 256 payloads and copied two metadata files; a retained payload hash was independently checked.

| Phase | Samples per side | Before median | After median | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Inventory + candidate snapshot | 3 | 11.333 s | 7.924 s | 30.1% faster; inventory shared copies 1 → 0 |
| Runtime retention | 3 | 0.306 s | 0.257 s | Unchanged control; no gain claimed |
| Full candidate Doctor | 3 | 54.452 s | 49.389 s | Unchanged control; no gain claimed |

Snapshot ranges were 11.167–15.484 s before and 7.811–10.619 s after, with an improvement in every pair. Retention ranges overlap (0.213–0.452 s before, 0.235–0.279 s after), as do Doctor ranges (47.918–57.451 s before, 48.957–54.004 s after). Both controls call identical implementations on the two sides; their variation is not attributed to the patch. The shared host's initial load averages were 10.56/11.94/14.54. An earlier complete phase bank on the original main base also improved snapshot medians (13.746 → 10.874 s, 20.9%); the table above is the final bank after integrating main.

Reproduce from the checkout:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/update-state-io-measure.ts \
  --baseline c77b791cf4fca27afe64a6da4ee9ba22f5133a28 --samples 3
```

The benchmark freezes the baseline snapshot owner and uses unchanged dependencies from this checkout. The measured candidate owner SHA-256 is `10803edc49c271cb969e33329bba72359e1b006173e5e502fb27ee92e8c22fe5`. This is phase proof, not an end-to-end update downtime or Windows throughput claim. Removing a whole SQLite backup also removes its reads and writes on Windows, but Defender and non-cloning filesystem performance were not measured here. Existing clone-aware copying, WAL online backup, publication hashes, and restore-time verification stay in place.

Validation:

- DELETE-journal and live-WAL regressions fail on the untouched base at the intended unnecessary-copy assertion, with source database/WAL bytes checked for preservation.
- Ran all 59 importer files in the original `rg` order with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --maxWorkers=1`: on the initial base, 1,005 tests passed, 29 platform/PostgreSQL cases skipped, and one rollback diagnostic case failed (1,877.5 s wall time). The failure expected `state-migrated-no-rollback` but received the preserved initiating `version-mismatch`; rollback and restart were both refused. The original admission error was not captured. An isolated base case and a full 45-test candidate file passed during diagnosis; these passing replays are not claimed as a fix.
- Advanced the task branch to current main for the relevant upstream stale-actor policy-retirement fix #187870. Fresh proof on this base passed all 99 tests across the actor-policy owner regression, inventory, capacity, and rollback files (301.75 s wall time). No rollback production logic or expectations were changed in this PR; the original intermittent failure remains disclosed rather than being declared cured by replay. The maintainer classified it as a pre-existing order-dependent flake observed on the pre-#187870 base and authorized publication with this disclosure.
- Publication rebase onto `548649e1dc47e16b26cc415e03f3e810f9ef5a65` preserved the measured inventory owner hash and the reviewed diff. The requested one-time rerun passed all 89 tests across inventory, capacity, and rollback (227.81 s wall time):

  ```sh
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/infra/update-candidate-state.inventory.test.ts \
    src/infra/update-candidate-rehearsal.resources.test.ts \
    src/cli/update-cli/update-command-rollback.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  ```

- Core, scripts, and infra-test TypeScript lanes passed; focused oxlint and oxfmt passed; madge reported zero cycles.
- Both ratchets passed: max-lines 404 existing suppressions, OPENCLAW names 458/458; test lines 6,277,521 below 6,327,270.
- Fixed an encountered test cost: the capacity test deep-compared two 8 MiB Buffers through the assertion framework. Native `Buffer.equals` retains byte-for-byte preservation and reduces test time from 30.035 s to 0.044 s. Focused replay: one pass; 45.19 s file wall time was 95% shared transform preparation.
- Existing slower coverage: lease scenarios totaled 252.387 s of test time; original-service scenarios 181.833 s; rollback scenarios 134.749 s; database-rollback scenarios 123.252 s. These repeatedly exercise real state workers and service recovery. The Doctor migration/native-bookkeeping case took 36.803 s and launches a separate source-runtime migration process; no timeouts, retries, or assertions were weakened.
- Fresh isolated Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Simplification pass retained one existing inspection owner and the recovery fallback.
- Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was skipped under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI supplies broad proof.

Production change: +15/-3 lines (net +12). Regression tests: +17/-8 (net +9). The benchmark and documentation are separate proof deliverables. No dependency, schema, product CLI, config, or baseline changes.

prs.title: fix(config): clobber snapshots skipped silently when the lock is not released
prs.body:
Related: #153482

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: config clobber snapshots are skipped with no log when the snapshot lock cannot be removed.

## User Impact

Operators see a warning naming the stuck lock and the 30s stale window.

## Why This Change Was Made

Lock release now warns on any error except ENOENT. It never throws. Snapshots still wait for the lock to go stale.

## Evidence

- `src/config/io.clobber-snapshot.test.ts`: red on base, 6 pass with the fix (sync and async, EPERM warns, ENOENT does not).
- `io.observe-recovery.test.ts` 32 pass; core tsgo, test tsgo, oxlint and format clean.
- Gap: release failure is injected, not reproduced on a real filesystem.


## Proof

Real CLI (`openclaw sessions`) on a throwaway HOME: clobbered `openclaw.json` plus a good `.bak`. A second process adds a file to the lock dir while it is held (the dir holds 100k empty files to widen the race), so the real `rmdir` fails with ENOTEMPTY. No mocks. Base 94cee2a vs this PR.

Before (base):
```
Config auto-restored from backup: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json (gateway-mode-missing-vs-last-good)
$ ls ~/.openclaw | grep clobber
openclaw.json.clobbered.2026-10-23T16-42-23-841Z
openclaw.json.clobber.lock
# same again within 30s
Config backup recovery deferred: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json; original config snapshot could not be saved. Retry recovery.
```

After (this PR):
```
Config clobber snapshot lock ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.clobber.lock could not be released (ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.clobber.lock'); snapshots are skipped until it goes stale (30s).
Config auto-restored from backup: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json (gateway-mode-missing-vs-last-good)
$ ls ~/.openclaw | grep clobber
openclaw.json.clobbered.2026-10-23T16-45-09-862Z
openclaw.json.clobber.lock
# same again within 30s
Config backup recovery deferred: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json; original config snapshot could not be saved. Retry recovery.
```

Async path, calling `recoverConfigFromJsonRootSuffix` (the function Doctor uses; not run via `doctor --fix`), after:
```
Config clobber snapshot lock ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.clobber.lock could not be released (ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.clobber.lock'); snapshots are skipped until it goes stale (30s).
Config auto-stripped non-JSON prefix: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json (original saved as ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.clobbered.2026-10-23T16-45-24-744Z)
recoverConfigFromJsonRootSuffix -> true
```

The config is restored and the snapshot saved in both runs. The only change is that the stuck lock is now reported.

prs.title: fix(macos): keep secrets when a Gateway config save fails
prs.body:
Closes #187600 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the macOS app writes `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__` over channel tokens and the Gateway auth token in `openclaw.json` when a settings save (Browser toggle, Tailscale apply) reaches the Gateway but `config.set` times out or fails while the Gateway restarts. ## User Impact A failed Gateway save now fails visibly (Tailscale shows the error, the Browser toggle reverts to the saved value) and `openclaw.json` is left unchanged. Before, the save reported success and the next Gateway start failed with "Gateway auth token is a known redaction sentinel" until the user ran `openclaw doctor --fix` and re-paired devices. ## Why This Change Was Made `ConfigStore.save` now sends Gateway-loaded documents only to `config.set`, the owner that restores redacted values. Documents loaded while the Gateway was unreachable come from the unredacted file with no lease and keep the direct local write, unchanged by this PR.
Root cause `ConfigStore.load` builds the document from `config.get`, which redacts secrets in place (`src/config/redact-snapshot.ts`). On a save error that `permitsLocalFallback` allowed (a timeout, a dropped connection), the `catch` in `ConfigStore.save` passed that same root to `saveLocal` → `OpenClawConfigFile.saveDict(preserveExistingKeys: true)`, whose merge lets every incoming leaf overwrite the file. `preserveGatewayAuthIfNeeded` protected only `gateway.auth`, and Tailscale passes `allowGatewayAuthMutation: true`. The save-time fallback dates from before #137502. Since that change a document without a Gateway lease is written locally before any Gateway call, so in production only lease-holding (redacted) documents reached the fallback. Removing it leaves `permitsLocalFallback` in use for `load`, which still falls back to the local file when `config.get` fails. Gateway-loaded documents also no longer reach the merge, so they no longer inline `$include` content or drop key removals. Saves of documents loaded offline are unchanged.
## Evidence ### Packaged macOS app, real `config.set` timeout Both builds were packaged ad hoc from this branch: `main` (with `ConfigStore.swift` from `upstream/main`) and this fix. Each ran under an isolated named profile in local mode. The profile's Gateway LaunchAgent ran a small WebSocket proxy in front of the real Gateway. The proxy forwards every frame and drops only `config.set` requests, so the app's own transport times out after 10 s. The config held test values `gateway.auth.token = test-gateway-token-0002` and `channels.telegram.botToken = 123456:test-bot-token`. The trigger was the status-menu **Browser** button. Both runs started from the same config file. main: ``` 16:55:05.039Z [proxy] client req config.get 16:55:05.050Z [proxy] client req config.set 16:55:05.050Z [proxy] DROPPED config.set id=00C705DD-... 22:25:15 local: openclaw.json rewritten by the app channels.telegram.botToken = __OPENCLAW_REDACTED__ gateway.auth.token = test-gateway-token-0002 (kept by preserveGatewayAuthIfNeeded; Tailscale apply passes allowGatewayAuthMutation: true and loses it too) browser.enabled = false ``` This branch: ``` 16:58:00.852Z [proxy] client req config.get 16:58:00.863Z [proxy] client req config.set 16:58:00.863Z [proxy] DROPPED config.set id=EF202F2C-... 16:58:11.390Z [proxy] client req config.get (menu reloads the saved value after the failed save) openclaw.json: byte-identical to the pre-click file (cmp), botToken = 123456:test-bot-token, browser.enabled = true ``` Screenshot of the main-build menu after the click: Browser shows off, matching the file. ### Offline editing The profile Gateway was stopped (port closed) and the Browser button clicked on each build. Neither build wrote the file: `browser.enabled` stayed `true`, and the menu showed "Cannot reach gateway at localhost:64313". The app logged repeated control-channel endpoint recovery during the save. The offline-load path is unchanged by this PR, and lease-less documents still go straight to `saveLocal`. Behavior with the Gateway down is the same before and after. ### Gateway and test evidence Isolated Gateway (`pnpm openclaw gateway run`, private `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, loopback port) seeded with `gateway.auth.token` and `channels.telegram.botToken`: - `openclaw gateway call config.get --json`: `hash` present, both secrets returned as `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__`. - Control: `config.set` with that raw and `baseHash`, `browser.enabled` flipped: the file keeps both real values. - Consequence on main: `openclaw gateway run` on a file with the sentinel exits with `Gateway failed to start: Gateway auth token is a known redaction sentinel, not a credential. Run openclaw doctor --fix ...`. The new Swift test runs the real `ConfigStore.load`/`save` against a temp `openclaw.json`, with the `config.get` document shape and the transport's `gateway request timed out after 10000ms`. It fails on main (`didThrow`, `after == before`) and passes here. `ConfigStoreTests`, `OpenClawConfigFileTests`, `TailscaleIntegrationSectionTests`, `BrowserControlSettingTests`, `HealthStoreStateTests` and the StatusMenu descriptor/reconcile/width/summaries suites: 80 tests pass. `StatusMenuRecoveryPresentationTests` (a screenshot capture test) fails on a `#require` of the unset `OPENCLAW_TEST_MENU_CAPTURE_DIR`; it does not use `ConfigStore`. ### Upgrade from latest stable (2026.10.9) Built from the merged head `9069abec3c0` (version 2026.10.9; `ConfigStore.swift` and its test identical to `0e36b5c84cd`, where the runs above were taken). 1. `openclaw@2026.10.9` from npm wrote a fresh isolated profile and installed its Gateway as the profile's LaunchAgent. Config: `gateway.auth.token = test-gateway-token-0004`, `channels.telegram.botToken = 123456:test-bot-token`, `agents.defaults.maxConcurrent = 4`, `messages.ackReactionScope = all`, `browser.enabled = true`, `meta.lastTouchedVersion = 2026.10.9`. 2. Update: stopped the 2026.10.9 service, ran this build's `openclaw doctor --fix` (pre-migration SQLite backups saved, state migrations applied), then installed the service from this build's runtime. Health ok. The upgraded app connected (operator and node). 3. Successful save, Browser button: `config.set` went through, and the Gateway logged `config hot reload applied (browser.enabled)`. The file now has `browser.enabled = false`, and the token, botToken, `maxConcurrent = 4` and `ackReactionScope = all` are unchanged. 4. Failed save, same Gateway behind the `config.set`-dropping proxy: three clicks, three `DROPPED config.set`, each followed by the menu's `config.get` about 10 s later. `openclaw.json` is byte-identical (`cmp`) to the file before the first click. Without step 2, the upgraded app first reported "Another OpenClaw process is using your data" because the old Gateway held the state database. That is the existing update sequence and not affected by this diff. Screenshot of the menu after the successful save: Browser off. Accepted edge: when the Gateway save fails, the Browser toggle reverts to the saved value without a message, as it already did for other save failures. The test replaces `local save can fall back to protected direct write when gateway is unavailable`, which asserted the removed behavior. Production delta +5/-12; test delta +33/-14. Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the fallback with no state or config migration. Blast radius is macOS app saves of Gateway-loaded config in local mode when `config.set` fails.

prs.title: fix(diagnostics): stuck-session recovery never runs on hosts with late heartbeat ticks
prs.body:
Fixes #142200.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where automatic stuck-session recovery stops running for the lifetime of a Gateway process on virtualized hosts, so a session that hangs is warned about repeatedly but never recovered.

The diagnostic heartbeat treats its own lateness as a sign the event loop is congested. When a tick fires more than one second past its 30 second deadline, recovery decisions are deferred to the next healthy tick:

`src/logging/diagnostic.ts:1165`

```ts
const shouldDeferRecovery = heartbeatOverdueMs >= DEFAULT_LIVENESS_EVENT_LOOP_DELAY_WARN_MS;
```

```ts
if (!recovery || shouldDeferRecovery) {
  continue;
}
requestStuckSessionRecovery({ ... });
```

That tolerates 3.3 percent slop on a 30 second timer. The reporter measured a WSL2 host waking a sleeping timer 1120 to 1681 milliseconds late on 32 consecutive ticks while the true event-loop delay stayed at 10 to 13 milliseconds and the Gateway sat at 2.2 percent CPU. Every tick deferred, so the next healthy heartbeat the deferral waits for never arrived:

```
13:16:26.368Z WARN liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=1483ms elapsed=31483ms; deferring recovery decisions
13:16:57.914Z WARN liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=1546ms elapsed=31546ms; deferring recovery decisions
13:17:29.472Z WARN liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=1558ms elapsed=31558ms; deferring recovery decisions
```

`logSessionAttention` still fires, so the operator sees stuck-session warnings, but `requestStuckSessionRecovery` is unreachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deferral protects a real case and is kept. What is wrong is the signal it reads. Wakeup latency is a property of the host scheduler; whether queued progress is stuck behind a blocked loop is a property of the event loop, and the Gateway already runs a sampler that measures the second one. On the reporter's ticks that sampler read 10 to 13 milliseconds while the heartbeat called the same ticks congested.

**The verdict belongs to the monitor, not the heartbeat.** Only the sampler knows whether its own next sample is overdue, and that turns out to be the whole answer:

`src/gateway/server/event-loop-health.ts`

```ts
eventLoopDelayed: () =>
  nowMs() - lastSampleAt >= EVENT_LOOP_DELAY_WARN_MS ||
  (lastSnapshot?.reasons.includes("event_loop_delay") ?? false),
```

`lastSampleAt` advances on every sampler callback, including the early-return path where a quiet window commits no snapshot, so it is a liveness marker for the sampler itself. A stall starves that 20 millisecond callback, which means the retained observation predates the stall and still reads healthy. The interval since the last callback is itself a delay measurement, so the monitor can answer correctly without waiting for a new observation to commit.

The Gateway passes that verdict for recovery and keeps the persistent filter for warnings, which are different questions:

```ts
readEventLoopDelayed: readinessEventLoopHealth.eventLoopDelayed,
```

`persistentDegradationSnapshot()` withholds anything under 60 seconds of continuous degradation (`event-loop-health.ts:14`, `:207-213`), which is right for an operator warning and wrong for a recovery decision, because a shorter genuine stall still holds queued progress.

Session ages continue to be measured against `recoveryObservationNow = now - heartbeatOverdueMs`, which is untouched, so timer jitter still cannot push a run past its threshold early.

Two earlier revisions of this PR got the mechanism wrong and are worth naming, since the current shape is a response to both. A counter capping consecutive deferrals gave chronic lateness a standing exemption. Comparing observation identity across ticks only proved that something had been published since the last heartbeat, which across a 30 second interval is about thirty commits, so a pre-stall observation still passed. Reading the pending sample interval has neither hole, adds no constant, and removes the third "no evidence" state entirely.

Because the callback is now a plain `() => boolean`, no freshness or identity semantics leak to SDK hosts implementing it. There is no longer a wrong way to return the value.

An earlier revision of this PR also carried a standalone fallback that read completed histogram samples when no verdict was supplied. That had the same ordering hole, with no way to detect its own pending sample, so it is removed rather than rebuilt. `startDiagnosticHeartbeat` is exported through `src/plugin-sdk/logging-core.ts`, and callers that omit the verdict now defer on a late tick, which is exactly main's behavior today. Only the Gateway changes.

No configuration option is added.

## User Impact

On hosts with chronic timer lateness, mainly WSL2 and other VMs, stuck sessions are recovered automatically again instead of only being warned about. A genuinely blocked event loop still defers recovery, including a stall shorter than the warning filter's minute and a stall that starved the sampler itself. The repeated warning now says which of the two it observed:

```
liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=1483ms elapsed=31483ms; event loop stayed responsive, keeping recovery decisions
```

## Evidence

Production change is +40/-5 across three files, of which the Gateway wiring is one line.

The contract is proven at its owner, against the real monitor rather than a fake:

```ts
harness.samples(50);
expect(harness.monitor.snapshot()).toMatchObject({ degraded: false, reasons: [] });
expect(harness.monitor.eventLoopDelayed()).toBe(false);
harness.elapseWithoutSampling(1_200);
expect(harness.monitor.snapshot()).toMatchObject({ degraded: false, reasons: [] });
expect(harness.monitor.eventLoopDelayed()).toBe(true);
```

Healthy sampling, then the heartbeat-before-sampler window, asserting the snapshot still reads healthy while the verdict does not. Reducing the verdict to snapshot-only, the pre-fix semantics, fails it:

```
× reports a delayed loop once its own sample is overdue, before any new observation
  AssertionError: expected false to be true
  Tests  1 failed | 20 passed (21)
```

Reverting `src/logging/diagnostic.ts` to main, so the deferral reads lateness again:

```
× keeps recovery running when ticks are late but the event loop stayed responsive
  Error: missing recoverStuckSession call
```

A companion test asserts ten consecutive keeping-up samples stay `false`, so the guard fails in both directions rather than only one.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/logging                              9 files, 110 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server/event-loop-health.test.ts,
  question.recovery.test.ts                                                    49 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway (recovery lane)             36 files, 697 passed
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                                  clean
oxlint / oxfmt on all five touched files                                         clean
```

Proof gap worth stating plainly: this is fake-timer coverage of the heartbeat decision plus real-monitor coverage of the contract it depends on, not a runtime trace on an affected host. I have no WSL2 or VM host and cannot manufacture chronic host wakeup lateness here, so producing that trace would mean fabricating it. For anyone who does have such a host: run the Gateway with diagnostics enabled, leave a session `processing` past `stuckSessionWarnMs`, and grep for `liveness heartbeat delayed`. Before this change every line ends `deferring recovery decisions` and recovery is never requested; after it, lines end `event loop stayed responsive, keeping recovery decisions` and recovery is requested.

AI-assisted: yes. I traced the source path by hand and ran every command above myself.

prs.title: fix(cli): openclaw agent waits silently when the model asks a question
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/187728

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw agent` prints nothing until the question timeout (900 seconds by default) when the model calls `ask_user`, because the terminal cannot show or answer structured questions.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw agent` returns promptly with the agent's question in its text reply, instead of hanging for up to 15 minutes and then continuing with an answer the user never chose. This holds for fresh sessions and for sessions an earlier client, such as the Control UI, already used. Runs with `--deliver` keep the delivery channel's question support.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186653 made the ACP bridge declare the `no-question-input` client capability, so its turns omit `ask_user` and the agent asks in text. `openclaw agent` sent no such declaration, so its turns were still offered `ask_user`.

- The CLI now declares `no-question-input` in its Gateway identity, unless the run is delivered to a channel.
- The tool list follows the capabilities recorded on the session, and only chat.send and channel ingress recorded them, so a session the Control UI used first kept offering `ask_user` to a later CLI turn. The Gateway `agent` method now records the caller's capabilities for visible operator turns, with the same rule chat.send ingress uses (now one shared function). Internal wakes, inter-session input, hidden runs and in-process callers such as plugin `subagent.run` turns, which use synthetic clients, record nothing and keep the recorded capabilities.

Docs for the command, the handshake capability, and `ask_user` availability name the new case.

Accepted edge case: the session keeps the capabilities of its most recent client turn. `openclaw agent` targets the agent's main session by default, which is also the Control UI's main chat. A CLI turn there switches the session's tool list (and its wakes') to the CLI's, without `ask_user`, `screen` or `show_widget`, until the next Control UI turn switches it back; each switch costs one prompt-cache miss. This is the existing contract when two chat.send clients with different capabilities alternate on one session.

Not changed: a CLI message that continues a run already active on the session keeps that run's client capabilities when they are a subset of the CLI's (the continuation rule in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority-inbound.ts`), so a run started by another client can still call `ask_user` until it ends. The `secrets` tool's `request` action also waits for user input and does not read `no-question-input`; that predates this PR and is left for a follow-up.

## Evidence

Both sides ran the built CLI against an isolated loopback Gateway (synthetic token, temporary state directory) and a deterministic OpenAI-compatible fixture provider. When `ask_user` is offered, the fixture calls it with a 30 second timeout; otherwise it asks the same question in text. The second scenario first sends one `chat.send` turn on the same session, as the Control UI does, then runs the CLI. Before ran on the base f25b36e95b0161b324ad772127264fb0021c4d6c (an independent reviewer's clean-base runs); After on this branch at 5424e0bc519.

| `openclaw agent` run | Before (base) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh session | 34.96 s, `ask_user` offered and called, no answer | 3.41 s, not offered, question in the reply |
| Session used by an earlier chat turn | 32.15 s, `ask_user` offered and called, no answer | 1.95 s, not offered on the CLI turn, question in the reply |
| Same session, real model (Gemini 3.8 Flash) | — | 5.72 s, no `ask_user` call, question in the reply |

On the base, the command printed nothing for the whole question timeout (30 s here, 900 s by default), then the agent went on with "No answer arrived, so I will use Blue." The chat.send turn still offers `ask_user` to its own client.

<details>
<summary>Fixture runs (request log condensed to one line per model request)</summary>

Fresh session, before:

```text
$ time openclaw agent --agent main --message "Pick a color for the banner." --json
exit=0 elapsed=34.959759580s

# fixture provider request log
{"call":1,"askUserListedDirectly":false,"askUserInToolDirectory":true}
{"call":2,"askUserListedDirectly":false,"askUserInToolDirectory":true}

# tool result returned to the model on call 2
"id": "openclaw:core:ask_user"
"text": "No answer arrived; proceed with best judgment.\n\n{\n  \"status\": \"no_answer\"\n}"

# final reply
```

prs.title: fix(onboard): migrate legacy credentials during onboarding instead of looping on AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED
prs.body:
Fixes #187903. Thanks @gibranrubio for the report.

## What Problem This Solves

Local non-interactive onboarding stops with AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED when a deployment wrapper writes legacy credential JSON before invoking it. Running Doctor manually does not resolve setup if the wrapper recreates that file on every attempt.

## User Impact

Onboarding now imports legacy credentials through Doctor's existing migration owner before applying an auth choice. Verified imports archive the original bytes, retain other providers' credentials, and let repeated setup complete. Migration warnings remain visible; failed imports retain Doctor's recovery behavior. Runtime credential reads remain SQLite-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Standalone fresh onboarding on both v2026.10.2 and current main already writes SQLite and creates neither auth-profiles.json nor models.json. Seeding agents/main/agent/auth-profiles.json reproduces the reported failure in both versions.

The Render template [pins AlphaClaw 0.9.37](https://github.com/render-examples/openclaw-render-template/blob/main/package.json). Its [saveAuthStore fallback](https://github.com/chrysb/alphaclaw/blob/v0.9.37/lib/server/auth-profiles.js) writes that JSON file whenever its direct agent-database SQLite adapter returns false, including a missing database. AlphaClaw should remove the JSON fallback and direct database writes, and use supported OpenClaw onboarding/model-auth operations. This investigation inspected wrapper source without executing third-party code or accessing the reporter's container.

The fix calls the existing Doctor repair owner after Gateway option validation and before provider setup. It introduces no schema, dependency, config option, or runtime compatibility reader. Production/test/docs delta: +13/+55/+6 lines. The simplification pass retained the existing migration, verification, receipts, and archival owners rather than introducing another credential writer.

## Evidence

All state and HOME were isolated; credentials and Gateway tokens were synthetic. No managed Gateway was started or modified.

- Exercised the reported onboarding flag set on published openclaw@2026.10.2 and current main, substituting an isolated workspace, a free port, and synthetic values. Fresh state succeeded on both; seeded legacy JSON failed on both with AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED.
- Fixed real CLI: onboarding succeeded with seeded legacy JSON, then succeeded again after recreating the same file. The archive remained byte-preserved, legacy JSON was absent, and Anthropic plus the unrelated OpenRouter credential remained in canonical SQLite. No models.json was created.
- Regression: red on the base at AuthProfileMigrationRequiredError; green after the fix. Final: 1 test passed, 6.045 seconds test time / 15.37 seconds runner wall time. Cold run: 11.413 seconds test time / 55.95 seconds wall time, dominated by shared transform preparation. CI seconds pending.
- Direct/barrel consumers and Gateway onboarding siblings: 8 files, 71 tests passed in original selected order; two Vitest shards, 138.16 seconds runner wall time. The first run hit the documented writable-volume temp-root artifact; correcting TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP to the private per-user temp root passed.
- Production and commands-test tsgo, targeted core oxlint, oxfmt, git diff --check passed. Test typechecking caught and corrected the regression's missing environment argument.
- Madge: 0 cycles. Both ratchets passed: max-lines 404 grandfathered suppressions; OPENCLAW_* names 458/458; test lines 6,277,864 / ceiling 6,327,305. No baseline edits.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the local diff against f421bd20a6fafed028f779666c0e9c97888f6acf, with Doctor migration context, completed scoped-clean at P0–P2. No actionable findings. A later test-only explicit environment argument correction passed typecheck and regression; production diff unchanged. Review did not independently execute tests or inspect the entire unchanged local setup flow.
- Per campaign gate budget, full check:changed SQLite inventory was skipped; PR CI supplies broad proof. No remote compute. No provider inference was attempted: this proves onboarding persistence and recovery.

Reproduction command, with isolated HOME / OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR and a safe private temp root:

```sh
openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --flow quickstart \
  --gateway-bind loopback --gateway-port "$FREE_PORT" \
  --gateway-auth token --gateway-token synthetic-onboarding-token \
  --no-install-daemon --skip-health --workspace "$PROOF_STATE/workspace" \
  --auth-choice apiKey --anthropic-api-key sk-ant-api03-synthetic-onboarding-fixture
```

The source checkout used `pnpm openclaw`; the release used its installed `openclaw.mjs` entrypoint. Regression command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/onboard-non-interactive.legacy-auth.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

prs.title: fix(update): size backups realistically and restart the Gateway after a refused swap
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #184254. SQLite-heavy updates can reserve agent-sized scratch for shared update history, refuse a backup that fits, and reduce the initiating package-swap failure to `[redacted-diagnostic]`.

## User Impact

Backup admission now sizes the retained backup and writable rollback outputs from measured database/journal families, with history scratch based on shared state. A refused swap reports needed and available capacity plus the backup/rollback volume role without private paths. Thanks @pawelbbdrozd for correlating the failed runs and supplying the disk and recovery diagnostics.

## Why This Change Was Made

#186980 already reduced one history charge on main, but two largest-family allowances still charged a large agent database for shared-history work. The remaining SQLite allowance is `2S + 3H + 64 MiB`, where S includes database and supporting files and H is shared state. Unknown/mixed ownership keeps the conservative fallback; actual rollback output space is checked again before current files move.

The swap result owner now passes its original error to the existing failure-fact owner. Closed capacity metadata survives the worker boundary and public report projection. The existing recovery owner already restarts and verifies an owned stopped Gateway when no data is at risk (#172784); that behavior was verified on main rather than duplicated. The new swap regression also verifies rollback of the untouched previous package and launcher after capture refuses. Installed updater and worker fixes are required for the complete diagnostic path; a newer candidate cannot retrofit an older parent's reporting.

Production: +34/-16 lines (net +18). Tests: +64/-6 (net +58), allocated in a separate regression record for the real swap/report/recovery boundary and closed public capacity templates. No shared baseline edits, config options, dependency changes, or database schema changes.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on base `2bc19eb1e725`: both WAL/non-WAL large-agent cases refused 74 MiB available because activation demanded about 80 MiB. The real swap/report regression also failed with `[redacted-diagnostic]` before the swap-owner repair. Both are green after the fix.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/package-update-swap.capacity.test.ts src/infra/package-update-swap.test.ts src/infra/package-update-swap.integrity.test.ts src/infra/package-update-swap.bounds.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **63 passed**, 4 files, 37.69 s wall. The new test itself took **370 ms**; its file's 26.30 s wall was dominated by compiler preparation.
- Consumer search using the changed production basenames, plus backup/restore siblings: **596 passed**, 23 files, 8 shards, **515.43 s wall**. This preceded the final one-line swap-result plumbing change, covered by the focused swap run above. `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-failure-recovery.test.ts`: **26 passed**, 29.57 s wall, including Linux/Windows safe recovery and data-at-risk refusal. No retries or timeout increases.
- Core typecheck, touched-file type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, Madge (0 cycles), `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check:test-lines-ratchet`, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, and `git diff --check` passed. The full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was skipped for time; the targeted gates above were used. PR CI supplies broad proof; CI timing is pending.
- Final independent **Codex autoreview**, P0–P2, on the local snapshot against `2bc19eb1e725` (identical committed source): **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The final review explicitly traced worker refusal → swap transaction callback → failure fact → public report.

Live proof used isolated HOME/state under a private temporary directory. A disposable 160 MiB APFS image was created with `hdiutil create -size 160m -fs APFS -volname OpenClawUpdateProof -type SPARSE ...`, mounted privately, and exercised with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/upd-l1977-capacity-proof.mts`. This temporary harness called the real preflight, subprocess backup, package swap, rollback, and public-report owners with real filesystem capacity; no statfs mock:

```text
SQLite family bytes: 4214784
Volume available: 77602816 bytes
Base estimate: 83959808 bytes
Fixed estimate: 75563008 bytes
PASS: preflight + subprocess capture; two snapshots passed integrity/content checks; originals retained.
Update database backup volume: needs 72 MiB; available 58 MiB
PASS: actual low-space worker refusal → swap failure → sanitized public report;
      previous package 1.0.0 and old launcher verified, rollback exit 0.
```

An isolated dev Gateway also passed `/healthz` and `/readyz` on a free port. `pnpm openclaw update --dry-run --json` finished as `skipped / dry-run` with a visible `target-git-cache-stale` diagnostic; it did not perform an update. The Gateway shut down cleanly in 164 ms. The APFS image was detached. The reporter's full Linux pnpm 2026.10.6→2026.10.7 upgrade was not replayed; Linux/Windows service recovery is boundary-test evidence, while the low-space backup/swap/report proof used real local filesystem operations.

prs.title: feat(cron): apply configured default tools before approval
prs.body:
Closes #187767.

## What Problem This Solves

An automation created with an explicit tool list can omit a prerequisite such as `read`, leaving it unable to follow its instructions when it runs.

## User Impact

Operators can configure `cron.defaultTools`. For example, `["execute_code"]` becomes `["execute_code", "read"]` before the existing creator-capability and approval checks. Defaults never grant unavailable tools. The request-level `toolsAllowMode: "exact"` opts out, and `[]` remains tool-less.

Unset configuration, omitted/null selections, saved jobs, unrelated edits, CLI/direct Gateway writes, and already approved request shapes keep their existing behavior. Existing automations need an intentional tool-selection revision. Hosts must integrate and enable the setting separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

One pure resolver serves the native automation tool and the narrow `openclaw/plugin-sdk/cron-tool-defaults` subpath so hosts can construct the same selection before binding approval. Only the concrete selection is persisted; execution-authority provenance is unchanged.

The optional configuration adds two core schema paths (array and item). SDK budgets increase only by the approved one subpath, two exports and one callable. Supporting repairs keep generated snapshots portable on Windows, update the browser test fixture for its existing navigation contract, and use the emitter's canonical path key when rendering SDK declarations. They do not change production browser guards or expand tool permissions.

## Evidence

- Native add/update reproductions failed before the fix; all 13 final native cases pass, including creator restrictions, exact/empty selections, flat requests and unrelated edits. Config (68), schema (45), SDK resolver (2), prompt snapshots (13) and affected browser fixture (10) cases passed on their recorded source revisions; subsequent repairs preserve those inputs.
- The existing real-emission fixture reproduced the Windows declaration lookup failure. The repaired owner suite passed 20 tests with one existing Windows process-join skip. Scoped formatting, generated config documentation and SDK export registration checks passed.
- Independent local Codex review through P2 covered the production change and each subsequent repair with no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper reviewed the production range with no actionable correctness or security findings. Hosted ClawSweeper's input-safety rejection is not a review verdict and was not overridden.
- Final-head canonical SDK comparison completed with exit 0 and successful cleanup at 2026-10-29 22:05 UTC: `20121545966a5212dc3783a0375333fb6cd29eeb` to `47db914b3815620bc3bef787d6ea77fcd0450203`. Acknowledgement: `7071bd34`. One new subpath, two added exports, no removed entrypoints/exports or changed existing export signatures. The 963 reachable-export changes derive from five additive declaration changes: the resolver/type, its native adapter, and the optional configuration schema in two views.
- Required CI is green on `47db914b3815620bc3bef787d6ea77fcd0450203`, including [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40938432222/job/123684003734), type/lint jobs, and [dependency/security review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40941023852). No manual CI retries were requested.

Known local limitation: the standalone SDK source-budget report counts 161 entrypoints / 3843 exports / 2227 callables against the narrowly adjusted ceilings 159 / 3824 / 2215. The base has 160 entrypoints against its prior ceiling of 158; exact aggregate base export/callable counts were not independently reproduced. The successful semantic comparison establishes only the intended additive API delta; this PR does not absorb aggregate excess into its budget. prs.title: fix(codex): preserve native continuation and yield acknowledgements
prs.body:
Related: #167410 (not a claim to close all reported timeouts).

## What Problem This Solves

Preserve a managed native parent's saved tool declarations while its last terminal child's completion is still awaiting delivery. This fixes a distinct gap after execution protection correctly ends: rebuilding the catalog for the completion turn could rotate the parent thread and make a follow-up to its original child fail lineage validation.

The PR also retains the original delayed-completion authority regression. Current main already owns that async-lifetime behavior; no stable-only lifetime patch is added to main.

## Reproduction and scope

A packaged Gateway + packaged native Codex test on the prior PR head completed two ordinary turns on one child, then genuinely yielded while the third result was pending. Automatic delivery resumed with a changed tool catalog, started a second native parent, and the original-child follow-up failed lineage checks. The provider was deterministic local scripted Responses, not a real model or OAuth acceptance test.

The new regression exercises the real harness lifecycle with a nonempty native tool catalog, holds terminal-child delivery after the execution pin releases, and admits the completion with no current executors. With only the catalog owner restored to the prior implementation, it fails with two native thread starts instead of one. With the repair, it preserves the original parent and rejects execution of the old tool.

## Follow-up: preserve terminal yield acknowledgements

A fresh live run on the separate stable candidate completed five original-child turns and automatically resumed all three delayed results, but two yield acknowledgements became `aborted by user`. It was not counted as a full acceptance pass.

The native dynamic-tool `item/completed` event precedes the handler's return. Interrupting at that point can replace the model-visible result with cancellation, even after OpenClaw has recorded terminal release. Waiting a JavaScript event-loop tick does not establish native output commitment.

The lifecycle owner now waits for matching `rawResponseItem/completed` function/custom output receipts in its existing model-response inventory. These prove recording in native model history before interruption. Nested Code Mode waits for the outer output; web/image calls are not incorrectly required to emit function outputs. No new protocol, timer, persisted state, or authority relaxation is introduced.

## Ownership and safety

- Read pending-delivery custody from the existing completion owner; no new custody registry or persistent state.
- Require the same physical native client, current assignment/history ownership, and the existing claimed delivery owner.
- Recheck catalog eligibility after reading native metadata.
- Keep execution pins released at terminal completion; never restore old executors.
- Release declaration eligibility when delivery settles, is abandoned, or loses custody.
- Share the existing child-execution predicate between its two monitor consumers; the oversized monitor file shrinks.

## Evidence — CI repair rebase, 2026-10-29

Source: `22540643f20c845ff5fea04408b89549d8448bbb`, rebased onto pinned main `02e19a39282d6af1cc93e01d7045681d0124b433`. All four PR commits are patch-identical to the previous series (`git range-diff` reports `=` for each); no continuation behavior or test assertion was changed in this refresh.

The previously failing `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` job reported 14 mock-export sites in two upstream Gateway tests. This base includes [upstream repair #187120](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187120) (`e25c026eb75`): justified whole-module isolation annotations for shutdown/startup tests and corresponding stale-baseline cleanup. The two red `openclaw/ci-gate` entries reflected that same underlying failure. All three PostgreSQL jobs on the previous head ultimately passed.

Current-head local validation in secretless Docker:

- Mock-export guard against pinned base: passed, 15.92 s.
- Focused continuation, native yield-output, same-child custody, Gateway shutdown/spawn-broker, and test-plan tests: 226 successful executions across 14 files, 413.22 s wrapper wall (the 54 configuration cases execute on both test runtimes).
- Production plugin types: passed, 25.40 s; scoped test types: passed, 16.18 s.
- Targeted type-aware lint with pinned runtime parity: passed, 216.57 s; formatting: passed, 0.47 s.
- Pinned-base line-cap and test-line budget: passed, 1.43 s and 4.65 s. No check or baseline was weakened by this PR.
- Independent native GPT-6-Sol source/rebase review of the full 15-file range `02e19a3..2254064`: no actionable P0–P2 findings. This is a source review, not CLI autoreview or live acceptance. Working tree and `git diff --check` are clean.

Hosted CI for this exact head passed on 2026-10-29: 132 check runs settled (68 successful, 62 skipped, 1 neutral CodeQL result, and 1 superseded/cancelled PR-context run), with zero failed or pending checks. The previously failing [baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40962090873/job/123758008168) and the [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40965138477) both succeeded. The exact tested base is pinned above; subsequent main changes are not included in this local verdict. The live 10.7/10.8 backport acceptances and stock-versus-patched Docker comparison below remain evidence for their named artifacts, not a new package or live-model acceptance of this rebased upstream head.

## Historical source validation — 2026-10-28 upstream head

Source: `9c948da8a43477fb375ba8c7e5c08b14ef4b8ec2`, rebased onto pinned main `a919e5ecc4f6c579e16ab21499ccda3acaa1fb07` on 2026-10-28.

- At source-equivalent predecessor `d2b9766017ba75a56c419f8a316214201a145bdc`, 108 targeted cases across ten files passed in 215.03 seconds wrapper wall time, including delayed-completion authority, pending catalog custody, same-child follow-up, lifecycle/steering/output receipt tests and the real native-process yield test.
- Production plugin types, scoped extension-test types, targeted type-aware lint (including pinned Bun parity), formatting, pinned-base line-cap and test-line budget checks passed.
- Independent source review of this exact range found no actionable P0–P2. The original production/test patch is unchanged; the old test-budget-only increase was removed because upstream now owns a larger shared ceiling. Upstream shutdown, subagent cleanup, sidebar and annotated UI receipt fixes are preserved.
- The real native case uses pinned Codex 0.164.0 and synthetic inference. Historical controlled-failure evidence below still documents the patch mechanism; neither a new full packaged upstream acceptance nor hosted CI success is claimed for this rebased head.
- The initial lint attempt on the preceding base could not stage the pinned Bun parity runtime in an offline container. Canonical staging resolved the tooling prerequisite; no lint gate or parity check was bypassed.

### Full-suite registration correction and hosted CI

That pre-rebase head added only the missing `run-attempt-lifecycle-controller.output-receipt.test.ts` entry to the database-worker test plan. Hosted CI on the predecessor caught that direct test selection was insufficient to prove full-suite discovery. The exact final head passed 54 configuration cases on both test runtimes plus four receipt cases (112 executions, 215.31 seconds wrapper wall), and scoped lint/format. Production/test source is otherwise unchanged, so the preceding source checks remain applicable.

A separate hosted `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failure lists 14 mock-export sites in `src/gateway/server-shutdown.runtime.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server.spawn-broker.test.ts`. Both files are byte-identical to pinned upstream main `a919e5e`; the same diagnostics reproduce locally. That pre-rebase check was **not green**; the later rebase described in current evidence below incorporates upstream’s repair. [Failing job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40791343185/job/123177622310). No gate or baseline was weakened.

## Historical source validation — pre-rebase head

Source: `7ac126cd15dc6f67d14944b4b4a97c1b8697313e`, based on pinned main `58bf6decb46a946365900bb6d2f93b96e9b52f69`.

- Controlled original-controller comparison: both new direct/nested receipt regressions fail on premature native interruption; candidate bytes restored afterward.
- 57 lifecycle/steering/receipt/native cases passed across four files (67.60 seconds total wrapper wall time). Existing fixtures now explicitly model recorded output; no assertions were weakened. Two native-sibling cases moved out of the oversized suite.
- 29 full-attempt dynamic-tool, parent-continuation and original-child follow-up cases passed across three files (59.52 seconds wrapper wall time).
- Real pinned native Codex process plus production run-attempt/bridge/lifecycle and a synthetic local Responses provider: recorded `yielded` output precedes `turn/interrupt`, no aborted acknowledgement, owned native process exits. The case took 6.464 seconds; it exercises an actual process/history boundary that the cheaper lifecycle tests cannot prove.
- The native test's host fixture supplies an eligible yield; it does not certify child-claim admission or automatic continuation. It uses isolated state and no operator credentials. The first setup attempts exposed test-lane/session-seeding omissions; those were corrected, not counted as product failures or successful proofs.
- Production plugin types, scoped test types, targeted lint/format, pinned-base line-cap ratchet and exact test-line budget passed. Fresh independent source review found no actionable P0–P2 findings in the production repair; native proof source was separately reviewed by the lead.
- Simplification: one receipt bit in the existing call inventory replaces the assumption that a flushed response is ready for interruption; no parallel lifecycle or registry. The production delta for this follow-up is 17 added / 3 removed lines.

## Historical packaged proof (prior head, not current-head certification)

`f8699fea349def102ef4377b5009a556819583ac` passed 52 targeted tests plus packaged continuation in a fresh isolated installation: one parent, one original child, five persisted child turns, three genuine yields and three once-only automatic consumptions (96.19 seconds). Archive SHA-256 `2bbc9dc04691464cd91545c296d64651bdced78f307751d3da1699262ad13839`; build ID `2026.10.7-pr184848-f8699fea349-20261027`; native Codex `0.164.0`.

That packaged proof used scripted local HTTPS Responses/WebSocket inference with no external network. It is historical after the acknowledgement repair, not a rebuilt-package or real-model/OAuth acceptance claim. The prior controlled catalog regression fails with two parent thread starts when only its owner repair is reverted.

## Evidence — live 2026.10.7 backport acceptance

On 2026-10-28, a fresh uninterrupted live native acceptance run passed against installed custom build `2026.10.7-custom-continuation-e7de3d6695e-20261028`, backport commit `e7de3d6695e0b4881b109291c666e60121989580`. The running Gateway reported `2026.10.7` and pointed to that installed package.

One native child completed two ordinary turns, then three delayed turns (25-second delay requested each). Each delayed completion automatically resumed the parent after an explicit `sessions_yield` acknowledgement of `status: yielded`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| Turns completed with the same native child | 5/5 |
| Confirmed yields on turns 3–5 | 3/3 |
| Automatic parent resumptions | 3/3 |
| Results consumed once | 5/5 |

No polling during delayed checks, manual wakeups, child replacements, or user interruptions. No `nothing_pending` or interrupted acknowledgements were counted. Mirrored notifications were deduplicated: this proves once-only consumption, not transport-level exactly-once delivery. An earlier interrupted run was inconclusive and is excluded from this table.

These live results apply to the **stable custom backport**, not the upstream PR head. [Live acceptance report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184848#issuecomment-6480604481).

## Evidence — live 2026.10.8 backport acceptance

On 2026-10-29, fresh live native acceptance passed on the installed custom 2026.10.8 backport. The reachable running Gateway reported `2026.10.8`; session status identified build `55e31f3`, matching the qualified custom source `55e31f3e44f82154a6ffdabe58e725bec094a09c` (`2026.10.8-custom-continuation-55e31f3e44f-20261028`). This was live model execution, not the earlier scripted-provider package proof.

One original native child completed two ordinary turns and three delayed follow-up turns (20-second delay requested per delayed turn). For each of turns 3–5, the parent called `sessions_yield`, received `status: yielded`, and was automatically resumed by that child's completion.

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| Turns completed with the same native child | 5/5 |
| Confirmed yields on turns 3–5 | 3/3 |
| Automatic parent resumptions | 3/3 |
| Results consumed once | 5/5 |

No polling during delayed checks, manual wakeups, replacement children, or user interruptions. No `nothing_pending` or interrupted yield acknowledgements were counted. Mirrored completion notices surfaced for turns 3–5 and were ignored after the first consumption, as in the 10.7 acceptance: once-only consumption is demonstrated, not transport-level exactly-once delivery.

This is additional **stable custom backport** evidence, not certification of the upstream PR head, unmodified 2026.10.8, or a new stock-versus-patched controlled comparison. No installation, restart, configuration change, or merge was performed for this acceptance. At that live acceptance, the upstream source head was `9c948da8a43477fb375ba8c7e5c08b14ef4b8ec2`; later rebases are separately qualified.

## Evidence — stock versus patched 2026.10.8 Docker control

On 2026-10-29, **stock failed and the custom stable backport passed the same continuation-focused probe**. These were real installed Gateway and native Codex processes with scripted local Responses inference, not live-model/OAuth acceptance or a rebuilt upstream-head test.

### Pinned inputs

- Stock: npm `openclaw@2026.10.8`, release commit `dc2523e5a5c7a309517fd7fa834add938231d526`; archive SHA-256 `7e36685a0b5fd9c8c3afcfa93ee33fad871f7c6c8b6e695cae6720d14a765f18`, also checked against registry SHA-512 integrity. Matching official `@openclaw/codex@2026.10.8` installed via the supported plugin CLI, with trusted-official registry ownership verified.
- Patched: custom stable source `55e31f3e44f82154a6ffdabe58e725bec094a09c`; archive SHA-256 `192509e3911ae9bba6437dc1f1f7dbac96525d612fc3f3ade82ceefef6b10f55`, using its bundled Codex plugin.
- Both: Node 24.22.1 and native Codex 0.160.0, identical native binary SHA-256 `12eb3e81114588aca3b7998f4f19e8997b056aca08e57a7ca7c8a3ec8c652aad`.
- Separate synthetic state; dependency staging online, execution with Docker networking disabled. No production credentials/state or Docker socket mounted. Installed packages owned Gateway/plugin execution; a read-only source client supplied only Gateway RPC transport.

| Check | Stock 2026.10.8 | Custom 2026.10.8 |
|---|---|---|
| Original-child completed turns | 3; stopped at first delayed continuation | 5/5 |
| Persisted confirmed yield outputs | 1 | 3/3 |
| Automatic completion wakeup | Observed after turn 3 | All 3 |
| Native parent identity retained | No | Yes |
| Current delayed-result payload supplied | No | Yes |
| Delayed results consumed once | 0 | 3/3 |
| Runtime phase, including setup/cleanup | 89.68 s; exit 1 | 54.31 s; exit 0 |

### Observed failure boundary

The stock child persisted three completed turns. Its original parent persisted `status: yielded` before the delayed third result was released. Automatic completion then arrived under a **different native parent ID**, carrying the inter-session wakeup placeholder without the current child-result payload. Both provider-visible instructions and input were inspected: the result marker occurred only in quoted earlier task/history text, not as the delivered completion. The current original-child event assertion failed before a fourth child turn could be requested. This was not merely failure to wake the parent or a timeout.

The patched control retained one parent and one original child, five distinct persisted completed child turns, three persisted `yielded` outputs, and three once-only delayed-result consumptions. No polling or manual wakeups drove delayed completion. A separate ordinary user turn requested the fifth child action only after the fourth result was consumed.

### Probe qualifications and limits

The old custom-package probe assumed bundled Codex; stock requires the official plugin installation above. Its first setup verification failure is excluded from behavior evidence. A separate strict assertion about inbound context residing in top-level provider instructions also failed before child execution: stock carries that context in input messages. That request-layout difference is **not counted as a continuation failure or missing-context proof**. A separately identified continuation-focused variant records the layout fact without blocking child execution; all payload, identity, yield and consumption assertions remain intact. Identical variant bytes were used for both compared packages, without modifying runtime implementations.

This comparison supports the continuing need for the **combined stable backport** in this scenario, not the independent necessity of every patch or certification of this PR's current upstream head. Registry-versus-bundled plugin packaging differs; this is not a single-change causal experiment. The narrower controlled regressions above remain the evidence for individual repair mechanisms. All eight task-created containers were removed by recorded creation IDs; production Gateway identity and availability were unchanged.

## Limits and operational impact

No live installation, restart, configuration change or merge is part of this PR-body update or the live acceptance run. The stable 2026.10.7 and 2026.10.8 backports remain separate from the upstream PR; both installed custom packages passed the respective live acceptance above. That does not certify a rebuilt package of the upstream PR head. The observed duplicate native notifications and intermediate visible-reply warnings are not claimed fixed by this acknowledgement patch. No claim of production restart recovery, provider/OAuth recovery, or all-plugin test-type coverage.

## Test-line budget

The upstream ceiling is preserved unchanged at 6,320,000. The old PR-specific budget increase is no longer part of the diff. The repository's exact test-line and pinned-base line-cap checks passed on the rebased head. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available for this head.

prs.title: fix: recover retained failed deployments without discarding evidence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the operator recovery gap when a retained failed deployment journal blocks preparing and accepting a reviewed replacement release without discarding the original recovery evidence.

## User Impact

Operators gain an explicit retained-repair path that preserves the original journal, history, and four-file controller closure. Ordinary deployment and rollback admission checks remain in place. This changes bundled operator tooling; installation and deployment still require separate approval.

**Qualification status:** the installed R4 public-shell/native rehearsal remains in progress, not passed; the final cleanup has not been separately native-qualified. No complete native qualification or live deployment acceptance is claimed. These are not installation or deployment approvals.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing controller remains the sole recovery owner. It binds the repair to the retained incident, retires old canonical readers before complete-closure adoption, and records crash-reconcilable preparation, startup, and acceptance transitions. PREPARE acquisition and later STATUS observations remain distinct.

R4 corrects the native R3 failure at `REPAIR_STARTED`: runtime process verification now uses the strict retained-repair lifecycle owner and admitted executable rather than feeding a valid v2 journal into the legacy v1 parser. Legacy journal validation remains strict; managed runtimes cannot bypass journal ownership checks.

## Evidence

- Final provenance covers **43 files** and **20 changed files**. Compared with frozen R4, 41 files are identical; final cleanup only removes two definition-only helpers, corrects two integration comments, and updates stale README descriptions. The original frozen manifest is retained.
- Final R4 focused tests: **86 total; 70 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped**. Fifteen skips require root/native coverage; one legacy runtime sibling requires the absent `/usr/bin/node`. Skips are not passes. The new runtime regression uses the real public action, filesystem, and deployment flock, with explicitly synthetic service/process observations and native-claim input. It is not full native qualification.
- The author’s isolated R3 contrast using the new runtime tests reports **4 passed, 7 failed, 1 skipped**, including the valid default-Node rejection and managed-runtime ownership bypass. The installed R3 public-shell/native run independently **failed at `REPAIR_STARTED` through the v1 parser**. Neither failure is relabeled as passed by R4's focused tests.
- Prior canonical root-only proof: **15 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, on frozen R2 plus the test addendum, using a rootless container with real systemd PID1, root identity, procfs/namespaces, FDs/flock, and crash/replay gates. Fixtures were synthetic. This covers those adoption/bootstrap cases, not full service activation, and was **not rerun on R4**.
- Earlier non-root selection remains **142 passed, 6 failed**. The six native-continuation cases emitted an unchanged `install` ownership error before rollback/assertion failures; that does not establish the sole cause of every downstream failure. A separate legacy-custody run reported **1 passed, 26 failed** at a missing canonical-lock fixture, with the first failure reproduced on R2. These are retained failures, not green broad-suite results.
- Canonical shared autoreview of the cumulative change against base `2f47962f2bdc6af710e2059b725c73423a3e1f7e` completed at P0–P2 with exit 1 and one P1 allegation, **not a clean machine verdict**. The parent independently rejected it: the ordinary marker payload already contains `sessionKey`, unchanged from base; two existing ordinary marker tests pass. No actionable findings remain after that disposition. Author simplification removed the unused helpers and stale text; focused tests were rerun after cleanup.
- All 16 changed JavaScript files pass syntax checks; Bash syntax, the supported Markdown formatting check (three files), and `git diff --check` pass. The repository-layout test **did not execute**: shared configuration loading requires `@solidjs/vite-plugin`, absent from the existing dependency tree. No dependency or configuration changes were made.

Human credit: @jalehman, @fuller-stack-dev, @vincentkoc, and @RomneyDa.

prs.title: fix: avoid PR publication fallback on incidental Git output
prs.body:
Fixes #187902.

## What Problem This Solves

PR preparation could start GraphQL publication after a failed or uncertain Git push merely because progress text contained `403`, `permission`, `denied`, or `forbidden`. The original CI failure matched `403` inside a commit ID and replaced the original lost-response status with a GraphQL failure.

## User Impact

Incidental Git output now preserves the original failure and stops publication. Genuine permission refusals retain the existing qualified linear GraphQL fallback. Signature, merge-ancestry, exact-lease, live-identity, and proof-purpose restrictions remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing classifier now recognizes complete refusal diagnostics instead of matching arbitrary substrings. The lost-response fixture uses a deterministic permission-like bare-remote path, so real Git supplies the triggering progress text independently of generated object IDs. Positive controls cover the existing refusal forms and contextual GitHub/HTTP 403 messages.

The change adds three production lines and 18 test lines. One exact 18-line allocation covers the stronger existing fixture and diagnostic matrix; the shared test-line baseline is unchanged. No new transport or retry is introduced.

## Evidence

- Conditioned baseline at `00df6e27`: the real publisher's linear lost-response case expected `74` and received `1`; 18 other capability cases passed. The failing case's later assertions were unreached.
- Final tree: **25 capability cases passed in 6.95s**, including both lost-response variants asserting status `74`, the physical candidate ref, exactly one push, no GraphQL event, and no success receipt. The permission controls preserve qualified fallback and merge refusal.
- Two direct-consumer files passed **66 cases in 87.78s**. Another **160 cases across six publisher/authority files** remain valid after verifying that the final refusal-form refinement leaves their executed paths unchanged. That is **251 distinct qualified cases across nine files**, with 91 executed on the final tree.
- Bash syntax, formatting/lint, affected types, and the canonical test-line check passed. Tests used Linux x64, Bash 5.3.9, Git 2.53.0, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Vitest 5.0.5, and pinned Bun `191755ec1`.

Git writes in the fixtures target local bare repositories; GitHub I/O is stubbed. No live GitHub permission failure or duplicate write is claimed. Exact-head CI, PR tooling Darwin, CodeQL, OpenGrep, and Workflow Sanity passed.

prs.title: [2026.10.10-beta.5] test(agents,gateway): realign completion-custody fixture and isolate first sign-in proof
prs.body:
## Problem

Qualifying FRV normalCi child run 40884994912, on C = 2f5ddf1b865b, job 123486863204, failed `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.completion-authority.test.ts` › "registered completion source custody > keeps current original completion custody after a same-human chat admission revokes automation" with `expected false to be true`.

## Root cause

- **Culprit: 2f7589ab17df**, the backport of #181260 ("settle consumed yield cohorts without retry"). I checked first-parent commits by hand, without `git bisect run`:
  - passes at beta.4, 43c5a84ecaf9, 9b8ee9c0c41d, 4643f86ac24e and 2f7589ab17df^
  - fails at 2f7589ab17df, 39f9bdea9b38, 013725091336 and the release head
- That commit drops findings that were already delivered from settle wakes. The shared fixture `subagent-registry.requester-completion.test-support.ts` marks its child as `delivery: { status: "delivered" }`, so the wake has nothing to deliver and returns `false`.
- This is the same cause as the settle fixtures realigned in #187589.
- It is **not** caused by #187589's guard on queued collector custody: the test still fails on head with `subagent-registry-run-launch.ts` restored to its state before #187589.

## Fix

Release-only test fix: the fixture's finding stays `pending`. Main has no copy of this fixture. The `revoked` variant still checks that delivery is refused with "Subagent completion authority is no longer active".

## Evidence

Local runs use Node 24.22.1.

| Test | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `subagent-registry.completion-authority.test.ts` | 1 failed, 62 passed | 63/63 |

## Other items from the same FRV (no code change)

- **`session-accessor.recovery.test.ts` › "preserves recovery success after committed owner retirement" (job 123486863598)**: flake.
  - Neither the test nor `session-accessor.recovery.ts` has changed since beta.4.
  - The spy counts any `captureOpenClawAgentDatabaseExecution` call anywhere in the process after `mockClear`, so background work in the shared runner can trip it.
  - #187589's change to the selected-listing projection doesn't call that function.
  - It passes 3/3 locally (9/9 cases each run).
- **`server.required-placement-scopes.test.ts` › "required placement survives disconnect…" (job 123486876387)**: flake.
  - The `sessions.create` RPC hit the 10 s client timeout in a 589 s shard with load average 9.
  - The test hasn't changed since beta.4.
  - It passes 3/3 locally (3/3 cases each run).
- **`setup-inference.first-signin.integration.test.ts` (job 123486876470): fixed by routing it to the isolated project (commit e35bc900aae).**
  - It failed 2/2 in shard `agentic-gateway-server-isolated-3` with "OpenClaw state database lifecycle is retired".
  - On release, this file runs in `gateway-database-workers`, which shares one module graph across all the test files in a worker (non-isolated runner). Its native provider imports can keep the module copy from an earlier file whose state lifecycle has since been retired, and `getOpenClawStateWorkerOwner` (guard from 62f0c60cfad6) refuses that retired copy.

prs.title: [2026.10.10-beta.5] test(doctor): preserve autostart policy in managed service fixtures (#185277)
prs.body:
## Problem

Qualifying FRV normalCi job 123486914133 (`checks-node-bundle-infra-small-private-qa-22`, release head 2f5ddf1b865b) failed 13 doctor-health managed-flow tests. Examples:

- `doctor-health.managed-admission.test.ts` › "coordinates the matching managed writer through multi-agent repair": archive-verification, clean-force-repair, update-legacy
- the matching cases in `doctor-health.managed-settlement.test.ts` and `doctor-health.managed-approvals.test.ts`

All of them fail with: `Gateway native autostart policy changed during Doctor repair; automatic restoration was refused.`

These tests are not new failures. They also failed in the provisional run on f488276ec06a (job 123354345833, same shard). Neither #187574 nor #187626 caused them; the tests fail locally at f35cf3ca5a6 and f5e7a02e5bf, both before those merges.

## Root cause

706512176647 backported #180356 ("enter maintenance before repairing source artifacts"). That change refuses automatic Gateway restoration when native autostart policy changes during Doctor repair, which is the intended behavior.

The managed doctor-health fixture modeled `isEnabled` as the Gateway's current running state (`isEnabled: async () => running`). When the fixture stops the Gateway for maintenance, that reads as an autostart policy change. Main fixed the fixture in #185277 (217817bc5906), and that fix was never backported. The release's `doctor-health.legacy-update.test.ts` already has an equivalent adaptation.

There is no product change. On real service managers, stopping a service does not change whether it is enabled.

## Fix

Apply #185277's managed test-support hunk: `isEnabled` returns the unchanged policy (`true`). It is applied by hand because the release file's structure diverged from main.

## Evidence (local, Node 24.22.1)

| Revision | `doctor-health.managed-admission.test.ts` |
