prs.title: feat(android): mute the Talk microphone without ending the conversation
prs.body:
Closes #187721

## What Problem This Solves

Android Talk users need to pause microphone input without ending the conversation or interrupting the assistant's work and response audio.

## User Impact

A separate, accessible microphone button beside End Talk lets users mute and unmute input while keeping the call, accepted work, and reply audio active. Mute remains set across Talk restarts in the app process until explicitly unmuted; standalone push-to-talk still works after ending Talk.

Realtime mute sends silence while the recording session stays open, so Android's microphone indicator may remain visible. Native Talk finishes already-recognized words before pausing recognition. No new permission, configuration, dependency, protocol, or release-version change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ending Talk and muting reply playback are different operations from muting input. Keep input mute owned by `TalkModeManager` and expose that state through the existing runtime/view model to the actual ChatScreen control. Reuse the capture ownership lock to retire native recognition and keep queued microphone audio from crossing a mute/unmute toggle at socket enqueue. Preserve upstream detach/abort behavior.

The patch excludes selected-chat routing, Health Connect, SMS, version bumps, and the unrelated chat-metadata warning repair. It adds no parallel capture manager: the necessary growth is one input state plus audio-frame invalidation and the control/proof. Production Kotlin delta: +132/-20; tests: +253/-1; README: +1.

## Evidence

- Built and tested against pinned main `6c672d42f2dec42b7917f34dfe5ae8157b9b0abb`; Initial Kotlin test/review head `750c924b8ec5e95018239108fd9f85382d936a7c`; current head `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc` adds only the generated source inventory entries described below.
- `:app:ktlintCheck` passed. `:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest` passed **121 tests**, zero failures/errors/skips: all 118 `TalkModeManagerTest` cases and three targeted `ChatComposerLayoutTest` cases covering the real toggle, accessible state, and 320dp/French/large-font controls. Gradle build/check wall time: **4m 11s**; recorded suite times: **17.745s** and **12.297s**, respectively. These are Kotlin/Gradle suites, not `pnpm test` suites. Hosted CI seconds are pending.
- Transport checks exercise microphone PCM replacement with silence, a read spanning a toggle, and queued audio waiting at the actual socket enqueue. Native/relay checks preserve admitted work and playback; push-to-talk checks cover muted admission and standalone use after Talk ends.
- The requester initially liked the feature during real voice use on the custom 2026.10.7 phone build, but subsequently reported that muting seemed to silence assistant playback as well. That observation is not yet reproduced or attributed; do not treat output preservation as accepted device proof. Source inspection confirms separate microphone and speaker controls, but does not establish what happened on that phone. This current-main port has not separately been installed on a device; do not treat the synthetic screenshots as live audio proof.
- Fresh independent Codex read-only review of the final mute-only snapshot against the pinned base found no actionable likely/high-impact findings. CLI AutoReview was attempted but unavailable because OpenAI returned HTTP 401; it is **not** counted as a passing AutoReview. `git diff --check` passed. Full Android framework/resource lint and broad hosted CI are not claimed passing.

### CI localization correction

The initial [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40892555492) passed Android third-party, Play, Wear, both native-accessibility jobs, and Kotlin style. Its one underlying failure was `native-i18n`: the source extraction inventory omitted the five new mute strings. `openclaw/ci-gate` reflected that failure.

Reproduced the same inventory failure locally before the repair. Ran `pnpm native:i18n:baseline`, which added exactly five generator-owned entries to `apps/.i18n/native-source.json`. `pnpm native:i18n:verify` now passes, including Android and Apple source safety checks; `pnpm android:i18n:gen` regenerates the Android lookup/resources with the new labels. Kotlin source and tests are unchanged, so the earlier focused test and independent review evidence remains scoped to that unchanged code. The [updated-head native-i18n job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40899576510/job/123538746357) now passes on GitHub for `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc`; the rest of that CI run is still pending.

Translated dictionaries and derived locale metadata remain owned by the serialized post-merge locale refresh ([publication policy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6c672d42f2dec42b7917f34dfe5ae8157b9b0abb/.agents/skills/openclaw-pr-maintainer/references/landing.md#open-or-update-the-pr)); this correction commits the source-owned inventory, not hand-edited translations. The new labels can use English fallback until that refresh.

### Remaining before merge

- Supply runtime evidence on this current-main Android port for native and realtime mute/unmute during an active answer, including input suppression and continued playback. The older custom-build user report and synthetic UI captures do not establish that evidence.
- Obtain the maintainer product decision on the separate input control, silence-based realtime mute, and mute lifetime across Talk restarts. The author's requested feature and phone acceptance are not represented as upstream maintainer approval.

### Synthetic ChatScreen captures

The images below come from the real ChatScreen Robolectric fixture at 320dp, not a mock-drawn control or a live provider call. They demonstrate the control/status and layout only.

**Before: pinned main, no input-only microphone control**

![Android Talk before the feature, with End Talk but no separate microphone mute](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f97c2d5-51c7-4f04-861e-ef117d1d4ea4)

The before capture used an isolated checkout of the exact pinned base, with a temporary UI-only proof asserting that the microphone toggle was absent (1 test passed; capture build wall time 3m 15s). No baseline proof code or generated images are included in the source branch.

**After: microphone enabled**

![Android Talk with the separate microphone toggle enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e8e6157-509b-4703-ae6d-e1018cdd7ce3)

**After: microphone muted**

![Android Talk with microphone muted while End Talk and active-run Stop remain visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4469f6c4-1561-4cee-a725-c3cc5990d9c0)

prs.title: fix(ui): Try again posts a visible continue message and keeps the failure notice
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking **Try again** on a failed reply in the Control UI posts "Continue from where you stopped. Check which actions already completed before retrying anything." into the chat as if the user had typed it, and the "Unable to finish this reply" notice stays above the continued answer.

## User Impact

User impact: **Try again** now simply resumes the reply. The failure notice goes away, the agent continues from the existing conversation, and nothing is posted on the user's behalf. This holds after a reload and for other viewers of the session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The continuation becomes a Gateway-owned hidden input, using the same trusted internal chat path the Gateway already uses for agent onboarding and progress-card refreshes:

- New `chat.retry` method (`operator.write`, session write access). It accepts only the session's latest `failed`/`timeout` run (optional `sessionId` fence, like `chat.abort`), then admits the existing continuation prompt as `internal_system` input with `display: false` and `provenance.runId` naming the failed run. The ack is the normal `chat.send` ack.
- `chat.history` drops the failure notice of a run that has such a retry input, so the notice stays gone after reload.
- The Control UI calls `chat.retry`, hides the notice immediately, and adopts the new run; on a rejected request it restores the notice and shows the error. The model-facing prompt is no longer a localized UI string.

Accepted edge cases: a history page that ends exactly between a failure notice and its retry input still shows that notice when scrolling back; in a streak of identical notices from different runs, only the retried run's notice is removed.

## Evidence

Before/after screenshots follow (synthetic Control UI e2e Gateway, 1160×760, light theme, captured right after clicking **Try again**).

**Before** — the continuation posts as a user message and the notice stays:

![Before: Try again posts a visible continue message under the failure notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94c9aff8-5748-4deb-bcb8-f14ea7b2d3b0)

**After** — the notice is gone and the reply resumes in place:

![After: Try again resumes the reply with no visible message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/14e5bbd1-d7dd-4d18-810f-f09829619d0b)

- New Gateway integration test `src/gateway/server.chat-retry.test.ts` (real Gateway, mock OpenAI Responses provider): the first run fails on every attempt; `chat.retry` starts a run whose model request contains the continuation; `chat.history` afterwards has no failure notice, no continuation text and only the original user message; retrying the same run again is rejected.
- `chat-display-projection.test.ts`: a retry input retires only its own run's notice. `chat-run-failure-streaks.test.ts` and `chat-pane-state.test.ts` cover the optimistic hide and the one-retry guard. `chat-retry-failure.e2e.test.ts` now asserts `chat.retry` is sent, the notice detaches, no `chat.send` is made, no continuation text appears and the draft is kept.
- Passing: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm protocol:check` (registry, Swift/Kotlin models, since-train), format check, `src/gateway/methods`, `packages/gateway-protocol`, and the full `ui/src/pages/chat` suite (5769/5770; the one failure, `chat-html-preview-element.test.ts`, passes alone on this branch and on `main`).
- Local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, local mode against `68b8bf71132`, P0–P2, 3 passes): scoped-clean, no findings.
- `pnpm lint --base origin/main`: Control UI i18n verification passed; oxlint failures are only in files this PR does not touch.

Reported and requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e9232195-913e-492b-921e-9ad758d69086)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: improve(releases): skip unused TestFlight source checkouts
prs.body:
Related: #187895

## What Problem This Solves

TestFlight attempts create a complete detached source checkout before discovering that review, processing, or an existing distribution makes it unnecessary.

## User Impact

Unchanged and deferred TestFlight attempts can finish sooner and avoid another source checkout. Uploads, staging, and saved-artifact recovery retain their isolated source worktree. There is no app behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gather the existing release plan from the already admitted clean checkout, then create and bridge the detached worktree only after planning and TestFlight no-upload decisions. Both platform planners use this shared order; Android's temporary Play edit still closes through its existing owner. Fastlane may write its existing ignored reports in the caller checkout, but planning does not change tracked source files.

The existing upload/staging worktree lifetime remains unchanged. Preflight errors now propagate before any source worktree exists; there is no retained-worktree warning at that point. The production change removes one net line, and an existing no-upload assertion now also covers rejection. No new helpers, cache, state, tests, or test-line allocation are introduced.

## Evidence

### Acceptance rule, recorded before measurement

Use pinned source/baseline `548649e1dc47e16b26cc415e03f3e810f9ef5a65` and candidate `76e34e3168f5438f6e581b3053db2a28a82a5d5f` on `xcode-27-xlarge`. Run five serial, interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, each with a fresh HTTPS depth-one checkout of the actual repository. Execute the actual baseline and candidate release entry points in TestFlight mode. Substitute only the external planner response with the same synthetic build awaiting beta review; all Git admission, remote release-ref lookup, source materialization and no-upload decision remain real. Allow planning at the baseline detached source or candidate admitted checkout as appropriate. Reject uploads, Git pushes, and all unexpected subprocesses; provide no Apple, signing, or model credentials. Install frozen tooling dependencies outside the measured samples.

Measure checkout plus the complete release CLI, and CLI preflight separately. Require at least 20% lower candidate median CLI time and at least 5% lower median complete-boundary time. Reject a 20% or greater regression in the observed maximum of either boundary; with five samples, the reported p95 is the maximum, not a population-tail estimate. All samples must preserve source SHA/tree and the same deferred-review result. Each baseline must create/remove one detached source worktree; candidates must create/remove zero and perform zero bridging scans. Both must stay shallow and perform zero full-history fetches. Retain every sample, component times, subprocess and Git Trace2 counts, object storage, host load/resources and observed spread. Fresh directories do not flush OS or remote caches. Synthetic planning excludes live Apple authentication/status, and this does not measure a productive archive/upload or full workflow setup.

### Hosted comparison result

**PASS:** both predeclared median thresholds and both maximum-regression limits passed. [Nonpublishing hosted run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40960552452) completed successfully at diagnostic commit `219311a30e3d13a6013d23c3a8c95807c8c5f848`. [Raw evidence artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40960552452/artifacts/12936432679) contains all ten samples, complete deferred-result receipts, subprocess audits, Git Trace2, component timings, object storage and host/resource observations. The diagnostic branch is proof-only and must not merge.

| Boundary | Baseline median | Candidate median | Median reduction | Baseline observed max | Candidate observed max |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Release CLI preflight | 17.788s | 3.536s | 80.12% | 18.157s | 4.062s |
| Fresh checkout + release CLI | 89.414s | 74.267s | 16.94% | 90.960s | 91.047s |

CLI ranges were 13.958–18.157s before and 3.353–4.062s after. Complete-boundary ranges were 87.139–90.960s before and 73.260–91.047s after. The complete-boundary maximum increased 0.095%, below the frozen 20% rejection limit; its candidate pair-4 checkout tail is retained below. Five samples describe this run, not a population-tail estimate.

All timings below are seconds; worktree components are included within CLI time.

| Pair | Version | Checkout | CLI | Complete | Worktree add | Worktree remove | Bridge scan |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | Baseline | 77.002 | 13.958 | 90.960 | 7.258 | 3.327 | 0.026 |
| 1 | Candidate | 70.788 | 3.536 | 74.324 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | Baseline | 74.602 | 14.812 | 89.414 | 7.592 | 3.888 | 0.025 |
| 2 | Candidate | 69.859 | 3.400 | 73.260 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 3 | Baseline | 69.351 | 17.788 | 87.139 | 10.708 | 3.908 | 0.032 |
| 3 | Candidate | 69.616 | 3.757 | 73.373 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 4 | Baseline | 71.106 | 18.157 | 89.263 | 11.185 | 3.726 | 0.024 |
| 4 | Candidate | 87.693 | 3.353 | 91.047 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 5 | Baseline | 71.771 | 17.811 | 89.583 | 10.990 | 3.771 | 0.026 |
| 5 | Candidate | 70.204 | 4.062 | 74.267 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Every sample used source `548649e1dc47e16b26cc415e03f3e810f9ef5a65`, tree `7936a8060730b5af0d9893c885cd2a019440b25e`, and produced the identical `deferred-review` receipt. Both stayed shallow with zero full-history fetches. Subprocess audits and independent Git Trace2 counts agree: five baseline worktree adds, five removes and five bridge scans; zero of each for the candidate. Each substituted the planner exactly once at its expected source location. No forbidden subprocess, upload or Git push occurred.

The hosted Mac reported five virtual Apple M2 Pro CPUs and 14 GiB RAM. Recorded one-minute load ranged from 6.96 to 16.14, and free memory from 0.12 to 1.51 GiB. CLI-process maxRSS was 65,040–65,312 KiB before and 64,464–64,864 KiB after; this excludes child Git and does not establish whole-job memory or CPU savings. Fresh sample sources had no installed tools, so the benchmark counts bridge scans but does not measure copying or symlinking installed dependencies. External Apple planning was synthetic; Apple authentication/status, full workflow setup, signing, notes generation and productive archive/upload performance remain outside this proof.

### Correctness and review

The existing CLI regression fails on the unchanged release entry point because a rejected TestFlight attempt leaves its unused source worktree. The candidate passes all 16 real CLI cases, including no-upload outcomes, both productive platforms with advancing main, and upload/staging recovery. The 27 iOS planner cases also pass. The changed CLI test file took 20.08s; both focused shards completed in 22.08s including startup. Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Fresh independent AutoReview found no actionable findings through P2. All 17 existing iOS/Android Fastlane gate cases pass as well (9.16s including startup). [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40960517516) completed successfully on `76e34e3168f5438f6e581b3053db2a28a82a5d5f`. Hosted ClawSweeper review found no actionable findings on that head. No Store or TestFlight upload is part of this campaign.

prs.title: fix: preserve requested hosts in chat entry HTTP tests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The real HTTP canonical chat-entry tests report a false 404 failure for token/password requests intended to use `Host: gateway.lan`. On Node 24.22.1, native `fetch` sends the loopback URL authority instead of that explicit Host header. The server therefore takes the loopback anonymous-document path, where returning 404 for a private conversation is correct.

## User Impact

There is no production behavior change. The tests now exercise their declared localhost, nonsecure host, verified-proxy and managed-Tailscale scenarios through the real HTTP listener. The existing confidentiality, public-sharing, authentication and access-revocation expectations remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use Node's HTTP client in the test's shared request helper so the requested Host reaches the listener. Retain the test AbortSignal, connection closure, response headers and gzip decoding, and preserve the existing no-redirect behavior. The seven test cases and their assertions and timeouts are unchanged.

The documented nonsecure token/password behavior already works: the Gateway returns an app shell without disclosing the private conversation. Changing that handler or weakening the expected response would conceal the fixture problem.

## Evidence

A native discriminator on the unchanged production code observed `Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>`, secure loopback classification and 404 for the fetch request. The same canonical request through Node's HTTP client arrived with `Host: gateway.lan`, received nonsecure classification and returned a 200 app shell without the private message. This established the request-transport cause at the server boundary.

On Node 24.22.1, changed-file formatting/lint, all seven selected compiler groups and all seven real HTTP cases pass. The cases retain the private/public, token/password, verified-proxy, managed-Tailscale and mid-delivery access-revocation controls. The literal-file Vitest run took 41.42s wall time including transformation (test execution 9%); its native build/preparation/test stage took 373.28s. The [hosted CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40959910336) completed successfully, including the same seven cases in its native Bun shard (42.32s Vitest wall, 29.91s suite setup and test time). Independent review completed with no findings.

The change adds 16 test lines for the direct HTTP client and gzip handling, with an exact 16-line allocation. No additional test case or production code was added.

A final comparison on current main `8650e947681f` reproduced the same token-case 404 at the unchanged assertion after successful native preparation, confirming the fixture correction is still needed.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): set API workspace at login
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- Interactive Anthropic API-key login omits the workspace required by unscoped keys, so subsequent requests fail with HTTP 400.

## User Impact

- Login collects an optional Claude Console workspace ID. Workspace-scoped keys can leave it blank; configured workspace headers and SecretRefs are preserved.
- The setting applies to the Anthropic provider, separately from an agent's local workspace directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Collect the missing input in the Anthropic plugin and persist it through the existing provider-header configuration.
- Closes #187018.

## Evidence

- HEAD 7d3f6266ae821fbca511178e8b0b2f39f3cf42f8.
- Published 2026.10.9 reproduced the missing-workspace rejection. After Doctor and API-key login at this head, the same key completed a real Gateway turn through Anthropic.
- A transparent relay forwarded one request per run without changing credentials, workspace headers, or request bodies. It recorded HTTP 400 before and HTTP 200 after.
- Published settings retained their model, auth declarations, headers, SecretRef, tools, and Gateway settings. The existing API key loaded before re-login; Doctor added an empty main-agent entry.
- CLI and response excerpts follow. Credential entry, workspace ID, local paths, and endpoints are redacted. Request metadata is recorded by the relay; configuration is read from the saved file.


prs.title: fix(macos): Mac tab shows a blank or stale page when a load fails
prs.body:
Related: #183927

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Mac tab shows a blank white page (new tab) or silently keeps the previous page (loaded tab) when a page fails to load, and Reload does nothing for a failed first load.

## User Impact

User impact: when a link is broken or the Mac is offline, the tab now keeps the address that was tried, says why it could not be opened, and offers Reload, which retries that address. Stopping a load, navigating somewhere else, and download or default-browser handoffs still keep the current page without an error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main-frame failures reached `DashboardNativeBrowserHost.navigationDidFail(for:)` without the error, so the tab only retired its link alias and published unchanged state (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardWindowController.swift:1467-1470`, `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardNativeBrowserHost.swift:269-272` on `70c70646d86`). Reload called `webView.reload()` (`DashboardNativeBrowserHost.swift:174`), which replays the last committed item; a failed first load never commits one, so nothing happens.

The tab owner now receives the error. Deliberate interruptions (`NSURLErrorCancelled`, and WebKit's policy interruption 102 used for response-policy cancels such as downloads and default-browser handoff) are ignored as before. Any other failure shows a native failure view over the tab's web view: a title, the system error description (no page content and no URL), and a Reload button. The tab keeps the failing URL; the published tab URL prefers it, and Reload (the button or the toolbar) loads it again. The next navigation that starts clears the failure.

The failure view is AppKit, added as a subview of the reading tab's `WKWebView`, so it follows the existing presentation frames and hiding and the untrusted page cannot script or restyle it. It is layer-backed and sets its background in `updateLayer()`: the first revision was a plain opaque view filled in `draw(_:)`, and in the running app it painted over the whole dashboard window (see the running-app proof below). No bridge, Control UI, or privileged dashboard failure-page code is involved. Favicon and alias handling from #184839 is unchanged: a failed navigation never commits, so the shown page keeps its icon.

## Evidence

### Running-app proof

The packaged app built from this branch (debug, ad hoc signed, `ai.openclaw.mac.debug` 2026.10.7) ran on macOS 27.2 arm64 with Xcode 27.1, launched with `--dashboard` against a task-owned loopback Gateway and HTTP fixture. Accessibility drove it by process id, and the native failure view, which WebKit keeps out of the accessibility tree, was read and clicked from the window via Vision text recognition. Window screenshots and a recording of only the app's windows.

1. A new tab opens an address nothing listens on. The failure view shows "This page couldn't be opened / Could not connect to the server.", the address bar keeps `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/first-load`, the fixture starts, and the failure view's Reload loads the page (fixture: one request for `/first-load`).
2. The loaded page follows a link to another unserved address. The failure view shows, the address bar keeps `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/broken`, the fixture starts, and the toolbar Reload loads it (one request for `/broken`). The failure view is gone after each recovery.

The first revision (`9ad45a61910`) passed the same flow, but while the failure view showed, its background covered the whole dashboard window: chat, tab strip, address bar and toolbar. `e164e6e589e` makes the view layer-backed, and it now stays inside the tab.

The Browser panel of `e164e6e589e` at full resolution, cropped from the window screenshots (the failure view's text is small grey on dark in the full-window shots below):

Failed first load, then after the failure view's Reload:

![panel-failed-first-load](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/panel-fixed-10-new-tab-failed.png) ![panel-recovered-native-reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/panel-fixed-11-new-tab-recovered-native-reload.png)

Failed navigation from the loaded page, then after the toolbar Reload:

![panel-failed-navigation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/panel-fixed-21-loaded-tab-failed.png) ![panel-recovered-toolbar-reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/panel-fixed-22-loaded-tab-recovered-toolbar-reload.png)

The same crop from frames of the `e164e6e589e` recording at 9 s (first load failed), 21 s (recovered), 25 s (navigation failed) and the last frame (recovered), so the sequence can be checked without playing the video:

![frame-09s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/frame-fixed-t09s.png) ![frame-21s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/frame-fixed-t21s.png) ![frame-25s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/frame-fixed-t25s.png) ![frame-end](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/frame-fixed-end.png)

Text recognized in each crop and frame: [text.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/text.txt).

Failed navigation, `9ad45a61910` (whole window covered) and `e164e6e589e` (failure view inside the tab; the address bar shows the attempted URL):

![before-loaded-tab-failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/before-21-loaded-tab-failed.png)
![after-loaded-tab-failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-21-loaded-tab-failed.png)

Failed first load and recovery with `e164e6e589e`:

![after-new-tab-failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-10-new-tab-failed.png)
![after-native-reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-11-new-tab-recovered-native-reload.png)
![after-toolbar-reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-22-loaded-tab-recovered-toolbar-reload.png)

Recordings: [`9ad45a61910`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/before-recording.mp4), [`e164e6e589e`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-recording.mp4). Build identity, scenario logs and fixture request logs are next to them ([fixed identity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-identity.txt), [fixed scenario log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-scenario.log)). The bottom-left avatar is masked.

With `e164e6e589e`, on the same Mac: `swift test --filter DashboardNativeBrowserTests` (Xcode 27.1): 27 tests in 4 suites passed. SwiftFormat and SwiftLint `--strict` on the changed file: clean. `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`: only the existing `DashboardManager.swift` file_length violation.

### Offscreen renders and regressions

Each image is an offscreen render of the reading tab's web view from the real `DashboardWindowController` in the regression harness. The grey band at the bottom is a test harness readout, not app UI: it prints the tab state `DashboardNativeBrowserHost` publishes to the dashboard (loopback port masked). The tab strip and address bar are Control UI web chrome and are not part of these renders.

New tab whose first load fails, before (blank white page) and after (native failure view with Reload; the tab state already reported the attempted URL on base):

![a-before-new-tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/a-before-new-tab.png)
![a-after-new-tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/a-after-new-tab.png)

Loaded tab whose navigation to `/next` fails, before (old page stays and tab state still reports `/article`) and after (failure view; tab state reports the attempted `/next`):

![a-before-loaded-tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/a-before-loaded-tab.png)
![a-after-loaded-tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/a-after-loaded-tab.png)

Focused real-WKWebView regressions in `apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/DashboardNativeBrowserTests.swift` (`DashboardNativeBrowserFailureTests`), driving `DashboardWindowController` and its navigation delegate against task-owned loopback `DashboardHTTPFixture` endpoints:

- a new tab opened on a released loopback port shows the failure, keeps the attempted URL in tab state, and after the endpoint comes back the failure view's Reload button loads it;
- the same from an already loaded page: the page and its favicon stay, tab state shows the attempted URL, toolbar Reload loads it, and Back stays available after the retry;
- stop, replacement navigation, and a non-displayable response (download policy cancel) show no failure.

Results on macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Swift 6.4 (Command Line Tools), base `70c70646d86`:

- `swift test --filter DashboardNativeBrowserFailureTests` on this branch: 3 tests (5 cases) passed.
- The same flows on base (tests rewritten to base APIs, failure-view assertions dropped): the failed first load never retries (`Time limit was exceeded`, still waiting for the retried load), and after a failed navigation from a loaded page the tab state still shows the old page's URL (`failed.url == attempted.absoluteString` is false).
- Siblings `DashboardNativeBrowser|DashboardHTTPFixtureTests|DashboardBrowserDownloadTests|DashboardBrowserCookieBoundaryTests`: 34 tests in 7 suites passed.
- `swift build --build-tests`, `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` (0 files need formatting), `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` (only the existing `DashboardManager.swift` file_length violation, also on base), `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `git diff --check`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base <current main>` on the stacked follow-up for #183928, whose diff against main includes every file of this branch (not run separately on this branch): every guard passed except `lint apps` (the existing `DashboardManager.swift` file_length violation) and `macOS app CI tests` (1 failed, 607 passed), whose one failure is the tooling test `test/scripts/generate-gateway-protocol-plugin.test.ts`, which builds the Swift package itself and fails on this machine with the Command Line Tools manifest link error (`Package.__allocating_init` undefined); it does not touch the files in this change.

## Related work

- #152668 (open, prepare integrated tab logins before opening links) touches `DashboardNativeBrowserHost.swift`, `DashboardWindowController.swift` and `apps/.i18n/native-source.json`. No shared lines: its host change removes `self.onOpen?()` in `open` (line 160 on `70c70646d86`), a few lines above this stack's `navigate`/`perform` changes; its controller hunks are in lines 99-559, ours at 1331-1496. It already conflicts with current main on its own. Whichever lands second regenerates the i18n inventory with `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` (the inventory records source line sites).
- No open PR covers #183927 or #183928 (searched by symptom and by the owner file names).

## Gaps

- The offscreen renders under "Offscreen renders and regressions" come from the real `DashboardWindowController` on a host without a logged-in GUI session; the running-app proof above is the window evidence.
- The offscreen renders and the test results under them were built with the Command Line Tools (Swift 6.4) only, no Xcode; the running-app proof and its test run used Xcode 27.1. Xcode-only SwiftUI macro plugins (`@State`, `@Entry`, `#Preview`) were replaced locally by equivalent desugaring plugins, and two unrelated XCTest-based test files were left out locally because the CLT ships no XCTest. Nothing in this change uses SwiftUI. The `macos-swift` CI job is the authoritative native run.
- A failure after a document committed (`didFail` mid-load) takes the same path but has no dedicated test.
- Known edges, unchanged in scope: the failure view sits over the tab's web view, so a snapshot of a failed loaded tab (for example Annotate) still captures the previous page underneath; a same-document navigation by that previous page (`pushState`, hash change) does not start a provisional load and so leaves the failure shown; Reload retries a failed POST as a plain GET of the same URL.

prs.title: fix(macos): iMessage replies stop after app updates until Automation is re-granted
prs.body:
Closes #178719

Related: #186117 reports Automation failures on the iMessage account; this PR keeps the grant across app updates.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: outbound iMessage stops after an OpenClaw.app update when the Gateway runs as the app-managed background service. Every send fails with AppleScript -1712 until Messages Automation is granted again by hand, while `channels status` stays green.

## User Impact

The Messages Automation grant given to the background Gateway carries over to later app updates. The first move onto the new path (including Node to Bun) still needs one approval, and when Automation is missing the send error now says which grant and which process to check instead of a bare AppleScript code.

## Why This Change Was Made

`BundledRuntime` keeps owning the runtime layout. App-managed services now pin `<state>/runtime/service/bun`, a clone of the selected build's Bun; the package and SQLite library still load from the concrete build. `matchesBundledRuntime` accepts the stable path only when it is byte-identical to that build's Bun, so the "one matching build" rule from #161709 holds.

- Installs stage the clone with an atomic rename. After a failed install the staged Bun follows the installed service: it stays when the service now runs this build, the previous clone comes back otherwise, and a first clone is never deleted.
- Runtime collection also checks the arguments of a process running the stable Bun, so it never removes a build that process still loads.
- Restoration keeps the retained executable: hosting-change recovery resolves the build from its package entrypoint, and installed-service custody binds the expected command and runtime pin to the executable the service actually runs.
- A paused service updated by the app keeps the stable Bun in its resume command, and Resume stages the new build there first. Operator-pinned runtimes keep their own path.
- iMessage: AppleScript -1712 and -1743 send failures now append guidance naming the Automation grant, the local Gateway runtime path (or the SSH host for remote Messages), and the one-time re-grant after a runtime move. Other errors and `bridge_v2` failures are unchanged.

<details><summary>Root cause</summary>

`installArguments` passed `--runtime-path runtime.bun.path` (`<state>/runtime/<buildId>/bin/bun`), and each app update reinstalled the service onto the new build's path. tccd attributes the Gateway's Apple events to that path (`responsible_path=…/runtime/<buildId>/bin/bun` in the report), so each update created a new TCC client. A `runtime/current` symlink does not help: the kernel records the resolved path (see Evidence).

</details>

## Evidence

### macOS keeps the Automation grant on the path

Bun copies on macOS 27.0.1, signed with a test certificate (hardened runtime, production Bun entitlements; certificate removed afterwards) or ad hoc. A LaunchAgent runs `<profile>/runtime/service/bun probe.js`; the probe asks Messages for `count of accounts`, an Apple event that needs Automation and sends nothing.

- Step 1: Bun A on the stable path prompts once; allowed.
- Step 2: Bun B (different bytes, same signing requirement) renamed over the same path: no prompt, still allowed.
- Step 3: Bun B re-signed ad hoc (new identifier and cdhash) at the same path: no prompt, still allowed.
- Step 4: the step 2 binary, unchanged, at a second profile's path: tccd prompts again and creates a new grant with `identifier_type=Path`.
- Step 5: an ad-hoc Bun on a third profile's never-granted path: prompt, Don't Allow, the Apple event fails with -1743 and Messages never answers.
- Step 6: a different ad-hoc Bun renamed over that denied path: no prompt, still -1743.

So the decision is keyed by the executable path, in both directions: moving the same signed binary to a new path costs a new approval, which is what every update did before this PR, and replacing the binary at a fixed path keeps whatever the user decided there, Allow or Don't Allow. A stable path does not let a new build inherit a grant the user refused.

<details><summary>Probe output and tccd log</summary>

Stable 2026.10.7 ran in service mode on a fresh isolated profile, with a config value (`agents.defaults.userTimezone`) and a disabled cron job added through its CLI. I quit the app and left its Gateway running, as a Sparkle update does (`willInstallUpdate` only records a receipt). Then I replaced the bundle at the same path and launched it.

With this PR's build (`e76bcc919e3`), the app stops at credential startup on first launch and again after reopening. The service stays on the stable per-build Bun. In an earlier attempt, this PR's CLI ran `openclaw --profile p178719 doctor --fix` on a seeded 2026.10.7 profile (state schema migrated to 35). `config get agents.defaults.userTimezone` still returned `Asia/Kolkata`. I did not see the cron job afterwards, because `cron list` needs a running Gateway and that attempt never started one.

- Since `e9d4d67c89d`, the only changes are the `serviceBun` doc comment and `docs/platforms/mac/bundled-gateway.md`.
- iMessage: `client.test.ts` passes 22/22 locally at `e9d4d67c89d`; `extensions/imessage` has no changes since.
- Swift focused tests: 5 tests in 4 suites pass (6 cases), run at `ba63f8265ff`; since then `apps/macos` has changed only in the `serviceBun` doc comment.
- Affected native suites (185 tests, 7 suites, default and named profile, isolated HOME/state): the same environment failures as on `upstream/main`. Two named-profile tests swap between runs; each passes 3/3 when run alone, so they are order-dependent, not regressions.

- Full Disk Access continuity. Tested and **not** shown to carry over: Full Disk Access is checked against the code signature, not only the path. - A packaged paused-update run (see above).
- An unassisted update of a stable profile that has data, ending with that data served by a Gateway on `runtime/service/bun`. Both this PR and plain main stop at credential startup first (see above).

prs.title: fix(imessage): report Automation failures after Gateway updates
prs.body:
Related: #178719

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Messages Automation send failures leave the iMessage account green, with no recovery guidance, when a Gateway reply uses AppleScript text, attachment delivery, or the auto fallback.

## User Impact

Failed sends report the affected account and Messages Automation recovery steps. A successful send clears that warning; a successful read probe does not. Delivery error identity and classification are preserved.

**Limitations:** This does not preserve TCC grants across upgrades. Signed macOS upgrade testing was not available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary sends and native attachment actions now share the existing account-warning publisher. The RPC-only publication and duplicated RPC error-message augmentation were removed. Successful ordinary and native message completion clear only a matching Automation warning, not unrelated watcher errors. No options, permissions, runtime identities, or automatic resend behavior changed.

## Evidence

**Fault-injected imsg on Linux:** real shipped Gateway, real iMessage plugin, and real process spawn. The executable emits the exact imsg v0.17.0 Automation diagnostic and exits non-zero. prs.title: fix(discord): codex detach and rebind are lost after a Gateway restart
prs.body:
Fixes #178330. Related to #175379.

## What Problem This Solves

A Discord thread detached with a typed `/codex detach` can become bound again after the Gateway restarts. A typed `/codex bind` that moves a bound thread to a new workspace can also be undone by a restart.

## User impact

Detached threads stay detached, rebinds keep their new workspace, and later binding changes remain durable. A refused write from a retired or revoked runtime no longer disables persistence for its replacement owner, and a refused binding change reports a failure instead of success. A replacement Discord provider that starts after its predecessor retires gets its own thread binding manager, so its bind, idle timeout and detach writes persist. No config change or migration is needed.

A row left behind by an earlier detach is still loaded at startup. That thread needs one more `/codex detach` on this build.

The repair reaches core runtime-owned state stores, so the Telegram, ClickClack and `/codex` caller suites are included below. Matrix's separate no-instance repair is #177372.

## Cause and repair

Discord looked up its plugin runtime in the slot of the plugin instance currently running, and a typed detach starts in the `/codex` instance, where the Discord slot is empty. The write threw `Discord runtime not initialized`, the manager changed memory and disabled persistence for the process, and the command appeared to succeed until restart.

Each Discord manager now retains its creating runtime and passes it into async and synchronous store opens, and session-wide idle timeout, max age and unbind helpers read the same runtime from a private WeakMap through the account registry. Core now checks a runtime-owned synchronous store at open and before all seven mutators, update and deleteIf also after their callback. Already-open handle reads are unchanged.

The state runtime marks its authority refusal with `PLUGIN_STATE_RUNTIME_INACTIVE`, and the worker client preserves it. Discord tells it from a storage failure through the SDK facade it already imports, drops the uncommitted write and leaves persistence on. For a retired runtime, async unbind, bind, detach and the session-wide idle timeout, max age and unbind updates reject with it, send no unbound notification and publish no record. The check runs before every shared-memory publication, including a touch inside the 15 s persist interval and a manager with persistence off or latched off. It opens a data-only V2 handle with no store operation before the operation module source is captured. Synchronous compatibility calls still return null or an empty array, a retired owner's touches resolve null, and a deleted thread still closes its sessions after a refused unbind. Real storage failures still disable persistence and apply the change in memory.

`createThreadBindingManager` used to return the account's cached manager even after its owner retired, so a replacement provider's own bind, idle timeout and detach were refused, and after the old stop removed the adapter nothing recovered until a later acquisition. Now, when the cached manager's runtime is inactive, acquisition checks that the caller's runtime is active, starts the old stop without waiting for it, and registers a new manager that retains the caller's runtime. The old manager's runtime is never reassigned, and its late stop clears the slot and adapter only while it owns them. A live owner's manager is still reused, an inactive caller still gets the typed refusal, and a reference taken while its owner was live stays refused after retirement.

Against main `e6b0f044d586`, manager method signatures, account queues and the runtime lookup for managers without a retained runtime are unchanged.

Public SDK semantics change for retired runtimes. New synchronous opens and writes through retained synchronous handles now refuse work, and async binding changes through a retired Discord manager now reject. An October 19 usage query found no resolved references to this member but covered only 2,047 of 2,432 eligible artifacts, so third-party impact is unknown. `createThreadBindingManager`, exported from the Discord runtime API, now also replaces the cached manager of a retired owner, and in that case it throws the typed refusal if the caller's runtime is inactive or missing.

## Evidence

At `d1e4495644c5` the 6 changed test files passed 206 tests, the 14 plugin-state files passed 172 with 1 skipped, and the line-cap, max-lines, mock-exports and assertion-safety ratchets passed against `e6b0f044d586`. My head-only real Discord/model checks are in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177691#issuecomment-6505159776. The checks passed, but the full runbook evidence remains inconclusive. Typed detach and rebind persisted across restart. These runs cover only the first half of the authority-chain item. Retirement and replacement writes ran in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177691#issuecomment-6507291299, a scripted driver over the built production modules at this head and not a Gateway reload. A checker's revoke run there covers revocation. Other results below ran at earlier heads.

### Tests at `22ea62d`

Head `d1e4495644c5` merges main `e6b0f044d586` into `67b59f2ef60e`, a merge of main `eb8fa7d6d105` into `22ea62d`. Commit `22ea62d` adds `src/plugins/conversation-binding.discord-handoff.test.ts` with three cases. A live owner's retained manager refuses a candidate's writes after retirement until an explicit acquisition hands off. A replacement started after retirement gets a distinct manager whose bind, idle timeout, touch and detach persist, and the old manager's late stop leaves it registered. An inactive candidate cannot replace a retired owner. All three fail with the two production files from `56cd59f` and pass at `22ea62d`. Wrong versions that borrow the caller's runtime at call time, fall back to memory on the typed refusal, hand off over a live owner, or skip the candidate's activity check each fail one of them.

On a mocked clock, an uncommitted diagnostic found that at `56cd59f`, after the owner retired, the candidate's idle timeout write was refused at five points from +1 s to +1 h. At main `e2da41f` the idle writes, bind, touch and detach all succeeded before the old stop. A probe then stopped the old instance from accepting calls, started the replacement with the old manager unstopped, and ran each operation in the replacement.

| Operation | `56cd59f` production files | `22ea62d` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bind | Refused | Persisted |
| `/session idle` | Refused | Persisted |
| Touch | Null, no write | Row updated |
| `/codex detach` | Refused | Removed |
| After the late old stop | `BINDING_ADAPTER_UNAVAILABLE` | Bind persisted |

At `22ea62d` the 14 Discord binding, listener and manager caller files passed 206 tests and the 7 conversation binding and contract files passed 128. The extensions type check, the core plugin-platform test type check, formatting and typed lint on the three files it changes, and the mock-exports and line-cap ratchets also passed. At `22ea62d`, max-lines, the other ratchets, the SDK exports check, plugin inventory and config documentation were not rerun. At the `56cd59f` production code they passed except max-lines, which flagged three unchanged UI files, and 17 Telegram, ClickClack and `/codex` caller files passed 310 tests.

The 19 retired Discord cases fail at `d5f8321`, and the bound-source and core open cases fail at `ed59bdf`. Real SQLite trigger failures verify the memory fallback. The `/codex detach` command file checks the failure reply and the restored native binding. A 30-cell guard matrix from `95d9afe` through `ed59bdf`, a 45-cell probe and an uncommitted 153-cell probe of earlier heads found no durable difference and were not rerun.

### Prior-head Gateway evidence, not rerun

The earlier local Gateway record used a Discord stand-in and mock model. It compares main `89e77376ccb` with local merge `3a4095bc93d`, the earlier `de7639b` repair. It was not rerun on a later head, and its typed detach reply predates the refusal path above. After detach, stop and a fresh start, main held 1, 1, 1 rows and the old binding returned after restart, while the merge held 0, 0, 0. A typed rebind run kept the new workspace through restart on the merge, not on main.

### Remaining limits

The live runs did not cover a base build, a DM, Always allow or registry retirement, which the scripted driver ran. The full Discord extension project passed at `67b59f2ef60e` and was not rerun after main changed 26 Discord files. #178330 holds its author's pre-fix reproduction on a real Discord bot, which was not rerun on this branch.

The typed detach failure reply and the real store's refusal were measured separately, not together in a Gateway. The reload ordering, with the old instance's calls stopped before the replacement provider starts, was read from source and modeled with an instance that no longer accepts calls. The time from retirement to the replacement's acquisition was not measured, and writes in it are still refused. The handoff for a caller with no runtime has no test. A channel restart inside the same plugin instance after a timed-out stop still shares one manager, so the old task's late stop removes its adapter until the next provider start, as on main. A session-wide call while no manager is registered still uses the ambient runtime lookup, whose failure still turns persistence off, as on main. A session-wide update across two accounts stops at the first refused row without rolling back earlier rows, startup reconciliation does not catch a refused stale unbind, and a refused thread-delete unbind leaves its row for the replacement owner's sweeper.

prs.title: fix(macos): app quits with "Client credentials unavailable" after an in-place update while the previous Gateway service is running
prs.body:
Related: #156712

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS app quits at launch with "Another OpenClaw process is using your data" / "Client credentials unavailable. Run openclaw doctor --fix before reopening the app." when it is updated in place (reproduced from the latest stable, 2026.10.8, and from 2026.10.7) while the previous build's app-managed Gateway LaunchAgent service is still running.

## User Impact

User impact: after an in-place update, the app now starts normally. The Gateway service moves to the new build's runtime, client credentials are migrated, and existing config and cron jobs are kept. Users no longer have to run `openclaw doctor --fix` by hand. Normal launches, where the installed service already matches this build, are unchanged.

Operators who chose their Gateway version keep it: with `update.channel = extended-stable` or a channel install policy (`stable`, `beta`, `dev`), startup does not replace the service. This is the same gate setup and post-update repair already use. In that case startup behaves as it does today: the credential step can still fail while the old Gateway runs, and replacing the operator-pinned Gateway without consent would be worse. This is an accepted edge case.

## Why This Change Was Made

At launch, the app prepares client credentials before anything that replaces the service (`ConnectionModeCoordinator.apply`, `PostUpdateController`). Stable builds up to and including 2026.10.8 have no `client/credentials.sqlite`, so preparation is `required`. `doctor --client-credentials` deliberately does not control services: it calls `beginDoctorMaintenance({ root: null })`, so the stop branch gated on `params.root` never runs. Its state acquire then runs into the old Gateway's state-ownership lease and throws `GatewayStateOwnerContentionError`. The app then terminates, so the post-update replacement never runs.

The CLI's own refusals force the order:
- While the old Gateway runs, both the credential migration and `gateway install` refuse.
- After a stop, `gateway install` still refuses until credentials are migrated ("Client credentials require backed-up migration custody").

At startup the app now detects an app-managed service pinned to a different build's runtime, provided `CLIInstallPrompter.managedRepairGatesOpen` allows a managed repair. It then:
1. stops that service with this build's CLI;
2. prepares credentials;
3. installs the service on this build's runtime.

Stop, restore and install all carry the service custody captured at detection (`expectedServiceAuthority`) and recheck `serviceUpdateAuthorityError` before dispatch. So a service the operator reassigns while this build seeds its runtime or migrates credentials is refused instead of stopped or overwritten.

If credential preparation fails, the app restarts the previous service and the error surfaces as before. If the install fails, the failure is logged and startup continues, because credentials are valid and `PostUpdateController` still owns the retry. The CLI is unchanged.

Stopping only, without the install, was tried and rejected. Credentials migrated, but the app then kept retrying "gateway ensuring launchd" through the stale stable CLI, and the Gateway stayed down.

## Evidence

**Reproduction from the latest stable (isolated profile `p178719`; never the live `ai.openclaw.gateway` or `~/.openclaw`).**
- Start: the official notarized `OpenClaw-2026.10.8-arm64.dmg` (sha256 `7974be75…a3e899`), with its app-managed service seeded with a custom timezone and a cron job.
- Replace the `.app` bundle in place with the candidate build and launch it, with no manual steps.
- Both candidates are ad-hoc packaged from this branch merged with current `main` (2026.10.8). The control build has the four changed files reverted.

Before the fix (`main`, 2026.10.8), red:
```
## before (stable 2026.10.8)
service bun: ~/.openclaw-p178719/runtime/2026.10.8-release-5413218d77df-2026-10-27T20-43-42.000Z/bin/bun
client credentials db: absent
timezone: Asia/Kolkata
proof cron: 1
stable Gateway still listening: pid 47099

## after replacing the bundle in place (180s)
service bun: ~/.openclaw-p178719/runtime/2026.10.8-release-5413218d77df-2026-10-27T20-43-42.000Z/bin/bun
listener pid: 47099
runtime dir: 2026.10.8-release-5413218d77df-2026-10-27T20-43-42.000Z current
client credentials db: absent
app log (credentials):
  credentials: Credential startup failed: Could not prepare local client credentials. [openclaw] The CLI command failed.
  [openclaw] Another OpenClaw process is using your data. Wait for it to finish before trying again.
  credentials: Client credentials unavailable. Run openclaw doctor --fix before reopening the app.
```

After the fix, green (first run at 396f68ca0a72; rerun at 3f4cc925 with detection-time custody, same result: service moved in 20 s, credentials present, timezone and cron kept, control channel connected):
```
## before (stable 2026.10.8)
service bun: ~/.openclaw-p178719/runtime/2026.10.8-release-5413218d77df-2026-10-27T20-43-42.000Z/bin/bun
client credentials db: absent
timezone: Asia/Kolkata
proof cron: 1
stable Gateway still listening: pid 19672

## after replacing the bundle in place (21s)
service bun: ~/.openclaw-p178719/runtime/2026.10.8-396f68ca0a72-2026-10-28T21-27-38.000Z/bin/bun
listener pid: 20188
app running: 19977
client credentials db: present
timezone: Asia/Kolkata
proof cron: 1
app log (credentials, control channel):
  credentials: Replacing the previous build's Gateway service before credential preparation
  control: control channel state -> degraded: Cannot reach gateway at localhost:29871 (old service stopped, new one starting)
  control: control channel state -> connected
  control: control channel recovery finished
  control: control channel state -> connected
```

**Service reassigned after detection, through real process dispatch.** These runs use the same isolated seeded upgrade from stable 2026.10.8, with an app packaged from clean `3f4cc925` (build `2026.10.8-3f4cc9259730-…`, release configuration, no DEBUG interception). Partway through startup, an "operator" rewrites `~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.p178719.plist`: same label, plus an `EnvironmentVariables.OPENCLAW_PROOF_OPERATOR` key. The rewrite is triggered by real effects, not sleeps.

Before stop. The trigger is the new build's runtime seed directory appearing, which happens after detection read the service. The operator also reloads the service:
```
## before (stable 2026.10.8, app quit, service running)
listener pid: 58900
plist sha: 3f9a0009d361d32c
client credentials db: absent
## in-place update
new build began seeding its runtime at +10s
reassigned at +10s: plist sha a15c66fc996d5df8
operator service loaded: listener pid 59937, launchd env marker 1
## app outcome (+20s)
plist sha: a15c66fc996d5df8 (operator wrote a15c66fc996d5df8)
service bun: ~/.openclaw-p178719/runtime/2026.10.8-release-5413218d77df-2026-10-27T20-43-42.000Z/bin/bun
launchd env marker: 1
listener pid: 59937
client credentials db: absent
  credentials: Replacing the previous build's Gateway service before credential preparation
  credentials: Credential startup failed: The Gateway service changed before dispatch; retry.
  credentials: Client credentials unavailable. Run openclaw doctor --fix before reopening the app.
```
The operator's service is not stopped: the same pid is still listening and the plist is unchanged. Startup then ends in the existing credential-recovery surface. This is the accepted edge case: an operator who reassigns the service during startup gets "retry", and their service is left alone.

After credential preparation, before install. The trigger is the old Gateway's listener going away after the app's stop:
```
## in-place update
old Gateway stopped by the app at +25s
reassigned at +25s: plist sha a15c66fc996d5df8
## app outcome (+33s)
plist sha: a15c66fc996d5df8 (operator wrote a15c66fc996d5df8)
service bun: ~/.openclaw-p178719/runtime/2026.10.8-release-5413218d77df-2026-10-27T20-43-42.000Z/bin/bun
client credentials db: present
  credentials: Replacing the previous build's Gateway service before credential preparation
  credentials: Stale Gateway service replacement failed: The Gateway service changed before dispatch; retry.
```
Credentials are migrated, the install is refused, and the operator's plist bytes are kept. The service is not moved to the new runtime.

The same flow starting from stable 2026.10.7 was also red on `main` (443530a55b7e) and green with the first commit, twice: the service moved to the new runtime in 20 s, and the timezone and cron job survived.

**Tests:** `swift test --filter "stale service replacement keeps|StaleGatewayServiceReplacementTests|ClientCredentialStartupTests|UpdateOrchestrationTests"` passes (35 tests, at 3f4cc925). The new tests pin:
- a service reassigned after detection being refused before dispatch (`The Gateway service changed before dispatch; retry.`, no daemon command recorded), while an unchanged service gets exactly `stop --force`. This test fails without the captured authority: the reassigned service receives the stop;
- the order stop → credentials → install;
- a credential failure leading to restore instead of install;
- a refused stop skipping credential preparation;
- detection admitting the default and `exact` policies, and rejecting `extended-stable`, `beta` and `stable`.

**Not covered:**
- The restore path (credential preparation failing after the stop) is unit-tested only. One packaged attempt reloaded the operator's service right after the stop so that preparation would contend. The reload did not come up before the migration took the state, so that run repeated the before-install refusal instead: plist kept, credentials present.
- After the install refusal, the app's existing `ensuring launchd` retries (a later owner) ran through the installed stable CLI and failed. They did not rewrite the operator's plist.
- Remote mode with a local companion Gateway is excluded by the `.local` gate and was not exercised.
- The policy rejection was unit-tested through detection, not run end to end.
- Local packaging needed a temporary, uncommitted change that skips Finder `.DS_Store` files in `src/infra/package-dist-inventory.ts`. A stray `dist/.DS_Store` otherwise breaks the inventory/tarball check. This touches build tooling only, not the app code under test.

prs.title: fix(macos): report the real element when a page hooks Mac tab Inspect
prs.body:
Closes #183929 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Inspect on a Mac tab reports a page-supplied fake element, and the page can detect the inspection, when the page replaces `document.elementFromPoint` or `Element.prototype` methods. ## User Impact Inspect on a Mac tab reports the element actually under the pointer, and page scripts can no longer intercept or observe the lookup. ## Why This Change Was Made `DashboardNativeBrowserHost.inspect` now runs `BrowserInspectScript` with `callAsyncJavaScript(..., contentWorld: .defaultClient)`, the pattern the favicon reader in the same file already uses (#145714). Coordinates are passed as arguments instead of interpolated into the source. The shared script, bridge contract, tab-identity check after the await, and reply shape are unchanged. The client world still reads the shared live DOM, so content the page writes (for example an `aria-label`) is still reported as written; only page JavaScript hooks are excluded.
Root cause `inspect` used `webView.evaluateJavaScript("(\(script))(\(x), \(y))")`, which runs in the page content world. Page-defined replacements for `document.elementFromPoint`, `getAttribute`, or `getBoundingClientRect` therefore answered the inspection and could count the calls. The line arrived with #140988, which does not discuss content worlds. It was the only page-world script call on native browser tabs; the favicon reader already used `.defaultClient`.
## Evidence Packaged the macOS app ad hoc twice from upstream/main 443530a55b7: once with the fix line reverted (main) and once with the fix. Each build ran under the same named profile, connected with `configure-remote --direct-url` to an isolated Gateway started from the app's bundled runtime (private HOME, state, and config; loopback port; token auth). A chat link opened a Mac tab on a loopback test page that replaces `document.elementFromPoint` and `Element.prototype.getAttribute` and prints how many times those hooks ran. Inspect element from the tab menu, hovering the page's `div#real`: | | Hooked page: Inspect tooltip | Hooked page: hook counter after Inspect | Control page (no hooks) | |---|---|---|---| | main | `button#spoofed` 0 × 0, Name "Spoofed by page script" | 18 calls, "page detected the inspection" | `div#real.article` 592 × 538 | | fix | `div#real.article` 592 × 538, Name "Real page content" | 0 calls | `div#real.article` 592 × 538 | | main | fix | |---|---| | | | | | | | | | New real-WebKit test `DashboardNativeBrowserInspectTests` drives the same owner (`DashboardWindowController.nativeBrowser`) on a loopback `DashboardHTTPFixture` page with the same hooks. As a control, the script run in the page world returns the fake element; then `inspect(tabId:x:y:)` is called. - Base (fix line reverted): `node.id == "spoofed"`, `tag == "button"`, hooks called 5 times. Test fails. - Fix: `node.id == "real"`, `tag == "div"`, hooks called 0 times. Test passes. - `DashboardNativeBrowser*` suites: 25 tests in 4 suites pass on the fix, including favicon and tab-ownership tests.
Test output ``` ✘ ... Expectation failed: node["id"] as? String == "real" → "spoofed" ✘ ... Expectation failed: node["tag"] as? String == "div" → "button" ✘ ... Expectation failed: hookCalls == 0 → 5 ✘ Test run with 1 test in 1 suite failed after 1.352 seconds with 3 issues. ✔ Test "inspection reports the real element when the page replaces the DOM lookups" passed after 0.957 seconds. ✔ Test run with 25 tests in 4 suites passed after 1.883 seconds. ```
Checks: `swiftformat --lint` clean on both files; `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` reports only the existing `DashboardManager.swift` `file_length` violation, which is also on main; `git diff --check` clean. Environment: macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.1. Production delta +6/-2; test delta +52/-0. Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the previous evaluation world with no state or config migration. Blast radius is the Mac tab Inspect request.

prs.title: fix(macos): Settings 404 with remote Control UI base path
prs.body:
Closes #164596 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the macOS dashboard and Settings return HTTP 404 when the app connects to a remote Gateway whose Control UI is served under `gateway.controlUi.basePath` and the connection address has no path (SSH tunnel, or a direct `ws://host:port` URL). ## User Impact Settings and the dashboard open under the Gateway's Control UI mount without editing the connection address. Both the app and the Gateway need this change; a mixed pair behaves as before. ## Why This Change Was Made The app cannot know the mount. SSH endpoints are always `ws://127.0.0.1:`, and remote mode deliberately fell back to `/` because the Gateway never advertised its base path (#15862 fixed local mode only). hello-ok already says where the Control UI lives through `controlUiUrl` (only with `publicOrigin`) and `snapshot.controlUiIdentityUrl` (only for HTTPS sign-in). This adds the bare mount beside them as the optional `controlUiBasePath`. On the app side, `GatewayEndpointStore.dashboardURL` stays the one place that picks the path, now using the advertised mount for remote URLs without a path. It is read from the same current hello as the identity URL. `config.get` (operator.read) can return the same value, but opening the dashboard reads only the hello, with no discovery RPCs (`GatewayConnectionDashboardIdentityTests` asserts this), and the Control UI location already lives in hello.
Root cause and rejected alternatives - With `basePath` set, the Gateway routes `/` outside the Control UI (`src/gateway/control-ui-routing.ts:92`), so `GET /` is 404 while WebSocket upgrades at `/` still succeed. That is why the node stays connected while the dashboard fails. - Redirecting `/` to the base path on the Gateway does not help: Settings appends its route to the dashboard's current URL, so it would still request `/settings/appearance`. - Keeping a path from `gateway.remote.url` in SSH mode does not help: the SSH editor writes the URL without a path, and nothing documents one there.
## Evidence Ad-hoc macOS builds from `c258ea68c3b` (main) and `c258ea68c3b` plus this diff, each against an isolated Gateway (`controlUi.basePath: "/__openclaw__"`) with remote URL `ws://127.0.0.1:28791` (no path). Settings opened from the app menu; screenshots are the dashboard window only. | Main | This PR | |---|---| | | | | "Dashboard unavailable. The Gateway returned HTTP 404 (Not Found)." at `http://127.0.0.1:28791/` | Settings → Appearance under `/__openclaw__/` | This PR, same connection, Settings → This Mac (the page blocked in the report): Request trace through a logging proxy (asset requests omitted): - Main, remote URL `ws://127.0.0.1:28792`: `GET / -> 404`. - Fix, same URL: `GET /__openclaw__/settings/appearance -> 200`, dashboard WebSocket upgrades at `/__openclaw__/`. - Control, `ws://127.0.0.1:28792/__openclaw__/`: Settings loads at `/__openclaw__/settings/appearance` on both main and the fix. - Fixed app against the main Gateway: unchanged 404 at `/`.
Fix run, root URL (asset requests omitted) ``` WS upgrade / HTTP GET /__openclaw__/ -> 200 HTTP GET /__openclaw__/control-ui-config.json -> 401 HTTP GET /__openclaw__/settings/appearance -> 200 WS upgrade /__openclaw__/ HTTP GET /__openclaw__/control-ui-config.json -> 200 -- dashboard window AXWebArea: Appearance — OpenClaw ```
Main run, root URL ``` WS upgrade / HTTP GET / -> 404 -- dashboard window AXStaticText: Dashboard unavailable AXStaticText: The Gateway returned HTTP 404 (Not Found). AXStaticText: http://127.0.0.1:28792/ ```
**Upgrade from latest stable (v2026.10.8)** `openclaw@2026.10.8` from npm in an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` with `gateway.controlUi.basePath: "/__openclaw__"`, settings saved through the stable CLI. The macOS app from this PR saved a remote profile at the bare `ws://127.0.0.1:` and paired. Then stable was stopped, this PR's `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` ran on the same state, this PR's Gateway started, and the app was relaunched on the saved profile without reconfiguring it.
Before → after on the same state and saved profile ```text Stable 2026.10.8 Gateway hello-ok: {"serverVersion":"2026.10.8","protocol":4,"controlUiUrl":null,"controlUiBasePath":null} macOS app, saved profile, Settings…: WS upgrade / HTTP GET / -> 404 AXStaticText: Dashboard unavailable AXStaticText: The Gateway returned HTTP 404 (Not Found). paired devices: [4526d030… openclaw-macos node]; state schema 20 Upgrade: this PR's `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` -> exit 0 Saved pre-migration SQLite backup ... schema=34, expected=34, pending=0 gateway block identical: True ui identical: True {'seamColor': '#FF4500'} paired devices: [4526d030… openclaw-macos node]; state schema 34 This PR's Gateway on the upgraded state hello-ok: {"protocol":4,"controlUiUrl":null,"controlUiBasePath":"/__openclaw__"} macOS app relaunched on the same saved profile, Settings… (asset requests omitted): WS upgrade / HTTP GET /__openclaw__/ -> 200 HTTP GET /__openclaw__/settings/appearance -> 200 WS upgrade /__openclaw__/ HTTP GET /__openclaw__/control-ui-config.json -> 200 AXWebArea: Appearance — OpenClaw ```
Saved connections and settings survive: the `gateway` and `ui` config blocks are identical, the paired Mac device is still paired after the schema 20 → 34 migration, and the saved pathless profile opens Settings under the mount after the upgrade. Doctor's other config additions and the migration come from main and are the same without this change. Before the upgrade the same app still gets 404, since v2026.10.8 does not advertise the mount. In an earlier v2026.10.7 run, the stable CLI's `gateway call health`, `status` and `device.pair.list` against this PR's Gateway all exited 0, so older clients accept the new optional hello field. Tests: `connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts` mount-path case fails on main (`expected undefined to be '/__openclaw__'`) and passes with the fix; both hello test files pass (56 tests). `remote dashboards open under the Control UI mount advertised by hello` fails with the old `/` branch and passes with the fix; the `GatewayEndpointStoreTests`, `GatewayConnectionControlUIAuthTests`, `DashboardTokenlessRouteTests`, `DashboardReconnectTests` and `GatewayConnectionDashboardIdentityTests` suites pass (92 tests). `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, format check, SwiftFormat, `pnpm protocol:check` and `git diff --check` pass. SwiftLint `--strict` reports `file_length` on `DashboardManager.swift`, which is already over the limit on main (1505 lines). Production delta +46/-15 (including the `#if DEBUG` test factory hunk); test delta +55/-1. Merge risk: two-way door; the field is additive with no wire-version bump, older apps ignore it and older Gateways omit it. Blast radius is remote dashboards whose connection URL has no path.
