prs.title: fix(macos): keep Gateway auth when Tailscale exposure is turned off
prs.body:
Closes #187597 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the Gateway's token, password and trusted-proxy settings are deleted when Tailscale Exposure is set to Off in the macOS Connection settings while the app is connected to its Gateway. ## User Impact After choosing Off, paired phones, other CLIs and the Control UI keep authenticating with the existing token. Before this change they were rejected after the Gateway restarted, and the Gateway ran with a new runtime-only token. ## Why This Change Was Made `TailscaleIntegrationSection.buildTailscaleConfigRoot` is the one place that maps Exposure to config. On Off it now removes only `auth.allowTailscale`, the key Serve writes, and leaves the rest of `gateway.auth` alone. The Gateway already treats a missing `allowTailscale` as false when Tailscale mode is not serve (`src/gateway/auth-resolve.ts:79-81`), so this does not widen access. The regression test goes through `saveTailscaleSettings`, the save boundary the settings view calls, with `ConfigStore` routed to its connected `config.set` path. `saveTailscaleSettings` is internal for that test, like `loadedSettings` and `applySettingsIfChanged` beside it; the builder stays private.
Root cause The original Tailscale settings (28ad475) skipped `auth` on Off. 850cbfe3698 ("route macOS remote config via gateway") replaced that with `gateway.removeValue(forKey: "auth")` without giving a reason. The connected save (`ConfigStore.saveToGateway`) sends the whole document to `config.set`, which replaces the stored config, so the deletion reached `openclaw.json`. On restart the Gateway found no token and generated a runtime-only one. The offline fallback (`saveDict(preserveExistingKeys: true)`) merges keys, so it never deleted `auth`.
## Evidence ### macOS app, connected Off save, after upgrading from the latest stable 1. `openclaw@2026.10.8` from npm (latest stable) wrote the config with `openclaw config set`: token auth, `allowTailscale: true`, and `agents.defaults.maxConcurrent: 7` as an unrelated setting. Its Gateway started on that state and accepted the token. 2. The Gateway from an ad-hoc build of this branch then ran on the same state as the named profile's launchd service, and the macOS app (same build, same profile, local mode) attached to it: "Using existing gateway (pid 90862)". Exposure showed "Tailnet (Serve)"; I chose Off in the Connection window. 3. The app's own UI connection sent `config.set`; the Gateway accepted the write and restarted; the app reconnected with the same token. The config diff against what 2026.10.8 wrote is only the two intended keys. 4. After the restart: the original token is accepted; a wrong token is rejected; a request carrying only Tailscale identity headers is rejected.
Gateway log and config diff ```text 19:56:02 [ws] client connected conn=03661c35-… client=openclaw-macos mode=ui role=operator auth=token 19:58:07 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ config.set 3898ms bytes=734 conn=03661c35…b1e8 19:58:13 [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (gateway.auth.allowTailscale, gateway.tailscale) 19:58:14 [reload] config source revision 2 accepted (write) 19:58:27 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting 19:58:43 [ws] client connected conn=5aba3fcf-… client=openclaw-macos mode=ui role=operator auth=token $ diff <(jq -S . openclaw.json written by 2026.10.8) <(jq -S . openclaw.json after the app's Off save) "gateway": { "auth": { - "allowTailscale": true, "mode": "token", "token": "proof-token-187597" }, "bind": "loopback", "mode": "local", - "port": 18998 + "port": 18998, + "tailscale": { + "mode": "off" + } }, ```
Stable 2026.10.8 writes the config ```text $ openclaw --version OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (dc2523e) $ openclaw config set gateway.auth.mode token $ openclaw config set gateway.auth.token proof-token-187597 $ openclaw config set gateway.auth.allowTailscale true $ openclaw config set agents.defaults.maxConcurrent 7 $ openclaw gateway call health --token proof-token-187597 # stable 2026.10.8 Gateway {"ok":true} ```
Authority after the restart ```text $ openclaw gateway call health --token proof-token-187597 # original shared token {"ok":true} $ openclaw gateway call health --token wrong-token unauthorized: gateway token mismatch $ curl /__openclaw__/assistant-media?meta=1 -H 'tailscale-user-login: peter' -H 'x-forwarded-for: 100.64.0.1' ... # identity headers, no token 403 (Gateway log: "observed unattributable proxy-shaped traffic from 127.0.0.1; Gateway-authenticated routes reject it") $ curl /__openclaw__/assistant-media?meta=1 -H 'authorization: Bearer proof-token-187597' 200 ```
### Main vs fix on the same connected save The same `config.get` → Off → `config.set {raw, baseHash}` sequence through the CLI against an isolated Gateway, starting from token auth plus `allowTailscale: true`. Main removes `gateway.auth`, the Gateway logs "auth token was missing. Generated a runtime token for this startup", and the original token is rejected. The fix keeps `auth.mode` and `auth.token`, removes only `allowTailscale`, and the original token still works. | main | fix | |---|---| | | |
Main output ```text $ jq -c .gateway openclaw.json # before {"mode":"local","port":18998,"bind":"loopback","auth":{"mode":"token","token":"proof-token-187597","allowTailscale":true}} $ openclaw gateway call config.get | jq '.gateway.tailscale.mode = "off" | del(.gateway.auth)' | openclaw gateway call config.set {raw, baseHash} config.set: {"ok":true} $ jq -c .gateway openclaw.json # after the save {"mode":"local","port":18998,"bind":"loopback","tailscale":{"mode":"off"}} 18:56:31 [reload] config change detected; reload (gateway.auth.mode, gateway.auth.token, gateway.auth.allowTailscale, gateway.tailscale, meta) 18:56:32 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting 18:56:33 [gateway] auth token was missing. Generated a runtime token for this startup (not persisted) $ openclaw gateway call health --token proof-token-187597 # same client after restart health: unauthorized: gateway token mismatch ```
Fix output ```text $ openclaw gateway call config.get | jq '.gateway.tailscale.mode = "off" | del(.gateway.auth.allowTailscale)' | openclaw gateway call config.set {raw, baseHash} config.set: {"ok":true} $ jq -c .gateway openclaw.json # after the save {"mode":"local","port":18998,"bind":"loopback","auth":{"mode":"token","token":"proof-token-187597"},"tailscale":{"mode":"off"}} 19:01:16 [reload] config change detected; reload (gateway.auth.allowTailscale, gateway.tailscale, meta) 19:01:17 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting $ openclaw gateway call health --token proof-token-187597 # same client after restart health: ok $ openclaw gateway call health --token wrong-token health: unauthorized: gateway token mismatch ```
### Swift test at the save boundary `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter TailscaleIntegrationSectionTests`. The test loads a document with token or password auth plus `allowTailscale: true` and calls `saveTailscaleSettings(.off)` with `ConfigStore` on its connected `config.set` path. On main's logic it fails for both cases at `TailscaleIntegrationSectionTests.swift:203` (`gateway["auth"]`) while `.saved` and `tailscale.mode == "off"` pass; with the fix the suite passes 10/10.
Test output ```text == MAIN logic == ✘ "turning tailscale off keeps gateway authentication" credentials ["token": "existing-token", "mode": "token"] TailscaleIntegrationSectionTests.swift:203:9 Expectation failed: gateway?["auth"] as? [String: String] == credentials ✘ "turning tailscale off keeps gateway authentication" credentials ["mode": "password", "password": "existing-password"] TailscaleIntegrationSectionTests.swift:203:9 Expectation failed: gateway?["auth"] as? [String: String] == credentials ✘ Test run with 10 tests in 1 suite failed after 0.017 seconds with 2 issues. == FIX == ✔ Test "turning tailscale off keeps gateway authentication" with 2 test cases passed after 0.005 seconds. ✔ Test run with 10 tests in 1 suite passed after 0.051 seconds. ```
Gaps: the main-branch failure is shown on the replayed connected save and in the Swift test, not by clicking in a main build of the app. Identity-only acceptance before Off was not exercised; it needs a real Tailscale Serve front end. Gates: `git diff --check` clean. swiftformat and swiftlint were not available locally. Production delta +6/-2; test delta +38/-0. Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the prior behavior with no config or state migration. Blast radius is Off saves from the macOS Tailscale section. Not included: Doctor recovery for hosts that already lost `auth`. That would be a Doctor change needing owner approval. Those hosts already had a new token saved by `ensureAppHostedGatewayAuth` and re-pair through the existing flow. The Serve display for Gateways with no Tailscale config is #187599.

prs.title: fix(macos): prevent duplicate voice sends and false sent feedback
prs.body:
Related: #127557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: manual Send and an already-queued auto-send can submit one voice transcript twice, and an RPC rejection can appear successfully sent.

## User Impact

One coordinator-owned attempt submits each active transcript. Pending sends show progress; only Gateway acceptance produces sent feedback. Rejection preserves editable text for explicit retry.

**Ready for maintainer review.** The conflict repair and Anmol's native compile fixes are published at d6c006bed106d1cb0c58be150d9d902e8f95b881, refreshed onto main dad7cbe17463dd9040f723d69f2826cf8e931fdf. GitHub reports the branch mergeable (no source conflicts). The earlier publication refusal came from a stale upstream Android release workflow in the older prepared base; the supported base refresh incorporated live main's definition. No permission change or guard bypass was needed. Exact-head focused native gates and real rejection/retry proof are now supplied by Anmol below. Ready status was requested by Anmol; no merge has been requested or performed. Skipped native CI jobs are not counted as passing.

There are no authored config, schema, durability, public protocol, dependency, or permission changes. This is not a durable outbox or exactly-once delivery guarantee; cancellation cannot retract an already-submitted RPC.

Contributor credit: @anmol0b requested this fix and supplied native verification, resolution choices, and follow-up compile fixes.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @anmol0b](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/f10d7d72-7d35-44c9-858b-62fbb32bf32f)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5eee3800-f321-48db-9daf-2f35ae11bae2)

## Why This Change Was Made

The coordinator claims a token before route lookup, retains one task, consumes the result, and retires work at replacement or dismissal start. Identical full payload and resolved route reuse the invocation key; edits or route changes get a fresh key. Queued auto callbacks cannot retry failures. The unowned coordinator forward and unconditional sent timer are removed.

Wake cleanup dismisses only its capture token, preserving pending PTT sends during ordinary lease release. Manual send, immediate/delayed auto-send, and PTT share the owner; the no-overlay wake fallback plays its chime only after acceptance.

The published repair preserves main's removed trace logging, source-free session API, context-free token/chime APIs, single state-bound action owner, canonical routeEntries lookup, and event-based lifecycle waits. It applies Anmol's fixes for mutually inferred lazy fixture types, the routeEntries fixture argument, and the long Forward typealias.

Risk is bounded to native voice submission and overlay lifecycle, with no stored-state migration. Exact-head focused native validation is documented below; no broad native CI pass is claimed. The published delta remains the same 16 task files relative to the refreshed main base.

## Evidence

### Native proof supplied by Anmol — exact published head

[Published-head native gates and live rejection/retry proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186271#issuecomment-6464391677), supplied by @anmol0b for d6c006bed106d1cb0c58be150d9d902e8f95b881 **as-is, with no local changes**, on macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Xcode 27.1 / Swift 6.4:

- Native app build and test build both exited 0 (the supplied capture reports 3m13.470s combined wall time).
- All 47 tests in the six focused voice suites passed in 0.307s; the suites then passed 10/10 repetitions.
- SwiftFormat 0.63.1: 0/33 files require formatting, exit 0. SwiftLint 0.65.1 reports no violations in this PR's files; the reported whole-run finding remains the preexisting, untouched DashboardManager.swift file-length error (1505 > 1500). This is not labeled an all-green global lint run.
- Localization verification passed on this exact head: entries=4545 changed=false, exit 0.
- The author audited the focused suites' injected Gateway/microphone/defaults/Keychain boundaries, then ran them under sandbox-exec with private HOME/state and restrictions on operator state, preferences, and the live Gateway port. These are author-provided native results, not execution performed by the Linux implementation agent.

prs.title: fix(workboard): release owner slots held by completed legacy executions
prs.body:
Related: #122911.

## What Problem This Solves

A completed Workboard card can retain a historical execution marked running. That stale execution incorrectly occupies the assigned worker’s global owner slot, so ready work on another board silently never starts.

## User Impact

Completed cards no longer starve later work for the same owner. Nonterminal running executions still block that owner; archived-card and expired-claim grace behavior keep their existing rules. Historical rows remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing done-card exclusion around all arms of the one private owner-slot predicate used by dispatcher selection and atomic SQLite admission. No duplicate SQL rule, row rewrite, migration, cap, permissions, schema, or SDK change. Keeps atomicdjt/David Turner’s contributor commits.

## Evidence

Final head `74364685305f43e196067ce10a863b3dcfed5913` changes tests only from the proven production repair.

Built Gateway, real bundled Workboard RPC/CLI, actual SQLite worker and worker sessions, deterministic local provider. Legal done/running legacy records seeded through cards.create. Main twice starts no same-owner work on another board; candidate twice starts one actual worker and accepts workboard_complete, reaching done with passed proof. Normal dispatch succeeds on both; nonterminal running executions remain blocking on both. Entire old card readback is unchanged.

Detailed actual RPC/worker receipts: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187880#issuecomment-6508868833

Corrected existing SQLite capacity table retains a completed-positive and nonterminal-negative case. Candidate capacity + dispatcher files pass 56/56; corrected completed case fails as intended on frozen main (15 other cases pass). Focused formatting passes. Removed duplicate new helper/dispatcher test blocks; whole-PR tests net -3 lines, no allocations. Production +2/-3.

Merge danger: two-way door. Revert restores prior slot admission without rewriting stored cards. Blast radius: global Workboard owner capacity when a terminal card retains a historical running execution; live/nonterminal ownership protection remains unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #187886; related to #187878. Installed-service diagnostics still inherited missing state selectors from the inspecting CLI after the core Doctor migration fix landed.

## User Impact

Gateway status reads the installed service's config and runtime intent, prints its journal/log guidance, and lets Doctor scan its updater context without borrowing an isolated CLI's state selectors.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `mergeGatewayServiceEnv` for the remaining direct environment merges. The shared helper now follows #187886's approach: clear the caller's four OpenClaw home/state/profile/config selectors, then overlay the installed service environment. Existing HOME fallback, Windows command-line profile handling, and native supervisor selection stay with their existing owners.

The identity producer in `run-main-service-installation.ts` and both of #187886's regression files are **unchanged from main**. The original migration fix and tests have been removed from this PR. Thanks @shakkernerd for the report and the landed identity-producer fix.

## Evidence

New sibling regressions fail against current main at `c77b791cf4fca27afe64a6da4ee9ba22f5133a28`: **7 failures across 5 files**, each at the intended selector leak.

| Consumer | Failure reproduced on main |
| --- | --- |
| Shared service-environment helper | Caller state survives an installed definition with absent/empty environment on macOS, Linux, and Windows |
| Status gathering | Installed service config resolves to the isolated caller config |
| Runtime-intent projection | Caller home/state/config selectors reach the service intent reader |
| Printed status | Journal guidance names the isolated caller's systemd profile |
| Doctor platform notes | Installed-service updater scanning receives caller selectors |

After the sibling-only fix:

- **476 passed, 16 platform-skipped** across ten selected Vitest lanes in **103.55 s**. Selection includes 26 direct/barrel consumer test files plus native process-environment, update service-selection, and both unchanged #187886 identity suites. Linux self-service cases remain platform-skipped locally.
- **Live compiled production CLI:** `gateway status --runtime-intent-only` with private temporary HOME/state/config and a synthetic unloaded LaunchAgent. Result: **exit 0, service runtime intent known**. A deliberately unsupported isolated caller runtime-pin store remained at schema **99**, proving it was not used as the installed service's store. No service was started or restarted. The live invocation took **5.438 s** of test time; shared compiler preparation took **25.4 s**. The first standalone cached-fixture attempt failed on a cleaned-up absolute module path; proof was completed under the active supported CLI harness.
- Core and targeted CLI/services/Doctor test typechecks, touched-file oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and Madge pass (**0 cycles**).
- Both ratchets pass: max-lines **404 grandfathered suppressions**, OpenClaw env names **458/458**; test lines **6,277,555 / 6,327,226**, slack **49,671**. No baseline changes.
- Local autoreview of the complete sibling diff against `c77b791cf4fc`: **scoped-clean at P0–P2**. Simplification keeps the existing shared helper as the sole sibling projection owner. Production **+26/−20 (net +6 LOC)**; tests **+90/−3 (net +87)**; docs **+5**.

prs.title: fix(ios): keep native Talk working while the phone is locked
prs.body:
Closes #185664

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native iOS Talk stopping after the phone locks or failing to resume listening after a reply.

## User Impact

With “Talk in the background” enabled, an established continuous session can keep speaking and answer another request while locked. iOS background voice remains best-effort.

## Why This Change Was Made

Protect live realtime transports and current native transcript work from competing starts. Keep the existing realtime recovery task able to restart an ended transport. Preserve an admitted background Talk session past ordinary connection expiry and reuse its active native audio session when returning to listening while locked. Foreground recovery, realtime fallback, PTT, and explicit route changes retain their configuration paths.

## Evidence

- Current head: `2b83d7d2937a92933c933d4f92c3a1d63d0e3778`. The P1 guard regression is repaired by distinguishing active native transcript processing from the retained continuous capture mode used by realtime recovery. The existing remote-close test now observes the scheduled restart passing through production start admission; it preserves the explicit-stop case and adds no new production test hook.
- The extended regression fails on `ec9605e4c39` because the scheduled restart never enters start. All 66 selected tests across Talk configuration, Gateway speech, and background lifecycle pass after the repair, including native speech ownership and cleanup after Talk stops. The green `xcodebuild` command exited 0. Native results are shown below.
- A new independent automated Codex review of the two-file P1 repair and public source context completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The earlier local review missed the realtime recovery interaction; the hosted review identified it. The new review did not run the project or establish a live provider connection.
- The earlier signed full-app device build succeeded, and physical native STT/TTS testing demonstrated a reply and a tester-confirmed spoken “hello” to a second request while locked. The inspectable diagnostic lifecycle timeline below now supplies the previously missing device evidence. It is not a fresh physical run of the realtime repair or a realtime provider-reconnection test.
- Formatting and normal commit hooks pass. Full-app native builds use the repository's advisory size-limit mode for an untouched oversized demo function, with correctness lint active. Fresh PR CI is pending. Realtime provider reconnection remains physically unverified; the new regression proves the reported scheduling/admission failure, not completed WebRTC negotiation or provider audio.

<details>
<summary>Realtime recovery regression, red and green</summary>

The existing relay remote-close callback clears its transport and schedules the actual production restart. An existing start-entry observer records admission after the guard, then stops before permission/provider I/O. This exercises the failed scheduling/admission path rather than just the recovery predicate.

Published head, expected native failure:

```text
✘ Test "relay close recovers disconnections but preserves explicit stop" recorded an issue with 1 argument explicitStop → false at TalkModeConfigParsingTests.swift:535:13: Expectation failed: result == .completed
✘ Test run with 1 test in 1 suite failed after 3.333 seconds with 1 issue.
```

The red run reported its complete failure result, then its Xcode reporter stalled and was stopped. That command exited 143 and is not claimed successful.

Repaired head, `xcodebuild` exit 0:

```text
✔ Test "background expiry preserves continuous Talk until it stops" passed after 0.054 seconds.
✔ Test "repeated start preserves an active continuous speech turn" passed after 0.041 seconds.
​✔ Test "relay close recovers disconnections but preserves explicit stop" with 2 test cases passed after 0.536 seconds.
✔ Test run with 66 tests in 3 suites passed after 2.249 seconds.
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Physical native Talk evidence, October 29</summary>

Environment: physical iPhone Duo, iOS 27.2, separate development app version 2026.10.8, build 121658, native speech-recognition/TTS path. The tester enabled Talk in the background and locked the phone while it spoke. Diagnostic scene markers confirm the preference was enabled.

These are inspected, allowlisted excerpts from the device's app cache. They contain timestamps, lifecycle booleans, and audio ownership events only. Temporary probes were removed before the original publication. These captures came from diagnostic candidates of the native fix, before the later realtime-admission repair; the native speech-ownership regression has been rerun after that repair. No raw device log, credential, identifier, account/provider configuration, transcript, or private endpoint is published.

Before the native repair, locking triggered a competing start while speech was still owned, followed by audio deactivation and an OS activation error. The tester heard the reply cut off:

```text
[2026-10-29T17:07:23.303Z] talk probe scene=inactive preference=true enabled=true eligible=true speaking=true
[2026-10-29T17:07:24.841Z] talk probe scene=active preference=true enabled=true eligible=true speaking=true
[2026-10-29T17:07:24.855Z] talk probe start accepted speaking=true continuousOwner=true
[2026-10-29T17:07:24.964Z] talk probe scene=background preference=true enabled=true eligible=true speaking=true
[2026-10-29T17:07:24.964Z] talk probe grace started seconds=25.0
[2026-10-29T17:07:24.964Z] talk probe suspend keep=true enabled=true speaking=true
[2026-10-29T17:07:25.117Z] talk probe deactivate caller=start() enabled=true speaking=true
[2026-10-29T17:07:25.821Z] talk probe start failed domain=NSOSStatusErrorDomain code=560557684
```

With the native repairs, the phone remained locked/backgrounded from 17:41:42.061Z until 17:42:34.309Z, approximately 52.25 seconds. This crossed the ordinary 25-second grace deadline. The tester heard the first reply, then asked “Reply with just hello” while still locked and heard “hello.” The reply's spoken and written counts both ended at 35, so this is not a claim that the last run counted to 60.

The timeline shows eligible Talk preserved at background entry, native restart admission after the first reply and again after the follow-up, and eligible Talk retained on unlock. There was no Gateway disconnect, reconnect suppression, activation failure, or audio deactivation in this interval. Deactivation occurs only after the tester turns Talk off at 17:42:43.388Z.

```text
[2026-10-29T17:41:28.996Z] talk probe enabled=true
[2026-10-29T17:41:29.062Z] talk probe start accepted speaking=false continuousOwner=false
[2026-10-29T17:41:40.496Z] talk probe scene=inactive preference=true enabled=true eligible=true speaking=true

[2026-10-29T17:41:42.061Z] talk probe grace started seconds=25.0
[2026-10-29T17:41:42.061Z] talk probe suspend keep=true enabled=true speaking=true
[2026-10-29T17:42:07.517Z] talk probe stopSpeaking speaking=false enabled=true
[2026-10-29T17:42:07.518Z] talk probe start accepted speaking=false continuousOwner=false
[2026-10-29T17:42:26.368Z] talk probe stopSpeaking speaking=false enabled=true
[2026-10-29T17:42:26.368Z] talk probe start accepted speaking=false continuousOwner=false
[2026-10-29T17:42:33.637Z] talk probe scene=inactive preference=true enabled=true eligible=true speaking=false
[2026-10-29T17:42:34.309Z] talk probe scene=active preference=true enabled=true eligible=true speaking=false
[2026-10-29T17:42:43.388Z] talk probe enabled=false
[2026-10-29T17:42:43.388Z] talk probe stopSpeaking speaking=false enabled=false
[2026-10-29T17:42:43.395Z] talk probe stopSpeaking speaking=false enabled=false
[2026-10-29T17:42:43.395Z] talk probe deactivate caller=stop() enabled=false speaking=false
```

The spoken “hello” and Listening state after unlock are tester observations, corroborated by this lifecycle timeline. The logs do not contain an audio recording or the speech transcript and do not independently establish audibility. No physical realtime-reconnection result is claimed.

</details>

prs.title: feat(signal): send TTS replies as native voice notes
prs.body: Related: #166408 ## What Problem This Solves Signal users get spoken replies as a downloadable `.mp3` file instead of a voice message, even when the reply asks for voice delivery. ## User Impact On native signal-cli transports (external daemon, UNIX socket), TTS replies arrive as Signal voice notes with the inline voice-message player. Other audio, such as generated music, and all other media stay ordinary attachments. Container mode (bbernhard REST) is unchanged and still sends an attachment. ## Why This Change Was Made Signal now advertises TTS voice delivery the same way iMessage does: `audio-file` synthesis with MP3 accepted as a voice memo. TTS output format and the default MP3 presentation from the docs stay the same, so no transcoding or new dependency is added. When a send carries `audioAsVoice` and the resolved attachment is audio, the Signal sender adds signal-cli's `voiceNote` JSON-RPC parameter (`--voice-note`, signal-cli 0.14.2+). The flag is forwarded on both Signal send paths: the core outbound adapters (`sendMedia` / `sendFormattedMedia`, used for final and durable replies) and the Signal monitor's own `deliverReplies`, which sends replies produced during an inbound turn, such as TTS tool audio. This takes the capability-driven option ClawSweeper recommended on #166408. Automatic and explicit TTS use native notes, and ordinary media stays attached. ## Evidence **Live on a real Signal account (2026-10-19)**: official `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.10.10-beta.2@sha256:c783708a…84beb` with `@openclaw/signal` packed from this branch at `3cd1ec26` (`scripts/plugin-npm-publish.sh --pack`, tarball sha256 `fa19b085…37575`). Native signal-cli JSON-RPC daemon, OpenRouter TTS (`elevenlabs/eleven-v4`, `responseFormat: mp3`), MP3 output. Same chat, same prompts before and after: | Case | Stock 2026.10.5 | This PR | |---|---|---| | Explicit TTS ("send me a voice message saying …") | `.mp3` file attachment | Native voice note, inline player | | Automatic TTS (`/tts chat on`, then a plain question) | — | Native voice note | | Ordinary audio (generated song via `music_generate`) | — | Normal audio file, unchanged | - **Upgrade from latest stable:** starting from 2026.10.5 with npm `@openclaw/signal` 2026.10.5, then the beta.2 image plus this plugin. The sha256 of the `tts`, `messages.tts`, `plugins` and `channels.signal` config blocks is identical before and after (`968104c2…0cd3cf`). `plugins doctor` shows only the expected local-archive provenance notice. - **Why beta.2 rather than 2026.10.5:** current `main`'s Signal plugin imports five plugin-SDK functions that 2026.10.5 does not export (unrelated to this diff), so a plugin packed from this branch only loads on beta.2. - **What the live test found:** the first live run on `adedb974` still delivered explicit TTS as a file. The agent transcript showed the TTS tool result had `audioAsVoice: true`, but inbound-turn replies go through the monitor's `deliverReplies`, which dropped the flag. `3cd1ec26` fixes that path and adds a regression test; the live table above is from `3cd1ec26`. **Recipient screenshots** (Signal iOS, same chat; an audio *file* shows a file-name header such as `voice---…`, a native voice note does not): | Before: stock 2026.10.5, explicit TTS → file | After: this PR, explicit TTS → voice note | |---|---| | | | | **After: automatic TTS (`/tts chat on`) → voice note** | **After: generated song → file, unchanged** | | | | **Tests and checks** - `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test:extension signal` (Node 24.22.0, macOS arm64): 43 files, 487 tests passed. - New tests: - `send.test.ts`: `voiceNote` set only for audio with `audioAsVoice`. - `outbound.media-limit.test.ts`: `outbound.sendMedia` forwards `audioAsVoice` as `voiceNote`. - `monitor.approval-reply-delivery.test.ts`: `deliverReplies` forwards `audioAsVoice` for reply media, not for text. Each fails without its source change, except the non-audio guard. - `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: format, lint, extension typecheck, plugin boundaries and import cycles pass. The remaining local failures are not from this diff: max-lines on existing `ui/` files, a Knip unused export in `extensions/copilot`, and the SQLite worker ratchet needing `rg`. - Codex autoreview (`--max-priority P2`) on `870f220f`: scoped-clean. - Size: production +16 lines in four Signal plugin files; tests +78; docs +3/-1. No core, schema, config or dependency changes. - Gaps: container transport unchanged (still sends an attachment). Only MP3 verified and advertised. signal-cli older than 0.14.2 is untested. Group chats not tested live. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix(codex): refresh connections after settled local transport failures
prs.body:
Closes #187023

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Codex reusing a failed connection after a managed turn settles with the parent-local inference transport's specific 502 error, without discarding an idle Incognito sibling's only native history.

## User Impact

An eligible ordinary conversation can continue on a fresh connection with its original saved thread and completed tool receipts. Recovery preserves the existing protection for active/protected siblings and idle Incognito conversations: while they own the process, this optional connection refresh is skipped. No automatic tool replay, new retry loop, configuration change, or migration is added. Supervised sessions and client-bound native tool catalogs remain excluded.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retire the exact failed shared client through the existing lifecycle owner only after terminal output reconciliation. An error notification alone is insufficient. Unexpected HTTP relay failures gain bounded stage/cause diagnostics without arbitrary exception text, private routes, or credentials.

The review correctly identified that shared-client leases alone do not preserve idle Incognito history. This revision consults the existing sibling-thread ownership owner before retirement, restoring the intent of #149000: ephemeral history has no disk resume source. The same conservative check protects active siblings and native-child custody. It deliberately favors preserving their ownership over refreshing a shared connection immediately. No new lifecycle manager or retention state is introduced.

This does not fix context-size compaction or background-worker authorization failures. Failed Incognito target cleanup retains its existing behavior; the new guard prevents collateral loss of sibling history.

## Evidence

Head: `1cbb55be1148a8f71fac80502015718a56e10bc5`.

- New regression fails on reviewed head `bb4728855f4c3720ce4d2f6f895c4c504651c2f9` because the shared client closes after the final active lease drains. With the repair, the idle Incognito conversation continues on its original native thread without another thread/start or thread/resume.
- Full run-attempt suite: **122 passed**; shared-client suite: **158 passed**; startup suite: **20 passed**. The existing transport regression still proves terminal ordering, completed tool evidence, replay safety, and subsequent same-thread continuation on a different client when eligible.
- Production and extension-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, one-file MDX validation and git diff checks pass.
- Local autoreview of the staged repair against `bb4728855f` returned **scoped-clean, P0–P2**, with no actionable findings. The preceding full-PR review against `3d96ad74cf7278fa0cb7b25b7c48090f1a75729c` identified only the original index's missing sibling guard; staging the repair resolved it. Reviews are static source evidence, separate from executed tests.
- New regression: **506 ms**. Full run-attempt file: **38.02 s wall**, approximately **28.5 s test time** for 122 existing/new cases; it reuses the suite's real lifecycle/wire fixture and adds no Gateway boot. CI timing for this head is pending.

### Native before/after proof

Ran the shipped Gateway entry point with public `sessions.create`, `chat.send`, `agent.wait`, and `sessions.describe`, actual native Codex **0.164.0**, and a deterministic local HTTPS CONNECT/TLS Responses fixture on macOS arm64 / Node 24.22.1. Build identity and compiled retirement code were checked against old head `bb4728855f` and repaired head `1cbb55be11`. No native client or fetch function was mocked. The fixture rejects external destinations, and no production session, media job, or external model service was used.

B is an Incognito conversation. Its first response contains a synthetic assistant-only marker absent from its later user prompt. B completes and is confirmed idle before ordinary A runs on the same native process. A executes one real native shell tool; after its receipt reaches the provider, the fixture destroys the upstream TCP connection until the exact parent-local relay failure settles. B then receives another message.

| Observation | Previous PR head | Repaired head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| B's process before → after A fails | **42508 → 42756** | **43367 → 43367** |
| B's native thread | **Replaced** | **Unchanged** |
| Earlier assistant-only marker in B's actual next provider request | **Missing** | **Present** |
| Retirement while B holds idle history | Yes; last active lease then closes client | Skipped |
| Real marker-tool executions | 1 | 1 |

This is an actual history-loss negative control, not merely a process-identity assertion. Native process associations were read from native logs; history presence was checked in the serialized provider request rather than inferred from success text.

**Exclusive recovery control on repaired head:** delete only synthetic B through the public session API, then fault A again with its original tool receipt still present. Once no sibling owns the process, A's failure retires it. A's continuation succeeds on **43367 → 43640**, retaining the **same native thread**, with **one tool call, one completed receipt, and one marker-file line** across both failures and continuation. No tool was replayed.

The fixture sets the existing host provider retry budget to zero to isolate one host attempt; native request retries remain enabled. Limits: controlled wire faults and synthetic provider responses, not an external provider outage or semantic model judgment. The earlier active-sibling retirement capture on `bb4728855f` is superseded by this conservative preservation behavior. Current-head CI is running with no failures observed at publication.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation commands</summary>

```sh
pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/shared-client.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm tsgo:extensions
pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.extensions.json extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-state.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.settled-finalization.test-support.ts
node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/plugins/codex-harness.md
git diff --check
```

The unchanged relay diagnostic classification/privacy regression passed on the preceding revision. Broad cross-platform checks are delegated to this head's PR CI.
</details>


## Maintainer original-main runtime reproduction

[Built Gateway + real Codex app-server red/green and ownership controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187375#issuecomment-6508971904), exact head `1cbb55be1148a8f71fac80502015718a56e10bc5`: main twice reuses the failed native client; candidate twice resumes the same saved thread on a fresh client. Idle Incognito and active retained-sibling guards preserve their process/history; first-turn sibling leases drain safely. Personally inspected sibling Codex source is cited in the evidence. Deterministic local TLS provider fixture; no real-provider outage or semantic-model claim. Local tests: 0; both builds and focused Oxfmt/Oxlint passed.

prs.title: fix(logging): mask single-quoted credentials in diagnostic output
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: ordinary credentials remain visible in diagnostic console output and log tails when a diagnostic contains single-quoted fields such as `{'password': 'opaque-value'}`.

## User Impact

User impact: diagnostics now mask single-quoted password, passwd, token, secret, and uppercase environment-style credential fields. Safe neighboring fields such as token_count and password_hint remain readable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing diagnostic redaction patterns to recognize these field spellings. Existing JSON and unquoted masking behavior, raw-file storage, and tool/message content handling are preserved. This remains best-effort diagnostic masking; it does not introduce a Python repr parser.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the real subsystem logger, physical file transport, and configured log-tail reader with isolated logging configuration on Windows / Node 24.22.1. On the unchanged base, console output and the returned tail contained the full synthetic credential values. With this fix, both mask them while preserving token_count, the raw file, and the byte cursor. This exercised the logging owner directly, without a live external service or full Gateway session.
- Five new physical log-tail regression cases failed before the fix and pass afterward. All 91 tests across the five focused logging redaction suites pass, including the unchanged byte-identity and large-text compatibility tests.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, test-line allocation check, and structured local review pass. The changed test file passes all 16 cases in 14.25 seconds of Vitest time; the five-suite run takes 10.16 seconds.

prs.title: fix: omit PR attribution instructions when disabled
prs.body:
Closes #186997

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary conversations receive repeated PR-attribution instructions even when the feature is off or has never been enabled.

## User Impact

Default/off and incognito requests no longer receive an attribution prompt block. Opted-in requesters still receive guidance for new PRs, explicitly limited to their current request.

CLI/shell attribution remains best-effort instruction following, not enforced by a Git wrapper. Upgrading does not rewrite existing conversation history: sessions retaining older, unscoped enabled instructions need a new session to discard that guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Return no attribution instructions when disabled, and omit the label along with the empty content. Enabled guidance explicitly forbids carryover to later requests or other requesters and treats the absence of a current enabled block as no opt-in.

Managed publication keeps its existing preference and revocation checks. Per-PR opt-out, incognito behavior, human credit, work-session links, and the rule against adding or restoring branding on existing PRs are preserved. No new state, configuration, or history-rewriting mechanism is introduced.

## Evidence

- **Shipped-runtime replay at `87a258609a521908ebfa671c52fa883927932745`:** an isolated process launched the built `dist/index.js` Gateway and completed six real agent turns. Real authenticated Alice/Bob profiles and `users.prefs.set/get` exercised default, enabled, disabled, re-enabled, requester-switch and incognito cases. Actual serialized provider requests are included in [openclaw-pr-187805-runtime-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34146965/openclaw-pr-187805-runtime-evidence.zip).
- **Retained-session result:** the first five turns share one session ID. Current attribution-block presence was absent/present/absent/present/absent; all prior input-message objects and earlier carrier text remained unchanged. Bob's current verified requester identity replaced Alice's, without inheriting her enabled block. Earlier enabled guidance remains historical; it was not erased to make the test pass.
- **Incognito result:** Alice's preference remained enabled, but a separate incognito session's provider input contained no attribution label or footer. Default input also contained neither. The standalone artifact verifier passed all 87 assertions; independent review checked decoded requester identities, raw/public captures, hashes and privacy.
- **Proof boundary:** Gateway, agent runtime, storage, authentication and HTTP request serialization were real. The local Responses endpoint returned fixed acknowledgments. This demonstrates prompt delivery and retained-history composition, not live-model compliance, generated PR bodies or native Codex behavior. No PR publishing occurred.
- Before the fix, the prompt regression failed on the unwanted disabled-state block; seven unrelated cases passed.
- Final revision: all 12 prompt-composition tests pass, including enabled, explicitly off, unset, and incognito preferences. The enabled case checks the footer and request-scoping contract.
- Earlier branch validation passed 13 managed-publication tests, 118 media/queue/reset consumer tests, and 14 prompt-prefix stability tests. Their relevant implementation paths are unchanged by the final prompt/test simplification.
- Core typecheck, messaging-test typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, docs lint, diff checks, and the staged test-line ratchet passed. Checks affected by the final revision were rerun.
- Independent native Codex review of the full branch and final revision found no remaining actionable findings.

The earlier composition tests use fixed preference-storage I/O; the new shipped-runtime replay uses real preference storage. `pnpm build:runtime` passed (259.6 seconds). The final six-turn E2E scenario passed in 19.6 seconds test time / 30.68 seconds runner duration; cold E2E prerequisite generation separately took 661.2 seconds. The artifact contains the runner, sanitized provider requests, session/preference receipts, logs, verifier and hashes. A full package/release build and live-model/native Codex replay were not performed. Hosted CI results are not summarized here.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands and test cost</summary>

Final prompt suite:

```sh
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/prompt-prelude.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

12 passed; 128.18 seconds total wall time, including worker compilation. The runner reported 120.83 seconds, with 92% attributed to transformation.

Earlier combined validation:

```sh
pnpm test \
  src/auto-reply/reply/prompt-prelude.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts \
  src/gateway/github-pr-attribution.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

154 passed at that revision; 421.73 seconds total wall time. The modified media/reset consumer file's runner duration was 137.99 seconds within this combined run, not a separately measured command wall time. The final revision replaces the original sequence-style prompt test with four direct composition cases.

CI seconds are unavailable; no hosted CI timing was collected. These are local Linux measurements using the repository's pinned Bun test runtime.

The test allocation is 35 lines, matching the net regression growth against the branch base: 42 added in prompt coverage minus seven removed from existing consumer tests. It covers the previously untested absence of disabled instructions and the opt-in scoping contract; the shared baseline is unchanged.

</details>

prs.title: fix(system-agent): use configured fallbacks when primary admission fails
prs.body:
Closes #151605

## What Problem This Solves

A maintenance conversation can be rejected even when its explicitly configured model fallback works. Reuse that exact successful fallback under the original agent, without substituting a different credential, runtime or plugin owner on later turns or approved writes.

## User Impact and Scope

A failed primary no longer unnecessarily blocks maintenance. Existing requester checks, tool permissions, explicit approval and native writers remain mandatory. Removing the fallback or changing its verified owner refuses reuse and persistence. No schema, migration, permission mechanism, resource-limit change or secret overwrite/delete is introduced.

Revision `82431c3dfdab4ec9687bc0c4204f7aed17060c75` normally merges main `00125bb5bbc0bb8e9fb91ee39e6420132041b90e`, preserving contribution history. The earlier setup/device fixture adjustments are superseded by upstream changes and removed from this contribution; both upstream fixtures pass with the candidate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follow configured fallback order and profile pins, retain the exact successful execution binding, and revalidate it on reuse and at persistent-effect boundaries. Native SQLite secret-commit admission validates the binding again before the existing requester check grants the commit.

The follow-up `3a49804a` centralizes the supported non-observing inference-config snapshot read for commit validation and opaque-runtime re-probes. An observing read could enqueue a health-state write behind the transaction awaiting that validation. This removes the incidental write rather than increasing a timeout or weakening authority checks.

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior addressed

Primary authentication failure uses the configured fallback; two maintenance turns retain their physical history. Native secret/config persistence requires a separate approval. Revoked fallback or credential ownership, including revocation after the initial caller check, must not create a secret or publish its reference. Candidate execution must preserve state created by official 2026.10.8.

### Real setup tested

The compiled CLI, Gateway and SDK at the revision above used isolated synthetic state, the real approval engine, physical history, native secret store/config writers and native audit. A separate official 2026.10.8 installation created the compatibility input. Only external inference responses were substituted. No production credential or production Gateway was used.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

1. Build the candidate runtime and SDK from the exact revision. Start the compiled candidate Gateway, then use SDK `openclaw.chat` with primary HTTP 401 and configured fallback HTTP 200.
2. Complete two turns; read their physical history through `openclaw.chat.history`. Request a config change, verify the secret reference is absent before approval, send a separate approval and read back the native persisted secret/config reference.
3. Stop the candidate Gateway and run `openclaw secrets audit --json`.
4. Independently create conversation history and a separately approved secret reference using official 2026.10.8. Stop it; preserve the same physical state; run the candidate's supported offline migration and start the candidate against that state.
5. Require the current spawned Gateway PID to own its listener and `GET /readyz` to return HTTP 200 with JSON `ready: true`, within 60 seconds, before SDK requests. Process exit fails the gate; a log message or open port alone cannot pass it.
6. Verify old history, the old credential reference and native resolution; repeat fallback conversation and a separately approved config write; stop and audit. Independently verify the disposable container, PID and cgroup are gone.

### Evidence after fix

```text
Exact-source runtime build: PASS; 343.06 seconds.
Compiled candidate CLI: OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (82431c3).
Current compiled-product flow: PASS; 30.37 seconds.
Two retained turns and physical history: PASS.
No new secret reference before separate approval: PASS.
Native secret/config write after separate approval: PASS.
Current audit: 1 reference checked, 0 unresolved.
Official 2026.10.8-created state -> candidate compatibility: PASS; 114.89 seconds.
Stable readiness: 14.821 seconds; candidate readiness: 24.599 seconds.
Same physical state, old history and old credential reference retained: PASS.
Native reference resolution and separately approved config write: PASS.
Stable and candidate compatibility audits: each 1 reference checked, 0 unresolved.
Independent disposable-resource cleanup: PASS.
```

The current-product result predates the readiness-fixture repair and was not rerun under the new gate. The compatibility result uses the repaired formal HTTP readiness gate. Earlier unsuccessful attempts remain failures; this successful rerun is not a controlled proof of their sole cause. Fixture-only tests include rejection of foreign listeners, unready responses, native exit and late HTTP headers/body; 17/17 pass, including two deadline cases that failed on the previous helper.

Source regressions separately reproduced physically persisted secrets after late revocation before the commit-admission fix. After the fix, unchanged authority saves the new secret/reference and revoked authority saves neither. The two final-source fallback suites pass 33 cases, including store-backed CLI credentials and the non-observing-read regression. These source cases supplement, not replace, the compiled-product evidence.

### Observed result after fix

The exact compiled candidate completes the conversation-to-approval-to-write path and continues on state created by official 2026.10.8. Approved unchanged authority writes; revoked authority cannot create the secret or publish its reference. The compatibility experiment is not a production deployment.

### What was not tested

Real-provider traffic, an independently installed candidate release archive and arbitrary third-party callbacks remain unqualified. Only external inference responses were substituted in the compiled-product scenarios. Local results bind the exact revision and integration base named above; they do not claim execution of later upstream commits. Current-head hosted CI and durable technical review must be assessed separately after publication. No security-approval override is requested.

## Source validation and test budget

On the integrated candidate: core types passed; all 29 planned changed-path consumer type graphs passed across two bounded runs (24 then 5, not one completed full invocation). The fallback suites passed 33 cases; upstream setup/device fixtures passed; seven adjacent SQLite/secret-store/config-CLI files passed 138 cases. Typed lint of the 20 changed paths reported zero warnings/errors; formatting, whitespace and native commit hooks passed. Overlapping historical counts are not added.

The canonical main control contains 6,256,302 test lines against its unchanged ceiling of 6,322,996. The candidate contains 6,257,374 lines, an own delta of 1,072, leaving 65,622 lines. No ceiling bump, test removal or resource-cap change is part of this update.

## Review boundary

**Proposed contract:** an explicitly configured fallback may satisfy maintenance inference only as its exact verified binding under the original agent. Requester authority, explicit approval and tool permissions are unchanged.

**Before merge:** assess current-head hosted CI, obtain maintainer review of that binding contract and the normally enforced final-revision security approval. Earlier-head checks/reviews are not a new-head PASS. No merge or deployment is requested.

## Related public context

[PR #156755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156755) addresses implicit Bedrock SDK credential proof, not configured fallback admission. [PR #181669](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181669) preserves explicitly pinned session models for automation events; this proposal does not relax ordinary session pins. The additional setup/boundary/fallback-ladder work inspected during this update does not replace the exact-owner binding and native secret-commit seam covered here.

prs.title: fix(active-memory): detect German recall intent in escalate mode
prs.body:
Closes #151766
Related: #151841

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Active Memory skips deep recall in its default escalate mode when users ask about earlier conversations in German.

## User Impact

German questions such as "Weißt du noch, was wir letzte Woche besprochen haben?", "Was hat Petra gestern gesagt?" or "Wie hieß noch mal der Handwerker?" now trigger recall when the lane-1 lookup has no strong hit. Both "ß" and "ss" spellings are supported ("weisst", "hiess"). Recall stays off for reminders ("Erinnere mich morgen an …"), storing ("Merk dir …"), future questions ("Was machen wir nächste Woche?") and everyday commands. Other languages and configuration defaults are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a German entry to the existing localized `{ intent, future, retrospective }` structure, next to French. A question counts as recall when it has one of these:

- recall phrasing (*weißt du noch*, *erinnerst du dich*, *kannst du dich erinnern*, *wie war/hieß das noch mal*)
- a W-question or verb-first question with *haben/hatten* (or a past-tense modal such as *wollten/sollten*) and a past-time marker or a completed-discussion verb (*besprochen*, *gesagt*, *ausgemacht*, …)

Questions about a third person (*Was hat Petra …*) need both a past marker and a completed verb, so "Was hat der Wetterbericht gesagt?" stays quiet.

On its own, *letzte/letztes* is not a past marker, because German uses it for "final" ("das letzte Wort"). Only *letzte Woche*, *letztes Mal* and similar phrases count.

The imperative *Erinnere mich* is a reminder request, not a question, so it never matches.

#151841 has been open since September. Its four outstanding review findings are reminder commands, future-plan discussions, *ss*/infinitive spellings and umlaut-leading future words. This PR covers all four, with regression cases (see Evidence).

## Evidence

**Unit tests on `893a3de7`:**
- `pnpm test extensions/active-memory/escalation.test.ts`: **213 passed**. 51 of these are new German cases, 27 positives and 24 negatives.
- `pnpm test:extension active-memory`: **311 + 97 passed**.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` were clean on `d6db4f71`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` was clean on `893a3de7`.
- All on Node 24.22.1.

The negatives include:
- the three reminder forms that review flagged on #151841, for example "Erinnere mich morgen an das, was wir gestern besprochen haben"
- "Weißt du noch, ob wir übermorgen Zeit haben?"
- "Weißt du noch mehr darüber?"
- "Der letzte Termin war schön"

**Live Gateway** (OpenClaw 2026.10.5, Debian 13):
- Active Memory `mode: "escalate"`, `promptStyle: "balanced"`.
- The recall model is a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible model.
- Messages go through the OpenResponses endpoint on a group session. That is the path a German home voice assistant uses.
- This PR's German entry as of `d6db4f71` was applied to the installed `dist/escalation-*.mjs` chunk and reverted afterwards.

| Message | Before (2026.10.5) | With this entry |
|---|---|---|
| "Weißt du noch, was wir letzte Woche über die Heizung besprochen haben?" | no recall start (`no-recall-intent`) | recall started, see note below |
| "Wie hieß noch mal der Wasserzähler, über den wir geredet haben?" | not tested | recall started, `done status=ok`, 200-char summary |
| "… Gestern habe ich Pizza gegessen." | no recall start | no recall start |

Note on the first message: the recall sub-agent passed `limit`, an argument `memory_search` does not accept. Recall ended with `status=unavailable reason=search-unavailable`. That failure comes from the recall model's tool call and is independent of the escalation gate. It is already fixed on main by #172630, which is not in a release yet. With that fix applied locally, recall runs finish with `status=ok`.


prs.title: fix(process): Windows claude-cli spawn picks the npm POSIX shim over claude.cmd
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #141382.

On Windows every `claude-cli` turn fails in 2026.9.2. The user sees a request timeout and the gateway logs `write EPIPE`, which is a red herring: it masks an asynchronous `ENOENT` from `spawn()`.

The real cause is PATH probe order. `resolveWindowsExecutableExtensions` returns the bare name before any PATHEXT candidate:

`src/infra/executable-path.ts`

```ts
const extensions = [...resolveWindowsExecutableExtSet(env)];
return includeExtensionless ? ["", ...extensions] : extensions;
```

and `resolveExecutableFromPathEnv` takes the first hit:

```ts
for (const entry of entries) {
  for (const ext of extensions) {
    const candidate = path.join(entry, executable + ext);
    if (isExecutableFile(candidate, { env })) {
      return candidate;
    }
```

A global npm install of `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` writes three files into a directory on PATH: `claude` (a 308 byte `/bin/sh` shim), `claude.cmd`, and `claude.ps1`. The bare shim matches first, and `CreateProcess` cannot execute it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The order is reversed so PATHEXT candidates are probed first and the extensionless entry becomes the last resort. On Windows an extensionless file is not directly executable, so it should never outrank a real `.cmd` or `.exe` of the same name.

Keeping the entry rather than dropping it preserves existing behaviour for callers that pass `includeExtensionless: true` and genuinely have only a bare file present; that case still resolves, it simply no longer wins when a PATHEXT sibling exists. Call sites that already pass `includeExtensionless: false` are untouched.

This is a one line ordering change. Nothing about acceptance, caching, or PATH parsing moves.

## User Impact

Windows installs where the CLI was installed through global npm can spawn it again, which is every `claude-cli` turn on that setup. The issue reports 2026.9.1 was unaffected because launching was delegated to the SDK.

## Evidence

Production change is +4/-1 in one file.

The regression test fails on unfixed code for the right reason. Restoring only `src/infra/executable-path.ts` from main:

```
× prefers a PATHEXT match over an extensionless shim of the same name
  → expected '…/claude' to be '…/claude.cmd'
  Tests  1 failed | 26 passed | 2 skipped (29)
```

It runs on any platform: the suite already has a `withMockedPlatform("win32", …)` helper, and under that mock `isExecutableFile` only checks the file and its extension, so no Windows host is needed.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/executable-path.test.ts        27 passed | 2 skipped
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra src/process src/tui     47 files, 688 passed
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                                clean
./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <both touched files>                         clean
```

One failure in that wider run, `btw-inline-message > sanitizes the question and successful Markdown result on every update`, reproduces identically with this file restored from main, so it is pre-existing and unrelated.

The existing `keeps extensionless lookup explicit with PATHEXT` cases still pass unchanged. They cover a bare file with no sibling, which this ordering does not affect; the new case is the ambiguous one they did not cover.

Proof gap worth stating: I have no Windows host, so this is verified through the mocked-platform path rather than by spawning the real CLI on Windows. The mock covers the resolver decision that the issue identifies, not the downstream `CreateProcess` behaviour.

AI-assisted: yes. I traced the source path by hand and ran every command above myself.

Secretless Node24.22.1 Docker, explicit isolated profiles/config/state/SQLite paths. No mocked directory responses, private helper imports, real personal account or UI claim.
- ASCII and same-form NFC/NFD controls pass on both refs.
- Actual alias GET URLs preserve their mixed case and NFD/NFC percent encoding on both refs. Actual peer POST `search_term` fields preserve exact raw casing/composition; evidence includes UTF-8 hex identities.
- All22 lookup CLI processes exited0; Synapse gracefully stopped with exit0.
- Focused regressions: **8 passed**. The retained bidirectional table fails on main in both forms. Consolidation replaces duplicated mock fixtures and the weaker mocked alias happy-path check with real Synapse alias controls; tests **+9/-11 (net−2)**.

Final head `8003b993e3f45ce9ef6cec1c0a9a1a2e6b7009a9` changes only tests after the proven contributor build; production remains **+3/-2**, unchanged. Contributor commit retained. No storage, schema, dependency, permission or SDK changes.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous local matching behavior; no data is rewritten or migrated. Blast radius is the Matrix joined-room name filter only. Direct alias lookup and delegated peer search retain their existing wire contracts, covered by real homeserver controls.

prs.title: feat(openai): support saved GPT-Live voices
prs.body:
Closes #175909

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw cannot select an existing prompt-created GPT-Live voice. OpenAI requires saved voices as `{ "id": "voice_..." }`, but Talk and Discord flatten `speakerVoiceId` into the same plain string `voice` field as named voices, so a saved ID reached the named-voice allowlist and silently fell back to `marin`.

## User Impact

Operators can select a saved voice with `gpt-live-1` through `talk.realtime.speakerVoiceId`, `channels.discord.voice.realtime.speakerVoiceId`, or `speakerVoiceId` in an OpenAI realtime provider block. Named voices keep their existing behavior and defaults. Saved voices on other models, and malformed IDs, fail session setup with a message that does not echo the configured value. Browser WebRTC reservations omit the ID.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenAI provider owns its voice identifiers, so the translation stays inside the plugin and needs no core or SDK change:

- `readOpenAIQuicksilverVoiceSetting` recognizes OpenAI's `voice_` prefix (case-insensitively) in the shared string and keeps the ID's case. Config reads never throw, so Talk catalogs and readiness checks are unaffected by a typo.
- `normalizeOpenAIQuicksilverVoiceInput` validates the ID when a bridge or browser session is created; `assertOpenAIGptLiveCustomVoiceModel` rejects saved voices for models other than `gpt-live-1`, including request-level overrides.
- Whitespace-only named voices normalize to unset again (the earlier head threw for them).

Behavior notes compared with main: a blank `speakerVoice` now falls through to `speakerVoiceId`/`voice` instead of masking them, and `speakerVoiceId` in a provider block is read the same way Talk already reads it. Docs: `docs/providers/openai/voice-and-speech.md`.

## Evidence

Local, Node 24.21.0, repo Vitest wrapper (pinned Bun test runtime), on `c5cc8a53` (merged with main `b1b3f500`):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` over the 7 touched OpenAI realtime test files: 105/105 passed.
- New caller-path tests: Talk's request-level `voice` and the provider block reach the broker as `{ id }`; Discord's override shape through the real `resolveConfiguredRealtimeVoiceProviderAsync` reaches `session.start` as `audio.output.voice = { id }`; GA and Codex models reject saved voices before session creation or socket open; malformed and mistyped-prefix IDs fail with the exact non-echoing message; blank `speakerVoice` stays unset.
- Fail-first: with the previous head's source and the new tests, the Talk, Discord and blank-voice cases fail (fallback to `marin`, missing `{ id }`, and a thrown custom-voice error respectively).
- `tsgo` for extensions and extension tests: passed. `oxlint` on the 12 changed files: passed. `oxfmt --check`: passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: all guards passed except two whole-tree checks that also fail on main: the max-lines suppression ratchet (three `ui/` files identical to main) and the Knip dead-export scan (99 entries in 32 files identical to main). The one entry from this PR (`OpenAIGptLiveVoice`) is fixed.
- `realtime-quicksilver-peer-worker.test.ts`: 3/3 local passes. The CI failure on `3a66dc68` (zero RTP packets in 10s) did not reproduce, the same test passed on `ae85e78d`, and this PR does not touch that media code.
- The session-lifecycle test change from the previous head was dropped in favor of main's deterministic fix for the same race.

Not proven: no live provider call was made. An end-to-end OpenClaw audio session with a real saved voice remains unverified; the earlier direct-provider check bypassed OpenClaw's configuration flow.

Known limitation: core's Talk gateway-relay presentation echoes the configured `speakerVoiceId` string to the operator's client, as it already does for every provider's voice ID. Hiding it there needs a core change outside this plugin.

## References and documentation

- [OpenAI custom voices guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/custom-voices): saved voices use `session.audio.output.voice.id`; prompt-generated voices work with GPT-Live only.
- [OpenClaw OpenAI voice and speech documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/openai/voice-and-speech.md).
- Related: [PR #174084](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174084) expands named Codex voices.
