prs.title: fix(doctor): an unrelated older Gateway service blocks migrating an isolated state
prs.body:
Closes #187878

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor --fix` refuses a forward schema migration for an isolated state (selected with `OPENCLAW_HOME` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_PROFILE`) when an unrelated, older Gateway service is installed under the same OS account, even though that service never uses the isolated database.

## User Impact

User impact: Doctor and other CLI commands can migrate an isolated state again while an older default Gateway service is installed. An older service that really uses the same database still blocks the forward migration, and a verified live Gateway process (the Linux self-service path) keeps using its own environment as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installed-service inspection resolved the service's database path from `{ ...cliEnv, ...service.environment }`. A service definition that omits a state selector therefore inherited the CLI's isolated value, so the older service was reported as the owner of the CLI's database and the migration guard (correctly, given that input) refused. For another installed service, the CLI's `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_PROFILE` are now dropped. The service's environment is then rebuilt through the existing `mergeGatewayServiceEnv`, which normalizes saved Windows keys such as `openclaw_state_dir` and applies a Windows argv profile, and a `--profile` on the service's command line is applied on the other platforms too. The service's database therefore comes from its own selectors, its own argv profile and the normal home fallback, which matches how `inspectInstalledGatewayStatePaths` already treats CLI overrides. When this process is the proven live service, its environment is the service's environment, so that path is unchanged. The migration guard itself is not relaxed.

## Evidence

- Regression test: `src/cli/worker-policy-regression-service-installation.test.ts` › "resolves an installed service's database without the CLI's state selectors". The CLI runs with isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_PROFILE`; the older service records only `HOME`.
  - On `main`: `"databasePath": "/isolated/state/state/openclaw.sqlite"` (the CLI's isolated database) instead of `/home/example/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite`.
  - With the fix: the service's own database.
- Same-database protection: "resolves an installed service's database from its own argv profile" (a service started with `--profile service` and only `HOME` recorded) and "reads a Windows service's saved selectors case-insensitively" (a task that saved a lowercase `openclaw_state_dir`). Both fail on the first revision of this PR and pass now.
- The existing "preserves protection for a genuinely older own effective package" test now also asserts that the live service keeps its own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; it passes on `main` and with the fix. The test file no longer mocks `resolveOpenClawStateSqlitePath`, so it checks the real resolver.
- `pnpm test src/cli/worker-policy-regression-service-installation.test.ts src/cli/run-main`: 7 files, 168 tests pass.
- Local checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, the core test typecheck shards for these paths, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files are clean; the test-lines, line-cap and mock-factory ratchets pass.
- Gap: no live Doctor run against a real older installed service. That would need installing and changing a Gateway service on the host, which I did not do.

prs.title: fix: keep unrelated services from blocking isolated Doctor migrations
prs.body:
Closes #187878.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can refuse a forward migration of an isolated state directory because an unrelated older Gateway service is installed under the same OS account. The service inspection combines the CLI environment with the installed service environment; when the service omits state selectors, it inherits the CLI's paths and is incorrectly reported as using the isolated database.

The failure was observed with a 2026.10.9 CLI and a separate 2026.7.1-2 LaunchAgent. The normal Doctor command exited before migration even though the older service did not select the target state.

## User Impact

A CLI using a separate state directory can migrate that state without being blocked by an unrelated older installation. The existing version fence still refuses forward migration when the installed service actually uses the same database, including a profile selected in the service command line.

The change neither updates nor restarts the installed service, and introduces no configuration option, schema change, or migration bypass. A Linux Gateway positively identified as its own installed service retains its live process state identity.

## Why This Change Was Made

The correction belongs to the producer of the installation facts. For a separate service, inspection clears the CLI's state selectors before applying the installed service's environment through the existing platform-aware merge. Windows saved environment keys keep their case-insensitive semantics. It then uses the existing service entrypoint and CLI profile parsers to honor root profile arguments. The state-path resolver and downstream migration guard retain their existing responsibilities.

The new regression follows the actual service-file, package-version, state-path and migration-guard path. Existing Linux self-service coverage now uses the real state resolver instead of replacing its answer with a constant. The test-line allocation covers this previously missing boundary proof.

## Evidence

The original native macOS Doctor command failed on 620e1fb because the service inspection paired an unrelated older installation with the isolated CLI database. The regression reproduces that path on the base; the explicit shared-state refusal control remains enforced.

Native macOS acceptance then passed on 193be43: the same normal Doctor command exited successfully, migrating retained isolated state from shared schema 34 to 36 and agent schema 37 to 38. The existing OCM launcher started a healthy Gateway and ready UI, and the existing guest browser connected with its retained identity and read-only Home. The old global service definition, command and package fingerprints, and global database identity metadata matched before and after. Protected configuration, profile/identity/project/projection original-column digests, and workspace file/HEAD/status fingerprints also matched.

That native run used the first patch commit. The final e1e01d18 correction preserves state resolution for the tested macOS service, whose saved environment contains HOME and no state/profile selectors or profile arguments; it adds the existing Windows key-normalization path. The native result is retained with its actual build identity. Session/input/event preservation checks are count based, and startup appended events; full conversation-content byte parity is not claimed.

On the final head, changed-file formatting and lint, all selected production/test type groups, and all 40 focused tests passed. These include environment and command-line shared-state controls, lowercase Windows saved selectors, and positively verified Linux self-service selection. A direct task-script reader/inspection/guard probe also confirms that both Windows key spellings resolve the shared database and refuse migration. That probe uses Windows platform selection on Linux; it does not claim native Task Scheduler lifecycle proof.

The final focused test batch took 44.16 seconds wall time. The earlier single-worker two-file measurement took 76.68 seconds, including 61.23 seconds of shared native transform preparation; its original five new cases totaled 231 ms. The exact-head hosted CI and required aggregate gate passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40952338348.

prs.title: fix(update): enable process-tree termination and signal forwarding in runUpdateStep
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a CLI-driven update step (`runUpdateStep` in `src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:218`) spawns a package-manager child tree (such as `npm i -g --prefix <stage-dir> openclaw@<version>`) that hangs in `ep_poll` and ignores `SIGTERM`, timeout or operator cancellation previously did not enable `killProcessTree: true` and `runStep` (`src/infra/update-runner-command.ts:65`) did not forward `signal?: AbortSignal` to the underlying command runner. Unlike `buildUpdateCommandRunner` (`src/infra/update-runner-command.ts:223`), which already sets `killProcessTree: true`, `runUpdateStep` dropped explicit `AbortSignal` cancellation and left `SIGTERM`-ignoring child and descendant processes alive instead of escalating through `createCommandTerminationController` (`src/process/exec-termination.ts:22`) to force-kill the process group and wait for descendant settlement.

### Root Cause & Architectural Fix

- **Architectural owner**: `src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts` (`runUpdateStep`), `src/infra/update-runner-command.ts` (`runStep`), and `src/infra/update-runner-types.ts` (`RunStepOptions`).
- **Canonical fix**:
  - Enable `killProcessTree: true` in `runUpdateStep`'s default runner (`src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:230`) while preserving caller-supplied `runCommand` overrides.
  - Add `signal?: AbortSignal` to `RunStepOptions` (`src/infra/update-runner-types.ts:98`), forward `signal` in `runStep` (`src/infra/update-runner-command.ts:96`), and derive `runUpdateStep`'s parameter type directly from `Parameters<typeof runStep>[0]` (`src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:219`) so `runUpdateStep` forwards `signal` and stays in sync with `RunStepOptions`.
  - Removed all unrelated layout/expression changes so 100% of touched production lines are inside `runUpdateStep`, `runStep`, and `RunStepOptions`.
- **Production LOC delta**: Net `-1` line across 3 production files (`+11 / -12`), plus `+69` test lines in `src/cli/update-cli/shared.command-runner.test.ts`.

## Evidence

### 1. Shipped CLI Update Flow: Timeout / Cancellation Stopping a `SIGTERM`-Ignoring Tree Before Recovery + Latest-Stable Upgrade Preserving Settings & Data

I executed the CLI package-update entrypoint (`runPackageInstallUpdate` in `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-package.ts:484`) against a global npm prefix initialized at `openclaw@2026.10.5` with `openclaw.json` (`gateway.port: 18789`, `agents.defaults.model.primary: "openai/gpt-5.4"`) and `state/openclaw.sqlite` (`kv` row `operator-setting = preserved-across-upgrade`):

1. **CLI timeout/cancellation on a `SIGTERM`-ignoring `npm` + worker descendant tree**: During `package-install`, the `npm` process and its spawned worker both ignore `SIGTERM` and hang. Under the CLI timeout, `runUpdateStep` force-terminates the entire process tree (`npmPidExitedBeforeRecovery: true`, `workerPidExitedBeforeRecovery: true`), discards the staging directory, and verifies recovery of the existing `2026.10.5` installation (`recovery: { serviceRestartSafe: true, version: "2026.10.5" }`).
2. **Transient hang auto-recovery (`package-install` hangs -> killed -> fallback `package-install-omit-optional` succeeds)**: When only the first `npm i` hangs, the timeout kills the hung `SIGTERM`-ignoring tree and the fallback install completes `2026.10.5 -> 2026.10.10` (`status: "ok"`).
3. **Latest-stable upgrade (`2026.10.5 -> 2026.10.10`) with settings and data intact**: Upgrading to `2026.10.10` completes with `status: "ok"`, updates `package.json` to `2026.10.10`, and preserves both `openclaw.json` (`configIntact: true`) and `state/openclaw.sqlite` (`sqliteDataIntact: [{ key: "operator-setting", value: "preserved-across-upgrade" }]`).

```text
=== 1. CLI Timeout / Cancellation on SIGTERM-Ignoring npm Tree ===
{
  "status": "error",
  "reason": "global-install-failed",
  "failedStep": {
    "name": "package-install-omit-optional",
    "termination": "timeout",
    "exitCode": 1
  },
  "npmPidExitedBeforeRecovery": true,
  "workerPidExitedBeforeRecovery": true,
  "recovery": {
    "serviceRestartSafe": true,
    "version": "2026.10.5"
  }
}
=== 2. Latest-Stable Upgrade Preserving Settings and Data ===
{
  "status": "ok",
  "mode": "npm",
  "beforeVersion": "2026.10.5",
  "afterVersion": "2026.10.10",
  "installedPackageJsonVersion": "2026.10.10",
  "configIntact": true,
  "sqliteDataIntact": [
    {
      "key": "operator-setting",
      "value": "preserved-across-upgrade"
    }
  ]
}
```

### 2. Red / Green Real-Process Regression Proof (Failing on Base `d4b913d4689`, Passing on PR)

Running `src/cli/update-cli/shared.command-runner.test.ts` (`terminates SIGTERM-ignoring child and descendant processes when runUpdateStep is aborted`) against base `src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts` and `src/infra/update-runner-command.ts` (`d4b913d4689`) fails because `runStep` drops `signal` (so `controller.abort()` is ignored until the step timeout fires):

```text
# Base (d4b913d4689) — RED (exit code 1)
 FAIL  cli  src/cli/update-cli/shared.command-runner.test.ts > update CLI shared helpers > terminates SIGTERM-ignoring child and descendant processes when runUpdateStep is aborted
```

prs.title: fix: retain Codex terminal errors after stderr warnings
prs.body:
Fixes #187863.

## What Problem This Solves

When a Codex app-server exits after emitting warning noise, OpenClaw can discard the terminal cause from its stderr diagnostic. The process exit still reaches the caller, but the preview can show only warnings, making the failure harder to diagnose.

## User Impact

Exit errors and startup diagnostics retain the end of stderr, where a terminal cause can follow earlier warnings. The existing 500 UTF-16-unit preview bound, overflow marker, 2,000-unit retained buffer, and credential redaction remain in place. Short diagnostics are unchanged. This improves diagnostic content without changing active-turn uncertainty, replay safety, or recovery decisions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The client already retains a bounded stderr tail, but the shared preview helper then selected its first 500 units. Selecting the end of the compacted, redacted buffer fixes both existing consumers at their common owner. The existing Unicode-safe slicer prevents a truncated preview from beginning with half a surrogate pair.

The existing client exit table now covers a terminal cause after warnings and a surrogate pair at the preview boundary. Its credential case crosses the preview limit to protect redaction before slicing, and the same table checks the direct diagnostic accessor. The five-line allocation records this focused extension of existing coverage.

## Evidence

On unchanged production at 620e1fb31537ea6a3df583f08173e66607fdd2e5, the client request/stderr/exit reproduction failed because the rejection contained only warnings and omitted the terminal marker; 24 existing cases passed. The fixture supplies child-process I/O while exercising the production client, stderr decoding, retained buffer, exit handler, and request rejection.

The corrected tree passed formatting/lint, all selected production and test type groups, and 206 tests across the client, private-transport, startup, shared-client, and compaction-closeout suites. The active-turn control retains its generic uncertainty message and non-replayable observed work.

`pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/client.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 25 cases in 62.05 seconds of runner wall time (58.82-second test-process duration, dominated by transformation/import; the changed regression took 5 ms). The published-head CI run also passed all selected jobs; per-file CI timing is not separately available. A separate local autoreview of the complete candidate against 620e1fb31537ea6a3df583f08173e66607fdd2e5 completed clean at its P0 scope. Full independent engineering review is clean, and hosted CI is green on the published head.

A separate shipped-CLI comparison now exercises `pnpm openclaw agent exec` with isolated configuration, state, and workspace. The configured app-server command starts a real Node child which waits for the CLI's `initialize` request, emits 100 harmless warning lines followed by a distinct terminal cause and a synthetic credential, then exits 23. The CLI, plugin loader, stdio transport, diagnostic formatter, and JSON error projection are production paths; only the external failing executable is a fixture.

The same scenario ran on unchanged production from target 1a472d79b2b530a0c9328f2a40277f10ae7cb0d7 and the exact published content tree df0f02e8ecd0c0855aec0f2faab0380654e87304. The runtime build metadata and clean remote Git tree were checked after execution.

| Observation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Child received `initialize` | Yes | Yes |
| Native exit diagnostic | Code 23 | Code 23 |
| CLI exit status | 1 | 1 |
| Terminal cause in CLI JSON error | Missing | Retained |
| Raw synthetic credential in CLI output | Absent | Absent; replaced by `<redacted>` |

The command used `agent exec --isolated --config-override <fixture config> --state-dir <owned directory> --cwd <empty workspace> --model openai/gpt-5.4 --timeout 30 --json`. Its environment contained only standard runner variables, isolated OpenClaw/Codex state paths, and a synthetic API key. The child failed during initialization, before authentication application or inference. Both runs also reported the existing pre-turn cleanup uncertainty warning; this change preserves that behavior and the error exit.

This proof establishes diagnostic loss and its correction through the shipped CLI. It does not identify a native crash cause, certify live guest deployment, or claim changed recovery behavior.

prs.title: fix: prevent shared-state hangs after service installation drift
prs.body:
Related: #186971

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes shared-state worker admission hanging when service-installation policy is copied or changes while an existing actor is retained. On Linux, a running system Gateway could also select an unrelated stale user-service installation and apply the wrong older-installation policy during startup.

## User Impact

Gateway startup and shared-state operations can reuse equivalent installation facts without waiting on their own retained actor. A Gateway identifies its own loaded service rather than preferring a stale definition in another manager. There is no schema or configuration migration, and the newer-CLI/older-service migration guard remains intact.

An actually incompatible policy still fails explicitly. This does not repair general detached-context propagation, nor does it by itself recover a previously failed deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Compare installation policy by value, matching the broker’s existing compatibility contract.
- Refuse incompatible admission while an actor is active or retiring, rather than waiting on the caller’s retained scope. Quiescent actors may still retire normally.
- Prefer an own-service command only after native loaded runtime, MainPID, scope, unit and cgroup agree. The narrow observation does not read EnvironmentFile secrets or query enablement. Unproven self-identity and non-Linux/ordinary CLI paths keep existing discovery.

## Evidence

- Test-only CI correction `9dacb83f40a81290f897a9ca188df4195ab2f1fd` (published head `c99a075a0e9aa13d92e4abc34065bde436a0ebfc`): **28 focused regression tests**, both affected test-type graphs, focused lint, formatting and the mock-export ratchet pass. Nineteen mock factories preserve real exports; two retain documented isolation contracts. Assertions and both production files are unchanged. Fresh independent review found no P0/P1/P2 issues. Current-head CI is separate from these local checks.
- Initial commit `7bd217f729de48500b1ca714bc0fdb5b4c780bfe`, based on `6d9dae85e408556a5e32217216928b4c6568c54c`: all **28 focused regression tests** pass through the official native test-projects wrapper; core typecheck, **29 selected test-type graphs**, focused lint and formatting pass.
- On incident source base `bbde2b822c133f615d83a9f1db109960c4d68f9e` with the initial four-file snapshot: **468 tests across 30 files** pass, plus core/test types, runtime build, and isolated built CLI version/help smoke. Both changed production files and the broker/direct-dependency comparison are unchanged between those bases; the earlier build is not represented as a current-main build or a rerun of the later test-only correction.
- An exact-source lifecycle harness using the real lease/client/async-context code reproduces the original clone deadlock and passes with the repair. External broker/database I/O is mocked there; native broker/SQLite suites were tested separately.
- Independent read-only review of final-v3 and its exact current-main integration found no P0/P1/P2 issues. The author simplification pass retained only the two owner fixes and their regressions (+92/-3 production lines; +395 test lines including the CI correction). This is a narrative independent review, not a helper-attested ClawSweeper result. Local ClawSweeper and Codex CLI are unavailable on this host.

Limitations: macOS/Windows fallback cases are simulated under Linux; the narrow service tests mock native facts. Production recovery and a real-systemd cutover have not been validated or performed. Earlier fixture/setup failures were corrected and retained separately, not counted as passing product checks.

## Worked on by

- @jalehman
- @fuller-stack-dev
- @vincentkoc

prs.title: fix: resume interrupted sessions after upgrading restart recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes interrupted sessions staying idle after the first upgrade from legacy main-session recovery to the graceful-restart redesign in #185730, while preventing historical recovery markers from waking abandoned or completed sessions.

## User Impact

A legacy cycle receives one ordinary resume input only when its entry is aborted, has status `interrupted`, and was updated within the six hours before the Gateway process started. Stale, future-dated, settled, tombstoned, `done`, and `killed` entries stay idle. Current session authority and execution-owner checks remain enforced.

Accepted edge: an installation stopped for longer than six hours before upgrading loses this one-time resume. Send a new message to continue that conversation. Modern graceful-shutdown markers retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old shutdown writes `status: "interrupted"` and bumps the entry's own `updatedAt`; cycle counters do not establish freshness. The canonical normalizer now keeps only an unsettled legacy cycle ID, discarding execution snapshots. The startup resume owner compares the entry timestamp against process start and consumes both accepted and rejected candidates before any admission. It uses the existing single resume input and current-authority path. The old persisted `running`/`queued` statuses still require their existing Doctor migration; this bridge does not broaden that contract.

Compatibility contract: persisted session data from the previous stable Gateway's pre-upgrade stop. Remove the temporary cycle retention and startup adoption once the stable channel includes the graceful-restart redesign from #185730. The removal condition is recorded in source comments. No old execution, queued inference, or saved authority is restored.

The whole change adds 35 production lines, zero net test lines, and 10 documentation lines. Existing fixture guards use Node assertions, and duplicate fixture/cancellation checks were removed while retaining behavioral checks. No schema, configuration, dependency, version, budget, or baseline changes.

## Evidence

- Red on original base `5ed97e5013787ed69be30c537c44e072188dfe35`: the startup regression expected one legacy resume input and received none (4 passed, 1 failed).
- Red on the earlier broad bridge `c1472dd7cc801eb3011bd00087487fbc478d6bde`: `nice -n 5 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-restart-resume.test.ts --maxWorkers=8` — 4 passed, 1 failed; it incorrectly resumed stale, done, killed, and future-dated entries alongside the recent interrupted entry.
- Exact-head `6dc2ff7198392f684d50af2cc2e2c7497ccd2f22` startup and canonical-entry suites: `nice -n 5 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-restart-resume.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-entry-json.test.ts --maxWorkers=8` — 15 passed. The regression checks two startup passes, all rejected cases, persisted candidate removal, and inert crash inputs. Canonical-entry coverage checks private projection, discarded snapshots, and generation/archive clearing.
- Plugin reservation contract: `nice -n 5 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/contracts/session-entry-projection.contract.test.ts --maxWorkers=8 -t 'rejects sessionEntrySlotKey values that collide'` — 1 passed, 12 unselected.
- Targeted lint, core and Gateway/config-test typechecks, format, `git diff --check`, test-line ratchet, and max-lines ratchet — passed. The exhaustive plugin reservation typecheck initially rejected the temporary field until its existing reservation moved into the typed core-key list; no casts or suppressions were added.
- Local Codex autoreview of the final staged range from `5ed97e5013787ed69be30c537c44e072188dfe35` to this change — scoped clean at P0/P1. Coordinator review and landing remain separate.

Proof uses synthetic legacy SQLite rows through the production startup, authority, and persistence path, capturing the session-event enqueue boundary. No released-binary upgrade or live-model execution was run. Startup remains best effort: process death or failed admission after consumption can require fresh user input. The age/status check is a bounded heuristic because the legacy marker has no stop timestamp; an interrupted historical cycle independently updated within that same six-hour window can still qualify.

prs.title: fix(slack): avoid duplicate approval prompts after lost responses
prs.body:
Related: #138221

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes possible duplicate native approval prompts in ordinary Slack workspaces when a message POST reaches Slack but its response is lost.

## User Impact

Approval delivery propagates an uncertain-send error instead of automatically replaying a potentially accepted write. Acknowledged sends and explicit HTTP 429 recovery keep working. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approval adapter passed Bolt's retrying listener client into the sender, overriding its existing write-client selection. Removing that override lets the sender own write retries. Qualified workspace and Enterprise targets retain their validated event scope and dedicated writer; reads and approval updates keep their existing clients.

This closes the workspace-native approval gap explicitly left in #138221 without adding another client cache or retry policy.

## Evidence

The regression uses the real approval presentation/transport adapter, sender and installed Slack SDK against a local HTTP receiver. After fully reading each POST, the receiver drops the response.

| Scenario | Base | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ordinary workspace, lost response | 3 POSTs; assertion fails | 1 POST; original request error propagates |
| Qualified workspace, lost response | 1 POST | 1 POST |
| Ordinary workspace, acknowledged response | Correct receipt | Correct receipt |

On Windows with Node 24.22.1 and Slack SDK 8.2.0, all 35 tests across the four approval/client suites pass, including existing explicit-429 and listener-read retry controls. Vitest wall time: 18.96s; wrapper: 22.36s. The new scenarios took 24ms, 5ms and 12ms. Hosted CI timings are pending.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/client.web-api.test.ts extensions/slack/src/approval-handler.runtime.test.ts extensions/slack/src/approval-handler.enterprise.test.ts extensions/slack/src/client.rate-limit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Fresh structured Codex AutoReview: `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`. Targeted TypeScript checking and type-aware Oxlint pass, as do formatting, diff whitespace and the test-line ratchet.

Production delta: -1 line. Test delta: +72/-3 (net +69), with an exact separate allocation for the real HTTP regression and success/scope controls; the shared baseline is unchanged.

This proves the approval adapter-to-HTTP boundary, not full Gateway ingress, live Slack delivery, rendered duplicate cards or human approval clicks.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes negative or inflated channel-probe durations when wall time changes during a probe.

## User Impact

Shared probe-duration reporting follows elapsed time when the clock moves forward or backward. The existing public start timestamp and explicitly supplied durations keep their contracts. No configuration or migration is required.

Measure the shared helper's elapsed duration with a monotonic clock while keeping its epoch start timestamp for existing callers.

prs.title: fix: clear Knowledge readiness export finding
prs.body:
Fixes #187887

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Knowledge readiness finding in production dependency validation. `pluginReadiness` is called locally by the live source-detection path, but its export exists only for tests that bypass that path.

## User Impact

Scribe readiness behavior stays unchanged. Missing, disabled and sign-in-required plugins retain their existing states, while unavailable or unauthorized reads remain unknown and do not block starting. Public plugin interfaces, permissions and configuration are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The helper now stays private to `scribes-state.ts`. Its two existing readiness cases exercise `detectSources` with method-specific Gateway replies and verify the Granola inspection request. Their six result assertions now observe the returned readiness map, including omission after an unauthorized read.

The fixture needs 11 additional test lines to exercise that boundary; one exact allocation accounts for them. No test case, readiness branch, view control or scanner rule is removed or relaxed.

## Evidence

- [Scheduled dependency validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40931480407/job/123651386206) reports the production export on the unchanged base. All three maintained scanner commands were run on the candidate: only this production finding disappears. The other two production and two full-tree findings remain; dependency/export aggregates still exit 1 for those unchanged findings. Script exports and both unused-file scans are empty.
- Changed-file formatting/lint, i18n validation, native-selected production/test types and the canonical test-line ratchet pass. The committed tree exactly matches the remotely tested tree.
- Complete `scribes-state.test.ts` and `scribes-view.test.ts` pass all 36 existing cases with no skips. They preserve the six readiness outcomes, conversation/memory/error detection, and the existing setup, dialog, prompt, lifecycle and write-access controls. The two-file batch took 5.89 seconds wall time; Vitest reported 4.29 seconds. No cases or timing waits were added.
- This proves the existing detection and view boundaries with fixed Gateway replies; live Granola authentication and model ingestion are outside this change. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40950640410) covers the broader repository checks.

prs.title: feat(diagnostics-otel): export cache-write TTL buckets on generic usage keys
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Backends that price `gen_ai.usage.*` usage types cannot price Anthropic's separately-reported cache-write TTL buckets: #171663 exported `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` / `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` only on the OpenClaw-specific vocabulary (`openclaw.model_call.usage.*`), where generic usage-type consumers never see them. That is already breaking live pricing, not just a missing feature: Langfuse's own default Claude pricing ships a distinct `input_cache_creation_1h` rate (`$4.00` per MTok vs `$2.50` for 5m/combined on `claude-sonnet-5`), and any deployment using 1-hour prompt caching today has those writes priced at the combined rate — a 37.5% undercount on the 1h tokens — because the reported bucket never reaches the pricing rows.

## User Impact

`model.call` spans now also carry `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.5m_input_tokens` / `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.1h_input_tokens`, exported verbatim when the provider reports them (explicit zero included) and absent otherwise. The keys sit in the standard's own cache-write sub-namespace (`gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.*`), in the same dotted breakdown shape Langfuse natively maps ([#19420](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/19420), merged 2026-10-28, first release after v4.71.0): current Langfuse normalizes them to its `input_cache_creation_5m`/`_1h` usage types — the exact rows its Claude default prices define — prices each bucket at its own rate, and rebalances the combined key to its unattributed remainder, so each write prices exactly once regardless of the backend price table. On earlier deployments the breakdown keys land as unpriced pass-through buckets (the split is visible in dashboards) and the combined total prices exactly once, unchanged from today. No producer-side configuration is needed either way.

## Why This Change Was Made

`gen_ai.*` is the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic-conventions namespace ([open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai); registry: [docs/registry/attributes/gen-ai.md](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/registry/attributes/gen-ai.md), all attributes Development status). The standard defines cache counters as subsets of one authoritative prompt total — `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` "SHOULD include all types of input tokens, including cached tokens", `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens` "SHOULD be included in" it — but no TTL attributes (the 5m/1h split is Anthropic-specific). These two keys extend the standard's cache-write sub-namespace with the provider-reported breakdown, in the same nested shape the standard already uses.

#171663's review kept the TTL split OpenClaw-specific so generic consumers could not price a total and its breakdown together. Since then the major generic consumer fixed that exact concern natively: Langfuse #19420 rebalances dotted `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.*_input_tokens` breakdown keys, normalizing them to the priced usage types its Claude default prices define. Emitting the breakdown in that shape means the decomposition is enforced by the consumer's own mapping (older consumers see unpriced extra buckets, never additive prices) rather than depending on producers to omit provider-reported facts. Draft status is intentional pending maintainer direction on that reversal.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof, current head `61f09a29e64`** (rebased onto upstream/main `4fc73d6995b`; built CLI) against a self-hosted Langfuse v4 deployment running past [#19420](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/19420) (worker bundle verified to contain the rebalance code; containers recreated 2026-10-29). One real non-streaming Anthropic Messages call, provider-reported counts verbatim, secrets/hosts redacted. The span: `openclaw.model.call` GENERATION, model `claude-sonnet-5-5`, 2026-10-29 14:04:00 UTC, trace `1d75af08dc8b5968b8b35002a2119d6b`, span `ca9195870b43044b`.

<details>
<summary>Dotted breakdown on a both-conventions price table: combined auto-zeroed, write priced exactly once</summary>

Provider reported a 9,170-token cache write (all 5m, `ephemeral_1h = 0` explicitly) plus a 36,162-token cache read. The deployment's price table for the model carries **both** conventions (combined `input_cache_creation` $2.50 + `input_cache_creation_5m` $2.50 + `input_cache_creation_1h` $4.00 per MTok) — the configuration that double-prices a total-plus-breakdown emission.

As ingested (`usage_details` → `cost_details`):

| token class | usage tokens | rate $/MTok | charged |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| input | 223 | 2.00 | 0.000446 |
| output | 1,135 | 10.00 | 0.011350 |
| cache read | 36,162 | 0.10 | 0.0036162 |
| cache write, combined | 36,162 → **0** (rebalanced remainder) | 2.50 | **$0** |
| cache write, 5m | 9,170 | 2.50 | 0.022925 |
| cache write, 1h | 0 | 4.00 | 0 |
| **span total** | | | **$0.0383372** |

The breakdown was normalized to `input_cache_creation_5m: 9170` / `_1h: 0` (priced against the TTL rows), and the combined key was rebalanced to its **unattributed remainder: 0** — so the combined row contributed nothing despite existing. One 9,170-token write → $0.022925, exactly once, with no backend row hygiene.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Contrast: the flat spelling on the same upgraded deployment does not rebalance</summary>

A control call emitted the earlier flat spelling (`gen_ai.usage.input_cache_creation_5m`) through a pre-switch build: same deployment, same price table. Its span (2026-10-29 13:59:21 UTC, trace `0da97d95e3b2ea22d56a16119d39ff77`, span `e35db4463bc30e8c`) shows `input_cache_creation: 36,162` — the full total, not a remainder — priced $0.090405 by the combined row alongside `_5m` $0.090405: the same write priced twice. #19420's rebalance triggers on the dotted breakdown keys only; the flat spelling leaves the combined total intact. The dotted emission shape is what makes the consumer-side decomposition apply.

</details>

**Tests and checks:** `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.otlp-export.test.ts` — one boundary test, `exports cache-write TTL facts on generic and OpenClaw usage keys` (single setup/event set), asserting both vocabularies verbatim: generic dotted TTL keys and OpenClaw TTL keys export mixed 1h/5m buckets, explicit zeros, and stay absent when unreported, with per-family key-set expectations. **Base-red verified:** with only `service-genai-attributes.ts` reverted to upstream/main, that test fails on the generic TTL assertions (keys absent on base) while the remaining 20 tests pass; restored, the suite passes. `tsgo:extensions`, formatting, scoped oxlint on the changed files, and `git diff --check` all pass on the rebased head. No attribute row other than the two new keys changes.

Closes #183705

## Current published candidate

**bd1798ae09a460e0a08f4e2e4285c8877829ee1f**, tree **76c97d0aa721ee59884375ebc7cd3b77c2130d16**, preserves HermanZeng's published history. Its parent 4f3d7366c82f9c8d0307597403ae32e84c0b2722 integrates the previous published 895 head with main 90a5029e427822745c59e4f1268db08ade257d5b. The conflict resolution retains both sets of Goal-test imports and all of main's continuation-authority behavior.

Against that main, the PR remains nine Goal production/test/helper paths (+982/-23), with no configuration, dependency or test-budget allocation. The final follow-up removes only 11 lines of fully subsumed assertions: the later, broader revoked-stream check and identical provider counters still run after a real positive publication. All distinct early history, chat-silence, sibling-denial and provider-cancellation checks remain.

## Verification and remaining merge gates

- **Independent peer review of bd is complete with no findings. Additional API-based review is INCOMPLETE; an assignment-corrected rerun remains pending and mandatory before merge.** Publication does not imply that review passed.
- **New-head CI is pending.** No passing result from a previous head is substituted for bd's required type, lint, runtime, baseline, security or dependency checks. The earlier successful 895 run is retained below as historical evidence.
- The affected real-source Gateway authority test passed **1/1 in 28.944 s** (110.79 s wall), including current-role restrictions, sibling denial, actual socket cancellation on revocation, and the authorized-publication/revoked-nondisclosure control.
- The **78 owner tests and direct/delegated/queued Gateway regression passed on 4f**. Their production/test/fixture inputs are unchanged in bd and that evidence is reused, not described as a new aggregate run.
- Focused type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks passed. The actual local native counter against main 90a passed at **6,272,482 / 6,326,764**, slack **54,282**, with main's ceiling unchanged. This is not a prediction of the later CI merge-tree count.
- Local bundling still reported unresolved externalization warnings for the gateway-client's @noble/hashes imports. The exercised Goal path passed; fresh-install CI must establish the wider dependency/type coverage. No local reinstall or packaging-success claim is made.

These are source-Gateway tests with scripted external-provider decisions, not new shipped-runtime, hosted-model or Windows proof. Historical failed exercises and their limitations remain below. **Merge remains held for complete API review and current-head CI.**

<details>
<summary>Historical published evidence and failed CI — not current-head results</summary>

### Historical published 895 evidence

The following successful CI evidence belongs to head 895, not the current bd candidate.

Closes #183705

## Historical integration

Published head **895f1f5b163428494bd7d1661367edce12586c47**, tree **2475e5698c8b199288c63b5e909e49062bfd7749**, is a normal merge of published 461391d111aa557440e0698d1ed3bbbad5f61aee and pinned main 8a3c02cb3c018c83193e6cfa9b0bad9cfd4b053c. HermanZeng's published history is preserved.

Main has fixed both failures from CI run 40800636327: #187162 restores its 6,320,000 test-line ceiling, and #187144 supplies the required braces in the inherited Slack-route test. The advisory max-lines warnings were not the lint failure. This integration takes both upstream fixes unchanged. The obsolete unpublished local repair was discarded before publication; **this PR adds no budget allocation or admission-test change**.

Against the pinned main, the scope remains the same nine Goal production/test/helper files, all byte-identical to the published 461391 candidate. The actual native counter on this integrated tree passes at **6,246,948 / 6,320,000**, with **73,052** remaining under main's unchanged ceiling. No tests were deleted, moved, minified or skipped.

## Verification and limits

- New focused checks of materially changed upstream inputs passed: **54/54 session-controller watchdog tests** and **37/37 canonical SQLite shared-state worker tests**, two shards, exit 0. These cover late assessment versus Stop/deadline/revocation and worker authority, cancellation, retirement and FIFO behavior. Diff checks passed.
- Current-head CI passed production and test type checks, all lint and baseline-ratchet checks, runtime, security and dependency checks. The actual Goal Gateway cases passed: authority/revocation **1/1 (20.144 s)** and direct/delegated/queued continuation **1/1 (18.397 s)**, both exit 0.
- CI tested merge ed0312327863e9320e29407e594cf7dc2809626a against main 5228f2425599f174d2bc84a5d1ff750de3b7ea83. Its actual test-line count was **6,246,985 / 6,320,000**, with **73,015** slack. This is distinct from the pinned local-tree count above; main owns the unchanged ceiling in both.
- The inherited brace-fixed admission file is identical to the previously audited and tested 18-case file and to main. No duplicate local production or test repair was added.
- **Exact-candidate independent review is READY, and [CI run 40806654694](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40806654694) completed successfully on this published head. The native CI observer reported GREEN and the final rollup had no failed or pending checks.** No PR merge is implied. Historical shipped-runtime, hosted-model and Windows proof limitations remain below; failed runs remain failed.



All wording and counts below refer to their named historical candidates. The current published head and CI status are identified above.

Closes #183705

## What this fixes

A Goal created during an admitted chat turn can stop after delegated work returns. The change binds that Goal to the existing return owner while preserving committed-yield, session, Stop, budget and current-operator checks. It adds no scheduler or autonomous command engine.

## Historical correction and integration

Candidate: 461391d111aa557440e0698d1ed3bbbad5f61aee (tree f9a603610c6ad92a94d53a621483a9db0f50d2d5). Its direct parent is the required main-integration merge 50907959005e92eb5e0b28140701291dece293bc, whose ordered parents are 70d9f737bafc9c129cc6d31e50f177e2e8df3359 and main cb5a4388f310d8b7c5d461e4f875561215260c1d.

HermanZeng's original history is preserved. The required main merge resolved two actual conflicts: it retains main's existing test-line ceiling and its current real actor-admission consumer fixture, including every distinct failure, transcript, registry and no-model-execution assertion. No unrelated production change was authored.

## Verification

- **79 selected tests passed across five files on the integrated parent:** two consumer tests, 75 Goal-owner tests, and both maintained real-Gateway regressions; the invocation exited 0. The final correction removes only an obsolete Goal-return mock from the context-read test, restoring main's exact real-owner fixture. Both affected consumer tests were then rerun and passed (2/2, exit 0). The unchanged Goal/Gateway production and test bytes retain their integration proof.
- The maintained cases cover direct, delegated and genuinely queued Goal creation, one automatic continuation, and exactly one final reply in the requester's subscribed session.message stream and canonical history.
- Revocation cancels the held producer before stale work is released, without later provider, sibling-session or Goal-completion effects. A separate real administrator chat.inject publication reaches the authorized observer and history exactly once while the revoked subscription receives no late content. A client may reconnect read-only; the tests do not require permanent disconnection.
- Focused source lint passed for six test/helper files and five production files. Formatting and whitespace checks passed. The integrated test count is **6,244,060 / 6,320,000**, using main's ceiling unchanged.
- This is source-Gateway proof with scripted external-provider decisions, not a new shipped-runtime or hosted-model exercise. Local dedicated typechecking was blocked before checking by the shared compiler-location guard. The published head's CI production and test type checks have now passed.

**Exact-candidate independent review:** READY for preparation at 461391d111aa557440e0698d1ed3bbbad5f61aee, with both coverage gaps and the obsolete context-read mock resolved. **CI:** [run 40800636327](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40800636327) completed with two independent failures; this is not an all-green result. Production/test types, Goal runtime checks, security and dependency checks passed. No merge is implied.

- [Lint failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40800636327/job/123208492630): a missing brace at `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.admission.test.ts:722`, in a file unchanged from main. The two max-lines annotations are warnings, not this failure's cause.
- [Test-line failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40800636327/job/123208126216): CI tested merge 799e7feacab2f0562f40c84fb675fb63c9e545e8 against main 64cb11485db8b0c30bab2e359124dcf99bd5fb0a, which adopted main's newer ceiling of 6,243,924. The actual CI count was 6,245,665, over by 1,741, with a PR delta of +920. The earlier local check used the older integrated main ceiling; it is not substituted for this failed CI measurement. No new reserve or automatic ceiling increase has been applied.

Historical hosted-driver failures remain failures; real-model revocation/reassignment was not exercised, and the earlier Windows alias-close timeouts are not claimed repaired by these source checks.

<details>
<summary>Prior-head evidence and retained failure history</summary>

The following text is the prior published description. Its “current” wording applies only to its named historical commits, not to the candidate above.

Closes #183705

## What Problem This Solves

An unfinished Goal created during a chat turn can stop after delegated work returns. Bind the actual newly created Goal to the existing admitted return owner, retaining committed-yield, current-session, cancellation and operator-authority checks.

## Evidence

### Historical budget-only follow-up

Current head `03b8a7485c6f3ffd86f6c1082413989d4d5ac51d`, tree
`3035ced419595b71cd357cfe0ef281bcfd9fab6e`, has the single published parent
`583ffe10b822eb26dd1133f322bd71c148bfb839`. Only the test-line ceiling changed;
all production/test blobs and the counting/authority contracts remain unchanged.

The three scoped session PRs now deliberately use identical **6,313,000**
single-line ceilings. Two latest actual comparison runs measured
6,311,267 / PR delta +617 and 6,311,148 / delta +498, respectively; each still
exceeded its prior small ceiling by 90 after queue-time base movement. This
does not invent a completed failure for this PR's then-running parent check.
All original failures and pending-state observations are retained below.

Same-pattern Git numstat checks confirm the three retained test additions occupy
disjoint paths and total **617 + 498 + 694 = 1,809**. Both observed CI totals
minus their PR deltas imply 6,310,650, so the explicit planning is
**6,310,650 + 1,809 + 541 = 6,313,000**. This is arithmetic, not an independent
main measurement or combined-tree/runtime test. The bounded one-time 541 reserve
addresses observed queued-base movement, and identical budget bytes avoid mutual
scalar conflicts between these changes. No automatic increase or future-fit
guarantee is introduced. The native owner permits manual increases with a PR
justification; no coverage, checker, assertion or timeout was removed.

This unchanged corpus retains its actual native count **6,311,232**, giving
arithmetic slack **1,768** under the new ceiling. The native scalar parser,
identical-byte/unchanged-corpus checks and whitespace checks passed; the count
was reused rather than newly executed. Normal commit hooks ran. Independent
P0-P3 review of all three budget-only deltas and the helpers found no actionable
finding (Codex-app narrative assessment, inherited model identity unverified;
not CLI/helper attestation). New-head CI remains an independent gate.

The model evidence stays bound to `cba507`: independently confirmed mid-turn Goal
creation, a real child/yield, restricted-member sibling denial, one automatic
continuation, and the final reply published/persisted. The combined driver still
**exited 1 and remains failed** because of its documented chat-vs-durable-message
observation mismatch. **B was not run; real-model revocation/reassignment proof
remains missing.** No new model call, accounting reset or new-head runtime proof
is claimed. Both older failed model attempts and Windows timeouts remain below.

counter passed at **6,311,232**, leaving **22** slack, independently matching the

Every feature/test blob matches the reviewed `cba507` candidate exactly. Their
upstream path OIDs also match between the old and fixed new base. Whitespace
checks passed, normal commit hooks ran, and independent P0-P3 integration review

independently verified every frozen blob, staged/working scope, budget and
publication route. This was a Codex-app narrative assessment with inherited

Transitive upstream inputs changed. The earlier build, type/test results and
model captures retain their named source commits rather than becoming executions

### Real-model proof: supported A facts and the remaining B gap

The real-model exercise remains bound to the tracked-clean `cba507` source

The combined driver still **exited 1 and remains failed**: its final marker wait
incorrectly required text inside a terminal `chat` event after the native owner
had already handed that text to durable `session.message`. The recorded terminal
event had no message, while actual member publication and persistence contained

**B never started and the real-model revocation/reassignment proof remains

tree `62de539fe524a809e2591b7cebf8df1d9fde8cb3`. Its ordered parents are

### Exact-head shipped Gateway and real-model evidence

Normal own-worktree frozen dependency installation and the maintained CLI build
completed with Node 24.22.1 / pinned pnpm 12.15.0. The default runtime build is
not a strict typecheck. Both native producer stamps name this tracked-clean

and runtime signature

  the same `session.message` to both the member and administrator observers
  (event orders 311 / 309). It exactly matched the final retained model output.

The failed driver's final-delivery wait required the marker inside `chat final`.
For this same continuation run, terminal chat events did arrive (313 / 314), but
contained no message because the native owner had already handed the committed
text to durable `session.message` publication. Native buffer/publication source
contracts and stopped persistence corroborate that observation-surface mismatch;
it is not evidence that the product failed to deliver the final reply. The
driver's original global failure phase was overwritten by asynchronous provider
assertions, so that saved label is not used as a precise wait-site diagnosis.
The original failed result is not rewritten into a passing combined run.

The child response was deliberately delayed only after its unmodified real body
was fully retained and usage settled, until public correlated `yielded` / active
Goal facts existed. No model decision, tool result or continuation instruction
was fabricated. This is controlled-boundary proof, not undelayed performance.
Original stopped database/WAL/SHM hashes were unchanged by independent inspection.
Owned cleanup joined with all admitted requests drained and no forced provider
abort or reported cleanup error; it does not certify global descendant exit.

**B never started:** no model request, role-revocation call, retained-return
cancellation observation or post-revocation final-effect proof occurred. The
original review's real-model revocation/reassignment requirement therefore remains
outstanding. Successful A observations do not close it. Both earlier failed model
attempts and both unexplained Windows configured-alias-close timeouts remain
retained below; no retry, longer timeout or green replay erases them.

<details>
<summary>Retained prior-head implementation, validation and failed proof history</summary>

The following description is retained as a historical record for its named commits. Its original “current”, “now” and “final” wording refers to those earlier candidates, not to the integration identified above. Earlier failures remain failures; earlier green CI is not current-head CI.

Closes #183705

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an unfinished Goal stopping after delegated work returns when the agent created the Goal during that same chat turn.

## User Impact

Users can keep pursuing an explicitly requested Goal across a same-process child handoff without sending another message to restart it. There is no schema/configuration migration, restart recovery extension, or new autonomous capability for independent commands or scheduled turns.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing return owner captured only Goals present before execution. Keep that owner unbound for an admitted built-in chat, then bind the actual `create_goal` result once to the current run/session/agent/store. Retaining the return still requires a committed yield; the existing queue, current Goal, cancellation, budget, and authority checks continue to decide whether another turn may run.

## Evidence

### Repair and Validation Status

Current repaired candidate: `98679a804ab787cb598b8d90979094da8eaf9f2c`, integrating the final bounded snapshot `f39b480c874d8acdae73f3b1c060dbd6cfc7a052`. The preceding `bdefe28105a066bf29a8565972140be3b947c9e4` integrated the observed CI comparison snapshot `23b53fd33fcd0fbaaf62546db23fb032541c9bdc` into `de7fed4b39fdfdd5f0b0c736d914533fbbed5e42`; a subsequent upstream budget edit caused the sole conflict resolved by this final integration. Earlier, `de7fed4` integrated fixed main `a6be2f6aee7fd9782563d54e33e4b60995853008` into `70159c5dc95809b55cb60713a558d871ef08ecad`, retaining both upstream placement coverage and the lifecycle-generation helper at its import conflict. No history was rewritten. All nine original PR files remain byte-identical to `de7fed4`; the only additional changes are the consumer fixture and justified test budget below. The five production-file changes are unchanged.

The focused Goal regression, type, and static gates below passed at the preceding candidate. CI subsequently found a missed consumer fixture and a test-line budget failure; their repair and the retained local failure are reported next. The additional hosted-model exercise did **not** satisfy all requested proof conditions. In particular, a successful shipped-runtime, real-model automatic-continuation demonstration and a real-model restricted-operator final-effect demonstration are still outstanding. These partial/failed exercises are not evidence of a newly identified production defect, and this update does not claim that all review feedback is resolved.

### CI follow-up: real consumer owner and explicit test budget

[CI on `de7fed4`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40535982697/job/122302639048) found `Operation has no controller owner` in the existing subagent cohort-conflict regression. Initially Goal-less admitted chat now enters the real Goal return owner, but that consumer fixture supplied an unregistered operation double. The fixture now creates the existing real controller operation with its captured physical store/session target, observes the real failure method through a call-through spy, and completes/joins owner settlement. Every original registry-conflict, visible-error, transcript, and no-model-execution assertion remains. No production owner or authority check was relaxed, and no Goal-wrapper mock was introduced.

The corrected case passed in the original three-file infra group (7.532 s). The command as a whole returned exit 1: **43 passed, one failed**, because the unmodified `refuses held row facts after configured-alias close` case timed out after 120 seconds on Windows. That same case had passed in the original CI job; this does not prove an inherited or platform-only defect. Static investigation found isolated fork workers and no new collection-time controller registration from this fixture, but the stalled await remains unidentified. No timeout was raised, test removed, or green replay substituted. The messaging test type graph, focused lint, formatting and whitespace checks passed. The local run used Node on Windows, not CI's Bun/Linux scheduling.

One bounded diagnostic ran only that failed alias-close case on the final fixed `f39b480` integration inputs; it also timed out after 120 seconds (one failed, 14 explicitly filtered cases). This is a different base from the first local group, not an identical-source replay. It does not establish a preceding-file cause, a Windows-only cause, or a repaired failure. The precise blocked await remains unknown. Both failed local receipts and the wrapper's conservative retained-namespace warnings remain recorded; no further replay or production workaround was added.

The separate [ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40535982697/job/122302638696) failed on positive test-line growth. The first fixed CI-snapshot integration measured 6,286,460 total lines and passed its explicit zero-slack budget check. After resolving the subsequent upstream scalar conflict on the final fixed `f39b480` snapshot, the native checker measured **6,286,640** total lines with a **+694** PR delta. The final deliberate ceiling change is exactly 6,285,587 to 6,286,640, with zero slack: 694 retained regression lines plus 359 lines already beyond the ceiling in the comparison tree. That split is arithmetic, not an independent failing run of main. The documented owner permits manual increases with a PR justification. No guard was disabled or required coverage deleted; the native checker passed after the edit.

The new fixture received an independent full-context P0–P3 agent review, and the mechanical integration/budget change received a separate independent assessment. Neither found an actionable issue; neither is a CLI/helper pass. Current-head hosted CI remains separate from the previous failed run and these local receipts.

### Passing Local Evidence

- Historical local Gateway/tool/child-return baseline: a pre-existing Goal continued once and completed; the otherwise matched model-created Goal received no Goal context or nudge and remained active after the child batch committed and Gateway work drained.
- The Gateway regression passes actual `create_goal -> sessions_spawn -> sessions_yield -> committed requester final -> Goal nudge -> complete`, plus a non-yield final control: delegated parent/child requests `6/1`, direct `4/0`, exactly one continuation in each, no provider errors.
- Added actual Gateway authority coverage with identified users and configured roles: a member restricted to `main` receives the real sibling `sessions_create` denial, creates no sibling session, and completes one Goal continuation. After a separate member's role is revoked through `users.setRole`, the held provider socket is actually cancelled; no subsequent provider requests, sibling session, Goal completion, or normal post-revocation assistant chat delta/final content is observed. This is a fixed-provider Gateway regression, not a real-model authority proof.
- At `de7fed4`, Goal owner/tool suites: **73 passed** (`66 + 7`). Both Gateway tests passed. Affected consumers and provider-prefix tests passed across eight files; their combined test total is not asserted because one summary was truncated in the captured output.

These Gateway tests use a scripted loopback Responses provider. They are not hosted-model, real-channel, restart, local Codex, or production-scale proof. Hosted CI for the repaired candidate and its CI duration are not established by these local runs.

All task content was synthetic. This was not a browser/Control UI exercise, and no production service or operator state was used.

The tested source was the tracked-clean preceding candidate `de7fed4b39fdfdd5f0b0c736d914533fbbed5e42`, not the current CI-follow-up head. Native preparation reported `build:false` and `runtime:false`, and the effective build/runtime input fingerprints matched that source. The unchanged producer stamps still record precommit producer HEAD `70159c5dc95809b55cb60713a558d871ef08ecad` with `inputsClean:false`. This is supported source-equivalent artifact reuse for that source, not a claim that the artifacts were freshly built at either repaired commit. No new model call accompanied the CI follow-up.

1. **First model attempt: failed, seven HTTP 200 requests.** The trace records real `create_goal`, `sessions_spawn`, one child request, `sessions_yield`, requester return, and later requests containing the automatic Goal nudge, including `update_goal`. The final harness assertion failed. That original capture omitted the exact assertion phase, last public Goal row, and final receipt, and its isolated state was cleaned. The model instead completed the Goal during the requester child-return, contrary to the synthetic task's instruction to leave an unfinished interim phase. It therefore did not exercise the required automatic-continuation case. This is not attributed to a production defect. The client, Gateway, remote I/O, and accounting writes were joined; only stopped synthetic state was retained privately before normal cleanup.

There were **13 physical hosted-model requests**, all HTTP 200 with usage reported: **96,997 input tokens and 1,164 output tokens**. No further model attempt was made. Private credential configuration and account/budget accounting are not part of this public evidence.

The failed artifacts and accounting are retained locally; no public hosted-model proof artifact is claimed. The unmet proof requirements above remain explicit.

Original tested source base: `ab68862753db1c083bf4bac921d642b4e194631b`; Node 24.22.1 on Windows 11. prs.title: fix(ui): prune the live cli-assistant segment when its row persists mid-run
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #180927. In a Control UI webchat session on a CLI backend with block streaming off, the assistant reply appeared twice: the live stream bubble kept the partial text while the durable row, persisted mid-run, was admitted beside it. The reporter measured the corresponding gateway failure 360 times in one day.

The pane already clears the live stream when a persisted row owns the active run — but that ownership check requires an explicit envelope run id (`event.runId` / row metadata), and the mid-run transcript publish can omit it. CLI assistant rows are self-proving: the Gateway stamps the run id into the persisted idempotency key (`cli-assistant:<runId>`), which the projection layer already canonicalizes into the row's run id.

## What Changed

`ui/src/pages/chat/session-message-apply.ts` only:

- A persisted CLI assistant row (`role: assistant`, `api: "cli"`) whose canonical idempotency-key run id is present now qualifies as producer-owned for the matching active run, even when the envelope omits the run id.
- That ownership feeds the existing persistence path, which clears the live stream so the durable row replaces the bubble instead of duplicating it.

The first revision of this PR keyed a different stream owner (`chatStreamSegments`) that the CLI assistant flow does not write; that path is gone. No other surface changes: rows without CLI provenance keep the terminal-stream behavior, and no delivery path gains or loses a send.

## Evidence

**Red/green regression** (`session-message-apply.test.ts`, real pane event path: live `chatStream` filled, then the persisted `session.message` row):

```
fix applied (9caa2aab):  ✓ 10 passed (10)
  - clears the live stream when a cli assistant row persists mid-run (without an envelope run id)
  - clears the live stream when a cli assistant row persists mid-run (with a matching envelope run id)
  - keeps the live stream for mid-run persisted rows without cli provenance

fix reverted, same tests:  × clears the live stream ... (without an envelope run id)
  Tests  1 failed | 9 passed (10)
```

**Adjacent suites after the change:**

```
session-message-apply + chat-pane-{session,snapshot}-hydration + tool-stream-fallback: 57 passed (57)
```

prs.title: fix(normalization-core): blockquote marker leaks into plain-text previews without a following space
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plain-text previews can show literal Markdown quote markers when an assistant message begins with `>quoted`, `>>nested`, or spaced nested `> >quoted`. This affects sidebar messages and session excerpts even though the full conversation renders the quote correctly.

## User Impact

Quoted text appears as ordinary readable text in plain previews. Inline comparisons such as `a > b`, escaped markers, heading/list whitespace rules, original transcript bytes, and rendered Markdown keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Repair the existing private normalization-core flattener once for all display consumers. The quote arm accepts repeated markers separated by horizontal whitespace and stays within each line. It adds no preview-specific path, SDK export, configuration, persistence change, or new parser. Keeps coaiMax/lijing’s contributor commit and completes its spaced-nesting/line-boundary handling.

## Evidence

Built Gateway-served Control UI in real Chromium with real sessions created through chat.send/agent.wait and a deterministic local provider. Main twice shows leaked markers; candidate twice removes them in both sidebar subtitles and actual session hover previews. Plain-text and inline `>` controls remain unchanged. Raw chat.history and rendered blockquotes remain intact.

Inspected before/after screenshots and detailed receipts: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187853#issuecomment-6507303963

Focused shared-owner suite: candidate 39/39 pass; same retained table against frozen main fails the intended marker case (38 other cases pass). Formatting passes. Whole-PR tests net 0 lines (+3/-3), no new allocations; production +2/-1.

Merge danger: two-way door. A revert restores prior preview formatting without rewriting data. Blast radius: private shared plain-text Markdown preview consumers, not rendered Markdown, model context, or stored message content.
