prs.title: improve(ios): reuse release Swift package downloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every iOS Store Release and daily TestFlight build downloads its Swift package sources and binary artifacts on a fresh runner. The latest signed archive spent about 46 seconds resolving its package graph.

Related: #187790. This is the next scoped iOS release performance improvement requested by a maintainer; validation of the earlier Watch RTC cache remains deferred while the existing TestFlight build waits for beta review.

## User Impact

No app behavior changes. Release jobs can reuse dependency downloads while still resolving packages normally and performing a clean archive. Cache misses and transfer failures retain the current cold path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The archive already resolves packages once and requires each dependency. Use a separate release cache for Xcode SourcePackages because the detached release project has a different default DerivedData identity from ordinary CI. Keys include platform, architecture, Xcode, manifests and available lockfiles. Compiled products and screenshot DerivedData stay outside this cache. The canonical recovery project path is retained; changing that path requires invalidating the cache namespace.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule recorded before measurement: five serial, interleaved cold/warm package-resolution pairs on one fresh xcode-27-xlarge runner. Clear the task-owned default package and global SwiftPM downloads and generated Package.resolved before each sample. Candidates restore the actual Actions cache. Require at least 20% lower median resolution time including cache restore, no worse p95 (maximum of five), identical resolved package/artifact identities, complete binary artifacts, and one successful clean unsigned archive consuming the restored packages. Report cache producer/save cost separately. No export, upload, signing credentials, or Apple state changes.

The committed, nonpublishing [proof workload](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ac680b7ed2d6a3b2a69598f83ad7b4580c979575/scripts/ios-source-packages-proof.mjs) runs only on a diagnostic branch; its workflow must not be merged. [Hosted comparison run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40940930496) completed all five pairs successfully. The full acceptance rule passed. The final clean unsigned archive succeeded in 5m36s after removing the generated Package.resolved, with no logged package fetches. Both Watch RTC device slices were verified cache hits. No export or upload ran.

| Metric | Cold | Restored, including transfer |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median | 36.07 s | 10.02 s |
| p95 / maximum of five | 40.40 s | 10.37 s |
| Minimum | 33.09 s | 9.61 s |
| Logged Git fetches per sample | 8 | 0 |

Median reduction: 72.2% (26.05 seconds at this boundary). All eight pinned package identities and both artifact records match; every recorded xcframework slice exists and is nonempty. The cache archive is 432,191,498 bytes, with a one-time save cost of 4.662 seconds. Restores took 4.94–5.54 seconds; that overhead also applies to release attempts that subsequently defer for Apple review or otherwise do not build. These measurements cover restore plus resolution, not the whole release duration.

The runner reported five Apple M2 Pro virtual CPUs, 14 GiB RAM, arm64, and Xcode 27.1 (27A9275). One-minute host load ranged from 9.53 to 15.06 across interleaved samples; full host readings, all ten results, commands and logs are in the run's comparison artifact. To rerun the committed workload, dispatch ios-store-release.yml from the diagnostic branch test/ios-source-packages-proof. That branch has no signing credentials, export, upload, or Apple mutation steps. The diagnostic workflow must not be merged.

The earlier diagnostic attempts stopped on fixture-only issues before producing valid timing evidence: missing workspace dependency links, then an unquoted timestamp expression. Both were corrected before this accepted comparison.

Local cache and release-routing tests passed. All required ci-workflow suites, Swift cache lifetime, and native test-launch suites completed: 1,027 passing tests and 10 existing skips, reusing the unchanged suites after the cache-write guard repair. The changed guard file passes 170 tests with eight existing skips (58.86 seconds Vitest wall; 64.93 seconds wrapper wall including the three small native scope/cache suites). Workflow lint, tooling typecheck, targeted lint, formatting and git diff --check passed. The global cache-write guard is extended by three net lines to admit only the new trusted release writer; its allocation covers that boundary.

Fresh independent AutoReview of the final local candidate against cfb5923c5eb4d513e6d600ba599c91c875c3679e completed scoped-clean through P2. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable due to its structured-output validation failure in the preceding campaign; the ready PR will receive its hosted review.

prs.title: fix(exec): require approval for legacy arithmetic arguments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: exec allowlist evaluation could automatically accept legacy Bash arithmetic arguments even though equivalent modern arithmetic already requires approval.

## User Impact

User impact: `$[...]` arguments now follow the existing approval policy for dynamic shell arguments. Ordinary literal builtin commands continue to run under the same settings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command explainer already identifies these arguments as dynamic. This adds the missing arithmetic form to the authorization planner's existing expansion check. No new policy owner or configuration is introduced.

## Evidence

- Reviewed head: `e9fe4f14b4c8a88531446c9fbfe5716fae85ab80`.
- Linux/Bash gateway execution proof uses the production exec tool, authorization planner, shell preparation, and real process supervisor with synthetic policy and isolated temporary state. The literal control `: benign; pwd` completes with one process launch. Encoded legacy and modern arithmetic commands are rejected before process launch, with zero launches and no marker-file side effect.
- The new gateway regression fails on the original base because the legacy arithmetic command completes instead of requiring approval; it passes with the fix. The new legacy-arithmetic policy cases also fail on base and pass with the fix.
- Focused command: `pnpm test src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.test.ts src/infra/exec-authorization-plan.test.ts src/infra/exec-authorization-render.test.ts src/infra/exec-authorization-allowlist.test.ts src/infra/exec-allow-always-persistence.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-safe-bins.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-system-run-allowlist.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-authorization.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Eight files passed: 113 tests passed and 3 platform/optional-shell tests skipped; total focused command wall time 96.61 seconds.
- Focused formatting, repository-supported focused lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Test-line and line-cap ratchets pass against the original branch base.
- The separate local typecheck could not run: its declaration wrapper refuses the borrowed dependency installation. Canonical PR CI `check-prod-types`, `check-test-types`, and all five `check-test-types-core-*` jobs passed at this head. Tests and formatting/lint ran without modifying the shared installation.
- Proof is local and isolated; no live external Gateway, channel, or model was used. The gateway boundary suite initially completed in 34.14 seconds wall time (23.84 seconds test-run duration); CI groups these files into broader shards, so isolated per-file CI timing is not available.
- Simplification retained a single expansion check and existing test fixtures: production +3/-1 lines, regression tests +36 lines. The separate test-line allocation covers exactly those 36 new regression lines, with the shared baseline unchanged.

### Standalone execution receipt

Command: repository-pinned `bun .local/gateway-runtime-proof.ts`, using Bun revision `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1` (the Node-compatible API reports v26.12.1); exit status 0. This standalone local harness runs outside Vitest. It seeds synthetic approval policy through the production maintenance API, calls the production `createExecTool`, and counts supervisor launches while delegating to the real process supervisor. It uses no Gateway or process mock. Only the observed scalar results below are captured; no inherited environment or credentials are logged.

prs.body:
Related: #160064

## What Problem This Solves

CLI startup metadata failures omit the child exit code when a help renderer exits unsuccessfully without stderr or a signal.

## User Impact

Failed build or update preflights now report that exit code, giving users a concrete diagnostic instead of only a generic render failure. This diagnostic change does not fix the original Windows update failure reported in #160064.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the child exit code as the existing error-detail fallback. Stderr still takes precedence over the signal, and the signal over the exit code; timeout, cancellation, and earlier-error precedence remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Windows x64, Node 24.22.1: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/write-cli-startup-metadata.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 15 tests; 6 POSIX/Linux process-lifecycle tests were skipped on Windows. Test-file time: 720 ms; wrapper wall time: 13.67 s. Hosted CI timing is not yet available.
- The real-child regression (`process.exit(23)`) failed on the base because the diagnostic omitted 23, then passed with this fix. It also verifies that failed metadata is not published.
- Scripts typecheck, a focused projection of the existing root-scripts test typecheck, changed-file lint and format, script erasability, and `git diff --check` passed.
- All 12 boundary probes passed for stderr/signal precedence, success, timeout, cancellation, output limits, and spawn/stream errors. These synthetic events do not prove native POSIX process cleanup.
- The required 18-line allocation exactly covers the new real-child regression; the test-line ratchet passed and the shared scalar is unchanged.
- Linux/macOS execution and a full build were not run locally. Hosted CI was not run before publication.

Shipped entrypoint capture on Windows x64, Node 24.22.1: disposable checkouts of unchanged upstream parent `74f111a74dbd` and PR head `f4e74e31eb85` both used the same ignored, injected `dist/root-help-proof.js` containing `export function outputRootHelp() { process.exit(23); }`. The generator and all tracked files were unchanged; no in-process metadata API or mocked spawn was used.

```text

node --import tsx scripts/write-cli-startup-metadata.ts

# Upstream 74f111a74dbd — generator exit 1
Error: Failed to render bundled root help from root-help-proof.js (elapsed 60ms)

# PR f4e74e31eb85 — generator exit 1
Error: Failed to render bundled root help from root-help-proof.js: exited with code 23 (elapsed 83ms)

Both generators exited **1**, retained `ECLI_STARTUP_METADATA_RENDER` / `nonzero-exit`, and published no `dist/cli-startup-metadata.json`. This controlled failure proves the entrypoint diagnostic; no full build or original Windows update failure was reproduced.

prs.title: fix(cron): announce jobs without an account deliver to a nonexistent "default" Discord account
prs.body:
Related: #186043

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an announce automation whose delivery block has no `accountId` (the older `{ "mode": "announce", "channel": "discord", "to": "…" }` shape) fails when Discord has only a named account such as `channels.discord.accounts.main`. Delivery is routed to an account literally named `default` (`Discord bot token missing for account "default"`), and a `discord|default` conversation is registered that later trips heartbeat replies (`Session binding owner changed for discord:default`).

## User Impact

User impact: these automations deliver through the channel's own default account (here `main`), as they did before the regression, and no new `discord|default` conversation rows are created for them. Jobs that name an account, agents with a channel binding, sessions with a remembered account, and channels whose default really is unnamed are unchanged.

This does **not** repair `discord|default` rows that affected installs already have. The reporter's follow-up shows that the stale row keeps heartbeat failing until it is removed. Cleaning up existing rows (self-heal, a Doctor repair, or skipping participant rows without an adapter) is a separate decision, so this PR uses `Related:` and leaves the issue open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron's delivery target tries the job's `accountId`, then the session's `lastAccountId`, then the agent's bound account. It never asks the channel for its default account, so the account could stay unset. Later routing and conversation-ref normalization then turned "unset" into the literal `default`. The target resolver now falls back to the channel plugin's own default account (`resolveChannelDefaultAccountId`, the same rule the Gateway's send-account route uses), so one resolved account flows through routing, persistence and transport. An unnamed default (`default`) stays implicit, as before, so existing behavior for single-unnamed-account channels does not change.

## Evidence

- Regression test: `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-target.test.ts` › "uses the channel's own default account when the delivery names none". The only configured account is `main`, there is no binding or session account, and the target is `{ channel, to }`.
  - On `main`: `expected { ok: true, channel: 'forum', … } to match object { ok: true, accountId: 'main', … }`, because the account stays unset.
  - With the fix: `accountId: "main"`.
- Discord's plugin reports `main` as its default account for a config with only `accounts.main`, since `defaultAccountId` comes from `resolveDefaultDiscordAccountId` (`extensions/discord/src/shared.ts`).
- `pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent src/cron/delivery`: 64 files, 552 tests pass.
- Local checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, the core test typecheck shards for these paths, and oxlint on the changed files are clean. `check:import-cycles` reports 0 runtime value cycles, and the line-cap, test-lines and mock-factory ratchets pass.
- **Live Discord proof (2026-10-29, this PR's head `69f1cf3` vs. its base `3263a51`):**
  - Setup: an isolated Gateway built from this checkout (separate state dir, loopback port), Discord configured with only `channels.discord.accounts.main` (a real bot), no top-level token and no binding. The model is a local OpenAI-compatible stub that returns a fixed text. The job is created by the CLI in the old shape, with no `--account`: `openclaw cron add --session isolated --announce --channel discord --to channel:<test channel>` → stored `delivery: { mode: "announce", channel: "discord", to: "channel:<id>" }`. Each run is `openclaw cron run <id>`, read back with `openclaw cron runs --json` and the agent DB `conversations` table.
  - Base build: the message reaches Discord, but no account is resolved and the conversation is recorded under the literal `default` account, which does not exist in this config:
    ```
    delivery.resolved: { ok: true, channel: "discord", to: "channel:<id>", source: "explicit" }   <- no accountId
    delivery queue id: cron-direct-delivery:v1:cron:<job>:<ts>:discord::channel%3A<id>:
    conversations: (discord, default, channel, <id>)
    ```
    On this config Discord's transport still found the token, so I did not reproduce the `Discord bot token missing for account "default"` error from #186043; the wrong `default` identity is what was reproduced.
  - PR head, fresh state: the same job resolves and records `main` end to end:
    ```
    delivery.resolved: { ok: true, channel: "discord", to: "channel:<id>", accountId: "main", source: "explicit" }
    delivery queue id: cron-direct-delivery:v1:cron:<job>:<ts>:discord:main:channel%3A<id>
    conversations: (discord, main, channel, <id>)
    status ok, delivered; the bot's message appears in the channel
    ```
  - Upgrade: the base build's state dir (job created by the base build, `discord|default` row already there) started on the PR head. The stored job loads unchanged, its next run resolves `accountId: "main"` and is delivered, and a `discord|main` row is added. The old `discord|default` row stays, as described above (not repaired here).
  - Upgrade from the 2026.10.8 release (2026-10-30): `npm i -g openclaw@2026.10.8` into an isolated prefix with its own `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `openclaw plugins install npm:@openclaw/discord@2026.10.8`, the same `accounts.main`-only config, and the same accountless job created with the release CLI. On the release, its run is delivered with no `accountId` in `delivery.resolved` and the agent DB gets a `(discord, default, channel, <id>)` conversation, as on the base build above. Then, with the Gateway stopped, `openclaw update --tag <release-shaped package of this head> --no-restart --yes` (package built with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs`, Discord not bundled):
    ```
    Update mode: npm / Update target: 2026.10.8
    Admission checks: config: ok, database-schema: ok, node-runtime: ok, plugin-availability: ok.
    Plugins updated; Gateway restart skipped (--no-restart).
    openclaw --version: OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (69f1cf3)
    ```
    After the update: `channels.discord` is unchanged (only `accounts.main`, same guild/channel allowlist, no top-level token); the only config changes are Doctor's `agents.entries.main: {}` and the `wizard` run record. `@openclaw/discord` 2026.10.8 is still installed and enabled. The job is still listed with its old `delivery: { mode: "announce", channel: "discord", to: "channel:<id>" }`. Its next `openclaw cron run` resolves `accountId: "main"` and is delivered (the bot's message appears in the channel), and a `(discord, main, …)` conversation is added next to the old `default` one, which stays as described above.
  - Disabled account: with `channels.discord.accounts.main.enabled=false` (hot reloaded), `openclaw message send --account main` is refused (`Account "main" for channel discord is disabled.`), but a cron run still delivers. This is the same for a job that names `--account main` explicitly, and on the base build as well, so cron delivery not checking the account's enabled state is existing behavior that this PR does not change. I have left it out of this PR; it is a separate fix at cron's delivery owner.
- Not addressed: the event-loop stall that the issue also reports is a separate problem.

prs.title: improve(ios): align app icon composition with Apple's design guidelines
prs.body:
Closes #187629
Related: #101411, #138002.

## What Problem This Solves

The iOS app icon’s mascot nearly fills the canvas, leaving little surrounding space instead of following Apple’s guidance to emphasize centered primary content with a simple background.

## User Impact

The iOS icon gains a more balanced composition while preserving its existing mascot, colors, and backgrounds. macOS, Debug icons, separate Watch app assets, and app behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apple’s [Human Interface Guidelines for app icons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/app-icons) recommend keeping primary content centered and using the production-template grids to guide placement. Apple also states:

> “you don’t need to fill the entire icon canvas with content.”

This reduces the iOS foreground to a centered 0.86 scale while retaining full-bleed backgrounds and leaving masking to the system. The chosen proportion is a design interpretation of Apple’s guidance, not an Apple-mandated percentage or a universal circular clipping boundary.

The unchanged macOS Original icon provides a supporting source-level sizing reference. A representative comparison with other iOS icons provides additional visual context; it is not the primary justification for this change.

The existing generator now produces release PNGs from a static, app-specific SVG rather than the animated browser favicon. Default remains opaque white, Dark retains transparency, and Tinted remains system-generated.

## Evidence

### iOS before and after

Actual baseline and regenerated PNG assets, shown with a presentation-only rounded mask. All annotations are in English. These are asset previews, **not native Home Screen screenshots**.

![iOS app icon before and after, with light and dark small-size previews](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/569b65bb-d646-4eab-8ae5-a307d1fe2316?raw=1)

### Supporting comparison with other iOS icons

Equal-size tiles using artwork returned by Apple’s US App Store lookup API for Shortcuts (915249334), WhatsApp (310633997), Signal (874139669), Telegram (686449807), Slack (618783545), and GitHub (1477376905). This representative asset comparison does not establish every app’s native appearance or system effects.

![Before and after alongside six other iOS app icons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23dccfd1-4ea8-4e31-ab9e-89ef0c0385b6?raw=1)

### macOS reference — unchanged

Both columns show the same source composition at 0.86 scale. Native Liquid Glass effects are omitted. No macOS source or compiled assets change.

![Unchanged macOS original icon as a sizing reference](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7187e880-ced5-4cc8-9de9-139ec6667139?raw=1)

### Validation

- All 29 release PNG assets regenerate byte-for-byte with `bash apps/ios/scripts/app-icon-variants.sh check`; existing manifest, alpha-channel, color-profile, and Debug checks pass.
- `bash -n apps/ios/scripts/app-icon-variants.sh`, `swiftc -typecheck apps/ios/scripts/app-icon-release.swift`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Repository-pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1: 0/1 files require formatting.
- Fresh independent source and asset review: no actionable findings. Original geometry and colors are preserved; no macOS, WatchApp, Debug, or manifest changes were found.
- Simplification pass reused the existing generation entry point and native rasterizer; no dependencies, runtime behavior, or settings were added.
- Baseline `37c408f2e32d7c8de48ea420ca5c9b1930e1d5fd`; the affected pre-existing generator/icon inputs are unchanged on fetched main `3263a51fc3a7a2ea36c48543cf62dd4035d4a7e8`.

**Draft / outstanding native proof:** native iOS asset-catalog compilation, Home Screen before/after captures, and installed-app light/dark/tinted validation have not been run. Local full Xcode/`actool` is unavailable and the paired Mac reports `COMPANION_APP_UNAVAILABLE`. Pinned SwiftLint 0.65.1 could not run because the local SourceKit framework is unavailable. No native build or lint success is claimed. Hosted CI and native visual proof remain required before marking this ready.

prs.title: fix(telegram): suppress duplicate DM transcript windows while preserving delivery-only context
prs.body:
Related: #89855, #112548, #130551, #172711, #179399

## What Problem This Solves

Existing plain Telegram DMs receive ordinary recent user/assistant turns twice: through canonical session replay and a supplemental transcript `chat_window`. Blanket suppression would also remove delivery-only context excluded from normal replay.

## Change

Keep the existing plain-DM suppression predicate and pass `deliveryOnly: true` through the shared transcript-context owner. Select the bounded recent window first, then restore only supported delivery mirrors. Fresh DMs, explicit replies, topics, and groups retain their existing context selection. No config, schema, or storage-format changes.

## Evidence

Current head: `df377682122984deb56e11e8d0e2ec4bdf929911`. Merged main `870c16e66d940d629f8676d3293fb87ab174b3ee` to incorporate the upstream test-line budget repair in [#186785](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186785). The failing CI snapshot had 6,294,266 test lines against a 6,294,048 ceiling. With upstream's reviewed budget, the refreshed tree has 6,302,332 lines against a 6,310,000 ceiling (7,668 lines of headroom). The standalone test-line ratchet passes. No PR-specific ceiling increase or test deletion was needed.

The six-file PR patch is byte-for-byte identical to the independently reviewed `9d5d58e2ed2` candidate. It preserves #186081's turn-identity/completed-answer reconciliation alongside bounded delivery-only filtering. Original commits, human credit, and both sets of SQLite regressions remain intact.

**Current-head focused validation:**
- All 41 tests pass: SQLite transcript (3), Telegram prompt context (15), shared transcript context (9), and tool-prefix stability (14), in 153.28 seconds across the four selected Vitest shards.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.sqlite.test.ts src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.runtime.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.prompt-context.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- `git diff --check` passes. Previous targeted lint and formatting results are reused for the unchanged six-file patch.
- Budget check: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 870c16e66d940d629f8676d3293fb87ab174b3ee --no-merge-base` passes.
- Local Codex autoreview covered the complete six-file candidate against base `b46d011db972a982bf8b8b94331505473dd07851`, at P0–P2 coverage, before committing that unchanged index as `9d5d58e2ed2`. Completed with no actionable findings; that result is reused for the byte-identical six-file patch after this mechanical merge. Source review is separate from runtime proof.

**Live Telegram Test Server proof passed on prior head `09618b32c5e141cd74e35b91d88b9388ac0727dc`.** Five actual Gateway processes shared isolated SQLite state across four orderly replacements. A Convex-leased, independently authorized TDLib user observed the dedicated Test Server bot's replies. All seven captured Google Gemini 3.8 Flash requests returned HTTP 200; the runner's mock server received zero conversational/generation requests and two ancillary embedding requests.

- Ordinary user and assistant history reaches the provider exactly once before and after restart.
- An announcement from a real Cron job remains in the next model context after restart, exactly once.
- A final `message.send` reply is observed by TDLib and remains in runtime context after restart. Its persisted mirror has `final: true` and tool-call/source-turn correlation; verification does not rely solely on the original function-call arguments.

[Live proof and reproduction source for `09618b32c5e1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183190#issuecomment-6430787664) contains redacted provider-request excerpts and counts, native message receipts, restart/cleanup evidence, exact setup and commands, and reproduction scripts. This refresh reuses that runtime evidence; the live scenario has not been rerun on `df377682122`. The personal Gateway was not modified or restarted.

[Historical fixture proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183190#issuecomment-6400568002) covers `57a4cb127d2a`, including the explicitly seeded legacy `cron-direct-delivery-context` compatibility check. The committed SQLite regression was also verified red on original parent `bfcaa1b2cd1cf2f0e7d617b773e4743218eb219c` and green with the fix.

```python
"""Exercise ClawHub credential diagnostics through the normal built public CLI."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import http.server
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import subprocess
import tempfile
import threading
import time


def run_cli(command, checkout, env):
    child = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=checkout, env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, start_new_session=True)
    try:
        stdout, stderr = child.communicate(timeout=30)
    except BaseException:
        if child.poll() is None:
            os.killpg(child.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        child.communicate()
        raise
    return child.returncode, stdout, stderr


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("checkout", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("phase", choices=["base", "head"])
    parser.add_argument("node", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    checkout = args.checkout.resolve()
    head = subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=checkout, text=True).strip()
    assert not subprocess.check_output(["git", "status", "--porcelain"], cwd=checkout), "Proof requires a clean committed checkout"
    build = json.loads((checkout / "dist/build-info.json").read_text())
    stamp = json.loads((checkout / "dist/.buildstamp").read_text())
    assert build["commit"] == head and stamp["inputsClean"], "Proof requires the clean normal build of this commit"
    started = time.monotonic()
    token = "fixture-K83-ordinary-secret"
    marker = "SAFE_CLAWHUB_OPERATOR_MARKER"
    cases = [
        ("config-query-json", "config", False, True, "reflection"),
        ("env-trending-json", "env", True, True, "reflection"),
        ("legacy-env-query-text", "legacy-env", False, False, "reflection"),
        ("ordinary-error", "config", False, True, "ordinary-error"),
        ("authenticated-success", "config", False, True, "success"),
        ("anonymous-success", "anonymous", False, True, "success"),
    ]
    records = []
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="clawhub-token-proof-", dir=args.output.resolve().parent) as temporary:
        root = Path(temporary)
        config = root / "openclaw.json"
        config.write_text("{}\n")
        auth = root / "clawhub.json"
        base_env = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items() if not key.startswith(("OPENCLAW_", "CLAWHUB_", "CLAWDHUB_")) and key not in {"GH_TOKEN", "GITHUB_TOKEN"}}
        base_env.update({"HOME": str(root), "XDG_CONFIG_HOME": str(root / "xdg"), "OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR": str(root / "state"), "OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH": str(config), "CLAWHUB_CONFIG_PATH": str(auth), "NO_COLOR": "1", "PATH": str(args.node.parent) + os.pathsep + base_env.get("PATH", "")})
        cli = [str(args.node), str(checkout / "openclaw.mjs"), "skills", "search"]
        help_status, help_stdout, help_stderr = run_cli(cli + ["--help"], checkout, base_env)
        assert help_status == 0 and "--json" in help_stdout, help_stderr
        for name, source, trending, json_mode, mode in cases:
            env = dict(base_env)
            auth.write_text(json.dumps({"token": token if source == "config" else "fixture-config-not-selected"}))
            if source == "env":
                env["CLAWHUB_TOKEN"] = token
                env["CLAWHUB_AUTH_TOKEN"] = "fixture-legacy-env-not-selected"
            elif source == "legacy-env":
                env["CLAWHUB_TOKEN"] = " "
                env["CLAWHUB_AUTH_TOKEN"] = token
            elif source == "anonymous":
                auth.write_text("{}\n")
            before = {p.name: hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in [config, auth]}
            received = []

            class Peer(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
                def do_GET(self):
                    authorization = self.headers.get("Authorization")
                    received.append({"path": self.path, "authorizationPresent": authorization is not None, "authorizationMatchesSentinel": authorization == "Bearer " + token})
                    if mode == "success":
                        text = json.dumps({"results": [{"score": 0.9, "slug": "fixture-result", "displayName": "Fixture Result", "summary": "SAFE_RESULT_TEXT", "source": "clawhub", "ownerHandle": "fixture-owner", "version": "1.2.3"}]})
                    else:
                        text = marker + (" refused " + token if mode == "reflection" else " ordinary upstream failure")
                    body = text.encode()
                    self.send_response(200 if mode == "success" else 400)
                    self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json" if mode == "success" else "text/plain")
                    self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
                    self.send_header("Connection", "close")
                    self.end_headers()
                    self.wfile.write(body)

                def log_message(self, *_args):
                    pass

            peer = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Peer)
            thread = threading.Thread(target=peer.serve_forever, daemon=True)
            thread.start()
            env["OPENCLAW_CLAWHUB_URL"] = "http://127.0.0.1:" + str(peer.server_address[1])
            command = cli + ([] if trending else ["fixture-redaction"]) + (["--json"] if json_mode else [])
            at = time.monotonic()
            try:
                status, stdout, stderr = run_cli(command, checkout, env)
            finally:
                peer.shutdown()
                peer.server_close()
                thread.join(timeout=5)
                assert not thread.is_alive(), "Peer cleanup did not finish"
            assert len(received) == 1, received
            assert received[0]["authorizationMatchesSentinel"] == (source != "anonymous"), received
            assert received[0]["authorizationPresent"] == (source != "anonymous"), received
            expected_path = "/api/v1/trending?kind=skills&limit=20" if trending else "/api/v1/search?q=fixture-redaction"
            assert received[0]["path"] == expected_path, received
            output = stdout + stderr
            if mode == "success":
                assert status == 0 and stderr == "", (status, stderr)
                result = json.loads(stdout)["results"]
                assert len(result) == 1 and result[0]["slug"] == "fixture-result" and result[0]["summary"] == "SAFE_RESULT_TEXT", result
            else:
                assert status == 1 and marker in output and "400" in output, (status, output)
                if json_mode:
                    failure = json.loads(stdout)
                    assert failure["ok"] is False and failure["error"]["type"] == "cli_error", failure
                else:
                    assert stdout == "" and marker in stderr, (stdout, stderr)
            present = token in output
            assert present == (mode == "reflection" and args.phase == "base"), (name, args.phase, "Unexpected credential-presence observation")
            after = {p.name: hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in [config, auth]}
            assert before == after, "Configuration/credential bytes changed"
            records.append({"case": name, "source": source, "mode": mode, "trending": trending, "json": json_mode, "command": command, "status": status, "requests": received, "stdout": stdout, "stderr": stderr, "sentinelPresent": present, "safeMarkerPresent": marker in output, "configAndCredentialBytesUnchanged": before == after, "elapsedMs": round((time.monotonic() - at) * 1000)})
    receipt = {"phase": args.phase, "head": head, "at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()), "buildInfo": build, "inputsClean": stamp["inputsClean"], "collectorSha256": hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest(), "helpStatus": help_status, "records": records, "cleanup": "all children completed without timeout; all peers closed/joined; temporary HOME/config/state removed", "elapsedMs": round((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000)}
    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2))
    print(json.dumps({"output": str(args.output), "phase": args.phase, "head": head, "cases": len(records), "collectorSha256": receipt["collectorSha256"], "elapsedMs": receipt["elapsedMs"]}))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the chat @mention picker labels a guest as `Person <ID>` when they have a verified GitHub handle but no saved display name.

## User Impact

User impact: unnamed guests with a linked verified GitHub account appear under a recognizable handle in the mention picker, including when offline. Saved display names still take precedence; email addresses are not used as a fallback. This addresses the anonymous-label case, not every possible missing-search-result report. No migration or permission change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The directory already searches verified GitHub handles. Reuse one of those handles for the visible label when the saved name is absent, before falling back to the existing neutral person label. No new state, lookup, or eligibility rule is introduced.

## Evidence

- The regression is folded into the existing verified-handle/name test: clear the saved name, then assert that the same profile is labeled with its verified handle. Named-profile, alias, and permission coverage remain in the existing suites; no new test case is added.

That browser fixture uses a mocked Gateway; the regression exercises the real `users.mentionable` handler.

Closes #187847.

## What Problem This Solves

The explicit command-timeout forwarding test can fail with `599999` instead of `600000` after maintenance-budget accounting moved to the monotonic clock. Its existing zero-elapsed fixture controls only wall time, leaving actual preflight elapsed time in an assertion intended to verify timeout forwarding.

## User Impact

This restores deterministic coverage of the explicit timeout contract. Production timeout accounting and command behavior are unchanged, including the requirement that real maintenance consumes its elapsed budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Freeze `performance.now()` at zero alongside the existing `Date.now()` freeze in this one case. Both exact, independent `600000` assertions still observe the real command/preflight/attempt boundary, and the existing awaited reset followed by mock restoration owns cleanup. Inlining the wall-clock snapshot keeps the test-line delta at zero.

## Evidence

The unchanged complete owner reproduced the exact assertion failure on `0fa1e0d`: 92 passed, one failed, with the second override assertion unreached. The corrected complete owner and the existing embedded-maintenance owner then passed all 114 cases on pinned Bun `191755ec1` / Vitest `5.0.5` through the maintained `infra` runner. Both timeout assertions now pass; the elapsed-budget, wall-clock rewind, unlimited, expiry/drain, and reply-lifecycle controls remain green. The combined two-file run took 29.15 seconds; this is focused coverage, not a broad CI-health claim.

Changed-file format/lint, the affected test type graph, and the canonical test-line check passed. No case, assertion, shared ceiling, allocation, or production code was changed. PR CI and independent reviews remain pending.

prs.title: fix(doctor): preserve legacy upgrade state and diagnostics
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177381

## What problem this solves

Legacy upgrades can fail backup discovery before Doctor retires valid heartbeat configuration, or retain legacy session stores after importing native assignments whose optional lifecycle revisions are absent. Doctor can also report pending state migrations when current database contents are valid but the published schema header is deliberately deferred for an unfenced older updater.

The repair preserves original backup bytes, native assignment ownership, and accurate state diagnostics. Malformed configuration, uncertain identity, stale assignments, and invalid database ownership or catalogs retain their refusal behavior. No configuration surface, schema version, execution permission, port admission, or publication fence changes.

## Owner changes

- Backup discovery selects the existing validated, read-only heartbeat projection. Writable automatic repair still cannot retire heartbeat before durable migration; original archive bytes and environment-reference provenance remain intact.
- Native assignment repair accepts equally absent optional lifecycle revisions only after binding-key, physical-session, and connection-fingerprint checks. One-sided absence remains unknown and populated mismatches remain stale. Released 2026.9.4 emitted optional host lifecycle revisions.
- State diagnostics use the canonical effective content version and full read-only maintenance admission on their existing private snapshot. The strict port descriptor stays unchanged. Decode failures retain the raw header; owner refusal after successful decoding retains the effective version. Async snapshot cleanup, service custody and non-state port preparation remain intact.

prs.title: fix(ui): chat composer requires Tabbing through every transcript control
prs.body:
Closes #180815

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where keyboard users Tabbing forward in the Control UI chat had to traverse every focusable control in the loaded transcript (126 stops in the reporter's session, growing with history) before reaching the composer. The only existing skip target ("Skip to main content") lands on the whole main area — before the transcript — and Shift+Tab from the top, while shorter, is undiscoverable.

- **Related:** #154524 (message headings for screen-reader navigation, distinct), #127321 (message-menu navigation, distinct), #180814 (transcript accessible name, distinct). None overlap with this change.

## User Impact

User impact: keyboard-only and screen-reader users can now reach the message composer in a few keystrokes — a "Skip to message composer" bypass sits in the forward tab order immediately before the transcript region and moves focus straight to the composer on activation. When the composer is unavailable (e.g. an archived session replaces it with a banner), activation lands on that recovery banner (its action, such as **Unarchive**, stays the next tab stop) instead of doing nothing, so the bypass always moves focus to something useful. Transcript controls remain individually reachable; the bypass only adds one stop before them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The chat view renders the transcript before the composer in DOM/tab order, and nothing between the session header and the transcript offered a way past the message controls. The bypass mirrors the shell's existing visually-hidden-until-focused skip-link pattern, reuses the pane's existing composer-focus path (`onFocusComposer`, which also targets the recovery composer), and is pane-scoped so split panes each get the correct target. Embedded suggestion composers (no transcript) are excluded. The shared focus path now falls back to lifetime-bound recovery targets — the composer-replacement banner registered through the composer's ref mechanism, or the already-bound footer as a programmatic-only (`tabindex="-1"`) focus target — when neither the composer textarea nor a plugin replacement element can receive focus, so states like an archived session cannot turn activation into a no-op. Refs, not DOM searches: focus routing stays on exact owned elements.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Playwright Chromium e2e against the built Control UI served by the repo's e2e harness (mocked Gateway data), in an isolated worktree of this branch — covering both the normal composer and an archived session whose composer is replaced by the recovery banner.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view-skip-link.test.ts                        # regression unit tests (fallback cases RED before fix, GREEN after)
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/e2e/chat-composer-skip-link.e2e.test.ts                     # real-browser tab-order + activation proof, incl. unavailable-composer case
  bash skills/fix-pr/scripts/validate.sh ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.tsx ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view-skip-link.test.ts ui/src/e2e/chat-composer-skip-link.e2e.test.ts  # oxfmt + oxlint + same-directory vitest + tsgo:core
  pnpm ui:i18n:verify
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-chat.json --builders 1
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e-chat.json --builders 1
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** 
  ```text
  ui/src/e2e/chat-composer-skip-link.e2e.test.ts
   ✓ reaches the composer skip link before transcript controls and focuses the composer on activation
   ✓ lands on the recovery surface when the composer is unavailable (archived session)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  2 passed (2)
  ```
  The e2e walks the real forward tab order from the top of the document in Chromium: the `button.chat-skip-link` stop is reached strictly before the `.chat-thread[role="log"]` region; pressing Enter moves focus to the composer textarea; the link enters the viewport on focus (hidden until focused, like the shell skip link). The archived-session case mocks an archived selected session (composer replaced by the banner, textarea absent) and asserts Enter moves focus to the recovery banner (programmatic `tabindex="-1"` target) with its Unarchive action reachable as the next tab stop, instead of leaving focus on the bypass. Regression unit tests cover the embedded-suggestion exclusion and both fallback states (recovery banner; footer as programmatic-only target) — the fallback cases fail before the fix because activation left focus on the bypass (matching the review finding).
- **Visual proof (running Control UI, mocked-Gateway e2e harness):** forward Tab focused the bypass before any transcript control: ![skip link focused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81350d0b-5f0e-4ecb-9717-7678aa4e64b8) — Enter after the bypass focused the composer textarea: ![composer focused after skip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fcd73479-8a71-4b81-b44d-a43200502387) — archived session (composer unavailable): Enter focused the recovery banner, and the next Tab focused its Unarchive action: ![archived recovery focused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c27cfcb-15bd-4587-a7cd-f13110257a9c). Captures were inspected: the skip-link capture differs from the composer-focused capture exactly in the top band (the bypass appears only while focused) and the composer band, with the transcript unchanged between them.
- **Observed result after fix:** forward Tab reaches "Skip to message composer" before any transcript control; Enter focuses the composer in one keystroke instead of 126+; when the composer is unavailable (archived session), Enter focuses the recovery banner with the Unarchive action as the next tab stop, rather than stranding focus on the bypass.
- **Before evidence:** without the fix, the regression test fails (`Error: expected composer skip link`) — no bypass existed between the session header and the transcript, matching the reporter's tab-stop count; the archived-session fallback tests likewise failed before the fix because activation left focus on the bypass.
- **What was not tested:** screen-reader announcements specifically (NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver narration), and non-English locales beyond the i18n verify pass; the bypass label falls back to the English catalog entry like every other string.
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** none
- **Review state:** Addressed the review's focus-destination finding and attached the requested visual proof; CI lanes pending on the new head.

---

> **AI-assisted: yes**

prs.title: fix(ui): let keyboard users skip to the composer
prs.body:
Related: #180815

## What Problem This Solves

Keyboard users entering a loaded chat must traverse transcript controls before reaching the message composer; the shell's existing skip link lands on the main region rather than the composer.

## User Impact

A focus-visible “Skip to message composer” link lets keyboard users bypass the transcript with Tab and Enter. Transcript controls remain normally reachable. When an archived session has no composer, the bypass lands on the footer and the next Tab reaches Unarchive.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing pane-level `onFocusComposer` path, a lifetime-bound footer ref, and the shell's existing skip-link style. The link sits before the transcript, has a pane-unique footer target, and is omitted from embedded suggestion composers. No global keyboard handler, DOM search, duplicated skip stylesheet, or separate recovery-banner registration is needed.

Includes #180917, preserving the original commits by @goutamadwant and @LiuwqGit. The two proposals are consolidated at one focus owner, not stacked as competing bypasses.

## Evidence

[Built-Gateway native-keyboard proof and inspected before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180896#issuecomment-6506667943)

Real Chromium exercised independently built main and candidate Gateways with their production Control UI bundles. On main, twice, the shell bypass lands on MAIN and forward Tab enters the transcript without a composer bypass. On the candidate, twice, native Tab reaches the new link before any transcript stop and native Enter focuses the actual textarea. Settled screenshots show the focus-visible link and composer caret.

Archived-session controls ran twice per revision: main traverses 21/22 transcript focus stops before Unarchive; candidate Enter focuses the footer and one additional Tab reaches Unarchive, without entering the transcript. Native Tab/Enter still activates Reply and opens its preview on both revisions. No screen-reader claim is made.

The existing footer/history/draft-preservation regression activates the bypass rather than directly focusing the textarea. It fails on main because the bypass is absent; candidate focused tests pass 2/2. Tests are net zero (+1/−1), with no added test files. Production is +26/−3 (net +23). Duplicate proposal tests and recovery-only plumbing were removed without weakening the existing history, draft, and focus assertions.

Focused formatting and keyless i18n baseline generation pass. Type-aware lint reports zero errors and one warning in an unchanged inline `merge(...)` expression.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting removes the bypass and footer focus fallback; no persisted state, configuration, or protocol changes occur. Blast radius is keyboard focus navigation within Control UI chat panes; message delivery and transcript actions are unchanged.

prs.title: fix: installer PATH hints fail for paths containing apostrophes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Copying the installer's PATH repair command fails when the npm prefix contains
an apostrophe, leaving `openclaw` unavailable in the user's shell.

## User Impact

Users can copy the printed command into Bash or zsh and run OpenClaw from paths
containing spaces, apostrophes and exclamation marks.

## Why This Change Was Made

macOS Bash3.2 preserves backslashes in the existing quoted replacement expression.
Expanding the standard single-quote escape from a variable produces literal path
bytes and retains the existing hint format, including the managed Node hint.

## Evidence

- Exact base: `d6883bcbc4b76d9ba56ec737c133b600af0f2fdb`. The existing quoted-prefix
  and zsh regressions fail on the base and pass with this patch.
- Native replay on macOS arm64: the standalone installer printed commands for
  ordinary and `home 'quote' !event` paths. Native Bash3.2.57 and zsh5.9 executed
  them against an owned prefix pointing to the real installed OpenClaw2026.9.6
  CLI. Both quoted-path base commands failed; all four candidate cells resolved
  the intended executable and returned its version. Two interactive Bash
  controls also passed with history expansion enabled. Temporary state removed;
  the real CLI was used only for `--version` with an isolated HOME.
- Full owning/assembly suites: **228 passed, 1 existing availability skip**
  across `install-sh.test.ts` and `standalone-installers.test.ts`;61.72s wall,
  60.45s aggregate test time. The targeted PATH cases also pass independently.
- Native Bash syntax and `git diff --check` pass. oxfmt excludes shell scripts;
  shellcheck is unavailable locally. No TypeScript inputs changed.
- Canonical Codex autoreview of the complete patch: P0–P3 **scoped-clean**.
  This was an independent static review of the supplied patch/tests; the reviewer
  did not execute project code.

This changes emitted shell text only, with no persisted state or upgrade step.
The existing meaningful regressions cover the defect; no duplicate tests added.

<details>
<summary>Native result and reproduction</summary>

```text
                             base       candidate
Bash / ordinary path         exit0      exit0, intended CLI found
zsh / ordinary path          exit0      exit0, intended CLI found
Bash / quoted path           exit2      exit0, intended CLI found
zsh / quoted path            exit1      exit0, intended CLI found
interactive Bash, history on             both candidate paths pass
```

The base prints an unmatched-quote command; the candidate prints the standard
single-quote escape. The runtime replay used the assembled standalone installer,
called `warn_shell_path_missing_dir` with the owned path, then executed its actual
printed command followed by `command -v openclaw; openclaw --version` in the
native caller shell. No PATH repair string was fabricated by the harness.

Maintained regression command:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 -t 'working PATH remedy|literal-safe direct PATH remedy|activates and persists'
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts \
  test/scripts/standalone-installers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

- [x] I understand what this change does.

prs.title: fix(ios): chat stalls while typing and receiving background events
prs.body:
Related: #124759

## What Problem This Solves

Native chat can stall during typing and background session activity, including with an empty transcript or hidden tool activity.

## User Impact

Removes unnecessary work competing with typing and scrolling while preserving model selection, sign-in, session refresh, settings, approvals and Talk behavior. This is a partial performance repair; it does not establish that all lag reported in #124759 is resolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Closed model menus eagerly group the full catalog while constructing composer controls. Their contents now use the existing deferred-content view. Sidebar and operator listeners filter their own event names on the Gateway actor before unrelated frames enter their bounded buffers or MainActor loops. Explicit cancellation releases replaced and stopped subscriptions; the sidebar's refresh-coordinator cleanup remains intact.

The original development-fork work also hoisted Home's alias lookup. That change is omitted here because #169197 already caches alias resolution on upstream. The port preserves current-main menu sign-in/disabled behavior and carries no development signing or build settings. One inherited empty-string assertion uses `isEmpty` to pass the pinned lint check; the broader formatting-only changes from the fork are omitted.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: constructing closed clean and full model pickers with 2,000 synthetic catalog entries must not observe projection-only favorites/recents; background subscriptions must retain their owner events after 500 unrelated frames exceed the 200-frame buffer. These are deterministic work/retention checks, with no wall-clock thresholds or inferred device speedup.

- On upstream base `b367b1fd64d8daa5f91aa7a8a78b9a90f92d0df6`, both new composer cases fail because changing favorites/recents invokes the observation callback. With the patch, both pass and the callback remains at zero. The candidate regression takes 0.121 seconds; no timing threshold is asserted.
- Fresh Xcode 27.1 / Swift 6.4 shared-package validation passed 120 tests in four suites (31.911 seconds of test runtime; 65.813 seconds for the incremental compile/test command). This includes composer state, model picker/selection and Gateway event-subscription tests.
- All six files pass SwiftFormat 0.63.1, SwiftLint 0.65.1 and Swift syntax parsing. Normal pre-commit protocol/determinism and native-i18n checks pass.
- Local AutoReview completed a full P0-P2 assessment of the functional patch against the base above, with no actionable findings. The subsequent one-line assertion cleanup is behavior preserving and passes the same focused checks.
- Current-upstream iOS app-specific event regression execution and physical-device latency profiling remain unverified. Hosted CI is pending; the shared-package result does not replace those checks.
- Prior development-fork verification passed 82 focused native tests on each iPhone and iPad simulator, including the event-buffer regressions, plus typing, model-menu, scrolling and draft-retention interactions. Those runs cover the original fork, not this new upstream base.
- A physical-iPhone user reported that the combined development build was substantially more usable, with minor stutters remaining. The build includes other fork changes, so this is subjective combined-build feedback, not an isolated measurement of this patch.
- Original implementation and review context: https://github.com/ben-milanko/openclaw/pull/13. No dependency on that fork's other changes is introduced.

Prepared by Alder, Ben's AI assistant, on Ben's behalf.

prs.title: feat(whatsapp): expose group membership actors to plugins
prs.body:
Related: #8495 (the group-event portion only; this proposal adds no auto-leave behavior).

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins cannot see who added the connected WhatsApp account to a group.

## User Impact

Plugins with the existing conversation-access grant can observe membership actors and affected participants, including groups whose messages are disabled. The proposed consumer is an operator-owned, read-only context plugin that uses configured trusted inviters as input to its group-admission policy.

Notifications are best effort and may repeat. A missing actor stays unknown, and a roster observation alone does not prove a new invitation. Group admission, tool access and send policy retain their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The observe-only `channel_group_membership_changed` hook carries event-scoped actor IDs, provider-supplied phone-number identities, affected participants and the connected account's identities. WhatsApp publishes live notifications through the existing hook runner and channel SDK subpath. The source connection owns cancellation; the timeout reference now lists the hook's two-second default.

Emitter calls rely on the existing [native plugin trust boundary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/SECURITY.md#plugin-trust-boundary). The conversation-access grant controls observer registration and dispatch. This draft proposes the public observation contract; it adds no configuration, storage or automatic approval rule.

## Evidence

- Both new socket-to-hook tests fail on base `bde3017359ed` because no event reaches the plugin, and pass with the patch. The full WhatsApp command passes, including 1,024 Vitest tests.
- A CJS fixture loaded through the production `loadOpenClawPlugins` proves no callback without the conversation grant, delivery with it, and no callback after native replacement removes it. The retained global-runner reference also sees the revocation. This case and the neighboring replacement regression pass.
- Core and WhatsApp consumer type checks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, SDK export synchronization and the existing test budget pass.
- Full build exited 0 on `5ca7ee39dff2`, including verification of all 160 public SDK subpaths. The review follow-up changes tests and documentation only. The build printed an advisory chat-boot gzip result of 1,276,937 B against 1,276,669 B; no budget was changed or base comparison made for that advisory.
- The committed SDK API comparison was stopped locally before completion; it produced no compatibility verdict. Current plugin/extension import-boundary checks and lint for the loader regression pass.

The local SDK declaration preflight exceeded its default five-minute limit. Generation and targeted lint passed with the supported `OPENCLAW_PLUGIN_SDK_BOUNDARY_ROOT_SHIMS_TIMEOUT_MS=1200000` setting. The broader plugin-contract aggregate was stopped after 20 minutes; reported SDK and entry guard cases passed, but there is no aggregate pass.

The simplification pass kept the existing socket, hook and SDK owners: +103 production lines and +233 testing lines, including routing, against the base. The loader test replaces weaker registration-only coverage. The tests fit the existing budget without raising its ceiling. Independent reviews found no actionable issue in the implementation or review follow-up. Fixtures are synthetic.

## Still Needed Before Merge

A redacted real WhatsApp membership notification through a loaded plugin remains outstanding; no live invitation or deployment was exercised. Maintainers also need to accept the concrete consumer and the pre-admission actor/roster disclosure under the existing conversation-access grant. The outstanding API comparison and broader required CI checks also remain before merge. This remains a draft for the contract decision.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep live standing grants through approval retention
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Always allow on a gateway automation mints a standing grant that should last until it is revoked, or until the expiry frozen at mint time. `tools.exec.grantExpiryDays` and `grantExpiresInDays` allow that expiry to be unset or as long as 3650 days.

Terminal approval rows are deleted 30 days after they resolve. The standing grant's `minted_by_approval_id` references that row with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, and the state database opens with foreign keys on. The same delete runs again when a later approval is inserted. After the parent row is gone, grant lookup returns `approval-missing` or `no-grant`, so the next matching automation run prompts again. A missing approval still stops the grant. Routine retention should not delete an approval that still anchors an unrevoked grant with no expiry, or with an expiry still in the future.

## Test-line ceiling

The standing-grant retention tests add 298 lines. Current main is already past `config/test-lines-baseline.txt`. The merged tree counted 6286755 test lines, 352 over the previous ceiling of 6286403. This branch sets the ceiling to that counted total.

## Evidence

Proved head `2be949460ef7840830bfea2f4c1c4a1cf8456ca7`. macOS arm64, Node v26.11.0. Isolated state directory and config. Gateway bound to loopback. `tools.exec.mode` is `ask` and `tools.exec.host` is `gateway`. Commands were `node scripts/run-node.mjs` from this branch. No Control UI click.

A connected operator client with the `approvals` and `exec-approvals` capabilities stayed on the gateway so an automation run could wait. Each answer was the shipped `approvals resolve` command. A one-shot CLI call does not stay connected as an approval route.

The cron job `aged-grant` (`4b234345-6955-4bd7-8e68-3e0b31d5f22e`) asks the agent to exec `/bin/echo aged-grant-launch` once. `approvals resolve <id> allow-always` minted grant `c7c1a8b5-7d5f-4b42-880d-7a53de707504` from approval `22c9052e-0a5d-4f83-8be3-bb4c4018596e`, with `expiresAtMs` null. That in-flight exec completed. Its tool result was status `completed`, exit code 0, text `aged-grant-launch` (session `db29f7e1`). The grant's `useCount` was still 0, because that spawn was the live approval.

The gateway was then stopped. That approval's `created_at_ms` and `resolved_at_ms` were moved 31 days earlier (`2678400000` ms). The grant row was not rewritten. After `gateway run` again, `approvals grants list` still returned the same grant, `expiresAtMs` null, `useCount` 0. The schema files in this diff did not change.

The next `cron run` of the same job launched with no new `exec.approval.requested` event. `useCount` became 1 and `lastUsedAtMs` became `1791976462271`.

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs cron run 4b234345-6955-4bd7-8e68-3e0b31d5f22e --wait --json
status: ok
completionStatus: succeeded
summary: aged-grant-launch
jobId: 4b234345-6955-4bd7-8e68-3e0b31d5f22e
sessionId: 351851a8-e2fa-42e1-ab19-cd5432532da0
durationMs: 24633
model: grok-4.3
```

Tool result for session `351851a8`: status `completed`, exit code 0, text `aged-grant-launch`.

Three forbidden runs then asked for a new approval. Each was `approvals resolve <id> deny`. None completed an exec, and `useCount` stayed 1.

| Run | Shipped result | Tool result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Job `130223bb-67bf-49e4-b07d-6e6561852c56`, command `/bin/echo not-the-grant`, agent `main` | approval `d8841a88-a776-45b1-a535-b0a6bcfe9dd6` denied. Cron status `error`: exec denied by gateway | status `failed`, no exit code |
| Job `b5364a97-eb7d-41d0-a6eb-4953ef4deb86`, same echo command, agent `main` | approval `5ee56dca-4bc8-420d-b325-49fb109b5a80` denied. Cron status `error` | status `failed`, no exit code |
| Job `58f6abf4-c3a5-4a47-b56e-c1b9f99aefe3`, same echo command, agent `other` | approval `e6817cc9-7fc0-41cf-9b6b-73276166a56d` denied. Source agent `other`. Cron status `error` | status `failed`, no exit code |

`approvals grants revoke c7c1a8b5-7d5f-4b42-880d-7a53de707504` returned `outcome: revoked`. The following list still showed that grant, `useCount` 1, `revokedAtMs` `1791976920376`, `revokedBy` `cli`, `lastUsedAtMs` unchanged. The next `cron run` of `4b234345-6955-4bd7-8e68-3e0b31d5f22e` emitted a new approval, `350726f9-2bae-48eb-9f0c-7f158b74d9c6`. Deny left the tool result status `failed` with no exit code. Cron status was `error`. After that write, `approvals grants list` returned no grants. The revoked grant no longer kept the 31-day-old approval.

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs approvals grants list --json
{"grants":[{"grantId":"c7c1a8b5-7d5f-4b42-880d-7a53de707504","mintedByApprovalId":"22c9052e-0a5d-4f83-8be3-bb4c4018596e","agentId":"main","cronJobId":"4b234345-6955-4bd7-8e68-3e0b31d5f22e","cronJobName":"aged-grant","command":"/bin/echo aged-grant-launch","expiresAtMs":null,"revokedAtMs":null,"lastUsedAtMs":1791976462271,"useCount":1}]}
```

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs approvals grants list --json
{"grants":[]}
```

The first list is after the aged launch and the three denials. The second list is after revoke plus the denied rerun.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A standing grant minted by allow-always still launches its cron command after the parent approval is 31 days old and the gateway has restarted. A different command, a different cron job, and a different agent do not launch. Revoking the grant before the next run makes that same job ask again, and denying the ask does not launch.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64, Node v26.11.0, OpenClaw head `2be949460ef`. Isolated state directory. Loopback gateway. Exec mode `ask`, host `gateway`. Shipped `node scripts/run-node.mjs` gateway, cron, and approvals commands. A connected operator client received approval events.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run` on the branch. `node scripts/run-node.mjs cron run <job> --wait --json` for the aged job, the forbidden command, the other job, the other agent, and the same job after revoke. `node scripts/run-node.mjs approvals resolve <id> allow-always` once, then `deny` for every later request. `node scripts/run-node.mjs approvals grants list --json` and `approvals grants revoke <grantId>`.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from those shipped commands.

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs cron run 4b234345-6955-4bd7-8e68-3e0b31d5f22e --wait --json
status: ok
summary: aged-grant-launch
sessionId: 351851a8-e2fa-42e1-ab19-cd5432532da0
tool: status completed, exit code 0, text aged-grant-launch
grant useCount: 1
approval event during that run: none
```

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs approvals grants revoke c7c1a8b5-7d5f-4b42-880d-7a53de707504 --json
{"outcome":"revoked"}
```

Forbidden command, other job, and agent `other` each produced `exec.approval.requested`, then a denied tool result with status `failed` and no exit code. After revoke, job `4b234345-6955-4bd7-8e68-3e0b31d5f22e` did the same. The later grants list was `{"grants":[]}`.

- **Observed result after fix:** The aged grant launched `/bin/echo aged-grant-launch` through cron after the gateway restart, with exit code 0 and no new approval. The three mismatched runs did not launch and did not increase `useCount`. After revoke, the original job asked again and the denied exec did not launch.
- **What was not tested:** A Control UI click. A revoke that lands after the grant is consumed and before the process is created. A second gateway built from the merge base. A copy of a production state database from another machine.

## Summary

Startup recovery and the retention delete inside approval insert share one query. That query skips an approval while an unrevoked standing grant names it and `expires_at_ms` is null or still in the future. Revocation, and a later approval write, still drop a parent that is past 30 days. This trace replaces the earlier helper-script transcript. It does not time a revoke between consume and spawn.

prs.title: fix(memory): indexing still fails when a gateway truncates the embedding batch-limit error
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: memory indexing fails terminally when an embedding endpoint rejects an oversized batch but a wrapping gateway pushes the batch-limit text (`batch size is invalid, it should not be larger than 10`) past the 220-char error-detail truncation, so the split-on-error recovery from #138391 never matches.

Closes #187788
Related: #137864, #129750, #140508, #141686

## User Impact

Memory indexing against wrapping gateways (a common shape for Java-based OpenAI-compatible gateways in front of DashScope and similar providers) recovers through the existing split path instead of failing terminally on every rebuild. Endpoints that return their error verbatim behave exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

#138391 and #140508 made reactive recovery split rejected batches using the provider's reported item cap. Both rely on the formatted error message, whose detail is truncated to 220 chars by `truncateErrorDetail` in `src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts`. Gateways that report their own wrapped exception string (rather than an OpenAI-style `error.message`) push the recognized wording past that preview — in the reproduced case the marker starts around char 260 — so the classifier never sees it and the whole index run fails.

This matters more since #141686: custom endpoints deliberately remain undeclared (`maxInputsPerRequest` is a provider-plugin contract only), so reactive splitting is the only recovery path for them.

The fix makes `embeddingRetryMessage` in the memory embedding policy append the already-preserved, bounded, redacted `ProviderHttpError.errorBody` preview to the searchable text. Safety notes:

- `errorBody` only exists on `ProviderHttpError`, which always carries an HTTP status; `resolveMemoryEmbeddingRetryBudget` checks status before any message-based classification, so retry budgets are unchanged. Transport-level errors have no body at all.
- `parseMemoryEmbeddingBatchItemLimit` runs on the joined text, so the cap parsed from the body now sizes the split directly (33 -> 10/10/10/3) instead of bisecting.
- The same extend-beyond-the-truncated-message approach was accepted for the thinking-recovery classifier in #161118 / #163662.

Deliberately out of scope: no new user-facing config. #141686 records the maintainer decision to keep `maxInputsPerRequest` a provider-plugin contract with custom endpoints undeclared.

## Evidence

- [Built-artifact main/candidate indexing and Gateway-search proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187797#issuecomment-6504583554): wrapped 400 twice per ref, unwrapped-cap and no-cap controls, and 33 ordered persisted vectors.

- Existing ordered-batch regression now covers a preserved wrapped-body cap with 33 inputs and `[33,10,10,10,3]` requests, ordered outputs, and per-slice cache candidates. [Consolidation evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187797#issuecomment-6505162119). Total PR test-line delta: 0.
- Focused suites pass: `manager-embedding-policy.test.ts` + `manager-embedding-ops.retry.test.ts` (86 tests), including all pre-existing splittable/non-splittable boundaries.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm format:check` pass.
- Live reproduction of the failure this fixes (wrapping gateway returns 400 with the full DashScope message; the message OpenClaw matches on is truncated at `messa…`) is in the linked issue. The affected code paths are unchanged on current `main` relative to the versions where this was observed (2026.10.8 release dists).

<details>
<summary>Failure being fixed (from the linked issue)</summary>

```
Memory index failed (main): openai embeddings failed (400): com.openai.errors.BadRequestException: 400: HTTP请求失败: response=Response{protocol=h2, code=400, message=, url=https://<gateway>/v1/embeddings}, body={"error":{"messa… [request_id=…]
```

Same gateway via curl: 10 inputs -> HTTP 200; 25 inputs -> HTTP 400 with `batch size is invalid, it should not be larger than 10` present only past the 220-char point of the wrapped error string.
</details>

The production export check still finds the unclaimed session-delivery producer after #185730 removed its production callers. Its remaining consumers construct persisted-state fixtures, leaving an unused host API and its exclusive record builder in production source.

## User Impact

There is no intended user-visible change. Claimed delivery, correlated completion, recovery, durable settlement, and media retention keep their existing behavior. Existing unclaimed rows remain readable; no schema or configuration migration is introduced.

The unused host function and record builder are removed. The existing test helper now composes equivalent unclaimed fixtures through the same session admission and SQLite worker command, preserving construction and serialization order and requiring the caller's captured context.

The restart-sentinel tests observe real session-delivery publication attempts through the existing worker probe. All six negative checkpoints remain, and an existing generated-media case verifies that the observer sees a real publication. One allocation covers exactly 68 additional test lines; the shared baseline and per-file caps are unchanged.

prs.title: improve(ci): isolate installed recovery checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Installed-package recovery cuts need independent scheduler cells so one interruption or timeout cannot erase the remaining campaign or its diagnostic receipt.

## User Impact

Release maintainers can select `package-installed-recovery` to schedule seven finite cuts independently. Product runtime is unchanged. All seven real-package cells and healthy follow-up updates passed on the earlier `ada1731` harness. **The published candidate's source CI is failed and its applicable Claw review is still missing. A further local baseline refresh remains unpublished because complete source review is blocked by the supported review capacity. The selected package's installed-entry budget remains failed.**

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the scheduler half split from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177381. Each cell uses one verified package, a private attempt directory and the existing process-group owner. The host publishes bounded, sanitized evidence after the lane group joins; missing publication preserves the lane outcome and fails the scheduler.

The composition preserves the landed timeout precedence, deferred-schema witness (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187502), and npm inventory owner (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187493). It does not resolve Doctor's final packaged compatibility hold in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186506.

The 24-path authored delta remains 1,121 lines of churn: harness +608/−84, tests +403/−22, metadata +3/−1, installed product runtime 0. The added harness code owns finite scheduling, joined publication, package identity and controlled evidence access.

## Real Package and Access Evidence


[Package Acceptance run 40855531828, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40855531828) ran the exact harness `ada1731befad961c7e3d39f1a65a16a9627a3df8` with selected package source `55de928c20e021a97e98c00b2109f769de301ea6`, version `2026.10.8`, and TGZ SHA-256 `7e28f620e1a7b55eeb29f725d70d66f68fb439f64c5f2be3f1758c397ce1324d`. The verified retained producer was run `40646385499/1`, artifact `12798427170`; this run reused that package through the existing artifact admission.

Each cut ran once, recovered through the independent installed helper, preserved the package/launchers/full configuration, recorded the original writer and command groups joined, and completed a distinct healthy sequence-7 update with an `anchor-retired` receipt. Every lane has exit 0, publication status 0, no timeout, and joined cleanup. The derived same-schema versions are `2026.10.9-first-hop.0` through `.6`, followed by `.7`; these are package fixtures, not claims about published releases.

| Cut | One attempt | Sanitized receipt artifact |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| partial-previous | 673 s | [12890387481](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40855531828/artifacts/12890387481) |
| anchor-before | 869 s | [12890109358](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40855531828/artifacts/12890109358) |
| anchor-after | 552 s | [12890496742](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40855531828/artifacts/12890496742) |
| anchor-sync | 768 s | [12890542129](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40855531828/artifacts/12890542129) |
| helper-before | 677 s | [12889944348](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40855531828/artifacts/12889944348) |
| helper-after | 864 s | [12890652286](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40855531828/artifacts/12890652286) |
