prs.title: fix: overflow summaries lose the summarized message's sender and room-event context
prs.body:
Related: #182176
Split from #182553 at a maintainer's request: this PR is only the drain-side restore. The `Queued #N context:` model-facing labels stay in #182553 for the prompt owner's call.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a busy turn lets the follow-up queue reach its cap, a message replayed from the overflow summary reaches the model without its sender and message context, and a summarized room event loses its "observed room activity, not a request" instructions.

## User Impact

User impact: in busy group rooms, a request replayed from an overflow summary still tells the agent who asked and in which message, and a replayed room event is still framed as ambient context.

## Why This Change Was Made

Overflow summary turns kept the `room_event` kind (#99145) but explicitly cleared `currentInboundContext`. The clear came from #90943, which made summaries standalone turns and kept the *live* item's runtime metadata out of them; #175837 carried it into the mailbox as an unconditional clear. Summary claims now have their own sources, so they can carry exactly those sources' contexts without touching the live item:

- Summary claims take context from the summarized sources through the existing collect pairing (`collectCurrentInboundContext`, now exported), limited to the sources whose lines the prompt shows (the newest `cap`). Summary claims only group sources with the same delivery and authorization key, and room events drain alone, so one sender's context is never applied to another sender's line. Run-level authority is unchanged (`resolveCollectedRun`).
- The compact retry source used for elided summary lines keeps its context.

No prompt text is added: a single-source summary carries that source's context unchanged, and a multi-source summary uses the same pairing collected turns already use. Which entries overflow evicts is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Live model, real Gateway** (QA Lab: isolated state and ports, the real Telegram plugin against the Crabline Bot API, live `claude-cli/claude-haiku-5-5`, `messages.queue: { mode: followup, cap: 2 }`, `unmentionedInbound: room_event`). An operator mention starts a ~20 s story turn; four group messages arrive while it is active, so the two oldest overflow into summary turns. The tables show what the model received with each summary turn and what it did.

Room events (Dee, Bea summarized; Cy and Ada's mention run normally):

| Summary turn | Base | This head |
|---|---|---|
| Dee, room event | no inbound context at all (only the date block); model replied in the group: "No, I haven't restarted any printer. I have no access to the printer from here…" | `[OpenClaw room event]`, Dee's Conversation info (`sender 200004 Dee`, `message_id 3`, `inbound_event_kind: room_event`) and the "observed room activity, not a request" rule; model: `NO_REPLY` |
| Bea, room event | no inbound context; model answered the chatter ("Noted: BEA-ROOM-P4M8 is back online…"), not delivered to the group in this run | same framing with Bea's own info (`200002`, `message_id 4`); model: `NO_REPLY` |

Four mentions, each "please greet me by my first name and include the code X" (Bea, Cy summarized):

| Summary turn | Base | This head |
|---|---|---|
| Bea | no inbound context; reply: "Hello, QA Operator. Code: BEA-P4M8. I only have the display name QA Operator for you…" (the operator who started the busy turn) | Bea's Conversation info only (`200002`, `message_id 3`); reply: "Hello Bea! Your code is BEA-P4M8." |
| Cy | no inbound context; reply: "Hello, QA Operator. Code: CY-W9T3. I still don't have your first name…" | Cy's Conversation info only (`200003`, `message_id 4`); reply: "Hello Cy! Your code is CY-W9T3." |

Each summary turn on this head carried exactly one sender's context, its own.

**Regressions** (red on base production files, green here):
- `queue.overflow-context.test.ts` (new): a request evicted by room events replays with its own sender context; room-event framing survives an elided summary line.
- `queue.collect.test.ts`: the standalone and retry-after-preparation-failure summary tests now expect the summarized source's own context instead of none.
- `queue.pending-inputs.test.ts`: a two-source summary that shows only the newest line carries only that line's source context.

**Gates:** `tsgo` core and `oxlint` on touched files clean; `oxfmt --check` clean; the three touched test files pass (96 tests).

**Cost:** the new file runs in `unit-fast`, 2 tests in about 11 ms (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall 33 s, mostly cold transform).

**Gaps:** no Telegram userbot run on the Telegram Test Server (no leased credentials here); the Telegram plugin ran against the Crabline Bot API with a live model.

prs.title: fix: release failed Talk startup registrations
prs.body:
Fixes #187838

## What Problem This Solves

Talk can retain phantom active agent work when synchronous preparation fails after the consultation has registered its run. The original error reaches the caller, but the failed unowned attempt can leave its relay registration behind because backend argument preparation happens before the promise cleanup is attached.

## User Impact

A failed unowned consultation now releases its registration resources. Providers that explicitly adopt delayed completion claims retain their existing opportunity to report the failure exactly once; successful runs, asynchronous failure handling, cancellation authority, and newer registrations keep their existing ownership rules. No configuration, permission, schema, or public API change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime already has a synchronous startup catch. This change extends that catch over the existing backend argument construction and invocation, so a preparation exception follows the same cleanup path as other startup failures. The client runner withholds early registration release for adopted owners because failure reporting checks that registration before settling it. Both parts are needed: widening the catch alone would retire the owned failure claim too soon.

The regression stays in the existing native relay fixture, with real registration, RPC-source, and voice-binding owners. Its preparation callback throws at the boundary under test. The 72-line test allocation covers the net growth for unowned cleanup, owned exactly-once failure reporting, and a pre-registration failure control; the shared test ceiling and existing tests are unchanged.

## Evidence

On production revision b2c22d4f023a49029beae047bde8c23e2e249af3, the extended registration fixture passed 26 of 27 cases. The unowned synchronous tool-context case retained one active agent registration instead of zero. With only this runtime/client correction and the identical fixture, all 27 passed, including original error identity, owned `[true, false]` failure claims, and newer-registration protection. The file took 62.05 seconds wall time, primarily transformation/setup; test execution was approximately 9 seconds.

Changed formatting/lint and the ten selected native type-check command groups passed; that type result is partial coverage. All 200 tests in 12 importing consumer files also passed on the complete candidate, and the native allocation check passed with 54,498 lines of remaining headroom. Independent review and the separate canonical automated review are clean. In an isolated Gateway at this exact head, two natural spoken requests on the same Talk connection updated a saved checklist through the real provider and OpenClaw backend. prs.title: fix(update): stop Gateway respawn loops during Doctor maintenance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway respawn loops during update Doctor maintenance when the outgoing Gateway has already released its state lease but launchd still has its KeepAlive job loaded.

## User Impact

Candidate Doctor unloads the owned, enabled LaunchAgent before maintenance and retains the existing receipt so finalization can restore it, including with `--no-restart`. Unloaded or disabled services stay stopped; foreign installations and foreground-owner protections are unchanged. No schema, config, or CLI option changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

A process lease disappearing does not mean its supervisor is stopped. Remove the candidate's lease-liveness shortcut and let the existing native service owner decide whether a stop is needed. This is a candidate-side fix; it does not require changes in an already-installed updater.

Simplification: removes a duplicate ownership decision and obsolete lease mocks. The regression covers the missing-lease respawn window and the unloaded/disabled controls; worker tests cover native stop outcomes, receipt persistence, and uncertain cleanup refusal.

## Evidence

### Review follow-up (October 29)

Those untouched baseline issues are excluded from this repair; this is not a claim that the aggregate local gate passed.

This was PR-related: the worker repair removed two mocks without pruning their exact baseline entries. The native `--prune` generator removed only those two obsolete entries; the ratchet reproduced red and then passed against the actual tested base `4ec4620f6f0f`. prs.title: fix(tlon): keep automatic group replies at supported depth
prs.body:
Related: #187658 (automatic reply targets only; its separate mention-policy request remains open).

## What Problem This Solves

Automatic Tlon group replies target the triggering child reply instead of the existing thread root, and top-level mentions unexpectedly create threads. Tlon supports one reply level, so targeting a child can drop the response despite local delivery success.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing per-turn `implicitCurrentMessage: "deny"` policy for groups only. The existing durable delivery owner already selects the root or channel; implicit normalization must not override that choice. Explicit reply directives, direct messages, mention policy and authorization are unchanged. No new SDK/API/config/default or target-depth policy.

Original fix by @HootRock; thanks to @Somlus for reporting. Contributor commits retained. The separate mocked-ingress suite was replaced by coverage in an existing thread case and full built-Gateway protocol proof, with **zero test-registration growth**. Whole-PR delta: production +2/-0, tests +6/-1, docs +4/-0.

## Evidence

Full main/candidate builds on Node 24.22.1 in secretless Docker, actual Gateway and bundled Tlon plugin against external Urbit HTTP/SSE protocol endpoints: real login/cookie authentication, scries, subscriptions, SSE event/ack handling and HTTP pokes. Deterministic local model output runs through the real OpenClaw agent runtime, normalization and durable delivery.

After integrating main `cfb5923c5eb4d513e6d600ba599c91c875c3679e`, clean complete builds of main and merged head `5ac1a59dfb5ee35c302bfe19fad122d747f4fb14` reran one key thread turn and one DM control per build. Main targets child `5.678`; candidate targets root `1.234`; both DMs target the same ship. Fixture readback matches; each build has two completed ingress events and an empty delivery queue. Main's monitor changes concern citation expansion/settings installation, not reply destination selection.

[Merged-head Gateway wire and durable-state evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187820#issuecomment-6506161368).

Prior head `c9f4573cfe8fbf78f769bd1adfa22adea7c300bd` additionally passed the [twice-per-build/full-control matrix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187820#issuecomment-6505313476), formatting, the focused **19/19** suite and the [Telegram Test Server DM control](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187820#issuecomment-6505378545), whose QA lease was released. These remain prior-head evidence, not relabeled merged-head runs. This is protocol-fixture proof, **not native Urbit/client acceptance**.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert fully restores old routing with no migration. Blast radius is implicit automatic Tlon group reply targeting; explicit directives and DMs retain their current behavior. Mention/admission and auth policies are not changed.

prs.title: fix(wear): live Talk ends when the watch screen times out
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: live watch Talk ends mid-conversation when the watch screen times out while the mic is listening.

## User Impact

The watch screen stays on for as long as realtime Talk is active or the mic is capturing. It returns to the normal timeout as soon as Talk stops.

## Summary

### High Level TLDR

If the watch screen times out during a live Talk session, Android stops the activity, and the app ends Talk on `ON_STOP`. You are mid-sentence and the session just ends. This change holds the screen on only while Talk is live, the same way a call app does.

### Root Cause

- `MainActivity` registers a lifecycle observer that calls `viewModel.suspendRealtimeTalk()` on `Lifecycle.Event.ON_STOP`.
- `suspendRealtimeTalk()` calls `stopRealtimeTalk()` whenever `realtimeTalk.active || realtimeCapturing`.
- Nothing kept the display awake during that state. The normal Wear OS screen timeout therefore stopped the activity, and that ended the session.
- Ending Talk on `ON_STOP` is correct for real navigation away. It is the screen timeout that should not trigger it.

### Exact change

- Added a `DisposableEffect` keyed on `realtimeTalk.active || realtimeCapturing` that sets `view.keepScreenOn`.
- `onDispose` clears the flag, so leaving the composition never leaves the screen pinned.
- No change to the `ON_STOP` stop policy.

### Scope boundary

- Watch app only, with no phone or Gateway changes.
- Leaving the app (back, home, side button) still ends Talk as before.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- Debug build installed on a Galaxy Watch (Wear OS 5) and used for live Talk sessions.
- Talk stayed open past the normal screen timeout.
- System logs show the window's `SCREEN_BRIGHT_WAKE_LOCK` held for the whole live session. It was released within about 30 ms of the session ending (`state:paused` / `abandonAudioFocus` for the Talk track, followed by `[api] release WakeLock SCREEN_BRIGHT_WAKE_LOCK 'WindowManager/displayId:0'`).

### Verification

- `./gradlew :wear:ktlintCheck :wear:testDebugUnitTest` passed.
- `./gradlew :wear:assembleDebug` passed.

### What was not tested

- There is no unit test for the Compose window flag. It is a view side effect, and this was verified on device instead.
- Ambient mode and other watch makers were not tested.

prs.title: fix(android): let opt-in speech interruption stop native Talk replies
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Related: #187511

> Linked as **Related** rather than `Closes` on purpose: #187511 reports two distinct defects and this PR only repairs the playback-interruption one. The separate native Talk admission/readiness defect stays tracked in #165481, so the issue must not auto-close on merge.

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where Android users who enabled `talk.interruptOnSpeech` could never interrupt (barge into) a native Talk reply: speaking while the assistant was playing audio did not stop playback, because the interrupt recognizer was never started during native reply playback.
- Also aligns the Talk documentation with the Android client default: `interruptOnSpeech` is opt-in (`false`) on Android because starting speech recognition during TTS playback creates audio-session conflicts on some OEM devices, while the config table previously showed only the `true` default.
- **Related:** #165481 covers the separate native Talk admission/readiness defect (part 1 of the issue) per the ClawSweeper triage review, which explicitly directed this fix to the playback-interruption defect and left admission to that PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** With `interruptOnSpeech: true`, recognized speech during a native Talk reply stops assistant playback and Talk resumes listening, while push-to-turn microphone ownership and the Android opt-in default are preserved.
- Native Talk clears the per-utterance `listeningMode` flag in `finalizeTranscript()` before `chat.send` and playback, but `shouldAllowSpeechInterrupt()` required `listeningMode`, so `ensureInterruptListener()` bailed out for the whole reply and the `_isSpeaking && interruptOnSpeech` branch in `handleTranscript` was unreachable. The fix tracks the admitted native Talk session in a separate `nativeTalkSessionActive` flag (set in `startNativeTalk`, cleared in `stop()`/`disableRealtimeModeLocked()`) and allows interruption when either per-utterance listening or the native session is active, keeping the `isRealtimeCapturePaused()` capture-ownership gate unchanged.
- **Out of scope:** No behavior change for the realtime relay route (the flag is only set on the native route), no change to the Android `interruptOnSpeech` default, and no gateway-side admission changes (handled in #165481).
- **Highest-risk area:** Microphone ownership races between the interrupt recognizer and push-to-talk turns.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The existing `isRealtimeCapturePaused()` gate still suppresses the interrupt listener for the full PTT turn, and the interrupt recognizer starts with `markListening = false` so UI listening state is untouched. Review round 2 replaces the reflection-based predicate test with `pushToTalkOwnsMicrophoneDuringInterruptibleNativePlayback`, which drives the handoff through the public capture operations (`beginPushToTalk` → `cancelPushToTalk`) during live native reply playback: the interrupt recognizer is retired and interruption is ineligible for the whole turn, then both are restored once the turn is released. `pausedPushToTalkTurnSuppressesSpeechInterruptListener` still pins the gate itself.

## User Impact

- Android users with `talk.interruptOnSpeech: true` can now speak over a native Talk reply to stop playback and take the turn; users who leave the setting unset keep the current opt-in behavior.
- **Success criteria:** During native Talk reply playback with the setting enabled, a recognized utterance (≥3 chars, not an echo of the reply) cancels audio playback and Talk resumes listening; PTT turns still own the microphone exclusively.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManager.kt` (session flag + `shouldAllowSpeechInterrupt`), regression tests `speechInterruptStopsNativeReplyPlaybackAfterCompletedUtterance` and `pushToTalkOwnsMicrophoneDuringInterruptibleNativePlayback` in `TalkModeManagerTest.kt`, and the `interruptOnSpeech` row in `docs/nodes/talk.md`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Robolectric JVM test harness against the real `TalkModeManager` with a mock gateway WebSocket (`withStartedTalk`), fake synthesizer/player, and the Android `SpeechRecognizer` shadow, in the issue worktree at head `723fb194d74`.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  ANDROID_HOME=$HOME/.android-sdk JAVA_HOME=$HOME/android-sdk-tools/jdks \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/run-android-gradle.mts :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest \
    --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.voice.TalkModeManagerTest' \
    --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.voice.PushToTalkRecognitionLadderTest' \
    --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.voice.PushToTalkTranscriptMergerTest'
  (cd apps/android && ./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck)
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 40s (GREEN_EXIT=0)
  TalkModeManagerTest:            tests=114, failures=0, errors=0, skipped=0
  PushToTalkRecognitionLadderTest: tests=4,  failures=0, errors=0, skipped=0
  PushToTalkTranscriptMergerTest:  tests=7,  failures=0, errors=0, skipped=0
  BUILD SUCCESSFUL (:app:ktlintCheck, KTLINT_EXIT=0)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** `speechInterruptStopsNativeReplyPlaybackAfterCompletedUtterance` completes a recognized utterance (silence finalization → `chat.send` → synthesis → `isSpeaking == true`), then a live interrupt recognizer receives "Please stop talking" during playback: `isSpeaking` flips to false, the audio player is stopped, and native Talk resumes listening. `pushToTalkOwnsMicrophoneDuringInterruptibleNativePlayback` starts from the same playing state with interruption eligible, then `beginPushToTalk(allowNewCapture = true)` cancels playback (`isSpeaking` goes false), destroys the interrupt recognizer, and makes `shouldAllowSpeechInterrupt()` false for the whole turn; `cancelPushToTalk()` returns `status == "cancelled"`, native Talk resumes listening, a fresh recognizer is live, and interruption becomes eligible again.
- **Before evidence (re-run at this head, `TalkModeManager.kt` restored from `origin/main`):**
  ```text
  TalkModeManagerTest > pushToTalkOwnsMicrophoneDuringInterruptibleNativePlayback FAILED
      java.lang.AssertionError: A live interrupt recognizer must listen during native reply playback
          at ...TalkModeManagerTest.kt:945
  TalkModeManagerTest > speechInterruptStopsNativeReplyPlaybackAfterCompletedUtterance FAILED
      java.lang.AssertionError: A live interrupt recognizer must listen during native reply playback
          at ...TalkModeManagerTest.kt:919
  2 tests completed, 2 failed  (BUILD FAILED, RED_EXIT=1)
  ```
  Playback was never interruptible because `ensureInterruptListener()` returned early on `listeningMode == false`.
- **What was not tested:** No shipped-APK run on a physical device. The ClawSweeper before-merge ask (a recording or redacted device logs from an APK containing this patch) cannot be produced from this environment: no Android device is attached (`adb devices` empty) and the host has no `/dev/kvm`, so the x86_64 `google_apis` emulator image cannot boot here. Everything above is proven at the Robolectric level against real manager logic, the real gateway protocol over a mock WebSocket, and the Android `SpeechRecognizer` shadow. Device confirmation would have to come from the reporter's Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 or a maintainer/CI emulator lane with hardware acceleration and audio.
- **Proof tier:** L2 (real component under test, mocked system boundaries)
- **Proof limitations:** Device-level OEM audio-session behavior during simultaneous TTS + recognition cannot be exercised in JVM tests, and no media proof (screenshot/recording) of the shipped app is available from this environment; the Android opt-in default is preserved precisely because of that OEM sensitivity.
- **Review state:** Review round 2 addressed — low-value reflection test removed, microphone handoff covered through public capture operations, issue link downgraded to `Related`. Device-level media proof still open (environment limitation above). CI lanes re-running at head `723fb194d74`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The relevant upstream advisories include [GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx) and [GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685). This change does not remediate that transitive edge or prove that all packaged dependency paths are patched. The release owner should assess it separately before treating the release as fully remediated.

- Separately, an isolated OpenClaw 2026.10.8 installation with Undici 8.12.2 passed gateway health and authentication checks, a local OpenAI-compatible fixture, an HTTP CONNECT proxy fixture, and a synthetic TLS regression check. This is compatibility evidence for that installation, not a build or end-to-end test of this release branch.

prs.title: fix(browser): preserve native CORS preflights
prs.body:
## Summary

Browser navigation guards used Playwright catch-all page routing, which made Chromium treat intercepted CORS preflights as permissive and could send a cross-origin request the destination rejected. This change moves guard handling into document-only CDP interception, preserves native CORS, and explicitly cancels a committed timed-out page opening while retiring successful committed document ownership without canceling healthy response bodies or child loads. It preserves the invocation-scoped navigation policy introduced by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104254 and does not depend on the unmerged policy-removal proposal in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167703.

## What Problem This Solves

1. In `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-navigation.ts`, guarded actions and guarded `goto` used catch-all Playwright routing. Playwright could synthesize a successful CORS preflight, so a rejecting destination received the non-simple `PUT`.
2. In `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-navigation-fence.ts`, the existing operation-owned fence tracked document redirects and out-of-process frames but did not own the route handler or limit Fetch interception to documents.
3. The first document-only implementation waited for a terminal Network event after a committed streamed document timed out. Chromium does not consistently emit that event after `Page.stopLoading`, so cleanup could replace the original Playwright `TimeoutError` and close a usable committed tab.
4. A successful action could also return before delayed response headers committed streaming main-frame HTML. Cleanup sampled commitment once, then waited 20 seconds even after the later commit, failed, and retained interception until page close, so later navigation on the otherwise usable tab was aborted.

5. Successful action cleanup also used page-wide stopLoading after main-frame commit, truncating healthy delayed finite HTML and simultaneous child loads. Ownership now retires independently at each document commit; failure and cancellation still stop loading.

The net effect was excess page-script network authority before this fix plus committed-page recovery and successful-load regressions in its first revisions.

## Why this design

- Intercept only `Document` resources through the operation-owned CDP session; leave preflights and subresources on Chromium's native network path.
- Keep top-level/subframe checks, redirect/OOPIF ownership, and live invocation authority in one fence.
- Establish a same-target protocol barrier before cleanup so a queued document cannot escape interception.
- On navigation failure, acknowledge `Page.stopLoading`, settle the fence's owned document state, and preserve the original navigation error.
- Retire each document at its own frame commit, including OOPIF sessions: committed responses cannot redirect, so their bodies can continue while uncommitted redirect chains and policy work remain fenced. Reserve page-wide stopLoading for failure or cancellation.
- Disable Fetch before detaching and retain interception when cancellation cannot be confirmed.
- Add no setting, dependency, public API, or migration surface.

## Why this does not conflict with related browser-navigation work

| PR | Governed layer | Relation to this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104254 | Invocation-scoped document policy for browser actions | The base includes it. This PR preserves its policy and changes only the interception mechanism and cleanup. |
| https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167703 | Unmerged proposal to retire native navigation-policy enforcement | This PR keeps the current contract and does not depend on that proposal. |

The shared navigation files compose with the existing policy: this branch narrows interception and repairs cleanup without redefining the allowed destinations.

## Evidence

| Path × mode | Final-effect observation | Reproducible command and result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original catch-all route mechanism | With no route, rejected CORS sent `OPTIONS` only; with the base catch-all `page.route("**", route.fallback)` mechanism, the same rejecting destination received `PUT` and no `OPTIONS`. | `node /tmp/openclaw-1129-probe/probe.mjs` against pinned `playwright-core` 1.64.1 reproduced the before/without-route differential shown below. |
| Guarded action; destination rejects CORS | Destination recorded `OPTIONS` and zero `PUT` requests. | `pnpm test:live -- extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-navigation-cors.live.test.ts` — rejected action case passed. |
| Guarded `goto`; destination rejects CORS | Destination recorded `OPTIONS` and zero `PUT` requests. | Same command — rejected `goto` case passed. |
| Guarded action; destination consents | Destination recorded `OPTIONS`, then exactly one `PUT`. | Same command — consenting case passed. |
| Denied document | The attempted `127.0.0.2` fixture destination recorded zero document requests under a policy allowing only `127.0.0.1`; source URL and title remained unchanged. | Same command — denied-document/source-preservation case passed. |
| Allowed redirects across main frame and OOPIF | Each allowed goto/action/early-return/existing/new/nested-frame case recorded exactly one destination request. | `pnpm test:live -- extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-navigation-authority.live.test.ts` — allowed cases 6/6. |
| Revoked redirects across main frame and OOPIF | Each revoked case rejected with the authority error and recorded zero destination requests; a subsequent new owner navigated successfully. | Same command — revoked cases 6/6. |
| Shipped create-page streamed timeout | `createPageViaPlaywright` returned the committed tab after the 1-second timeout; URL, title `Committed stream`, and body `ready` remained usable. | `pnpm test:live -- extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-create-page-timeout.live.test.ts` — 1/1 passed. |
| Committed action stream | The guarded action returned before the fixture's one-second-delayed response headers, cleanup observed the later main-frame commit, completed without response EOF, retained URL/title/body, and a subsequent navigation succeeded. The earlier reviewed implementation failed the immediate-header variant after 20.1 seconds. | CORS live suite delayed-commit streamed-action case passed in 1.176 seconds. |
| Successful action; delayed finite main HTML and simultaneous child response | At action return both response tails were absent; afterward the main form, child tail, late script/title, and page load completed. Original production failed waiting for load at 5 seconds; repaired production passes. | CORS live regression: preserves delayed finite HTML and simultaneous pending child loads after success. All three browser live suites passed 18/18; acceptance 75/75. |
| Unit and repository gates | Fence lifecycle/create-page tests passed 45/45; the connection-owner acceptance set passed 75/75 after migrating its CDP fixture; format, production/test types, scoped type-aware lint, structural guards, and import-cycle checks passed. | `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-browser.config.ts ...` and `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main`. |

The sink observations come from fixture HTTP-server request counters and the real Chromium page's committed URL/title/body; fixtures use loopback only and contain no credentials or private endpoints. The redacted current-head terminal trace below comes directly from opt-in output after each sink assertion.

<details>
<summary>Original base-mechanism differential (real Chromium)</summary>

```text

Here `guarded=true` installs the original base's exact catch-all Playwright route/fallback mechanism; the rejecting destination receiving `PUT` is the regression this PR removes.

</details>

<details>

```

</details>

## Boundary decisions requested from browser owners

1. Confirm that document-only interception remains the intended owner for top-level and OOPIF navigation policy while Chromium owns CORS and subresources.
2. Confirm that per-document commit retires successful response ownership without canceling its body, while acknowledged top-level `Page.stopLoading` remains the failure/cancellation boundary for retaining a usable committed tab.

## Testing

- Added `pw-session-navigation-cors.live.test.ts` for rejected/consenting CORS and denied-document source preservation.
- Extended it with delayed-header infinite-stream recovery and delayed finite HTML plus simultaneous child-body completion proof, with opt-in redacted sink traces.
- Added `pw-session-create-page-timeout.live.test.ts` through the shipped `createPageViaPlaywright` entry point.
- Re-ran `pw-session-navigation-authority.live.test.ts` for allowed and revoked redirects across main-frame and OOPIF paths (12/12).
- Updated the fence lifecycle suite and removed two mock cases that no longer exercised their named failures.
- Migrated `pw-session.connections.test.ts` from the removed route rendezvous to an EventEmitter-backed CDP session and `Fetch.enable` interception rendezvous; Clawsweeper's exact four-file acceptance command passed 75/75.
- Focused unit suites passed 45/45; all 18 live Chromium cases passed.
- Scoped changed-file gate passed against `upstream/main`; the documented dead-code skip applies only to an unrelated full-tree finding.

prs.title: fix(backup): redact bundled plugin credentials from Git exports
prs.body:
## Summary

Secret-redacted Git backups retain credentials embedded in bundled plugin state. Filter the identified credential scopes before SQLite serialization and PostgreSQL image materialization while preserving unrelated plugin records and blobs. This extends the backup redaction policy introduced in #122485 and shared across engines in #174698.

## What Problem This Solves

1. `src/state/secret-state-tables.ts` and `src/snapshot/git-backup-sanitizer.ts` now classify bundled account credentials, identity keys, callback signing secrets, hosted-media bearer records, and Discord Activity token stores. Their opaque values and token keys previously reached Git history even with `--exclude-secrets`.
2. Discord thread bindings contain webhook credentials alongside routing data. Remove only `webhookToken` from those JSON records, preserving routing fields. Unreadable records in that credential scope are omitted.

Redacted exports withhold these credentials while retaining allowlists, spending counters, memory settings, widget records, relay grants, registration identities, and unrelated durable blobs.

## Why this design

- Keep the existing export sanitizer as the policy owner for both engines.
- Match plugin IDs, credential namespaces, account variants, and individual keys in mixed namespaces; cover retained namespaces without dropping entire plugin tables.
- Preserve full-fidelity backups and existing user configuration, schemas, SDK signatures, and manifest formats.
- Document reauthentication and registration after redacted restores. Custom opaque plugin payloads require their own credential classification; these rules cover the identified bundled scopes.

## Why this does not conflict with #122485 and #174698

| PR | Governed layer | Relation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #122485 | Git snapshots and secret-redaction policy | Extends the existing policy to credentials inside plugin records. |
| #174698 | PostgreSQL export redaction | Reuses its shared row-transform seam before portable image materialization. |

Both changes are already in the base. The plugin tables remain present; selected rows or fields are redacted.

## Evidence of Fix

| PostgreSQL 17.11 portable image and fresh server restore | On original base `903394cceb1`, both state cases fail: seven plugin rows instead of four, credential bytes and webhook token still present. The two agent controls pass. | Four real-server conformance cases passed. Redacted state image/restores retain four nonsecret/mixed plugin rows and one ordinary blob; full mode retains seven rows and both blobs. Raw redacted image bytes contain no secret marker. Normal and generic identities cover export; normal identities cover actual fresh PostgreSQL namespace restore. |
| `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/snapshot/git-backup-plugin-secrets.test.ts src/snapshot/git-backup.test.ts src/snapshot/git-backup-codec.test.ts src/state/secret-state-tables.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | New regression failed on the original code; full-fidelity control passed. | 29 tests passed; one Windows-only case skipped on Linux. Following the Discord repairs, the changed regression and registry suites passed again: five tests. |
| Unclassified custom plugin JSON and blob in `credentials` | Namespace names alone carry no sensitivity declaration. | Explicit controls retain custom records and public blob bytes in pushed history and restored data in both redacted and full modes. Classified bundled credentials are still omitted. |

Integration and CLI assertions inspect committed JSONL in the bare remote and query restored SQLite data. The PostgreSQL test inspects portable-image bytes and queries fresh restored server namespaces, including spending counters, memory-disable settings, relay grants and field-redacted Discord bindings.

CLI proof used isolated synthetic state with `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. `$REPO`, `$REMOTE` and `$TARGET` below name fresh task-owned temporary paths:

```bash
pnpm openclaw backup git init --repository "$REPO" --remote "$REMOTE" --json

pnpm openclaw backup git verify --repository "$REPO" --global --json

```

The full-fidelity control ran the same commands without `--exclude-secrets`. Real PostgreSQL proof used the repository-pinned pgvector image with PostgreSQL 17.11 and this supported wrapper:

```bash
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection "$OPENCLAW_DATABASE_DSN" -- src/infra/database-engine/git-backup-secrets.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The same PostgreSQL conformance command shown above was also run in a temporary worktree at the original base with the extended regression copied in. The following is its expected failing baseline output, not a current-head CI failure:

```text
BASELINE_PG_PLUGIN_EXPORT {"generic":false,"pluginRows":7,"secretMarkerInPortableImage":true,"discordThreadBinding":{"value_json":"{\"threadId\":\"thread\",\"webhookToken\":\"synthetic-secret-must-not-appear-in-export\"}"},"credentialBlobCount":1}

   → expected 7 to be 4 // Object.is equality
   → expected 7 to be 4 // Object.is equality
      Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)
```

The fixed tree passed all four real PostgreSQL cases, including portable-image verification and fresh server-namespace restore.

</details>

## SDK / caller upgrade contract

Plugin storage APIs remain unchanged. Redacted restores require affected integrations to sign in or register again; recreate omitted bearer sessions and hosted-media links. Existing Git history retains previously exported values.

## Boundary decisions requested from backup and security maintainers

1. Review the credential-scope inventory and the field-only treatment of Discord thread bindings before landing.
2. Confirm the targeted boundary: unclassified custom-plugin data, including a namespace named `credentials`, remains included. Additional credential stores need explicit classification by the backup/security owners.

## Testing

The branch integrates `main` at `0f364cc3f4bdb566151fc134095421a384b73ffe` in merge commit `c3ae7cb0163600e3a2f547fa8f96be0118901bc8`. Both base refreshes were conflict-free; the final three upstream commits touch streamed replies, performance scripts and release feeds, leaving all six PR files unchanged.

On this head, the plugin-redaction integration and secret-table policy suites passed **five tests** through the repository wrapper on Node. On the preceding base refresh, the four focused backup/codec/policy files passed **29 tests with one Windows-only skip**; targeted typecheck, lint, documentation parsing for both changed docs, the test-line ratchet and `git diff --check` also passed. The shared test budget remains unchanged by this PR. Earlier sibling coverage passed all eight Git-backup suites plus the secret-table policy tests: **48 passed, one Windows-only skip**. The three updated plugin-redaction cases also passed on Node and the repository-pinned Bun runtime.

The scope probe uses the same secret-absence assertions for known bundled stores. Its original arbitrary `some-plugin/credentials` blob is unclassified and remains included under this policy; changing only that fixture's plugin ID to the classified `zalouser` makes the absence assertions pass. The committed integration retains its original known-credential blob fixture and adds an explicit unknown-plugin blob preservation control. This clarifies the selected boundary without changing production redaction behavior or reserving namespace names globally.

The [current-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40914378041) passed for `c3ae7cb0163600e3a2f547fa8f96be0118901bc8`: **40 successful jobs and 29 scope-skipped jobs**, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards, the changed Node tests, lint and baseline ratchets. Four real PostgreSQL cases also passed locally using the pinned PostgreSQL 17 image and a fresh isolated server, which was removed afterward. Live provider login remains untested.

prs.title: feat(ui): clear failed session alerts from the Subagents panel and session hovercard
prs.body:
Related: #185192, #185054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when several child sessions fail or time out, the parent's sidebar row stays red ("Child session X failed: reason") and each failure can only be cleared by opening that child, one at a time; the Subagents panel lists the failures but cannot acknowledge them.

## User Impact

User impact: failure alerts can be cleared in place. In the Subagents panel each unread failure has a **Mark {name} as read** control and the Failed heading has **Mark all as read** (two or more), on desktop and mobile. The session hovercard shows **Dismiss** under a failure, including a child failure folded into its parent row. Acknowledging clears the sidebar alert and hovercard notice on every surface and device, survives reload, and a later failure of the same session alerts again. Panel grouping does not change: failed runs stay listed under Failed, exactly as on main after you open them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already decides whether a failure is still an alert: a failed session alerts until its read time passes its failure time, and opening the session writes that read time. These controls send the same conditional `sessions.patch { unread: false }` (fenced by `expectedSessionId` and `expectedMarkedUnreadAt`), so there is one acknowledgement shared by every surface, tab and device, and no new state, option or API.

- Controls appear only where the viewer can patch the failed session. For a child failure folded into a parent row, the hovercard uses that child's own sharing role and manual-unread marker, so a session-scoped owner gets Dismiss and a manually unread child is acknowledged instead of rejected as stale.
- The alert stays until the Gateway row reports the read. If the Gateway rejects the write, an error toast says so with the Gateway's reason ("Couldn't mark as read. Try again. ..."), and the alert and its control stay, so the same click retries; the next successful acknowledgement replaces that toast with "Marked as read". It is a toast rather than an inline line because the hovercard can close before the reply arrives (session deletion reports its failures the same way).
- Focus: on desktop it moves to the next failure's control, then to the acknowledged row; on mobile it stays on the row. The hovercard keeps its existing focus restoration.
- Known limits: the acknowledgement is fenced to the session, not a run, so a newer failure that lands between render and click is acknowledged too (opening the session behaves the same today). While the parent conversation is open, main's existing hidden-run read for subagents can acknowledge a child whose retry fails immediately; this PR does not change that path.

## Decision for the area owner

The open question is only whether the Subagents panel and the session hovercard should offer these acknowledgement controls (per row, Mark all as read for two or more, Dismiss in the hovercard). They add no state, option, setting or API: each control sends the same conditional read receipt the Control UI already sends when you open a failed session, so the Gateway stays the single owner of "is this failure still an alert", grouping stays by run outcome exactly as on main, and declining the direction means simply not merging. Approving it on this PR is enough; nothing else depends on it.

#185054 (open, another contributor) makes the same choice for the composer failure cards that #185192 has since removed from main; this PR covers the surfaces that remain.

<details><summary>Surface inventory</summary>

| Surface | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subagents panel, desktop Failed group | Lists failures, no acknowledgement | Per-row Mark as read, Mark all as read (2+); rows stay in Failed |
| Subagents panel, mobile Finished list | Failed rows with red indicator, no acknowledgement | Same controls; rows keep their Failed indicator |
| Sidebar row failure indicator (own or folded child) | Own failure via row menu Mark as read; folded child only by opening it | Cleared by any acknowledgement of the failed session |
| Session hovercard failure section | No action | Dismiss, acknowledging the failing child when folded |
| Background session toast, sidebar issues inbox, chat details tally, native roster | Unchanged | Unchanged (transient, no session failures, or counts only) |

</details>

<details><summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- `isUnacknowledgedSessionFailure` (`ui/src/lib/session-attention.ts`) is the single failure-alert rule; `sessionRowAttention` and the chat pane's read acknowledgement use it instead of two copies.
- Error attention carries the failed session's `sourceSessionId`, `sourceMarkedUnreadAt` and `sourceSharingRole`, so the hovercard targets the failed session with its own fence and role.
- `canDismissSessionFailure` / `dismissSessionFailures` (`ui/src/lib/sessions/session-failure-dismissal.ts`) own the access check, the conditional write and its rejection feedback (the shared `showToast` owner with `severity: "error"`).
- The hovercard error section moved to `session-hovercard-error.tsx` to keep `session-hovercard-solid.tsx` under the file line cap.
- New copy: `chat.subagentsPanel.markFailureRead` ("Mark {name} as read") and `chat.subagentsPanel.markAllFailuresRead` ("Mark all as read"). `sessionsView.markFailureReadFailed` ("Couldn't mark as read. Try again. {error}") and `sessionsView.markFailureReadDone` ("Marked as read"). The hovercard reuses `common.dismiss`.

</details>

## Evidence

### Real Gateway, real failed subagents (Chromium 156 and WebKit 27.2)

An isolated Gateway built from this branch (`dist/` plus `dist/control-ui`, served bundle hash checked against the build) on loopback with a synthetic config. A parent turn spawns four real subagents through `sessions_spawn`; only the loopback model provider is scripted, and it rejects every child request with HTTP 400, so each child run fails through the real runtime (`status: "failed"`, `lastRunError: "LLM request rejected: Synthetic provider rejected the request | synthetic_rejection"`). No WebSocket interception; frames are observed passively. Two browser contexts are paired as two devices.

| | Before (main) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subagents panel with four real failures | ![main: Failed 4, no controls, parent row red](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-before-panel.png) | ![branch: Mark as read per row and Mark all as read](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-after-panel-controls.png) |
| Parent row hovercard (child failure folded) | ![main: failure notice, no action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-before-hovercard.png) | ![branch: Dismiss under the child failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-after-hovercard-dismiss.png) |
| After acknowledging | | ![one row read](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-after-panel-one-read.png) ![all read: rows stay in Failed, parent row no longer red](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-after-panel-all-read.png) |
| Second device after reload | | ![device B: no controls, no red row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-device-b-after-reload.png) |
| Same child fails again | | ![device B sidebar alert returns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-refail-sidebar-device-b.png) ![device B panel offers Mark as read again (WebKit)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-refail-panel-device-b-webkit.png) |

Sequence asserted in both browsers (all pass):

1. Main build: Failed 4, zero acknowledgement controls in the panel and hovercard, still 4 after reload.
2. Branch build: the hovercard on the parent row names one failed child. That child is also marked unread by hand (`sessions.patch { unread: true }`); Dismiss then sends `expectedMarkedUnreadAt` equal to its marker and the Gateway advances `lastReadAt`.
3. Mark as read on one row, then Mark all as read on the remaining two: controls go, all four rows stay in Failed, the parent row's red indicator clears.
4. Reload: still acknowledged. A second paired device: no controls, no red row.
5. The operator asks the parent to retry one child; the parent's real `sessions_send` runs it again and it fails again. Both devices show the red parent row with "Child session ... failed" and that one row's Mark as read control.

Captured `sessions.patch` request/response pairs for the four acknowledgements (Chromium; WebKit identical in shape):

| Child | Sent | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| folded child, manually unread | `{ unread: false, expectedSessionId, expectedMarkedUnreadAt: <its marker> }` | ok, `lastReadAt` set |
| row control | `{ unread: false, expectedSessionId, expectedMarkedUnreadAt: null }` | ok, `lastReadAt` set |
| Mark all as read (2) | same shape, one per child | ok, `lastReadAt` set |

Real-seam red for the hovercard fence: the same harness against the previous head of this PR sends `expectedMarkedUnreadAt: null` for the manually unread child; the Gateway answers ok with the entry unchanged (no `lastReadAt`) and the alert stays.

### Rejected acknowledgement and retry (mocked Gateway, Playwright Chromium and WebKit 27.2)

The mock Gateway holds the first `sessions.patch` and answers it with `UNAVAILABLE: Session store unavailable`; the second click goes through. Asserted in both engines: the error toast text, the alert and control still present and enabled, a second `sessions.patch` on the same control, the alert cleared, and the error toast replaced by "Marked as read".

| | Rejected | Retried |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subagents panel (WebKit) | ![error toast, Mark as read control still on the failed row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2d5dcf1e9bfb8adfbd5b5b3065fdff84142fbcf1/dismiss-failed-alerts-r3/webkit-panel-mark-read-rejected.png) | ![Marked as read toast, control gone, row still in Failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2d5dcf1e9bfb8adfbd5b5b3065fdff84142fbcf1/dismiss-failed-alerts-r3/webkit-panel-mark-read-retried.png) |
| Session hovercard (Chromium) | ![error toast, sidebar row still red, Dismiss still offered](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2d5dcf1e9bfb8adfbd5b5b3065fdff84142fbcf1/dismiss-failed-alerts-r3/chromium-hovercard-dismiss-rejected.png) | ![Marked as read toast, sidebar alert cleared](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2d5dcf1e9bfb8adfbd5b5b3065fdff84142fbcf1/dismiss-failed-alerts-r3/chromium-hovercard-dismiss-retried.png) |

A rejection was not forced on the real Gateway: the session store would have to be broken under a running Gateway, or the row changed between render and click, which races the live row update. The retry sends the same request as the real-Gateway acknowledgements above.

### Mobile (mocked Gateway, 390px)

![mobile before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/mobile-before.png) ![mobile after marking one read: control gone, Failed indicator kept](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/mobile-after-one-read.png)

### Tests (macOS arm64)

Red = the new tests on the previous head's production code; green = this branch.

- `ui/src/components/session-progress-hovercard-target.test.ts`, new: Dismiss on a folded child failure under `operator.sessions.write` sends that child's `expectedMarkedUnreadAt` and `expectedSessionId`. Red: Dismiss is absent (child role dropped); with broad `operator.write` it sends `expectedMarkedUnreadAt: null`. Green: pass.
- `ui/src/lib/session-attention.test.ts`: failure stays an alert until read and alerts again later; error attention carries the source session id, marker and role. Red: source facts missing. Green: pass.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-subagents-panel.test.ts`, 2 cases: desktop controls only on unread failures the viewer can patch, exact conditional params, rows stay in Failed, focus to the next control then to the row; mobile acknowledged in place with its Failed indicator and focus on the row. Red: fail. Green: pass.
- `ui/src/components/session-hovercard.test.ts`: Dismiss renders and calls its owner only when supplied.
- Rejected write, new: `chat-subagents-panel.test.ts` (desktop and mobile) and `session-progress-hovercard-target.test.ts` reject the first `sessions.patch`, then expect the error toast with the Gateway reason, the control still present and enabled, a successful second click, and "Marked as read" replacing the error. Red on the previous head: 3 fail (no toast; the rejection was swallowed). Green: pass.
- Playwright (mocked Gateway) `subagents-panel.e2e.test.ts` and `session-progress-hovercard.e2e.test.ts`, including the two new rejection cases: 19/19 pass in Chromium and 19/19 in WebKit.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`, oxlint, oxfmt and stylelint on the changed files: pass.
- Full `pnpm lint`: exits 1 on 11 errors, all in files this PR does not touch (`extensions/copilot`, `extensions/knowledge`, `extensions/oc-path`, `extensions/qa-lab`, `extensions/tlon`, `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-run.ts`, `src/agents/code-mode-execution.ts`); no changed file appears in its output.

prs.title: fix: dotted path insertions fail in JSON and YAML
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw path set` rejects an insertion such as `oc://data.jsonc/plugins.entries.+example` with `unresolved`, even though its parent containers exist and the equivalent slash-separated address works. The inserted key is missing; this change does not auto-create missing parent containers.

## User Impact

JSON/JSONC and YAML users can insert a key, append an item, or insert at an array index after a dotted parent path. Quoted parent keys and whole-slot keys such as `+literal.dot` retain their meaning. No configuration change or schema migration.

## Fix

The existing shared insertion detector separates the final dotted marker from its parent for JSONC and YAML, reusing the same quote-aware splitter as their readers. Both resolve and set consume that one decision. Markdown and JSONL retain their existing insertion rules.

## Evidence

[Built CLI differential, persisted readback and byte diffs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187828#issuecomment-6505826302):
- Built main `2f47962f2bdc6af710e2059b725c73423a3e1f7e`: twice per format, resolve/set return exit1 and `unresolved`; files remain unchanged.
- Built candidate: twice per format, resolve recognizes the insertion point, set persists it, and a new shipped-CLI resolve returns the nested boolean `true`.
- Real JSONC with comments and actual YAML files; byte diffs show only the inserted key plus the required JSON comma. Removing those exact additions reconstructs original bytes, comments, indentation, siblings and final newline.
- Existing-key, slash-insertion, quoted-dot-parent and literal-dot-key controls pass on both refs and both formats. Quoted dotted-parent insertion also changes from main refusal to candidate success.
- Normal bundled `oc-path` activation through `plugins enable`; no private imports in the runtime proof. Explicit isolated profiles/config/state/SQLite paths, secretless Node24.22.1 Docker, generic data files only—not live OpenClaw configuration.
- Existing owner suite: **49 passed**. Three retained dotted keyed/append/indexed table cases fail on main with `unresolved`. No new test cases or allocation; tests **+3/-3 (net0)**.

Final head `029a41f386b99edbd8935d935301dfb444a3b2e5` only consolidates tests after the proven contributor build; production remains **+11/-5** and is unchanged. Contributor commit retained. Simplification keeps the existing owner and reader splitter, with no new abstraction or alternate path.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: no stored-format or schema migration. Reverting restores the old refusal for dotted insertion addresses; previously written ordinary JSONC/YAML keys remain readable. Blast radius is recognition of insertion markers in JSONC/YAML addresses; existing writers still own persistence, formatting and validation.

prs.title: fix(typesafe): prepare socket test policy before request deadlines
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The TypeSafe socket-reuse fixture starts request deadlines before preparing Gateway request policy, unlike its transport siblings.

## User Impact

No application behavior changes. This aligns the test setup while preserving all three hosts, five requests per host, 1000 ms deadlines, and socket, authentication, body, and DNS assertions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare the existing public request-policy resolver once for each actual endpoint after server and environment setup. This runs before the timed requests and follows the test runtime's metadata reset lifecycle. Cold-import and deadline-admission coverage remains in the existing registration suites.

## Evidence

- Exact source: `0adf936836360270fdf083eb4e27a088c1076a8d`. Independent source review and fresh autoreview found no actionable issues; guarded formatting passed.
- [Native focused proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40932315181): all four complete suites passed under both pinned Bun191755 and Node24.22.1: **111 cases per runtime, 222 total**, zero skips or failures. Coverage includes all three socket hosts, preparation-exhausted/remaining-deadline cases, cold-import revalidation, shared initialization, and cancellation. Linux x64, pnpm12.15.0, Vitest5.0.5; serial four-file proof.
- Independent raw-result audit confirmed exact source/runtime, normal nested and outer process/pipe completion, source preservation, and cleanup. Native exit0/settledtrue; no forced cleanup. This is the native receipt, not a claim about the backing Actions aggregate.

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.3 to 4.39.1
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.39.1 - 21 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

4.37.9 - 26 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.4. #4106

4.37.8 - 21 Aug 2026

No user facing changes.

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.3. #4085

prs.title: refactor(ui): load Template creator on first use
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening chat currently constructs the Template creator flow and loads its implementation and review copy before anyone starts creating a template. The sidebar action also imports that full flow eagerly.

## User Impact

Chat boot loads less JavaScript. The first creator action loads the existing implementation on demand; direct Templates navigation and chat review still share the same flow. Creating, reviewing, retrying and publishing keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

A lightweight context-owned publication slot connects the sidebar, direct Templates route and dormant review. It reserves the clicked agent and connection before loading, deduplicates repeated clicks, and keeps only the latest eligible target while the import is pending. Retired connections can collect before that import settles.

The full flow and creator-only English copy move to a cold chunk. English catalogs still merge synchronously in either registration order. Existing idle warmups, locale behavior and issued-write lifetimes are unchanged.

CI identified a static flow/owner import cycle in the first implementation. The publication slot now owns an explicit leaf contract with no implementation backreference; both the full flow and its observers use that one slot. The actual failed Madge guard first reproduced the cycle and now reports zero cycles.

Production: +230/-63 lines (net +167); tests: +925/-4. The added production code owns first-use admission, bounded pending custody and publication, including the shared leaf contract. It replaces eager construction without duplicating the creator workflow. Release-note context: defer Template creator implementation and copy until first use.

## Evidence

- The actual two-entry emitted-closure regression fails on frozen base `76985e4c31c4c94c91e7ed79411c8189180b7ea8` and passes with the new boundary.
- Held-import, exact connection/capability, duplicate-click, direct-route takeover, loader retry and retired-client collection tests pass. Collection first failed with the unbounded waiter implementation.
- The repaired boundary passes 23 focused owner/flow/review/closure tests, nine affected compiler graphs, UI types and targeted lint/format checks. Catalog composition and chunking checks also pass.
- Four mock-socket browser cases pass together: allowed cold-sidebar/duplicate-click admission; held import followed by actual Connection settings replacement; held import followed by a read-only hello on the same client and revision; and the existing close-during-publish/failure/retry flow. The two retired-authority cases await the actual runtime module plus a browser task, then observe zero `templates.drafts.create` and zero `chat.send` requests. This uses production GatewayBrowserClient framing through the existing MockWebSocket transport, not a live Gateway.
- The task-opt-in real Gateway proof also passes in that same five-case invocation. The served UI entry matches the qualified build, browser traffic uses native WebSocket connections to two isolated real Gateways, and inference is local and synthetic. The allowed path creates a real draft artifact, receives successful create/send responses and reaches inference once. Held-import actions after actual Connection Apply replacement or actual device-token revocation and disconnect send neither write and leave both Gateways' draft artifacts unchanged. The chunk is evaluated and a browser task completes before checking absence. Child registry credentials/config are isolated; this does not publish to ClawHub.
- Safe final-effect verdict (all cases use the authenticated built UI and evaluate the held runtime):

prs.title: fix: resume Codex conversations after background cleanup settles
prs.body:
## Current revision

Head `e756e6ab7c86b766b61db4a34b176b0b384f03ee` changes tests only from the proven runtime head. Whole-PR tests **net -3 lines**, no new allocations. Retained settlement/cancellation/deadline regressions fail on frozen main; candidate targeted files pass 15/15. Consolidation and exact commands: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187776#issuecomment-6505020151

The earlier test inventories below describe historical revisions and are superseded by this zero-growth consolidation. Production/native proof remains unchanged.

Related: #186524.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: resuming a Codex conversation can fail with “claimed by active work” while a stopped turn’s background cleanup is still settling and refreshed creation instructions require unloading the retained subscription.

## User Impact

Users can resume after background cleanup finishes without discarding the conversation. Foreground claims, sibling work, cancellation, and the existing cleanup deadline remain protected; unfinished work is never force-released.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wait for unclaimed, background-only ownership to settle before the cold-resume unload, then recheck current authority and client state through the existing admission guards. Timeout remains a refusal, with an error that distinguishes unfinished background work from a foreground claim.

The ownership module owns the wait and its listener cleanup. Existing ownership and instruction helpers are reused rather than duplicated in the client adapter. This is separate from #186524’s explicit Goal Start/Resume admission fix and changes no configuration, permissions, persistence schema, or automatic-pursuit policy.

## Evidence

- Current pushed head: `2b62819f70eab6e5eca9490400c30c02f046961b`. Production repair: `6b66ecfc61ea711cf01d788d7462514e48b14e67`, based on `726705edca0`. The follow-up changes only two tests and their 14-line test-budget allocation; runtime code is unchanged.
- **11/11 lifecycle tests passed on production commit `6b66ecfc61e`** via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.warm-cleanup.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.warm-cleanup.native.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (38.25s Vitest). Regression coverage: settlement, cancellation, and deadline paths; native background-command cleanup followed by continuation; preserved sibling ownership. Native cases use a real Codex subprocess with a synthetic test provider, not a hosted model-quality evaluation. Windows skips the native-process suite.
- Targeted six-file formatting, lint, and whitespace checks pass. The supported production extension typecheck also passes: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo`. An initial direct root-config typecheck failed on repository-wide JSX/rootDir/package-resolution configuration and is not claimed as passed.
- Independent native Codex reviewer inspected the complete six-file parent-to-head range at P0–P2 and found no actionable defects. Static review only, without helper-owned isolation or structured validation; the configured shared autoreview installation was unreadable and no Codex CLI was available on PATH. This is not an autoreview-helper pass.
- Live operational observation: after deploying the integrated repair bundle, the previously paused existing Goal accepted Resume and its session entered running state with the same identity and objective. The deployment also contained separate admission/continuation fixes; this observation is not isolated proof of this six-file patch and does not claim the underlying Goal is finished.
- Simplification: ownership decisions and wait state remain with the existing thread-ownership owner; no second cleanup manager or forced release. Original production delta +104/-20; original tests +106/-2. The test-only follow-up adds +24/-8 including the allocation file.

Hosted CI has not yet been verified. No merge or release inclusion is claimed.


## P2 test follow-up and fresh Gateway rerun (2026-10-29)

Pushed head: `2b62819f70eab6e5eca9490400c30c02f046961b`.

- Both outdated assertions reproduced before editing: 2 failures, 9 passes. Both now require `AgentHarnessPreflightError` and the exact background-cleanup refusal diagnostic. Protection, subscription, lifecycle, and turn-count checks remain; owner reentry now explicitly checks protection and absence of unsubscribe after refusal.
- **11/11 follow-up tests passed across both changed files** with `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.native-background-outcome.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-continuity.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (32.37s Vitest; 37.21s command wall time). Targeted extension-test typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, and whitespace checks passed. No production timeout or sleep changes; the existing protected-cleanup refusal budget remains.
- Fresh isolated real-Gateway rerun reused the exact base and production-candidate builds above because this follow-up is test-only. Base again refused with “claimed by active work”; candidate waited **2,713 ms**, resumed the **same thread and client**, and returned `CLEANUP_RESUMED_OK`. This is real native-runtime/subscription-model behavior, not a synthetic provider run.
- Both test-owned Gateway processes stopped and both disposable state/auth homes were verified removed. The first rerun attempt hit the worker-compilation no-output watchdog before Gateway startup; the successful retry used the supported 300-second compilation deadline, with no production timeout change.
- Earlier static review covers the original six-file repair, not an independent review of this test-only follow-up. Hosted CI for the new head is not claimed as verified; no merge, release inclusion, or new live deployment is claimed.

The detailed earlier run below is retained as prior-run evidence; its 2,463 ms wait is distinct from the fresh 2,713 ms rerun.

## Isolated real-Gateway before/after proof (2026-10-29)

Fresh built Gateway processes, separate disposable state and ports, real native Codex runtime and subscription model. Production difference is only the six-file PR commit; no integrated deployment bundle is used.

| Build | Commit | Second turn | Cleanup wait |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base | `726705edca0d8cc7e39b71f4a42e40369dda9384` | Failed: claimed by active work | No wait |
| Candidate | `6b66ecfc61ea711cf01d788d7462514e48b14e67` | `CLEANUP_RESUMED_OK` | 2463 ms |

## Reproduction

1. Start an ordinary concrete-model chat; launch a native shell command that prints BACKGROUND_READY and waits on finish-background, then finalize BACKGROUND_LAUNCHED without collecting it.
2. Change only the model's authored contextTokens cap from 128000 to 127000; wait for Gateway hot reload. Use a route-neutral bundled-provider overlay with no API/base URL/auth override and the legacy context engine.
3. Send the next message to the same session; the external driver releases the command after 3 seconds. Base refuses early. Candidate waits for cleanup and resumes the same thread and client.
