prs.title: fix(discord): native slash commands fail in a plugin-bound thread
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Native slash commands in a plugin-bound Discord thread fail with `Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.` The log says `Session key does not contain an agent id; resolve it with the configured default agent.` I saw `/status` and `/codex binding` fail on main at da60d41, and `/codex detach` on earlier main 572cb278b243. Plain messages work. DMs, top level guild channels and ACP or subagent-bound threads do not hit it.

## User impact

Commands now use the thread's normal routed session and agent, and plugin commands receive the thread and parent ids that find their binding. No config change is needed.

At earlier head 59a4746d, an in-process non-default-agent run got a status card, but `/codex binding` failed before its handler because the binding record named another agent, which this change also fixes.

With `match: { channel: "discord", accountId: "*" }` and no narrower scope, bound-thread `/new` and `/reset` under a disabled parent crashed on main with the session-key error and now reach the existing `binding.channel` recovery exception, as unbound threads do. That crash was no disabled-parent rule to keep. Without that route binding, a test still pins `/new` to `This channel is disabled.`

Source at v2026.8.1-beta.1, sampled stable tags through v2026.10.5 and main has this failure. I did not run those releases. v2026.7.35 resolved the key to the default agent.

## Why this change was made

The native route feeds an opaque `plugin-binding:codex:...` key into `resolveDiscordEffectiveRoute`, then `resolveAgentIdFromSessionKey`, which requires an agent id. The message path has skipped plugin-owned records since #45318 at `message-handler.routing-preflight.ts:57-59`. This change gives `native-command-route.ts` the same ownership guard, and plugin commands find their binding from the conversation.

The guard returns `undefined`. The message path's empty string would become the native command session key at `src/channels/native-command-session-targets.ts:13` and pass `boundSessionKey != null` in the `/new` and `/reset` guard bypass, skipping a disabled-parent denial.

Plugin bind metadata supplies no agent id, so the stored agent can differ from the channel route. For plugin-owned records, `native-command.ts` now takes the agent for session lookup, plugin dispatch and reply recording from `effectiveRoute.agentId`. Other records and configured bindings keep their precedence. Otherwise the shared plugin runtime at `src/plugins/plugin-command-execution.ts:58` rejects the mismatched agent/session pair before its handler.

Telegram and Slack already classify plugin-owned records through core runtime binding routes, so this fix is Discord only. #146898 overlaps only on the call chain and edits free ACP keys in `route-resolution.ts`, untouched here.

## Evidence

Focused tests fail on main and pass with the fix.

`extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command.interaction-boundary.test.ts` adds a five-case `plugin-bound thread` group to main eb8fa7d's 16, 21 in all. It drives the real internal Discord client with REST, session lookup, status construction, the agent turn, reply recording and the `codex` handler stubbed. Parsing, access policy, routing and plugin dispatch are real.

- Three main-route cases pin status to `agent:main:discord:channel:<thread id>`, `/codex binding` to that key, `args: "binding"` and thread/parent ids, and disabled-parent `/new` denial with no context build or agent turn.
- The work-route case gives the record `main` and the route `work`. Status, session lookup, handler execution and reply recording must all use `agent:work:discord:channel:<thread id>` and `work`.
- An agent-owned record naming `main` with `agent:work:subagent:bound` must still refuse before its handler with `⚠️ Command failed. Please try again later.` Since #180173 the shared runtime catches this mismatch instead of throwing, and drops the error text.
- At 8ffec518, all 17 passed. Reverting only the route file to da60d41 failed the work case and three main cases on the session-key error, 13 passed. Reverting only `native-command.ts` to 59a4746d failed the work case with `The agent-scoped session key belongs to "work", not "main".`, 16 passed. Always choosing the effective agent failed the refusal case, 16 passed. Recording replies on the record agent failed the work case, 16 passed.
- At 99f07dc0, all 21 passed. Reverting both source files to eb8fa7d failed the same four cases, 17 passed. Always choosing the effective agent failed the refusal case, 20 passed. Each listed variant ran once.
- At 59a4746d, defaulting the agent in `session-key.ts` failed three main cases and returning an empty string failed two. Dropping every bound key passed this file but failed `loads model picker data from the effective bound route`. Keeping the configured-binding fallback passed all 15 and is equivalent, since `native-command-route.ts:53-65` skips that resolver when a thread record exists.
- At 2b6df40b, production-equivalent to 8ffec518, `native-command.status-direct`, `message-handler.preflight.acp-bindings`, `acp-bind-here.integration`, `native-command.model-picker` and `native-command.plugin-dispatch` passed 6, 2, 1, 31 and 25 tests. The full Discord project passed at 99f07dc0, 257 files and 2627 tests.
- Test cost, per `docs/help/testing/writing-tests.md:30-36`. At 2b6df40b the 17-case file took 16.28, 19.62 and 20.39 s. At 59a4746d the 15-case file took 19.15, 26.91 and 27.86 s, with tests at 9 to 16 percent of that, under the 5 s target. Back to back, da60d41's 12 cases took 15.75 s and the 15 cases 17.48 s. No CI seconds recorded here.
- At 8ffec518, `tsgo:extensions:test` passed, and `oxfmt --check` and the type-aware extensions lint passed on the test file. At 2b6df40b with `--base da60d41 --no-merge-base`, the line-cap, assertion-safety and mock-export checks passed, and the database-worker, database-dialect and timeout-race checks, `config:docs:check` and `plugins:inventory:check` passed on the same production code with an earlier fixture. `check:max-lines-ratchet` failed with `New max-lines suppressions are forbidden` for three UI files that are byte-identical to da60d41, as is the baseline, and a da60d41 tree fails the same way.

The default-route Gateway runs at da60d41 and 915f97d used isolated homes/state, fake tokens, a loopback mock model and a Discord stand-in, with a local shim injecting native commands and Allow once as `INTERACTION_CREATE` events. Native `/codex bind` plus Allow once persisted one `plugin-binding:codex:` row with `pluginBindingOwner: plugin` on both builds.

| Native command | Main da60d41 | Fix 915f97d |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/status` | `Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.` | Card naming `Session: agent:main:discord:channel:<thread id>` |
| `/codex binding` | Same failure | `Codex conversation binding:` block naming the workspace |

Main logged two session-key errors, one per command, the fix none. The binding row was unchanged on both. The route file at 8ffec518 is byte-identical to 915f97d. `/codex detach` and the other native commands share it but did not run on that build.

## Additional Evidence

Built Gateway through mocked Discord gateway/REST: main twice fails /status and plugin /proofprobe after plugin binding approval; candidate twice returns status and matching agent/session context. Default-route controls pass on both. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177850#issuecomment-6432527783

### Not fixed here

Unrelated slash-command failures are outside this fix. This additional transport proof covers the default-agent route, not non-default-agent or unauthorized-user behavior.

## Authority proof

On real Discord at `99f07dc0` with `gpt-5.6-luna`, bound-thread `/status` showed the `work` session while the record still named `main`. A sender on no allowlist was refused with no binding change or model request. All observed checks passed, but the run is inconclusive against my evidence plan. Limits are in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177850#issuecomment-6494748481.

The local runs below, detailed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177850#issuecomment-6491720075, used built Gateways at `9b7db694` and `99f07dc0`, a loopback Discord stand-in, fake tokens and mock models.

A2 binds with only `main`, then fully restarts with a `work` route. Head's `/status` and both probes use `agent:work:discord:channel:<thread>`, and its one model request hit the work mock with `Bearer fake-work-key`. Base fails all three with the session-key error. The binding row stays byte-identical and names `main`.

B's six denied commands in the bound thread got `You are not authorized to use this command.` before any plugin handler or model call, in the single-agent fixture.

With `accountId: "*"` and no `commands.allowFrom` or `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, B2's denied `/new` and `/reset` fail on base with the session-key error and reach core refusal on head, which B2-U also finds on main unbound threads and plain channels. No final reply, reset or model call, but session metadata is written.

C's local unit test, outside this PR, defers the session lookup and revokes `commands.allowFrom` during it. The handler never runs. Removing only post-lookup `authority.assertActive()` at `native-command.ts:538` makes it fail. Source shows no Discord-observable step inside that window, so a Gateway run cannot hold it.

Main's unbound work-routed thread already selected `work` and sent `fake-work-key`, so routed-agent credential selection pre-exists. On both revisions the sender gate at head `native-command.ts:383-385` rejects before route state at 391, except in the `/new` and `/reset` bypass. This PR adds no await and moves no authorization check.

prs.title: fix: show recovery guidance for interrupted conversation startup
prs.body:
Closes #168200
Related: #167873 (native-thread recovery; separate runtime work)

## Problem and user impact

When the agent cannot load its saved conversation or fails to prepare a code workspace, users receive generic or implementation-heavy errors. The first revision replaced those with vague language, unsupported refresh advice, and a Control UI prerequisite for messaging-channel users.

## Changes

- Present a specific failure and a concrete next step across live chat, persisted reports, session summaries, and channel replies.
- Keep channel recovery in the current channel: `/new` for a conversation that cannot be resumed, or resend the request to retry workspace setup. No requirement to open the Control UI.
- Preserve certified, redacted startup diagnostics through production history projection, including the canonical exact-run failure envelope. Details and Copy error still work after reopening; unrelated diagnostic payloads remain excluded.
- Preserve main's compact mobile disclosure/actions and readable recovery text outside collapsed Details. Refresh remains a status read: it preserves drafts and sends no additional turn.
- Include shared presentation/failure-notice dependencies in the wrapper extraction inventory.

### Current user-facing copy

| Failure | Control UI | Messaging channels |
|---|---|---|
| Missing saved thread | **OpenClaw couldn't find the saved conversation data needed to continue.** Start a new conversation and send your request again. | **OpenClaw couldn't find the saved conversation data needed to continue.** Send /new to start a new conversation, then send your request again. |
| Lost/expired workspace allocation lease | **Couldn't finish preparing the code workspace.** Send your request again to retry workspace setup. | Same as Control UI; no UI access required. |

Known underlying runtime bug: Codex can remove an unused internal thread while OpenClaw retains its binding. The inference preflight then fails on that stale reference before the existing lifecycle recovery runs; [PR #167873](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167873) addresses that separate runtime gap. This does not establish cleanup as the cause of every missing-thread error or imply the visible OpenClaw transcript was deleted.

Presentation only: no automatic retry/replay, lease repair, thread rebinding, runtime error-code changes, or reconstruction of missing conversation state. The message does not guess why setup lost its lease or claim all work was rolled back.

## Review disposition

The prior ClawSweeper findings concerning persisted diagnostic loss and channel recovery are addressed. Channel recovery now follows explicit maintainer feedback: actionable instructions in the current channel, not a Control UI prerequisite. Independent Codex AutoReview of the October 22 revision (`c6cb7884cefa`) found no actionable P0–P2 issues. This follow-up changes only the approved explanatory sentence and its existing consumer expectations; it does not change executable flow.

## Conflict repair validation (2026-10-29)

Resolved nine conflicts against main `2f47962f2bdc`; repair head `2b5b74d8b70a`. Preserved the approved wording, main's extracted lazy notice renderer, session-error formatting owner, terminal lifecycle publication, model-change history projection, and repeated-failure count. Startup presentation now lives in the extracted owners rather than restoring their removed implementations. Added missing polling-helper imports in the touched browser fixture.

- 174 Gateway tests passed: lifecycle summaries, display projection, persisted `chat.history`, and live chat events.
- 53 copy/channel tests and 36 UI notice tests passed.
- Four startup browser scenarios passed, including desktop/mobile guidance, reopened Details/Copy, draft preservation, and no resend on Refresh. Fresh mobile screenshots inspected; wording and appearance intentionally unchanged by this repair.
- Core and UI production typechecks, targeted typed lint, formatting, and PR-relative `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh Codex AutoReview: no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Previous wording-revision proof below remains historical; fresh CI owns broad validation for the repair head. First browser attempt stopped before launch because pinned Chromium was missing; installation resolved setup. The first runtime attempt was invalidated by import formatting during compiled-artifact capture; the settled-source Gateway run above passed. No shared install or live Gateway/state changed.

## Prior wording validation (2026-10-25)

Copy explanation revision: `3dc262639693`. Earlier code/flow review and conflict repair remain prior-head evidence; fresh PR CI owns broad proof for this head.

| Focused proof | Result |
|---|---|
| Runtime: failover copy, external reply, command lifecycle, session lifecycle, history projection, persisted history | 178 passed across 6 files |
| Composer notices, including changing errors and compact mobile rendering | 22 passed |
| Startup browser scenarios: live desktop/mobile, topbar, restored Details/Copy, draft/no-resend | 3 passed; 6 unrelated/unchanged cases not selected; screenshots inspected |
| Core production typecheck (`tsconfig.core.json`) | Passed |
| Targeted typed lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` | Passed |

Consumer-test wrapper: 441.01s including cold compilation (unit lane 153.49s; Gateway/history 98.64s; command lifecycle 137.35s; UI 9.97s). Browser lane: 306.58s including SDK artifact-lock wait and production build, not isolated browser-test time. New-head CI timing is pending.

The removed repair checkout had no reusable pinned install. An initial attempt with the canonical checkout's mismatched dependencies failed during setup; a frozen, isolated worktree install resolved it. The missing pinned Chromium was restored before the successful browser run. No shared dependency install or live Gateway/state was modified.

Direct checks also confirm the exact approved UI/channel sentences, normalized-summary recognition, and the 160-character persisted-summary budget. Full `check:changed`, broad test type graphs, and the previously reported test-shard root-budget failure were not rerun. Live Telegram delivery remains unverified; browser captures use synthetic Gateway fixtures, not a live provider/channel.

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent's managed GitHub OAuth credential expires, `github_identity_status` can diagnose it but cannot open the reconnect flow from the active session. The operator has to find the agent's Tools settings manually.

## Why This Change

- Add a capability-negotiated `screen` action, `github_identity_settings`, that opens the current agent's Tools settings only in the requesting Control UI.

- Derive tool listings from session-stable capabilities, while reconnect guidance and Gateway routing honor current-client capabilities and effective tool/action policy.
- Retain manual Settings guidance when the reconnect action is not callable.
- Regenerate the compiled Gateway validator from its schema so the new command passes actual dispatch.

## User Impact

An active session can diagnose an expired GitHub identity, open the reconnect surface, and verify recovery without exposing credentials or losing the session.

## Evidence

## Limits

prs.title: fix(memory-core): memory_search times out while indexing through a same-host OpenAI-compatible embedding server
prs.body:
Closes #187531

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `memory_search` times out while the Gateway indexes memory through an `openai-compatible` embedding server on the same host, such as llama-server on `127.0.0.1`.

## User Impact

Searches stay usable during background indexing when the embedding server runs on the Gateway host behind `openai-compatible`, as they already do with the managed `local` provider. On such a server, indexing now sends one request at a time, so full rebuilds can take longer on hosts with spare parallel capacity. That is the same tradeoff #137484 accepted for `local`. No configuration changes and no reindex are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Memory indexing sends four embedding requests at once to every provider except the hardcoded ids `local` and `ollama`. A same-host server like llama-server handles requests in arrival order, so a search's query embedding waits behind the whole indexing backlog.

Embedding providers already declare their own inline timeouts in the provider runtime, and the memory config reference says concurrency is provider-owned. This adds the same kind of optional declaration, `inlineIndexConcurrency`, and makes it the only source of the non-batch index concurrency:

- memory-core reads the declaration (a positive safe integer; otherwise the existing default of 4) and drops the hardcoded provider ids.
- `local` (llama.cpp) and `ollama` declare 1, so their behavior is unchanged.
- The generic OpenAI-compatible adapter declares 1 when its base URL is loopback (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`). Remote and LAN endpoints keep 4. Adapters that reuse it, such as oMLX on its default loopback URL, inherit the declaration.

No new config, as maintainers decided in #68812 and #68822. Batch embedding keeps its own concurrency. Inline timeouts are unchanged: index requests already get 10 minutes, and the 30 s `memory_search` deadline is what the queue was exceeding.

## Evidence

**Live e2e, isolated Gateway (real `memory_search` tool call).** This ran on this patch applied to main 40b1f0175 (commit 37e334ae7), before the rebase. The rebase onto 0801814cff only conflicted in the test file. The production code this PR touches is unchanged between those two bases, except an unrelated import in the llama.cpp runtime file. A Gateway from current main could not be live-tested on this host; see Gaps.

Setup: `pnpm openclaw gateway run` on an isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME`, with the QA mock model and llama-server b11960 in Docker limited to 2 CPUs on `127.0.0.1`. It ran EmbeddingGemma 300M Q8_0 with the managed preset's flags (`--embedding --parallel 1 --ctx-size 2048 --ubatch-size 2048`) and `memory.search.provider: "openai-compatible"`. Each run: start the Gateway, check that `memory_search` finds the `MEMORY.md` note on the idle server, add 12 Markdown notes of about 40 KB, then 10 s later run an agent turn that calls `memory_search`. Queue depth comes from llama-server `/metrics`; the tool result and its duration come from the session transcript.

| Build | Gateway log `indexing memory files` | llama-server deferred tasks at search | `memory_search` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main 40b1f0175, run 1 | `concurrency: 4` | 17 | 30.05 s, `timedOut: true`, no results |
| main, run 2 | `concurrency: 4` | 19 | 30.07 s, `timedOut: true`, keyword-only partial |
| main, run 3 | `concurrency: 4` | 19 | 30.07 s, `timedOut: true`, keyword-only partial |
| this branch, run 1 | `concurrency: 1` | 1 | 1.63 s, semantic hit `MEMORY.md` |
| this branch, run 2 | `concurrency: 1` | 1 | 2.37 s, semantic hit `MEMORY.md` |
| this branch, run 3 | `concurrency: 1` | 1 | 1.31 s, semantic hit `MEMORY.md` |

During indexing, main kept 16-23 tasks deferred and the branch kept 1-5.

prs.title: fix(compaction): preserve active request provenance
prs.body:
## Problem

Compaction could replace the active human request with a later internal observation, or revive completed human work during an independent internal run. The first revision also rejected a second recovery after the production semantic-window reader archived the original admitted request.

## Solution

- Carry the admitted request boundary from the runtime through AgentSession into core compaction, with explicit unresolved/none/legacy-inference selection.
- Centralize recorded-source attribution for summary input, preserved excerpts, and token accounting. Clear stale generated pending asks without rewriting unrelated summary sections.
- When a **processed** request is outside the current semantic window, reuse the existing bounded checkpoint request. Newer human steering wins; internal updates preserve that request or authoritative none. Missing **unprocessed** admitted input still rejects.
- Reuse the existing compaction checkpoint; no new persisted state, configuration, or schema. Replace the redundant in-memory mapping test with persisted, repeated-recovery coverage.

This is an independent remediation related to #178477, with credit to @dmitryvostryakov for the original report and implementation. Request provenance remains separate from general model-quality concerns.

## Verification

- **Base red:** all three repeated-recovery cases fail at `a085f281e904` with `invalid_session: Compaction cannot find the admitted request.` on the second recovery.
- **Rebased head:** `a9c37408306168b27b2b777de4e9165e0c9eb76b`, based on main `3523ef6747820e3253442a633dc09888c4cdf5fe`. Both commits are patch-identical to the published pre-rebase revision; no conflicts or new behavior changes.
- **Current-head focused proof:** 96 tests passed across eight files, including persisted repeated recovery, compaction provenance and request selection, registered safeguards, runtime recovery, and host seed handling.
- Persisted boundary cases reopen through production `SessionManager.openAsync(..., { compaction: true })`, verify the original request is absent, and complete a second automatic compaction: human request survives internal updates; internal selection remains none; newer human steering supersedes the old request. Missing pending input still rejects.
- Focused lint, formatting, mock-export ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed on the rebased tree. The mock-export ratchet was the failing check in the prior CI run.
- The prior repair's independent P0–P2 review was scoped-clean; unchanged patches retain that review. Earlier core, agents-sessions tests, and Plugin SDK test TypeScript checks passed.
- Proof uses the real SQLite reader and AgentSession with deterministic fallback; it does not claim a live-provider run. Broad CI must run on the new head.

## Scope

Ready-for-review preparation only. Do not merge or backport.

prs.title: fix: keep parent dashboard publishing after subagent completion
prs.body:
Closes #187524. Related: #182191. ## What Problem This Solves A parent conversation cannot publish its dashboard update after yielding to a subagent, even when its verified completion retains permission to use `show_widget`. Observed workflow: publishing was available in the browser-origin parent turn, disappeared after child completion, and remained unavailable in a later CLI turn. A fresh browser-origin turn republished the existing widget without a reset, restart, runtime patch, or access change. That recovery leaves the completion defect unresolved. ## User Impact An authorized completion can finish pinned updates on its requester’s dashboard. The executor requires `pin: true` and rejects `presentation.target` before board writes, document hosting, or device presentation. Inline output, untrusted inter-session input, requester tool denials, and revoked execution authority remain restricted. No configuration or migration is needed. **Maintainer decision requested:** approve this bounded pinned-authoring exception to the current-client execution gate preserved by #182191. This PR supplies the implementation and proof; it does not assume owner approval or request a general permission bypass. ## Why This Change Was Made The synthetic completion caller has no browser capabilities. Catalog stability preserves discovery but still refuses widget execution. Reuse the existing pinned-without-inline-client mode only after the capability profile verifies the completion handoff and the requester session records an inline-widget surface. Keep execution policy, live delegation guards, board routing and widget grants. ClawSweeper correctly found that the reused mode could reach a `node_panel` presenter. The shared widget executor now enforces the mode’s promised pin-only contract while preserving operator/completion schemas and descriptions. The new device-negative cases fail on the original submitted head and pass with the guard. ## Evidence Candidate: `20e74311344052168446455c62fc39d7decc6bab`. **Normal Gateway with a real model:** passed on this candidate, using the built CLI Gateway process and the native Codex app-server with an existing signed-in account. The parent and child both ran real inference; there was no local model endpoint, scripted response, mocked tool executor, mocked board RPC, or paused storage in this run. A browser-capable authenticated WebSocket client submitted one public `chat.send`; no manual follow-up turn or session reset supplied the completion. The parent first pinned `status` with `

before real child

`, spawned one isolated child, and called `sessions_yield`. After the child finished, a separate parent completion run pinned the same name with `

after real child

`, read the dashboard, and returned `LIVE_PROOF_COMPLETE`. Public `board.get` returned widget revision **2**; fetching its returned frame URL gave **HTTP 200**, and the response body contained `after real child`. These were driver assertions, separate from the model's success statement. Redacted native Gateway events (UTC; run IDs replaced with local aliases): ```text 2026-10-29T10:27:22.030Z parent run-1 show_widget start 2026-10-29T10:27:22.161Z parent run-1 show_widget result 2026-10-29T10:27:24.346Z parent run-1 sessions_spawn start 2026-10-29T10:27:24.830Z child run-2 lifecycle start 2026-10-29T10:27:29.360Z parent run-1 sessions_yield start 2026-10-29T10:27:29.584Z parent run-1 lifecycle end 2026-10-29T10:27:30.662Z child run-2 lifecycle end 2026-10-29T10:27:31.183Z parent run-3 lifecycle start 2026-10-29T10:27:36.036Z parent run-3 show_widget start 2026-10-29T10:27:36.094Z parent run-3 show_widget result 2026-10-29T10:27:38.689Z parent run-3 dashboard result 2026-10-29T10:27:40.930Z parent run-3 lifecycle end assertions: widget=status revision=2 publishedHtmlReadback=200 bodyContainsAfter=true real-model driver: 1 passed; 34.536 seconds body; 48.91 seconds wrapper ``` Replay setup: build through the normal CLI launcher, start an isolated full Gateway with Canvas hosting enabled, opt into the existing native account with `appServer.homeScope: "user"`, refresh the native model catalog, and connect with `inline-widgets` and `tool-events`. The one-off driver used the upstream `createOpenClawTestInstance` process launcher, subscribed to both run-scoped `agent` and session-scoped `session.tool` events, and allowed only `show_widget`, `dashboard`, `sessions_spawn`, and `sessions_yield`. The disposable Gateway/state were cleaned up after the assertions; production was untouched. This is Gateway/model/persistence proof, not a rendered Control UI interaction or live channel-transport test. - **Real Gateway flow and persistence:** `src/gateway/server.dashboard-completion.product.test.ts` starts one isolated Gateway and exercises public `chat.send` → real `sessions_spawn` → `sessions_yield` → verified child-completion → `show_widget` → native `board.widget.put` → SQLite content readback. The model endpoint is a deterministic local Responses fixture. The final board RPC is not mocked; a call-through storage gate permits a controlled await before the real write. - **Authorized publication:** the same named widget advances revision 1 → 2, and persisted HTML changes from `before child` to `after child`. - **Final-effect controls:** public `chat.abort` or `sessions.reset` while that write is paused leaves revision 1 and the original HTML unchanged. Reset’s lifecycle rotation is verified. Both rejected writes return `BoardGatewayUnavailableError`; neither commits the new content. - **Red/green:** restoring the original main `agent-tools.ts` assembly from `2df9f694f2` makes the same Gateway fixture fail with `Completion publication refused before the board write`. The new registered-device tests fail on the submitted head for both `pin: false` and `pin: true` plus `node_panel`. - **Current checks:** Gateway regression passes (1 test, 3 scenarios; 62.24 seconds wrapper wall time, 14.29 seconds test body). Widget, presenter, prefix and scheduled-widget suites pass (63 tests; 53.72 seconds wrapper). Existing scoped-role board admission controls pass (6 selected, 17 unselected; 28.67 seconds wrapper), including role revocation and session replacement during the native write reservation. Targeted typed lint, Gateway-root test typecheck, formatting and whitespace pass. Both required CI checks have passed on this head. - **Independent review:** the fresh P0–P2 pass identified only the old indexed device bypass, explicitly recognized the working-tree fix and Gateway proof, and found no additional code defects. That guard and its regression are now committed together. - **Test cost:** one shared Gateway boot covers the 3 lifecycle cases; only model responses and a call-through storage await are controlled. The 324-line allocation covers the original 69-line completion regression, 33 lines for device controls and 222 lines for the Gateway flow. No new runtime test seam, timers, sleeps, or per-case Gateway boots. Representative redacted Gateway output: ```text allowed: parent show_widget -> sessions_spawn -> sessions_yield -> child complete -> completion show_widget; revision=2 revoked: same flow, chat.abort while write waits; revision=1; native write rejected reset: same flow, sessions.reset while write waits; revision=1; native write rejected ``` **Coverage limits and broader scope:** the separate deterministic Gateway regression covers abort/reset and red-on-base controls; the real-model demonstration above covers the allowed completion path. No WhatsApp transport, production runtime patch, or actual-device presentation was used. The device control registers an eligible presenter and verifies that availability, presentation, board write and document hosting are never reached. Separate isolated WhatsApp-context Gateway investigation retained all 47 tool names and executed a backend read after child completion, but reproduced personal-library `skill_workshop` schema churn. prs.title: fix(cli): observe ambient cancellation on stdin byte reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a CLI command reads its payload from stdin (`--script -`, `--value-file -`, `--message-file -`, piped auth/credential input, etc.) and the operator presses Ctrl-C while stdin is held open, the command hangs waiting for an EOF that never comes; if the operator then types a late payload, the command still completes its mutation (a cron job write, a secret-store write, an agent message dispatch, a browser action batch, …) despite the cancellation.

- Problem: `readByteStreamWithLimit` (`packages/media-core/src/read-byte-stream-with-limit.ts`) only had `maxBytes`/`onOverflow` and no way to observe ambient cancellation, and the CLI read sites awaited it with no abort guard before turning the bytes into a mutation.
- Solution: add an optional `signal` to `readByteStreamWithLimit` that destroys the held-open upstream stream and rejects with `AbortError` on abort; pass `getAsyncWorkSignal()` at the eight CLI/extension stdin read sites and `signal?.throwIfAborted()` before the mutation.
- For a WHATWG `ReadableStream` (e.g. `response.body`) the abort is delivered through an owned reader (`getReader()` + `reader.cancel()`); async iteration locks such a stream, so `cancel()` on a locked stream rejects and is swallowed, leaving the held-open read never settled. Native streams still tear down via `.destroy()`.
- What changed:
  - `packages/media-core/src/read-byte-stream-with-limit.ts` — `signal` option with per-chunk `throwIfAborted()`; abort listener tears down the held-open upstream and surfaces the error as `AbortError`; Web streams read through an owned reader (`isWebReadableStream` + `readWebReadableStreamWithLimit`).
  - Six CLI sites: `src/cli/cron-cli/trigger-options.ts`, `src/cli/secrets-store-input.ts`, `src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.shared.ts`, `src/commands/agent-message-input.ts`, `src/commands/agent-exec-input.ts`, `src/commands/models/auth-manual-input.ts`.
  - Two extension sites: `extensions/matrix/src/cli-shared.ts` (recovery-key stdin), `extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/shared.ts` (`--actions-file -`).
  - `src/plugin-sdk/concurrency-runtime.ts` re-exports `getAsyncWorkSignal`.
- Not changed: byte limits, overflow errors, the shared read contract's return shape, the update-executor/update-capability stdin that are private updater-protocol holders.

## Why This Change Was Made

The same ambient signal (`getAsyncWorkSignal`) already cancels async work across the CLI; the stdin byte read was one of the few hot paths that never consulted it. Patching every caller individually with `addAbortSignal` would leave the shared `readByteStreamWithLimit` contract signal-unaware and force each site to reinvent held-open-stream teardown, so the fix lives in the shared reader plus a per-site throw-if-aborted guard before the mutation.

- Best fix: a shared `signal` option that both tears down the held-open upstream and rejects with `AbortError`, so every stdin site gets identical cancellation semantics and the `throwIfAborted()` immediately after the read guarantees a cancellation that lands after EOF is still not turned into a mutation.
- Rejected: per-site `addAbortSignal(signal, process.stdin)` only, because it leaves the shared reader unaware of cancellation and duplicates teardown at eight sites.
- Risk: the abort listener is registered only when `signal` is non-undefined; when no signal is present behavior is unchanged. `config-cli-input.ts` (the same family) is fixed separately by #187336 and is out of scope here.

## User Impact

Pressing Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or SIGTERM while a CLI command waits on stdin now stops the read and exits promptly (`130`/`143`) instead of hanging until EOF or a hard timeout; a late payload typed after the interrupt is rejected and no longer completes the cron/secret/message/browser mutation.

## Evidence

**Real built CLI + real signals, main vs this head (bidirectional).** Same command (`cron add myjob --script - --cron '0 0 * * *'`) and same timing, stdin held open by a FIFO write-holder, signals injected by `kill`. Exit codes captured from the wrapper:

| scenario | main (pre-fix) | this head (post-fix) |
|----------|----------------|----------------------|
| SIGINT while waiting | **137** (hung, killed by timeout) | **130** immediate exit |
| SIGTERM while waiting | **137** (hung, killed by timeout) | **143** immediate exit |
| SIGINT then late input | **137** (still hung, not rejected) | **130** ~0 s, `CLI stopping (SIGINT)`, late input ignored |
| normal script + EOF | reads script, reaches `gateway cron.add` | reads script, reaches `gateway cron.add` (identical) |

Post-fix on SIGINT prints `CLI stopping (SIGINT)` and exits `130` in ~0 s, never reading the late payload; pre-fix prints only `Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.` and hangs until the wrapper kills it (`137`), and in the late-input case stays hung rather than rejecting.

**Web ReadableStream cancellation, bidirectional.** A stalled WHATWG `ReadableStream` (never enqueues/closes) read with `readByteStreamWithLimit(stream, { maxBytes, signal })`, then `controller.abort()`:
- pre-fix (read via `for await`, abort calls `cancel()` on the locked stream, rejection swallowed): the read **never settles** — the test run hangs until timeout (EXIT 124), reproduced in isolation with a real `ReadableStream`.
- post-fix (owned reader, abort calls `reader.cancel()`): the pending `read()` settles with `AbortError` and rejects with `{ name: "AbortError" }` immediately.

**Unit tests** (`packages/media-core/src/read-byte-stream-with-limit.test.ts`): 7/7 green — original 5 plus Web-reader read, stalled-read abort (`AbortError`), and Web overflow-cancel cases (a low-value `aborting after EOF` case that only asserted the resolved buffer was removed per review).

**Regression**: `src/cli/cron-cli/trigger-options.test.ts` 113/113; media shard 403 green.

**Type check**: core + media-core + async-work-scope compile with 0 errors under a temp tsconfig inheriting the root config/paths; the two extension files compile with 0 errors on the changed regions.

prs.title: fix: collected turns lose which queued message each runtime context belongs to
prs.body:
Related: #182176
Narrowed at a maintainer's request: the drain-side restore of overflow summary context moved to #187833. This PR now holds only the model-facing `Queued #N context:` labels, which need the prompt owner's call. It does not depend on #187833.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when several queued messages are answered in one turn, the model cannot tell which queued message a runtime context (sender, message id, room-event framing) belongs to, because the per-source labels are dropped from what the model sees and a lone context among several messages is not labeled at all.

## User Impact

User impact: in a collected turn (and, with #187833, a multi-source overflow summary), each runtime context the model sees is labeled with the queued message it belongs to, so one message's sender is not read as the sender of every queued message.

## Why This Change Was Made

`collectCurrentInboundContext` already labels each source's context (`Queued #N context:`) in `text`, but session v4 projects the `fragments` to the model, and the fragments were concatenated without those labels. It also skipped labeling whenever only one source had context, so a lone context read as covering every queued message. Each context now gets a `runtime-instruction` label fragment before its own fragments, and labeling applies whenever the turn has more than one source.

This adds model-facing prompt text (one short label line per context in multi-source turns). Single-source turns are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Regression** (red on base production file, green here): `queue.collect.test.ts` › "labels a lone source context in collected text and model fragments": two collected messages, only the first with context; the turn's `text` and the projected fragments both read `Queued #1 context:` before the context.

**Gates:** `tsgo` core and `oxlint` on touched files clean; `oxfmt --check` clean; `queue.collect.test.ts` 88/88 pass.

**Cost:** one test, about 2 ms, in the existing `queue.collect.test.ts`.

**Gaps:** no live-model run for this label change; it is a prompt-content change and the regression pins the exact projected text.

**History:** the branch keeps the earlier commit and adds a merge of current main whose tree is main plus only these labels, so the PR diff is the two files above.

prs.title: fix(gateway): startup fails on a transient database lock while clearing stale turn claims
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/187723

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway startup fails with `database is locked` and stays down until it is restarted when another writer holds the state database while startup clears turn claims left by the previous Gateway process.

## User Impact

User impact: a transient lock during that startup step is retried and logged, as it already is for tool recovery and workspace-journal pruning, so the Gateway comes up. A lock that outlasts the retries, and any error that is not a lock, still stops startup as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186920 (sibling of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178326) routed the worker startup recovery writes through `retryGatewayWorkerStartupRecovery`, a bounded retry that only fires on SQLite lock errors. The turn-claim clear runs between the two wrapped steps, but it still called the state writer directly. The clear is repeatable (the placement store notes that the next boot can repeat it), so it now shares the same retry. A lock error means the write did not commit, so it is not the uncertain result that comment says aborts startup; other errors, and a lock that outlasts the retries, still abort startup. It uses the worker operation label `workerPlacements.clearLocalTurnClaims`, which the worker's own lock diagnostics already print. The existing harness from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186920 gets one more row for this step, and the Gateway docs list it among the retried steps.

## Evidence

Tested at `63d961b972f` (base `upstream/main` `76f483876f86`), Linux, Node 24.22.1.

The proof uses the lock-contention harness from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186920. The Gateway is real (`startGatewayServer` on a loopback port, isolated state, plugins, cron and channels off) and so is the state SQLite database. When the turn-claim clear starts, a second SQLite connection takes `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and the harness releases that lock after the first lock error. A spy around the real store method only decides when that happens.

Before (base `76f483876f86`, with the new test row):

```text
$ pnpm test src/gateway/server-startup-worker-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t clearLocalTurnClaims
 × clearLocalTurnClaimsAfterRestartAsync: release 10998ms
   → database is locked
Error: database is locked
 ❯ createError src/state/openclaw-state-worker-error-identity.ts:248:14
 ❯ receiveSqliteWorkerReply src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-reply.ts:390:19
Serialized Error: { code: 'ERR_SQLITE_ERROR', errcode: 5 }
      Tests  1 failed | 4 skipped (5)
```

After (this PR):

```text
[sqlite/transaction] SQLite transaction lock wait failed ... operation=workerPlacements.clearLocalTurnClaims code=ERR_SQLITE_ERROR elapsedMs=5009 failureKind=lock-contention sqliteErrcode=5 step=begin
[worker-environments] workerPlacements.clearLocalTurnClaims: database is locked; retrying attempt 2/5 in 1000 ms.
[gateway] http server listening (0 plugins, 9.5s)
[gateway] ready
 ✓ clearLocalTurnClaimsAfterRestartAsync: release 11811ms
      Tests  1 passed | 4 skipped (5)
```

Observed result: on the base, the first lock error aborts startup. With the fix, the clear logs one retry, succeeds once the lock is released, and the Gateway reaches `ready` with `GET /readyz` returning 200 (asserted by the test). The four existing rows (tool recovery release, exhaustion and non-lock error; journal pruning release) pass on both sides.

Checks: the touched test file (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, 5/5) and `pnpm check:changed` (core typecheck, lint, core tests and ratchets passed). Its format and dead-export steps were red only on an untracked local file and on unused exports in files this PR does not touch. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file                                           | `--maxWorkers=1` wall |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `src/gateway/server-startup-worker-recovery.test.ts` | 106.9 s               |

Not covered: the lock is taken by a test-controlled second connection at a chosen moment, not by a real concurrent OpenClaw process, because a separately launched Gateway cannot be made to meet a lock at exactly this step. The added row adds about 11 s to the file, the same cost as each existing row.


## Maintainer shipped-entry-point and compatibility proof

[Exact-head built Gateway real-SQLite proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187724#issuecomment-6504792491) binds candidate `63d961b972f538ff1a19c26ddc79b8a0719fa74f` against current main `bbde2b822c133f615d83a9f1db109960c4d68f9e`. A second real SQLite connection holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE until the actual cleanup reports native SQLITE_BUSY. Main fails startup twice on its first call; candidate logs a retry and reaches public /readyz HTTP 200 twice on its second call, reusing prepared store identity 1 across attempts. Both no-lock controls pass. Existing claim rows/history are preserved apart from the intended cleanup fields, and subsequent public agent runs complete.

Persistent-lock exhaustion (five calls), a real non-lock SQLite trigger failure (one call), and real SQLite worker termination with outcome-unknown (one call) all refuse readiness without unsafe replay. Integrity checks pass for all nine core-case databases.

The published latest stable openclaw@2026.10.9 also creates a real completed conversation and then stops normally. The documented existing offline doctor --fix --non-interactive procedure upgrades its agent schema 25 to 38; no migration or Doctor source is changed. Candidate startup on that same state under real contention retries and becomes ready, preserving the public session ID, original history, original setting values and byte-identical workspace note, and a new turn completes. Doctor adds its normal migration/default metadata; config bytes are not represented as identical. See the linked receipts.

Normal builds and focused changed-file lint/format pass. Zero tests run in this maintainer pass. The contributor patch is retained unchanged after simplification: reuse one existing bounded retry owner around the omitted write, with no new settings/schema/API/workspace-recovery bypass. Whole-PR deltas: production +5/-1, tests +5/-1, docs +3/-2.

Merge danger: two-way door; revert restores transient-lock failure without a PR-specific migration. Blast radius is local-turn-claim cleanup during Gateway startup; persistent, fatal and uncertain failures remain admission-stopping.

prs.title: fix(imessage): use a PostgreSQL-safe recovery cursor key
prs.body:
Closes #184862

## What Problem This Solves

With the `state` database family on PostgreSQL, the iMessage channel exits on every start: the recovery cursor's plugin-state key is `` `${accountId}\^@${dbIdentity}` ``, and PostgreSQL plugin state rejects NUL in keys (`assertPluginStateKey`, `PLUGIN_STATE_INVALID_INPUT`). The Gateway auto-restarts the channel until it gives up. SQLite stores NUL inside TEXT, so SQLite installs never hit it.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `recoveryCursorStoreKey()` now returns `sha256(JSON.stringify([accountId, dbIdentity])).hex.slice(0, 32)`, the same 32-hex shape `state-contract.ts` uses for the catchup-cursor and reply-cache keys. I chose a hash over another separator because it has no character-set or length concerns (`dbIdentity` is a filesystem path or a remote host plus path, and keys are capped at 512 bytes), and because the JSON array encoding keeps distinct `(account, identity)` pairs distinct. A hashed key can match the legacy account-only key only if an account id equals the hash of its own pair.
- The one-time adoption of the legacy account-only key (`consume(accountId)` → `registerIfAbsent`) and the retired catchup-cursor migration are unchanged.
- SQLite installs may already hold a cursor under the old NUL key. On a miss under the new key, the cursor namespace is listed (`entries()`, bounded by `maxEntries: 64`). If the old composite key for this `(account, identity)` is present, it is consumed and re-registered under the new key once, through the same adoption path. The old key is never passed to `lookup`/`consume` unless `entries()` returned it. Nothing on PostgreSQL can return it, so PostgreSQL never sees a NUL key operation, and the plugin does not need to detect the engine or catch the validation error. Swallowing the error would hide real read failures; #175442 deliberately surfaces those.

## User Impact

The iMessage channel starts and stays up on a PostgreSQL-backed Gateway. SQLite users keep their existing high-water mark across the upgrade.

## Evidence

**Discriminating test (real PostgreSQL):** `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/recovery-cursor.postgres.test.ts`. It selects PostgreSQL for the `state` family (same harness shape as `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/account-state.postgres.test.ts`), then loads, advances and reloads the cursor through the iMessage plugin runtime. It is registered in `scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs` and the extension database-workers lane.

Base (`71eacdfe9b5`, source change reverted, test kept):
```
 FAIL  extensions/imessage/src/monitor/recovery-cursor.postgres.test.ts > iMessage recovery cursor on PostgreSQL state > loads, advances, and reloads the cursor at channel start (#184862)
AssertionError: promise rejected "PluginStateStoreError: PostgreSQL plugin … { …(3) }" instead of resolving
Caused by: PluginStateStoreError: PostgreSQL plugin state keys cannot contain NUL characters.
 ❯ assertPluginStateKey src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.kernel.ts:125:11
 ❯ readRecoveryCursor extensions/imessage/src/monitor/recovery-cursor.ts:130:29
Serialized Error: { code: 'PLUGIN_STATE_INVALID_INPUT', operation: 'lookup', ... }
      Tests  1 failed (1)
```
Head:
```
 ✓  extensions/imessage/src/monitor/recovery-cursor.postgres.test.ts > iMessage recovery cursor on PostgreSQL state > loads, advances, and reloads the cursor at channel start (#184862)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```
SQLite adoption of the old NUL key is covered by a new case in `recovery-cursor.test-support.ts` (a different database does not inherit the cursor, the active one adopts it once, and the NUL entry is consumed). The existing unit cases now seed the new key.

**Real product: isolated Gateway on PostgreSQL** (`state` and `agent` families on PostgreSQL 17, fresh state after `doctor --fix`, imessage plugin enabled, one account with `cliPath` = Homebrew `imsg` and `dbPath` = a read-only copy of a Messages `chat.db`; `dmPolicy`/`groupPolicy` `disabled`; nothing was sent).

Base build (`71eacdfe9b5`):
```
[gateway] http server listening (3 plugins: anthropic, imessage, memory-core; 2.3s)
[imessage] [default] starting account (reason: startup)
[imessage] [default] starting provider (<imsg> db=<snapshot>/chat.db)
[imessage] [default] channel exited: PostgreSQL plugin state keys cannot contain NUL characters.
[imessage] [default] auto-restart attempt 1/10 in 5s
...
[imessage] [default] channel exited: PostgreSQL plugin state keys cannot contain NUL characters.
[imessage] [default] auto-restart attempt 3/10 in 21s
```
Head build, same config and fresh state, watched for 2 min 40 s:
```
11:42:36 [gateway] http server listening (3 plugins: anthropic, imessage, memory-core; 3.0s)
11:42:37 [imessage] [default] starting account (reason: startup)
11:42:38 [imessage] [default] starting provider (<imsg> db=<snapshot>/chat.db)
(no "channel exited" / "auto-restart" lines through 11:45:16)

$ openclaw channels status
Gateway reachable.
- iMessage default: enabled, configured, running, connected
```

**Real product: SQLite upgrade from the latest stable release.** The released `openclaw@2026.10.7` (npm, `157d8c2`) builds the same `` `${accountId}\^@${dbIdentity}` `` key. Setup: isolated state on SQLite (no `database` section), the same iMessage account and policies, and `cliPath` pointing at a small wrapper that appends the JSON-RPC requests sent to `imsg` to a log and then execs the real `imsg`. That shows the `since_rowid` each build subscribes from. chat.db `MAX(ROWID)` was 16535 throughout.

1. 2026.10.7 first start, no cursor: `watch.subscribe {"since_rowid":16535}`.
2. Gateway stopped. One cursor row inserted in the format 2026.10.7 writes (key `default` + NUL + `local:<snapshot>/chat.db`, 53 bytes; `{"lastRowid":16530}`). Nothing new had arrived, so 2026.10.7 had no inbound row to advance it. Restarting 2026.10.7 consumed the row as its own cursor:
   ```
   {"method":"watch.subscribe","params":{...,"since_rowid":16530}}
   [imessage] suppressed stale inbound backlog account=default ... recovery=true (5 suppressed since start)
   ```
   2026.10.7 then advanced and persisted its NUL-keyed row itself: `plugin_state_entries` → `53 bytes | has NUL | {"lastRowid":16535}`.
3. Upgrade to this PR's build on that same state. 2026.10.7 installs iMessage as a managed npm plugin in the state dir, so I ran `openclaw plugins uninstall imessage --force` (plugin state rows are kept) and put back the identical config, so that the bundled iMessage plugin from this branch loads (`plugins list`: imessage, source = the branch `extensions/imessage`).
   ```
   [imessage] [default] starting account (reason: startup)
   [imessage] [default] starting provider (<imsg wrapper> db=<snapshot>/chat.db)
   {"method":"watch.subscribe","params":{...,"since_rowid":16535}}
   plugin_state_entries (imessage.recovery-cursor): 32 bytes | no NUL | 4749f4dc428df92860bc9f5f54542742 | {"lastRowid":16535}
   ```
   The NUL row 2026.10.7 wrote is gone. Its value is now under `sha256(JSON.stringify(["default","local:<snapshot>/chat.db"]))[:32]`.
4. To make the replay position distinguishable from the no-cursor default (the watermark), the cursor was set back to the step-2 value. The Gateway was stopped, and the namespace was replaced with the 53-byte NUL-keyed `{"lastRowid":16530}` row from step 2. Then this PR's build was started:
   ```
   {"method":"watch.subscribe","params":{...,"since_rowid":16530}}
   plugin_state_entries (imessage.recovery-cursor): 32 bytes | no NUL | 4749f4dc...2742 | {"lastRowid":16535}
   ```
   The build subscribes from 16530, the adopted cursor, not 16535. It consumes the NUL row and advances the hashed row after the replay. 2026.10.7 subscribed from 16530 with the same row in step 2. No `channel exited` or `auto-restart` lines in any run.

**Other checks:** `extensions/imessage` tests pass except `monitor.plugin-payload.test.ts > settles rich-link final delivery ... (true)`, which fails the same way on unmodified base on this machine. The red `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1` job ([run 40382310876](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40382310876/job/121782242862)) is that same case (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called once with arguments: [ 'send', ... ]`). It reproduces deterministically on base `71eacdfe9b5` with every change in this PR stashed, so I attribute it to main, not to this change. I could not re-run the job (it needs admin rights). `extension-test-plan`, `database-conformance` and the doctor-contract guard tests pass. Format and the extension typecheck in `pnpm check:changed` pass. Its remaining failures (oxlint in `extensions/copilot`, `extensions/knowledge`, `extensions/qa-lab`, `extensions/workboard`; dead export `PROJECT_CHECKOUT_WAIT_MS`) are in files this PR does not touch.

## Not measured

- No message was admitted during the real-Gateway run (DM and group policy were disabled and nothing was sent), so the Gateway run proves the startup load path, not a live cursor advance on PostgreSQL. The PostgreSQL test covers advance and reload.
- In the SQLite upgrade run, the 16530 cursor was inserted directly into SQLite while 2026.10.7 was stopped, because no new message arrived during the test. 2026.10.7 then consumed it and wrote 16535 itself. I did not test an upgrade where both a NUL-keyed cursor and a pre-database-scoping account-only cursor exist. In that case the NUL-keyed one is adopted, and the account-only one stays as on current main.
- I ran only the new test against PostgreSQL, not the full `test-database-conformance.mjs` suite. Its catalog pre-check needs a role privilege that the local test role lacks.

prs.title: improve(ios): reuse Watch RTC libraries in release archives
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

iOS Store Release and daily TestFlight rebuild both Watch RTC device libraries on every fresh runner, even when their inputs have not changed.

## User Impact

Release operators can reuse verified compiled Watch libraries. Cold builds remain available, both Watch device architectures remain supported, and cache transfer failures do not block releases. There is no app behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Connect both destinations to the existing content-addressed build-phase cache, using a release-specific namespace separate from simulator CI. Only the existing trusted main release job populates it. Each slice still validates its source/toolchain/SDK fingerprint and checksum; signing, export, qualification, and uploads retain their existing paths.

The repeated Rust compilation is required for changed inputs and cannot be deleted, batched, or carried across fresh runners without retaining the existing finished-library artifacts. This change adds workflow wiring and documentation, without adding a cache implementation or another state owner. Ordinary CI cache authority stays unchanged.

## Evidence

- Extended the existing cache test to cover simulator and both Watch device architectures, fresh output directories, changed source/SDK/deployment target, damaged archives, and trusted-main release scope: 5 tests pass.
- Focused lint and tooling test typecheck pass. Workflow actionlint/zizmor and `git diff --check` pass.
- AutoReview reviewed the complete local change against `50bb9ed9160849ac428c72c8cb5da0c254094d0a`, including the existing build and environment-forwarding owners, at P0–P2: scoped-clean. The local ClawSweeper committed-range attempt could not produce a valid report (its structured-output schema rejected an unexpected `nextStep` key). AutoReview is the completed local review. Hosted ClawSweeper also reviewed current head `e4c444614725f0683f351bf7d4ac39f1b7dcac6a` and reported no actionable findings; its then-pending benchmark evidence is supplied below.
- The required workflow/native-launch regression run had 1,016 passing tooling cases and one failure: the central cache policy did not yet recognize the new writer. Its scoped release-writer contract was added and that failed case now passes. The independent native/cache-lifetime shard also passed. The final complete diff was reviewed again by AutoReview at P0–P2: scoped-clean. Reused unaffected passing proof; targeted lint and tooling typecheck pass after the guard change.

### Benchmark acceptance rule (recorded before measurement)

Run five interleaved cold/cached pairs of unsigned Release archives on one `xcode-27-xlarge` runner, using one pinned source SHA and toolchain. Every sample starts with fresh DerivedData, archive products, and Watch output; SwiftPM source packages and Cargo downloads are shared. Cached samples remove local library copies before restoring an exact run-scoped Actions cache, proving service restore rather than accidental same-run reuse.

All ten archives must succeed. Each cold archive must compile both `aarch64-apple-watchos` and `arm64_32-apple-watchos`; each cached archive must verify both slice hits and run zero Cargo builds. Including measured cache restore overhead, the cached median must improve by at least 5%, and p95 must regress by less than 20%. Report individual samples, median, p95, spread, cache population overhead, and host pressure. With five samples per group, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum and is limited evidence.

The temporary benchmark uses the canonical release-project preparation and archive command with code signing disabled; it does not export, upload, or contact App Store Connect. It measures compilation/cache behavior, not signing/export readiness.

### Measured archive results

[Archive-only benchmark and downloadable evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40914933892) passed all ten archives and the acceptance rule. The rerunnable workload is committed on `test/ios-watch-rtc-cache-proof` at `919b6519931533cbf5cf764b458e6eb88a683588`; its iOS app, RTC, release preparation, and resource collector sources match this PR. The proof branch adds the temporary workflow/helper and predates the final cache-policy test-only adjustment; compiled inputs are identical. Those proof-only changes are excluded from this PR.

Runner: `xcode-27-xlarge`, 5 observed CPUs, 14 GiB RAM, arm64; Xcode 27.1 (27A9275), watchOS SDK 27.0. Dispatch the temporary archive-comparison workflow on the proof branch to repeat the committed workload. The run artifact contains `summary.json`, per-sample JSON/build logs, and resource timelines (seven-day retention).

| Pair | Cold archive (s) | Cached archive + restore (s) | Included restore (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 592.85 | 360.10 | 1.71 |
| 2 | 462.16 | 363.37 | 2.20 |
| 3 | 406.49 | 330.80 | 1.80 |
| 4 | 502.42 | 354.55 | 3.85 |
| 5 | 494.66 | 410.35 | 2.04 |

| Metric | Cold | Cached, including restore |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median | 494.66 s | 360.10 s |
| p95 (maximum of five) | 592.85 s | 410.35 s |
| Range | 406.49–592.85 s | 330.80–410.35 s |
| Cargo release builds per archive | 2 | 0 |
| Verified device-slice cache hits | 0 | 2 |

The median improves **27.2% (134.57 seconds)**, including restore overhead. Observed p95 improves **30.8%**. Every cold archive compiled both device targets; every cached archive verified both target fingerprints/checksums with zero Cargo release builds. The 28.09-MiB compressed cache took about two seconds to save; measured restore/setup was 1.71–3.85 seconds. Cold samples already include local finished-library population, and the one-time remote save is reported separately.

Resource observations: both groups reached full host CPU utilization in some intervals. Per-sample mean CPU busy was 65.1–89.3% cold and 61.1–81.9% cached. Every sampled memory-pressure value was normal (1), no sample recorded a swap-out increase, and all resource probes completed. The collector used under 0.5 CPU-seconds per archive (Node process only, excluding probe subprocess CPU), with 0.76–1.84 seconds of aggregate probe wall time. These are five pairs on one runner, not a production failure-rate or long-tail guarantee; the final cached sample was slower than the earlier cached samples and remains included.

Implementation growth is 24 workflow lines and two documentation lines; the existing Rust build/cache owner is unchanged. The 52 net test lines extend device/invalidation coverage and the central trusted-cache-writer policy without increasing a baseline. Cache misses and transfer failures retain normal compilation.

### Final CI

[Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40926972219) completed successfully for `e4c444614725f0683f351bf7d4ac39f1b7dcac6a`: 31 passed, 29 intentionally skipped, zero failed or pending jobs. The exact-head CI watcher reports GREEN. The CI gate, dependency review, and security-sensitive review statuses are all successful. No branch-related repairs were needed after publication.

One earlier ClawSweeper dispatch was cancelled before executing any steps; its same-head replacement completed successfully. This is an automation cancellation in check history, not a failing test or release job. The PR remains ready for review and unmerged; this campaign did not export or upload any builds.

prs.title: fix(cli): help flags are missing from shell completion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generated shell completions omit Commander's implicit help flags at root and nested commands. For example, `openclaw gateway status --he` does not suggest the accepted `--help` flag.

## User Impact

Completion offers help flags where the command accepts them. Existing cached scripts can be refreshed with `openclaw completion --write-state`. Manually entering help still works; completing a command does not execute it.

## Fix

Reuse Commander's public help projection in the existing shared completion-option owner, while retaining declared hidden options needed to consume operands. Commander continues to own disabled, hidden, custom and shadowed help spellings. No new configuration, dependencies or completion engine.

## Evidence

[Built CLI / real bash and zsh PTY differential](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187799#issuecomment-6504532985):
- Main `ae3561e289dc95232b362329bd7657ddc46adfe0` twice in each shell: help flags omitted at root, nested command, action-looking command and after `--profile`.
- Built candidate twice in each shell: the same inputs offer/complete `--help`.

prs.title: fix(tlon): unlisted citations stay opaque when auto-discovery is off [AI]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tlon could use the bot ship's authenticated session to fetch a cited post from a channel the operator did not list while auto-discovery was off, then prepend that content to the agent input.

## User Impact

With auto-discovery off, Tlon now expands citations only from channels in `groupChannels`, including channels added through the settings store. Citations to other channels remain opaque references.

With auto-discovery on, citations continue to expand from any channel the bot ship can read, including Notebook and Gallery channels in joined groups. Tlon still listens and replies only in auto-discovered chat channels. Cross-channel citations within this operator-selected scope continue to work.

The owner's verified 1:1 DMs continue to expand citations from any channel the bot ship can read. This exemption does not apply to channel messages or group DMs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Citation resolution now receives a predicate that reads the live channel configuration before constructing or fetching a post path. Explicit-list mode requires the cited channel to be in the current `groupChannels` (file config plus settings store); auto-discovery mode permits ship-readable citations because that setting selects joined groups as a whole. The DM path additionally permits the verified 1:1 owner case. Owner authority is rechecked from live settings before each citation read, so reassignment revokes the exemption even while a multi-citation message is being processed.

Sender admission still happens before citation expansion, and approval replay remains unexpanded.

This pull request was prepared with AI assistance.

## Evidence

- Red/green boundary proof:
  - Against base `8014c48bb9f`, the explicit-list table failed because an admitted citation to unlisted `chat/~private/leadership` was fetched.
  - Against previous PR head `3ac509b8f3f`, the auto-discovery regression failed because a Notebook citation made zero authenticated reads.
  - Against previous PR head `9fd3c54b525`, the configuration-transition regression failed because a removed settings-store channel was still fetched from the cumulative watch set.
  - At current head `92b47b163e9`, the focused command passed all 61 tests in 5 files (26.30 s harness time), including settings-helper and Urbit client coverage.
- Per changed test file with one worker: `cites.test.ts` passed 7 tests in 23.66 s, `index.thread-mentions.test.ts` passed 19 tests in 28.03 s, and `index.club-sender.test.ts` passed 15 tests in 28.41 s. Compiler preparation dominated these wall times.
- Every expanding citation table row now also verifies that `CITED-CONTENT` reaches the agent input's `message.rawBody`, rather than only checking that a fetch occurred. Explicit settings additions are eligible immediately, while a concurrent settings-store removal is not overwritten by completion of an older groups-UI persistence request.
- A temporary production-monitor fixture used the real authenticated Urbit client against a synthetic local endpoint. With auto-discovery enabled, Notebook and Gallery citations each made exactly one authenticated post fetch. The test passed in 226 ms (90.96 s wall time including cold compiler preparation); the fixture was deleted after capture.
- The explicit-list production capture remains valid: same-channel and DM-to-listed citations fetched once; channel-to-unlisted, channel-to-Notebook, and non-owner-DM-to-unlisted citations made no post request. The owner-DM exemption fetched once.
- A second temporary production-transport fixture used the real `UrbitSSEClient` and guarded HTTP path. A permitted citation made one cookie-bearing request; authority revoked while request preparation was awaiting the final guard made zero additional HTTP requests. The sanitized fixture passed in 73 ms (105.75 s cold wall time) and was deleted after capture. The committed resolver regression also revokes authority after a nonempty scry response and verifies that no cited content is returned.
- The test-lines ratchet passed locally at 6,310,558 lines against a ceiling of 6,310,560 (2 lines slack), with a net test delta of +20. The branch merged `main` because the named baseline gate exceeded the former ceiling; this PR did not raise the baseline. Line-cap and max-lines ratchets, changed-file formatting, extension production/test typechecks, targeted lint, documentation checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The full Tlon run passed all 299 assertions across 35 files, but Vitest exited 1 after the unchanged `write ECONNRESET` teardown error in `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/channel-ops.transport.test.ts`. Its isolated rerun also passed all 10 assertions and reproduced only that teardown error.
- Required local agentic review was run. Suggestions to add per-sender or club restrictions were rejected because those are membership hardening outside the operator-selected channel boundary; its documentation wording concern was incorporated. ClawSweeper's later findings were reproduced and fixed: live citation authority now reaches the guarded HTTP boundary, and groups-UI persistence preserves approval-owned state while installing the complete settings-derived snapshot. A follow-up local review also prompted the post-response authority recheck.
- Known gaps: no live Urbit ship was used, and the agent's generated reply was not exercised.
- Accepted edge case: if `session.dmScope` is not per-peer, other DM senders share the session and can see content the owner cited in a DM. The monitor already warns about that configuration.

### Sanitized production-path capture

Cookie values and the loopback port are omitted.

```text
[explicit-list-citation-boundary]
sameChannel.authenticatedFetches=1
dmToListed.authenticatedFetches=1
ownerDmToUnlisted.authenticatedFetches=1
channelToUnlisted.postFetches=0
channelToNotebook.postFetches=0
nonOwnerDmToUnlisted.postFetches=0

[auto-discovery-citation-boundary]
notebook.authenticatedFetches=1
gallery.authenticatedFetches=1
PASS index.citation-transport.test.ts (1 test, 226 ms; 90.96 s wall time including cold compiler preparation)

[tlon-citation-authority-boundary]
permitted.authenticatedFetches=1
revokedDuringPreparation.postFetches=0
PASS citation-authority.transport.test.ts (1 test, 73 ms; 105.75 s wall time including cold compiler preparation)
```

The earlier owner-reassignment fixture also remains valid: the first owner citation fetched once, a settings update reassigned `ownerShip`, the former owner's second citation made no post request, and the dispatched role was `user`.

prs.title: fix: Gateway stops report cleanup failure after an exec is refused before launch
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after one exec call is refused before its command starts, every later Gateway shutdown reports an owned-process cleanup failure. A typical trigger is a tool call whose signal times out while the relay waits for launch permission.

## User Impact

User impact: a clean stop or restart no longer fails with "Plugin runtime still owns resources" or "service child cleanup identity lost" just because an exec was cancelled before launch earlier in the process. Real identity loss is still reported.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the relay anchor sends `prepared`, it has no command yet. It is waiting for the launch frame. If the launch-authority check threw before the host wrote that frame, the relay host treated the refusal as identity loss and rejected cleanup without a receipt. The process supervisor keeps that rejection for the life of the process, so every later `shutdown()` rethrew it.

Now the POSIX control sender returns a distinct `ServiceChildLaunchNotInitiatedError`, but only when `launch()` was never called. In that case the host fails startup with the original refusal, starts the normal cleanup deadline and sends `cancel`. The anchor already handles that message. It reports "command startup cancelled before spawn", and its closing receipt retires the relay through the usual extinction join.

Cleanup still fails closed when the frame may have been written, when the anchor never answers (the hard deadline fires), or when the relay has already left `starting`. That matches the rule from openclaw/openclaw#183247 that missing closing evidence rejects cleanup.

`bash-tools.exec-launch-policy.integration.test.ts` used to require shutdown to reject after a retained-child refusal before launch. That expectation pinned the bug. The test now checks that the refusal reached the relay's launch boundary and that shutdown is clean, and its unused `expectedCleanupFailure` plumbing is gone.

Start-frame construction moves into `service-child-relay-preparation.ts` without behavior changes, so `service-child-relay-host.ts` stays under its 700-line cap. The Windows `BrokerChild` launch path is unchanged.

## Evidence

- New real-relay test `supervisor.prelaunch-initiation.real.test.ts`. A refusal before the launch frame rejects with the original `TimeoutError`, the command never runs, a later spawn succeeds, and `shutdown()` resolves. The negative control refuses after calling `launch()`, and shutdown stays fenced.
- `service-child-relay-host.test.ts`. The revoked-at-`prepared` case now plays the anchor's `startup-error` and `closing` replies and gets the original refusal back. A new case checks that a silent anchor still hits the hard deadline.
- Red/green on `d44b7df3`. With the new tests on unmodified sources, 4 of 58 fail, and they are exactly the new and changed cases. With the fix, all 58 pass across the six affected relay, supervisor and exec launch-policy files.
- `pnpm test -- src/process/supervisor src/process/spawn-broker` passed 356 tests with 0 failures and 77 platform skips.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed typecheck for core and core tests, lint, format, and the line-cap and max-lines checks. Two checks failed on code outside this diff. The first-party mock export check flags `src/gateway/server-shutdown.runtime.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server.spawn-broker.test.ts` and fails the same way on clean `origin/main`. The dead-export scan lists 41 exports, none in files this PR touches.
- Seen in production. A refusal at 19:58Z showed up at a 20:23Z Gateway stop as "Failed to reset global singleton lifecycle state", wrapping "service child cleanup identity lost: TimeoutError: request timed out".
