prs.title: fix(ui): catch empty typing avatars in remote-draft tests
prs.body:
Closes #165045

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: remote-draft browser checks pass when the typing avatar loses its content but its frame remains visible.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The existing direct and group browser cases now reject empty or hidden avatar initials. Shipped-entry-point verification remains outstanding.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing remote-draft scenario owns this check. It now requires visible Owner initials with the expected text while preserving the avatar frame's absolute-position assertion. No production renderer or additional test scenario is introduced.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and scope</summary>

The original selector accepts either an avatar or its layout slot. A sized frame can remain visible after its content disappears; pending slots also hide their children without hiding the frame. The new descendant assertion checks the initials themselves, not the wrapper or accessible label. The fixture supplies Owner without an image URL. Both direct and group cases use this checkpoint; image/fallback rendering remains unchanged.

The earlier repair, #173786, was closed without merging. This change independently verifies the content-removal control on the selected base.
</details>

## Evidence

Final local checks: isolated Linux container, supported Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Chromium 156.0.8078.4. All three checkpoint controls were repeated on this runtime for both direct and group cases; the older Node 24.20.0 runs are retained separately. Base `50c3ff63fcd42100dbf0bd0ff677c759ffee3178`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Content removed; original avatar checkpoint | Direct and group both pass incorrectly with empty text and classes/role/name retained. |
| Content removed; repaired checkpoint | Both fail at the expected initials assertion. |
| Content restored; repaired checkpoint | Both pass with visible `O` initials and the placement check intact. |
| Full existing spec on base and fix | Both report 4 passed / 5 failed. The later RTL CSS matcher and browser-cleanup failures are unchanged. This is not a passing full-suite claim. |
| UI E2E typecheck | `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json`: exit 0. |
| Focused lint | `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json ui/src/e2e/session-suggestions.e2e.test.ts`: exit 0. |
| Focused format | `pnpm format:check ui/src/e2e/session-suggestions.e2e.test.ts`: exit 0. |
| Test-line ratchet and `git diff --check` | Exit 0. |
| Independent source/diff review | Complete, P0–P3, for the full two-file diff at `14fee5abe8df86db19134b893b78c7732a473847`: no findings. Simplification steps 1–3 and slop pass clean. |
| Worktree setup | `node scripts/worktree-setup.mjs full`: exit 0. The unchanged UI build reports an advisory chat-boot gzip overage. |

The mutation probes temporarily stop immediately after the avatar checkpoint, before unrelated later assertions. Their instrumentation is not committed. These runs exercise the existing browser suite with its fixed-response Gateway fixture; they are not real-Gateway proof. The restored checkpoint on supported Node completed in 17.00 seconds including setup; the full fixed file took 19.00 seconds wall time. CI seconds are pending.

<details>
<summary>Content-removal output</summary>

```text
base/direct: avatarContent="", legacyAssertion="passed"
base/group: avatarContent="", legacyAssertion="passed"
fix/direct and fix/group: toHaveText("O") failed; observed avatar text ""
restored/direct and restored/group: avatarContent="O", contentAssertion="passed"
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Browser-fixture controls, not real-Gateway proof</summary>

Content removed while the frame remains visible:

![Browser-fixture avatar with initials removed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/def53b42-a995-464e-bd20-1f155b4f60c8)

Restored visible initials:

![Browser-fixture avatar with O initials restored](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18a4ebe8-3e87-49d0-820f-4da0ef23e516)

</details>

Production code delta +0/-0; browser-test delta +5/-1. The existing-format allocation record grants exactly the four added test lines; no test is added.

Merge risk: two-way door; the blast radius is the existing remote-draft browser assertions, not shipped application behavior.

Pending verification: real-Gateway attempts on Node 24.20.0 and supported Node 24.22.1 stopped at the executor's native child-process cleanup boundary before producing completed proof; the latter also reported watcher exhaustion. Auto Review aborted before producing a report. The completed independent source/diff assessment above is separate from that failed tool attempt and is not an Auto Review result. The full-spec failures above remain unresolved and predate this patch. The batched macOS proof run remains outstanding.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/22e87ec9-1af6-4e99-be52-ab7eb2c427df)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/edd39895)

prs.body:
Related: #96692; complements #119737. Compared with merged backport #180878, this draft retains observed-deletion lifecycle and per-physical-write/retry coverage; neither check and publication are atomic.

## What Problem This Solves

A threaded reply can outlive its parent. An observed parent deletion currently becomes only an informational event, so queued output, native buffered output, and files can continue publishing to a destination that no longer exists.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retire the exact active publishing address after an authorized deletion, without cancelling the underlying agent work. Carry that publication-only signal through deferred replies, previews, native streaming, and ordinary delivery. At the ordinary sender boundary, verify the live parent before each physical text/card send and file completion, including known-safe transport retries. Native retries and preview/final edit retries honor observed parent retirement too. Managed writers and deletion signals reach partial updates, both finalization paths, explicit rate-limit retries, and invalid-block replacement; ambiguous final-edit readback keeps the original reader. Keep earlier accepted parts and do not turn a later failure into permission to replay them.

This complements the confirmed-placement receipt work in #119737. It does not replace that PR or claim to repair every existing receipt/reconciliation inference. A parent read and Slack write are not atomic. Native streams without an observed deletion remain a separate limitation.

## User Impact

After OpenClaw observes deletion of an active reply parent, it stops publishing further output to that parent, including buffered native output. Child deletions and another workspace's matching timestamp leave unrelated publishers intact; explicit top-level sends remain supported. Ordinary threaded sends now require a readable live parent, adding bounded read requests and failing without publication when that evidence is unavailable. Workspace/listener and direct-handoff authority stay scoped to the existing delivery owner.

## Evidence

- Independent review found a native HTTP429 replay gap, and hosted review found a preview/final edit replay gap. Both are corrected in this candidate. A fresh frozen review of the complete staged candidate reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. Its confidence is limited by unavailable surrounding source and unrun tests, types, lint and formatting; live behavior remains unverified.
- Candidate base: `7dcc40f7addb9e45ce3e36768c505ff9cb005209`.
- Regression cases cover deletion before pending final text/file output, deferred delivery, native buffered append/stop, workspace/child isolation, queued sender release, multipart acceptance, upload completion, and identity/transport retry boundaries.
- All 23 original changed TypeScript files and the seven follow-up files passed Node syntax parsing, and `git diff --check` passed. These do not establish type or runtime correctness.
- Local dependency setup is blocked: Corepack's fetch of the repository-pinned pnpm version received HTTP 403 from the managed package registry before installation. No alternate registry, package-manager version, or credentials were used.
- The focused repository test wrapper exits before collection because `node_modules` is unavailable. Tests, typecheck, lint, formatting and CI are pending; syntax-only checks and source review are not substitutes.
- No live Slack test messages, service changes, deployment or release performed. The incident's original raw Slack response is unavailable, so this is boundary repair rather than proof of the provider's exact fallback behavior.

Draft: validation and independent review must be resolved before readiness.

Production growth is needed to propagate exact-parent retirement across existing ordinary, preview, deferred and native publishing owners and to verify queued writes at the transport boundary. No configuration, schema, dependency or persistent-state changes.

Known readiness blocker from the #180878 comparison: the published head can drop the configured account reader when a monitor supplies its writer, and Enterprise parent reads can inherit the listener lookup policy. A six-file correction with credential-isolation and transport-deadline regressions is staged locally. Syntax and whitespace checks pass; fresh frozen review of the complete staged candidate reported no actionable P0–P2 findings, with unavailable unchanged source context and unrun checks as limits. The configured signing agent refused the normal commit signature, so the correction is not yet committed or pushed. No signing configuration or security hooks were bypassed. Runtime/type/lint/format validation remains pending.

prs.title: fix(ui): match canonical Unicode in multi-select option search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI `MultiSelect` (Agents panels multi-value picker) only lowercased both sides before `includes`. A stored NFD option label did not match an NFC query, and the reverse also failed.

## Solution

Normalize comparison copies at the option filter:

- query: `custom.toLowerCase().normalize("NFC")`
- candidates: `text?.toLowerCase().normalize("NFC").includes(search)`

No display rewrite, no storage change, no new option.

## Impact

- Agents panels multi-select: NFC/NFD labels are searchable.
- No behavior change for pure-ASCII labels.

## Evidence

- Browser unit: `multi-select.browser.test.ts` — `matches canonically equivalent Unicode when filtering options` (NFC query finds NFD label; non-match still empty). Fixture uses `allowCustom: false` so the custom row does not pollute `values(element,"option")`.
- Same NFC comparison contract as chat workspace catalog search (#187036) and workspace attachments (#187674).
- Real matcher + live Chromium MultiSelect (head `064e988b1b0`): stored NFD `Café notes` (`101,769`); NFC query `Café` (`U+00E9`). Production filter has NFC; before miss / after hit.

Before / after (filter + live component):

![MultiSelect NFC before/after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3e149d1-e719-49f0-ae91-112a08788d3b)

Live MultiSelect mounted in Chromium with NFC query matching the stored NFD option:

![MultiSelect live NFC query](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eccc0bb4-2cfa-4c1d-a591-02fb1474c895)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.browser.config.ts ui/src/components/multi-select.browser.test.ts
```

prs.title: fix(ui): match canonical Unicode in workspace attachment search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Canonically equivalent Unicode queries miss uploaded transcript attachments and fallback-model options: a stored decomposed `e` + combining acute does not match a precomposed `é` query, and the reverse fails too. ASCII case-insensitive search already works.

## User Impact

Uploaded attachments and configured fallback models remain discoverable regardless of the query's canonically equivalent Unicode form, without changing their original names or values.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply lowercase-then-NFC only to comparison copies in the existing transcript attachment predicate and MultiSelect filter. The attachment predicate covers desktop and mobile Files panels. This also includes #187679's two commits, preserving all five commits by @huwei-xydt.

There is no shared/global normalizer and no rewrite of attachment names, displayed catalog labels, selected model IDs, custom input values, stored data, or server requests.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway + Control UI proof and inspected before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187674#issuecomment-6504023447)

Real Chromium exercised actual file uploads and Agent Settings → Fallbacks against isolated, built Gateways and production Control UI bundles. Desktop attachments, mobile attachments, and MultiSelect each ran both Unicode directions twice on main and twice on candidate, plus same-form and ASCII/negative controls: 72 observations. All 12 cross-form misses on main become matches on candidate; controls remain correct.

Both consolidated regressions fail on main for the missing match. Candidate picker browser suite: 16 passing. Attachment E2E file: 3 passing, 1 existing skipped. Focused formatting and type-aware lint: zero warnings/errors.

The helper-only attachment test and appended picker fixture were consolidated into existing browser owner tests, retaining description selection and attachment layout contracts. Merge-base delta: production +6/−3 (net +3); tests +8/−9 (net −1).

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the old comparisons; no state or config migration occurs. Blast radius is Control UI transcript attachment search and MultiSelect option filtering; identities and backend behavior are unchanged.

releases.body:
## 2026.10.10-beta.5

### Highlights

- Node compatibility: installs and updates work again on Node `>=24.16.0 <25 || >=26.1.0`; Node 24.22.1 or 26.12.1 is now a security recommendation instead of a hard requirement, and Node 26 workers no longer abort when stdin is a file. (#186589, #187516) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Gateway streaming: replies that contain tool-call-like XML, look like tool calls, or end long HTML at a partial tag no longer stall the Gateway. (#181397, #183252, #180765; related #175156, #180720) Thanks @RomneyDa, @JasonBuildAI, and @LeizhenZhang.
- Updates and rollback: a failed npm rollback no longer strands the installed package, an immediate Git rollback keeps operator edits, and an update whose executor dies recovers its offline state. (#185160, #185201, #181695; related #184889, #184887, #181649) Thanks @LiuwqGit, @RomneyDa, @syxscott, @wr-web, and @PonySlayer28.

releases.body:
## 2026.10.9

### Highlights

- Patch vulnerable runtime dependencies: fast-uri 4.2.3 rejects malformed URI schemes and hosts in MCP schema validation, oversized Zod collections are rejected early in A2UI and the Discord embedded app SDK, IMAP sender parsing uses nodemailer 10.1.4 so spoofed senders cannot pass the sender token gate, and Microsoft Teams uses patched MSAL Node 7.1.1. (#187294) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Apply `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` to Gateway-built tools, so delegate changes still require approval and media tools stay inside the workspace. (#185094) Thanks @eleqtrizit, @RomneyDa, and @shakkernerd.
- Keep live credentials out of MCP CLI inspection and mask Google OAuth client secrets in logs. (#180321, #180308, #183193) Thanks @brandon-julio-t, @wr-web, @LeizhenZhang, and @RomneyDa.
- Make failed update rollbacks safe: Git-source rollbacks preserve operator edits instead of resetting the checkout, and npm rollbacks retry transient Windows denials and report the exact move that restores a bootable install instead of stranding the package root. (#185201, #184887, #185160, #184889) Thanks @wr-web, @syxscott, @LiuwqGit, @shakkernerd, and @RomneyDa.
- Recover intact agent databases and stale full-text indexes after SQLite tokenizer changes, including update snapshots. (#176234, #176220, #176833, #181206) Thanks @ndakota79 and @RomneyDa.
- Repair publication-complete updates after a remount while retaining the original launcher and sealed recovery helper. (#186557, #186527) Thanks @ericcaiwx-star, @sennyhoney, and @RomneyDa.
- Migrate large transcript archives without exceeding Node.js string limits. (#170853, #170847) Thanks @iamonlv426 and @RomneyDa.
- Allow agents to recover after a full disk once space becomes available, without requiring a restart. (#176902) Thanks @RomneyDa.

### Changes

This maintenance release focuses on security dependency patches, recovery, data preservation, and reliability fixes.

### Fixes

- Resolve local media in Codex steering messages from the session's own workspace instead of the agent's default workspace. (#181528) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Report uncertain process cleanup from buffered commands, such as local CLI speech providers, instead of presenting it as an ordinary command failure. (#184270, #184237) Thanks @shakkernerd and @RomneyDa.
- Keep reapproved node connections alive by publishing the approval with its committed pairing facts before the request resumes. Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Recover stopped Gateways when service activation cannot be verified; retain untouched-recovery behavior in Windows triage. (#172784, #181577, #181698) Thanks @SMF12138 and @RomneyDa.
- Avoid uninstalling a Gateway service during a passive macOS stop when no service is installed. (#181257) Thanks @shakkernerd, @LiuwqGit, @eleqtrizit, @syxscott, and @RomneyDa.
- Recover CLI Node runtimes when launched from the filesystem root, including launchd jobs. (#178112, #177739) Thanks @downingkeys and @RomneyDa.
- Start new ACP sessions in the requested working directory instead of the default workspace. (#176852, #123557) Thanks @yinx65588-boop, @crappier, and @RomneyDa.
- Prevent overlapping model refreshes from failing requests. (#179144) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Honor an explicit SSH port 22 in `openclaw gateway probe --ssh` instead of the alias's configured port. (#171092) Thanks @zhangguiping-xydt, @obviyus, and @RomneyDa.
- Keep skill metadata such as icons and homepages when an inline YAML metadata value has a trailing comment. (#171224) Thanks @zhangguiping-xydt, @Takhoffman, and @RomneyDa.
- Show provider-ignored options in `openclaw infer video generate` text and JSON output. (#171172) Thanks @ly85206559, @obviyus, and @RomneyDa.

releases.name: openclaw 2026.9.36
releases.body:
This is a gateway-only `extended-stable` release, which is our current equivalent to LTS. This release is OpenClaw from the end of September 2026, plus critical security updates, reliability and performance fixes, and features like new model support. The latest version of OpenClaw at the time of this release is [2026.10.9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases#release-v2026.10.9)

## 2026.9.36

### Highlights

- **Failed updates stay recoverable:** a failed npm rollback no longer leaves the installed package missing, and update checks keep Doctor recovery guidance, stop recopying private rehearsal databases, and no longer reopen candidate-migrated state. Fixes #184889. (#185160, #186177) Thanks @syxscott, @LiuwqGit, and @RomneyDa.
- **Workspace restrictions reach Gateway-built tools:** with `tools.fs.workspaceOnly`, `openclaw` delegates built through Gateway loopback and skill dispatch now require approval as intended, and media tools stay inside the workspace. (#185094) Thanks @eleqtrizit and @RomneyDa.
- **Microsoft Teams allowlists stay restrictive:** name-keyed `teams` or `groupAllowFrom` entries that do not resolve now grant nothing instead of opening the bot to every team or group. (#184989) Thanks @eleqtrizit, @RomneyDa, and @shakkernerd.
- **Untrusted input is bounded:** malformed media metadata, inbound mail addresses, TOML, URIs, oversized collections in custom A2UI schemas and Discord's embedded SDK, and response-controlled Microsoft authentication routing can no longer cause unbounded work or alter identity. (#187288, #187282, #187283, #187305, #187289, #187287) Thanks @RomneyDa and @cyyynthia.
- **Replies keep their text:** comparison prose after emoji and other astral characters is no longer stripped from outbound replies. (#187415) Thanks @RomneyDa.

### Changes

- **Certificate trust and Docker images:** the eMudhra trust remediation is applied, and Docker release images carry source/version-bound evidence with more reliable architecture builds. (#186639) Thanks @RomneyDa.

### Fixes

- **Credential and content boundaries:** derive the filesystem policy for Gateway-built OpenClaw tools, keep unresolved Microsoft Teams allowlists closed, and scope the patched MSAL to the affected Teams and Azure Identity consumers. (#185094, #184989, #187287) Thanks @eleqtrizit, @RomneyDa, and @shakkernerd.
- **Untrusted parsing:** bound Matrix media metadata and IMAP mail parsing, the TOML key parser, URI parsing, and oversized Zod collections in custom A2UI schemas and Discord's embedded SDK. (#187288, #187282, #187283, #187305, #187289) Thanks @RomneyDa and @cyyynthia.
- **Reply delivery:** keep comparison prose after astral characters in the outbound sanitizer. (#187415) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **xAI:** allow `off` for older models without configurable reasoning effort instead of rejecting it as an invalid thinking level. (#187425) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Update, install, and Doctor:** restore the installed package root after a denied rollback rename, keep Doctor recovery guidance and migration rollback restrictions, preserve cleanup uncertainty in buffered command results, keep the update compatibility inventory out of published packages, and stop retrying broken worktree metadata on every cleanup sweep. Fixes #184889, #184237. (#185160, #186177, #184270, #187424, #187475) Thanks @syxscott, @shakkernerd, @LiuwqGit, and @RomneyDa.
- **Node uploads:** recheck cancellation after opening a staged upload snapshot so a cancelled upload no longer surfaces an `AbortError`. (#162567) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Dependencies:** update the ClawHub `undici` pin, Vercel toolchain packages, and the Vitest cohort on this line. (#187261, #187258, #187275) Thanks @RomneyDa.

issues.title: PermissionError [WinError 5] when rewriting the gateway client lease on Windows
issues.body:
# `PermissionError: [WinError 5]` when the gateway client lease is rewritten on Windows

## Summary

On Windows, rewriting `~/.nanobot/run/gateway.clients.json` intermittently fails with
`PermissionError: [WinError 5] 拒绝访问 (Access is denied)`.

The file is the on-demand gateway client lease (`{"auto_stop": ..., "clients": {...}}`).
It is written with a temp-file + `os.replace()` pattern, and Windows refuses the rename
whenever any other handle has the target open without `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, or when a
real-time scanner is briefly holding the temp file.

Because Python's `Path.read_text()` (used by the same class to read the lease) does not
grant delete sharing, a reader on the other side of the race is enough to make the write
fail. The failure is not retried, so it escapes as an exception to the calling client.

Related: a failed write also means the client is *not* registered in the lease, which is
the data structure that decides whether an on-demand gateway may auto-stop.

## Environment

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Windows 11 (AMD64) |
| Python | 3.14.9 |
| nanobot | 0.4.0 |
| Commit | `4a14faa47e9af06a66968cb59f5b5d46754dc6fe` |
| Install | source checkout, `python -m nanobot gateway --foreground --port 18790` |
| Data home | `%USERPROFILE%\.nanobot` |
| File system | local NTFS, not a network drive, not OneDrive-synced |

## Actual behaviour

```
PermissionError: [WinError 5] 拒绝访问。:
  '%USERPROFILE%\.nanobot\run\gateway.clients.json.d8y0i3t6.tmp'
  -> '%USERPROFILE%\.nanobot\run\gateway.clients.json'
```

Observed while a single gateway service was running (one launcher process plus its
worker child, the worker owning ports 8765 and 18790). The run directory was writable —
`run/gateway.json` was being written successfully in the same time window — so this is
not a directory ACL problem, and the lease file was not marked read-only. No `.tmp`
leftovers remained, i.e. the `finally: temporary.unlink()` cleanup ran each time.

## Expected behaviour

The lease write should tolerate a transient sharing violation, since the file is
short-lived state that is read roughly once per second by
`monitor_gateway_clients()`.

## Root cause

`nanobot/gateway/runtime.py`:

- write path — `GatewayClientLease._write_state()` (lines 782–798):

  ```python
  fd, temporary_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
      prefix=f"{self.state_path.name}.", suffix=".tmp", dir=self.state_path.parent
  )
  temporary = Path(temporary_name)
  try:
      with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
          json.dump(state, handle, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
          ...
          os.fsync(handle.fileno())
      temporary.replace(self.state_path)      # <-- single attempt, no retry
  finally:
      temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
  ```

- read path — `GatewayClientLease._read_state()` (lines 766–773):

  ```python
  payload: object = json.loads(self.state_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
  ```

- poller — `monitor_gateway_clients()` (lines 801–815) calls
  `lease.begin_orphan_shutdown()` every `poll_interval_s` (default `1.0`), and
  `begin_orphan_shutdown()` (lines 622–637) reads *and* writes the lease.

On POSIX, `os.replace()` over a file that another process has open simply succeeds.
On Windows it maps to `MoveFileExW(..., MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)`, which returns
`ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (5) when the destination has an open handle that did not specify
`FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, or when the destination is read-only.

Python's `open()` / `Path.read_text()` on Windows requests read+write sharing but **not**
delete sharing, so any concurrent `_read_state()` — in the gateway process, in a second
client process, or in a status/UI reader — is enough to make the replace fail.

Note that `begin_orphan_shutdown()` does take `transition_lock` before touching the file,
so the *application-level* readers and writers it controls are serialised. The remaining
windows are:

1. external handles that do not participate in the app-level lock (real-time antivirus /
   Defender scanning the freshly written `.tmp`, Windows Search indexer, backup agents,
   an editor with the file open), and
2. any future/third-party reader of the lease that calls `_read_state()` outside the
   transition lock.

Either way the mitigation is the same: don't let a transient share lock turn into a
hard failure.

## Minimal reproduction of the underlying Windows behaviour

```python
import os
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

d = Path(os.environ["TEMP"]) / "share-lock"
d.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
target = d / "gateway.clients.json"
target.write_text('{"old": 1}', encoding="utf-8")

handle = open(target, "r", encoding="utf-8")   # same sharing as Path.read_text()
tmp = d / "new.tmp"
tmp.write_text('{"new": 2}', encoding="utf-8")


def replace():
    try:
        os.replace(tmp, target)                 # nanobot line 796
        print("ok")
    except PermissionError as exc:
        print("failed:", exc)                   # -> [WinError 5]


thread = threading.Thread(target=replace)
thread.start()
time.sleep(0.01)
handle.close()
thread.join()
```

A single `os.replace()` fails here; a short bounded retry succeeds as soon as the reader
closes.

## Proposed fix

Retry the replace with a bounded, short backoff. The whole function is state that is
rewritten immediately afterwards anyway, so a few milliseconds of patience is harmless,
and it keeps a scanner/reader blip from raising into the client.

```diff
--- a/nanobot/gateway/runtime.py
+++ b/nanobot/gateway/runtime.py
@@ -793,7 +793,7 @@ class GatewayClientLease:
                 handle.write("\n")
                 handle.flush()
                 os.fsync(handle.fileno())
-            temporary.replace(self.state_path)
+            _replace_with_sharing_retry(temporary, self.state_path)
         finally:
             temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
@@ -820,3 +820,20 @@ def _instance_suffix(*, workspace: str | None, config_path: str | None) -> str |
     if not raw:
         return None
     return hashlib.sha1(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
+
+
+def _replace_with_sharing_retry(source: Path, target: Path, *, attempts: int = 10) -> None:
+    """Atomically replace ``target`` with ``source``, retrying Windows share locks.
+
+    Windows reports a concurrent reader of ``target`` (or a scanner briefly
+    holding ``source``) as ``ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED``; the window is short, so a
+    bounded retry clears it where a single ``os.replace`` would fail.
+    """
+    for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
+        try:
+            os.replace(source, target)
+            return
+        except PermissionError:
+            if attempt == attempts:
+                raise
+            time.sleep(0.005 * attempt)
```

`time` is already imported in this module. Worst case adds ~0.23 s before the original
`PermissionError` is re-raised, so a permanently locked file still fails loudly instead
of hanging.

Verified locally against both cases:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Reader holds the file briefly, then closes | replace succeeds, new content visible |
| Reader never closes the file | `PermissionError` still raised, after ~0.23 s |

## Possible follow-ups for maintainers

- If `_read_state()` should never block a writer, the read could be done through a
  handle opened with `FILE_SHARE_DELETE` (ctypes `CreateFileW`) so `os.replace()`
  succeeds even while a read is in flight. The retry above makes that optional.
- Consider logging a warning plus retry-scheduling instead of propagating, so a client
  attach never fails because of lease bookkeeping.

## Workaround for users (no code change)

- Add `%USERPROFILE%\.nanobot` to antivirus exclusions.
- Make sure only one gateway service runs (`nanobot gateway status` / one `gateway start`).
- The error is transient: the next lease write succeeds, and the client can usually
  attach again.

prs.title: feat(email): filter by recipient alias
prs.body:
## Summary

A mailbox is sometimes shared across multiple addresses (aliases that all deliver to the same inbox — e.g. `assistant@example.com` and `team@example.com` landing in the same mailbox). Today the email channel processes every message it receives regardless of which address it was actually sent to, so a bot configured against a shared mailbox ends up acting on mail that wasn't meant for it.

This adds an `alias_address` config option: when set, only messages actually addressed to that alias are processed. Everything else is skipped — logged, deduped, added to `skipped_uids` — exactly like the existing self-sent/SPF/DKIM/allow-list filters already do, so it's never marked `\Seen` either (per #5605).

The match checks `To`/`Cc` (multiple comma-separated recipients handled via `email.utils.getaddresses`), plus `Delivered-To`/`X-Original-To`/`Envelope-To` as a bonus for providers that set them (Exchange Online does not, but Postfix/Gmail-style servers often do).

Leaving `alias_address` unset preserves current behavior exactly — the mailbox processes everything it receives, as before.

This is stacked on top of #5605 (deferred mark-`\Seen`) since the filter's skip path relies on that behavior. Until #5605 merges, this diff will also show that commit — it'll collapse to just the alias filter once #5605 lands.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest nanobot/channels/email/tests/` — 60 passed (6 new: accepts alias match, rejects non-match without marking `\Seen`, matches via Cc, case-insensitive match, matches via `Delivered-To`, no-op when unset)
- [x] Full suite: `pytest` — 6792 passed, 12 skipped (one pre-existing, unrelated failure in `tests/cli/test_tui_launcher.py` reproduces identically against unmodified `upstream/main`)
- [x] `ruff check nanobot/channels/email/`
- [x] `uv run --no-sync basedpyright` (strict type check, per CONTRIBUTING.md) — 0 errors
- [x] WebUI locale parity: `aliasAddress` label/placeholder/help added to all 10 locale files (not just `en.json`), satisfying `channel-locale-registry.test.ts`

prs.title: fix(email): only mark \Seen on messages that are actually delivered
prs.body:
## Summary

A message polled from IMAP was marked `\Seen` as soon as it passed the channel's filters (self-sent, SPF/DKIM, allow-list), *before* it was actually delivered to the agent. This meant:

- A message rejected by a filter (self-sent, SPF/DKIM failure, not allow-listed) was still marked `\Seen`, even though the bot never acted on it — a human checking the mailbox couldn't tell what the bot actually handled from the unread state.
- A message could be marked `\Seen` and then fail delivery to the agent right afterward, silently dropping it.

This PR defers marking `\Seen` until a message has passed every filter **and** been successfully handed off to the agent — mirroring the existing `post_action` (delete/move) gate, which already only applies after successful delivery.

Three related bugs fixed along the way:
- A UID that failed delivery was left in the in-memory dedup cache (marked "already processed") even though it was never marked `\Seen`, so it silently never got retried on a later poll. It's now evicted from that cache on failure.
- A mark-`\Seen` batch failure (e.g. a dropped IMAP connection) could suppress a configured `post_action` for the same successfully-delivered messages. The two are now isolated from each other.
- A mark-`\Seen` batch failure otherwise left the affected UIDs unmarked with no retry, which would redeliver them as duplicates after a restart (the dedup cache is in-memory only). Failed UIDs are now retried on the next poll without re-delivering the message.

No behavior change to filter outcomes or message content — only when `\Seen` gets set.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest nanobot/channels/email/tests/` — 54 passed
- [x] Full suite: `pytest` — 6792 passed, 12 skipped (one pre-existing, unrelated failure in `tests/cli/test_tui_launcher.py` reproduces identically against unmodified `upstream/main`)
- [x] `ruff check nanobot/channels/email/`
- [x] `uv run --no-sync basedpyright` (strict type check, per CONTRIBUTING.md) — 0 errors

prs.title: fix(api): cancel disconnected request work and drain cleanup
prs.body:
## User-visible result

Closing a normal JSON/SSE API connection cancels only that request's work and waits for its actual cleanup. It does not silently detach work, stop another request sharing the session, or release the next same-session request while cleanup is incomplete. Closing a Gateway WebUI/TUI subscription remains a different action and does not become a session Stop.

Resolves NAN-222.

## Scope and root causes

Only `nanobot/api/server.py`, focused public HTTP tests and API documentation change relative to the base. No new execution engine, shared cancellation helper, SDK/Provider/Gateway change, transport polling or blanket session Stop.

The production aiohttp assembly did not enable handler cancellation, so JSON waiting for a result and SSE waiting before the first token could outlive a disconnected TCP client. Real AppRunner/TCP/AgentLoop counterexamples reproduced it; TestServer's implicit cancellation default was explicitly excluded as production-assembly evidence. The app now uses aiohttp's supported `handler_cancellation` setting. Resolved aiohttp 3.14.5 was inspected, not inferred from a requirement range.

JSON and SSE own a request task. Disconnect cancels that task once and drains it through actual settlement. An independent review found the reverse cancellation ordering: after disconnect began asynchronous cleanup, the still-armed execution timeout could cancel it again. The request now keeps only its entered, active Timeout handle and disarms a non-expired deadline synchronously before cancelling. Queued work has no handle; leaving the context clears it; an already expired deadline is not rescheduled. Both original reverse-order counterexamples failed before correction and passed after it. No cleanup timeout or weakened execution deadline was introduced.

## Verification

Final head: `27e104af102892bf764d0ca6a9f5e1c607f7af14`. Required CI and all selected exact-head checks passed: **12 success, 2 out-of-scope skips**. Ready was executed and REST readback confirms OPEN, non-Draft, the same head, base main and mergeable.

- Authenticated real TCP plus AgentLoop checks cover JSON before-result, SSE before-first-token/midstream, queued same-session disconnect, another independent request, both timeout/disconnect orderings, ordinary timeout JSON 504/SSE error behavior, and completed tool checkpoint replay. Cleanup gates must finish before handler settlement or same-session readmission; a cancellation acknowledgement is not the proof.
- Real foreground exec workers prove actual resource exit and a subsequent same-session successful response. Native Windows holds a handle to the exact live worker before disconnect and requires that handle to signal exit; POSIX reap and following-request checks remain. The fixture accepts only the specific Windows WinError 64 closure difference and explicitly awaits its observer so unrelated errors still propagate. Final native Windows CI passed these assertions, not merely an EOF assumption.
- Final-source API selection: 119 passed; the original reviewer probe separately passed both reverse-order cases with ResourceWarning as error. Parent actual Python 3.11.13 ran the 14 disconnect cases from this API checkout. Combined-source regressions also passed; overlapping scopes are not summed.
- Existing auth, media, usage, session, HTTP and SSE error regressions remain. Ruff, API strict types and import boundaries passed. All listeners/workers/private state were cleaned up.

## Matrix ownership and limits

The ordinary CLI already drained its own resources on normal exit; a real CLI process with an authenticated local HTTP provider fixture freshly verified that existing behavior, not a new benefit of this patch. Gateway disconnect/background-child semantics are separately verified in #6519. SDK owner-close/resource lifetime is separately handled in #6522; these PRs are not mislabeled as API implementation.

The first final-head Windows suite failed in an unchanged WebSocket-ready connection test; one bounded retry passed without relaxing that gate, and its first failure's cause remains unconfirmed. Actual API requests must close the connection for disconnect cancellation; a client timeout retaining its socket is not a cancellation signal. Cleanup remains cooperative, already-executed tool effects are not rolled back, and no external model/platform or all-version compatibility proof is claimed. Ready is not formal approval, merge or deployment; Linear remains In Review.

prs.title: fix: keep long-running command activity honest (NAN-262)
prs.body:
## User-visible result

Repeated observations of one long command update one public activity instead of inventing a new task or successful completion at each wait. Two actual executions with the same command text keep independent states and output. Successful stdin/close/inventory control calls stay quiet; real command success, failure, cancellation, enforced timeout and necessary control errors remain visible.

Resolves NAN-262.

## Design and corrected findings

- The execution owner attaches immutable facts to the existing string-compatible ToolResult: a non-control public ID, per-command sequence, observed state and bounded cumulative filtered output. One boundary projects those facts into live and saved-history events. Clients do not infer lifecycle from stdout or filter lists of tool names.
- Nonterminal copy says running/stopping **at the last check**. A command ending after its last observation is not given a fabricated completion event. Model-facing control strings and arbitrary assistant prose are not rewritten.
- Existing per-tool success/error hooks publish facts when available, before a later serial tool's start. The iteration callback does not repeat them. This fixes the independently reproduced `exec/read_file` ordering reversal without announcing a speculative successful command start.
- WebUI rows, state, output and counts use public call IDs. This fixes an independently reproduced collision where two real processes with the same command text inherited the first process's failure or success. Legacy history without execution metadata retains its existing display; no history rewrite or compatibility platform was added.
- The process wait, runtime/idle budgets, exit, retention, cleanup and permission rules are unchanged. No Shell-specific protocol was added to AgentLoop/Runner.

## Verification

Final head: `ab1886d2c8b79ee5c771d7e97e02a8dad0d80daf`. Required CI and all selected exact-head checks passed: **12 success, 2 out-of-scope skips**. Ready was executed and REST readback confirms OPEN, non-Draft, the same head, base main and mergeable.

- Real authenticated WebSocket/reconnect/HTTP-history boundary and actual gated subprocesses prove stable command identity, running snapshots, real exit 7, cancellation, hard deadline, summary/detail/live agreement and preserved output. Actual Telegram adapter behavior was checked with only its external send mocked; nothing was sent to a real channel.
- Independent counterexamples were retained as regressions. After the identity/order fix, disjoint focused Python groups 137/139 passed and nine WebUI files/192 tests passed; parent combination checks and the original external failure probes also passed. Counts from overlapping parent/worker scopes are not summed.
- Actual full Gateway, Bearer-authenticated local model HTTP fixture, real identical commands in different working directories exiting 7 and 0, and Chromium's formal View activity/output controls: old UI showed the first failure twice; final saved history shows separate failed/Exit 7/first output and successful/Exit 0/second output on desktop and 390px. Parent directly inspected both final screenshots; zero page errors. Owned processes, listeners and private state were cleaned up.
- Final Windows fixtures retain real process and Unicode/privacy assertions: PowerShell uses its own quoting rules; cancellation waits for actual partial output; the Unicode-producing test explicitly emits UTF-8 and retains the existing 200-character log budget. Production bytes did not change in those last fixture commits, so the recorded browser evidence remains source-matched inheritance, not a fabricated rerun.

## Limits

No paid/external LLM, real Telegram delivery, every-channel field acceptance or arbitrary old/new client combination is claimed. Local optional-module collection skips were disclosed; they are not passes or substitutes for the selected CI matrix. Earlier Windows failure diagnostics did not prove a unique root cause; the final explicit fixture and native matrix passed without changing product codec/privacy policy or relaxing gates. Ready is not formal approval, merge or deployment. Linear remains In Review.

## User and maintenance scenario

A model's shell tool should return a bounded observation and keep the same long-running command available for later checks. A trusted user `!command` should instead wait for its full literal result. Those existing behaviors remain; changing how trusted commands wait or construct their replies should not require the model execution loop to know the concrete Shell implementation.

- Make the existing command route directly own trusted user Shell execution, scope setup and full-result handling in `command/user_shell.py`.
- Remove the Loop's Shell-specific callback and concrete ExecTool dependency. This is not a new generic tool/plugin capability or a duplicate execution service: both paths still use the configured Shell tool and existing process/session owner.
- Keep trusted-source checks, workspace/access policy, temporary/log-content scope, turn scopes, literal rendering, model bounded observations and existing timeout/cleanup rules.

The narrow internal `AgentLoop.execute_user_shell_command` method is removed; use the existing command route. No new public SDK/API behavior is promised. This is a concrete maintenance boundary, not a faster shell command, memory optimization or claim that every client/Loop coupling is gone.

## Verification

- **199 Python tests passed**: commands, exec session isolation/tools and task cancellation; real model-observation yield vs user full-result coverage, scope unwinding, existing restricted paths and literal output.
- Touched strict Python types, Ruff, import boundaries and diff checks passed.
- Actual isolated authenticated Gateway + WebSocket user Shell + HTTP saved history: full stdout/stderr/exit status, Markdown preserved literally, restricted traversal rejected. No model request, real credentials, production sessions or daily services. Owned Gateway exited cleanly.

Limits: real process probe on Linux; cross-platform execution is covered only by the selected CI matrix. No merge, deployment or formal review.

prs.title: fix(providers): retire unused clients without closing in-flight runs (NAN-232)
prs.body:
## User-visible result

A long-lived Gateway or SDK instance no longer retains every superseded model client until shutdown. Connections still used by active or queued work stay alive; retired unused clients close, unchanged configurations keep their reusable connection, and borrowed clients are not taken over accidentally. SDK close drains only its own work, including an unconsumed full stream, while preserving buffered events of streams that already completed normally.

Resolves NAN-232.

## Ownership and API boundaries

- Separate resolver cache eligibility from explicit execution leases. Immutable runtimes share a typed resource; retirement closes it only after its final in-flight reference ends. Failed cleanup stays observable instead of disappearing from the owner.
- Pin real handoffs before SDK override/MCP awaits, direct-session locks, turn/child admission, queued execution, archive/compaction and title background work. No scheduling/UI policy or plugin-resource platform is introduced.
- Preserve unchanged default/preset/equivalent SDK override reuse; changed/removed entries retire and redundant factory snapshots are disposed of. Snapshot loaders transfer ownership unless they explicitly declare a borrowed provider.
- AgentLoop-injected providers are borrowed by default; `owns_provider=True` explicitly transfers ownership. `from_config` owns what it builds; CLI/Gateway composition transfers its fresh provider. Bedrock borrows explicitly supplied SDK clients. Low-level callers holding a runtime across awaits/queues must hold a lease; normal SDK/direct execution does so itself. These intentional contracts are documented in the SDK guide.
- SDK shutdown cancels/drains its own admitted work before closing owned resources. The Chat Completions reader uses a same-task idle deadline so Python 3.11 cannot lose external cancellation in `wait_for`'s ready-read window. Returned/late Bedrock streams and thread workers finish cleanup before owned clients close.

## Required parent

This PR is stacked on **#6520**, branch `refactor/heartbeat-to-scheduled-task`, exact parent `76a873e9b31acd4a030cc7e617a5e2d9d19d1dd6`. The retired Heartbeat evaluator was an unleased direct provider consumer; the authorized parent removes that caller rather than preserving it behind a temporary wrapper. Land the parent first. This stack was assembled with a normal local merge, not rebase/force push; no GitHub PR has been merged here.

## Evidence and independently corrected findings

Current head: `e296657b42e9b87b115595f3e57a2d7bb26ec012`.

- Public SDK/direct execution with real OpenAI/httpx clients against an owned synthetic loopback HTTP fixture checks cache reuse, effective-setting replacement, held old execution, cancellation/close, borrowed/transferred ownership and preset/queued-child handoffs. Existing real Codex WebSocket and Bedrock worker/stream tests cover their resource boundaries.
- Controlled A/B loads only the resolver from baseline `cb3ba453...`, keeping the current SDK/HTTP fixture equal: six unchanged runs use one client/one TCP connection in both cases. After 20 effective-setting changes, baseline retains 21 open clients versus one in the candidate; holding an old execution gives two, returning to one after it finishes. Both reach zero after owner close. **Not a full old-version A/B; no RSS, MB, FD, speed or token-saving claim.** The fixture does not forward external traffic.
- Independent failing regressions reproduced Python 3.11 ready-read cancellation loss and SDK owner-close blocked on a full event queue. Owner close now reuses RunStream's queue-release/cancellation contract and drains the original tasks. Another independent review then caught normally completed streams being cleared before registry-removal callbacks ran: checking actual completion when the closer executes preserves their successful events. A real HTTP regression failed before correction and passes after it. Green checks on the superseded head were not used to waive that defect.
- Final local selection: Python 3.11.13 **384 passed**; Python 3.12.10 **117 directly affected cases passed**; strict types/Ruff/import checks passed. Earlier 3644-scope/HTTP-client measurements and wider 3.12 runs retain their original snapshot identities, not relabeled as new executions. Parent all-changes combination passes 378 focused cases, with source-matched WebUI/API/Gateway evidence; overlapping scopes are not summed.

## Verification limits

prs.body:
## What changes for users and channel maintainers

Reply-format instructions now belong to the channel that knows how its replies should be written. Telegram, QQ, Discord, WhatsApp, email and MoChat declare their guidance in their existing dependency-free manifests. Feishu keeps the generic prompt and its current Markdown/card rendering capabilities.

A maintainer can change an existing channel's reply style in that descriptor alone, without editing AgentLoop or the shared identity template. A local descriptor-only adjustment was exercised through a real SDK run and an actual HTTP model request. This is an ownership and correctness improvement, not a measured performance optimization.

## Design and boundaries

- Add one optional static `ChannelPlugin.reply_format` value; derive the mapping from existing descriptors, not a new channel-name switch or executable plugin mechanism.
- Gateway/SDK composition snapshot those trusted strings; the CLI adds its own terminal guidance. ContextBuilder selects the current route's value, including scoped channel instances. The core consumes only a string mapping and imports no client/channel runtime.
- No declaration means generic formatting. In particular, the SDK's legacy logical `cli` label no longer imposes terminal restrictions; the actual CLI still does.
- User message text, SDK attributes, session metadata and HTTP request fields cannot supply formatting instructions. No schema, persisted message envelope, hot reload or global fallback is added.
- Preserve current short-paragraph/list guidance for Telegram/QQ/Discord and plain-text guidance for WhatsApp. Do not infer Markdown support from platform names: Telegram already has local HTML/rich rendering and Feishu supports Markdown cards. Remove MoChat's inaccurate claim that its HTTP chat transport is a terminal while retaining the same minimal-format preference.
- Subagents retain their independent prompt builder; parent turns keep their own per-route guidance.

## Verification

- **854 passed, 1 existing skipped** across focused context, memory/compaction, SDK, CLI/Gateway, HTTP API, channel descriptor and Telegram/Feishu/WhatsApp adapter regressions. Final run used a private HOME/XDG/TMPDIR and isolated venv.

- Local HTTP-model public acceptance: **12 checks / 12 actual model requests** through public SDK, CLI and HTTP API. Includes restart/compaction/channel changes, a descriptor-only style fixture, correct CLI terminal guidance, generic SDK/API output, and rejected promotion of untrusted format fields. Owned CLI/API processes exited 0; both private listeners closed.
- `basedpyright`: 0 errors/warnings/notes; Python Ruff and 13-rule import-boundary checks passed; `git diff --check` passed.

## Limits

No external model or live chat-platform credentials were used, so these checks establish actual model-input policy, not external LLM compliance or live platform delivery. No native TUI rendering or cross-platform packaging changes are claimed. No merge, deployment or formal review is claimed.

prs.title: refactor: replace Heartbeat with ordinary scheduled tasks
prs.body:
## Why

Existing Heartbeat instructions were outside normal task management: a protected cron job read a file on each run, chose a recent chat, ran a separate agent turn, and asked a second model pass whether to notify. Users could not edit, pause, run, or delete it like their other automations.

Resolves NAN-341

Related to NAN-222

## What changes for users

- On the first upgraded Gateway start, import an existing `HEARTBEAT.md` / `heartbeat.md` as one ordinary **Imported Heartbeat** automation, every 30 minutes, linked to a dedicated WebUI topic with the workspace's configured permissions.
- Keep the original file. Subsequent file edits do not overwrite the task. Normal edits, disabling, deletion, results and restart behavior are authoritative; empty templates and previously disabled checks import paused.
- Remove protected Heartbeat registration, recent-chat selection, per-run file inspection and notification evaluation. The imported task runs through the existing bound scheduled-turn path, with normal output and cancellation rules.
- Retire `gateway.heartbeat` and `/evaluator-prompt`; no compatibility runtime or plugin framework. Preserve Dream and unrelated transport keepalives. Ordinary jobs named `heartbeat` or `dream` remain ordinary jobs.

## Persistence and safety

Import receipt, new job and removal of the old protected record commit together in the cron store under its existing lock. A deleted task cannot be recreated just because its old source remains. Pending offline actions and prior run history are retained. Source read / persistence failures are surfaced; a failed commit never publishes an uncommitted runnable job. Restricted workspaces cannot import an outside symlink. No most-recent-target or permission fallback.

The normal automation destination is explicit rather than whichever chat last happened to be active. There is no special quiet-result gate, so active imports may produce more routine reports and different model usage; review/pause/edit them in Automations. No memory or latency percentage is claimed. The old implementation already used cron, so this does not claim removal of an extra timer process.

## Verification

- Python scoped regression: **582 passed, 2 skipped**; HTTP/Gateway/WebSocket/helper suite: **164 passed**.
- WebUI related Vitest: **146 passed**; TypeScript, lint, production build, targeted strict basedpyright, Ruff and diff checks passed.
- Real isolated Gateway + authenticated HTTP/WebSocket + local HTTP model stub: three starts; ordinary edit/pause/enable/run/delete; restart after edits and deletion; result persisted after client disconnected during execution; source preserved. Actual desktop and narrow browser task list/details inspected with project Playwright Chromium.
- Migration covers active/paused/empty/missing sources, old protected records, ordinary same-name jobs, offline edits, persistence failures before/after replacement, restricted outside symlinks, ambiguous file names, and repeated startup. No real credentials or sessions, no production service changes.

Limits: local deterministic model, not external model/chat-platform delivery; no universal compatibility or RSS claim. Exact-head CI is tracked separately before Ready. No merge or deployment.

prs.title: refactor(runtime): structure model, stop, and restart controls (NAN-289)
prs.body:
## User-visible result

Stop is not just an acknowledged button press: it waits for the old session's owned work and cleanup before conflicting work can start, keeps the final output and completed tool context, and rejects a stale target instead of stopping the next turn. Closing a WebUI/TUI client still does not stop Gateway-owned work; a Gateway-owned child can outlive its parent's reply.

Resolves NAN-289.

## Implementation and scope

- Route WebUI Stop, TUI Ctrl+C and exact `/stop` through structured runtime requests, ordered with input admission. Keep the session-level Stop scope, actual target/instance checks and textual adapters; do not undo external side effects.
- Fix three independently traced gaps: children remaining after the parent reply were missing from stoppable identity; pending child/exec cleanup could be reported stopped too early; and an admitted side-channel user Shell still preparing could launch after Stop. Cleanup failure retains the admission barrier and an explicit retry path rather than reporting success.
- Keep control receipts separate from the original turn's terminal event and durable output. Empty/stale targets cannot cancel a newer execution.
- Retain and check the existing candidate's explicit model/restart controls, without making their design a prerequisite for the Stop fix. A first message carries a draft model choice without prematurely creating a topic; explicit invalid presets remain errors, while an unconfigured global empty preset keeps the setup action. Restart uses application-owned normal teardown/handoff, existing restart modes and new-instance readiness; controls are not replayed blindly after reconnect.
- The gateway owns execution/security. Clients do not guess cleanup completion from an idle visual state. The optional runtime-control capability does not add a fallback that sends hidden commands to an unsupported host.

## Verification

Final pushed head: `b315f87384e0156a1697339cbfc4519954315490`, normal commits, no rebase/force push.

- Authenticated isolated Gateway, actual WebUI/TUI TCP client implementations and six actual OS work processes: disconnect/reconnect, stale Stop, parent-finished background work, root/descendant and side-channel Shell termination, final output ordering, durable completed tool results and next input. Actual process exit was checked, not inferred from a control acknowledgement. Backend production bytes remain unchanged since the `798fd6c...` public-process probe; later changes maintain stale test assembly/health-lifecycle contracts and narrowly fix first-run UI setup. This is explicitly inherited source-matched evidence, not a fresh process probe on each commit.
- Actual TUI entry in official **WezTerm 20240203**, on an owned Linux Xvfb/Openbox display with private state. Real XTest keyboard Ctrl+C cancelled the Gateway model task, retained its final cancellation tail, then a newly typed message received a new reply and returned to Ready. Parent inspected the final screenshot/result and cleanup records. This keyboard run did not execute an OS command; OS-process cleanup is the separate TCP/process probe above. No private Windows desktop is claimed for this run.
- Local focused regressions: worker Python 184, WebUI 339 and TUI 76; parent affected Python 73, expanded WebUI 471, CLI 172 with one Windows-only skip; applicable type/lint/build/import checks passed. These scopes overlap and are not summed as a coverage count.
- **All 15 exact-head checks succeeded**, including required CI, Linux/minimum/latest/Windows, native packages, Docker, WebUI/browser and TUI selections. Windows initially failed in an unchanged star-prompt lock test; one rerun instead failed in an unchanged Linear webhook test; the second bounded rerun succeeded. Neither successful rerun establishes the first failures' root cause. No timeouts/locks were relaxed and no gate was deleted.

## Delivery and limits

PR remains OPEN and Ready; readback confirms non-Draft, the same final head and base main. Ready is not formal approval, merge, release or deployment. Linear remains In Review.

Terminal interaction was verified on Linux, not as a native Windows terminal appearance test. External chat-platform delivery and unified cross-chat UI projection were not newly added to the public acceptance scope. Cooperative Python cleanup cannot be force-killed safely: a dependency that never finishes cleanup can hold the barrier; Stop does not falsely report success or roll back previous side effects. Early isolation limitations and failed fixture attempts are retained in the task evidence rather than erased by later private-state runs.

prs.title: feat(email): add Microsoft delegated OAuth for Office365/Outlook
prs.body:
## Summary

Office365/Outlook is moving away from basic auth (IMAP/SMTP username+password) toward mandatory OAuth2 for mailbox access. This adds a Microsoft identity platform delegated-user OAuth flow (authorization code grant, confidential client) as an alternative to password auth for the email channel, so it keeps working against tenants that have disabled basic auth.

- `nanobot channels login email` opens a browser for Microsoft sign-in and completes the flow via a local loopback callback server (`http://localhost:<port>/callback`), or lets a headless user paste the final callback URL if no browser could be opened.
- Access/refresh tokens are persisted per `(tenant, app, mailbox)` fingerprint (so a stored token isn't silently reused after reconfiguring for a different tenant/app/mailbox) and refreshed transparently; IMAP/SMTP authenticate via XOAUTH2 when OAuth is configured instead of a password.
- WebUI: new tenant ID / client ID / client secret fields, mutually exclusive with password auth — mirroring the existing `matrix` channel's password-or-token pattern — plus a sign-in status/action control.
- No PKCE: this is a confidential client (it has a client secret), and Azure AD validates `redirect_uri` against a different registered-URI bucket when PKCE parameters are present (public/native client flow) than when they're absent (confidential/web client flow); the OAuth `state` parameter is the forgery defense instead, required and verified on every callback.
- The callback listener treats a request with a missing/mismatched `state` as non-terminal — it responds with an error page but keeps listening, since the legitimate Microsoft redirect may still be in flight (a stray probe or forged request must not be able to kill a pending sign-in).

Leaving OAuth fields unset preserves current behavior exactly — IMAP/SMTP password auth works as before.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest nanobot/channels/email/` — all passing, including new coverage for the OAuth module (token fingerprinting/refresh, XOAUTH2 wiring, callback-server state validation, headless paste rejection of a bare code) and WebUI validation
- [x] Full suite: `pytest` — one pre-existing, unrelated failure in `tests/cli/test_tui_launcher.py` reproduces identically against unmodified `upstream/main`
- [x] `ruff check nanobot/channels/email/`
- [x] `uv run --no-sync basedpyright` (strict type check, per CONTRIBUTING.md) — 0 errors
- [x] WebUI locale parity: new labels/placeholders/help text added to all 10 locale files (not just `en.json`), satisfying `channel-locale-registry.test.ts`
- [x] Verified live against a real Exchange Online mailbox (IMAP + SMTP XOAUTH2, full sign-in flow through Azure AD consent)

prs.body:
## What

Adds [Serply](https://serply.io) as a web search provider, following the same pattern as the existing Serper provider (#4406). Serply is a Google SERP API; selecting it routes the `web_search` tool through `https://api.serply.io/v1/search/` with the user's own API key.

## Why

Gives users another API-key-backed Google search option alongside Serper, useful when they already hold a Serply key or want an alternative to avoid rate limits on free backends. Like every other keyed provider, it falls back to DuckDuckGo when no key is configured.

## Notes

- Serply support is optional, and behavior is unchanged when `SERPLY_API_KEY` is unset. The provider falls back to DuckDuckGo without a key, matching Serper and the other keyed providers.
- Follows the existing provider pattern in `nanobot/agent/tools/web.py`: an entry in `SEARCH_PROVIDER_OPTIONS` (which feeds the WebUI settings picker and CLI onboarding), a branch in `_effective_provider`, and a `_search_serply` method mirroring `_search_serper`. The request sends an explicit `User-Agent` because Serply sits behind Cloudflare, which rejects requests without one.
- Tests added in `tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py`, mirroring the six Serper tests: keyless concurrency fallback, mocked search (URL, headers, params, formatting), env key resolution, DuckDuckGo fallback, HTTP error, and rate limiting. Network is mocked.
- Docs updated in `docs/configuration.md`: provider table row, config example, and the provider enum. See the [Serply documentation](https://serply.io/docs) for the response fields used (`results[].title/link/description`).

## Testing

- `uv run python -m pytest tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py -q`: 51 passed (45 existing plus 6 new).
- `uv run ruff check nanobot/agent/tools/web.py tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py`: all checks passed.
- `uv run basedpyright nanobot/agent/tools/web.py`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Live-tested against the real Serply API with a valid key: `execute(query="retrieval augmented generation", count=3)` returned three normalized results in the shared plaintext format, and `_effective_provider()` resolved to `serply` with a key and `duckduckgo` without one.

Disclosure: I work with Serply. Happy to adjust scope, naming, or drop this
entirely if it isn't a direction you want for the project.

prs.title: refactor(channels): move tool hint rendering out of core
prs.body:
## Why

Tool activity should describe what happened, not decide how every chat platform must display it. The runner currently generates both structured events and a universal shortened hint; this change moves that presentation decision to each channel while preserving existing delivery behavior.

## What changed

- Core hooks publish tool start/end/error facts with call IDs, arguments and results, without generating hint text; remove the presentation-length plumbing from the agent loop and hook assembly.
- Add channel-owned `prepare_tool_events()` before queueing. Plain-text channels reuse the shared formatter, while WebSocket, Linear and Weixin's native progress path consume structured events directly. Project once so retries retain the same envelope and multipart delivery cursor.
- Migrate both classic CLI paths and document the channel/callback contract. WebUI and TUI keep their existing grouping and rendering.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Core: structured tool facts] --> B[Target channel]
    B --> C[Native activity / WebSocket events]
    B --> D[Optional shared text formatter]
    C --> E[Platform-specific presentation]
    D --> E
```

## Scope

Preserves the current wire/storage formats, per-channel visibility defaults and overrides, tool start versus terminal visibility policy, hint-length setting, thread metadata and FIFO/retry handling. No execution, model-context, WebUI layout or file-list UX redesign.

## Tradeoffs

Reuse `ProgressEvent` rather than adding a second tool-event protocol. Third-party channels inheriting the default text projection retain readable starts; native consumers opt out of that projection. Direct `on_progress` consumers must accept `tool_events` to display tool activity instead of relying on core-generated text.

## Blast Radius

The change touches tool progress for local and provider-hosted calls, channel adapters, and classic CLI output. Regression coverage retains Telegram quotes, Feishu cards, Slack text, Linear actions, Weixin native/legacy delivery, Email suppression, and same-envelope WhatsApp multipart retries.

## Verification

- Final head `0216b1cc292938ab6415161c9a40f5095c628dc3`: [GitHub Test Suite](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40706269848) passed all 15 selected jobs, including Python 3.11, Python 3.14 with coverage, Windows Python 3.14, strict BasedPyright, WebUI checks/build/browser, TUI on Linux and Windows, native package acceptance on both platforms, Docker, and the required aggregate gate.
- Local focused regressions: 1,041 passed, 3 optional-channel dependency skips. A separate serial CLI process matched CI's test grouping: 254 passed, 1 Windows-only skip. Full Ruff and Python import-boundary checks passed locally; the shared local environment did not provide a clean full BasedPyright run, so complete strict typing is established by the fresh CI environment.
- The CI follow-up fixes an overlooked privacy-test expectation: tool starts now carry empty core text rather than a core-rendered hint. Exact visible-text and final-response assertions still protect against internal reasoning leaking into progress. No tests were disabled and no CI gates were relaxed.
- Incorporated `main` at `55210eb9f1217bcddb53b8987bcd74ecadd975af` with an ordinary merge, preserving the centralized WebUI outbound owner and WebSocket's structured-event opt-out. Kept wire/transcript/history regression coverage and did not restore the removed socket-side projector.
- No live third-party IM credential tests were performed. The PR remains Draft; this update does not approve, merge, or deploy it.

Contributes to NAN-375

prs.body:
## Why Users need to correct a sent message without creating another sidebar topic. This implements the approved in-place edit: keep the prefix before the selected user message, replace that message and its entire suffix, and generate a new reply in the same session. Related to [NAN-92](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92/webui-支持编辑并重新发送已发送的用户消息). ## What changed - Add **Edit message** beside Copy in the existing desktop/mobile message actions, using the existing `EditIcon`. Edit directly inside the native user-message bubble with its own draft, Cancel/Resend controls, actionable errors and translations in all 10 locales. Composer drafts, quotes, attachments and waiting input remain separate. - Commit the replacement model records and display facts in one session-owner SQLite transaction. Preserve session identity and settings, rotate the history generation, invalidate obsolete summaries/provider continuation, and record retry identity so an accepted input executes once. Both histories now live in the same database; there is no file-backed replacement journal. - Reuse ordinary latest-thread reads for the source snapshot. Confirming the edit is the only mutation. Validate one page-independent source revision and stable message identity inside the transaction, rather than maintaining a separate prepare protocol and an eight-field anchor. - Share prefix retention between in-place replacement and the existing **New conversation** fork. Keep idle admission, the normal execution queue, cancellation safety, and generation fences across drafts, streams, HTTP pages, trace details, navigation caches and late subagent results. - The historical cleanup removed 106 net production lines without moving the implementation into a replacement framework. Original message text is used for the current source check, not retained in the retry receipt. - Retain two Windows PowerShell installer regressions for unrelated uv/pipx modules; main now supplies the equivalent no-auto-import implementation. - Keep a native touch input round attached to its original target across lazy Markdown replacement, including move/end/cancel and listener cleanup. - Admit supported Windows baseline TUI builds with a bounded 160 MiB executable budget; retain the download, required-file, checksum/source/license and oversize guards. ## Scope The first version supports persisted ordinary user text in saved WebUI sessions. Attachments, quotes, session/CLI/MCP mentions, slash/shell commands and special/system deliveries are explicitly rejected rather than resent with lost metadata. Temporary Chat has no persisted edit target; shared history cannot be edited from an individual conversation. The WebUI and gateway ship together, without an edit-specific compatibility gate or older-gateway fallback. Resend is the only destructive authorization, with no second modal. The URL, session ID, handle, title, creation identity, workspace, permissions and model settings remain unchanged. There is no backup topic, hidden persistent fork or version tree. Previously executed file/Shell effects are not rolled back. ## Tradeoffs Model history and display facts remain separate projections, but replacement is atomic in the existing SQLite store. A pre-acceptance failure preserves the previous effective history and editable draft. A model failure after acceptance keeps the new failed turn instead of restoring the discarded suffix. prs.title: fix(mcp): flag business-error envelopes returned with isError=false
prs.body:
## Problem

Some MCP servers report failures by embedding an error payload in the tool
result content — for example:

```json
{"code": 404, "msg": "data not exist", "data": null}
```

— while leaving `CallToolResult.isError` set to `False`. nanobot then treats
the call as successful, so the agent keeps retrying the same tool call until
the tool timeout fires. The generic timeout message (`... timed out`) hides
the real cause, making the failure confusing and wasting tokens.

See issue #5237.

## Solution

After rendering a successful `CallToolResult`, detect a business-error
envelope and surface it as a tool error so the agent can react to the real
failure instead of looping.

The detector (`_looks_like_error_envelope`) is deliberately conservative: it
only fires on a single JSON object that explicitly signals failure:
- an HTTP-style `code >= 400`, or
- `success: false`, or
- `isError: true`, or
- a non-empty scalar `error` field.

Normal prose and success envelopes such as `{"code": 0, "data": {...}}`
(including text that merely *starts with* "Error:") remain successful, so
existing behavior is preserved.

## Testing

Added two focused tests in `tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py`:
- `test_execute_flags_error_envelope_returned_with_is_error_false` — a
  `{"code":404,...}` envelope with `isError=False` is now reported as a tool
  error.
- `test_execute_keeps_success_envelope_as_success` — a `{"code":0,...}`
  envelope stays a successful result.

`ruff check` passes and the full `tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py` suite passes
(91 passed; the 2 unrelated `test_connect_mcp_servers_http_clients_reject_unsafe_redirect_targets`
tests fail identically on unmodified `main` due to an environment/mock issue
and are untouched by this change).

## Scope

- 2 files changed, +79 / -3 lines.
- No new dependencies, no architectural changes — localized to the MCP tool
  result handling.

prs.title: fix(gateway): reduce lease writes and use Windows-safe I/O
prs.body:
## Why

Gateway status queries and the local-client monitor currently rewrite the lease JSON even when nothing changes, performing unnecessary file synchronization and atomic replacement. Necessary lease I/O also bypasses the Windows-safe atomic file helpers already used by gateway process records.

## What changed

- Keep lease snapshots read-only while still reporting only live clients, including PID-reuse detection.
- Persist monitor cleanup only when client records change; continue committing orphan shutdown under the existing lifecycle locks.
- Reuse `read_atomic_bytes()` and `replace_atomic()` for lease I/O, preserving UTF-8 decoding and allowing existing snapshot readers to retain the previous file during replacement on supported Windows filesystems.

## Scope

Keep the existing JSON format, cross-process locks, and lifecycle behavior. No database or retry policy is added. External handles that deny the required sharing can still block writes; this does not claim to resolve every cause of #6514. Process-record cleanup outside the lease is unchanged.

Related to #6514. Thanks to @BBTAN-bot for the report, and @balabommablock-cpu (B Rishabh Rao) for the Windows-safe I/O proposal and [patch](https://github.com/balabommablock-cpu/nanobot/commit/8d671457935e44579f37ceffe6dbaf61b36b00be), adapted here with a real snapshot-replacement regression test. Both contributors are credited in the commit history.

Resolves NAN-385

## Tradeoffs

Status queries filter stale clients in memory rather than cleaning the lease on disk. The monitor and lifecycle mutations remain responsible for persisted cleanup.

## Blast Radius

Local TUI/WebUI gateway status and lease monitoring on all platforms. Registration, release, and shutdown coordination retain their existing lock order. Windows uses the shared atomic-file implementation; POSIX continues to use ordinary reads and `os.replace()`.

## Verification

- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Regression coverage checks unchanged lease bytes/mtime during queries and steady polling, stale-client cleanup, and explicit versus on-demand lifetimes; existing lifecycle-race tests retained.
- Added a deterministic test that opens a real snapshot through the lease read path, performs an actual replacement before closing it, and verifies that the old reader sees the old state while a subsequent reader sees the new state. This test is included in the existing Windows and Linux Python CI suites.
- Local lint, type checking, and tests were not run; validation of the updated head is delegated to this PR's GitHub Actions.
