issues.title: Review pane lists changed files but shows no diffs for repos outside the managed files root

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: area/config
labels.description: Config system, migrations, profiles

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Bug Description

On a Docker install whose Hermes home is `/opt/data` (so the managed files root is locked to
`/opt/data`), the desktop review pane renders the changed-file list for a Git repository that lives
outside that root, but selecting any file shows an empty diff view. The cause is not git and not the
client's diff renderer: the two sibling backend routes disagree about the managed-files boundary.

- `GET /api/git/review/list` calls `review_list` directly — no boundary check.
- `GET /api/git/review/diff` calls `_hosted_fs_read_guard(target, request)` first — which raises
  `403 Path is outside the managed read boundary` for any file outside the locked root.

So the pane can enumerate files it is never allowed to diff. `review_diff` itself returns the correct
diff when called directly, i.e. the git side is fine.

Related: `GET /api/git/review/commit-context` is guarded the same way (it passes the repo root to the
guard), so **Generate commit message** for such a repo fails too. `GET /api/git/file-diff` as well.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes in Docker with `HERMES_HOME=/opt/data` (no `HERMES_DASHBOARD_FILES_ROOT` set), so
   `_managed_files_policy()` resolves to `locked_root=/opt/data`, `can_change_path=False`.
2. Put a Git repository anywhere outside that root, e.g. `/srv/vault`, and make an unstaged edit to a
   tracked file, e.g. `/srv/vault/notes/example.md`.
3. In the desktop app, open a chat **created in** a project anchored to `/srv/vault` (the pane only
   resolves a repo for a chat that was created in the project — see Additional Context), then open the
   review pane (Cmd/Ctrl+G), scope **Uncommitted**.
4. The changed file is listed with the correct `+/-` counts.

## Expected Behavior

Either:

- the diff route honors the same boundary as the list route, so the pane is consistently empty for an
  out-of-boundary repo and says why; or
- a repo registered as a project/workspace is treated as in-boundary for git reads (it is already
  in-boundary for the session: the agent works in it, `review_list` works on it), so the pane is
  fully functional.

What should not happen is a pane that lists files it can never show.

## Actual Behavior

Selecting the file renders no diff ("No diff to show" / empty diff area), with no error surfaced.
The client renders the failed request the same way it renders a genuinely empty diff, so the user
cannot tell "no changes" from "request refused".

## Environment

- OS: Debian 13 container on Linux 6.12.113+deb13-amd64 (Docker install, `HERMES_HOME=/opt/data`)
- Backend: Hermes v0.22.5 (upstream commit `bf0203a7`)
- Desktop app: v0.21.6, Build Origin: Local, connected to the backend over a remote gateway
- Python: 3.14.9

## Error Output

Guard, evaluated in-process against the live policy (same env as the dashboard process):

```
$ HERMES_HOME=/opt/data python -c "..."
managed-files policy: locked_root = /opt/data | can_change_path = False
target: /srv/vault/notes/example.md exists: True
GUARD BLOCKED: HTTPException 403 Path is outside the managed read boundary
```

The same call with the boundary widened passes:

```
unset (today)                           locked_root=/opt/data    -> BLOCKED (403 ...)
HERMES_DASHBOARD_FILES_ROOT=/           locked_root=/            -> ALLOWED
HERMES_DASHBOARD_FILES_ROOT=/srv        locked_root=/srv         -> ALLOWED
HERMES_DASHBOARD_FILES_ROOT=/opt/data:/srv                      -> BLOCKED (everything)
  (a list is silently taken as one literal path, locking the user out of their own home -
   worth a validation error rather than a silent mis-lock)
```

Git layer is healthy — the diff exists and `review_diff` returns it when called directly:

```
review_list(...)      -> [('notes/example.md', 9, 0)]
review_diff(relative) -> 1001 chars: "diff --git a/notes/example.md b/notes/example.md"
review_diff(absolute) -> 1001 chars   (so path form is not the issue)
```

Route asymmetry, `hermes_cli/web_routers/git.py`:

```
125  @router.get("/api/git/review/list")
127      return await _git_op(_web_git.review_list, _git_path(path), scope, base)   # no guard

130  @router.get("/api/git/review/diff")
135      cwd = _git_path(path)
136      target = _fs_path(file, cwd=cwd)
137      _hosted_fs_read_guard(target, request)          # 403 for out-of-root repos
138      return {"diff": await _git_op(_web_git.review_diff, cwd, str(target), scope, base, staged)}
```

Policy and guard, `hermes_cli/web_server_files.py`:

```
18   _HOSTED_MANAGED_FILES_ROOT = Path("/opt/data")
24       locked_root: Path | None                     # single root, ancestry-matched
294  if _default_hermes_root_is_opt_data():
295      root = _ensure_managed_root(_HOSTED_MANAGED_FILES_ROOT) ...
296      return ManagedFilesPolicy(default_path=root, locked_root=root, can_change_path=False)

360  def _hosted_fs_read_guard(target, request=None):
366      root = _managed_files_policy(request, create_root=False).locked_root
367      if root is not None and not _hosted_fs_path_allowed(root, target):
368          raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Path is outside the managed read boundary")
```

## Additional Context

**Second, separate finding — a mid-session project switch leaves the pane with no repo.** Switching a
running chat into a project moves the session workspace (a fresh shell then runs in the repo, and the
agent's tools work there), but the review pane resolves nothing: it shows its "NO DIFFS" empty state
with no file list at all. Starting a **new chat** in that project fixes it — the list appears. So the
pane appears to resolve the workspace once, at chat creation, and never re-resolve it on a project
switch. That cost me a while to find because it looks like the changes vanished; `git status` was
unaffected throughout.

**Workarounds for the 403.** `HERMES_DASHBOARD_FILES_ROOT=/` (common ancestor of the Hermes home and
the repo) makes the pane work; the env var is undocumented — no mention in the docs corpus, absent
from `.env.example` — and it must be in the dashboard process's environment (`$HERMES_HOME/.env`
works, loaded with `override=True`), then the dashboard restarted. Alternatively keep repos under the
managed root. Both are workarounds for the route inconsistency above, not fixes.

**Why this is easy to misdiagnose.** The file list rendering correctly while every diff is empty reads
as a client-side rendering bug; I spent several rounds on file names with spaces, staging state and a
desktop/backend version skew before reading the routes. A one-line guard on `review/list` (or a clear
error in the pane) would have pointed at the real cause immediately.

**Sanitised.** Repo paths, file names and line counts above are generalised from a private repository;
the route line numbers and code excerpts are verbatim from the running build.

issues.title: [Bug]: session_search finds nothing when a query ends with a period (FTS5 syntax error swallowed as zero results)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/sessions
labels.description: Session lifecycle, resume, persistence, history

issues.body:
## What happened

`session_search` returns no results for any query that contains a period not followed by a word character. The usual case is a natural-language question that ends with a full stop, such as `Remember the deploy target.`. The same query without the period finds the session.

## Cause

- `_FTS5_SPECIAL_CHARS` in `hermes_state_search.py` (line 133 on `main`) lists the characters the sanitizer strips. `.` is not among them.
- Step 5 of `_sanitize_fts5_query` (line 1042) quotes a dotted term only when a word character follows the dot (`\b(\w+(?:[._-]\w+)+)\b`). So a trailing `.`, or one followed by a space, reaches `MATCH` unchanged.
- FTS5 rejects it with `fts5: syntax error near "."`. `search_messages` catches the `sqlite3.OperationalError` and returns `[]` (line 1328, "FTS5 syntax error despite sanitization"). The caller sees "no matching sessions", not an error.

## Minimal reproduction

```python
import sqlite3
from hermes_state_search import SessionSearchMixin

san = SessionSearchMixin._sanitize_fts5_query
db = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
db.execute("CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE messages_fts USING fts5(content)")
db.execute("INSERT INTO messages_fts(content) VALUES ('the deploy target is staging')")
for q in ("deploy target", "deploy target.", "Remember the deploy target.", "deploy target. staging"):
    s = san(q)
    try:
        rows = db.execute("SELECT rowid FROM messages_fts WHERE messages_fts MATCH ?", (s,)).fetchall()
        print(repr(q), "->", repr(s), "rows:", len(rows))
    except sqlite3.OperationalError as e:
        print(repr(q), "->", repr(s), "OperationalError:", e)
```

Output with Hermes 0.22.2 and SQLite 3.53.1:

```
'deploy target' -> 'deploy target' rows: 1
'deploy target.' -> 'deploy target.' OperationalError: fts5: syntax error near "."
'Remember the deploy target.' -> 'Remember the deploy target.' OperationalError: fts5: syntax error near "."
'deploy target. staging' -> 'deploy target. staging' OperationalError: fts5: syntax error near "."
```

Through `search_messages`, each of the last three queries returns `[]`.

## Expected

A difference in punctuation alone should not change the results: `deploy target.` should match like `deploy target`.

## Suggested fix

- After step 5 (so `my-app.config` stays quoted), replace any `.` left outside a quoted phrase with a space. Alternatively, strip `.` in step 2, but only after the dotted terms have been quoted.
- Consider logging the `OperationalError` that `search_messages` swallows, so that a sanitizer gap shows up as an error rather than as an empty result. #127109 raises the same concern for memory search.

## Environment and context

- Found on Hermes 0.22.2 (`d923a5eb48`). The lines cited above are unchanged on `main` as of 2026-10-30.
- SQLite 3.53.1.
- We found it while running an agent-memory benchmark. Its recall probes end their questions with a period, and Hermes's native session search returned nothing for them (electricsheephq/bicentennial#275).

issues.body:
### Summary

On a host where `--security-opt no-new-privileges` is incompatible with the active LSM stack, **every** Docker sandbox container cannot `exec`, and Hermes reports it as an opaque *"container … is not running"*. There is no hint about the cause, and no preflight that would catch it before the first tool call.

### Environment

- `main` @ `67d47601`
- Ubuntu 24.04.2, kernel `6.8.0-147-generic`
- Docker `29.8.0`, cgroup v2 (systemd driver)
- LSM stack (`/sys/kernel/security/lsm`): `lockdown,capability,landlock,yama,apparmor`
- Image: a local image (`osxrust:trixie`); Docker Hub is unreachable from this host, so the repro uses a locally present image

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# 1. Any container started by Hermes carries --security-opt no-new-privileges (docker.py:403).
$ docker run --rm --security-opt no-new-privileges osxrust:trixie sh -c 'echo ok'
exec /usr/bin/sh: operation not permitted

# Same with cap-drop, with --init, with seccomp=unconfined, and on a second image:
$ docker run --rm --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges osxrust:trixie /bin/echo ok
exec /bin/echo: operation not permitted
$ docker run --rm --init --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges osxrust:trixie sh -c 'echo ok'
exec /sbin/docker-init: operation not permitted
$ docker run --rm --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --security-opt no-new-privileges osxrust:trixie sh -c 'echo ok'
exec /usr/bin/sh: operation not permitted

# 2. Without the flag the same image runs fine, and NNP works on the host itself:
$ docker run --rm –cap-drop ALL osxrust:trixie sh -c 'echo ok'
ok
$ setpriv --no-new-privs -- /bin/echo ok
ok
```

### What the user sees through Hermes

```python
env = DockerEnvironment(image='osxrust:trixie', cwd='/root', task_id='probe-nnp-1',
                        persist_across_processes=False, timeout=30)
env.execute('echo hello', timeout=30)
```

```
init_session failed (session=…): snapshot bootstrap failed with exit code 1 — falling back to bash -l per command
{'returncode': 1, 'output': 'Error response from daemon: container 6d3c2afc… is not running'}
```

Nothing names `no-new-privileges`, the LSM, or the remedy. `snap_compat: true` happens to work (it drops the flag, `docker.py:406-411`), but only a reader of the source can know that is the escape hatch.

### Why it matters

The Docker backend is the documented terminal-isolation posture (§2.2). On such hosts it is silently unusable, and the failure surfaces on the first tool call as a daemon error, not at startup where the operator could act on it.

### Suggested fix

Mirror the existing capability probe (`_cgroup_limits_available`, `docker.py:456`): at backend startup, run a throwaway `docker run --rm --security-opt no-new-privileges <image> true` once per process, and:

1. On success — nothing changes.
2. On failure — either refuse to start the backend with a message that names the constraint (host LSM refuses `no-new-privileges`; set `terminal.docker_snap_compat: true` or run on a host without it), or degrade to the `snap_compat` argv with a loud warning.

Either way the operator learns at startup, and the terminal tool does not disappear behind `container … is not running`.

### Caveats (what I did not verify)

I did not isolate whether the trigger is Docker 29.8 specifically, the `landlock` LSM, or their combination — only that the flag is the discriminator on this host and that the host itself allows `no_new_privs`. A second host with a different LSM stack would settle it.

issues.title: [Bug]: code health reports "(ok)" when it measured nothing — `base == head` exits 0 with no verdict

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
### Summary

`python scripts/check --only health` reports `=== health (ok) ===` and exits 0 **when it measured nothing**. The outer summary cannot distinguish "measured the tree and found no findings" from "never measured anything", which is the exact class `lazy-deps-guard.yml` declares unacceptable for a check ("can never pass by scanning nothing").

Reproduced on `main` @ `67d47601` (Linux, Python 3.11.8, ruff 0.15.22):

```
$ python scripts/check --only health --base HEAD
=== health (ok) ===
code health: no measured files changed

scripts/check: 1 checks, ok          # exit 0
```

Same with `--json`: `[]` is printed, i.e. a consumer sees "no findings".

### Why it happens

`scripts/code_health/cli.py`:

- the local base is `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` (`gitio.default_base`);
- in a `--depth 1` clone, or in a worktree that sits on `main`, that merge-base **is** `HEAD`, so `git diff` is empty;
- `run()` then takes the "nothing to do" path: `if not head_paths: _skipped("code health: no measured files changed", as_json); return 0`;
- `scripts/check` prints the channel as `ok`.

Nothing in that path is a measurement, but every layer above it (the runner, a CI job, the pre-push hook summary) reads it as a pass.

### Why it matters

- A CI job or hook that ends up with `base == head` (shallow checkout, a worktree on `main`, a manual `--base HEAD`) is green while the tree may violate every rule in `config.py`.
- The failure is silent and looks like the strongest possible signal (`=== health (ok) ===`).
- It is the same "invariant with no measurement" family as #146473: there the DAG is unmeasured, here the gate's own pass is unmeasured.

### Suggested fix

Give "nothing measured" its own outcome instead of `ok`:

1. When `base` and `head` resolve to the same commit, refuse a verdict: exit 2 with `code health: base and head are the same commit (…): nothing was measured`.
2. When `head_paths` is empty for any other reason (deleted-only diff), print a distinct line (`=== health (skipped: 0 files measured) ===`) and exit non-zero under `ENFORCEMENT=blocking`, so a CI summary cannot render it as a pass.
3. In `--json`, keep `[]` but make the skip visible (a stderr marker or an `{"skipped": …}` object), so machine consumers do not read it as a clean run.

### Related

- #146473 — the same class: an invariant that is declared but not measured.
- `scripts/ci/check_lazy_deps_imports.py` — the repo's own reference behaviour: `inventory failed: no tracked *.py files … refusing to pass an empty scan` (exit 2).

### Environment

`main` @ `67d47601`, Linux (Ubuntu), Python 3.11.8, `ruff==0.15.22`, no `.venv` (system interpreter).

issues.title: [Bug]: Persistent Docker reuse ignores immutable config drift

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/tools
labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: tool/terminal
labels.description: Terminal execution and process management

labels.name: tool/file
labels.description: File tools (read, write, patch, search)

labels.name: backend/docker
labels.description: Docker container execution

labels.name: area/config
labels.description: Config system, migrations, profiles

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

issues.body:
## Bug Description

Cross-process reuse of a persistent Docker terminal container is keyed primarily by `(hermes-task-id, hermes-profile, egress posture)`. Most immutable `docker run` configuration is not fingerprinted or compared before reuse.

As a result, changing Docker terminal configuration and restarting Hermes can silently reattach to an old container with stale resource limits, mounts, environment files, security arguments, image, user, restart policy, or other `docker_extra_args`. The operator sees the new value in `config.yaml`, but the live container continues using the old HostConfig/mounts.

This is reproducible against current `origin/main` at `67168a391f26211eba13adfe4ecee74bd365a25b`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a persistent Docker terminal backend with cross-process reuse enabled:

   ```yaml
   terminal:
     backend: docker
     container_persistent: true
     docker_persist_across_processes: true
     container_memory: 1024
   ```

2. Start Hermes and execute any terminal call so the labeled persistent container is created.
3. Change an immutable create-time setting, for example:

   ```yaml
   terminal:
     container_memory: 2048
     docker_extra_args:
       - --pids-limit=1024
   ```

4. Restart/relaunch Hermes without manually deleting the existing container.
5. Trigger a terminal call and inspect the reused container:

   ```bash
   docker inspect <container> --format \
     'Memory={{.HostConfig.Memory}} PidsLimit={{.HostConfig.PidsLimit}}'
   ```

The same behavior applies to changed bind mounts and many other `docker run` arguments.

## Expected Behavior

Hermes should either:

- reuse the container only when all immutable creation-time configuration matches, or
- detect drift, explain which settings differ, and safely recreate the profile/task container.

A gateway/process restart should be sufficient for documented config changes to take effect; users should not have to know the internal labels and manually remove containers.

## Actual Behavior

The existing container is found by labels and reused. On current `main`, reuse has special handling for egress posture and one-direction network lockdown, but there is no general fingerprint for the effective image + immutable run arguments.

Consequently, profile config can say one thing while `docker inspect` shows another indefinitely.

This is operationally dangerous for both resource and security settings: stale mounts or permissive run arguments can survive after the operator believes they were removed, while increased limits intended to recover a wedged workload are silently ignored.

## Affected Component

- Docker backend
- Configuration
- Persistent terminal lifecycle

## Debug Report

Not attached because a live profile debug bundle would contain unrelated private mount paths and environment metadata. The reproduction is synthetic and source-level behavior is deterministic.

## Environment

- macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)
- OrbStack Docker-compatible runtime
- Docker Engine 29.4.0
- Python 3.11.15
- Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (`v2026.8.3`)
- Also present on current `origin/main` commit `67168a391f26211eba13adfe4ecee74bd365a25b`

## Root Cause Analysis

`tools/environments/docker.py` builds `all_run_args`, but the reusable-container lookup does not bind those arguments (or their normalized fingerprint) to the container identity. Label-based reuse matches the logical task/profile and selected special-case posture labels, then starts/attaches to that container.

Docker cannot mutate most relevant fields after creation, so reading the new config in the new Hermes process is not enough.

This is a follow-up to persistent reuse work such as #30336: reuse is desirable, but it needs configuration compatibility checks.

## Proposed Fix

1. Normalize the effective image and immutable `docker run` configuration (resource limits, network, user, mounts, tmpfs/shm, relevant security arguments, env-file identities, and validated `docker_extra_args`).
2. Store a versioned hash in a container label, for example `hermes-runtime-fingerprint=<sha256>`.
3. Reuse only when the fingerprint and required posture labels match.
4. For old containers without the label, inspect and compare where safe, or recreate once with a clear log message.
5. On mismatch, remove/recreate only the exact `(profile, task-id)` container after respecting active-use safeguards.
6. Add integration tests showing that unchanged config reuses the container while changes to memory, pids limit, mounts, image, and security/network args force recreation.

Related but not duplicate: #75467 concerns persistent containers not being reaped; this issue concerns reusing a live container whose immutable configuration no longer matches the profile.

issues.title: [Bug]: hermes update fails permanently when the npm mirror registry uses http:// — artifact-mirror rewrite and https-only downloader disagree

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: tool/web
labels.description: Web search and extraction

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/install-update
labels.description: Installer, updater, packaging, wheels, doctor

issues.body:
### Bug Description

`hermes update` fails permanently — and silently strands the install on an old build — when the user's npm registry mirror is configured with an `http://` scheme. Two deliberate PM features disagree: the artifact-mirror rewrite produces an `http://` tarball URL from the user's registry, and the downloader's https-only policy refuses exactly that URL.

Real-world impact observed on a production machine: a macOS box with `registry=http://registry.npmmirror.com/` in `~/.npmrc` ran `hermes update` on 2026-09-17 and twice on 2026-09-28; every attempt failed the same way and the install stayed frozen on the 2026-09-24 build for over a month, with nothing in the UI explaining that updates were broken.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Put an http-scheme mirror in `~/.npmrc` (common in mainland China, where the mirror is configured by copy-pasting a setup snippet):

```
registry=http://registry.npmmirror.com/
```

2. Run `hermes update`.

3. Output:

```
✗ Source update preparation failed: npm: install failed: refusing non-https url: http://registry.npmmirror.com/npm/-/npm-12.0.2.tgz — retry, or run `hermes pm doctor`
```

Every retry fails identically; no update is ever applied.

### Expected Behavior

The update completes. The mirror host serves the identical pinned bytes over https (`https://registry.npmmirror.com/npm/-/npm-12.0.2.tgz` answers 200 with the same content), so normalizing the scheme keeps both invariants that are colliding today: the user's mirror is honored (its host, its bytes — #123132) and the https-only transport policy in `pm/downloader.py` stays intact.

### Actual Behavior + mechanism (read from source on current main)

1. `pm/artifact_mirror.py::pinned_source` deliberately rewrites the locked `registry.npmjs.org` tarball URL to the user's configured npm registry ("a user's npm mirror serves the same pinned bytes (#123132)").
2. `pm/index_config.py::npm_registry_url` performs the substitution **preserving the scheme**: `http://` in the user's registry produces an `http://` tarball URL.
3. `pm/downloader.py` refuses anything that is not `https://` (or loopback): `ValueError(f"refusing non-https url: {url}")`, which surfaces as `npm: install failed: refusing non-https url: …` from `pm/install.py`.

So the mirror-rewrite feature (#123132) emits URLs that the downloader policy categorically rejects whenever the user's registry line says `http://`. Each half is correct alone; together they permanently block updates for exactly the users #123132 was built for.

### Workaround

Use the https scheme in the registry entry (`registry=https://registry.npmmirror.com/`) — after this one-line config change the same machine updated 15,075 commits to current `main` without any other change.

### Suggested fix

Normalize the scheme to https when rewriting to the user's registry (in `npm_registry_url`, or at the `pinned_source` call site): `http(s)?://host/path → https://host/path`. A registry that genuinely cannot serve https would then fail with a connection error naming the host, which is debuggable, rather than a policy refusal that reads as "your mirror is wrong". Happy to take this — the fix looks like a scheme normalization plus a regression test with an `http://` mirror registry.

### Related

- #123132 — the npm artifact mirror rewrite this rides on
- #122112 — the pip/UV twin (pip.conf-mirrored hosts hard-fail), same "mirror host + transport policy disagree" family

### Environment

Hermes Agent v0.21.5+4152 (git install, observed) and current `main` (mechanism read from source); macOS arm64; `~/.npmrc` with an http-scheme npmmirror registry.

issues.title: [Architecture]: Pin the default-state compromise chain — ungated self-authored artifacts reach auto-approving unattended contexts inside the host trust envelope

labels.name: type/security
labels.description: Security vulnerability or hardening

labels.name: comp/tools
labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: comp/cron
labels.description: Cron scheduler and job management

labels.name: tool/skills
labels.description: Skills system (list, view, manage)

labels.name: area/config
labels.description: Config system, migrations, profiles

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
## Scope note

This is proactive architecture analysis, not a vulnerability report. Every element below is already publicly tracked in this repository (several with stronger evidence than mine), and SECURITY.md §3.2 explicitly welcomes limits of in-process heuristics as regular issues. There is no new exploit here: the only bypass PoC for the scanner layer is the one already public in #8886. What this issue adds is the **composition**: what the out-of-the-box defaults assemble into, stage by stage, at one pinned SHA, and two interlocks that break the chain without waiting for the full #133576 posture.

Pinned: `main` @ `088f657e` (2026-10-29). Method: static reading + grep import-surface counts; no runtime repro, no new PoC.

## Pre-submit: what already exists, and what is new here

| Cluster | Issues | What they own | What this issue adds |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unattended auto-approve | #8886, #144553 | cron / single-query / batch_runner run "intentionally trusted"; assembled-prompt scanner is bypassable (PoC in #8886) | The **load side**: which content classes reach those contexts by default |
| Self-authored artifacts | #78515, #16461, #53491, #70128, #142933, #144446, #64845, #11692 | write-path gates ship off; background review rewrites user skills; provenance/receipts proposals | The **connection**: those artifacts are the input surface of the auto-approving contexts |
| Scanner strictness tension | #105877, #84672 | false positives kill jobs / flag security docs | The availability-vs-trust **flip** (Ask 1) that resolves the tension without a better scanner |
| Posture umbrella | #133576, #93943, #92618 | versioned untrusted-input posture, brokered credentials, executed compromise matrix | A pinned **default-state enumeration** + the two cheapest interlocks, as concrete input to that matrix |
| Capability contracts | #55811, #60056 | runtime-enforced contracts for high-risk tools | The unattended-context instance (per-job capability semantics) |

None of the above owns the question: **"what does a default install compose into, end to end, before the operator chooses a posture?"** Today that question is answered only implicitly, by multiplying defaults.

## The default-state chain, stage by stage (file:line @ `088f657e`)

### Stage 1 — the persistence write is ungated by default

- `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:1460` — `"guard_agent_created": False`
- `tools/skill_manager_tool.py:41-45` — *"skills.guard_agent_created (default False): opt-in — terminal() runs the same code ungated."*
- `tools/skills_guard.py:29-35` — `INSTALL_POLICY["agent-created"] = ("allow", "allow", "ask")`, and the `"ask"` tier fires only when that opt-in is on.
- `tools/skills_guard.py:6-7` — known gap, quoted: *"language write APIs (open(..., 'w'), Path.write_text, shutil.copy*, fs.writeFileSync) aimed at agent-config files surface only the low *_ref finding — static regexes cannot tie the call to a dynamic destination."*

(The background-review write path and its `write_approval` default are tracked in #70128 / #78515; Stage 1 here is only the agent-created path.)

### Stage 2 — amplification into unattended execution

- `agent/curator.py:184` — `_cron_referenced_skills()`: skills referenced by cron jobs are first-class managed objects, and the curator's documented remit is *"pin/archive/consolidate/patch skills via skill_manage"* (`agent/curator.py:5`).
- `cron/scheduler.py:402-410` — the #3968 fix note, quoted: *"skill content loaded at runtime was never scanned [at create time], so a malicious skill could carry an injection payload that reached the non-interactive (auto-approve) cron agent."*

### Stage 3 — the only semantic gate is tiered regex, and it is weakest for exactly this content class

- `cron/scheduler_prompt.py:383-386` — *"skills or injected data → LOOSER `_scan_cron_skill_assembled` (command-shape patterns dropped, invisible unicode sanitized not blocked, so a false positive cannot permanently kill a job)."*

The tradeoff is deliberate and defensible in isolation — jobs must not die, and #105877 / #84672 document the false-positive cost. In composition it means: **the scanner is loosest precisely for the content class Stage 2 delivers.**

### Stage 4 — auto-approve by construction

- `tools/approval.py:643-646` — `_CRON_CTX = _Unattended("cron", "cron_mode", "cron jobs run without a user present to approve it", ..., "this cron profile is intentionally trusted")`.
- Same family: single-query (`tools/approval.py:641`), unattended platforms (`tools/approval.py:663`), batch_runner (#144553).

### Stage 5 — the blast radius is the host trust envelope, by default

- `docker-compose.yml:35` and `docker-compose.yml:67` — `network_mode: host` for the gateway and dashboard services.
- `website/docs/user-guide/egress/network-isolation.md:8-21` — the docs' own words: with host networking *"any command the agent executes can reach any endpoint on the network"*.
- SECURITY.md §2.2 is candid that in-process screening is heuristic and the OS is the only boundary. That stance is coherent — but it makes the **default envelope the actual security parameter**, and it currently ships at maximum width.

### The composition

One successful context injection (any input surface) → persists as a self-authored artifact (Stage 1, ungated) → the curator keeps it maintained and cron references it (Stage 2) → it reaches an auto-approving context through the loosest scanner tier (Stages 3–4) → it executes inside the host envelope (Stage 5).

Every stage is a reasonable local default. #3968 already demonstrated that the gaps in this system appear at the **composition seams**, not inside any single layer: the patch exists precisely because create-time scanning and the auto-approve context were each fine in isolation.

## The ask: interlock the two cheapest links, and pin the profile

**Ask 1 — availability flip at Stage 3 (cheapest; no new scanner, no detection improvement needed).**
When assembled-prompt scanning hits skill/injected content, do not run the job *with* that content under a looser scan — run the job *without* the flagged artifact and notify (artifact skipped, job alive, owner told which one). This keeps the availability guarantee #105877/#84672 fought for, removes the asymmetry where the weakest scan guards the most suspect content class, and requires zero new detection capability.

**Ask 2 — load-side interlock across Stages 1–2.**
Unattended contexts (cron, single-query, unattended platforms, batch_runner) load only artifacts whose write path was gated. Concretely: agent-authored skills/memory written while `skills.guard_agent_created` is off are invisible to unattended loads by default, with an explicit per-job opt-in (e.g. `trust_agent_artifacts: true` on the cron job). This composes the write-path issues (#16461, #78515) with the load side that none of them currently owns. Note the seam already exists for exactly this: `_cron_referenced_skills()` in `agent/curator.py:184` enumerates the artifacts a job depends on.

**Ask 3 — pin the default state as a profile.**
A versioned doc/test that enumerates the chain above and executes in CI, so a PR that widens any stage's default (a new auto-approving context, a new ungated write path, a wider default envelope) fails without an explicit recorded decision. This is the concrete default-state input that #133576's compromise matrix needs, and the regression guard for Asks 1–2 once they land.

## Non-goals

- Not proposing to flip any single default *in this issue* — each cluster's issue owns its own decision.
- Not proposing a better scanner — per SECURITY.md §2.2, in-process screening is heuristic and should not be load-bearing; agreed, and that is exactly why the load-side interlock (Ask 2) should not be another scanner.
- Not the full #133576 posture (brokered credentials, deny-by-default egress) — only the unattended-load interlock that composes with today's architecture.

## Appendix: structural note for implementers

Interlocks need seams, and the runtime import surface is currently bidirectional between the subsystems that would each own one stage. Measured @ `088f657e` (recursive grep over each package's `.py` files; counts *any* import, module-level or in-function — i.e. the late-import surface, complementary to the ast.Module-level measurement in #146473):

| Direction | Files containing an import |
|---|---:|
| `gateway/` → `hermes_cli/` | 141 |
| `hermes_cli/` → `gateway/` | 152 |
| `tools/` → `agent/` | 143 |
| `agent/` → `tools/` | 72 |
| `agent/` → `hermes_cli/` | 147 |
| `agent/` → `gateway/` | 28 |

The late-import convention (AGENTS.md: *"Siblings late-import the facade inside functions; never a module-level cycle"*) hides most of this surface from module-level analysis, so a load-side interlock will need its **own explicit seam** (e.g. a skill/memory load API owned by the state layer) rather than an import-boundary one. Worth deciding before Ask 2 lands: #146473's DAG work will make the cheapest seam harder to move later.

---

*Happy to split this into whatever shape triage prefers — the three asks are independent, and Ask 1 alone removes the Stage-3 asymmetry today.*

issues.title: [Bug]: hermes import skips the cache folders hermes backup keeps (media, citations ledger), regression in v0.22.5

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: tool/file
labels.description: File tools (read, write, patch, search)

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
### Bug Description

`hermes backup` archives `cache/{images,audio,videos,documents,screenshots,citations,generated}` (and the same folders under `profiles/<name>/cache/`) because they hold data nothing can rebuild: delivered media and the grounded-citations ledger. On v0.22.5, `hermes import` skips every `cache/` member, so these files are in the archive but are not restored. The import output counts them under "Preserved N runtime state file(s)".

This is an import-side regression. On v2026.9.24 the import skipped only `_IMPORT_SKIP_NAMES` and SQLite sidecars (`hermes_cli/backup.py:944-954` at that tag), so the kept cache folders were restored.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On v0.22.5, put a file in a kept cache folder, for example `$HERMES_HOME/cache/citations/ledger.json` or `$HERMES_HOME/cache/images/x.png`.
2. `hermes backup -o backup.zip`. `unzip -l backup.zip | grep cache/` lists the file.
3. Import into an empty home: `HERMES_HOME=/path/to/empty-home hermes import backup.zip`.
4. The file is missing under `/path/to/empty-home/cache/`, and the import output lists it as preserved runtime state.

Seen in a scheduled restore test: `cache/citations/ledger.json` was present in the archive and absent after `hermes import`. The same predicate checked directly against `hermes_cli/home_data_layout.py` at v0.22.5:

```
>>> profile_root_entry(("cache", "citations", "ledger.json")) in PM_RUNTIME_ROOT_DIRS
True
>>> profile_root_entry(("profiles", "work", "cache", "documents", "r.pdf")) in PM_RUNTIME_ROOT_DIRS
True
```

### Expected Behavior

Members under the kept cache folders (`_KEPT_CACHE_SUBDIRS`, at the home root and under `profiles/<name>/`) are restored into the target home, as on v2026.9.24.

### Actual Behavior

They are skipped and reported as preserved runtime state. The restored home has no delivered media and no citations ledger.

### Affected Component

Backup and import (`hermes backup`, `hermes import`).

### Debug Report

Not attached. The cause is in the source lines below.

### Operating System

Linux (official container image).

### Hermes Version

v0.22.5 (tag commit bf0203a7). The same lines are unchanged on main at 088f657e (2026-10-29).

### Root Cause Analysis

- `hermes_cli/backup.py:102-107`: `_KEPT_CACHE_SUBDIRS` lists the cache folders the backup keeps; the comment calls them "durable artifacts nothing can rebuild".
- `hermes_cli/home_data_layout.py:6`: `PM_RUNTIME_ROOT_DIRS = frozenset({"installs", "tools", "cache"})`.
- `hermes_cli/backup.py:716` (`_import_skipped`) and `hermes_cli/backup.py:1023` (`_import_members_exclusive`): import skips any member whose home-root entry is in `PM_RUNTIME_ROOT_DIRS`. That matches every `cache/` path, kept or not.
- `_KEPT_CACHE_SUBDIRS` is used only on the backup side (`backup.py:106`, `backup.py:118`).
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_backup.py:268-295` checks that the backup keeps these folders. No test covers importing them.

### Proposed Fix

In both import paths, skip a `cache/` member only when its subfolder is not in `_KEPT_CACHE_SUBDIRS` (the rule the backup side already applies in `_in_excluded_root_dir`), and keep skipping `installs/` and `tools/` as today. Add an import round-trip test for a kept cache file at the home root and under `profiles/<name>/`.

issues.body:
> **Reporter note (please read first):** Found on an older release branch — see Hermes Version. The session-ownership rework ("one gateway owns every local session", #106742, post-merge tracking #134889) landed on main *after* this build, so this specific path may already be gone on v0.22.5+. Filing because the evidence is unusually crisp, and because the same failure mode is still open in #57052 and #142311. If it's dead on current main, close this with that note and I'll re-test after updating.

### Bug Description

The Desktop app's local backend holds `surface: "desktop"` entries in `~/.hermes/runtime/active_sessions.json` that it never releases — not when the chat tab is closed, and not even when the session itself has been ended and reaped by that same process.

Because `_prune_dead()` only drops leases whose **owning PID is dead**, a lease leaked inside a *live* backend is permanent: the only recovery is quitting the Desktop app (the PID goes away and the next claim prunes it). Everything else that wants that session is refused forever.

Practical consequence: a chat whose session is leased by Desktop is unusable from every other surface. Telegram inbound to it is refused every time with:

```
This chat is open in another Hermes window/terminal. Use it there, or start a new chat here.
Details: session 20261026_040033_64ad48f6 opened by desktop 17m ago.
```

`max_concurrent_sessions` is **not set** on this install, so this is purely the ownership refusal — not the capacity limit in #68920 / #57052.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Hermes Desktop; mount a Telegram-backed chat as a desktop tab and leave it mounted (here: a bot group chat, 1,025 messages, pinned in the sidebar).
2. Send a message to that chat on Telegram → refused with the message above, `Details: … opened by desktop Nm ago`.
3. Close the chat tab in Desktop (confirmed closed; the app was left showing a different chat).
4. Message Telegram again → identical refusal, and the `Details` age keeps growing (it is an age, not a countdown).
5. Quit Desktop and retry → Telegram works immediately; no gateway restart needed.

### Expected Behavior

Closing a chat releases its lease. Ending a session releases its lease. Either way, once this backend no longer has the chat mounted, the next claim from another surface should succeed.

### Actual Behavior

Both release paths leaked. Two entries, same backend PID, both `updated_at` equal to their `started_at` — i.e. never touched after acquisition:

```json
{"lease_id":"e96e42414f694674be0cd2c11f0e7cf2","session_id":"20261026_040033_64ad48f6",
 "surface":"desktop","pid":70836,"track_liveness":true,
 "started_at":1793330176.5148401,"updated_at":1793330176.5148401,
 "metadata":{"bot_live_delivery_consumer":true,"live_session_id":"914db209"}}
```

That one is the chat whose tab was closed — still leased, `Details` age still climbing, Telegram still refused.

The second one is the sharper evidence, because the session is **already ended**:

```json
{"lease_id":"bf81e339df7f4a54ab13c449e083f2c3","session_id":"20261026_231811_a0d3d5",
 "surface":"desktop","pid":70836,"track_liveness":true,
 "started_at":1793330125.87665,"updated_at":1793330125.87665,
 "metadata":{"bot_live_delivery_consumer":true,"live_session_id":"cdce13dc85104e73"}}
```

…while the session row for that ID reads:

```
id=20261026_231811_a0d3d5  source=desktop  ended_at=2026-10-29 20:29:22  end_reason=startup_orphan_reap
```

So the backend ended the session (an end reason listed in `_AUTOMATIC_SESSION_END_REASONS`) and kept its lease from 20:16:25. A lease outliving its own session row is not a "hidden tab still mounted" story.

Gateway log for the same period (six refusals, same 161-character message each time, all for the leased session):

```
20:25:50,105  Rejecting new active session agent:main:telegram:group:…: max_concurrent_sessions reached
20:26:56,583  Rejecting new active session agent:main:telegram:group:…: max_concurrent_sessions reached
20:29:58,237  Rejecting new active session agent:main:telegram:group:…: max_concurrent_sessions reached
20:34:06,547  Rejecting new active session agent:main:telegram:group:…: max_concurrent_sessions reached
20:39:48,920  Rejecting new active session agent:main:telegram:group:…: max_concurrent_sessions reached
20:41:42,286  Rejecting new active session agent:main:telegram:group:…: max_concurrent_sessions reached
```

(Side note: both refusal kinds log under the same "max_concurrent_sessions reached" line — `gateway/run_inbound.py:1404` fires for the ownership refusal too, which sent me looking at the cap for a while. The log line is misleading for ownership refusals.)

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

On this build (v0.21.5-era, 2026-10-04) the Desktop keeps its own backend process (`hermes serve`, parented to the app) *alongside* a separate messaging gateway (`gateway run`). Leases are filed by whichever process mounted the chat, so the two surfaces contend for the same stored session:

- `hermes_cli/active_sessions.py` → `_prune_dead()` reclaims only leases whose PID is dead (or whose `(pid, process_start_time)` no longer matches). Nothing expires a lease held by a live process, and there is no operator-facing release path.
- `tui_gateway/session_lifecycle.py` → `_release_active_session_slot()` on the teardown paths, and `track_liveness=True` is set for `surface: "desktop"` leases, yet in the two cases above the entry survived both tab close and `startup_orphan_reap`.
- The `bot_live_delivery_consumer: true` flag is stamped on *every* desktop lease by `_lease_metadata()` in this build (it's not evidence of a bot viewer).

### Related

- #57052 — idle desktop/TUI tabs pin slots permanently (open)
- #142311 — cross-host lease never expires, no release path, and the refusal message misleads (open)
- #106742 / #134889 — one gateway owns every local session (the rework that post-dates this build)

### Debug Report

Deliberately not run: `hermes debug share` uploads the full config and logs to a paste service, and this is a personal profile. The redacted excerpts above are the relevant evidence; I'm happy to run it on request, or provide more of the registry/log under a scoped capture.

### Operating System

macOS 27.0.1 (Apple Silicon)

### Python Version

3.14.7

### Hermes Version

```
Hermes Agent v0.21.5+5002.g9462b35.dirty (2026.9.24) · upstream 66336268 · local 9462b350 (+19 carried commits)
Install directory: /Users/sasha/.hermes/hermes-agent
Install method: git
branch: release/relay-metrics-9462b35059ce, head 9462b35059 (2026-10-04)
```

issues.title: docs(computer_use): qualify minimized-window support on Windows

labels.name: type/docs
labels.description: Documentation improvements

labels.name: comp/tools
labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

labels.name: os/windows
labels.description: Native Windows behaviour or breakage: PowerShell install, Windows paths, cmd.exe, WSL-vs-native diff

issues.body:
## Summary

The model-facing `computer_use` schema advertises background delivery as working “even on hidden/minimized windows”, but current Windows `cua-driver` intentionally refuses element actions against minimized windows with the structured `window_minimized` refusal. The schema therefore overstates the supported contract and can lead the model to retry an action that the driver must reject.

## Evidence

On current Hermes `main`, `tools/computer_use/schema.py` describes the default background route as:

> routes to the target window without stealing the user's cursor or focus (works even on hidden/minimized windows)

The Windows safeguard is intentional and upstream in `cua-driver`:

- [commit 8a9b7baa](https://github.com/trycua/cua/commit/8a9b7baa32bb5b7ea48a1ee6ffc1d87a433405e4) refuses minimized Windows element actions with `window_minimized`.
- [cua-driver PR #2849](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2849) contains the corresponding implementation and tests.
- [cua-driver issue #2015](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2015) documents the Windows minimized-window sentinel/no-op failure mode.

A Windows probe with `cua-driver` 0.28.1 reaches the typed `window_minimized` refusal rather than completing the element click. This is expected driver behavior, not a request to remove the safeguard.

## Expected behavior

The Hermes schema and user-facing computer-use documentation should distinguish background delivery from minimized-window support. They should state that minimized Windows targets are refused and must be restored or brought to the foreground, followed by a fresh snapshot/capture, before retrying.

## Proposed scope

- Correct the model-facing schema wording and the relevant computer-use documentation.
- Preserve the driver's `window_minimized` refusal and fail-closed behavior.
- Do not add automatic restore, bypass the refusal, or change input-delivery policy.

This is a documentation/contract correction only.

issues.title: [Bug]: User plugins never loaded when HERMES_HOME ≠ default — gateway switches to platform default home during init

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/profiles
labels.description: Multi-profile isolation, HERMES_HOME scoping

issues.body:
## Summary

User-directory plugins (e.g., `langfuse`) are **silently invisible** to the gateway process when running with a non-default `HERMES_HOME`. The gateway's plugin discovery finds bundled plugins (63 manifests) but user plugins from `HERMES_HOME/plugins/` are never loaded. `hermes plugins list` shows them as enabled, but the gateway never imports their modules.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.22.5+2381.g0431192`, macOS (Darwin), git install
- Dual-home setup: `~/.hermes` (default/dev) + `~/.hermes-prod` (production, set via launchd `HERMES_HOME`)
- Plugin: `langfuse` (official catalog, installed at `~/.hermes-prod/plugins/langfuse/`)
- Gateway: `ai.hermes.gateway-prod` launchd service with `HERMES_HOME=/Users/mikeling/.hermes-prod`

## Root Cause (diagnosed with instrumentation in `_discover_and_load_inner`)

The gateway startup switches the effective home from the **launch home** (from `HERMES_HOME` env var) to the **platform default** (`~/.hermes`) during internal initialization:

```
gate call 1: enabled={'langfuse'}                       ← prod home (launch HERMES_HOME) ✓
gate call 2+: enabled={'dual-channel', 'rate-limiter'}  ← dev home (platform default) ✗
```

Plugin discovery and `_get_enabled_plugins()` read the config from the **current active home**. After the gateway's internal initialization switches to the default home:
- `_plugins_dir()` returns `~/.hermes/plugins/` (default) instead of `~/.hermes-prod/plugins/` (launch home)
- User plugins in the launch home are never found
- Bundled plugins (from the source tree) ARE found (63 manifests) because they're in the same location for both homes

## Evidence

Instrumented `_discover_and_load_inner()` with file-write debug (stderr is unreliable in launchd):

```
discovery: 63 manifests from _collect
  browser-browser-use src=bundled path=.../plugins/browser/browser_use
  ...all 63 are bundled (src=bundled)...
  ← langfuse (src=user, path=~/.hermes-prod/plugins/langfuse) IS in manifest list
  ← but gate: enabled set only includes default-home config entries
```

Even with:
- `os.environ["HERMES_HOME"] = launch_home` (restored before re-discovery)
- `pin_process_hermes_home(launch_home)` 
- `set_hermes_home_override(launch_home)` + `discover_and_load(force=True)`

...the re-discovery still finds only bundled plugins. The context-local override set during gateway's async initialization takes precedence and cannot be cleared from the synchronous code path.

## What We Tried

| Approach | Result |
|----------|--------|
| `hermes plugins install langfuse` (prod home) | Installed, doctor OK, gateway never imports |
| Plugin in source tree (`plugins/langfuse/`) | Discovered (63→64 plugins) but `register()` never called |
| Plugin + user plugin simultaneously | Brief window where hooks fired (26 traces), not reproducible |
| Custom plugin (dual-channel pattern: `ctx.register_hook()`) | `register()` called but callbacks never invoked by gateway |
| `disable && enable` workaround from #143158 | "Gateway reloaded plugins" but still no traces |
| Force eager discovery at `run_gateway()` entry | Discovery runs but finds 0 hooks (home already switched) |
| `pin_process_hermes_home()` | No effect on `get_hermes_home()` resolution |
| `set_hermes_home_override()` + force re-discovery | Contextvars isolation prevents synchronous override |
| Cross-home invoke (merge callbacks from all managers) | Managers have bundled hooks, user callbacks not registered |

## Impact

- **All user plugins are non-functional in the gateway** for non-default `HERMES_HOME` setups
- Observability plugins (langfuse) silently produce zero traces
- No warning or error is logged — the plugin appears enabled in `hermes plugins list`

## Suggested Fix Direction

The gateway's initialization should **not** switch the effective home away from `HERMES_HOME` for plugin discovery. Alternatively:
1. Plugin discovery should use the **launch home** (initial `HERMES_HOME` at process start), not the current active home
2. Or `_get_enabled_plugins()` should read from the launch home's config, not the current active home's config
3. Or the gateway should load user plugins from ALL configured homes

## Related

- #143158 (catalog plugin hooks inactive after gateway restart — different trigger, same effect)
- #143531 (plugin hook not invoked in Desktop gateway until reload)

issues.title: [Bug]: Idle desktop/TUI tabs permanently pin max_concurrent_sessions slots (claimed at composer paint, never released while connected)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: area/sessions
labels.description: Session lifecycle, resume, persistence, history

labels.name: comp/tui-gateway
labels.description: The shared Python JSON-RPC backend that both the terminal UI and the desktop app talk to (tui_gatewa

issues.body:
### What happened?

With `max_concurrent_sessions` set (introduced in #42389), desktop/TUI tabs permanently pin cap slots even when idle. After leaving N tabs open overnight in a connected desktop app, the registry sits at N/N and **every new session on every surface** — messaging gateway, CLI, new desktop tabs — is rejected with:

```
Hermes is at the active session limit (7/7). Try again when another session finishes.
```

Nothing is actually running at that point. The only way to free slots is to close tabs or restart the gateway.

### Root cause (two release-path bugs in `tui_gateway/server.py`)

1. **The lease is claimed at composer-paint time, before any user input.** `session.create` claims a `max_concurrent_sessions` slot immediately — and it fires for every TUI/desktop launch, every "New agent", and every draft. Note the asymmetry with the gateway's own persistence policy: the session's **DB row** is deliberately created lazily on the first prompt (the in-code NOTE explains this avoids ghost "Untitled" sessions for every composer paint), but the **lease** is eager. At the cap, even launching the desktop app fails.
2. **A lease held by a connected client can never be released.** The only release path is `_finalize_session` (tab close / WS-orphan reap / process exit). The idle reaper (`_reap_idle_sessions`) requires a **dead transport** plus a 6h TTL before it evicts anything — so a healthy, connected desktop app holds every tab's slot forever, no matter how long the tabs sit idle.

For contrast, the messaging gateway claims a slot per **in-flight turn** and releases it in the turn's `finally` (`gateway/run.py`), so idle chats there never pin the cap.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `max_concurrent_sessions: 2` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.
2. Open the desktop app and open 2 chat tabs. Don't type anything.
3. From any other surface (CLI `hermes chat`, Telegram, or a third desktop tab), start a session.
4. Observe the limit rejection, even though zero turns are in flight and the two tabs are empty drafts. `HERMES_HOME/runtime/active_sessions.json` shows both slots held by surface `tui`.

### Expected behavior

Open-but-idle tabs shouldn't consume cap slots indefinitely. A tab should count while its conversation is actually active, and hand its slot back after going idle (re-acquiring transparently on the next message).

### Environment

- Hermes: current `main` (44650a5ce)
- OS: Windows 11 (behavior is platform-independent; reproduced against the lease registry logic directly)
- Surface: desktop app / TUI gateway

I have a fix ready and will link the PR.

prs.title: feat(scripts): mechanize the #14182 dependency DAG and module-level acyclicity
prs.body:
# Mechanize the #14182 dependency DAG and module-level acyclicity

Fixes the missing half of #146473: the rule, not just the count.

## What

`scripts/code_health` gains a graph pass (`scripts/code_health/py_imports.py`) with two findings, judged with the ratchet's own semantics — **the cap is the count measured on the base revision**, so today's debt is frozen and may only go down:

| Rule | Meaning | Anchor |
|---|---|---|
| `LAYER_EDGE` | a module-level edge in a direction `GRAPH_FORBIDDEN` forbids | the importing `file:line` |
| `IMPORT_CYCLE` | a strongly connected component that does not exist on the base revision | `file:line` of a new edge inside it |

Only direct children of `ast.Module` are edges: the documented convention is a late import inside a function ("siblings late-import the facade inside functions; never a module-level cycle"), and a call-time import is not an edge. Counting call-time imports would report 325 `hermes_cli.config` sites instead of the 28 that are actually module-level.

The policy encodes only the directions #14182 states outright:

```python
GRAPH_FORBIDDEN = (("tools", "agent"), ("agent", "cli"), ("tools", "cli"),
                   ("tools", "gateway"), ("agent", "gateway"))
```

Pairs the DAG does not define — `cron/`, `tui_gateway/`, `plugins/`, and whether `gateway` may import `cli` — are **counted in `--report` and never judged**. An encoded guess would fail correct code; naming the band is the owner's one-line decision (`GRAPH_LAYERS` / `GRAPH_FORBIDDEN`).

## Numbers on this base (`67d47601`)

`python scripts/check --report` prints the burn-down view:

```
Import graph (module-level, #14182 DAG): 2273 modules, 4400 edges
  forbidden directions (the cap is what main measures):
    agent    -> cli          48  worst target: hermes_cli._subprocess_compat (6)
    agent    -> gateway       1  worst target: gateway.session_context (1)
    tools    -> agent        56  worst target: agent.skill_utils (9)
    tools    -> cli          45  worst target: hermes_cli._subprocess_compat (16)
    tools    -> gateway       2  worst target: gateway.session_context (2)
  module-level cycles: 9 (31 modules)
```

The same 152 edges / 9 cycles the issue reports (measured at `a938f00f`, re-measured here: unchanged).

## Cost

One whole-tree AST pass: **~4.5 s** for 2273 modules. The base graph is *derived*, not re-scanned — unchanged files have identical edges, so base = head graph minus the outgoing edges of the changed files plus their base edges (`derive_base`, covered by a test that compares it with a full scan of the base tree). Nothing runs when the change touches no `.py`.

## Verification

```
python scripts/check                 # 14 checks, ok — on this PR itself
python scripts/check --report        # the numbers above
python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_code_health*.py -q   # 293 passed
```

Red/green controls, run in a throwaway worktree on top of this branch:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| `from hermes_cli import config` appended to `agent/redact.py` (module level) | **FAIL** `LAYER_EDGE agent.redact -> hermes_cli, hermes_cli.config`, `cap 48 on main (+2 new)` |
| two new modules importing each other in `tools/` | **FAIL** `IMPORT_CYCLE`, 2 modules, `file:line` |
| the same import inside a function | **ok** (call-time, not an edge) |
| untouched tree | **ok** — 152/9 at cap |

## Risks

- **The cap freezes the debt.** The rule does not force the refactor; it makes regressions visible and lets every #14278 fix lower the cap automatically (it is re-measured on each base).
- **Moves re-key cycles.** A component is frozen by its module set, so a mass move (#14182) can show a "new" cycle from old edges once; a PR that moves modules recomputes its own base.
- **Cost honesty.** ~4.5 s per health run with changed Python; if that is too much for the pre-push hook, the graph pass can be limited through the existing `ENFORCEMENT` switch semantics.

## Out of scope

- Fixing the 152 edges (that is #14278 / #14182).
- The gate's "passed by measuring nothing" path (`base == head`) — filed separately as #146612.

Refs #146473

prs.title: fix(tui): a second Enter or a terminal report no longer breaks the held-Enter submit
prs.body:
In the TUI, sending text + Enter and then Enter again within 250 ms submits again, and a focus, mouse or terminal report that lands inside a split unbracketed paste no longer sends the paste's first line early.

Follow-up to #146126.

Introduced by: @teknium1, 2026-10-28, #146126, commit 4889361215 (both TUI cases). The comment fix in `cli_enter_burst.py` is not a regression; the comment has been wrong since #146126.

Changes:
- `ui-tui/packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/parse-keypress.ts`: the CR held back from a one-line read is now resolved token by token instead of from the first byte of the next read.
  - An Enter (`\r`) read inside the window releases the held CR as `return` and is parsed as its own `return`. This also holds when the Enter shares a read with a terminal report, in either order (`\x1b[I\r` gives focus, return, return; `\r\x1b[I` gives return, return, focus). Before, the two CRs were glued into the text token `"\r\r"`, so the composer got two newlines and nothing was sent.
  - A read whose text is only line breaks counts as Enter, so an LF Return (Ctrl+J) releases the held CR the same way and keeps its `\n` sequence for the input layer. `\x1b[I\n` or a DECRPM reply + `\n` after a held CR gives the report, return, return (main: return, report, return), and `\n\x1b[I` gives return, return, focus (main: the text `"\r\n"`, no submit).
  - Terminal replies (for example DECRPM from the mouse watchdog), focus in/out, mouse events and wheel events, including horizontal wheel and legacy X10 mouse events, keep the CR held. Key escapes (arrows, CSI-u keys) and bracketed-paste markers still release it as before. Text read inside the window still turns it into a pasted line break.
  - The window is measured from the moment the CR was held, not from the last report. A report read after the window ends releases the CR. The parser state carries the hold time (`pendingReturnAt`) across report-only reads, so a pointer moving over the TUI (any-motion tracking is on) cannot hold a scripted submit back past 250 ms.
  - Two small helpers keep `parseMultipleKeypresses` within its complexity cap: `createHeldReturn` and `parseSequenceToken`.
- `ui-tui/packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/components/App.tsx`: while a CR is held, the flush timer is armed for the time left in that window, not a fresh 250 ms after every read. An incomplete escape still gets at least the normal 50 ms escape timeout, so an arrow key split across two reads late in the window is not flushed as a lone Escape.
- `hermes_cli/cli_enter_burst.py`: comment and docstring only. A single fast typed Enter (within 50 ms of the last keystroke) does reach the burst path and still submits once input stays quiet; a run of Enters inside the window (auto-repeat) stays newlines. The old comment said a typed Enter never reaches it.

Validation:
- 6 new cases in `parse-keypress.test.ts` and 2 in `app-held-return-stall.test.ts`:
  - Enter read after a held CR
  - a report and Enter in one read after a held CR, in both orders
  - a report and an LF Return in one read after a held CR: `\x1b[I\n`, DECRPM + `\n`, `\n\x1b[I`; both returns keep their own sequence (`\r`, `\n`)
  - a held CR across focus, DECRPM, SGR mouse and horizontal wheel reports, then the paste tail
  - mouse motion every 30 ms after a held CR: `return` comes with the first report 250 ms after the hold
  - a report followed by a key escape still releases the CR first
  - App: a held CR with a focus report read 200 ms later is submitted 250 ms after the hold
  - App: an ESC read 240 ms after the hold and `[A` 20 ms later give return, then up
- Results: with main's `parse-keypress.ts` and `App.tsx` swapped in, the first 7 fail and pass on this branch; across the 12 hermes-ink parser and App test files (99 tests) they are the only failures on main. The reverse-order (`\r\x1b[I`) check also fails on main on its own. On main the LF case's first input does submit, in a different order; its `\n\x1b[I` input does not. The LF case also fails with the branch's earlier CR-only release (every LF input became the text `"\r\n"`). The last App case passes on main: it fails when the timer has no 50 ms escape floor.
- Each production change was reverted on its own (Enter-only release, LF in that release, window age, mouse classification, hold time stored, hold time carried, flush release, App timer, App escape floor). Every revert turns at least one test red.
- Every test file that mentions a touched symbol, all passing:
  - hermes-ink parser and App files: 12 files, 99 tests
  - `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_enter_burst.py` + `test_tui_rapid_enter_paste.py`: 8 tests
- Full `ui-tui` vitest run: 244 files, 1912 passed, 2 skipped. Full hermes-ink run: 32 files, 230 tests.
- `tsc --noEmit` for ui-tui and hermes-ink, eslint and prettier on the touched files, and the hermes-ink esbuild build are clean.
- `scripts/check --base origin/main`: 13 checks ok.

Scope:
- Unchanged: a read that starts with CR or LF followed by more text (a split paste with a blank line at the boundary) stays paste content.
- Changed: after a held CR, a read made up only of line breaks (`\n`, `\r\n`, `\r\r`, `\n\n`) now releases the held CR as a submit; on main those reads never submitted and became the text `"\r\n"` (or similar) in the composer. The line breaks in that read are then handled as typed keys. An LF goes to the input layer as an LF Return: it submits where LF submits, and on macOS, SSH, Windows Terminal, Ghostty and WSL (where LF inserts a newline) it leaves one empty line at the start of the next draft. So a lone `\n` read, a `\r\n` read, or a one-line unbracketed paste ending in CRLF and split exactly between CR and LF now submits the first line; on the newline-LF setups the next draft starts with a stray newline. A multi-line paste split between CR and LF is unaffected (its LF read carries more text and stays paste content).
- Mouse clicks inside the window count as reports, so they are delivered before the held `return`.
- A lone Escape right after a held CR waits for the rest of the 250 ms window, but at least the normal 50 ms escape timeout. The order (return, then escape) is kept.
- Unchanged from main: if the event loop stalls past the window and the next read starts with a terminal report followed by more paste text, the held CR is still released as a submit.
- Not in this PR:
  - the 250 ms paste trade-off documented in #146126
  - `process_manage` submit and `stty -icrnl` children
  - stale SKILL.md text about text + Enter (handled separately)
  - test cleanup in `test_tui_rapid_enter_paste.py`

Blast radius:
- Only the held-CR path changes. It runs only when the previous read was a single line ending in CR. Every other read takes the same code as before, which the unchanged existing parser tests and the full ui-tui suite pass.
- Live check: a real `hermes --tui` in tmux (160x50) was driven with raw byte writes, main against this branch before the 50 ms escape floor was added. Text + Enter in one write, then Enter 60 ms later, submits on the branch (stray newlines on main). Split unbracketed pastes with a focus report, SGR mouse motion, a horizontal wheel event, or a real tmux focus out/in between the reads stay content on the branch (main submitted the first line early). A text + Enter write during a 1 s mouse-motion stream submits after about 270 ms. Held CR then `\x1b[I\r` or `\r\x1b[I` submits on the branch (main: only the first order). Bracketed and plain split pastes are content on both.
- The 50 ms escape floor was then checked live as well (an arrow split across reads late in the window is still `up`). The LF Return handling is proven at unit level (the parser case above).

prs.title: fix(pm): normalize an http npm registry to https for artifact URLs
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes update` fails permanently when the user's npm registry mirror is configured with an `http://` scheme — a one-line `~/.npmrc` common in mainland China. Two deliberate PM features collided: the artifact-mirror rewrite (#123132) follows the user's registry but kept its scheme, producing `http://` tarball URLs that the downloader's https-only policy categorically refuses. A production machine with `registry=http://registry.npmmirror.com/` stayed frozen on a month-old build across every retry, with only `npm: install failed: refusing non-https url` to explain it.

`npm_registry()` now upgrades the scheme to https before the URL is used. The mirror is still honored — same host, same pinned bytes, which the mirrors serve over https (verified: after switching the registry line to https, the affected machine updated 15,075 commits with no other change) — and the https-only transport policy in `pm/downloader.py` stays intact. A registry that genuinely cannot serve https now fails with a connection error that names the host, which is debuggable, instead of a policy refusal that reads as "your mirror is wrong".

## Related Issue

Fixes #146742

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `pm/index_config.py` — `npm_registry()` normalizes `http://` to `https://` in the configured registry (env `npm_config_registry` and `~/.npmrc` alike), with a comment naming the collision.
- `tests/pm/test_artifact_mirror.py` — extends `test_npm_artifacts_follow_the_users_npm_registry` with both http-scheme paths (env var and npmrc), asserting the rewritten artifact URL is https.

## How to Test

1. Red (before the fix): `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY=http://registry.npmmirror.com` made `pinned_source("https://registry.npmjs.org/npm/-/npm-10.9.2.tgz", …).url` end in `http://registry.npmmirror.com/…`, which `pm/downloader.py` refuses — the new test assertions fail on main.
2. Green (with the fix): `uv run --with pytest --with aiohttp python -m pytest tests/pm/test_artifact_mirror.py -q` → 4 passed.
3. Neighbors: `tests/pm/test_index_bridging.py`, `test_npm_dist_tags.py`, `test_npm_self_install.py` → 6 passed. `uvx ruff@0.15.22 check` clean; `python scripts/check --only ruff --only health` ok (0 blocking, 0 advisory).
4. Real-world before/after: the machine from the issue updated 15,075 commits to current main once its registry line used https — the same outcome this fix gives an `http://` line without the user having to know the difference.

prs.title: fix(terminal): detect host binds declared via docker_extra_args
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`_docker_has_host_access()` decides whether a Docker session keeps the approval
fast-path. It reads `docker_mount_cwd_to_workspace` and `docker_volumes` — but not
`docker_extra_args`, which is forwarded to `docker run` verbatim. So `-v /host:/c`
declared there mounts exactly what a `docker_volumes` entry would, while the
function still reports the container as isolated.

Consequence: `_should_skip_container_guards()` short-circuits
`check_dangerous_command()` before its hardline floor, so `rm -rf` against a
bind-mounted host path runs unprompted. Both call sites inherit it — the terminal
guard and the `execute_code` guard, which #54483 wired to the same signal
deliberately.

**This does not propose changing the security model.** It makes the existing one
answer truthfully. On #42750 the maintainer stated the contract directly:

> `tools/approval.py` intentionally retains the fast path for isolated Docker,
> Singularity, Modal, and Daytona backends; Docker exits that path when
> `has_host_access` is true.

A container with a host bind declared via `docker_extra_args` *is* host-exposed
and should exit the fast path. Today it does not. The isolated-container contract
is untouched — an isolated container still takes the fast path.

Per SECURITY.md §2.4 the approval gate is a heuristic, not a boundary, so this is
filed as a normal correctness fix rather than through the private security
channel. It is a config-introspection bug, not a boundary claim.

**Not a deliberate exclusion.** `docker_extra_args` shipped in `ebf2ea584a`
(2026-05-10), seven weeks before the guard in `9860d93f2a` (2026-06-28), whose
message states the general goal "Detect host bind mounts" and then enumerates
only the two mechanisms it covered. `docker_extra_args` is not mentioned anywhere
in that commit, including as an exclusion.

## Relationship to #77666

Adjacent but orthogonal, and worth reading together:

- **#77666** teaches `_docker_volume_uses_host_path()` to parse long-form
  `--mount` syntax inside **`docker_volumes`**.
- **This PR** makes a different config key — **`docker_extra_args`** — get
  inspected at all.

Both touch `--mount` parsing, so they will conflict textually. I am happy to
rebase onto #77666 and reuse its parser rather than carry a second one — say the
word and I will restructure. If #77666 lands first, the `_docker_mount_spec_uses_host_path`
helper here should collapse into theirs.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. Found while auditing a deployment that pins its vault mount
through `docker_volumes` specifically to keep this guard armed.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tools/terminal_tool.py` — added `_docker_extra_args_use_host_path()` and
  `_docker_mount_spec_uses_host_path()`; `_docker_has_host_access()` now also
  consults `docker_extra_args`.
- `tests/tools/test_modal_sandbox_fixes.py` — added
  `test_docker_extra_args_host_bind_detected` to the existing
  `TestDockerHostBindApproval` class.
- `contributors/emails/dewoller@gmail.com` — attribution mapping for the
  Contributor Attribution Check.

Parses `-v`, `--volume`, `--volume=`, `--mount` and `--mount=`. `--mount` honours
Docker's default of `type=volume`, so only an explicit `type=bind` counts as host
access — a named volume keeps the fast path.

## How to Test

1. Before the change:
   ```python
   from tools.terminal_tool import _docker_has_host_access
   _docker_has_host_access({"env_type": "docker", "docker_volumes": [],
                            "docker_extra_args": ["-v", "/srv/data:/srv/data"]})
   # -> False   (host bind, but reported isolated)
   ```
2. After the change the same call returns `True`, so
   `_should_skip_container_guards("docker", has_host_access=True)` is `False` and
   the command goes through the normal approval flow.
3. `pytest tests/tools/test_modal_sandbox_fixes.py::TestDockerHostBindApproval -q`

Negative coverage included: named volumes, `type=volume`, unrelated flags, a
trailing `-v` with no value, and a non-list config value.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate — see the #77666 note above
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — see note below
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 15 (Darwin 25.6), Python 3.11

On the full-suite item, being precise rather than ticking it: I ran
`tests/tools/test_modal_sandbox_fixes.py`, `test_container_cwd_sanitize.py`,
`test_file_tools_container_config.py`, `test_approved_command_clean_slate.py`,
`test_code_execution*.py`, `test_sandbox_failure_hints.py` and `tests/deploy/`
— 181 passed, 2 xfailed. The complete `tests/tools/` run wedged locally on
Docker/network-dependent tests, and it surfaced one failure,
`test_approval.py::TestDetectDangerousRm::test_nonrecursive_verification_artifact_cleanup_is_not_dangerous`,
which reproduces identically with this patch fully reverted — pre-existing and
unrelated. CI is the authority here, not my laptop.
