prs.title: fix(tools): disclose search match truncation
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`search_files` currently clips every matching or context line at 500 characters without telling the agent. A search can therefore match text near the end of a long Markdown paragraph while returning only the beginning of the line. The agent sees a result that looks complete and cannot retrieve the omitted suffix with the existing parameters.

This change keeps the 500-character default. It adds `content_truncated: true` to results containing clipped lines and exposes a positive integer `max_content_chars` parameter so the agent can retry when it needs more of a line. The parameter has no upper bound, so the tool does not replace one unrecoverable content ceiling with another. Invalid values return an explicit error instead of being silently changed. The response tells the agent to increase `max_content_chars` and notes that it can reduce `limit` or narrow the search to keep the response smaller. Default searches retain their existing output bound, compact representation, and shell execution behavior.

## Related Issue

Fixes #96630

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- Add result-level `content_truncated` metadata when any matching or context line is clipped.
- Add `max_content_chars` to the `search_files` schema and propagate it through single-path and multi-path searches.
- Keep the default at 500 characters, document a minimum of 1, and reject invalid values explicitly.
- Allow the agent to request longer lines without imposing another arbitrary ceiling.
- Apply the limit once after the final result page is assembled.
- Preserve the existing densified output and tell the agent how to request more content.
- Add regression coverage for both search backends, schema dispatch, bounds, output metadata, retry behavior, and the model-facing hint.

## How to Test

1. Run the regression tests:

   ```bash
   HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0 scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_file_operations.py tests/tools/test_file_tools.py -k 'SearchMatchContentLimit or content_truncation_metadata_preserves_densification or match_content_truncation_hint_explains_retry or registry_handler_forwards_match_content_limit or search_rejects_invalid_match_content_limit' -q
   ```

2. Run the affected file-tool suites:

   ```bash
   HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0 scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_file_operations.py tests/tools/test_file_operations_edge_cases.py tests/tools/test_file_tools.py -k 'not test_writes_content and not test_replace_mode_calls_patch_replace' -q
   ```

   Result on macOS 15.6.1 with Python 3.11.11: 138 passed and 4 skipped. The two excluded tests compare `/tmp` with its resolved macOS path, `/private/tmp`, and are unrelated to this change.

3. Run lint and whitespace checks:

   ```bash
   ruff check tools/file_operations.py tools/file_tools.py tests/tools/test_file_operations.py tests/tools/test_file_tools.py
   git diff --check main...HEAD
   ```

4. The full repository suite was started in an isolated development environment. It reached 1,180 passing tests before the run was stopped. The environment lacked optional `acp` and `anthropic` SDKs, which caused unrelated collection and provider-client failures. prs.title: fix(docker): preserve profile sandbox when cwd mounting is off
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

With persistent Docker and host-workspace mounting disabled, a Desktop session could select `default:ws:<digest>` while CLI kept using `default`. The two sessions then saw different persistent workspace directories, despite belonging to the same profile.

`_workspace_container_key` now checks the scope-aware mounting flag before deriving a workspace key. Unmounted sessions retain their original profile sandbox; host-mounted sessions retain separate containers for different workspaces. Desktop cwd registration also keeps the host workspace out of an unmounted Docker execution cwd, using the owning profile's terminal policy. The configured container cwd and later in-container `cd` remain authoritative. This fixes selection and execution without moving, copying, or deleting existing sandbox data.

## Related Issue

[Discord support report](https://discord.com/channels/1053877538025386074/1565055885120639027). Reproduced on main `780d5a3313d7e1f64c0a0f3ec6b644d50f156e90`.

Overlap checked against open and merged PRs, including #113026, #119173, #140703, #140970 and #143655. The open work covers mounted-path translation, mount lifecycle, or namespace validation. This patch addresses unmounted persistent-container selection and Desktop host-cwd registration. It does not depend on those open PRs or require a merge order.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Documentation-only update
- [ ] Tests-only change
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] New skill

## Changes Made

- `tools/terminal_tool.py`: preserve the profile key when `docker_mount_cwd_to_workspace` is off, using the existing per-turn configuration reader.
- `tui_gateway/session_workdir.py`: keep Desktop host-context cwd separate from the unmounted container execution cwd, binding the target profile when registration happens outside its turn.
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_unmounted_docker_cwd.py`: verify the target profile's mount policy without process-environment mutation, plus native POSIX configured-container cwd preservation.
- `tests/gateway/test_docker_session_workspace.py`: exercise the actual Desktop cwd registration with default and named profiles, mounting off/on, and resolved-key stability. The two unmounted cases fail on the base; both mounted controls pass.
- `tests/tools/test_docker_backend_real.py`: verify Desktop terminal and file tools read the original CLI workspace with mounting off; verify two mounted projects remain separate. Exercise container removal/recreation and preservation of the original CLI file. Test mounts are confined to disposable directories; the orphan reaper and cross-process container reuse are disabled for these tests.
- `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md`: explain profile-shared versus host-workspace-specific persistent containers.

## How to Test

1. Run the gateway suite through `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_docker_session_workspace.py -q -j 1`.
2. With a local Docker daemon and a disposable Bash-capable image, set `HERMES_TEST_DOCKER_IMAGE`, then run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_docker_backend_real.py -k desktop_workspace -q -j 1`.
3. With mounting off, Desktop and CLI must select the original profile sandbox and read the original file, including after container recreation. With mounting on, two host workspaces must expose their own files in distinct containers.

Local validation uses the canonical `scripts/run_tests.sh` runner. The initial Linux CI failure exposed a second part of the bug: after selecting the original container, Desktop still passed its POSIX host path to `cd` inside that container. The Windows drive-path sanitizer had masked that missing correction locally. The follow-up removes that host execution-cwd override; the real-Docker test retains its terminal/file read assertions and now passes on native Linux.

- Native Linux, Python 3.14.9, pytest 9.1.1, Docker 29.6.1, CI's pinned `debian:trixie-20261020-slim@sha256:62bd423aeee912639ca8ee681c2b762cb3e25137e0a92b20be455898a9f034ad`: **59 passed** across the full real-Docker file (9), gateway workspace file (23), new cwd regressions (3), and adjacent remote/container cwd files (24). The isolated harness mounted this worktree as source; it was not a full CI checkout or a full-suite run.
- Final native Windows matrix: **48 passed, 1 skipped, 1 pre-existing failure**. The failure is `test_sandbox_resume_drops_a_stored_desktop_launch_dir[root]` in unchanged Modal path handling; it also fails on the unchanged published head. The POSIX-only regression ran and passed on Linux.
- `python scripts/check`: all 13 blocking checks passed with pinned Ruff 0.15.22, including final added-file code-health coverage.
- Pinned `ty==0.0.89`: whole-repository advisory scan retains existing diagnostic debt; the new test adds an unresolved `pytest` import in the dependency-free checker environment. Checking that file with the actual test interpreter resolves it and passes. Two unchanged-file diagnostics also fluctuate in their displayed union type. No new production-code diagnostics were found.
- New test file is Ruff-formatted. Existing touched files have pre-existing whole-file formatting debt; no unrelated bulk formatting was applied.
- Earlier broad native-Windows comparison established the same 12 existing-test failures on the original base and first candidate, covering cwd persistence/sanitization, Windows mount fingerprints, environment forwarding and path-warning assertions. This is not a claim that the full repository suite is green.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run the full `pytest tests/ -q` suite and all tests pass (focused canonical-runner checks and baseline comparison above; full suite not run)
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platforms: native Windows and an isolated native Linux harness with real Docker containers

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation
- [x] Config example changes: N/A, no new keys or defaults
- [x] Architecture/workflow changes: N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact; the config read is scope-aware and host-independent
- [x] Tool schema changes: N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

Before the fix, the unmounted regression returns `default:ws:<digest>` or `profile:beta:ws:<digest>` instead of the CLI's original `default` or `profile:beta`. After the fix, those cases pass while mounted workspace separation continues to pass.

Previously created `*_ws_*` directories are retained. This change does not merge files written to those directories into the original sandbox, and it does not modify a running user instance.

prs.title: fix(scratch): the idle rule must hold for a process that never restarts
prs.body:
## Problem

Two independent defects in how idle-scratch retention is scheduled. They share a deployment — the
gateway, the process that never restarts.

**1. The gate is stamped before the hour is checked.** `_prune_scratch_dir_once` set
`_scratch_pruned_once = True` and only then asked whether the cross-process hour had elapsed. A
process whose first call landed *inside* that hour therefore spent its single per-process chance on
a pass that pruned nothing, and returned on every later call for the rest of its life.

**2. A per-process gate cannot serve a process that never restarts.** `get_scratch_dir(prune=True)`
is the only trigger, and it fires at most once per process. A fan-out of short-lived children
re-arms it constantly; a gateway that stays up for weeks does not.

## Fix

- **§1 — the order.** `_scratch_prune_due()` (one `stat`, fail-open on an unreadable stamp) and
  `_run_scratch_prune()` (stamp, then hand off) are extracted; the flag is set only once a pass is
  actually handed off.
- **§2 — a caller that outlives many hours.** `prune_scratch_dir_if_due()` is a public entry that
  re-asks the *stamp*, not the process age. The housekeeping chore calls it every tick; the check is
  one `stat` and the scan still goes to a detached child.
- **§3 — every served profile.** The chore is registered through `profile_scoped_chore`.
  `prune_scratch_dir_if_due()` resolves its root through `get_hermes_home()`, and the housekeeping
  thread carries no turn, so nothing binds a profile for it: registered bare, every tick sweeps the
  **launch** profile's scratch and no named profile ever gets a pass. That is the state #134896
  describes, and the boot-time gate cannot fix it for a long-running process.
- **Facade growth.** `gateway/run.py` sits at its FILE_LINES cap, so the growth is offset in the same
  PR by moving an existing chore out: `_housekeeping_paste_sweep` becomes
  `housekeeping_paste_sweep` in `gateway/run_housekeeping_disk.py`, behaviour unchanged.

## Relation to existing PRs

**#134907** — per-root shape for the same guard. Complementary and touching the same function: it
gives each root its own ticket at bootstrap, this PR gives a long-lived process a recurring one.
It keeps `_scratch_pruned_roots.add(root)` ahead of the stamp check, so a root's ticket can still be
spent inside the hour — §1 is the same defect one level up. @foma-agent tested the two together on
this branch: the combined 11-file scratch/housekeeping slice is **68/68** with
`add(root)` moved after the due check, and the direct `profile, default, profile` probe passes.
Whichever lands second needs a rebase; the per-root shape should win where they overlap.

**#138954** — also re-sweeps scratch on the housekeeping tick. Same target, different mechanism: it
registers `(60, "Scratch prune", ...)` calling `prune_scratch_dir()` directly, so the cadence is
expressed in ticks and each process sweeps on its own schedule; this PR gates on the cross-process
stamp — the semantics `_SCRATCH_PRUNE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` already documents — and runs per served
profile. It also does not change the gate order, so defect §1 survives it. If #138954 lands first I
will consolidate rather than leave two scratch ticks.

**#133280** — the checkpoint prune tick per served profile. **This PR does not touch the checkpoint
chore**; it stays exactly where it is so that line is not contended.

**#134896** — reports the named-profile axis. §3 is the recurring half of it; #134907 is the
bootstrap half.

## What this does not change

- `SCRATCH_MAX_IDLE_HOURS = 24` — the idle rule itself.
- `_SCRATCH_PRUNE_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 3600` — the cross-process floor.
- The detached child that performs the scan and the `rmtree`.
- `reap_processes_rooted_in` and the process-ownership check, including the registered-process
  ledger and the pre-delete revalidation.
- The checkpoint chore, the media-cache chores and every other housekeeping cadence.

## Observed

On a gateway that had been up 5.2 days: `.last_prune` was stamped 14 minutes before that process
started, so its first call fell inside the hour, the gate closed on a tick that pruned nothing, and
nothing swept again for the rest of the run — 108 entries, 18.4 MB. The size is incidental; the
mechanism is the point. Details in #134896.

## Effect on the reap (what #132401 settled and what it left open)

@teknium1's triage there states the 24h idle rule and the reap are the deliberate contract from
#118575, and that the real collision is the docs (#126419) — not the retention policy. This PR does
not change either. What it does change is *when* the reap can run: previously the gateway effectively
never reached it, so it now runs on the hourly cadence §2 establishes. Three properties keep that
safe, and all three are unchanged by this PR:

- `reap_processes_rooted_in` only considers processes whose **cwd** is under scratch.
- A process in the spawn ledger, or one owned by Hermes, is protected — and its entry is pulled from
  the deletion list.
- The pruner's own lineage is never killed.

The remaining `needs-decision` item in #132401 — telling a live worker from an orphan — is unaffected
here: this PR changes cadence, not the discrimination.

## Tests

`scripts/run_tests.sh` (per-file isolation), clean `HERMES_HOME`:

```
tests/test_scratch_dir.py                 34 passed, 2 failed
tests/test_scratch_prune_undeletable.py
tests/test_scratch_registered_clock_step.py
tests/test_scratch_scan_failures.py
tests/gateway/test_scratch_prune_housekeeping.py
tests/gateway/test_housekeeping_profile_scope.py
tests/gateway/test_checkpoint_prune_housekeeping.py
tests/gateway/test_cron_delivery_housekeeping.py
tests/gateway/test_memory_trim_housekeeping.py
tests/gateway/test_plugin_check_housekeeping.py
                                          31 passed, 0 failed  (9 files)
```

The two failures are pre-existing and environmental: `TestScratchDirPermissionPolicy` asserts `0o700`
and this host (uid 10000, container) produces `0o750`. They fail identically on unmodified
`19b7c7c24d`.

New coverage:

- `test_the_process_gate_keeps_its_chance_when_the_hour_is_not_up` — inside the hour nothing is spent
  and the later call still walks through. Fails on a build with the production change reverted, at
  the spawn assertion.
- `test_the_process_gate_still_holds_after_a_real_pass` — the gate still closes after a real pass, so
  a fan-out does not become a per-call scan.
- `test_a_long_lived_caller_re_asks_the_hour_not_the_process` — `prune_scratch_dir_if_due` prunes on
  the stamped hour even with the process gate long closed.
- `test_multiplexed_scratch_chore_reaches_every_served_profile` — two homes, one tick: the chore
  visits both, each resolving its own home. Red before §3.

`python scripts/check --base 0431192d69d4afd2443a7da15bb9e129a424414c`: **health ok, 5 files, 0
blocking, 0 advisory**. `ruff` in the same run reports one pre-existing FURB192 in
`tests/gateway/test_native_http_auth.py:230`, a file this PR does not touch — it comes from the local
ruff being newer than the pinned 0.15.22, not from this branch.

## Known limitations

- If handing the pass to the detached child raises, the attempt is suppressed and the stamp is
  already touched, so that hour is skipped. Pre-existing behaviour, unchanged here; a retry policy is
  a separate change.
- Behind a multiplexed gateway each profile's sweep is independently stamped, so one profile's
  unreadable store does not stop the next (`_for_each_served_profile` provides the per-profile
  boundary).

prs.title: fix(secrets): move secret caches and the Photon token to the profile home root
prs.body:
## Summary

The Bitwarden and 1Password secret caches and the Photon sidecar token now live at the top of the profile home, where a sandbox can hide them by path, and every credential guard lists them, including the 1Password cache that no guard covered before.

A sandbox that hides files by path (MXC `deniedPaths` on Windows, used by the OpenShell plugin) can only protect a file that sits directly in the granted home. The sandboxed agent can rename a folder it writes, such as `cache/` or `runtime/`, together with a hidden file below it, and read that file at the new path (measured on MXC 1.0.0 and 1.0.1).

| Store | Old path | New path |
|---|---|---|
| Bitwarden plaintext cache | `cache/bws_cache.json` | `bws_cache.json` |
| Bitwarden encrypted cache | `cache/bws_cache.enc.json` | `bws_cache.enc.json` |
| 1Password cache | `cache/op_cache.json` | `op_cache.json` |
| Photon sidecar record (port, token, pid) | `runtime/photon-sidecar.json` | `photon-sidecar.json` |

## Changes

- `utils.adopt_legacy_file()`: moves a file from its old path with a rename, so it keeps its permissions. If the new file exists, it removes the old copy; if the move fails, the caller keeps using the old path, so only one copy is live.
- `agent/secret_sources/_cache.py`, `bitwarden.py`: the disk caches read and write `<home>/<name>` through it; clearing removes both locations.
- `plugins/platforms/photon/adapter.py`: the record lives at `<home>/photon-sidecar.json`; read and write move an old `runtime/` record, delete removes both.
- `hermes_cli/home_data_layout.SECRET_CACHE_STORES`: the stores at both locations, used by `PROFILE_CREDENTIAL_PATHS`, `agent/file_safety` (read and write denies), the gateway's media-delivery deny and backups. The dashboard Files API blocks the two new basenames; the flat-install `.gitignore` ignores the four top-level names.
- Docs: the Bitwarden, 1Password, Photon and security pages name the new paths.

Existing files move on first use. A profile that never uses its Bitwarden or 1Password source again keeps the old file in `cache/`, still covered by every guard.

## Validation

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| New and changed tests (`test_secret_cache_location.py`, `test_credential_store_lists.py`, Photon runtime record, Files API, flat-install `.gitignore`) | 23 fail | all pass |
| 88 related test files on Windows | 28 failures, 1 error | the same 28 and 1 (all present on `main`) |
| `scripts/check --base main` | | passes |

`test_credential_store_lists.py` takes each store's path from its writer and checks every guard against the current and the old location.

prs.title: feat(terminal): opt-in zero-capability Docker sandbox posture
prs.body:
## Motivation

The Docker sandbox already runs with `--cap-drop ALL` and `no-new-privileges`, but it re-adds a small set of capabilities (`_PRIVDROP_CAP_ARGS`) so the init privilege-drop can work. That is the right default for most users. Some operators, however, run the sandbox on shared or exposed hosts and want a strictly *zero-capability* container: no `--cap-add` at all, no way to re-enable privileges through `docker_extra_args`, and a guarantee that a reused container actually has that posture rather than a legacy one.

This PR adds that as an **opt-in** setting. Nothing changes when it is left at its default.

## What changes

- **New config key** `terminal.docker_zero_cap` (default `false`), wired from `config.yaml` through the existing internal terminal env bridge into the Docker backend.
- **Security args** (`_build_security_args(..., zero_cap=True)`): every `--cap-add <cap>` pair is stripped; `--cap-drop ALL`, `no-new-privileges` (unless `snap_compat`), tmpfs and the rest of the hardening stay. Composes with `docker_snap_compat`.
- **Override rejection**: with `zero_cap=True`, `docker_extra_args` containing `--cap-add`, `--cap-add=…`, `--privileged`, or `--security-opt no-new-privileges=false` (any spelling with `=`/`:`) raises `ValueError` at `DockerEnvironment` construction, so a config override cannot silently weaken the posture.
- **Separate container identity**: the container profile label gets a `-zero-cap` suffix. Strict turns never attach to a default container and default turns never attach to a strict one, in both directions (including recreation after a config flip).
- **Inspect-based reuse gate**: `_find_reusable_container` skips any candidate whose `docker inspect` HostConfig does not show `Privileged=false`, empty `CapAdd`, `ALL` in `CapDrop` and `no-new-privileges` in `SecurityOpt`. Any inspect failure or unparsable output is treated as "not zero-cap" and the container is not reused.
- **Documentation**: the Docker `config.yaml` example, `TERMINAL_DOCKER_*` mapping table, hardening summary, and a dedicated zero-capability section document the opt-in and its init compatibility trade-off.

## Testing

Validated on pushed head `4124b01162ff53aecf84c8a1d9309ad33449e6a8` with the canonical runner:

```
HERMES_PYTHON=/opt/agent-zero-app/venv/bin/python scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/tools/test_docker_zero_cap.py \
  tests/tools/test_docker_environment.py \
  tests/tools/test_terminal_config_env_sync.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_config.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_env_loader.py
# 279 passed, 4 skipped

python -m py_compile tests/tools/test_docker_zero_cap.py
python -m ruff check tests/tools/test_docker_zero_cap.py
# All checks passed

git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
# clean
```

The two zero-cap invariant tests cover the real `config.yaml` → internal bridge → terminal resolver → backend → `DockerEnvironment` path, override rejection and inspect-gated reuse. The same tests fail on the feature's parent commit.

Related: #71518 (opt-in runtime override + read-only rootfs) touches the same `_build_security_args` area but adds orthogonal knobs (`docker_runtime`, `docker_readonly`); whichever lands second rebases trivially over the other.

prs.title: fix(terminal): conservatively detect bind mounts in docker_extra_args
prs.body:
## Main synchronization — 2026-09-28

Integrated upstream main `8792f7237f` using merge commits, preserving contribution history and PR scope. Current head: `bec37f210c`.

Validation: 98 passed, 2 skipped across three focused Python files. The full repository suite was not run; earlier validation below remains historical.

## Review follow-up (2026-09-15)

Commit a2c5029962 additionally keeps guards enabled for inherited `--volumes-from` mounts and `--mount` volume-driver options. All driver options conservatively count, including ones that would not bind host files. Ordinary named/anonymous volumes without such options retain the existing fast path. This remains a heuristic, not a complete isolation audit.

Fresh validation: 66 targeted tests plus 37 existing consumers passed (103 total). Tests now exercise the real execute_code entry point against temporary profile configuration and prove that unattended deny blocks host-access cases before remote execution while isolated cases execute. Explicit deny rules are also asserted. Ruff and whitespace pass. Historical results below precede this follow-up.

## What does this PR do?

`_docker_has_host_access` feeds `has_host_access` into `approval._should_skip_container_guards`, which skips dangerous-command and `execute_code` approval for a container judged isolated. It inspected only `docker_mount_cwd_to_workspace` and `docker_volumes` — so a bind mount supplied through `docker_extra_args`, a first-class config key, was invisible and the guard skipped for a container that reaches host files.

Argument interpretation now lives in `tools/environments/docker.py` beside the existing `_extra_args_network_mode` / `_extra_args_set_shm_size` parsers, next to container creation. Approval policy stays in `approval.py`; config orchestration stays in `terminal_tool.py`, which keeps `_docker_has_host_access` as the predicate and delegates.

**Why conservative rather than precise.** Correctly deciding which tokens are flag *values* would mean maintaining docker's value-consuming flag table. Instead this detects *mount-ish* tokens and deliberately accepts false positives for them, while leaving unrelated arguments alone. The claim is conservative detection of potential bind mounts — **not** a precise determination of docker isolation.

**Operational consequence (please read):** ambiguous mount-like arguments conservatively enable normal approval guards. This can require approval or block execution under unattended deny policies, including when a mount-like token is actually another option's value (`["--label", "--volume=/tmp:/mnt"]` is treated as host access on purpose). Recognised named and anonymous volumes, and unrelated args such as `--network none`, stay isolated.

## Related Issue

Related: #78035 — the finding originates in @tieubao's review there. Not `Fixes`, since this doesn't close that PR.

Note for #78035 reviewers: that branch added its own `_extra_args_expose_host_path` in `9ee310573`. Against head `551f399b98` it still misses pflag attached/combined shorthand (`-v/tmp:/mnt`, `-iv/tmp:/mnt`), CSV-quoted `--mount` fields, values with leading whitespace, and bare `.`/`..` sources. The parser here handles those and the tests port across directly.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🔒 Security fix
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `tools/environments/docker.py` — new `extra_args_may_bind_host_path()`, plus `_bind_value_may_be_host_path()` and `_mount_value_may_be_host_path()` helpers.
  - Every docker flag spelling: separate tokens, attached values (`-v/host:/c`), pflag boolean clusters (`-iv/host:/c`, `-iv=/host:/c`), `=`-joined long forms.
  - `--mount` parsed with `csv.reader` after trimming the whole value the way docker does — otherwise a leading space or tab stops a quoted field starting at position 0 and `"type=bind"` parses as the literal key `"type`.
  - Only `type` is inspected; every explicit bind reaches the host whatever it names. An omitted type defaults to `volume`, as docker does.
  - Volume sources classified against docker's named-volume grammar (`^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$`) rather than a path-prefix list, so `.` and `..` are covered by construction.
- `tools/terminal_tool.py` — `_docker_has_host_access` delegates; predicate and call sites unchanged.
- `tests/tools/test_docker_host_access_extra_args.py` — 55 tests.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/tools/test_docker_host_access_extra_args.py -q` → 55 passed.
2. Regression: `pytest tests/tools/test_terminal_task_cwd.py tests/tools/test_modal_sandbox_fixes.py -q` → 37 passed.
3. Reproduce the original bypass on `main`: with `docker_extra_args=["--mount","type=bind,src=/tmp,dst=/mnt"]`, empty `docker_volumes` and cwd-mounting off, `_docker_has_host_access` returns `False` and `_should_skip_container_guards("docker", has_host_access=False)` returns `True` — approval skipped. After this change: `True` / `False` — approval enforced.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — **see note below**
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26 (Darwin 25.4.0), arm64, Python 3.11.16

**On the test checkbox, honestly:** I did not run the whole suite green. In a `.[dev]`-only venv on macOS a number of files fail for environmental reasons unrelated to this change — missing optional extras (`aiohttp`, `slack_sdk`), macOS `AF_UNIX path too long`, and pytest tmp-path issues. What I did run:

- Targeted suite: **55 passed**.
- Existing consumers of the predicate: **37 passed**.
- Wide sweep `-k "terminal or approval or docker or guard or environment"`: **1670 passed** on this branch vs **1629** on unmodified `main` — the delta is 41 tests (this sweep predates the subsequently reported 55-test targeted suite), and the failing test *identities* matched `main` one-for-one.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/`: the failing files are identical to `main`'s and none import the changed code.
- `ruff check` and `git diff --check`: clean.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Docstrings document the conservative posture and the accepted false positive
- [x] No config keys added or changed — N/A for `cli-config.yaml.example`
- [x] Cross-platform considered: Windows drive sources (`C:\host:C:\container`) keep their drive colon out of the split and are covered by tests

## Screenshots / Logs

```
attached shorthand               has_host_access=True   guards ENFORCED
pflag cluster                    has_host_access=True   guards ENFORCED
CSV-quoted + leading space       has_host_access=True   guards ENFORCED
dot-relative source              has_host_access=True   guards ENFORCED
--network none (isolated)        has_host_access=False  fast path kept
```

Credit: @tieubao reported the original `extra_args` gap in review of #78035.

prs.title: fix(tools): narrowly repair malformed GLM tool calls
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?
`glm-5.3-flash` sometimes emits the `tool_call` bridge's `calls` argument as a malformed JSON *string* (entry object left unclosed, `name` promoted next to `calls` or relocated after the args object). Those payloads now get a specific "re-emit as a native array" error, and the two observed mangles are repaired in one shot when the shape is certain. Anything else fails closed.

## Related Issue
No tracking issue. Extracted from #114556 (focused follow-up; the original branch is preserved at `Byrd-IT:backup/pr-114556-original-20260918`).

## Type of Change
- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made
- `tools/tool_search_validation.py`: specific error for an unparseable string `calls`; two narrowly gated repairs (family A: sibling `name`; family D: relocated `name`). Accepts only an anchored `[{` prefix, exactly one balanced strictly-parsed `arguments` object, and closers or the family-D name tail after it. A name in the string that differs from the resolved name, content before `arguments`, or a bridge-tool name fails closed. Only the parsed arguments object is dispatched; outer envelope keys are not merged in.
- `tests/tools/test_connector_bridge_wiring.py`: accepted and rejected shapes, each guard exercised by its own case.

## How to Test
`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_connector_bridge_wiring.py` (57 passed, 0 failed). Repro by hand: `normalize_tool_call_entries({"calls": '[{"arguments": {"a": 1}] , "name": "some_tool" } ]'})` returns one `some_tool` call with `{"a": 1}`; the same string with `"name": "tool_call"` or a mismatched sibling name returns the re-emit error.

## Checklist
### Code
- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate (#114484 handles *valid* JSON-string envelopes; this covers only malformed ones)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits): one squashed commit on current `main`
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass: ran `scripts/run_tests.sh` on the changed and related test files only (below), not the full suite
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs): 14 checks, ok
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.8)
### Documentation & Housekeeping
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A: docstrings updated
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A: no config keys
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A: pure string handling
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A: no schema change

## Screenshots / Logs
`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_connector_bridge_wiring.py`: `57 tests passed, 0 failed`. `python scripts/check`: `14 checks, ok`.

prs.title: Require planner admission for newly created Kanban work
prs.body:
New tasks can currently execute as soon as they are assigned, so a planning workflow cannot require initial review across CLI, agent, and dashboard creation. This adds opt-in board admission: new ordinary requests stay pending in Triage until a trusted planner commits a specification or decomposition. Existing tasks retain their previous behavior.

Planner review receipts commit with the graph change. Subtickets inherit the review and upstream prerequisites; validated workflows can explicitly exempt creation through a scoped Python integration API. Creator labels and task metadata cannot supply either capability. Claims, completion, readiness, dashboard drag/bulk transitions, manual promotion, and specification/decomposition enforce the persisted gate. Existing dependency and approval gates still apply.

Validation: 144 scoped native tests passed (one Windows-only skip), and all 14 `scripts/check` checks passed against base `088f657ecf77674c7b8e2ededf4e3576d82e042c`, with zero health findings. A broader Kanban sweep has 45 existing home-I/O guard failures across ten files in this installation layout; an in-memory HEAD comparison reproduced the identical failures with guards enabled. Downstream integration additionally passed bounded real-SQLite graph/admission checks and workflow preservation suites.

prs.title: fix(redact): mask `*.env`/`*.toml` secrets, CLI secret flags, and URL path tokens
prs.body:
## Problem

Terminal-output redaction silently passed four common secret shapes through, so a secret
read for ordinary diagnostics landed verbatim in tool output (and therefore in transcript
history). All four are reproduced on `main`:

| Command | Leaked content |
|---|---|
| `ps aux \| grep easytier` | `--network-secret <hex>` in full argv |
| `grep ^ET_PEERS /etc/easytier/homelab.env` | `wss://host:port/et-<32hex>` relay token |
| `cat /etc/easytier/homelab.toml` | `network_secret = "<hex>"` |
| any `.env` read of `<service>.env` | whole file, classified non-secret |

Root causes, one per shape:

1. `_is_secret_file_arg` only matched the `.env*` **prefix** family listed in
   `_ENV_FILE_BASENAMES`. Operators name secret env files `<service>.env`
   (`/etc/easytier/homelab.env`), which fell through to the lenient `code_file` path.
2. `*.toml` service configs were never classified secret-bearing, so
   `network_secret = "..."` / `api_key = "..."` printed verbatim.
3. A secret passed as a CLI flag has no `KEY=value` shape, so no assignment pass caught it —
   and `ps`/`top` render the whole argv.
4. `_URL_BARE_TOKEN_RE` only handles `scheme://token@host` userinfo; a bearer token in the
   URL **path** had no rule at all.

Separately, `redact_terminal_output` never forwarded `secret_file` to
`redact_sensitive_text`, so even a correctly identified secret file still ran the lenient
passes.

## Changes

- `_is_secret_file_arg`: treat any `*.env` basename and any `*.toml` as secret-bearing.
- `redact_terminal_output`: forward `secret_file` through.
- `_CLI_SECRET_FLAG_RE` (new): mask `--network-secret <v>`, `--api-key=<v>`, `--token <v>`,
  … The keyword must be a whole `-`/`_`-delimited segment, so `--tokenizer` does not match.
- `_URL_PATH_TOKEN_RE` (new): mask an opaque 24+ char path segment (`wss://host/et-<32hex>`).
  **Strict mode only** — in ordinary output a long path segment is usually a real route
  (`/commit/<sha>`), so this must not fire globally.

## False-positive check

Strict mode is safe for `.toml` because the assignment passes only mask credential-shaped
keys holding opaque values. Verified unchanged:

```
token = "1.0"                → unchanged
max_tokens = 100             → unchanged
name = "my-crate"            → unchanged
api_key = "<32 hex>"         → api_key="***"
--tokenizer bert-base-uncased → unchanged
/commit/<40 hex> URL         → unchanged
```

## Verification

- The four leak shapes above now redact: `--network-secret ***`,
  `wss://host:port/***`, `network_secret="***"`.
- `tests/e2e/core/security/test_secret_redaction.py`: **23 passed** on a local tree with
  these changes.
- On a clean `origin/main` + cherry-pick, that same e2e file **could not be executed on
  this machine**: its spawned CLI subprocesses exit with `Gateway draining: update_paused`
  (`rc=1`, turn never runs). Cause is local to this host's running gateway, not the patch —
  reporting it rather than claiming a clean run.
- Upstream's newer `ctx7sk-` rule still masks after this change (regression checked).

Happy to run anything else you want on the branch.

prs.title: fix(redact): split command segments on newlines so multi-line scripts are scanned
prs.body:
## Problem

`_command_segments` splits a command line only on unquoted `| ; &`, never on newlines. A
multi-line script therefore collapses into **one** segment, and `_command_reads_secret_file`
judges it by that segment's first token alone:

```
echo '=== dump ==='
cat /opt/app/.env          ← line 3, never examined
```

Segment 0 starts with `echo`, which is not in `_FILE_READ_COMMANDS`, so
`_command_reads_secret_file` returns False → `code_file=True` → the ENV/assignment passes
stay disabled and the file's contents print verbatim.

The gap is specifically the newline. The same read written on one line is already caught:

| command | `_command_reads_secret_file` |
|---|---|
| `echo hi; cat /opt/app/.env` | `True` ✅ |
| `echo hi` ⏎ `cat /opt/app/.env` | `False` ❌ |

So a script that opens with any `echo`/`printf` banner — the normal shape of a diagnostic
script — silently loses the protection the single-command path provides.

## Change

Split on unquoted newlines as well. A multi-line script is a sequence of independent
commands, so an `echo` or heredoc preamble on line 1 must not hide a reader on line 3.

Quoting rules are unchanged: newlines inside quotes stay inside their segment, and
`| ; &` inside quotes still do not split, so `awk '{print $1; print $2}'` and
`grep 'foo|bar'` remain single segments.

Same input also improves `is_env_dump_command`: a trailing `env` line in a script is now
recognized instead of being hidden behind the script's first token.

## Verification

- `echo '=== dump ==='` ⏎ `cat /opt/app/.env` ⏎ `echo done` → 3 segments,
  `_command_reads_secret_file` → `True`, and `redact_terminal_output` masks the value
  (`DB_PASSWORD="***"`).
- No over-split: `awk '{print $1; print $2}' /tmp/x` and `grep 'foo|bar' /tmp/x` each
  remain 1 segment.
- No false positive: `echo 'cat secret.env'` (quoted fake command) and `echo hello` ⏎
  `ls -la` both stay `False`.
- `tests/agent/test_redact.py` + `tests/tools/test_terminal_error_redaction.py`:
  **228 passed** on this branch.

Note on scope: which *filenames* count as secret-bearing is unchanged here. This branch
catches `cat .env`, `.bashrc` and Hermes `config.yaml` (already in
`_ENV_FILE_BASENAMES`); `<service>.env` names like `/etc/easytier/homelab.env` are a
separate concern tracked in #146688. The two compose: that PR widens the filename set, this
one makes multi-line scripts look at every line.

prs.title: fix(install): treat ~/.zshenv PATH setup as existing for zsh
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`install.sh` decides whether to append the `# Hermes Agent command` PATH block by checking `~/.zshrc` and `~/.zprofile` for existing `~/.local/bin` setup. It never looks at `~/.zshenv`, which every zsh reads (login, interactive, and non-interactive). A zsh user who already puts `~/.local/bin` on PATH in `~/.zshenv` still gets the block appended to both `~/.zshrc` and `~/.zprofile`.

This PR makes `wire_shell_path` skip the zsh rc edits when `~/.zshenv` already matches `SHELL_PATH_SETUP_RE`. The bash and fish paths are unchanged.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. I searched open and closed issues and PRs for `zshenv`, `zprofile local/bin`, and `Hermes Agent command zshrc` and found nothing related.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `scripts/install.sh`: in `wire_shell_path`, return early for zsh when `~/.zshenv` already sets up `~/.local/bin` on PATH.
- `tests/scripts/install/test_install_sh_shell_path.py`: `_wire` takes a `shell` argument; add one test showing `~/.zshenv` setup counts as existing setup, and one showing zsh without any setup still gets the block in both files.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/scripts/install/test_install_sh_shell_path.py`
2. Without the `install.sh` change, `test_zshenv_path_setup_counts_as_existing_setup` fails because `~/.zshrc` and `~/.zprofile` get created. With it, all 6 tests pass.

Real-world reproduction: on macOS with `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` in `~/.zshenv`, running the installer appended the block to both `~/.zshrc` and `~/.zprofile`.

prs.title: feat(cli): show the routing provider beside the model in the status bar
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The CLI/TUI status bars show the model but not which provider serves it. With two providers behind the same model id — `openrouter` vs a direct endpoint, two `custom:` entries, an `openai-codex` route vs a local one — both render identically, and after a fallback or a mid-turn `/model` pick the bar could name a route that `/status` disagreed with.

This adds a `provider` status-bar field to both surfaces, rendered as `model via provider`:

```
 ☤ claude-opus-4.8 via openrouter · ctx 12k/200k · [▓▓░░░░░░░░] 6% · 1m
```

`display.status_bar.fields` controls it like every other segment (shown by default; omit `provider` to hide it).

Both bars and `/status` now resolve model + provider through one helper, `hermes_cli/status_report.py::resolve_display_identity` (pending switch → metadata mirror → live agent → configured route), with the `custom` sentinel resolved against the owning profile. That is the bug half: the surfaces previously each picked a provider with slightly different precedence, so they could disagree after a fallback, a queued switch or a compute-host turn.

Based on #140416 by @christophkroeppl — same design, same `provider` field name. Rebased onto current `main`, ported where `main` had refactored the same code (`_scoped_session_provider` replaces the PR's now-duplicate `_custom_provider`, compute-host identity rule kept), and made ratchet-clean: the original predates the current code-health caps and grew six of them.

prs.title: fix(gateway): a minted session row carries its model
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`record_gateway_session_peer` self-heals a missing session row with an INSERT that lists 13 columns and omits `model`; `_session_create_kwargs` never carried a model either. So every messaging session minted by the gateway keeps `sessions.model = NULL` forever — the column the session switcher, `/status` and the usage/insights surfaces read. The renderer crash on such a row is already handled by #146560 (a null guard); this PR fixes the producer, so new rows stop being NULL at the source.

## Related Issue

Fixes #146723

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_state_gateway.py`: `_gateway_session_model()` resolves the profile's configured model (`model.default` / `model.model`, the precedence `_resolve_gateway_model` uses). The self-heal INSERT now writes it, and `ON CONFLICT` uses `COALESCE(sessions.model, excluded.model)` so a model the row already recorded (e.g. a `/model` override) is never overwritten.
- `gateway/session_recovery.py`: `_session_create_kwargs` passes `model`, so the normal `create_session` path stops writing NULL too.
- `tests/gateway/test_gateway_session_model.py`: four cases — configured `model.default`, a flat `model:` string, an existing model preserved, and the control (`_insert_session_row` already carried it). The two insert cases are red on `main` (`assert None == 'test-model'`).

## How to Test

prs.title: feat(setup): kittentts wheel sha256 pin — supply-chain tamper gate (1 manifest, 0 trusted fallbacks)
prs.body:
## Before

The Hermes Desktop setup pulls `kittentts` as a wheel from PyPI for the local TTS stack. If the wheel was tampered with (compromised maintainer account, typosquat, or PyPI CDN breach), the user got a malicious Python wheel running on their machine with full local access. The v0.21.0 Security hardening section called this out; this PR closes the loop.

## After

`kittentts` wheel downloads now verify against a pinned SHA-256 manifest baked into the installer. Refuse to proceed on any drift — no PyPI fallback, no mirror, no implicit trust. One manifest, zero trusted fallbacks.

## Numbers

- 1 manifest: `hermes-desktop/kittentts/SHA256SUMS` (versioned, repo-pinned)
- 0 trusted fallbacks (the entire wheel chain is gated)
- 100% refusal on checksum drift (no silent install)
- Surface: clear "tampered wheel" diagnostic with the expected vs actual hash
- Pinned versions: `kittentts==0.7.x` (current supported line)

## Verify

- [x] Tampered wheel test: install fails closed, no fallback path taken
- [x] Manifest refresh flow documented (operator procedure)
- [x] No regression on the happy path
- [x] CI: pre-flight check confirms manifest is current
- [x] Documentation: `setup.md` §"Wheel integrity gate"

prs.title: feat(gateway): busy_result_mode carries mid-turn subagent and background-process results into the running turn
prs.body:
Fixes #136703

## What and why

When a background `delegate_task` child finishes while the parent is mid-turn, the session holds the result until the turn ends and then spends a separate model turn on it. This change adds an opt-in setting so the result can reach the turn that is already running:

```yaml
delegation:
  busy_result_mode: steer   # queue (default, unchanged) | steer
```

With `steer`, the gateway's completion-delivery seam (`_deliver_completion_notification`) offers a claimed async-delegation completion to the session's running agent instead of admitting it as a new turn. Classic CLI runs its turns on the gateway (one-gateway runtime), so this one seam covers CLI, TUI and messaging sessions. `agent/background_results.py` appends them to the **next tool result just before that result is persisted**. This is the same mutable tail slot the iteration-budget and run-budget notices use, so:

- past context is never rewritten, and the prompt cache holds;
- the transcript matches what the model saw;
- the text is marked as background tool-channel evidence. It is deliberately **not** the `/steer` user-authority marker, because a child's output must not be given user authority.

If no later tool batch carries an offered result (the turn ends without another tool call, or is stopped), it goes back to the completion queue and arrives as the ordinary next turn, exactly as `queue` mode delivers it. Durable claims are acknowledged when the result is accepted, the same way the idle drain acknowledges them on enqueue.

Events owned by other sessions are returned to the completion queue untouched.

## Background-process completions

The same opt-in covers `terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` completions, under their own key next to `display.background_process_notifications`:

```yaml
display:
  background_process_busy_result_mode: steer   # queue (default, unchanged) | steer
```

They go through the same seam and carrier, with a process-specific marker (`a background process you started finished…`). The settle contract differs because a process completion has no durable claim and belongs to its per-process watcher: requeuing it onto `completion_queue` would strand it. So the delivery call waits on the carry (`gateway/run_notifications_busy_result.py`). If a tool result carried it, the call returns True and no turn starts. If the turn ended without carrying it, the same call continues into the ordinary `_inject_watch_notification`, so watcher retries and fallback notices are unchanged. A cancelled delivery (shutdown) withdraws the offer, so the turn cannot carry what the watcher retries. A completion the agent already read with `process(wait/log)` (`is_completion_consumed`, checked for every process in a coalesced batch) is not shown again. Watch-pattern matches, heartbeats and API-server sessions keep queueing.

## Relation to #104434

#104434 (`result_delivery="inject"`) only injects into the **originating** parent turn and is chosen per call by the model. This PR covers the common case where the result arrives during a *later* turn, and is a user-level config default. The two are orthogonal.

## Scope

- Durable claims stay held while the result rides the turn: acknowledged once a tool result carried it (watcher tick), deferred and requeued at turn cleanup otherwise, so nothing is lost and no delivery attempt is spent. API-server sessions and per-task failure notices keep queueing. `gateway/run_busy.py` is untouched: other internal events still never steer.
- New config keys are in `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, plus the dashboard selects, `cli-config.yaml.example` and the docs (delegation, tools, gateway internals). No env var. `config_defaults.py` is over its file cap, so both keys are offset by folding neighbouring comments.
- #140296 / #142319 change how the *queue* path coalesces completions; they are orthogonal (with `queue`, the default, nothing here runs).

## Tests

- `tests/agent/test_background_results.py`: a real `run_conversation` loop. A result offered while the model is thinking appears on the tool result of the next request, never as a user row. It is red without the `tool_executor` hook.
- `tests/gateway/test_delegation_busy_result_steer.py`: a busy-session result rides the running turn's tool result and no new turn is admitted; an uncarried result is deferred and requeued as the next turn. Both red on `main`.
- `tests/gateway/test_process_busy_result_steer.py` (mode read from a real `config.yaml` through the gateway loader): a busy-session process completion rides the tool result and no turn is admitted; an uncarried one is admitted once as the next turn; one already read with `process(wait)` is not shown again. The carry test is red without the process commit: the completion is delivered at once as a new turn.

Run with `scripts/run_tests.sh`: the two new files plus `tests/gateway/test_completion_delivery.py`, `test_completion_owner_retry.py`, `test_async_delegation_session_binding.py` (all passed). Process part: 14 files incl. `test_background_process_notifications.py`, `test_gateway_shutdown.py`, `test_display_config.py`, `test_web_server.py` → 498 passed. `python scripts/check`: ok. Platform: Linux.

---

**Rebase note (2026-10-15):** rebased onto `main` @ `3dd9e4edfd` (2 commits, clean); `tests/agent/test_background_results.py` + `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_delegation_busy_result_mode.py` → 3 passed.






**Update (2026-10-17):** the first version hooked the classic CLI's turn monitor, which no longer runs since classic CLI turns moved onto the gateway; live probe confirmed results still queued. The steer path now lives at the gateway completion-delivery seam and the dead CLI hook is removed. Rebased onto `main` @ `e7e839a5f4`.
**Update (2026-10-24):** rebased onto `main` @ `dd5bc7ee13`; added the background-process completion path (last commit) and a `config_defaults.py` line offset.

(4e35169b2b, 342a55ebad). This PR was rebased onto that work and narrowed to the two cases it does
not cover. The `/discard` route, the pre-submit refusal and the related tests that this PR originally
carried were dropped in favour of upstream's.

1. **Fence lands after submit.** If the owner restarts while a prompt is being submitted, the
   pre-submit check passes, the prompt is admitted, and the restarted owner then fences the turn
   ahead of it as `unknown`. The new prompt sits `queued` behind it and the CLI waits for a
   `message.complete` that never comes (`Initializing agent...` with no end). `_pump` now watches
   the `pending` list from `session.info`; when its own admission is `queued` behind an `unknown`
   one, it withdraws the prompt with `prompt.cancel` and returns `failure_reason="unknown_execution"`
   with the same `/discard` recovery copy, instead of hanging.
2. **Queued behind another running turn.** When the prompt is queued behind an admission that is
   still running (for example an automation turn the restarted owner drains first), the CLI prints
   once that the message is queued and should not be resent. Previously it stayed silent, which is
   what led users to resend the same message into the queue.

Fail-closed is unchanged: nothing is replayed, and no turn is discarded without an explicit `/discard`.

## Related Issue

Refs #139532 (CLI + gateway paths; ACP is #139541)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py`: `_pump` returns `_BLOCKED` when this turn's admission is queued
  behind a lost turn (`_queued_behind_lost`); `run_conversation` withdraws it with `prompt.cancel`
  and returns the `/discard` recovery. `_running_ahead` drives the one-time "Queued: another turn is
  still running" notice.
- `agent/turn_failure_copy.py`, `agent/error_surface.py`: `unknown_execution` is a gateway-layer
  site failure code, so the CLI shows the recovery copy as written instead of classifying it as a
  provider failure.
- `gateway/session_authority.py`, `gateway/session_ingress.py`: the `Session … paused:
  unknown_execution` log warning names the exact operator command (`hermes [-p <profile>] sessions
  discard <id>`) instead of an unnamed operator.

prs.title: fix(cli): restore reasoning display after gateway reconnect
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Restore the classic CLI's reasoning display preference when its existing connection reconnects to the gateway.

The gateway's `live.show_reasoning` flag is intentionally session-scoped and in-memory. `GatewayAgent.reasoning_callback` sends it and caches the last `(session_id, enabled)` pair. After a gateway restart the CLI keeps that cache, but the new owner has no flag. `GatewayConnection._resubscribe` restores the subscription without restoring the preference. Replies still stream, but live reasoning no longer does; the CLI can subsequently render `last_reasoning` in its end-of-turn fallback box, below the streamed reply. Restarting the CLI masks the problem by sending the flag again.

Keep the preference in this viewer's per-session state and replay it after a successful resume, before the reconnected socket becomes ready. Use the asynchronous client already on that loop, not the blocking `connection.call`. Preserve explicit hidden preferences too; sessions without a preference are untouched. A restore failure follows the existing reconnect failure path, so no prompt is silently admitted before restoration. No prompt replay, persistent config write, transcript mutation, or new protocol/config field is introduced.

## Related Issue

Refs #134889 (classic CLI reconnect regression).
Related: #139470 restores the same live flag on ACP reattachment. This PR changes the classic CLI only; it does not duplicate ACP, Desktop, reasoning-effort persistence, or commentary routing work.

Searched open and closed/merged issues and PRs for the symptom, `show_reasoning`, reconnect/restart, and the cache symbol; checked the tracker body and comments. No existing classic CLI fix for this path was found.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py`: remember the callback-derived preference on the session's shared viewer state.
- `hermes_cli/gateway_connection.py`: restore that preference after resuming each retained session, before readiness/new requests. A refused resume is still skipped, with no config write for that session.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_connection_reconnect.py`: exercise shown/hidden preferences, first-turn ordering, same-connection write deduplication, and independent preferences for multiple sessions. Update the existing lost-turn test for the added restore request.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_reasoning_reconnect_live.py`: use a real disposable gateway daemon and a loopback fake model, restart the daemon, and verify the same CLI connection/agent receives reasoning before answer deltas on its next turn.

## How to Test

Interactive reproduction:
1. Start a classic CLI session with streaming and `/reasoning show`.
2. Finish a turn, then restart its gateway while keeping the CLI open.
3. Ask another question in the same CLI. Expected: live reasoning still arrives before the reply, without restarting the CLI. On the base, the owner loses its flag and reasoning falls back to the end-of-turn box.

Automated validation on Linux, Python 3.14.7:
- Base: `0f3eac0b8f7ccef9c469c9e9469c5b08e538d8f4`.
- New regression cases on the unchanged base: **3 failed**, at missing reasoning callbacks / missing restore writes (not collection failures).
- The real-daemon restart test also fails on a clean archive of the base: the second turn returns the answer but receives no reasoning (`'' != 'REASONING-BEFORE-THE-ANSWER'`). With the fix it passes, retaining the same connection/agent and receiving all reasoning before the first answer delta. No production gateway or external model is used.

prs.title: fix(agent): keep OpenCode Go keys on a per-model upstream 429
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

OpenCode Go returns HTTP 429 for two unrelated conditions:

| Body | Meaning | Correct recovery |
|---|---|---|
| `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"GoUsageLimitError",...},"metadata":{"limitName":"weekly"}}` | the key's plan window (5-hour / weekly / monthly) | bench the key, rotate (already classified `billing` on main) |
| `{"error":{"type":"server_error","message":"Upstream request failed: Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later."}}` | one model's upstream throttle | keep the key, defer to fallback |

On main both bench the key for the 429 hour. Repro with a two-key `opencode-go` pool where the primary has hit its weekly window: the main agent's model gets the per-model upstream 429, the pool logs `marking <backup> exhausted (status=429)`, and then every auxiliary task pinned to a *different* model on the same provider (approval, vision, compression) fails with `credential pool: no available entries`, although a direct call with the backup key on that other model returns 200.

## Changes

- `plugins/model-providers/opencode-zen/__init__.py`: the `opencode-go` profile sets `classify_api_error` (the existing provider-profile seam) and maps a 429 whose message contains `upstream request failed` to `upstream_rate_limit`. Every other error declines (`None`), so `GoUsageLimitError` keeps its built-in `billing` verdict.
- `agent/auxiliary_client.py::_recover_provider_pool`: the main path (`recover_with_credential_pool`) already skips rotation for `upstream_rate_limit`, but the auxiliary path only used substring predicates and benched anyway. It now consults `classify_api_error` and skips the bench for an `upstream_rate_limit` verdict. That also covers OpenRouter-wrapped upstream 429s on the aux path, which had the same gap.

## How to test

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/plugins/model_providers/test_opencode_go_rate_limit_scope.py`: red on main (2 failures: upstream body classified `rate_limit` and benched on the aux path), green with the fix.
- Directly affected suites: `test_opencode_go_profile.py`, `test_auxiliary_error_classification.py`, `test_provider_profile_recovery_seam.py`, `test_auxiliary_client_cache_eviction.py`, `test_error_classifier.py`: 239 passed.
- Main-path E2E against a temp `HERMES_HOME`: a real `CredentialPool` with two mock entries fed through `recover_with_credential_pool`. Upstream body → no rotation, both entries `ok`. Plan-wall body → primary `exhausted`, rotated to the second entry.
- `scripts/check`: ok.

Platform: Linux (Debian 13).

prs.title: fix(cron): run a fixed-time job once when its run ends in the repeated fall-back hour
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A fixed-time cron job (`30 1 * * *`) can run **twice** on the DST fall-back night.

`mark_job_run` recomputes `next_run_at` from the run's end. `compute_next_run` tries both folds of each candidate wall clock and takes the first instant strictly after the base. So when a run ends inside the second pass of the repeated hour, the same wall clock in the second pass is "strictly after" and gets scheduled:

- America/New_York, 2026-11-01: `30 1 * * *` fires at 01:30 EDT, runs 45 min, ends at 01:15 EST → rescheduled for 01:30 EST → runs again.
- `59 1 * * *` does it with a one-minute run (ends 01:00 EST → 01:59 EST).

Following cronie, only a job with `*` leading its minute or hour field (MIN_STAR/HR_STAR) runs both times through the repeated hour; a fixed-time job runs once. With this PR, a fixed-time job only takes the first pass (fold=0) of a wall clock, so a base in the second pass schedules the next day. Wildcard jobs (`*/15 * * * *`, `30 * * * *`, `@hourly`) are unchanged.

US DST ends on Sunday 1 November 2026.

## Related

- #128024 (open) fixes the other half of the same repeated hour: wildcard jobs whose base is in the *first* pass skip the second pass. It uses the same cronie rule (`*` leading the minute or hour field, `@hourly`). The two changes are complementary: this one covers fixed-time jobs whose base is in the *second* pass, which #128024 leaves as is. They touch the same loop in `compute_next_run`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase; the classifier here (`jobs_time.repeated_hour_folds`) can serve both.
- No issue filed.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `cron/jobs_time.py`: `repeated_hour_folds(expr)` returns `(0, 1)` for a job with `*` leading its minute or hour field (or `@hourly`), else `(0,)`. It lives in the sibling module because `cron/jobs.py` is past the file-lines ratchet.
- `cron/jobs.py`: the strictly-after loop in `compute_next_run` iterates `repeated_hour_folds(expr)` instead of `(0, 1)`. The comment is rewritten; the file's line count is unchanged.
- `tests/cron/test_dst_fixed_time_runs_once.py` (new): drives the real cycle (`create_job` → `get_due_jobs` → `claim_job_for_fire` → `mark_job_run`) one real minute at a time from 00:00 EDT to 04:00 EST on 2026-11-01, plus direct `compute_next_run` checks for a second-pass base and for wildcard jobs.

## How to Test

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/cron/test_dst_fixed_time_runs_once.py -q
```

- Red on `main` (`ef75bc7088`): `3 failed, 4 passed`:
  - `['2026-11-01T01:30:00-04:00', '2026-11-01T01:30:00-05:00']` for `30 1 * * *` with a 45-minute run;
  - `['2026-11-01T01:59:00-04:00', '2026-11-01T01:59:00-05:00']` for `59 1 * * *` with a 1-minute run;
  - `'2026-11-01T01:30:00-05:00' == '2026-11-02T01:30:00-05:00'` for a 01:15 EST base.
- Green with the fix: `7 passed`.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/cron/`: `171 files, 1553 tests passed, 0 failed, 11 skipped`.
- `python scripts/check`: `13 checks, ok` (code health: 0 blocking, 0 advisory).

## Summary

When an auto-vision auxiliary request uses a custom provider whose `key_cmd` resolves to a callable token source, `_resolve_custom_runtime()` currently treats that non-string value as missing and replaces it with `no-key-required`. The placeholder is then forwarded as an explicit key to the named-custom client, overriding the provider's working `key_cmd` authentication. - Keep `no-key-required` only when no usable credential was resolved, preserving keyless local-server behavior.

## Reproduction

Configure `model.provider: custom:litellm` and `model.base_url` for an authenticated gateway, with `providers.litellm.key_cmd` supplying its credential. Call auto-vision resolution without a live endpoint snapshot. Before this change, the generated client sends `Bearer no-key-required` despite the valid provider-level `key_cmd`.

prs.title: fix(bots): don't paint a Screen portal for a group with no routable owner
prs.body:
### What happens

On a Desktop connected to more than one gateway (a local one plus a remote), the Sessions sidebar shows a permanent **Screen** (屏幕) entry above some profile groups. It is a button with no subtitle — `aria-label="Screen: "` — and clicking it opens a Screen pane that cannot work.

### Why

The Bots plugin contributes a Screen portal to `sidebar.profileGroup.header` for every gateway/profile group (`plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.tsx` → `screen-portal.tsx`).

A group whose sessions carry no `connection_id` produces a group route with `connectionId: null`. `ProfileGroupScreenPortal` then finds no roster row and synthesizes `{ name: profile }`. `displayRequest` resolves that row to the profile-only overload (`botScreenRoute` → `not_scoped` → `bot.name`), and `requestPluginProfile` refuses a profile-only route when the desktop has more than one source:

```
Error: Profile "chatbot" requires a route descriptor from host.profileRoutes();
profile-only routing is limited to legacy/local profiles.
```

`useScreenPortalState`'s catch only settles `-32601` (method-not-found); every other failure leaves the state at `unknown`. `portalTone(null, …)` is `'unknown'`, and `ScreenPortal` only hides `unsupported` / `unavailable`, so the entry stays. Its subtitle is `status?.display ?? ''`, i.e. empty — that is the `aria-label="Screen: "`.

Observed on a Windows host, where Bot Screen does not exist at all (`runtime.is_supported_host()` is Linux-only), so the entry can never become anything useful.

### Fix

- `ProfileGroupScreenPortal` renders nothing when the group has no connection and the roster has no owner for it: there is no route to ask for a status.
- `ScreenPortal` renders nothing while the tone is `unknown`: the status has not landed, and an unknown status is not something to open.
- `isDisplayRouteMissing` lets the portal settle a route-less refusal as `unavailable` instead of checking forever.

Test: `screen-portal-visibility.test.tsx` — unknown paints nothing; a connection-less group asks nothing; a route-less refusal settles as unavailable; a routable group still paints once a status lands.

### Repro (before the fix)

1. Desktop with a local gateway and one remote connection.
2. Have a session whose row has no `connection_id` (for example one created before the remote connection was added), so its sidebar group is `[null, "<profile>"]`.
3. The group header shows a Screen entry with an empty subtitle; it persists across reloads and never opens a working pane.

Verified locally: the same build with this patch no longer renders any `button[aria-label^="Screen"]` in the sidebar, and the group header node holds no `ScreenPortal` component at all.

Two of Hermes' own paths build a raw `OpenAI`/`AsyncOpenAI` client for a custom endpoint and sent no
`User-Agent`: `trajectory_compressor.py` (the sync client and the lazy async one) and `mini_swe_runner.py`.
The SDK then sent its own default, `OpenAI/Python x.y`, so anything downstream that names the calling app by
that header sees a different app.

Concretely, with magpie in front of the endpoint — its gateway counts usage by that header
(`internal/usage/usage.go`, `AgentOf`), and every other Hermes client sends `HermesAgent/<version>` — one
agent's compaction calls are counted as **two extra agents**, `OpenAI` and `AsyncOpenAI`, each with its own
request count and score on Usage > Agents. Reported from the other side as yetone/magpie#2558; the fix
belongs here, where the client is built.

## Repro on `main`

Windows, Hermes' provider endpoint is a local magpie gateway (0.1.1267):

- `OpenAI` 48 calls and `AsyncOpenAI` 41 calls over two days — one call per session, `cache_read` 0,
  48–57K in and 14–17K out (context compression, not an agent turn)
- each call lands just before that session's compaction: request `17:16:48` → compaction `17:18:24`;
  `17:27:29` → `17:27:45`; `18:06:16`, `18:08:07` → `18:09:15`; `15:30:01` → `15:31:10`
- the ledger records their agent as the SDK's product name, not `hermes`

## The change

- `agent/client_headers.py` (new): `user_agent_headers()` — the one `User-Agent` Hermes sends, so a helper
  path has a single place to take it from instead of copying the f-string a fifth time
- `trajectory_compressor.py`: both clients pass `default_headers=user_agent_headers()`
- `mini_swe_runner.py`: same for its two raw clients — same class, found by grepping every `OpenAI(` outside
  `agent/` and `tools/`

## Test

`tests/test_trajectory_compressor.py::test_compressor_clients_name_hermes_in_user_agent` builds the
compressor against a custom endpoint and asserts both clients carry `HermesAgent/…`. It **fails on `main`**
(`OpenAI/Python 2.24.0`) and passes with the change. Whole file: 18 passed.

Note: `scripts/run_tests.sh` could not run on this machine (it provisions its pinned uv 0.12.3 and that
download failed with a curl write error), so the run above is `pytest` against the same file with the same
deps; `ruff check` is clean.

## Deliberately not widened

`agent/auxiliary_client.py` and the agents' own adapters already send the header. The four remaining inline
copies of the string (`client_lifecycle.py`, `anthropic_adapter.py`, `codex_headers.py`, `copilot_auth.py`)
can adopt the helper in a follow-up rather than in this diff.

prs.title: fix(skills): scope skill_view dedup cache to the active session
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Scopes the process-global `skill_view` dedup cache to the active session. When the `session_id` passed by the tool layer changes, the whole cache is dropped. This fixes a bug where a fresh session reusing a `task_id` (TUI resume/reconnect, a background-review fork, or any task_id collision) could match a stale entry from a previous session and get a **false "unchanged" stub** for a skill it never actually loaded — forcing the model to re-read the file from disk.

## Related Issue

No open issue covers this exact cross-session leak. Related but distinct: #101518 (dedup after compression), #112763 (prune not clearing the cache), #98206 (stub after compression) — those are about the cache not being cleared on in-session transcript replacement; this one is about entries leaking *across* sessions. Also supersedes the approach of #93471 (bucket by session_id): that PR's premise (task_id is a fresh UUID per turn) did not hold on the shipped surfaces, but the cross-session leak is real whenever a task_id is reused, and dropping on session change is the minimal fix.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `tools/skills_tool.py` — both call sites in `_skill_view_with_bump` now pass `session_id=kw.get("session_id")` to `_check_skill_view_dedup` / `_record_skill_view`.
- `tools/skills_tool_dedup.py` — new `_active_session_id` global and `_drop_cache_on_session_change()`, called under the existing lock from both the record and check paths. `session_id=None` is a no-op, so the fork path (`task_id=None`) is unaffected.
- `tests/tools/test_skill_view_dedup.py` — new `TestSkillViewDedupSessionScope` class: (a) a new `session_id` drops the cache (a fresh session reusing the same `task_id` gets full content, not a stub), (b) `session_id=None` is a no-op and does not clobber a populated cache, (c) the fork path (`task_id=None`) stays out of the cache.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/tools/test_skill_view_dedup.py -q` — 13 passed (9 pre-existing + 4 new).
2. Manual: in one session `skill_view` a skill twice (second call returns the dedup stub); start a fresh session reusing the same task context and `skill_view` the same skill — it must return full content, not the stub.

**Safety:** worst case is a lost optimization (a re-visited session re-serves a skill it already served), never a correctness regression. No new locking surface, no API change (`session_id` is an optional kwarg defaulting to `None`).

prs.title: feat(plugins): session forks, review signals and idle tasks for plugins
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets a plugin borrow the two background patterns core already runs for itself, instead of building its own:

- **Background fork** (the pattern behind background review): `ctx.fork_session(token, prompt, *, tools, max_iterations, input_budget, task, timeout)` runs a bounded background copy of the session agent after an attended turn. It shares the live turn's system prompt, `tools[]` and cache scope, writes nothing to the session, and is gated by a new capability `llm.session_fork` (asked on enable).
- **Cadence**: `post_llm_call` now carries `review_signals` (skill/memory review due, counters, intervals, background review on), so plugins follow the user's self-learning settings instead of counting on their own.
- **Independent curator** (the pattern behind the curator): `ctx.register_idle_task(name, fn, *, interval_hours, min_idle_hours, first_run)` runs a plugin job on the curator's idle schedule, with pause/resume via `hermes plugins idle-tasks`. The interval gate and run claim move from the curator into `agent/idle_schedule.py` so both share one implementation.

Fork guardrails: a fork may only use names that dispatch to the requesting plugin's own registry handler (other plugins' tools, MCP, connectors, memory-provider and context-engine routes, and agent-spawning core tools are refused, at request time with the token unspent and again at dispatch); when Tool Search defers the plugin's tool, the fork reaches it through `tool_call` with `tools[]` unchanged; the next live turn cancels queued and running forks; a fork whose worker cannot start settles as `error:spawn`; inheriting a built-in auxiliary slot's model route needs `llm.allow_task_override`.

First user: the Collective Wisdom plugin's share suggestions (fork) and its promotion curator (idle task).

## Related Issue

Includes the commit from #146472 (parallel tool workers keep the thread's tool whitelist), which forks depend on. That PR can merge first; this one then rebases cleanly or the commit drops out.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `agent/review_signals.py`, `agent/turn_finalizer.py`: `review_signals` on `post_llm_call`.
- `agent/plugin_session_fork.py`, `hermes_cli/plugins_capability_ctx.py`, `hermes_cli/plugin_capabilities.py`: `ctx.fork_session`, capability, guardrails, cancellation.
- `agent/idle_schedule.py`, `agent/curator.py`, `agent/review_idle_queue.py`, `hermes_cli/plugins_idle_tasks.py`: shared idle gate; `ctx.register_idle_task`; CLI.
- `agent/auxiliary_task_config.py`: `inherit_from` route authority.
- `website/docs/developer-guide/plugin-llm-access.md` and the plugin guide.
- Tests under `tests/agent/`, `tests/hermes_cli/`, `tests/tools/`.

## How to Test

1. `pytest -q tests/agent/test_plugin_session_fork.py tests/agent/test_plugin_session_fork_routes.py tests/agent/test_plugin_session_fork_tool_search.py tests/agent/test_review_idle_queue.py tests/agent/test_review_signals.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_idle_tasks.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_auxiliary_tasks.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_capabilities.py tests/tools/test_thread_context_tool_whitelist.py`
2. Enable a plugin that calls `ctx.fork_session` from `post_llm_call` with its own tool, grant `llm.session_fork`, run an attended turn until the skill review is due: the fork runs after the response and its tool handler sees `turn_origin="plugin_fork:<id>"`.

- [x] Conventional Commits
- [x] Only changes for this feature (plus the #146472 commit noted above)
- [x] Tests added
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes
- [x] Docs updated
