prs.title: Add Olympus agent workstation monitor
prs.body:
## Summary

- Bundle Olympus as a dashboard-only Hermes plugin under `plugins/olympus/`.
- Add a read-only agent workstation monitor for readiness, tuning, profiles, sessions, Kanban, skill hygiene, policy, performance, Trace Spine, Operational Evals, Metrics Spine, and evidence-source diagnostics.
- Add plugin-local privacy/metrics/unit tests, a plugin README, a screenshot asset, and the built-in plugin docs entry.

## Why

Hermes already owns the underlying control surfaces: Kanban, Profiles, Sessions, Skills, Config, Logs, Analytics, and Desktop Command Center Usage. What is missing is a single operator workstation view that answers: what needs tuning, routing, unblocking, or review so agents perform better?

Olympus provides that synthesis layer without taking ownership of mutations or ledgers. It reads Hermes evidence, explains the reason behind each recommendation, and links back to the Hermes page that owns the fix.

## Safety and boundaries

- Read-only FastAPI routes: no task moves, profile edits, cron edits, gateway changes, config writes, shell execution, installs, or deletes.
- Routes mount under `/api/plugins/olympus/` and use the dashboard session-token flow.
- Local paths, raw ids, session titles, Kanban task titles, cron names, prompt text, and secret-like strings are hidden by default.
- `.env` scanning reads variable names only, never values.
- Config policy reports safe counts and flags only; it does not return prompt text, base URLs, API keys, env values, or local paths.
- Usage and cost totals remain owned by Hermes Analytics / Command Center Usage; Olympus uses those fields only as tuning and risk evidence.

## Validation

- `python3 -m py_compile dashboard/plugin_api.py`
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'` — 17 tests passed
- `node --check dashboard/dist/index.js`
- `git diff --check`
- Booted a fresh Hermes `origin/main` worktree at `a590c5efd` with a temporary `HERMES_HOME`; Hermes discovered Olympus as a bundled plugin, served `/olympus` with status 200, and returned 200 from `/api/plugins/olympus/health`, `/overview`, and `/tuning`.
- Standalone Olympus live gates also passed against the local Hermes dashboard: `test:compat`, `test:visual`, `test:live`, `test:performance`, `test:security`, `test:desktop`, and `npm audit --audit-level=moderate`.

In Hermes Desktop, top-level projects can be dragged to reorder in the sidebar project overview. However, when entering a multi-folder project, the individual folders/repositories within that project were rendered in a static order with no drag-to-sort support.

prs.title: fix(tools): version files by the stat view on Windows, skip ctime in the comparison
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #146022 with a live repro as the premise, not just code reading.

**Premise (reproduced on Win11 + CPython 3.14.9):** for the same just-written file, `os.fstat(fd)` reports `st_ctime_ns=...749735300` while `os.stat(path)` reports `...486366300` (mtime/size agree). `_file_version()` required all five fields to agree, so it returned None for every version call: no write baseline was ever recorded — reads even actively purge it — and `write_file` refused forever after any full read, exactly as reported.

**Fix (`tools/file_tools_read_tracking.py`):** split stored vs compared fields — on win32 only, `st_ctime` is skipped in the before/after comparison, and the stored version is the path (stat) view. The stored-stat-view choice is load-bearing, not cosmetic: `tools/file_tools.py:551` and `read_tracking.py:184` compare stored baselines against the stat-view `_file_metadata()`. ctime on Windows is creation time and cannot signal a content rewrite; digest + size + mtime still guard content, so tampered bytes keep refusing (guarded by test).

This completes a stashed local WIP for the same issue (prior session left it un-PR'd believing it duplicated an open PR — I scanned all 200 open PRs: none touches this file, and the issue has 0 comments and no PR references).

prs.title: fix(kanban): honour dispatch_stale_timeout_seconds in the standalone daemon and CLI dispatch
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`kanban.dispatch_stale_timeout_seconds` (merged-config default 14400) is only honoured by the gateway-embedded dispatcher. The standalone daemon and one-shot CLI dispatch never resolved or passed it, so `dispatch_once` fell back to its `stale_timeout_seconds=0` parameter default and `detect_stale_running` never ran on those entry points:

```text
kanban.dispatch_stale_timeout_seconds (default 14400)
  -> gateway dispatcher (_resolve_dispatcher_settings)  -> detect_stale_running runs
  -> hermes kanban daemon --force (run_daemon)          -> never passed, 0 = off
  -> hermes kanban dispatch (_cmd_dispatch)             -> never passed, 0 = off
```

On a `--force` daemon host (the shipped systemd path for hosts that cannot run the gateway), a worker wedged before its first heartbeat is therefore never reclaimed as stale, even though the config documents a 4-hour default. Both affected functions already claim gateway-identical semantics for the sibling `max_in_progress` setting; this key was missed when that parity was added.

This PR resolves the key the same way on both paths. The change is deliberately limited to config resolution and passthrough: it does not change the stale criteria in `detect_stale_running`, the claim-TTL backstop in `release_stale_claims`, or gateway behaviour. An explicit `0` still disables stale detection everywhere.

## Related Issue

Fixes #146433

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_config.py`: new sibling holding the shared `kanban.*` config resolvers — `configured_max_in_progress` moved verbatim from `kanban_db_dispatch.py` (re-exported under the same name) plus the new `configured_stale_timeout_seconds`.
- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py`: `run_daemon` re-resolves `configured_stale_timeout_seconds()` every tick (same shape as `max_in_progress`) and passes it to `dispatch_once`.
- `hermes_cli/kanban_ops.py`: `_cmd_dispatch` reads `dispatch_stale_timeout_seconds` from the config it already loads and passes it to `dispatch_once`; unreadable/invalid config resolves to `0`, as on the gateway path.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_stale_timeout_parity.py`: resolver parsing plus daemon and CLI passthrough regressions.

## How to Test

1. Red on `main` (`ef75bc7088`) with the regression tests kept and the production fix absent:

   ```text
   test_run_daemon_passes_stale_timeout_from_config
   AssertionError: assert None == 14400
   test_cli_dispatch_passes_stale_timeout_from_config
   AssertionError: assert None == 7200
   3 failed
   ```

2. Green with this PR, using the canonical test runner:

   ```sh
   scripts/run_tests.sh \
     tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_stale_timeout_parity.py \
     tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_host_cap.py \
     tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli_dispatch_passthrough.py -q
   ```

   Result: **18 tests passed, 0 failed** across the three files, including the existing `max_in_progress` passthrough and daemon-resolution contracts the moved resolver sits next to.

3. `python scripts/check`: **13 checks passed**, including code health. Moving `configured_max_in_progress` into the new sibling also keeps `kanban_db_dispatch.py` from growing past its file-size cap.

Overlap checked: #129545 honours `kanban.failure_limit` on these same two entry points (different key; touches a neighbouring region of `kanban_ops.py`, so whichever lands second rebases trivially). #118164 adds a separate progress-stall detector and does not resolve this key. #119199 seeds `last_heartbeat_at` at claim time (claim side, complementary). #50907 wires `stranded_*` config through the daemon. None of them pass `dispatch_stale_timeout_seconds` outside the gateway path.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Reverting restores the previous behaviour, with no schema, storage, configuration, or migration effects.

**Blast radius:** the standalone daemon and CLI dispatch only gain the behaviour the config already promised; the gateway path is unchanged (`configured_max_in_progress` is a verbatim move and remains importable from `kanban_db_dispatch`). The one judgement call: on `--force` daemon hosts, heartbeat-stale workers now actually get reclaimed at the configured timeout where before they never were — that is the documented default taking effect, and an explicit `0` still opts out.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate

- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

Before this PR, both the daemon tick and the CLI dispatch call `dispatch_once` with no stale timeout:

```text
run_daemon tick:   captured.get("stale_timeout_seconds") -> None
_cmd_dispatch:     captured.get("stale_timeout_seconds") -> None
```

After this PR, the new regressions prove the configured values reach `dispatch_once` (14400 via the daemon resolver, 7200 via CLI config), so `detect_stale_running` runs with the same setting on every dispatch entry point.

prs.title: fix(gateway): settle a lost turn instead of pausing its chat forever (-z and human)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Two related fixes to the same dead-end: a turn fenced `unknown` across a gateway restart pauses its session's FIFO, and on a headless gateway nobody is there to clear it.

Both settle through the fenced resolution `/discard` already uses — terminal `interrupted`, never requeued, never replayed (the GW-10 rule stands).

### 1. `-z` one-shot turns (commit `845a8dce`)

`gateway/session_finite.py:admit_finite` commits `unattended: True` onto the admission payload for exactly one reason — its docstring says it: *"`hermes -z`: nobody can answer a prompt"*. `is_unattended()` decided whether a lost turn settles or pauses, but never read that flag. So a `-z` turn fell through to "a person's turn": it paused, and the session waited for a resend from someone who by construction is not there.

```python
 return ('local_automation_v1' in payload or 'kanban_card_v1' in payload
+        or payload.get('unattended') is True
         or 'automation' in native or 'webhook_delivery' in native)
```

Strictly `is True`, matching `admit_finite`'s own validation (`type(params['unattended']) is not bool` → `invalid_params`).

### 2. A human's own lost turn (commit `059d131a`)

`recover_session_inputs()` fences every `started` admission from a dead epoch `unknown`. That is correct — the turn cannot be trusted to have finished. But `settle_recovered_unattended` deliberately skips these rows (`is_unattended` is False), and an `unknown` head pauses the FIFO until a person types `/discard`. On a headless gateway nobody is at the boot to type it, so the chat stays paused indefinitely and every message queued behind it stalls.

Measured on a live gateway — four sessions fenced `unknown` by one restart, two of them stuck waiting:

```
Native session startup recovery 20261030_021616_090f99ce: unknown_execution
Native session startup recovery 20261029_210109_7c2f6bc1: unknown_execution
Session 20261030_021616_090f99ce paused: unknown_execution
Session 20261029_210109_7c2f6bc1 paused: unknown_execution
```

`settle_recovered_human` runs at boot immediately after `settle_recovered_unattended` and settles each non-automation `unknown` row with `FAILED_TURN_NOTICE` ("Your request was not processed. Send it again…") as its transcript boundary.

`oneshot` sessions are excluded: a `-z` session has no chat to resend into, so pausing it remains the honest outcome.

Net effect: a restart costs the turn, not the conversation.

## Related Issue

Refs #139532. The scope note that previously deferred item 2 is now delivered — with one deliberate change to its framing: the repair does **not** re-drive the session with `hermes chat --resume`. It settles `interrupted` and asks the person to resend, which is the same terminal state `/discard` produces, just without the indefinite wait. Nothing is replayed.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/session_unattended_unknown.py` — `is_unattended()` also treats `payload['unattended'] is True` as unattended; new `settle_recovered_human()` + `_resumable_unknown()` + `_session_platform()`.
- `gateway/session_authority.py` — call `settle_recovered_human` at boot, right after `settle_recovered_unattended`.
- `tests/gateway/test_unattended_unknown_settlement.py` — `-z` regression (6 tests).
- `tests/gateway/test_recovered_human_turn.py` — human-turn regression (12 tests).

## How was this tested?

Against a clean checkout of `main` (`19b7c7c2`) and with the patch, via a scratch venv with the project installed editable:

- **Unpatched — RED:** `tests/gateway/test_recovered_human_turn.py` → `12 failed`.
- **Patched — GREEN:** `18 passed` across `test_recovered_human_turn.py` + `test_unattended_unknown_settlement.py`.
- **`ruff check` on all three changed files:** `All checks passed!`

The tests pin both directions, so neither change can quietly widen the fence:

- a person's ordinary turn is now resumable; a cron/webhook/kanban/`-z` row is **not** (those belong to `settle_recovered_unattended`, never double-handled)
- `started` / `terminal` / `queued` rows are never touched
- `oneshot` sessions are skipped
- every interactive surface (`discord`, `telegram`, `cli`, `tui`, `api_server`) resumes
- an end-to-end boot pass on a real temp SQLite DB: the row resolves and `FAILED_TURN_NOTICE` is the committed boundary
- the pre-existing automation shapes still settle exactly as #141357 decided

**Known limitation of this run:** `tests/gateway/test_restart_interrupt_notice.py` reports `28 failed` **both with and without the patch** in this environment (identical counts), so it is a pre-existing/missing-runtime-dependency result, not a regression from this change. Ran in the repo's own CI venv, that lane is the real gate.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
- [x] The change is minimal and confined to one predicate plus one boot-time pass

prs.title: feat(agent): subturn poc
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

 This PR introduces the initial Proof of Concept (PoC) for hierarchical agent execution (Sub-turns). This is a foundational step to enable multi-agent steering and interruptability within the execution loop, as
      proposed in Issue #1316.

 By allowing agents to safely spawn, monitor, and cancel sub-agents (sub-turns) without polluting the main session history, we lay the groundwork for more complex, multi-layered reasoning and tool execution.

 ### Key Changes
 - **Core Lifecycle Management**: Added `spawnSubTurn` to manage nested turn executions safely, including a configurable depth limit (`maxSubTurnDepth`).
 - **Ephemeral Sessions**: Implemented `newEphemeralSession` to ensure sub-turns use isolated memory. This prevents the parent's session history from being polluted by intermediate child reasoning.
 - **Context & Interruptability**: Sub-turns now inherit a cancelable context (`context.WithCancel(ctx)`). If a parent turn finishes (`ts.Finish()`), all running children are automatically aborted, effectively
      preventing goroutine leaks.
 - **EventBus Integration (Mock)**: Introduced core events (`SubTurnSpawnEvent`, `SubTurnResultDeliveredEvent`, `SubTurnEndEvent`, `SubTurnOrphanResultEvent`) for full observability into the sub-turn lifecycle.
      Currently utilizing a `MockEventBus` for the PoC.
 - **Concurrency & Robustness**:
   - Added deferred panic recovery within sub-turns to guarantee the emission of `SubTurnEndEvent(Err)`.
   - Handled "Orphan Results": If a delayed child result arrives after the parent has already finished, it routes to `SubTurnOrphanResultEvent` to avoid state corruption or history pollution.

 ### Notes for Reviewers
 - This is currently a PoC and uses a mocked EventBus (`MockEventBus`) and fixed-size channels for pending results.
 - Further iterations will focus on integrating the real EventBus and handling dynamic channel capacities / backpressure for high concurrency scenarios.

prs.title: WIP: feat: base multi-agent collaboration framework & shared context
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

**WIP** — Base multi-agent collaboration framework with shared context pool, agent handoff, and discovery tools.

Builds on top of the merged PRs #213 (provider protocol refactor) and #131 (model fallback chain + multi-agent routing) to add:

- **Blackboard** — Thread-safe shared key-value context pool (`pkg/multiagent/blackboard.go`) for inter-agent data sharing with scoped entries (author, scope, timestamp)
- **BlackboardTool** — LLM-callable tool for read/write/list/delete on the shared context
- **Agent Handoff** — Synchronous delegation between agents via `ExecuteHandoff()` with automatic context propagation through the blackboard
- **HandoffTool** — LLM-callable tool that resolves target agent, writes context, builds system prompt, and delegates via `RunToolLoop`
- **ListAgentsTool** — Discovery tool listing all registered agents with ID/Name/Role
- **AgentResolver interface** — Decouples `pkg/multiagent` from `pkg/agent` to avoid circular imports
- **AgentLoop integration** — Blackboard snapshot injection into system messages, per-session blackboards via `sync.Map`, tools auto-registered when >1 agent configured
- **Config extensions** — `Role` and `SystemPrompt` fields on `AgentConfig` and `AgentInstance`

### Architecture decisions
- Zero overhead for single-agent setups (multi-agent tools only registered when `len(registry.ListAgentIDs()) > 1`)
- `registryResolver` adapter bridges `AgentRegistry` → `multiagent.AgentResolver` at the integration boundary
- Blackboard entries carry authorship metadata for audit/debugging

prs.title: feat(feishu): add tool progress feedback with verbose toggle
prs.body:
## Description

**Problem:** When the agent processes a message, users see no feedback until the final response arrives. For complex tasks involving multiple tool calls (web search, file operations, shell commands), this creates a "black box" experience — users don't know if the agent is working, stuck, or what it's doing.

**Solution:** Add real-time tool execution progress feedback for the Feishu channel with a configurable verbose toggle, so users can:
- See what the agent is doing at each step (e.g., "Searching golang tutorials", "Executing make build")
- Understand which tools are being called and with what arguments
- Watch progress accumulate in a single evolving card (EditMessage) instead of receiving multiple messages

**Changes:**
- **Config**: Add `FeaturesConfig` with `Verbose` flag (`features.verbose` in config, default `false`). When disabled, progress updates are silently discarded (old behavior). Users opt-in to verbose mode.
- **Bus**: Add `IsProgress` field to `OutboundMessage` to distinguish progress updates from final responses
- **BaseChannel**: Add `Bus()` accessor so channel implementations can access the `MessageBus`
- **Feishu channel**: Send "Thinking..." placeholder card on message receive; accumulate tool progress lines in a single evolving card via EditMessage; gate all progress on `features.verbose`
- **Agent loop**: Send human-readable progress updates during tool execution (`formatToolProgress` / `formatToolResult`)

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## AI Code Generation

- [x] Mostly AI-generated code with human review and testing

## Technical Context

The progress feedback uses the existing `OutboundMessage` mechanism with a new `IsProgress` bool flag so channels can distinguish progress updates from final responses. The Feishu channel maintains per-chat placeholder state (`sync.Map`) to track the evolving card. When `features.verbose` is false (default), the channel's `Send()` method returns nil immediately for progress messages, preserving the old silent behavior.

## Test Environment

- Radxa Cubie A7A (arm64), Debian 11
- Feishu channel (WebSocket mode)
- Tested with `verbose: true`: progress messages appear during tool calls as an evolving card
- Tested with `verbose: false` (default): old behavior, no progress messages

prs.title: fix: support custom model protocols (e.g., zai-org/GLM-4.7)
prs.body:
## Problem

When using custom models with unknown protocols (e.g., \`zai-org/GLM-4.7\`), the system returns an error:

\`\`\`
Error creating provider: failed to create provider for model "zai-org/GLM-4.7": unknown protocol "zai-org" in model "zai-org/GLM-4.7"
\`\`\`

## Root Cause

In \`pkg/providers/factory_provider.go\`, the \`ExtractProtocol()\` function splits the model string by the first \`/\` character. For \`"zai-org/GLM-4.7"\`, this results in:
- \`protocol="zai-org"\`
- \`modelID="GLM-4.7"\`

Since \`"zai-org"\` is not in the list of supported protocols, the system returns an error.

## Solution

Added a \`default\` case in \`CreateProviderFromConfig()\` that treats unknown protocols as OpenAI-compatible HTTP providers instead of returning an error:

\`\`\`go
default:
    // Treat unknown protocols as OpenAI-compatible
    logger.WarnF("unknown protocol, falling back to OpenAI-compatible HTTP provider",
        map[string]any{"protocol": protocol, "model": cfg.Model})
    if cfg.APIKey == "" && cfg.APIBase == "" {
        return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("api_key or api_base is required for HTTP-based protocol %q", protocol)
    }
    apiBase := cfg.APIBase
    if apiBase == "" {
        apiBase = getDefaultAPIBase("openai")
    }
    return NewHTTPProviderWithMaxTokensFieldAndRequestTimeout(
        cfg.APIKey, apiBase, cfg.Proxy, cfg.MaxTokensField, cfg.RequestTimeout,
    ), cfg.Model, nil
\`\`\`

Key points:
- Returns \`cfg.Model\` (full model name) instead of just \`modelID\`, so \`"zai-org/GLM-4.7"\` is sent to the API as-is
- Uses \`NewHTTPProviderWithMaxTokensFieldAndRequestTimeout\` — consistent with all other HTTP provider cases
- Logs a structured warning via \`WarnF\` so operators can see the fallback

## Configuration

\`\`\`json
{
  "model_name": "zai-org/GLM-4.7",
  "model": "zai-org/GLM-4.7",
  "api_base": "https://your-custom-api-endpoint.com/v1",
  "api_key": "..."
}
\`\`\`

## Testing

Added unit tests covering all three scenarios:

| Test | Scenario |
|------|----------|
| \`TestCreateProviderFromConfig_UnknownProtocol\` | Unknown protocol + \`api_key\` → fallback succeeds, returns full \`cfg.Model\` as model ID |
| \`TestCreateProviderFromConfig_UnknownProtocolWithAPIBase\` | Unknown protocol + \`api_base\` only (no key) → fallback succeeds (unauthenticated local endpoint) |
| \`TestCreateProviderFromConfig_UnknownProtocolNoAuth\` | Unknown protocol + no credentials → returns error |

## Backward Compatibility

- All existing protocol configurations continue to work unchanged
- Unknown protocols now fall back gracefully instead of hard-erroring

Fixes #661

prs.title: fix(telegram): give the getUpdates long poll a client-side deadline
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->
## Summary

Telegram inbound no longer stalls for ~15 minutes after a network change.

- **Problem**: `@chat-adapter/telegram` long-polls `getUpdates` with no client-side timeout. On a black-holed connection (no RST, e.g. after a Wi-Fi/NAT change) the request hangs until the kernel gives up on retransmits. No inbound message arrives meanwhile, while outbound keeps working on fresh sockets.
- **Fix**: `installPollDeadline` wraps the adapter instance's `telegramFetch`: `getUpdates` is aborted after its long-poll `timeout` + 30 s and fails with a plain error, so the poll loop backs off and retries. Every other Bot API method is untouched.
- **Scope guard**: an abort the adapter itself requests (polling stopped) still surfaces as `AbortError`. If a future adapter drops `telegramFetch`, the bridge logs a warning and polls as before.

## Related work

No issue; seen on a live install on 2026-10-03 (inbound dead for ~20 min, `ss` showed the getUpdates socket stuck with unacked data). Carried as a local patch since.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- New `src/channels/telegram-poll-deadline.test.ts`: a hung poll becomes a retryable error after 60 s (fake timers); an outer abort still stops cleanly; other methods pass through; installs on a real adapter instance -> 5 passed

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->
## Summary

Agent reactions (and edits of inbound messages) reach the platform with the platform's message id, not the session row id.

- **Problem**: the router stores inbound rows as `<platform msg id>:<agent group id>` (`messageIdForAgent`). `add_reaction` hands that row id back as the target, so Telegram gets `<chat>:<msg>:ag-…`, answers `message to react not found`, and the reaction is dropped after 3 retries. The tool already reported success to the agent.
- **Fix**: `deliverMessage` strips a trailing `:<session agent group id>` from `messageId` of any `operation` payload before handing it to the adapter. Plain chat messages pass through byte-identical.
- **Why host-side**: the host knows the session's agent group exactly, so no `:ag-` pattern guessing, and no container image rebuild.
- **Out of scope**: emoji-name normalization (#3553) and best-effort reactions (#3121).

Closes #2042

prs.title: fix(delivery): tell the agent when a message permanently fails to deliver
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->
## Summary

The agent is told when one of its messages permanently fails to deliver, instead of believing it was sent.

- **Problem**: after `MAX_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS` the delivery loop only marks the outbound row failed in the session DB. Nothing reaches the agent, so it reports the message as sent ("sent — check the DM") while the user never sees it. Seen with a file Slack rejected with `missing_scope`.
- **Fix**: `noticeDeliveryFailure` sends a system note through `notifyAgent` (id `delivery-failed-<msg id>`; names the files/text, a fixed reason category and the message id for the host log) and wakes the container. Called once, right after `markDeliveryFailed`. The note tells the agent not to resend to that destination.
- **Reason categories**: not connected (unknown/detached messaging group, no adapter, no a2a module), rejected by the platform, not authorised, other. Host-side causes throw `DeliveryTargetError`; `MissingChannelAdapterError` maps to not connected.
- **Bounds**: no note when the failed message answers a delivery-failure note (`in_reply_to` starts with `delivery-failed-`); at most 3 notes per session and destination within 10 minutes (in memory, resets on restart), the rest are logged as suppressed.
- **Scope guard**: `system` and `task_log` rows get no note; a failure to write the note is logged and never breaks the delivery loop.

## Related work

No issue; carried as a local patch on a live install since 2026-10-01.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `src/delivery-failure-notice.test.ts`: text names files, text, reason category and log pointer; truncation; error classification; system/task_log rows and replies to a note are skipped -> pass
- `src/delivery.test.ts`: permanent failure writes the note without the remote error text; new test drives repeated failures on one destination (a reply to the note gets none, then notes stop at the cap) -> pass. Both bounds mutation-checked (removing either makes the test fail).
- Full host suite: 2157 passed; 3 failures in `src/cli/stdin-json*` fail identically on current `main` (Node 26 environment)
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` -> clean
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
When a message can't be delivered after all retries, the agent now gets a note saying so and the reason category, instead of assuming it was sent.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- The note is written as `sender: 'system'` into the same session's own inbound mailbox only.
- Remote platform error text never enters the note (it could carry attacker-influenced text into a system-voice message); only a fixed category and the outbound message id. The full error stays in the host log.
- Notes can't amplify: replies to a note get none, and each destination is capped at 3 notes per 10 minutes per session, so a permanently failing destination can't drive an unbounded wake loop.

prs.title: feat: add /add-agentmail-calendar-tool skill (calendar CLI for AgentMail inboxes)
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-agentmail-calendar-tool`, which gives agents the calendar of their AgentMail inbox: agenda, event writes, answers to emailed invitations, and start-time alerts. Anyone outside the owner and known contacts gets an invitation only with the owner's recorded OK.

- **CLI**: `cal`, a dependency-free Bun script shipped as the `agentmail-calendar` container skill. It has no new packages and needs no image rebuild.
- **Commands**: `agenda`, `list` (window or `--stored`), `get`, `create`/`update`/`delete` (all-day, `--rrule` recurrence, `--mode single|future` for one date of a series), `respond accepted|declined|tentative`, `check`.
- **Send guard (enforced)**: `--send-invites` and `respond` email people. They go out freely only to the owner's addresses and `known` contacts. Anyone else needs `--approved-by-owner "<their words, where/when>"`, or the CLI refuses before any API call. Owner lookalike addresses are always refused. This is the same rule as `mail`.
- **Ledger**: every write goes to `groups/<folder>/calendar/ledger.jsonl` (recipients, approval text, result, ids), so a timed-out write can be checked before a retry.
- **Concurrency**: `update`, `delete` and `respond` send the event's etag in `If-Match`. A `412` reports that nothing changed.
- **Alerts without a public URL**: `cal due` is a task gate (`ncl tasks create --script`). It wakes the agent for events starting within N minutes and for new emailed invitations, dedupes, treats the first run as a baseline, and always prints JSON and exits 0.
- **Timezone**: wall-clock input and output use the calendar's own timezone (`GET /calendar`), with a `--tz` override.
- **Config/credential**: none new. It reads `/add-agentmail-tool`'s per-group `email/config.json` (inbox, owner, known, lookalike) and uses the same gateway credential for `api.agentmail.to`.
- **Out of scope**: AgentMail calendar webhooks (they need a public endpoint) and sharing or subscribing to calendars.

## Related work

Builds on #4075 (`/add-agentmail-tool`) and needs it applied first. It is a separate skill so that installs without a calendar don't carry it. No issue. #2530 (`/add-caldav-tool`) covers CalDAV servers and doesn't overlap: AgentMail calendars use their own REST API. This is a new opt-in skill with no core changes, so it's safe to review directly.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `bun test` in `container-skills/agentmail-calendar/` (Bun 1.4.4, the image's pinned version) -> 13 pass, offline fake API. Covers the guard (owner/known pass, outsider refused, approval accepted, lookalike refused even with approval), no API call on refusal for create/delete/respond, `--no-reply`, `If-Match`, ledger entries, the `due` baseline/dedupe/new-invite path, `due` JSON on API failure and missing config, and DST-correct wall-clock conversion and formatting.
- `tsc --noEmit --strict` with `types: ["bun"]` on `cal.ts` + test -> clean.
- Live against a real AgentMail inbox: `check`, `agenda`, `list`, `list --stored` and `due` -> ok. `create --send-invites` to an outside address with no approval -> exit 2, nothing sent. A lookalike address with approval -> refused. One create, get, update, delete cycle on a no-attendee event -> 201/200/202, three ledger lines, and `due` reported the event once and then deduped it. The event was gone afterwards (404).
- Not yet covered: applying the skill on a fresh clone in a freshly built agent container.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

The skill has no in-tree integration point. The container skill is found by the directory scan of `container/skills/`, its config is `/add-agentmail-tool`'s per-group state, and the credential lives in the gateway. SKILL.md says so explicitly, per `docs/skill-guidelines.md`.

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New /add-agentmail-calendar-tool skill: agents get a `cal` CLI for their AgentMail inbox's calendar (agenda, events, invitation replies, start-time alerts), with the same owner-approval rule as `mail` before emailing outsiders.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- **Credentials**: gateway only. The container sends `Bearer gateway-managed`, and the skill adds no new secret.
- **Outbound email**: invitations, cancellations and organizer replies are refused for anyone outside owner and `known` addresses unless a recorded owner approval is passed. The check runs before any API call, and every write is logged with its recipients and approval text.
- **Untrusted input**: events from emailed invitations (`source: email`) are labelled as invites. The container skill tells the agent to treat their organizer, title and description as data and not to answer without the owner's OK.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

Footprint: copies `container/skills/agentmail-calendar/` (4 files). Per chosen group, it adds one `## Calendar` line to `instructions.prepend.md`. At runtime `cal` creates `groups/<folder>/calendar/` (ledger and gate state). `REMOVE.md` reverses each step, asks before deleting the ledger, and leaves `/add-agentmail-tool`'s config and credential alone.

prs.title: test(skills): cover main and companion skills
prs.body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

Close the CI gap where a base skill could pass alone while its real companion sequence was broken. The composition matrix grows from 21 to 31 jobs and now covers every currently deterministic project-mutating `add-*` installer plus every declared companion composition.

These are ten additional composition jobs, not ten previously untested skills. Existing focused unit and conformance tests remain in place.

## Runtime companion registry

Move companion declarations and branch-backed materialization from the channel-specific registry into `setup/skill-compositions.ts`. Production setup and CI now read the same ordered declaration:

`add-slack → slack-a2a-rooms → slack-agent-flow`

The Slack install order, degraded-mode warning, and single deferred-restart behavior are unchanged. The channel setup files now delegate companion lookup and materialization to the generic registry.

## Changed files

- `setup/skill-compositions.ts` and `.test.ts` — generic ordered companion registry and materializer.
- `setup/channels/companions.ts` — retain channel pre-steps; remove the duplicate companion registry.
- `setup/channels/run-channel-skill.ts` — consume the generic registry while preserving existing restart and failure behavior.
- `setup/channels/slack-auto-register.ts` and `.test.ts` — keep Slack auto-provision registration and verify the Slack chain in the generic registry.
- `setup/channels/wizard-hooks.test.ts` — exercise companion order, degradation, and deferred restart through the new registry.
- `scripts/test-registry-skills.ts` — discover local deterministic installers and companion chains, materialize each step, run declared build/tests, and compare project state after a second apply.
- `scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts` — validate all checked-in and nested skill directories and require every declared companion chain to appear in the E2E matrix.
- `scripts/skill-apply.ts` — export the existing remote resolver for reuse by the generic materializer.
- `src/templates/skills.ts` — expose content-based validation so branch-loaded `SKILL.md` files use the existing validator.
- `.github/workflows/registry-skills.yml` — run checked-in conformance and active branch-document validation before the composition matrix.

## Slack regression protection

Slack is protected at four levels:

1. A focused test fixes the exact ordered chain in the generic registry.
2. A discovery test fails if a declared companion chain is missing from the E2E matrix.
3. Wizard tests verify ordered application, degraded behavior, and the final restart boundary.
4. CI applies `add-slack → slack-a2a-rooms → slack-agent-flow` to a disposable clone, builds and tests the composed result, reapplies it, and fails if the second apply changes the project.

Instruction-only, container, and platform/external-only skills receive anatomy and conformance validation rather than installation execution.

## Verification

- Focused companion, Slack registration, wizard, and conformance suites: 317 tests passed.
- GitHub-hosted standalone Slack and full Slack companion composition jobs passed.
- Full local `act` workflow: 31/31 compositions passed. Local `act` uses #3675 for path compatibility; GitHub-hosted CI passes against the current `channels` branch.

prs.title: fix(runner): skip wrap-nudge when the turn already sent via tools
prs.body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

`#3284` already skips the wrap-nudge when a *streaming* provider delivered mid-turn (including MCP `send_message`). Result-door providers never passed `turnDelivered`, so a welcome/`send_message` turn that finished with an unwrapped self-summary still got "your response was not delivered" — the model re-sent, and the user saw a duplicate greeting.

Always consult `turnDelivered` (chat **and** chat-sdk rows since the turn boundary) so `ask_user_question` cards count too. Bare unwrapped results with no prior send still nudge.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd container/agent-runner && bun test src/poll-loop.test.ts`
- [ ] Result-door agent: `/welcome` via `send_message` / `ask_user_question`, then an unwrapped summary — only the tool-sent messages go out
- [ ] Bare unwrapped reply with no prior send still gets the wrap-nudge

## 问题现象
两个 LobsterAI（有道龙虾）账号近期无法登录/使用，系统提示账号已被封禁或异常。
本人声明：**两个账号均未进行过恶意使用、未刷接口、未批量调用**，封禁认定疑似误判。

## 补充说明（可能的误判来源）
我曾在本地第三方 DSH 插件（dsh-comprehensive-platform / our-free-model）中配置过 LobsterAI 账号凭据，用于调用有道模型服务。
该插件存在自动化流量：
1. 每日自动签到（每天 1 次，模拟正常 App 行为）；
2. 之前版本的模型目录自动刷新间隔为 5 分钟，会带真实账号凭据轮询 `GET /api/models/available`，每渠道每天产生约 288 次带凭据请求。

我已意识到这可能被上游风控系统判定为“异常活动（unusual activity）”，导致账号被封。**现已从本地彻底移除相关 LobsterAI 凭据，且修复了刷新间隔（已改为默认 6 小时 + 抖动 + 无已登录账号时零请求），不会再产生自动化流量。**

## 诉求
1. 查明封禁原因，并告知两个账号的封禁时长；
2. 若确认为误判，请解除封禁，恢复正常使用；
3. 若无法解封，请提供可申诉的客服联系方式或申诉入口。

## 时间线
- 发现封禁：约 2026-10-23 起
- 已移除本地凭据：2026-10-24
- GitHub 申诉提交：2026-10-24

---

感谢配合。

issues.title: [Bug] Auto-Dream silently drops memory: unusable extract receipt still gets checkpointed, files never retried
issues.body:
## Description

Auto-Dream silently discards a whole day of memory when the extract step cannot parse the agent's reply, and then **checkpoints those files anyway** — so they are never retried. The run still reports `success=True`, and nothing user-visible indicates that the content was dropped.

The affected content never reaches `digest/`, so downstream `memory_search` keeps returning stale older knowledge, and the agent behaves as if the newer facts never existed.

## Environment

- QwenPaw: v2.2.2 (Docker on NAS)
- Memory backend: `remelight` (default)
- Config: `dream_cron_enabled: true`, `dream_cron: "0 23 * * *"`, `auto_memory_interval: 5`
- OS: Linux 5.19.17

## Reproduction / evidence

Real run on 2026-10-28 at 23:00 and 23:05, from the agent log:

```
[DreamExtractStep] agent done has_result=True
[DreamExtractStep] extract attempt 1 returned an unusable receipt; retrying once
[DreamExtractStep] dream extract skipped unusable agent receipt after retry; expected units and topics lists
[DreamExtractStep] parse done keys=(none)
[DreamExtractStep] Extracted 0 unit(s), 0 topic(s) from 9 changed file(s) across 2 day(s)
[DreamIntegrateStep] skip no units
[DreamFinishStep] start changed=9 failed_paths=0 checkpoint=9 ...
[DreamFinishStep] finish success=True checkpointed=9 failed_units=0 errors=0
```

Note `changed=9` but `Extracted 0 unit(s)` yet `checkpoint=9` and `success=True`.

## Root cause

Three pieces combine into a permanent, silent data loss:

1. **Extract failure does not mark files as failed.**
   In `reme/steps/evolve/dream/extract.py` (~L148-160), when the agent reply cannot be parsed into `units` + `topics` lists, after one retry the code deliberately takes a warning-only path instead of raising:

   ```python
   # Keep the warning-only result checkpointable after one retry so a bad source cannot loop forever.
   warning = "dream extract skipped unusable agent receipt after retry; expected units and topics lists"
   state.warnings.append(warning)
   ```

   The anti-infinite-loop intent is reasonable, but `state.failed_paths` is **never populated** on this path.

2. **Finish checkpoints everything not in `failed_paths`.**
   In `reme/steps/evolve/dream/finish.py`:

   ```python
   failed_paths = set(state.failed_paths)
   checkpoint = [p for p in state.changed_paths if p not in failed_paths]
   ```

   Since `failed_paths` is empty, `checkpoint` == all 9 changed files, and their current mtimes are written into the file catalog.

3. **"Changed" is computed by mtime comparison against the catalog.**
   In `extract.py`:

   ```python
   changed = [rel for rel, mt in existing.items() if indexed.get(rel) != mt]
   ```

   Because those 9 files were just cataloged with their current mtimes, every subsequent Dream run sees them as **unchanged** and skips them forever. The content is never retried unless the file itself is modified again.

**Net effect: one unusable model reply permanently drops a day of memory, silently, with `success=True`.**

## Impact

- Whole day of memory never enters `digest/` (in my case: a music-library consolidation and tag-rewrite session).
- `memory_search` continues to return the **older, now-incorrect** digest nodes, so the agent confidently answers with stale facts (observed: it reported a stale path convention and stale playback constraints).
- Not self-healing: this is not a transient failure that the next scheduled run fixes.
- No visibility: the only trace is a `WARNING` line in the log; `response.success` is `True`, and the Inbox push treats it as a successful no-op.

## Suggested fix

1. On the warning-only (unusable receipt) path, also do `state.failed_paths = list(state.changed_paths)` so `DreamFinishStep` does **not** checkpoint them, allowing the next run to retry. A small retry counter / backoff is fine to avoid infinite loops on genuinely unparsable input.
2. Alternatively/additionally: when `len(changed) > 0` and `len(state.units) == 0`, do not report a plain success. Set `success=False` or emit an explicit Inbox warning such as "dream skipped N files: unusable receipt".
3. Consider logging the parse failure with the reply prefix (truncated) so the failure mode (e.g. model returned prose instead of a JSON receipt) is diagnosable.

## Additional context

Same "false success" family as #8184 (cron records false success after gate termination) and related to #6116 (doom loop / missing budget gates), but the root cause here is distinct: **parse failure → warning-only path → full checkpoint → permanent skip**.

Happy to test a patch in my deployment (v2.2.2, 29 cron jobs, daily Dream runs) and report back.

issues.title: [Bug] 桌面端 HTML 预览「在浏览器中打开」失效：中文路径弹「找不到文件」，工作区外文件点击无反应
issues.body:
## 环境

- QwenPaw Desktop **v2.3.0b1**（Windows 11 x64，系统区域中文，默认浏览器 Edge）
- 后端：`qwenpaw.exe --version` → `QwenPaw, version 2.3.0b1`
- 工作区路径包含中文目录（下文记作 `<workspace>`）
- 场景：Agent 生成一个依赖 JS 渲染的单文件 HTML（日报仪表盘），在右侧文件预览面板点「在浏览器中打开」

## 复现步骤 A（文件在工作区内，路径含中文）

1. 在工作区 `<workspace>\digest\us\report.html` 生成任意 HTML
2. 在预览面板点击「在浏览器中打开」

**实际结果**：弹出 Windows 对话框

```
file:///E:/%E5%B7%A5%E4%BD%9C%E5%8C%BA/digest/us/report.html
Windows 找不到文件
```

（URL 里的中文目录被 UTF-8 百分号编码）

**期望结果**：默认浏览器打开该文件。

## 复现步骤 B（文件在纯 ASCII 路径下）

1. 把同一个文件复制到 `<ascii-dir>\report.html`（全 ASCII，无空格）
2. 在预览面板点击「在浏览器中打开」

**实际结果**：**无任何反应**——不弹错误框、不新开窗口、不出新标签页，前台窗口仍是 QwenPaw，浏览器窗口标题未变。

**期望结果**：默认浏览器打开该文件。

## 系统层对照实验（排除文件损坏与关联问题）

在同一台机器上用 `ShellExecuteW`（shell32）分别打开三种形式：

| 传入形式 | 返回值 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|
| 原生路径 `<ascii-dir>\report.html` | 42 | **成功打开** |
| `file:///E:/<ascii-dir>/report.html`（纯 ASCII URL） | 42 | **成功打开** |
| `file:///E:/%E5%B7%A5%E4%BD%9C%E5%8C%BA/.../report.html`（UTF-8 百分号编码） | 2 | 失败（`ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`） |

即：**文件本身可打开、系统关联正常、ASCII 的 `file:///` URL 也能打开**，问题出在应用传入的形式上。

## 分析（供参考）

1. **中文路径失败的机制**：Windows 对 `file:///` URL 的百分号解码使用当前 ANSI 代码页（中文系统为 GBK/936），而应用传的是 UTF-8 编码。`%E5%B7%A5%E4%BD%9C%E5%8C%BA` 被按 GBK 解码成乱码，路径不存在 → `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`。
   **建议**：调用 `ShellExecute` 时 `lpFile` 直接传**本地路径**（不要先转成 `file:///` URL 再百分号编码），或对含非 ASCII 字符的路径走 `os.startfile(path)` / `explorer.exe` 原生路径分支。

2. **工作区外文件点击无反应**：疑似 handler 以 `root`（工作区目录）为基准解析 `filePath`，文件在工作区外时解析失败并**静默 return**。
   **建议**：解析失败时至少给出 toast/错误提示；或对绝对路径直接放行。

3. **预览面板的认知成本**：预览不执行 JS，含动态内容的页面只显示模板骨架（本用例里显示的是模板默认标题与空容器），用户容易误判为「文件坏了」。建议动态内容场景下把「在浏览器中打开」做成明确可用的主操作，或提供「以独立窗口打开」。

4. **附带问题（可选）**：该窗口通过 UI Automation 枚举到 **0 个按钮/控件**（疑似 Qt WebEngine 未挂 UIA 桥），导致自动化测试与读屏软件都无法操作该界面。

## 影响

- 任何工作区路径含中文的 Windows 用户（国内用户大概率如此）都无法使用「在浏览器中打开」
- 生成的报告/看板类 HTML（依赖 JS 渲染）在应用内完全无法查看，只能由用户自己去资源管理器双击

*附：问题为使用过程中实测；系统层对照实验在同一台机器上可复现。*

issues.title: [Bug]: 手动 /compact 无视会话级模型切换，始终使用 agent.json 的 active_model 生成压缩摘要

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2.post1

## Description

### 现象

在会话 UI 中把模型从 M1 切换为 M2 后，点击手动压缩 `/compact`，压缩摘要请求**仍然发给 M1**（agent 级默认模型），而不是当前会话正在使用的 M2。当 M1 对压缩请求携带的参数严格校验并返回 400 时，无论切换到什么模型，手动压缩都会失败。

### 实际复现案例

- 会话上下文约 34 万 token（模型配置 max_input_length=1M，未达自动压缩阈值）。
- agent 级默认模型为 `glm-5.3-flash`（provider: 火山方舟），该端点对摘要请求中的 `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` 返回 400 `InvalidParameter`（摘要路径由 `agents/context/scroll/manager.py` 的 `_generate_plain_summary` 显式传 `disable_thinking=True`——scroll 策略路径，默认策略；`providers/openai_chat_model_compat.py` 的 `_consume_disable_thinking()` 将其翻译为 `enable_thinking: false` + `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` 双发，该端点拒收后者）。
- 在 UI 中将本会话模型切换为 `deepseek-v4.1-flash`（同 provider，实测接受 `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`、无 `generate_kwargs.max_tokens` 冲突），点击 `/compact` → 压缩仍然失败，日志报错依旧是 glm 的 `thinking.type 'disabled' is not supported by this model`。
- 尝试切换多个其他模型（不同 provider 的 deepseek 系列）结果相同：全部失败，报错始终来自默认模型。
- **验证**：将 agent 级默认模型（agent.json `active_model`）改为 `deepseek-v4.1-flash` 后，手动 `/compact` 立即成功——确认 /compact 的摘要模型来自 agent 级默认，而非会话当前模型。

### 期望行为

手动 `/compact` 的摘要生成应继承**会话当前生效的模型**（`chats.json` 中 `meta.runtime_context.model`，即用户在 UI 中切换后的模型），与普通消息的行为一致。

### 实际行为

手动 `/compact` 的摘要生成固定使用 **agent 级持久默认模型**（`agent.json` 的 `active_model`），完全无视会话级模型切换。会话内切换模型、或切换后先发普通消息，均不影响手动压缩使用的模型。

### 根因分析（源码链路）

1. **slash command 在 agent build 之前被拦截**：`runtime/runtime.py` 的 8-phase 生命周期中，`[fixed 1] slash command dispatch` 位于 `[fixed 2] build agent` 之前；`/compact` 命中 dispatch 后 `skip_agent = True`，普通消息链路的 `runtime/builder.py` `builder.build(ctx)`（其中 `apply_session_thinking()` 会把会话级模型改写进 `agent_config`，见根因 5）根本不会执行。且 `/compact` 是无条件注册的会话命令（`runtime/builtin_commands.py` `_CONVERSATION_COMMANDS`），禁用压缩时也只是返回提示，不会退化成普通消息。

2. **standalone CommandHandler 不携带 agent**：`runtime/builtin_commands.py` `_make_conversation_adapter()` 构造 `CommandHandler(agent_name=..., state=state, ...)` 时**不传 `agent=`**（"Loads AgentState directly from session — no agent instance required"）。

3. **临时 agent 的模型只来自 agent 配置**：`agents/command_handler.py` `_process_compact()` 中 `self._agent is None` → `agent = await self._build_tmp_agent(agent_config)`；`_build_tmp_agent()` 调用 `create_model_and_formatter_async(agent_id=..., agent_config=...)`，**不传 `model_slot_override`，也没有任何参数入口携带会话级模型**。

4. **model_factory 只认 agent_config.active_model**：`agents/model_factory.py` 中 `settings.model_slot = agent_config.active_model`；`_resolve_model_slot_override(None)` 返回 None。已核查 `_build_tmp_agent → create_model_and_formatter_async → create_model_and_formatter → _load_agent_model_settings` 全链：不存在读取 `chat.meta` / `runtime_context.model` / `ctx.request.model_slot_override` 的分支。

5. **对照：会话级切换如何作用于普通消息、/compact 又如何绕开**：UI 切换模型只写 `chats.json` 的 `meta["runtime_context"]["model"]`（`app/chats/manager.py` `set_session_model()`，docstring "Persist a model override without changing agent defaults"）。普通消息之所以跟随切换，**主通道**是 `runtime/builder.py` `build()` 内的 `apply_session_thinking(ctx, agent_config)`：`services/session_thinking.py` 的 `session_model()` 从 `chat.meta.runtime_context.model` 读出会话模型并**直接改写 `agent_config.active_model`**，随后才构建模型。`ctx.request.model_slot_override`（`runtime/builder.py` 在 `build_model` 前读取）是前端显式传参的**次要通道**。而手动 /compact 的 `_build_tmp_agent()` 使用 `load_agent_config()` 的原始 agent 配置（`agents/command_handler.py`），**上述两条通道全部绕开**——会话级模型切换对手动压缩完全不生效。

6. **补充对照（自动压缩不受影响）**：auto-compact（`agents/middlewares.py` `on_compress_context`）运行在 agent 正常执行内，使用的是经过 `apply_session_thinking` 改写后构建的 agent 模型，**会跟随会话级模型切换**。即：只有手动 `/compact`（standalone 路径）存在此问题。

### 影响

- UI 的会话模型切换对手动压缩形同虚设，用户切换到压缩可用模型后依然压缩失败，且从 UI 无法察觉实际执行的是另一个模型（日志报错归属端点与 UI 显示的当前模型不一致，排障成本高）。
- 数据流向与用户预期不符：用户以为摘要是用模型 M2 生成，实际全量上下文被发给了模型 M1 的 provider。若两者分属不同服务商，属于轻微的数据流向偏差（见 Security considerations）。
- 当默认模型对压缩请求参数严格校验时（如本例 `thinking` 参数 400），手动压缩在默认模型不更换的前提下永远失败。

### 复现步骤

1. agent 级默认模型设为 M1（本例：火山方舟 `glm-5.3-flash`，该端点拒收摘要请求中的 `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`）。
2. 创建会话并积累较长上下文（本例约 34 万 token）。
3. 在 UI 中将会话模型切换为 M2（本例：同 provider 的 `deepseek-v4.1-flash`，实测可作为压缩摘要模型正常工作）。
4. 发送 `/compact`。
5. **实际**：压缩失败，服务端日志的 400 报错来自 M1（`thinking.type 'disabled' is not supported by this model`，Request id 为 M1 所属 provider 的格式）。本例切换后未再发普通消息，故日志期内所有 `builder: built agent ... model=` 记录均为 M1；即便切换后先发普通消息（普通对话会用 M2、日志也会出现 M2 的构建记录），手动 `/compact` 依然使用 M1——见根因 5 的双通道绕开。
6. **验证锚点**：把 agent.json `active_model` 改为 M2（改文件即生效，`load_agent_config` 为指纹缓存）后再次 `/compact`，压缩成功。

### 修复建议

`_build_tmp_agent()` 应继承会话级模型覆盖。两个可行方向：

- (a) **复用现有机制**：对 `_build_tmp_agent` 拿到的 `agent_config` 执行与 `build()` 相同的 `apply_session_thinking(ctx, agent_config)`（按 `ctx.session_id` 经 `ChatManager` 读取 chat 的 `meta.runtime_context.model` 后改写 `active_model`，`services/session_thinking.py` 已有现成函数可复用）；
- (b) 读取会话模型后作为 `model_slot_override` 传给 `create_model_and_formatter_async()`（该参数已存在）。

两法均可使手动 /compact 与普通消息、auto-compact 三条路径的模型选择语义一致。

**Related PR(s):** 无

**Security considerations:** 摘要请求携带会话全量上下文；在默认模型与切换后模型分属不同 provider 时，全量上下文实际被发送给了用户未选择的 provider（UI 无任何提示）。建议修复时一并考虑在文档/UI 中说明手动压缩所使用的模型，或修复后由会话模型承接。

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI

issues.title: [Bug] 2.3.0-beta.1: all backend plugins fail to load at startup — unguarded `importlib.invalidate_caches()` in `module_isolation.py:220` (same root cause as #8265, new call site)
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0-beta.1 (PyPI `qwenpaw==2.3.0b1`; also present on `main`)

## Description

In 2.3.0-beta.1, **every plugin that declares a backend entry point fails to load at server startup** — 12 out of 12 on this host — with the same error, thrown before any plugin code runs:

```
TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'
```

This is the same class of failure as #8265, but it is **not** the install/hot-update path that #8265 describes. It happens on the plain **startup load** path, and it was introduced by a call site that did not exist in 2.2.2:

```
loader.py:1210  _load_plugin_unlocked()
loader.py:760   _load_backend_module()
module_isolation.py:220  PluginNamespaceFinder.register()
                         → importlib.invalidate_caches()      # unguarded, new in 2.3.0
```

`src/qwenpaw/plugins/module_isolation.py#L220` calls `importlib.invalidate_caches()` unconditionally inside `PluginNamespaceFinder.register()`. Since `register()` runs once per backend plugin during startup, one raising stdlib call takes out the entire plugin system instead of one operation.

The two open PRs for the older report (**#8345**, **#8107**) both patch `src/qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py` only. They will not fix this: after either merges, 2.3.0-beta.1 still dies at `module_isolation.py:220` on the affected environments. `module_isolation.py:154` (bytecode purge helper) has the same unguarded call.

### Why the stdlib call raises

Since CPython 3.11.9, the interpreter's frozen `PathFinder.invalidate_caches()` ends with:

```python
from importlib.metadata import MetadataPathFinder
MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches()
```

`MetadataPathFinder` is resolved through `sys.path`. When an older distro stdlib sits ahead of the bundled one, that name resolves to a version where `invalidate_caches` is a **plain function without `@classmethod`**, so the call raises. Debian 12 ships such a version (3.11.2). Verified against CPython tags:

| CPython tag | `PathFinder.invalidate_caches()` calls `MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches()` | `importlib/metadata` defines it with `@classmethod` |
|---|---|---|
| v3.11.2 | no | **no** |
| v3.11.8 | no | **no** |
| v3.11.9 | **yes** | **yes** |
| v3.11.17 | yes | yes |
| v3.12.0 | no | **no** |
| v3.12.8 | yes | **yes** |

A consistent install is fine; a **mixed** one (new frozen loader + old `importlib.metadata` on `sys.path`) is not. That is exactly what a container with `PYTHONPATH` containing the distro stdlib produces:

```
PYTHONPATH=/app/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages:/usr/lib/python3.11:/app/user-packages/python
```

and the traceback shows both stdlibs in one stack: `/usr/lib/python3.11/importlib/__init__.py` (3.11.2) under `<frozen importlib._bootstrap_external>` (3.11.17).

Hence a `sys.version_info` guard would not help — the interpreter is new, only the shadowed module is old. Guarding the call is the portable fix.

Cache invalidation is a best-effort hint; a failure must not be fatal.

**Related PR(s):** #8345, #8107 (same root cause, `loader.py` only — do not cover this site)

**Security considerations:** None

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0b1 (upgraded from 2.2.2.post1, which loaded all plugins fine on the same host)
- **OS:** Linux x86_64, kernel 5.10.134-18.0.12.lifsea8, glibc 2.36
- **Install method:** pip (venv at `/app/venv`)
- **Python version:** 3.11.17 (bundled) — but `importlib.metadata` is loaded from the distro's 3.11.2 stdlib because of the `PYTHONPATH` above
- **Plugins:** 13 installed; 12 with `entry.backend`, 1 frontend-only

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On an affected environment, confirm the stdlib behaviour:

   ```bash
   $ /app/venv/bin/python -c "import importlib; importlib.invalidate_caches()"
   TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'
   ```

2. Install 2.3.0-beta.1 and start the app with at least one plugin that has an `entry.backend` (e.g. `qwenpaw-hub`, `qwenpaw-creator`).
3. Every backend plugin fails at startup with the error above; `GET /api/plugins` reports `active=1, failed=12`.

Pure QwenPaw-level reproduction, no plugin install needed:

```python
from qwenpaw.plugins.module_isolation import get_namespace_finder
get_namespace_finder().register("plugin_x", {})
# TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'
```

A single local fix (`@classmethod` added to the shadowed copy) makes all 13 plugins load again — confirming this call is the only blocker.

## Actual vs Expected

**Actual:** all backend plugins are marked `failed`; the exception is produced by QwenPaw's own namespace-isolation bookkeeping, not by plugin code. The only surviving plugin (`qwenpaw-mobile-optimizer-v2`) is the one with no `entry.backend`, which takes the frontend-only branch and never reaches `register()`.

**Expected:** the plugin loads. A failed cache refresh should degrade to a debug/warning log; the namespace is registered regardless.

### Blast radius observed (why this is more than a cosmetic plugin list)

| Failed plugin | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `egress-connect-http11` | Python HTTP egress broke: `urllib` → `Tunnel connection failed: 426 Upgrade Required`; the QQ channel could not fetch a token and retried 51 times; plugin-catalog fetch failed every 20 s |
| `qwenpaw-creator` | Its backend routes never registered → `GET /api/qwenpaw-creator/version` returned **404** (200 before the upgrade) |
| `tg-send-resilience` / `tg-intermediate-cleanup` | Their hooks were never installed → retry/cleanup protection silently absent |

## Logs / Screenshots

```
2026-10-28 10:02:48 | INFO  | plugins/loader.py:429 | Discovered plugin: qwenpaw-hub
2026-10-28 10:02:49 | ERROR | plugins/loader.py:1225 | Failed to load plugin 'qwenpaw-hub': MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py", line 1210, in _load_plugin_unlocked
    plugin_def = await self._load_backend_module(
  File "/app/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py", line 760, in _load_backend_module
    get_namespace_finder().register(module_name, plugin_builtins)
  File "/app/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/qwenpaw/plugins/module_isolation.py", line 220, in register
    importlib.invalidate_caches()
  File "/usr/lib/python3.11/importlib/__init__.py", line 70, in invalidate_caches
    finder.invalidate_caches()
  File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap_external>", line 1409, in invalidate_caches
TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'
```

The same 12-line block repeats for `aliyun-hub`, `clawhub-hub`, `modelscope-hub`, `qwenpaw-hub`, `qwenpaw-creator`, `egress-connect-http11`, `tg-send-resilience`, `tg-intermediate-cleanup`, `qwenpaw-nfs-guard`, `gemini-image-tool`, `gpt-image2-tool`, `wan27-tool` — every plugin with `entry.backend`, deterministically, on every boot. Restarting the app or container does not help.

## Suggested fix

Wrap the new call sites (`module_isolation.py:220` and `:154`) the same way #8345/#8107 wrap the `loader.py` sites — ideally with one shared helper so future call sites cannot reintroduce this:

```python
# module_isolation.py — no module-level logger exists today, so add one
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

def _refresh_import_caches() -> None:
    """Best-effort import cache refresh; never fatal."""
    try:
        importlib.invalidate_caches()
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - cache refresh is a hint, not a requirement
        logger.debug("importlib.invalidate_caches() failed, continuing", exc_info=True)
```

Two optional hardening notes:

- `register()` is called once per plugin, so a raising call scales the damage linearly; registering the namespace first and refreshing caches afterwards (or once per scan cycle) would bound the blast radius.
- `/api/plugins` reports `status: failed` with no cause for 12 plugins, which reads as 12 independent breakages. Exposing the underlying exception per plugin would have made this a one-glance diagnosis.

## Workaround (for other users hitting this)

Make the shadowed copy match the interpreter's stdlib:

```bash
F=/usr/lib/python3.11/importlib/metadata/__init__.py
cp -a "$F" "$F.bak"
sed -i 's/^    def invalidate_caches(cls):/    @classmethod\n    def invalidate_caches(cls):/' "$F"
```

Restart the app afterwards. Note this is a container-level patch and is lost on image rebuild — which is why the guard belongs in QwenPaw.

---

<sub>This report was assembled with the help of an AI assistant from real logs. Every command output and traceback quoted above was executed and captured on the affected host.</sub>

issues.title: [Feature Request] save_decision() API — 结构化决策持久化，防止上下文压缩丢失关键决策
issues.body:
## 背景

在长对话中，用户确认的关键决策（如行程方案、技术选型、设计方案）会随着上下文压缩被驱逐，导致 agent 回退到旧决策执行。相关讨论见 #5998。

当前的 agent 级 workaround（确认后写入 MEMORY.md）存在鸡生蛋问题：agent 已经因压缩丢失了决策信息，无法可靠地触发存档动作。

## 建议：`save_decision()` API

提供一个框架级的结构化决策存储原语：

### Agent 侧

```python
# 用户确认方案后，agent 显式调用
save_decision(
    key="current_travel_plan",
    value="Plan B: 郑州→平遥→大同→乌兰察布→太原→郑州",
    expires="7d"  # 可选过期时间
)
```

### 框架侧

1. **持久化存储**：决策存入独立存储（如 decisions 表或 KV store），与对话历史解耦
2. **自动注入上下文**：框架将所有活跃决策注入 system prompt 或保留上下文槽位，**不参与压缩**
3. **生命周期管理**：支持 overwrite（同 key 更新）、delete、自动过期

### 工作流示例

```
User: "我确认方案B"
Agent: save_decision("travel_plan", "方案B: 郑州→平遥→大同→乌兰察布...")
Agent: "已记录确认方案"
[... 50轮后上下文压缩 ...]
Agent: [生成文档前检查 decisions store，获取方案B内容]
Agent: [严格按照方案B生成文档]
```

## 为什么需要框架级支持

| 层面 | 当前方案 (MEMORY.md) | 建议方案 (save_decision) |
|------|---------------------|------------------------|
| 可靠性 | 依赖 agent 自觉写入 | agent 显式 API 调用，有确定性 |
| 注入方式 | 需要 memory_search 工具调用 | 框架自动注入，零开销 |
| 结构化 | 自由文本，解析不确定 | key-value，确定性查询 |
| 压缩保护 | 无保障 | 专门的保留槽位 |

## 与现有机制的关系

- `scroll_context`：保护**已驱逐轮次的索引**，但不保护决策内容
- `active_turns`：保护**当前活跃轮次**，但不跨轮持久化
- `save_decision()`：保护**跨轮关键决策**，填补上述两者之间的空白

## 复现案例

#5998 中的内蒙古攻略场景：
- 用户确认方案B（seq 4789）→ agent 按方案A生成文档（seq 8932）
- 如果有 `save_decision()`，方案B会持久存储并在生成文档时自动可用

感谢考虑！

issues.title: [Bug] Doom loop: agent repeatedly triggers same tool call in single turn

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: wontfix
labels.description: This will not be worked on

issues.body:
## Description

The agent falls into a doom loop, repeatedly calling the same tool with the same parameters multiple times within a single user turn. The system eventually detects this after ~6 consecutive repetitions and shows a warning, but by then many API calls and tokens have been wasted.

**This did NOT occur in previous versions with the same model.** The regression suggests a framework-level change is involved.

## Reproduction

- **Session**: 5ff775cf
- **Channel**: Feishu
- **Model**: Qwen (same model that previously worked without this issue)
- **Date**: 2026-07-14

### Scenario

User asked a simple question. The agent called web_search, got results, then called web_search again with identical query 2-3 times. Then when analyzing the issue, called sequential-thinking once (got thoughtNumber=1, totalThoughts=1, nextThoughtNeeded=false), then called it again with nearly identical thought 3-5+ times before being stopped by doom loop detection.

## Evidence

The doom loop warning appeared 6+ times across the conversation:

[WARNING] Repetitive pattern detected. You are repeating similar actions without progress. Try a completely different approach

## Root Cause Analysis

1. **LLM layer**: Model generates tool calls, receives results, but re-generates the same tool call in the next cycle. Known weakness with long/compressed context.

2. **Framework layer - no tool call deduplication**: QwenPaw does not detect or prevent duplicate tool calls within the same turn. If the agent calls web_search and gets results, the framework could block a second identical call.

3. **Doom loop detection is reactive not preventive**: Warning only fires after ~6 repetitions. Earlier intervention (after 2-3) would save tokens.

### Why this is a regression

Same model, same agent config, same channel. Previous versions did not exhibit this at this frequency. Behavioral rules in AGENTS.md cannot fix a framework-level issue.

## Suggested Improvements

1. **Tool call deduplication**: Track tool calls per turn. If same tool + same params called again, inject a blocking system message.
2. **Earlier doom loop detection**: Trigger after 2-3 repetitions instead of 6.
3. **Tool result injection**: Ensure results are prominently visible in context for next generation cycle.

## Environment

- QwenPaw version: latest 2026-07-14
- OS: Linux 5.19.17-z4pro-generic x86_64
- Channel: Feishu
- Session ID: 5ff775cf

issues.title: [Bug] Desktop build omits visual_compression assets → "FileNotFoundError: atlas-gray-native.ts", Visual Compact silently no-ops
issues.body:
## Summary

On the **desktop / PyInstaller build** of `2.3.0-beta.1` (Windows), Visual Compact never runs: the glyph atlases are not shipped, so every eligible model call raises

```
FileNotFoundError: <install>\binaries\qwenpaw-backend\_internal\qwenpaw\agents\context\visual_compression\assets\atlas-gray-native.ts
```

The middleware catches it and **fails open** (`Visual compression failed; sending the original request`), so the conversation continues unchanged and nothing is surfaced to the user.

`pip install qwenpaw` is **not** affected: `pyproject.toml` declares these files as `package-data` (`include-package-data = true`). Only the PyInstaller/Tauri bundle misses them.

## Environment

- QwenPaw Desktop `2.3.0-beta.1`, Windows 11 26H2 (build 26300.9807)
- default config: `light_context.visual_compact.enabled = true`, `effort = "low"`
- any model that reports `supports_image: true`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install QwenPaw **Desktop** `2.3.0-beta.1` (Windows).
2. Keep the defaults (`enabled = true`, `effort = "low"`).
3. Build a conversation with **≥ 3 real user turns** and at least one image in a turn older than the last two (`HISTORY_KEEP_RECENT_TURNS = 2`).
4. Send one more message.
5. The log shows `Visual compression failed; sending the original request (model=… effort=low)` plus a `FileNotFoundError` traceback for the atlas path above.

## Root cause

`scripts/pack-tauri/qwenpaw.spec` collects package data from a **hard-coded directory whitelist**:

```python
_data_dirs = [
    ("agents/skills", "qwenpaw/agents/skills"),
    ("agents/md_files", "qwenpaw/agents/md_files"),
    ("tokenizer", "qwenpaw/tokenizer"),
    ("security/tool_guard/rules", "qwenpaw/security/tool_guard/rules"),
    ("security/skill_scanner/rules", "qwenpaw/security/skill_scanner/rules"),
    ("security/skill_scanner/data", "qwenpaw/security/skill_scanner/data"),
    ("app/channels/yuanbao/proto", "qwenpaw/app/channels/yuanbao/proto"),
    ("providers/data", "qwenpaw/providers/data"),
]
```

`agents/context/**` is not in the list, so `_internal/qwenpaw/agents/` ships only `md_files` and `skills`. The runtime resolves the atlas relative to the frozen module:

```python
# rendering/renderer.py
_ASSET_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "assets"
_DENSE_ATLAS_PROFILES = {
    "low":    (_ASSET_ROOT / "atlas-gray-native.ts",   8, 16),
    "medium": (_ASSET_ROOT / "atlas-gray-readable.ts", 6, 13),
    "high":   (_ASSET_ROOT / "atlas-gray.ts",          5,  8),
}
```

→ the path it looks for cannot exist in the bundled layout. The same whitelist is on `main`, so the next desktop build will most likely miss it as well.

## Suggested fix

```diff
 _data_dirs = [
     ("agents/skills", "qwenpaw/agents/skills"),
     ("agents/md_files", "qwenpaw/agents/md_files"),
+    (
+        "agents/context/visual_compression/assets",
+        "qwenpaw/agents/context/visual_compression/assets",
+    ),
     ("tokenizer", "qwenpaw/tokenizer"),
```

(≈23 MB; the three `*_LICENSE.txt` files in that directory should be shipped too.)

## Two further suggestions

1. **Startup self-check**: if `visual_compact.enabled` is true but the configured atlas is missing, log one `WARNING` at boot (optionally auto-disable the feature) instead of raising on every request.
2. **Rate-limit the log**: the fail-open path currently emits a full traceback per model call; one line per session plus a counter is enough.

## Workaround for other desktop users

Copy the three atlases (and the three license files) from the tag into
`<install>\binaries\qwenpaw-backend\_internal\qwenpaw\agents\context\visual_compression\assets\`.
They exist in the source tree at `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/visual_compression/assets/` (`atlas-gray-native.ts` = 12,157,200 B, `atlas-gray-readable.ts` = 7,576,000 B, `atlas-gray.ts` = 4,093,877 B). Desktop upgrades recreate the `binaries` folder, so the copy has to be redone afterwards.

Raw logs can be provided on request if useful.

issues.title: [Bug]: Opening the Voice Transcription settings page imports whisper into the server process (~690 MB RSS, never released)
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

`2.3.0b1`, installed from source at commit `b12b06ed`.

## Description

`GET /api/workspace/local-whisper-status` calls `check_local_whisper_available()`, which performs a real `import whisper` just to tell the UI whether the optional dependency is installed:

```python
# src/qwenpaw/agents/utils/audio_transcription.py
whisper_ok = False
try:
    import whisper as _whisper  # noqa: F401
    whisper_ok = True
except ImportError:
    pass
```

Importing `whisper` pulls in `torch` and the whole CUDA runtime (`libtorch_cuda`, `libcublasLt`, `libnvrtc`, `libnvJitLink`), plus `librosa` → `numba`/`llvmlite` and `tiktoken`. Measured on this machine: **163 MB → 853 MB RSS (+690 MB)** for a single call. Python imports are permanent, so the memory stays in the server process until it is restarted.

The Console calls this endpoint unconditionally when the **Voice Transcription settings page** mounts (`api.getLocalWhisperStatus()` inside the `Promise.all` in `loadSettings`), regardless of the configured provider:

```ts
// console/src/pages/Settings/VoiceTranscription/useVoiceTranscription.ts
const [modeRes, provTypeRes, provRes, lwStatus] = await Promise.all([
  api.getAudioMode(),
  api.getTranscriptionProviderType(),
  api.getTranscriptionProviders(),
  api.getLocalWhisperStatus(),   // even when provider_type is "whisper_api"
]);
```

Consequence: a user who only uses the remote Whisper API (or has transcription disabled) permanently pays ~690 MB of RSS for visiting a settings page once. In the observed instance an otherwise idle `qwenpaw app` process sat at ~1.9 GB PSS / 1.6 GB anonymous memory, with 14 torch/CUDA/numba `.so` files mapped, while the remote transcription provider was the one actually configured.

**Related PR(s):** #8431 (converts local Whisper into an SDK plugin — may relocate this code, but the probe still runs in the main server process today)

**Security considerations:** none.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0b1 (source, `b12b06ed`)
- **OS:** Ubuntu (Linux 7.3.0)
- **Install method:** pip editable install from source, `openai-whisper` installed in the same environment
- **Python version:** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install QwenPaw in an environment that also has `openai-whisper` installed (so `import whisper` succeeds).
2. Start `qwenpaw app` and record the server process PSS (`/proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup`).
3. Open **Settings → Voice Transcription** in the Console.
4. Record PSS again, and check `/proc/<pid>/maps` for `libtorch*` / `libcublas*`.

Standalone reproduction of the underlying call (no HTTP needed):

```bash
python -c "
import sys
def rss():
    return [int(l.split()[1])/1024 for l in open('/proc/self/status') if l.startswith('VmRSS:')][0]
from qwenpaw.agents.utils.audio_transcription import check_local_whisper_available
before = rss(); check_local_whisper_available()
print(f'{before:.0f}MB -> {rss():.0f}MB, torch={ \"torch\" in sys.modules }')
"
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `check_local_whisper_available()` costs ~690 MB RSS and loads torch/CUDA permanently; the process never returns to its pre-visit footprint.
- **Expected:** a read-only availability probe should be effectively free. `importlib.util.find_spec("whisper")` answers the same question with 0 MB and ~4 ms, because it only performs a file-system lookup.

## Logs / Screenshots

Memory-map evidence from the affected process:

```
Pss / Pss_Anon / Pss_File = 1886 MB / 1646 MB / 240 MB
14 unique mappings matching libtorch*, libcublas*, libnvrtc*, libnumba, libllvmlite
GPU memory in use: 15 MiB (CUDA context created, nothing running)
```

Probe cost, same interpreter:

| Probe | RSS delta | wall | torch loaded |
|---|---|---|---|
| `importlib.util.find_spec("whisper")` | +0 MB | 3.8 ms | no |
| `check_local_whisper_available()` (current) | **+690 MB** | 1.35 s | **yes** |

## Additional Notes

Suggested fix (opened as a PR): resolve the module instead of importing it —

```python
try:
    whisper_ok = importlib.util.find_spec("whisper") is not None
except (ImportError, ValueError):
    whisper_ok = False
```

A broken install would now be reported as "installed" by the probe and fail later, but `_transcribe_local_whisper()` already logs that failure as a warning, so no functionality is lost while the 690 MB is avoided.

Optional follow-up on the Console side: only request `/local-whisper-status` when the selected provider is `local_whisper` (the value is currently only consumed by `AudioModeCard`), so the endpoint is not called at all for remote/disabled setups.

Related memory reports: #7222 (unbounded growth of a long-running backend), #7818 (UI freeze / high memory) — different root causes, but they explain why a permanent ~690 MB baseline is noticeable.

prs.title: feat(providers): extract local model management into plugin
prs.body:
## Description

Extract local model management into a Plugin Provider. The plugin owns model downloads, llama.cpp installation and service lifecycle. The host keeps model selection and unified inference.

- Preserve existing users' configuration and model files.
- Move download dependencies into the plugin and import them lazily.
- Reuse plugin registration, dependency preparation and lifecycle management.

### TODO / Follow-ups

- **Provider:** Prepare cloud Provider pluginization. 
- **Dependencies:** Review a shared design for optional per-feature dependencies and explicit install/repair flows. This PR declares ModelScope and Hugging Face as required plugin dependencies with lazy imports.
- **CLI / doctor:** Add shared plugin CLI registration, then restore local model commands and diagnostics. They are deferred even when the plugin is installed. Other core commands and diagnostics remain available.
- **SDK release:** Assign a release version to the contract additions; the SDK version currently remains 1.0.0.
- **Streaming:** Review the shared stream-close policy for cloud and local runs.

### Advantages

- Makes local model management optional, preserves existing model data, and prevents cloud-only startup from restoring unused llama.cpp services.
- Measured cloud-only initialization: **1 → 0** local managers, **6 → 0** local modules, and **~0.9 MiB lower host RSS** (5-run median, partial startup path). Core no longer requires ModelScope (**~21.7 MiB** of installed package files in the measured environment).
