prs.title: feat(jobs): add thinking_level to JobRuntimeSpec for per-job reasonin…
prs.body:
…g control (#8439)

feat(jobs): add thinking_level to JobRuntimeSpec for per-job reasoning control  Close #8439

## Description

Adds per-job reasoning control to cron jobs by introducing `thinking_level` (and optional `thinking_budget`) on `JobRuntimeSpec`.

Today every cron job inherits the agent-level thinking configuration. Users running many pipeline-style jobs (data collection, report generation, format conversion) must create a separate lightweight agent for every job just to turn reasoning off, which is error-prone and hard to maintain. This change lets each job choose:

- `inherit` (default): keep the existing agent/session behavior.
- `off`: disable reasoning for this job.
- `minimal` / `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` / `max`: force an effort level for this job.
- `budget`: use an explicit token budget via `thinking_budget`.

The value uses the existing `ThinkingLevel` enum instead of inventing a new `enabled` string. `CronExecutor` passes it through `request_context`, and `AgentBuilder` applies it to a request-scoped copy of `agent_config` after session-level thinking resolution and before model construction. It is never persisted to the shared chat/session.

Backward compatibility:
- New jobs default to `inherit`.
- Existing `jobs.json` files without the new fields load as `inherit`.
- Replacement requests from older clients that omit the fields preserve the stored values.
- `inherit` adds no `request_context` keys and leaves the agent config unchanged.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8439

**Security Considerations:** No authentication, channel, or secret-handling changes. The override is request-scoped and never written to the shared session or persisted agent config, so `share_session=True` cannot leak per-job reasoning settings into another conversation. `runtime` is authoritative in `CronExecutor`; stale or hand-written `cron_thinking_*` keys in the passthrough payload are removed. Invalid hand-written `request_context` overrides are ignored with a warning rather than reaching model construction. `off` remains best-effort, matching existing agent-level behavior: models without a disable control keep their defaults. `thinking_budget` is clamped by the existing model-card resolver.

prs.title: fix(cli): mask env var values by default in `env list` and `env set`
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`qwenpaw env list` prints **every environment variable value in plaintext**, and `qwenpaw env set` echoes the value it just stored:

```
  Key                             Value
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  OPENAI_API_KEY                  sk-...
```

Those values are API keys / service-account tokens, so a single `env list` copies every secret into:

- terminal scrollback, screen shares, screenshots
- CI logs and saved shell output
- **any agent session that runs the command as a tool** — the tool output is forwarded to the model provider verbatim

This is not hypothetical: someone ran `env list` only to check *whether* a key existed, and 20+ credentials ended up in an LLM transcript. The only information actually needed was the key name.

## Change

Display layer only — no storage, API or UI changes.

- `env list` masks values by default (`s3cr3t-value-1234` → `s3cr***34`; values with ≤8 chars → all `*`) and prints a one-line hint
- new `--reveal` flag restores the previous plaintext output
- `env set` echoes the masked value instead of the raw one
- the interactive `configure_env_interactive()` helper behaves the same way

```
  OPENAI_API_KEY                  sk-p***yz
  Values are masked. Use 'qwenpaw env list --reveal' to print plaintext.
```

## Compatibility

- Anyone who really needs raw values keeps them via `--reveal`, which is explicit and greppable in scripts
- The default changes on purpose: printing secrets should be opt-in
- `qwenpaw env set` output changes from `✓ KEY = value` to `✓ KEY = abcd***yz`

## Evidence

New `tests/unit/test_cli_env_masking.py`:

- `list` masks by default, `--reveal` prints plaintext
- `env set` masks the echoed value
- `_mask_value()` edge cases (empty / short / long)

Also verified manually against a live 2.2.x install (list / reveal / set).

## 中文摘要

`qwenpaw env list` 会把所有密钥明文打印，`env set` 也会回显明文；这些值可能是 API key，在自动化/agent 场景里会被原样转发出去。本次改动只在展示层：默认掩码 + 新增 `--reveal` 显式还原，`set` 与交互式配置同样掩码。存储、API、UI 均未改动。

prs.title: fix(providers): bound inline media per request, not just per file
prs.body:
## Summary

The per-file inline cap (`MAX_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES`, 2 MB) does not bound the
**request body**. Media counts ~0 tokens, so token-based context eviction
never fires, and a session that accumulates many *in-spec* images keeps
sending a multi-megabyte body on every turn. Once a gateway's byte limit
answers 413 the session is unusable until the history is stripped by hand.

This adds a cumulative inline-media budget to the shared capping
formatters, so the request body is bounded independently of tokens.

Refs #7671

## What Problem This Solves

The reporter's incident: a design-review session accumulated ~20 MB of
inline base64 screenshots — every one *under* the 2 MB per-file cap — and
every subsequent turn failed with provider 413 until the session JSON was
surgically stripped. A 2,979,813-byte PNG also became
`[Image unavailable: ... exceeds the 2097152-byte image limit.]`, i.e. an
image marginally over the line was dropped even though a slightly smaller
version would have been fine.

PR #7965 fixed the Scroll-side half (reclaim historical media, fold media
into the existing compression flow) and explicitly listed this as remaining:

> **Out of scope / TODO** — HTTP request-body limits: accumulated media can
> still exceed a gateway's byte limit without exceeding the token threshold.

This PR closes that TODO.

## Changes

`src/qwenpaw/providers/capping_formatter.py`:

- New `max_total_bytes` field (default `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` = 8 MB
  = 4× the per-file cap; `0` disables it, restoring per-file-only behaviour).
- The budget is spent in two passes. A **measuring** pass records the size of
  every media block in wire order; only when the measured total exceeds the
  budget does an **enforcing** pass run, replacing the oldest media (a byte
  prefix of the wire order) with placeholders. The newest media is what the
  request keeps.
- `_cap_media` runs the per-file cap first, so a file that is already a
  placeholder is never charged to the budget.
- `inline_media_size()` also sizes inline `data:` URLs, and the OpenAI Chat /
  Responses formatters route PDF attachments through `_format_file_source()`,
  so `data:` URLs and PDFs count toward the budget like any other media.
- The per-request media **dedup scope** lives next to the budget policy
  (`SEEN_MEDIA_KEYS`) and is reset between the measuring and the enforcing
  pass — both passes have to observe the same media, otherwise the enforcing
  pass sees every source as "already shown above" and drops all media,
  including the newest one the budget keeps.

`src/qwenpaw/agents/model_factory.py`:

- The Anthropic formatter now only remembers a media source as *seen* once it
  has actually reached the wire. A source the budget dropped is not part of
  the request, so a later copy of it stays eligible: with **A → B → A**
  (512 bytes each, 900-byte budget) the request keeps the newest **A**
  instead of folding it as "already shown above" while the dropped copy is
  nowhere in the request.
- A folded duplicate still occupies a slot in the wire order, but it is never
  sent, so it costs the budget nothing: the plan drops oldest occurrences only
  until the *deduplicated* payload — the distinct sources that actually reach
  the wire — fits the budget, and a folded copy is re-inlined when the budget
  dropped every earlier copy of its source (so A → B → A still keeps the
  newest A).

Because formatting walks the conversation oldest-first, spending the budget
as it is spent **keeps the newest media and drops the oldest** — the
direction the issue asks for.

A `ContextVar` rather than instance state, because formatter instances are
shared across concurrent requests and a running total on the instance would
let one session spend another's allowance
(`test_concurrent_requests_do_not_share_a_budget` pins this).

Placeholder wording distinguishes the two causes, and every provider shape
is preserved: Chat Completions / Anthropic / DashScope `{"type":"text"}`,
Gemini `{"text"}`, Responses API `{"type":"input_text"}`.

## Evidence

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers/test_capping_formatter.py -q
67 passed
```

`TestCumulativeBudgetEndToEnd` drives the **real** formatters (OpenAI,
Anthropic, Gemini, DashScope, and the Responses formatter) over a
three-image conversation with a budget that fits only one:

```
[media omitted from model context: this request already inlines 513 bytes
 of media, exceeds the 900-byte per-request limit]     <- oldest, dropped
[media omitted from model context: ... 900-byte ...]   <- middle, dropped
{"inline_data": {...}}                                 <- newest, inlined
```

`TestCumulativeBudgetThroughProductionWrapper` drives the same scenario
through the production formatter wrapper, and
`TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget` pins the repeated-source case through
the Anthropic wrapper, the same case with the newest copy arriving in a tool
result, and the OpenAI Chat / Responses paths:

```
A (512 B) -> B (512 B) -> A (512 B), 900-byte budget
  before:  A dropped by the budget, B inlined, newest A folded as
           "[Image omitted - already shown above]"
  after:   A dropped by the budget, B dropped by the budget,
           newest A inlined
```

The two Anthropic cases fail without the fix (verified by reverting the
`model_factory.py` change):

```
FAILED TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget::test_anthropic_wrapper_keeps_the_newest_repeated_media
FAILED TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget::test_anthropic_wrapper_keeps_the_newest_repeated_tool_media
2 failed, 62 passed
```

Wider runs — no regressions. The failures below are pre-existing in this
environment (missing optional dependencies: `acp`, `playwright`, `reme`, …)
and are identical on the unmodified head commit:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers tests/unit/agents -q
# this branch:        148 failed, 4224 passed
# unmodified head:    148 failed, 4219 passed   (+5 = the new tests)

$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00) / mypy   # clean
```

### The 8 MiB budget is raw media, not wire bytes

`MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` counts the **decoded** media bytes; base64
encoding expands them by 4/3 on the wire. An 8 MiB raw budget therefore
becomes roughly **10.7 MiB** of base64 in the request body — still above the
**6 MiB** limit of the `dash_anthropic` gateway. To stay inside that gateway
the raw budget has to stay at or below ~4.5 MiB (6 MiB x 3/4).

The default is therefore a bound on the request body, not a guarantee that
every gateway accepts it: deployments behind a 6 MiB gateway should lower
`MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` (or `max_total_bytes` on the model) to match
their gateway limit.

## Notes for review

- **The default changes behaviour**: a request that used to inline ~20 MB of
  media now inlines 8 MB and placeholders the rest. If you would rather this
  be opt-in, set `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES = 0` and I will drop the
  default; the plumbing and tests are unaffected.
- `model_factory`'s tool-result video path (`_video_oversize_placeholder`)
  applies its own per-file cap and is untouched — it does not go through
  these formatters, so it is not covered by the cumulative budget. Worth a
  follow-up if you want one budget for both paths.
- The issue's other asks (auto-downscale an oversized attachment instead of
  dropping it, and making the cap configurable per provider) are not
  included; the cap is already a provider field, so only the downscale is
  new work.

prs.title: feat(memory): add OpenViking memory plugin
prs.body: ## Description Adds an OpenViking memory backend plugin with automatic recall, completed-turn persistence, and an explicit `memory_search` tool through the OpenViking REST API. ### Review follow-up This revision addresses the feedback: 1. **Fix concurrent first-time installation-ID initialization (P2)** - Write, flush, and fsync the complete ID to a temporary file before atomically publishing it with `os.link()`. - Preserve create-if-absent semantics: concurrent callers read the winning ID rather than observing an empty marker or overwriting an existing ID. - Add regression tests verifying that concurrent callers receive the same complete ID and concurrent managers start successfully. 2. **Fix small-budget automatic recall (P3)** - Reserve the synthetic-message overhead and complete untrusted-history notice before requesting remote context. - Pass the remaining token budget to OpenViking. - Keep a local UTF-8-safe clipping guard that clips only the recalled body, preserving the complete notice. - Skip injection when the remaining budget is insufficient or no recalled content remains. - Add regression tests near the supported minimum budget, including the reported 96-token case. 3. **Remove redundant client response checks** - Reuse the dictionary validation already performed by `_request()` in `commit()`, `search_context()`, and `search_memories()`. - Retain response-envelope and `memories`-list validation. 4. **Simplify the internal recall path** - Return `str | None` directly from `_search_context_for_session()`. - Remove the intermediate successful `ToolChunk`, redundant state check, and subsequent text extraction. **Related Issue:** Relates to #7252. Implements the plugin-based rewrite requested in this PR following #7616. ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Breaking change - [x] Documentation - [ ] Refactoring ## Component(s) Affected - [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models) - [x] Console (frontend web UI) - [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.) - [ ] Skills - [ ] CLI - [x] Documentation (website) - [x] Tests - [ ] CI/CD - [ ] Scripts / Deploy ## Checklist - [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes - [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks - [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass - [x] Documentation updated (if needed) - [x] Ready for review ## Testing Regression coverage for the review feedback includes: - **Concurrent installation-ID initialization:** concurrent callers receive the same complete, valid ID; concurrent managers sharing a fresh host directory all start successfully. - **Small automatic-recall budgets:** cover the reported 96-token case and nearby budget boundaries; preserve the complete untrusted-history notice, account for synthetic-message overhead, and skip injection when insufficient room remains for recalled content. - **Client response handling:** verify rejection of malformed response envelopes, preservation of commit results, and correct handling of populated and empty explicit-search result lists. - **Simplified internal recall path:** verify successful recall and skipped injection through the direct `str | None` return path. ## Evidence Local validation passed 258 targeted tests, including 126 plugin tests and 132 related host tests. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed. Live integration checks covered OpenViking v0.4.16 and an upgrade to v0.5.2.1. Screenshots, commands, and recorded results follow below. ### OpenViking v0.4.16 — persistence and cross-session automatic recall ### OpenViking v0.4.16 — explicit memory search With automatic recall disabled, the chat record contained an explicit `memory_search` tool call. ### OpenViking v0.5.2.1 — existing memory after upgrading The R3 fact created before the upgrade was correctly recalled: device `JL-1029-6492`, maintenance window Saturday at 21:35. ### OpenViking v0.5.2.1 — newly persisted memory The R4 fact created after the upgrade was correctly recalled: device `OV-UP-B610E899`, maintenance window Sunday at 20:45. prs.title: feat(models): run local Piccolo with bidirectional candidate scoring
prs.body:
## Description

Allow downloaded Piccolo models to supply QwenPaw's native Jev decisions for automatic tool review and ReMe context compaction. Piccolo uses bidirectional prompt attention and candidate-token scoring, so a causal Chat Completions adapter cannot reproduce its trained inference behavior.

- Reuse AgentScope's Jev question/answer mapping and call the managed llama.cpp runtime's native `/v1/systemone` endpoint, with request compression disabled. Read candidate-token probabilities instead of generating probability JSON.
- Preserve the existing Download → Start → default Decision model flow and the separate automatic-review and decision-compaction switches. Starting Piccolo does not enable either feature or change another provider's chat selection.
- Group the local selector into independently scrollable **Chat models** and **Decision models** sections, with Chinese labels **对话模型** and **决策模型**. Remove the redundant Local Models heading, Piccolo purpose subtitle, and blue repository links. Keep a single managed runtime.
- Use current `agentscope-ai` Hugging Face repositories for QwenPaw-Flash recommendations; preserve stored IDs for existing downloads and their lifecycle actions.
- Recommend separate `agentscope-ai/Piccolo-{4,9,27}B-BF16` and `-Q8_0` repositories according to machine memory. BF16 downloads use the standard complete GGUF shard set, with known total sizes; BF16 repository IDs retain the native decision role through download, restart and activation. Recognize only the Piccolo family IDs; no legacy Blink repository or cache aliases are added. Preserve the decision role after download, restart, and API activation. Download GGUF/runtime metadata only.
- Launch Piccolo with a complete-prompt budget, one slot, no prompt cache, and no context shifting. Reject runtimes that report Piccolo as a text-generation model.
- Include a focused companion llama.cpp patch and build instructions in `docs/local-piccolo.md`. Ordinary Ollama Chat Completions is not enabled for this contract.

The companion patch targets llama.cpp `f4d8af608a6b39946406f9439edfb6e83ca6a923`. It adds Piccolo metadata and the checkpoint's exact `flex_twice` layout to the existing native SystemOne implementation. Full-attention layers use bidirectional prompt attention; linear-attention layers keep their native computation. Candidate softmax at temperature 1 is equivalent to renormalizing the candidate token log probabilities. No answer tokens are generated.

**Related work:** Reuses the decision configuration and review integration in #8205 and #8360.

**Security considerations:** Existing approval thresholds, human-confirmation fallback, context recovery, and opt-in switches remain in control. Candidate probabilities are model outputs, not a calibration or safety guarantee.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Refactoring
- [ ] Breaking change

## Components

Local model lifecycle and catalog, provider adapter, Console capability detection, English model guide, and tests. No workflow files are changed.

## Evidence

- BF16 catalog follow-up: 177 focused backend/API tests and 35 model-selector tests passed, covering memory boundaries, GGUF-only downloads, BF16 decision identity and existing Start controls. Changed Python hooks and Prettier passed.
- Rename follow-up: 188 focused backend tests and 34 model-selector tests passed. The renamed companion patch applies to the pinned source.
- 258 focused backend tests passed (one existing tar extraction deprecation warning).
- 5 relevant Console test files / 117 tests passed; production frontend build passed.
- Changed Python hooks passed: AST, encoding, private-key scan, whitespace, trailing commas, mypy, Black, flake8, and pylint. Changed Console/docs passed Prettier. The full-repository pre-commit run is not claimed as passing; unrelated formatter/actionlint bootstrap and full CI remain outstanding.
- Companion runtime: 49 server-component tests / 191 assertions passed. The patch applies cleanly to the pinned upstream source.
- Exact C++ versus checkpoint-tokenizer comparison: 33 cases across three tokenizers, 78 prompt rows, including 255 options, ordered scores, Chinese, special tokens, and non-repeated long prompts.
- Complete original 4B, 9B, and 27B checkpoints ran in the Transformers reference. BF16 and Q8 GGUFs were compared on four smoke questions per size. Q8 maximum absolute candidate probability differences were approximately 0.00564 / 0.00286 / 0.00298, with matching top choices.
- On a Mac M4 Pro, the complete 4B checkpoint ran through the CPU reference, and 4B Q8 GGUF ran on Metal through the actual native classifier, `assess_tool_call()`, and ReMe decision component. These smoke tests did not execute a reviewed tool or change approval settings.

### Local model selector

English:

![English local model selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Xinji-Mai/QwenPaw/58d7ec350cfd83e3fe8313115f2971820aa564b9/docs/images/local-models-en.png)

![Chinese local model selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Xinji-Mai/QwenPaw/58d7ec350cfd83e3fe8313115f2971820aa564b9/docs/images/local-models-zh.png)

## Limitations and release status

A Piccolo-compatible llama.cpp binary is required; the companion patch is not in a released upstream binary. The build/install step is documented and the capability gate rejects an incompatible runtime. The local runtime serves one model at a time. This initial Piccolo integration caps each complete question prompt at 8,192 tokens, including repeated layout, to bound full-attention memory allocation even when the shared chat window is 64K. Oversized prompts fail to the existing fallback.

The complete 4B, 9B and 27B checkpoints and their Q8_0 and Q4_K_M variants are public under `agentscope-ai/Piccolo-{4,9,27}B`, with separate `-Q8_0` and `-Q4_K_M` repositories. All nine renamed repositories were independently checked for public revisions, manifest file sizes and unchanged LFS weight hashes. Model cards retain Apache-2.0 and FlexDM attribution. The catalog now recommends BF16 as well as Q8_0 according to memory; Q4_K_M can be downloaded by repository ID. BF16 uses separate `Piccolo-{4,9,27}B-BF16` repositories. All three BF16 repositories are now public. Their complete standard GGUF shard sets (4B: 8.42 GB / 2 shards; 9B: 17.92 GB / 4 shards; 27B: 53.81 GB / 12 shards) were independently checked against the published HEAD, file sizes and SHA-256 receipts. Its model cards disclose the expanded synthetic 265-request / 556-judgment regressions and measured differences. Repository existence or successful loading is not a task-quality benchmark.

The actual QwenPaw-managed runtime then passed classifier, automatic-review, and ReMe compaction smoke calls (1.77-second classifier, 3.10-second review, 0 generated answer tokens). The recommendation tiers are 16/24/48 GB for Q8 and 24/32/80 GB for BF16 (4B/9B/27B). prs.title: fix(console): persist market install provenance so 'Update All' covers third-party plugins (#8176)
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8176.

When a plugin is installed from the AgentScope plugin market, the install URL is discarded after download. The console later re-derives the market identity by string-matching the local `author` field against the market `owner`/`developer` logins. Real plugin.json `author` strings frequently differ from the market owner login (the issue's reporter has owner `onesix` but author `onesixth`), so third-party plugins never match, never enter the `updates` map, and the `Update All` button silently skips them.

Changes:

- Stamp a small `.qwenpaw-market.json` marker with the scoped market id (e.g. `@onesix/qwenpaw-plugin-tool-wait_agent_task`) into the freshly extracted plugin tree before the loader copies it into the install directory. The marker rides through install, gets overwritten on update, and is removed with the plugin on uninstall.
- Expose `market_id` on every entry in `GET /api/plugins`, in both the loader path and the pre-loader disk-scan fallback.
- `marketPluginMatches` treats a recorded `market_id` as authoritative; the existing author heuristic is the fallback for legacy installs that have no provenance yet.

Non-market install sources (local paths, third-party hosts, uploads) are untouched — the marker is only written for official-market archive URLs that match `{host}/plugins/{owner}/{name}/archive/zip/{ref}`.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8176

**Security Considerations:** None. The marker is derived from the install URL after the hostname is verified to match the official market; no user-supplied path or query is persisted. Local-path and third-party-host installs do not write the marker.

prs.title: fix(channels): keep control-command routing on the user's own text in quoted replies
prs.body:
## Description

Replying to a message with a control command such as `/stop` in Feishu, QQ, WeChat, WeCom, DingTalk, OneBot or Yuanbao never routed as a command. These channels prepend the quoted (replied-to) message before the user's own text, so the inbound text becomes:

```
[quoted message: Alice: quarterly report]
/stop
```

Three shared consumers classify or dispatch on that first text block:

- `manager.enqueue` -> `CommandRegistry.get_priority_level`: `/stop` received normal priority 20 instead of critical 0.
- `BaseChannel._consume_one_request` -> `CommandRegistry.is_control_command`: the reply took the normal tracked-message branch instead of the control branch.
- `Runtime.run` -> `SlashCommandRegistry.dispatch`: even when routed fast, the command was not resolved and reached the agent as plain chat text.

Root cause in all three: they must look at the user's own text, but see the quote-first rendering (source probes in #8342).

### Fix

Add one shared recognizer, `strip_quote_context_prefix()` (`src/qwenpaw/utils/quote_context.py`), that removes leading `[quoted ...]` context blocks (some channels stack more than one, e.g. `[quoted media: download failed]` before `[quoted message: ...]`), and apply it at the two extraction points those consumers share:

- `BaseChannel._extract_query_from_payload`: command classification, queue priority, and the ACL "first message" record now see the user's own text, for both dict and `AgentRequest` payloads.
- `Runtime.run` slash-command dispatch text.

Behavior contract (pinned by tests):

- Quote + own `/stop` -> classified and dispatched as the command.
- Command only inside the quoted text -> not a command (unchanged).
- Quote-only reply (no new text) -> no command.
- Normal quoted chat -> unchanged; quote-first input still reaches the model, and text without the prefix is extracted byte-identically.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8342

**Security Considerations:** None. Quoted content is not modified; only the text used for routing and classification is stripped. The full quoted message still reaches the model.

- [ ] New feature

- New `tests/unit/runtime/test_runtime_command_dispatch.py` (3 cases): `Runtime.run` dispatches `/stop` (not the quoted context) for a quoted reply; plain command unchanged; normal quoted chat does not dispatch.

prs.title: feat(pawapp): redesign the SDK and app control plane
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PawApps can expose durable work to Main Chat and their own UI through a shared, scoped Host contract. Small Apps register an `app.action` handler; external runtimes implement the adapter protocol. Host owns task identity, retries, permissions, setup, questions, approvals, results, artifacts and continuation delivery.

For example, Creator can pause production for generation authorization or content review. Main Chat shows what is being approved and the task's approval progress. Users can authorize clearly scoped generation in chat; content review opens the exact pending review and revision in Creator. Decisions resume the same project/task through Creator's existing mechanisms. A manual review no longer appears as ongoing planning.

This PR includes:

- Generated Python/JSON Schema/TypeScript contracts, validated results and scoped clients.
- Durable task execution/recovery, grants, artifacts, handoffs and App-owned configuration prompts.
- Main Chat discovery/delegation tools, generic task cards and scoped continuation back into the originating chat.
- Typed execution/review approvals with immutable proposal digests, stable decision IDs, optional cost information and expiry, authenticated user identity and persisted decision receipts. Ordinary agent answers cannot approve. Retries retain the same command identity; stale or conflicting decisions are rejected.
- Revoked action grants block new work and approvals while scoped owners retain redacted control status and can request cancellation. Cancellation delivery is durable; unavailable or incompatible executors remain unconfirmed. Recovery backs off without fabricating terminal states and observes already-started work without restarting managed handlers. Managed approval waits report expiry to App handlers, wake on decisions with a durable fallback, and preserve the current proposal across progress updates. Large artifact hashes run off the event loop.
- Approval cards show bounded object/operation scope, operation count and revision, with authenticated inspection handoffs. App-only review is enforced on the server. Mutable progress counts stay separate from the immutable proposal; future counts distinguish unknown, estimated and exact. Creator reports authoritative handled/pending counts and leaves future approvals unknown.
- Creator story-writing integration: the bilingual skill hands the full StoryPackage and exact script to `prepare-production`; `revise-story` preserves revisions; `produce-video` continues the same project with setup/approval gates and verified final-film publication. Generation approvals and content review use shared cards; new content reviews require inspection and decisions inside Creator.
- An App-independent word-counter quickstart, managed-handler approval API and generic conformance tests.

## App integrations are separate

- **Data integration: #8363.** Adapter, native Console task routing, Engine compatibility pin, Data-specific tests and external Engine CI. Depends on this SDK and [QwenPaw-Data #85](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw-Data/pull/85).
- **File Browser reference App: #8364.** Managed listing, directory setup, frontend, persistence, legacy recovery adapter, attribution, tests and dedicated CI. Depends on this SDK independently of Data.

Both are draft follow-ups to rebase after this SDK merges. Neither App implementation is included here. The shared conformance suite runs without either integration or an external Data Engine.

## Compatibility and behavior

- Existing authorization/event digests and accepted task identities remain compatible. Legacy persisted question-shaped approval events retain their original replay payload; new events use typed approvals.
- Versioned PawApps require explicit activation. Managed child services inherit OS basics plus explicitly declared environment variables.
- Each new Creator action needs its own grant. Setup completion, action permissions and per-operation approval remain separate. Host does not change App YOLO settings or model/credential configuration.
- Creator validates its authoritative authorization/review token before applying decisions. A lost response reuses the existing decision journal; decisions already made inside Creator invalidate stale chat proposals.
- Artifacts remain reusable across sessions within authorized user/workspace/App scope; cross-App handoffs require exact-version grants.
- Story references and notes are retained. Binary reference transfer and multi-film production are outside this increment.

## Evidence

Local verification for the review follow-up (2026-10-27): **734 backend tests passed**, including the PawApp conformance and Creator workflow suites. Regression cases cover revoked-grant cancellation, status redaction, unknown cancellation for missing/changed executors, recovery backoff and restart, App-side approval observation, approval expiry/restart, progress interleaving and artifact hashing. Changed-file pre-commit checks and contract drift checks passed. The isolated deterministic Creator browser acceptance passed with fake providers (image/video approvals, reload, exact handoff and artifact download); no paid calls.

Local verification for the approval contract and Creator adaptation (2026-10-23):

- **575 backend tests passed:** `tests/unit/pawapp`, Creator's video-workflow suite and project-file review tests. Covers authenticated decisions, cross-scope rejection, expiry/replacement, concurrent decisions, restart/replay, App-side decisions and lost-receipt recovery; also immutable approval content during progress updates, App-only decision enforcement, and stale inspection rejection.
- **135 frontend tests passed:** 129 Console task-card/API/SDK tests plus 6 Creator decision-tray/plugin-entry tests. Covers scope details, forecast certainty, precise inspection routing and revision mismatch handling.
- TypeScript, both frontend builds, generated-contract drift checks, `git diff --check` and changed-file pre-commit hooks passed.
- Deterministic browser acceptance passed: image approval, video approval, reload recovery, exact Creator authorization inspection, completion and verified artifact download. No paid provider calls. The local 8088 instance was updated and restarted; Main Chat and Creator health checks passed.

Documentation: `docs/design/pawapp-app-quickstart.md`, `docs/design/pawapp-approvals.md`, `docs/design/pawapp-task-runtime.md`, `docs/design/pawapp-creator-story-handoff.md`, and `docs/design/pawapp-contract-progress.md`.

prs.title: fix(memory): require non-empty api_key for ReMe reranker enablement (#8276)
prs.body:
## Description

Resolves two related issues in `src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/reme_reranker.py`:

1. **Enablement requires non-empty credential:** `load_reranker_config()` previously evaluated enablement from `config.enabled and config.model_name` alone. Since `RerankerConfig.api_key` defaults to `""`, a configuration without an API key was accepted as enabled, causing memory searches to over-fetch `max_results * candidate_multiplier` candidates for a rerank call that cannot succeed. This aligns the reranker enablement rule with the existing embedding path (`src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/reme_config.py:717`), requiring `bool(config.api_key and config.api_key.strip())`.

2. **Pre-flight guard for missing API key:** `call_reranker_api()` previously checked `base_url` but not `api_key`. An empty or whitespace-only API key resulted in an invalid `Authorization: Bearer ` header, which failed serialization in HTTP transport and was caught as an opaque `[rerank] unexpected error`. A pre-flight check now logs `[rerank] api_key not configured` and returns `None` early, matching the `base_url` error reporting pattern.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8276

**Security Considerations:** None. The API key is validated for presence/non-emptiness and is never logged.

prs.title: fix(memory): inject automatic recall as reference context
prs.body:
## Description

Automatic memory recall was represented as an assistant-authored thinking/tool-call/tool-result sequence. Models could imitate that synthetic trajectory and call `memory_search` again in the same turn.

This change represents automatic recall as transient, untrusted `TextBlock` reference data attached to a request-local copy of the current user message. The fixed system prompt and conversation history remain unchanged for cross-turn prompt-cache reuse. The request copy is not persisted, and explicit model-initiated `memory_search` calls are unchanged.

Persisted caches from the previous synthetic format are versioned out and searched again on restore. Evidence block IDs are retained on the request copy so repeated preparation is idempotent.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8361

**Security Considerations:** Retrieved memory is explicitly labeled as untrusted reference data. It is not added as another external user query, does not change the system prompt, and is skipped when the current turn cannot be identified.

prs.title: feat(console): navigable fullscreen image gallery for chat media
prs.body:
## Description

Improves how images are **viewed** in the console chat. Each image in a tool card is an
**isolated** antd `<Image>`, so the fullscreen preview shows only that one image with no way
to move between images.

This PR wraps the conversation in a single `Image.PreviewGroup`, so clicking any image opens
a fullscreen gallery with prev/next buttons (plus zoom/rotate). User-posted images join the
same group automatically, since the chat library renders them with antd `<Image>` too.

It also adds **keyboard navigation**: left/right arrow keys switch images while the preview is
open. antd ships no built-in keyboard nav for `PreviewGroup` (long-standing request,
ant-design/ant-design#29323), so a small `keydown` handler drives antd's own switch buttons —
reusing its bounds handling (no-op at the first/last image).

**Scope note (rebase 2026-08-11):** this PR originally also made media tool cards open
expanded via a new `ToolCardShell` `defaultOpen` prop. That part is now **upstream** —
`ToolCardShell` has an `expanded` state and the four media cards pass
`defaultExpanded={Boolean(media)}`. Those changes were dropped in the rebase rather than
reimplemented, which is why the diff shrank from 6 files to 1. What remains is only the
gallery, which has no upstream equivalent.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #1211 (which is orthogonal — that PR covers the *input* side:
clipboard paste / compression / storage. This PR is purely the *viewing* side.)

**Security Considerations:** None. No changes to file access, URLs, or backend; purely
frontend rendering of already-resolved media URLs.

prs.title: fix(skill): avoid scanner false positive in make-skill validator
prs.body:
## Description

The built-in `make-skill` is blocked by QwenPaw's own skill security scanner when it is imported into the skill pool or a workspace:

```
[CRITICAL] Dangerous code execution functions that can execute arbitrary code
(scripts/validate_skill.py:432) rule_id=COMMAND_INJECTION_EVAL
```

The flagged line is the validator's syntax check for generated scripts:

```python
compile(path.read_bytes(), relative, "exec")
```

`compile()` only produces a code object, which is never executed here, so this is a false positive. However, `COMMAND_INJECTION_EVAL` matches any bare `compile(` call. This PR replaces it with `ast.parse(path.read_bytes(), filename=relative)`, which performs the same syntax check and raises the same `SyntaxError` (with the same filename and line) without producing a code object. Applied identically to `make-skill-en` and `make-skill-zh`.

I chose to fix the skill rather than relax the scanner rule, since loosening a CRITICAL rule to let one built-in pass seems like the wrong trade.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8320 (same validator, different failure)

**Security Considerations:** No behaviour change beyond removing `compile()`; the scanner rule is untouched.

prs.title: fix(memory): stop leaking auto-memory-recall payload to channels
prs.body:
## Description

The auto-memory-recall pipeline injected a synthetic `memory_search` tool interaction (`ToolCallBlock` + `ToolResultBlock`) into the LLM context. Two problems followed from that:

- models that observe a tool interaction in their own context tend to imitate it out loud in the next user-facing reply ("I'll check memory for relevant context…"), which leaks the internal recall flow to the user and to outbound channels;
- the payload had to be kept off the wire with a dedicated `AUTO_MEMORY_SEARCH_BLOCK_HIDDEN_KEY` metadata flag plus a channel-renderer guard and a console tool-card guard — three cooperating layers, none of which was actually connected (see *Root cause*).

This PR carries the recall payload in a single `HintBlock` instead. Every provider formatter (OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / DashScope / Ollama) turns a hint into a separate `role="user"` message, so the request never ends with an assistant turn; and the console / PawApp history converter skips hint blocks entirely, so the payload never reaches a transcript. Because the block type already covers both concerns, the hidden flag and the two guards are gone. The middleware recognises the message through the pre-existing `AUTO_MEMORY_SEARCH_BLOCK_IDS_KEY`, which the block-cleanup path already uses, so the transient injection and cleanup behaviour are unchanged.

The branch is rebased onto the latest `main`.

## Root cause

Two independent issues, both reproduced against the real converter and the real formatters before the change:

1. **Assistant prefill.** With the payload in a `TextBlock`, the Anthropic formatter emitted the recall as an assistant turn, so the request ended with `role="assistant"`. Anthropic reads a trailing assistant turn as a prefill continuation, which Claude 4.6+ rejects.
2. **The hiding logic was not connected.** `agentscope_msg_to_message()` nests the original metadata under `message.metadata["metadata"]`, while the renderer guard only checked the top level, so `_is_auto_memory_recall_message()` never fired and the recall text was rendered to the channel as an ordinary assistant message. The console guard did not help either: it lived on the tool-card path, which the payload no longer used, and the tool-card adapter did not forward the metadata the guard checked.

## Evidence

The two issues above were reproduced against the real converter and the real provider formatters before the change, and the same paths were re-checked after it. The payload never appears in an outbound message, and the model request never ends with an assistant turn.

### Before / after, against the real converter and formatters

Request tail, Anthropic:

```
before: [{"role": "user",     "content": [...]},
         {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "<auto_memory_recall>..."}]}]   # assistant tail -> prefill
after:  [{"role": "user",     "content": [...]},
         {"role": "user",     "content": [{"text": "<auto_memory_recall>..."}]}]   # no assistant turn
```

History conversion:

```
before: agentscope_msg_to_message([recall]) -> 1 message containing the payload
after:  agentscope_msg_to_message([recall]) -> 0 messages
```

The renderer guard before the change:

```
message.metadata = {"original_id": ..., "original_name": "memory_search",
                    "metadata": {"auto_memory_search_hidden": true, ...}, ...}
                                   ^ nested here
guard checks:    message.metadata.get("auto_memory_search_hidden")   # top level -> misses
=> rendered parts: 1  (full recall payload sent to the channel)
```

### Formatter coverage

The request ends with a `user` turn and contains no `assistant` turn for: Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Gemini, DashScope, Ollama (and DeepSeek / MiniMax, which share the OpenAI base formatter).

### Local verification evidence

- `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_base_memory_manager.py` + `tests/unit/agents/test_memory_middleware.py` + `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_auto_memory_recall_payload.py` + `tests/unit/app/chats/test_utils.py`: **131 passed**
- `black --line-length=79`, `flake8 --extend-ignore=E203`, `pylint` (repository pre-commit arguments): clean, **10.00/10**

### Regression tests added

`tests/unit/agents/memory/test_auto_memory_recall_payload.py` — four test functions, ten execution cases:

- `test_final_request_carries_the_recall_as_a_user_turn` (parametrized over the six QwenPaw formatter wrappers — Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Gemini, DashScope and Ollama): the request ends with a `user` turn carrying the recall, the recalled text itself is present, and there is no `assistant` turn;
- `test_recall_is_injected_and_reused_from_the_cache`: the recall is injected right after the user turn without touching the agent context, and the same turn then reuses the serialized cache instead of searching again — the reloaded message is compared against the original payload (same hint text, same block id);
- `test_recall_is_omitted_from_the_converted_transcript`: the real conversion path (`agentscope_msg_to_message`) drops the recall — exactly the user message and the normal reply remain;
- `test_next_user_turn_replaces_the_cached_recall` (parametrized over a second turn with fresh results and with no results): the stale evidence disappears either way.

The two middleware tests that this supersedes — `test_search_result_only_updates_current_model_input` and `test_new_turn_replaces_search_cache` — are removed: they patched the extraction step out, while the new test drives the real path. The tool-call follow-up test and all six formatter variants are kept.

## Changes

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/base_memory_manager.py` | carry the recall payload in a `HintBlock` instead of a text/thinking/tool_call/tool_result quartet |
| `src/qwenpaw/agents/middlewares.py` | `_is_auto_memory_recall_msg` helper; memory-extraction filter accepts the recall message |
| `src/qwenpaw/constant.py` | remove the now unused `AUTO_MEMORY_SEARCH_TEXT` / `_THINKING_PREFIX` |
| `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_auto_memory_recall_payload.py` | new regression tests (final request, conversion path, middleware injection path) |
| `tests/unit/agents/test_memory_middleware.py` | drop the two middleware tests that the new real-path test supersedes |

5 files, +345 / -127 lines. No new metadata flag and no renderer or frontend guard: the block type handles both, so the payload cannot reach a transcript even if a future channel renders messages directly.

prs.title: fix(cli): discover Ollama models before activation
prs.body:
## Description

The Ollama setup flow used by `qwenpaw init`, `qwenpaw models config` and `qwenpaw models set-llm` can prompt for a model name without first discovering the server's models. Even when `/v1/models` returns that model, activation rejects it because it has never been registered locally.

prs.title: fix(providers): honor thinking defaults and declared wire controls
prs.body:
## Description

Fix a mismatch between the thinking setting displayed by the Console and the parameters sent by OpenAI-compatible providers.

For a custom Chat Completions model declaring native effort control (`low`, `medium`, `xhigh`, supports off), saving the model default as off (`thinking_enabled=false`) currently has two effects:

1. An inherited request omits the default altogether, although the Console displays off.
2. An explicit off preference is incorrectly routed to compatibility flags because `_uses_compat_thinking_controls()` treats the presence of `thinking_enabled` as a protocol declaration. Changing a default must not change the wire protocol.

An explicit session preference also leaves stale `extra_body.chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking/reasoning_effort` values behind. A serving engine such as vLLM can give these template arguments precedence over the new request setting.

### Changes

- Apply the existing model-default hook before agent/session preferences.
- Serialize configured OpenAI model defaults through the same declared-control mapper used by explicit preferences.
- Share model-default interpretation between the display and provider construction paths; include configured budgets and nested chat-template settings.
- Honor an explicit model/provider wire declaration before the legacy compatibility fallback.
- Replace conflicting nested template controls when applying a higher-priority preference, preserving unrelated JSON and the original provider/model state.
- Add SDK-boundary regression tests for native and compatibility protocols, inherited defaults, reset/reload, and request isolation.

No model-name matching, global default change, frontend change, or database migration is introduced. Unsupported effort labels are not silently renamed.

**Related Issue:** No matching backend issue identified.

**Security Considerations:** Settings are resolved into request-local dictionaries. Tests verify that shared provider/model configuration is unchanged.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (providers, services)
- [x] Tests

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] I ran pre-commit on every changed file and it passes after committing auto-formatting changes
- [x] I ran the relevant tests locally and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (not needed for restoring existing behavior)

```

## Evidence

Validated on Windows with Python 3.12.3. Tests capture the final SDK Chat Completions arguments before transport; no remote model service is contacted.

Before the fix, the initial regression set reproduced **10 failures / 12 passes**, including missing `reasoning_effort` for an inherited off default and conflicting nested template arguments.

After the fix:

```text

| Model default | Request preference | Native Chat Completions request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| off | inherit | `reasoning_effort="none"` |
| off | off | `reasoning_effort="none"` |
| off | low / medium / xhigh | the selected `reasoning_effort` |
| unset | inherit | no new thinking parameter |

The full commands were attempted; this PR does not claim that they passed:

- Plain `pytest -q --maxfail=3 --tb=short` stopped during collection because both `tests/integration/test_backup.py` and `tests/unit/routers/test_backup.py` import as `test_backup`. Neither file is changed here.

## Additional Notes

The native off mapping uses the existing `reasoning_effort="none"` contract, not a vLLM-specific model-name exception. vLLM 0.28.0 documents automatic `enable_thinking=false` for this value: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.28.0/features/reasoning_outputs/#automatic-enable_thinking-activation

prs.title: feat(website): add JSON-driven evaluation index
prs.body:
## Description

Add a bilingual evaluation leaderboard at `/evaluation/` with a shared SVG cost/performance chart, dashed Pareto frontier, SDK history, downloadable records and concise benchmark setup notes. Points render without a plotting-library download; details appear on hover or keyboard focus. The public page displays reviewed official results.

The website accepts a strict v1 aggregate publication contract. Three compact QwenPaw default-mode files cover 12 benchmark observations and 3,645 tasks, replacing 60,141 lines of per-task JSON with 525 lines of summaries. Internal task identities, trajectories and private evidence remain outside the website. Summary metadata retains release/artifact identity, budgets, benchmark revisions, judge configuration, confirmed costs, coverage and elapsed time.

The default view selects GAIA, SpreadsheetBench Verified, SWE-bench Verified and PawBench at 25% each. Users can edit the selected benchmarks and relative weights in an anchored desktop panel or mobile sheet; applying a draft updates scores, costs, runtimes, rankings and the frontier together. Restore-preset and cancel preserve predictable behavior, and custom weighting is visibly identified. Missing selected benchmarks remain incomplete, rather than receiving a different weighting per record.

Execution/scoring exceptions count as zero. Each benchmark's confirmed model and judge spending is divided by its full task count, with coverage retained; CNY amounts use the fixed rate of 7 CNY per USD. Runtime averages use recorded task durations. Public inputs retain the reviewed QwenPaw 2.2.2 cohort across qwen3.8-max, glm-5.2 and deepseek-v4-pro; the DeepSeek cohort reuses the release-equivalent evaluation with its original artifact digest, scores and timestamps. PawBench notes identify the qwen3.8-max judge and the official published Claude Opus 4.6 judge.

Run IDs include the profile fingerprint and are checked for uniqueness. Scoring-version options and details include the version ID; mobile English chart titles wrap, and cancelled StrictMode requests cannot overwrite loading or data state. These changes affect website/reporting behavior, not QwenPaw agent execution.

## Validation

- Website production build, `format:check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- All 12 benchmark summaries were checked against 3,645 original tasks for scores, failure counts, model/judge spending and coverage.
- Regression fixtures produce four unique detail IDs for two profiles × two scoring versions; selecting an 80-point record opens the 80-point detail.
- Arithmetic checks cover the 25% preset, custom 60/40 score/cost/runtime, and missing benchmark coverage.
- Browser checks cover bilingual controls, draft/cancel/apply/reset, invalid weights, focus restoration, 375px/320px sheets, wrapping titles and delayed StrictMode detail loading.

## Security Considerations

CI validation uses read-only permissions and no secrets. Publication summaries contain no OSS links, credentials, trajectories, internal snapshots or private harness observations.

prs.title: fix(models): honor conversation model settings across runtime paths
prs.body:
## Description

After a conversation switches from model M1 to M2, standalone `/compact` still builds its temporary agent from M1's persisted agent defaults. Normal messages resolve the conversation override through `AgentBuilder`, but slash-command dispatch bypasses that builder.

This change shares model-override parsing, conversation selection, and model-owned thinking resolution across the affected paths:

- Scroll and native `/compact` use the conversation/request model and share one resolved configuration snapshot with their system prompt.
- `/history` context limits, chat titles, `/model` display, and model-list active markers follow the same selection. Explicit request overrides are resolved before model validation and thinking lookup.
- Media capability checks and probes read the executing model, including its active fallback. The model context is isolated per task and reset before stream events are yielded, including cancellation and cross-task stream closure.
- Token-recording wrappers expose the same `model_key` identity as retry wrappers, including Hub models. Invalid override values are sanitized before logging.
- Spawned subagents and their automatic titles resolve parent conversation settings using the carried parent owner and channel, including Console native payloads. Explicit subagent models use the parent conversation's thinking preference for that model. Ordinary requests use their own conversation settings, and titles are persisted to the current child chat. Missing parents follow the same model/thinking defaults as execution.
- `/model` switching/resetting continues to update agent defaults and explains when a conversation override remains active.
- English and Chinese command, Console, and context-management documentation describe model scope, precedence, compaction, titles, and media capabilities.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8464

**Security Considerations:** Compaction and title generation now honor the selected conversation/request provider instead of silently using the agent-default provider. Conversation settings do not mutate agent defaults, and media model context is isolated across concurrent requests.

prs.title: fix(agents): avoid importing whisper in local whisper status probe
prs.body:
## Description

`check_local_whisper_available()` decided whether the optional `whisper` dependency is installed by importing it:

```python
try:
    import whisper as _whisper  # noqa: F401
    whisper_ok = True
except ImportError:
    pass
```

Importing `whisper` loads `torch` plus the CUDA runtime (`libtorch_cuda`, `libcublasLt`, `libnvrtc`, `libnvJitLink`), `librosa` → `numba`/`llvmlite`, and `tiktoken`. Measured cost of a single call: **+690 MB RSS** (163 MB → 853 MB), and module imports are permanent, so the server keeps the memory until restart.

This probe backs `GET /api/workspace/local-whisper-status`, which the Console requests unconditionally when the Voice Transcription settings page mounts — even when the configured provider is a remote Whisper API. One page visit therefore raised an otherwise idle `qwenpaw app` process to ~1.9 GB PSS in the reported instance.

This PR resolves the module with `importlib.util.find_spec()` instead. It answers the same question via a file-system lookup (+0 MB, ~4 ms). A broken install now reads as "installed" and fails later, but `_transcribe_local_whisper()` already imports whisper for real and logs any failure as a warning, so no behaviour is lost on the transcription path.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8490

**Security Considerations:** none — read-only dependency probe, no new inputs or config surface.

prs.title: feat(memory): allow a separate model for ReMeLight memory writing
prs.body:
## Description

`ReMeLightMemoryManager` currently injects the agent's main model into ReMe's `as_llm` component before every memory-writing job (`auto_memory` / `auto_dream` / `daily_paper` / `auto_fin`), so memory writing always consumes the same (often expensive) model used for chatting.

This PR adds an optional `memory_model` slot to `reme_light_memory_config`, so memory writing can run on an independent, lighter model:

- Uses `{"provider_id": "...", "model": "..."}` as the canonical format; a string is treated as a bare model name that inherits the main model's provider, including version-tagged names such as `qwen2.5:7b`.
- When unset, behavior is unchanged (main model is used).
- If dedicated-model construction fails (including non-`ProviderError` SDK exceptions), the manager logs a warning and injects the usable main model. Runtime failures before output can also fall back to that model. Main-model failures still propagate. Image jobs exclude the main-model fallback unless it has confirmed image support.
- The injected model is refreshed before every LLM job, so config changes take effect without a restart.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7664

**Security Considerations:** `memory_model` stores only a provider/model reference; no credentials are written to `agent.json` (API keys stay in the provider store).

prs.title: fix(plugins): do not abort a plugin install when invalidate_caches fails
prs.body:
## Description

The plugin loader called `importlib.invalidate_caches()` unconditionally. On Python builds where that stdlib call itself raises (the issue shows `TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'` on a distro-patched 3.11), the exception aborted the whole plugin install or hot-update. Refreshing import caches is best effort, so a failure should not be fatal.

After the merge with the rewritten loader on `main`, the remaining calls (`_publish_plugin_site_path()` in `loader.py`, plus `clear_plugin_bytecode()` and `PluginNamespaceFinder.register()` in `module_isolation.py`) go through `_invalidate_import_caches()` in `module_isolation.py`, which catches the error and logs it at debug level.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8265

**Security Considerations:** None

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Tests

## Checklist

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes (I ran `black -l 79 --check` on the three changed files only)
- [x] I ran tests locally: `tests/unit/plugins/test_loader_helpers.py`, the four new `TestInvalidateImportCaches` tests fail without the change and pass with it. Three existing tests in that file (`test_symlink_escape_rejected`, `test_catalog_waits_for_default_hubs`, `test_hub_config_rebuild_replaces_provider`) also fail on my Windows machine on `main`; they are unrelated to this change.
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed): not needed
- [ ] Ready for review

## Evidence

Behavior before the change: when `importlib.invalidate_caches` raises (the `TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'` from #8265), the exception escaped `PluginLoader` and aborted the plugin install / hot-update.

Behavior after the change: the new tests in `tests/unit/plugins/test_loader_helpers.py` patch `importlib.invalidate_caches` to raise `TypeError`; the helper, `_publish_plugin_site_path()` and `PluginNamespaceFinder.register()` now complete with the error logged at debug level. The tests fail on the base commit with the raised `TypeError` and pass with this change (run locally with `pytest tests/unit/plugins/test_loader_helpers.py`).

## Description

Scroll summary requests can fail with HTTP 400 on OpenAI-compatible providers when a model card sets `generate_kwargs.max_tokens`: AgentScope 2.0.10 injects `max_completion_tokens` while Scroll also passes `max_tokens`. Per-call summary limits now also override configured defaults for GPT and o-series models.

Make Scroll's continuation-summary timeout configurable with `running.light_context_config.scroll_config.summary_timeout_seconds`, and increase the default from 60 to 300 seconds for slow reasoning models. prs.title: perf(history): reuse workspace-owned SQLite connections
prs.body:
## Description

Each request builds a new agent and previously opened a separate SQLite history connection. Although main caches successful `quick_check` results, repeated connection initialization still performs schema setup and attempts an FTS integrity check.

Move HistoryStore ownership to Workspace's existing ServiceManager. Requests share the workspace connection while retaining separate context managers and session bookkeeping.

- Inject the shared store through AgentBuilder; standalone callers retain ownership of their connections.
- Reuse the store across compatible reloads, checking both the configured path and database file identity.
- Preserve outgoing requests when a reload changes the history path or disables Scroll.
- Release borrowed connections on request cleanup, wiring failure, or abandoned builds.
- Defer final connection closure until outstanding borrowers release it. Report incomplete shutdown so callers cannot treat an active database as closed.
- Recreate previously absent optional services when configuration enables them.

Relates to #7639 and #7930.

## Type of Change

- [x] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Tests

## Testing

Focused lifecycle regressions cover connection reuse across requests, compatible and incompatible reloads, discarded reload candidates, shutdown with an active borrower, cancelled construction, and failed component wiring.

Existing context, persistence, cancellation, workspace lifecycle, and reload regressions were also run.

## Evidence

- Related regression suite: **750 passed**.
- After refining the wiring-failure regression to fail after acquiring the shared store: **8 passed** in the affected test file.
- All applicable commit-time pre-commit hooks passed, including AST, Mypy, Black, Flake8, and Pylint.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Additional Notes

This change retains the existing connection lock and worker-based persistence. It does not introduce a connection pool or move durable writes into fire-and-forget tasks.

Retention scheduling and transaction batching remain separate follow-up work. Database replacement still requires stopping its writers first. Production latency improvements have not yet been benchmarked.

prs.title: feat(console): browse memory files by tags
prs.body:
## Description

Memory tags were shown as raw frontmatter values and could not be used to browse related memories. Add clickable preview tags and a Tags tab for agents using ReMe Light, with indexed file counts, recent-file ordering, and pagination.

- Read the existing ReMe tag index and file catalog through the memory-action lifecycle lease, without LLM calls or semantic search. Ordinary queries use the tag index; canonical tags expanded beyond ReMe 0.4.2.0's source-length limit are matched against catalog metadata without reading file bodies.
- Resolve Workspace, Daily, Digest, and legacy memory file aliases in one editor-opening path. Reuse dirty buffers in both directions, follow the server's legacy digest-prefix and Markdown-suffix rules, honor custom memory directories, and preserve project-root isolation. Retry failed configuration reads while keeping exact open tabs usable.
- Render one preview tag row from resolved YAML, including merge keys, quoted keys, and duplicate keys. Preserve PyYAML scalar and Unicode casefold behavior with 18 shared frontend/backend contract fixtures.
- Hide tag navigation for unsupported backends, discard stale agent responses, refresh on focus, and offer retry after index failures.
- Document indexed search scope in English and Chinese and keep navigation usable in narrow layouts.

**Security considerations:** Endpoints are read-only, resolve the requested agent through the existing manager, and accept tag names rather than filesystem paths.

## Latest review fixes

- **P1 — legacy digest identity:** normalize directory separators before extracting the configured digest basename, including Windows backslashes, trailing separators, and mixed separators in nested directories. With `daily_dir=notes\daily` and `digest_dir=notes\knowledge`, `memory::knowledge/note.md` resolves to `notes/knowledge/note.md`; opening the separate `notes/daily/knowledge/note.md` creates its own buffer. Reopening the actual Digest file preserves the dirty legacy buffer and its original save route. Default directories and the server's automatic `.md` suffix remain covered.
- **P2 — configuration recovery:** discard rejected configuration promises so another file click can retry, and prevent a late aborted request from discarding a newer request. If configuration is unavailable, reuse an exact existing tab; without an exact match, keep the operation retryable rather than creating a potentially conflicting buffer.
- Use the same decoded tab identity for tag-result highlighting, loading, saving, and downloading, including persisted tabs without optional source/root metadata. Legacy digest tabs now highlight the actual Digest result instead of a Daily namesake.

## Validation

Validation of `f0bd08915` on 2026-10-29:

- Five additional Windows regression cases failed before the fix and pass afterward. They cover backslash directories, trailing and mixed separators, bidirectional alias reuse, separation from a distinct Daily file, dirty-buffer preservation, and the original save route.
- Frontend: file identity, configuration recovery, FilesWorkspace, MemoryTagsNavigator, FilesNavigator interactions, FilesDrawer, memory tree, FilePreview, memory-tag parsing, and agents API suites — **10 files / 193 tests passed**.
- Changed frontend files pass ESLint, Prettier, and `git diff --check`.
- `npm run build` passed TypeScript, the production Console build, Monaco CSS validation, asset precompression, and initial-bundle verification.
- This correction changes frontend identity normalization only. Backend tests and the earlier manual browser checks were not rerun; no Windows machine or conflicting-file disk-write validation was performed.

Validation of `29d58b4fc` on 2026-10-28, before the Windows directory correction:

- Backend: `pytest tests/unit/agents/memory tests/unit/app/routers/test_agents_router.py tests/integration/test_reme_tags_contract.py -q --disable-warnings` — **382 passed**, including real `reme-ai==0.4.2.0` offline integration. One existing proactive-trigger test warning. Used a temporary virtual environment; existing conda dependencies were unchanged.
- Frontend: affected Files workspace, project-directory, FilePreview, TabbedEditor, memory-tag parser, and agents API suites — **26 files / 336 tests passed**. Added regressions cover legacy default/custom/nested directories, optional metadata, `.md` suffixes, correct save routing, selected-result identity, shared retries, stale failures, exact-tab fallback, and repeated-click recovery without losing unsaved content.
- `npm run build` passed TypeScript, production Console build, Monaco CSS validation, asset precompression, and initial-bundle verification. All changed frontend files pass ESLint and Prettier; changed-file pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

Manual browser acceptance used the production Console with a real isolated API and disposable files:

1. Restored a persisted `memory::digest/note.md` tab without optional metadata and added `BROWSER-UNSAVED-8470` in the editor. Opening `memory/digest/note.md` through Workspace opened a separate tab showing **Daily namesake**. Opening `digest/note.md` reused the original tab and retained the unsaved marker; the total remained two tabs.
2. Saved the legacy tab in the browser and checked both files on disk: only `digest/note.md` received the marker; `memory/digest/note.md` retained its original content. Reloaded the final production build, followed the Orion tag result back to the same legacy buffer, and verified that only **Digest actual** had `aria-current=true`.
3. Injected a temporary 503 on the agent configuration endpoint. Opening an ordinary `retry.md` file failed safely. Restored the endpoint and clicked the same file again without reloading or refocusing; the file opened with **Configuration recovered.** The proxy recorded configuration responses **503 → 503 → 200**.

The full repository suite was not rerun. Browser checks used default memory directories; custom and nested directory behavior is covered by regression tests.

issues.body:
## Problem

The interactive `zeptoclaw agent` output looks broken (screenshot from a DeepSeek session: a stuck "Thinking..." line, two empty separator rules, an unindented reply).

Root causes found in `src/cli/agent.rs` / `src/cli/shimmer.rs`:

1. **Spinner races the reply.** `ShimmerSpinner::stop()` only flags a background task. The final line-clear runs later, so it erases whatever line the reply has moved onto, and the "Thinking..." frame stays on screen.
2. **Feedback is rendered out of order.** Tool feedback is drawn by a separately spawned task while the reply is printed by the main task. Nothing orders the two.
3. **Duplicate separators.** The streaming path emits `ToolFeedbackPhase::ResponseReady` twice (`loop.rs` ~2788 and ~2813). `had_tools` is never reset between turns, so after any turn that used a tool, every later reply gets two `────` rules.
4. **No layout.** The reply is printed raw at column 0 with no wrapping. Markdown is shown as raw `**`/``` text. Interactive mode has no per-turn footer (only `-m` mode prints one). The prompt is a bare `> `.
5. **Approval prompts collide with the spinner.** The y/N prompt is printed while the spinner keeps animating.
6. `format_tool_failed` slices `&error[..80]` by bytes, which panics on a multi-byte character at the boundary.

## Goal

A polished, line-based (scrollback-friendly, not full-screen TUI) chat UI with no new heavyweight dependencies. Binary size stays within budget; `unicode-width` is already in the dependency tree via rustyline.

- One render path: feedback and the reply are drawn by the same task, in order. The spinner stops synchronously and clears its own line.
- Live status line: spinner + "Thinking…" or the running tool name + elapsed time. Completed tools become permanent `✓ tool → hint · 12ms` / `✗` lines.
- Reply indented and word-wrapped to the terminal width, with light markdown: headings, bold/italic, inline code, bullets/numbers, fenced code blocks, quotes, rules, links. Works for both streaming and non-streaming.
- Per-turn footer: `model · tokens · tools · time`.
- Banner and accent prompt; approval prompt pauses the spinner and is formatted to match.
- Plain output when stdout is not a TTY (pipes, `-m` into files), and `NO_COLOR` / `TERM=dumb` respected.

issues.body:
## Problem

The mandatory pre-push checklist (CLAUDE.md, `.git/hooks/pre-push`) is:

```
cargo fmt && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo nextest run --lib && cargo test --doc && cargo fmt -- --check
```

None of these steps compile integration tests (`tests/*.rs`). With GitHub Actions CI removed (#699/#700), nothing does.

This let a real break land on main: #712 added fields to `providers::Usage`, and the struct literals in `tests/e2e.rs` stopped compiling. It went unnoticed until #714 fixed it in a separate commit.

Separately, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` currently fails on main with pre-existing lints in test code (`context_monitor.rs`, `loop.rs`, `api/routes/ws.rs`, `kernel/gate.rs`), so it cannot simply be switched on.

## Proposal

1. Add `cargo check --tests` (and `--features panel` where relevant) to the checklist and pre-push hook. This is compile-only, so it's cheap compared with running the suites.
2. Optionally fix the existing `--all-targets` clippy lints, then move the clippy step to `--all-targets`.
3. Update CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / `docs/claude/testing.md` to match.

issues.body:
## Problem

`tests/cli_smoke.rs` runs the real binary (`run_cli`) without isolating its config, so it reads the developer's actual `~/.zeptoclaw/config.json`. Local settings then decide whether the tests pass.

Observed while validating #714: four tests exit 1 instead of 0:

- `cli_auth_status`
- `cli_heartbeat_show`
- `cli_skills_list`
- `cli_skills_list_all`

The local config has a private-network `providers.openai.api_base`, which the endpoint safety check rejects, so every command that loads config fails:

```
Failed to load configuration: Configuration error: Invalid endpoint configuration at providers.openai.api_base: Endpoint targets local/private network. ...
```

`zeptoclaw heartbeat --show` reproduces it directly.

## Proposal

Have `run_cli` point the binary at a fresh temp home/config dir (e.g. `HOME` / `ZEPTOCLAW_*` dir overrides to a `tempfile::TempDir`), and clear inherited `ZEPTOCLAW_*` env vars, so smoke tests never see the developer's real config, skills or workspace.

## Acceptance

`cargo nextest run --test cli_smoke` passes regardless of what is in `~/.zeptoclaw/`.
