issues.body:
## Problem

`zeptoclaw serve` (`src/cli/serve.rs`) exposes `POST /v1/chat/completions` and `GET /v1/models` with no authentication at all. The module doc says so: "No panel UI, no auth middleware — intended for local or trusted-network use."

The default bind is `127.0.0.1`, but nothing stops `--bind 0.0.0.0`. Once bound off-loopback, anyone who can reach the port can:

- spend the operator's provider credits: the route is a pass-through to the configured provider chain, using the operator's API keys
- pick any model the provider accepts, with any `max_tokens`, at any rate (no rate limiting)
- enumerate configured models via `/v1/models`

Nothing warns at startup when it binds to a non-loopback address without auth.

For comparison, the panel server (`src/api/server.rs`) mounts the same `/v1/*` routes behind `auth_middleware`, which requires a Bearer token and skips only CSRF for `/v1/`. That router also applies a 1 MiB `DefaultBodyLimit`, which `serve` lacks. So the gap is specific to the standalone `serve` command.

Minor: the comment in `server.rs` ("auth skipped by auth_middleware for /v1/ prefix") is stale. Only CSRF is skipped; the middleware regression test confirms `/v1/` requires Bearer auth.

## Proposal

1. Add an optional bearer token: `--api-key` / `ZEPTOCLAW_SERVE_API_KEY`, checked with a constant-time comparison on every `/v1/*` request (`401` + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` otherwise). OpenAI clients already send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
2. Fail closed off-loopback: refuse to start when `--bind` is not a loopback address and no key is set, unless the operator passes an explicit `--insecure-no-auth`.
3. Apply the same 1 MiB `DefaultBodyLimit` the panel router uses (shared constant).
4. Optionally reuse `SlidingWindowRateLimiter` per peer IP, as panel login does.
5. Fix the stale comment in `server.rs`.

## Acceptance

- Tests: no key + loopback serves as today; key set → missing/wrong token is 401, correct token is 200; non-loopback bind without key and without `--insecure-no-auth` errors at startup.
- `docs/claude/commands.md` and CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md describe the new flags.

prs.title: fix(serve): require an API key for the OpenAI-compatible serve API
prs.body:
## Summary

- `zeptoclaw serve` exposed `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/models` with no authentication. A non-loopback `--bind` let anyone reaching the port spend the operator's provider credits with any model at any rate. With `ZEPTOCLAW_SERVE_API_KEY` or `--api-key` set, every `/v1/*` request now needs `Authorization: Bearer <key>`: constant-time compare, and an OpenAI-style `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` otherwise. Blank keys count as unset.
- Fail closed off-loopback: without a key, `serve` refuses to start on a non-loopback bind unless `--insecure-no-auth` is passed, and logs a warning when it is. The default `127.0.0.1` bind with no key behaves exactly as before.
- Applies the panel's 1 MiB body limit, now a shared `api::server::API_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`. The router and bind guard live in the new `api::serve` module, so they are unit-tested; `cli/serve.rs` is a thin wrapper. The key is read from the env by hand, because clap's `env` feature isn't enabled and adding it isn't worth the binary size.
- Fixes the stale `server.rs` comment: the panel's own `/v1/*` routes already require its Bearer token and skip only CSRF.
- Separate commit: fixes `tests/e2e.rs`, which stopped compiling after #712 added fields to `Usage`. The lib-only checklist doesn't build integration tests, so it slipped through.

Not included: per-IP rate limiting (optional in the issue); can follow if wanted.

## Related Issue

Closes #713

## Pre-submit Checklist

- [x] I branched from `upstream/main`
- [x] This PR contains only commits related to this change (plus the e2e compile fix from #712, as its own commit)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` passes
- [x] `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` passes (default and `--features panel`)
- [x] `cargo nextest run --lib` passes
- [x] I added or updated tests for my changes
- [x] New constants/limits are shared (not duplicated across files)
- [x] No new dependencies unless necessary (we target ~6 MB binary)

## Security Considerations

- Untrusted input: the `Authorization` header is compared in constant time (`api::auth::constant_time_eq`, `subtle`). Bodies are capped at 1 MiB.
- Network listener: auth is on whenever a key is set. An unauthenticated non-loopback listener now requires an explicit `--insecure-no-auth`. `localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8` and `::1` / `[::1]` count as loopback; hostnames and anything unparsable count as non-loopback (fail closed).
- Secrets: the key is never logged. The `--api-key` help text recommends the env var, since flags are visible in `ps`.

## Test Plan

- `cargo nextest run --lib --features panel`: 3826 passed, 6 skipped (8 new tests in `api::serve`)
- `cargo nextest run --lib`: 3615 passed, 6 skipped
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy --features panel -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt -- --check` clean
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test --doc`: 133 passed, 27 ignored
- `cargo nextest run --features panel --test e2e` builds and passes again. 4 `cli_smoke` tests (`auth status`, `heartbeat show`, `skills list`, `skills list --all`) exit 1 locally because the smoke tests read the real `~/.zeptoclaw/config.json`, whose `providers.openai.api_base` is a private-network URL that the endpoint safety check rejects (`heartbeat --show` reproduces it directly). Not caused by this PR.
- New tests:
  - loopback detection
  - non-loopback refusal without a key
  - allow on loopback / key / opt-out
  - key resolution (flag over env, blank ignored)
  - no key → 200
  - missing / wrong / non-Bearer tokens → 401 with `WWW-Authenticate`
  - correct token → 200
  - oversized body → 413

issues.title: perf(runtime): activating a deferred tool via tool_search changes the system prompt and busts the prompt cache

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: runtime
labels.description: Auto scope: src/runtime/** changed.

labels.name: agent:prompt
labels.description: Manual prompt, context, and response guidance across agent/channel/memory/provider/runtime.

issues.body:
**Affected component:** runtime/daemon (the `Agent` turn path used by ZeroCode and gateway WS)
**Severity:** S3 - minor issue (cost; only with `mcp.deferred_loading = true`)

### Current behavior

With deferred MCP loading on, activating a tool through `tool_search` changes the system prompt on the next turn. That invalidates the provider prompt cache for the whole conversation, once per activation.

Code path, read on `origin/master` @ `f12da7462a0f`:

- `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/agent.rs:Agent::build_system_prompt_with_dispatcher_and_cap` appends `ToolSearchTool::deferred_prompt_section()` to the system prompt. That function runs on every turn through `rebuild_system_prompt_for_dispatcher`, which is the same rebuild #11696 describes.
- `crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/tool_search.rs:ToolSearchTool::deferred_prompt_section` passes the currently activated tool names as the exclude set to `mcp_deferred::build_deferred_tools_section_excluding`.
- So the `<available-deferred-tools>` list shrinks each time a tool is activated. The system prompt heads the cached prefix, so the next request re-bills the full conversation.

This is the same class of problem as #11696, but a separate trigger. #11698 freezes only the personality-file section, so this one stays.

### Expected behavior

Activating a deferred tool shouldn't change the cached system prefix. The tool's schema already reaches the model through the per-request tool specs (`agent/turn/tool_specs.rs` rebuilds them each iteration "so newly activated deferred tools appear"), so the system prompt doesn't need to drop the tool from the advertised list.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# 1. [mcp] deferred_loading = true, with at least one MCP server exposing several tools.
# 2. Open a ZeroCode session; run a few turns until requests are ~fully cached.
# 3. Ask the agent to call tool_search with "select:<one deferred tool>".
# 4. Send the next message: its first request reports cached_input_tokens ≈ only the
#    part before the system prompt's deferred section, and is billed at full input rate.
```

### Options (not choosing one)

1. **Keep the advertised list fixed per session.** Render it once, including tools that are later activated, and let the tool specs say what's loaded. That means no misses. The cost: the prompt's "NOT yet loaded" wording becomes inaccurate for activated tools, so the wording would need to change (for example, "may need `tool_search` first").
2. **Move the deferred list out of the system prompt** to the end of the request or into the tool-spec channel, where a change doesn't invalidate the earlier prefix. This keeps accuracy. It's a bigger change, and placement interacts with the provider cache breakpoints.
3. **Leave it as is and document it** as one accepted miss per activation. That's cheap if activations are rare.

### Impact

- Affected: sessions with `mcp.deferred_loading = true`. It's off by default (`default_deferred_loading() -> false`).
- Frequency: once per activation, per session.
- Consequence: one full-price request per activation, the same order of cost as #11696's per-edit miss.

Related: #11696 (same rebuild, personality files), #11698 (its fix), #8321 (cache policy for volatile context).

### ZeroClaw version

Read on `origin/master` @ `f12da7462a0f`. I found this from the code while fixing #11696, not from a measured miss. Our own deployment runs with deferred loading off.

### Operating system

macOS (Apple Silicon)

### Regression?

Unknown

### Pre-flight checks

- [x] Code path read on latest master.
- [x] Secrets, tokens and personal data redacted.

issues.body:
### Which RFC trigger does this meet?

Capability boundary: a new subsystem or project-wide capability boundary

### Problem

The agent should be able to answer from **documents the operator keeps**, language and tool
documentation, OS references, security standards, container/command references, this project's own docs,
UI and architecture books, internal runbooks,  and from documents that arrive over time (chat uploads,
fetched pages, a cloned repo's `docs/`). Today it can but not in a fast and proper RAG way.

What exists is two unrelated things, neither of which is this:

- `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rag/mod.rs` — module doc at `:1` says "RAG pipeline for hardware datasheet
  retrieval". `HardwareRag { chunks: Vec<DatasheetChunk>, … }` (`:113-117`) is an **in-RAM vector with no
  persistence**; `load()` reads only `.md`/`.txt` from the directory named by `[hardware].datasheet_dir`
  (`crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs:7582`) with `max_tokens = 512` hardcoded (`:137`); `retrieve()`
  (`:210-244`) scores by substring `contains()` (`:227`) — no embeddings, no vector search, no text index.
- The memory plane (`zeroclaw-memory`): embeddings + FTS5 + cosine over the agent's **own stored
  memories**, reached through `RetrievalPipeline { memory: Arc<dyn Memory> }`
  (`crates/zeroclaw-memory/src/retrieval.rs:100-122`).

The gap has a measurable cost, not just a conceptual one. Verified defaults: 512-token chunks, 1536
embedding dimensions (`schema.rs:13005-13007`), f32 → **6,144 bytes per vector**. A 1,000-page technical
book is ~1,300 chunks.

| corpus | chunks | vector bytes | cost per query today |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 book | ~1,300 | ~8 MB | fine |
| 10 doc sets | ~13,000 | ~80 MB | slow |
| ~50 doc sets (the case above) | ~65,000 | **~400 MB** | unusable |

Because the current vector path is a full scan — `sqlite.rs:909` issues
`SELECT id, embedding FROM memories WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL` and computes cosine per row
(`:957-968`), with no ANN index anywhere in the repo — that whole blob is read and deserialized **per
query**.

Also relevant: `docs-extract` and `knowledge_document` are cited in AGENTS.md as examples of default-off
gated features, but **no such feature exists in the root `Cargo.toml` or any `crates/*/Cargo.toml`**. There
is no document corpus lane to extend.

### Proposal

Create a **knowledge corpus plane** — a third plane next to agent memory and the hardware datasheet
matcher — with two governing properties:

1. **It is not a `memory.backend`.** The `Memory` trait
   (`crates/zeroclaw-api/src/memory_traits.rs:304-570`) is a memory-management contract: agent-scoped
   families, session/namespace purge, `rename_agent`, `supersede`, GDPR-shaped
   `ExportFilter`/`export_for_principal`, and a nine-method `*_for_principal` private-memory family whose
   defaults **`bail!`** by design (`:380-383`, "The defaults FAIL CLOSED"). Documents must not be decayed,
   deduplicated, consolidated, importance-scored, or session-purged, and a corpus backend must not pretend
   to implement that surface.
2. **The files are the source of truth; the index is derived and rebuildable.** That keeps the corpus out
   of #9103's "second authoritative store" problem — provided the spec holds that line. If a deployment
   ingests documents and discards the originals, it has built an authoritative store and the full #9103
   owner/erasure/migration requirement returns.

The plane decomposes into four store-independent traits plus one config unit:

```
Source     → (identity, media-type, bytes-or-path, version-token)
             fs tree · explicit paths · git ref · channel upload · HTTP fetch
Extractor  → media-type → text, out of process, default-off gate per type
Index      → upsert · search(query, filter, top_k) · delete_by_source · rebuild
             sqlite+FTS5 (first) · ANN engine (measured later) · LanceDB (see Design sketch)
Surface    → knowledge_search(query, collection, top_k, since?) → cited chunks
```

`Collection` is the config unit that makes this general — a new use case must be a config stanza, never a
new module. If a use case needs a new module, the seam is wrong; that is the test this design has to pass:

```toml
[[knowledge.collection]]
name = "rust-docs"
paths = ["~/docs/rust"]            # resolved through the existing tool path policy
include = ["**/*.md"]
chunk_tokens = 512                  # configurable; no hardcoded 512
embedder = "custom:http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1"   # per collection; local by default
backend = "sqlite"                  # "lancedb" once its gate clears
visibility = ["agent:main"]         # ACL scope
```

**Decisions already recorded with the proposer (2026-09-28):** untrusted sources (channel uploads, fetched
pages) are in scope for the PDF slice, which makes extractor sandboxing mandatory there; OCR is
out-of-process `tesseract`; local embeddings are the documented default; the support owner is `@ConYel`
(details under Risks).

### Design sketch

### Affected surfaces

New: `[knowledge]` config section (`zeroclaw-config`), corpus tables + `Index` seam (new crate or
`zeroclaw-memory` module — decision for the implementation PR), `knowledge_search` tool registered through
the canonical `ToolRegistry::builtin()` path (`zeroclaw-tools`), docs/book chapter, release-note entries.
Untouched: `memory.backend` and the `Memory` trait, `[hardware].datasheet_dir` and `HardwareRag`.

### Ingestion and trust tiers (the Qubes part)

Qubes PDF Converter renders **each page into an RGB bitmap inside a DisposableVM**, sends only bitmaps
across qrexec, and rebuilds a new PDF in the client qube. The useful insight — and the trap:

- **The security property comes from the VM, not from the pictures.** Rasterising a page still requires a
  PDF parser to interpret the file; Qubes' safety is that the parser runs in a machine that is thrown away
  and has no path to real data. Converting to images in-process on the host keeps the entire parser attack
  surface and gains nothing.
- It is also the wrong default shape for RAG: the output is an
  **image-only PDF with no text layer**, so every document would need OCR — re-deriving by inference what
  arrived as exact characters. Code listings, tables, identifiers and ligatures degrade, at per-page model
  cost across the whole shelf.

But ZeroClaw already has the containment primitive that makes the useful part available:
`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/security/traits.rs:7` defines

```rust
pub trait Sandbox: Send + Sync {
    fn wrap_command(&self, cmd: &mut std::process::Command) -> std::io::Result<()>;
    fn is_available(&self) -> bool;
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    …
}
```

with implementations at `security/bubblewrap.rs`, `security/firejail.rs`, `security/landlock.rs`
(`sandbox-landlock`), `security/seatbelt.rs`, `security/docker.rs`. So the Qubes idea lands as
**isolation tiers on the extractor**, not as a default image round-trip:

| tier | input | extraction |
|---|---|---|
| T0 | operator-owned paths (`trust = "owner"`) | `pdftotext` unsandboxed is defensible: the operator already controls those bytes |
| T1 | anything that arrived from elsewhere: channel upload, HTTP fetch, third-party docs | `pdftotext` / `pdftoppm` **under `Sandbox::wrap_command`**, chosen by `is_available()`, with the active `name()` recorded in the ingest report |
| T2 | T1 + `sanitize = true`, or no parser available on host | render pages → OCR only. Qubes-shaped, still sandboxed, accepted cost: lossy text |

No sandbox ⇒ T1 collections **refuse to ingest and say so**, rather than degrading silently. That is the
same fail-closed discipline as #11209/#11208, applied to ingestion.

### Security requirements (spec, not follow-ups)

**Path authority — highest severity.** Tool path enforcement is **not inside the tools**:
`crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/file_edit.rs:134-136` states "Rate limiting and path-allowlist checks are
applied by the `RateLimitedTool` + `PathGuardedTool` wrappers at registration time", with resolution in
`crates/zeroclaw-config/src/policy.rs:4471` (`resolve_tool_path`). A corpus indexer that walks the
filesystem itself therefore sits **outside every path control the agent's file tools are inside of** — a
read-any-file primitive wearing a retrieval feature as a costume. Requirement: `Source` resolves through
`resolve_tool_path`/the same policy, and `knowledge_search` registers behind
`PathGuardedTool`/`RateLimitedTool` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs:124`).

**Untrusted content screening.** Retrieved document text enters the prompt. The repo already has the
canonical handling: `crates/zeroclaw-memory/src/scanned.rs:1-8` — `ScannedMemory` is a "transparent
decorator applied to every backend by the memory factory", enforcing `[memory.policy]` at the write **and**
read boundaries — and `threat.rs:1-8` lists patterns including "instructions that rewrite agent
instruction files". The corpus must pass through the same screen and the same read-boundary policy. A
corpus that skips this is a file-drop route into the prompt, which is easier to exploit than a channel
message.

**Secrets must not persist into a derived index.** `redact.rs:1-7` rewrites configured categories to
`[REDACTED:<category>]` before content is persisted when `[memory.policy].redact_on_write` is on. Apply it
to corpus tables, and apply the existing `sqlite_permissions` handling to the corpus DB file, or the index
becomes an unpermissioned secret copy sitting next to the memory DB. Developer libraries contain
`.env`-adjacent files and copy-pasted tokens.

**Embedder route is an exfiltration decision, per collection — local is the default (recorded decision).**
Embedding ships plaintext to whoever serves the provider. `"openai"`/`"openrouter"`
(`embeddings.rs:202-219`) leave the machine; `custom:<base_url>` (`:220-224`) can be local and adds
**zero dependencies**. Local is the documented default; a remote provider is an explicit per-collection
opt-in that emits "content from this collection is sent to `<host>`" at config validation. With no
embedder configured, the collection works keyword-only over FTS5 with a loud startup note — cosine over
`NoopEmbedding` is 0 for every row (`sqlite.rs:4477`), so it must not pretend to rank. Two things must be
verified before documenting a local recipe: config validation only checks provider non-empty and dims > 0
(`schema.rs:22857-22862`) — no URL-scheme or loopback check was found — and whether
`zeroclaw-infra/net_guard.rs`'s `is_private_or_local_host` (`:411-415`) is applied to embedding calls at
all.

**ACL and provenance.** Collections are visible per agent/principal (`PrincipalScope`
(`memory_traits.rs:14-30`) is the existing shape); a channel-facing agent must not read the operator's
private shelf. Retrieved chunks must be delivered as labelled data with source, section, and version — never
as instruction-looking text. A query that matches nothing returns "no match"; the agent must not be handed a
plausible-looking empty set to hallucinate over.

**`delete_by_source` is real.** A stale chunk re-surfaces deleted content in retrieval indefinitely.
This is why LanceDB's MVCC is a cost, not a footnote: `delete()` may leave readable historical versions
until compaction, so "that document is gone" is only true after GC. **Verify** before promising it in docs.

### Extraction: out of process, and no in-tree PDF crate

Precedent to reuse, not reinvent: ZeroClaw already depends on poppler for a shipped feature —
`docs/book/src/channels/whatsapp.md:96-104` documents `pdftoppm`/`pdfinfo` from poppler-utils, and
`whatsapp_web.rs:2637-2710` runs them via `run_preview_tool` (`:2857-2871`) with a 5 s timeout
(`DOCUMENT_PREVIEW_TIMEOUT`, `:2462`), `stdin(Stdio::null())`, `kill_on_drop(true)`, and graceful
`note_preview_skipped` degradation. `pdftotext` is the same package. Extractors inherit that shape:
bounded timeout, no stdin, no network, bounded output, per-file success/failure report, clear
"install poppler-utils" message instead of a silent skip.

Text-layer-first policy (cheap and exact): extract with `pdftotext`; if the result is empty or near-empty
relative to page count, classify the file as **scanned** and route it to OCR. Classification needs no
crate. Scanned books are the *only* place OCR earns its cost.

Surveyed alternatives, with the reasons they are rejected for the default tree:

| crate | license | why not in-tree |
|---|---|---|
| `mupdf` 0.8.0 | **AGPL-3.0** | incompatible with `MIT OR Apache-2.0`; `default = ["js","xps","svg","html","epub","tesseract",…]` — a JS engine on by default; 8.9 MB crate, C library build |
| `pdf_oxide` 0.3.78 | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | **342,258 lines of Rust** in one dependency; self-reported benchmarks in its own description; ~15 debug/benchmark bins shipped in the published crate; `ocr` feature pulls `ort` (ONNX Runtime) |
| `pdf-inspector` 1.25.2 | MIT, `default = []` (good hygiene) | `ocr` feature = `render-pdfium` (PDFium) + `ocr-oar` (`oar-ocr` + `ort`) + `model-download` (`ureq`) — i.e. **runtime model fetch**, the exact pattern #8547 retired; 115k LoR; published 2026-09-28, 106 downloads |
| `extractous` 0.3.0 | — | shells out to a natively-compiled Apache Tika: a JVM-derived external binary as a hard dependency |
| `kreuzberg` 4.10.4 | — | 91+ formats as one dependency; the opposite of a narrow seam |

**OCR (recorded decision: out-of-process `tesseract`, S3, default-off gate).** Consistent with #8547's
doctrine — no model distribution inside the binary; the system package + language data are documented
provenance. The in-tree alternative, `ocrs` 0.13.1 (MIT OR Apache-2.0, 2,381 lines, active 2026-09-13), is
credible but `default = ["export-wasm","rten","onnx"]` — the `rten` inference engine — and needs
recognition model files either bundled (release size) or downloaded (rejected pattern). Revisit only if
operators need OCR without a system package, decided on measured size/quality.

### Store: start on the engine we run, decide LanceDB with numbers

First slice uses the existing store: SQLite + FTS5 in new `corpus` tables, behind the `Index` trait.
LanceDB is then **one `impl Index`**, adoptable without touching ingest/extract/screen/ACL/surface code.

Adoption gate for LanceDB (current state, verified): the crate does not compile in its own default
configuration. `v0.39.0` (latest release) and `main` both have `default = []`, `lib.rs` declares
`pub mod job;` ungated while `error.rs` gates `Http`/`Retry` behind `#[cfg(feature = "remote")]`, and
`job.rs` builds `Error::Http` ungated in `TerminalResult::decode`; a code search on `main` finds the same
pattern in a second non-`remote` file, `table/checkpoint.rs`. Plus a `protoc` build requirement, 406
packages / **+156 marginal** on our 1,113-name lock, `datafusion` + 7 sub-crates, and `lance-index` with
`tokenizer-jieba`/`tokenizer-lindera` enabled unconditionally. Resolution path: upstream issue + pinned
version with a recorded reason. Enabling `remote` to satisfy the compiler is rejected (pulls
`tonic`/`prost`/`arrow-flight` and a cloud client we would not use). If only the format layer is needed,
`lance` (core) is a separate candidate to measure — and the cheaper ANN libraries measured at **+10
marginal packages** (`turbovec`, 13 s cold check; `usearch`, +10, 203 s) solve the §Problem scan problem
without any of it. `sqlite-vec` was 0.1.8 and does not build as published.

### Slices, each independently shippable

| slice | content | exit criteria (measured, in the PR body) |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Markdown/text corpus e2e: `Source`(fs) + `Index`(sqlite+FTS5) + `knowledge_search`; chunk/embed/store/reindex; security requirements enforced; incremental by content hash; `delete_by_source` | agent answers from a real doc set with citations; recall@10 vs a hand-labelled query set; p50/p99; **no new dependencies** |
| S2 | PDF text-layer path: `pdftotext` via the template above, **T1 sandbox tier mandatory** (recorded decision), scanned-vs-text classification with **per-file empty-extraction reporting** | ≥ N real PDFs indexed; a collection with no available sandbox **refuses ingestion with a named error**; scanned ones reported as "no text layer", not silently empty |
| S3 | OCR for scanned documents — **out-of-process `tesseract`**, default-off gate with provenance + startup compatibility check (recorded decision) | quality on 20 sample pages vs `pdftotext` ground truth, wall-clock per page, RSS; missing binary/data → named error, not silence |
| S4 | Vector indexing: measure the §Problem table at real size, then pick ANN library or LanceDB | p99 at target corpus size, build time, `cargo tree --duplicates`, four cross-target lanes, binary-size delta |
| S5 | HTML→Markdown (not `html2text` flattening), Office via LibreOffice headless, EPUB — each its own gate | heading structure survives into chunks (asserted in tests) |

Why HTML is **not** in S1 despite `nanohtml2text` already being in the tree (`web_fetch.rs:401`,
`link_enricher.rs:115`): `html2text` flattens to plain text and destroys the headings that
`chunker.rs:3` promises to preserve ("Preserves heading context"). Indexing flattened HTML would silently
degrade chunk attribution. Proper HTML ingestion is a converter that yields Markdown, which is S5.

Prerequisites before S1 merges: land #11209 (fail-closed selector — an unrecognised value currently
becomes Markdown silently in unreleased builds); then registry unification (`selectable_memory_backends()`
has zero consumers outside its own crate while `src/main.rs:2282` and `:2338-2345` hardcode their own
lists); then surface the swallowed construction errors (`daemon/mod.rs:739` `Err(_e)` → fixed string;
`daemon/mod.rs:2234-2240` `.ok()` per heartbeat tick).

### Deployment defaults (per-collection config, not design inputs)

| input | default | why it stays a config value |
|---|---|---|
| formats | **first slice: `.md` + `.txt` only.** PDF/Office/EPUB/HTML each behind their own default-off gate, each requiring a documented external binary | each gate is a system dependency, not a crate |
| chunk size | configurable, no hardcoded 512 (`rag/mod.rs:137` is the bug being avoided) | books and API references want different sizes |
| embedder | per-collection route; `custom:` local first, remote requires explicit opt-in | exfiltration decision, above |
| path authority | collections outside the workspace require a policy allowlist entry | highest-severity security item, above |
| retrieval surface | tool-called; auto-inject opt-in per collection with a token budget | a 50-book corpus injected every turn is a latency and context disaster |
| corpus size | measured, not assumed | no documented corpus-size limit exists in `docs/book/src`; the §Problem table is arithmetic on repo defaults |

### Alternatives considered

- **Qubes-style bitmap round-trip as the default PDF pipeline.** Rejected as a default (kept as T2):
  safety comes from the DisposableVM, not the bitmaps; in-process rasterising keeps the full parser attack
  surface; and the image-only output forces OCR on every document, including ones with perfect text
  layers.
- **In-tree PDF/OCR crates.** Rejected for the default tree — see the survey table (AGPL license, 342k-line
  dependencies, runtime model fetch, vendor self-reported benchmarks). Out-of-process extraction follows
  the project's own post-#8547 position.
- **LanceDB first / corpus lane second.** Rejected: the crate does not compile in its default configuration
  today, the corpus lane does not exist to host it, and §Problem's scan problem is solved by a +10-package
  ANN index if measurement demands it. Store choice is a measured fork in S4.
- **Build it as a `memory.backend`.** Rejected: wrong trait shape (memory-management contract vs document
  index), drags GDPR/purge/`*_for_principal` semantics onto books, and couples corpus lifecycle to memory
  lifecycle.
- **Do nothing.** `retrieve()` stays substring matching (`rag/mod.rs:227`) — "pin" matches "shipping" —
  over operator-unreachable documents, and the agent keeps answering from the conversation and its memory
  rows while the reference shelf sits unread.

### Non-goals

- Not a `Memory` backend; no decay/dedup/importance/consolidation on documents.
- No PDF parsing in Rust in-process; no `mupdf` (AGPL); no 300k-line PDF dependency in the default tree.
- No runtime download of models or binaries during build or first run (#8547 precedent).
- No default-on image round-trip for PDFs; no OCR applied to documents that have a text layer.
- No LanceDB, and no ANN index, before the §Problem number is measured at real size.
- No auto-injection of corpus text into every turn; retrieval is a tool call, with per-collection opt-in
  injection under an explicit token budget.
- No LanceDB Cloud / `remote`.

### Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| `lancedb` does not compile in its default configuration (verified at v0.39.0 and `main`); adopting it today blocks the build. | S4 is gated on an upstream fix + pin with recorded reason; until then the `Index` seam runs on SQLite/FTS5 and a +10-package ANN library if measurement demands. Sponsorship for the pin is an explicit maintainer ask (see Decision and revisit surface). |
| The support owner is a contributor without `push` (`@ConYel`, verified `pull: true` only). | Recorded in the proposal: duties 2-5 (boundary tests, matrix claim, triage, ratchet) are carried by the owner; duty 1 (the upstream pin) is paired with an explicit maintainer-sponsorship ask. If the ratchet is not met, the backend is removed with a fail-closed message — Lucid's disposition. |
| Lance MVCC may leave deleted-document content readable until compaction (unverified). | Verify in the S4 spike before documenting erasure semantics; docs promise only post-GC deletion, or the corpus stays on SQLite. |
| Local embedding endpoints may be blocked or unguarded at the loopback/net-guard boundary (unverified). | Trace `net_guard` application to embedding calls before documenting the local recipe; until traced, the local route is documented as requiring explicit config. |
| OCR quality on code listings, tables, ligatures is materially worse than embedded text layers. | Text-layer-first policy; OCR only for classified-scanned documents; S3 exit criteria measure quality against ground truth before the gate ships. |
| Feature-gate propagation bugs (#6066 class: gate only reached one binary). | Each gate is exercised in tests for both binary targets per repo law; #6066 is the regression test case. |
| Silent ingestion failures (unreadable file → empty content: `rag/mod.rs:140`; ignored `read_dir` errors: `:96-98`) make a half-read library indistinguishable from an empty one. | Fixed in S1: per-file ingest report, per-file empty-extraction reporting, named errors for unreadable sources. |
| Corpus becomes an exfiltration or prompt-injection channel (untrusted documents, remote embedders). | Security requirements are spec: screening via `ScannedMemory`/`threat.rs`, redaction via `redact.rs`, provenance labels, per-collection embedder warning, path authority via `resolve_tool_path` + tool wrappers. |
| Scope creep into "a second authoritative store". | Files stay the source of truth; index is derived and rebuildable; if a deployment discards originals, #9103's full owner/erasure requirements apply and this RFC's owner accepts them. |



### Breaking change?

No

### Decision and revisit surface

This issue is the decision surface (Core vote, per #9496 FND-003 scope rules). S1 is ready for an
implementation PR on acceptance. Revisit triggers: a `lancedb` release that compiles with `default = []`
(removes the pin); a maintainer sponsor signing on for — or declining — the pin (S4 go/no-go); results of
the two unverified security traces (MVCC erasure, net-guard/loopback); S4's measured numbers against the
§Problem estimate.

### Data hygiene checks

- [x] I removed personal/sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

issues.body:
### Affected component

tools

### Severity

S2 - degraded behavior

### Current behavior

`SendViaTool::resolve_target` in `crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/send_via.rs` uses the first `external_peers` entry as the recipient, both when selecting a peer group directly and when resolving a channel covered by one group. Matrix peer groups identify users as `@user:server`, but Matrix's `resolve_room` accepts only room IDs beginning with `!` or room aliases beginning with `#`.

A Matrix peer group containing a valid user identity therefore supplies a recipient that the Matrix sender rejects with `matrix: not a room id or alias: {id_or_alias}`. The same ambiguity affects wildcard peer entries: an authorization selector is not a delivery address.

This source-established follow-up from #10489 has not been reproduced through a live Matrix deployment. It is distinct from #9646's tool ownership scope and #10925's input-modality feature.

### Expected behavior

Keep authorized peer identities separate from outbound room destinations. Provide an explicit room ID or alias through a scoped delivery-address contract and validate it before delivery. Do not guess a shared room, choose an arbitrary membership match, create a DM automatically, or reinterpret the peer authorization list as a room list.

The implementation needs a maintainer decision on where that explicit destination belongs. Preserve agent peer-group membership checks and applicable channel/room authorization. If no valid destination is available, return a clear actionable error rather than attempting to send to a user ID.

### Steps to reproduce

```text
Source-derived scenario; live delivery not executed:
1. Configure an agent in a Matrix peer group whose external_peers contains a permitted Matrix user ID.
2. Invoke send_via targeting that peer group with a message body.
3. Observe resolve_target select the first external peer as the recipient.
4. Follow that recipient into Matrix resolve_room, which rejects the @user address.
Also cover an exact channel target with one matching group and a wildcard peer entry.
```

### Impact

Cross-channel or proactive delivery through send_via cannot use the documented Matrix user-based peer group as a valid room destination. This affects addressing regardless of text or voice modality; ordinary replies already carrying a room target are not the reported failure.

### Logs / stack traces

_No response_

### ZeroClaw version

Source inspected on master during follow-up reconciliation of #10489; inspected baseline `3df68fb2236c6f089c25005d0ebb780c9c7fd642`.

### Rust version

Not measured; source-based report.

### Operating system

Not platform-specific in the inspected code; no live platform reproduction performed.

### Regression?

Unknown

### Pre-flight checks

- [ ] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [x] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

issues.body:
### Affected component

plugins

### Severity

S3 - minor issue

### Current behavior

With #11236, `zeroclaw plugin install` builds each package in a leased transaction, `.<name>.installing-v1-<id>/`, which holds a `lease` file and a `package/` directory. It then publishes `package/` under the real name. If the process is killed after creating the transaction and before publishing, the stage stays behind:

```text
plugins/.tool-fixture.installing-v1-<id>/lease
plugins/.tool-fixture.installing-v1-<id>/package/
plugins/.zeroclaw-package-lock-v1
```

Nothing breaks because of it. Discovery ignores hidden entries, `plugin list` shows nothing, a re-install publishes normally and loads, and `plugin remove` of that installed package succeeds. But the stage is never cleaned up. It is still there after a full re-install and remove cycle, and no command removes it.

That is because the staging sweep (`remove_stale_staging` in `crates/zeroclaw-plugins/src/host.rs`) runs in only two cases. One is after `plugin remove` has claimed a stranded final directory and judged it recoverable. The other is a retry that finishes a delete an earlier remove had begun. A normal install, a remove of a loaded package, and a remove of a name with no final directory never sweep. #11236 states this scope deliberately, so this issue is a follow-up, not a regression.

The stage is provably abandoned. Its lease was held by a process that no longer exists, so the lease can be taken, which is the same test the existing sweep uses to tell abandoned transactions from active ones.

### Expected behavior

An abandoned leased stage for a package is eventually removed by an ordinary plugin command, without manual cleanup, and an active stage is never touched. One possible shape:

- `plugin install <name>` and `plugin remove <name>` sweep recognized `.<name>.installing-v1-*` transactions whose lease they can take, while holding the package lock.
- Legacy PID-named stages (`.<name>.installing-<pid>`) keep their current treatment: retained and reported, because their ownership cannot be proved.
- Alternatively, or as well, `plugin list` reports retained stages with the command that clears them.

### Steps to reproduce

The writes take a few milliseconds after a load check of several seconds, so the interrupt has to be timed on the stage's creation. One way, with `inotify-tools`:

```bash
C=$(mktemp -d)
zeroclaw --config-dir "$C" plugin list >/dev/null
mkdir -p "$C/plugins"
zeroclaw --config-dir "$C" plugin install <tool-package-dir> &
pid=$!
inotifywait -q -m -e create --format '%f' "$C/plugins" | grep -m1 -q 'installing-v1' && kill -9 "$pid"
find "$C/plugins" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 2           # the .<name>.installing-v1-<id>/{lease,package} stage
zeroclaw --config-dir "$C" plugin install <tool-package-dir>   # succeeds
zeroclaw --config-dir "$C" plugin remove <name>                # succeeds
find "$C/plugins" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 2           # the abandoned stage is still there
```

Killing the process a few hundred microseconds later usually lands after publication, and then nothing is left over.

### Impact

Cosmetic and small: an empty `package/` directory and a lease file per interrupted install. It does not block install, remove, update or discovery. It does accumulate across interrupted installs, and an operator inspecting the plugins directory sees hidden transactions with no supported way to clear them.

### Logs / stack traces

```text
(none: no command reports the stage)
```

### ZeroClaw version

#11236 head `5a3604e6237106f1a6bcd261198c0f10df1e5daa` (debug build with `plugins-wasm-cranelift`)

### Rust version

1.98.0

### Operating system

Linux

### Regression?

No, first-time setup

### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [x] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

### Task

When a dashboard tab completes a normal (full-page) OIDC sign-in, tell the browser's other dashboard tabs, as the re-auth window already does. A tab showing the sign-in screen then picks up the new session.

### Context

Follow-up from the review of #11965 (dashboard sign-in).

Dashboard tabs share the session cookie and coordinate over the `BroadcastChannel` named by `AUTH_CHANNEL`. A tab on the sign-in screen that hears `signed-in` re-reads the session and adopts it. A tab still holding another account's page reloads.

Only the re-auth window posts `signed-in`. The sign-in callback's popup page does it (`signed_in_popup_page` in `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_oidc.rs`). A full-page sign-in redirects back to the dashboard instead, and the dashboard adopts the session on load without posting anything.

So after a normal sign-in in one tab, another tab showing the sign-in screen stays there until it's reloaded, although the session is already usable there.

### Acceptance criteria

- After a full-page sign-in in one tab, other dashboard tabs on the sign-in screen pick up the session without a reload, and a tab holding another account's page reloads, as after a popup sign-in.
- Opening or reloading a dashboard that was already signed in doesn't make every other tab re-read the session.
- A test covers the full-page case.

### Likely files or areas

- `web/src/hooks/useAuth.ts` (the initial `signed-in` case, the channel)
- `web/src/lib/authSession.ts` (`signInUrl`, channel messages)
- `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_oidc.rs` (the callback's redirect), only if the gateway marks a fresh sign-in. Alternatively, the tab that starts the sign-in can note it, for example in `sessionStorage`, and post once it has adopted the session.

### Contributor fit

maintainer-scoped task, not yet ready for pickup labels

### Mentor, reviewer, or contact

@JordanTheJet

### Risk notes

Low. The message carries no secret: each tab re-reads the session through its own cookie.

issues.title: [Task]: show a detached chat turn's answer when the socket reopens before the turn ends
issues.body:
### Task

When a dashboard chat socket closes mid-turn and reopens while the turn is still running on the gateway, keep track of that turn and reload the transcript once it ends.

### Context

Follow-up from the review of #11965 (dashboard sign-in).

When a chat socket closes in the middle of a turn, the page stops showing the turn as running. The close can come from a session ending, a gateway reload or a network drop. The page then reloads the transcript once when a socket opens again (`resyncOnOpenRef` in `web/src/contexts/AgentContext.tsx`).

The gateway keeps running the turn after its viewer goes, and saves it only when the turn ends. The new socket doesn't receive the turn's result.

So if the socket reopens before the turn ends, that one reload fetches a transcript without the answer. Nothing triggers another reload, so the page sits idle with the answer missing until the user reloads the page or switches conversations. Since #11571, the prompt itself stays on screen.

The existing test covers only a turn that ends before the socket reopens: "a socket closed mid-turn stops the turn and reloads the transcript when it reopens" in `web/src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts`.

`GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` already reports whether a session's turn is still running. #9002 proposes the wider reconnect contract for detached turns: polling that state and keeping the composer locked while a turn runs. #9641 tracks browser tests for it. This task is the narrow case that the resync on reopen left open, and it should fit whichever of these lands first.

### Acceptance criteria

- If the socket reopens while the turn is still running, the page shows that the turn is running, and the answer appears once the turn ends, without a page reload.
- The watch stops when the turn ends, when the conversation changes and when the session ends. It never loops.
- Without session persistence the state route answers 404. The page then keeps today's single reload.
- A test covers a socket that reopens before the turn ends, next to the existing test.

### Likely files or areas

- `web/src/contexts/AgentContext.tsx` (the socket close and open handlers, transcript hydration)
- `web/src/lib/api.ts` (a call for `GET /api/sessions/{id}/state`; the web client has none yet)
- `web/src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts`

Related: #9002, #9641, #11571.

### Contributor fit

maintainer-scoped task, not yet ready for pickup labels

### Mentor, reviewer, or contact

@JordanTheJet

### Risk notes

Low to medium. It is web only, but it touches chat hydration, which #11571 just changed: keep a prompt the gateway hasn't saved yet on screen.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): steer the running turn when you send a message mid-turn
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - #11132 added daemon `session/steer`; eligible ZeroCode Submit now offers plain text to the running turn when the queue is empty, preserving message order. Attachments, cancellation, approval prompts, and existing queued work retain their current paths.
  - An accepted steer appears after text already streamed, without starting another client turn. Acceptance confirms enqueueing, not consumption by the agent.
  - An explicit refusal or RPC error reply queues the text. A timeout restores it to the input with `zc-steer-unconfirmed`, without automatically resending it.
  - If a turn with an accepted steer ends `Cancelled` or `Failed`, `zc-steer-ended-early` warns that the text may not have been read. The flag resets at terminal settlement, fresh turn start, resync reset, and session reset. `Completed` does not show this warning.
- **Scope boundary:** `apps/zerocode` only. No daemon/runtime changes, Cargo files, CI, new key bindings or settings, attachment steering, or async key-action refactor. Inject continues to cancel the turn. The synchronous steer await can still pause the TUI for up to 5 seconds.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode's running-turn Submit path, client RPC wrapper, turn settlement, and localized info notices. Idle Submit and other daemon clients retain their behavior.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11132, Related #9487. Daemon steer-consumed/steer-dropped signaling remains follow-up work; no dedicated open issue was found in the issue search. No issue is closed by this PR.

### What this does, simply

When the agent is working, type a follow-up and press Enter to offer it to the same turn. Before, it waited in the client queue and started a separate turn. Only plain text with no earlier queued messages takes this path.

The agent can read a steer between steps. It cannot interrupt a single long tool call, such as a build, until that call returns. An explicit refusal sends the message to the queue. If delivery times out, the message returns to the input with a reminder to check before sending again.

If the turn is cancelled or fails after accepting a steer, an info notice says: “This turn ended early; a message you sent into it may not have been read. Check before sending it again.” The client cannot tell which accepted messages the daemon consumed. Some daemon drops still end as `Completed`, so this warning cannot detect them. Steered text can appear in the transcript yet be absent from session history after reload.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. A live cancel-after-steer capture on the final repaired head is still pending from Dan's Air.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface`: `tui`; messaging channel: N/A, this is the direct daemon TUI.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A current daemon with `session/steer` and ZeroCode built from the final repaired revision. Use a session with an empty queue and a multi-step task. A long tool call makes the cancel path easier to observe.
- **Steps to run:** Start “list the files in this repo one directory at a time”. While tools run, type “also count them” and press Enter. In a separate run, send that steer during a long tool call, then press Esc before it finishes. The failure state is covered by `chat::tests::an_accepted_steer_then_failed_turn_shows_delivery_notice` rather than a live provider failure.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** On acceptance the message appears in the transcript, the queue stays empty, and no new client turn starts. Cancellation or failure shows the early-end delivery warning. Successful completion shows no such warning. Sending the next ordinary prompt clears the notice and starts with a clean accepted-steer flag. A timeout restores the input and warns without automatically queueing or resending.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same mid-turn message waits in the client queue instead of steering the active turn. On the published pre-repair PR head, accepted steering followed by cancellation or failure leaves a sent-looking transcript row with no delivery warning.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Historical `CI Required Gate` is SUCCESS on published head `7060b30a84890dac38166f4476521614ae46f3fa`, including Format, Lint, Test, and Zerocode RPC Boundary. This does not validate the local repair or its merged base. No final-repair CI result is claimed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Fresh CI runs on the pushed head `46f3999a5`. Live transport and the cancel-after-steer case are not covered by automated tests; a real screenshot is pending.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  Run on head `46f3999a5` (master merge `ef039234e` + `5a261d989` early-end notice + `46f3999a5` removal of the rendered evidence tests), Mac mini, `zc-cargo-narrow`, `-j2`, `--test-threads=2`:

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  ok
  cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings        ok
  cargo test -p zerocode
    zerocode (lib)       54 passed; 0 failed
    zerocode (bin)       1572 passed; 2 failed; 2 ignored
    terminal_disconnect  3 passed
  ```

  Both failures also fail on clean master `5a51398dd` on this machine and are not touched by this PR: `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` and `app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events` (timing-sensitive under load; failed 3/3 on master here).

  Focused tests in that run (all pass):

  - `client::session_method_tests::session_steer_sends_content_and_reads_accepted`
  - `chat::tests::steering_is_offered_only_for_a_plain_message_into_a_running_turn`
  - `chat::tests::a_steered_message_joins_the_running_turn_without_starting_one`
  - `chat::tests::a_steer_on_the_last_output_does_not_repeat_the_answer_at_completion`
  - `chat::tests::a_steer_timeout_is_not_treated_as_a_refusal`
  - `chat::tests::submit_during_a_running_turn_steers_and_falls_back_to_the_queue`
  - `chat::tests::an_unanswered_steer_returns_the_text_to_the_input_instead_of_queueing`
  - `chat::tests::an_accepted_steer_then_cancelled_turn_shows_delivery_notice`
  - `chat::tests::an_accepted_steer_then_failed_turn_shows_delivery_notice`
  - `chat::tests::an_accepted_steer_then_completed_turn_has_no_delivery_notice`
  - `chat::tests::a_turn_after_cancelled_steering_starts_without_delivery_uncertainty`

  The existing `i18n::tests::en_catalogue_parses` and `i18n::tests::argument_messages_format_in_all_builtin_catalogues` also remain relevant catalogue checks. New key presence and distinct translations were checked statically in all five locale sources; this is not a Fluent parser or runtime test.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Historical live acceptance run on experiment build [`20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d), carrying this change and #11725 on dogfood base [`20261008T194402Z-0341618f9d69`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/dogfood/zerocode-builds/20261008T194402Z-0341618f9d69). During a multi-step file-listing task, “also count them” appeared immediately in the transcript, no new turn started, and the agent acted on it at its next tool step. This is acceptance evidence on a stacked build, not a live test of this repair. The final-head cancel-after-steer run remains pending from Dan.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshots of the current head (46f3999a52): see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11621#issuecomment-6514782111 (steer accepted into the running turn with an empty queue; Esc cancel showing the early-end delivery notice).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Real screenshots pending.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Real screenshots pending.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Covered by the lifecycle tests above: an accepted steer followed by a cancelled or failed turn shows the delivery notice; a completed turn and the next turn do not. The live cancel-after-steer screenshot is pending.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace-wide tests were skipped; the change is confined to `apps/zerocode`. No live capture of the repaired state was made.


## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. Existing daemon session authorization and steering admission apply.
- New external network calls? Yes. Eligible Submit sends `session/steer` over the existing authenticated daemon connection. It adds no destination or connection type, and refusal uses the existing queue.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Test text is synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new untrusted source. User-authored follow-ups use the daemon's existing steering admission instead of waiting for another turn.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The new RPC can time out after enqueueing. Unknown delivery returns the text to the input without automatic resend; accepted steering followed by cancellation/failure shows a caution. Session permissions and admission rules remain daemon-owned.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. An older daemon that lacks `session/steer` returns an error, so the text queues as before. No wire schema or persisted data format changes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No config, environment variable, command syntax, or key binding changes. TUI Enter behavior during eligible running turns changes as described above.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A - no configuration migration or toolchain upgrade is required. Update ZeroCode normally; localized catalogue updates are distributed through the existing locale fetch path.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

This is `risk:medium` behavioral work. The low-risk default does not apply.

Medium/high-risk PRs must fill:

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Before merge, switch to the previously working ZeroCode binary. After squash merge, `git revert <merge-commit-of-this-PR>`, rebuild, and redeploy ZeroCode through the normal release path. The daemon and stored sessions need no rollback or migration; eligible mid-turn messages return to the client queue behavior.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A steered message appears in the transcript but is missing from session history after reload; cancellation/failure leaves no warning; duplicate execution after a timeout; duplicate final answers; or drawing, streamed updates, and key handling freeze for up to 5 seconds after Enter while awaiting steering. Completed-path daemon drops remain undetectable without consumed/dropped signaling.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A - no Supersedes

- Superseded PRs + authors (`#<pr> by @<author>`, one per line): N/A - no Supersedes.
- Scope materially carried forward: N/A - no replaced PR.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? No.
- If `No`, why (inspiration-only, no direct code/design carry-over): N/A - no incorporated superseded contributor work.

---

**Labels** live in the GitHub label UI, not in the body. The PR path labeler owns path/scope labels from `.github/labeler.yml`, and the PR size labeler owns canonical `size:*` labels. Maintainers and reviewers with label permissions still set `risk:*` and any missing manual labels via the sidebar. Contributors without label permission can note obvious label mismatches in a comment. Canonical colon-scoped labels use no-space spelling; during migration, copy exact live label spelling from the GitHub UI.

**Do not add bot/AI attribution footers** such as `Co-authored-by: Claude ...`
or `Created with Claude Code` to the PR body or commit-message tail. Human
co-author trailers are appropriate only for incorporated contributor work under
the supersede-attribution section and privacy contract.

**Privacy contract** (`docs/book/src/contributing/privacy.md`) is a merge gate. Never commit real identities, secrets, personal emails, or PII in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): reopen open sessions when zerocode restarts
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - zerocode's sidebar list of open sessions lived only in memory. The daemon keeps every transcript, but quitting zerocode lost which sessions were open, so each launch started from an empty sidebar.
  - The list (session ids, agent aliases, order, focus, and the last Chat/Code pane on screen) is now saved whenever it changes, as an owner-only JSON file per connection target under `<config-dir>/open-sessions/`.
  - At launch the saved list goes to the existing reconnect resume path (`set_resume_sessions`), so restored sessions reattach by id exactly as they do after a daemon reconnect: focused first, the rest in the background.
  - On by default (`[sidebar] restore_sessions = true`). `zerocode --fresh` starts one launch with an empty sidebar and still saves its own list.
  - Each zerocode window on a daemon keeps its own list in a numbered slot, held by an OS file lock. A window takes the lowest free slot, so closing a second window and opening it again while the first runs reopens the second window's sessions. At restore, sessions another running window has in its list are skipped with a notice. Without that, two windows would reattach the same live session, and either window could cancel the other's turn. That stale-session and multi-tab hazard is why #8911 (silent auto-resume, for #8653) was closed in favour of the #8922 picker. The lock is released when the owning window exits, including on a crash.
  - Each window publishes the list it is about to reopen before its panes start (an empty list on `--fresh`), so other windows never judge by the previous occupant's stale list.
  - Saved Code sessions the daemon no longer lists, and saved Chat sessions with no stored history (for example deleted), are dropped with one notice.
  - When the daemon refuses to reattach a restored session because this terminal's environment differs from the one the session started in (FORBIDDEN `-32012`, "Session environment differs" or "Session retains a local operator environment"), the entry stays where it was, with the same order and focus. Its pane shows a translated notice that the saved session can't be reattached from this terminal environment and that the daemon still keeps the old conversation, plus an explicit "start a new conversation" action (the existing new-session key, Ctrl+N by default). Only that action opens a fresh session in the same slot, with the same agent and mode, and the saved list then tracks the new id. If creating it fails, the refused entry and its notice stay. Nothing is replaced automatically, other errors behave as before, and the daemon's environment check is unchanged.
  - Fully resuming the old conversation in that case is left to upstream #11921 (history persistence so tasks can resume after restart).
  - Local daemon connections only. Over WSS the daemon admits a resume only from the client identity that owns the session (`capture_session_access`), and a relaunched window connects with a new one, so a saved remote list could only produce failed rows. Reclaiming a remote identity per window slot is a follow-up.
- **Scope boundary:** Local connections only; remote (`--connect`) windows are unchanged. Client only (`apps/zerocode`); no daemon, RPC or runtime change. Queued messages, unsent drafts and attachments are not saved. A turn that was running when zerocode quit is not resumed or rerun.
- **Blast radius:** zerocode startup (one extra `session/list-acp` call and/or one `session/messages` probe per saved Chat session on a local connection when a saved list exists) and the per-frame sidebar derivation (a cheap comparison; the file is written only when the list changes, and never while disconnected).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8653, #8911, #8922.

### What this does, simply

When you quit zerocode and start it again, the sessions you had open in the sidebar come back: same order, same one focused, on the pane you were using. The conversations themselves were always kept by the daemon. What was lost was the list of which ones you had open. If a saved session has since been deleted, it is skipped with a short notice. If a saved session can't be reattached from the terminal you relaunched in, it stays in its place with a notice and an option to start a new conversation there. Each zerocode window keeps its own list: close a second window and open it again, and it gets its own sessions back. A session already open in another window is not opened twice. Use `zerocode --fresh` to start one launch with an empty sidebar, or set `restore_sessions = false` under `[sidebar]` to turn the feature off.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `tui` (zerocode Chat and Code panes)
- **Setup / preconditions:** A local daemon with at least two agents.
- **Steps to run:** Open two Code sessions and one Chat session from the sidebar, focus the second Code session, quit zerocode, start it again. Then quit and start once more with `zerocode --fresh`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** With one `zerocode` open, open a second window, add a session there, close it and reopen it: it comes back with that session, and the first window is unchanged. The second launch opens on the Code pane with the same three sidebar rows in the same order and the second Code session focused, transcripts loaded. The `--fresh` launch starts with an empty sidebar.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Every launch starts with an empty sidebar (or the recent-session picker); the previous launch's open sessions must be reopened one by one.

### How I tested

- **Tested revision:** `d05cdf055cb2a9a61f343643619abe730dc78b4c` on the Mac mini.
- **Formatting:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- **Package suite:** `cargo test -p zerocode`, through `zc-cargo-narrow` with `-j2` for compilation and two test threads: library 54 passed; binary 1,600 passed, 1 failed (the known failure below). The TestBackend evidence-frame tests were removed in this revision; the behaviour tests stay.
- **Deleted-Chat regressions (new or updated, all pass):** `open_sessions::tests::deleted_chat_session_is_skipped_at_restore`, `open_sessions::tests::chat_sessions_survive_startup_without_a_complete_daemon_listing`, `open_sessions::tests::chat_restore_drops_only_the_specific_missing_session_refusal`, `open_sessions::tests::mixed_restore_prunes_code_by_list_and_chat_by_history_in_order`. Each saved Chat entry is probed with `session/messages` (limit 1): no stored history, or the daemon's "Session not found or not owned by this principal" refusal, drops it with the existing notice; any other error keeps it for the normal resume path. I ran the first test against `409b7725ef` and it fails there (`dropped` is 0, expected 1), because that head kept every saved Chat ID.
- **Environment-refusal regressions (all pass):** `chat::tests::focused_restored_environment_refusal_keeps_slot_focus_and_notice`, `chat::tests::background_restored_environment_refusal_keeps_slot_and_opens_notice_on_focus`, `chat::tests::restored_environment_refusal_new_conversation_replaces_only_the_selected_slot`, `chat::tests::failed_refused_session_replacement_keeps_saved_id_and_notice`, `chat::tests::unrelated_forbidden_restore_keeps_existing_error_behaviour`, `chat::tests::session_picker_environment_refusal_keeps_selected_entry_and_notice`, `chat::tests::chat_entry_retry_adopts_restored_environment_refusal_action`, `chat::tests::restored_environment_refusal_requires_typed_code_and_specific_message`. On `c4f45eb508` the focused-refusal case promotes the background session over the refused one and shows no notice, so the first test's focus and notice assertions fail there.
- **Known failures:** `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` also fails on clean master `f2b432db` on this Mini (it passes when run alone). `app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events` is a known timing flake (it passed in this run).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** That both guards are load-bearing: with the local-only gate removed, `remote_connections_neither_save_nor_restore` fails; with the early publish removed, both `*_publishes_*` tests fail; with the live-window check removed, `sessions_open_in_another_running_window_are_not_restored` fails. Not yet verified: a real launch against a live daemon (see Screenshots below).
- **Intentionally skipped:** Full workspace tests; this change is confined to `apps/zerocode` and its docs page.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots pending.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: zerocode writes one new file plus an empty lock file per window slot and connection target under its own config directory. It is written owner-only (`0600`) and atomically, through the same `secure_file::write_private_atomic` funnel as `zerocode-config.toml`.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. The file holds session ids, agent aliases and the connection label (socket path or WSS URL). The label is already shown on the dashboard. Credentials are not stored.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: see the first item.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. A config file without `restore_sessions` restores (default on); a missing, damaged or newer-format list file is ignored.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: `[sidebar] restore_sessions` (env `ZEROCODE_sidebar__restore_sessions`) and the `--fresh` flag. Documented in `docs/book/src/zerocode/config.md`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: nothing to do on upgrade. To keep the old behavior, set `restore_sessions = false` under `[sidebar]`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. Without a revert, set `restore_sessions = false`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[sidebar] restore_sessions`, `--fresh`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a launch that reopens sessions the user closed, or the toast "Could not save the open-session list".
