prs.title: feat(runtime): let the operator override an exceeded cost limit
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `cost.allow_override` was documented but read by nothing, so an exceeded shared limit always failed the turn and the only way on was a daemon restart. With it on, the main tool loop now pauses before a provider call that would exceed the shared daily or monthly limit and asks through the turn's approval channel (`tool_name = cost_limit_override`, exported as `COST_LIMIT_OVERRIDE_APPROVAL`). Deny, no answer within 10 minutes, or a channel that cannot ask stops the turn exactly as before. ZeroCode, ACP and Telegram wait the full 10 minutes; other chat channels keep their own `approval_timeout_secs` (300 s by default), so there the shorter wait applies.
  - Approval calls `CostTracker::grant_override`, which records the override for the current UTC day or month on state shared by every derived tracker, so one answer covers every session and delegation of the daemon. `check_budget` skips that limit (and its warning) while the stored period matches, so it expires on its own at rollover. Per-hop and per-agent ceilings still bind, and `grant_override` refuses when `allow_override` is off.
  - The grant is written to `state/cost-overrides.json` beside the ledger (temp file plus rename, best effort) and loaded when the tracker starts, so a daemon restart keeps it until rollover. An unreadable file means no override, and a stored grant is ignored while `allow_override` is off.
  - A turn waiting on its own prompt also watches for a grant from another session (a `watch` channel on the tracker). When one arrives it drops its request and continues. `RpcApprovalChannel` sends a new `session/update` type, `approval_withdrawn` (`request_id`), for any approval that ends without an answer from its client, and ZeroCode takes that prompt down. Before this, approving in one session left the same prompt up in the other, and that turn stopped at the 10-minute timeout although the limit was already lifted.
  - `RpcApprovalChannel` and `AskUserApprovalBridge` now implement `request_approval_attributed_with_timeout`. The trait default wrapped `request_approval_attributed`, whose own 120 s deadline fired first, so the 10-minute wait would have been cut short.
  - ZeroCode renders a `cost_limit_override` approval as a centred, bold red notice with Override and Stop buttons instead of the tool card. Only Override or Stop (key or click) closes it.
- **Scope boundary:** no warning at `warn_at_percent` (#10950) and no notice for a turn that stops with no override possible; both need a daemon-to-client budget event this PR does not add. `cost.enforcement.mode` stays unread. Applying `config/set` limit changes to the live tracker is #11587.
- **Blast radius:** turns that hit a shared limit with `allow_override = true` now wait for an answer instead of failing, on any channel that answers approvals (ZeroCode, ACP, Telegram inline buttons). The approval bridge's timeout plumbing is used only by callers that pass a budget; tool approvals are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11585
- **Labels:** (set after open)

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can stop the agent when spending passes a daily or monthly limit. There was a setting meant to let you go past the limit, but nothing used it: once the limit tripped, every message failed, and the only way to continue was to raise the limit and restart, which closes every open session.

Now, with that setting on, the agent pauses when it reaches the limit and ZeroCode shows a red box asking whether to keep going. Say yes and the same task carries on, and the limit stays lifted until the day (or month) ends, even if the app or daemon restarts. If several sessions were waiting at the limit, one yes lets all of them continue. Say no, or leave it for ten minutes, and the task stops as it does today. Chat apps that cannot show the question, and scheduled jobs, still stop at the limit.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` `tui` (ZeroCode Code tab over RPC)
- **Setup / preconditions:** `[cost] enabled = true`, `allow_override = true`, `daily_limit_usd` just above today's recorded spend.
- **Steps to run:** in ZeroCode, run a prompt that makes a few model calls until spend passes the limit. When the red notice appears, click Override. Then open a second session and send a prompt. Separately: get two sessions waiting on the notice at once and Override in one; and restart the daemon after an Override and send a prompt.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first turn pauses on the red notice and continues after Override; the second session is not asked again; with two waiting, the other notice closes and its turn continues; after a restart nobody is asked again that day. With Stop instead, the turn ends with the budget error.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the turn fails with `Budget exceeded: ... Cannot make further API calls until the budget resets.`, there is no prompt, and every later turn fails until a restart.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check   # rustfmt --edition 2024 on the changed files
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib cost::tracker
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib budget_override
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib approval_
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- budget_override_tests rpc::approval_channel
cargo test -p zerocode --bins -- approval parse_approval cost_limit
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode cost_limit
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode approval
scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust test and clippy jobs for the four crates; Docs Style for `docs/book/src/ops/cost-tracking.md`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no end-to-end test drives a real provider turn into the gate; the gate tests call it under a scoped tracker with a scripted channel.
- **Commands run and tail output:** on `225c52bb636f` (rebased on master `f12da7462a0f`): clippy `-D warnings` clean on the four crates; `cost::tracker` 50 passed; runtime `budget_override_tests rpc::approval_channel` 17 passed; zerocode `approval parse_approval cost_limit` 13 passed; comment hygiene gate passed. With each fix disabled, `override_survives_a_restart_and_stops_counting_when_disallowed` and `approval_in_another_session_releases_a_waiting_prompt` fail. Earlier run at `58a7050d`: clippy `Finished`, no warnings. `cost::tracker` 47 passed, `budget_override` 3 passed, `approval_` 106 passed, zerocode `cost_limit` 2 passed, zerocode `approval` 9 passed, docs gate 0 errors.
- **Greptile round 3 (on the master merge `e7c4aa6b3f68`):** the typing wrapper now resumes typing when another session's grant releases a waiting prompt, and keeps it off for a cancelled turn (`abandoned_approval_resumes_typing_unless_the_turn_was_cancelled`, which fails with the guard disarmed). Clippy `-D warnings` clean on `zeroclaw-channels` and `zeroclaw-runtime`; channels `approval_typing abandoned_approval approval_wait_resumes unsupported_approval_resumes` 5 passed; rustfmt and the comment hygiene gate pass.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Coverage: tracker override (day lifts, rollover expiry, derived trackers share it, per-hop and per-agent ceilings still bind, day does not lift month, refused when not allowed); gate (approve continues and does not ask twice, deny and runtime timeout stop, no prompt without `allow_override` or a channel); RPC channel honours a 600 s budget through `dyn Channel`; ZeroCode notice render and button clicks; restart persistence, unreadable file, cross-session release, `approval_withdrawn` sent only for unanswered prompts and cleared only for the matching id. I ran the override live in the experiment build; the two follow-up bugs above came from that run.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshots of the current head (ab919d606c): see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11589#issuecomment-6514704152 (cost-limit prompt with period, spend and limit; Ctrl+O override continuing the waiting turn). Earlier build: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11589#issuecomment-6160109618 (the warning and the choice dialog).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `225c52bb636f` on master `f12da7462a0f`; tests on a remote macOS arm64 builder. Live: experiment build https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T015950Z-b89c9e407c42 (commit https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/b89c9e407c4279bbfb05f9d0e0cdec7e34b6e561).
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** See the comment linked above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full crate suites not run locally; CI runs them.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (one new file, `state/cost-overrides.json`, in the existing cost state directory)
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The override is off by default and only an operator answer grants it; a runtime timeout or unreachable client does not.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. With `allow_override = false` (the default) behaviour is unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new keys; one new RPC `session/update` type, `approval_withdrawn`, which older clients ignore; `allow_override` now does what its docs say, and the docs are corrected.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 225c52bb636f 0c7a8844d260 312ffc65d3ae` (newest first).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `cost.allow_override = false` restores the hard stop without a revert.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** turns stuck waiting at the limit; grep the runtime trace for `cost limit overridden by the operator` and `cost limit override prompt failed`.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): open local file paths from the transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - ZeroCode only recognised HTTP(S) links. Terminal link detection splits paths at spaces and wrapped rows, so a continuation-row click can target the wrong path. Existing absolute and `~/` paths now use ZeroCode's wrapped link hit map.
  - Plain click opens a document. Right-click offers Open, Reveal in Finder or Show in folder, Copy path, and Add path to chat. The optional `:line[:col]` suffix stays highlighted but is not passed to the opener.
  - Existence checks run on background threads, with five-second cached answers and at most 32 checks in flight. Completed checks request a redraw, including when another path was skipped at the limit.
  - Open and Reveal canonicalize the target first. The launch gate checks that canonical path for script and installer extensions, executable bits, and bundle metadata, then uses the same path in the opener arguments. Recognised launching targets are revealed instead of opened, with a notice.
  - Path links are enabled only for local sessions and disabled on Windows. Known host-keyed automount roots `/net`, `/Network`, and `/automount` stay plain text without existence probes.
- **Scope boundary:** No relative-path links, Cmd-click handling, OSC 8 hyperlinks, editor line navigation, remote-path transfer, daemon or wire changes, or new configuration. Paths are not limited to the workspace: this launch gate is not a filesystem sandbox. Finder aliases and file replacement between validation and launch remain limitations.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode transcript styling, wrapped hit regions, context menus, local filesystem probes, and platform opener invocation. HTTP(S) links retain their existing behavior.
- **Linked issue(s):** N/A - no linked issue or Supersedes relationship.

### What this does, simply

File paths in a local ZeroCode chat become clickable, including paths with spaces and paths that wrap onto several rows. A click on a continuation row targets the whole path. You can also copy the path or add it to your next message. Files recognised as scripts, applications, or installers are shown in the file manager instead of opened. This is a launch precaution, not a sandbox or a guarantee that an arbitrary file association cannot run code.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Real macOS Open and Reveal interaction evidence is still needed.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Chat and Code panes over the local daemon transport. Also check a remote WSS session for unchanged URL links and plain file paths. No messaging channel applies.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build this branch and `master` separately. On macOS, use a local session and a narrow pane that wraps a long file path. Create a harmless document in a temporary directory containing a space, a non-executable `.command` fixture, and a `notes.md` symlink to that fixture. Use synthetic paths and no private data.
- **Steps to run:** On each revision, send the same document path, a `~/` path with `:12`, and a missing path. Left-click the document's continuation row. Right-click it and exercise Open, Reveal in Finder, Copy path, and Add path to chat. Click the `.command` fixture and its `notes.md` symlink. Capture the actions, default-app or Finder result, and the reveal-instead notice. In a WSS session, send a path that also exists locally and an HTTPS URL. Inspect both. Use automated tests for automount exclusion rather than probing an actual host.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Existing local paths are underlined across wrapped rows. The continuation-row click opens the whole document path. Copy and Add path to chat preserve the full path. The `.command` and symlink clicks reveal the canonical target in Finder and show `zc-chat-path-revealed-instead`. Missing paths remain plain. WSS paths remain plain while HTTPS URLs remain actionable. Windows path links are disabled.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** File paths have no ZeroCode link hit regions or path-specific menu. A plain click does not invoke the file opener. Terminal-managed Cmd-click may stop at a space or interpret a wrapped continuation row as a relative path. HTTPS links already work.

### How I tested

The published head e0ca66ae08a129f29b5081ab45796436da9cc15d has green GitHub CI. The master merge at 95808cfbe490a403675da11671c100015af39395 was validated locally (results below). It leaves `apps/zerocode` unchanged from that published head.

The previous validation report at e0ca66ae08 records formatting and all-target ZeroCode Clippy passing, and `cargo test --no-fail-fast -p zerocode` with 1,647 passed and one failure in `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`. The author reported that failure on clean master f2b432db on the same host. Those are historical results, not a test run of the local merge.

Focused coverage already present includes `path_open::tests::symlink_launch_checks_and_opener_use_the_canonical_target`, which tests a `notes.md` symlink to non-executable `.command`, `.terminal`, `.fileloc`, `.webloc`, and `.inetloc` targets and asserts `OpenOutcome::Revealed` and canonical opener arguments. Other tests cover automount exclusion before the existence callback, background-probe scheduling, busy-slot retries, exact punctuation, Markdown backticks, installer extensions, wrapped continuation-row hit regions, and remote-session path rejection.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [CI Required Gate and its jobs](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40938144081) passed at published head e0ca66ae08. Format, Lint, workspace Test, default-feature all-target Check, and Zerocode RPC Boundary cover formatting, compilation, regressions, and the client dependency boundary at that revision. They do not validate the later local master merge or real Finder interaction.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Fresh CI runs on the pushed merge. Unit tests assert launcher arguments without launching the default app or Finder. The real macOS Open and Reveal gestures, including the symlink case, remain unrecorded.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  Run on head `95808cfbe` (master merge), Mac mini, `zc-cargo-narrow`, `-j2`, `--test-threads=2`:

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  ok
  cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings        ok
  cargo test -p zerocode
    zerocode (lib)   54 passed; 0 failed
    zerocode (bin)   1583 passed; 2 failed; 2 ignored
    terminal_disconnect  3 passed
  ```

  Both failures, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` and `app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events`, also fail on clean master `5a51398dd` on this machine (1561 passed; same 2 failed) and are not touched by this PR.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** This recheck inspected the full local diff, every review and inline reply, the master changes affecting the integration, and all five locale catalogues. No live opener was run. The earlier interface smoke used a scratch configuration, a dead provider URI, and a 110×32 tmux pane with a demo home directory. It showed wrapped absolute and home-relative links, a missing path remaining plain, the continuation-row context menu, and Add path to chat inserting a code span. That earlier smoke did not launch Finder or a default app.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `b1c0571f9211`, ZeroCode Chat pane, 110×32, rendered from `tmux capture-pane -e`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**

  ![Wrapped paths underlined across rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/b1c0571f9211e1d4093c8c7029a7209c9565cd35/.pr-evidence/pr-path-links-00-wrapped-path.png)

  ![Path context menu opened from the continuation row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/b1c0571f9211e1d4093c8c7029a7209c9565cd35/.pr-evidence/pr-path-links-01-wrapped-path-menu.png)
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Historical right-click on the wrapped second row opened the menu for the full path, and Add path to chat inserted the full code span. Default-app opening, Finder reveal, and the symlink reveal notice have not been verified live.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace-wide tests were skipped: the change is confined to `apps/zerocode`. No live macOS opener capture was performed; it needs a real interactive session.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes. Rendering path-shaped transcript text schedules background `metadata` probes without a click, and an explicit click can hand a local path to the platform opener. Any existing absolute or home-relative path can qualify, including paths outside the workspace.
- New external network calls? Yes, indirectly possible through filesystem lookup. There is no new network client, but metadata probes can contact mounted filesystems, custom automount maps, or symlinks into them. Known host-keyed roots `/net`, `/Network`, and `/automount` are excluded before probing, including lexical dot-component variants. This reduces that risk without eliminating all filesystem-triggered network I/O; the automount concern was assessed in code and was not reproduced live.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Tests use temporary synthetic fixtures and the existing captures use demo paths.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Model or quoted text can nominate local paths for probes and user-triggered opening.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Background checks are capped at 32, cached, and kept off the draw thread. Remote sessions and Windows do not enable path links. Open and Reveal revalidate and canonicalize at action time, reject relative and control-character paths, and pass separate arguments without a shell. Recognised launching extensions, executable bits, and bundle metadata cause a reveal with a notice. This is not a workspace sandbox or a complete code-execution barrier: Finder aliases are not resolved by canonicalization and remain a follow-up, file associations can have side effects, and replacement between validation and launch remains possible.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing URL links, transcript data, and daemon protocol remain compatible.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. This adds TUI link and menu behavior without new configuration, environment variables, or command-line flags.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A - no migration or new configuration is required. Windows and remote sessions retain URL-only transcript links.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

This is a high-risk launch interaction confined to ZeroCode. No wire, configuration, or persisted-data migration is involved.

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After squash merge, run `git revert <actual-squash-commit-sha>` through the normal reviewed rollback process. This restores URL-only transcript links. The squash SHA does not exist yet; do not revert the master-refresh merge as a feature rollback.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Roll back the feature commit and rebuild ZeroCode.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A continuation-row click opens the wrong file, paths remain unlinked after checks complete, a remote path links locally, clicks appear to do nothing, or a launching target opens instead of revealing. Look for the localized `zc-chat-open-path-failed` and `zc-chat-path-revealed-instead` notices. No new log metric or alert is added. Opener subprocess completion is not reported, so confirm the actual app or Finder result.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A - no Supersedes

- Superseded PRs + authors (`#<pr> by @<author>`, one per line): N/A - no Supersedes.
- Scope materially carried forward: N/A - no superseded work.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? No.
- If `No`, why (inspiration-only, no direct code/design carry-over): N/A - no incorporated superseded contributions.

---

**Labels** live in the GitHub label UI, not in the body. The PR path labeler owns path/scope labels from `.github/labeler.yml`, and the PR size labeler owns canonical `size:*` labels. Maintainers and reviewers with label permissions still set `risk:*` and any missing manual labels via the sidebar. Contributors without label permission can note obvious label mismatches in a comment. Canonical colon-scoped labels use no-space spelling; during migration, copy exact live label spelling from the GitHub UI.

**Do not add bot/AI attribution footers** such as `Co-authored-by: Claude ...`
or `Created with Claude Code` to the PR body or commit-message tail. Human
co-author trailers are appropriate only for incorporated contributor work under
the supersede-attribution section and privacy contract.

**Privacy contract** (`docs/book/src/contributing/privacy.md`) is a merge gate. Never commit real identities, secrets, personal emails, or PII in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs.

prs.title: fix(zerocode): use local Linux clipboard writers and report copy outcomes
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Try an optional local Linux clipboard writer so Copy can work when the terminal ignores OSC 52.
  - Report successful local writes, unconfirmed terminal requests, and errors distinctly across Chat, Code, Logs, queued messages, links, and composer copy/cut.
  - Bound native input delivery and process completion, retain selected text on known failures, and consume failed composer copy keys before quit handling.
  - Preserve the first copy badge when the bottom notice resizes the transcript, and translate the new feedback in all five shipped catalogues.
- **Scope boundary:** ZeroCode text clipboard delivery and feedback. No daemon, RPC, configuration schema, clipboard-image cleanup, native macOS/Windows writer, dependency, lockfile, or CI changes.
- **Blast radius:** Explicit user copy/cut actions, transient feedback, and transcript feedback invalidation during redraw.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11418.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode is the terminal interface for chatting with agents. Its Copy actions previously asked the terminal to update the clipboard and immediately showed "Copied." The reporter confirmed that GNOME Terminal ignored both that request and a direct OSC 52 probe, while Alacritty worked.

This PR tries `wl-copy` or `xclip` on a local Linux desktop. A successful writer reports "Copied." SSH sessions, macOS, Windows, and Linux sessions without an installed compatible writer keep terminal copying, with "Requested" feedback because the terminal does not acknowledge delivery. Known write failures show an error and preserve selected text. Composer Cut keeps its existing undoable behavior after a terminal request.

The result belongs to the existing clipboard module and existing transient feedback. There is no new configuration setting, dependency, persistent state, or daemon call. One deadline covers pipe backpressure and helper completion. The helper is killed and reaped on failure. Copy badges survive the notice-driven viewport change when captured content still matches; width and content changes invalidate them.

The relatively large diff covers the shared writer, each existing copy consumer, and tests in their owning modules. A writer-only change would leave misleading feedback; a feedback-only change would leave the local GNOME clipboard failure.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Final-head desktop feedback and clipboard delivery need real-interface verification.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface:tui`, ZeroCode Chat/Code, composer, and Logs. N/A for messaging channel; these are local terminal panes.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use the same Ubuntu GNOME Terminal desktop and daemon configuration for `master` and this branch. Use `wl-copy` on Wayland or `xclip` on X11. Use an OSC 52-capable terminal for the separate SSH case. Record the binary's source revision. No provider changes are required.
- **Steps to run:** On each revision, launch `zerocode`; click a message Copy target once and paste into another application; repeat for a code block. Select composer text, press Ctrl+X, paste elsewhere, then Ctrl+Z to Undo. Repeat Copy without a compatible helper on PATH. Repeat through SSH in an OSC 52-capable terminal. In a disposable test environment, use a failing clipboard helper and copy a Logs selection; record the visible error and retained selection. Capture the first-click badge and Logs error with surrounding TUI context. Also repeat with enough history to scroll, so opening the bottom notice changes the viewport.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** A successful local writer copies the intended text and shows Copied on the first action. Without a helper, or over SSH, feedback says Requested; terminal support determines delivery. Known writer errors report failure and retain selected text. Cut after an emitted terminal request remains undoable. The new regression targets first-action badge retention during notice resize; real-interface confirmation is still needed.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Copy always requests OSC 52 and reports Copied even when GNOME Terminal ignores it. There is no local Linux text writer. The copy badge can disappear when the bottom notice changes the viewport. Cut removes text after an unconfirmed terminal request.

### How I tested

Local Cargo results for the pushed head `caa009b0b` are below.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39024301235/job/117373409734) passed for published head `f607e1b8ee6d187a538f82d0b914a3cdca841d4a`. Its Test, Lint, Format, MSRV, platform checks, and ZeroCode RPC boundary jobs supply historical compilation/test evidence for the original implementation. prs.title: feat(runtime): show a foreground delegate's tool calls in the parent turn
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A foreground agentic delegate ran its tool loop with an inert observer, so while it worked the parent turn, the RPC stream and ZeroCode showed nothing until the child answered. A long delegate looked the same whether it was working, looping or stuck.
  - Each tool execution in a turn that streams events now scopes the turn's event sender and the call id (`agent/tool_execution.rs`, next to #11298's cancellation scope). A foreground agentic delegate gives its child loop an observer (`tools/delegate_activity.rs`) that turns each child tool start and finish into one new live turn event, `TurnEvent::DelegateActivity` in `zeroclaw-api`: the tool name, a secret-redacted argument summary (`approval::summarize_args`), and a 400-character output preview of the already-scrubbed result. Parallel workers carry the scope across their spawn. A delegate inside the child reports one level deeper (`depth`) against the same parent call.
  - The observer sends with `try_send`, so a full parent channel drops activity instead of slowing the child or the parent turn.
  - RPC forwards it as a `delegate_activity` `session/update` (`rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs`). ZeroCode shows a child-call count and the running tool under the delegate card, and the call list when the card is expanded.
  - A tool's own `approved` input is left out of child summaries: under a successful call, `approved: false` read as a refusal.
  - While the delegate's turn runs, its card's Response line now says "Waiting for response" instead of "Result not recorded". The card only says that for a call this pane saw start in the running turn; restored history and calls a finished or cancelled turn left without a result keep the neutral wording from #11446.
- **Scope boundary:** no persistence: the event isn't written to the turn checkpoint or session history, so restored sessions look as before. Background delegates don't forward (their turn may be gone; #11292's `check_result` progress covers them). The child's text, reasoning, usage and approvals aren't forwarded. No config key and no opt-in. Other channels (ACP server, gateway WS, chat channels) ignore the new variant through their existing fall-through arms.
- **Blast radius:** the tool-execution scope wraps every tool's `execute` when the turn streams events, but only the delegate tool reads it. Foreground agentic delegates now run with a forwarding observer instead of the no-op one. RPC clients get a new `session/update` type; older ZeroCode builds ignore it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Part of #10531 (its observer-forwarding piece; #11292 shipped the first piece). Related #8763 (live half of the ZeroCode subagent view), #11446 (the neutral wording kept for restored cards). Holding-crate exception row: #11697 (merged).

### What this does, simply

When one agent hands work to a helper agent and waits for the answer, you used to see nothing until the helper was done. Now the waiting card in ZeroCode shows how many tools the helper has used and which one it's running right now, and expanding the card lists each of them. Only the tool names and a short, secret-stripped summary of each call are shown, never the helper's full inputs or outputs. Nothing is saved; reopening the session shows the card as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: I ran it live in the experiment build; the tests below drive the delegate path end to end with a scripted provider.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Chat with an agent that has an agentic delegate target.

### How I tested

```bash
zc-cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::delegate agent::tool_execution rpc::dispatch::tests::delegate rpc::types
zc-cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" zc-cargo doc -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime --no-deps
rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <changed files>
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Test and Parallel Runtime Test run the new runtime and ZeroCode tests; Lint covers clippy, rustdoc and comment hygiene; Docs Style covers the `rpc-socket.md` addition.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no test drives a real daemon and ZeroCode together; the RPC mapping and the ZeroCode handler are tested on each side of the wire.
- **Commands run and tail output:** clippy clean (exit 0). Runtime filter: `318 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`. ZeroCode: `1459 passed; 1 failed` — the failure is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, which also fails on master on the machine I ran it on. Rustdoc exit 0, fmt clean, hygiene gate passed, docs gate `0 error(s)`.
- New tests:
  - `foreground_agentic_delegate_reports_child_tool_calls_to_the_parent_turn`: a scripted agentic child calls `echo_tool`; the parent sink gets exactly one start and one finish with the parent call id, agent, child call id, a summary and an `echo:` preview.
  - `background_delegate_does_not_report_to_the_parent_turn`: same child with a progress sink (the background shape) runs its tool and sends nothing to the parent.
  - `tools_see_the_parent_event_sink_only_in_a_streaming_turn`: the scope is visible inside `execute` with the call id, absent without an event sender, and gone afterwards.
  - `delegate_activity::tests`: secret argument redacted, preview bounded, id-less calls get one id shared by start and finish, a full parent channel drops instead of blocking.
  - `delegate_activity_notification_is_flat_and_round_trips` (RPC), `parses_delegate_activity_update` and `delegate_card_shows_child_activity_while_running_and_keeps_it_after` (ZeroCode).
  - `subagent_card_says_waiting_only_while_its_turn_runs`: a live delegate card says "Waiting for response"; after its turn settles without a result it says "Result not recorded". The existing `subagent_card_restored_missing_result_does_not_claim_live_work` passes unchanged.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Swapping the forwarder back to the no-op observer makes the foreground test fail and leaves the background one passing; forcing the card's waiting flag off makes the waiting test fail. Both restored afterwards. Live run in the experiment build ([branch](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d), dogfood base `0341618f9d69`): a foreground delegate to another agent running four slow read-only tool calls; the parent's card counted the calls, showed the running one, said "Waiting for response" until the child answered, and kept the list afterwards.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Screenshot`
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** ZeroCode TUI, experiment build [20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d), which carries this PR's three UI-facing commits; the later commits are the E0275 type-erasure fix and a rebase, neither of which changes rendering.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6232092560
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** asked the agent to delegate in the foreground to a helper agent that runs several slow tool calls. While it runs, the card shows the call count, the running tool and "Waiting for response"; expanded, it lists each call with its redacted summary; after the helper answers, the list stays and the result replaces the waiting line.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full `zeroclaw-runtime` suite; I ran the delegate, tool-execution and RPC-type filters, which hold every test touching the changed code.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6232092560 (experiment build). Real screenshots of the current head pending.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Child arguments go through the same redacting summarizer as approval prompts, and the output preview comes from the result the loop has already credential-scrubbed. Tested with an `api_key` argument.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The activity goes to the client only; it never enters a model request. ZeroCode renders it through the existing terminal-safe text path.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: n/a

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The `session/update` type is additive; older clients fall through their unknown-type arms.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a delegate card without a child-call line while its child runs tools, or child calls shown under the wrong card.

prs.title: fix(runtime): keep personality files stable per session so edits don't bust the prompt cache
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `Agent` renders the `## Project Context` block (the personality files: `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `TOOLS.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `USER.md`, `HEARTBEAT.md`, `BOOTSTRAP.md`, `MEMORY.md` when injected) once, on its first system-prompt build, and reuses that text every turn. Before this, `IdentitySection` re-read the files on every turn's rebuild. The system prompt heads the provider's cached prefix, so any edit to one of those files made the next request of every live session of that agent miss the prompt cache for the whole conversation (#11696).
  - New `PromptContext::identity_snapshot` carries the pre-rendered text. `prompt::render_identity_section` is the shared renderer, and `None` keeps today's read-now behavior for other builders.
  - New `Agent::reload_personality` re-reads the files on purpose and rebuilds the system prompt. It's exposed as `session/reload_context` (RPC, `sessions:update` grant, owner-only, refused with `SESSION_BUSY` while a turn holds the agent) and as the ZeroCode `/reload-context` command. After its session lookups, the handler re-resolves the caller's current grants and holds it to ownership of the admitted record right before the reload, as `session/append` and `session/abort` do. ZeroCode says whether anything changed and that the changed prompt may reduce cache reuse on the next request.
- **Scope boundary:** this doesn't touch the CLI `loop_::run` path or the channel orchestrator (the channel path already builds once). It also doesn't touch the `tool_search` deferred-tools section, which still changes the prompt when a tool is activated (noted in #11696). No config switch.
- **Blast radius:** long-lived `Agent` sessions (ZeroCode/ACP, gateway WS). **Behavior change:** an agent that edits its own rules mid-session no longer sees the new text in its system prompt on the next turn. It already has the edit in its conversation context, and other live sessions get it on `/reload-context` or in a new session.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11696. Related #8321.
- **Holding-crate exception:** the `zeroclaw-runtime` changes are covered by the pending personality-snapshot row in #11697 (ADR-016), which has merged.

### What this does, simply

Each agent has a few notes files that are pasted into the start of every conversation. ZeroClaw re-read those files before every turn. If anything in them changed, even one line, the provider couldn't reuse its cached copy of the conversation, and the next request was billed at full price. That happened for every open session of that agent, not just the one that edited the file. With long sessions this cost about $1–2 per session per edit.

Now a session reads the notes once and keeps that copy. New sessions see edits right away. An open session picks them up when you type `/reload-context`. Its prompt then changes, so the next request may get less use out of the provider's cache; you choose when that happens.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `tui` (ZeroCode Code pane over RPC)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a provider that reports cached input tokens. Two ZeroCode sessions of the same agent, each a few turns in.
- **Steps to run:** append a line to the agent's workspace `AGENTS.md`. Send one message in each session. Check `cached_input_tokens` in the cost ledger. Then run `/reload-context` in one session and send one more message.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first request after the edit stays cached in both sessions. `/reload-context` shows "Context reloaded…", and only that session's next request reads less from the cache. A second `/reload-context` says "Context unchanged".
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the first request after the edit is uncached (`cached_input_tokens` null/0) in both sessions.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test/clippy jobs for `zeroclaw-runtime` and `zerocode`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known.
- **Commands run and tail output** at head `3794bcf4a254` (rebased onto `ee2f5f58f7d7`), through the remote cargo wrapper:
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- reload_context a_reload_` → `4 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` → `5811 passed; 2 failed`. The two failures are `relay::local_dial_tests::a_closed_route_releases_a_dial_parked_on_a_stalled_listener` and `a_dial_that_never_connects_ends_on_its_own_budget`, which fail the same way on `ee2f5f58f7d7` in a clean detached worktree. This PR doesn't touch `relay`.
  - `cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode` → `1550 passed; 2 failed`. `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` and `app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events` also fail on `ee2f5f58f7d7` (the second is timing-sensitive; it passed once and failed three times there).
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` and `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` → clean.
- **Earlier runs** at `f0fd4f895a78`, before the rebase:
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- personality_edit_mid_session session_reload_context new_session_methods_are_classified remote_dispatch_rejects_every_foreign build_system_prompt_omits_memory_md method_all_no_duplicates method_from_wire_roundtrip agent::prompt::` → `test result: ok. 35 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent:: rpc::dispatch tools::delegate` → `2149 passed; 1 failed`. The failure is `new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, which fails the same way on the base `f12da7462a0f` in a clean detached worktree (`0 passed; 1 failed`). It isn't caused by this change.
  - `cargo test -p zerocode -- input_bar chat::tests::old_daemon reload` → `160 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` → clean. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the changed files → clean.
- **Regression guard:** `personality_edit_mid_session_keeps_system_prompt_byte_stable` runs two streamed turns with an `AGENTS.md` edit between them and asserts the provider-visible system prompts are byte-identical. It then checks that `reload_personality` reports the change and that turn 3 carries the new text. With the snapshot disabled (render every turn) it fails: `assertion left == right failed: a mid-session AGENTS.md edit must not change the cached system prompt`.
- **Authority regression guard:** `a_reload_is_refused_when_its_grant_is_revoked_while_it_waits` and `a_reload_by_a_demoted_administrator_is_held_to_ownership` pause the reload after its gate, republish the policy, then release it. Both expect `FORBIDDEN` and an agent that still holds its first snapshot. `a_reload_of_an_own_session_survives_an_unrelated_policy_change` is the permitted control. With the recheck removed, the first two fail and the control still passes.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I'm verifying this in the experiment build. I didn't run a live provider cache check on master.
### Screenshots

Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11698#issuecomment-6514495140 (macOS Terminal.app captures of `725dcbbf69`).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The new RPC re-reads the same workspace files the prompt already read, for the session's own agent, and needs `sessions:update` plus session ownership like `session/rename`.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. It's the same text as before; only the time it's read changes.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: n/a

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes on the wire: the new method is additive, and an old daemon returns method-not-found to `/reload-context`, which ZeroCode shows as an error line. The behavior change is described under Blast radius.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No config. The RPC method `session/reload_context` and the ZeroCode command `/reload-context` are new.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the PR's merge commit (head `3794bcf4a254`).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** an agent ignoring a personality-file edit in an already-open session (expected until `/reload-context`). Report it if a new session doesn't see the edit.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): show readable Config labels and full field details
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Config field rows use readable labels and bounded value previews so long arrays do not consume the visible row.
  - The selected field's Help view starts with its exact path, complete description, and current masked value. It follows the selected row on regular field tabs, including filtered results.
  - Shared help prose uses the existing Unicode-aware text wrapper so long paths and array items wrap and remain reachable by scrolling.
- **Scope boundary:** Presentation and field help only; configuration keys, defaults, validation, registry, and save behavior are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode Config rendering, prose wrapping in the shared Help overlay, and Config documentation.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11489. Related #9363 for localization completeness and #8062 for structured JSON editing.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `risk:medium`, `size:M`, `zerocode`, `docs`.

### What this does, simply

Config currently shows raw setting names and clips descriptions into a small fixed area. This PR makes the rows easier to scan and lets you open Help to read the full setting information, including its exact configuration path and long value. Secrets stay hidden. Unset values and environment overrides remain distinguishable; unit and default explanations come from the schema description, without inferring how a current value was configured.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The change reuses the existing Config descriptors, Fluent catalogue, Help overlay, and text-input wrapping. It adds no metadata registry, RPC method, dependency, or persisted state. One-line rows preserve existing list and mouse geometry. The inline Enter-to-edit hint is removed to leave room for the label and preview; the existing edit binding remains available. The supporting shared-help change is needed because whitespace-only wrapping permanently clipped long unbroken paths and values.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config and Help.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Connect ZeroCode to your existing daemon. Use an existing agent with a precheck timeout or a risk profile with a long command/path list; no configuration change is needed.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config and select a field with a long value (for example a risk profile's command list). Inspect its label and preview, then press `?` (or Ctrl+G) to open Help and scroll through the complete path, description, and value. Close Help, open the filter, type part of a setting path, move to a match with the arrow keys, and press Ctrl+G; while the filter box is focused, `?` is typed into the filter and Enter opens the editor. Help should describe the highlighted match. Repeat on a secret field. Run the same steps on `master` to compare. The filter matches setting paths, not values.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Readable labels, an ellipsis on clipped previews, the highlighted field's exact path and full description/value accessible through scrolling, and hidden secret contents.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Raw path labels, clipped long row values, and descriptions limited to one or two rows. Field information is absent from Help; long unbroken help prose can be clipped.

### How I tested

prs.title: feat(zerocode): confirm config deletion and reset
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Require target confirmation before deleting a Config alias or Costs resource, or resetting a configured field.
  - Keep deletion refusals, cleanup warnings and refresh failures in a scrollable result panel until dismissed. A completed or uncertain mutation cannot be retried by dismissing its result.
  - Name the actions Delete and Reset in Help and rebinding while preserving existing stored binding identifiers.
  - Show the resolved Delete shortcut in the footer for an existing alias or Costs entry, so deletion is discoverable without opening Help.
- **Scope boundary:** ZeroCode only. No new cascade rules, daemon mutation semantics, undo storage or secret-value display.
- **Blast radius:** Config input routing, client response handling and Config action labels. Skills archival and local keybinding override clearing retain their behavior.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11487. Related #11172 for the optional daemon deletion preview.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode's Config editor can remove aliases and restore fields to their default behavior. Previously, pressing the deletion or reset key sent the change immediately. The daemon could reject an unsafe deletion, but it could not tell whether a valid deletion was accidental.

This PR shows the selected target first. You can confirm or cancel; moving the underlying selection cannot change the captured target. After confirmation, the result stays readable, including warnings when cleanup was incomplete or the list could not be refreshed.

When the daemon supports `config/delete-plan`, the confirmation shows its blockers and references that would be removed. Older daemons show an explicit unavailable-preview notice. The daemon still makes the final authorization and deletion decision.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

Delete and Reset share one Config dialog: either a confirmation with a captured target, or a result that cannot send a mutation. The outer input loop gives it priority over pane navigation and paste. Typed client responses preserve the daemon's applied flag and optional warnings; no second cascade planner is introduced. The larger diff includes request-recording regressions for destructive input and failure paths, plus existing action consumers that follow the renamed Rust variants.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the running TUI's presentation.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a disposable Config alias or Costs entry, or a non-secret field whose reset is safe. Use a ZeroCode binary built from this PR with an existing daemon connection.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config and focus an existing alias or Costs entry. Check that the footer shows the resolved Delete binding (`x` by default), then press it. Check the displayed target and cancel with Esc. Reopen confirmation and confirm only a disposable target. For a field, use the resolved Reset binding (`d` by default). The Delete hint should disappear on the Add row or when Delete is unbound.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Opening and cancellation do not change configuration. Confirmation applies one change to the displayed target. The result remains visible until dismissed; long text can be scrolled.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same Delete or Reset key sends the mutation immediately, without a target-confirmation step.

### How I tested

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
passed

cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
passed

cargo test --no-fail-fast -p zerocode
1646 passed; 2 failed
```

- **Validation revision and environment:** I ran the checks above on the Mac mini at `0ab51b9854b6e6e8e91d05053e06c06116ed6a67` through `zc-cargo-narrow`, with two Cargo jobs and two test threads for the package run. These are local results; CI results for this head are not included.
- **Known test failures:** `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` also fails on clean master `f2b432db` on this Mini. `app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events` is a known timing flake. The package run therefore has two failures.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source and response-contract comparison. Recorded outbound requests exercise the real Config handlers and client: open/cancel/mouse/paste/repeat, captured alias and Costs targets, reset tab/cursor preservation, blocked and unavailable previews, preview failure and committed refresh failure. The footer regression covers custom and unbound Delete shortcuts, independent alias/Costs selection, and Add/filter/pane suppression. Master integration preserves SecretMap container refusal and Config RPC-timeout handling; their focused tests passed alongside confirmation. Existing Config editing tests also passed. No live configuration was deleted for this verification.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11510#issuecomment-6233163044 (experiment build, taken before the current head). Real screenshots of the current head pending.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Automated confirmation sent one mutation for the captured target; cancellation sent none. Refresh failure retained the committed result and warning without retrying.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full-workspace validation was not run locally. The package checks and their two known failures are recorded above. Real-terminal captures remain pending.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots of the current code: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11510#issuecomment-6514492960 (macOS Terminal.app captures, built from `7564c57fe8`; the head since then only removes test code). Earlier screenshots from my experiment build: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11510#issuecomment-6233163044.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No; the optional read-only preview uses the existing daemon RPC connection.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Confirmation displays paths and aliases, not field values or the planner's raw reference values.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No; fixtures use neutral names.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for stored configuration and daemon mutation contracts. Delete and Reset now require confirmation.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Help and rebinding labels change; stored `config_tab.toggle_secret` and `config_tab.delete_row` identifiers remain valid.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: No configuration migration. Costs deletion uses Delete (`x` by default); the old redundant Reset (`d`) deletion shortcut is removed. Existing custom Delete bindings still resolve through the preserved identifier. Only `METHOD_NOT_FOUND` permits the unavailable-preview path; other preview failures are shown instead of enabling confirmation.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commit and use the prior ZeroCode binary. This restores immediate Delete/Reset behavior; it does not undo changes already confirmed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Existing keybinding overrides continue to apply.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Confirmation does not open, displays a wrong target, disappears instead of preserving an error, or a confirmed mutation reports a refresh failure. The daemon's authorization and deletion safeguards remain unchanged.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): add multi-select editors for alias-reference arrays
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Offer searchable multi-select editing for Config arrays that reference existing names, using the same schema metadata and alias lookup as scalar references.
  - Keep changes local until Ctrl+S. Preserve the existing order and unresolved entries, append newly selected names, and send an array when saving, including an empty array.
  - Read the daemon's TOML array display correctly so quotes, backslashes, and untouched text fallback entries survive a save.
- **Scope boundary:** Ordinary text arrays and structured JSON editing retain their current editors. Alias rename, MCP grants, config serialization, and provider fallback execution are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Generated Config field metadata, reference-name lookup, and ZeroCode Config field editors. Five arrays receive reference metadata: agent `skill_bundles`, `knowledge_bundles` and `mcp_bundles`, and MCP bundle `servers` and `exclude`. Provider `fallback_models` and channel-reference arrays keep the text editor; they can be added later with the same `#[alias_source]` attribute.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11485. Related #8062 and #7468 remain separate.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `risk:medium`, `size:L`, `config`, `zerocode`.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode's Config tab lets you choose the bundles an agent uses. Several settings take a list of existing names, but the editor previously asked you to type each name on a separate line.

This PR lists those names with selection boxes. Search with `/`, toggle a name with Enter or a double-click, and save the staged list with Ctrl+S. Escape cancels the edit; while searching, the first Escape clears the search.

Opening the editor keeps every saved entry, including names that no longer appear in the available choices. Existing entries keep their order. New choices are appended. Fields without reference metadata, or without available lookup results, keep text editing.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The schema remains the owner of reference metadata, and the existing alias lookup RPC supplies choices. MCP server names use the existing lookup of server `name` keys. The editor adds one ordered staging list; it does not maintain another catalogue of valid aliases. Tests exercise both generated metadata and input handlers with RPC save/readback. The added wire enum variant follows the existing requirement that the daemon and ZeroCode come from the same build.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. A real Config session provides useful visual confirmation of the selection boxes and help.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Run a daemon and ZeroCode built from the same checkout. Use an existing agent and at least two skill bundles (`[skill_bundles.<alias>]`; with `directory` unset, each resolves to `<install>/shared/skills/<alias>/`). With none configured, the field falls back to the text editor with "None configured yet. Enter manually." No provider request is required.
- **Steps to run:** In Config, open Agents, select the agent, open Bundles, and edit `skill_bundles`. Search with `/`, use Enter to toggle a name, clear the search with Escape, then cancel with Escape. Reopen, toggle a name, save with Ctrl+S, and reopen to check the saved selection. Repeat with `knowledge_bundles` or `mcp_bundles`. For MCP bundles, edit `servers` or `exclude` using existing server names.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Reference arrays show available names with checked/unchecked boxes. Toggles remain staged until Ctrl+S. Cancellation leaves the saved list unchanged. An empty selection saves an empty list with the field's existing meaning.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same arrays open a one-entry-per-line text editor, requiring you to type valid identifiers.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Required CI passed](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37142265772/job/111260581062) on the pre-rebase head `280fc9ca851147e21a0976ca3c399e053e08bdfb`; CI is rerunning on the current head `aa8a7dfd5acfb42af178a67f51edf2fb544d1589`. Workspace tests, formatting, lint, schema/build checks, Windows compilation, and the ZeroCode RPC dependency boundary supply the broader coverage.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI cannot provide direct visual evidence from a real interactive Config session.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo test --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode config_manager::tests -- --test-threads=8
64 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib alias_metadata_tests
3 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-macros --lib alias_source
2 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode mcp_servers_alias_source_round_trips
1 passed; 0 failed
cargo fmt --all -- --check
Passed
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source tracing confirmed that keyboard and mouse selection use the same staging handler and that MCP names use the canonical resolver. Automated input/RPC tests cover filtered toggles, ordered and unresolved selections, cancellation without a write, empty saves, scalar selection, lookup failure/empty-result text fallback, TOML quote/backslash handling, and reopening after TOML-string readback. I also ran the picker in a real ZeroCode Config session: two skill bundles listed with selection boxes on the agent's `skill_bundles` field, and `/` search narrowed the list.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Two screenshots in [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11502#issuecomment-6232005804): the `skill_bundles` picker with bundles listed, and a search.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Automated tests used the current head `aa8a7dfd5acfb42af178a67f51edf2fb544d1589`, ZeroCode Config input/RPC boundary. The screenshots come from my experiment build [`experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d) (commit [`af67956b5e9d`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/af67956b5e9d1b9a9f0521dab4a1f48c999d6e71)), which carries this PR's changes in its dogfood base [`0341618f9d69`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/0341618f9d69e31bf38300d134ba86e98491d49d), plus a one-line fixup adapting the save path to a newer `config/set` return value. That fixup is now part of this PR after the rebase onto master.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11502#issuecomment-6232005804 (experiment build, taken before the current head). Real screenshots of the current head pending.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Handler tests stage filtered additions without `config/set`, save one JSON array followed by one readback, preserve original order/unknown entries, and send no write on cancellation.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full local workspace validation is delegated to required CI.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots of the current code: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11502#issuecomment-6514491857 (macOS Terminal.app captures, built from `40fe196e0f`; the head since then only removes test code). Earlier screenshots from my experiment build: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11502#issuecomment-6232005804.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No. The existing daemon RPC supplies choices and saves.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for saved configuration. The existing matched daemon/ZeroCode version requirement remains in effect.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. Reference arrays have a multi-select Config editor, and field metadata includes array alias sources and `mcp_servers`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: Rebuild and restart the daemon and ZeroCode from the same checkout, as required by the current wire protocol. No config migration is needed. Missing metadata or failed/empty lookup results use the text editor.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the editor commit, then the metadata commit, and rebuild both binaries: `git revert --no-edit aa8a7dfd5acf 2198666216cb 779bc969bb`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. The text editor remains the fallback for unsupported arrays and failed/empty lookup results.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Incorrect checked names, lost references or changed priority after save/reopen, a write after cancellation, or an array editor sending a scalar value. Check the saved field and Config RPC payload.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A. This PR does not supersede another contribution.

### What this does, simply

The log reader resumes older pages using byte offsets. Its current cursor tests use ASCII message content, where character and byte counts coincide. prs.title: fix(tools): report a dismissed ask_user choice as an answer, not an error
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - A structured-only channel can return `Ok(None)` when the user dismisses a choice question. `ask_user` previously reported a tool failure and explicitly told the agent to retry. It now returns success, no error, and `DISMISSED: the user closed the question without choosing.`
  - The existing immediate return is preserved: dismissal does not fall through to `send` + `listen`. Selected answers, channel errors, timeouts, and free-form-capable fallback keep their existing behavior.
  - The existing dismissal regression checks success, the exact output, no error, no listener fallback, and prompt completion. Two more tool-level tests, added in fe92ee9cb, cover a selected answer and a channel failure on structured-only channels.
- **Scope boundary:** `crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/ask_user.rs` only. No changes to `poll`, channel protocols, configuration, approval policy, or ZeroCode rendering. Free-form questions remain unsupported on structured-only channels.
- **Blast radius:** Choice-style `ask_user` results on structured-only channels, including ACP and the RPC approval bridge used by ZeroCode. Success classification also reaches existing tool observers, receipts when enabled, and provider history. The channel API also uses `Ok(None)` for missing form capability; that case receives the same dismissal text even if no question was displayed.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11623. Companion to #11624, which handles client-side prompt withdrawal and question/outcome presentation. This PR alone does not resolve the broader lost-prompt and transcript issue.

### What this does, simply

An agent can ask you a question with several choices. If you close that question without choosing, the agent should learn that you did not answer. Previously it received an error telling it to ask again. This change reports the dismissal as a completed tool result. It removes that retry instruction; it does not guarantee what the agent will do next. A client that never replies still produces a timeout error.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. A real ZeroCode dismissal verifies the visible result and interaction that tool unit tests cannot establish.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Code pane using its RPC approval bridge. ACP clients are additional affected consumers; no ACP-client capture is supplied.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build matching daemon/client revisions separately for `master` and this branch. Configure a working provider, enable `ask_user` in the effective tool selection, and use a client advertising form elicitation. Keep the same client revision and configuration for both runs; record whether companion #11624 is included. Use a synthetic question and choices.
- **Steps to run:** In the Code pane, request that the agent call `ask_user` with `question: "Continue?"` and `choices: ["Yes", "No"]`. While the choice prompt is visible, press Esc. Inspect the tool result card and record its completed state. Repeat on `master` with the same setup. Separately select Yes to check ordinary answers.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Dismissal completes promptly with success, no tool error, and output `DISMISSED: the user closed the question without choosing.` Selecting Yes returns Yes. Exact card styling and companion-dependent transcript behavior still need real captures.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same dismissal returns a failed tool result explaining that the structured choice was not completed and telling the agent to retry `ask_user`.

### How I tested

Source review covered the full change against `origin/master`, the local merge, channel trait contracts, ACP/RPC handling, factory registration, and runtime success-result propagation. This is historical support for the published implementation, not validation of the local merge or prepared tests. [CI run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39027742759).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Fresh CI runs on the pushed head `fe92ee9cb`. Tool-level tests do not exercise the ZeroCode renderer or a real Esc interaction.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Run on head `fe92ee9cb` (master merge `36cd3065d` + the two new tests), Mac mini, `zc-cargo-narrow`, `-j2`, `--test-threads=2`:

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                      ok
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings      ok
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools ask_user                           16 passed; 0 failed
  ```
