prs.title: fix(providers): use the shared stream idle bound for Anthropic
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Anthropic streaming used a fixed 90-second byte-idle timeout. OpenAI Responses and OpenAI-compatible streams already use the shared 300-second floor introduced by #10886.
  - Gateways that route Claude requests through Bedrock can stay silent during large tool inputs. The original investigation reported failures when that silence exceeded 90 seconds.
  - Anthropic now uses `stream_idle_timeout(timeout_secs)`: 300 seconds by default, raised by a larger configured timeout. The schema field description and both provider guides describe the same policy.
  - Body-read timeout errors name the effective bound and the `timeout_secs` setting instead of reporting only reqwest's decoding error.
- **Scope boundary:** This PR changes Anthropic stream-idle enforcement, diagnostics, tests and documentation. Request payloads, authentication, retry policy and non-streaming timeouts retain their existing behavior. It adds no configuration key.
- **Blast radius:** Anthropic-family streaming and its operator-facing timeout description. A genuinely stalled stream now waits 300 seconds, or a higher configured bound, before failing. Consumer cancellation still aborts the parser immediately.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10886, Related #10884. Depends on #11541. Per the maintainer's review, land #11541 first, then refresh and recheck this branch with its extra-header and redirect protections preserved.

### What this does, simply

When a Claude stream stops sending data, ZeroClaw waits for a limited time before ending the turn. The Anthropic adapter allowed only 90 seconds. Some gateways send no keep-alive events while the model prepares a large tool input, so a working generation could exceed that limit and fail with a vague error.

Anthropic streams now use the same 300-second floor as the two OpenAI streaming paths. Setting the provider's existing `timeout_secs` above 300 extends that window. Each body read resets the idle timer; this is not a deadline for the whole generation. A read timeout now explains which limit fired.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Real-interface evidence for the changed configuration description and timeout diagnostic is still needed. A controlled endpoint can demonstrate the timeout change without a paid provider call.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli` for an interactive streamed request, and `surface=tui` for the Zerocode configuration editor. Messaging channel: N/A, this recipe uses no messaging channel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use synthetic configuration and a local Anthropic-protocol mock that returns successful SSE headers and an initial text event, stays silent for 100 seconds, then sends a terminal event. Configure an Anthropic profile with `timeout_secs = 120` and an agent named `idle-proof` that uses it. Use the same configuration and mock on captured master 5a51398dd5 and this branch. Do not use production credentials.
- **Steps to run:** Start the mock, select its Anthropic profile, and run `zeroclaw agent -a idle-proof`, then enter `Reply with the mock response` at the prompt. Use interactive mode so the CLI supplies the streaming sink. Record the emitted text, completion or interruption, and elapsed silence. Restart the mock for each revision. In Zerocode, open that provider's `timeout_secs` description and capture the full rendered description. For the named-error case, repeat with the endpoint silent beyond 300 seconds and capture the actual supported-interface error output. A larger configured bound needs its own elapsed-time check if claimed as wire-tested.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The 100-second silence completes successfully. The configuration description includes Anthropic. A body timeout names the 300-second bound and advises raising `timeout_secs` above that bound.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same 100-second silence reaches Anthropic's fixed 90-second read timeout. The configuration description omits Anthropic, and a stalled body lacks the shared named-bound diagnostic.

### How I tested

The earlier published head 107783d22773242936e78ae93317507ca4ef178d has passing hosted CI. The refreshed revision 70009f64d6cd31261dec9e978c73537f1156d895 merges master 5a51398dd52469644f2c2a017296b4ff89c8e02a. Its full diff and overlapping master changes were inspected. The docs style and links gates and `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD` pass on that refreshed revision. Rust compilation and execution results for that revision are pending.

The PR adds `anthropic::tests::stream_idle_bound_uses_shared_floor_and_timeout_secs` for the 300-second floor and a 900-second override, and `anthropic::tests::sse_read_timeout_names_idle_bound` for the parser diagnostic. The latter uses a 100 ms test client with a supplied 300-second diagnostic bound. It verifies the error path and text, not elapsed-time agreement or the production client's configured deadline. Production client/parser wiring was checked separately in source.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Historical [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37471074798/job/112299840714), [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37471074798/job/112294405441), Format, Lint and Docs Style pass for published head 107783d227. They cover the original provider/config changes and Markdown, but do not certify the refreshed revision or the future #11541 integration.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Fresh CI runs on the pushed head `70009f64d`. The timeout-message test does not measure the production 300/900-second client deadline. Combined header/redirect/timeout validation after #11541 lands is still needed.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  Run on head `70009f64d` (master merge), Mac mini, `zc-cargo-narrow`, `-j2`, `--test-threads=2`:

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                    ok
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings   ok
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-config
    zeroclaw_config     1817 passed; 1 failed
    zeroclaw_providers  1980 passed; 1 failed; 4 ignored
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers openai::tool_round_policy_tests             ok (rerun)
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers anthropic                                   ok
  ```

  `policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception` also fails on clean master `5a51398dd` on this machine. `openai::tool_round_policy_tests::native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults` failed once with connection refused and passed on rerun. Neither is touched by this PR.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected the shared timeout helper, factory forwarding, streaming client, parser error mapping, cancellation guard and master integration. A read-only merge preview with #11541 finds conflicts requiring preservation of both changes. The original author reported timestamped probes: Anthropic direct, 2 pings and 30.0 seconds maximum silence; a header-authenticated gateway pool, 2 pings and 30.1 seconds; Bedrock via gateway, no pings and 51.2 seconds. Those are historical reports, with no attached raw capture verified in this pass. The live Bedrock request was not rerun on this branch.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshots pending.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Real screenshots pending.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Real screenshots pending.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Source and tests show Anthropic using the shared floor and configurable increase, with the corrected description and named-bound diagnostic. The real-interface A/B observations described above have not been collected on the refreshed revision.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Live provider probes were not run; no current gateway credentials were used. Workspace-wide tests were skipped; the change is limited to the providers and config crates.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No. Existing Anthropic calls can remain open longer while idle.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. #11541 owns the separate header/redirect work and is not incorporated here yet.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A, all answers above are No. The longer resource-holding interval is documented under blast radius and rollback.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The existing setting gains the same stream-idle semantics for Anthropic as for the two OpenAI paths.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. The existing `timeout_secs` setting now raises Anthropic's stream-idle bound above 300 seconds; its config-editor description and timeout diagnostic reflect that behavior. No key, flag or environment variable is added.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: No migration is required. Keep existing configuration for the 300-second floor. Set `timeout_secs` above 300 on the Anthropic profile only when a longer idle wait is needed, then apply the provider configuration through the existing configuration workflow.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After merge, `git revert <squash-commit>` restores Anthropic's fixed 90-second idle limit and prior diagnostics. Revert this PR's squash commit, preserving separately landed #11541 protections.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. `timeout_secs` raises the new idle bound but cannot reduce it below 300 seconds.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Search provider warnings for `SSE read error` or `stream idle timeout`. A hung stream can now take 300 seconds, or its higher configured bound, to fail. Incorrect bound text or unexpected interruption indicates a regression. Reverting also restores the earlier risk of failures during long silent tool-input generation.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors (`#<pr> by @<author>`, one per line): N/A, no Supersedes.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): expose settings actions and filter keybindings
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Client settings now show contextual action hints using the effective keymap. Keybindings can be searched by action name, action identifier, or effective key without executing settings actions while typing.
- **Scope boundary:** Existing settings writes, preset application, and modified global shortcuts keep their existing behavior. Effective-key collision handling and Shift+Tab normalization remain separate work.
- **Blast radius:** The ZeroCode client settings pane, its Config footer and input routing, and its English Fluent catalogue. No daemon, RPC, configuration schema, or dependency changes.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11492.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode's Config screen lets you change client preferences such as themes, keybindings, and connection settings. Several pages previously left their action hints blank, and some instructions named Enter or Esc even when those keys had been overridden. Finding an action to rebind also required scrolling through the whole list.

The footer now identifies the current client-settings page and active pane and shows the controls that can actually reach it. The Keybindings page adds a search field. Typing edits the query; confirming it lets you browse the matching actions, and a separate activation starts rebinding. Searching, clearing, and cancelling do not save a binding. Rebind and reset still operate on the action displayed in the selected row.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The change reuses the existing action registry, resolved bindings, search controls, Config footer, and locale loader. The full binding list remains authoritative; search derives visible row indices from it. Config and global routing yield ordinary query text so characters cannot accidentally reset a binding or switch sections. Modified global shortcuts retain their established priority, and hints omit local keys those shortcuts intercept.

The source and catalogue changes are accompanied by tests at the pane, Config, and global input boundaries. No new persistence owner, API, registry, or dependency is introduced.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for actual terminal presentation and focus.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config client settings.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build this revision and use your existing compatible daemon, client profile, and keybindings. No additional feature settings are needed.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config, switch the outer section to ZeroCode, and select Keybindings. Open detail, start search with the resolved search key, and enter an action name such as `clear input` or a key such as `Ctrl+z`. Confirm the query, select a result, and activate it. Cancel capture, clear the filter, and return to the section list. Inspect the other settings pages and Connection editing. Use the same steps on `master` for comparison.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Contextual controls reflect your effective bindings. The filter narrows the actions; query confirmation does not start capture. Capture/reset target the displayed action. Clearing preserves useful selection. Mouse or keyboard departure stops query editing while retaining its text.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Keybindings has no filter; client-settings footers generally lack contextual controls, and some titles/editor instructions use fixed keys.

### How I tested

The original implementation was validated on `c75f24e832eb1437b6614bbaeddd2d537814d7e1`:

- `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode`: 1,431 passed, 0 failed, 2 existing ignored tests. This includes filtering, correct capture/reset targets, empty results, cancellation, repeated search selection, typing without config writes, mouse list/query geometry, paste isolation, effective hints, locale fallback, and narrow footer rendering.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Touched-file rustfmt, `git diff --check`, comment hygiene, and the ZeroCode RPC-only dependency gate passed.
- The [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37142730934) passed on `c75f24e832eb1437b6614bbaeddd2d537814d7e1`, including workspace nextest, lint, cross-platform checks, and the ZeroCode RPC boundary. All applicable checks passed; conditional checks were skipped. prs.title: feat(zerocode): show message times in the transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The ZeroCode transcript never showed when anything happened. When an automated prompt, a refused queued message and a long tool call overlap in one session, there was no way to tell the order or the durations from the screen. A time on every message proved to be too much (an earlier revision of this PR did that). The transcript now shows time context in two places only:
    - a dim, centered divider (`── Today 01:00 ──`, `── Yesterday 22:20 ──`, or a date) before a prompt that starts the transcript, comes 15 minutes or more after the previous activity, or starts a new day. A quick back-and-forth gets no dividers.
    - a dim footer (`─── 01:00 → 01:31 · 31m 40s`) under a turn that ran for a minute or more. Short turns get none.
  - `session/messages` entries gain an optional `created_at` (RFC 3339) wherever the store has one: ACP full loads, ACP cursor pages, and the Chat backend via `load_with_timestamps`. It is skipped when absent and `#[serde(default)]` on the client, so either side can be older.
  - **Store fix underneath.** Checkpointed ACP turns write all their visible rows at finalization with one timestamp, so a turn's prompt read as the time the turn **ended**. A divider or footer built on that would be wrong by the whole length of the turn. The checkpoint row now records `started_at` (a nullable column, added on upgrade), and finalization and crash recovery stamp the turn's prompt row with it. The other rows of the turn keep the finalization time, which is the turn's end: exactly what the footer needs.
  - Live turns: entries are stamped on receipt, and the footer is placed when the turn settles. A later terminal frame for the same turn does not move it. A history load taken mid-turn hands the footer to the live settle.
  - A reloaded turn that ends in a recovery marker gets no footer, because recovery stamps its rows when it runs, which can be hours after the turn stopped.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Individual tool calls and replies in ACP history still share the turn's finish time. Giving each its own time would need a time on every checkpoint journal event; it isn't needed for dividers and footers.
  - No toggle. The only existing display toggle is thoughts; a timestamp toggle would need a new action, keybinding and help text.
  - The Chat-backend path (gateway SQLite) is affected by #11420, which rewrites every row's `created_at` on each turn. This PR passes through what that store holds.
- **Blast radius:** the ACP store's write path for checkpointed turns (only the prompt row's `created_at`) and one additive column on `acp_turn_checkpoints`; the `session/messages` wire shape (additive, optional); ZeroCode transcript layout (divider and footer rows drawn outside each entry's line range, with the tail re-render accounting for them).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11620. Related #11420.
- **Holding-crate exception:** the `zeroclaw-runtime` part (`created_at` on `session/messages`, confined to `handle_session_messages` and the entry builder) is covered by the row added in #11697 (merged).

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode now shows a small grey date-and-time line when you come back to a conversation after a break or on a new day, and a small grey line under any turn that took more than a minute, saying when it started, when it finished and how long it took. Quick exchanges look exactly as before. Under the hood, the daemon's database used to record every message of a turn as happening when the turn finished; this PR records when the prompt was sent, so those lines are right after a reload too.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode over the daemon socket)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a daemon and ZeroCode built from this branch; any agent.
- **Steps to run:** send a prompt that runs a tool and takes over a minute. Then send a quick follow-up. Wait 15 minutes (or reload a session from yesterday) and send another. Switch away from the session and back to force a `session/messages` reload.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** a `── Today HH:MM ──` divider above the first prompt; a `─── start → end · duration` footer under the long turn; nothing around the quick follow-up; a new divider after the gap. The same marks after the reload. A session from an older daemon shows no marks rather than wrong ones.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no times anywhere.

### How I tested

All builds and tests ran through `scripts/zc-cargo` on the remote build host.

- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the touched files: clean.
- `zc-cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
Results below are for head `c57119d62da9` (rebased on `master` 2026-10-17) unless marked.

- `zc-cargo test -p zerocode`: `test result: FAILED. 1537 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored`. The one failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, fails the same way on unmodified `master` on the same host.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra acp_session_store`: `test result: ok. 88 passed; 0 failed`.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::`: `test result: ok. 850 passed; 0 failed`.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib`: `5627 passed; 4 failed` at the earlier head. The 4 (`relay::local_dial_tests` x2, `new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, `peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget`) fail the same way on unmodified `master` on the same host. The runtime diff is unchanged since.

Each new test fails with its fix reverted and passes with it restored:

- Store: `finalized_turn_prompt_keeps_turn_start_time_and_reply_keeps_finalization_time`, `recovered_turn_prompt_keeps_turn_start_time` (fail when the prompt keeps the finalization time); `turn_checkpoint_start_column_is_added_to_an_existing_database` (fails without the migration).
- RPC: `conversation_message_entries_carry_each_source_message_time` (fails when the projection drops times).
- Rules (`chat::entry_time`): `dividers_mark_the_first_prompt_gaps_and_day_changes_only` (fails when every prompt divides), `a_day_change_divides_even_after_a_short_gap` (fails without the day check), `footers_follow_finished_turns_of_a_minute_or_more` (fails without the one-minute floor), plus label and parsing tests.
- Transcript: `transcript_shows_gap_dividers_and_long_turn_footers_not_message_times` and `a_live_turn_gets_its_footer_when_it_settles` (fail when the layout drops the footer row, when a settle doesn't invalidate the tail, or when a later frame may move the end); `a_history_load_taken_mid_turn_hands_the_footer_to_the_live_settle` (fails when a moved footer doesn't force a full rebuild); `a_footer_on_a_divided_entry_keeps_one_divider` (fails when the tail re-render ignores the divider row); `a_recovered_turn_gets_no_footer_from_its_recovery_time`.

`rpc::dispatch::tests::cursor_pages_equal_legacy_projection_for_valid_tool_groups` was updated: cursor pages now carry times, so its full-load reference uses the timed projection.

- **CI checks relied on:** the Rust lanes for the three crates.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** no end-to-end daemon+TUI run in CI for this.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The divider and footer rows were checked in a live ZeroCode pane against a scratch daemon (seeded history plus a live turn), by reading the terminal's text.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11622#issuecomment-6232571932 (experiment build, taken before the current head). Real screenshots of the current head pending. Daemon/store verification is also pending.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** none.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11622#issuecomment-6232571932 (experiment build, taken before the current head). Real screenshots of the current head pending.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. Times are display-only and never reach the model.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The new wire field is optional both ways. The new column is nullable and added on open; an older binary ignores it (its inserts name their columns). A checkpoint begun by an older binary has no start time, and its prompt keeps the finalization time as before.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the PR's commits. The added `acp_turn_checkpoints.started_at` column is harmless to the reverted code and needs no down-migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** no dividers or footers (old daemon or missing `created_at`), or a footer whose start is later than expected (start time not recorded).

prs.title: fix(providers): send configured extra_headers on Anthropic requests
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Native Anthropic configuration already accepts `extra_headers`, but its factory dropped them. Forward the existing runtime options into `AnthropicBuilder` so gateways receive their configured headers on buffered and streaming requests.
  - Validate header names and values once, skip invalid entries with a warning that omits values, and mark valid values sensitive. Install them as client defaults. Headers the provider actually sets on a request take precedence over those defaults.
  - Build a dedicated buffered client when headers are present, propagate construction failures without a headerless fallback, and apply the existing host/port redirect restriction to both header-bearing clients. Retain the allowed redirect, denied destination, hostname-only, and construction-failure controls.
  - Preserve master's endpoint-based single-tool-round support while forwarding headers. Extend existing tests to cover both credential modes, capability selection with extra headers, and streaming-test isolation from runtime proxy changes.
- **Scope boundary:** Only `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/anthropic.rs` and its factory wiring/tests change. No new config key, auth-selection rule, request-body format, shared redirect-policy implementation, other provider behavior, dependency, or CI change. No decoupled redirect repair is included. The draft remains held for the outstanding credential-boundary review described in the [latest maintainer review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11541#pullrequestreview-5520939876).
- **Blast radius:** Native Anthropic entries with valid configured extra headers now transmit them. Buffered requests with no valid extra headers retain the shared cached client. Streaming requests retain the existing timeout and proxy behavior. Request wrappers introduced on master retain their tool-round controls.
- **Linked issue(s):** No linked issue. Related #11544 for subsequent Anthropic streaming header/timeout integration; this PR does not implement that PR's timeout change.

### What this does, simply

Some model gateways require a custom authentication header. ZeroClaw already lets users configure those headers, but the native Anthropic provider ignored them, so those gateways could reject requests with 401 responses. This change sends the configured headers on Anthropic requests, including streaming requests.

The provider's own header wins when it sets the same header on the request. API-key requests set `x-api-key`; setup-token requests set `Authorization`. A configured header for the other authentication mode is still sent. A provider-generated `anthropic-beta` replaces a configured default rather than merging it. Invalid configured entries are skipped with a warning. The remaining credential-boundary review must be completed before this draft can proceed.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` - existing loopback wire tests exercise header delivery and redirect behavior; refreshed exact-revision execution is still required before relying on them.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** N/A - no rendered `web`, `tui`, or `cli` state changes; the affected boundary is Anthropic provider HTTP traffic.
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A - no additional manual setup is requested; automated fixtures use synthetic credentials and loopback endpoints.
- **Steps to run:** N/A - use the focused automated validation recorded below rather than a credentialed manual gateway test.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Configured valid headers reach native Anthropic requests; request-set credentials win collisions; disallowed host/port redirect targets receive no request; buffered client-build failures send no fallback request.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The native Anthropic factory ignores configured extra headers, so a gateway requiring one receives no such header.

### How I tested

The existing suite covers buffered and streaming header delivery, factory forwarding, invalid entries and sensitive values, allowed same-host redirects, denied different-port redirects, denied different-host/same-port redirects, and buffered/thinking-stream client-build failures with zero receiving requests. The refreshed tests also cover setup-token `Authorization` precedence and official/custom endpoint capability selection while extra headers are configured.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [CI Required Gate, Format, Lint, Test and platform checks](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37699203609) passed for published head 745f0add9d42579215d54b944b9867971d91c787. These are historical evidence for the earlier provider code, not validation of the refreshed merge or latest test edits. The [maintainer's earlier review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11541#pullrequestreview-5475206102) records the test job's 19,366 passed / 39 skipped result on its merge snapshot.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Fresh CI runs on the pushed head `94d90cc15`. The local fmt, Clippy and provider tests below cover the merge and the test edits. No live gateway retry on this revision.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  Run on the master merge `9af933d21` and on head `94d90cc15`, Mac mini, `zc-cargo-narrow`, `-j2`, `--test-threads=2`:

  ```text
  # 9af933d21 (merge only)
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                              ok
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings          ok
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers   lib 1987 passed; 1 failed; 4 ignored; integration tests ok
    failure: openai::tool_round_policy_tests::native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults
    (connection refused; passes on rerun here and on clean master; not touched by this PR)
  # 94d90cc15 (head)
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                              ok
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings          ok
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers anthropic                              210 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers factory                                128 passed; 0 failed (+7 integration)
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source review traced factory forwarding, all buffered-client callers, streaming/thinking error handling, credential precedence, and composition with master's single-tool-round changes. Direct Rust formatting and whitespace checks passed. No live gateway retry was performed for the refreshed revision. Earlier live-body reports of mutation tests and a mixed local build reaching a gateway are historical author reports, not exact-revision evidence for this refresh.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` - no rendered user-interface state or presentation changes. Real screenshots and recordings supplied for this refresh: none. None are required for this transport-only change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Local runs cover merge `9af933d21` and head `94d90cc15` (provider HTTP traffic, no rendered interface). Historical public CI covers `745f0add9d`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** No screenshots apply (no interface change). Command output is above. No live-gateway capture is claimed.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The provider tests send synthetic configured headers through the real provider clients and check the received headers, or zero requests at denied redirect targets. All pass on `94d90cc15`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full `-p zeroclaw-providers` suite ran on the merge. On the head only the `anthropic` and `factory` filters ran, because the head commit changes only those tests. No live gateway retry.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No - existing Anthropic calls now carry configured headers; no new endpoint or operation is introduced.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No - test credentials are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Operator-configured headers may contain credentials and now leave the machine on native Anthropic requests. Values are marked sensitive, invalid-entry warnings omit values, and request-set authentication headers override matching configured defaults. Existing host/port redirect restrictions and loopback controls remain on both header-bearing clients. Those controls do not constitute clearance of the outstanding credential-boundary review; no broader security guarantee is claimed. Buffered construction errors propagate without a headerless fallback. Streaming's pre-existing invalid-proxy behavior remains a separate follow-up.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes - entries without valid extra headers retain existing behavior; explicitly configured headers now take effect as intended.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No - `extra_headers` already exists.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A - no schema or toolchain migration. Operators who configured previously ignored Anthropic headers should review them before upgrading because they will now be transmitted.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After merge, `git revert <squash-commit>` restores the prior native Anthropic behavior of ignoring configured extra headers. Reverting does not revoke credentials already transmitted.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added. Removing `extra_headers` disables the new header-bearing path for that entry, but a gateway requiring those headers may reject requests.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Gateway 401/403 responses, Anthropic client-construction errors, or failures after redirects. A 403 alone does not establish successful gateway authentication. Investigate without logging credential values.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A - no Supersedes

- Superseded PRs + authors (`#<pr> by @<author>`, one per line): N/A - no Supersedes.
- Scope materially carried forward: N/A - no superseded work.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? (`Yes/No`) No
- If `No`, why (inspiration-only, no direct code/design carry-over): N/A - no superseded contributor work incorporated.

---

Maintainers and reviewers with label permissions still set `risk:*` and any missing manual labels via the sidebar. Contributors without label permission can note obvious label mismatches in a comment. Canonical colon-scoped labels use no-space spelling; during migration, copy exact live label spelling from the GitHub UI.

or `Created with Claude Code` to the PR body or commit-message tail. Human

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(zerocode): show temporary local file-write diffs
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions).
- **What changed and why:**
  - Eligible local ZeroCode `file_write` calls show red removed lines and green added lines from a bounded observation before a successful write. Overwrite cards show `Overwrote existing file`, and six-row previews offer Show all when rows are omitted.
  - Previous text uses a private local notification outside ordinary tool results, model messages and saved history. The private inbox and view share a five-minute deadline. The runtime drops the entire pair if `scrub_credentials` changes either the previous or written text, so ZeroCode falls back to the labelled preview.
  - Direct ACP clients stop constructing creation diffs from write input across live events, restored history and approval requests. Capture admission uses the executor's canonical live resolver, native provenance, exclusions and read-approval policy.
- **Scope boundary:** Capture requires existing native read authority, workspace containment and supported readable text. It adds no durable diff history or remote/direct-ACP diff transport. The pre-write observation cannot guarantee the exact inode contents replaced by a concurrent external writer. ACP separation, Unicode format-character handling and tab presentation are outside this revision.
- **Blast radius:** File-write observation, transient native RPC events, local ZeroCode Chat/Code cards and ACP write presentation. File authorization and atomic replacement remain in force. No new dependency, configuration or durable schema is introduced. Runtime adapters stay in the owners covered by the temporary file-write diff exception approved in [#11436](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11436#pullrequestreview-5474715854).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10294. Remote and direct ACP diffs remain unavailable, so this PR does not close the issue.
- **Release notes:** ZeroCode can show temporary local file-write diffs when existing read authority permits capture and credential scrubbing leaves both sides unchanged. ACP clients, including Zed, no longer get a `file_write` creation-diff preview. Base64 writes now put raw base64 in `rawInput.content`, with `rawInput.encoding` preserved.

### What this does, simply

An agent can replace an existing file with `file_write`. Showing only the new text as green additions makes a replacement look like a creation. ZeroCode can now show what was removed and added when the agent already has permission to read that workspace file. Old text disappears from this view after five minutes and is not saved with the conversation. Reopening shows the saved write summary. If private evidence is unavailable or would require credential redaction, the card uses the supplied-content preview instead of a diff. Recognized overwrite results still have an overwrite heading.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, with disposable synthetic files.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, local native ZeroCode Chat and Code through RPC (`channel=rpc`). Direct ACP presentation also has adapter-level automated coverage; interactive ACP client verification remains pending.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build daemon and client from the same revision. Use an agent with native `file_write` and `file_read`, no read exclusion and no pending read approval. Use an English tool-result catalog for compact-summary recognition. Start a fresh conversation with a disposable workspace file. A write-only profile intentionally receives the fallback preview.
- **Steps to run:** On both `master` and this branch, ask the agent to use `file_write` to create `write-demo.txt` with eight numbered lines, then overwrite it with three different numbered lines. Inspect the six-row preview, choose Show all, then wait five minutes or disconnect and reopen the conversation. Repeat with read authority disabled or an allowed path outside the workspace. Rewrite a file with identical content. For the scrub cases, put a synthetic labelled credential in the previous file, then separately in the written content. Check `file_edit` independently for its existing diff behavior.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Eligible overwrites show `Overwrote existing file`, red removals, green additions, `Changes · temporary local view` and Show all when rows are omitted. An identical rewrite says `Content unchanged`. Expired, restored, unsupported or credential-scrubbed overwrites show the recorded size summary and `Content preview · diff unavailable`. Pending and unknown calls acquire no success claims. Direct ACP preserves original write arguments without synthesizing a creation diff.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Results report bytes written and path. Write previews look like additions regardless of previous contents, without execution-time overwrite evidence.

### How I tested

The new focused runtime regressions are `agent::tool_execution::tests::local_file_diff_executor_drops_previous_credentials` and `agent::tool_execution::tests::local_file_diff_executor_drops_written_credentials`. Each drives a real filesystem overwrite through the production executor with admitted native read authority and synthetic `token=supersecretvalue` on one side. They assert a successful write, the ordinary correlated result and no `LocalFileDiff` event. Execution of these regressions and compilation of the refreshed revision are pending.

The earlier PR body reported 79 selected API/tools/runtime/ZeroCode tests and a matched daemon/client build. Those reports predate this revision and are not validation of the merge resolution or scrub gate. Existing coverage includes read exclusion and approval, foreign and write-only roots, binary/control text, credential filenames, hard links, size limits, failed writes, nonlocal transport, revoked grants, full queues, inbox retirement, expiry, reused IDs and restored history.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Historical [CI run 39022116522](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39022116522) completed successfully at published head `a95e2d235f11dd909e939a6e624f6a4f8fdda41d`, including `CI Required Gate`, Format, Lint, Test, Docs Style and platform/feature checks. This replaces the stale Quality Gate link in the prior body. These checks cover the published implementation, not this unpublished refresh. Fresh validation is required before review approval.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Fresh CI runs on the pushed head `b06b42f8b`; local results are below. Automated coverage does not replace the requested real interface screenshots.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  Run on head `b06b42f8b` (master merge `9620d88a0` + scrub fix `11bff1f01` + translations `b06b42f8b`), Mac mini, `zc-cargo-narrow`, `-j2`, `--test-threads=2`:

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                   ok
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings   ok
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-tools -p zerocode
    zeroclaw_api      324 passed; 0 failed
    zeroclaw_tools    1390 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored
    zerocode (bin)    1571 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime
    zeroclaw_runtime  5899 passed; 2 failed; 9 ignored   (all integration test binaries ok)
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels
    zeroclaw_channels 2031 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored   (integration tests ok)
  ```

  Both new regressions pass: `agent::tool_execution::tests::local_file_diff_executor_drops_previous_credentials` and `agent::tool_execution::tests::local_file_diff_executor_drops_written_credentials`. The three failures also fail on clean master `5a51398dd` on this machine and are not touched by this PR: `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` (zerocode), and `relay::local_dial_tests::a_closed_route_releases_a_dial_parked_on_a_stalled_listener` / `a_dial_that_never_connects_ends_on_its_own_budget` (macOS loopback backlog never fills).

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source review checked the canonical resolver, native provenance, read approval, scrub-before-event gate, ordinary-result fallback and master API initializers. Standalone Rust formatting and the docs quality and links gates passed. No interactive interface smoke or screenshot capture was performed for this revision.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshots pending.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Real screenshots pending.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Real screenshots pending.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Pending real captures for overwrite preview/expansion, expiry/reopening, restricted-read fallback and identical rewrite. No new visible result is claimed here.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace-wide tests were not run; the change is limited to the api, tools, runtime, channels and zerocode crates, which were all tested. No screenshots were captured for this revision.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes, an authorized write can make a bounded previous-text observation for local display using existing native read authority, readable-path policy and workspace containment. Tool names or model arguments grant no native trust or new read permission.
- New external network calls? No. Private evidence goes only to the trusted local native RPC connection. Remote RPC, direct ACP, gateway and channel adapters do not receive it.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. Before emitting `TurnEvent::LocalFileDiff`, the runtime drops the entire pair if the existing credential scrubber changes either side. It preserves exact diffs for admitted text rather than rendering partially redacted pairs. Filename and pattern exclusions are not a general secret detector.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Test content is synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Successful results gain pre-write existence and byte counts. Captured previous text stays outside ordinary output, model messages, hooks, observers, receipts, checkpoints and saved history. Rendering escapes terminal controls.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Each snapshot is limited to 16 KiB and 1,024 lines. Capture rejects unsupported text, listed credential filenames/key extensions and Unix files with multiple hard links. Capture is a read that does not count toward the `file_read` rate limit and emits no observer or audit read event. Existing written-content exposure through `ToolCall` arguments is unchanged by the scrub gate.

The inbox and view each cap raw pairs at 64 KiB and 16 entries per session. The inbox tracks at most 16 sessions and each pane at most eight. The generic notification ring holds only opaque tokens. Delivery rechecks live read grants under an authority lease and drops evidence if the writer queue is full. Expiry, disconnect, retirement and history replacement clear owned payloads and derived rendering, selection and copy caches. Explicit copies, terminal scrollback, screenshots and operating-system memory remain outside that lifetime guarantee; memory is not cryptographically erased. Capture or delivery failure does not fail an authorized write.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for ACP consumers that relied on synthesized `file_write` creation diffs or `rawInput.newText`. Tool arguments and durable history remain compatible. Successful human-readable result text changes, and matched-version native RPC gains an optional local-only notification.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Build daemon and ZeroCode together. ACP clients must read original `rawInput.path`, `rawInput.content` and optional `rawInput.encoding`; base64 content remains raw base64. They must not treat write input as a creation diff. No configuration migration is needed. Compact summaries recognize saved English results with a matching argument path. Unknown or localized results keep their original display. Historical results without pre-write evidence remain unknown.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commits, then rebuild daemon and ZeroCode together.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No new toggle. Exclude native `file_read` or require read approval for the agent to prevent capture and use the fallback preview.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Missing temporary diffs despite eligible read authority, old lines appearing after expiry or in restored history, incorrect overwrite headings, credential-bearing private diff events, or failed write cards. ACP clients lose the creation-diff preview as a deliberate compatibility change. The labelled fallback remains available when private capture or delivery is unavailable.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A - no Supersedes

- Superseded PRs + authors (`#<pr> by @<author>`, one per line): N/A, this PR supersedes no other PR.
- Scope materially carried forward: N/A, no superseded work is incorporated.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? No.
- If `No`, why (inspiration-only, no direct code/design carry-over): N/A, no superseded contributor work is incorporated.

---

**Labels** live in the GitHub label UI, not in the body. The PR path labeler owns path/scope labels from `.github/labeler.yml`, and the PR size labeler owns canonical `size:*` labels. Maintainers and reviewers with label permissions still set `risk:*` and any missing manual labels via the sidebar. Contributors without label permission can note obvious label mismatches in a comment. Canonical colon-scoped labels use no-space spelling; during migration, copy exact live label spelling from the GitHub UI.

**Do not add bot/AI attribution footers** such as `Co-authored-by: Claude ...`
or `Created with Claude Code` to the PR body or commit-message tail. Human
co-author trailers are appropriate only for incorporated contributor work under
the supersede-attribution section and privacy contract.

**Privacy contract** (`docs/book/src/contributing/privacy.md`) is a merge gate. Never commit real identities, secrets, personal emails, or PII in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs.

prs.title: fix(zerocode): answer dropped elicitations and record them in the transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A pending `ask_user` / `poll` prompt could be cleared on the client with no reply. The daemon then waited out the tool's own timeout (600 s for `ask_user`) while the user saw nothing. Every clear that isn't the user's answer now goes through `withdraw_pending_elicitation`. `Chat::answer_withdrawn_elicitations` (run each transport tick, after the resync drain) sends the `cancel` and notes it in the transcript.
  - A modal that outlives its turn is closed on `TurnComplete` and recorded as expired.
  - The `ask_user` / `poll` tool card now leads with `question:` and lists the choices. Before, the collapsed card showed the first 120 bytes of key-sorted input JSON, so `channel` and `choices` came first and the question was cut off. The card is the one record of the question.
  - The card's `result:` is the record of the outcome. For `ask_user` / `poll`, the pick (or the `DISMISSED` marker from #11815) is shown in the warn colour the old outcome line used. An outcome line (answered, dismissed, withdrawn, expired) is written only when no matching `ask_user` / `poll` card is on screen, such as an older history or a card that never arrived. In dogfooding, a line under the card repeated its `result:`.
- **Scope boundary:** Client only (`apps/zerocode`). No daemon or wire change. Overlay placement and the sidebar needs-input dot are unchanged; the dot already exists (`ChatState::sidebar_status`). Free-form `ask_user` on the Code tab is still unsupported.
- **Blast radius:** The ZeroCode Code and Chat panes' elicitation path, and how the `ask_user` / `poll` tool cards render. A dropped prompt now gets a `cancel` reply where before it got none. The daemon already handles `cancel` (`Ok(None)` → "user cancelled").
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11623. Related #11117 (durable human-question primitive; it scopes ACP elicitation out). Companion #11815 makes `ask_user` return a `DISMISSED` result rather than an error when the user presses Esc, so the card's `result:` reads as a dismissal.

### What this does, simply

When an agent asks you a multiple-choice question in ZeroCode, a box pops up with the options. If the pane reloaded while that box was up (which happens when the client falls behind the live stream) or you started a new session in place, the box disappeared and nobody told the agent. The agent sat waiting for up to ten minutes and then failed with a timeout. Nothing about the question stayed on screen either, so afterwards you couldn't tell what had been asked.

Now the agent is told "cancelled" right away whenever the box goes away without your answer. The `ask_user` tool card shows the question, its options and what happened. A separate note appears only if the card isn't on screen.

**Why the record is client-side.** The prompt asked whether the record belongs in the daemon so it survives reload. It already partly does: the daemon persists the `ask_user` tool call with its full input, and with this change that card shows the question and choices. So after a reload the question is still on screen. The card's `result:` carries the answer or the cancel, and it is persisted with the card. Making the outcome durable means a new daemon event and storage, which is the job of the #11117 durable-question primitive. I kept this PR to the client.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The failing path needs a notification-lag reload to land while a prompt is up, which is hard to trigger by hand. The regression test drives it directly.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode Code pane)

### How I tested

All through the remote wrapper (`scripts/zc-cargo`) on the build host.

- `zc-cargo test -p zerocode elicitation` → `test result: ok. 19 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1410 filtered out` (at the third commit)
- `zc-cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Finished `dev` profile`, no warnings
- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check apps/zerocode/src/chat.rs` → clean
- Full `zc-cargo test -p zerocode` → `1426 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored` at the second and third commits (first commit: 1425/1). The one failure is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` ("SIGINT was swallowed while the insecure-TLS prompt was blocked", `main.rs`). It fails the same way on unmodified `origin/master` 05f9fe95d4 on the same host (`0 passed; 1 failed; 1422 filtered out`), so it's environmental on that host, not this change.

**Mutation check, third commit.** `elicitation_question_choices_and_answer_are_recorded` now applies the card's result and asserts no outcome line; `elicitation_with_a_card_adds_no_outcome_line` (renamed from `elicitation_outcome_sits_under_its_card_inside_the_agent_turn`) asserts the entries stay `agent, tool:ask_user, tool:shell` after Esc and the browse cursor is untouched. Writing the line even when a card exists: `17 passed; 2 failed`, both tests. Restored → 19 passed.

**Mutation check, second commit (placement since superseded by the third).** `elicitation_question_choices_and_answer_are_recorded` now streams the agent turn and asserts no line on arrival, one outcome line, and the question exactly once in the rendered transcript. The new `elicitation_outcome_sits_under_its_card_inside_the_agent_turn` delivers the request before the turn streams in (the router order), adds a parallel `shell` call, presses Esc, and asserts the entry order `agent, tool:ask_user, system:dismissed, tool:shell`, the rendered order agent label < `question:` < outcome < shell card, and that the browse cursor follows the shift.
- Asked line restored on arrival: `18 passed; 2 failed`. Both tests fail; the order assertion shows `["system:The agent asked: Pick one…", "agent", "tool:ask_user", …]`, which is what my screenshot shows.
- Outcome appended instead of placed: `19 passed; 1 failed`, with `["agent", "tool:ask_user", "tool:shell", "system:You dismissed…"]`.
- Index shift removed: fails with "the browse cursor stays on the shell card" (`Some(2)` vs `Some(3)`).
Restored → 20 passed.

**Mutation check, first commit.** I reverted each piece of the fix in one mutant (reload clears silently again, no asked-record, no `TurnComplete` close, card arm disabled, `reset_for_session` clears silently): `14 passed; 5 failed`. All five new tests failed:
`elicitation_installed_during_reload_is_answered_not_dropped`, `reset_for_session_queues_a_cancel_for_the_dropped_elicitation`, `elicitation_question_choices_and_answer_are_recorded`, `turn_complete_closes_a_stale_elicitation_and_records_it`, `ask_user_card_leads_with_the_question_and_lists_choices`. Restored → 19 passed.

- **CI checks relied on:** the zerocode test and clippy jobs.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** none for this surface.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11624#issuecomment-6233889542 (experiment build, picked result and dismissed). Real screenshots of the current head pending. I dogfooded the second commit on 2026-10-17: the question showed once, but the answer was repeated, which the third commit fixes.
- **Not verified:** a live reproduction of the lag-reload race against a daemon.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The question text was already rendered (in the modal); it's now also rendered in the transcript through the same terminal-safe path as tool input. Nothing new reaches the model.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): configure per-pane session cap
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A ZeroCode pane could track at most 8 sessions (focused, background, and retained reconnect entries), fixed by a compile-time constant. Workloads that keep one session per worktree hit it quickly, and the daemon's own ACP `max_sessions` setting does not affect it.
  - A new `[sessions].max_tracked_per_pane` setting replaces the constant. The default stays 8; valid values are 1 through 32, so two panes at the maximum still fit the daemon's 64-session store.
  - The value is resolved once at startup. An out-of-range or malformed value stops startup with an error naming `[sessions]` instead of being silently normalized, as the issue asks for validation. The `ZEROCODE_sessions__max_tracked_per_pane` env override goes through the same check.
  - Every admission path uses it: the sidebar "+", Change directory, opening an existing session, and reconnect resume. The `zc-chat-session-cap` notice shows the configured value. The entry-retry pane carries the value so a retry does not reset it to 8.
  - The three per-session result channels are sized by the configured cap, as they were by the constant.
- **Scope boundary:** no daemon, RPC or runtime change; no Config-pane control yet (file and env only, documented as such); no sidebar UI change.
- **Blast radius:** `apps/zerocode` only (config loading, the two chat-like panes, the config reference page). Existing config files load unchanged; without `[sessions]` the limit is 8 as before.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10665. Supersedes #11729 (same feature as `[chat].max_sessions_per_pane` with clamping; closed in favour of this one).

### What this does, simply

Each ZeroCode window side can keep a limited number of conversations open at once. That limit was fixed at 8. This adds a setting for it. Nothing changes unless you set it: the default is still 8 and the highest allowed value is 32. A value outside that range is reported at startup rather than quietly changed.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface`: `tui`
- **Setup / preconditions:** a running daemon; in `zerocode-config.toml` add `[sessions]` with `max_tracked_per_pane = 3`.
- **Steps to run:** start ZeroCode, press the sidebar "+" until it stops adding sessions. Then set the value to `0` and start again.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the fourth press shows "Session limit for this pane reached (3)" and the focused session stays as it was. With `0`, startup fails with `max_tracked_per_pane must be between 1 and 32`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the setting is ignored; the limit is reached at 8.

### How I tested

```sh
rustfmt --edition 2024 --check apps/zerocode/src/{acp,app,chat}.rs apps/zerocode/src/config/mod.rs
cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zerocode
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the zerocode build, clippy and test jobs cover the changed crate; `Docs Style` covers the config reference page.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known.

The one failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, also fails on untouched master on my build host and is unrelated.

prs.title: feat(session): implement append-only session event history
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Make versioned, append-only session events the canonical conversation and execution history, so replay rebuilds state without repeating external effects.
  - Separate the kernel coordinator, storage implementations and host composition into explicit ownership boundaries. CLI, RPC, ACP, gateway and channel adapters use the same Session model and authorized history queries.
  - Capture provider attempts, reasoning and multimodal output, tool progress and outcomes, approvals, model/policy observations, context compression and linked child execution. Preserve provider item identities and supplemental fields without copying normalized bodies.
  - Provide SQLite and JSONL persistence, crash recovery, idempotent receipts, branches, search and auditable payload erasure. Interrupted external effects retain diagnostics and an unknown outcome when completion cannot be proved.
  - Upgrade legacy SQLite, JSONL and ACP history into the configured native format with resumable imports, writer fencing and renamed source backups. No per-session locator or independent ACP history database remains after upgrade.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not replace the file/blob, memory, cost, task or live-config authorities; their historical references remain session evidence. No additional at-rest encryption, dashboard redesign or complete runtime/plugin extraction.
- **Blast radius:** Session startup, persistence and recovery; provider and tool dispatch; approvals; child agents; CLI/RPC/ACP/channel/gateway history; session cleanup, alias lifecycle and existing storage configuration.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10526. Related #9600. Related #9487. Related #9488. These broader coordination issues are not automatically closed.

### What this does, simply

A saved transcript currently cannot fully explain how a session reached its final answer. This change saves the observed execution as ordered events: what the user supplied, which model ran, what the model returned, which tools and approvals were involved, and what happened when execution failed or stopped. Conversation views and retained context are rebuilt from those facts.

All entrances use the same session storage. Existing histories are imported automatically and the original files become backups. Historical permissions explain past execution; they never grant permission to a resumed session. Unknown completion remains unknown, and reading or replaying history never reruns a tool.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, using a disposable configuration/data directory on each branch.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`, plus the ACP protocol entrance and messaging-channel adapters covered by automated tests.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Configure an agent named `fixture` with a working provider and tool policy in a disposable copy of an existing installation. Stop other processes using that directory. Use separate copies for `master` and this branch. Select `channels.session_backend` as `sqlite` or `jsonl` and repeat for both.
- **Steps to run:** Run `zeroclaw agent -a fixture --session-state-file /var/tmp/session-events-review.json`, exchange a message, request a harmless permitted tool action, exit, then reopen with the same command. Inspect the installation's `sessions` directory and the imported source backups. Repeat with a copy containing legacy ACP history, then open/resume it through ACP.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** A native event history and installation manifest are created; user/provider/tool/approval observations and retained context survive reopening. Legacy sources are renamed after successful import. ACP uses the standard session store. An interrupted effect without a proven outcome is not silently rerun.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Mutable transcripts and separate persistence paths retain conversation messages but do not provide the common execution-event history or installation-wide migration described above.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None claimed before PR creation. Local checks below provide the current evidence; PR CI remains to run.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Full workspace/all-features, cross-platform/MSRV builds, million-event performance and VM power-loss scenarios were not rerun in the final validation round. Summary/catalog queries still scan event history; this is not a constant-time performance claim.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Linux, Rust 1.99.0, locked dependencies, `TMPDIR=/var/tmp`. Tested production source matches commit `61d3eb2d24`; the only subsequent test change replaced a prohibited error macro with an equivalent constructor and its regression was rerun.

```sh
cargo +1.99.0 test --locked   -p zeroclaw-kernel -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-session-host   --lib --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4
# kernel:       137 passed; 0 failed
# providers:   2017 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored
# session-host:  10 passed; 0 failed

cargo +1.99.0 test --locked   -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway   --lib --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4
# runtime:  5777 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored
# channels: 2025 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored
# gateway:   674 passed; 0 failed

cargo +1.99.0 test --locked   -p zeroclaw-kernel -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-session-host   --lib provider_content_metadata_survives_complete_and_interrupted_capture   -- --test-threads=4
# providers: 1 passed; 0 failed (SQLite/JSONL, complete/interrupted)

cargo +1.99.0 clippy --locked   -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-kernel   -p zeroclaw-session-host -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-tools   -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway   -p zeroclaw --all-targets -- -D warnings
# Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 58s

cargo +1.99.0 fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0

git diff --cached --check
# exit 0

DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/architecture/session-events.md   bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
# Linting: 1 file(s); Summary: 0 error(s)

python3 scripts/ci/check_internal_docs_links.py
# Checked authored Markdown links in 219 file(s); no broken local targets.
```

Earlier validation of the session-unification stage also passed API 346, infra 357 and tools 1,368 library tests, plus three standalone ACP CLI component tests. The infra round skipped the expensive commit-byte-boundary test after its separate passing run; these earlier checks are not represented as a final full-workspace rerun. The final all-targets Clippy compiles the updated test and entrance call sites.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reviewed migration publication and source-backup ordering, canonical field ownership, live read/effect authorization, partial/error/unknown distinctions and payload-reference reuse. Automated boundary tests exercise both stores, reopening, concurrent metadata observations, queued input recovery, owner isolation, reasoning access, erasure and child policy. No live-provider or production-data manual smoke is claimed. The staged secret scan flagged two synthetic redaction fixtures, including one moved existing fixture; both were inspected and contain no real credentials.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. This changes execution and storage behavior, not interface layout or styling.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `61d3eb2d24`; library/integration boundaries and ACP wire tests listed above. Public storage and recovery contract: `docs/book/src/architecture/session-events.md`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A for presentation; relevant automated output tails are included above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Complete and interrupted provider captures retain supplemental fields in both backends; queued inputs retain the admitted workspace; ACP wire resume uses the shared store; current authorization remains effective after reopening and policy changes.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The complete feature/platform/MSRV and VM power-loss matrices require separate environments and were not repeated in the final round. Focused checks and the ten-crate all-targets lint cover the implemented boundaries without claiming those matrices.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Introduces session command/query capabilities and native history files within the existing configured data directory. They default to current owner/policy checks; history and reasoning access are separately authorized, and stored policy evidence cannot mint live grants.
- New external network calls? **No.** Existing provider, tool and delivery transports remain the effect owners.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** No history-content credential filtering or new encryption system is added in this PR. Ordinary messages, reasoning, media, and execution history remain plaintext under the existing local authorization model. Existing configuration credentials retain their current handling.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Fixtures use synthetic values; private audit documents and local reports are excluded.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Context is restored from event-backed projections. Provider metadata and unknown fields remain classified evidence, cannot confer authority, and are not blindly injected into model-visible text; replay does not execute external effects.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Authorization is resolved live for reads and effects, incoming metadata cannot alter storage-graph identity, and erasure follows referenced content leaves. Backups remain outside an erasure guarantee and must follow the operator's retention policy.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for persisted writers after cutover; existing histories are imported.** Supported old fields/records remain readable, missing historical facts remain absent, and unknown variants do not fabricate successful execution.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes, existing CLI persistence behavior changes.** Reuses `channels.session_backend` and existing CLI options; no new storage-selection key or environment variable is required. Recorded model-provider aliases cannot be renamed while native history depends on them.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** The declared Rust 1.96.0 floor is unchanged; local validation used 1.99.0.
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: Stop all old writers; take a consistent backup of the complete configured data directory, including SQLite WAL state where applicable; keep the desired `sqlite` or `jsonl` backend selected; start the new binary. Installation import resumes after interruption and publishes ready only after successful import and source archival. Legacy files are renamed as backups, including `acp-sessions.db`. Do not reopen the migrated installation with an older writer.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Before migration, reverting this commit is sufficient. After migration, stop all processes, preserve the native directory separately, restore the complete pre-upgrade data/config backup and deploy the prior binary. Reverting code alone does not reverse the storage cutover; writes made after migration must be retained separately for recovery.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None to restore legacy writers. Existing `channels.session_backend` selects SQLite or JSONL and native switching preserves event identity; it is not a rollback to the old format.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Startup/history admission refuses an incomplete or conflicting import; capture errors stop execution; interrupted effects appear as unknown with diagnostics. Inspect session initialization/migration/capture errors and the installation manifest state. Never bypass the fence or clear the manifest to force an older writer.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. This PR does not supersede another PR.
