prs.title: feat(gateway): forward plugin webhooks to the core over RPC
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (`a0f70b7925`). **Depends on #11320** and **#11186** (`zeroclaw-rpc-client` and the gateway's core RPC seam). The branch merges #11320 at its current head `864b58d76e` (with #11319 `c352574198`, #11339 and #11165 `19e41b09fa` beneath it) and #11186 at its current head `ed92285a87` (restacked 2026-10-23 and refreshed 2026-10-29, see below); their commits show in the diff until they land. Review this PR's own commits: `d15729ebff` (the forwarder), `5926ddde14` (docs), `c02e5c0bac` (the in-process seam tests get a TUI signing key), `7702fe138c` (the forwarder's failure records keep the webhook path out) `c02417bfac` (change filter path restored after the restack) and `6d8ed835a8` (the forwarder ends a connection the daemon has stopped recognising, so the link dials again; from Greptile's review); `de5cd570ab` (the connector fix) is superseded by #11186's `535b43829a`.
- **Refresh of 2026-10-29 (`fee8af1cb8`):** merges #11320's new head, which brings master `5a51398dd5` (the one `rpc/types.rs` conflict against it was master editing a doc comment inside the block #11165 moved into `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`; the moved-out file stays and the doc line now lives on the proto copy) and #11320's admission re-check: the daemon re-resolves the forwarder's live grants at admission instead of trusting the binding its dispatch task copied, so a revoked or narrowed caller is refused and the forwarder answers 503 for it, as for any core refusal. No change to this PR's own slice.
- **Second refresh of 2026-10-29 (`6d8ed835a8`):** merges #11320's `864b58d76e` (`2f1fa249a4`: a rename or delete over the socket now refuses a cascade outside the caller's config write grants; the forwarder connects as the shared operator and is not affected) and adds `6d8ed835a8`, from Greptile's review of this PR: when a policy change removes or revokes the gateway's identity while its connection is open, the daemon keeps the socket and answers `AUTH_REQUIRED`, and the link redialed only after a close, so webhooks stayed 503 after the operator restored access. The forwarder now ends the connection at the first such answer (record `plugin_webhook_core_identity_lost`) and the redial is accepted once access is back, or refused into the slow backoff while it is not; `FORBIDDEN` stays on the connection. Two tests: the close seen from both sides, and the whole sequence over a local socket ending with a webhook served on the new connection.
- **Restack of 2026-10-23 (`bb5eb8a1ca`, `c02417bfac`, `54dc89c97f`):** #11165 and #11186 were refreshed onto master by their author on October 22, so this branch merges #11320's restacked head (which carries #11165 `19e41b09fa` and #11319) and then #11186 `ed92285a87`, and is mergeable with master again. The hand-resolved files against #11320 were the CI workflow registry, the CI guide, the plugin backend change filter (each side's lines kept; the filter's own test caught one path the first pass dropped, restored in `c02417bfac`), the root `Cargo.toml` (the rpc-client member, dependency, dev-dependencies and the two-process test target on top of #11320's) and the proto boundary test, taken from #11186's head, which already reconciles #11165's new wording with the rpc-client checks. Against #11186 only `inproc.rs` conflicted, and this branch takes #11186's file: its `535b43829a` is the connector fix this PR carried as `de5cd570ab`, so that commit is now redundant here and ownership sits in #11186 as asked, and its `e4bd5853e9` treats the in-process connection as remote in every local-only check, alongside this PR's `plugin-webhook/*` refusal arm.
- **Fix for #11186 on top of the merge** (`fix(rpc): release the in-process connector's context when its generation retires`): the daemon hands the gateway a clone of the generation's `InprocConnector` through its reload controls, and the connector kept the generation's `RpcContext` (its sessions and their lifecycle leases) until the last clone dropped. With #10621, a reload waits for that state to drain before it releases process ownership, so `reload_waits_for_detached_write_before_releasing_process_ownership` failed 3 of 3 runs on the merge. Sealing admission now releases the context in the same critical section, `bind` leaves a sealed connector unbound, and a `connect` waiting for a bind gives up once the generation is sealed. Two new connector tests cover it, and the daemon test passes. It belongs in #11186: I asked for it there (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11186#issuecomment-5942108575; it cherry-picks cleanly onto `84f31b29cb`), and this branch drops it once #11186 has it.
- **Audacity88's review (both blockers):**
  - **Webhook paths stay out of failure logs.** Some vendors use an unguessable webhook path as their shared secret, and log records are persisted as written. `7702fe138c` drops the path from the five `plugin_webhook_core_*` records, which keep their error key and code. `core_failure_records_keep_a_secret_path_out` sends a secret-shaped path through each core failure and asserts no record contains it. The daemon-side part belongs to #11319 (`fc5f3e95b9`: the ingress's route-closed, reply-dropped and worker-answer records, plus the gateway's `plugin_webhook_request_invalid` record). It arrives here through #11320. The gateway's `plugin_webhook_rate_limited` record still logs the path, as on master.
  - **Removed-binding admission.** Merging #11320 at `d6ef5dc0af` (`853e49dfab`) brings its fail-closed fix `fcf4f6121c`: a route whose `[channels.plugin.<alias>]` binding a live config write removed is refused until reload retires it. #11320's `plugin_webhook_dispatch_refuses_a_published_route_once_its_binding_is_removed` proves that interval, and the forwarder answers that refusal 503 (`core_rpc_errors_map_to_503`). The two-process test still checks the state after reload.
- **#10621 and the standalone gateway:** a running daemon now owns its config state exclusively, so `zeroclaw gateway start` on the daemon's config dir exits with `config lifecycle is already owned`, on master too. Next to a daemon, the standalone gateway therefore runs on a config dir of its own and names the daemon's socket with `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET`. The gateway API guide documents this, and the two-process test runs that way.
- **Channel scoping from #11320:** the forwarder connects as the shared operator, which is `admin`, so `allowed_channels` does not narrow it. A channel instance or agent with `accept_injected_webhooks = false` still refuses its dispatches: that path answers 503, logged `plugin_webhook_core_refused`, while the connection stays up and other paths keep forwarding. A connection the daemon has stopped recognising is different: its `AUTH_REQUIRED` answer ends the connection (`6d8ed835a8`, logged `plugin_webhook_core_identity_lost`) so the link dials again. The gateway API guide lists both.
- **What changed and why:**
  - The standalone `zeroclaw gateway` is the separate gateway process that exists today. Its `/plugin/{path}` route used an empty in-process route table and answered 404 for every path. It now forwards each request to the running daemon over the local RPC socket through `plugin-webhook/dispatch`, so channel-plugin webhooks work across the process boundary. The daemon-supervised gateway keeps calling the core ingress in process.
  - Forwarding: shared request validation, base64 body under a process-unique `request_id`, strict result decoding with the reply bound re-checked, the same `outcome_response` mapping as the in-process path, and a best-effort `plugin-webhook/cancel` when the HTTP request is dropped. The daemon decides 404; while it is unreachable every path answers 503.
  - Daemon identity: on Unix the gateway forwards only to a socket whose peer uid equals its own effective uid, checked before any frame is sent. On Windows, where pipe names share one namespace and the server cannot be verified yet, forwarding stays off and the route keeps answering 404.
  - `core_rpc`: one maintain loop serves the in-process and local dialers; the forwarder owns its own `CoreRpc`, separate from the extension other routes can reach.
  - `plugin-webhook/*` are refused on in-process RPC connections as well as WSS (the arm the transport match needs once #11186 is in).
  - A two-process test runs the real daemon and the real standalone gateway binaries.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to the supervised gateway's behavior, to vendor webhook handlers, WIT, or config. No gateway service identity (the standalone gateway authenticates by peer credentials; see Security). The standalone `zeroclaw-gw` binary is #11002.
- **Blast radius:** standalone `zeroclaw gateway` (start, restart, bare); gateway `core_rpc` seam from #11186; RPC transport refusal; CI plugin legs and path filters.
- **Changes to #11186's in-process seam (for its author):** after a lost connection the loop waits a backoff before redialing (it redialed immediately); logs only on state transitions with error keys `core_rpc_{lost,unreachable,refused}` (and `core_rpc_untrusted_peer` for the local dialer); a FORBIDDEN refusal logs at INFO; `CoreRpc` stores a `CoreLink` (Disconnected, Connected, Refused) with `client()` and `is_connected()` unchanged; new public `CoreLink`, `CoreRpc::link()`, and Unix-only `attach_local` and `daemon_endpoint`. Refusals still end the in-process loop. `GatewaySupervision::standalone(readiness, &config)` returns a `Result`, because it builds the live config authority master now requires.
- **Follow-ups from the review, not in this PR:** route `run_gateway` through `GatewaySupervision::standalone` or make it test-only, so an embedder does not get the old unrouted `/plugin/{path}` (#11568); a scoped service identity for the forwarder's connection, tracked in #11569 under #11002.
- **Merge-order note:** this PR carries the `TransportKind::Inproc` refusal arm and test that #11320's exhaustive match needs with #11186. If #11186 lands before #11320, move them into #11320. The arm must keep refusing `Inproc` with FORBIDDEN, never treat it like `Local`. #11289 replaces the free-text `AuthDenied::forbidden(message)` this arm uses, so if #11289 lands first the arm needs its `RpcDenialReason` (the variants are listed in #11320).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003 (acceptance: separate-process flow). Related #7432 (G4 transport; vendor migration stays under #8850). Related #11000. Related #11002. Depends on #11186.

### What this does, simply

You can run the web gateway on its own with `zeroclaw gateway`. Until now, webhooks meant for channel plugins did not work there, because the plugin routes live in the daemon. Now that gateway passes each plugin webhook to the daemon over the local socket and returns the daemon's answer, exactly as the built-in gateway would. If the daemon is down, senders get 503 so they retry, and nothing is forwarded to a socket owned by another user.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional (Unix).
- **Interface(s) exercised:** gateway HTTP (`/plugin/{path}`) plus the local RPC socket.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a config with an installed channel plugin that claims a webhook path and an enabled agent routing it, plus an empty second config dir for the gateway (for example `~/.zeroclaw-gateway`).

- **Expected on this branch (after):** the plugin's normal answer while the daemon runs; 503 `webhook unavailable` while it is down; the answer again after it restarts; after a policy change that removes the gateway's identity, 503 until the operator restores it, then the answer again at the next redial.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** 404 `webhook not found` from the standalone gateway for every path.

- **Refresh for Audacity88's review (head `7702fe138c`):** the same suite again: gateway lib 33 plugin webhook tests with the new one, golden frames (x2 plus all 12), `plugin_channel_runtime_e2e`, the two-process `plugin_webhook_ipc_e2e` (3 passed, x3), architecture (61), the OpenRPC check, workspace and no-default-features checks, and clippy on the touched crates and the root targets. ## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: under the default policy (`security.trust_daemon_uid = true`) the standalone gateway authenticates by peer credentials as the shared operator, which holds every grant. Only the `/plugin/{path}` route uses that connection; it is separate from the core RPC extension other routes can reach.
- New external network calls? No (local socket only)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes: webhook headers, including vendor signature headers, now cross the local socket to the daemon. Mitigation: on Unix the gateway verifies the socket's peer uid equals its own before sending anything; on Windows forwarding is off until the pipe server can be verified.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new path: messages reach the same plugin channel listener as before.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: a publicly bound standalone gateway now exposes the daemon's plugin routes on that listener (same exposure as the supervised gateway on that address). The connection appears as a TUI client (`/api/tuis`) and keeps an `--ephemeral` daemon alive. A refused redial writes a daemon audit record, backed off from 30 seconds to 5 minutes. `zeroclaw gateway restart` first POSTs `/admin/shutdown` to the configured address, which stops a supervised gateway listening there (unchanged, now documented).

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for the supervised gateway. Standalone gateway: `/plugin/{path}` changes from 404 for every path to forwarding (Unix); 503 for every path while the daemon is unreachable or the socket belongs to another user; 503 `plugin_webhook_core_unsupported` against an older daemon without the method. New error keys: `plugin_webhook_core_{unavailable,refused,identity_lost,unsupported,unexpected,timeout}`, `core_rpc_{lost,unreachable,refused,untrusted_peer}`, `plugin_webhook_forwarding_disabled` (Windows). Rust API: `GatewaySupervision::standalone(readiness, &config)`; `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` is an optional gateway dependency behind `plugins-wasm`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new keys. The standalone gateway resolves the daemon socket like other local clients (`ZEROCLAW_SOCKET` or `<data_dir>/daemon.sock`); next to a running daemon it runs on its own config dir, so it needs `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; the standalone gateway returns to answering 404 for plugin routes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** stop the daemon, or build without `plugins-wasm`; `security.trust_daemon_uid = false` without a `[users]` entry for the gateway's uid makes the daemon refuse the connection (webhooks then answer 503).
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `plugin_webhook_core_*` and `core_rpc_*` error keys in the gateway log; 503 bursts on `/plugin/*` from a standalone gateway; `RPC authorization denied` records for the gateway's connection in the daemon log.

milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(rpc): dispatch plugin webhooks over the core RPC
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (`a0f70b7925`). **Depends on #11319** (core ingress, which itself now builds on #11339) and **#11165** (`zeroclaw-rpc-proto`). The branch merges #11319 at its current head `c352574198` and #11165 at its current head `19e41b09fa` (restacked 2026-10-23, see below); their commits show in the diff until they land, so review this PR's own commits, `7962184961` (the methods), `b5d9ebd577` (channel scoping), `fcf4f6121c` (the review's two non-blocking warnings), `4e9a208600` (channel rename and delete carry `allowed_channels` grants), `d6ef5dc0af` (the removed-binding interval test) and `1147d81ac2` and `2aeb57ae9b` (test adaptation to master: config edits go through `publish_test_config` on the read-only live config, `RpcContext::for_authority` sets the ingress handle, the WSS refusal test selects its audit record by reason too, and master's channel WebSocket e2e spreads the plugin channel default), `f3364f9c67` (the RPC socket guide says a rejection record carries the plugin name, channel alias and error key, not the path or the plugin's rejection text; from Greptile's review), `ad161acc03` (admission re-resolves the caller's live grants; from Greptile's and Audacity88's reviews), `13fd6a42e1` (the two denial-record tests drain past a lagged broadcast receiver instead of stopping at it) and `864b58d76e` (a rename or delete refuses a cascade outside the caller's config write grants; from Greptile's review). **Needs the holding-crate exception from #11317 approved first.**
- **#11165 (restack of 2026-10-23, `534a7e41c3` and `82dc407331`):** #11165's head `19e41b09fa` merges master and moves #11132's `session/*` methods into `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`, so the master conflicts in `dispatch.rs`, `session.rs` and `types.rs` are resolved there and this branch merges it without conflict in those files. The hand-resolved files are the CI workflow, its gate registry, the CI guide and the plugin backend change filter, where master, #11165 and #11319 each add their own lines (every side's lines are kept), plus the regenerated OpenRPC document (`cargo generate openrpc`, 107 methods, `--check` clean). #11165's `session/prompt` fix (`SessionPromptAck`) comes along with its head. The branch is now mergeable with master.
- **Channel scoping (maintainer decision on this PR):** `channels:execute` and `channels:read` reach only the channel instances a profile names, and config can close the path for a channel or an agent whatever the grants. Field names and defaults:
  - `[permission_profiles.<name>] allowed_channels = ["plugin.<alias>", ...]`: a channel selector like `allowed_agents`. Entries are `<type>.<alias>` names of configured instances, validated at load; `"*"` grants every instance; empty (the default) grants none. `admin`, including the same-uid shared operator, reaches all.
  - `[channels.plugin.<alias>] accept_injected_webhooks = true` (default): `false` refuses webhooks delivered through `plugin-webhook/dispatch` to that instance.
  - `[agents.<alias>] accept_injected_webhooks = true` (default): `false` refuses such a delivery to any channel the agent handles.
  - Checked at dispatch, not only when routes are listed: `PluginWebhookIngress::dispatch_admitted` runs the check on the owner the request would be queued to, before anything is queued or reserved, so a republished route cannot redirect an admitted request. A refusal is `FORBIDDEN` with an audit record. `plugin-webhook/routes` lists only granted channels.
  - The docs say what `channels = ["execute"]` and `["read"]` unlock (authentication guide and RPC socket guide), and that a route path can be a vendor's shared secret.
  - From the review's non-blocking warnings (`fcf4f6121c`): the refusal for an ungranted channel names no channel, while its audit record still does, and a route whose channel instance the live config no longer binds is refused (fail closed) until the next reload retires it. `d6ef5dc0af` proves that interval: a route admitted while its instance is bound is refused `FORBIDDEN` once a live config write removes the instance, while the route is still published, and its worker receives nothing (asked for in Audacity88's review of #11322).
  - Admission does not trust the grants the spawned dispatch task copied at the read loop's check (`ad161acc03`): `admit_plugin_webhook` re-resolves the caller's live grants with `recheck_authority_after_admission`, the same check `session/new` and `session/prompt` run after admission, so a credential revoked or a profile narrowed between the check and the task's admission refuses the delivery. `plugin_webhook_admission_rechecks_the_live_grants` narrows `allowed_channels` and then drops `channels:execute` after `spawn_handle` and asserts both refusals while the copied grants still allow.
  - Renaming or deleting a channel instance carries its `allowed_channels` grants along (`4e9a208600`): a rename rewrites them to the new name, a delete drops them, and the changed profiles are saved, so a grant never blocks the change. A caller does not reach a profile through that cascade (`864b58d76e`): the rename and the provider-model alias delete check every entry the cascade dirties against the caller's live config write grants and refuse the whole change, with nothing saved, when one of them is outside those grants, the write-set rule the gateway's config routes already follow (`config_map_key_rename_refuses_a_cascade_outside_the_callers_write_paths`: a `channels.*` writer is refused FORBIDDEN naming `permission_profiles.ops`, then succeeds once `permission_profiles.*` is granted).
- **What changed and why:** A gateway in another process needs to hand channel-plugin webhook requests to the core that owns the route table. Three daemon RPC methods over the core ingress:
  - `plugin-webhook/dispatch` (`channels:execute`): method, raw query, headers, and the body as standard base64 under a caller-chosen `request_id`; answers a typed outcome (`ack`, `reply` with `body`, `not_found`, `queue_full`, `unavailable`, `unauthorized`, `bad_request`, `invalid_response`, `timeout`, `cancelled`). Validated by the same shared constructor the HTTP adapter uses.
  - `plugin-webhook/cancel` (`channels:execute`): cancels an in-flight dispatch on the same connection; the dispatch response stays authoritative.
  - `plugin-webhook/routes` (`channels:read`): current route owners, for diagnostics.
  - Local IPC only: an exhaustive transport match refuses all three on WSS with FORBIDDEN and an audit record.
  - Dispatch runs in a task spawned from the dispatcher like `session/prompt`, so the serial read loop stays live for cancel and other requests. Each connection tracks in-flight dispatches for cancel and duplicate-id checks and holds at most 1024 until their responses are queued; the next gets `queue_full`. Connection close and daemon reload cancel in-flight work and send nothing; shutdown joins the tasks and never waits on a full writer queue.
  - The daemon registry hands the generation's ingress to the RPC context, and the daemon always builds one ingress.
- **Scope boundary:** No gateway change (the forwarder is the next PR). No new principal or credential. Runtime edits stay within the #11317 row: `src/rpc/{dispatch,context}.rs`, `src/daemon/{registry,mod}.rs`, and the denial message keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl`. The new config field also updates `PluginChannelConfig` literals inside the test modules of `src/plugin_runtime.rs` and `src/tools/mod.rs` (mechanical, test-only). The grant selector and config fields live in `zeroclaw-api` and `zeroclaw-config`.
- **Blast radius:** runtime RPC dispatcher (new arms, per-connection state, shutdown join), daemon registry, `RpcContext` (all 14 literals), the OpenRPC document (regenerated), `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` (8 wire types, 3 `Method` variants), `zeroclaw-api` (route listing, the `allowed_channels` selector), `zeroclaw-infra` (route listing, `dispatch_admitted`), `zeroclaw-config` (three fields).
- **Follow-ups from the review, not in this PR:** one local-only gate shared with `file/upload/*`, with a per-method "local only" classification `xtask` can emit (#11566), and `schemars` bounds on the dispatch wire fields so the OpenRPC document states them (#11567).
- **Merge-order note:** #11186 adds `TransportKind::Inproc`. The transport match here is deliberately exhaustive, so whichever of this PR and #11186 lands second must add the `Inproc` arm (refused, with its test; #11322 carries both). #11289 replaces the free-text `AuthDenied::forbidden(message)` with `RpcDenialReason`: whichever of this PR and #11289 lands second needs variants for this PR's four refusals (for example `local_ipc_only`, `channel_not_granted`, `channel_refuses_injected_webhooks`, `agent_refuses_injected_webhooks`) and the updated audit assertions, which now read `reason` as a stable identifier.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003. Related #7432. Related #11000. Related #11001. Depends on #11165.

### What this does, simply

The daemon already answers RPC calls from local clients such as zerocode. This PR teaches it three more calls so a separate web gateway can say "here is a webhook request for this plugin URL, what should I answer?" and get back the same result the in-process gateway gets today. Only local connections may use them, and only callers allowed to operate the specific channels they ask for. An operator can also switch the path off for one channel, or for one agent, in config, whatever access a caller has.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** local RPC socket.
- **Steps to run:** start a daemon with a configured channel plugin that claims a webhook path, then over `socat READLINE UNIX-CONNECT:<data_dir>/daemon.sock` send `initialize`, then `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"plugin-webhook/routes","params":{},"id":2}` and a `plugin-webhook/dispatch` for that path.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** routes lists the owner; dispatch answers `{"outcome":"ack"}` or the plugin's reply.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `METHOD_NOT_FOUND`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` (runtime `rpc::` and `daemon::` suites, proto tests), `Parallel Runtime Test` (runtime/channels interference), `Installer Drift` (OpenRPC `--check`), plugin legs for the ingress and gateway parity.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Windows named pipes are not exercised by a required job.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `b5d9ebd577`: this PR with #11319 `98e1666b31` and #11165 `ec00bf0a12` merged, on master `a0f70b7925`; macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0)

```text
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::
test result: FAILED. 784 passed; 1 failed   (configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock, see below)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::dispatch::tests::plugin_webhook   (x3)
test result: ok. 26 passed   (includes plugin_webhook_dispatch_reaches_only_granted_channels and plugin_webhook_dispatch_honors_channel_and_agent_refusal)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib daemon::
test result: FAILED. 101 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored   (a_live_config_write_reaches_the_daemon_pricing_refresher_without_a_reload, see below)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra --lib ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib
ok. 295 passed, ok. 335 passed ; ok. 1760 passed   (channel selector, allowed_channels validation, accept_injected_webhooks defaults, dispatch_admitted)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto --features schema-export
ok. 29 passed ; ok. 32 passed
$ cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin generate -- openrpc --check ; cargo test --locked -p xtask openrpc
openrpc: docs/book/src/architecture/zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json is in sync ; ok
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib ; --test golden_frames plugin_webhook
ok. 653 passed ; ok. 5 passed (fixtures unchanged)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib plugin_runtime:: ; cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e ; --test architecture
ok. 17 passed ; ok. 5 passed ; ok. 57 passed
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets ; cargo check --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --tests ; RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
Finished ; Finished ; Finished, no warnings
$ cargo clippy (api, infra, config, gateway, rpc-proto; with and without zeroclaw-gateway/plugins-wasm; root bin and e2e) --no-deps -- -D warnings
Finished, no warnings
$ TMPDIR=/private/tmp ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh ; ZEROCLAW_PARALLEL_TEST_SCOPE=channels ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh
runtime run 1/3: 5466 passed; 1 failed (peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget; the gate stops there) ; channels x3: ok. 1967 passed
$ comment hygiene, change filter, docs quality and docs links gates
all pass
```

The three failing runtime tests fail identically on untouched master `a0f70b7925` in this environment (two runs each), and this PR does not touch them. `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` stops only on the pre-existing macOS `unused import std::sync::mpsc` in `service/mod.rs`; no lint in any changed runtime file.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Mutations caught by the new tests: releasing the permit before the send, shutdown not joining dispatch tasks, releasing the id after the send, allowing WSS, removing the send's race against connection cancel, and skipping the denial audit record.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Restack onto #11165 `19e41b09fa` and #11319 `c352574198` (head `2aeb57ae9b`, 2026-10-23):** the whole suite again on this head: proto (30, schema export 33), api and infra (339), config (1821 of 1822), channels listing (8), gateway with `plugins-wasm` and the plugin webhook golden frames (5, fixtures unchanged), runtime `rpc::` and `daemon::` (104), plugin admission (34), `plugin_channel_runtime_e2e` (5), architecture (81), `cargo generate openrpc --check` in sync, workspace and root `plugins-wasm-cranelift` checks, `--no-default-features` with `-D warnings`, clippy on the touched crates, the root binary and e2e, and runtime clippy, the comment hygiene, change filter, docs and links gates, and the parallel runtime gate (runtime x3 at 16 threads, channels x3), all green. The one failure is `policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception`, a master test that fails on macOS (PR 11646) and that this PR does not touch; the earlier pre-existing runtime failures no longer reproduce on this master.
- **Refresh for the #11322 review (head `d6ef5dc0af`):** the same suite again: `rpc::dispatch::tests::plugin_webhook` 27 passed (with the new test), and the only failures are the same three pre-existing runtime tests and the macOS `std::sync::mpsc` clippy warning described above. The new test fails if a missing binding is admitted.
- **The parallel-gate failure of `plugin_webhook_dispatch_reaches_only_granted_channels` (`13fd6a42e1`):** the test reads its audit record from the process-wide log broadcast, and its drain stopped at the first lagged-receiver error, which the channel reports once a noisy neighbour floods the window between the subscription and the drain under 16 threads, so the record was never reached; the WSS refusal test had the same latent stop. Both now subscribe right before the call under test, drain past a lag with a two-second deadline for a late record, and report on a miss whether the capture layer was active and whether the broadcast hook changed since the subscription. `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::dispatch::tests::plugin_webhook -- --test-threads=16` x3 passes (28 tests); the parallel gate's result on this head is in CI.
- **The cascade write-set check (`864b58d76e`):** `rpc::` 865 passed at 16 threads, with `config_map_key_rename_refuses_a_cascade_outside_the_callers_write_paths`; runtime clippy (`--all-targets`, `-D warnings`) clean; the docs quality and link gates pass on `authentication.md`, whose RPC selector bullet now says a cascade's rewrites are checked too.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --no-default-features --features agent-runtime` fails on six pre-existing dead-code helpers in `src/main.rs` whose only caller is gateway-gated; unrelated, reproduces on master.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: `Resource::Channels` gains its first RPC consumers, scoped to named channel instances through `allowed_channels`. `admin`, including the same-uid shared operator, reaches every route; any other profile reaches only the instances it names. `accept_injected_webhooks = false` on a channel instance or an agent refuses the path whatever the grants. Plugins still verify vendor signatures.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No (headers pass through to the guest as they do over HTTP)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new path: dispatched messages enter the same plugin channel listener as HTTP webhooks.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: local IPC only (WSS refused with an audit record); grants checked at admission; the core enforces the shared request bounds, so a local caller bypassing the gateway's rate limit still cannot exceed them; 1024 in-flight dispatches per connection; no diagnostic detail in results.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (additive methods). Builds with plugins but without the gateway now build the ingress, so webhook-capable plugin channels validate and publish their route claims instead of activating poll-only. A worker that drops its reply after the caller cancelled now reports `cancelled` instead of `unavailable`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes, additive: `[permission_profiles.<name>] allowed_channels` (default empty, so a profile with `channels` grants but no selector reaches no channel; nothing consumed `channels` before this PR), and `accept_injected_webhooks` on `[channels.plugin.<alias>]` and `[agents.<alias>]` (default `true`).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; the methods disappear (`METHOD_NOT_FOUND`) and nothing persisted changes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** remove `channels:execute` or the channel from a profile's `allowed_channels` to deny dispatch; `accept_injected_webhooks = false` on a channel instance or agent closes the path whatever the grants; `plugins.enabled = false` publishes no routes.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `RPC authorization denied` records for `plugin-webhook/*`, with reasons naming the channel or agent that refused; `queue_full` answers at the per-connection cap; WARN `plugin_webhook_dispatch_notification` for notification-form dispatches.

milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(cli): zeroclaw user commands for roster password lifecycle
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Depends on #11264 and #11313. This branch carries both until they merge: merge commit `5f679fe103` joins them, and `9707c30981` reconciles them (`is_auth_input_path` names `security.password_auth`, which #11264 made an authorization input, and the publication tests' roster literals spell out `password_hash`; whichever of the two lands second takes that commit). This PR's own change is the `zeroclaw user` commit as reviewed (`29fb0e0272`), the rework that addresses the review (`54cabe9ec8`), and `eede22bce7`, which checks the daemon's roster again just before a commit (from tidux's approval). The remaining commits merge #11264's updates and `master`; the latest, `ef5dcf3a61`, merges #11313's current head (`78ccdc1478`, its own merge of `master`) and leaves the tree unchanged.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #8076 requires a documented way to create the first admin and to rotate or disable a password (`zeroclaw user …`), and a way to repair a forgotten password on the daemon host. Hand-writing scrypt PHC strings is not that.
  - `zeroclaw user list | add | passwd | disable-password | remove | hash-password`. Every edit is checked as a complete authorization policy (`validate_accepted_auth_config`) before a password prompt and again before it is committed. A refused edit writes nothing.
  - **Edits go through the running daemon.** While a daemon serves the configuration, each edit is committed through #11313's verified daemon client, the same path `config set` uses for an authorization edit: `add` and `passwd` as `config/set-many`, `disable-password` as `config/delete` (the daemon's way to clear a secret, which `config/set` refuses to overwrite with an empty value), and `remove` as `config/map-key-delete`. The daemon validates, saves, and publishes the edit as one step, so `user remove` ends the entry's uid binding for established and new connections, and `user add --uid` grants it, with no restart.
  - With no daemon running, the command saves `config.toml` itself, as before. When the daemon refuses the caller at the handshake (a uid outside the roster, or the deny-all state), or cannot be asked (the reasons #11313 lists, such as a Windows named pipe), the command saves the file and reports the edit pending until the next reload or restart, which keeps it a lockout repair path. When the daemon identifies the caller and refuses the edit (`add` and `passwd` need `update` on config, `disable-password` and `remove` need `delete`), or rejects it, nothing is saved. The closing notice says which of these happened.
  - **The file and the daemon's roster can differ** while a hand edit or an edit reported pending waits for a reload, and the command decides from the file whether an entry exists. So before a password is typed, it reads the daemon's roster (`config/map-keys`, a config read) and refuses an `add` of a name the daemon still holds, which would merge into that entry and keep its other credentials live, and a `passwd` or `disable-password` of an entry the daemon has not loaded. It reads the roster again just before the commit and refuses, to be run again, an edit whose entry another writer added or removed through the daemon while the prompt was open. A `remove` of an entry the daemon never loaded gets `deleted: false` back (`Publication::DaemonUnchanged`), and the command removes it from the file itself, so a later reload cannot bring it back.
  - When the command saves the file itself, it refuses if `config.toml` changed since the edit began (a password prompt can take a while). That comparison and the write are separate steps, and the docs say so. It also refuses when the roster, profile, or OIDC section failed to load, or when an environment override sets a value the check reads but the file does not hold.
  - `passwd` checks the policy as it will be after the edit, so it also repairs an entry the policy refuses (no credential yet, or a hash outside the bounds).
  - Passwords come from a hidden prompt (typed twice) or one line of standard input (refused on a terminal), never from arguments, and are scrubbed from memory once hashed. A new password needs at least 15 characters (NIST SP 800-63B-4's minimum for a single-factor password) and at most 1024 bytes, with no composition rules.
  - **Hash policy decisions before the first stored hash** (from the #11264 review): passwords are hashed and checked as their NFKC normalization, as NIST SP 800-63B-4 recommends, so the same characters typed on another keyboard or input method still match. A new password needs 15 characters both as typed and once normalized (one typed ligature can normalize to 18), and may not contain a code point Unicode leaves unassigned, as UAX #15's process for stabilized strings requires, since a later Unicode version could change how it normalizes. scrypt work is capped at the top of OWASP's table, N times p at most 131072, which also bounds p (the separate `p <= 16` ceiling is gone).
  - Help text for `zeroclaw user` and its six subcommands is in all five CLI catalogs.
  - `hash-password` needs no config and prints only the hash, so it is dispatched before any config is loaded. The two dispatch arms that can never run now fail with an error, like the other pre-runtime commands.
- **Scope boundary:** No daemon, RPC, or gateway change: the commands use the daemon's existing config methods through #11313's client. Nothing presents a password to the provider yet (the session and gateway work that follows). Translating the shared validators' English refusals is #11570. The two-process lost-update window Audacity88 described stays a follow-up: an edit the daemon commits is validated and saved under its write lock, but two commands that both save the file themselves are only narrowed by the byte comparison.
- **Blast radius:** `src/main.rs` (the command, two early dispatch points), `src/config_publication.rs` (`commit_delete`, `commit_map_key_delete`, `live_map_keys`, and `Publication::DaemonUnchanged` for a delete that finds nothing; `config set` and `config patch` never produce it), `zeroclaw-config` (`check_new_password`, NFKC, the work cap, `Decoy::as_phc`; `unicode-normalization` and `zeroize` become direct dependencies, both already in the lockfile), five CLI catalogs, the authentication docs, and `zeroize` as a direct dependency of the root crate.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8076, Depends on #11264, Depends on #11313

### What this does, simply

The previous PR taught ZeroClaw to check a password against a stored hash. This one gives operators the tool that writes those hashes: `zeroclaw user add` creates a user, `passwd` changes a password, `disable-password` and `remove` take access away, and `list` shows who has what without printing a hash. When the daemon is running, each change takes effect immediately, so removing a user cuts off their access right away. When it is not running, or refuses the person running the command, the change is written to the config file and applies at the next restart, which is also how a lockout gets fixed. A user added this way cannot sign in with a password yet: the sign-in surfaces come in the next PRs.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** a scratch config dir: `mkdir /tmp/zc-user && printf 'schema_version = 3\n\n[permission_profiles.operator]\ngrants = { sessions = ["read"] }\n' > /tmp/zc-user/config.toml`
- **Steps to run:** `zeroclaw --config-dir /tmp/zc-user user add zeroclaw_user --profile operator --uid 4101 --password`, then `zeroclaw --config-dir /tmp/zc-user user list`; then start `zeroclaw --config-dir /tmp/zc-user daemon` and run `zeroclaw --config-dir /tmp/zc-user user remove zeroclaw_user`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the add succeeds after two masked prompts; `list` shows `password set`; with the daemon running, `remove` prints `Authorization change applied to the running daemon.`
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `zeroclaw user` does not exist.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the workspace test run executes `tests/component/user_cli.rs` and the new `zeroclaw user` cases in `tests/component/config_auth_publication_cli.rs` (a real `zeroclaw daemon` on a private config dir, the CLI in a separate process, and a raw JSON-RPC client), plus the unit tests in `src/main.rs`, `src/config_publication.rs` and `zeroclaw-config`; Rust lint; `Docs Style`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the live-daemon tests are Unix-only, like the rest of that suite; on Windows the CLI never sends an edit over the named pipe and reports it pending. The interactive prompt needs a terminal; see the evidence below.
- **Commands run and tail output** (macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0, head `4954238bbc`; head `ef5dcf3a61` has the identical tree, `git diff 4954238bbc ef5dcf3a61` is empty, so these results and the terminal evidence below hold for it unchanged):

```text
$ cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check                                                  # clean
$ cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings   # exit 0
$ RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo +1.98.0 check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features   # exit 0
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --no-run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop          # exit 0
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw --test component -- config_auth_publication_cli user_cli
test result: ok. 42 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw -- user_add roster_edit only_overrides config_publication
test result: ok. 24 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw --test architecture                          # ok. 55 passed
$ TMPDIR=/private/tmp cargo +1.98.0 nextest run --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-api
     Summary [  52.841s] 7918 tests run: 7918 passed (2 leaky), 8 skipped
$ cargo +1.98.0 deny check                                                             # advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok
$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh / docs_links_gate.sh / comment_hygiene_gate.sh        # clean
```

- **Re-run on `ef5dcf3a61`** (the restack onto #11313's `78ccdc1478`; its only conflict was the `config-lifecycle.md` CLI row, resolved to this branch's row naming `zeroclaw user`): `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0; `cargo check -p zeroclaw --no-default-features` exit 0; `cargo test -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw` ok. 555 passed; `cargo test -p zeroclaw --test component config_auth_publication -- --test-threads=1` ok. 30 passed; `cargo test -p zeroclaw --test component user_cli -- --test-threads=1` ok. 12 passed; `cargo test -p zeroclaw --test component config_patch_cli` ok. 25 passed; `cargo test -p zeroclaw --test architecture` ok. 55 passed; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- rpc::auth:: daemon:: rpc::local::` ok. 183 passed, 1 ignored; `cargo doc` clean; docs, links and comment hygiene gates clean; `Cargo.lock` unchanged.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `4954238bbc` (same tree as head `ef5dcf3a61`), `zeroclaw user passwd` at a pseudo-terminal (80x24, `LC_ALL=C`), driven by a script that types a freshly generated password and records every byte the terminal received; disposable config dirs under `/tmp`.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:**

```text
revision: 4954238bbc
binary: target/debug/zeroclaw, built at that revision
os: Darwin 25.5.0 arm64
--- case 1-no-daemon-match: exit=0 password_in_terminal_output=False
  screen, first entry typed, before Enter:
    | New password
    | ••••••••••••••••••••••••
  screen, second entry typed, before Enter:
    | New password
    | Repeat the password
    | ••••••••••••••••••••••••
  final screen:
    | New password
    | Repeat the password
    | Set the password for users.zeroclaw_operator.
    | Password sign-in is off. Set security.password_auth.enabled = true to turn it on.
  saved hash line: password_hash = "enc2:59...
  config changed: True
--- case 2-no-daemon-mismatch: exit=1 password_in_terminal_output=False
  screen, first entry typed, before Enter:
    | New password
    | ••••••••••••••••••••••••
  screen, second entry typed, before Enter:
    | New password
    | Repeat the password
    | •••••••••••••••••••••••• (+1)
  final screen:
    | New password
    | Repeat the password
    | Error: The two passwords do not match.
  config unchanged: True
--- case 3-daemon-running-match: exit=0 password_in_terminal_output=False
  screen, first entry typed, before Enter:
    | New password
    | ••••••••••••••••••••••••
  screen, second entry typed, before Enter:
    | New password
    | Repeat the password
    | ••••••••••••••••••••••••
  final screen:
    | New password
    | Repeat the password
    | Set the password for users.zeroclaw_operator.
    | Authorization change applied to the running daemon.
    | Password sign-in is off. Set security.password_auth.enabled = true to turn it on.
  saved hash line: password_hash = "enc2:44...
  daemon pid: 83528
ALL CHECKS PASSED
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The pseudo-terminal runs above: both entries stay masked (the transcript never contains the password), matching entries save the hash `enc2:`-encrypted, a mismatch writes nothing, and with a daemon running the edit is applied by the daemon. Not verified: Windows.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact terminal output above (locale `C`, 80x24; the prompt draws a masked placeholder, no styling).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** None. The tests nextest flags as leaky (`rpc::dispatch::tests::operator_lists_any_directory` and `uses_memory_true_cron_run_keeps_memory_tools`) are unrelated to this change; the flag marks a test that left a handle open, and which tests trip it varies between runs.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (writes the same `config.toml` that `config set` writes, or asks the daemon to, through the existing config methods)
- New external network calls? No (the local daemon socket only, through #11313's verified client)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: the CLI reads a password and writes its hash. The password is never an argument (no shell history or process-list exposure), is read masked or from a pipe, the buffers the command holds (including the normalized copy) are scrubbed once hashed, and the hash is stored as an encrypted secret, by the daemon or by the CLI. Only the hash crosses the local socket, to a daemon whose identity #11313's client verifies first. `list` never prints a hash.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: new `zeroclaw user` command. The hash policy narrows from N times p up to 16 times 2^17 to at most 131072; no shipped release wrote hashes.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Upgrade steps: none.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the commits. Hashes this command wrote remain valid config for #11264, but a revert also takes NFKC out of `verify_password`, so a password whose typed form is not already NFKC (an accent typed as a combining mark, a full-width letter) stops matching its stored hash until a new one is set.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `security.password_auth.enabled` governs whether stored hashes are used at all.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `zeroclaw user` exits non-zero with a reason, and nothing is saved; or it reports the edit pending, with the reason, when a running daemon did not take it.

prs.title: fix(agents): share durable committed-rename recovery across CLI, gateway, and RPC
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - An agent rename commits its config change before the workspace, memory, cron, ACP, and session state follow. A failure in between stranded that state under the old alias: the CLI could not resume (it reported the old alias as not configured), gateway and RPC resumed only through surface-local probes that read an unreadable store as clean, and a new agent created under the old alias inherited whatever was left.
  - Adds a durable recovery journal, `<data_dir>/agent-lifecycle-recovery.json` (`zeroclaw_config::agent_recovery_journal`), with a sidecar lock, atomic writes, and fail-closed reads. A record is written before the config commit and removed only after every follower is verified converged.
  - Adds one runtime-owned contract, `zeroclaw_runtime::agent_rename_recovery`, that gateway, daemon RPC, and CLI all run: validate both aliases before any path is derived, resolve the request against live config and the journal, arm the record, commit, converge the followers, re-probe, clear. Followers probe before they act, never create a store, and treat an unreadable store as unfinished work.
  - Refuses to create or reuse an alias retired by an unfinished rename at the two config-layer places an agent alias comes into existence (`alias_refs::create_map_key_checked` and the property-path auto-create), so CLI `agents create`, `config set|patch|init`, gateway map-key/section/prop/PATCH, RPC create/set, quickstart, and the agent-facing model routing tool are all covered. Deleting or renaming the pending target is refused too, and the delete previews report the same refusal.
  - Runs inside the lifecycle coordinator that just landed: the per-alias leases, the non-cancellable lifecycle job, channel-generation retirement, and CLI daemon routing are unchanged; the recovery contract replaces the rename follower cascade inside that job.
  - Fixes rename bugs found on the way: the memory follower was not retry-safe (a second `rename_agent` dropped an empty destination identity row or refused to merge), the cron residue probe ignored run-history ownership, the resume branch derived paths from unvalidated aliases, and restored ACP sessions kept the old default workspace as their working directory.
  - Adds `zeroclaw agents rename <old> <new> --abandon` as the explicit way out of a rename that cannot finish; it lists the state that stays under the old alias before dropping the record.
- **Scope boundary:** Followers are the default per-alias workspace, memory attribution, cron ownership (jobs and run history), ACP sessions (owner and persisted working directory), and session attribution. Not moved by a rename today and out of scope: control-plane task rows (delegate and peer-inbox), SOP references, parked SOP runs, and the cost ledger; each needs separate follow-up. Permission-profile references are covered by #11226. Knowledge-graph ownership is not on `master`. Delete recovery for a custom workspace is #10149. An agent added through an environment override or a hand edit of `config.toml` is not refused; config load logs a warning for it.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-config` (journal, create guards, protected runtime file names), `zeroclaw-runtime` (contract, path classifier, cron probe, RPC rename and delete), `zeroclaw-infra` (ACP and session store probes), `zeroclaw-memory` (factory path accessor), `zeroclaw-gateway` (rename, delete, delete plan), `zeroclaw-tools` (model routing tool), the CLI (`agents rename|create|delete`, `config set|init|patch`), docs.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #10373. Related #10149, #9745, #11226. Builds on the lifecycle coordinator from #10621.
- **Merge order:** with #11226, whichever lands second ports its per-dirty-path write-authority recheck into the agent rename path (`rename_agent_alias` on RPC). With #9745, if this lands first, #9745 registers a knowledge follower in the recovery contract instead of editing the removed cascade; if #9745 lands first, this PR adds that follower before merging. Either way a rename cannot clear its record while knowledge rows remain under the old alias.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `agent`, `config`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `memory`, `cli`, `tool`, `docs`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`

### What this does, simply

Renaming an agent moves its files and records to the new name after the config change is saved. If a move failed, the rest stayed under the old name, the command line could not finish the job, and a new agent created with the old name quietly took the leftovers over. Now every rename writes down what it is doing before it starts, any interface can finish it by running the same rename again, and the old name is not handed out again until everything has moved or the operator explicitly abandons the rename.

## Testing (required)

- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw agents rename|create|delete`), gateway `POST /api/config/rename-map-key` and `POST /api/config/map-key`, daemon RPC `config/map-key-rename`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A config with an agent `agent_a` that has a default workspace containing a file, a cron job, and some memory.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Make the destination unwritable, for example create a regular file at `<install>/agents/agent_b`.
  2. `zeroclaw agents rename agent_a agent_b`: the config commits, the command exits non-zero and names the workspace follower.
  3. `zeroclaw agents create agent_a`: refused, naming the rename to re-run.
  4. Remove the blocking file and re-run step 2: exits 0, the workspace, cron job, and memory are under `agent_b`, and `<data_dir>/agent-lifecycle-recovery.json` is gone.
  5. `zeroclaw agents create agent_a`: succeeds, and the new agent owns none of the old state.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** as above. Gateway and RPC answer the failed rename with `renamed: true` plus warnings, and the CLI can finish a rename the gateway started.

v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(cli): publish authorization edits from config set and config patch into the running daemon
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `zeroclaw config set` and `zeroclaw config patch` saved `config.toml` and printed "updated" while a running daemon kept enforcing the previous authorization policy until someone reloaded it. When an edit writes or changes an authorization input (`[users]`, `[permission_profiles]`, `[oidc]`, `security.trust_daemon_uid`) and this configuration's daemon is running, the CLI now commits the edit through the daemon's own RPC config path (`config/set`, or `config/set-many` for a patch). The daemon's admitted config commit (`begin_config_commit`, then `save_and_publish_config`) already validates the policy, saves the file and publishes the new configuration and the next accepted authorization revision under the process-wide config writer lock, so the policy is in force before the CLI reports success and established connections re-resolve at their next operation. Nothing is reloaded and no connection is dropped. A `--comment` travels with the edit and the daemon writes it under the same lock, so the CLI does not touch `config.toml` after the daemon saved it.
  - The CLI only talks to the daemon that belongs to its configuration directory. That daemon counts as running while its heartbeat file beside `config.toml` is recent and names a live process. Before anything is written to the socket, the peer must be this account or root and, where the kernel reports it, the peer process must be the one the heartbeat names; otherwise the pid the daemon reports at `initialize` must match. With no confirmed daemon the CLI contacts no endpoint (an exported `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET` included), but it does probe the configuration's ownership lock: if another process holds it (a daemon still starting, before its first heartbeat, a standalone `zeroclaw gateway start`, or a `zeroclaw agent` session), the edit is saved and reported pending instead of passing silently. On Windows the CLI does not verify a named pipe's server, so it never sends an authorization edit there and reports it pending.
  - A refusal is judged by phase. When the daemon refuses the caller at the handshake (a uid outside the roster, the deny-all state), the CLI keeps its direct write and reports the edit as **pending reload**; that is the lockout-recovery path. When the daemon identifies the caller and then refuses the edit (its principal lacks the config-write grant), the command fails and nothing is saved. Pending is also reported, with the reason on stderr and as a `daemon` member in the `--json` envelope, when the daemon runs another release, fails the handshake, cannot be reached, is not this configuration's daemon, or for writes its config methods do not take (clearing a secret, creating a keyed-list row, a patch over the 256-entry batch cap). Before any such local save the CLI refuses an edit that would turn a policy that compiles into one that does not, so a pending edit can never become a deny-all state at the next reload, while a file that is already broken can still be repaired one field at a time. When the daemon rejects the edit, or is asked and never answers, the command fails and nothing is saved. A `config patch` that the daemon would apply fails before the daemon is asked if it carries any `test` op, whatever path it checks, because the `test` would be checked against the CLI's on-disk copy while every write in the patch lands on the daemon's live configuration.
  - Whether an edit is an authorization edit is decided by path (`is_auth_input_path`) or by a change in `auth_inputs`, the comparison the daemon's own publication makes, so re-asserting a value that is only on disk still reaches the daemon. Both live in `zeroclaw_runtime::rpc::auth`, and a guard test walks every configuration property and fails when changing a property moves `auth_inputs` without `is_auth_input_path` covering it, so adding a new authorization input cannot leave the path list behind. The heartbeat's format and freshness bound have one reader next to its writer (`daemon::recorded_daemon`), and the daemon's refusal to overwrite a secret with a placeholder is one function (`refuses_secret_placeholder`) that both the daemon and the CLI call. Edits outside the authorization inputs never contact the daemon and their output is unchanged. `config init` never commits authorization entries through the daemon: while one runs it reports such an entry as pending, and refuses one that cannot compile until filled in (`users.<name>`, `oidc.<alias>`).
  - The authentication guide documents the full contract next to the `--json` reason codes, and no longer describes dashboard writes as reload-bound (since the supervised gateway and RPC share one authority and one live configuration, a stale statement this PR corrects deliberately); the config lifecycle and gateway API pages summarize it and link there.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to what the daemon accepts, publishes or writes, and no new RPC method. The CLI never triggers a reload. Edits outside the four authorization inputs keep their reload-bound semantics. `config migrate`, the alias helpers and the model helpers are unchanged. A standalone `zeroclaw gateway start` (like `zeroclaw agent`) holds the ownership lock without writing a heartbeat, so an authorization edit made while it runs is reported pending (`owner_unconfirmed`); it publishes its own config-API edits and picks up CLI and hand edits at its restart. `config set` still does not run the full `Config::validate()` when no daemon runs (tracked separately). The ownership lock is probed, not held: holding it from `config set` would make a daemon that starts at that moment refuse to run. The identity-checked client stays in the CLI for now; moving it into `zeroclaw_runtime::rpc::local` so `route_agent_mutation` and the shared RPC client crate can use it is #11324. Verifying a Windows named pipe's server process so Windows can publish live is #11325.
- **Blast radius:** the `config set`, `config patch` and `config init` arms in `src/main.rs` and two new modules beside it; in the runtime, `auth_inputs` made public and `is_auth_input_path` added (`rpc/auth.rs`), `refuses_secret_placeholder` extracted from `stage_config_set` with identical behavior and `CONFIG_SET_MANY_MAX_ENTRIES` made `pub const` (`rpc/dispatch.rs`), and `RecordedDaemon` / `recorded_daemon` added beside the heartbeat writer (`daemon/mod.rs`, writer unchanged); English Fluent keys only; three book pages. Built on #10621, which landed first: agent-targeting paths keep its routing through `route_agent_mutation`, and authorization paths, which it does not route, take this PR's. They use separate one-shot clients for now: `call_local` neither verifies which process serves the socket nor separates a refusal at the handshake from a refused request, a rejected edit and an unanswered request, and this issue needs those distinctions (#11324 tracks consolidating them).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10876. Closes #11323 (implements the decision recorded in this PR's review: an identified principal's refused edit fails; the save-and-pending fallback stays for refusals at the handshake). Related #11324, #11325, #11202, #10621, #11186, #10320, #10892.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's roster and permission profiles decide who may do what over the daemon's RPC socket. The daemon recompiles that policy whenever a config write goes through it, which is what zerocode's config editor and the web dashboard do. The command line did not: `zeroclaw config set users.alice.permission_profiles reader` rewrote the file and said "updated" while the daemon, which had never been told, kept alice's old, wider grants until someone reloaded it.

Now the command hands such an edit to the running daemon, which applies and publishes it before the command says it succeeded. If the daemon identifies the user and refuses the edit, the command fails and saves nothing. If the daemon cannot be reached, or cannot identify the user at all (the way out of a lockout), the command still saves the file as before but says plainly that the daemon is still enforcing the previous policy and that the change waits for the next reload or restart. It refuses to save an edit that would leave a working policy unable to load. Edits to anything other than the authorization sections behave exactly as they did.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, one A/B if you want to see it by hand; the same scenarios are automated in `tests/component/config_auth_publication_cli.rs`.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` against a supervised daemon's local socket.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a config with `[security] trust_daemon_uid = false`, `[permission_profiles.admin] admin = true`, `[permission_profiles.reader] grants = { sessions = ["read"], config = ["read"] }`, and `[users.me] uid = <your uid>, permission_profiles = ["admin"]`; `zeroclaw daemon` running from it.
- **Steps to run:** keep a zerocode session (or a raw socket client) connected and confirm `config/set` is permitted; run `zeroclaw config set --no-interactive users.me.permission_profiles reader`; retry `config/set` on the open connection; then run `zeroclaw config set --no-interactive permission_profiles.reader.admin true`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** stderr says the change was applied to the running daemon; the open connection's next `config/set` is refused (`-32012`), a fresh connection binds as the reader, and `config.toml` holds `["reader"]`. The reader's attempt to grant itself admin then fails with a non-zero exit and leaves `config.toml` unchanged.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the CLI prints only "updated"; the open connection keeps admin and a fresh connection still binds as admin until `config/reload` or a restart; the second command saves `admin = true` for the next restart.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` (fmt, clippy, rustdoc warnings, workspace tests including the new `component` and `architecture` cases, docs style and links).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the non-Unix branch (the CLI sends nothing and reports `unverified_endpoint`) is compiled only by the Windows `cargo check` leg, which runs no tests and no `-D warnings`. It uses no platform APIs; it was read, not compiled, here.
- **Commands run and tail output** (macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0, head `7c3b89b495`, which merges master `5a51398dd5`):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                              exit=0
cargo build -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --tests                          exit=0
CLI_ONLY=$(cargo run -p xtask --bin generate -- features --selection cli-only --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)   (CI's CLI-only set, no gateway)
cargo test -p zeroclaw --no-default-features --features "$CLI_ONLY" --test component config_auth_publication -- --test-threads=1
  test result: ok. 23 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw --no-default-features --features "$CLI_ONLY" --bin zeroclaw -- daemon_rpc:: config_publication:: config_set_ config_init_ config_patch
  test result: ok. 54 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw --all-targets --no-default-features --features "$CLI_ONLY" -- -D warnings   exit=0
```

- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** step 2 narrows the caller through the CLI and the already-open connection is refused on its next `config/set`; steps 3 and 4 are that caller, now a reader the daemon identifies, trying to grant itself admin: the command fails, `config.toml` stays byte-identical and the live policy does not move; step 5 is unchanged output once the daemon has stopped.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo fluent check` builds xtask in release with fat LTO; every new key is rendered through the real Fluent path by unit tests instead (`notices_carry_their_evidence`, `commit_failures_name_the_reason_and_the_property_to_check`). `daemon::tests::a_live_config_write_reaches_the_daemon_pricing_refresher_without_a_reload` is skipped in the runtime filter: on master `f151c2e00d` without this change it fails the same way when it runs alongside the other `daemon::` tests, and it passes alone, so it is a pre-existing race between tests that share the process-wide pricing setting. The macOS-only unused import in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs` predates this branch and affects only that crate's test build.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The CLI connects to the daemon's owner-only local socket, which it could already reach as the same account, and presents no credential; the daemon authorizes the connection by peer credential against its accepted policy exactly as it does for zerocode, including `selector_config_write` and the recheck under the write lock.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. A value given to `config set` for `oidc.<alias>.client_secret` (or a secret inside a mixed `config patch`) now travels over the local socket to the daemon when the daemon commits the edit, as zerocode's config editor already sends it. It is written only after the peer uid and peer pid checks pass, never over a Windows named pipe, it is not logged, and the CLI's `--json` envelope keeps the `{path, populated}` shape for secrets.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Tests use the running test uid and synthetic names.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: the risk is a plaintext secret reaching an endpoint that is not this configuration's daemon. The uid check keeps it from another account's process; the pid check keeps it from another daemon of the same account (`config_set_refuses_to_publish_through_another_daemon`); with no running daemon for this configuration nothing is contacted (`config_set_ignores_another_daemon_when_this_configuration_has_none`); Windows never sends. A principal the daemon identifies cannot get around its verdict through the file: `config_set_refused_to_the_bound_principal_saves_nothing` proves a reader's attempt to grant itself admin exits non-zero, leaves `config.toml` byte-identical and leaves the live policy unchanged. Only a refusal at the handshake keeps the file write, which the same OS account could already make by hand; that is the lockout-recovery path (`config_set_refused_at_the_handshake_is_saved_and_pending`, `config_set_repairs_a_deny_all_daemon_through_the_file`), and the CLI says the edit is not in force.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No, in four cases, all only while this configuration's daemon is running. (1) An authorization edit the daemon refuses for a principal it identified, for example a reader granting itself admin, now exits non-zero with nothing saved, where it used to save and exit 0; an edit refused at the handshake (a uid outside the roster, the deny-all state) still saves and exits 0, reported as pending with reason `refused`. (2) An authorization edit that would turn a compiling policy into one that does not (for example `config set users.bob.uid 1002` for a new entry with no `permission_profiles`, or `config init users.bob`) now fails with nothing saved instead of saving a state the next reload would turn into deny-all. (3) A `config patch` with a `test` op, on any path, fails when the daemon would apply it. (4) A `config patch` that touches the authorization sections is applied by the daemon as one batch, so its other paths also take the RPC apply boundary instead of waiting for a reload. With no daemon running, `config set`, `config patch` and `config init` are unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: exit status as above; a stderr notice on authorization edits while a daemon runs (none with `--json`); and an optional `daemon` member in the `--json` envelopes of `config set`, `config patch` and `config init`: `{"applied": true}` or `{"applied": false, "pending_reload": true, "reason": ...}` with the reasons `refused`, `version_mismatch`, `handshake`, `unreachable`, `other_daemon`, `unverified_endpoint`, `owner_unconfirmed`, `not_replayable`, `offline_command` (documented in the authentication guide). Existing members are unchanged.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: none. Scripts that create a roster or OIDC entry field by field with `config set` or `config init` while the daemon runs should send the fields in one `config patch`; scripts that relied on a refused CLI edit still landing at the next restart should make the edit as an account with the config-write grant.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. No schema, wire, config or daemon behavior change to unwind.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** an authorization `config set` that reports `pending_reload` with reason `other_daemon`, `owner_unconfirmed` or `unreachable` while the daemon is healthy; a `config set` that waits up to about 38 s on a stuck daemon before failing with an unknown outcome; `RPC authorization denied` audit lines on the daemon for a CLI caller. `grep 'did not answer an authorization edit'` in the CLI's trace output catches the unknown-outcome case.
