milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(memory): add per-agent attribution and scoping to the knowledge graph
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds mandatory agent ownership to the shared SQLite knowledge graph. `KnowledgeScope` is bound from trusted registration; writes keep caller ownership and directional `read_knowledge_from` grants widen reads only.
  - Makes legacy attribution explicit and fail-closed, with a sole-agent automatic path or configured `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent` for ambiguous multi-agent upgrades.
  - Makes agent delete/rename recovery lifecycle-specific: delete probes exported memory while rename detects even an empty agent identity row; filesystem inspection errors retain residue; workspace/knowledge archives surface failures; cron and ACP rows are purged only after durable export.
  - Makes the fail-toward-residue rule uniform across surfaces. The gateway workspace mover and committed-rename probe no longer collapse a metadata error into absence, and the CLI deletion path archives through the shared helper instead of a hand-rolled copy that swallowed its errors.
  - Makes that fail-toward-residue rule platform-independent. A workspace whose parent is a file surfaces as an error on Unix and as an ordinary "not found" on Windows, so every surface now classifies a path through one shared `inspect_lifecycle_path` helper that re-walks the ancestors of a negative probe. An uninspectable workspace is residue on every supported platform, and the regressions assert that classification instead of the platform's error shape.
  - Gives every deletion archive an exclusively created leaf, so a duplicate delete inside the same clock second cannot adopt another attempt's directory, and writes the archive artifacts with `create_new` so a shared leaf could not replace a durable export even if one were reached.
  - Prevents shared inbound edges from suppressing the caller's own relation and requires a scope-visible anchor for every direct graph-neighbor query after grant revocation.
  - Validates lifecycle aliases before any recovery probe or filesystem path derivation, keeps unreadable RPC rename workspaces retryable, and serializes the global node cap across per-agent SQLite connections.
  - Boxes the RPC map-key delete future, which the master merge showed is needed to keep `process_line` inside the two-megabyte stack budget `master` now pins.
  - Resolves grants from live policy for each graph operation after acquiring the database connection. Purge verifies the archived snapshot in an immediate transaction, using durable edge generation identities to distinguish recreated relations.
  - Refuses to recreate an agent over a retired agent's knowledge on every config creation path. Explicit creation and property writes that would create the agent (`zeroclaw config set` and `config patch`, gateway PUT and PATCH, RPC `config/set` and `config/set-many`) share one admission rule: never the reserved `default` agent, and never an absent alias whose knowledge remains or whose store cannot be inspected without waiting. The refusal is a 400 `validation_failed` on HTTP (explicit creation previously reported it as 404) and a localized message on RPC and the CLI. The `model_routing_config` tool's `upsert_agent`, which inserts agents directly, runs the same retirement check against the store the runtime opens; an agent defined by environment overrides is live and is not probed. The probe re-walks the ancestors of a store reported as missing, so a store under a regular-file parent is refused on Windows as on Unix.
  - Merges current `master` (`5d4b18d335`) and ports the knowledge-ownership paths onto its atomic live-config publication: the live knowledge scope reads a `LiveConfigHandle`, and agent delete and its committed-delete retry admit a `ConfigCommit` and publish only when config changes.
- **Scope boundary:** Knowledge ownership is per agent alias, not per authenticated principal; different principals using the same agent share its knowledge. The unwired Postgres graph is unchanged. Knowledge tool schema/shape is unchanged, but row visibility is intentionally narrowed by `KnowledgeScope`. Gateway and RPC can retry committed rename residue; CLI cannot yet, and #10373 owns that shared recovery follow-up. Lifecycle requests now enforce the canonical alias grammar before touching recovery state. #10149 owns durable recovery for a failed custom workspace archive. Not changed here, and predating this PR: an environment override that names a new agent is applied at config load without the retirement check (documented as an operator caveat), and the `model_routing_config` tool's `remove_agent` removes an agent without the owned-state cascade.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-memory`, tools/runtime registration, config, gateway/RPC/CLI alias lifecycle, SQLite knowledge/session/memory stores, cron and ACP cleanup, workspaces, and documentation.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #9647. Related #9646. Related #10149. Related #10373.

Agent aliases remain the canonical ownership key already used by configuration, workspaces, grants, and lifecycle operations. The storage API requires scope so foreign rows behave as absent even if a caller knows an ID. Disabled configured siblings remain valid explicit read sources; they do not become writers.

### What this does, simply

Agents previously shared the same knowledge graph. This change gives each row an owning agent and limits an agent to its own knowledge unless an operator grants read access to another agent's rows. Deletion archives owned knowledge before removing it, and rename moves its ownership. The latest repair makes revoked sharing take effect for retained tools and stops cleanup from purging rows that differ from its archive. If cleanup fails, creating that agent again through any config surface is refused until a retried delete removes the old knowledge, so a new agent with the same name never inherits it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` and `tui` through the registered `knowledge` tool and alias lifecycle RPC/CLI paths.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Enable knowledge and configure neutral agents `agent_a` and `agent_b`.
- **Steps to run:** Capture a unique node as `agent_b`; search, inspect statistics, traverse, and relate by ID as `agent_a`; then add `read_knowledge_from = ["agent_b"]`, restart, and repeat. Exercise rename/delete once with a temporarily unavailable configured memory/workspace path, restore it, and retry. For the archive path, issue the same `agents delete` twice inside one second and inspect `<data_dir>/agents/_deleted`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Foreign rows are absent before the grant; reads become visible after the directional grant while writes remain caller-owned. Failed lifecycle cleanup retains retryable residue. Creating the alias again, explicitly or through a property write such as `zeroclaw config set agents.<alias>.enabled true`, is refused while its knowledge remains or the store cannot be inspected, and is admitted once a retried delete converges. The duplicate delete lands in its own archive leaf and the first attempt's export is untouched.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Agents shared one unscoped graph, and several committed lifecycle failures could be mistaken for completed cleanup.

### How I tested

- **Current head:** `e248cfe531`. `959cb698a3` merges `master` at `5d4b18d335`, and `e248cfe531` is the alias-recreation fix. Results below are from macOS arm64 at that head unless noted. Hosted CI was still running on this head when this was written.

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
    -> clean
  cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
    -> clean
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-memory -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --features channel-linq -- -D warnings
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --all-targets --features gateway,agent-runtime -- -D warnings
    -> clean
  cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
    -> no warnings
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --test-threads=1
    -> 5951 tests run: 5951 passed, 9 skipped
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features channel-linq
    -> 727 tests run: 727 passed, 7 skipped
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --test component
    -> 263 tests run: 263 passed
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --features gateway,agent-runtime
    -> 526 run: 525 passed; filesystem_adapter_drives_a_run_with_maintenance_disabled
       timed out under full-suite load and passes alone
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-memory
    -> 2531 run: 2530 passed; policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception
       fails identically on master on macOS (open PR #11646)
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-tools -E 'test(/model_routing_config|knowledge/)'
    -> 56 tests run: 56 passed
  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
    -> no prose em-dashes; 0 errors
  ```

- **Not run as scripted here:** this machine's `rg` cannot load `libpcre2`, so `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` and the provider-dispatch step of `rust_quality_gate.sh` abort, and nine `content_search` tool tests fail for the same reason. The comment hygiene checker passed when given the same file set through `git ls-files`, and the fix adds no `ModelProvider` method calls. Hosted CI runs both gates.
- **Regression coverage for the blocker:** a failed knowledge purge followed by recreation is refused at each boundary: config unit (`auto_create_refuses_retained_knowledge_and_uninspectable_store`), gateway PUT, PATCH and explicit create (`property_writes_cannot_recreate_agent_with_retained_knowledge`), RPC `config/set` and `config/set-many` after a real committed delete with a blocked store, then admitted after the retried delete converges (`config_set_cannot_recreate_agent_until_retired_knowledge_converges`), the CLI binary (`config_patch_refuses_to_recreate_agent_with_retained_knowledge`), and the `model_routing_config` tool (`upsert_agent_refuses_alias_with_retained_knowledge`, `upsert_agent_admits_env_defined_agent_that_owns_knowledge`). Busy and uninspectable stores fail closed; the Windows-shaped not-found branch is driven directly (`missing_store_under_a_file_ancestor_is_uninspectable`).
- **Mutation checks:** restoring the old auto-create path (retirement check skipped, reserved check kept) makes the config, gateway, RPC, and CLI regression tests fail; probing the tool's env-free file config or skipping its probe fails the tool test; disabling the env-defined-agent check fails its test.
- **Known gap:** no Windows execution here; the gateway and RPC uninspectable fixtures rely on the new ancestor walk on Windows and are untested there until the advisory Windows job runs.

### Earlier validation (historical)

- **Previously reviewed head:** `be62e0b5160f65f3ddc937c427691395d968eb75`. The required [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36767407780/job/110069381765) passed. That re-review inspected source and regression assertions; it did not run local Cargo.
- **Historical validation below:** Commands, counts, and Windows results below were reported for `4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`; they are not current-head execution claims.

- **Historical head under test:** `4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`, which merges `origin/master` (`46479bdca7`) into the branch and adds the two portability repairs described below.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The required `CI Required Gate` rollup plus the advisory Windows nextest job. This head exists to repair a Windows-only behavior, so the advisory Windows job is the one that actually exercises what changed; the required gate covers everything else.
- Hosted CI on this head (`4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`): `CI Required Gate` SUCCESS, run 34554821248.
- **Advisory Windows disclosure:** On historical head `4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`, [Windows job 103129316312](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34554821248/job/103129316312) ran the repaired unreadable-workspace, path-classifier, duplicate-archive, existing-export protection, and refused-move tests successfully. The job remains failed: its initial batch reported 13,163 tests run, 13,160 passed, 3 failed, and 20 skipped. The remaining failures are the architecture publish-contract test and two runtime PowerShell tests; none is one of the repaired lifecycle regressions. Subsequent scoped batches passed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No Windows execution is available locally, so the Windows result for that historical head comes from the runner; what is proven here is that the shared classifier returns `Uninspectable` for the `Ok(false)` shape Windows reports and that every lifecycle surface routes through it. No live two-agent daemon A/B, and no live multi-process duplicate delete. The duplicate-archive regression drives two cascades of the same alias inside one clock second in-process, which is the interleaving the finding described, but it is not a two-daemon race. CLI committed-rename retry remains #10373.
- **Commands run and tail output (historical head `4291450ec`):**

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all --check
    -> clean (exit 0)

  bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
    -> Comment hygiene gate passed.

  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
    -> No prose em-dashes in changed docs files.
    -> No blocking markdown issues on changed lines.
       (one pre-existing MD038 on an unchanged line of agents/internals.md, reported non-blocking)

The required `CI Required Gate` passed; the single failure was the advisory Windows nextest job described above. Local focused suites at that head passed, which is the asymmetry this head removes: the assertions they made were Unix-only. That head also needed one master-driven repair, kept here as history: `process_line_session_new_creates_session_on_two_megabyte_stack` landed on `master` after the branch's previous head and aborted on the merged tree because the agent-delete branch of `handle_config_map_key_delete` left the owned-state cascade's future inline in the caller; it passed on `origin/master` alone, aborted on the merged head, and passed again after the delete future was boxed.

- **Historical evidence (earlier head `ab20806838a56a5ed9027e34c2517d4ee8af950e`):** the exact-head hosted rollup completed 38/38 successful check runs, including the required aggregate gate, strict lint, tests, Landlock, security, platform checks, MSRV, and the parallel runtime gate. Focused suites at that head were `zeroclaw-memory` knowledge_graph 30 passed, `zeroclaw-tools` knowledge 18 passed, `zeroclaw-config` knowledge 5 passed, `zeroclaw-runtime` `config_map_key_` 10 passed, and the gateway `agent_delete_`/`agent_rename_` suites 7 and 4 passed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I read the exact-head Windows job log rather than inferring the failures from the summary, and confirmed that five of its six failures are this PR's own `try_exists().is_err()` assertions and the sixth is the inherited packaging assertion. I re-audited every filesystem probe on the lifecycle surfaces so that all of them, including the deletion archive and the knowledge-database probe inside the residue predicate, now route through the one classifier. I mounted a separate filesystem locally to reproduce the reviewer's cross-device failure instead of taking it on faith, and confirmed after the fix that the test leaves the install root untouched. Earlier rounds established the master baseline for the stack regression in a separate worktree. I did not run a live daemon interaction, I did not exercise the duplicate delete across two operating-system processes, and I cannot execute Windows here.
- **Visual interface changed?** N/A; no visual presentation changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo deny check` was not re-run locally; it is unchanged by this head and the hosted security job covers it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes**; `read_knowledge_from` is an explicit directional read grant. It defaults empty, validates aliases, and never widens writes.
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**; output shape is unchanged and storage authorization reduces visible rows.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Trusted config is the only grant source; mandatory storage-layer predicates, foreign-as-absent results, and caller-owned writes constrain it.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No** for ambiguous multi-agent legacy knowledge; it remains hidden until assigned. Single-agent upgrades are automatic.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes**; adds `agents.<alias>.workspace.read_knowledge_from` and `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent`; alias lifecycle commands now cascade owned state and reject noncanonical/reserved aliases before recovery I/O. Explicit creation, rename, and property writes that would create an agent refuse retained knowledge or an uninspectable knowledge store, and the explicit HTTP create reports that refusal as 400 `validation_failed` instead of 404.
- Storage schema: Adds durable `edges.generation` identities and an insert trigger for archived-snapshot comparison.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Multi-agent operators with legacy knowledge set `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent = "<enabled-alias>"`, restart, verify ownership, then remove the migration setting. Add read grants only when deliberate.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Disable knowledge, back up its SQLite file, then revert the eventual PR landing commit. An old binary does not enforce ownership and may create unattributed rows, so rollback is containment only. The `edges.generation` column and insert trigger remain in the SQLite database across a binary downgrade.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[knowledge].enabled = false`; remove `read_knowledge_from` entries to revoke sharing.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `still owns knowledge` or `cannot inspect retired knowledge` refusals when recreating an agent (WARN `config.retired_agent_vivify_refused` for property writes), legacy-ownership ambiguity warnings, owned-state cascade warnings, retained cron/ACP rows after archive failure, `workspace inspection failed` warnings on a delete or rename result, or repeated delete/rename results reporting configured-but-unavailable residue.

prs.title: fix(channels): honor Telegram 429 retry_after via shared per-token flood gate
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Telegram Bot API 429 responses were treated like formatting failures: `sendMessage` retried immediately as plain text (a markdown→plain double-hit), draft edits kept their cadence, and the typing loop never noticed — so a rate-limited token got hammered, its penalty escalated, and finalized replies were lost (issue #11615).
  - This adds a flood-control gate (`TelegramRateLimiter`) shared **by the clones of one channel instance** (channel fields, spawned typing loop, approval paths) — it is *not* a registry keyed by bot token: separately constructed channels on the same token, including repeated one-off announcement factories, keep independent windows. Gated surface: the channel's text traffic — `sendMessage` (final answers, draft creation, approval prompts), `editMessageText` (draft updates, finalize), and `sendChatAction` in the recurring typing loop. Initial inbound typing hints, model-picker sends and text/markup edits, approval-resolution text edits, acknowledgement reactions, media uploads, `deleteMessage`, and `answerCallbackQuery` still post directly and are not covered by this gate.
  - Droppable calls (typing, draft edits) skip silently while the window is open. Deliver calls wait the window out bounded by a caller-side budget (`rate_limit_max_wait_secs`), **re-check the shared gate after sleeping**, and stop with a distinguishable budget-exhausted outcome if the window is still active — the budget bounds how long the caller waits, never the server deadline, so nothing is sent into an active window. On a fresh 429 a Deliver call retries once; a second 429 contributes its own (possibly longer) `retry_after` to the shared window and stops the formatting/resume/resend fallbacks — a 429 is not a formatting failure.
  - The recorded deadline keeps the later of the active and new values, so out-of-order concurrent 429 responses cannot shorten the window; an unrepresentable delay is rejected rather than clamped into permission to send sooner.
  - Honors `retry_after` from the JSON envelope (`parameters.retry_after`), with a `retry after <N>` description fallback and a 5s fallback when nothing is parseable.
  - Partial deliveries still suppress the orchestrator's full-answer resend via `FinalizePartialDelivery`, and flood-control exhaustion now stops the chunk-resume path as well instead of burning the wait budget twice. The pending-narration loop in multi-message finalization also stops on the terminal gate outcome: instead of burning three narration retries plus a final-answer wait on fresh budgets, it propagates the gate error, so the outer resend is suppressed without reporting an undelivered final answer as delivered.
  - Two new optional telegram channel config keys: `rate_limit_max_wait_secs` (default 60; `0` restores the default — it is not a disable switch) and `typing_refresh_interval_secs` (default 4, previously hardcoded). Both resolve from the live config authority at each use, including per-tick in the typing loop, so a published change applies to a running channel without a rebuild.
- **Scope boundary:** adaptive draft throttling and any listener-side changes are explicitly out of scope (per maintainer triage on #11615); no behavior change when no 429 occurs — the pre-send gate is a no-op on `Clear`.
- **Blast radius:** Outbound paths of the Telegram channel only (`send_text_chunks`, `send_draft`, `update_draft`, `finalize_draft`, `start_typing`, approval send) plus one guard in the orchestrator's finalize-fallback arm. No change to inbound/listener logic, other channels, or the agent loop. Defaults keep today's behavior for well-behaved tokens.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11615. Related #11608.

### What this does, simply

Telegram tells throttled bots exactly when to come back (`retry_after` in the 429 body), but the channel ignored that and fired again immediately — markdown attempt, then plain attempt, then more draft edits and typing ticks. Each ignored window made the next one longer, and when the final reply finally hit the limit it was dropped: users saw drafts vanish mid-sentence. Now the channel records "blocked until N seconds" per channel instance (shared by its clones) the moment a gated call sees a 429, keeping the longest active deadline. Gated cosmetic traffic (recurring typing indicator, live draft edits) stays silent during the window; user-visible sends wait out the server-directed window up to a bounded caller budget and try again once. When the window clears within budget, the reply is late instead of dropped. When the window outlasts the budget, nothing is sent into it: the answer is held and an error is returned — this slice has no durable delivery queue or automatic later redelivery, so such a reply can go undelivered (WARN-logged) until the sender retries; the gated callers stop retrying inside the recorded window and suppress blind resends of accepted chunks. The direct-call exclusions listed above still apply.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the rate-limit interaction is fully covered by mock-server tests (429-then-success, repeated limiting with escalating deadlines, blocked-window skipping, budget expiry without resend, mid-wait window extension, cancelled waiter, cross-chat window sharing, gated draft creation, live-config resolution, pending-narration finalize stop with zero and nonzero accepted prefixes); a live 429 cannot be induced reliably without flooding a real bot token.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels telegram
env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels finalize
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** channels/config unit and integration tests cover the changed surface (telegram channel + config schema).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` at workspace level shows pre-existing warnings in platform-conditional code outside this diff (unix-gated code on a Windows host, Windows-only service code); none originate from this change, and the channels crate itself is `-D warnings` clean. Two pre-existing `zeroclaw-config` test failures reproduce on unpatched master (`agent_bundle::…outside_shared_is_dropped_with_its_content`, `platform::native::…powershell_full_scripts_execute_with_native_semantics`).
- **Commands run and tail output (head `fe42c5d30`):** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels telegram` → `test result: ok. 429 passed; 0 failed`; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels finalize` → `test result: ok. 23 passed; 0 failed` (including the two new `finalize_stops_on_flood_gate_with_{zero,nonzero}_accepted_narration_prefix` regressions and the retained transient-retry controls).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Author-reported live observation (distinct from CI signals): ran an earlier revision of this change as a production Windows service against live Telegram for 24h — 3 real 429s observed (previously 7+ per incident), zero `failed to reply` events, every post-429 turn delivered after the gate window. This predates the review-round semantics tightening; the current head's budget/no-resend and pending-narration-stop behavior is covered by the mock-server regressions above, not by live observation.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no presentation change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `fe42c5d30` on branch `fix/telegram-429-retry-after`; terminal test output above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib` run from the previous round was not repeated at this head; the changed surface (pending-narration finalization, flood gate) is covered by the `telegram` (429 tests) and `finalize` (23 tests) filters above. `cargo test --test integration telegram_` remains un-run locally (link step needs more free disk than this host currently has); the equivalent behavior is covered by the in-crate wiremock tests.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`Yes`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- Upgrade steps: none required. The two new telegram channel keys are optional with defaults matching prior behavior (`rate_limit_max_wait_secs = 60`, `typing_refresh_interval_secs = 4`). Existing configs load unchanged.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge-sha>` of this PR's merge commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none — `rate_limit_max_wait_secs = 0` restores the default 60s wait budget; it is not a disable/rollback switch. Rollback is reverting the PR.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** grep runtime trace for `failed to reply` or `Telegram sendMessage failed` reappearing, or users reporting vanished drafts/answers again.

prs.title: fix(deps): bump pulldown-cmark to 0.13.5 for RUSTSEC-2026-0414
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - RUSTSEC-2026-0414 was added to the RustSec advisory database on 2026-10-28 and matches `pulldown-cmark` 0.13.4 in `Cargo.lock`.
  - The `Security` job fails on every build, so `CI Required Gate` blocks every merge.
  - This moves `pulldown-cmark` from 0.13.4 to 0.13.5, the patched release, which came out on 2026-10-21.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Only `Cargo.lock` changes, in one package entry: its version and checksum.
  - The manifests don't change, and no other package moves. The entry's dependency list is unchanged.
  - No advisory ignores are added.
- **Blast radius:** `pulldown-cmark` renders Markdown in `zerocode`'s chat view, in the email channel's HTML part and in the orchestrator, and parses the book in `xtask`. With `channel-matrix`, it also reaches the Matrix channel through `ruma-events`. This is a patch release in the same 0.13 line, with the same dependency list and minimum Rust version.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12094. Related #12018 (the dependabot group update that also carries this bump, among 35 others).

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw uses a Markdown library, `pulldown-cmark`, in the terminal chat, the email channel and the docs tooling. A security advisory was published against the version in our lockfile, so the security check now fails on every pull request and nothing can merge. The flaw only affects an optional Markdown feature (wiki-style links), which ZeroClaw never turns on. This moves the library to its fixed release and changes nothing else.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: this is a one-entry lockfile bump. The `Security` job is the check, and the build and test jobs compile and run against the new version.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:**
  - `Security` (cargo-deny) clears the advisory.
  - The Check, Test and Lint jobs build and run the workspace against `pulldown-cmark` 0.13.5.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux, toolchain 1.98.0, cargo-deny 0.19.9 as pinned by the `Security` job; advisory database at 40f5be6fb1, fetched 2026-10-29 05:34 UTC):

```text
$ cargo deny check                                   # master 99bd353c75
error[vulnerability]: Exponential event growth with `ENABLE_WIKILINKS`
    ├ ID: RUSTSEC-2026-0414
advisories FAILED, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok

$ cargo update -p pulldown-cmark --precise 0.13.5
    Updating pulldown-cmark v0.13.4 -> v0.13.5

$ cargo deny check                                   # this branch
advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok

$ cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1 >/dev/null     # exit 0
$ cargo verify-project && cargo fetch --locked              # exit 0
$ python3 scripts/ci/lru_advisory_scope_test.py             # exit 0

$ cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-channels -p zerocode -p xtask
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 18s

$ RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 54s
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - The new checksum matches the crates.io index entry for `pulldown-cmark` 0.13.5 (`278e9268…36eb`). The release's dependencies and minimum Rust version (1.71.1) are the same as 0.13.4's.
  - No ZeroClaw code sets `ENABLE_WIKILINKS` or uses `Options::all()`:
    - `zerocode` enables tables, strikethrough and task lists;
    - the email channel enables tables and strikethrough;
    - the orchestrator uses no options;
    - `xtask` uses the defaults.
  - `ruma-events` 0.35.0 enables tables and strikethrough only.
  - So the vulnerable path isn't reachable on `master` either. The bump clears the advisory.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** this branch's head; the commands above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I didn't run a full local `cargo test`. This is a patch release with an unchanged dependency list, and the CI build and test jobs cover it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. This removes an advisory match.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert <merge sha>`. This brings the advisory match back, so `Security` fails again.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. This PR is stacked on #11225 (delegated memory principal scope), which introduces the retained `Agent.delegate_tool` handle and the delegate `principal_scope` cell this change builds on. Until #11225 merges, the branch shows both commits; please review the top commit only (`fix(runtime): withhold session-data tools from non-admin principals`).
- **What changed and why:**
  - `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, and `sessions_send` list, read, and append to other sessions with no principal-ownership check. A non-admin principal that held them (wildcard tool and agent selectors included) could read or append to another principal's transcript on the same agent. Applying a non-admin principal's grants (`apply_principal_grants_to_agent`, which runs at session creation, at rehydration, and before every prompt) now withholds them. `sessions_current` stays: it takes no target and reports only the caller's own session.
  - The tool names live in one place, `zeroclaw_tools::PRINCIPAL_UNAWARE_SESSION_TOOL_NAMES`, with a sync test against the constructed tools. Skill aliases of those tools (a `builtin` or `mcp` skill tool whose `target` is one of them) are withheld with them, because a name-only denylist is bypassed by a renamed wrapper.
  - Nested executors that cannot carry the withholding go too: `spawn_subagent` rebuilds a full registry from config, and `execute_pipeline` runs the tool set captured at construction, which includes the session tools. Both are already marked `requires_unrestricted_principal`; that existing marker is what selects them, so their skill aliases follow as well.
  - The delegate is kept for wildcard principals, but the Agent marks it through the retained handle. The mark is an `Arc<AtomicBool>` shared with background, parallel, and nested bounded delegates exactly like `principal_scope`, and every child registry the delegate builds filters on it: the bounded base (the parent's build list, which still holds what the parent's registry withheld) and the independent target's own registry. An Agent whose registry holds a delegate it has no handle for drops the delegate instead.
  - Source of truth: the principal's resolved grants, re-evaluated by `apply_principal_grants_to_agent` on every prompt. The registry removal and the delegate flag are narrowing-only effects of that evaluation, like the existing selector narrowing; nothing snapshots policy, and nothing is ever restored to a live session. The system prompt is rebuilt only when the withholding actually removed a tool, so later prompts do not rebuild it.
- **Scope boundary:** This is containment: it withholds principal-unaware tools from the sessions of non-admin principals. It does not make the session tools principal-aware (principal-scoped read views and predicates for list, history, and the chat append path); that repair belongs under the session-ownership contract in the #8290 tracker. The agent-ownership scoping in #9746 is related but does not provide principal isolation. This PR does not touch `sessions.rs` or the runtime's session-tool registration. `sessions_reset` and `sessions_delete` are not registered by the runtime; the name list's doc comment now says each must join it if it ever is. Administrators and the unauthenticated shared operator keep every tool.
- **Not covered, and now documented:** runs that execute later under the agent's own identity, with the agent's configured tools, can still call the session-data tools. These are agent jobs created with `cron_add`, or given a new prompt with `cron_update` and started with `cron_run` (the same through RPC cron grants), whose output comes back through `cron_runs`; SOP runs; and the turns `send_message_to_peer` starts in another agent. None of them carries a principal today. The authentication docs now say so and give the interim mitigation: list `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, and `sessions_send`, plus any skill tool that targets them, in `excluded_tools` of the risk profile of each agent those runs use. That removes the tools from every run of the agent, administrators' sessions included. Carrying a principal into scheduled, SOP, and peer runs is follow-up work under #8290. `schedule` creates shell jobs only; shell execution as the daemon account is the existing, separately documented limitation.
- **Blast radius:** RPC sessions of authenticated principals without `admin`, including wildcard ones, lose `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, `sessions_send`, `spawn_subagent`, and `execute_pipeline`, plus skill aliases of any of them and of `delegate` (wildcard principals keep the `delegate` tool itself). Their delegation children lose the same tools. Principals with a constrained selector already lost the nested executors and their aliases. Channel and CLI sessions do not go through this RPC posture and are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11127. Depends on #11225.
- **Labels:** `agent`, `channel`, `channel:core`, `docs`, `domain:security`, `memory`, `needs-author-action`, `risk:high`, `runtime`, `size:XL`, `tool`, `tool:delegate`.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw lets several people (principals) use the same agent over RPC, each with their own sessions. A few agent tools can look at other sessions: list them, read their history, or post a message into them. Those tools only check which agent a session belongs to, not which person, so one user's agent could read or write another user's conversation on the same agent. Until the tools learn to check the person, this change simply takes them away from every signed-in user who is not an administrator, even users whose permissions say "all tools". It also takes away two helpers that could hand the tools straight back (starting a sub-agent and running a tool pipeline), and it makes delegated helper agents drop the tools too. The tool that reports "which session am I in" stays, and administrators and single-operator installs see no change. When a user is demoted from administrator, their open session loses the tools at its next prompt. This is not complete isolation yet: work that runs later under the agent's own identity, such as a scheduled agent job, a standard operating procedure, or a message to another agent, can still use these tools. The documentation now says so and shows operators how to switch the tools off for those agents until the tools learn to check the person.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the boundary is the RPC dispatcher's session construction and prompt posture, which the new dispatcher tests drive end to end with two roster principals; a manual check needs a second OS user for peer-credential auth or an OIDC provider.

### How I tested

Run on macOS with rustc 1.98.0. New tests:

- `rpc::dispatch::tests::scoped_principals_cannot_reach_session_data_tools_even_with_wildcard_selectors`: two roster principals with `allowed_tools = ["*"]`, `allowed_agents = ["*"]`, and `tools:execute`. Alice's ACP and chat sessions, and her ACP session after rehydration, hold none of the three tools (`execute_tool_for_test` is `None`; production dispatch of `sessions_send` and `sessions_history` against Bob's chat key returns `Unknown tool`), keep `sessions_current` and `delegate`, lose `spawn_subagent`, and their delegate is marked. Bob's transcript is byte-identical afterwards. The shared operator's session keeps all four session tools and `spawn_subagent`, and its delegate is not marked.
- `rpc::dispatch::tests::demoted_principal_loses_session_data_tools_at_its_next_prompt`: an admin principal's session holds the tools; after the profile drops `admin`, the post-admission path (`current_prompt_authority` then `apply_principal_grants_to_agent` with the fresh grants) removes them and `spawn_subagent`, keeps `sessions_current`, `calculator`, and `delegate`, and marks the delegate.
- `tools::delegate::tests::withheld_session_tools_do_not_reach_delegate_children`: a control delegation offers the child `sessions_history` and a nested `spawn_subagent` probe from the parent build list; after `withhold_session_data_tools()`, the sync, parallel, and background children are offered none of the three tools nor `spawn_subagent`, and still get `sessions_current` (checked on the captured provider requests).
- `tools::delegate::tests::withheld_session_tools_do_not_reach_independent_targets`: an independent target's own registry holds the three tools, `spawn_subagent`, and a skill alias (`peek__history`, a `builtin` skill tool targeting `sessions_history`) as a control; after withholding it holds none of them and keeps `sessions_current` and `shell`.
- `tools::delegate::tests::withheld_session_tools_do_not_reach_an_independent_grandchild`: caller, then bounded `middle`, then independent `leaf`. As a control, the leaf's captured request offers `sessions_history` and `spawn_subagent`; after the caller withholds, the leaf is offered none of the three tools nor `spawn_subagent`, and keeps `sessions_current`. This pins the flag the bounded child's target-bound delegate shares.
- `agent::agent::tests::withholding_session_data_tools_removes_aliases_and_nested_executors`: as a control, the raw tool, a skill alias, and an `execute_pipeline` step each reach a `sessions_history` probe; after withholding, all three are unknown tools, the probe is not called again, `sessions_current` and the handle-bound delegate remain, and a delegate without a handle is dropped.
- `session_tool_names_guard::principal_unaware_session_tool_names_match_tools` (zeroclaw-tools): the const matches the constructed tools and excludes `sessions_current`.

Each new runtime test was also checked against a deliberately broken build: removing the dispatcher call, giving the parallel, background, or bounded target-bound delegate a fresh flag, removing the independent filter, dropping alias names, or dropping the nested-executor clause each makes the corresponding tests fail.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(cron): wait for a competing writer when switching a new store to WAL
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The cron store's switch to WAL now waits out lock contention within the same 5 s window that `busy_timeout` gives every other phase. While a new database file is still in rollback-journal mode, SQLite fails `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` at once if another connection holds a lock, without consulting the busy handler. Two connections opening a fresh cron database together therefore refused one of them within about 0.2 ms.
  - The 5 s value is now one constant, shared by the pragma and the retry deadline.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - An existing store is unaffected: once the file is in WAL mode, the switch is a no-op and never contends.
  - Contention that outlasts the window is still refused with the same retryable message.
  - Other stores that set WAL are not changed. Cron is the store that opens a new connection per operation from several threads, which is what makes the race reachable. I didn't audit the others.
- **Blast radius:** the opening of every cron store connection, in `apply_schema_and_migrations`. The retry only runs when SQLite reports lock contention on the WAL switch.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11904. Related #11441 (its reminder test hit this in a fresh temp workspace).

### What this does, simply

The cron store opens its database for every operation and first makes sure it is in WAL mode, which lets readers and a writer work side by side. Every other setup step waits up to five seconds when another connection is busy. The WAL step didn't: on a brand-new database file, if a second connection was setting up at the same moment, one of them was refused straight away. In practice this could hit the very first cron job someone adds, if it raced a scheduler poll. Now that step waits like the others. Nothing changes once the database exists.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The two new tests reproduce the race directly: one deterministic, one under load.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on `zeroclaw-runtime` runs the cron store tests, including the two new ones.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-runtime -- --check                                        ok
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- opening_a_fresh_database_waits_for_a_competing_writer two_connections_opening_a_fresh_database_both_succeed
  test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- cron::
  test result: ok. 229 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings                ok
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Finding the phase: a probe on master ran two threads calling `add_job` on a fresh database for 150 rounds. 30 to 38 rounds were refused, all on the pragma step. With the pragmas split, every refusal was on `journal_mode = WAL`. The same probe against an existing database, two pollers against 300 `add_job` calls, gave 0 errors.
  - `opening_a_fresh_database_waits_for_a_competing_writer`: a second connection holds the write lock on a new, rollback-mode file for 300 ms. `add_job` now waits and succeeds after it is released.
  - `two_connections_opening_a_fresh_database_both_succeed`: 40 rounds of two threads opening a fresh database together, all succeeding.
  - Negative check: with the old pragma batch restored, both tests fail with the refusal above. The deterministic test is refused at once instead of waiting, and the stress test fails in its first round.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full workspace test run was skipped because the change is confined to the cron store.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`.

- **Observable failure symptoms:** "Failed to set cron DB journal mode" in a refused cron operation would mean contention outlasted the 5 s window during the WAL switch.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose bounded plugin webhook RPC placement exception
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Adds one row to the active-exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, proposing a bounded holding-crate exception for the three plugin webhook RPC methods (`plugin-webhook/dispatch`, `plugin-webhook/cancel`, `plugin-webhook/routes`) that carry channel-plugin webhook dispatch across the core IPC boundary for #11003. ADR-016 requires the row to exist, approved by the Core Team, before the feature it covers merges.
- **Scope boundary:** Documentation only. The permission covers `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`, `src/rpc/context.rs`, the denial reasons for these methods in `src/rpc/auth.rs`, the ingress setter and taker in `src/daemon/{registry.rs,mod.rs}`, and their denial message keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl`. Route ownership, admission, deadlines and dedup live in `zeroclaw-infra`, outside the holding crate.
- **Channel authority (updated after the #11320 review):** the row names the one new authority these methods add, as the maintainer decision on #11320 requires. `channels:execute` lets a local caller deliver a webhook request to a plugin channel's route and cancel its own deliveries, and `channels:read` lists the routes with their owners. Each grant covers only the channel instances its permission profile names. Config can make a channel instance refuse injected webhooks, and an agent refuse turns that arrive through them, checked at dispatch whatever the caller's grants. The grant scoping and the config fields live in `zeroclaw-api` and `zeroclaw-config`, outside the holding crate. No new runtime module, routing, parsing or authentication.
- **Blast radius:** Contributor placement guidance only. No runtime behavior changes. The row is not active until a Core Team member other than the author approves this PR.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003. Related #7432. Related #11000.
- **Labels:** `docs`, `release-gate`, `risk:high`, `risk:manual`, `size:XS`, `topic:plugins`, `type:docs`

### What this does, simply

The runtime crate is a holding area: new functionality needs a recorded Core Team exception first. The follow-up PRs for #11003 add three RPC methods to the daemon's dispatcher so a gateway in another process can hand webhook requests to the core. The dispatcher still lives in the runtime crate until the planned kernel IPC extraction, so this row asks for permission for exactly that, and nothing more.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: a one-row documentation change with no executable behavior.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Docs Style` (the docs gate only scans `docs/book/src`, so it does not lint this file; the row adds no em-dashes).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `git diff master -- crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` shows one added table row.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The row names all four fields ADR-016 requires (scope, destination, approving authority, review condition) and follows the bounded SOP RPC exception format proposed in #11111.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** N/A

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Not in this PR, which is documentation only. The row it proposes approves the scoped channel authority above for #11320.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

prs.title: feat(session): extract the atomic session-ownership claim into a shared SessionBackend contract
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; the branch includes `master` through `05f9fe95d4` (#11232).
- **What changed and why:** Adds one shared atomic agent-ownership claim/adoption contract to `SessionBackend`, implemented by SQLite and consumed by RPC Chat admission, persistent WebSocket admission, and the operator migration command. A conflicting owner or ownerless transcript is refused before restoration/publication.
- Backends that cannot claim durable agent ownership are refused for empty and nonempty RPC Chat sessions, including operator/admin callers. This restores the uniform refusal requested in review and removes the stale-admin exception related to #11126. Persistent WebSocket admission uses the same fail-closed rule.
- WebSocket identity is fixed from the query or a generated UUID before the first client frame. The server sends its greeting without waiting for a client frame; a later `connect.session_id` may only echo that identity. Transcript read failures preserve master's `SESSION_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE` refusal and cannot become an empty restored session.
- The WebSocket also pins the agent incarnation it claimed under. The greeting still goes out immediately and the socket still holds no deletion lease while it waits for its first client frame; instead the handshake records the alias generation and refuses the connection with `AGENT_REPLACED` if a committed delete or rename advanced that alias before the first frame arrives. Without that fence, an operator could delete and recreate the alias while a socket waited, and the socket would restore the previous incarnation's transcript into the replacement agent under the replacement's provider and tools.
- Noncanonical display ids (anything outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, for example an id containing a dot) are refused before the session is reached, so a punctuation-distinct id can never collapse onto another session's key. This applies to resuming an existing session too; see the Compatibility section for what that means for pre-existing sessions. `session/new` refuses a supplied id at the top of the method, before the ownership probe reads the store, and the check also sits in the shared turn body, so `session/prompt` and `session/run-once` refuse their caller-supplied ids before any write.
- Adds `zeroclaw migrate session-ownership` to list or explicitly adopt legacy ownerless sessions, with localized CLI text and persisted-state/component regressions.
- Documents the durable state owner and the RPC Chat/WebSocket admission boundaries in the runtime state map and authentication chapter, including the remaining migration deletion race.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not resolve every stale-grant path in #11126 or implement the separate HTTP adapter in #8486. Existing principal authentication, current-master session admission/queueing, and transport boundaries remain the owners of their respective policy.
- **Blast radius:** The `SessionBackend` contract and its SQLite implementation, the gateway WebSocket admission gate (including its new agent-incarnation fence), RPC Chat admission (gated to `ChatMode::Chat`; ACP does not pass through it), the canonical session-key helpers, and the operator migration CLI. Backends without atomic claim support (JSONL and custom) refuse RPC Chat and WebSocket admission rather than degrading to a read-then-write.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9600 (ownership slice of the L2 `SessionBackend` contract), #10526, #8486, #8603, #8550, #11126. The remaining acceptance for #11126 is outside this PR.

### What this does, simply

Sessions are keyed by a caller-supplied id. Before this PR, that same key could be handed to a different agent, which would then restore someone else's transcript. This PR gives the session backend one atomic operation that means "claim this session for this agent, or refuse." RPC Chat, the WebSocket gateway, and the operator migration command all use it, so an admission either wins the claim or is refused before any transcript is read or shown to a client. A session that nobody owns yet can be handed over only by the explicit `zeroclaw migrate session-ownership` command, never by ordinary traffic.

The companion change is the WebSocket handshake. A connection now settles its identity immediately (from the query string, or a server-generated UUID) and receives its greeting before it sends anything. A later `connect` frame can echo that identity but cannot switch the session. Ids have to be simple (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`); an id that is not is refused outright, because two ids that differ only in punctuation must never share one memory scope.

Because identity is settled at the greeting while the transcript is used later, the handshake also records which incarnation of the agent it claimed under. Deleting or renaming an agent closes its incarnation and opens a new one; if that happens while a connection is still waiting for its first frame, the connection is refused instead of handing the old transcript to the new agent.

### Issue and solution

A caller-controlled session identifier must not overwrite another agent's ownership and then restore its transcript. The backend now performs a conditional ownership claim and returns explicit claimed/conflict/migration outcomes. Normal admission refuses unsupported ownership rather than assuming that an administrator can safely bypass an absent durable owner. Trusted migration has a separate atomic adoption operation.

The WebSocket path has an ordering gap that RPC does not: it claims and loads before the client speaks, but can only take lifecycle admission after the client's first frame. Recording the alias generation at claim time and comparing it after that frame closes the gap without making the greeting wait, and without holding a deletion lease for as long as a client may idle.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — real WebSocket greeting/error and RPC admission regressions exercise the repaired boundaries; CLI subprocess tests cover migration behavior in required CI.

### How I tested

- **Current revision:** `931d4fd1a737f11800a7587b05ab67e8c8c3eef7`. This merges `master` (`05f9fe95d4`) and adds three commits on top: the agent-generation fence and its regression test; the canonical-id check moving into the shared turn body, followed by a review follow-up commit (the SQLite adoption transaction closed on every path, the `session/new` id check moved ahead of the ownership probe, an unused `SessionStore` method dropped, and the WebSocket ownership gate narrowed to the already-resolved session id); and documentation.
- **Code-tested revision:** the same `931d4fd1a737f11800a7587b05ab67e8c8c3eef7` — production code and tests are identical at the current revision.
- **Current documentation checks:** `bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` (0 errors) and `git diff --check` passed. `docs_links_gate.sh` needs `rg`, which is not installed in this environment, so it was not run for this revision; the documentation changes are prose inside existing files and add no links.
- **Commands run and tail output:** At the current revision, all with `umask 0022`:
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings` — exits 0.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime` — 5625 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets` — 657 passed in the lib target, plus 5 and 9 in the auxiliary targets; 0 failed.
  - `cargo test --test architecture` — 54 passed, 1 failed (see the gap below).
  - `cargo test --test component` — 272 passed, 1 failed (see the gap below).
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra --lib` — 327 passed. `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config` — 1771 passed.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required CI passed at `931d4fd1a737f11800a7587b05ab67e8c8c3eef7`, including the workspace tests and lint covering the changed runtime/gateway/backend/component paths. `CI Required Gate` succeeded.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live deployment migration or independent external WebSocket-client interoperability run was performed during this repair. Two local test targets cannot be fully green here for host reasons, in both cases a missing host binary rather than a code failure: `release_workflow::scoop_publisher_metadata_follows_canonical_url_template` invokes `scripts/release/scoop_metadata.sh`, which needs `jq`; `component::daemon_startup_feedback::daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions` needs `expect` for its PTY fixture. Both targets pass in CI. The prior review's compatibility acceptance and focused regression coverage remain recorded in the review history.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Independent review checked uniform unsupported-owner refusal, claim-before-transcript restoration/publication, immutable WebSocket identity, SQLite guarded claim/adoption operations, and preservation of current-master failure propagation. Three focused regressions pin the boundaries, plus one merge-integration check:
  - The WebSocket test forces `try_load` to fail and asserts the first server frame is `SESSION_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE`, panicking if the lossy `load` fallback is used.
  - A second seeds a stored session under a noncanonical (dotted) key, connects with that id, asserts the first frame is an `INVALID_SESSION_ID` error with no `session_start`, and then asserts the seeded transcript is still present and still ownerless.
  - A third is the production-boundary regression for the blocking review item: it seeds the transcript, adopts it to the alias, completes the handshake, then commits a delete of that alias and clears its stored attribution before sending the first frame. It asserts the response is an error with code `AGENT_REPLACED`, that the stored transcript is untouched (still one message, same content), and that no attribution was adopted.
  - Merge integration was checked separately: the architecture gate that scans RPC methods acting on a caller-supplied `session_id` (`tests/architecture/auth_boundary.rs`) failed on the first merge result because `master` had moved `authorize_session_owner` into the extracted shared turn body while this branch's canonical-id check stayed in the wrapper. Moving that check into the shared body, ahead of the authorization, restores the wrapper to `master`'s shape and the gate to green.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text CLI evidence remains in existing component tests; this repair changes RPC/WS refusal behavior without layout changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Revision above; RPC dispatch and real loopback WebSocket regressions, plus existing migration CLI component tests.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The WebSocket error codes are `SESSION_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE`, `INVALID_SESSION_ID`, and `AGENT_REPLACED`; unsupported RPC ownership returns `INTERNAL_ERROR` and no live session.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Empty/nonempty unsupported-owner sessions are refused for operators and scoped callers. Failed history reads do not emit a successful greeting or install empty history. Noncanonical ids are refused before any transcript is read. A socket whose agent is deleted or renamed before its first frame is refused without executing or adopting the ownerless history.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full local workspace tests are left to required CI; targeted checks cover the repaired boundaries. `docs_links_gate.sh` was skipped locally because `rg` is unavailable.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes — an operator migration command can attach an agent owner to legacy session records after confirmation. Backend adoption refuses conflicting ownership; normal RPC/WS admission cannot adopt nonempty ownerless history.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No — synthetic fixtures only.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- **Known nonblocking follow-up:** The migration CLI still tries ordinary claim before adoption. Concurrent deletion after preflight can therefore leave an empty ownership row. Audacity's prior review accepted this as a follow-up (#11229); it does not restore deleted transcript contents or overwrite a different owner. Use existing-session adoption directly in a separate repair, and avoid concurrent deletion during migration meanwhile.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No. RPC Chat and persistent WebSocket sessions require a backend with durable agent-ownership claims, even for administrators. SQLite implements the contract; JSONL/custom backends without it refuse admission.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes — additive `zeroclaw migrate session-ownership` command. No existing key or environment variable changes.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- **Upgrade steps:** On SQLite, adopt required legacy ownerless histories with `zeroclaw migrate session-ownership --claim <key> --agent-alias <alias>`; `--list` shows candidates. On JSONL, switch to SQLite first; the factory imports legacy history, then explicitly adopt ownerless sessions. Unsupported backends permit listing but refuse ownership writes. WebSocket clients must supply their chosen session ID in the query; `connect.session_id` may only echo the server's identity. The bundled web client already uses the query path. Display ids must also be canonical (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`) to be resumed. A WebSocket session whose stored display id is not canonical, for example one containing a dot, can therefore no longer be resumed: connecting with that id is refused with `INVALID_SESSION_ID` before the session is reached. Nothing re-keys stored sessions, so that transcript is left on disk unchanged and stops being reachable through admission; recovering it means reading the stored history directly rather than re-keying it. Finally, a WebSocket connection that is still waiting for its first client frame when its agent alias is deleted or renamed is refused with `AGENT_REPLACED`; the client should reconnect, which claims the session under the current incarnation.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the merged squash commit as one unit, after assessing the ownership protections that would be removed. Existing owner metadata does not require destructive cleanup.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Switching to an unsupported backend is not an authorization bypass or a supported opt-out.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unsupported backends return `BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_OWNERSHIP` over WS or `INTERNAL_ERROR` over RPC; ownerless history requires migration; divergent or noncanonical WebSocket ids return `INVALID_SESSION_ID`; unreadable histories return `SESSION_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE`; a socket whose agent alias changed before its first frame returns `AGENT_REPLACED`.

prs.title: feat(providers): honor runtime-profile thinking for OpenAI
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Carry the existing opted-in runtime-profile thinking level with each request, independently of native token budgets, so two profiles sharing an OpenAI alias can select different reasoning efforts.
  - Resolve the neutral level against the actual selected OpenAI model, API, tool mode and public/subscription capability set, including fallback attempts and lazy streams.
  - Preserve the selected level across existing runtime adapters and disable response-cache reuse for explicit native-thinking overrides; document precedence, capability fallbacks and Rust source migration.
- **Scope boundary:** OpenAI Responses, native Chat Completions and the existing Codex subscription path. No new configuration key, global `runtime.reasoning_effort` values, authentication path, compatibility retry, provider family or runtime subsystem. Other providers keep their existing native budgets and wire behavior. Approval and dispatch authority, receipt/observer-event formats, history handling and cancellation semantics are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust request construction, runtime CLI/channel/Agent/RPC/delegate request propagation, routing and recovery, streaming/tool rounds, and response-cache eligibility. This requires cross-owner review and the separate runtime exception before merge.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12054. Depends on #12057. Related #10705 concerns accepting literal global `max`, which this PR does not implement.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12054
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12057
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10705

### What this does, simply

A profile could change thinking prompts or temperature while OpenAI's native reasoning effort still came from global provider options. The native Chat Completions path also lacked profile-derived effort. With `native_thinking = true`, a turn now carries the selected level to the actual OpenAI model making that request. Inline override takes precedence over session override, then the profile default; direct Agent/RPC sessions use their profile default.

`off` becomes `none` when supported, otherwise the lowest supported effort. `minimal`, `low`, `medium` and `high` use the matching effort, or the next higher supported effort capped at the maximum. `max` selects the model's highest supported effort. Public API and subscription capabilities stay separate. Unknown models or unverified API/tool combinations retain existing global/default behavior and emit an explanatory diagnostic.

The level survives tool rounds, max-iteration summaries, request rebuilding, recovery, fallback model changes and deferred streams. Independent delegates use their own profiles; bounded delegates inherit their caller's level. Legacy auxiliary one-shot requests keep their existing behavior. Explicit raw-body overrides retain their precedence.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: automated mock HTTP regressions exercise the real CLI/channel/Agent/delegate paths and assert outgoing efforts; judging model answers manually would not verify the wire setting. The real CLI regression is reproducible with `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::loop_::tests::native_thinking_cli_profiles_override_global_effort_on_the_shared_endpoint -- --exact`.

### How I tested

Current branch integration: `ae3e8dbe812d3c58cc753c487ad8de5c75f10438` merges `master` at `3158c45d1d7b076abd9cfce682e4e9b4a9768d4d`. The conflict resolution retains the upstream per-turn repetition guard, including steering/model-switch reentry, and the explicit `Send` future contracts on all three turn-loop wrappers. The feature still uses the existing guard in both Agent APIs. The separate bounded exception has [Core approval recorded in its discussion](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12057#issuecomment-6502718792); PR #12057 still needs that approval recorded in its table before it lands. Required owning reviews for the new implementation head remain merge gates.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12057

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** On `ae3e8dbe812d3c58cc753c487ad8de5c75f10438`, [Quality Gate run 40970195978](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40970195978) succeeded, including `CI Required Gate`, full workspace `Test`, `Parallel Runtime Test`, lint/Rustdoc, Linux and Windows checks, MSRV, docs, and the new CLI-only build/tests/artifact ratchet. All checks were terminal at the post-push snapshot: 52 successful and five expected non-blocking skips. The skips cover master-push debounce, non-PR benchmark compilation, unchanged-version crates preflight, and the label-gated advisory Windows lane; required Windows checks ran successfully. Conditional skips do not supply executed coverage.

Fresh local validation on this integrated candidate:

The three full-config failures reproduce on exact `master` at `3158c45d1d7b076abd9cfce682e4e9b4a9768d4d` (1815 passed, three failed): an inaccessible host PATH entry changes error wording, the macOS case-insensitive filesystem collides on `nul`/`NUL`, and an outer configuration-directory override defeats a test's default-path premise. The earlier revision-bound validation below remains historical evidence, with its original limitations.

- **Earlier CI evidence (historical):** On `45e47dcded9400d035d612ee9c4eab6855b03491`, [Quality Gate run 40482915746](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40482915746) completed successfully, including `CI Required Gate`, `Test`, `Parallel Runtime Test`, lint, build, platform/MSRV and docs checks. Local validation covers all five owning crates, real turn/delegate/channel mock HTTP boundaries, schema persistence and export, strict workspace Clippy, Rustdoc, documentation and both comment gates.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local host is macOS. CI pins Rust 1.98.0; strict local validation used installed 1.98.1, while local tests and nextest ran on Rust 1.99.0. - Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No: existing thinking-prompt selection is preserved.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Explicit overrides can increase model calls, latency and token cost. The existing `native_thinking` opt-in and rollback path control this behavior. - Backward compatible? No for downstream Rust source constructing or exhaustively destructuring affected public structs. Existing TOML values, schema enum values, provider defaults and serialized configuration remain compatible.

- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
