Callers of `default_budget_tokens()` through that path must import `zeroclaw_config::scattered_types::ThinkingLevelBudget`. Public runtime `ThinkingParams` literals need `native_level`; use the existing resolution helper where applicable. Recreate/reconnect Agent/RPC sessions after changing their profile defaults.

A successfully mapped non-`none` public OpenAI reasoning request omits optional `temperature`, as the verified models require. Existing runtime prompt/temperature policy, unmapped/global requests and other providers retain their behavior. Effort changes may affect latency and token usage; subscription model access still depends on the account's existing entitlements. Public API capabilities were checked against [official OpenAI model pages](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models) on 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27; subscription sets come from list-visible entries in the [Codex catalog at commit `126a0ee92ed2c5e73cd8a8f7e37563e8527552d7`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/126a0ee92ed2c5e73cd8a8f7e37563e8527552d7/codex-rs/models-manager/models.json). Client delegation modes such as `ultra` are excluded and never sent as wire efforts.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Set `native_thinking = false` on affected runtime profiles and apply it through the existing runtime reload or restart lifecycle, including recreating/reconnecting Agent/RPC sessions, to return OpenAI requests to the existing global/default effort path. For a full rollback, revert this PR's merge/squash commit; if merged as separate commits, revert the complete feature commit range, including its API, config, provider and runtime changes together.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Existing `native_thinking` only. Disabling it on a mixed-provider profile also disables its existing native token budgets; revert the complete feature when those budgets must stay enabled.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Upstream request rejection, unexpected latency/token use, an unmapped-level diagnostic, or an effort substitution inconsistent with the serving model. Inspect `requested_level`, `effective_effort`, provider/model and mapping outcome diagnostics without logging request bodies or credentials.

prs.title: feat(gateway): opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds opt-in dashboard sign-in through a configured `[oidc.<alias>]` provider. Until now the dashboard could only be unlocked with a pairing code, so every paired browser was the shared operator, even though the CLI, zerocode and RPC already sign in with OIDC.
  - **New `[gateway.dashboard_sign_in]` table**, empty by default. With it absent nothing changes: no new screen, no cookie is read, and every existing route behaves as before. Turning it on requires `gateway.require_pairing = true`. The config error names the fix, including for the Docker image's default config.
  - **The browser flow reuses the existing relay:** Authorization Code + PKCE on the existing flow store, limits and `/oidc/callback` redirect URI.
    - The flow is bound to the browser that started it by a per-flow cookie.
    - The ID token is required as evidence of the sign-in (a new `Enrollment::pkce_exchange_requiring_id_token`), then discarded.
    - The access token is verified by the configured provider exactly as RPC verifies a bearer. Service principals and identities with no mapped profile are refused.
    - The token only ever goes to the provider it was issued by. The callback takes the provider's issuer and client and its code-exchange client from one reading of the configuration. Sign-in and every later re-verification then check that issuer and client against the same accepted policy that would send the token (a new `RpcInboundAuth::authenticate_bound` in the runtime). A provider repointed meanwhile gets nothing.
  - **The gateway keeps the token in memory** behind an opaque `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` session cookie (`__Host-` and `Secure` over HTTPS at the root). Every request carrying the cookie is checked again against the same inbound authority RPC uses: expiry, the introspection deadline, and grants at the current policy generation.
  - **CSRF:** requests that change state need the session's `X-ZeroClaw-CSRF` token, and cookie-carrying requests and WebSocket upgrades must come from the dashboard's own origin. An `Authorization` header always wins over the cookie.
  - **What a signed-in account reaches:**
    - administrators (a profile with `admin = true`) reach every page, as a paired browser does;
    - other accounts reach the config pages their grants allow, and get 403 `operator_required` elsewhere.
  - **Re-verification across a policy change:** a re-verification that a policy publish lands in the middle of is tried once more with the same token and the same provider, as the grants check already is. A compatible change then keeps the session.
  - **Expiry, sign-out and sockets:** an expiring session shows a re-auth prompt in a popup that keeps the page. Sign-out is local and spans tabs. The chat socket, event stream, canvas and SOP-run feeds close at once when their session ends or loses access. That includes a running chat turn, which finishes unattended with any pending tool approval refused. They also close when the gateway reloads, so the new configuration decides on reconnect. A check that has to verify the session again with the identity provider cannot admit anything after the session's hard expiry or the reload; a request that reaches the gateway being replaced, over a connection that stayed open, gets `503` and is retried.
  - **Web:** the sign-in screen with provider buttons above the unchanged pairing form, session state, the CSRF header, 401/403 reason routing, one close rule for every signed-in socket (chat, Runs, Canvas and the event stream), the account menu, navigation by access, and strings for every locale. Desktop keeps pairing.
    - The close rule: no timed reconnect on 4401/4403 or while a re-auth is pending, one reconnect after re-authentication, and a normal reconnect on 1001.
    - A 4401 first re-checks the session, so an early re-authentication moves the socket to the new session without another prompt.
    - A chat turn whose socket closed mid-turn ends locally, and the transcript reloads when the socket reopens.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No refresh tokens: the user signs in again on expiry.
  - No single sign-out at the identity provider.
  - No password login (#8076), SCIM or SAML.
  - No change to pairing, the CLI, zerocode or RPC.
  - Chat for non-administrator accounts through the core's session methods is a follow-up.
  - Nothing for the separate `zeroclaw-gw` process.
- **Blast radius:**
  - **Gateway auth on every route.** A router-wide layer classifies cookie-carrying requests, and `require_auth`, the config route layer and the inline pairing checks (event stream, chat, canvas, SOP runs, plugin list) admit a session. With sign-in off, the layer never reads a cookie.
  - **Config:** `zeroclaw-config` gains one additive table.
  - **Runtime:** `zeroclaw-runtime` gains one exchange variant and `RpcInboundAuth::authenticate_bound`. Their placement exceptions are proposed in #11963 (see Depends on). Plain `authenticate` is unchanged.
  - **Gateway serving:** the native TLS listener now serves HTTP/1 upgrades, as the plain listener does, so the dashboard's sockets work over `[gateway.tls]`. Before, they were dropped right after their `101` (#11951). This is one self-contained commit, which can also ship on its own.
  - **Web:** `web/src/lib/{auth,api,ws,sse}.ts` and `hooks/useAuth.ts`, which every page goes through. In pairing mode their behaviour is unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):**
  - Closes #11961
  - Closes #11951
  - Part of #8289
  - Related #7432
  - Depends on #11963 (the placement rows for this PR's two runtime additions; it must merge first, with the Core approval recorded in each row)
  - Depends on #11901 (this branch carries its commits until it merges)
  - Depends on #11903 (this branch carries its commits until it merges; without it, concurrent re-verification after an unrelated config publish can end valid dashboard sessions)

### What this does, simply

A team that already signs in to ZeroClaw's CLI with its identity provider still had to hand out pairing codes for the web dashboard, and anyone with a code got full access. With this change an operator can add one table to the config and the dashboard offers "Sign in with <provider>".

The browser never holds the token: the gateway keeps it and gives the browser a cookie that script cannot read. Each request is checked against the same rules the CLI and RPC already follow. Administrators get the whole dashboard. Other accounts get only what their profile allows, which in this change is the configuration their profile grants.

When a sign-in expires the page stays as it was and asks the user to sign in again in a small window. Signing out of ZeroClaw doesn't sign the user out of the identity provider. Installs that don't add the table see no difference at all.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, once CI is green.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web` (dashboard), through the gateway.
- **Setup / preconditions:**
  - An OIDC provider (Keycloak works) with a client that uses Authorization Code + PKCE (S256).
  - The client's redirect URI is `<dashboard origin>/oidc/callback`, its access tokens carry the configured `audience` (RFC 9068 `at+jwt` for JWKS validation), and it has a groups claim.
  - The config: `[gateway] require_pairing = true`; `[gateway.dashboard_sign_in] oidc = ["corp"]`; and `[oidc.corp]` with `interactive_clients = ["<client id>"]` and a `profile_map` with one group mapped to an `admin = true` profile and one to a profile granting `config = ["read"]`.
  - Serve over HTTPS, or open the dashboard on `localhost`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Open the dashboard and choose "Sign in with corp". Sign in as an administrator.
  2. Open a few pages.
  3. Sign out in one tab while another tab is open.
  4. Sign in as the other account; open a non-config page by URL.
  5. Set the client's token lifespan to 60 s and wait.
  6. Remove the table and reload.
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  1. You land on the dashboard with no token in local or session storage, and `document.cookie` doesn't show the session.
  2. Every page loads.
  3. Both tabs show the signed-out screen.
  4. "Not available for your account".
  5. A re-auth prompt keeps the page; the same account resumes.
  6. The pairing dialog is back, and the old cookie no longer works.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** only the pairing dialog. There is no way to sign in with the provider, and the callback page shows a token to copy.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:**
  - Rust format, clippy (`-D warnings`) and tests for `zeroclaw-config`, `zeroclaw-runtime` and `zeroclaw-gateway`, which cover:
    - the config validation (four tests);
    - the required-ID-token exchange (two);
    - the token's provider binding: a sign-in callback with publications landing between its steps and during a delayed exchange, a sign-in whose pin no longer matches, and a re-verification whose provider is repointed to another issuer or client mid-verification. Each must send the token to no other provider. A compatible publish keeps the session;
    - the runtime's `authenticate_bound` (another issuer, another client, no such provider);
    - a signed-in socket over native TLS closing `1001` when the gateway stops, and an upgrade racing the stop over TLS;
    - the gateway sign-in flow against a mock provider (start, binding, callback, session, sign-out), origin and CSRF refusals, bearer precedence, refusals of service and unmapped identities, HTTPS-or-loopback, the return-path guard, the store caps, expiry, a removed or repointed provider, a policy change, re-verification after a reload, turning sign-in off, and socket watches. It also covers real chat sockets that close on sign-out, expiry or a lost admin grant, both mid-turn and between turns, including a message waiting for the session's turn; an approval sent after sign-out that resolves nothing; a canvas feed that does not outlive a reload; the zeroizing token store; and the idle sweep of expired sessions.
  - The architecture tests.
  - The docs gates for the authentication guide and the ADR-017 text.
  - `Web Permission Tests` (`cargo web check`, `tsc -b`, the existing web suites and the new `npm run test:auth`), which cover:
    - the startup decision;
    - CSRF and no-bearer headers;
    - 401/403 routing;
    - socket close codes, including the Runs page itself and a socket closed mid-turn;
    - navigation access;
    - the sign-in screen ("sign-in off renders the old pairing dialog");
    - expiry and re-auth;
    - cross-tab sign-out;
    - every locale carrying the new strings.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:**
  - No run against a real identity provider in CI.
  - The revert-the-fix checks below are not CI jobs.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux, on this head's tree `17c1be71c2`, master `89bd18484b` merged in; every test run inside a private network namespace with only loopback):
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
  - `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings` (the CI lint command): clean.
  - `cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`: clean, no warnings.
  - `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop` (CI `Test`): 19414 tests run: 19413 passed, 1 failed, 41 skipped. The failure is `daemon_startup_feedback::daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions`, which needs `expect`; the test machine doesn't have it (CI installs it), and the test fails the same way on master there.
  - CI `Test (opt-in tools)` (`cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway --features tools-compat --lib --test integration -E '…'`): 12811 tests run: 12811 passed, 168 skipped.
  - Gateway golden-frame replay (informational in CI): 7 passed (no drift with sign-in off).
  - `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` (markdownlint), `docs_links_gate.sh` and `comment_hygiene_gate.sh`: pass (markdownlint: 0 errors in the authentication guide and ADR-017).
  - The web tree is byte-identical to the one reviewed and tested earlier (`cargo web check`, `npm run test:auth` 128/128 and the build), and master's changes since don't touch `web/`; `Web Permission Tests` runs it again in CI.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Revert-the-fix checks. Each guard below was removed and its test was shown to fail, then the guard was restored:
  - Revert-the-fix checks, gateway: the binding cookie, the CSRF header, the `Origin` check on POST and on the WebSocket upgrade, the required ID token, the service refusal, the return-path guard, grants after a profile-map edit, the provider pin, and off-by-default.
  - More gateway revert checks:
    - the chat socket's session arm mid-turn, the per-frame checks mid-turn and between turns, and the turn-permit wait and its re-check;
    - a session watch ending at its gateway generation's stop, and the canvas close code;
    - the idle sweep, and an ended session keeping its cookie;
    - a check cut short by the hard expiry or by the generation's stop, and the hard expiry enforced after a slow re-verification;
    - a watch built after its generation stopped, and a stopped generation refusing cookie requests;
    - a pending recheck dropped when its session ends, and a detached chat turn releasing its watch;
    - sign-out clearing an ended session's cookie;
    - sign-in turned off ending sessions with no request (at the next sweep, and when a generation is built with it off);
    - an unsafe request without `Origin` refused, and the global session cap refusing rather than evicting;
    - the SOP feed, the event stream and a dropped generation's sweep, each with its wiring removed;
    - the token's provider binding: the runtime's check (against the gateway test and the runtime test), sign-in's bound call, the retry's bound call, and the callback's single configuration read;
    - the restart 503 shaped for the request's protocol, a closed stop channel read as retired, the re-verification retry, and WebSocket upgrades on native TLS.
  - Revert-the-fix checks, web: expiry keeps the page, socket close codes 4401/4403 stop the reconnect loop, a different account reloads the page, a 4401 re-checks the session before prompting, the Runs close rules, no retry while a re-auth is pending, and the mid-turn close resync.
  - Every check above failed with its fix reverted, and the tree was clean afterwards. Repeated on this head for the gateway, runtime and TLS-upgrade guards (18 checks): each test failed with its fix reverted, the suites above pass with every fix in place, and the tree was clean afterwards.
  - Earlier browser runs against a Keycloak realm covered:
    - off by default;
    - administrator and scoped sign-in;
    - expiry and popup re-authentication, including another account changing the principal;
    - sign-out across tabs with the chat socket closing 4401;
    - the pairing fallback;
    - a policy change while signed in;
    - six probes: CSRF, a foreign `Origin` on POST and on the WebSocket upgrade, a cross-site sign-out, an open redirect, and a callback finished in another browser;
    - over plain HTTP, reloads mid-session and sign-in turned off and on across reloads;
    - over native TLS, the same reload scenarios, a kept connection across a reload, and a chat socket that stays open.
  - Exact-source acceptance was repeated after the provider-binding fixes on 12c57796df, which adds only TLS test-helper provider setup to the reviewed sign-in change (d013d3f3b0); this branch's later merges bring in only #11901, #11903 and master. The first plain-HTTP dashboard run passed 13/13; native TLS passed 10/13. Repeated provider-repointing runs passed 8/12: the four failures match #11902, and a separately labelled diagnostic build with #11903 passed 10/10. The CLI pairing-code command still constructs an HTTP URL, so it cannot exercise pairing-code rotation against a native-TLS listener. The intermittent sync-Python TLS chat-socket open timeout also reproduced against an independent TLS responder without ZeroClaw. Its precise client/library root remains unresolved; the original failed cases remain recorded.
  - A follow-up using native Chromium WebSockets on the same exact-source binary and dashboard snapshot reached OPEN 23/23 times, with zero open timeouts or browser error events. Genuine expiry returned HTTP 401 and clean socket close 4401; same-account popup reauthentication restored HTTP 200 and a successful native reopen; sign-out returned 204, the other tab saw 401, and the held socket closed cleanly with 4401. No chat prompts or application messages were sent. The raw three-case run remains 1/3 because additional immediate-client-close assertions received 1006 instead of 1000 for ordinary opens and the reopened socket. Two separate HTTP control opens show the same 1006. An earlier master has the same source branch, but an earlier-master binary was not run as a behavioral control. This is a bounded transport and session-watch check, not full frontend chat-protocol or production certificate-trust coverage.
  - The pinned Keycloak acceptance harness passed 21/23; the known master failures require #11737 and #11423. Logto without the optional compatibility changes passed 16/19: two human-token cases need the RFC 8707 resource parameter, and JWT introspection is unsupported by that provider. This is not a claim that every provider gate passes.
  - The test-only provider follow-up passed seven affected tests under the CI package/feature set, failed all seven with the provider setup removed, and passed again after byte-identical restoration. These tests cover the workspace's two-provider rustls ambiguity that the earlier gateway-only run did not exercise. Repeated on this head: with both provider installs removed, all seven TLS tests fail with the rustls provider panic; restored, all seven pass.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot. The sign-in screen, an administrator's account menu, the re-authentication prompt and the not-available page, plus the dashboard with sign-in off for comparison: it shows the same pairing form, without the provider button.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** tree `17c1be71c2` (this head); `web` through the gateway for the browser runs above, which used the reviewed source with the same sign-in, web and gateway files.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** headless Chromium at 1280×800 against this head (tree `17c1be71c2`), with a local mock identity provider and placeholder accounts:
  - The sign-in screen with sign-in on:
    ![Sign-in screen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f194f0de-36c5-49be-ac70-01ff3c2880d6)
  - An administrator's account menu:
    ![Account menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca9d1284-6304-4d90-b78c-39dea799decd)
  - The re-authentication prompt after the session's token expired:
    ![Re-authentication prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ececa0db-2f09-4418-be11-37076b912a66)
  - A non-administrator account on an operator-only page (`/logs`):
    ![Not available for your account](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a1d714a-3008-421a-b864-92baf7531458)
  - Sign-in off, for comparison:
    ![Sign-in off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/142b7980-ebb7-497a-9095-f9eddfc9cd14)
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the browser runs above (sign-in, expiry and re-auth, cross-tab sign-out, pairing fallback).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** none. The one CI `Test` failure above is environmental (`expect` is not installed on the test machine).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- **New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope?** Yes.
  - An account whose permission profile has `admin = true` can now use the whole dashboard after signing in, as a paired browser can.
  - Other accounts get only the config routes their grants allow; everything else answers 403.
  - Each sign-in is logged with the principal it resolved to.
- **New external network calls?** Yes, to the configured provider only:
  - the code exchange, which the existing relay already makes;
  - the provider's JWKS or introspection endpoint when a session is verified again (at the introspection deadline, after a reload, or after a policy change).
  - A token is only ever sent to the issuer and client it was issued by, checked against the policy that would send it. A sign-in or session whose provider was repointed to another issuer or client is refused or ended without its token being sent anywhere.
- **Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed?** Yes.
  - The access token is kept in gateway memory for the session's life, in a buffer that is wiped when the session ends: on sign-out, expiry (expired sessions are swept every minute even when no request arrives), revocation, or when sign-in is turned off. It is never logged or written to disk. A refresh token the provider returns anyway is wiped unused.
  - The browser holds only an opaque `HttpOnly` cookie and a CSRF token in memory. A cookie whose session ended is left in place, so every tab keeps hearing `session_expired`: it names nothing and holds no token. Sign-out clears it, also once the session has ended, and a new sign-in replaces it. The ID token is checked, then discarded. Its subject is not compared with the access token's principal: both come from the same back-channel exchange, and the account is the one the access token resolves to.
  - Refresh tokens are neither relayed nor kept.
- **PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs?** No. The account display name comes from the verified token's claims and is shown only to that user.
- **Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed?** No.
- **Mitigations:**
  - login-CSRF binding per flow;
  - origin and CSRF checks, including WebSocket upgrades;
  - `__Host-` cookies where the deployment allows;
  - HTTPS required except on the gateway's own machine;
  - no CORS grants on cookie responses (asserted in tests);
  - session store caps that never evict another account (256 total, 8 per account; at the cap a sign-in is refused).
- **Documented limits ("Things to know" in the authentication guide):**
  - removing an administrator at the identity provider does not revoke devices they paired;
  - loopback HTTP cookies are port-agnostic;
  - an unreachable introspection endpoint ends a session that is due for revalidation (fails closed).

## Compatibility (required)

- **Backward compatible?** Yes.
- **Config / env / CLI surface changed?** Yes: the optional `[gateway.dashboard_sign_in]` table (`oidc`, `session_lifetime_secs`).
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No.
- **Upgrade steps for existing users:** none; it is off unless configured. To turn it on, see "Dashboard sign-in" in `docs/book/src/security/authentication.md`. Behind a reverse proxy, the browser's `Host` must reach the gateway unchanged.
- **Carried from #11903 until it merges:** with an OIDC entry that validates by JWKS (the default), a signed-in session could need a fresh sign-in after a reload.
  - Each reload starts with an empty key cache. While its first key fetch was in flight, the provider refused other verifications as misconfigured, and a browser's reconnects arrive together, so one of them could end the session.
  - #11903 makes concurrent checks share one fetch. This branch merges it unchanged (its patch is identical to #11903's own); this PR changes nothing else in that code. A re-verification that still fails logs `dashboard session ended: verifying its token again failed`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** remove `[gateway.dashboard_sign_in]` (or empty `oidc`). Every session ends at its next request, or within a minute if none arrives, and the dashboard falls back to pairing. Then `git revert <sha>` if needed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `gateway.dashboard_sign_in.oidc`; empty means off.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - gateway log events `dashboard sign-in` / `dashboard sign-in refused` / `dashboard sign-out`;
  - 401 bodies with `reason` `session_expired` / `session_invalid`, 403 with `csrf` / `origin` / `operator_required`, and, during a reload, 503 with `gateway_restarting`;
  - a pairing-only install showing anything other than the pairing dialog;
  - dashboard requests from a signed-in browser carrying `Authorization`.

## ADR note

ADR-017 (`proposed`) gains the dashboard session model under its token-purpose decision: a dashboard session is the browser's connection, and its token is kept in gateway memory as that session's revalidation context. Its OIDC acceptance gate now names dashboard sign-in, sign-out and re-authentication.

milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(tools): add agy_cli coding-CLI tool for Antigravity CLI
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Google has moved terminal Gemini use from Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI (`agy`), and Gemini CLI has stopped serving most accounts (Google Developers Blog, June 2026). ZeroClaw can delegate coding tasks to Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI and OpenCode, but not to `agy`.
  - Adds `agy_cli`, a peer of `codex_cli` / `claude_code` / `gemini_cli` / `opencode_cli`. It is built on the shared coding-CLI executor, so it inherits the same authorization, working-directory validation, timeout, output bounding and runtime-executor routing.
  - Headless `agy` exits 0 and reports `status: SUCCESS` even when it auto-denies a tool permission, so the exit code alone would report a blocked task as a success. `agy_cli` requests JSON output and decides success from it. A run succeeds only when the process exits 0, `status` is `SUCCESS`, and `denied_actions` is empty. Non-JSON or status-less output fails closed.
  - Tool-owned flags are attached (`--print=<prompt>`, `--model=<id>`, `--print-timeout=<n>s`) and placed after operator `extra_args`. A model-supplied prompt that starts with `-` cannot be parsed as a flag, and the tool's own settings take precedence over operator arguments.
- **Scope boundary:** `gemini_cli` is not changed or deprecated here. There is no `agy` model provider. The shared coding-CLI executor is unchanged apart from recognising the new tool name in the env-boundary helper. The sandbox and permission defaults of `agy` itself are left to the operator's agy settings.
- **Blast radius:** Opt-in only. The new `[agy_cli]` section defaults to `enabled = false`, and nothing changes for existing configs. Shared test fixtures changed in two places: the budget-test fake now returns agy-shaped JSON, which the other adapters pass through unchanged, and the runtime routing test now expects `agy_cli` to fail closed on its plain-text probe.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11075. Related #4879, whose closing comment suggested Antigravity CLI support as the follow-up. Related #10381 (merged): `agy_cli` builds its command through the shared `CodingCliCommand`/`CodingCliExecutor` path, so it inherits that PR's host-launcher resolution before the workspace working directory is applied.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw agents can hand a coding task to an external coding CLI. Google has replaced Gemini CLI with a new tool called Antigravity CLI (`agy`), so Gemini users had no supported way to do that. This PR adds an `agy_cli` tool that works like the existing Codex and Claude Code tools. It stays off until you turn it on in config.

The main difference from the other CLIs is how failure is detected. When `agy` runs without a terminal and wants to do something that needs permission, such as running a shell command, it refuses automatically but still exits successfully. `agy_cli` reads agy's JSON result, reports those refusals as a failure, and tells the user how to allow the action in agy's own settings.

ZeroClaw checks that the requested working directory is inside the workspace, but it does not sandbox what `agy` does once it is running. That is governed by agy's own permission settings. The docs section added in `tools/overview.md` states this plainly.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The behaviour is covered by unit tests with fixtures copied from real agy 1.2.9 output. Manual testing needs an authenticated `agy` install, which most reviewers will not have.

### How I tested

- **Revision (2026-10-11):** one commit, which supersedes `76275ecf6`. It was authored and validated at `34d7aea0825a1e7cd7701135e4dc3f341271a56b` on master `0f8fb9d372a5cf850e87f9464c7f5c216a717fee`. **Rebase note (2026-10-11):** the then-current head `6239f29f26fcbe1e6b520016cb98b9eade20f329` was a base-only rebase of that commit onto master `d03325172eb6c64272f01042b60fd7f66d74c711` with GitHub's update-branch (`git range-diff` shows the commit identical; the local validation and review below were recorded on `34d7aea08`). **Rebase note (2026-10-14):** the then-current head `dc09ad4048d50e3960e9d8c44132a8fec3b4b1cd` was a base-only rebase of `6239f29f2` onto master `329e66f76` with GitHub's update-branch. Master had moved 32 commits and four files this PR touches changed upstream (`orchestrator/acp_server.rs`, `orchestrator/mod.rs`, `config/schema.rs`, `docs/book/src/tools/overview.md`); a trial merge was clean and the rebase applied without conflicts. `git range-diff` shows the commit unchanged apart from one context line in `docs/book/src/tools/overview.md` (the neighbouring heading was renamed upstream); the file set is unchanged (18 files). The local validation and review below were recorded on `34d7aea08`; required CI runs on the current head. **Rebase note (2026-10-17):** rebased again with GitHub's update-branch onto master `4e82ce46e` (32 commits, including the rustls/Wasmtime advisory fix #11755 that the earlier Security failure was waiting on). `git range-diff` shows the commit identical, with no content change; the new head is `91da937b6051c182654f7ba5d0cc240b722cece8`. A trial merge was clean; five files this PR changes were also touched on master (`zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs`, both `tools.ftl` files, `zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs`, `docs/book/src/developing/tool-inventory.md`) without conflict. What changed:
  - Inventory: `agy_cli` is registered in `BUILTIN_TOOLS` as a Host-tier tool, listed in the tier table and prose of `tool-inventory.md`, and enabled in the runtime maximal-config inventory test. This fixes the `matrix_safe_policy_names_only_inventoried_tools` failure that appeared after master's typed tool inventory landed, and Greptile's inventory finding.
  - i18n: the tool description, parameter descriptions and errors are Fluent `tool-agy-cli-*` keys in the canonical English catalogue, with the generated tools-crate mirror regenerated. This addresses Greptile's localization finding.
  - Hardening of `agy_cli`'s own contract: a bare `--` in `extra_args` is dropped from the agy argv and flagged by config validation, so it can no longer turn the tool-owned flags into positionals. An explicit JSON `null` for `response`, `denied_actions` or `error` no longer breaks parsing, so agy's real status and error are reported; success still requires `status == SUCCESS` and no denied actions. The `--print-timeout` margin scales with small timeouts instead of collapsing to `1s`. The attached form `--dangerously-skip-permissions=<value>` now triggers the risky-flag warning (agy only; Codex matching is unchanged). Stderr appended to errors is capped like stdout. `agy_cli` is added to the Integrations-group test.
  - Not changed: the shared coding-CLI workdir refactor, Codex helper naming, the model-visible remediation text, and tolerance for non-JSON banner lines.

- **Rebase note (2026-10-18):** rebased onto master `c473221313341a853e04122f93bb9bd26b5e6c47` (8 commits after `4e82ce46e`). GitHub's update-branch could not be used: master's #11221 (`8ed287bd4`) moved the coding-CLI tools behind per-tool Cargo features and conflicted in `zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs` and `zeroclaw-tools/src/coding_cli.rs`. I resolved it locally in an isolated worktree, starting from master's versions of both files and re-applying this PR's change on top. The new head is `400553d30eed7e316b68860003553e61700825c5` (previous head `91da937b6`). `agy_cli.rs` is byte-identical to the previous head; the previously approved behaviour is unchanged. What changed:
  - New `tool-agy-cli` feature, chained like its peers (`zeroclaw-config` -> `zeroclaw-tools` -> `zeroclaw-runtime` -> root) and added to the full-tool feature list.
  - `OptInTool::AgyCli` (`ALL` is now 13 entries) with section `agy_cli` and feature `tool-agy-cli`; the inventory entry now carries `compilation: OptIn(AgyCli)`.
  - `agy_cli` module, attribution and runtime registration are gated on the feature, with `warn_tool_compiled_out` otherwise; `any_coding_cli_tool_enabled` and the shared coding-CLI executor gates include it.
  - `collect_agy_cli_extra_arg_warnings` returns early when the tool is not compiled in (as the Codex collector does), so a build without `agy` reports only the compiled-out warning. Tests that need the feature are gated, and one new test covers the compiled-out case.
  - `tool-agy-cli` is added to the 13 generated feature lists (`Containerfile`, the Dockerfiles, `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml`, `dist/aur/PKGBUILD`, `flake.nix`, `setup.bat`); `cargo run -p xtask --bin generate -- installers --check` reports every surface in sync.
  - The file set grows from 18 to 31 files: 13 additional files, namely the Cargo manifests, the packaging surfaces and `opt_in_tools.rs`.
  - Local validation (aarch64 Linux, rustc 1.97.1) on `0fee975c651b3302a16aafaab6bd30ac4df7492e`, which has the same patch-id as the published head and differs only by the base (two later master commits that touch none of this PR's files): `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `installers --check`; `zeroclaw-config` lib `agy_cli` 3 passed without the feature and 6 passed with `tool-agy-cli,tool-codex-cli`; `zeroclaw-tools` lib `agy_cli` 31 passed, environment-boundary 1, `coding_agent_budget_tests` 2, inventory docs-drift and source-scan 1 + 3; `zeroclaw-runtime` `registered_coding_cli_tools_use_configured_runtime_executor` 1 and `docker_without_workspace_mount_does_not_register_coding_cli_tools` 1 (with `--skip tunnel::tailscale`); `cargo clippy -D warnings` on `zeroclaw-config` and `zeroclaw-tools`; `git diff --check`; all exit 0. The numbers above supersede the `34d7aea08` figures below for the wiring; the `agy_cli.rs` unit-test evidence still applies.
  - Review: exact-SHA Gemini review via Agy (`gemini-3.8-flash-high`, complete diff bundle, no tools) returned READY with no findings on `0fee975c6`. An earlier candidate was rated NEEDS_WORK for missing feature gates on some config tests; that is fixed and re-reviewed. This is the only review lane for this revision.
  - CI: the two `Format` jobs fail on `tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs`, added unformatted by master's #11837 (`c47322131`); `rustfmt --check` on that file at master reproduces it, and this PR does not touch it. Other required jobs were still running when this was written. Approval was given on earlier heads; since this revision changes the feature wiring, a fresh look at the gating is welcome.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required Rust CI (fmt, clippy, tests) covers the new tool, config section, and wiring.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI has no `agy` binary. The live behaviour against real agy was checked locally (below).
- **Validation at `34d7aea08` (aarch64 Linux, rustc 1.97.1):** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` 0; Fluent generator `--check` 0; `zeroclaw-tools` lib 43 passed; `zeroclaw-tools` inventory docs-drift/source-scan integration tests 1 + 3 passed; `zeroclaw-config` lib agy/section filters 26 passed; `zeroclaw-runtime` `coding_cli agy_cli` filters 17 passed; `zeroclaw-channels` inventory/matrix filters 2 passed; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on tools, runtime, channels and config 0; `git diff --check` 0.
- **Mutation checks:** reverting the explicit-`null` handling fails 3 of the new tests; reverting the bare-`--` filtering fails 1 test in `zeroclaw-tools` and 1 in `zeroclaw-config`. The tree was restored byte-identical afterwards.
- **Review:** exact-SHA Gemini review via Agy (`gemini-3.8-flash-high`, bundle of the complete `0f8fb9d37..34d7aea08` diff, no tools) returned READY with no findings, blockers or test gaps. This is the only review lane for this revision; a second review was not run.
- **CI:** on `34d7aea08`, all required Linux, lint, check, build and test jobs passed. `Platform Test (macOS)` and `Platform Test (Windows)` failed there with 13 failing tests, identical by name to master's scheduled platform run (`38021228494`); none is specific to this PR. CI on the rebased head `6239f29f2` is pending and is not carried over from the earlier head.
- **Live use (earlier revision, before the 2026-10-11 hardening):** the same patch ran in a local `release-fast` integration build (master `1d64833a9` + this PR + #11080) on aarch64 Linux since 2026-09-29; a live agent-driven `agy_cli` call returned the expected reply.
- **Historical local checks** (aarch64 Linux, rustc 1.97.1), from earlier heads with the same agy_cli patch: `411d9ec42` amends `0543611e8` only to name `agy_cli.extra_args` as the ZeroClaw-side remedy in the auto-denied-permission error, plus one assertion. `500590f3c` changes only `agy_cli.rs` relative to `5d4b5bc7e`.

```text
# at 411d9ec42 (differs from 0543611e8 only in agy_cli.rs error text + 1 assertion)
cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-tools -- --check                        -> exit 0
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings  -> exit 0
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- agy_cli
  test result: ok. 25 passed; 0 failed
git diff --check                                            -> exit 0

# at 500590f3c
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  -> exit 0
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings  -> exit 0
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- agy_cli coding_cli coding_agent cli_discovery attribution
  test result: ok. 41 passed; 0 failed
git diff --check                                            -> exit 0

# at 5d4b5bc7e (differs only in agy_cli.rs)
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime \
  -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets -- -D warnings          -> exit 0
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- agy_cli codex_cli sections validation_warnings
  test result: ok. 68 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::tests::registered_coding_cli tools::tests::coding_cli
  test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::tests::docker_without_workspace_mount_does_not_register_coding_cli_tools
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- map_tool_kind matrix_safe
  test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I ran the real tool code (`AgyCliTool::execute`) against agy 1.2.9 with a throwaway, local-only `#[ignore]` test that is not part of this PR:
  - A plain prompt returned `success=true` with the expected text.
  - With `extra_args = ["--sandbox"]`, a prompt that needs a shell command returned `success=false` with the auto-denied `RunCommand` explanation. agy itself exited 0 with `status: SUCCESS`.
  - A prompt beginning with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` was treated as prompt text, returning `success=true` with the expected reply, not as a flag.
  - The scratch workspace was empty afterwards.

  Not verified: behaviour on macOS or Windows, and agy versions other than 1.2.9. The live run was at `5d4b5bc7e`; `500590f3c` only adds stderr to the non-`SUCCESS` status error and two unit tests.

  Operator misconfiguration: a bare `--` in `extra_args` made agy 1.2.9 reject the following tool-owned flags (`Error: unexpected argument "--output-format=json"`, exit 2) without running anything. As of `34d7aea08`, `agy_cli` drops bare `--` entries from the agy argv and config validation warns about them, so the flags stay flags; a trailing value-taking flag in `extra_args` (for example `--effort`) is still operator argv and is documented as such in the tools overview.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No user-visible interface state changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** A full-workspace `cargo test` was not run locally. The changed surfaces are covered by the focused tests above and required CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes**
- New external network calls? **Yes**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - Permissions and network: when enabled, `agy_cli` launches `agy`, which acts on files and calls Google's services under its own permission model, like the existing coding-CLI tools. The tool is disabled by default and gated by the same security policy, autonomy level and rate limiting as its peers, and the working directory is canonicalized and must stay inside the workspace. Operator `extra_args` that widen agy's permissions (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--add-dir`) produce a non-blocking config-validation warning that does not echo the values.
  - Prompt injection: agy's response is returned to the model as tool output, the same as for the other coding CLIs. Output is bounded by `max_output_bytes`.
  - Containment limit, stated in the docs: ZeroClaw validates only the starting directory. What `agy` touches after launch is governed by agy's own settings.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes**

---

Cause was mine: when I added the Agy config tests in `schema.rs` I dropped the `#[cfg(feature = "tool-codex-cli")]` gate on that existing Codex test, so it ran (and failed) in a default-features build. My earlier local runs filtered on `agy_cli`, so they did not exercise it. The gate is restored (the only gate differences from master are now the four new `tool-agy-cli` tests). Rebased onto master `24938afc6` (no overlap with this PR's files).

prs.title: fix(providers): retry Codex streams as streams on the default endpoint
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - After a streaming decode failure, `send_responses_request` retried once with `stream: false` (#6668). The default ChatGPT Codex endpoint accepts only streaming requests and rejects that retry with `400 {"detail":"Stream must be set to true"}`, so on the subscription route the recovery could never succeed. A truncated stream became a non-retryable "provider rejected the request" error.
  - On the default endpoint (`!custom_endpoint`), the one retry is now a streaming retry. Custom endpoints (`provider_api_url`) keep #6668's non-streaming recovery unchanged.
  - The final error and log attributes name the retry kind (`streaming retry` / `non-streaming retry`).
- **Scope boundary:** one retry, as before. No change to which failures are retried: API error events and non-success HTTP statuses still are not retried. No config keys, no change to the request shape, `reliable.rs` classification, or other providers.
- **Known limit:** the retry kind follows `custom_endpoint`, which is derived from the configured URL. A custom `provider_api_url` that proxies the ChatGPT Codex backend still gets the non-streaming retry, as on master.
- **Blast radius:** OpenAI Codex provider on the default endpoint (OAuth / ChatGPT subscription) when a stream fails to decode. Custom-endpoint deployments are unaffected.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12072. Related #6668.

### What this does, simply

Sometimes the ChatGPT Codex backend ends a response stream before sending any output. ZeroClaw tried to recover by asking again without streaming, but that backend refuses non-streaming requests outright, so the recovery always failed and the user saw a misleading "request rejected" error. Now ZeroClaw asks again the way the backend accepts, once, and if that also fails the error says what actually happened.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: covered by deterministic mock-server tests. Live reproduction depends on the backend truncating a stream, which is intermittent.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `provider` = `openai-codex`

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The `Test` job runs the `zeroclaw-providers` lib tests, including the new and existing `openai_codex` retry tests; `cargo clippy` CI covers lint.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live ChatGPT Codex call.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
# at eaec11f46, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, aarch64 Linux
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib -- openai_codex::
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_custom_endpoint_reports_non_streaming_retry_failure ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_default_endpoint_reports_streaming_retry_failure ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_default_endpoint_retries_streaming_after_empty_stream ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_default_endpoint_streaming_retry_http_error_is_not_retried_again ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_does_not_retry_failed_http_status ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_does_not_retry_stream_api_error_events ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_retries_non_streaming_when_stream_contains_malformed_frame_after_text ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_retries_non_streaming_when_stream_decode_fails ... ok
# test result: ok. 55 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1932 filtered out

cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings
# exit 0, no diagnostics

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/openai_codex.rs
# Comment hygiene gate passed.

cargo fmt --all -- --check
git diff --check origin/master
# both exit 0
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - RED/GREEN: the test module from this branch was run against the production code of unpatched master `99bd353c7`. The three default-endpoint tests fail there with the exact production error, `OpenAI Codex API error (400 Bad Request): {"detail":"Stream must be set to true"}`, because the stream-only mock rejects the `stream: false` retry the way the real backend does. All pass with the fix.
  - The default-endpoint tests give the mock provider an OAuth profile and `custom_endpoint = false`; their mock server rejects `stream: false` with that 400 without consuming a queued reply. The custom-endpoint path is pinned by the existing `codex_retries_non_streaming_*` tests and by `codex_custom_endpoint_reports_non_streaming_retry_failure` (passes before and after: behaviour preserved).
  - The fallback block is identical on master and on the build where the failure was observed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo test` was not run locally (Raspberry Pi host); the change is confined to one function in `zeroclaw-providers`, covered by the focused run above and by CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No (same single retry, now with `stream: true` on the default endpoint)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Log text changed: the warning "retrying without streaming" is now "retrying once" with a `retry` attribute (`streaming retry` / `non-streaming retry`), and the final error says "stream decode and retry both failed". Log matches on the old strings need updating.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; no data or config migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** On the default Codex endpoint, a turn whose first stream is truncated fails with "streaming retry failed (...)" instead of recovering, or a custom endpoint stops recovering via the non-streaming retry.

prs.title: fix(channels): keep allowlisted Discord bots from answering approvals
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A plaintext Discord approval reply (`<token> yes|no|always`) whose author is a bot is now `Rejected` even when that bot is allowlisted. `listen_to_bots` plus `external_peers` exist so the agent can converse with another bot; they shouldn't also make that bot an approver of the agent's tool calls.
  - The gateway now computes the payload author's `bot` flag once (the value the `listen_to_bots` gate already read) and passes it to `resolve_approval_reply`, which treats a bot responder as not allowed. Rejection reuses the existing `Rejected` path from #9574: the pending approval is kept and the message is not forwarded to the agent.
  - Component (button) approvals are unchanged; only a human can click a Discord component.
- **Scope boundary:** Discord plaintext approvals only. No config keys, no change to `listen_to_bots`, message admission, peer resolution, destination binding, component approvals or other channels. Slack's `allow_bots` text-approval path looks similar and is left for a separate change.
- **Blast radius:** Discord deployments with `listen_to_bots = true` where a bot is allowlisted and answered approval prompts in text. Human responders are unaffected.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12064. Related #9574.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can ask in Discord for permission before running a sensitive tool, and someone replies with the approval token to allow or deny it. Since #9574 that someone must be on the allowlist and reply in the same channel. When two agents share a channel (`listen_to_bots = true`), the operator allowlists the other bot so the agents can talk. Until now that also let the other bot answer approval prompts, so one agent's model output could approve the other agent's tool calls. After this change only humans can approve; a bot's approval reply is refused, and the prompt stays open for a human.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the change is covered by deterministic unit tests at the resolver and a source-scan test for the gateway wiring; a live repro needs two Discord bot accounts.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `discord`

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The `Test` job (`cargo nextest run --locked --workspace`) builds `zeroclaw-channels` with default features, which include `channel-discord`, and runs both tests below; `cargo clippy` CI covers lint.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live Discord gateway run.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
# at bd646bac4, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, aarch64 Linux
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- discord:: approval
# test result: ok. 369 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1649 filtered out; finished in 3.13s

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- plaintext_approval_requires_authorized_responder_and_destination gateway_plaintext_approval_passes_payload_bot_flag
# test discord::tests::plaintext_approval_requires_authorized_responder_and_destination ... ok
# test discord::tests::gateway_plaintext_approval_passes_payload_bot_flag ... ok
# test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed

cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets -- -D warnings
# exit 0, no diagnostics

cargo fmt --all -- --check
git diff --check origin/master
# both exit 0
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A/B on unpatched master 99bd353c7: a throwaway test (not committed) with an allowlisted `peer-bot`, `listen_to_bots = true` and a pending approval for `c1` got `Resolved` from `resolve_approval_reply("tok123 yes", "peer-bot", "c1")`, and the receiver got `Approve`. On this branch the same reply with `responder_is_bot = true` returns `Rejected` and the pending approval remains, while the allowlisted human still resolves it. Not verified: a live Discord gateway with two bot accounts.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo test` was not run locally (Raspberry Pi host); the changed surface is one function in `zeroclaw-channels`, covered by the focused runs above and by CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (narrows who can resolve approvals)
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The change removes a path where another agent's model output could act as the human approval for this agent's tool calls.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No, intentionally: an allowlisted bot can no longer resolve Discord approvals by text.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No`: a setup that relied on a bot relaying approvals must have a human answer the prompt (text or buttons) instead.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; no data or config migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A human allowlisted responder cannot resolve a Discord text approval in the prompt's channel (the pending approval times out instead).

prs.title: fix(plugins): clear abandoned install stages on the next install
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - An install stopped after creating its leased stage and before publishing leaves `.<name>.installing-v1-<id>/` (a `lease` file and a `package/` directory) behind. No command removed it. The staging sweep, `remove_stale_staging`, ran only from `plugin remove` after it claimed and judged a stranded final directory, from a retry finishing a delete an earlier remove began, and from update recovery. A normal install never swept, although its own comment already counted on "the sweep of abandoned stages" to clear what it leaves.
  - `install_admitted` now sweeps the abandoned `installing` stages of the package it installs before it stages its own copy. That includes the replacement an interrupted `plugin update` staged, which update recovery would discard anyway. The sweep runs under the package lock install already holds, and after install has refused an occupied name, so a refused install still changes nothing. Its ownership test is the existing one: a stage is cleared only when no process holds its lease. A stage whose lease is held is left alone. So are legacy PID-named stages (`.<name>.installing-<pid>`), whose owner cannot be proved, every other package's stages, and the name's `replacing` and `recovering` transactions, which can hold the only copy of a package.
  - Install's sweep goes on past a stage it cannot clear, for example one holding a file this user may not delete, and logs a warning naming the package. So one stuck stage never fails the install or keeps the other stages from being cleared. A changed plugins root or lock still refuses at once, before anything is staged. `plugin remove` and update recovery keep their sweep unchanged, and it still stops at the first error. The loop body moved into a helper so both modes share it.
  - Retries no longer pile up copies. An install that could not publish keeps its stage and tells the operator to run the install again. Once that install's process has ended, the next install clears the old stage instead of adding another next to it.
  - An install whose source is inside one of that name's `installing` stages is refused before anything is cleared, with a new `PluginError::SourceInStage`. Admission keeps the manifest and component bytes, but `skills/` is still copied from the source after the sweep. So installing a skill package from the `package/` path a failed publication reports keeping would have deleted that stage first, leaving neither an installed package nor the copy. The stage is matched by directory identity against the resolved source and every directory above it, so a trailing separator, a `..`, a symlink, or another path to the plugins directory still finds it. The source is resolved only when the name has a stage. The error names the stage and says to copy the package out and install from the copy; that install then clears the stage. Refusing was chosen over keeping the stage, because a kept stage would sit next to the installed package, the case under "Not covered" below.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - `plugin remove` is unchanged. A remove that refuses still leaves stages untouched, and a remove of a name with no final directory still does not sweep.
  - Discovery stays read-only and lock-free. There is no startup sweep, because the daemon and every read-only command discover plugins without taking the package lock. The only new CLI message is the `SourceInStage` refusal, which `plugin install` prints as it prints its other errors.
  - Not covered: a stage left next to an *installed* package. That happens after a crash between publishing and finishing the stage, or when finishing the stage fails (install ignores that failure). Install refuses a name that is already installed, and removing a loaded package never sweeps. Such a stage is therefore cleared only by update recovery (`plugin update`), or by a remove followed by a reinstall. It holds an empty `package/` at most.
- **Blast radius:** `PluginHost::install_admitted`, so `PluginHost::install`, `zeroclaw plugin install`, and quickstart's plugin install. The only new filesystem effect is deleting this package's abandoned `installing` stages inside the plugins directory, through the same handle-based delete the remove sweep uses. Callers already handle every error this path can return (`NamespaceChanged` was already possible). The new `SourceInStage` refusal returns before anything is swept or staged and reaches callers unchanged. The one exhaustive match on `PluginError`, `is_structural_admission_failure`, counts it as not structural. The remove and update-recovery sweeps behave as before.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11792

### What this does, simply

If `zeroclaw plugin install` is killed at the wrong moment, it leaves a hidden folder in the plugins directory. Nothing loads that folder and nothing breaks, but no command ever cleaned it up, so these folders piled up. Now the next install of the same plugin clears them first. It clears only folders no running install still owns, skips one it cannot delete without failing, and never touches another plugin's folders, the older PID-named ones, or what an interrupted update or remove set aside. If you point an install at the package inside one of those hidden folders, it refuses, leaves the folder alone, and tells you to copy the package out first.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** A build with `--features plugins-wasm-cranelift`, `inotify-tools`, a fresh config directory, and any tool package directory.
- **Steps to run:** the steps from #11792:
  ```bash
  C=$(mktemp -d)
  zeroclaw --config-dir "$C" plugin list >/dev/null
  mkdir -p "$C/plugins"
  zeroclaw --config-dir "$C" plugin install <tool-package-dir> &
  pid=$!
  inotifywait -q -m -e create --format '%f' "$C/plugins" | grep -m1 -q 'installing-v1' && kill -9 "$pid"
  find "$C/plugins" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 2
  zeroclaw --config-dir "$C" plugin install <tool-package-dir>
  find "$C/plugins" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 2
  ```
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the second `find` lists only `.zeroclaw-package-lock-v1` and the installed package.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the second `find` still lists `.<name>.installing-v1-<id>/lease` and `.<name>.installing-v1-<id>/package`, and they survive a later `plugin remove` too.

### How I tested

Regression tests. Two of them pass on `master`, because they pin what the sweep must not do. For each test, the red column names the change that makes it fail: taking the install sweep out (the `master` behaviour), taking out the refusal of a source inside a stage (this PR's first commit, 0fdf97750a), or one targeted mistake in either. Each of those changes was applied to this branch and run, then reverted.

| Test | Pins | Fails when |
|---|---|---|
| `host::recovery_tests::the_next_install_clears_the_stage_a_killed_install_left` | the issue's case: a real child install killed at the `rename-before-move` barrier, holding the lock and the lease, then a second install leaves only the lock and the package (Linux, Android, macOS: that barrier lives in their no-replace move) | the install sweep is taken out |
| `host::recovery_tests::an_install_keeps_a_stage_whose_lease_is_held` | a stage whose lease a child process holds is kept, entry, lease and bytes, while an abandoned stage beside it is cleared | the sweep is taken out; the sweep takes held leases |
| `host::recovery_tests::an_install_whose_sweep_meets_a_replaced_lock_refuses_before_staging` (Unix) | a child install paused inside its sweep at `before-stage-delete`, with the lock file replaced, refuses with `NamespaceChanged`, publishes nothing and stages nothing; the abandoned stage keeps its bytes | the sweep is taken out |
| `host::tests::install_clears_abandoned_stages_of_its_name_only` | only the name's `installing` stage goes; another package's stage, a legacy PID stage, and the name's `replacing` and `recovering` transactions keep their bytes | the sweep is taken out; the sweep matches every transaction kind of the name |
| `host::tests::a_refused_install_leaves_abandoned_stages_alone` | an install refused because a file holds the name leaves the abandoned stage as it was | the sweep runs before the occupied-name refusal |
| `host::tests::install_goes_on_past_a_stage_it_cannot_clear` (Unix, skipped as root) | a stage holding a file in a mode-0555 folder is kept, and the install still succeeds | install propagates sweep errors |
| `host::tests::install_clears_the_stages_after_one_it_cannot_clear` | with a test-only fault failing whichever stage the sweep reaches first, exactly one of two abandoned stages is left, whatever order they are listed in | the sweep is taken out; install propagates sweep errors; install's sweep stops at the first error |
| `host::tests::install_keeps_a_stage_another_host_in_this_process_holds` | a stage a second `PluginHost` in the same process is building, so with its own lease descriptor, is kept, while an abandoned one is cleared | the sweep is taken out; the sweep takes held leases |
| `host::tests::an_install_from_the_stage_a_failed_install_kept_refuses_and_keeps_it` (Linux, Android, macOS: a test-only rename fault fails the publication) | the reviewed case: a skill package whose publication failed is installed again from the `package/` path `RecoveryRetained` reports. It refuses with `SourceInStage` naming that stage, which keeps its `skills/` bytes, and a second abandoned stage is kept too. A copy taken out of the stage then installs with the same bytes and clears both stages | the refusal is taken out |
| `host::tests::an_install_refuses_a_source_in_its_stage_however_the_path_is_spelled` | the same refusal, with the stage's bytes kept, for the package path with a trailing separator, through a `.`, through `..` and the plugins directory's parent, as its `manifest.toml`, and (Unix) through a symlink to the package and through a symlinked plugins directory | the refusal is taken out; the stage is matched by path spelling (`source_dir.starts_with(stage)`) |

Run on `master` c473221313 plus this patch, on Linux:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib -- <the 8 tests above>` | 8 passed |
| the same 8 tests with each change from the red column applied, then reverted | each change fails exactly the tests whose row names it, and no others |
| `cargo test -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib` | 425 passed |
| `cargo test -p zeroclaw-plugins --lib` | 286 passed |
| `cargo test --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --bin zeroclaw -- plugin` | 164 passed |
| `cargo test -p zeroclaw-plugins --test legacy_plugin_migrate` | 11 passed |
| `cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-plugins -- --check` | clean |
| `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-plugins --all-targets --features plugins-wasm-cranelift -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` on both changed `.rs` files | passed |
| `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` and `scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh` on both changed docs | 0 markdownlint errors; no added links |

The second commit, at head 4f72cd21b9 (`master` c473221313 plus both commits), run on macOS (aarch64), lib tests only:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib -- <the 2 new tests>` | 2 passed |
| the same with `-- <the 8 tests above>` | 8 passed |
| the 2 new tests with each change from their red column applied, then reverted | the refusal taken out fails both; matching by path spelling fails only the spelling test |
| `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --lib` | 288 passed |
| `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps -p zeroclaw-plugins` | clean |

v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.
